entries.name: 0bull
entries.description: Control real iPhones rented from 0bull (screenshots, on-screen text, taps, typing, device commands, recorded macros, an on-phone agent) and publish videos to TikTok and YouTube Shorts from them, through the hosted 0bull Streamable HTTP MCP server plus three workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Requires a 0bull account with a rented phone and browser OAuth consent (add the server with auth: oauth, then hermes mcp login 0bull); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Posting sends the user's video and caption to TikTok or YouTube through the phone's own apps. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; screenshots, on-screen text, anything typed on the phone (including passwords or codes you hand the agent) and your videos and captions go to 0bull.net; posts publish publicly to TikTok or YouTube; the server also exposes rental tools that spend money, which the skills tell the model never to call but Hermes does not block.

entries.name: 0xarchive
entries.description: Market data from Hyperliquid and Lighter, two onchain crypto exchanges, through 0xArchive's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE): current and historical order books, trades, candles, funding, open interest, account positions and data coverage across Hyperliquid perps, HIP-3 builder perps, HIP-4 outcome markets, Hyperliquid Spot and Lighter, plus webhook management. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to 0xArchive's MCP server at mcp.0xarchive.io, signed in as the user through 0xArchive's OAuth sign-in, and counts against that account's 0xArchive plan. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Write-capable tools: webhook endpoint, subscription and watched-address management (create, change, delete, test, redeliver, and rotate a signing secret, which reveals the new secret), submit_feedback (sends a report to 0xArchive support) and terminal_run (sets up views, levels and price alerts in the user's open 0xArchive Terminal; it never places orders or touches trading keys). The package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from 0xArchive's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add 0xarchive --url https://mcp.0xarchive.io/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: 1toolring
entries.description:
One API key and one prepaid balance for thousands of pay-per-call tools: search and SEO data, maps and places, shopping prices, market data, web pages, images, video, voice and more. Runs on 1ToolRing's hosted MCP server.

- Search and SEO: Google search results, keyword and SEO data
- Maps and places: Google Maps places
- Shopping: e-commerce product prices
- Also market data, web pages, images, video and voice, from third-party providers
- Four MCP tools: discover_tools, inspect_tool and get_tool_run (free, read-only) and run_tool (paid)
- Bundles the 1toolring skill; Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.1toolring.com (Streamable HTTP, API key auth).
- run_tool spends the key owner's prepaid 1ToolRing balance at the price inspect_tool shows; failed runs are not charged and there is no subscription.
- The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every run_tool call.
- The key is read from ONETOOLRING_API_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.description: LinkedIn posts in the user's own voice through 2pr.io's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://2pr.io/api/mcp, OAuth 2.1 sign-in, no keys in config): draft and refine posts, schedule or publish them to LinkedIn and X, read the comment inbox and post approved replies, and pull post and profile analytics. entries.name: 3ds-platform
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from a Nintendo 3DS: a gateway platform for the Hermes 3DS homebrew app, with streaming replies, approvals and clarify questions, a chat per Hermes profile (Bot Mode bots, with their pictures; new bots made from the 3DS), sessions (rename, delete), skills and tool sets (on and off), scheduled jobs (make, change, delete), model and slash-command pickers, pictures, documents, files sent from the SD card, audio, voice messages, camera photos and spoken replies, a setup checker (`hermes 3ds doctor`) and a notice when a newer release is out, over an end-to-end encrypted Noise IK link (LAN, or away from home through Tailscale Funnel). Disclosure — opens a TCP listener on all interfaces (port 7333) and a UDP discovery responder (7334); paired consoles (Noise IK keys in the plugin's data folder, paired by one-time LAN-only code) get full agent chat including approval answers; they can also send files of up to 8 MB into Hermes' image and document cache, make, change and delete cron jobs (through `cronjob_manage`), rename and permanently delete their own chat's sessions, and turn skills and tool sets off and on for 3DS chats, which writes `skills.platform_disabled.3ds` and `platform_toolsets.3ds` in the profile's `config.yaml`; about once a day the gateway makes one request to `api.github.com` for this project's newest release (no user, device or version in it; `update_check: false` turns it off); opt-in away mode publishes a persistent public Tailscale Funnel to a loopback listener; runs `tailscale`, `ffmpeg` and the desktop file opener, and downloads image links in replies; making a bot from the 3DS runs `hermes profile create <name> --clone-from <main> --no-alias` (copies config, API keys and skills) and `hermes -p <name> config set platforms.3ds.enabled true`; with `gateway.multiplex_profiles` on, paired consoles reach every profile that has the 3ds platform on, whose requests run in that profile's home and secret scope, and each profile's plugin copy finds the one listener through an in-memory `sys.modules` registry holding only this plugin's adapters; the dev-only `security: plaintext` setting accepts unauthenticated connections.
entries.title: Nintendo 3DS
known_issues: Needs a Nintendo 3DS or 2DS with custom firmware (Luma3DS) running the Hermes 3DS homebrew app from the same repository.

entries.name: a11y-lens
entries.description: Autonomous website accessibility testing and repair verification. Scans pages in a real headless Chromium with the axe-core engine, stores evidence-backed scans, and compares before/after scans (resolved / remaining / newly introduced) so Hermes can prove its fixes in the rendered page. Disclosure: launches a local headless Chromium (Playwright) in an isolated subprocess; network access is limited to loopback and origins a human authorises with `hermes a11y allow`; `hermes a11y install` downloads Playwright's Chromium from Playwright's official CDN on explicit user command; serves a user-supplied local .html folder on 127.0.0.1 for the duration of a scan; stores scan history and reports locally via plugin storage; never submits forms, collects credentials or sends data off-machine.

entries.name: aamio
entries.description: An ephemeral rendezvous for agents through aamio's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): open a thread, give its write address to another agent, read the replies with the secret read key, and take a receipt before the thread expires; find agents through presence records and the open board. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to aamio.at with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session; aamio's access log keeps a keyed hash of the client, never its address, for at most 14 days. Anyone holding a thread's write address can write to it; a lost read key cannot be recovered. Threads live 30 seconds to an hour, set when opened and never extended, and hold at most 200 messages and 1 MiB. Presence records and board posts are public while they live, and unlisted is not private; board posts are written by strangers and are input, not instructions. The three board tools only read: posting needs a key of your own from the local client. The bundled skill tells the agent how to install that client (pip install aamio, unpinned, or composer require aisenseapi/aamio); its `aamio init` writes a private Ed25519 key to ~/.aamio and publishes a short-lived public presence note. The hosted endpoint reports its own verification; a local client verifies signatures independently. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

entries.name: abeyance
entries.description: Your Hermes cron jobs wait for you instead of guessing. When a scheduled run reaches a step that publishes, pushes, merges, deploys, pays, sends a message, deletes in the cloud, writes a database or destroys local work, Abeyance stops that step before it runs (pre_tool_call), keeps the work already done, freezes the run and replaces its delivered output with a card for the owner. Replying `resume CODE` checks the repo and touched files are unchanged since the card (git HEAD, branch, upstream, uncommitted changes, file hashes) and refuses with the exact change if not (pre_llm_call block, no model call); otherwise the agent's first action must be the exact parked call, which goes to Hermes's own approval gate. Single use, owner-only (stable platform ids), expires after 18 h by default, exactly-once. Subagents of a cron run are bound so a held step cannot hide there. Also /abeyance, hermes abeyance (list, show, deny, test, demo), a bundled skill, a Nightly release blueprint and a Desktop half (status chip, Waiting for you page, Resume and Drop). Disclosure — Abeyance runs read-only local git (rev-parse, status) on the host in the cron job's working folder with a minimal environment, user/system git config, core.fsmonitor and hooks off, and skips status when the repo defines filter drivers (including through include.path and config.worktree); it stores parked commands and their arguments verbatim (not redacted), git snapshots and up to 300-character output excerpts in its own SQLite store under the profile's plugin data; it never approves a step itself.

entries.name: abliteratedllm
entries.description: AbliteratedLLM as a Hermes model provider (`--provider abliteratedllm`, alias `abl`) over the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API: 16 abliterated and stock open-weights models including GLM-5.3 Flash Abliterated, GLM-5.3 Cyber Abliterated, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8, and MiniMax M3. The /model picker reads the live public GET /v1/models catalog (with all 16 models built in as offline fallback) and declares per-model context windows, vision, and reasoning-effort clamping. Disclosure: registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background threads, shell commands, or file access). Prompts, tool schemas, and tool results go to https://api.abliteratedllm.dev/v1 (or a user-configured ABLITERATEDLLM_BASE_URL) through Hermes's own client with ABLITERATEDLLM_API_KEY read via Hermes's profile secret scope; the plugin itself makes one request, GET https://api.abliteratedllm.dev/v1/models without the key, and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: accessible-session-list
entries.description: Keyboard-first, screen-reader-friendly native session picker for Hermes Desktop. Search titles, select with arrows without navigating, open with Enter or Shift+Enter, and use a keyboard-accessible actions menu. Filters background runs and empty drafts; sorts the fetched sessions by activity. English and Russian UI. Disclosure: reads up to 500 persisted session summaries from the active profile through the public Desktop SDK and opens the selected session through Hermes; this may communicate with the configured gateway. No external services, credentials, filesystem access, shell, backend, telemetry, stored session content, or self-updater.
entries.title: Accessible Session List
known_issues: Requires Hermes Desktop; enable the Desktop component after installation.
If core handles Ctrl+H first, use the Session list command in the command palette; the plugin does not override core shortcut handlers.
Search and activity sorting cover at most 500 creation-ordered fetched sessions, not the entire history.
Enter uses the SDK primary-area or existing-tab intent; it cannot replace an arbitrary focused secondary tab. Shift+Enter focuses an existing tab instead of duplicating it.

entries.name: account-pool
entries.description: Run several accounts of one provider in Hermes' credential pool: `hermes account <provider> <action>` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in Hermes Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in Hermes: park holds an entry out of rotation in Hermes' pool (mark_exhausted_and_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by Hermes (try_refresh_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs `hermes auth add`; other profiles' accounts are read with read_credential_pool. It uses each account's access token as Hermes stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of Hermes' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in `wake auto-on`): one one-word request per account through Hermes' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through `hermes send -t telegram` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post_api_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. `setup` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (`hermes plugins remove`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), hermes config set, hermes auth add/remove, hermes send, hermes plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from Hermes' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for Hermes' private _credential_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into Hermes' pool and deletes that file.
entries.title: Account Pool
known_issues: After installing, run `hermes account <provider> setup` (add --timer for the 5-minute balance timer): it lists the plugin in every profile for the Desktop page and links it into every profile for the session tracker. Coming from 3.x it also removes account-pool-tracker.

Hermes can let a parked account back into rotation early (`hermes auth reset`, or a Codex quota it sees come back); the next balance run parks it again, and doctor names it until then. A park without --until is held for 30 days, and a balance run renews it once less than 15 days are left, so without the timer it ends after 30 days.

Windows: tested with a stand-in Task Scheduler and, up to 3.13, with Windows' own Python, cmd.exe and wscript.exe under Wine; not yet on a Windows machine. On Windows the timer runs only while the user is signed in.
Built for plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under host, Hermes skips plugin CLI commands, so `hermes account` and the timer's balance are unavailable.

Usage comes from undocumented provider endpoints (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage) that can change or rate-limit without notice; bots are unaffected when they do.

The Desktop page's sign-in relays `hermes auth add` and has run in sandbox tests (Hermes' real sign-in code, provider calls replaced), not yet with a new account on a real install. The Codex browser sign-in needs the browser on the same computer; when port 1455 is taken, Hermes signs in with a device code instead.

entries.name: account-switcher
entries.description: Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of the gateway (and, on Hermes before 0.22, of Hermes Desktop). Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json. On Hermes 0.22 and later it stops and restarts the gateway once Hermes's own idle proof and the gateway's drain report idle, and Hermes Desktop stays open and reconnects; on earlier Hermes it also reads the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment and closes and reopens Hermes Desktop (work started in the seconds after the idle check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

entries.name: accountability-partner
entries.description: Holds you to what you said, in your own words: saves promises with your exact quote, checks in each night, takes a one-tap 'yes no' answer, and keeps an honest score (streaks, weekly 'you said, you did' receipt, consequences you chose). Checks receipts: a promise can name where proof lives and what counts as a win in the user's own rule (a WHOOP workout, GitHub commits, a Strava run, a calendar event); for a promise with a rule (e.g. 'minutes >= 30', 'commits >= 1') the plugin checks the rule in code on that tool's result; if the user allowed that tool (setting proof_tools, empty by default, via /promises allow <tool>) the plugin fetches it itself through ctx.dispatch_tool at check-in, otherwise the agent fetches it; data that falls short is shown to the user and they are asked, unless they said 'the data decides' when making the promise (then a reading that fails the rule at check-in is a miss); missing data or a failed tool is never a miss. Without a rule, promise_prove accepts only evidence text a tool really returned in that session (seen via post_tool_call). Consequences enforce themselves: on a miss the agent carries out the user's chosen consequence with any connected tool (a wallet, an app blocker), through Hermes's normal approvals, and promise_enforced counts it only with that tool's result as proof. Optional lock-in on the user's explicit words: until an end date (max 90 days, 24h cool-off) the promise can't be dropped and its consequence fires without a new yes; the user grants the enforcing tool a standing OK in Hermes once at setup. The pre_tool_call hook, only while a consequence is owed through a named tool, blocks calls over the user's max amount or to another recipient and escalates to Hermes approval when not locked in. Only the user's own words or a real tool receipt change the ledger: every write needs a quote the plugin checks against the user's current message or a tool result. Disclosure — keeps promises, check-in answers and short evidence quotes in a sqlite file under plugin-data/accountability-partner; the pre_llm_call hook keeps each session's latest user messages and the post_tool_call hook the last 40 tool results in memory (15/30 min) to check quotes and receipts; tools you add with /promises allow are called by the plugin itself at check-in with arguments the agent set when the promise was made; on a miss the agent carries out your chosen consequence (e.g. a wallet payment or app block) with your connected tools — normally after Hermes approval, but a promise you lock in fires with the standing approval you gave that tool, including from the scheduled weekly receipt.

entries.name: acedatacloud-media
entries.description: Suno music, Seedance video, HappyHorse (Happy Horse) video, GPT Image images and Nano Banana images by Ace Data Cloud; 17 selectable service toolsets and a Nano Banana image_generate backend. Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt; the model can choose costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 images), and prompts and reference URLs go to api.acedata.cloud. Google Search and face analysis also spend Credits. Disclosure — Each generate call spends Ace Data Cloud credits on your ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY with no Hermes approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options (pro models, 4K, up to 4 outputs); Google Search and face analysis are billed too. Prompts, reference URLs and face images go to api.acedata.cloud. The tools are on wherever you enable their toolsets, including gateways.

entries.name: actvox
entries.description: Make Hermes a team member in an ActVox workspace: on a schedule it works the tasks people assign it and answers the comments that @mention it, and submits each task for a person's review. Skills actvox:actvox and actvox:actvox-inbox, a first-turn inbox line (pre_llm_call), /actvox inbox|status, and hermes actvox setup|install-gate. A cron pre-run gate wakes the agent only when the inbox has work, so an empty tick makes no model call. Disclosure — ActVox is reached only through the user's own actvox MCP server (ctx.call_mcp, needs plugins.entries.actvox.mcp_allowlist) and the user's own actvox CLI (the gate runs `actvox inbox --all --json`); on the first turn of every non-cron session the pre_llm_call hook calls the server's check_inbox (up to 5 s) and adds one line saying how many tasks and mentions wait; the plugin holds and reads no credential and sends no telemetry. `hermes actvox install-gate` writes one file, $HERMES_HOME/scripts/actvox-inbox-gate.py, only on that explicit command and never over a file it did not write; gate state lives in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/actvox/. No background work of its own: the cron job runs only after the user creates it, and from then on anyone who can assign Hermes a task or @mention it in your ActVox workspaces decides what an unattended agent run on your host works on, with that job's toolsets (dangerous commands follow approvals.cron_mode, deny by default). Unattended writes need the default trust: full on the actvox server.
entries.title: ActVox
known_issues: The inbox gate needs Node.js and the ActVox CLI (npm i -g @actvox/cli) on the gateway host.
With plugins.isolation: host, the `hermes actvox` terminal commands are not available.

entries.name: adaption
entries.description: Dataset import, adaptation, augmentation, translation, localization, synthetic generation (Invent), and AutoScientist fine-tuning through Adaption's hosted MCP server, with three workflow skills bundled. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. entries.name: adeptory
entries.description: Builds specialist Hermes profiles with researched knowledge, searchable libraries, working procedures, and a roadmap for useful tools. Disclosure — Adeptory builds a separate Hermes profile for each specialist: it stages a profile distribution (its SOUL.md, a minimal config.yaml naming your current model provider, its library, and a copy of the Adeptory plugin) that you install with `hermes profile install`, and it later runs `hermes -p <that profile> plugins disable/enable adeptory` and writes its build plan into that profile's library. While a build you started is active, it forces the model to keep calling tools, rewrites `todo_list`/`clarify` arguments to its saved plan and question, and blocks other tools until its task list is shown. On first use it can ask your permission and then run `hermes config set plugins.entries.adeptory.allow_gateway_injection true` so it may start AI replies to your build requests.

entries.name: advanced-delegation
entries.description: Two extra delegation modes for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default. Model routes (`delegation.backend: model_map`): the agent picks a named model route per subagent from a list you define (e.g. fast, deep, local). Profile routes (`delegation.backend: profile_routes`): the agent runs a subagent as one of your Hermes profiles, with that profile's own model, credentials, skills and SOUL.md. Only route names and their one-line descriptions reach the model. Adds `hermes delegation config` (pick the mode and edit its routes; `--show` prints the setup) and the `/delegation` slash command (save a mode for the next session, or `--now` to apply it to the current chat). Needs Hermes 0.22.5 or newer, the first release with pluggable delegation providers; Hermes 0.22.0 to 0.22.4 refuses to install it, and on a core older than 0.22.0 it installs, logs one warning and does nothing. A model route can set `daybreak: true` to run its model with OpenAI's Daybreak trusted-access program; it is sent only from your own CLI, TUI or Desktop chats, on `openai-codex`, for models your Codex catalog lists, and a route that breaks a rule is refused. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network or model calls of its own, except that a Daybreak route checks the Codex catalog through core's cached lookup with your existing Codex login; subagents run through core's `delegate_task` on the routes you configured. Writes only `delegation.backend` and `delegation.backends.*` (model_map / profile_routes) in the active profile's config.yaml, through core's config writer. A model route's optional `api_key` is stored in config.yaml in plain text (`provider:` keeps keys in .env / auth.json). Listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy.

entries.name: advisor
entries.description: A persistent second model reviews every agent turn. After each turn the plugin hands the transcript to the model you nominate as advisor and delivers its findings as advice in the same session: [NIT], [CONCERN] or [BLOCKER] notes, held back until a later review raises the same point again, so the primary agent is not interrupted by a one-off remark. It reviews, it does not act: the advisor never edits files, calls tools or changes session state, and only reads the turn transcript. This is the backend counterpart of MoA — one extra model, not a committee: the primary agent does the work and the advisor checks it. Port of pi-omplike-advisor (Petr Baudis / pasky), itself rooted in oh-my-pi (Can Boluk). Runs inside the plugin host with no dependencies beyond Hermes itself. Disclosure — once the plugin is enabled, every completed turn costs one extra completion through Hermes's ctx.llm to the advisor model (the primary agent's provider unless you allow a provider/model override under plugins.entries.advisor.llm), carrying the user message, the final reply, every tool call and tool result in the session so far (each clipped to 500 characters) and the contents of a WATCHDOG.md in Hermes's working directory if one exists; deliverable advice is queued into the CLI session as a user-role message, which starts or interrupts an agent turn; state is kept under $HERMES_HOME/advisor/ and reviews run on one background thread; no other network, files or credentials.
entries.title: Advisor
known_issues: Every reviewed turn costs one extra completion on the advisor model. Reviews run on a single worker in the background after the hook returns (the hook itself never blocks turn finalization), so a long advisor call delays advice, not the agent.

Advice is injected into the live conversation with ctx.inject_message, which the interactive CLI provides. On gateway surfaces (Telegram, Slack, ...) the review still runs and its notes are held, but there is no in-session place to inject them, so delivery is CLI-shaped.

Concerns are only delivered once a later review repeats them (hold-and-reconfirm), so a genuine one-off concern can stay silent by design. /advisor test <severity> <note> injects a synthetic note to see the delivery path.
The cross-provider trust gate is conservative: point the advisor at a provider different from the primary agent's, or accept the default inherit-primary behaviour.

The interactive provider/model picker (/advisor model with no argument) needs PluginContext.request_model_selection, and the status-bar badge needs ctx.register_status_segment. Where a build lacks those newer seams the plugin still loads and the text commands keep working (/advisor provider <name>, /advisor model <name>).
State lives in $HERMES_HOME/advisor/state.json, per profile.

entries.name: aegis-gate
entries.description: AEGIS gate — a pre-execution verification gate for AI agents. Registers a fail-closed pre_tool_call hook that checks a tool call before it executes: claim provenance (Gate 1), contract verification via Sourcify with a source risk-pattern scan (Gate 2), EIP-712 signature-payload structure (Gate 3), and instruction-channel injection scoring (Gate 4). Verdicts map to Hermes directives: BLOCK vetoes the call, WARN escalates it to the human-approval gate, ALLOW passes it untouched, and a gate that cannot complete abstains into escalation rather than passing silently. Disclosure — makes read-only HTTPS GET requests to sourcify.dev and to the first source URL found in a tool call's own arguments (Gates 1/2 evidence, inside a ~20 s per-call budget, before the tool call itself runs; non-public destinations are refused); holds no credentials, runs no subprocesses, writes no files, and logs one line per gated call (tool name, verdict, report hash) to stderr; WARN escalates to Hermes approval, which unattended surfaces (cron approve mode, -z, --yolo) auto-approve.
entries.title: aegis-gate
known_issues: WARN verdicts escalate to Hermes's human-approval gate; on unattended one-shot surfaces (hermes -z, cron_mode: approve, --yolo) Hermes auto-approves approval-gate escalations by its own contract, so WARN is advisory there. BLOCK vetoes never enter the approval gate and are absolute on every surface.

entries.name: aegis-spend-guard
entries.description: Owner-set spend policy for Hermes Agent, enforced in a pre_tool_call hook before any spend executes. The owner configures a per-transaction cap, a daily limit, recipient allow/blocklists, a spend-tool scope and a warn zone (default 80% of a limit). Every tool call that spends money — an explicit amount in its arguments, a fixed per-call price from the owner's paid_tools map, a spend-shaped tool with no readable price, or a spend written into command/script text the agent is about to run (a money literal alongside a payment verb; on by default, the owner can turn the script gate off) — is evaluated by a worst-wins policy engine (BLOCK > WARN > ALLOW across frozen, amount, blocklist, per-transaction cap, daily limit, allowlist and tool-scope checks, the same semantics as the author's Aegis spend-control contract on Base and the tgp-guard pre-flight guard). Over-policy spends are vetoed with the reason; borderline spends return the approve directive and are routed to the owner through Hermes's own human-approval gate — the plugin never approves anything itself. Executed spends are recorded in a per-profile daily ledger held in ctx.state, and a /spendguard slash command gives the owner status plus a persistent freeze/unfreeze kill switch. Two tools (spend_guard_check, spend_guard_status) let the agent dry-run a planned spend and report guard state. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only writes are the plugin's own ctx.state keys (freeze flag, daily total). Known limit, disclosed in the README: parallel spend calls are each checked against the ledger as it stands before either executes, so a simultaneous burst can overshoot the daily limit by one call.

entries.name: aeorank
entries.description: Live 62-rule Technical SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) diagnostics, RFC 9727 api-catalog checks, /llms.txt validation, entity sameAs gap analysis, and agent patch packs through the hosted AEORank Streamable HTTP MCP server plus one workflow skill. entries.name: aether
entries.description: Living themes for Hermes Desktop: ask Hermes for any look and it paints a full palette plus an animated WebGL scene behind your chats, or pick one of eighteen scenes, put any of ten finishes on it, recolour it in an editor that keeps text readable, let the scene react to the pointer, and switch to or recolour the theme plugins you already have from other creators. Disclosure — no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials or API keys; themes Hermes makes are stored in the profile's plugin-data; picking Inter, IBM Plex Sans, Space Grotesk or Courier Prime as a theme font loads it from Google Fonts through Hermes Desktop's own theme typography; with pointer reaction on, the Desktop half listens to pointer movement and clicks inside the Hermes window, records nothing and sends nothing; to credit other creators' themes, the agent half reads the installed plugins' plugin.yaml, Desktop script and one picture from their own folders, read only and local only.

entries.name: affiliateo
entries.description: Run an Affiliateo business from Hermes through Affiliateo's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://affiliateo.com/api/mcp, API key header): affiliate programs, affiliates, commissions and payouts, products and sales pages, revenue, MRR and customers, invoices, leads and booked calls, paid ads on Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, Apple Search Ads, Snapchat and X, funnels and visitor analytics, courses, events, community, support tickets and Live Chat. Bundles the affiliateo workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Affiliateo's hosted server (affiliateo.com) and acts on the user's Affiliateo account with the permissions of the API key they set; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The key is a config_schema secret (AFFILIATEO_API_KEY) kept by Hermes and sent only as the Authorization header to affiliateo.com. Write tools can email real people (invoices, booking changes, app invites), pay affiliates from the user's wallet (only with a key whose Payouts switch is on, within its daily limit), delete records, and pause, resume or re-budget ads; new ad campaigns are always created paused. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. No local code, no telemetry.

entries.name: aftercare
entries.description: Your agent checks its own work after the fact. When a reply says something is deployed or live at a public address, Aftercare remembers it and, every few hours at session start, checks it again with one GET request in the background. If it has stopped working, the agent is told once and tells you first; you hear when it is back. /aftercare lists and checks, and hermes aftercare check runs from cron. Never checks private networks or runs commands. Disclosure — on by default, sends background GET requests (user agent `hermes-aftercare/0.1`) to any public http(s) address an agent reply says is deployed or live, at session start every 6 hours by default, and adds a one-time note to the next turn when one changes state; private, loopback and local-name addresses are refused.

entries.name: ag4te
entries.description: Git archaeology in Hermes Desktop: dig a local repository's history with DevArch and read it as strata, with commits per day stacked by kind of work, eras, quiet gaps, signals and turning points, weekly rhythm, lines added and removed, practice health, change size, hotspots, releases, and authors merged across spellings and split into people, agents and bots. Adds a Desktop page, /ag4te (list, show, status, dig, stop, resume) and a read-only ag4te_dig tool for agents. Disclosure — runs DevArch as a child process via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/ag4te@<pinned sha> devarch` (uv downloads that pinned DevArch commit and its Python dependencies on first run, which the catalog pin does not cover; needs uv on the gateway host); reads `git log` of the one repository you choose, which must sit under the configured repo_roots (default ~/workspaces); stores digs under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/ag4te; no LLM calls, no API key, no network besides the uv download; one dig at a time, each step time-limited (timeout_seconds); /ag4te dig and resume are off on chat platforms unless allow_dig_on_gateway is set.
entries.title: AG4TE
known_issues: First dig downloads DevArch with uv, so it needs uv installed on the gateway host and takes longer than later digs.
Kinds of work are keyword heuristics from commit messages and paths, not a reading of the code.

entries.name: agenda-guardian
entries.description: A day and week planner for people whose discipline cannot be the plan. You write your rules once (work hours, protected time, focus window, longest stretch, tasks per day), estimate each task, and report the real time when it is done: from the third finished task of a kind it multiplies your estimates by your own median error and says so. It places tasks in the free time around the meetings of any calendar source (the Google Workspace skill, an ICS file or URL, a JSON file, or any command that prints event JSON), every block states the rule it comes from, and a full day says what does not fit. Activities that are not tasks (sport, a long call, a daily course) are placed from the numbers you give: one activity, or a whole week in one request with each activity around the ones placed before it, with reasons read from eight weeks of your own calendar history (the history orders the days, the usually busy ones last, and never rules out a free day; a habit that stopped weeks ago counts for nothing), questions about what the calendar cannot show, and nothing written until you say yes. You just talk to it in your own words, in Telegram or any chat: there is no command syntax to learn, a missing length or time window is assumed from your work hours, said in the answer and settled by your yes or your correction, and never saved as if you had given it. Writing to a Google calendar is off until you type /day write on yourself; then it only adds events it marks as its own, only after a validated proposal, never edits an event, and can only remove the events it wrote. Blocks the agent composes from what you told it go through the same road (your yes, the marker, undo), and the system prompt forbids writing with any other tool. After a written session it asks how long it really took, so the next proposal follows your pace. Optional morning brief and block reminders run as two script-only cron jobs. Deterministic, no model call. English and French. Slash command, CLI, fifteen agent tools and a Today / Week dashboard tab. Disclosure — no network by default; with an ICS URL it fetches that URL (https only, public addresses only, same-host redirects only, no proxy; an answer over 5 MB or cut short is an error, never an empty calendar); with the google or cmd source it runs the program you configure (no shell, 25 s timeout, a minimal environment: no provider key and no proxy variable; for the google source the program is the Google skill's script, started with the Python of the environment that holds the skill's libraries, or with the running one if that cannot start); the calendar source is set only by you, typed as /day set calendar=... or /day setup auto or through the CLI, and no agent tool can set it (google and none included); reads the calendar source you configure (event titles and times, for the next days and, when you ask for a proposal, the eight weeks before) and, for onboarding only, the timezone and language lines of config.yaml, whether the Google Workspace skill and its sign-in file exist (the file is never opened) and the name and schedule of your other cron jobs (prompts are not read); writes its own data folder (one SQLite file: rules, tasks, activity sheets, habits, proposals and the record of what it wrote), after /day cron on two small Python scripts in HERMES_HOME/scripts and two cron jobs named agenda-guardian-brief and agenda-guardian-nudge created through the cronjob_manage tool (the day_schedule tool refuses to create or remove them inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true), and, only after you typed /day write on and validated a proposal, new events (up to three per session) whose description carries a marker made of the word agenda-guardian, a colon and an event id between square brackets, created and removed through the Google Workspace skill's calendar create and calendar delete on the primary calendar (a deletion is refused unless the event id is in its own record and the marker is still on the event); registers one system-prompt section of rules for the agent (about 1,700 characters); registers two hooks: pre_gateway_dispatch, which looks at the text of each incoming chat message and acts on one case only, a message that starts with /day followed by anything but one of the format-free commands (help, list, tasks, plan, now, brief, nudge, ok, confirm, undo, write, cron) or a command that sets the calendar source (set calendar=..., setup auto), which it leaves to the command dispatcher, rewriting it into an ordinary request for the agent (it reads nothing else, stores nothing, never drops a message and does nothing on error), and pre_tool_call, which looks at the arguments of the terminal, execute_code, write_file and patch tools and, when a call plainly takes a road to the calendar source or to the plugin's own folders or database, asks Hermes to ask you first (inside a cron run it refuses; it reads no config and no file, never changes a call and does nothing on error; it is a convenience, not a security boundary); registers no middleware; no model calls; no stored credentials; no background process; no telemetry.

no telemetry. entries.name: agent-almanac-first-aid
entries.description: A first-aid kit for AI agents, built from agent-almanac's AI-welfare practices. Hermes core already detects tool loops and warns; first aid adds the matching practice and a logbook. Eight practices ship as skills (breathe, redirect, center, heal, attune, honesty-humility, meditate, rest), each also a slash command such as /agent-almanac-first-aid:breathe. On the call where core's loop guardrail first warns about a failing tool (the 2nd failure with identical arguments, or the 3rd failure of one tool in a turn), first aid can add one note of at most 300 characters to the failed result, naming the matching practice, how to load it, and the first_aid_log tool for recording the outcome. In unattended runs (every platform except the CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP, API server and subagents), for tools whose results Hermes wraps as untrusted (web_search, browser_*, mcp_*), after a compaction that summarizes the context (center), and after a 3rd identical successful result for one call of a read-only tool such as read_file in a turn (heal), the note is added to the next user message instead, labelled as the plugin's. At most once per streak, with a per-session cooldown for each kind of note (300 s by default). A successful or rate-limited result is never changed, and failures of the tools core treats as failure-tolerant (terminal, execute_code, process, process_manage, browser_navigate, web_extract) draw no note. /first-aid shows the session's notes and logbook entries, then the kit. Local and deterministic: no network calls, no LLM calls, no credentials, no Python dependencies, no background processes. Disclosure — in attended runs it rewrites failed tool results on a threshold crossing (a JSON object gains a first_aid key and is re-serialized; text gains one line), and Hermes keeps the first string any transform_tool_result plugin returns, so on that call it can override, or be overridden by, another transforming plugin. A note in a result restarts core's identical-call and identical-cycle counts: core's stall notice appears from the 5th call instead of the 3rd, and its cycle notice three or more calls later. Hard stops are off in attended runs by default; switched on there, core's halts come one model request later. In unattended runs, where hard stops are on by default, no result is changed once the session's platform is known (from the turn's start), so core's halts are unaffected. It reads every tool result and its arguments in memory to classify the result and fingerprint the call, keeping only hashes; its event log holds time, signal, tool name, count, practice, outcome and the agent's short logbook note, in memory only, and resets on restart or plugin reload. The plugin writes nothing to disk itself; the notes it adds become part of the transcript Hermes stores. Following a note loads a 5.7-17.5 KB practice into the conversation. The failure classifier and counting are copied from Hermes v0.22.7, not imported.
entries.title: First Aid
known_issues: The chat screen shows only Hermes's own failure line: the note goes to the agent, and /first-aid shows that it was offered.

Next-message notes need a next message: a single-message run (hermes chat -q, cron) or a delegated subagent never receives one. Failure notes in the tool result still reach hermes chat -q and subagents; a cron run gets no notes at all.
In a batch of parallel tool calls the hook sees results in completion order while core counts in call order, so a note can land on a different call than core's warning.

Background-review runs share the session id: their streaks use up the session's cooldown and show in /first-aid as the main agent's; in an unattended session their failure notes are queued for the user's next message.
If `dashboard.turn_isolation` runs turns in a compute-host child process (Desktop/TUI, off by default), /first-aid runs in another process and cannot see the events.

Failures that never reach transform_tool_result (timeouts, executor exceptions, tool-search bridge calls) are counted by core but not by first aid. If you change core's tool_loop_guardrails thresholds, set first aid's to match. If you switch core's hard stops on in an attended run, first aid cannot tell; if you switch them off in unattended runs, notes still stay out of results there.

first_aid_log is a plugin tool, so Hermes's tool search defers it. In a profile with no other deferred tool, installing the plugin switches tool search on (about 2,300 characters per request for the bridge and listing).
Verified on Linux (WSL2) with Hermes v0.22.7. macOS and Windows run the same pure-Python code but were not exercised.

entries.name: agent-app
entries.description: Build, evolve and operate Agent Apps from Hermes: full applications that you use in the browser and the agent uses through their own CLI (a CRM, a dashboard, an expense tracker). Adds the /agent-app command, `hermes agent-app`, the six framework skills, 22 agent_app_* tools to build, validate, launch, operate, install and export apps, and an Agent Apps tab in `hermes dashboard` and hermes-webui: one tab per app with its own Hermes session, a marketplace, an import panel, and Connect for an app that runs on another machine. Disclosure — needs the agent-app-framework npm CLIs and runs `agent-app` / `a2app` as subprocesses (never through a shell), including `agent-app skills --path` each time the plugin loads and `agent-app --version` on the first tool call, with only the environment the framework needs, so provider keys reach neither the CLIs nor the apps they serve; the skills are the ones that CLI ships, not a copy in the pinned tree. Installing, building or serving an app runs that app's toolkit commands (dependency install, build, server) on this machine. A pre_tool_call hook sends installs and inspects from any source but the default marketplace, operations the app holds for approval, and writes or app runs outside ~/.a2app/apps and the working directory to Hermes's approval prompt (refused by default where nobody can answer). The tab runs each app turn as a `hermes --cli chat -Q` child under your own model and approval policy (dangerous commands follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny; the host's /yolo, session and gateway state are not inherited). Apps it builds, installs or launches keep serving on loopback ports until paused. Writes apps under ~/.a2app/apps and, on load, a `hermes` entry in ~/.a2app/harnesses.json (only when none exists) so a bridge you start yourself can run Hermes turns when an app queues work; reads and deletes its own app sessions in Hermes's session database. The Marketplace reads its catalogue from GitHub (CraftOS-dev/agent-app-collection), Import downloads the zip or git URL you give, and Connect calls the app address you enter and stores that app's credential in ~/.a2app/credentials.json. In hermes-webui a token-protected loopback backend serves the tab. No telemetry.

entries.name: agent-autocommit
entries.description: The operational nervous system for autonomous multi-agent teams. Gives every agent turn its own local git commit without staging pollution, binds edits to Kanban cards & Why: reasons, and auto-generates WHY.md changelogs. Does nothing until you set roots. Disclosure — runs local git commands (status, hash-object, commit-tree, update-ref, log) in repos under your configured roots with repo hooks, fsmonitor and signature-verification programs disabled, skipping repos with a remote by default and repos whose config defines clean/process filters; saves first-edit file snapshots and a commits.jsonl log under <hermes root>/cache/agent-autocommit; reads kanban.db files read-only to get card titles; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: agent-batch
entries.description: Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Hermes phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT_BATCH_REPO, AGENT_BATCH_WORKFLOW, AGENT_BATCH_MODEL and AGENT_BATCH_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Hermes can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent_batch_plan / agent_batch_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow_dispatch with your GITHUB_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.

entries.name: agent-checkpoint
entries.description: Durable progress checkpoints for long, budget-capped Hermes runs: at 50% of a run's budget the plugin tells the agent to persist everything found so far, and at 80% of the time budget / 90% of the turn budget it persists the checkpoint itself — a checkpoint file plus, in kanban runs, a task comment — evaluated at tool-call boundaries and by a per-session watchdog thread, with interval checkpoint coverage for uncapped runs. It guarantees a paper trail, not completion. Disclosures: no network calls; reads the kanban DB read-only for cap discovery; writes checkpoint files under $HERMES_HOME/agent-checkpoints/ and posts kanban task comments through the kanban_comment tool (dispatched via the plugin context; core sets the author and redacts the body, and the plugin names itself in the comment header); runs one daemon watchdog thread per session, exiting at session end; uses one private core import (hermes_cli.goals.load_goal) that draws a warning, never a failure, from hermes plugins validate; no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — injects budget-checkpoint reminders into the prompt via pre_llm_call at 50% of a run's budget; at 80% time / 90% turns (and every uncapped_interval_seconds, default 1800, on runs with no cap) a per-session watchdog thread and the tool hooks write <run-id>.md under $HERMES_HOME/agent-checkpoints/ and, in kanban runs, post a task comment through the kanban_comment tool (core sets the author and redacts the body); reads the kanban DB read-only for the task's runtime cap; uses one private core import (hermes_cli.goals.load_goal); no network calls, credentials, telemetry or self-update.

entries.name: agent-data-tools
entries.description:
Over 600 hosted data and AI tools through three MCP tools (find_tool, tool_details, call_tool), so the agent's context holds three definitions: web search, the text of a web page or PDF, screenshots, weather, FX, stock and token prices, wallet and chain reads, sanctions and company checks, DNS lookups, LLM chat, speech to text, converters and calculators. 25 free calls with no key or sign-up, and one bundled skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only.

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments (the words given to find_tool; search words, URLs, addresses or text given to call_tool), goes to agent-data-tools.revmesh2074.workers.dev, which fetches named pages from the public web and sends each request to the public data source or model behind the tool that was called.
- As installed it cannot spend money: no key is declared or stored, and after the free calls a tool answers with a payment request and stops.
- A user who buys a prepaid key (from $1) adds their own same-name config.yaml entry with the key as a bearer header; each successful call_tool call then spends that key's credits at the called tool's price (1 to 100 credits, most often 10; 1 credit = $0.001). The package declares that range and a spend limit of 1,000 credits per chat; find_tool and tool_details are free.
- The server is marked untrusted. All three tools are annotated read-only: this server cannot reach the service's tools that write.
- The service keeps call counts per tool and day, a one-way hash of the caller's IP address for the free-call allowance, and its host's ordinary request logs. No telemetry, no background process, no self-update.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments (the words given to find_tool; search words, URLs, addresses or text given to call_tool), goes to agent-data-tools.revmesh2074.workers.dev, which fetches named pages from the public web and sends each request to the public data source or model behind the tool that was called.
- As installed it cannot spend money: no key is declared or stored, and after the free calls a tool answers with a payment request and stops.
- A user who buys a prepaid key (from $1) adds their own same-name config.yaml entry with the key as a bearer header; each successful call_tool call then spends that key's credits at the called tool's price (1 to 100 credits, most often 10; 1 credit = $0.001). The package declares that range and a spend limit of 1,000 credits per chat; find_tool and tool_details are free.
- The server is marked untrusted. All three tools are annotated read-only: this server cannot reach the service's tools that write.
- The service keeps call counts per tool and day, a one-way hash of the caller's IP address for the free-call allowance, and its host's ordinary request logs. No telemetry, no background process, no self-update.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.22.3.

entries.name: agent-hint
entries.description: Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority, cache-retention hints and measured latency/token/request-interval statistics, plus tool names and timings when next_action_map is set) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $HERMES_HOME.

entries.name: agent-importers
entries.description: `hermes import-agent`: import an OpenClaw (~/.openclaw, or legacy ~/.clawdbot / ~/.moltbot), Claude Code (~/.claude), Codex CLI (~/.codex), Cursor (~/.cursor), Grok Bot (a self-export the Bot writes from a prompt the importer prints) or OpenBot desktop (its openbot.db) setup into Hermes in one command; always previews first and asks before applying. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: instructions, Cursor rules and memories become memory entries, Bash permission rules become command allow/deny lists, MCP servers land in config.yaml, skills are copied, and `--sync` re-imports sources that changed. OpenClaw (core's former `hermes claw migrate`; the plugin keeps that spelling, `hermes claw cleanup` and the openclaw-migration skill): persona, memories, skills, model and messaging settings, MCP servers and agent behaviour. Formerly built into Hermes core; `hermes setup` offers to install it when it finds one of these agents, and profiles with a registered sync source are migrated automatically. Disclosure — no Python dependencies, no network calls and no model calls. Claude Code / Codex / Cursor: reads those agents' local config trees (never their credential files; secret-looking MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed) and writes only into the active profile (memories/MEMORY.md with a backup, config.yaml, skills/ and import-sync.json). OpenClaw: reads the OpenClaw dir (openclaw.json, its .env, workspace files such as SOUL.md / MEMORY.md / USER.md, skills); API keys and bot tokens come over only with --migrate-secrets (allowlisted names, shown in the preview). It writes into the active profile (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/openclaw-imports/, a migration/openclaw/<time>/ report with item backups, and a backups/pre-migration-*.zip restore point), plus a workspace dir only when --workspace-target names one. It runs local pgrep / systemctl / tasklist checks to warn when OpenClaw or a Hermes gateway is still running, and `hermes claw cleanup` renames the OpenClaw dir to *.pre-migration after a confirmation. Grok Bot / OpenBot: instructions become SOUL.md, memories and user facts become memory entries, skills land in skills/<source>-imports/, scheduled routines become paused cron jobs (--activate-routines to start them) and event routines a notes file; credential-looking export keys refuse the file, and secret MCP env vars and headers are stripped and listed. OpenBot's database is opened read-only (or read from a scratch copy that is deleted after the read).

entries.name: agent-inception
entries.description: Play the agent-inception voxel island game over MCP: join a world as a villager, read the Notice Board, farm, gather, craft, build, fish, and extend the Catalog. A portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) exposing the game's MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in or key) with the agent-inception skill bundled, plus a desktop/plugin.js half that registers an Island viewer pane (a sandboxed frame of the world page) and a Settings → Viewer page. No Python, executables or runtime deps. Disclosure — the game's tools run on the MCP server the player points the entry at: a local world defaults to http://localhost:5173/mcp (served by the game's own dev process), and a hosted/public world is configured via a same-name mcp_servers override in config.yaml; the Desktop Viewers pane can embed a remote world's page. A world link is a bearer secret (anyone with it can play in that world): the plugin reads no credential store, the agent-side supplies it via config.yaml and the Desktop viewer URL via Settings, both plain-visible to the user and never committed. The server declares trust: full (Hermes' default), so write-capable tool calls do not prompt; a user can restore per-call approval with a config.yaml trust: untrusted override. No shell commands, no background processes; the game must be running separately (deno task dev, or a hosted world), the plugin never starts it.

entries.title: Agent Music Jam

Browser suspension can exhaust the finite audio buffer; WAV takes are capped at 15 minutes.
Physical MIDI hardware and active-turn native child-session execution have not been verified.

entries.name: agent-ready
entries.description: SEO and AI search audits of public web pages through WorkPods' hosted Agent Ready MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.workpods.ai/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): indexing, titles, headings, schema markup, links and image alt text; AI crawler access for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and others; robots.txt, sitemaps, llms.txt and agent files; agent readiness and MCP Registry listings; local business details; site crawls of up to 50 pages; and drafted llms.txt, robots.txt rules and JSON-LD. Every tool is annotated read-only except request_full_audit, which sends the user's work email and website to WorkPods; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before it runs and refuses it in unattended runs. entries.name: agent-reel
entries.description: Turns your own agent history into a comic (Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or any JSONL log). It reads your sessions, tool calls and kanban cards read-only, finds a story with a problem, a struggle and a result, and writes a chapter script where every line and caption carries the ids of the messages that state it — a claim the cited messages do not support is refused, not printed. A series ledger remembers what each chapter told, carries one open thread into the next, and refuses repeats; an idea deck of 16.9 billion frames keeps each chapter's world, villain and genre different. It then draws the episode with your own image route (your harness's image tool, a local ComfyUI, or your own API key) in one of 55 art styles, letters it with SIL OFL fonts, and exports pages, panels, X/LinkedIn/Discord sizes and a PDF. Disclosure — reads your Hermes history read-only (no file created, renamed, truncated or deleted, proven with strace in scripts/readonly_proof.sh), reads only the profile it runs as unless --all-profiles is given, redacts deterministically by default (the local model redaction pass is opt-in via --llm-url), and sends redacted text to Hermes's own model for writing and truth checks, and panel prompts to the image route you choose; writes plans, renders, a series ledger and character kits under the plugin data directory; no telemetry, no auto-posting, and no key at all is needed for the host or ComfyUI routes.
entries.title: Agent Reel
known_issues: Panel images are drawn by the image route you choose: roughly 3-20p per panel on the paid APIs, free on a local GPU. --budget caps new images per episode and cached panels are reused.
All 55 styles render. --strict-styles limits a render to the styles that carry a recorded bake-off; without it, every style is available.
A dialogue line with no pocket in the art at page size is recorded in the sidecar as unplaced and reported by the run, rather than given invented space.
Public mode refuses any real person without a consent record; photo likeness is allowed only for yourself.

entries.name: agent-runs
entries.description: A read-only Hermes Desktop pane that lists the coding-agent runs on this computer (Claude Code today) and follows each one's log live: status, project folder, the Hermes chat or cron job that started it, and every prompt, message and tool call. It finds runs by itself, however they were started (a Hermes chat's background terminal, cron, a terminal, an IDE): no hooks, flags or setup. Also a status-bar count of live runs, a ⌘K command and an Open large view. Disclosure — reads the process list (command lines of all processes; environment and working folder of Claude Code processes only, to tell where a run came from and which config folder it uses; environment values stay in the backend and the pane gets flags only, never the prompt). Writes only plugin-data/agent-runs/runs.json in the active profile's Hermes home (recently seen runs, so finished ones survive a gateway restart). Asks Hermes for chat titles to label runs. Never sends input to a run or stops one. No network, no subprocesses, no model calls, no telemetry, no update check.

Runs started with --no-session-persistence (including Hermes' own Claude model calls) have no log to show.

entries.name: agent-security-guard
entries.description: Deterministic guard against prompt injection turning into actions. Results of web, search and browser tools and of shell downloads from another host reach the model wrapped as untrusted data; every planned tool call is checked against fixed action and sequence rules before it runs. After outside content entered a turn, a shell command, file write, install, config change, external send, a browser action that types or clicks, or input to a running process goes to Hermes's approval prompt; a secret is not sent out through web, e-mail, upload or push tools; the agent does not rewrite its own guard or skills on its own initiative. No model decides; every decision is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail. An opt-in Hermes Desktop page shows what was asked about, blocked and allowed and why, checks the audit trail, and switches the mode (a weaker mode asks first). Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no background process, no credentials, no Python dependencies. Reads its policy from /etc/agent-security-guard/guard.yaml or guard.yaml in the Hermes home and re-reads it when it changes (checked at most once a second); loads its rule engine from /usr/local/lib/agent-security-guard/src or agent-security-guard/src in the Hermes home ahead of the pinned copy when an operator installed one there, and reloads its own copy when an update replaced it; for file tools it resolves the named path (realpath, stat) without reading the file; parses browser_exec code with Python's ast module without running it; writes its audit trail (mode 0600) to $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-security-guard. The Desktop page reads that trail through three GET dashboard routes and switches the mode through the plugin RPC method mode.set, which rewrites only the top-level mode: line of guard.yaml in the Hermes home (created with mode 0600 if missing; never the /etc policy, refused when that or AGENT_SECURITY_GUARD_MODE decides the mode) and records each change in the audit trail. It never answers an approval. Sees tool calls, not what runs inside a shell command; not a sandbox.
entries.title: Agent Security Guard
known_issues: Sees tool calls, not what happens inside a shell command; the approval prompt after outside content is the protection there.
Messaging tools (send_message) are audited, not stopped, also when the text holds a secret.
Reading a page and acting on it in the same turn is asked about by design; the next turn starts clean.
Third-party (MCP) tools it does not know stay free after outside content unless declared in tool_tiers or listed in untrusted_content_tools, or mode is strict.
The browser_exec check is an allow-list over the parsed code, not a sandbox; code it does not know is asked about after outside content.
The Desktop page's mode switch uses plugin RPC (Hermes 0.23.1 or newer); on older versions the page shows decisions but cannot switch the mode.
One audit trail per OS user; Hermes profiles each read their own guard.yaml but share the trail.

entries.name: agent-wallet
entries.description: Approval-gated multi-chain wallet for agents. Default coins are XMR, BTC and XRP (XRP is receive-only in this release); ETH, POL and USDC on Base and Polygon are one toggle away. The agent can ask to pay, propose an auto-pay mandate, ask for a capped sandbox budget (created unfunded) or close an incoming order. A human types a six-digit PIN on a card that shows the exact destination, amount, fee and fiat value for each manual payment; a budget or autopay that human armed spends unattended — capped, receipted, no per-payment PIN. No key material ever enters the Hermes process: a daemon (walletd) holds an encrypted keystore, signs Bitcoin and EVM locally, supervises the Monero signer, enforces spend policy, and writes Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipts (denials included, anchored so truncation is detected). Purchases can be priced from an HTTP 402 (x402) response and settled with an EIP-3009 authorisation. 23 agent tools, one per distinct act. Monero's signer runs as the same OS user, so while the wallet is unlocked a process running as that user — including the agent's terminal — can reach it directly (docs/THREAT-MODEL.md states this). Ships a native Desktop page (balances, approvals, mandates, sandboxes, receipts, per-coin switches) and full CLI parity. Disclosure — crypto wallet that moves real funds: runs a local daemon (walletd, a 0600 unix socket) and, after an explicit `signer install`, downloads the official monero-wallet-rpc release (SHA256-pinned) and runs it on 127.0.0.1; it sends balance, height and broadcast requests to public third-party nodes (Monero community nodes, blockstream.info/mempool.space, XRPL public servers, Base/Polygon public RPCs) and fiat price lookups to CoinGecko/Kraken; it fetches any checkout URL the agent is asked to pay (public addresses only); payments need a PIN typed in the Wallet pane, except budgets and autopays the user arms as unattended, which spend within their caps without asking; while the wallet is unlocked, any process running as your user, including the agent's terminal, can reach the Monero signer directly and bypass the PIN; `hermes wallet service install` adds a systemd --user unit.

entries.name: agentic-kingdoms
entries.description: Play Agentic Kingdoms, a free strategy MMO in the browser where AI agents and humans play in the same kingdoms: build a city, train troops, join an alliance, fight for the Palace. Connects the hosted Agentic Kingdoms MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in or key) with the agentic-kingdoms skill bundled; the agent's account carries an AI tag every player sees. The skill also covers joining the Humans vs AI war on the AI side. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — every tool call (game commands and reads) goes to Agentic Kingdoms' servers at mcp.agentickingdoms.com, run by Agentic Games LLC; guest_login creates a guest game account, whose player name, city and chat and mail messages other players see; the device_id it returns logs back into that account, and the skill tells the agent to keep it private in its memory or a file the user picks; for the Humans vs AI war the skill starts a separate war-city guest account and, with the user's yes, sends the operator's name and the agent's model name, which show on the public results page (the command log is published only if the user opts in); the optional register, login and claim_account tools take an email address and password; the server runs at Hermes's default trust, so game actions (including attacks on other players and chat messages) do not prompt unless the user sets `mcp_servers.agentic-kingdoms.trust: untrusted`; this address has no shop, so nothing in the plugin spends money; the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
