entries.name: agentline
entries.description: A real phone number for Hermes: place calls that a hosted voice carries out and get the transcript back, send and read SMS, text your agent like any other chat, and let a live caller's question reach Hermes mid-call, with the answer spoken on the call or texted if it takes too long. Disclosure — talks only to api.agentline.cloud: HTTPS from the tools, plus one outbound WebSocket (wss://api.agentline.cloud/v1/events/ws) held open while the gateway runs, so no public URL or open port is needed; sends call briefs, text bodies, destination numbers, contacts and the agent's answers to live caller questions; AgentLine carries the call audio and produces transcripts, the plugin never handles audio; calls, texts and numbers are billed to your own AgentLine account; agentline_call, agentline_sms, agentline_buy_number and agentline_agent go through Hermes's approval gate from a pre_tool_call hook, which shows the whole call brief, greeting, voice or text and fails closed when nobody can approve; texts sent outside the agentline tools (Hermes's send_message, cron jobs delivering to agentline:, gateway replies) only reach AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS, the home channel and allowed_numbers, an empty allowlist meaning deny, and a cron job targeting any other number is refused when created and again when it fires; inside a cron run the call and SMS tools are refused for unconfigured numbers; emergency, premium-rate and non-US/Canada numbers are refused on every path, including the gateway's own send paths, and every text counts against the daily SMS limit; only numbers in AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS can text or call the agent, everyone else is ignored without a reply; stores today's call and text counts in plugin data, no transcripts, messages or credentials; the API key is read through Hermes's secret scope; one Python dependency (websockets>=12,<16); no shell commands, child processes, telemetry or self-update.
entries.title: AgentLine
entries.capability_summary: agentline (community, maintained by prakhar-raj-031104) A real phone number for Hermes: place calls that a hosted voice carries out and get the transcript back, send and read SMS, text your agent like any other chat, and let a live caller's question reach Hermes mid-call, with the answer spoken on the call or texted if it takes too long. Disclosure — talks only to api.agentline.cloud: HTTPS from the tools, plus one outbound WebSocket (wss://api.agentline.cloud/v1/events/ws) held open while the gateway runs, so no public URL or open port is needed; sends call briefs, text bodies, destination numbers, contacts and the agent's answers to live caller questions; AgentLine carries the call audio and produces transcripts, the plugin never handles audio; calls, texts and numbers are billed to your own AgentLine account; agentline_call, agentline_sms, agentline_buy_number and agentline_agent go through Hermes's approval gate from a pre_tool_call hook, which shows the whole call brief, greeting, voice or text and fails closed when nobody can approve; texts sent outside the agentline tools (Hermes's send_message, cron jobs delivering to agentline:, gateway replies) only reach AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS, the home channel and allowed_numbers, an empty allowlist meaning deny, and a cron job targeting any other number is refused when created and again when it fires; inside a cron run the call and SMS tools are refused for unconfigured numbers; emergency, premium-rate and non-US/Canada numbers are refused on every path, including the gateway's own send paths, and every text counts against the daily SMS limit; only numbers in AGENTLINE_ALLOWED_USERS can text or call the agent, everyone else is ignored without a reply; stores today's call and text counts in plugin data, no transcripts, messages or credentials; the API key is read through Hermes's secret scope; one Python dependency (websockets>=12,<16); no shell commands, child processes, telemetry or self-update. This plugin registers tool(s): agentline_status, agentline_agent, agentline_buy_number, agentline_call, agentline_call_result, agentline_hangup, agentline_sms, agentline_messages, agentline_contacts; hook(s): pre_tool_call; requires env var(s): AGENTLINE_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0.

entries.name: agentmemory
entries.description: Persistent memory provider with automatic recall, conversation capture, and native memory_save, memory_recall, and memory_search tools. Memory is scoped to the active Hermes profile, project, and message author by default. Requires a separately running AgentMemory server. Disclosure — recall queries, conversation excerpts (up to 500 user and 2,000 assistant characters per turn), native memory writes, workspace paths, and scoped session identifiers are sent to the configured AgentMemory URL (localhost:3111 by default). Credentials come through Hermes's scoped secret API. Runs git rev-parse to resolve the project and stores non-secret URL configuration and memory ownership records in the active Hermes home. Remote plaintext HTTP warns but is permitted unless AGENTMEMORY_REQUIRE_HTTPS=1. No telemetry, self-updater, or background daemon is started by the plugin.
entries.title: AgentMemory
known_issues: Run hermes memory setup after installation to select AgentMemory and configure the backend credential.
There is no durable offline capture queue. Profile and author filters are application-level scope, not separate server credentials.
Native memory replacement tracking uses POSIX file locking; this entry is limited to Linux and macOS.

entries.name: agentpay-guard
entries.description: Deterministic spend and risk policy for any Hermes tool call. A pre_tool_call hook reads the tool name and arguments, finds amount, currency and payee, and applies per-call and daily limits, a payee allowlist, a currency list and an approval threshold. Hard-limit violations are blocked; over-threshold calls go to Hermes's own approval prompt (escalate mode) or are blocked into a local approval queue that only a person can release with /guard approve <id> as a single-use, exact-call, expiring grant with limits rechecked (strict mode). Executed spend is recorded in a local ledger from post_tool_call; /guard status|queue|ledger|policy|kill and a read-only guard_check dry-run tool. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no subprocesses, no background process, no credentials, no Python dependencies; writes queue, ledger, grants and kill switch only under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agentpay-guard (argument hashes, not raw arguments); reads an optional policy.json from that same directory.
entries.title: AgentPay Guard
known_issues: Classification is heuristic: a value-moving tool with an unrelated name and no recognized amount field is not treated as spending.
In escalate mode, Hermes decides escalations; with --yolo or approvals.mode smart Hermes may approve without a person. Use mode: strict for person-only grants.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-memory
entries.description: Private AgentPlaybooks memory for Hermes: explicit recall by default, optional bounded automatic recall, native memory-write mirroring, archive and history. Registration, initialization, unused prefetch and profile switching make no network requests. Disclosure — explicit searches and opted-in automatic recall send query keywords to the configured AgentPlaybooks service for your personal and configured team sources; explicit native memory writes are mirrored there. Automatic recall has acknowledgement filtering, brief repeated-query suppression, a request/time budget and per-source failure cooldown. Defaults to agentplaybooks.ai over HTTPS; localhost HTTP is supported, and remote intranet HTTP requires an explicit opt-in that sends the API key unencrypted. Team and shared playbooks are configured explicitly: the agent can write, archive and permanently delete entries in configured team playbooks (shared playbooks are read-only), and teammates' entries are recalled into context.

entries.name: agentplaybooks-tools
entries.description: Connect AgentPlaybooks skills and hosted MCP/OpenAPI tools to Hermes, with guided setup, profile selection, permission diagnostics and an authenticated MCP check. Requires Node.js 20+ and @agentplaybooks/cli@0.10.0; the CLI is installed separately. Disclosure — skill-only; the separately installed apb CLI does the work. `apb hermes setup --apply` restores complete skill trees into the chosen project and edits the selected Hermes profile's config.yaml to register those skills and a local stdio relay for the hosted playbook MCP endpoint. The relay is a child process that forwards actual requests, answers MCP pings locally and sends no idle HTTP keepalives; existing HTTP configurations need an explicit migration. Local writes require --apply; setup also probes MCP initialization and tool listing using a scoped key from the process environment, without invoking tools. `doctor` checks profile credential variable names without exposing their values. Hosted operations contact agentplaybooks.ai (or an explicitly configured service); skill restore uses `apb login`, and `apb push --apply` uploads project configuration (secret references, not values).

entries.name: agentpurse
entries.description: Search, quote, and buy from an AgentPurse allowance on the PayPal sandbox. Every purchase waits for Hermes' approval prompt and is sent only after a person approves it; YOLO, approvals off, auto-approve modes, and smart (model) approval cannot spend. A per-chat spend limit and /purse kill sit in front of the clerk. Disclosure — calls the author's AgentPurse service at agentpurse.vercel.app (POST /mcp and GET /api/spends/:id; the server uses the PayPal sandbox and Channel3 for product data) with AGENTPURSE_API_KEY from Hermes's secret scope, sending quotes, purchase sentences and the task/page excerpt the agent supplies; request_purchase and watch_price each wait for a person to answer Hermes's approval prompt (YOLO, approvals off, smart approval and unattended runs cannot spend), but an approved price watch later lets AgentPurse file the purchase server-side with no second Hermes prompt (/purse kill cancels open watches); a kill switch, quote cache, one-time approval grants and per-chat spent cents live in plugin state; PayPal sandbox money only, and a receipt is not a retailer order.
entries.title: AgentPurse
known_issues: PayPal sandbox only. A captured payment is not a retailer order.

entries.name: agents-hub
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop page for coordinating profiles, chats, approvals, project goals, Kanban tasks, and Codex / Claude usage. Disclosure — reads profile state and project/Kanban databases, runs Git status/diff, and writes its own Hub state; explicit owner actions can manage profiles, cron jobs, file rollback, blocked Kanban drafts and logins; the Kanban heartbeat (every 60 s, may promote or create Kanban cards) and Codex/Claude account switching (every 5 minutes, plus an earlier check when usage hits a limit) are each opt-in and off by default; account switching only changes credential priority with hermes auth priority and never removes credentials, and only a confirmed owner click runs hermes auth remove; Claude login runs hermes auth add anthropic; usage is read through Hermes's account-usage API; no telemetry.

entries.name: agentstatus-index
entries.description: Live public MCP Index through Carmel Labs' hosted server (Streamable HTTP at https://index.mcp.agentstatus.dev/mcp, no authentication, no keys). Search, recommend, compare, and look up public MCP servers, then call one published tool with call_indexed_tool. Bundles the agentstatus-index skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to index.mcp.agentstatus.dev. call_indexed_tool forwards one call to a public MCP server the user already picked from a search or recommendation. The Index does not store credentials. Destructive tool names are not forwarded. The tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: agenttrust-seal
entries.description: Seal a file and verify the seal later, so one Hermes agent can prove to the next that a handoff was not changed. Adds an agenttrust_seal tool (seal, verify) and an /agenttrust-seal slash command. Verify answers SEAL HOLDS, SEAL BROKEN or NO SEAL, with codes 0, 1 and 2, so the receiving agent can stop before it builds on a changed file. Standard library only. Disclosure: no network calls, no credentials, no background process. When sealing it runs one shell command, git rev-parse --short HEAD, in the file's folder to record the commit. It writes one file, <file>.seal.json, next to the sealed file, holding the sha256, size, author name, UTC time, short git commit and the machine's hostname. A seal detects change; it is not a signature and does not prove who sealed the file.
entries.title: AgentTrust Seal
known_issues: Tested on Hermes Agent 0.22.2 (Linux) and 0.22.7 (Windows); macOS is not tested.
A seal is not a signature; anyone who can rewrite both the file and its seal can make a new seal that holds.

entries.name: agentvault
entries.description: Search archived coding conversations and retrieve exact session revisions through the separately installed Agent Vault macOS app. Launches the app's existing MCP server through sh; reads the authorized archive through its local daemon. Vault handles storage-provider traffic. No bundled binaries, telemetry, credential-file reads, self-updater, or new background service. Disclosure — launches the separately installed Agent Vault app's own bundled Node MCP server (/Applications/Agent Vault.app or VAULT_APP_PATH) through sh with your VAULT_MCP_TOKEN binding token; that server code ships with the app, not in this repository. Its tools return archived conversations from Cursor, Codex, Claude Code and Hermes stored under ~/.vault (or VAULT_HOME) into the model's context, which is sent to your model provider. The app handles its own storage-provider traffic; the plugin adds no telemetry, network calls, credential-file reads or background service.

entries.name: agora
entries.description: Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Hermes profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an `hermes agora` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit `hermes agora setup`. Disclosure — creates a Hermes profile per worker by asking core to provision it (`hermes profile create --clone-from default`, or the source profile the caller names, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials; with the default source the copied skills are then removed from the new profile and it is marked to skip bundled-skill seeding); spawns `hermes -p <profile> chat -Q -q` subprocesses to speak in discussions (explicit toolset list: no kanban/clarify/cron; override via AGORA_SPEAKER_TOOLSETS) and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive `--yolo --accept-hooks` ONLY when the project opted in via `agora_start_project(allow_unattended=True)`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task_comments, task_events, task_runs, task_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in `scheduled` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to HERMES_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into HERMES_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Hermes dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Hermes subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.

entries.name: ai-bot-access-checker
entries.description: Check whether AI crawlers and search bots can reach a web page: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Googlebot, Google-Extended, bingbot, Applebot-Extended and CCBot. For each bot it reports the robots.txt rule that applies (RFC 9309, including rules added by Cloudflare's managed robots.txt) and whether the server or firewall refuses that User-Agent while a normal browser gets the page. Bundles the ai-bot-access-check skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — the check_ai_bot_access tool runs on the author's hosted server at tools.seopaslaugos.io, which receives each URL you ask about, fetches it about 14 times from Cloudflare's network with crawler User-Agents, and caches the result for 10 minutes; the tool set is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
entries.title: AI Bot Access Checker
entries.capability_summary: ai-bot-access-checker (community, maintained by Mantas Tamošaitis (seopaslaugos.io)) Check whether AI crawlers and search bots can reach a web page: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Googlebot, Google-Extended, bingbot, Applebot-Extended and CCBot. For each bot it reports the robots.txt rule that applies (RFC 9309, including rules added by Cloudflare's managed robots.txt) and whether the server or firewall refuses that User-Agent while a normal browser gets the page. Bundles the ai-bot-access-check skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — the check_ai_bot_access tool runs on the author's hosted server at tools.seopaslaugos.io, which receives each URL you ask about, fetches it about 14 times from Cloudflare's network with crawler User-Agents, and caches the result for 10 minutes; the tool set is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.name: ai-executive
entries.description: Ask your AI Executive assistant a question and see today's calendar, open tasks and the calls that need you, through AI Executive's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with a daily-brief skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to connect.aiexec.me, signed in as the user with the Google account on their AI Executive membership (a paid AI Executive or After Hours AI plan is required; sign-in does not create an account). Calendar, task and conversation summaries from the user's account are pulled into the session context, and so reach the user's model provider; phone numbers arrive masked. Both tools are read-only; nothing is booked, sent, purchased or published. AI Executive logs each call's metadata. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add ai-executive --url https://connect.aiexec.me/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: ai-subscriptions
entries.description: Your AI subscriptions and token usage in Hermes Desktop. A page with Overview, Usage and Plans tabs, plus a status-bar chip where you pick which subscriptions to keep. Quota comes from Hermes's own model.options and usage.bars RPCs; the page polls Hermes' cached windows (Hermes refreshes them in its own background threads) and only its Refresh button asks for an explicit refresh; token usage covers Hermes, Claude Code and the Grok CLI, clicking a day shows that day's per-source, per-model and hourly breakdown, and measured tokens per second are shown per model, per day and overall. Disclosure: read-only reads outside the plugin's data - Hermes state.db and models_dev_cache.json, ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl and ~/.grok/logs/unified.jsonl plus ~/.grok/sessions/*/*/summary.json (token counts only). No credential, .env or auth.json reads, no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: ai-visibility-geo-audit
entries.description: Check from chat whether ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude mention, rank and cite a brand against its competitors, which Google searches show an AI Overview, where buyers ask for recommendations on Reddit, and what to fix on a site's pages so AI engines can read and cite them. Four workflow skills (AI visibility check, GEO site audit, AI Overview check, cost estimate) drive seven Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of an Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.005 to 0.06 per result, up to USD 0.16 for a rank check with both add-ons, plus about USD 0.005 to 0.0125 per run; a ten-prompt, four-engine rank and citation report is about USD 4.42). Brand and competitor names, domains, prompts, URLs and search terms are sent to Apify; the Actors send the prompts to the AI engines through the Actor owner's model access, fetch the user's public pages, load Google results pages or search public Reddit, and the results (AI answers, cited URLs, audit scores, public Reddit posts with usernames) are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Hermes runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `hermes mcp add ai-visibility --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Hermes asking before each paid run. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with OpenAI, Google, Perplexity, Anthropic or Reddit.

entries.name: aichipmunk
entries.description: Pairs this machine's Hermes bots with the AI Chipmunk mobile app from inside Hermes Desktop — pick a bot, get the reachable host, profile and API key as a scannable code. Registers a `hermes aichipmunk` CLI command, a desktop page and a dashboard API; no tools or hooks. Disclosure — on an explicit confirmed "Switch to Tailscale" it adds a persistent tailscale serve handler putting the API server's own port (plain HTTP inside the tailnet, API_SERVER_KEY auth) onto the tailnet; on a machine with no Tailscale CLI it instead runs hermes config set platforms.api_server.host <tailnet IP> on the owning profile and restarts that gateway; reads API_SERVER_KEY from every profile's .env on this machine on each status poll (masked in lists, the full key only in the pairing link and QR returned to an authenticated dashboard caller, which may be the phone over a published dashboard); shells out to the tailscale and hermes CLIs and probes only this machine's own /health; no third-party network calls.

entries.name: aigarage
entries.description: Search AI Garage's YouTube videos (answers link to the exact chapter), the AI Garage Weekly newsletter and the creator's own X posts, plus the Agent Wikis reference library (source-backed wikis, skills, agent tools and routines), through two hosted MCP servers on agentwikis.com, with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no code. Disclosure — hosted-only connectors: every tool call goes to agentwikis.com (/content/aigarage/mcp and /mcp); IP addresses are used in memory for rate limiting and not stored, and wiki searches are kept only as anonymous counts of the query text (agentwikis.com/privacy). X results are links only, searched server-side with the publisher's own X API access. Free without a key; an optional Agent Wikis Pro key is added with hermes mcp add, kept in the profile's .env and sent only to agentwikis.com/mcp. With Pro, read_agent_tool can return a short-lived download link for an agent tool that runs on your machine; the bundled skill tells the model to explain it and get your explicit OK before downloading, running or scheduling anything. No telemetry.
entries.title: AI Garage
known_issues: The Agent Wikis Pro key is optional and needs one extra command, because a portable mcp.json cannot carry an optional header: hermes mcp add agentwikis --url "https://agentwikis.com/mcp" --auth header, answer yes, paste the key, then /reload-mcp. Without it everything free keeps working.

entries.name: aimlapi
entries.description: AI/ML API — 10,000+ models and MCP tools, with an OpenAI-compatible chat API and an optional MCP server; /model picker lists the hottest and tool-capable chat models, and on builds with model_setup_flow `hermes model` can sign you up and top up in the browser. Disclosure — sends your prompts and AIMLAPI_API_KEY to api.aimlapi.com, a third-party API that routes to upstream vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek and others), billed in prepaid aimlapi.com credits; the guided `hermes model` step (interactive terminal only) sends your email to auth.aimlapi.com / app.aimlapi.com, can create an aimlapi.com account and an API key named "Hermes Agent", and opens an aimlapi.com / Stripe checkout in your browser for a top-up of $20 or more with auto top-up preselected (answer Off to decline); new accounts are created as partner checkouts under this integration's partner id. At the end of that step it asks (default No) whether to add the aimlapi.com MCP server; on yes it writes mcp_servers.aimlapi to config.yaml (url https://mcp.aimlapi.com/mcp, header Authorization: Bearer ${AIMLAPI_API_KEY} as an env reference, never the key itself, trust: untrusted so every billed generation/chat/Toolbox call asks first), or auth: oauth with no key when the aimlapi provider points at a non-aimlapi.com endpoint; an existing entry is never overwritten. Opt-in AIMLAPI_ATTRIBUTION=1 adds integration attribution headers on requests to aimlapi.com (on the MCP entry only for the exact host mcp.aimlapi.com).

entries.name: air-agent-kya
entries.description: Know-Your-Agent with AIR: you delegate your AIR identity to Hermes once in the AIR Console (`hermes air login`, device code, P-256 agent key, credentials.verify scope, no wallet signing); the kya_visit tool then enters KYA stores that publish /.well-known/air-kya, gets a one-time SD-JWT presentation from AIR that discloses only the claims the store requests (e.g. membership tier), and returns the catalog that credential unlocks; agents that aren't delegated get the store's public catalog. Disclosure — network calls to the AIR Console (sandbox.agents.air3.com, during login only), the AIR API (air.api.sandbox.air3.com) and AIR credential API (credential-testnet.api.sandbox.air3.com), and to each KYA site the agent visits (https only, plain http allowed for localhost); stores a P-256 agent private key and the AIR delegation bundle in its own plugin-data directory with mode 0600, removed by `hermes air logout`; on first run after the rename it reads the old air-kya plugin-data directory once to carry a delegation over; a live kya_visit asks for approval through Hermes's approval gate before any claim is disclosed and sends the presentation only to the origin that issued the nonce; the model never sees the presentation, key or tokens; endpoints are plugin settings, no secrets or env vars read; no shell, subprocess, background thread or telemetry.
entries.title: AIR Agent KYA
known_issues: Defaults point at the AIR sandbox; production needs the endpoint settings.
`hermes air login` runs in a terminal only and waits for approval until the device code expires.

entries.name: aircraft-doppler-geolocation
entries.description: Detect aircraft flyovers in a recording (Doppler tones, plus experimental ground-reflection broadband jet passes) and estimate where it was made by scoring them against adsb.lol ADS-B history, with a posterior heatmap, 68/95% areas and a confidence flag. Provides the doppler_detect and doppler_locate tools and a dopplergeo CLI. Results on unseen real recordings are weak (2 of 18 held-out runs under 3 km); treat output as a hypothesis. Disclosure — doppler_locate / dopplergeo locate makes unauthenticated HTTPS GETs to GitHub (adsb.lol release assets, streamed, about 3 GB read per uncached day; only the crop is cached), raw.githubusercontent.com (tar1090-db types), the Copernicus DEM S3 bucket and Open-Meteo, caching results under ~/.cache/doppler-geo (or DOPPLER_GEO_CACHE); offline mode uses the local cache only; no credentials, uploads or telemetry. doppler_detect and the skill scripts make no network calls; the tools and scripts run ffmpeg/ffprobe (no shell) on the recording you name and write CSV/PNG/JSON at the output path you give (default `<recording>.doppler/`). PyPI packages (numpy, scipy, soundfile, matplotlib, tifffile) install only after Hermes dependency consent. The method can geolocate where a recording was made, so use it only on recordings you are entitled to analyse.

Calls your Airflow REST API; optional docker run sandbox. Disclosure — calls only the Airflow REST API at your configured base_url with your Airflow credentials; while a DAG folder is configured it inspects Hermes' write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls and blocks or asks approval for changes to DAG files; task retries ask Hermes approval unless you enable auto_remediation_enabled, which lets it retry tasks it classified as transient on its own (including inside the optional night-watch cron job); the optional sandbox (off by default) runs your DAG code plus the model's patch in a local `docker run --network none` container through Hermes' terminal tool.

entries.name: airlock-sandbox
entries.description: Terminal backend that routes Hermes command execution through an operator-chosen Airlock HTTPS API and disposable sandbox, then surfaces receipts (RFC 8785 JCS, SHA-256, Ed25519) as BLOCKED / ALLOWED / VERIFIED (`hermes config set terminal.backend airlock_sandbox`). Requires an explicit HTTPS origin `base_url` (no built-in default host). When `verify_receipts` is true (default), requires a locally configured `public_key_hex` obtained out-of-band — the verifying key is never fetched from the Airlock API at verify time. VERIFIED binds signed decision + execution digests/exit_code only; it does not prove command text and does not verify full receipt-chain linkage (`prev_hash` is informational). Disclosure — HTTPS calls to the configured origin only (`/healthz`, `/api/arena`, `/api/receipt/{id}`); optional secret `AIRLOCK_API_TOKEN` via Hermes secret scope; no host shell of its own (commands run only inside Airlock when policy allows). Hermes dangerous-command approvals are not bypassed. File-tool stdin pipes and non-default cwd are refused (Airlock arena has neither process-stdin nor cwd).

entries.name: airlock
entries.description: Guardrails that follow what a conversation has read. Once a session reads untrusted content (a web page, a browser snapshot, an MCP or third-party plugin's output, a customer's message), airlock seals it: messages to anyone but the owner, network writes, pushes and deploys, memory, skill and cron writes, browser input, URLs that could carry data out and code that reaches the network go through Hermes's own approval gate. Walls hold in every session: credential paths and secret files, the guard's own files and Hermes's config, shell startup files, other profiles, commands that switch approvals off. Shell commands are read the way the shell reads them, so a command that computes or hides what it runs (eval, base64 | sh, $G push, wildcards, write-then-run) is refused until written in clear. Subagents inherit the seal. A project's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules or .hermes.md that Hermes loads at startup seals the session from its first turn until the owner has reviewed it (`hermes airlock trust`), and again when its content changes (a cloned repository, a pull). It also catches an injection by its signature: recognized secrets never leave in a call; a private marker in the agent's context locks the session if it shows up in a tool call; a send to an address the untrusted content named is blocked; repeated refusals lock the session; lookalike Unicode in commands is refused. A file behind a wall cannot leave as a message attachment, and attached files are checked for secrets. A call that names a cloud metadata service is refused. Plugin and MCP tools nobody admitted need approval. Observe mode, stop switch, `hermes airlock check|demo|log|trust`. On Windows, paths are read in every form Windows and Git Bash give them, and a path on another machine is refused without being opened. Tested on a corpus of 362 attacks and everyday commands, on Linux, macOS and Windows, and end to end in the official image. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call, subagent_start, on_session_reset, post_approval_response), no tools. No network, no LLM call, runs no command. Reads the profile's config.yaml (home channels, approvals mode) and its own policy file (<HERMES_HOME>/airlock.yaml); lists directories to expand wildcards in commands it checks; reads the first 200 KB of each file a send_message attaches, locally, to look for secrets. On Windows, reads the machine's own name (no lookup), tests which drive letters exist, and imports tools.environments.local._find_bash to know Git Bash's root. On a session's first turn, imports agent.prompt_builder.discover_context_files and _project_context_suppressed and agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_context_cwd (guarded) to know which project context files Hermes loaded, and hashes them (sha256). Imports Hermes's attachment reader (gateway.platforms.base.BasePlatformAdapter.extract_media) to see exactly what a message would attach, with its own reader as a fallback. Writes under plugin-data/airlock: a journal of decisions, taints and approvals that includes tool arguments, truncated (journal.args: none leaves them out), the taint state, the stop switch and the context files the owner trusted (path and sha256). When nobody can approve (--yolo, /yolo, hermes -z, approvals.mode: off, cron, -q or webhook set to approve, a subagent under delegation.subagent_auto_approve) it blocks instead of letting Hermes auto-approve; to know it, it imports gateway.session_finite.unattended_turn and reads tools.approval (_yolo_active, _unattended_contexts, approval_context._get_approval_mode), each guarded, config.yaml as fallback (policy approvals_off: follow restores Hermes's behaviour). Install scan: caution, because the default policy and the shell reader name the patterns airlock guards against (startup files, crontab, credential commands, exfiltration shapes).

known_issues: Built for in-process plugins (Hermes's default): under plugins.isolation: host it cannot tell third-party plugin tools from Hermes's own.

entries.name: airpods-approvals
entries.description: Hear Hermes approvals and questions in your AirPods and answer with your head: nod to approve, shake to deny. Gestures are recognised by rhythm, with a tap in each ear as you go, and drive the real approval through approval.respond. A nod only ever approves once, and a timeout or lost AirPods sends nothing. Desktop-only plugin with a small native helper built from source on your Mac, because head motion isn't reachable from a plugin: Install in the plugin's settings opens the bundled desktop/Install Helper.command in Terminal, which builds and starts it. Set up then walks through a Gemini key, Motion access and AirPods on the same page. Disclosure — Desktop-only, macOS. Install opens the bundled desktop/Install Helper.command in Terminal, which builds a native helper app from the plugin's Swift source into ~/Applications/Hermes AirPods.app (ad-hoc signed); once paired, Hermes Desktop launches it at every start and it runs without a window or menu bar item until Desktop quits. The helper listens on 127.0.0.1 with a paired handshake and reads AirPods head motion only during a question, which never leaves the Mac. A completed nod answers a real Hermes approval with approve-once (never session or always) and can answer clarify questions; timeouts and lost AirPods send nothing. Prompts are written and spoken by Gemini: each approval's description and Hermes-redacted command, and each clarify question with its choices, are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using your Gemini key, which the helper keeps in the macOS Keychain; by default you hear Gemini's one-line summary of the command rather than the literal command. On Gemini's free tier, Google may use this content to improve its products. No telemetry.

entries.name: aisecuritywarden
entries.description: Secret source that loads the API keys a revocable aiSecurityWarden machine token may read (end-to-end encrypted, optional phone approval) at Hermes startup. Bulk source "aisecuritywarden"; runs the aiSecurityWarden client's swctl, so the token never enters Hermes. Disclosure — when enabled, runs your installed aiSecurityWarden `swctl` client (argv only, allowlisted environment, up to 180 s to allow a phone approval) at Hermes start-up, which contacts the aiSecurityWarden server your machine token was set up with, and loads every secret in that token's project into Hermes's environment (existing values are kept unless `override_existing` is on); the plugin itself makes no network calls and never reads the token.

entries.name: aisense
entries.description: 77 free tools for agents through AI SENSE's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no account, no key): time and time zones, hashing and encoding, QR codes, HTML to PDF, JSON and CSV, images, and workflow tools (temporary storage, webhook capture, human approval, queues, leases, heartbeats, an agent inbox, typed decisions from weighted rules, semantic search, one-time secrets), with one tool-choice skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to AI SENSE's MCP server at aisenseapi.com with the arguments the agent passes, which also reach the user's model provider through the session, and request logs hold the caller's IP address. Tools that create something return bearer tokens; stored data, files and captures are readable by anyone holding their id or URL and expire within 24 hours; webhook schedules and notify URLs make the server call a URL the agent supplies. 5000 requests per address per day across all tools. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. No sign-in: the bundled mcp.json works as installed.

entries.name: aixy
entries.description: Run Hermes on Aixy: guided setup picks a model from your project's catalog, and optional MCP tools connect through browser OAuth, off by default. Disclosure — exposes CLI commands only, with no automatic hooks or runtime tools. Explicit inference setup sends the project key in an authenticated GET /models to the configured Aixy gateway (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/v1 by default), rejects redirects, and asks before updating the selected Hermes profile's provider and main model settings. The key is stored through Hermes' credential writer as AIXY_API_KEY; provider settings contain a variable reference. Model requests send Hermes' opaque conversation scope in X-Aixy-Session-ID for grouping in Aixy Activity. No inference requests are sent during setup. Optional MCP setup starts the installed Hermes CLI as a child process for browser OAuth, credential storage and tool selection against the independent MCP endpoint (https://api.aixy-gateway.com/mcp by default). The child uses the selected profile, disables inherited unattended and YOLO flags, and receives no key in command arguments. Setup requires an interactive terminal. No additional dependencies, telemetry, persistent background processes or self-updater.

entries.name: alans-way-computer
entries.description: Computer-use provider for Hermes: with computer_use.backend: alans-way-computer, the stock computer_use tool drives apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the alans-way plugin's workspace setup. Disclosure: starts the workspace router as a long-running node child per session (filtered environment; desktop input enabled only for that private child, behind Hermes's computer_use approval gate); reaches the user's computer over SSH on the tailnet; resends a call refused as desktop_busy for up to 30 s without a second approval. The provider makes no network calls and stores no credentials.
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin: Computer Use
known_issues: Needs a Hermes build with the pluggable computer-use API (Hermes 0.21.6 or newer). On older Hermes the plugin installs and does nothing. Install alans-way first and run its workspace setup, which writes the workspace_browser block this provider reuses.

Hermes asks for approval on every computer_use action type until it is granted. For an unattended Telegram bot, grant them once with Always in Telegram, or add cua:<action>:background entries to command_allowlist (see the README). Takes effect after a gateway restart.

The pinned README requires in-process loading and says plugins.isolation: host is unsupported because the provider hands Hermes a live router session. The current admission validator reports host readiness; remote isolation compatibility has not been verified.

Typing without a target field types into the focused field (still approval-gated). On the user's Mac this needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9: the target app is brought forward only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds, password fields are refused, and the focused field must belong to the target app.

The VM desktop path needs xdotool, a screenshot tool (scrot, maim or ImageMagick import), the AT-SPI bus and python3-gi on the VM. Without them those calls fail and the agent reports it; setup.sh warns about what is missing.

A default som capture skips the screenshot request when snapshot geometry establishes 35% named-control coverage; older apps without geometry still require a screenshot to check it and may omit it from the model. Use mode vision to request it explicitly, or mode ax for an element-only capture. When a screenshot is omitted, coordinate= and element bounds are screen pixels.

Mac and Windows action replies update the held element list without shifting surviving numbers. On Linux, capture again before acting by number after a tree change; cut replies do not prove an unseen control is gone. A timeout or hung app can leave the action's outcome uncertain: capture before retrying.

focus_app launches a named app, or opens a document or folder by absolute path in its app on the user's computer (needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9 with computer-open-v1; app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps are refused). It binds the window showing the opened item. When an action lands on an unfocused window it returns that error and tells the model to ask for a raise explicitly (focus_app with raise_window=true, or delivery_mode='foreground'), which Hermes approves under its foreground scopes; the provider never raises on its own. It follows the focused window after an app shortcut, and passes the app's step notes to the model. Older apps refuse path opens and keep the earlier behavior.

Admission validation passes with a private-import warning: __init__.py uses tools.mcp_tool_config._resolve_stdio_command to resolve the router launcher; this internal helper may change across Hermes releases.

When the Mac reports desktop_busy (another agent holds the desktop), launch, menu and action calls are resent for up to 30 s of waiting, following the host's retry-after hint or every 2 s, then fail with desktop_busy naming the holder. Hermes does not ask for approval again on a resend; the host refused the call before running it.

The current admission validator reports host readiness; remote isolation compatibility has not been verified.; Typing without a target field types into the focused field (still approval-gated). On the user's Mac this needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9: the target app is brought forward only after the user has been idle for at least 2 seconds, password fields are refused, and the focused field must belong to the target app.; The VM desktop path needs xdotool, a screenshot tool (scrot, maim or ImageMagick import), the AT-SPI bus and python3-gi on the VM. Without them those calls fail and the agent reports it; setup.sh warns about what is missing.; A default som capture skips the screenshot request when snapshot geometry establishes 35% named-control coverage; older apps without geometry still require a screenshot to check it and may omit it from the model. Use mode vision to request it explicitly, or mode ax for an element-only capture. When a screenshot is omitted, coordinate= and element bounds are screen pixels.; Mac and Windows action replies update the held element list without shifting surviving numbers. On Linux, capture again before acting by number after a tree change; cut replies do not prove an unseen control is gone. A timeout or hung app can leave the action's outcome uncertain: capture before retrying.; focus_app launches a named app, or opens a document or folder by absolute path in its app on the user's computer (needs Alan's Workspace 0.21.9 with computer-open-v1; app bundles, executables, scripts and off-limits apps are refused). It binds the window showing the opened item. When an action lands on an unfocused window it returns that error and tells the model to ask for a raise explicitly (focus_app with raise_window=true, or delivery_mode='foreground'), which Hermes approves under its foreground scopes; the provider never raises on its own. It follows the focused window after an app shortcut, and passes the app's step notes to the model. Older apps refuse path opens and keep the earlier behavior.; Admission validation passes with a private-import warning: __init__.py uses tools.mcp_tool_config._resolve_stdio_command to resolve the router launcher; this internal helper may change across Hermes releases.; When the Mac reports desktop_busy (another agent holds the desktop), launch, menu and action calls are resent for up to 30 s of waiting, following the host's retry-after hint or every 2 s, then fail with desktop_busy naming the holder. Hermes does not ask for approval again on a resend; the host refused the call before running it..

entries.name: alans-way
entries.description: Idle check-ins, a texting voice and workspace-browser skills for a Hermes gateway on a Linux host or macOS guest VM. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, 08:00-22:00 user time, backing off when unanswered) the primary bot checks in once; morning briefs, a weekly time-saved report and cross-bot proactivity are opt-in. The workspace-setup skill walks the user through Alan's Workspace, a separate desktop app, and Tailscale. Disclosure: injects internal prompts into the bound DM (needs allow_gateway_injection); turn hooks see every session; reads ~/.config/alans-way/config.json when present; default-on Telegram reply pacing (up to 2.5 s) and remove-only reply cleanup; ships a long-running Node workspace router (SSH to the user's computer over the tailnet, VM fallback) and an operator-started HTTP bridge; setup, run by the human outside the gateway, installs services and packages, adds a tailnet-only SSH key and restarts the gateway; cross-bot proactivity shares sanitized owner-DM excerpts between profiles on one gateway. Full list: the README's Disclosures section at this pin. The plugin's Python makes no network calls; no telemetry, no stored credentials.
entries.title: Alan's Way Plugin
known_issues: Install this on the machine that runs Hermes (a Linux host or a macOS guest VM), not on the user's primary computer. Windows guests are new and untested on real hardware. If the plugin is already installed from the catalog, setup leaves it as it is, so this pin stays.

Setup turns off Hermes's stock browser toolset for Telegram and cron so the agent uses the workspace browser (pass --keep-browser to skip disabling it; this does not re-enable it). It never turns off computer_use: on Hermes with the computer-use provider API, desktop input goes through the gated computer_use tool and its alans-way-computer provider.
Check-ins need plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection: true and a bound Telegram DM (setup does both). A background thread checks every 60 seconds once the gateway connects Telegram.

Setup may install Chrome, Chromium, Playwright's Chromium or Xvfb with root or passwordless sudo, and may drain-stop and start the profile's gateway to apply a plugin change Hermes refuses while it runs. Pass --skip-services to skip the services and their packages.
The computer's SSH key is only accepted from the tailnet (from= restriction). An existing unrestricted line for the same key is rewritten with it.
A copy of the workspace-operations skill under a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's and never gets its updates. Setup only warns; move anything worth keeping out of it, then delete it.

The texting voice is default-on for Telegram, desktop, TUI and bot_room source tags. /tone default disables its note and final-opener polish per profile. CLI, cron, webhook and API-server sources retain the default voice. Check-ins and morning briefs keep their own short style. Fixed Hermes progress/error/approval messages, direct sends and cron reports are outside these hooks; interim messages get the tone note but no polish, and streaming can show raw chunks before a final edit. Consistent real-model quiet behavior remains unverified.

Morning briefs are opt-in (/proactivity brief on), use the existing bound DM and gateway-injection permission, and may read calendar/email through tools already available to the model. /proactivity now is user-only from that chat and bypasses pause/hours for one requested check-in.

Telegram browser Approve buttons need Hermes v0.21.6 or newer including commit 239740a19e (first in date tag v2026.6.19), despite the generic >=0.21.5 install floor. Without MCP form elicitation support commits fail with approval_unavailable; unattended cron declines them. The gate protects against agent mistakes and malicious pages, not a deliberately hostile bot with same-user terminal/file access.

The router appends approval details and detected targets to commit-decisions.jsonl beside mac-watch state, shared by routers using that path; no retention or rotation is implemented. Keep this local log private. CAPTCHA handback, recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still block takeover. If the router reports human_has_control before a commit approval, wait or claim the tab through the normal app control flow first.

Long-chat pruning is an agent-guided, separately consented config option per profile, not a setup.sh default. It preserves customized values and summary routing, rewrites sent history and can break the prompt-cache prefix; undo affects future pruning and cannot restore tool bodies already pruned from active context.

web-errands and integrations are agent guidance, not setup steps. Any Himalaya, rclone, Taskwarrior, Home Assistant or Honcho install happens only after the user agrees in chat, never from setup.sh or plugin load. Taskwarrior is built from source (CMake >=3.24, Rust >=1.91.1 and several GiB of temporary space). The Google Workspace route requests Hermes's fixed scope list, which includes write access.

Guided setup can change a profile's busy-input, intent-ack continuation, Telegram display, notification, reaction, memory-notice, cron-wrapping and timezone settings, but only after explicit answers. Busy mode, intent-ack continuation, memory-notice hiding, cron.wrap_response and timezone reach beyond Telegram within that profile; the autonomy choice takes effect after restart and preserves existing deliberate choices. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing; neither setup script writes these keys.

setup.sh --bind also sets TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL for the bound profile through hermes config set and clears TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID; it loads on gateway restart. If that fails, send /sethome in the primary DM.

Desktop control needs a Hermes with tools.computer_use.backend.ComputerUseProvider (commit 63f5e0ea45726c5d8d7d207d140613997730aab3 or newer); a version string alone does not prove it. setup.sh --verify exits 2, not 0, for a partial install.

This pin needs the paired workspace/remote browser host with approval-binding-v1 support for approved browser actions. Older hosts fail closed when that proof is unavailable; update and verify the paired workspace before rollout.

Cross-bot proactivity is off by default and requires operator configuration and per-bot /proactivity cross on; activation needs a gateway restart. It exports bounded completed owner-DM excerpts across enabled profiles on one gateway. /proactivity cross off stops sharing/receiving/dispatch immediately and purges local shared text and permits; body-free hashes remain for 48 hours. Sanitization skips credential/payment-looking exchanges but cannot guarantee secrecy. Digest TTL is 24 hours, queued asks two hours; offline expired files remain until an activated profile prunes them. Copied context in Hermes history, sidecars, compaction, memory-provider records and model-provider retention is not erased by expiry or opt-out. The no-memory instruction is model policy. Shared storage requires POSIX owner-only directories/files. Dormant profiles do no store access.

During a permitted primary check-in the model may automatically schedule one read-only/draft-only ask into an enrolled target bot's existing owner DM, with primary attribution. sent means scheduled, not delivered or completed; there is no delivery receipt or replay. A separate off-by-default results opt-in in both owner DMs permits one sanitized summary (280 UTF-8 bytes) per future ask, held in private results.json for at most two hours from the ask and consumed once at the primary's next owner turn or permitted check-in. There is no wake/retry; missing means unknown. Result opt-out purges pending outcomes and cross opt-out revokes the choice; already copied chat/provider context remains. Imported-session restrictions last at most 30 minutes and survive restart; terminal/code, desktop input, delegation, messaging, scheduling and unknown connectors are blocked, while existing gated browser calls remain possible. Existing approval/CAPTCHA/ownership gates apply; this is not universal read-only enforcement. Targets require gateway-injection permission and verified same-bot routes; missing permission, routing, busy/pause/hours or expiry can prevent delivery.

proactivity.py and voice.py read gateway.session_context.get_session_env, which current Hermes flags as private imports that may break across releases. cross_bot_ask is not in provides_tools: it registers only for an activated primary cross-bot profile, which the isolated admission probe does not activate.

When the computer's ssh link drops while mac-watch reports it online, the router reconnects at most once a minute and replays only read-only and never-sent calls; an action that may already have run is answered as uncertain, never repeated. After a failover to the VM, a call naming a computer tab is refused.

Telegram reply pacing is on by default and holds a reply up to 2.5 s (/tone pace off turns it off). A ~/.config/alans-way/config.json, when present, sets identity, persona, voice, reply length and proactivity hours, timezone and on/off, and an invalid file stops the plugin from loading. The weekly time-saved report is off until the user sends /proactivity report on; its minutes are a fixed per-task estimate.

Remote MCP clients set up with the repository's scripts/setup-remote-agent.sh or the bundled, operator-started remote-agent bridge get desktop input when the operator sets HERMES_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_DESKTOP_ACTIONS=1, without Hermes's computer_use approval prompts. The bridge serves plain HTTP on loopback or a private address; add TLS in front before exposing it.

entries.name: alchemy-task
entries.description: Alchemy Task does the work before the work: it turns messy real-world work into finely researched tasks, ready for your agent to do for you. Disclosure — research and discovery start read-only Hermes subagents on your model that can read your files, past sessions, Hermes memory files and the Git history of repositories under your home folder (credential files excluded; a pre_tool_call hook blocks write, shell, send and credential reads); discovery readers must be read-only tools and scheduled runs cannot create or change scheduled jobs unless you set cron.allow_agent_scheduling; task files are Markdown in a Git workspace you choose, committed and pushed with your own git setup; setup copies loader scripts into $HERMES_HOME/scripts/ and creates scheduled jobs after you approve them (a 30-minute research sweep, an hourly script, and one per discovery stream that checks every 30 minutes and wakes the agent only at your chosen time, on a manual run or for a pending follow-up), and can change Hermes's timezone if you agree; background threads poll the Start-in-chat queue every second and, for chats linked to a task, write automatic checkpoints (one small model call, a commit and push) after 30 idle minutes; Start in chat posts into your messaging chat only if you grant allow_gateway_injection; optional iPhone Reminders sync uses the Hermes mobile connector. No telemetry.
entries.title: Alchemy Task
known_issues: iPhone Reminders sync needs the Hermes mobile app (beta) with Reminders access; the current app beta does not offer it for Nous Cloud agents.

entries.name: aletheia
entries.description: Evidence-bound scoped memory for Hermes agents, over the Weft substrate: turns are queued for a local SQLite store under the active profile by default, recall is scoped before it is ranked (deny-by-default, deterministic, never widened by anything read), and every recall returns a receipt naming the scope consulted, the ids selected and the tier. Duplicates are not re-ingested, deletions cascade, corrections preserve lineage. Registers as memory.provider: aletheia and exposes weft_recall, weft_ingest, weft_forget and weft_receipt, with recall on a worker thread so a turn's prefetch is not blocked; the built-in memory store keeps running alongside it. Disclosure — the plugin's code ships in the weft-memory PyPI package (installed as weft-memory>=1.1.1,<2, so it is outside this catalog pin); primary-agent turns are queued for storage in local SQLite under the active profile by default (the path is configurable; writes may be interrupted on process exit); no network calls, telemetry, or credentials on the Hermes path; the required bge-m3 embedder and cross-encoder reranker (~0.7 GB) must already be in the local Hugging Face cache, downloaded from their official Hugging Face repositories, and are not vendored; the Hermes provider exposes text ingest only; the separate Weft substrate supports optional image and audio adapters; macOS on Apple silicon only (mlx); AGPL-3.0, and weft-memory is AGPL-3.0 as well.

entries.name: alibaba-token-plan-media
entries.description: Self-contained native whole-file WebSocket TTS and synchronous file ASR with its own catalogue. Native Token Plan speech synthesis and file transcription through Hermes voice delivery and transcription tools. TTS and ASR have isolated Global/China Personal/Team providers and read scoped keys through public Hermes APIs. ASR may invoke existing ffmpeg/ffprobe found with shutil.which; no binary download, PAYG fallback, telemetry, automatic model substitution, paid resubmission, PCM streaming or realtime calling. One selected account key is needed, not every optional variable. Disclosure — sends the text to synthesize, or the audio file to transcribe, with the selected account's Token Plan key to Alibaba's fixed regional Token Plan host (token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com for Global, token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com for China); transcription may run the ffmpeg/ffprobe already installed on the machine (never downloaded) to convert audio; keys are read through Hermes's secret API; no telemetry.

entries.name: alice-voice
entries.description: Private Yandex Alice voice input for Hermes, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL.
entries.title: Alice Voice Input
known_issues: Default profile and one existing authorized Telegram DM session only; a private Alice skill and operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy are required.
Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram connect factory receives the native Application and is not supported by plugins.isolation: host.
The webhook URL contains a bearer secret. Yandex request signatures are not verified; body skill/account IDs are not cryptographic authentication.
Alice acknowledges asynchronous scheduling, not completion or delivery. Replies are sent to Telegram, not spoken by Alice.
Deduplication is bounded and memory-only; no durable queue, exactly-once guarantee, or built-in global rate limiter.
entries.capability_summary: alice-voice (community, maintained by bablobanov) Private Yandex Alice voice input for Hermes, with replies in Telegram. Disclosure — off until you set enabled: true and allow_gateway_injection: true; then, while the Telegram gateway is connected, it listens on 127.0.0.1 (port 8788 by default) for webhooks forwarded by your own HTTPS reverse proxy. The secret URL path (ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) is the only authentication: Yandex request signatures are not checked, and the skill and account IDs in the request can be forged by anyone who has the URL. Each accepted request becomes a user message in one fixed Telegram DM session and runs with that session's tools; approvals stay in Telegram and slash commands are refused. Leaving owner_user_id empty accepts any Alice account presenting the URL. This plugin requires env var(s): ALICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.21.3. Known issues: Default profile and one existing authorized Telegram DM session only; a private Alice skill and operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy are required.; Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram connect factory receives the native Application and is not supported by plugins.isolation: host.; The webhook URL contains a bearer secret. Yandex request signatures are not verified; body skill/account IDs are not cryptographic authentication.; Alice acknowledges asynchronous scheduling, not completion or delivery. Replies are sent to Telegram, not spoken by Alice.; Deduplication is bounded and memory-only; no durable queue, exactly-once guarantee, or built-in global rate limiter..

entries.name: ample

entries.name: annotary
entries.description: Review your agents' plans and documents with comments, from Desktop, the Webapp and your phone: an agent shares a Markdown plan, you comment on exact lines in the Annotary page, and Send back or Approve wakes the agent in the chat that shared it (an @mention wakes only the Bot it names; a plain comment wakes nobody). Disclosure — at first use downloads one `annotary` binary from Annotary's official GitHub Release (josh-andrews-dev/annotary), pinned by version and SHA-256 in the source and checked before use, never self-updated; runs it as a long-lived background server (`annotary serve`) on 127.0.0.1 only, with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, TZ and its own ANNOTARY_* settings, never provider keys), detached so it outlives gateway restarts, with its data under $HERMES_ROOT/annotary/; stores a generated owner password and one Annotary Token per profile in mode-600 files in its own data folders; reads each profile's folder names, profile.yaml and avatar to keep one Annotary Member and face per profile; runs `hermes` subcommands (`plugins enable` on `hermes annotary enable`, `-p <profile> config get` to read that profile's wake-up consent, and a single-query `hermes chat` turn to wake a Bot that has no chat yet, only after the person turns wake-ups on); no third-party network calls and no telemetry.
entries.title: Annotary
known_issues: Windows is not supported (Annotary ships for macOS and Linux; WSL counts as Linux).
In the Webapp, turn on Annotary once per browser in Capabilities → Plugins before the page shows.
After updating the plugin, restart the gateway and the dashboard; Hermes reloads neither for a loaded plugin.

entries.name: antemuse
entries.description: Five short agent states, one at a time: walk, daydream, doomscroll, dream, unstuck. /walk takes 6 hops across the concept map and comes back with the path while your work keeps going. /daydream puts two things you said side by side. /doomscroll pulls 3 posts from public feeds. /dream mixes up your day. /unstuck suggests one next move from your day and the map. /explore is the map you fly yourself. No model calls on the state path. What it reads: daydream reads this chat's own recent messages. Dream and unstuck read this chat's own day - your messages and concepts the plugin served - and use local git commit subjects when the chat is in a repository. Doomscroll feed text is untrusted and never saved. A read-only scan of the last 14 days of sessions is controlled by the `session_scan` setting. What it keeps: a 60-entry state journal whose text is cut to 800 characters per entry, holding the material a state served and its closing account - for daydream, dream and unstuck that is drawn from what you said in this chat - plus at most 24 of your recent turns per chat at 400 characters each, for the last 8 chats. Feed text is never kept. Disclosure — By default, once per session, reads the last 14 days of your Hermes session messages (read-only) to steer walks away from ground you have covered (turn off with the `session_scan` setting); daydream, dream and unstuck use this chat's own recent messages, and the plugin keeps up to 24 of your recent turns per chat for the last 8 chats (400 characters each) plus a 60-entry state journal in its data folder; dream and unstuck read recent commit subjects, and walks read the README/AGENTS.md, from the chat's current git repository; walks can read corpus graph JSON files you place in the plugin's `graphs/` data folder; doomscroll fetches public RSS feeds from theonion.com, reddit.com (r/BrandNewSentence) and hnrss.org, sending no user data, and treats their text as untrusted and never stores it.
entries.title: Antemuse
known_issues: The picture is two desktop panes — the Antemuse map, and the cockpit /explore is flown in. Chat carries no visualization and a terminal gets the same text record; there is no terminal takeover since 0.10.30.
Windows: the installer and runtime are pure Python and the suite passes on Linux; there is no Windows-specific path, so the pane is expected to work but is unverified there.
The exploration library (spark, keep, collider, selection) is present but runtime-gated behind experimental.enabled and makes no quality claim.

entries.name: antenna
entries.description: Signed messaging with paired Hermes and OpenClaw agents, with receiver-controlled live and opt-in non-YOLO headless delivery. Disclosure — runs a loopback-only Node receiver when listen_port is set (you expose only its HTTPS receive route); messages from paired peers become agent turns in the sessions you approve and may cause tool use, and opt-in background delivery runs them in non-YOLO sessions only; smart scanning sends message text through your configured provider; ClawReef Public Groups use a plaintext relay that ClawReef can read; identity keys, peer credentials, holds and receipts live in the profile's plugin-data/antenna (0700/0600) and backups contain credentials; policy and storage commands rewrite config.yaml (comments and formatting are lost).

entries.name: antigravity-agy
entries.description: Run Hermes on a Google Antigravity subscription through the official agy CLI, with agy as the model only: a generated custom agent removes agy's built-in tools, Hermes tools are exposed through an inventory-only MCP server with native function calling, and every tool call is handed back to Hermes. Fails closed on any non-Hermes tool step or silent agent fallback; pre-warms agy for fast tool loops. Disclosure — routes inference through Google's official agy CLI and counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to; the plugin never reads, copies or links agy's credential files. agy runs in your real HOME with the gateway's environment; by default the plugin moves the agy conversation records created by its own idle pre-warmed processes under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ to the trash (trash-put from PATH; ANTIGRAVITY_AGY_CLEANUP=off disables) and pre-warms up to 4 idle agy processes (~400 MB each).

entries.name: antigravity-oauth
entries.description: Sign in to Google Antigravity with `hermes auth add antigravity-oauth` (or one command, `npx hermes-antigravity-oauth`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run_command, view_file, grep_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Hermes system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).

entries.name: antigravity-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Runs Hermes on an Antigravity subscription via the agy CLI. Supports native multimodal vision and video, streams progressively and opts into host streaming when the profile declares it; persists trajectories via agy --conversation (239k); discovers models per account; maps effort; reports /usage quota; aborts native tool steps; reaps orphaned plugin workers whose owner temp dir is gone and cleans every ephemeral session dir on close; declares per-model vision capability so attached images route natively. Windows console children spawn with CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Inference and /usage reads count against your subscription; links the antigravity-oauth-token into a private temp HOME deleted on close; probes keyring presence (Secret Service, Keychain, Credential Manager), reading no secrets; symlinks ~/Library/Keychains on macOS; never writes vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking env vars before spawning agy (ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT allow-list); ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR writes every prompt to disk. Disclosure — routes inference and /usage quota reads through Google's official agy CLI under your subscription (usage counts against it); links (symlink, else hardlink/copy) the antigravity-oauth-token into a per-session private temp HOME deleted on close; probes OS keyring presence (Linux Secret Service, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) without reading secrets; on macOS symlinks ~/Library/Keychains for CLI session reuse; never writes to vendor credential stores; strips credential-looking environment variables before spawning agy (name heuristic; ANTIGRAVITY_ENV_STRICT for an allow-list) and disables agy's background auto-updater in its child environment; image, video and audio inputs (data URLs, local media files and public http(s) URLs, which the host downloads up to 25 MB) are passed to agy and uploaded to Google, and files it downloads into its own media cache are deleted when the session closes. Disclosure — the opt-in ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR env var writes every outgoing prompt (full conversation text) to that directory.

entries.name: anvilads
entries.description: Read-only access to your AnvilAds Google Ads data from Hermes, via the AnvilAds Connect AI MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://anvilads.com/mcp): connected ad accounts, campaigns from the latest stored snapshot, performance summaries (spend, clicks, conversions, CPA), the latest morning or weekly report, lead totals, and ad audit grades, plus a bundled skill teaching the morning-check workflow. AnvilAds is an AI agent that builds, launches, and optimizes Google Ads; the owner approves every launch in the AnvilAds dashboard. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to anvilads.com, authenticated with your ANVILADS_API_KEY (a per-business key created in the AnvilAds dashboard, sent as a bearer header only to that host). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the vendor documents it as read-only (seven tools over stored data, no writes, no live Google Ads calls).

entries.name: aphrodite
entries.description: CCR compression plugin - multi-type classifier, 13 tools, default-on context engine (middle-turn archiving + engine_offload), TOML-driven templates, auto-expand, live containers, prompt knobs, recursion/body caps. Priced retrieval: a marker's size is its retrieval cost - previews answer the structural questions, deferral is safe, batch the retrievals you need. Disclosure - hook and tool logic runs in prebuilt native binaries (libaphrodite_hermes + aphrodite proxy, v1.8.1) built from the public PlayForm/Aphrodite source and fetched by an explicit download.sh step checked against in-tree SHA-256 sums; register() starts a background proxy on 127.0.0.1:9797/9798 whose management routes are open to local processes unless APHRODITE_MGMT_TOKEN is set; pre_tool_call by default rewrites slow terminal commands (cargo/npm/pip/docker/curl...) to run in the background (background=true, notify_on_complete=true) and splits chained commands when enabled; aphrodite_prefetch reads files the model names into its store (refuses .env, auth.json, ~/.ssh and the Hermes home); requires its own APHRODITE_API_KEY for an upstream LLM endpoint (default api.openai.com). entries.name: api-indonesia
entries.description:
Indonesian public data from official sources, right inside your agent: regions down to villages, postal codes, holidays, prayer times, BMKG weather and earthquakes, and more. Connects to API Indonesia's hosted MCP server with your API key.

- Regions and places: provinces down to villages with Kemendagri codes, postal codes, region boundaries
- Calendar: public holidays and cuti bersama, prayer times, Hijri dates
- Public services: schools, universities, hospitals, BMKG earthquakes, weather and warnings
- Money and checks: Bank Indonesia exchange rates, minimum wage (UMP), NIK/NPWP format checks, QRIS parsing, rupiah terbilang
- References: halal and BPOM lookups, OJK investment lists, KBBI, Al-Quran and Alkitab
- Bundles the api-indonesia skill; Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only

Disclosures
- Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.apiindonesia.id.
- Successful calls spend the key owner's API Indonesia credits; failed calls are not charged.
- The key is read from API_INDONESIA_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header.
- All tools are read-only lookups and calculators.
- The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.apiindonesia.id and successful calls spend the key owner's API Indonesia credits (failed calls are not charged; current rates at apiindonesia.id/#harga). The key is read from API_INDONESIA_KEY in the profile .env (or the plugin's settings form) and sent as a bearer header. All tools are read-only lookups and calculators; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.
