entries.name: apinex
entries.description: APInex as Hermes model providers on one key: `apinex` serves Claude 5.5 and Free-tier Claude models over APInex's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and extended thinking apply), and `apinex-openai` serves GPT-6.1, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4.1, GLM 5.3, Qwen 3.8, Kimi K3.1, Grok 4.7 and 17 Free-tier ($0.00/1M) chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, omitting non-tool and media endpoints, with 1M/500K context windows and native image input declared per model. Maintained by APInex. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and APINEX_API_KEY go to https://api.apinex.bond (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and APInex forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Hermes' standard GET https://api.apinex.bond/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

entries.description: Record from the Hermes composer and inspect screen, voice and drawing recordings as timestamped instructions and visual evidence. entries.name: apple-health-mcp
entries.description: Read the user's Apple Health export (workouts, steps, heart rate, HRV, sleep, cycle tracking) through the local apple-health MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Runs the `apple-health-mcp-unofficial@0.8.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: no network service: it parses the user's own Apple Health export on disk (the connector's `setup --auto-import` looks for exports in ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop and ~/Documents and copies them under `~/.apple-health-mcp/`). It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json`, and its connection-status tool reads `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: apple_health_profile_update (local profile only); apple_health_reimport (re-reads the local export); apple_health_clear_incremental_cache (clears the local parsed cache). No live sync: data is as fresh as the last export the user imported. The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

entries.name: apple-keychain
entries.description: Load Hermes secrets from macOS Keychain, with interactive setup, safe rotation and recovery. Reads explicitly configured Keychain items; operator commands can write items and manage recovery copies. Does not read or edit .env files. Compiles the included C helper locally with Apple developer tools and uses Security.framework and local macOS commands. Imports some private Hermes configuration helpers. Disclosure — registers the apple_keychain secret source: on macOS, once secrets.apple_keychain.enabled is true, Hermes startup reads the configured generic-password items from macOS Keychain and loads them as environment variables, overriding .env and inherited values by default (override_existing: true); on first use it compiles a small native helper from the plugin's own C source with the local Xcode Command Line Tools clang and caches it in ~/Library/Caches/hermes/apple-keychain (shared by all of the user's profiles; a plugin update can require re-authorising the new helper in Keychain Access), and it keeps empty per-item lock files in /private/tmp; the operator commands hermes keychain setup, set, provision and recovery write secrets.apple_keychain in config.yaml and create, rotate, restore or delete Keychain items, and provision copies the inherited environment values of the configured names into Keychain; rotation keeps the old value as a recovery item in the same keychain until the new value verifies (kept with --keep-backup or after a failed rotation until discarded); items the plugin creates trust the helper and /usr/bin/security (so other programs running as the same user can read them through the security CLI without a prompt), or any application with --allow-any-app; subprocesses get only PATH, HOME and TMPDIR; no network calls, no self-update; imports a few private Hermes helpers that can change between releases.

entries.name: arachne-flow
entries.description: Visual workflow canvas for Hermes Desktop: wire Hermes tools, MCP tools and LLM calls into typed graphs with conditions, bounded loops, JSON/list transforms, per-step caching and media previews (image, audio, video and an in-place 3D model viewer). Build with Hermes edits a graph from a description; seven agent tools and /flow list, build, run and inspect the same saved flows; twelve starter templates and user-saved templates. Disclosure — tool nodes execute through ctx.dispatch_tool on a background thread with Hermes' own tools, credentials and approvals (commands held for manual approval are denied or time out on the canvas and under cron), and other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks do not see these calls; shell, file-writing, browser, session-mutating and known code-running MCP tools are blocked by name by default, an explicit allow_tools setting can unblock them, and other MCP tools are not blocked; provider, LLM and media-generation calls can cost money, and Build with Hermes sends the prompt, node catalog and current flow to the active model before any run; a File node reads only files the user dropped (copied into the plugin's uploads folder) or picked with Browse… for that node, any agent edit or flow_run input drops the pick, and those files and media under Hermes' folders can be passed to the tools they are wired to, possibly to remote providers as data URLs; Hermes credential stores and .env files are never read; media URLs in tool output are downloaded with Hermes' SSRF-safe client (every redirect hop checked, 200 MB cap); user regexes in If/Switch run in an isolated Python subprocess killed after 0.5 s; the Send message node uses Hermes' official messaging bridge only after a per-recipient consent bound to flow, node and target plus a separate file consent, never caches or retries, and reports timeouts as unconfirmed; a local HMAC key (messaging-secret) signs that consent and the file picks; trigger nodes (schedule, RSS/Atom feed, local webhook, folder watch, after another flow) start a flow in the background without an agent turn only after the user switches them on in the canvas (agents and flow_apply can switch them off, never on), and one Hermes process per data folder fires them; the webhook listens on 127.0.0.1 only (default port 8649) behind a per-node HMAC token URL; feed URLs are checked with Hermes' is_safe_url before the request and on every redirect (2 MB cap); a folder watch reads only a folder the user picked for that node and skips secret files; flows, runs, uploads and cache live under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/arachne-flow/; the Desktop UI uses only @hermes/plugin-sdk; no stored provider credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: archytan-lite
entries.description: Every tool call is decided by Archytan Lite, an authorization gate that runs outside Hermes with its own signing key, before the tool runs. A call becomes checks on what it touches (each file path, each program and git subcommand a command runs, every path and URL it names, each host fetched, MCP and plugin tools by name); all must be ALLOWed, and each ALLOW is a single-use permission spent just before the tool runs. Refusals use the block directive, so they hold under /yolo and approvals.mode: off. Anything the plugin can't read precisely ($VAR, $(...), loops, unpinnable paths), any error, an unreachable gate or a bad signature is refused. Every decision is an Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipt; `hermes archytan verify` checks the whole log. Starter policy for one workspace, edited as JSON and applied with `hermes archytan reload`. Disclosure: the gate is proprietary software by the plugin's maintainer, free under its Community license, run from ghcr.io/high-archytech-solutions/archytan-lite@sha256:699cc1b1f2a4e40d94d095e7256e0fac3d94bddd8f5672c9750f9b4b7ece64e9 (2.7.3), which the plugin never pulls unless you pass --pull; `hermes archytan setup|reload|verify` and `/archytan verify` run docker with a minimal environment and create the volume archytan-hermes-data and the container archytan-hermes (restart unless-stopped, bound to 127.0.0.1:8431); the hook sends each gated call's action, resource (path, program, host or tool name) and hermes:<session id> to that local gate, never argument contents or results; stores its caller token through Hermes's credential store as ARCHYTAN_LITE_HERMES_TOKEN; writes the gate's policy, callers file (token hash only), public key and a capped decisions.jsonl under plugin-data/archytan-lite; carries the gate's MIT Python client (archytan-lite 2.1.1 client.py, byte-identical) so it has no Python dependencies; no telemetry. Until setup has run, every gated tool call is refused.

entries.name: arcmira
entries.description: YouTube transcript search and monitoring for your AI. Arcmira understands YouTube and podcasts like it watched them: the exact quote, often who said it, the full transcript and sponsors. Add "use arcmira" to any question to send it to Arcmira first. Sign in with Hermes-managed OAuth in your browser, no key needed, or set ARCMIRA_API_KEY. Bundles Arcmira's hosted MCP server and eleven research skills; portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Arcmira's MCP server at mcp.arcmira.com with the search terms, names, video links and JavaScript programs the agent writes (programs run on Arcmira's servers, never on your machine), authenticated with a Hermes-managed OAuth sign-in through api.arcmira.com or ARCMIRA_API_KEY. Reads, transcriptions and alerts use the account's credits. arcmira_execute_write creates and changes monitors that alert by email, Slack or webhook, and starts Premium transcripts; the package marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before each write-capable call, but a `hermes mcp add arcmira` entry in config.yaml replaces that setting unless it also sets `trust: untrusted`. arcmira_feedback sends the agent's note to Arcmira. Arcmira logs each tool call on the account. The tool list is served at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

known_issues: Sign in once after installing: merge examples/oauth.yaml from the plugin repo into your profile, then run hermes mcp login arcmira
On a machine with no browser, open the printed sign-in link on any device and paste the redirect URL back into Hermes, or use ARCMIRA_API_KEY.
Hermes does not prompt for ARCMIRA_API_KEY at install. Set it with hermes config set ARCMIRA_API_KEY <key> only if you skip OAuth.

entries.name: ard-kit
entries.description: Agentic Resource Discovery — search a local tool catalog by intent and inspect an entry to get its invoke command. entries.name: argorant
entries.description: Argorant through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.argorant.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the user's Argorant account, no keys in config): find B2B leads by job, industry, company and place, with free counts and masked previews; reveal or export checked work emails; save lists; check email lists the user already has; write, test and launch cold email campaigns from the user's own mailboxes; and read, label and answer replies. Bundles the argorant workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Argorant's hosted server (mcp.argorant.com) and acts on the user's Argorant account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Revealing, exporting, finding emails, checking email lists and adding people to a campaign spend the user's Argorant credits; launching a campaign and answering a reply send real email from the user's connected mailboxes; buying credits or ordering mailboxes can charge the card saved in the workspace after the user's yes. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: argos
entries.description: Lets Hermes agents drive a live Godot 4 editor through a local MCP server with trust=untrusted: read the scene tree, create / move / delete nodes, undo-grouped action.batch, AnimationPlayer/AnimationTree play/stop, set properties with the editor's real undo/redo, open / save / create scenes, play and stop the game, validate GDScript with --check-only, and capture PNG screenshots (named sessions under .argos/captures/). Launch / check / play require ARGOS_PROJECT allowlist. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — the Godot addon opens a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 only (ports 9080-9090) guarded by a random token rotated each editor start and stored in <project>/.argos/; writes state, history and screenshots under <project>/.argos/ (captures only under .argos/captures/ or res://, never absolute paths, `..` or overwrites); for projects on ARGOS_PROJECT / ARGOS_ALLOWED_PROJECTS it launches the Godot editor, runs `godot --check-only` and plays scenes, which executes that project's own GDScript (use on trusted projects); the MCP server is untrusted, so Hermes asks before every editing tool and argos_raw forwards any ARGOS action; needs a Python with websockets; no third-party network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: ariadne-thread
entries.description: n8n-style flows for Hermes Desktop: each cron job, webhook route and skill drawn as a chain of steps, with the scheduler's true cron status, run output, delivery targets and a health bar, plus in-place editing with history and undo. Disclosure — reads cron/jobs.json, cron/output/<job id>/, every SKILL.md under skills/ and skills.external_dirs, config.yaml (skills.external_dirs only), a script in scripts/ when opened, and profiles/ folder names; reads webhook routes and cron delivery targets from Hermes' own GET /api/webhooks and GET /api/cron/delivery-targets through the raw window.hermesDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no route to core endpoints), never opening webhook_subscriptions.json; writes only on Save, in the active profile only: SKILL.md (atomic, inside skills/ only), files in scripts/, and a cron's prompt and deliver target through Hermes' cron.jobs.update_job, each save first keeping the replaced text under plugin-data/ariadne-thread/history (0600, newest 10 per target) and refusing if the file changed since it was opened; webhook prompts are read-only; "Ask agent" only drafts a new chat and nothing runs until you send it; no shell commands, no network beyond the local Hermes backend, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: ariadne
entries.description: Record a Hermes session once, then replay it with no model, no network and no tokens to see exactly what Hermes does differently: check whether updating Hermes is safe by replaying your own sessions (with your plugins loaded) on the new version, replay on a new build, compare two installs, bisect the Hermes commit that changed a session, fork a recorded session to a live model from any model call, export trajectories and preference pairs, and check Hermes's documented hook contracts on every run. Disclosure — recording is off until you turn it on; cassettes are written locally under plugin-data with secrets scrubbed (tool output can still hold private file contents); play, compare, bisect and fork start Hermes (python -m tui_gateway.entry) as a child process and drive it over JSON-RPC; replays copy this profile's SOUL.md, memories/ and skills/ and only an allowlist of request-shaping settings from config.yaml (never hooks, MCP servers, terminal, auxiliary endpoints or credentials; --trust-config keeps all) into a throwaway home, never .env or auth.json, decode only openai/anthropic SDK model types from cassettes, answer every approval with deny, neutralise tool arguments and block outbound network through a closed local proxy; fork makes real model calls with your configured provider inside your own home (the forked session appears in your history) and runs tools after the fork point only with --live-tools; upgrade-check (CLI, or a button in Desktop) runs git ls-remote and git clone against github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent and uv against the package index to install that Hermes, plus the python_dependencies your enabled plugins declare, into its own venv under plugin-data/ariadne/hermes/ (your install is not touched), then replays offline and loads your enabled plugins in both scratch homes; bisect checks out commits in a Hermes checkout you name, refusing a dirty tree and restoring the original commit; the optional Desktop half (off until you enable it) adds an Ariadne page, a REC status-bar chip, a mark on recorded sessions, palette commands and a theme, and its backend routes (dashboard/plugin_api.py, loaded only when ariadne is in plugins.enabled) read the plugin's own data folder and start replays and forks as background jobs; fonts are bundled, nothing is fetched from third-party hosts; no telemetry.

entries.name: art98
entries.description: Drive a real Windows 98 SE VM through art98 (screenshots, pointer, keys, windows, Win32 calls) and render scene scripts to video, with a dashboard tab that has a live view. Disclosure — art98_render runs the agent's scene script as Python on the Hermes machine, in a child process outside the terminal backend and not sandboxed (it can read HOME and the VM token); it refuses unless the allow_render setting is on (off by default) and the user approves that script content through Hermes's approval gate: a pre_tool_call hook asks for approval naming the scripts and the sha256 of the scene and its imported animations/ modules, and the tool re-hashes its snapshot and refuses on a mismatch. Unattended runs (-q, cron, unattended platforms) are refused unless the matching approvals.*_mode is set to approve; --yolo and approvals.mode: off approve without a prompt; "always" covers only that exact script content, and content approved with "always" also runs unprompted in unattended runs. The dashboard's own Render button skips that approval. art98_win32 is off unless allow_win32 is on. Network is loopback only: the art98 VM's control API (token-authenticated) and optionally its view-only VNC port. One stored credential, the VM token, kept by Hermes as the vm_token secret. Needs ffmpeg and ffprobe for art98_combine, and the user's own Windows 98 SE install via the art98 repo; no Windows files ship with the plugin.
entries.title: art98 (Windows 98)
known_issues: Needs a running art98 VM (github.com/StanLukuvka/98artware) and your own Windows 98 SE disc and key; the art98-install skill walks through it.
The art98_render approval hash covers the scene and its static animations/ imports; data files beside them are linked in unhashed.
Render approvals are held in process memory, so a Hermes restart between the prompt and the render refuses it (not_approved).

entries.name: artifacts
entries.description: Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to HERMES_ARTIFACTS_URL with the machine credential HERMES_ARTIFACTS_TOKEN, resolved through Hermes secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact_publish reads a resolved local path only after Hermes read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Hermes write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.

entries.title: ASCII Worlds
known_issues: The author reviewed the 1.4.0 release candidates on macOS with Hermes Desktop (a general test; Desktop version and per-scene results were not recorded). The screenshots are browser captures of the plugin's own preview and settings page.
Fine glyph density at full speed, high counts, Depth and the optional whole-window layer use noticeable CPU. Battery saver and a bolder density turn the cost down.

entries.name: ask-ledger
entries.description: Keeps a durable ledger of what you asked and promised: each message becomes an ask (A1, A2 ...) with a state (open, in progress, needs you, answered, closed), and todos (T1, T2 ...) that you add, or that the agent adds when you commit to something (marked added by agent; at most 2 a turn and 10 a day; can be turned off), with a category and due date. Snooze, done and drop work by command (/snooze, /done, /drop) or in plain words; the agent can only suggest them, and a words action must match your current message. Unresolved items are reminded to the agent every turn across restarts and compaction, and /asks, /todos plus a static no-JavaScript page show where everything stands. Disclosure — stores your messages and todos (trimmed, common secret shapes redacted) in plaintext under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ask-ledger/, append-only and never pruned, with local counts of how you snooze and close; injects a short block of your unresolved asks and up to 3 todos into each turn's user message, so they reach your model provider; appends up to 3 plain reminder lines and a hint to the assistant's reply (transform_llm_output); keeps one plain Open todos message per chat, edited in place, only in conversations it is already part of (setting board, on by default); in group, channel and thread chats it shows only counts, no todo text, unless the chat is listed in trusted_chats; an optional ntfy push (off by default, https only) sends only a count and the page link; no shell commands, no reads outside its data folder, no telemetry.

entries.name: asset-curator
entries.description: Find assets or create them from code with user-controlled access, host-confirmed asset review and preserved licensing/provenance. Disclosure — Asset Curator downloads third-party assets and writes files on your machine. With no access mode set it saves only to Downloads and asks before each download. In "project" mode it writes only inside the workspace you set. "review" mode stages assets in Downloads and asks you before moving each one into your project. In "hermes" or "full" mode the plugin applies no path limits of its own, so the agent can write wherever your user account can, and Hermes' approval prompt is the only check.

entries.name: assetrizz
entries.description: Assetrizz for Hermes: search 14,641 original 2D game assets and have the agent compose them into rendered scenes, with a live preview pane. assetrizz_search runs full-text search over slugs, tags, descriptions, styles and categories across 23 style packs (for example pixel_32 and cozy_cartoon). assetrizz_scene creates a canvas, tiles floors and walls, places, moves, scales, flips and layers props and characters, renders a PNG, and saves or loads scene JSON. Its op=compose builds a whole scene from one compact spec using four gameplay templates (topdown_farming, topdown_shooter, dungeon_crawler, side_platformer) and returns layer lint for collisions, HUD/playfield overlap and off-canvas items. Skill id assetrizz:assetrizz-composer. On Hermes Desktop 0.23 or newer, a dark Assetrizz pane live-previews the current scene through ctx.rest, browses assets and installs or removes a local library (deletion needs confirmation). The two tools also run without the pane. It is for game jams, prototypes, level mockups and pitch art that need consistent tiles and sprites quickly. To start, run hermes plugins install assetrizz and hermes plugins enable assetrizz, then ask: "Search assetrizz for pixel_32 grass and dirt path tiles, then compose a 640×320 meadow with a path, a couple of trees, a ranger and a hare. Render a PNG." Search works at once from the bundled catalog; the first search builds a lean SQLite + FTS5 index in the plugin data directory. Renders come back as file paths. No keys are needed. Disclosure — in the default on_demand mode the plugin downloads individual PNGs from raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/assetrizz at the pinned v0.1.0 tag (SHA-256-verified against the bundled catalog) and caches them under the plugin data directory; the Desktop pane and CLI can download whole style packs (up to about 1.65 GB) to a local folder and delete that folder or the cache after confirmation; rendered scenes are written to the plugin data directory or the user's configured export directory.
entries.title: Assetrizz
known_issues: The Desktop compose pane has not yet been proven on a live Hermes Desktop host; the two tools and the mocked pane API tests still run without it.

entries.name: assumption-ledger
entries.description: Persistent operational-assumption ledger. Captures the assumptions an agent states in its own messages (never from tool output), keeps the sentence each came from as provenance, verifies them with deterministic checks, and warns in context when work recorded in a session depends on an assumption evidence has contradicted. Disclosure — all state is local: assumptions, evidence and decisions are stored in a plain SQLite database under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/assumption-ledger/ (created on first use, never pruned by the plugin; delete the directory to clear it). It needs no credentials. HTTP checks (http_status, http_json_field) are the only outbound traffic; they accept only http/https and refuse loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and cloud-metadata destinations unless you set allow_private_urls, and metadata endpoints stay blocked even then. Command checks (command_succeeds) are disabled until you set command_allowlist; only a listed bare executable name runs (a path is refused), resolved to an absolute path on the child's PATH, with a minimal environment. The allowlist restricts which program may run, not the safety of the arguments the model passes it. Git checks run in a model-chosen directory with the repository's core.fsmonitor and core.hooksPath settings overridden and with a minimal environment; filter drivers set in that repository's own .git/config still apply to git status, so point git checks only at repositories whose local git config you trust. It reads local files, git state, environment variables and SQLite databases, warns rather than blocking a turn, scopes warnings to the session that recorded the decision, and exposes no tools that write to external systems.

entries.name: astro-agents
entries.description: Verifiable planetary timing data for market analysis and backtesting through the Astro Agents MCP server (24 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://astro-agent.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): geocentric and heliocentric positions, declination, Gann planetary lines, a to-the-minute event calendar (ingresses, stations, eclipses), sky analogues and crypto token launch charts and synastry, plus full Western and Vedic astrology (birth chart, transits, synastry, kundli D1-D60, dashas, doshas, KP, yogas, panchang, Gun Milan), computed from the NASA/JPL DE440 ephemeris with no LLM; every result carries a SHA-256 hash. Data for your own analysis, never a trading signal or forecast. Bundles the astrology skill (when to call which tool, input conventions). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call sends the dates, times and coordinates it is given to astro-agent.dev, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. 1 free call per client on the $0.01-0.02 routes only (REST, MCP or A2A); every other route, finance included, is always paid. Over MCP a paid tool returns a standard x402 offer (USDC on Base or Solana) and is paid per call only if the user's own x402 MCP client signs it, or with prepaid credits when the user sets an X-Credits-Token header; the package holds no wallet, key or token.

entries.name: asyntai
entries.description: Run your website's Asyntai AI support agent from Hermes through Asyntai's hosted MCP server (73 tools): add knowledge, edit agent instructions, change the widget, read conversations, leads and analytics, answer tickets and emails, and reply live to visitors. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure: runs the pinned @asyntai/mcp@1.0.2 bridge over npx stdio (Node.js 18+); every tool call goes to https://asyntai.com/mcp. The first call opens a browser for OAuth 2.1 PKCE sign-in, and the tokens are stored in ~/.asyntai/mcp-credentials.json; in unattended runs the call fails at the MCP timeout. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that is not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: athena
entries.description: The local AI-app store for Hermes: browse a constantly growing catalogue of apps, install an app from any git repository, launch it, read its logs and stop it. It declares HF_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN so Hermes offers to set them, and reads each one through Hermes' own secret route rather than scavenging another program's token store. An app is handed a credential only after you approve that app, as an environment variable for the life of its process - never written to disk and never sent anywhere by Athena itself. Apps run on your machine on loopback; third-party install scripts run as you, and the README states the network endpoints, the WSL/QEMU command paths and the GitHub publish path in full. The panel and the CLI are two doors into the same engine. Agent control is in active development. Disclosure — installs apps by cloning third-party git repositories and running their own install and launch scripts on your machine as you (each install and first launch asks through Hermes' approval prompt); provisions a pinned app engine from npm at setup after consent; hands HF_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN to an app only after you approve that app, as an environment variable of its process; sends the GitHub token only to GitHub hosts; can manage WSL/QEMU machines and publish your store to a GitHub repository you name.
entries.title: Athena
known_issues: Windows-tested only. The panel, the engine and app launches are exercised on Windows; Linux is expected to work but is untested, so the entry declares `platforms: [windows]`.
The bundled engine is provisioned at setup from npm at a pinned version behind a consent step, so first setup needs network access to the npm registry; an offline machine cannot start the engine.

An app whose menu marks no entry as default (FaceFusion, for example) is opened on its first runnable script - the install step on a fresh clone, the start action after. Athena falls back to the app's own menu rather than refusing to run it.

entries.description: The athlete's own training and health data from 39 apps (Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, Hevy, Apple Health, Intervals.icu and more) through athletedata's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.athletedata.health/mcp): activities, training load, HRV, sleep, readiness, nutrition, body composition, race predictions, and structured workouts pushed to the athlete's watch. Bundles one skill that tells the agent when to use it. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.athletedata.health and needs an athletedata account (paid, 7-day free trial) with its API key in ATHLETEDATA_API_KEY; the athlete's health and training data is returned from that server. Write tools (push a workout to the watch, log food, create a Hevy routine) change the athlete's own accounts; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: atlas-sidecar-excel
entries.description: Sidecar by Atlas Omnia — your Hermes agent in desktop Excel for Mac. The plugin runs an HTTPS localhost bridge on ports 47640-47644, exposing 28 sidecar_excel_* tools and opt-in workbook plans. Manual CA trust and one sidebar Allow are required. Allowing lets the configured site use your Hermes agent and all its tools until revoke; use a site you control or trust and open only documents you trust. API_SERVER_KEY is read through Hermes, never sent to the sidebar or stored by the plugin; TLS private keys are owner-only. For TLS it can only vouch for localhost. The trust command does not limit the certificate to TLS, so protect the key file and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. Latest live run: 2026-11-11 about 00:26 in desktop Excel for Mac, plugin and sidebar built from a7b3fd7. Connect, Allow, a 3-row table with header in A1:B4 and =SUM(B2:B4) in B5 read back from the workbook; revoke dropped the sidebar to needs your OK. The bridge answered 200 to the configured origin and 403 to another origin. The sidebar used a private test site via addin_base, with CA trust in the login keychain; this Mac also has it in the System keychain. Earlier the same night at 35ef09e (behaviour unchanged since): reversal on request by clearing the range (no real undo), plugin reload with the sidebar open (it reconnected by itself and edited again), approval remembered after restarting Excel, next Connect after revoke asked for approval again. Not tested: Windows desktop Excel, dark theme, keyboard-only use, public Pages origin, TLS-only trust or all workbook tools/plans. Reopen the sidebar if it does not reconnect. The Excel test Mac also has System-keychain trust; that was not required in our Word and PowerPoint runs, which used login-keychain trust only. By default the plugin serves its bundled sidebar from the same HTTPS bridge at https://localhost:<actual-port>/sidecar-excel/; GitHub Pages or self-hosting is not required. A custom HTTPS site remains available through addin_base. Office.js loads from Microsoft. Hermes may send chat/workbook data to the configured provider. CLI approval/status never starts a listener. Remove matching CA trust manually before deleting the plugin tls directory; uninstall/revoke does not remove OS trust. No telemetry or self-updater. Apache-2.0; LICENSE and NOTICE included. No Microsoft or Nous Research endorsement. Disclosure — While the gateway runs, this plugin keeps an HTTPS listener on 127.0.0.1:47640-47644 and asks you to trust, by hand, a per-install root CA in your macOS login keychain. The CA can only vouch for localhost in TLS, but the trust command does not limit it to TLS, so protect its key file in the plugin's data folder and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. After you click Allow in Hermes, the sidebar site (by default the plugin's own localhost page) can run your full Hermes agent with all its tools through your API server until `/sidecar-excel revoke`. Workbook content goes to your configured model provider, and an opened workbook can inject instructions, so open only documents you trust. Dangerous-command approvals cannot be answered from the sidebar and time out as denied. Office.js loads from Microsoft. Uninstalling does not remove OS trust.
entries.title: Sidecar for Excel
known_issues: The plugin-served localhost sidebar (1.1.0 default) is live-tested in desktop Word for Mac at 74a6c41; the identical bridge change is covered by Excel's automated suite but has not yet been live-tested in Excel.
Live-tested only for the limited desktop Excel for Mac flow in the README; reload with an open sidebar reconnected and edited again. Windows desktop Excel is untested.
The sidebar must reach https://localhost with the per-install local CA manually trusted; network restrictions or missing trust leave the sidebar on 'Hermes is not reachable'.

The optional public GitHub Pages override has not been live-tested; hosting is not required for the bundled localhost default. TLS-only trust (-p ssl) and a server-auth EKU on the CA are planned hardening.

entries.name: atlas-sidecar-libreoffice
entries.description: Sidecar for LibreOffice by Atlas Omnia — your Hermes agent works on the Calc, Writer and Impress documents you already have open in LibreOffice, with a native sidebar chat panel. 55 tools read and edit the open documents the agent names by document_id; supported edits are one named undo step and Hermes can undo its own changes. Setup: install the plugin, then download the companion LibreOffice extension (.oxt) from the v0.4.1 release or build it from that tag (Hermes does not install it) and add it in LibreOffice's Extension Manager (Tools > Extensions), pair with Tools > Copy Sidecar pairing token and save the token as LIBREOFFICE_LIVE_BRIDGE_TOKEN; the optional sidebar chat is off by default and also needs the Hermes API server with API_SERVER_KEY and the plugin setting chat_port (8661). Disclosure — the extension runs a token-checked plain-HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8660 inside LibreOffice while LibreOffice runs and stores its pairing token owner-only in the LibreOffice profile; Hermes keeps a copy in its secret store. The plugin's token-checked sidebar chat endpoint is off by default and is not started unless the user sets chat_port (8661); then, inside the Hermes gateway process (plugins.isolation: in_process, the default), it listens on 127.0.0.1:8661 from when the gateway loads the plugin until the plugin is unloaded or Hermes exits and forwards panel chats to the user's Hermes API server on loopback (setting api_server_port, default 8642) with API_SERVER_KEY, read through Hermes's profile-scoped secret lookup, kept in memory, never logged or sent to LibreOffice. Both listeners authenticate the client only, so a local process that holds one of the ports while the real listener is down could receive the pairing token or the API key. On Windows both listeners bind 127.0.0.1 on their port with SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE (since 0.4.1; 0.4.0 used SO_REUSEADDR), so while they listen a second socket cannot bind that same address and port; a bind of the same port number on the wildcard address still succeeds (in a Windows 11 check it did not receive a connection made to 127.0.0.1). A panel chat is the user's full Hermes agent with its tools limited by a pre_tool_call hook to this plugin's tools plus skill_view, skills_list, tool_search and tool_describe; the hook does not cover external-agent model runtimes, which are unsupported for the sidebar chat. calc_get_overview lists the titles and file locations of all open LibreOffice documents, and there is no per-edit approval. There is no upload step, but document excerpts and chat go through Hermes to its configured model. The extension and plugin run no shell commands, make no third-party network calls themselves (LibreOffice may when it evaluates document content) and have no telemetry or self-updater. Sidecar is developed by Atlas Omnia. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by The Document Foundation, Microsoft or Nous Research. LibreOffice is a trademark of The Document Foundation.
entries.title: Sidecar for LibreOffice
known_issues: Hermes installs only the plugin. The companion LibreOffice extension (.oxt) is attached to the v0.4.1 release or built from that tag (the README gives its SHA-256; the build is byte-identical on macOS, Linux and Windows) and added by hand in LibreOffice's Extension Manager (LibreOffice with Python-UNO required). Upgrading: remove any earlier build of the extension (the 0.4.0 extension has a new identifier, LibreOffice installs it alongside the old one, and both would bind port 8660), and after replacing a plugin build before 0.4.0 (libreoffice-live) restart the Hermes gateway once, because the old plugin's chat listener keeps port 8661 until then.

Native tests ran on LibreOffice 26.8.2.2 on macOS 27.2: the 0.4.0 .oxt in a disposable profile, and an earlier compressed build of the same extension files in an everyday install. On Windows 11 (LibreOffice 26.8.3.1) a compressed build of the same extension files was installed through the Extension Manager dialog, shown in the sidebar and passed the plugin-handler matrix, driven by synthetic window messages on a locked console; the 0.4.0 .oxt built there with the same SHA-256 and registered with a command-line unopkg in a disposable profile. 0.4.1 changes only the Windows socket options of both listeners and the plugin's unload order; its .oxt was installed into disposable LibreOffice profiles on macOS (a fresh install and an upgrade over 0.4.0 that kept the pairing token) and on Windows 11 (command-line unopkg), and its plugin was loaded by a throwaway Hermes 0.23.1 gateway on macOS with a stand-in model (start, 30 plugin reloads, stop on disable during a reply); unit suites ran on macOS, Linux and Windows, and a Windows 11 check bound and rebound both listeners. Hermes itself was not available on the Windows host: the plugin has not been installed or loaded by Hermes on Windows, and the sidebar chat has not connected there (the panel was seen only in its not-connected state). Double-click install and real mouse and keyboard input were not run on Windows either. On Linux only the unit tests run (CI on Ubuntu with Python 3.11 and 3.13); the unit tests also run in CI on macOS and Windows. Hermes versions: tested with Hermes Agent 0.23.1 (installed: CLI, plugin manager, one gateway chat); on the v0.23.3 source, run with the 0.23.1 installation's Python environment and without a gateway or model, plugin validation passed with no warnings and the plugin-manager probe (default off, failing polls, unload) gave the same results.

The sidebar chat is off by default (chat_port 0); the plugin starts no chat endpoint unless the user sets chat_port. Its tool fence is a pre_tool_call hook, not a Hermes-enforced limit. External-agent runtimes are unsupported for restricted sidebar chat. Keep chat_port: 0 when using one. The dedicated-profile recipe restricts Hermes tools only; it does not disable an external runtime's built-in tools. Use a Hermes-managed model/tool loop for that recipe, explicitly configure it in the dedicated profile, disable MCP and other toolsets there, and verify the resulting configuration before enabling sidebar forwarding. External agents such as codex_app_server run their own tools, which never reach Hermes hooks. Another gap (an older non-default API execution mode after compaction) is in SECURITY.md.

Accepted limitation, only after the user turns the sidebar chat on: when the plugin is disabled or reloaded, Hermes removes its tool restriction (the pre_tool_call hook) as soon as the unload callback returns, possibly before the plugin's 10-second stop budget has run out; a sidebar chat that was not confirmed stopped keeps running without the restriction, with the user's full Hermes tools. This is accepted and disclosed for 0.4.0; the fix needs a Hermes-side per-run tool restriction. Unload first asks the runs whose IDs it knows to stop (a run whose creation was never answered has none). A gateway shutdown or restart does not unload plugins first: Hermes drains, then interrupts, its API-server runs, and they end with the gateway process.

When turned on, the sidebar chat starts only with plugins.isolation: in_process and needs the Hermes API server enabled with API_SERVER_KEY; in a gateway serving several profiles, the first profile to bind a given chat port gets it. A run whose status can no longer be read is asked to stop and stays tracked until it is seen to settle; run creation uses an Idempotency-Key. The chat endpoint was checked through Hermes 0.23.1's plugin manager against fake Runs API servers, and in real chats through a 0.23.1 gateway with a model on macOS, once with an earlier build of the plugin and once with the 0.4.0 plugin code with the chat turned on (read, edit, undo, a terminal command refused by the fence; the plugin was also replaced in the running gateway and the chat endpoint rebound); stopping a run on unload, recovery from a lost Runs API answer and a chat across a compaction were not exercised with a gateway.

calc_activate_sheet and calc_recalculate are not undoable; some Impress undo restores text without its mixed formatting; protection does not block the bridge's own writes; shape colours set by impress_add_shape are saved to .pptx as theme colours.
Slide reorder is not available (LibreOffice exposes no identity-preserving API) and pivot tables are not implemented. The sidebar panel shows plain-text replies (no streaming or Markdown).

entries.name: atlas-sidecar-powerpoint
entries.description: Sidecar by Atlas Omnia — Your Hermes agent, in the sidebar of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Sidecar puts your Hermes agent in a side panel next to the file you're working on. Ask it to draft, edit, analyze, or build without leaving your document, spreadsheet, or deck. In PowerPoint it reads slides, adds slides, text boxes and shapes, replaces and formats text, and reorders, deletes or re-lays out slides. After one manual local-CA trust step, connect with one click; approval authorizes subsequent chat-driven edits, not per-edit confirmation; runs on your machine, no API key files (protected TLS keys in plugin data). Your agent: it runs on your own Hermes setup, with the models and tools you already use. Setup: install the plugin, enable the Hermes API server, manually trust the per-install local CA using the printed command (never run automatically), run /sidecar-powerpoint manifest to write a manifest for the actual bridge port and sideload it into PowerPoint, click Connect to Hermes and allow it in Hermes with /sidecar-powerpoint. Disclosure — the plugin serves its bundled sidebar at https://localhost:<actual-port>/sidecar-powerpoint/ from an HTTPS listener bound to 127.0.0.1:47650-47654 (first free port) inside the process that runs the Hermes gateway (or plugin host) from when the gateway loads the plugin (setting autostart, default on; off: from the first /sidecar-powerpoint or sidecar_powerpoint_* call) until the plugin stops or Hermes exits; by default it accepts the same exact https://localhost:<actual-port> origin and exactly one Host localhost:<actual-port>. An external HTTPS site remains optional through addin_base; the default needs no web hosting. A per-install CA and localhost certificate are generated in plugin-data/atlas-sidecar-powerpoint/tls/; private keys are owner-only, never logged. For TLS it can only vouch for localhost. The trust command does not limit the certificate to TLS, so protect the key file and remove the trust when you stop using Sidecar. Critical permitted DNS localhost subtree and IP 127.0.0.1/32; no IPv6; CA validity is at most 825 days, leaf at most 397. known_issues: The plugin-served localhost sidebar (1.2.0 default) is live-tested in desktop Word for Mac at 74a6c41; the identical bridge change is covered by PowerPoint's automated suite but has not yet been live-tested in PowerPoint.
TLS-only trust (-p ssl) and a server-auth EKU on the CA are planned hardening; neither is implemented yet.

Live-tested in desktop PowerPoint for Mac at `315f1f0`, 2026-11-11 about 00:32: Connect and Allow; one prompt changed slide 1's title and subtitle, verified by readback from the deck, and produced exactly one request to Hermes. After a plugin reload with the sidebar open, it showed “Lost the connection to Hermes on this computer.” with a Try again button; Try again reconnected. Revoke dropped the sidebar to “needs your OK”. In the earlier run at `3682e5f`, about 00:01 the same night (behaviour unchanged since), one prompt changed slide 1's title and subtitle and added a second slide with three bullets, verified by readback. The request stayed open for about 24 seconds with no timeout or repeat. After a plugin reload in that run the sidebar showed “Not connected” and did not reconnect within 10 seconds; reopening it connected. Reversal on request restored the deck (no real undo). Approval was remembered after restarting PowerPoint; the next Connect after revoke asked for approval again. PowerPoint needs Try again (or reopen the sidebar) after a plugin reload; Excel and Word reconnect by themselves. entries.title: Sidecar for Word
known_issues: Live-tested 2026-11-11 about 19:40 in desktop Word for Mac at 74a6c41 with the plugin-served localhost sidebar (no external hosting): Connect, Allow, and a prompt that wrote a heading and a sentence into a new document.

After updating or reloading the plugin, reopen the sidebar if it does not reconnect. Sidecar provides no real undo tool: use native Office Undo, verified for a supported short edit only. Asking Hermes to reverse an edit edits again.

Trust the per-install local CA once using the printed login-keychain command. Remove it in Keychain Access > login > Certificates > Sidecar for Word local CA … > Delete (older installs: Sidecar local CA …), then delete the plugin tls folder.

Historical pre-repair failure, superseded by accepted d4d0de9 repair: tested live in desktop Word for Mac on 2026-11-11 at about 00:29, with the plugin and sidebar built from 7eaf1fc. Connect and Allow worked. The prompt “Write the line Quarterly Summary as a Heading 1, then one short paragraph about fruit prices” wrote both paragraphs, which were read back from the document, but the first line ended as Normal, not Heading 1. OOXML merged the heading/body before an apply_edit_plan search failed with SearchStringInvalidOrTooLong on a retained 312-character ASCII find. Later recovery restored separate text paragraphs, but final style readback was Normal; the precise style-loss operation is unisolated. Revoke dropped the sidebar to “needs your OK”. Earlier the same night at 2387154 (historical run): heading text and a bulleted list written with readback; Heading 1 style applied when asked; reversal on request removed the text but left empty paragraphs (no real undo). Plugin reload with the sidebar open reconnected by itself; approval was remembered after restarting Word; the next Connect after revoke asked for approval again. The sidebar was served from a private test site via addin_base; the CA was trusted in the login keychain only. Windows desktop Word is not tested. Dark theme, keyboard-only use, Word for the web, the public GitHub Pages origin, and TLS-only trust are not tested.

Retained evidence identifies the failed search as 312 ASCII characters, beyond Word’s 255-character search bound. OOXML had already merged the heading/body before that failure; final Heading 1 was Normal, but the exact operation losing style remains unisolated. Accepted d4d0de9 repair passed 429 JavaScript and 213 Python tests and bounded native Word 16.114.4/macOS 27.2 tests for heading/body styles, targeted repair, search boundaries, short-edit native Office Undo and revoke. Picture-only paragraph sharing, arbitrary rich formatting, fields/content controls and comprehensive native Unicode/5000-character replacement remain unqualified. The repaired bounds are: source and encoded queries are capped at 255 UTF-16 units, replacement capacity stays 5000, actual styles are read back, and failed searches must stop destructive recovery. Guidance is not a hard execution fence; use native Office Undo for recovery after uncertain mutations.
Two internal error messages still say Hermes for Word.

The sidebar must reach https://localhost from its HTTPS page with the local CA manually trusted for the current user. Local network policies may still block it; backend TLS tests are not live Office acceptance.

The installer can override addin_base. The public default is https://atlasomnia.github.io/sidecar-word/; first public-origin live test is at publication. Planned hardening: TLS-only trust (-p ssl) and a server-auth EKU on the CA.

entries.name: atlas
entries.description: Keeps your Pursuits current across your AI Harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Hermes, and Sessions run through T3 Code) and sends you a daily brief with the next Step for each. Disclosure — reads, never writes, the Session stores of those tools under your home folder, and reads through a Harness folder that is a link; copies their transcripts verbatim into a local record folder (default ~/atlas, mode 0700), with detected secrets masked, best effort, in every derived file but not in the raw copies; once you add ChatGPT or claude.ai, reads the export zips you drop in ~/atlas/inbox/ (in memory, capped, never group_chats.json), keeps their conversations verbatim the same way (claude.ai attachment text included), and deletes each zip after it imported every conversation in it, keeping one it cannot read; sends Session text, detected secrets masked, to the model your Hermes is configured with, during `hermes atlas backfill` and then unattended on every tick (up to 20 Sessions per tick, one model call each, plus the Journal, which a late Session such as an imported one makes it write again, and one call a day that adds to your Profile from that day's Steps, Journal lines and Session times, never transcript text), which costs model calls; a model's answer can change what the record says about one Pursuit, and can list the Session under at most 2 other Pursuits that are active, which splits its Active Time with them, so text inside a conversation can influence the next brief; claims messages addressed to Atlas in your Telegram home chat (the word atlas, a reply to a brief or to the weekly Review, a 10-minute window, /atlas), which then do not reach the Hermes agent, and answers there; sends the daily brief to that chat unprompted by running `hermes send`, and the brief and resume answers name this machine's host name, the folder and the git branch of each Step (for a web chat, the conversation's title and day), which a group home chat shows to everyone in it; sends a second unprompted message, the weekly Review, once a week (Sunday 18:00 by default) to the same chat, also by running `hermes send`; it proposes Focus, ending and reopen changes and never changes a Pursuit by itself, and replies to it are claimed; `hermes atlas setup` writes $HERMES_HOME/scripts/atlas_tick.sh and creates the `atlas-tick` Hermes cron job, which runs `hermes atlas tick` every 10 minutes; parks a Pursuit by itself, when it composes a daily brief, after it asked about that Pursuit twice and the latest ask went unanswered, and never ends one; serves a read and write API for its dashboard tab under /api/plugins/atlas/, behind the dashboard's own sign-in; deletes files in its own record folder when you tell it to forget a Session; records this machine's host name in the record; reads its own /proc/self/fd and /proc/self/maps to check which file SQLite opened. entries.name: atmorouter
entries.description: AtmoRouter — OpenAI-compatible gateway; one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Grok models, with the /model picker fed by the live GET /v1/models catalog. Disclosure — sends your prompts, conversation history, tool definitions, tool results and ATMOROUTER_API_KEY to atmorouter.dev, which forwards each request to the infrastructure serving the chosen model; that infrastructure's processing location and retention vary per model and zero retention is not promised (AtmoRouter states its usage and billing records keep metadata rather than prompt or response content, and that it does not train on API request content; https://atmorouter.dev/privacy). Usage is billed per token from a prepaid AtmoRouter balance (QRIS, or USDT/USDC on Solana, BNB Chain or Polygon); prices vary by capacity offer and, with no saved budget, a request can route to any offer up to the highest advertised catalog tier, unless you set a minimum discount off official rates or exact rate caps under Budgets; failed upstream requests are not billed and the plugin itself makes no payments.

entries.name: atomicmail
entries.description: Gives a Hermes agent its own @atomicmail.ai address in one command, with no account or signup form (proof-of-work sign-up). Mail from the user's allowed addresses wakes the agent and its reply goes out in the same thread; every allowed sender's DKIM signature is checked first, so a forged From: cannot drive the agent. Tools read, search, send and reply, and schedule meetings with real calendar invitations (send, update, cancel, read RSVPs, answer invitations). Disclosure — gives the agent its own @atomicmail.ai inbox: mail from addresses in ATOMICMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS (none by default) that passes a DKIM check reaches the agent as a chat message and the agent's reply is emailed back; ATOMICMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true turns the DKIM check off, so a forged From: can then drive the agent; the model can send new mail, replies, calendar invitations, updates, cancellations and RSVPs from that address to any recipient without a Hermes approval prompt (the tools only ask the model to confirm with the user first), and Atomic Mail adds a "Sent from Atomic Mail Agentic" footer; network calls to Atomic Mail only (auth.atomicmail.ai for sign-up and sign-in, api.atomicmail.ai for JMAP: polling, reading, sending, invitations, and downloading each new allowed message for the DKIM check) plus DNS TXT lookups for DKIM keys (system resolver; when it returns nothing, DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com, then dns.google; ATOMICMAIL_DNS_OVER_HTTPS=off disables that); a background polling task (every 20 s) while the gateway runs; Atomic Mail's anti-spam proof-of-work (scrypt, not cryptocurrency mining) costs about 20-45 CPU-seconds per sign-in, roughly every 10 minutes while the gateway polls (a few percent of one core) and once per tool session otherwise; the inbox API key is stored in Hermes's .env through hermes_cli.config and read with the profile-scoped secret reader; seen-message ids in plugin-data/atomicmail/state.json; no telemetry.

entries.name: attest
entries.description: Paper trading ledger for agents. Orders, balances and P&L live in a local SQLite ledger the plugin owns, and the agent gets its figures from get_portfolio, get_pnl and get_quote instead of stating them. Orders are priced from live public exchange quotes with slippage and a fee, after a per-order size limit, a daily loss kill switch and duplicate-order checks. No real money, no exchange account, no keys. Disclosure: network use is read-only HTTPS GETs of public ticker data, each sending only the trading pair and the User-Agent attest-paper-trading/0.6.1, with a 3 second deadline: www.okx.com /api/v5/market/ticker?instId=BTC-USDT first, then api.kraken.com /0/public/Ticker?pair=XBTUSDT, then data-api.binance.vision /api/v3/ticker/bookTicker?symbol=BTCUSDT as fallbacks. Requests happen on an order, on get_quote, when marking open positions, and for the claim check. It writes one SQLite ledger in its Hermes plugin data folder: account, trades (with the quote that priced each one, the full tool result and the optional order note), positions, risk state, each day's starting equity, and the ids of sessions that called an attest tool or the guarded tool (removed after 90 days); no other conversation text. pre_tool_call blocks only the one tool named in the intercept_tool setting (empty by default) while paper_mode is on, and simulates that order on the ledger instead; every other tool returns untouched. transform_llm_output appends one line under a reply that states a balance or P&L figure the ledger contradicts, only in sessions that used attest, and never edits the reply. /attest check runs the bundled self test in a separate Python process against a temporary database. The demo_stub_tool setting (off by default) registers a test-only demo_broker_order tool.

entries.name: attune
entries.description: Daily learning that drives evidence-linked, permission-bound project build previews. Disclosure — after you approve a proposal (/attune approve) or grant a standing preview window (/attune project-mode … preview, up to 30 days and 3 builds/day, which also applies to unattended cron runs), it runs your selected project's unit tests together with model-written code changes on this machine inside a Bubblewrap sandbox (Linux only; no network, cleared environment, read-only copy; the original project is never modified).

entries.name: audionotes
entries.description: Search and read your Audionotes voice notes, meeting transcripts and AI summaries through Audionotes' hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.audionotes.app/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration, scope notes:read, paid Audionotes account required). Four read-only tools (search_notes, list_notes, list_folders, get_note) plus the retrieve-notes skill, which tells the agent to cite the notes it used and to keep generated summaries apart from source transcripts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Audionotes' hosted server (api.audionotes.app) and reads the signed-in user's own notes; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Note titles, summaries and transcripts that match a request enter the session context and are sent to the user's model provider. The tools cannot create, edit, delete or share notes. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted; all four tools are annotated read-only.

entries.name: augur
entries.description: Your agent knows your 3 priorities for the week, notices when you drift, parks the detour, and on Friday clears what it can and shows where your attention actually went. Labels each request in the background, asks one short question on the 2nd detour in a row ("Park it" or "Do it now", buttons on Telegram), runs a guarded research-and-draft Friday cron job over the Queue, and sends a weekly report image with planned vs actual per goal and a hidden 4th priority. Disclosure: one short model call per message through its own auxiliary task (augur_classifier), one per weekly report (augur_insight); stores only model-written 60-char summaries, goals and parked items, redacted, in its own data folder; a pre_tool_call guard limits its own cron run to its Queue tools, web_search and file work inside its drafts folder. No network of its own, no shell, no telemetry, no self-update, no binaries.

entries.name: author-feed
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile_get, author_feed and author_watch. It reads public posts and profiles from the Bluesky social media network, which is built on the AT Protocol (atproto), without signing in. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key. Hermes starts the watch Python when the cron job fires. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. hermes author-feed schedule writes a script and creates one cron job that does not call a model. Each run costs 0 tokens and has no daily cap. Empty script output sends nothing. Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run hermes author-feed unschedule before removal. That removes the job and the script. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with hermes cron remove <id>. The scheduled script does not run under plugins.isolation: host, so that setting does not stop the watch. The author_watch tool still refuses a run that is not the saved cron job, including under plugins.isolation: host, and posts that notice on every run of the tool. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall. Seen post URIs advance only on the saved cron job after a successful fetch. The script allows that when cron/executions.db shows that job running under the parent pid and cron/jobs.json names author-feed-watch.py. A direct run and another cron job exit 3 with no GET and no write. The author_watch tool allows that only for the saved job id. Delivery accepts origin, local, all, bot-chat, the Hermes 0.21.6 cron platform names, and public registry names that declare a cron delivery env var. A refused name can be set with hermes cron edit <id> --deliver. bot-chat places the watched account's post text in another model turn that has the profile's tools. hermes cron create cannot set a per-job tool list. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. On Hermes 0.21.4 and 0.21.5 this plugin does not load, and a leftover job keeps its model turn until hermes cron remove <id>. Running schedule again updates the interval and deliver target and switches an existing model job to the script.

The author_watch tool still refuses a run that is not the saved cron job, including under plugins.isolation: host, and posts that notice on every run of the tool. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall. Seen post URIs advance only on the saved cron job after a successful fetch. The script allows that when cron/executions.db shows that job running under the parent pid and cron/jobs.json names author-feed-watch.py. A direct run and another cron job exit 3 with no GET and no write. The author_watch tool allows that only for the saved job id. Delivery accepts origin, local, all, bot-chat, the Hermes 0.21.6 cron platform names, and public registry names that declare a cron delivery env var. A refused name can be set with hermes cron edit <id> --deliver. bot-chat places the watched account's post text in another model turn that has the profile's tools. hermes cron create cannot set a per-job tool list. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. On Hermes 0.21.4 and 0.21.5 this plugin does not load, and a leftover job keeps its model turn until hermes cron remove <id>. Running schedule again updates the interval and deliver target and switches an existing model job to the script. This plugin registers tool(s): profile_get, author_feed, author_watch. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.name: autonoma
entries.description: Earned autonomy: a trust score per kind of action (file edits, deletes, git push, network, messages, spending, system) that rises with clean work and falls on denials, corrections and failures. Below a class's threshold the call goes through Hermes's own approval prompt; at or above, it runs without asking. Catches the agent routing around a block (shell redirects, inline python/node code, `bash -c`), asks again for risky actions after the turn read outside content, revokes "session"/"always" grants after a correction, writes handoff notes from the tool log when a session ends unfinished, and adds a live dashboard tab. Disclosure — stores tool names, action classes, hashed arguments, file paths, command verbs, host names, short error excerpts and short excerpts of your messages and the agent's last reply (up to 500 characters) locally in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/autonoma/data.db (90-day retention, configurable); injects a handoff note into the first turn after an unfinished session and a progress list after compaction; can raise Hermes approval prompts for actions below their trust threshold or after outside content and, when hard_floor_enabled is on, block a class for a number of turns after a correction; the dashboard tab's local routes read the ledger and can reset, set or freeze scores; makes no network calls, no telemetry, reads no credentials; optional corrections_llm (off by default) sends the previous assistant message and current user message to the active model to confirm a correction.
known_issues: trust-ladder also registers /trust; with both installed, use /autonoma trust for Autonoma's scores.

entries.name: autorag
entries.description: Search your own files and configured chat/mail archives from Hermes with AutoRAG Lite. Local hybrid retrieval, file-name search, cited evidence and duplicate detection without editing original documents. Supports PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, Markdown and Korean HWP/HWPX; existing integrations include Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, KakaoTalk, email, Notion and Obsidian. Bundles four skills and a Hermes Desktop Finder pane. Requires Node.js 24+; runs pinned @autorag/librarian@2.13.12 through npx stdio. The Desktop backend installs that same pinned package once in plugin data, with npm lifecycle scripts disabled. First refresh can provision minsync and jikji and download local embedding models (roughly 1.5 GB). Reads only configured folders and archives; writes its own index/report state. User-requested automation also writes rule/scripts and creates Hermes cron jobs. No telemetry, self-update or stored-login discovery. Search snippets read by Hermes reach its selected model provider; configured remote connectors or embedders use their selected services. Disclosure — runs the pinned @autorag/librarian@2.13.12 MCP server through npx (Node.js 24+); the Desktop pane installs the same package once under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/autorag with lifecycle scripts disabled, but its own dependencies are version ranges (plus an xlsx tarball from cdn.sheetjs.com, allowed via npm_config_allow_remote=all) resolved at install time; the first refresh downloads local embedding models (~1.5 GB) and helper tools; it reads only the folders and crawler archives you configure and writes its own index under the workspace's .autorag/ and plugin data; on request the schedule/automate skills write scripts under $HERMES_HOME/scripts/ and create Hermes cron jobs (remove deletes them); search snippets Hermes reads go to your model provider, and configured remote embedders/connectors get your content; no telemetry.

known_issues: The endpoint must be the Foundry *resource root* (for example https://your-resource.services.ai.azure.com); the provider appends /mai/v1 itself and rejects pasted /mai/v1 paths.

entries.name: babelii-diofis
entries.description: Buy Indonesian digital products (pulsa, data vouchers and packages, PLN tokens, bill payments, e-wallet top-ups, game vouchers) plus physical goods, food, hotspot vouchers and services from other vendors, on Babelii, an Indonesian commerce platform, through its hosted commerce MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://babelii.diofis.net/mcp/commerce/, no sign-in, no keys in config) plus two skills (a buying workflow and a signed-in account guide). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to babelii.diofis.net, which receives the destination phone number or account identifier and the buyer name the user gives, to place the order; the plugin itself never contacts a payment provider, it hands the buyer a payment link that opens in the buyer's own browser. execute_purchase places a real order that becomes payable; agent orders are limited by the server (currently Rp25,000 per order and 3 per hour per identity). The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that is not annotated read-only (prepare_purchase, inquire_purchase, execute_purchase, renew_purchase) and refuses them where nobody can answer. No shell commands, no background processes, no files read outside the plugin, no stored credentials, no telemetry. Buyers with a Babelii account can point the same server key at https://babelii.diofis.net/mcp/account/ with OAuth sign-in (Hermes keeps the token, not the package) to pay from their balance by default or by payment link on request, and to read their own account (balance, ledger, top-ups, schedules, notifications; read only), or use a personal agent token from their account on a server without a browser; the package itself starts without sign-in and ships a second skill for that case. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: babysit
entries.description: Watches a long job's log (training run, build, migration) with zero model calls, keeps one chat message updated in place, and wakes the agent only when the job hits a non-finite value, out-of-memory error, traceback, stall, process exit or a line containing your alert text. With `on_failure: pause` it freezes the job on a non-finite value, out-of-memory error, memory pressure or traceback, and a restart linked with `resume_of` gets a recovered or relapsed verdict once it passes the old failure step. Disclosure — Babysit reads the selected log file through one read-only handle, opened without following symlinks and checked again from the handle itself, so replacing the path afterwards changes nothing it reads. It accepts absolute paths only and refuses files inside the active profile's Hermes home, the Hermes root that holds every profile, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.config`, `/etc`, `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev`, files with credential-looking names such as `.env`, `id_*`, `*.pem`, `*.key` and `auth.json`, shell and database history files (`.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`, `.python_history`, `.psql_history` and every other `.*_history`), `~/.pgpass`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, hard-linked files, and anything that is not a regular file. When a PID is given, every 4 seconds it reads that process's resident memory through psutil, plus the cgroup memory limit from `/sys/fs/cgroup` or the system's available memory, and when the process ends it reads its exit status without reaping it. It never writes to the log, makes no network requests of its own, spawns no child processes, and sends no signals unless a watch sets `on_failure: pause`: then it sends `SIGSTOP` to the one PID the watch was given, and `SIGCONT` on `babysit_resume` or `/babysit resume`, each only after re-checking that PID's uid and start time. It never kills a process, never signals a process group or another PID, and refuses Hermes' own process and its parents. `checkpoint_dir` reports the newest checkpoint's name, size and age without reading its contents. For the Desktop pane it writes one JSON file per watch, `<hermes home>/plugin-data/babysit/watches/<watch id>.json`, owner-only and replaced atomically whenever the state changes and at least every 4 seconds. Each file holds the watch's file name, log path, PID, metric series, memory samples, events, counters and the last 12 log lines (200 characters each). With `on_failure: pause` it freezes the job on a non-finite value, out-of-memory error, memory pressure or traceback, and a restart linked with `resume_of` gets a recovered or relapsed verdict once it passes the old failure step. Disclosure — Babysit reads the selected log file through one read-only handle, opened without following symlinks and checked again from the handle itself, so replacing the path afterwards changes nothing it reads. It accepts absolute paths only and refuses files inside the active profile's Hermes home, the Hermes root that holds every profile, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.config`, `/etc`, `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev`, files with credential-looking names such as `.env`, `id_*`, `*.pem`, `*.key` and `auth.json`, shell and database history files (`.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`, `.python_history`, `.psql_history` and every other `.*_history`), `~/.pgpass`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, hard-linked files, and anything that is not a regular file. entries.name: backstop
entries.description: A build or test that fails in your own PowerShell, bash or zsh gets a read-only Hermes diagnosis (cause, quoted evidence, file:line, fix) that opens in Hermes Desktop; Fix it drafts the change into a normal chat you send yourself, and the next passing run closes the incident. Disclosure — each failure automatically starts one diagnosis session on your configured model (output tail redacted, command, cwd, project excerpts); reads project files and their size/mtime, never dot-paths or files on Hermes' read denylist, and never diagnoses a failure run from home, HERMES_HOME or a dot-directory; shell hook functions plus an opt-in profile/rc line; one gateway thread polls its spool every second. No own network calls, credentials or telemetry. One internal import (session-policy guard) is version-coupled; no runtime overrides or self-updater.
known_issues: Needs the Hermes Desktop app open: a failure waits up to 30 minutes for a Desktop window, then expires.
End-to-end tested on Windows (PowerShell); bash and zsh hooks are tested in CI up to the spool record.
Some gateways reject the max_turns request; Backstop then runs the diagnosis without a turn limit and shows a warning.
One private core import (gateway.session_policy.active_policy, the read-only guard) may break on a Hermes release; the tools then refuse to run.
