entries.name: backupdrill
entries.description: Back up a Supabase project to your own S3, R2 or B2 bucket with the open-source backupdrill CLI (the Postgres database, plus Storage files once their S3 keys are set), then restore the snapshot into a throwaway Postgres in Docker to check it comes back. Disclosure — a skill only, with no Python, hooks or server: it has the agent run npx -y backupdrill@2.7.1 in shell commands, which npx downloads from npm on first run. The CLI connects to the user's Supabase project and their own bucket, and a drill pulls a postgres image from Docker Hub. The connection string and bucket keys stay in a .env.backupdrill file the user fills in; each command loads it in a subshell and never prints it. Nothing is sent to BackupDrill.

entries.name: bae
entries.description: Your eBay sidekick for Hermes Agent: drop in item photos and quick notes to draft accurate listings, strip generic AI filler from existing Magical Listings, check active comps alongside your own past sales, and preview real net profit after Final Value Fees, Promoted Listings ad rates, and July 2026 USPS 139 dimensional weight before anything goes live. Includes a 4-station Seller Desk (/bae) and 350px Side Pane in Desktop and Webapp, built-in Casual C2C and Pro Store sample tours, Seller Hub Draft CRLF CSV export, inkFrog and myFitment CSV migration, category playbooks, Best Offer floor triage, bin-sorted packing lists, and zero-token scheduled checks. Every live eBay write waits for your approval: Hermes's own approval prompt when you approve in chat, or an Approve click in the Seller Desk; the agent cannot approve its own staged changes. Starts on sample data; connecting a live eBay account waits on Hermes support for eBay's sign-in (hermes-agent#142687), and Seller Hub Draft CSVs work today. Disclosure — makes zero network calls in sample mode (the default), sample tours or offline CSV mode; in live mode, when connected via hermes auth add hermes-ebay-ops:ebay, calls api.ebay.com, apiz.ebay.com, and apim.ebay.com exclusively through Hermes's OAuth broker; reads local photo paths passed to ebay_stage_listing, after checking each against Hermes's read denylist, and CSV text passed to ebay_import_migration_csv; registers one pre_tool_call hook that sends every agent-issued approval of a staged write to Hermes's approval prompt; writes only inside its own Hermes plugin data folder (SQLite ledgers and exported draft CSVs); runs no shell commands or background daemons; typing in the Seller Desk dock submits your prompt to a visible Hermes conversation."

entries.name: barehand
entries.description: Lets an agent operate a machine with no OS, network or agent on it (firmware menus, boot loaders, installers, rescue shells such as grub>) through the screen and keyboard alone. It provides a computer_use provider for QEMU virtual machines over QMP (or a VNC console), a barehand_machine tool, a hermes barehand CLI, a skill and a flight recorder. In recorded runs a model installed Debian 13 from the network installer (it repaired a grub> prompt on first boot from the installer's rescue mode) and Ubuntu Server 26.04 (it finished the stalled installer by hand) on blank aarch64 machines. `hermes barehand demo` replays a bundled recording. Evidence is in the README and docs/results. Disclosure — `hermes barehand up` starts local qemu-system/qemu-img processes that keep running after Hermes exits until `hermes barehand down`. The guest has QEMU user-mode (NAT) networking and can reach whatever the host can. QMP is unauthenticated on a 0700 unix socket (or a loopback TCP port fallback). The optional VNC transport is unencrypted. The flight recorder is on by default and stores screenshots and key chords (typed text as length only) under the plugin data dir. `barehand_machine` runs status, snapshot_list, snapshot_save under a new name, calibrate_text (types a fixed ASCII test line) and wait_for_text without an approval prompt.
entries.title: Barehand
known_issues: With `plugins.isolation: host`, Hermes skips register_cli_command, so the `hermes barehand ...` commands are unavailable. The default mode (`in_process`) registers them. The plugin was not run in host mode, so whether the barehand_machine tool and the computer_use provider load there is unverified. Use the default.
Only QEMU guests on an Apple Silicon Mac were run. The Linux KVM and Intel Mac paths are covered by unit tests only.

The VNC transport (transport: vnc) was tested only against QEMU's own VNC server. No KVM-over-IP hardware, BMC, PiKVM or other hypervisor was tested. VNC is not encrypted and has no snapshot, reset, eject or power control.
One model per machine, because QEMU serves one QMP client. Typing is US-layout ASCII. Windows hosts are unsupported.
Screen text was measured under QEMU on Alpine 3.24, Debian 13.7 and Ubuntu Server 26.04.1. Their GRUB menus are text consoles and read without calibration. Fedora and other distros are untested.
Calibration is per console font: run calibrate_text at a shell on the same console as the screens to read.

Debian-installer dialogs and graphical installers return no text. Screens dominated by non-ASCII are partly readable, with unreadable cells marked by a replacement character. Box drawing reads as a shade glyph on the Linux console. aarch64 UEFI shell text reading is unverified.
A slowly changing screen (period near 0.8 s) can be reported as a confirmed change.
You supply QEMU, UEFI firmware (edk2/OVMF) and the ISO; Barehand installs and downloads nothing. The model must receive tool-result images.
Every key, type and click is a Hermes approval prompt; grant a session scope for long runs. Unattended (cron or gateway) use needs approvals granted beforehand.

QEMU receives an environment allowlist (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_* and similar), never Hermes' environment. The guest has QEMU user-mode networking. QMP is unauthenticated: a unix socket in a 0700 directory by default, loopback TCP as a fallback, non-loopback only with allow_remote. The optional VNC transport is unencrypted (weak DES password, keystrokes in clear), contacts only the configured host, and needs allow_remote for a non-loopback host.

The flight recorder is on by default: screenshots and key chords under the plugin data dir (mode 0600). Typed text is off by default (length only). `record: false` disables the recorder and `hermes barehand recordings purge --yes` deletes recordings.

One pre_tool_call hook only escalates reset, power_off, eject_media, send_ctrl_alt_del, snapshot_load, snapshot_delete and a snapshot_save that overwrites an existing snapshot to Hermes' approval prompt. status, snapshot_list, snapshot_save under a new name, calibrate_text (types the 94 printable ASCII characters at a Linux prompt) and wait_for_text do not ask.

entries.name: baro
entries.description: Hand a software goal to Baro and watch it run as a live, dependency-aware kanban: baro_plan returns the plan as stories with dependency edges, baro_run starts a run, baro_status shows each story as blocked, ready, running, done or failed with what it waits on and what it blocks, and baro_cancel stops the run and its process tree. Disclosure — every baro_run and baro_plan call is sent to Hermes's human-approval gate by the plugin's pre_tool_call hook, whatever the approval mode, because once approved Baro's coding agents execute shell commands in the target repository without further prompts (each in its own git worktree; on Baro's default Claude backend inside Claude Code's OS sandbox, which allows writes only to that worktree and Baro's package cache, denies reading credential stores and limits network to package registries; with --llm openai only shell writes are OS-confined on macOS and Linux relies on Baro's command guard; no push or pull request; agents run with the user's account); baro_run starts one long-running background process per run (baro-ai@0.132.0 through npx, pinned exactly) via Hermes's terminal tool; Baro's agents make network calls to the model provider the user configured for Baro, or to the Hermes subscription proxy on this machine when the plugin's opt-in setting is on (the plugin first checks that the proxy answers on its local /models route; it calls nothing off the machine); a tool call cannot name a backend, base URL or model, and the approval message says where a run's model calls go; boards, and a tee'd copy of each run's event stream for the live board, are stored only in the plugin's own Hermes plugin data; the plugin reads no credentials and no files outside that state, has no telemetry, and refuses to start or stop runs under cron and the messaging gateway.

entries.name: basekit
entries.description: Read-only live Base (chain 8453) intelligence — gas and real USD cost estimates, wallet portfolios, decoded transaction receipts, token facts with proxy detection, and windowed transfer/approval reads — plus a desktop pane, status-bar chip and a standard-library-only core with no PyPI dependencies. Disclosure — sends the wallet addresses, transaction hashes and token addresses you ask about to public Base RPC endpoints (base-rpc.publicnode.com, mainnet.base.org, base.drpc.org, base.meowrpc.com; a custom rpc_url still fails over to these), prices to coins.llama.fi and api.coinbase.com, and to api.etherscan.io only when a Basescan key is set; a pre_llm_call hook adds one line of live Base state to turns that mention Base or crypto terms (off with inject_chain_context); keeps a local read ledger in its plugin-data folder; no signing, no keys, no telemetry.
known_issues: Public Base RPC endpoints rate-limit under load (HTTP 429) — a tool call then raises and names the endpoint instead of returning empty data, and the hook fails open; set your own rpc_url in settings to avoid it.
base_activity and base_allowances read a bounded block window by design, so they can only ever answer about that window — the reply states the exact from/to block rather than implying all history.

entries.name: baton
entries.description: Hand your session and repository to your remote Hermes agent (Hermes Cloud, a VPS or a Docker container) with /baton "fix the parser, done when pytest passes": the remote works in a throwaway worktree, cannot return verified until the agreed check is green on the exact tree it returns, and `hermes baton land <id>` fetches the tested branch baton/<id> without touching your HEAD, index, working tree or stash. Code travels by git, the order by the Hermes Runs API, state by git refs; every step resumes after a network cut. Disclosure — pushes a snapshot commit of the repository (tracked changes and untracked files not ignored by .gitignore; a blocking secret scan first refuses .env files, keys and tokens, and symlinks that point outside the repository are refused) to the git remote you configure in remote_git and fetches baton refs from it; sends the task and a redacted session transcript (`hermes sessions export --redact` plus an extra redaction pass, capped at 64 KB) to the peer Hermes API server at the URL you register, with the peer key read through Hermes's secret scope; runs `git` (with a minimal environment) and `hermes sessions export` as subprocesses; on a machine set to role remote or both, runs the agreed check without a shell only when its argv matches the remote's allowed_checks plus safe flags, with an empty throwaway HOME, no HERMES_* variables or provider keys, and a timeout. Without a usable bubblewrap (e.g. the official Docker image) or with sandbox: off, the project's code runs with the remote user's rights and can read the Hermes home, so only accept batons from your own machines. Landing creates branch baton/<id> without touching HEAD, the index or the working tree; no telemetry.
entries.title: Baton
known_issues: Tested on Linux; macOS is not tested yet. Windows is not supported.
Both sides need the plugin installed and a git remote they can both push to and fetch from.
Reaching a Hermes Cloud instance depends on that instance exposing the API server (not verified on Hermes Cloud).

Without a usable bubblewrap on the remote (the case inside the official Docker image, tested with demo/run-docker.sh), the check runs unsandboxed and the project's code can read the Hermes home by absolute path.

entries.name: benchforge
entries.description: The flight simulator for AI-written Arduino firmware. Describe what the board should do and approve the checks in plain English; BenchForge compiles the sketch with arduino-cli, runs it instruction by instruction on a simulated ATmega328P with simulated sensors, buttons, relays, servos and buzzers, crash-tests it (noisy sensors, button bounce, millis() rollover, a cut sensor wire) and has Hermes fix it until every check passes, with a reproducible proof receipt, an animated board GIF and a live browser board. A pre_tool_call flash gate stops the agent flashing any firmware without a passing receipt against checks a person approved. Disclosure — hermes bench setup downloads the official arduino-cli 1.4.1 (SHA-256 pinned) from downloads.arduino.cc or GitHub, then the arduino:avr@1.8.6 core and Servo@1.2.2 library through arduino-cli's own package index, and Node.js through Hermes's package manager only if it isn't installed; at run time it compiles the model-written sketch on the host with arduino-cli (compile only, in a sealed temp folder with a fixed environment) and runs the firmware in an emulated chip under node (Node's permission model), and makes no network calls; /bench sends the request, bench, sketch and failure details to the user's own model provider through ctx.llm; the "watch it run" link opens the author's GitHub Pages site (ohjay-official.github.io) with the firmware and checks in the URL fragment; writes only under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/benchforge (receipts, firmware, drafts kept 7 days, approvals stored as platform plus a hashed user id); the flash gate reads the .hex file an upload command names.
entries.title: BenchForge
known_issues: Simulates an Arduino Uno (ATmega328P) with LEDs, relays, buzzers, servos, buttons, potentiometers, LM35 and NTC temperature sensors and HC-SR04 sonar. Parts it can't simulate are listed as not simulated when the checks are written.
Live progress and the approval message use ctx.post_message, so BenchForge runs in-process (plugins.isolation: in_process, the default), not in the plugin host.
Needs Node.js 18 or newer for the simulator; when it is missing, hermes bench setup gets it through Hermes's own package manager.

entries.name: berrys
entries.description: Turn one product photo into on-brand listing images, campaign visuals and short product videos through Berrys AI's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.berrys.io/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). The agent plans the work on Berrys' visual canvas — hero, lifestyle and detail shots for a storefront, coordinated image sets and copy variants for a campaign, or a storyboarded multi-shot clip that keeps the product identical across cuts by seeding each shot from the previous frame — and the results stay on a shared canvas the user can edit, undo or restore. Uses Berrys' curated multi-model image and video stack, so there is no provider key to configure. Bundles the Berrys workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Berrys' hosted server (app.berrys.io) and acts on the user's own Berrys account and credits; the tool set and the playbooks it loads are served by that server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha. Generation spends Berrys credits: the server quotes a price first and every paid generation requires explicit approval in the conversation before it runs. Nothing is published to a marketplace or storefront on the user's behalf — assets are produced on the canvas for the user to download or use. The server signs in with OAuth (Berrys account). The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: better-tg-cli
entries.description: Telegram on your own account (not a bot) through a local MCP server and a skill: read and search chats, threads, comments and forum topics, press bot buttons, and send, edit, react or forward only after you approve each action. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Runs the `better-tg-cli@0.39.6` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+; no runtime dependencies, downloaded from npm on first start), in the plugin's data folder. Network: Telegram's own servers over MTProto; the project's login service (better-tg-cli.com, API at tg-cli-broker.login-c2d.workers.dev) only while you log in with a login key; a once-a-day version check to registry.npmjs.org only when the CLI runs in your own terminal (never under Hermes; off with TG_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1). No telemetry. Login happens once in your own terminal (`npx -y better-tg-cli onboard`), and the skill may install the CLI globally from npm, brew or scoop after asking you; the session and the app's API hash are the CLI's own, stored in its own items in the macOS Keychain, the Linux Secret Service, Windows DPAPI, 1Password (when configured) or a 0600 file in ~/.config/tg, and anyone holding that session controls the Telegram account. It never reads Hermes' secrets or another tool's login. mcp.json forwards only DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and the CLI's own TG_PROFILE, TG_READ_ONLY, TG_LOG_LEVEL, TG_FLOOD_WAIT_MAX, TG_TRANSPORT, TG_NO_UPDATE_CHECK; no credential. Tools that change state (send, edit, delete for everyone, react, forward, pin, leave a chat, and saving media or exports to a folder the agent names) go through MCP elicitation, one Allow Once / Deny per action; unattended runs time out and nothing is sent. Writing without asking can only be switched on in a terminal or OS dialog, never over MCP; on Linux without a secret store that setting is a plain 0600 file the agent's terminal could edit. Login, logout and account transfer are not exposed. Every write is logged locally. The server runs its bundled CLI as a child process per tool call. The tool set comes from the pinned npm version.

entries.name: betterdb
entries.description: BetterDB long-term memory provider — semantic recall on Valkey / valkey-search via the betterdb-agent-memory SDK. Completed turns are embedded and stored in a vector index; the next turn recalls the most relevant memories with a composite similarity/recency/importance score. Explicit betterdb_remember / betterdb_recall / betterdb_forget tools. Disclosure — turn text and tool-stored facts are embedded through an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint you configure (embeddings_base_url, default api.openai.com) and written to the Valkey instance you point it at; plaintext http:// to a remote host is refused. Opt-in, off by default: a discovery marker (set discovery=true to let BetterDB Monitor enumerate the tier) and SDK usage analytics (set telemetry=true).

entries.name: bhived
entries.description: Shared lessons for AI agents over MCP: before a task, the agent can look up fixes, known mistakes and API changes that other agents already verified, and write back what it verifies itself. Lessons rise or sink as other agents corroborate or contradict them. Bundles a skill that tells the agent when to query and when to write. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — Disclosure: the server runs locally as `npx -y bhived-mcp@1.4.2` (Apache-2.0), fetched from npm on first run, so the npm package is not covered by the pinned sha. Queries and written lessons go to the bhived API at mcp.bhived.ai, authenticated with BHIVED_API_KEY or the key `npx bhived setup` saves in ~/.bhived/config.json after a browser sign-in. With a personal key a written lesson is public; with a team key it stays private to that team. The optional `npx bhived setup` also adds the bhived MCP server and a bhived instructions block to other agents' user-global config and instruction files it detects (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Continue and others; never Hermes or the open project), and later bhived commands refresh that block. Activating a skill or MCP server found on the network starts that capability locally (npx or uvx, plus skill scripts, which get only system variables and the variables the skill declares). The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write-capable tool (writes, outcome reports, activation, script runs, proxied tool calls) and refuses them in unattended runs; query, inspect and list tools are read-only.

entries.name: bilinc
entries.description: Hosted memory for Hermes with a full history: see what your agent remembered, when it changed and why. Recalls relevant memories before each turn, adds bilinc_recall, bilinc_remember, bilinc_revise and bilinc_forget tools, and mirrors Hermes built-in memory writes. Maintained by ReARC Labs; free plan available. Disclosure — recall queries (the text of each message, when auto_recall is on), tool arguments, mirrored built-in memory writes, the Hermes session id and, only if memory.bilinc.capture_turns is turned on, each turn's user and assistant text are sent over HTTPS to bilinc.space under your BILINC_API_KEY; requests carry User-Agent bilinc-hermes/<version> and X-Bilinc-Client: hermes-plugin headers. Secret-looking strings are redacted before sending. Recall and writes run on background threads inside Hermes; no separate process, local database or telemetry.

entries.name: biomimetic-brain
entries.description: Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND_AGENT_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.

entries.name: birdie
entries.description: Lets each Hermes conversation message the other AI agents on this machine, such as Claude Code, Codex and Grok, through birdie, a local open-source message bus, and, if you allow it, be woken by their messages. Each conversation gets its own address, so an answer comes back to the conversation that asked. Five tools: list agents, send, check the inbox, wait for a reply, read a thread. Disclosure: talks only to the local birdie service (http://127.0.0.1:7777 by default), with no telemetry or third-party calls of its own, though agents connected to birdie may be online services that receive what is sent to them; a background thread per active conversation reports it to birdie every 30 seconds, including its working folder's name and full path, which agents connected to birdie can see, and with waking on another waits for new messages; waking is off by default and, when turned on with `birdie setup hermes --wake`, lets any agent connected to birdie start a turn, which spends model credits and can use tools under the usual approval rules, and sets allow_gateway_injection for this plugin; Hermes stores this agent's birdie token as the BIRDIE_HERMES_TOKEN secret, which the user gives it; `birdie setup hermes`, run by the user, writes birdie.json in the plugin folder, changes Hermes settings only through Hermes's own commands (enables the plugin, removes any old birdie MCP server, sets the waking permission when asked) and backs up config.yaml first; it never writes Hermes's .env.
entries.title: birdie
known_issues: Needs the birdie service running on the same machine. Install it from https://github.com/koshikraj/birdie, then run `birdie setup hermes` and restart Hermes.

entries.name: birta
entries.description: Artifacts for Hermes. Birta is a shared workspace where people and agents turn drafts into finished work: Hermes publishes a website, HTML page, landing page, portfolio, report, docs or slide deck at a link you can share, and people leave feedback right on the page. With mention events on, @mention Hermes in a comment and it picks the request up on its own: makes the change, replies in the thread and publishes the next version. Disclosure — hosted-only: every tool call goes to birta.dev and acts on your Birta projects; publishing makes a version visible at the project address; optional mention events (off unless you set `events: true` and run the webhook gateway, and approved per subscription) let anyone who @mentions Hermes in your Birta review threads start an unattended agent run.

entries.name: bitquery
entries.description: On-chain data in Hermes: token prices and candles, DEX trades, trader PnL, transfer tracing on 19 chains, address labels and risk reports, Hyperliquid and Polymarket data, through Bitquery's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE), with eight workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Bitquery's MCP server at mcp.bitquery.io, signed in as the user through Bitquery's sign-in, and a first sign-in creates a Bitquery account on a free 7-day trial. The addresses, tokens and questions in a call are sent to Bitquery, each call uses credits from the user's Bitquery plan, and results are pulled into the session context, so they reach the user's model provider. Every tool is read-only (readOnlyHint on all of them): none signs or sends a transaction, places an order or changes the user's account. The tool list comes from Bitquery's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Connect with browser sign-in, `hermes mcp add bitquery --url https://mcp.bitquery.io/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300` (Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens), or, where no browser can open, with a Bitquery access token, `hermes mcp add bitquery --url https://mcp.bitquery.io/mcp --auth header --connect-timeout 300` (Hermes keeps it as MCP_BITQUERY_API_KEY in the profile's .env and sends it as a Bearer header). The bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: blackbox
entries.description: Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; `hermes blackbox setup` (also started by the Set up button on Blackbox's Hermes Desktop page) installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), joins the DKG peer-to-peer network, and asks the threat graph's owner to admit the node (its node address; admission to sync only, not sharing); package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; `blackbox attach` copies the plugin into the Hermes homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set `auto_attach: true`); `hermes blackbox chat` creates an `agent-blackbox` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700, and the Hermes Desktop page reaches it through Blackbox's own Desktop routes, which also hold the audit/block switch; in block mode Blackbox refuses an agent's attempts to change its settings or disable it.

entries.name: blastradius
entries.description: Reads a destructive shell command before it runs and reports what it would actually delete: how many files, how many git can restore, how many it cannot, the total size, and which of them look valuable, then lets policy decide whether to show the report, block the call, or demand a one-shot blast_allow. Covers rm and rm -rf, git clean, git reset --hard, truncate -s 0, `> file` and `: >` truncating redirects, and mv overwrite, including nested bash -c, subshells, and chained commands with cd tracking; anything it cannot resolve is reported as unmeasured instead of guessed. Snapshots and verified restore exist as a separate step (blast_snapshot, blast_restore); restore skips files edited after the snapshot unless overwrite_conflicts is set. Disclosure - no network; reads file metadata, directory listings, and the output of read-only git calls (git ls-files, git check-ignore, git rev-parse); writes snapshot copies under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/; strict policy blocks the tool call while balanced and relaxed report and continue; local terminal backend only; no telemetry. Disclosure — no network and no telemetry; on every terminal call it reads file metadata, directory listings and the output of read-only git calls (git ls-files, git check-ignore, git rev-parse); it writes snapshot copies under the Hermes plugin data dir (or BLASTRADIUS_SNAPSHOT_DIR), and blast_restore with confirm writes snapshotted files back to their original paths, skipping files edited since unless overwrite_conflicts is set; its blocks add to Hermes approval and never replace it, and the agent can relax them through blast_policy or a one-shot blast_allow (BLASTRADIUS_ALLOW=1 turns them off); local terminal backend only.

entries.name: blender
entries.description: Official Blender Lab MCP server over stdio, pinned to upstream v1.0.3, with a Blender workflow skill. Needs Git and uv; Blender 5.1+ is not needed at install. The skill opens Blender itself when a task needs it and, after you agree, installs Blender and Blender Lab's MCP add-on. First startup downloads Python dependencies; prepare the uv environment before connecting. Disclosure — tools execute arbitrary Python in Blender with your privileges; the skill starts Blender with online access for that session only (your saved preference is unchanged), and the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password, so any program on this computer can use it while Blender is open; only after you agree does the skill download Blender from download.blender.org (about 400 MB, about 1.5 GB unpacked), check it against blender.org's sha256 list and install it in your own folder without administrator rights (Linux ~/.local/opt, macOS ~/Applications, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation; never over an existing Blender), and download the v1.0.3 add-on, check its hash and install or enable it; first start downloads the pinned Blender Lab MCP server and its Python dependencies with uv. Server discovery does not prove scene readiness.

entries.name: blind-accessibility-reader
entries.description: Describes the images and videos on any website for blind and low vision people, through their screen reader or an AI voice. A bundled Chrome extension outlines the image or video you're on, and Hermes sends it to a vision model through OpenRouter. Auto mode describes as you scroll and narrates videos as they play; manual mode waits for a shortcut. A daily limit and a per-video limit keep the cost in check. Disclosure — runs a local server on 127.0.0.1:47823 that answers only the bundled extension; the bundled Chrome extension has access to all sites and fetches page images without cookies; sends downscaled images and video frames to the vision model configured for its auxiliary task (OpenRouter by default) using the key held by Hermes; fetches OpenRouter's public price list with no key.

Streaming services protected by DRM return black frames and can't be described.

entries.name: bluff
entries.description: Does your model make things up? Bluff asks about things that sound real but don't exist (Python functions, built-in exceptions, chemical elements), mixed with real ones and phrased as if they all exist, and checks whether the model admits the made-up ones aren't real. The result is a bluff rate, with real items as a control. Every item is checkable by machine, so no model judges another. Runs on your active model through ctx.llm, no setup.

It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Hermes Desktop; the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate_* tools, approval widgets included, and binds sessions, usage and cron widgets to live Hermes data. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/HERMES_NODE_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under HERMES_HOME/boardstate-state/. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

entries.name: bonsai-garden
entries.description: A live isometric bonsai garden for Hermes Desktop: every profile on the roster is one bonsai on a drawn shelf, the focused busy agent's tree steps down onto a stand and returns to its exact shelf slot when it goes idle, and clicking any drawn tree opens that agent's conversation, exactly like its roster row; a monk walks its stretch of garden from elapsed time — drifting slowly at rest, faster while its agent is busy — and a cat spawns at random and can be dragged. Four opaque black plaques carry local time, local date, recurring agent routines and reported session cost, and can be dragged anywhere over the drawing, while each agent row opens that agent's conversation or stops its live session. Season and month come from the local clock in English, with one care line per month shipped inside the artwork, and every pot is signed with the agent's name and shipped avatar; the interface is English throughout. Disclosure — the page talks to the host only through the plugin SDK: it subscribes to the host's focused-session atoms (busy state, profile, session id, reported usage cost and tokens), asks each profile's own gateway cron store for its recurring jobs on demand (cron.manage list, scoped per profile), reads the focused session's own title metadata through session.info, and calls session.interrupt only when the user presses Stop. Reported cost is shown as reported; when only tokens are available a cost line marked with a tilde is estimated at one documented blended rate and the README says so, and unreported cost stays Unavailable rather than a fabricated zero. It reads no message content and no transcript, makes no outbound network requests of its own (every read goes through the host's own SDK socket), needs no credentials and no environment variables, installs nothing and patches no Hermes core file. Derived from office-3d (listed): same isometric-room idea and the same MIT lineage, but a materially different implementation and behaviour — one bonsai per agent on a shelf grid measured on the artwork instead of desks and a cost leaderboard, no Python backend, no agent tool, no CLI-wide monitoring and no login backend.

entries.name: booking-bridge
entries.description: Find free time, then book, list, reschedule and cancel real Google Calendar consults (for example a Strategy consult) from Hermes. Signs in with the user's own Google OAuth client through hermes auth add booking-bridge:google; all calls go through credentialed_provider_request to www.googleapis.com only. Disclosure: network calls to Google Calendar API v3 only (scopes calendar.events and calendar.freebusy); write tools (book, reschedule, cancel) change the user's calendar, can email invitations to listed attendees, and are sent to Hermes' own approval gate by a pre_tool_call hook (action approve), so Hermes asks the user first and by default denies the call in cron, single-query and one-shot runs, webhook-style platforms and CLI sub-agents; they also require confirm=true and refuse, changing nothing, outside an allowlist of platforms and sources (interactive CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP and the chat platforms Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WhatsApp Cloud, Signal, Mattermost, Matrix, BlueBubbles), so cron, single-query, kanban, webhook-style, email, SMS and any unrecognized platform or source are refused; booked events carry a private hash property to prevent duplicates; revoke with hermes auth logout booking-bridge:google; no shell commands, background processes, telemetry or stored credentials.
entries.title: Booking Bridge
known_issues: Needs the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app) with the Calendar API enabled; sign in once with hermes auth add booking-bridge:google.
Google may show an unverified-app warning for a personal OAuth client in testing mode.

Hermes settings the user controls switch the approval gate off: approvals.mode off, YOLO mode, approvals.cron_mode / single_query_mode / unattended_mode set to approve, delegation.subagent_auto_approve true. Then only the plugin's own confirm=true and platform allowlist remain.

The plugin's own allowlist cannot tell a library caller or a delegated sub-agent from an interactive CLI, because the CLI and ACP bind no platform or source and the plugin has no public signal for sub-agents. The approval gate covers them by default.
Not yet exercised against live Google Calendar: no OAuth client sign-in has been run, so the Google request and response shapes are covered by mocked-HTTP tests only.

entries.name: borealwork
entries.description: Give Hermes verified human hands: hire a verified person on boreal.work for a step no agent can do online (confirm a supplier is real, check a shelf price, photograph a site), with the money held until the result passes review against your criteria and a public rulebook. Twelve native tools for the task loop; a spend guard (pre_tool_call) that sends every money-moving call (funding at any amount, accepting a pass, judging a result yourself) to Hermes's approval prompt, enforces per-task and daily caps on funding, and blocks terminal payments that aren't paying a boreal.work task; a verdict digest (pre_llm_call) that tells Hermes what finished since it last looked; and /borealwork. With --yolo or approvals.mode: off Hermes approves these calls without asking, and only the caps apply. Disclosure — HTTPS to the configured boreal.work site only (https://boreal.work by default, live PayPal money; testnet.boreal.work for the sandbox), from tool calls, from the spend guard (a task read before funding, accepting or judging, and the account's last-24-hour spend before funding) and from the digest (one task list on a session's first turn); every funding, acceptance and self-judged verdict asks through Hermes approval, and funding is also capped at max_task_usd (default $10) per task and max_daily_usd (default $50) per day; with --yolo or approvals.mode: off Hermes approves these calls without asking and only the caps apply; the guard also blocks terminal NEAR/USDC transfer commands that do not carry a boreal:<taskId> memo; stores the boreal.work agent key it collects in plaintext in its own plugin state, or reads BOREAL_API_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no self-updates, no compiled code; standard library only.

entries.name: borrowed-hands
entries.description: Lend your Mac's Xcode to a cloud Hermes. Hermes finds your paired Mac, compiles the Xcode project you granted (macOS arm64 or generic iOS Simulator, compile only) at an exact commit on a bh/* branch, and gets structured compiler diagnostics back: ask "Build my demo project on my Mac", or have Hermes edit a repository with its own git tools, build its bh/* branch, fix what the compiler reports and check with `hands_job` `check_pr_ready` before it opens a pull request (the plugin never pushes, opens pull requests or holds GitHub credentials). Needs the separate Borrowed Hands Mac helper (Python source in the same repository) on an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode; the Mac connects out to Hermes and decides what may build. Disclosure — when `listen.enabled` is set (off by default) the plugin runs an HTTP/WebSocket listener inside `hermes gateway run` (default bind `0.0.0.0:8790`, routes `/bh/v1/ws` and an unauthenticated `/bh/v1/healthz`) that paired Macs dial into; connections are authenticated by a single-use pairing code and per-device Ed25519 keys. It keeps a server signing key and a SQLite database (paired device keys, signed job contracts, build diagnostics, audit log) in its plugin data dir; anything the agent can reach on the gateway host can read that key, and a holder of it can sign build requests to paired Macs within their grants. For a build with no commit it makes one anonymous HTTPS read of the granted public repository's branch list (public addresses only, no credentials, no redirects). With `check_pr_ready` it makes one more such read, for that build's repository. It registers one read-only skill, `borrowed-hands:xcode-build-pr` (text only: the order to use the tools in), and its system prompt section tells the agent to run the bundled standard-library script `templates/new_swiftui_app.py` with its own shell tool to write a new Xcode project into its working directory (no process, no network, nothing overwritten). `/hands whoami`, in a DM, tells any sender their own platform:user_id and nothing else. Builds ask for Hermes approval; an "always" answer covers the same Mac, workspace, scheme, configuration and destination but not the commit or branch, so later commits build without a new prompt. The separate Mac helper is installed by the user from the repository, is not covered by this catalog pin, and installs a LaunchAgent, a hidden build user, a root-owned dispatcher and a sudo rule limited to six exact dispatcher commands. No telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Borrowed Hands
known_issues: hands_screen_capture is registered but unavailable: no helper executor in this version.
iOS Simulator support is compile-only: no boot, install, UI or tests.
Public HTTPS repositories and bh/* commits only; private repositories and remote Swift packages are unsupported.
Builds report wipe_ok=false for protected per-user state; complete persistent-state removal is not established.

entries.name: bot-activity
entries.description: Live per-Bot activity timeline for Hermes Desktop: turns, tool calls (arguments, result, duration), approvals and Group Chat streams, grouped by Bot or by Group Chat, with one-click tracking for new Bots. Disclosure — local only, no network or telemetry; records every Bot profile's turns, assistant replies, tool arguments and results, approval commands and Group Chat streams (redacted with agent.redact, capped per field, 3-day / 20k-row retention) into one SQLite file shared by all profiles under plugin-data/bot-activity; reads each Bot profile's state.db, profile.yaml and config.yaml read-only; Track now / Update runs `hermes -p <bot> plugins install <same source> --ref <same sha> --enable --yes-deps` (or copies the plugin and runs `plugins enable`) in the Bot profiles you track, never re-enabling one you disabled.
entries.title: Bot Activity
known_issues: Group Chat attribution relies on Desktop's member-session title and room prompt header, which are not public APIs.
A Bot's first turn in a new Group Chat thread, or a re-titled session, can show its room without a thread label.

entries.name: bot-cabinet-v2
entries.description: Tell Cabinet the job you need done and it answers with the smallest setup that does it (one chat, a skill, a routine, a Bot or a crew), shows which answers led there, then helps you act: add one of botcabinet.com's 20 Bots (each with its test record shown) as a Hermes profile, plan a new Bot line by line, or set up a crew of Bots in a handoff order with blocked Kanban cards. Everything Cabinet makes can be removed again from My Bots, and a Bot that Hermes's own Bots catalog carries is handed over to it, never duplicated. Disclosure — fetches its Bot catalog from https://botcabinet.com/catalog.json on open and Refresh (data only, 2 MB cap) and, after you confirm, creates Hermes profiles whose instructions (SOUL.md) come from that catalog; can create and archive Kanban cards for a crew; deletes only profiles it created that you have not changed; reads ~/.hermes/profiles and hashes profile files to track what it made; calls private Hermes modules (hermes_cli.profiles, kanban_db), so a Hermes update can break it; no shell, credentials, telemetry or self-updates.

entries.name: bot-chat-agent
entries.description: Hermes Bots: a calmer Hermes Bot Chat that still does the work: short agentic replies, a block-only safety guard, a Desktop status card, mid-turn asks that are no longer dropped, background results delivered back to the same chat, a local short-term / long-term memory (decisions, project state, lessons; /memoria) with no API keys, and an opt-in panteón: Hermes may offer in one line to create a specialist bot and creates it only after your yes. Other sessions untouched. Disclosure — in sessions titled "Bot Chat" (and their subagent children) it injects a reply-style instruction, a bounded context / memory block, pending-ask reminders and (Desktop half enabled) a one-line specialist offer; blocks tool calls matching its rules (secrets, deletes, destructive git, protected-branch pushes, outbound messages, expensive models, kanban-lock bypasses, obfuscated exec, memory-injection) and, when team.assignees is configured, rewrites kanban_create arguments to add serialization parents and the teammate assignment; wraps tool output that looks like a prompt injection in an "untrusted data" label; it never approves anything. It opens <HERMES_HOME>/state.db, <HERMES_HOME>/kanban.db and <HERMES_HOME>/cron/executions.db (plus cron output files) read-only; writes plugin-local files under <HERMES_HOME>/bot-chat-agent/ (memory.db, deliveries.db, status.json, panteon-auto.json, dm-delegations.json, optional project-card.md) and its own team.assignees plugin setting; registers /memoria, /botmemory, /panteon and /pantheon; serves a small dashboard API at /api/plugins/bot-chat-agent; the Desktop half (opt-in in Capabilities → Plugins) calls the app's own profiles.create / profiles.configure for ONE preset profile, only after the user's explicit yes; changes the Desktop reasoning.collapsedByDefault setting while a Bot Chat is focused and restores it on leave/disable; makes no third-party network calls, no telemetry and no credential reads. Background work uses Hermes kanban / the gateway dispatcher when team.assignees is configured; on Hermes 0.23, results are offered into the next turn. A ContextEngine named bot-chat is registered but off until context.engine: bot-chat is set.
entries.title: Hermes Bots
known_issues: Per-turn cost: the plugin's own pre_llm_call hook takes about 15 ms p50 / 20 ms p95 on a Windows 11 PC and about 5 ms p50 on Linux (SQLite connections are shared per turn). Measured only with a mock model, so real-model time-to-first-token and the quality of the deterministic compactor are not measured; with context.engine: bot-chat requests were ~30% smaller than without the plugin in a mock 300-turn run. The engine is off by default.

The panteón offer is an instruction injected into Bot Chat turns; a real model follows it most of the time, not guaranteed. The Desktop half must be switched on in Capabilities → Plugins for offers and profile creation.

Background-result delivery on Hermes 0.23 uses the next-turn offer path; durable in-transcript writes need the core B1 API, which 0.23 does not expose. The core bot-loop guard (gateway.bot_loop_guard.max_hops, default 4) can refuse later delegations to the same teammate in one chat; the card then shows an error.

Long-term memory is written only when the turn text contains clear cues (Decision:, Decisión:, We decided, Decidimos, Lesson:, Remember that, Recuerda que, From now on, …). There is no model and no network.

Language follows the user (es/en/fr/pt/de, detected offline from the latest message; language: es|en|fr|pt|de forces one). Plugin-written text (status card, /memoria, /botmemory, /pantheon) is translated; lines the model writes (panteón offer, ready notice, stop explanation) get an instruction to answer in that language, which a real model usually but not always follows. Specialist role prompts and guard block messages stay en/es.
hermes plugins remove takes out the Python half only; your data folder and the Desktop half (installed by the core) stay until you delete them.

Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5. Known issues: Per-turn cost: the plugin's own pre_llm_call hook takes about 15 ms p50 / 20 ms p95 on a Windows 11 PC and about 5 ms p50 on Linux (SQLite connections are shared per turn). Measured only with a mock model, so real-model time-to-first-token and the quality of the deterministic compactor are not measured; with context.engine: bot-chat requests were ~30% smaller than without the plugin in a mock 300-turn run. The engine is off by default.; The panteón offer is an instruction injected into Bot Chat turns; a real model follows it most of the time, not guaranteed. The Desktop half must be switched on in Capabilities → Plugins for offers and profile creation.; Background-result delivery on Hermes 0.23 uses the next-turn offer path; durable in-transcript writes need the core B1 API, which 0.23 does not expose. The core bot-loop guard (gateway.bot_loop_guard.max_hops, default 4) can refuse later delegations to the same teammate in one chat; the card then shows an error.; Long-term memory is written only when the turn text contains clear cues (Decision:, Decisión:, We decided, Decidimos, Lesson:, Remember that, Recuerda que, From now on, …). There is no model and no network.; Language follows the user (es/en/fr/pt/de, detected offline from the latest message; language: es|en|fr|pt|de forces one). Plugin-written text (status card, /memoria, /botmemory, /pantheon) is translated; lines the model writes (panteón offer, ready notice, stop explanation) get an instruction to answer in that language, which a real model usually but not always follows. Specialist role prompts and guard block messages stay en/es.; hermes plugins remove takes out the Python half only; your data folder and the Desktop half (installed by the core) stay until you delete them..

entries.name: bot-dashboard
entries.description: Two desktop panes in one plugin. Bot shows the focused bot's dashboard - profile and model, scheduled jobs, notes, the custom widgets that bot pinned for you, and optional tasks and projects from a markdown notes vault you point it at in the plugin settings; Group shows a group chat's members, activity, shared tasks and projects, and follows a group chat you open. Ships two agent tools in its own bot_dashboard toolset - bot_panel edits the bot's own panel, group_dashboard lets any member bot read or shape a group's dashboard - plus a pre_llm_call hook that adds a short panel snapshot on the first turn only (and an optional per-turn instruction, empty unless the user writes one). Disclosure - reads the local Hermes home (bot profiles, config.yaml, group room records) and, only if the user sets vault_path, markdown notes in that folder; writes only each bot's own panel files (widgets, notes, layout) under its profile and, when the user creates or ticks a task, that task's note in the configured vault folder. Widgets render in a sandboxed opaque-origin frame with a no-network Content-Security-Policy. The panes talk to the Hermes API on 127.0.0.1, with no third-party network calls, no shell commands and no stored credentials. Disclosure — reads the local Hermes home (every bot profile's profile.yaml, config.yaml, SOUL.md, skills list and avatar, plus the gateway's group-room tables in state.db/shared-state.db, read-only) and, only if the user sets vault_path, markdown notes in that folder; the bot_panel/group_dashboard tools can copy any .html file the model names into a widget, and any bot can edit any local group's dashboard; writes only panel files (widgets, notes, layout) under each bot's profile and under plugin-data/bot-dashboard/groups, plus, when the user creates or ticks a task, that task's note in the configured vault folder; widgets render in a sandboxed opaque-origin frame with a no-network Content-Security-Policy; an optional panel_rule setting (empty by default) adds the user's own instruction to every turn; no third-party network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials.

entries.name: bot-drops
entries.description: Share a Hermes bot as a link and a card, and adopt bots other people share as new profiles. A preview shows the bot's card, what it needs, the full text of each scheduled task and what was left out before anything is installed; adopting runs Hermes' own profile install on the exact reviewed commit and never changes existing profiles. Sharing packages the personality, the author's own text skills and any scheduled tasks (name, task text, schedule and skills only, arriving paused), renders a link card and a story image locally, and publishes them as a new public GitHub repository with a GitHub Pages bot page. Disclosure — a preview clones a public GitHub or GitLab repository over HTTPS with size, time and file limits and never installs anything; adopting creates a new profile through Hermes' own profile install with the shared bot's scheduled tasks paused. Publishing runs git and the user's own gh login to create a new PUBLIC GitHub repository and GitHub Pages page, only after an explicit confirmation in the plugin screen; the shared package holds the personality, the author's own text skills, the model provider/name and scheduled tasks (name, task text, schedule and skill names only). Keys, settings, memory, chats, plugins, MCP servers, Skills Hub skills and the delivery targets, scripts, folders and endpoints of scheduled tasks are never shared. Shared pages and cards carry a "by BrainArts" credit link to the author's X profile that the sharer can turn off. No telemetry, self-updater or background process.
entries.title: Bot Drops
known_issues: Publishing needs the GitHub CLI signed in (gh auth login). Without it Bot Drops prepares the files for a manual upload.
Shared bots are public repositories; private sharing is not supported.
Built and tested on macOS. Windows support is new in 0.5.0 and not yet confirmed on a Windows machine, so this entry lists Linux and macOS.
On Hermes 0.23.0 a bot name that was removed earlier cannot be reused for a new bot; fixed in Hermes 0.23.1.
Profiles are not a security sandbox. Only adopt bots from people you trust.

entries.name: bot-forge

Then hire a whole crew in one call, ask what is waiting on you, and edit, teach, share and health-check Bots by chatting. entries.name: boxcompute
entries.description: Give Hermes its own cloud Linux VMs through the hosted BoxCompute MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR): create and start VMs, run commands and background processes, read and edit files under /workspace, and open one-hour public preview links, with the sandboxes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.boxcompute.ai, and commands and files run in the user's BoxCompute VMs, not on their machine. A running VM spends the user's BoxCompute credit per minute until it stops (it stops itself 30 minutes after its last command, file or preview call); preview_create makes a URL anyone can open for one hour; sandbox_delete permanently removes a VM and its files; email_send emails only the account owner's own address. Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the boxcompute MCP server. No telemetry. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `hermes mcp add boxcompute --url https://mcp.boxcompute.ai/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

entries.name: brainvault
entries.description: Memory you own for Hermes, by Wave OS. Hermes remembers on this computer right away, and a pasted page becomes memory cards. You mint the ones worth keeping to your own wallet's vault on the Theta blockchain with one approval in Wave Web (private by default, encrypted to you and this Hermes), and any Hermes you pair reads them back, fingerprint-checked. Ask Wavey answers Wave questions from chain-verified public cards. Disclosure — never signs, mints or holds wallet keys: minting happens on web.oswave.io, approved in the Wave Wallet Mint browser extension, and costs a one-time TFUEL network fee. Network calls go only to web.oswave.io (your vault's card index, sending your public wallet address; one-time end-to-end encrypted drops for pairing and Send to Wave, with the key kept in the link fragment; Wavey's public cards) and Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only card reads and gas price). Stores a decrypt-only, wallet-revocable agent key in the OS keyring if installed, else a 0600 file in $HERMES_HOME/brainvault; reads Hermes's config.yaml only for its setup check, and Hermes's plugin list (names and versions, never sent anywhere) to show which Wave plugins you have. A background thread syncs every 10 minutes. Opens Wave Web in the browser for pairing and minting. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating. Recall runs locally; recalled memories reach the user's model provider like any context.

entries.name: branchpoint
entries.description: Explore the same task with 2-8 independent agent plans (default 4), optionally on different models. Build selected routes in isolated Git worktrees (default top 2), compare them with three blind reviewers and an evidence-linked decision record, then adopt or converge their ideas into another candidate. Includes a loopback live view, decision log, rewind anchors and reversible adoption. Disclosure — Branchpoint spawns git and up to 8 headless Hermes agents (file tools only, your configured model and credentials) in git worktrees it creates in your repository, writes branches, snapshots and refs/branchpoint/ there (a snapshot on every prompt unless anchor_on_turn is off), and changes your working tree only when you run /branchpoint adopt. It runs your project's test, lint and type commands, including code the agents wrote, inside a bubblewrap or sandbox-exec sandbox (no network, home masked, allowlisted env), and refuses real builds without a sandbox unless you pass --unsafe-checks. Goal, source excerpts and route ledgers go to your configured model with best-effort secret scrubbing. A live view is served on 127.0.0.1 behind a token.
entries.title: Branchpoint
known_issues: Screenshots are pinned to the 0.2.1 release commit: the docs images are unchanged, and that is the revision whose immutable raw URLs are on the review-approved list.
Real builds require matching Branchpoint hooks installed and enabled in the child's Hermes home; absent, disabled or stale hooks stop the build.
Child token caps are not a live cross-process budget. Missing usage is explicitly estimated; inherited failing checks and skipped evidence remain visible.
Replay produces a paste-ready prompt, not a programmatically forked Hermes session. Undo restores the entire pre-adopt tree, replacing later edits.
POSIX file locking is required: Linux/macOS; use WSL on Windows. Native Hermes integration is tested on Linux, with offline CI on Linux and macOS.

entries.name: breadcrumbs
entries.description: Memory and a context engine in which every line has an address. Each turn, tool step and tool result is a crumb in a content-addressed, append-only store (CRC32C ids, Merkle commits). One tool, crumb(id, level), shows any memory from a one-line handle (0) to its exact bytes (1). crumb_find searches with BM25: no vectors, no model. Each recall, find, open and fold writes a record of what the model saw. With context.engine breadcrumbs, a long chat folds into a layer of crumbs with no model call, and the model opens any folded turn by its id. /island gives each codebase its own profile. A read-only explorer shows the sessions, the zoom and the context of each turn. Disclosure — Every turn, tool step and tool result is stored word for word, append-only, in $HERMES_HOME/breadcrumbs/, with a usage.log of ids, model names and token counts for every model request (BREADCRUMBS_USAGE_LOG=0 turns it off). When config.json lists hive peers, crumb_find queries go to those peers and crumb fetches blobs from them. An optional background thread runs your local llama-completion binary on a local GGUF model after a span or session closes, with a minimal environment (BREADCRUMBS_SUMMARIZE=0 turns it off). Per-model request options you set in config.json are merged into chat-completions requests. The dashboard and log views read config.yaml and state.db of your profiles read-only, the memory slot setup writes non-secret values to config.yaml, and the `slot` command sets memory.provider through `hermes config set`. The explorer's settings panel lists every profile on this Hermes install and, when you click a switch, sets memory.provider and context.engine of the profile you choose through `hermes config set` (keeping the earlier value so that it can revert) and edits breadcrumbs' own config.json dials for that profile or a scope. When a chat starts in a terminal, the plugin opens its token-protected explorer once per process (a split in cmux, tmux, WezTerm or Kitty, else your default browser, on 127.0.0.1; BREADCRUMBS_VIZ=0 turns it off), and /viz opens it on demand.
entries.title: breadcrumbs
known_issues: Select it: `hermes config set memory.provider breadcrumbs`, and `hermes config set context.engine breadcrumbs` for the context engine. An install alone turns nothing on.

The tools crumb and crumb_find come through the memory provider, not ctx.register_tool, so the plugin's tool list is empty. Their names carry the prefix mcp__ (mcp__crumb, mcp__crumb_find): Anthropic OAuth maps only registry tools back to their names. BREADCRUMBS_TOOL_PREFIX changes the prefix.
Windows has no flock: use one writer per store there.

Each turn, tool step and tool result is a crumb in a content-addressed, append-only store (CRC32C ids, Merkle commits). A read-only explorer shows the sessions, the zoom and the context of each turn. entries.name: breeze-tts
entries.description: Breeze Blue text-to-speech as a Hermes voice provider (tts.provider: breeze-blue), driven by the Breeze Blue Developer API. Voices come from the Breeze console — stock, cloned or designed — and the provider speaks whole replies through text_to_speech and read-aloud, with mp3 (default), wav, flac, opus, aac or pcm output, so Opus voice notes work on messaging platforms. No new Python dependencies: the plugin posts directly to the ElevenLabs-shaped endpoint. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice id and model, and your BREEZE_API_KEY (header xi-api-key) to api.breeze.blue, or to BREEZE_BASE_URL when you set it; synthesis is billed to your Breeze Blue account; generated audio is written to Hermes's audio cache; the text is not logged; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry. Not implemented: realtime/WebSocket streaming (voice-mode replies are spoken sentence by sentence instead) and voice listing.
entries.title: Breeze Blue TTS
known_issues: The provider is named breeze-blue, not breeze: 'breeze' is the self-hosted local streaming server keyed under tts.streaming.provider (PR #105299), so the hosted API provider takes its vendor name.
tts.voice is mandatory: Breeze Blue has no built-in voice and every voice id is account-scoped, so the provider raises instead of guessing one.
No voice listing or realtime streaming; per-sentence synthesis covers voice mode at higher latency.

entries.name: briq
entries.description: Run Hermes' terminal, file and execute_code tools in a briq sandbox, a microVM with its own disk, instead of on this machine. Select it with terminal.backend: briq. Disclosure — every command and file operation is sent over HTTPS to the briq API (https://api.briq.cloud, or the URL in BRIQ_API_URL) and runs inside the sandbox; Hermes' file sync uploads the credential, skill and cache files it syncs for every remote backend to that sandbox; the sandbox has outbound network access; a sandbox the plugin creates is billed to the briq account of the key and sleeps when idle (terminal.briq_sleep); at cleanup it is stopped and kept with its disk when container_persistent is true (the default), its id recorded in a small JSON file under the Hermes sandbox directory so the next session reuses it, or destroyed when it is false. The API key is read only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret (BRIQ_API_KEY), is stripped from the environment of every command, and is never written to disk or logged. The plugin sends no environment variables into the sandbox and makes no network calls other than to the briq API. It imports private Hermes modules for its environment base classes (tools.environments.base, base_output and file_sync), as the built-in remote backends do.
known_issues: A running command cannot be interrupted: cancelling a command stops the sandbox, and the next command wakes it.
A command longer than about 6 KB, or one that reads stdin, is staged as a file in the sandbox first.
Imports private Hermes modules (tools.environments.*); a Hermes release can change them.

entries.name: brownout
entries.description: Power-cut guard for the machine Hermes runs on. When mains power drops it messages you (Telegram or any hermes send target) with the battery level, measures the real drain and sends a runway, and on /brownout park (or by itself at critical battery if you don't answer) pauses active cron jobs and blocks new tool calls with a pre_tool_call hook. When power is back it resumes only the jobs it paused and tells you. Nothing is killed or deleted; it stops the next tool call, not one already running. Undelivered alerts are retried in order. Disclosure — one daemon thread per Hermes home polls power every poll_seconds (default 15) by running `pmset -g batt` (macOS), reading /sys/class/power_supply (Linux) or running `upsc` (NUT UPS, opt-in); alerts go out by running the documented `hermes send --to <notify_target> --file -` CLI with a 30 s timeout, using the gateway's own credentials. No network calls of its own, no credentials read, no telemetry. Writes only to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/brownout/ (events log, state, command queue, watcher lock).
entries.title: Brownout
known_issues: Proven on real hardware on macOS (pmset). Linux sysfs and NUT UPS readers are covered by parser tests on recorded formats only.

entries.name: browser-viewer
entries.description: Live view and human takeover of the browser Hermes drives: stream its tabs to a web page on another device and click, type and scroll yourself to log in, pass 2FA or a CAPTCHA. Disclosure — starts a detached aiohttp server that listens on explicit IPv4 addresses (loopback plus the Tailscale address if tailscale is installed; never 0.0.0.0), over plain HTTP by default or HTTPS when the user opts in with hermes browser-viewer tls (tailscale cert contacts the Tailscale control plane and Let's Encrypt, and the machine name appears in public Certificate Transparency logs); login links are single-use (10 minutes) and are exchanged for an HttpOnly session cookie (7 days by default, Secure over HTTPS), and the start and link actions return such links to the session transcript; launches Chromium, or chrome-headless-shell when one is installed under the Hermes tools directory or on PATH (per-browser engine choice: auto, shell or chromium), with a persistent profile (cookies and logins) and CDP on 127.0.0.1, which makes its usual background connections; headless browsers send the user agent of a windowed Chrome, hide navigator.webdriver and send Accept-Language from the system locale; each managed headless browser also gets a detached Python process (standard library only, the same minimal environment) that holds one CDP connection for the life of that browser and rewrites client-hint headers on requests that still carry the browser's own values (BV_UA_OVERRIDE=0 turns it off); the link action starts the viewer server if it has stopped; stop closes the browser over CDP (Browser.close) before any signal so recent cookies reach disk; the server is started with the Python of the virtualenv that holds aiohttp; the server and Chromium get a minimal environment, not the Hermes one (proxy settings and desktop-session variables are passed on); runs chromium --version and chrome-headless-shell --version (answers cached in the plugin data dir), tailscale ip -4, tailscale status and tailscale cert (HTTPS mode only) and hermes config set|unset browser.cdp_url (the use action changes browser.cdp_url for every session of the profile, and browser_exec then acts with that browser's logins); status and list return each tab's origin and a truncated title to the session transcript; reads /proc and /proc/net/tcp on Linux (the same process facts through psutil on macOS) and Chromium builds under the Hermes tools directory; no telemetry from the plugin. Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon).
known_issues: Plain HTTP unless HTTPS is enabled with hermes browser-viewer tls: without it the session cookie and the stream are not encrypted on the wire, so use a private network such as Tailscale.
A cold start can block the tool call for about 75 seconds, longer if tls tailscale has to fetch a certificate.

entries.name: browserless
entries.description: Run Hermes' built-in browser tools on Browserless cloud browsers: stealth mode, residential proxies, captcha solving and ad blocking, with no local Chrome. One Browserless browser per task; Hermes' agent-browser daemon and CDP supervisor share it through a local CDP multiplexer, and the browser is reconnected after network drops and closed when the task ends. Disclosure — while a browser task runs, starts a background thread with a WebSocket listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, secret path, local Host header only); connects to Browserless (production-*.browserless.io) with BROWSERLESS_TOKEN, read via get_secret; Browserless usage is metered on your plan, and residential proxy traffic costs more; connections to Browserless carry a browserless-hermes-plugin/<version> User-Agent so Browserless can count plugin usage (opt-out: BROWSERLESS_SOURCE_TAG=false; the browser's own user agent is unchanged); no files written unless BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG is set; no other telemetry.
entries.title: Browserless
known_issues: If the Browserless session can't start (e.g. wrong token or plan concurrency limit), Hermes falls back to a local browser; set BROWSERLESS_MUX_LOG to see the reason.

entries.name: browsersolver
entries.description: Fetch web pages behind Cloudflare, DataDome and similar protections for the built-in web_extract tool, through the BrowserSolver web unlocker API. Extract only; pair it with a search backend for web_search. Disclosure — sends each URL to api.browsersolver.com with your BROWSERSOLVER_API_KEY so BrowserSolver fetches the page past Cloudflare, DataDome and similar bot protection; the default engine is webunlocker, the most expensive tier, and calls use BrowserSolver credits (set engine to crawler or rendering for cheaper fetches). Reads the key only through Hermes's secret scope. Registers no tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

entries.name: bsc-mint-guard

entries.name: btw-studio
entries.description: Side-channel /btw workspace, $0 read-only SQLite session radar, and Δτ steer playbook for Hermes Desktop, CLI, Gateway, and Dashboard. Intercepts /btw mid-turn in the composer (with attachments, opt-in voice STT/TTS, and @session context) to render Markdown answers in a strip, popover, floating pane, or dialog without mutating the transcript or L0 prompt cache. Reads state.db?mode=ro at $0 for token/cache metrics, AST syntax checks, 10 loop-guard detectors, and cross-session file write conflicts, steers conversation_id-stable turns or child subagents mid-flight, formats output via a 6-axis reading lens ([0,1]^6), and retains only rules verified by 3-call Δτ behavioral contrast in BTW.md. Disclosure — registers 12 observer-only hooks returning None, a btw-studio.verified-playbook system-prompt section (lite/full modes), the BTW_CONVERSATION_ID session env, auxiliary tasks btw_studio_fast and btw_studio_title calling the user's own model via ctx.llm (redacted <=32 KB session digest; optional fast_base_url restricted to https:// or loopback, no redirects), 57 dashboard routes under /api/plugins/btw-studio/, 14 CLI subcommands, 12 gateway RPCs and 8 Desktop host RPCs. Reads $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only (sibling profiles' state.db only when scan_sibling_profiles is on), curator logs, .git/HEAD, config.yaml, MEMORY.md, up to 8 cwd-confined edited .py/.json files (parsed, never run) and denylisted workspace attachments. Off by default: allow_web_search (web_search/web_extract/browser_exec), allow_media_tools, wake_word_enabled, live_voice_enabled, tts_auto_speak, memory_md_sync_mode, scan_sibling_profiles, gamify_enabled. Opt-in voice sends audio/text to the host's STT/TTS providers, the Nous audio gateway, Groq or OpenAI (keys via agent.secret_scope: TOOL_GATEWAY_USER_TOKEN, TOOL_GATEWAY_DOMAIN, GROQ_API_KEY, VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY), or Microsoft Edge TTS when the edge provider is chosen. Writes stay in the plugin data dir unless memory_md_sync_mode is on (rewrites a marked block in $HERMES_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md) or companion pet adoption installs a pet into $HERMES_HOME/pets; no shell commands, subprocesses, servers or self-updater.

entries.name: bubblewrap
entries.description: Bubblewrap terminal backend for Linux: every terminal and execute_code command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's own paths, with a read-only root, a writable working directory (per profile: restricted, workspace or network), the dot entries of the home directory (credential stores always) and the Hermes home hidden, private temp and process directories, agent and docker sockets masked, and per-command memory, CPU and process limits (`hermes config set terminal.backend bubblewrap`). Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own: it runs your commands through the `bwrap` and `prlimit` binaries you install (bubblewrap, util-linux), and under the default `network` profile those commands share the host network. It reads no credentials. File tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) run inside the sandbox too, and because the working directory is a real host directory Hermes keeps its dangerous-command prompts, as for the local backend.

entries.name: budget-leash
entries.description: Hard budget enforcement for Hermes sessions. Tracks estimated model spend (token usage x per-model prices, cache read/write tokens included) and tool-call counts against a per-session cap and a persistent per-day cap; blocks tool calls via pre_tool_call once a cap is exhausted and cuts off the model calls themselves via the llm_execution middleware, answering with a synthetic budget-exhausted reply so the provider is never invoked (fail-closed), so unattended agents cannot run up unbounded cost; warns at 80% of a cap via context injection, keeps a flock-guarded day-ledger on disk that survives restarts and is shared safely across processes, and writes a per-session JSONL spend report. Disclosure — local code only; meters estimated model spend from token-usage metadata and tool-call counts, and with the defaults ($2 per session, $10 per day, 200 tool calls per session, 1000 per day) refuses tool calls and answers model calls with a synthetic budget-exhausted reply once a cap is reached; spend figures are estimates from a user-editable price table (default $1/$3 per million input/output tokens), not provider bills; reads its settings from budget-leash.json in the Hermes home and writes ledger.json, its lock file and reports.jsonl under plugin-data/budget-leash/ there; no network calls, no subprocesses.

entries.name: bulk
entries.description: Apply one instruction to hundreds of independent files, CSV rows or JSON records from a /bulk slash command, with job state in SQLite, background processing, bounded concurrency, automatic retries, shared rate-limit waits, pause and resume, Bulk-enforced token limits, restart recovery and a combined Markdown or CSV export. Disclosure — sends each item to the configured model provider through ctx.llm, billed to the user; reads the paths given to --over, including outside the plugin data directory; runs background threads inside the Hermes process while a job is active; token limits are approximate and are not a billing limit; interrupted items can be sent to the model again.
