entries.name: bulkpublish
entries.description: BulkPublish (https://www.bulkpublish.com) social media scheduling through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.bulkpublish.com/mcp/full, 80 tools): draft, schedule, publish and retry posts on Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Pinterest, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Discord, Telegram, Tumblr and Snapchat, with media uploads, bulk actions, team approvals, labels, templates, recurring schedules, RSS autopost, Inbox replies and analytics. Bundles 33 BulkPublish skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, with its arguments, goes to mcp.bulkpublish.com and needs a BulkPublish account with its API key in BULKPUBLISH_API_KEY, sent as a Bearer header. Publishing tools post to the user's connected social accounts and Inbox tools reply to real people; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Recurring schedules and RSS autopost, once approved, keep publishing from BulkPublish's servers without further prompts, and the media skill has the agent upload local files to a BulkPublish-issued URL with curl. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: bumblebee-guard
entries.description: Supply-chain guard: runs the local Bumblebee scanner bridge (read-only, no sudo), exact-matches every installed package, MCP server and editor/browser extension against curated catalogs of known-compromised packages, and adds OSV.dev advisory counts via the bridge's OSV layer. Tools: bumblebee_guard_scan / _status / _diff (baseline diff of findings). A rate-limited pre_llm_call hook injects a one-line supply-chain alert only when curated findings exist (never when clean, at most once per hour). /bumblebee slash command plus a bundled triage skill covering confidence classes, OSV alias deduplication and a documented false-positive pattern (scanner fixtures containing threat-intel strings). Disclosure — the plugin itself makes no network calls and holds no credentials; the wrapped bridge's scan queries OSV.dev and an opt-in, off-by-default catalog refresh fetches threat-intel JSON from the upstream perplexityai/bumblebee repository; scans run daily_scan.sh as the current user and read package metadata in $HOME (never .env or token files, never executes package managers); a full scan takes up to ~3 minutes and honors a configurable timeout; the hook fails open and never blocks turns, so cron and unattended runs are unaffected.

entries.name: bundlebees
entries.description: bundlebees: dispatch sandboxed coding workers (bees) from Hermes, watch their attempts, and keep the apply, test and push step in your own hands. Four tools with 571 o200k tokens of schema between them. bundlebees_status reports launcher health, capacity, live attempts, events, containers and authorized projects. bundlebees_dispatch validates a file-leased brief and starts a worker in a disposable Cua sandbox (default model deepseek-v4.1-flash), optionally linked to a Hermes kanban card. bundlebees_attempt gets, follows, cancels or reviews one attempt (cancel and review need confirm=true and a Hermes approval). bundlebees_host_prompt writes a paste-ready setup prompt for a worker host and never takes a host, token or URL. When an attempt finishes, you run hermes bundlebees verify <attempt_id>: it applies the patch on a clean feature-branch worktree, enforces the file lease, runs the named tests and a secret scan, and on green commits and pushes that feature branch (main and master are refused; --dry-run applies and tests without pushing). The plugin never merges, tags or force-pushes. Hermes Desktop 0.23 or newer shows a dark pane with Health, Containers, Models, Concurrency, Projects, Live attempts, Verify results and Remote host tabs; the four tools still run without it. Skill id bundlebees:bundlebees-operator. It is for developers who split repo work into small parallel briefs and want cheap workers on a machine they control, with a human gate before anything lands. To start, you need Hermes 0.23.0 or newer and a worker launcher (by default the Orbit local-workers adapter on the same machine). Run hermes plugins install bundlebees and hermes plugins enable bundlebees, store the launcher token as the Hermes secret BUNDLEBEES_LAUNCHER_TOKEN (never in chat), load bundlebees:bundlebees-operator, and begin with bundlebees_status op=health. hermes bundlebees doctor checks the token, the adapter and the schema size without printing values. Disclosure — network and cost: talks to a local or user-configured worker launcher (loopback by default; a private or LAN launcher URL requires allow_private=true in plugin settings and is never a tool argument); dispatching a bee can spend model budget on that worker machine. Worker events and logs are treated as untrusted text. Cancelling or reviewing an attempt asks for Hermes approval first. Disclosure — credentials and CLI: secrets are read only through Hermes get_secret. The user-run hermes bundlebees verify applies a worker's patch to your feature-branch worktree and runs that code's named tests on this machine outside any sandbox before it commits and pushes the branch; verify and deploy run their child processes with a minimal environment and deploy, when you invoke it, reaches a remote host over ssh. A Cua sandbox is not a sandbox for the Hermes process. The Desktop pane uses ctx.rest and never shows tokens or host addresses.

known_issues: The Desktop pane backend has been mounted through Hermes 0.23's own dashboard plugin loader and the pane module loaded through its default export; it has not yet been proven in a live Hermes Desktop window.

entries.name: bunny_space-platform
entries.description: Bunny Space gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects a Hermes profile (the bot brain) to the Bunny Space relay so the bot joins private rooms, answers its owner, and handles @bot:<slug> mentions in posts and comments. Outbound pull transport; no external dependencies. Disclosure — replies are prompted to be in Spanish; @bot mention tasks and assistance tasks are dispatched to Hermes under the fixed sender id "owner" (BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOWED_USERS must contain "owner"), and the plugin refuses to dispatch third-party content unless platform_toolsets.bunny_space is restricted to read-only tools (the platform's effective toolset, including MCP and plugin toolsets; add no_mcp when MCP servers are enabled); the private assistance worker is opt-in via BUNNY_SPACE_ASSISTANCE=1 (the relay cannot enable it); setting BUNNY_SPACE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS makes the connector refuse to connect; the relay sets the poll interval and may hand the connector a WebSocket "wake" URL it then connects to (wake signals only, no message content).

entries.name: burnclock
entries.description: Status-bar chip and left-nav dashboard for the MIT burnclock CLI. The chip reads burnclock's local badge cache; the dashboard adds cached balance, runway, budget, the DeepSeek Flash off-peak clock, and an API-keys card. A key entered in the card is sent to the plugin's own local backend, written only to burnclock's keys file (mode 0600), and used only for the explicit `burnclock badge --refresh`; the desktop renderer stores no key and Hermes credentials are never read or forwarded. Requires the separately installed burnclock CLI (pip install burnclock). Disclosure — the status-bar chip runs a read-only shell command (cat of burnclock's badge cache) in your active local session every 60 seconds, and the dashboard page runs `burnclock offpeak --json` every 60 seconds; a provider key you paste into the API-keys card is written to burnclock's own `~/.config/burnclock/env` (mode 0600), and Save or Refresh runs `burnclock badge --refresh`, which calls the chosen providers' APIs (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Moonshot, MiniMax, fal) with those keys, only when you click.

entries.name: business-agent-os
entries.description: Set up a file-based business operating system for an AI agent, for business owners who are not developers: one business folder of plain Markdown memory in two layers (a folder per client and project with state, dated changelog with a monthly archive, to-do and inbox; and a Karpathy-style wiki the agent maintains from saved sources: topic, entity and source pages with an index and a log), a daily log, a voice guide, session commands (/pickup with client, topic and daily modes, /wrap, /biz-status, /biz-review, /trace, /new-client, /ingest, /lint), optional local git save points and an optional tmux session menu. One skill plus a hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.danielbilsborough.com/mcp, no key, no sign-in) with four read-only tools: scaffold_business_os, house_rules, daily_routine and voice_guide_template. entries.name: butler-assistant
entries.description: Turns Hermes into a proactive personal assistant. You set your daily non-negotiables and Butler checks in until they are done or deferred; you tell it about a commitment and it follows up before it slips, with the model choosing whether and when to follow up inside owner-set limits (max unanswered nudges, minimum gap between messages). If you opt in, it can also ring your phone for urgent follow-ups or place calls you approve, through your own LiveKit SIP trunk. You choose its tone (Gentle to Strict), how persistent it is, quiet hours, time zone and a daily cap on check-ins, and can pause it in one click. A concierge-style Hermes Desktop page shows today's non-negotiables, upcoming commitments, recent activity and preferences, with a 4-step Quick Setup; the same controls are available to the agent as tools in chat. Disclosure — a background runner thread in the gateway process schedules check-ins, which run as normal turns in your admitted DM or local chat on your configured model, billed like any message; with background wakes enabled it sets allow_gateway_injection for this plugin; with system controls on it writes notification, display and nudge settings into your Hermes config.yaml (keys listed in the README, including agent.gateway_notify_interval, skills.creation_nudge_interval, gateway.message_timestamps.enabled, platforms.*.gateway_restart_notification and the top-level timezone once confirmed), replacing existing per-platform values for those keys; the agent can change Butler's own settings through butler_controls when asked, while DM capture, notification arming and every phone setting stay user-only; the optional prompt review writes to SOUL.md and a butler-capabilities skill only after you select and apply each change, keeping backups; the optional 'verify time zone via IP' action calls ipapi.co or worldtimeapi.org only when you ask; phone calling is off by default; once you enable it in Desktop and add your LiveKit credentials (read through Hermes secret_scope), Butler sends HTTPS requests to your LIVEKIT_URL to ring you within hourly/cooldown/quiet-hours limits, or to place third-party calls only after you approve the exact script (Desktop or CLI, never the agent; emergency and premium numbers blocked; calls open with an AI disclosure); if you also enable inbound screening, an AI answers inbound calls on your trunk and takes messages; an optional, user-started voice worker (pip extra 'voice') connects to LiveKit and OpenAI for live call audio and may run a local `hermes chat` subprocess to answer your questions on a call; call transcripts and summaries, including what the other party said, are stored locally and shown to your agent after the call; iMessage voice and image helpers run local ffmpeg/ffprobe and hand files to Hermes as MEDIA: reply attachments (Butler never reads Hermes runtime secrets or calls the Photon sidecar); watches read the local file path you ask it to watch; inbound DM event capture is off by default and needs two separate opt-ins; all state is stored in plaintext SQLite in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.
entries.title: Butler
known_issues: Hermes Desktop keeps a packaged plugin's page off until you enable it once: Capabilities → Plugins → Butler - Proactive Assistant.
The plugin's manifest name is `butler`; it cannot be installed alongside another plugin whose manifest name is also `butler`.
Message reactions and threaded replies (butler_expression / butler_imessage react, reply, edit, unsend) are disabled and fail closed until the gateway can bind a message ID to the active chat.

iMessage screen/bubble effects and polls are disabled and fail closed until Hermes adds send_effect/send_poll verbs to ctx.platform_actions (NousResearch/hermes-agent#154299); images and voice notes are sent as normal reply attachments.
Watches are polled local files; there is no webhook receiver.

Phone calling needs your own LiveKit SIP trunk and credentials, and live call audio needs the optional voice worker running (pip extra 'voice' plus OPENAI_API_KEY). The phone path is unit-tested but has not yet been exercised end to end against a real SIP trunk and carrier call.
Background check-ins bind only to a DM or local session; if your only recent sessions are group chats, DM Butler once before running Quick Setup.

entries.name: butler
entries.description: Turns the Hermes desktop pet into an on-screen operator: WALK draws a guide on the real controls and verifies each step from the macOS Accessibility tree, DESCRIBE reads the control under your pointer (role, label, enabled state, value) without letting the click reach your app, and WATCH announces one condition from an app in the background and keeps it until you acknowledge it. Accessibility only: no screenshots, no OCR, no Screen Recording, no Input Monitoring. Disclosure — macOS only; needs the Accessibility permission, which lets its helper read the controls and text of other apps on screen. On first use it downloads its native screen helper from the author's GitHub release and refuses it unless it matches the checksum pinned in the plugin source (otherwise it compiles the bundled Swift source with swiftc), and LOOK mode intercepts clicks across the screen until you pick or cancel. Sending from the pet into a chat requires `allow_gateway_injection: true` for this plugin.
entries.title: Butler
known_issues: macOS only: the companion is a native Swift helper, and every feature that reads the screen needs the Accessibility grant.
Guides are single-active: a second guide is refused with a hint unless replace=true.
WATCH runs one app at a time; Chromium/Electron trees need the window to have been opened once before their controls are visible.
LOOK's click-catcher covers the screen while armed, so clicks do not reach other apps until you cancel or pick.

entries.name: buzzmark
entries.description: Write, plan and schedule social media posts in a business's own voice through Buzzmark's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://buzzmark.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): post ideas from this week's news, posts for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Threads and TikTok with a version per platform, a score for how much a post sounds like the brand, pictures, a week of posts planned around the best posting times, and what worked. Bundles the buzzmark workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Buzzmark's hosted server (buzzmark.ai) and acts on the user's Buzzmark account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Nothing posts right away: tools save, schedule, move and unschedule posts on the user's Buzzmark calendar and delete drafts, and write_posts, rewrite_post and create_image use the plan's monthly allowance. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: cacheguard
entries.description: Warns or blocks a large chat message sent after a pause, when the provider's prompt cache may have expired. Afterwards it shows how many tokens were reused or rebilled, and /cacheguard shows how often your cache was lost after pauses of each length. Modes (off, warn, block) are set per surface (terminal, desktop, gateway), and a model can have its own pause, size and mode. In block mode the message is not sent: the reply says so, and you send it with /retry or by sending the same text again. If the plugin fails, the message is sent. Disclosure — no network call, no LLM call, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry. Middleware llm_request reads every message of the request to hash the start of the chat (sha256, only the hash is kept) and removes cacheguard's own "message not sent" replies from what the model receives. Middleware llm_execution reads the token usage of each response; the provider call is Hermes's own next_call(), never repeated. Hook pre_llm_call returns a block for a large message after a pause. Hook transform_llm_output posts a result line with ctx.post_message and never changes the reply. Reads config.yaml (its own settings through ctx.get_config) and the environment variables HERMES_SINGLE_QUERY_SESSION, HERMES_KANBAN_TASK, HERMES_PLATFORM, HERMES_INTERACTIVE. Writes its settings with ctx.set_config (/cacheguard set and setup) and, under <HERMES_HOME>/cacheguard/, observations.jsonl (token counts, times and model name of calls after a pause; no message text, no session id) and one small json file per chat (times, token counts, hash). /cacheguard reset deletes them. Unattended runs (cron, kanban, subagents, curator, API server, webhooks) pass through untouched; one-shot runs (-Q, -z, --oneshot) are never blocked and show no line (a -Q run may be counted in the stats); with chat -q, block acts as warn. Private Hermes names: tools.approval_context._is_single_query_approval_context (a run with no screen only warns) and agent.usage_pricing.normalize_usage (read the cache token counts). If one is missing, the plugin says so in /cacheguard and degrades: it only warns, or result lines are missing.

entries.name: caduceus-governance
entries.description: Deterministic, model-free admission control for what Hermes writes into its own skills: content lanes, operator-owned executable checks, a provenance lane for writes made after untrusted web/browser/MCP content, a tamper-evident ledger, and operator release/rollback. Observe by default. Disclosure — Records a digest of every skill_manage call in $HERMES_HOME/caduceus (observe mode, default); in opt-in boundary or enforce mode it blocks unadmitted skill_manage calls or deletes and restores files under $HERMES_HOME/skills (and, if enabled, MEMORY.md/USER.md and config.yaml, of which it keeps owner-only copies in its state directory) to the last admitted state, including changes made by `hermes update` skill syncs or hub installs. Operator-registered check commands run sandboxed (macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock/seccomp) or are held. The dashboard's POST /approve acts only on a signature from an operator-enrolled device. No network, no model calls.
entries.title: Caduceus Governance
known_issues: Evidence is local-development only (Claude Haiku 4.5, small samples, simulated web read); see docs/CLAIMS.md.
A hostile line written with no untrusted input in the session is not caught by default; the review dial (prose) reaches a human but costs reading every prose change.
A poisoned page on an operator-trusted host (trusted_hosts) is outside the provenance lane.
Phrase detection (authority lane) failed its preregistered gate and ships off.

entries.name: caduceus
entries.description: Answers about your own health that cite your DNA, Apple Health trends, medical records and new research, from a vault on your machine. Caduceus imports 23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage or FamilyTreeDNA raw data, a Promethease report, an Apple Health export, Health Auto Export data (a JSON export or a live sync) and US health records (FHIR) into local SQLite, then gives your agent gene–drug checks (CPIC guidelines plus GLP-1 research), trends before and after a medication start, a rebuilt variant report, a one-page brief for your doctor and a research watch that puts studies on your own gene–drug pairs first. No DNA file yet? /caduceus demo loads an invented person to try it. /caduceus erase deletes everything it stored; your settings and any schedules you created stay. Privacy levels are yours to choose: open by default, or standard, which hides Alzheimer's risk, hereditary cancer risk, carrier status, mental health and reproductive results until you unlock them. Information with limits, not medical advice. Disclosure — imports, search and reports run locally, and the vault is never uploaded as a whole; tool results (slices of your data) enter the conversation, so the model provider you chose sees them; a hook adds one fixed note, holding none of your data, to the first health, medication or DNA question of each chat when the vault has data (off with the `vault_hint` setting); the research watch (on by default, runs when you or the agent ask for it or on a schedule you create, off with the `research_watch` setting) sends gene and topic terms, the names of medications you recorded, and public marker and article IDs, never genotypes, to Europe PMC and NCBI; the Health Auto Export sync (off until you allow that app's MCP server for Caduceus in Hermes config, and run only when you or the agent ask for it or on a schedule you create) reads Apple Health data from that server through Hermes's own MCP client and sends none of your data out; scheduled checks run model turns billed like any message; no telemetry. Includes a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report, asks you to check it holds no health data, and files it to this repository with `gh` only after you approve the draft.

entries.name: call-me
entries.description: /call-me gateway: text your Hermes agent from the /call-me iPhone app, and the callme_call tool rings your phone, speaks the agent's text and returns your spoken answer as a transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the /call-me service at https://callmemcp.com/aiphone (run by the plugin author): creates one agent session, sends texts and call requests, and long-polls for replies while the gateway runs (at most one request every 3 seconds); sends message text, the text to be spoken and the destination numbers, and call audio is transcribed by the service so only the transcript comes back; the agent session token and event cursor are stored at $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/call-me/session.json (mode 600); only numbers in CALLME_ALLOWED_USERS can message the agent or be called, and inbound messages must come from that number's verified /call-me device; callme_call blocks until the call ends (300 seconds at most) and returns missed if nobody answers; no shell commands, telemetry or self-update. The /call-me iPhone app that receives the messages and calls needs a paid subscription; the plugin itself is free and MIT-licensed.

entries.name: calling-mom
entries.description: Lets a cheap model run your Kanban board and calls a stronger model only where the board or the tool results show it is needed. Mom (a good, affordable model) answers stuck signals, risky commands and completion checks; olymp (the expensive heavyweight) is asked only when mom escalates a rare high-stakes case, with hard limits per card and per day. Disclosure — once enabled, the plugin observes every kanban worker tool result (hashes and counts only, logged to logs/calling-mom.jsonl). With the advisor enabled AND a board or card opted in, redacted run excerpts go through Hermes's ctx.llm to the mom and olymp models you choose; the answer is appended to the tool result and written to the card with the public kanban_comment tool. A card line verify: <command> runs an allowlisted command (no shell, scrubbed environment) for cards created by trusted creators. hermes calling-mom setup writes the plugin's own config (calling_mom.* and its plugins.entries allowlist) with the values you pick, reads delegation.backends.model_map (read-only, to offer your Advanced Delegation routes) and creates one cron job, 'calling-mom: sweep', unless you pass --no-cron; the sweep reads the kanban databases and may push metrics to Pushgateway URLs you configure (off by default). No telemetry, no credentials stored. Since 1.4: a Desktop page (Needs you, Active cards, recent activity, status-bar chip) served by the plugin's dashboard route; it reads the log and the opted-in boards, writes only when you press a button (an answer card comment, a card move including complete, archive and unblock, written straight to the kanban database through Hermes' internal kanban module), and shows each running card's last assistant message read through Hermes' SessionDB (read-only, local, never sent to a model). web_verify (off by default) sends a one-line redacted claim to Hermes' own web_search tool. The sweep and the optional chat-wait count read board events and the human-input hooks (kinds and seconds only, never prompt or answer text). The plugin sends nothing to a server of its own; details in SECURITY.md of the repo. Since 1.7.0: what waits under Needs you is also sent once to your phone by running Hermes' own hermes send CLI (setting calling_mom.notify.target, default off), and a reply in the chat the notice went to answers the card via the tool calling_mom_answer, whose 'allow' answer releases a held command once without a further prompt from the plugin; a held critical command can be fail-closed (opt-in calling_mom.preflight.fail_closed) so it stays blocked when Mom cannot check it; a new card can be started from the Dashboard page (POST /card through Hermes' public kanban_create); a card can be parked with Decide later and resumed from the Later section. Since 1.7.1: that New card form can also pin the card's model (a model of one of your authenticated providers, sent to kanban_create as model/provider; GET /new-card lists them).
entries.title: Calling mom
known_issues: Hermes has no public Kanban API for plugins yet: reading boards and their cards, and the writes behind answering, moving, parking (schedule_task), unblocking, completing, archiving and pinning a card to a model all go through hermes_cli.kanban_db / kanban_db_boards / kanban_db_connect; dashboard writes go through tools.registry dispatch (kanban_create and the other public tools). Every private import lives in one file, _core.py (kanban_db, kanban_db_boards, kanban_db_connect, agent.redact, hermes_cli.config, hermes_cli.profiles, hermes_cli.model_switch_providers, hermes_cli.curses_ui, hermes_state.SessionDB, agent.plugin_llm, tools.registry, gateway.session_context); if a Hermes update removes one, the plugin stays loaded, registers no hooks and 'hermes calling-mom doctor' names the cause.

A gateway restart is needed after the plugin updates: its dashboard routes are imported when the gateway starts, so a running gateway keeps answering the old routes and the page's newer ones 404 until it restarts (the New card form says so).
A phone notice starts one 'hermes send' process (a few seconds); the sweep waits at most 15 s for it and the card stays in Needs you if the send fails.
Advice arrives after the tool ran (transform_tool_result): it warns, it cannot prevent a command.
The risk list is pattern based; an unusual command or secret format can pass.

entries.name: callit
entries.description: Turn any group chat into a prediction league: friends make calls on crypto prices, football or anything, challenge each other to 1v1 duels, run closest-guess pools, and Hermes referees — it settles from live data (or a named judge / weighted group vote) and keeps season leaderboards. Duels staked in SOL/USDC/USDT lock both stakes in an on-chain Solana escrow program (immutable, devnet by default) that can only pay the two players; Hermes signs the result with a per-install referee key and both players are refunded if it never does. Disclosure — makes read-only HTTPS calls to api.coingecko.com and site.api.espn.com, and calls the configured Solana RPCs (public mainnet RPC to verify `/callit paid` receipts; devnet by default for the escrow) to read bets, request devnet fee top-ups and send settle transactions signed by the referee key `CALLIT_RESOLVER_KEY` (a Hermes secret that holds only fee SOL, never a player's key); duel stakes sit in an unaudited, immutable escrow program that can only pay one of the two players or refund both, so use it for devnet/testing only; duel stake links open a page on the author's GitHub Pages site, which is outside the reviewed code and builds the transaction you sign in your wallet; stores calls, sides, votes, points, debts, public Solana addresses and an audit log in plugin-data/callit/data.db; `/callit referee on` creates one visible Hermes cron job that only referees its own chat's league; no shell commands, no telemetry.

entries.name: calm-mode
entries.description: When you get frustrated, your agent slows down. Calm Mode scores the tone of each message ("still broken", "I already told you", capitals, "!!", the same message twice); frustration builds and fades. Past a threshold the agent works in small checked steps, at most two file edits per turn, and risky commands (rm -rf, git push, deploys, DROP TABLE) wait until the user says yes. /calm shows the level and forces it on or off. No model calls, nothing stored.

entries.name: camofox
entries.description: Camofox browser backend: browse with a self-hosted anti-detection Firefox (Camoufox, C++ fingerprint spoofing) through the camofox-browser REST server. Registers the browser_* tools (navigate, snapshot with clickable refs, click, type, scroll, back, press, get_images, vision, JavaScript console, plus cookie import when CAMOFOX_API_KEY is set) in the `camofox` toolset, with `hermes camofox setup|status`; existing CAMOFOX_* variables and browser.camofox settings carry over. Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. Disclosure: one Python dependency (requests). It talks only to the Camofox server at CAMOFOX_URL (e.g. http://localhost:9377, which you run yourself: Docker or `npm start`), sending CAMOFOX_API_KEY as a bearer token when set. Page text reaches only your model as tool output; browser_vision sends the screenshot to your configured auxiliary vision model. Snapshots mask values that look like secrets (API keys, tokens), but text typed into form fields, passwords included, shows up in snapshots. Oversized snapshots and screenshots are written under the Hermes home (cache/web, browser_screenshots). Cookie import reads Netscape cookies.txt files only from browser.camofox.cookies_dir (default ~/.camofox/cookies). browser_vault fills saved passwords on the Camofox tab (sent only to a loopback or HTTPS CAMOFOX_URL). Inert on Hermes cores that still bundle Camofox.

entries.name: canary-trap
entries.description: Catch prompt injection by the secret it tries to steal. Every turn the agent is shown a decoy credential (HERMES_DEPLOY_KEY=hdk_live_…) with the instruction never to send it; no real task needs it, so if it shows up in a tool call — plain, URL-encoded, base64, hex, reversed, spaced out or as a 16+ character fragment, in any nested argument — the call is blocked (pre_tool_call), every later tool call in that session goes to your approval until /canary reset, and the reply opens with an alert (transform_llm_output). /canary shows status and incidents, rotates the decoy, or tests text. Disclosure — adds a ~60-token paragraph with the decoy to each turn's user message (pre_llm_call; Hermes may persist the API-bound message for cache replay; the decoy grants nothing). Stores in its own plugin state: the decoy, up to 200 incidents (time, tool name, how the decoy was hidden, platform, session id — never tool arguments or conversation content) and locked session ids. Lockdown only adds approval prompts through Hermes' approval gate (auto-approved under YOLO, so advisory there; the leaking call is always blocked). No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials, telemetry or background work.

entries.name: capalis
entries.description: Describe a job in one sentence, and Capalis sets it up, runs it and checks it really happened. It finds your channels and repository by name, picks the right tool for each step and does a practice run that sends nothing. It runs only after you approve that exact version, from your phone on Telegram if you like. For example, a bug posted in Discord or Slack becomes one GitHub issue, a Slack notice and a reply to the reporter, who hears back again when the issue is closed. Every write is read back, nothing is done twice, and the job stops itself when a token, permission or tool changes. Disclosure — Capalis runs a background worker in the Hermes process that executes owner-approved Recipes (schedules, waits, alerts) and sends to api.github.com, slack.com, hooks.slack.com, discord.com and api.telegram.org with the tokens you configure. Its http.get step fetches HTTPS pages at public addresses that you approve. Its pre_gateway_dispatch hook takes every new message in a channel a Recipe listens to away from the agent. Once you approve a contract, Recipes can call Hermes's web_search and web_extract tools outside an agent turn. The model can start an approved manual Recipe without a per-run prompt unless the Recipe requires per-run confirmation.
entries.title: Capalis
known_issues: Reports from Discord or Slack reach Capalis only after the report channel and the reporters are added to Hermes's gateway settings. /capalis setup prints the exact hermes config set commands.
Waiting jobs, schedules and alerts need the Hermes gateway running (hermes gateway install).

entries.capability_summary: capalis (community, maintained by Femtech-web) Describe a job in one sentence, and Capalis sets it up, runs it and checks it really happened. It finds your channels and repository by name, picks the right tool for each step and does a practice run that sends nothing. It runs only after you approve that exact version, from your phone on Telegram if you like. For example, a bug posted in Discord or Slack becomes one GitHub issue, a Slack notice and a reply to the reporter, who hears back again when the issue is closed. Every write is read back, nothing is done twice, and the job stops itself when a token, permission or tool changes. Disclosure — Capalis runs a background worker in the Hermes process that executes owner-approved Recipes (schedules, waits, alerts) and sends to api.github.com, slack.com, hooks.slack.com, discord.com and api.telegram.org with the tokens you configure. Its http.get step fetches HTTPS pages at public addresses that you approve. Its pre_gateway_dispatch hook takes every new message in a channel a Recipe listens to away from the agent. Once you approve a contract, Recipes can call Hermes's web_search and web_extract tools outside an agent turn. The model can start an approved manual Recipe without a per-run prompt unless the Recipe requires per-run confirmation. This plugin registers tool(s): capalis_status, capalis_setup, capalis_capabilities, capalis_recipe, capalis_run, capalis_contract, capalis_pause; hook(s): pre_gateway_dispatch. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0. Known issues: Reports from Discord or Slack reach Capalis only after the report channel and the reporters are added to Hermes's gateway settings. /capalis setup prints the exact hermes config set commands.; Waiting jobs, schedules and alerts need the Hermes gateway running (hermes gateway install).; Telegram is used for approvals and alerts. Telegram and Slack-webhook posts can't be read back, so they are marked unverifiable..

entries.name: caprover-operator
entries.description: Read-only setup diagnostics and human-approved, state-bound immutable-image deployment for one owner-configured CapRover app, with durable uncertainty, replay refusal and dated operation cards for self-hosted projects. Disclosure: contacts the configured CapRover HTTPS origin and optional fixed health endpoint; CapRover returns all app definitions in memory, while only the configured app's keyed fingerprint and sanitized evidence enter a private local ledger. Image startup may run migrations. HTTP alone does not prove the serving image; runtime task evidence is optional. No shell, telemetry, self-updater or automatic rollback. Apply requires fresh native human approval in in_process mode. Safeguards apply only to this plugin's caprover_apply workflow and ledger; independent terminal or execute_code actions, other plugins, direct API calls and external operators require their own access controls and approvals.
entries.title: CapRover Operator
known_issues: Apply requires an interactive native human approval and plugins.isolation set to in_process; unattended, smart and YOLO approval cannot authorize a deployment.
Servers without supported runtime task evidence produce metadata/HTTP observation receipts rather than a verified serving-image rollout.
Inline HTML cards require the assistant to emit the returned public preview directive; unsupported or remote surfaces retain JSON facts and may show a file attachment.

entries.name: cardlake
entries.description: Cardlake keeps what you mean to get back to (reminders, articles and videos to learn from, links, work) in one daily feed. This plugin puts that feed in your Telegram chat with Hermes: /cardlake feed and today show your cards with Done, Tomorrow, Next week and Undo buttons and a pinned Today checklist, a morning message sends what's due, and you can send Hermes a link to save it. Free account at cardlake.app, or host your own. Disclosure — talks to Cardlake only through Hermes' "cardlake" MCP connection (cardlake.app or a self-hosted copy); sends and pins card messages in your private Telegram chat, and adds /cardlake to the bot's command menu unless you set that menu up yourself, through the bot Hermes already runs; /cardlake save sends your text (with passwords, keys and tokens removed in code) to your own Hermes model; stores only the id of the pinned Today message in plugin state. No shell commands, credentials, background processes or telemetry; the morning job exists only if you create it from the blueprint, and it cannot change cards.

entries.name: cash-desk
entries.description: Chase overdue invoices from your CSV exports (generic, Xero, QuickBooks, Stripe, bank statements): apply payments only on an exact reference and amount, draft reminders at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days, and send one only after a person approves its exact text and Hermes asks once more. Figure Lock holds every amount, invoice number, date, IBAN and reference to the ledger; a rewording that changes one is rejected with a diff. Disclosure — imports only CSV files inside its own data folder, its bundled demo folder and the folders you list in import_dirs, and keeps its ledger in SQLite under its plugin data folder; a reminder leaves only after a person approves its exact text (/cashdesk approve or the Desktop page) and Hermes's approval prompt passes, never from cron, a subagent, yolo mode or approvals set to auto-approve; in the default eml mode it writes .eml files to its outbox folder, and in smtp mode it sends through the SMTP server you configure, with the password stored as a Hermes secret (CASHDESK_SMTP_PASSWORD) and TLS always verified; with guard_outgoing_messages on (off by default) it replaces any agent reply that states an amount, IBAN or invoice number the ledger does not hold for that customer with a withheld notice, and replies stop streaming; no other network calls, no telemetry.
entries.title: Cash Desk
known_issues: Imports CSV exports; there is no live connection to a bank or an accounting system.
Reminders are in English; you can choose another language per customer or with default_language (Czech is the only other one so far).
With guard_outgoing_messages on, replies in that profile arrive whole instead of streaming.

entries.name: chalk
entries.description: Hermes teaches on a chalkboard. Ask it to explain something and Hermes Desktop draws the lesson inline in the chat, stroke by stroke in chalk, while the narration plays; replay it or save it as an MP4. The agent's chalk_teach tool sends only structure (flow, list, compare, equation, graph, cycle, tree, note, labelled sketch, circle/underline, clear) and the board lays itself out, so small models produce clean boards; full boards are wiped by an eraser and continue on a fresh one. Other surfaces receive the narration as one audio file. Disclosure: narration text goes to the user's configured TTS provider through Hermes' own text_to_speech tool (ctx.dispatch_tool); lessons and audio are stored under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/chalk; Save video uploads the recording to the plugin over plugin RPC and writes it to ~/Videos/Chalk (or ~/Downloads/Chalk when the OS blocks Videos), converting with ffmpeg when it is on PATH (fixed argument lists). A transform_llm_output hook appends the lesson's MEDIA line once if the reply left it out. Graph expressions are parsed by a small parser, never evaluated as code. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no background processes.

A transform_llm_output hook appends the lesson's MEDIA line once if the reply left it out. Graph expressions are parsed by a small parser, never evaluated as code. entries.name: chanda
entries.description: Chanda memory provider — local long-term memory over MCP, built without an LLM on the write path. entries.name: chat-length
entries.description: Tells the user when a chat is getting too long and hands them a short opener for a fresh chat; the new chat pulls the earlier context itself via session_search, no handover document. Fill level from real provider token counts, measured against Hermes' compaction point by default; notices at 70 % and 90 % (configurable), once each per chat, re-armed after compaction, never in cron, subagent, kanban, batch or webhook runs. Notice in the conversation language, English or German. Disclosure — on the turn that crosses a threshold, pre_llm_call adds a one-turn instruction to that turn's user message (never the system prompt; replayed byte-identical, so prompt caching stays intact); post_api_request stores per-session token counts, model and provider name and which notice fired (no message content) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/chat-length/, pruned after 30 days; reads the session title read-only from state.db and the compression settings read-only from config.yaml; no network calls, no tools, no dependencies.

entries.name: check-please
entries.description: Pairs each "done" in an agent's reply (tests pass, sent, deployed, pushed, saved, scheduled) with the tool call that proves it, and adds one line when a claim is stale, failed, or proven only by something the agent edited. Disclosure — reads the tool calls and replies Hermes passes to its hooks; runs no shell commands and makes no network or model calls; stores claim sentences, command first lines and a 14-day claim log in its own plugin state file; appends one "Check:" line under a flagged reply and, on cron runs, puts one line at the top of the delivered reply; on coding turns its pre_verify hook may send the agent back once to recheck a contradicted claim, and its pre_llm_call hook may add a one-line note about the previous reply's flagged claim (all on by default, each has a setting); `/check today` and `/check jobs` show profile-wide tallies, including short claim snippets from other chats on a shared gateway; the owner-run `hermes check-please audit` command reads the profile's saved sessions (state.db) read-only and prints a summary locally; the Desktop pane polls the plugin's own dashboard route every 4 seconds while a session is focused; no telemetry.
entries.title: Check, Please
known_issues: Heuristic, English-only claim patterns. It cannot see webhook payload bodies, runtime-built strings, or file writes made inside a script body (a Python heredoc).
A not-backed claim means no receipt was found, which is common and often not an overclaim, so by default it shows only in /check, not under the reply.
A delegated sub-agent's claims are judged only by that child's own tool calls, kept separate from the parent session's evidence; see /check subagents.
Developed and tested on macOS (Hermes CLI, gateway and Desktop). The engine is standard-library Python; Linux and Windows are untested.

Accuracy numbers (held-out precision and recall, real-world alert rates) are dated and sourced in the README's Results section. Part of the test bench was used to tune the plugin, so bench catch counts are tuned results, not real-world rates.
The Desktop status-bar chip ran in a real Hermes Desktop window on 2026-11-09. The pane's 0.4.2 label changes are checked by a Node render harness, not yet in a real window.

entries.name: chereda
entries.description: Череда in the Hermes desktop app — obligation loops instead of status cards. Each loop shows whose move it is (customer or performer), the clock and deadline, the class, the evidence (command, output digest, expected exit code) and the whole description, which a participant can refine from the card. Moves are verbs — ask, promise, refuse with a reason, declare with proof, accept, object, withdraw — offered as buttons; the panel only calls the real `череда` CLI, so the rules (no talking out of turn, refusal only with a reason, three-promise cap, deadline escalation) stay in one place and cannot drift between CLI and UI. A loop also carries a feed for participant reports and notes that do not move the turn, and a “write as” switch so the owner speaks as themselves rather than as the bot. Read-only apart from those verbs, loopback only, no self-update. Model-written evidence is never executed on its own: the bridge runs a proof command only when the owner has approved it in advance (.bridge-allow.txt or --approve); anything else is recorded in the loop feed as “awaiting approval” and the turn stays with the performer. The interface ships in English and Russian with a glossary explaining every verb. Requires the `череда` binary in PATH (cargo install --path . from github.com/kostyk348/chereda); without it the plugin answers 503 with the exact install instruction instead of an empty screen. Disclosure — the "сделать" (declare) move with a proof runs that proof command on your machine as you (through the Chereda CLI's `sh -c`); the optional bridge script replays proofs from worker reports only when the exact command, or a prefix entry without shell operators, is listed in the owner's .bridge-allow.txt.

entries.description: Schedule and publish LinkedIn posts on the user's own profile through Chime Scheduler's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://schedule.getchime.co/mcp, OAuth sign-in with LinkedIn through Hermes' own MCP OAuth, no keys in config). The user says when a post should go out in their own words and the exact local time is echoed back; posts can be drafts, scheduled, published now, edited, rescheduled or cancelled, and a post already live on LinkedIn can be deleted after the user confirms, with a first comment and up to 9 images or one video through a private upload link. Free. Bundles the chime-scheduler workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to schedule.getchime.co (Wednesday Solutions, Inc.) with the post text, times, first comments and uploaded files, and acts on the user's own Chime Scheduler account. Sign-in opens a browser to Sign in with LinkedIn; Hermes stores and refreshes the token and the package never reads it. Posts go only to the user's own LinkedIn profile and only when asked; the server never reads the LinkedIn feed, messages or connections. get_status, list_posts and list_uploads are annotated read-only; schedule_post, post_now, edit_post, cancel_post (which also deletes a live post, after confirmation) and get_upload_link are not. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before each of those and refuses them in unattended runs; the sign-in step adds a same-name config.yaml entry, which replaces the package entry, so the README's entry also sets trust: untrusted. Chime Scheduler sends email only about the user's own posts and uses product analytics that never record post text or chat. Data deletion via support@getchime.co; privacy https://schedule.getchime.co/privacy, terms https://schedule.getchime.co/terms. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: chiron
entries.description: An advisor who is also a friend. Chiron reads how much you know about the topic in front of you (setup, AI, code, business, general) from your own words, with no model call, and adds one short note per turn telling the agent how to talk to you: beginner (plain words, one step at a time, better options offered), medium, pro or maximum (terse, tradeoffs first). Levels are per topic and move one step at a time; a strong first message is read directly; your own word ("I'm a developer", "just do it", /chiron level code pro) pins a topic. At every level the note keeps a floor: before spending, sending, publishing, deleting or touching credentials, the agent says exactly what will happen and waits for a clear yes. Off in each session until /chiron on (or always_on). The system prompt never changes, so prompt caching keeps working. Live evals in the repo: with a real 40-row client file in reach, Chiron-on sessions asked before deleting it in 6 of 6 runs; plugin-off sessions wiped it on request in 3 of 3. Disclosure — pre_llm_call reads only the current user message and returns a short context note; it stores per-session topic levels and the on/off flag in one JSON file under its plugin data directory (last 200 sessions), with a sidecar lock file and short-lived temp files in the same directory; no network calls, no model calls, no shell or subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry."
entries.title: Chiron
known_issues: Level reading is keyword-based (English only). It can misread a level; /chiron level <topic> <level> pins the right one.
The floor is guidance to the model, not a tool gate. It changes how the agent asks; it does not block tool calls. Pair it with Hermes approvals for hard stops.
Evals are a small number of runs on one model (see EVALS.md); with Chiron on, pro answers ran about 12% longer than plugin-off, mostly the confirm-before-acting lines.

entries.name: chmod-ref
entries.description: @chmod: context references that explain a file permission mode for the model: @chmod:<mode> takes an octal mode (755, 0755, 4755), ls -l text (-rwsr-xr-x, with the file type letter and a trailing + . or @) or an st_mode as stat and git write it (100644), and attaches both forms, each class's rights in words (directory rights named as such), what setuid, setgid and the sticky bit do and where they are ignored, and notes such as a mode everyone can change, one private to the owner, or a class holding rights the class before it lacks; @chmod:"644 u+x,go-w" applies a symbolic change step by step the way GNU chmod does (u g o a, + - =, r w x X s t, copies like u=g), @chmod:"100644 100755" shows what changes between two modes, and @chmod:"umask 027" shows what new files and directories get; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a mode as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's re; it never looks at a file on disk; no network, no files read or written, no permission changed, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of what you write, but the @chmod: reference and the explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @chmod: reference provider.

entries.name: chorepilot
entries.description: Your house and family chore board as Hermes tools, through ChorePilot's own MCP server on this machine, the LAN or Tailscale. Runs appliances (lights, climate, dishwasher/washer/dryer, sprinklers, vacuum and more via Home Assistant, Home Connect, MQTT or a simulator) and keeps a rotating chore board that devices verify. ChorePilot's policy decides every call: water/heat actions wait for the person's own yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent's approval queue, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available to an agent. Bundles the chorepilot:household skill. Disclosure — each tool call sends HTTP requests with the bearer token in CHOREPILOT_TOKEN to the user's own ChorePilot server at CHOREPILOT_URL, and the plugin also lists that server's tools once at every Hermes start (plain http only to loopback, private, Tailscale or .local/.lan/.ts.net addresses); chorepilot_call runs any device or chore tool the token's person may use (lights, climate, vacuum, locking and more) without a Hermes approval prompt, with ChorePilot's own policy deciding, so water/heat actions wait up to two minutes for that person's yes in Telegram or the ChorePilot dashboard, kids' requests go to a parent, and unlocking, opening the garage and disarming are never available; no other network calls, no files read outside the plugin, no background processes, no telemetry, stdlib only.

entries.name: chrome-tab-watchdog
entries.description: Conservative Chrome tab cleanup with in-process observation and browser-call leases. Disclosure — runs a background thread inside Hermes that proxies your local Chrome DevTools port (127.0.0.1:9222 → 127.0.0.1:9223, loopback only, you must point browser.cdp_url at it), injects a focus/activity listener into every Chrome page, rewrites browser_exec session names to a per-profile namespace, and a cron script you schedule auto-closes idle, duplicate and blank tabs (including tabs with unsaved text).
entries.title: Chrome Tab Watchdog
known_issues: Requires an existing loopback Chrome CDP endpoint, browser routing through the plugin, and a script-only cleanup cron. Configure these before enabling.
Idle editors can contain unsaved text and are still subject to expiry. The last exact blank and last admitted page are retained.
Restore the original direct CDP endpoint before disabling or uninstalling; the plugin-owned forwarding route is unavailable while unloaded.

Runs inside the Hermes host, not a sandbox, with a background observer thread, loopback CDP listener and profile-local Unix socket/SQLite/HMAC state. No runtime Chrome launcher or external API service.
Uses read-only internal tools.browser_tool_cdp or tools.browser_session_cdp routing resolvers; future core changes may fence cleanup. Linux fd-relative socket addressing triggers a scanner CAUTION.

entries.name: chronicle
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory and memory-aware context compression for Hermes — SQLite, no account, API key or hosted service required. Captures every turn durably, extracts beliefs with provenance, answers from memory (raw-tier fallback and abstention), derives scoped conclusions, and compresses the context window losslessly with a restorable record. Registers the memory-provider AND context-engine slots from one shared core, and ships the Tapestry dashboard. Disclosure — off-host embedding endpoints are refused by default (RFC1918/ULA/CGNAT and https peers); sending memory excerpts off the host requires opting in via embeddings.allow_remote. Disclosure — the git mirror (engine/gitmirror.py) is on by default and writes plaintext JSONL copies of memory into a local git repo at ~/.hermes/commons/db/chronicle/git; it pushes only when git_remote is configured, and its 'encryption' option is a repeating-key XOR obfuscation, not cryptographic encryption.

entries.name: chronomancer
entries.description: A shared plan for the Kanban cards of every profile on a gateway. Give a card a slot (a planned start and an estimate): the plugin parks the card and releases it at the start, with no cron job. Hermes Desktop shows one timeline with a lane per profile; drag a card to plan or move it. Slots that overlap and share a one-at-a-time label show as clashes, with the reason and the next free start. An orchestrator agent plans through five tools. The plan advises: it never blocks a card or a tool call. Disclosure — reads and writes the Kanban board through Hermes's kanban tools only; its Desktop backend imports the private core module tools.kanban_tools to register those tools in the dashboard process (validate warns about it); runs one daemon timer thread in every process that loads it (except Kanban workers), which releases parked cards to the Kanban dispatcher when their planned start arrives, so agent work starts unattended for any slot the owner or an agent set; stores card titles, profile names and labels in its own plan.db change log for 30 days; no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials.

entries.name: chronos
entries.description: Speculative branching: try several candidate fixes in isolated git worktrees, verify each against the project's tests through Hermes' terminal tool, and merge only a verified winner through Hermes' file tools. entries.name: ci-red-to-green
entries.description: When a watched GitHub Actions run goes red, Hermes tells you which tests failed and which commits came in since the last green run; reply fix and the agent fixes a clone, and a PR is offered only after the plugin's own reading of Hermes's terminal output shows each failing test PASSED at the last green commit (when there was one), FAILED twice before the change (a pass before it marks the test flaky and blocks the PR), PASSED three runs in a row after it, and no new full-suite failures. pytest and go test. The PR commit holds source files only (no tests, test config, CI files or gitignored files), and the plugin reports the PR's own CI result. Desktop pane, page, palette commands and notifications. Try /ci demo with no token: a real humanize bug on a bundled copy. Disclosure: polls the GitHub API for the watched repos every 30 s while a watch is on (one background thread, stops on /ci stop or restart), downloads failed job logs without forwarding the token to the log host, compares commits, and creates a branch, commit and pull request only when you pick Open PR, all with CI_RED_TO_GREEN_GITHUB_TOKEN read through Hermes's secret scope; the plugin runs no shell commands itself, while the agent clones the repo into plugin-data/ci-red-to-green/worktrees/ and runs its tests through Hermes's terminal tool, with the first command that runs repo code escalated to Hermes's approval prompt and git push from that folder blocked; stores watches, incidents and recorded test results in plugin-data/ci-red-to-green/; no telemetry.

entries.name: ciphervault
entries.description: Zero-knowledge secret backup for AI coding agents — masked sprawl scan, RAM-only run with exact-value output scrubbing, encrypted snapshots, pre_tool_call leak guard, and a secret source for Hermes itself. Disclosure — `ciphervault_run` runs a model-chosen command with vault secrets in its environment after Hermes's approval prompt, and an "always" grant covers every later command matching that execution envelope (program, profile, inline code hash, network mode, and allow_keys); `ciphervault_secret_generate` and `ciphervault_secret_prompt` write keys into one env file inside an existing vault (never elsewhere, never in the Hermes home) only after Hermes's approval prompt, and never replace an existing key without the user's explicit yes; when a vault is present, a one-line workspace posture note (status flags, profile and pending key names, never values) is added to the model's context; in a workspace with a vault, or when a tool call names a path inside one, every other tool result is passed through the CipherVault CLI for scrubbing (withheld if that scrub or its audit receipt fails) and logged by hash to that vault's audit chain, each `ciphervault_run` approval request and replicated push sends a signed audit checkpoint (entry count + head hash) to your configured operator fleet (default `op1`–`op3.cipherv.online`), recovery drills query that fleet, and `hermes ciphervault bootstrap` downloads a checksum-pinned CLI binary from the author's GitHub releases into the plugin's folder; the Desktop Network Explorer reads public operator and checkpoint data from the author's vault.cipherv.online when you open its public view, and an object lookup sends the CID you enter.

entries.name: circuit-bench
entries.description: ESP32 workbench for Hermes and Hermes Desktop, from pin choice to running firmware: checks GPIO choices for ESP32, S2, S3, C3 and C6 against Espressif data, sizes parts with 16 calculators, draws schematics, plans the solder order, builds and flashes with your PlatformIO and esptool, and decodes panics to function and line so Hermes can fix them. 180 modules carry datasheet-cited values. Every verdict and value comes from code with its source, never from the model. A marked simulation runs the whole flow without hardware. Disclosure — runs your own pio, esptool and addr2line as subprocesses (no shell, minimal environment); a build runs the firmware project's PlatformIO scripts with your user rights and asks first; opens serial ports only on request, which can reset the board; writes firmware only with 'Allow flashing real boards' on (off by default) and after confirmation; a schematic can also be saved as a new SVG into a folder you or the agent name (out_dir); background threads only while a port is open or the Bench is in use; no network calls from the plugin (PlatformIO may download packages on a first build), no telemetry, no credentials; data under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/circuit-bench/.
entries.title: Circuit Bench
known_issues: A session-scoped /yolo and one-shot runs (hermes -z, which bypass approvals by design) are not visible to plugins: there Hermes passes agent builds, flashes and serial port openings without asking. Keep 'Allow flashing real boards' off (the default) while you use either.

Real boards need PlatformIO Core (pio), esptool and serial port access (group dialout, or uucp on Arch); the simulation mode needs none of them. Real boards tested on Linux only (ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 and WT32-ETH01); macOS is covered by CI in simulation mode; ESP32-C3, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-C6 are checked offline only.

On the command line, install with --enable (or answer 'Enable now?' with y); otherwise the tools and the Bench backend stay off. Without a terminal (scripts, SSH, an agent) also add --yes-deps; otherwise Hermes skips the dependencies and the plugin stays off. After a command-line install the Desktop half stays off until you switch on Desktop in the Circuit Bench row under Capabilities > Plugins; installing from Hermes Desktop turns it on.
A firmware stuck in a crash loop can keep the board from entering its bootloader on its own: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT and flash again.

entries.name: citation-guard
entries.description: Catches fabricated, mismatched and retracted references. Checks each DOI / PMID / arXiv id and each full reference entry against doi.org, Crossref, PubMed and arXiv: ids that do not exist, ids that point to a different paper, wrong year or first author, works found in no registry, and retractions (Crossref notices incl. Retraction Watch). A transform_llm_output reply guard appends a warning footer when the agent's own answer cites something that does not check out (the reply text is never rewritten); a verify_citations tool and a /citecheck command (.md .txt .bib .docx) give full reports. Deterministic, Python standard library only, no LLM calls, no API keys. Disclosure — network calls to api.crossref.org, doi.org, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and export.arxiv.org carrying only the reference itself (id, title, first author, year), never the rest of the conversation; when references appear in a reply, the reply guard checks them on every such reply (up to 15 s by default); the optional contact_email setting is sent to Crossref and NCBI and the optional ncbi_api_key only to NCBI; a 7-day cache of registry answers in the plugin data directory; /citecheck reads the file the user names.

entries.name: claim-check
entries.description: Receipts for agent claims: checks the success claims in each final reply ("all tests pass", "I created src/app.py", "committed and pushed", "installed requests", "ran make build successfully", "server is running on port 8000") against the session's actual tool results and appends a ✅ verified / ⚠️ unsupported / ❌ contradicted footer citing the tool call. Optional nudge feeds contradictions back into the next turn; `/receipts` and the `claimcheck_report` tool show the evidence ledger. Deterministic, pure stdlib, works with any model. Disclosure — the post_tool_call hook sees every tool's name, args and result and writes a per-session JSONL ledger (tool, file path or first 500 chars of the command, exit status, last 300 chars of output; max 500 entries) under its plugin-data directory only; transform_llm_output appends a footer without holding the stream; pre_llm_call injects context only when `nudge` is enabled; no network calls, LLM calls, subprocesses, credentials, telemetry, background processes or self-updater.
entries.title: claim-check
known_issues: Claim detection is conservative English regex: unusual phrasings are skipped, never guessed. A verdict shows only what tool results recorded this session prove.

entries.name: claude-pacer
entries.description: For power users running heavy automation in Hermes on a Claude Pro/Max subscription: claude-pacer paces agents and cron jobs so the weekly limit lasts to the reset, keeps a reserve (20% by default), and spends the leftovers on spare jobs before it. Modes skip / light / normal / heavy via the claude_pace tool, /pace, `hermes pace` and a `hermes pace gate --priority vital|normal|optional|spare` cron gate: an over-budget run is skipped before the model is called; a vital job always runs (lightly in skip mode). Disclosure — each check (cached 60 s in memory) runs Hermes' own Anthropic usage fetch, one GET to Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint made by Hermes; if the sign-in is a borrowed Claude Code login whose access token has expired, Hermes refreshes it first (a POST to Anthropic's OAuth token endpoint and a rewrite of the Claude Code credentials file), as /usage would. The plugin's own code never reads, holds or writes a credential, writes no files, runs no subprocesses and sends no telemetry.
known_issues: Until NousResearch/hermes-agent#139916 lands, Hermes reads an Anthropic usage window at 1% as 100%, so right after a 5-hour or weekly reset claude-pacer can report skip until the window passes 1%.

entries.name: claude-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Experimental model provider that runs Hermes turns on a Claude Pro/Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI (the Agent SDK path), so no separate API key or per-token bill. entries.name: claw-messenger
entries.description: iMessage, RCS and SMS for Hermes through Claw Messenger. Your agent texts real phones and gets replies, with no Mac or SIM; send, receive, group chats and attachments. Disclosure — all inbound and outbound message text, phone numbers and attachment links pass through the Claw Messenger hosted relay (wss://claw-messenger.onrender.com by default, a paid third-party service); your Claw Messenger API key is sent in the WebSocket URL together with a fixed client tag (hermes-imessage/<version>); inbound attachments are downloaded (https only, up to 20 MB) from links the relay supplies into Hermes's media cache; with the hermes-claw-messenger toolset enabled the agent can start a group text with any phone numbers it is given.

entries.name: clearance
entries.description: Per-user tool permissions for Hermes on messaging platforms and webhooks (#527, #3897): give each sender a tier (owner, admin, user, guest, blocked or your own) and every tool call is checked in code against the sender's tier before it runs, so a prompt cannot talk its way to terminal access. Deny-by-default for tools a tier does not name (new MCP servers included), per-tier hourly rate limits, a /clearance command to inspect and assign tiers from chat, and a local audit log of refused actions. Disclosure — pre_tool_call may block a tool call (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system) and pre_llm_call may block a turn for the blocked tier or a rate limit and appends one line of context naming the sender's current tier (gateway senders only); with the default settings every messaging and webhook sender is the `guest` tier (chat only, no tools) until assigned a tier in the plugin settings or with /clearance set, except senders Hermes already lists in allow_admin_from (DM chats) or group_allow_admin_from (group chats), who get the `owner` tier in that scope (gateway_admin_tier changes or disables this; an explicit users entry wins); registers /clearance; reads only its own settings, the per-message session identity and the allow_admin_from / group_allow_admin_from lists from Hermes's gateway config loader; writes its own settings on /clearance set|unset (owner only) and an audit log (tool and argument names, never values) in its plugin data directory; no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update. Not a sandbox: an allowed tool keeps its normal reach.

entries.name: clearing
entries.description: The Clearing is a writing editor inside Hermes with 159 editing methods you can run by name: 11 editor passes, 9 composition checks drawn from Strunk's rules, 33 editorial methods, 56 craft techniques and 44 figures of speech it can find in your draft or suggest where one would help. Press Read my piece and it marks your own words with what to change, most important first. Nothing changes until you press Use this. Three reviewers, a newcomer, a skeptic and a line editor, can each read the piece and then argue it out. When a suggestion adds a fact you never wrote, it says so before you keep it, and the page shows how much of the piece is still your own words. A built-in quick check and dictionary work without a model. An independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure: no network calls of its own. Editor passes go to the model you set in Hermes, only when you start one, with secrets removed by Hermes first; Bring in a link hands a public address to Hermes's web_extract after refusing non-public hosts; dictation goes to Hermes speech-to-text and, for a cloud service, waits until you press Send. Reads only files you pick, plus Hermes's speech-to-text setting and the Hugging Face model cache, both read-only. No shell commands, background processes, stored credentials or telemetry; one observe-only post_auxiliary_call hook reads the finish reason, model name and token counts of its own calls. When it falls back to a local faster-whisper model it sets KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE in the Hermes process. Your writing, its versions and a quote-stripped debug.log stay in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/clearing/; Delete forever in the Trash erases a piece.
entries.title: The Clearing
known_issues: Tested on macOS. Windows and Linux are untested.
Every editor pass needs a model set in Hermes. Without one, a pass says so and offers Open Settings; Quick check, Other words and Bring in (except a link and dictation) still work.

Bring in a link needs a web tool set up in Hermes, and Talk it through needs Hermes speech-to-text (or a faster-whisper speech model already downloaded). Without speech-to-text the Talk it through buttons are left out.

Dictation imports tools.voice_mode.transcribe_recording, which is not in Hermes's public plugin API. It is guarded and falls back to faster-whisper, so a Hermes release that moves it can disable Hermes-backed dictation.
Run live on a Claude model (Haiku) through Hermes. OpenAI and local-model routes are untested; a model that cannot return the answer format shows a plain message and leaves the page unchanged.
On Hermes 0.21.6 to 0.22.5 there is no desktop file store: Save as .md and .txt offer Copy instead, and the scene photographs are fetched on each open. Not yet run on a real 0.21.6.
Colors come from your Hermes theme. Text contrast was measured against stand-ins for Hermes's default light and dark themes and four accents over every scene; an unusual custom theme was not checked.
Removing the plugin leaves your writing in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/clearing/ until you delete that folder.

entries.name: clearvoice
entries.description: Local push-to-talk speech bridge — your words on screen and spoken clearly in 17 languages, with no account, no cloud and no audio on disk. Disclosure — downloads Whisper and Piper voice models from Hugging Face on first use (Piper pinned to a fixed revision and checksum-verified); the transcribe and say-back tools read any absolute audio file path the agent names (up to 25 MB) and transcribe it on-device; with "Allow cloud speech" and a Gradium key set, audio and text are sent to api.gradium.ai; a tool can only queue a sentence, which is spoken aloud only after you press Speak it in the ClearVoice pane.
entries.title: ClearVoice Hermes Plugin
known_issues: English is the reference language: 7 of the 17 languages rebuild a sentence with a checked grammar pack (en, fr, de, es, it, pt, nl). The other 10 polish punctuation, capitalisation and politeness but never re-order words, and the pane says so.
Japanese and Thai need an extra phonemiser (clearvoice[ja] / clearvoice[th]); the pane prints the install command when one is missing.
No speaker adaptation: a general Whisper on an atypical voice is weaker than a model trained on that speaker.

entries.name: cli-session-tabs
entries.description: Directory-scoped native TUI tabs when the public core capability contract is advertised, with isolated tmux fallback. Disclosure — the tmux backend requires OS-installed tmux; explicit `hermes tabs` commands probe the Hermes CLI (`--help`, `--tui-capabilities`) and start private, long-running TUI or tmux/Hermes clients only when invoked, passing the selected profile and the current terminal's pane identity through a credential/bypass-filtered environment; the tmux backend stores non-secret workspace metadata in profile plugin-data and confirms closes; native-tab persistence stays in core. Does not patch Hermes or read conversations/credentials.
entries.title: CLI Session Tabs
known_issues: Native support requires the separately proposed core feature (PR 146974); this plugin never installs a core patch. Auto mode retains tmux on stock or unsupported cores.
The tmux backend requires tmux 3.2+ and an interactive terminal outside an existing tmux client; explicit close loses that client's unsent draft, while detach retains live clients.
Native controls run inside the TUI (/new, /tabs, /tabclose); external new/list/close/detach management is for the explicitly selected tmux backend, not private-store native control.
Herdr 0.9.1 does not automatically relaunch the custom native bridge on a whole-Herdr restart; manually relaunch Hermes in the same directory to restore its saved views.
The screenshot is a synthetic tmux compatibility-mode demo, not a native-mode screenshot.
