entries.name: clotho
entries.description: Spin every future of a Hermes task before any of it happens. Every side effect is captured in a ledger instead of performed, you review one report, untick what you don't want, and Apply replays exactly the effects you kept with no model calls. `hermes clotho fork` runs the same task as several timelines under different models, compares their effect ledgers and applies the one you keep; `cron` rehearses a scheduled job; `demo` replays a recorded real fork with no API key. Disclosure — during a rehearsal, read-only tools run for real (file reads and search, skills, session search, web_search, clarify, todo, delegate_task in `hermes clotho run`), so a web search reaches its search provider and may be metered, and a skill_view bumps Hermes' skill usage counters as a normal read does; page fetches (web_extract, vision_analyze and similar) are held. File writes go to an APFS copy-on-write clone of your workspace under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/clotho/; a write or patch to a file outside the workspace works on a copy in a private temp folder that is removed when the rehearsal ends, and the rehearsal keeps only what changed (its diff is made from the live file). A file-tool write, patch, delete or move aimed at a path Hermes' own write guard refuses, inside the workspace or outside it, is refused before anything is copied: the tool does not run, the agent gets Hermes' refusal, and the report shows a BLOCKED row that cannot be applied; that guard is Hermes' credential and system-file deny-list, so a write to Hermes' own config.yaml, which Hermes' file tools refuse separately, is rehearsed on a copy and can be applied if you name it with --only. Shell commands and execute_code run inside that clone under macOS sandbox-exec with no network, no writes outside it and a short allowlist of environment variables, so a rehearsed `env` shows none of the keys Hermes runs with; on Linux, or without sandbox-exec, they are captured without a preview. Messages, web requests, MCP and other plugins' tools, cron changes and memory writes are captured, never run; the agent is told the reply is unknown and carries on, so its final text may say things happened that did not (the report is the truth), and captured calls still fire other plugins' post_tool_call hooks with status ok. Hermes' background memory and skill review can run during a rehearsal and spends model tokens; its writes are captured and cannot be applied. Reads outside the workspace are allowed except Hermes' own read deny-list for file reads, and, for shell commands, a deny-list of credential stores (the SSH, GnuPG, AWS, Kubernetes and Docker folders, the GitHub CLI login, .netrc, git credentials, the keychains, every .env file, and Hermes' own .env and auth.json); the ledger and report store command output and file contents in plain text under plugin-data, so they can hold whatever the rehearsed commands printed. Every effect is ticked by default, messages and web requests included, except tools Clotho does not know, held fetches, commands it cannot preview, and effects outside the workspace (with the whole command that made one), which run only if you name them with --only. Apply runs the kept effects through Hermes' real tools in your terminal, where Hermes auto-approves its own dangerous-command prompt in non-interactive use, so your tick is the approval; a single plain curl or wget call is re-run as that exact command. Apply stops before any change when a file changed since the rehearsal, when a folder on an effect's path became a symlink, or when a ticked effect certainly depends on an unticked one (--force applies anyway); it also stops before any change when an effect would write a path Hermes' own write guard refuses, and --force does not change that. It never re-sends what it already sent. Fail closed: a plugin error during a rehearsal blocks the tool call, and `hermes clotho run` refuses to start the model unless its tool middleware runs ahead of every other middleware, and refuses ACP providers and any Claude-subscription provider whose native tools it cannot verify are off. `/clotho on` in a live session keeps its state in memory only, so a gateway restart or failed plugin reload ends the rehearsal and later calls run for real. `fork` starts one `hermes clotho run` process per timeline at the same time, each making real model calls up to --max-calls. `demo` makes no model calls: it clones Hermes' runtime copy-on-write into a temp folder with no keys, runs a local sink, proxy trap and stand-in model endpoint on 127.0.0.1, and leaves that folder in place. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no stored credentials. Each rehearsed command's process group is killed when it returns, and so is a child that started its own session; one that clears its environment and leaves the rehearsal's folders lives on, still inside the sandbox.

entries.description: Cloudflare Web Search backend for Hermes' existing web_search tool, with Ceramic, Exa, or Linkup selected in plugin settings. Search only; keep a separate extract backend. entries.title: Cloudflare Web Search
known_issues: Set web.cache_enabled: false in every profile using this backend. entries.name: cmi
entries.description: Deterministic, zero-LLM context engine (context.engine: cmi): fewer tokens resent on every request, so sessions last longer on the same plan. Old tool results and stale screenshots become short digests and old write payloads are removed from past calls, while tool pairs and a byte-stable cache prefix are kept; every original is stored first and comes back byte-exact with cmi_recall. When enabled, a pre_tool_call hook blocks a write whose payload is a CMI stub; a stub write that went through is flagged at the next request with the file's last known content. Replay of 26 real sessions with the provider cache modelled: 30% fewer tokens on average (modelled API cost -25%); live 195-request sessions: 49% fewer tokens. Disclosure: originals and a full-text index (SQLite FTS5) are written under $HERMES_HOME (0700/0600, 30-day retention, 512 MiB cap); regex credential detection skips recognized secrets but can miss some; no network calls, no LLM calls, no dependencies. Project memory (experimental) is on for sessions opened in a Hermes Desktop project folder and stores only claims a model publishes with the user's exact words as proof; turn it off with context.cmi.auto_project_binding false.
entries.title: CMI — Context Manager Intelligence
known_issues: Imports private Hermes core helpers (token estimator, tool-summary helper, ContextCompressor, pricing) that can break on a Hermes release; public seams requested in NousResearch/hermes-agent#152139.

entries.name: coach
entries.description: Four modes: Consult on demand, Active per-turn review, Review before claiming done, and Decide for forks with Jev. Disclosure — once you configure a coach model, Coach sends turn transcripts, tool-call summaries, short records of memory/skill/cron/connection/kanban actions, and up to 160,000 characters by default (up to 400,000 if you raise it) of `git` diff and changed-file contents to that model through Hermes' model routing, covering every file the agent edited in the session, including files outside your working repo; the optional Decide mode (off by default) sends the agent's question, options and state to `openrouter.ai` (Typesafe's Jev model, your `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) or `api.typesafe.ai` (your `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`); it runs read-only `git` in your session directory, keeps a background review thread, can hold a "done" reply once for review, and `/coach grant` writes its own model-override permission into `config.yaml`.

entries.name: cobrain
entries.description: Shared Markdown memory for Hermes, Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and any MCP client: load a project's notes and decisions in one call, search, and save as you work. Portable Agent Plugin v1 package (plugin.json, Streamable HTTP mcp.json, one skill). Disclosure — connects to Cobrain's hosted MCP server (cobrain.space, EU-hosted) and needs a Cobrain account (free plan available); after sign-in its tools read, search, create and update the user's own notes, and can move or delete them (deleted notes go to a 30-day trash that only the owner can restore, never reachable from MCP). Writes are version-checked so two agents cannot silently overwrite each other. No telemetry, no local process, no stored credentials beyond Hermes's own OAuth token store. The remote tool list can change without a new pin of this package.
entries.title: Cobrain – Shared memory for all your AIs
known_issues: Portable mcp.json cannot complete OAuth. Add mcp_servers.cobrain with url https://cobrain.space/mcp auth: oauth and trust: untrusted to config.yaml, then run hermes mcp login cobrain and hermes mcp test cobrain.
Cobrain is an MCP memory, not a memory.provider: it does not replace Hermes's built-in memory. The skill tells the agent when to read and save.

entries.name: code-assurance-engine
entries.description: Change-assurance engine: evaluates an immutable repository candidate against an explicit, reviewer-approved check contract and returns machine-readable evidence, findings and unverified gaps, so a green result has a defined scope. Disclosure — 6 tools plus a `hermes assure` CLI and an `/assure` slash command; `assure_inspect` reads the candidate repository read-only with git (minimal git environment, option-like base/head refs refused, repositories whose own git config defines filter drivers refused); the candidate is frozen and identified by content before the contract is agreed; `assure_run` is the only operation that executes repository code, and it refuses unless the assessment is APPROVED and its venue gates pass; state stays inside the plugin's data directory, including an explicit `--state-dir` given from `/assure` or `hermes assure`; the `--owner-keys` file is a path the caller supplies, so owner approval is only as strong as control of that path and of `/assure`; reports are private, local and render without external assets; no third-party network calls, no stored credentials, no telemetry and no self-updater.

entries.name: codecoach
entries.description: Teach yourself to code in C, C++, Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby or Bash: build a real program one small step at a time, practice by predicting what code prints, and take no-hints tests. Every example really ran in a sandbox, every pass is a real test, and it warns you when your model is weak in a language. Disclosure — Code runs inside a bubblewrap sandbox (no network; system folders and a language's own toolchain folder are mounted read-only, the rest of your home folder is not mounted); if you turn on `allow_unsandboxed_code` on a machine without bwrap, learner and model-written code runs directly on your host as your user with no Hermes approval prompt. Imported .txt/.md/.pdf files (any non-hidden path you or the agent names) are sent to your configured model. It makes background model calls you did not press a button for (the next step, a spare drill, and five short warm-ups per language; the setting `auto_fit_check` turns the warm-ups off).
entries.title: CodeCoach
known_issues: Running code needs bubblewrap (bwrap) and each language's own compiler or interpreter. A language is offered only after a hello-world compiled and ran in the sandbox on your machine; without bwrap CodeCoach refuses to run any code and says what to install. That is why the entry lists Linux only.

Speed depends on your model. On a local 27B model the first lesson of a project you describe appeared 2 to 3 minutes after Start (measured on 1.0); later steps are built in the background while you code. The ready-made project needs no model and opens in seconds.
PHP, Lua, Perl, Haskell, Zig, Elixir and Lisp are offered too, without a ready-made project and with less testing than the nine languages in the description. TypeScript is not supported.

In Practice, a drill's explanation is the model's own prose and can be wrong even when the answer key, the program's real output, is right. Since 1.1.1 an explanation that names a printed number the real output does not hold is left out; one that is wrong in words only can still get through.

entries.name: codex-truly
entries.description: Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Hermes only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model_overrides.<provider>.<model_id>.context_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI_API_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: [openai-codex]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model_overrides entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset), through Hermes's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex_truly tool write scoped model_overrides context_window entries and image_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and `probe` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.
entries.title: Codex Truly
known_issues: Full 1M of input is not reachable on the Codex OAuth route: ~1.05M total context is shared with a 128K output reserve, leaving ~920K of input. The plugin defaults to 900,000 and clamps to 918,000 rather than promising more.

An over-large window fails late - the request streams response.created and then returns context_length_exceeded - so it surfaces as a mid-turn crash rather than a configuration error. Lower target_context_window and re-apply if a turn dies that way.

entries.name: cognee
entries.description: Memory that understands, not just stores: Cognee turns your Hermes sessions into a knowledge graph that connects the decisions you make with the reasoning and conversations that led to them, and recalls relevant context on every prompt. Works with Cognee Cloud or a self-hosted cognee server. Maintained by Cognee. Disclosure — each turn plus its tool calls and results (redacted, capped) goes to Cognee Cloud or COGNEE_BASE_URL in remote mode, or to the local cognee server and on to your configured LLM provider (OpenAI by default) in local mode; unless recall is pinned, the server picks which of your readable datasets each recall searches; turns the server could not take are queued in ~/.cognee-plugin; the store lives in ~/.cognee, outside HERMES_HOME, shared across profiles and with Cognee's other plugins. Local mode installs cognee==1.6.6 and its dependencies (about 1 GB from PyPI) into ~/.cognee-plugin/hermes/runtime only when you choose it (`hermes memory setup cognee` or `hermes cognee install-runtime`; never at session start), runs a local cognee server from it (uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8011) and a session-close watcher in the background; `install-runtime` asks before stopping a local server the plugin started; cognee sends anonymous telemetry unless TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. The system prompt tells the agent to prefer Cognee memory over MEMORY.md/USER.md (COGNEE_MEMORY_STEER=false turns it off), and an answer that used recalled memory may end with a one-line Cognee credit drawn with the Cognee logo by a transform_llm_output hook (COGNEE_PLUGIN_CITE_MEMORY=off turns it off); the same hook appends a one-time note about recall modes to the first reply when a non-default dataset is pinned by default.

entries.name: coldstart
entries.description: Evidence-gated answering with a provenance hierarchy, for any local AI deployment. Material you feed it (internal: transcripts, contracts, code, spreadsheets, PDFs, emails) is retrieved first and cited first; public reference material is used only when internal material does not cover the question, and every answer that leans on it is labelled as public; when nothing covers the question the reply is refused instead of invented. Every reply is then checked mechanically against the passages that turn actually retrieved -- quoted spans must be verbatim, and figures, dates, URLs and identifiers must appear in a retrieved passage (line and passage references are masked so citations are not mistaken for claims); prose paraphrase is reported but never blocked. No model is asked to grade its own answer. The clearance rule covers every path that touches private material: the model is taken from the turn the host actually runs (`pre_llm_call` reports it, recorded per session), so a session switched with `/model` or a turn that lands on a cloud fallback counts as remote; when it is not local, internal passages are withheld, `corpus_ask` requires both its endpoint and the turn to be local and otherwise answers from public material only, and `corpus_audit` / `/trust` refuse rather than sample internal passages into it. `/trust` runs a battery against the configured deployment and scores it: invented quote and invented figure must be caught, verbatim quote and paraphrase must pass, and the pipeline must abstain on questions the corpus cannot answer. Ships an agent half (2 hooks, 3 tools, 1 command, 1 skill) and a Desktop half (evidence pane, status-bar chip, mode switch, audit button) over the plugin's own `/api/plugins/` backend. Stdlib only -- no embeddings, no third-party dependency, no model call for retrieval. Disclosure -- reads only the directories configured in `corpus_roots` / `public_roots` plus its own index under `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/coldstart/`; makes model calls through Hermes's configured model or the OpenAI-compatible `endpoint` the user sets; shells out to `pdftotext` and `tesseract` only when present and only for the user's own files; optional `COA_API_KEY` is read through Hermes's secret scope, never from a file; no telemetry, no self-update. Enabling the plugin holds the reply until the gate has run, so token-by-token streaming is off while it is enabled. Disclosure — reads only the directories configured in `corpus_roots` / `public_roots` plus its own index under `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/coldstart/`, which stores copies of the indexed passages; makes model calls through Hermes's configured model or the OpenAI-compatible `endpoint` the user sets; judges a model local from its URL host (loopback, RFC1918, Tailscale `100.64.0.0/10`, `.local`/`.lan`/`.internal`/`.home` names), any configured fallback, and the model name the turn reports compared by its last path segment, so a local proxy that forwards to a cloud API, or a `/model` switch to a cloud model with the same name, counts as local; shells out to `pdftotext` and `tesseract` only when present and only for the user's own files, with a minimal environment; optional `COA_API_KEY` is read through Hermes's secret scope, never from a file; the Desktop pane's mode switch writes `plugins.entries.coldstart.settings.strictness`; no telemetry, no self-update. Enabling the plugin holds the reply until the gate has run, so token-by-token streaming is off while it is enabled, even with the gate set to `off`.

entries.name: comemo
entries.description: Composite memory meta-provider for Hermes Agent. Comemo multiplexes Honcho, Mem0, and Supermemory simultaneously. Write fan-out goes to all configured providers in parallel, reads merge and deduplicate results across them. Failed writes are queued in a local SQLite retry store and replayed at the next session start. Maintained by Anda Usman. Disclosure — conversation turns and recall queries are sent to every enabled backend (Honcho at api.honcho.dev or your configured base_url, Mem0 at api.mem0.ai or MEM0_BASE_URL, Supermemory at api.supermemory.ai) under that backend's own API key, and writes that fail are kept in a local SQLite retry queue under HERMES_HOME/comemo/ and replayed at the next session start.

entries.name: comfy-recipe
entries.description: Visible ComfyUI sessions, consent-based setup, workflow tools and media preparation inside Hermes. Disclosure — on first use it can install its own ComfyUI in a folder you choose: it downloads uv 0.13.7 (checksum-verified) from GitHub, Python 3.13, the latest ComfyUI release, PyTorch and ComfyUI-Manager (unpinned upstream versions), then starts ComfyUI on 127.0.0.1 with ComfyUI-Manager enabled, plus background installer, download and watchdog processes that can outlive the chat. Model downloads fetch public https URLs that workflows declare or that the agent supplies (bundled ones use Hugging Face; private and internal addresses are refused, and localhost mirrors need the allow_local_mirrors setting), and node packs install third-party code through ComfyUI-Manager with your permissions. Discovery reads process command lines and ComfyUI Desktop / StabilityMatrix settings. Prompts, workflows and uploaded files go to the selected ComfyUI. Media tools run ffmpeg. Session titles are written through the public SessionDB. Cloud Recipe workflows spend Comfy account credits when run in your signed-in ComfyUI window; the plugin's instructions tell the agent to ask first, but Hermes itself does not prompt before a paid run. No self-updater.

known_issues: Windows 11 verified; macOS and Linux paths are implemented but not live-verified.
Workflow models, suitable hardware and optional custom nodes are separate requirements; cloud runs need ComfyUI sign-in, credits and consent.

entries.name: comfyrizz
entries.description: Chat-as-frontend for the Comfyrizz film pipeline: brief, plan, revise, explicit accept, generate, CPU assemble, export, and retake. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, stdio mcp.json, comfyrizz-film skill) with the MCP server in-tree. Disclosure — the stdio server launches local Node that talks only to a loopback Comfyrizz engine URL (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL); optional Streamable HTTP binds 127.0.0.1 only when deliberately enabled and has no authentication, so any local process or web page in your browser can call its tools while it runs. Paid generation (Google Colab, Comfy API, or ComfyUI) is dispatched by the agent with an approval id it reads from the engine's spend card; the bundled skill tells the model to get your explicit yes first, but Hermes itself does not prompt before paid generation or retakes. Env vars are forwarded as ${VAR} from the user environment (COMFYRIZZ_ENGINE_URL, COMFYRIZZ_MCP_HTTP, COMFYRIZZ_TOKEN, and optional provider keys); no credentials are stored in the package. No self-updater.

entries.name: command-ledger

entries.name: command-reviewer
entries.description: Reviews every `terminal` and `execute_code` call before execution: deterministic hard rules block credential reads and destructive patterns, script contents are ingested and judged (not just filenames), an LLM reviewer with an injection-resistant prompt issues SAFE/SUSPICIOUS/MALICIOUS verdicts, and operator approve/deny decisions are recorded content-hash-bound so an unchanged script is never re-asked. Disclosure - the reviewer reads the contents of script files the command names (inside the Docker sandbox via `docker exec` when available, otherwise from the host path), with the command text, and sends both to your configured auxiliary LLM; keeps an audit log, a precedent database of your approval decisions, and verdict caches keyed by script content hash and by command+content combination — the reviewer's own SAFE and MALICIOUS verdicts are reused for identical commands and scripts with no LLM call, while SUSPICIOUS is never cached and always reaches the approval prompt — all under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/command-reviewer/; reads config.yaml (read-only) to see whether you answered \"Always\" to one of its prompts, and — for terminal commands only — whether your own approvals.deny globs will refuse it before spending LLM tokens on it; can only block or escalate to the approval prompt, never auto-approves; ships in shadow mode (log only) until you set `mode: enforce`.

entries.name: commonly-hermes-plugin
entries.description: Gives Hermes tools to read a Commonly pod and post to it, through the @commonlyai/mcp server (stdio), plus a skill for working in a pod. The tools work while Hermes is running. Nothing wakes Hermes when someone @mentions it in the pod. Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — On first use, npx downloads @commonlyai/mcp from npm and runs it locally; that package is published from Team-Commonly/commonly but is not covered by the pinned sha. Every tool call goes to https://api.commonly.me with the Commonly agent token kept in the profile .env as COMMONLY_AGENT_TOKEN. The server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before any tool that posts or comments, deletes the agent's own messages, uploads a local file, changes tasks or memory, messages other agents, joins or creates a pod, or runs commonly_catch_up (which marks an unread backlog as skipped on the server); read-only tools run without a prompt. File uploads are limited to the folder the server starts in or folders listed in COMMONLY_ATTACH_ROOTS, and hidden and key files are refused.

entries.name: commonplace
entries.description: Commonplace — local-first curated memory in plain Markdown files on your own machine. Standing rules kept verbatim, a curated store with lexical recall, a handover card for fresh sessions, and a fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint (API v2) that archives the transcript before Hermes may compress it — and blocks compression when the archive cannot be written. No cloud, no API keys, no third-party dependencies. Maintained by Chris Newton. Disclosure — stores everything as plain, unencrypted Markdown under the active Hermes home's `commonplace/` directory, including a verbatim journal of every user/assistant turn and full-transcript archives written before each compression; none of it is pruned automatically. No network calls, credentials or third-party dependencies.

entries.name: commons
entries.description: One live skill library for every profile on one machine. `hermes commons setup` scans every profile, reports identical, contained and conflicting copies of each skill, proposes a merge plan and changes nothing until you apply it; apply backs up every profile, moves old copies into a backup (never deletes), points each profile's skills.create_dir at the shared folder and verifies every skill still resolves. Each skill create, edit or patch made through Hermes' skill tool is committed to git in the shared folder, labelled with profile and session. Optional consistency settings (`hermes commons config`): `lock shared` points every profile's skills/.locks at one folder so Hermes' own per-skill lock serializes writes across profiles (the default for a new setup; existing installs keep each profile's own lock), and `guard warn|strict` refuses or logs a write based on an old read (off by default; its pre_tool_call/post_tool_call hooks are registered only when it is on). Commands: `hermes commons setup|config|status|check|merge|promote|demote|log|undo|restore` and a read-only `/commons status|check`. Disclosure: reads every profile's config.yaml, skills folders, bundled manifest, hub lock and cron jobs.json. After confirmation it writes the shared skills folder, runs local `git` there (hooks disabled, no prompts, 30 s timeout), sets skills.create_dir and adds commons to plugins.enabled through `hermes config set`, moves replaced skill folders into <hermes home>/commons/backups (these hold copies of config.yaml, kept outside git and outside every skills folder), and rewrites old skill paths in cron prompts only where the new file exists. Optional hourly script-only cron job, created only with `setup --apply --schedule`. No network calls, no credentials stored.

entries.name: completion-proof
entries.description: Revision-bound receipts for operator-configured checks; changed source, tests or artifacts make earlier passes stale. Disclosure — proof_verify, `/proof verify` and `hermes completion-proof verify` run the check commands the user configures (argv, no shell) in the configured workspace with the user's OS privileges, unsandboxed, with a minimal environment (no credentials); the model can start these runs by check id without an approval prompt but cannot add or change commands; `hermes completion-proof init` writes a starter test command (pytest, npm test or unittest) into the plugin's settings for review; receipts, redacted output excerpts and hashes of tool commands/results are stored in the plugin's own database; once per coding turn the pre_verify hook may ask the model to run the checks; no network or telemetry.
known_issues: Native Windows and macOS are untested; Linux validation was performed under WSL2.
Configured checks run with the user's OS privileges and are not sandboxed.
The pre_verify reminder is bounded, not a fail-closed completion gate.
Receipts are local records, not cryptographic attestations.

entries.name: conductor
entries.description: Hermes leads coding agents on your machines: any terminal coding agent, T3 Code threads, and Orca terminals. It starts a run, waits with no model, and puts one message into the chat that asked when the run finishes, errors, stalls, or needs an approval; T3 and Orca runs can be steered and stopped. It can run 10+ agents at once, one ping each. Two skills: brief researches, asks one round of questions and writes the brief; lead runs the work and checks each report. Disclosure — every start and steer of a coding agent goes through Hermes's approval prompt; it runs only the built-in agents on this machine unless the owner lists extra commands and SSH hosts in plugins.entries.conductor.settings (both empty by default); runs the agent, git status, and ssh and tmux on listed hosts (argv only, no shell strings from user text, never an approval-bypass flag); the agents edit files and run commands with your user rights under their own approval settings; children get a minimal environment plus only the keys that agent needs; keeps one wait thread per run plus a detached agent process or tmux window; writes run records to its plugin data folder and event files, exit codes and logs under ~/.conductor on the machine running the agent; reads and stores no credentials; no telemetry. Finish messages on a messaging gateway need plugins.entries.conductor.allow_gateway_injection: true. In drive mode, which only the user can turn on, it asks Hermes to send up to 5 follow-ups per run on its own.

entries.name: confidential-mode
entries.description: Hermes Confidential Mode locks a Hermes profile to one tier: attested (a Tinfoil enclave, or NEAR AI Cloud's gateway and models, verified and pinned to a build you approve) or on-host-only (loopback and hosts you list). While locked, the plugin refuses off-tier main model calls before they are sent; refuses to lock while a side call, fallback, memory, MCP URL or delegation route would leave the tier; on the attested tier encrypts request bodies to the verified enclave or model key and pins every inference connection to the TLS key of the attestation the plugin accepted (the attestation fetch itself is not pinned, by design), with headers, sizes and NEAR images still visible to the vendor; and asks you the first time each tool it does not class as on-host (by where the tool's data goes) runs in each conversation during a lock, blocking the call when nobody can answer. The plugin logs each model call's host and size, never its text, and renders a receipt whose attached enclave evidence replays offline; the rest of the receipt is the plugin's own record. The attested tier needs TINFOIL_API_KEY or NEAR_AI_API_KEY. Shell and code execution are not inspected for network access, and a side call that strays mid-turn is recorded, not stopped. Disclosure — the plugin contacts the vendor (atc.tinfoil.sh, the Tinfoil router and the *.tinfoil.sh collateral proxies, or cloud-api.near.ai), Intel Trust Authority (portal and portal.eu), Sigstore's TUF CDN, and GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com, api.github.com) for NEAR compose files, also in the background after a verification stages a NEAR entry; the plugin sends no telemetry. The plugin writes under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/ (including the ledger, evidence blobs, pins.yaml, allowlist.yaml, state and SDK caches), Hermes' tool-discovery cache on a terminal lock, and, on a revoke only, config.yaml, removing its own plugin_rule:confidential-mode:tool entries from command_allowlist and no other entry, through Hermes' save_config, which also normalises legacy model and max_turns keys as any Hermes config save does; the plugin reads config.yaml and script files a locked tool call runs. The plugin reads TINFOIL_API_KEY and NEAR_AI_API_KEY through Hermes' secret scope, checks only whether OPENROUTER_API_KEY and NOUS_API_KEY are set (to report Hermes' side-call fall-through), reads TERMINAL_ENV, TERMINAL_CWD, HERMES_HOME, CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_PROGRESS and CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_NO_FETCH, sets XDG_CONFIDENTIAL_MODE_TOOL_PROCESS, stores no credential and runs no shell command or subprocess. The plugin starts daemon threads of five kinds: an attestation, a pins.yaml match record, a NEAR compose-file fetch, the own-host-name DNS lookup, and, while locked, one long-running re-verification thread per attested provider. During each Tinfoil attestation and each hermes confidential replay, the plugin wraps the Tinfoil SDK's fetch functions and requests.Session.request process-wide, inert for every other thread, and puts the original functions back afterwards; before its first verification it also re-points the Tinfoil SDK's cache-directory constants and sigstore-python's TUF directory function at its plugin-data directory for the rest of the process. The plugin adds a locked-mode note to each locked turn's context and may append one notice line to a reply. hermes plugins validate counts 31 private core import sites, all reads (docs/DISCLOSURE.md).
known_issues: Auxiliary calls (compression, titles, vision and other side jobs) bypass the llm_execution middleware, so the plugin refuses to lock while one is routed off-tier and records a breach if one strays; it cannot stop the call.
Hermes' CLI approve directive grants on any answer except 'deny'; the plugin's tool_execution middleware runs a tool only on an exact once, session or always.

terminal, execute_code, process_manage and MCP servers launched as a command run on this host while locked and can reach the network; the plugin scans shell and code text only for its own commands, not for network access.
Locked mode requires Hermes' local terminal backend: the lock is refused on any other backend (Docker included) and while Hermes holds a cached terminal environment on one.
Locked mode does not apply in safe-worker mode, where Hermes loads no plugins.
Every plugin in the same process shares the trust boundary; under plugins.isolation: host the attested provider is invisible and the lock is refused.
Tinfoil attests its router, not the model backend behind it, and its report carries no client nonce; the plugin's own timestamps are the host clock.
The plugin reads keys only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret, so a key held only in Hermes' credential pool (hermes auth) reads as not set and the lock refuses until the variable is set.
AMD and Intel routers have different enclave fingerprints, so a restart can ask for a new pin; set confidential.tinfoil.enclave to one router to stop this.
An 'always' tool grant lives in Hermes' command_allowlist and outlives the lock until /confidential revoke <tool>.
After a runtime switch to a hosted provider, Hermes' start-up model-list request goes out with your API key (no conversation text) before any plugin seam runs; the plugin then refuses the turn.
If Hermes runs on someone else's machine, that operator sees every prompt; locked mode protects the road out of the Hermes process, not the process.

hermes confidential replay uses the evidence's own trust root and capture time unless you pass --trusted-root and --as-of, identifies the repository by name only unless you pass --expected-repo-id and --expected-owner-id, and the first pin is trust on first use.
There is no mixed 'attested or on-host' tier yet, so side jobs cannot run on an on-host model while the main model is attested.

The attested tier admits only models served inside Tinfoil or NEAR enclaves (open-weight families such as Qwen, DeepSeek, Llama and gpt-oss); no Claude or GPT model is in tier, and because fallbacks are refused while locked, a vendor outage ends the turn.

While locked, tool calls not classed as on-host are blocked rather than asked under yolo, approvals.mode off, cron, one-shot (-q, -z) and unattended runs, since nobody can answer; 46 of Hermes' 73 built-in tools ask (docs/TOOL_CLASSES.md), the kanban writes and text_to_speech among them.

NEAR AI Cloud: streaming is refused; images reach NEAR's gateway in plaintext unless confidential.near.image_parts: refuse; the gateway reads model id, parameters, headers, sizes and timing, can read a reply by swapping the client key header (caught only afterwards), and instances share one key (docs/LIMITATIONS.md section 14).

An agent with terminal access on the same host can reach the approval prompt for a pin or a locked-allowlist tool by some routes; the ledger records every approval with its surface (docs/LIMITATIONS.md section 15).

entries.name: constraint-vault
entries.description: Pins the user exact constraints (numbers, addresses, hard rules) as structured local data and re-injects them verbatim into the model context on every turn and immediately after every context compaction, with a SHA-256 hash-logged injection record, because memory providers and compression silently paraphrase or drop exact values. Not a memory provider and not a compressor: a guard layer above both. Disclosure — local code only, no network or processes; stores constraints in constraint-vault.json in the Hermes home and appends a hash record to constraint-vault-injections.jsonl on every turn; the model can pin or drop constraints through its own tools without asking, and pinned text is injected into the model context on every turn of every session until dropped.

entries.name: construct
entries.description: Persistent, editable objects for Hermes, not one-off images or meshes. Hermes researches a thing; Construct keeps its parts, sizes and sources, checks it, and lets you change, combine and reuse the same object across worlds, film and print. Disclosure — runs Construct's bundled Python (source, no binaries) in local subprocesses with a minimal allowlisted environment (no provider keys); optionally runs local programs the user already has (a Chromium-family browser headless over a local debugging port for review stills, ffmpeg, FreeCAD, Blender, and NetLogo/Java), each found via the plugin's settings, `CONSTRUCT_*` variables or PATH, never from tool arguments and never downloaded; NetLogo runs with agent-written setup/go code or a model outside the installed Models Library always go through Hermes' approval prompt and are refused in scheduled runs; other program runs ask first, once for each program, while the "Ask before running programs" setting is on (on by default since 1.3.2; scheduled runs are then refused); reads model and scene files at paths the agent or user gives it, and writes only in its data folder and the user-chosen projects folder; long work runs as local background jobs; in Desktop, the Construct pages run the plugin's own `/construct` commands in a "Construct page" session it creates per profile; one network call only, downloading a gallery construct (its scene JSON, at most 8 MiB a file) from Construct's own GitHub repository at this version's tag, after the user approves it in Hermes' prompt and never in scheduled runs (curl, with a minimal environment and no keys, only when Python has no certificates); no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: contagion
entries.description: Taint-aware execution. Once a session reads untrusted content, its commands lose network, secrets and out-of-project writes at the OS layer. Disclosure — Contagion replaces the local terminal backend (`terminal.backend: contagion`): until a session is marked tainted its commands and file tools run on the host like the local backend, and core's local-only locked-skill terminal guard does not run for it. Taint detection is pattern-based on tool names and terminal/code text and is kept in memory only, so a restart or `/contagion clear` lifts it for every session; while tainted, jailed commands can still read files outside your home directory and write inside the project folder, and egress tools are gated only by an approval prompt. The URL, query or first 120 characters of each command that caused taint are logged to the plugin's data folder.

entries.name: contract-necromancer
entries.description: Hermes's done doesn't count until your tests pass. Type /necro freeze in your project: it finds your tests and the command that runs them, writes necro.toml, locks the test files and the settings that choose what runs by hash, and runs them once to say where they stand. When Hermes says it is finished, the plugin runs them itself at the verify step and sends Hermes back with the failing test named; the final reply says when Hermes was sent back and ends with a receipt anyone can re-check, also in a fresh clone (/necro verify: CONFIRMED, MISMATCH or SUPERSEDED). Edits to locked tests are blocked, and any change that gets through fails the check. Only a person can freeze: /necro is a slash command the agent cannot type, and from its shell freezing refuses. A prompt or skill can only ask the model to test its work; these hooks run whether it asks or not. Disclosure — runs the test commands in the project's frozen necro.toml (split into words, no shell; a command the person types after /necro freeze that uses shell syntax such as && or | is stored and run as sh -c) in the project folder with the user's permissions, unsandboxed, with a small environment (no API keys unless a contract names them), at /necro freeze, from pre_verify, from the final-reply hook when project files changed or the reply claims done, from the necro_check tool (the model can call it but cannot change the commands) and from /necro check; verify re-runs them only for a lock the person approved for that folder, or with --run; with no necro.toml, /necro freeze reads file names and test settings (package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, Cargo.toml) to pick the command, and may run that command's Python with -c "import pytest" in an empty folder (a project interpreter such as .venv/bin/python only when the person typed it); contracts run with the PATH of the Hermes process that runs the agent, minus Hermes's own runtime; reads project files to hash them but never opens credential files such as .env (their pins hold only presence, size and file times); never opens or follows a link (its pin is the link's own text); runs git ls-files with fsmonitor and hooks off and the same small environment; writes .necro/ and necro.toml in the project, and approval records plus the key that seals them (HMAC) under the plugin's data directory; adds NECRO_AGENT_SESSION to the environment of commands the agent runs; runs ps when someone runs freeze, approve or unfreeze from a shell; no network, no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes.
entries.title: Done only when your tests pass
known_issues: Tested end to end on macOS with Hermes 0.23.1 and 0.22.7 (a scripted stand-in model drives the real agent loop, and a recorded run used a local qwen3 4B model); unit tests run in CI on Ubuntu and macOS; Windows is untested.
The verify gate is bounded by agent.max_verify_nudges (3 by default); after that the reply goes out stamped Not done.

Guard rails, not a sandbox: the guard stops the agent's ordinary routes early and the hashes are the backstop (a changed frozen file fails its test, a removed lock fails closed); a same-user process that sets out to evade both can still change files and approvals.

In a very large mixed-language repo, zero-config freeze locks every test-looking file under the listed sources, including tests the chosen runner never runs; list narrower sources in necro.toml to lock less.
Freeze, approve and unfreeze are done with /necro in the Hermes chat; from a shell they refuse (Hermes marks every hermes process as an agent harness) and say what to type instead.

A prompt or skill can only ask the model to test its work; these hooks run whether it asks or not. Disclosure — runs the test commands in the project's frozen necro.toml (split into words, no shell; a command the person types after /necro freeze that uses shell syntax such as && or | is stored and run as sh -c) in the project folder with the user's permissions, unsandboxed, with a small environment (no API keys unless a contract names them), at /necro freeze, from pre_verify, from the final-reply hook when project files changed or the reply claims done, from the necro_check tool (the model can call it but cannot change the commands) and from /necro check; verify re-runs them only for a lock the person approved for that folder, or with --run; with no necro.toml, /necro freeze reads file names and test settings (package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, Cargo.toml) to pick the command, and may run that command's Python with -c "import pytest" in an empty folder (a project interpreter such as .venv/bin/python only when the person typed it); contracts run with the PATH of the Hermes process that runs the agent, minus Hermes's own runtime; reads project files to hash them but never opens credential files such as .env (their pins hold only presence, size and file times); never opens or follows a link (its pin is the link's own text); runs git ls-files with fsmonitor and hooks off and the same small environment; writes .necro/ and necro.toml in the project, and approval records plus the key that seals them (HMAC) under the plugin's data directory; adds NECRO_AGENT_SESSION to the environment of commands the agent runs; runs ps when someone runs freeze, approve or unfreeze from a shell; no network, no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes. This plugin registers tool(s): necro_status, necro_check; hook(s): pre_verify, transform_llm_output, pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7. Known issues: Tested end to end on macOS with Hermes 0.23.1 and 0.22.7 (a scripted stand-in model drives the real agent loop, and a recorded run used a local qwen3 4B model); unit tests run in CI on Ubuntu and macOS; Windows is untested.; The verify gate is bounded by agent.max_verify_nudges (3 by default); after that the reply goes out stamped Not done.; Guard rails, not a sandbox: the guard stops the agent's ordinary routes early and the hashes are the backstop (a changed frozen file fails its test, a removed lock fails closed); a same-user process that sets out to evade both can still change files and approvals.; In a very large mixed-language repo, zero-config freeze locks every test-looking file under the listed sources, including tests the chosen runner never runs; list narrower sources in necro.toml to lock less.; Freeze, approve and unfreeze are done with /necro in the Hermes chat; from a shell they refuse (Hermes marks every hermes process as an agent harness) and say what to type instead..

entries.name: contractguard
entries.description: Hermes-native API contract assurance: validates proposed requests before they are sent, verifies live responses even when the status code is 200, compares candidate contracts against a human-approved baseline, and keeps redacted evidence receipts. Disclosure — makes HTTP requests only to a loopback address (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) the user registered explicitly, and only with GET or HEAD; write methods are validated offline and never dispatched. Reads the OpenAPI document at the exact path named in a tool call, and writes only to the Hermes plugin database (service registrations, immutable contract baselines, redacted evidence receipts). No telemetry, no third-party calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials; secret-bearing headers are rejected from tool arguments. Baseline promotion requires human approval and fails closed when approval is unavailable.
known_issues: Live verification targets loopback addresses only; remote targets are refused.
Live requests are limited to GET and HEAD; write methods are preflight-only.
Compatibility classification covers a bounded ruleset; complex schema composition is reported as unclassified rather than guessed.

entries.name: conxt
entries.description: Conxt governed memory provider — recall before each turn (personal, plus a team's approved memories), conversation capture in batches, and tools to search, remember, and propose team memories that a person approves in Conxt before anyone recalls them. Disclosure — Each turn's message (first 500 characters) and the conversation's user and assistant messages are sent to the Conxt API at mcp.conxt.dev (or an https CONXT_BASE_URL you set) with your CONXT_API_KEY; tool results are not sent, but text the assistant repeats is. Every entry Hermes's built-in memory tool adds is also copied to your Conxt memory, and conxt_remember / conxt_propose send the memory text they are given. No telemetry, no shell commands, and nothing is written automatically from cron or subagent runs. Requires a Conxt plan that includes API keys.

entries.name: cooldown
entries.description: Checks every package Hermes is about to install with pip, uv, poetry, pipx, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun or npx. Blocks versions OSV lists as malicious, and holds the install in Hermes's own approval prompt when a release is younger than 3 days (the rule Hermes uses for its own dependencies), the package is brand new, or the name is not on the registry. Disclosure — for each package named in an install command the agent runs in the terminal, it sends the package name and version (never your code, files or prompts) to api.deps.dev, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and api.osv.dev (keyless, no account, no telemetry); it keeps the last 50 checked install commands (first 300 characters each, as typed) and their verdicts in its own plugin state; a lookup can add up to about 20 seconds before an install command runs; it never runs the install itself and only ever blocks or asks through Hermes' approval prompt.

entries.name: coolifybruecke
entries.description: See what needs you across your Coolify instance, deploy with your approval, and let Hermes explain failed deploys. Disclosure — Talks only to your Coolify instance with the tokens you give it, Coolify's public release feed (cdn.coollabs.io) and, for "branch ahead", your apps' git hosts (an optional git token is sent only to the host you name, or GitHub). entries.name: corkboard
entries.description: One shared board, across every profile, of things only you can do. Agents pin a task, a yes/no question, a choice of up to four (their recommendation starred) or a text question instead of burying it in chat; you answer from a Desktop side pane, the full Corkboard page, `hermes corkboard` or `/corkboard`. Blocked kanban cards are pinned automatically and your answer goes back to the card as an "Owner decision" comment, which resumes the worker. Pins can clear themselves when a check passes (nameservers changed, a kanban card unblocked). Text pins never ask for secrets; credential needs are always tasks. Disclosure — keeps one SQLite board shared by all profiles at ~/.hermes/plugin-data/corkboard/data.db, so every profile with the plugin enabled (and any authorized gateway user via `/corkboard`) can read, answer, complete or dismiss every profile's pins and answers; runs `dig +short NS` for DNS checks and `hermes kanban show/list/comment` to read cards and post owner answers (an agent chooses which card a pin's answer is posted to); owner-added `--check-command` checks run a shell command (5s timeout) on `hermes corkboard check` without an approval prompt (the agent tool cannot create them); no network calls of its own beyond DNS lookups, no background process, no cron, no telemetry.

entries.name: corpus-open
entries.description: For pro se and self-represented litigants: people handling their own lawsuit or court case without a lawyer. Legal citation checking for AI drafts. Under every reply, a citation guard lists each case, statute and code cite with what CourtListener (case law), Corpus (statutes from all 50 states) and the person's own case file hold at it, and flags a fake (hallucinated) citation before it reaches a court filing; a cite that cannot exist is caught with no lookup at all. A quote guard refuses a write that misquotes a filed document or cites the wrong page. Each session opens with the case's court deadlines, and an intake skill interviews the person one plain question at a time. Twelve tools keep a local litigation case folder (labeled facts with sources, evidence, deadlines, brief check, a packet for an attorney deciding whether to take the case, court rules, hash verification), /matter shows it, and Hermes Desktop gets a Case pane. Disclosure — cite checks are on by default for every case and send bare citations (never case text) to CourtListener (only once a key is set) and corpuslaw.us; each request is logged in the case folder, and checks can be turned off per case or everywhere (citation_guard local). Case files stay on the computer. The CourtListener key is read through Hermes's secret settings, falling back to the key the kit's own matter.py saves in ~/.config/matter-kit. On a session's first turn it adds the case's deadlines to the agent's context, and it asks for Hermes approval before shell or file commands that look like they change a registered case document. /matter watch on writes a deadline-check script into Hermes's scripts folder and prints a cron command for you to run; it schedules nothing itself. PDFs are read with the local pdftotext program when installed. Not a lawyer and not legal advice.
entries.title: Corpus Open
known_issues: Looking up case citations needs a free CourtListener key. Statute and code citations need none, up to Corpus's 250 lookups a month from one network; a free Corpus key raises that.
It checks that a source exists at a citation, not that the source says what a draft claims. It is not legal advice.

entries.name: corsair
entries.description: Work in Corsair from Hermes: track issues in Corsair's PM, keep people, companies and deals in its CRM, use the apps you've connected to Corsair (Gmail, Slack, Linear, GitHub and others), search across them, hand them files, and set up automations that run on app events or a schedule. Corsair's hosted MCP server plus seven skills. Disclosure — connects to Corsair's hosted MCP server at mcp.corsair.dev (by Corsair / corsairdev) and sends it the requests the agent makes; Corsair acts in the apps you connected, with the access you gave each one. Sign-in is Hermes-managed OAuth through a native `mcp_servers.corsair` entry with `auth: oauth`; the package carries no credentials. Some apps run on Corsair's own account and bill each call to your Corsair credits. upload_file, and save_skill with a folder, return a curl command that uploads a local file or skills folder you asked to upload. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so every tool not annotated read-only goes through Hermes's approval prompt.

entries.name: cortive
entries.description: Adds Cortive, a private knowledge base for your Mac, to the agent's memory, alongside Hermes's built-in memory: automatic recall of the pages, PDFs, screenshots, documents and notes you saved, plus cortive_search, cortive_get and cortive_collections tools. Finds by meaning while the Cortive app is running, by words otherwise. Read-only and local. Disclosure — reads the local Cortive library file (~/Library/Application Support/cortive-ai/cortive.db, SQLite opened read-only), which is outside the plugin's own data; connects to the Cortive app's owner-only Unix socket on the same Mac (~/Library/Application Support/Cortive/agent/search.sock) to send search text and receive capture ids and scores; writes exported screenshots and an optional config file inside its Hermes plugin-data folder. No network calls, no credentials, no background services, no telemetry. Recalled excerpts reach the model Hermes uses, like any context; passwords and keys are hidden first, and the plugin is off in group chats by default. Two tool hooks enforce that: pre_tool_call refuses other tools' calls that point at Cortive's data folder, and transform_tool_result hides passwords saved in Cortive from other tools' output.
entries.title: Cortive Memory
known_issues: Needs the Cortive app (free beta, Apple silicon, macOS 14+) from https://github.com/KadenDevAi/cortive-releases; select it with `hermes config set memory.provider cortive`.
Meaning search needs Cortive 0.2.0 or later running; otherwise search and recall match words only, and automatic recall waits for messages that refer to saved material.
Voice recordings have no transcript, so the agent can find them but not read what was said.

entries.name: cost-forecast
entries.description: Quotes a task's cost before it runs and stops for your OK when it would go over budget. Before a task starts it estimates the number of model calls and tokens (P50 and P90), prices them at your model's rates, and shows a quote when the task is large or could exceed your per-task cap. While the task runs it costs every call (subagents included), re-forecasts after each call, and pauses or stops at the soft cap, hard limit or daily cap. Estimates learn from your own finished tasks. API-key users only. Disclosure — fetches public prices from https://models.dev/api.json on a short background thread, at most once a day when the fetch succeeds (it retries on later lookups after a failure); if the optional cheap-model estimate (l3_mode, off by default, needs the llm.model_override grant) is on, one extra short call per quote sends up to 1,500 characters of your message through Hermes to your own provider; stores spend, task history (message text removed, only hashed word counts kept), learned coefficients and, for up to 30 minutes, the text of a request held for your OK in a SQLite database under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/cost-forecast/; reads model.provider and agent.reasoning_effort from your config and whether the working directory is inside a git repo (a .git check, no commands); no credentials, no shell commands, no telemetry.
entries.title: Cost Forecast
known_issues: API-key billing only. Subscription logins are not priced, and local models show token counts only.
Cron, webhook and API-server runs get no quote because nobody can reply. The hard limit and daily cap still stop them.
Image generation and provider-side tool fees (such as per-search web search charges) are counted but not priced yet.
The first few quotes use defaults and are the least accurate. Calibration starts after 3 finished tasks.

entries.name: cost-sentinel
entries.description: Live cost ledger and daily budget guarddog for Hermes Agent, per profile or fleet-wide — every LLM call is priced with Hermes' own pricing engine into a per-profile SQLite ledger plus a shared fleet ledger (all profiles of the install roll into one daily number); /cost rules the budget (set, block, warn, off, scope fleet or profile, resume, reset), the cost_report tool lets the agent read it, and the hard pre_llm_call gate stops an over-budget turn with an escape-hatch message. Desktop pane shows the gate number (fleet or profile) with a spend ring, per-model and per-day breakdowns and a status-bar budget chip. Disclosure — writes a per-profile SQLite ledger and a ledger shared by every profile of the install at <default hermes root>/plugin-data/cost-sentinel/fleet.db, which also holds the daily budget settings, so /cost set, block, resume or reset in any profile changes the budget for all profiles; rows store tokens, cost, model/provider, session/turn/request ids, platform and error type plus the first 400 characters of provider error messages, never prompt, response or tool-argument text; the hard gate is off by default, is checked once before each turn (a turn already running can overshoot), and counts calls Hermes cannot price as $0; no network of its own (pricing goes through the host pricing engine), no MCP, shell, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: costguard
entries.description: A brake pedal for model spend. Meters every API call per session and per day from the provider's own usage block; dollar figures are estimates computed only for models in its price table and are never invented for unknown models. When a provider reports no usage (common with streaming OpenAI-compatible endpoints), it falls back to request-size estimates and flags those calls as estimated in every total, never pricing them. Warns the agent at a configurable ratio of any configured budget and blocks tool calls once a session or daily token/cost budget is exceeded, stopping the tool loops where runaway spend happens; with no budget configured it only meters and reports. Disclosure: observes API request/response metadata (token usage, model, session id) and tool call names in profiles where it is enabled; stores only aggregate counters locally under $HERMES_HOME/costguard/; makes no network calls; the brake cannot cancel the reply already being generated when a budget trips, it stops the tool work that reply tries next.

entries.name: costory
entries.description: FinOps harness MCP for platform teams. Bills normalized in BigQuery and allocated to teams. Build on it, or try it next to your tool. Read-only on cloud. Starter from $300/month, 30-day free trial. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) connecting Hermes to Costory's hosted MCP at https://app-api.costory.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Bundles seven FinOps skills: query, cost-change-investigation, virtual-dimensions, dashboards, reports, recipes and bigquery. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code beyond the pin; every tool call goes to app-api.costory.io after browser OAuth (enterprise SSO on Costory Team and above). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Costory has write-capable tools that create or change Costory objects only (alerts, reports, dashboards, events, allocation rules, archives), never cloud resources; plugin.json sets extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.servers.costory.trust: untrusted so Hermes asks before writes and refuses them in unattended runs. entries.name: counterparty
entries.description: Screens the companies your agent is about to pay, email, sign with or buy from. Before any outward action (email, payment, order, transfer, signature, form submit) a pre_tool_call hook reads the vendor, email domain or URL from the call and checks it against the DoD Section 1260H list, the FCC Covered List, Section 889, the UFLPA Entity List, the BIOSECURE list and OFAC sanctions, with the ownership chain from public records, then escalates hits through Hermes's own approval prompt with the finding and its legal citation (never auto-approves; fails closed under cron). Search and page results that mention a listed vendor get a one-time note. Tools cp_screen, cp_lookup, cp_credit, cp_who_owns_address and cp_brief answer on demand; /whoowns gives a cited one-page brief. Works offline from a bundled list snapshot and says so. Disclosure — Sends the counterparty name, email/URL domain label, and (for cp_screen/cp_brief) the description and amount, or a street address and ZIP for address lookups, over HTTPS to shop.tensorust.com (Tensorust LLC, the plugin author's company) whenever a matching outward tool call (email, payment, order, signature, submit), one of its tools or /whoowns runs, plus a daily list-membership refresh; message bodies are matched locally only; optional TENSORUST_API_KEY through Hermes's secret scope; no telemetry, no shell, no file reads outside its bundled data.
entries.title: Counterparty
known_issues: The alias index covers the vendor groups the lists name and their named subsidiaries (18 groups as of the 2026-11-06 pull), not every shell company; a clear result means not on these lists under this name.
Address ownership (cp_who_owns_address, /whoowns <address>) covers a set of US counties and says when an address is outside it.

entries.name: courier-by-autolane
entries.description: Restaurant pickup delivery in Austin, Texas: the user places a pickup order, and an Autolane vehicle collects it and drives it to them for a flat fee, through Autolane's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE; the user links a mobile number with a texted code), with one ordering skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Autolane's MCP server at mcp.goautolane.com with store and drop-off addresses, the customer's name and order details, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. reserve_delivery, confirm_delivery, update_delivery and cancel_delivery book, change or cancel a real delivery and take payment; the package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Autolane's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Invite-only for now. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add courier-by-autolane --url https://mcp.goautolane.com/courier-mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: coursebook
entries.description: A native Hermes Desktop learning workspace where a lesson is governed state rather than chat: one objective at a time, typed checks, bounded grading, transactional transitions, inspectable evidence, and sourced visuals and audio, plus parent-prepared lesson packs. Disclosure — schoolwork, progress and evidence stay on this machine in profile-scoped SQLite under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/coursebook/; pack import reads a local archive the user picks and pack export writes a local file. The Workshop "Share to store" button publishes a course you wrote: after a confirmation step it uses your local git and gh CLI login to push a branch (forking DeseretSaint/hermes-classroom under your GitHub account if needed) and open a public pull request with the course content. No telemetry, no credential store, no self-update. Provider calls go through Hermes: lesson chat uses the selected chat provider, plan/lesson/Parent Studio generation uses the host plugin LLM route (optionally a configured validator model/provider) with the goal or parent brief and research excerpts, generated illustrations are sent to the host vision tool for review, and research uses the host web_search/web_extract tools. Its own direct requests are limited to downloading generated images from fal.media/fal.run and a first-use download of faster-whisper model weights from Hugging Face; pronunciation practice runs the local ffmpeg binary. It starts background job threads at load that run Desktop-queued generation jobs, injects lesson context into bound lesson chats through pre_llm_call and can block a turn when its lesson state cannot be read, and imports undocumented Hermes modules (hermes_cli.sqlite_util, tools.web_tools) that may break on a Hermes update.

entries.name: coursewright
entries.description: `/course <topic>` turns a subject into one self-contained HTML course at three depths, novice, intermediate and advanced, switched in place without a reload. It researches before it writes: it searches through whatever web backend the host has configured, reads the pages it finds, collects videos that carry captions, and lists every source, dead end and filtered result in a footer. The model never writes HTML; it fills a validated spec and a renderer draws the page. Figures are drawn from the course's own outline — layered diagrams, sequence diagrams, small charts — and every section ends with an exercise that answers back. Disclosure — needs network access: the course is written by the host model through ctx.llm, pages are read over the web with the host's own extractor, an opt-in scraper URL you configure, or the plugin's own guarded direct fetch (public addresses only), and video lookups run yt-dlp and youtube-transcript-api. /course starts the build by sending a turn to the agent, and a background build reports back into the chat when it finishes. It writes only its own plugin data directory plus an optional copy under ~/Courses, and owns no credentials of its own.

entries.name: covsift
entries.description: Exact, local analysis of code coverage reports: LCOV (c8, nyc, Jest, Vitest, cargo-llvm-cov, lcov), Cobertura XML (coverage.py, Jest/Vitest, coverlet, gcovr, PHPUnit), JaCoCo XML, Clover XML, SonarQube generic XML, coverage.py, gcovr and Coveralls JSON, and Go cover profiles, from one file or a directory of them. coverage_diff takes a unified diff (git diff) and returns the added lines no test ran, per file, with diff coverage and an optional fail_under gate; coverage_summary gives exact line, branch and Go statement coverage, the least covered files with their uncovered lines and a per-directory rollup; coverage_file lists one file's uncovered lines and partial branches; coverage_compare shows which files lost coverage between two runs. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs git or tests; the diff is passed in), no third-party dependencies, no self-update; XML entity declarations are refused. Disclosure: reads the local report and diff paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.

entries.name: cpa-status
entries.description: /cpa in chat for CLIProxyAPI (CPA) pools: account health per provider (active, limited, cooling, error, disabled), the CPA version with an update hint, and on request each account's live quota (Claude, Codex, xAI, Antigravity, Devin, Kimi, Kiro), the same usage reads as CPA's own web UI. Companion to cliproxyapi-provider and reads the same cliproxyapi config. Disclosure — only when you type /cpa, and with the management key env var you name per instance: GETs the credentials list from your configured CPA and CPA's own update check (at most once per 6 hours); for /cpa quota, POSTs CPA's api-call so CPA sends each built-in vendor's private usage request (Anthropic, ChatGPT/Codex, xAI, Google Antigravity, Codeium/Devin, Kimi) with that account's token, using the vendor clients' own User-Agent and client headers as CPA's web UI does (Antigravity and Devin are vendor POSTs, the rest GETs), then one plan request per Claude account (GET api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile) and per Antigravity account (POST loadCodeAssist on daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com), from which only the plan fields are read, and GETs CPA plugin quota for Kiro; at most 20 accounts and 4 requests per account per run, 4 requests in flight. entries.name: crash-lab
entries.description: Fault-injection and recovery testing for AI agents. Crash Lab manufactures the failure modes that break real agent workflows — a write that succeeds while the API reports a timeout, a malformed response, transient 503s — behind four registered tools (crash_start, crash_book, crash_inspect, crash_report), wrapping a deterministic, fictional booking service. An independent state oracle reads the persisted service state — verified by deterministic replay, so damaged or edited state is never certified — and returns PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED. PASS means the booking-state safety condition holds (exactly one booking, no duplicates); it does not prove the agent reasoned correctly or followed an optimal recovery procedure. Retry diagnostics (call_count, allowed_calls, reconciled, excessive_retries) are reported separately and never affect the verdict. Fully offline: the booking service is fictional — no network calls, no real bookings, payments or customer accounts; no telemetry, background services or stored credentials. Zero Python dependencies; writes JSON run files only in its own plugin-data directory. Concurrency: per-run exclusive write lock (kernel flock on POSIX; owner-release lock file elsewhere, no automatic stale-break). Integrity checking is replay-based consistency verification, not authenticated tamper-proof storage. Tested on Linux (WSL2); Windows/macOS unverified. Scenarios are fixed code constants, not a general fuzzer. Disclosure — verdicts certify simulated service state only, not the agent's reasoning; integrity checking is replay-based consistency, not tamper-proof storage; scenarios are fixed code constants, not a general fuzzer.

entries.name: crash-recovery
entries.description: Durable, hash-chained tool-call journal that blocks protected actions while a previous outcome is unknown, including after a crash or a new session. Operator reconciliation releases the recovery gate; actions are never automatically replayed. Disclosure — after any non-read-only tool call fails, errors or is interrupted, blocks every tool except the configured read-only list (default read_file, search_files) until the operator reconciles the action with the plugin's operator_cli.py; stores tool/session metadata, argument and result hashes, a local integrity checkpoint and operator evidence under the active profile's plugin-data directory and never auto-prunes; serializes protected calls per profile; no network, shell execution, credential reads or background tasks in the plugin itself; optional demos spawn and force-kill owned local workers, and the native demo opens a temporary loopback provider and starts/stops an isolated Hermes CLI/gateway.
entries.title: Crash Recovery
known_issues: V1 serializes protected calls per profile; nested protected tools and concurrent protected calls can be refused.
A rejected approval or guardrail decision can conservatively require operator reconciliation.
Local tamper detection does not protect against complete replacement of both the journal and checkpoint; retain independent checkpoints when that threat matters.

entries.name: crash-test
entries.description: A safety rating for AI agents. For one armed turn it breaks tools the way real systems break (timeouts, outages, empty or cut-off results), then rates what the agent did: retried, worked around it, told the truth, or claimed success anyway. 1-5 stars and an HTML report, comparable across models by seed. Blocked calls never run, silent faults only touch reads, and the agent gets no tools from it, so it cannot tell it is being tested. Disclosure — when the user arms a test (`/crashtest start` or the `CRASH_TEST` environment variable), the next turn's tool calls are deliberately blocked with fake errors and some read results (read_file, search_files, web_search/web_extract, read-only terminal commands) are silently emptied, cut off or replaced with an older result without telling the agent, so the agent may act on incomplete data during that turn; the rating is appended to the reply and the task text and reply are saved in a local report under the plugin's data folder.

entries.name: crashlab
entries.description: Test recovery before delivery, after commit and across restart; inspect saved records, verify the repair and keep a reusable regression. Disclosure — After a Hermes approval prompt, runs the `app.start` command declared by a case file or a model-prepared experiment as a local process outside the Hermes sandbox, and drives it with a Node/Playwright runner and a local Chromium launched with `--no-sandbox`; stores runs, experiments, exports and watch files under `~/.local/share/crashlab` (or `CRASHLAB_DATA_DIR`), shared across Hermes profiles; the opt-in `crashlab_experiment_watch` adds a `pre_verify` reminder that asks Hermes to continue after edits in a watched project; the dashboard tab can start an approved run after its own confirmation.
entries.title: CrashLab
known_issues: Reconciliation requires one selected original identity and one selected readback query value; missing or repeated selections are rejected.
Execution needs human approval for the captured plan; trusted local cases and applications remain required.
Historical bundles require their recorded evaluator; prepare new experiments explicitly after evaluator changes. VERIFIED status never transfers.
Noninteractive install can require npm ci; local application runtimes and dependencies are separate.
Restart needs an owned foreground process group and record-level observation; numeric-only HTTP counts are rejected.
Replay requires identical evaluator hashes and a direct Python launch; dependencies remain separate.
Kist and Flaskr retain model-repair records; Shiori is a supplied-diagnosis guided model patch with operator verifier runs, not autonomous discovery or adoption.
Flaskr repair covers fresh databases; existing databases need migration and legacy tokenless POSTs are unprotected.
Project freshness covers tracked and nonignored untracked files, not ignored files, dependencies or runtime configuration.
Completion reminders are opt-in, project-scoped and bounded by Hermes continuation limits; they are not an execution barrier.
The native Desktop pane is view-only; approved execution uses Hermes tools or the web dashboard. The pane is SDK-validated, not visually verified in an installed Desktop app.
External application templates require their own checkout, dependencies and case configuration.
HTTP state observers trust application responses; SQLite observers read directly but are not an operating-system isolation boundary.
Legacy mixed browser/inventory campaigns remain validation-only; inventory uses a deliberate fixture scheduling gate. Recovery campaigns execute supported local apps.
Requires Node.js 20+, playwright-core and local Chromium; uses --no-sandbox, so run only trusted fixtures in isolation.
Only the first matching request is interrupted; other fault.occurrence values are unsupported.
