entries.name: creator-studio
entries.description: Make media with Hermes from one request: researched lesson videos, two-host podcast episodes, captions for any recording, narrated step-by-step tutorials, and clips cut from a YouTube video or stream by reading its transcript. Bundles five plugins (YouTube Studio, Podcast Studio, Caption Studio, Tutorial Creator, Clip Studio) into one entry. Disclosure — Research pages are fetched through the Camoufox browser you set in the plugin settings, in a fresh anonymous profile (public addresses only). On first use it lists the voices and speech recognizers this computer has and asks you which to use; it never picks one for you. If you choose Gemini narration, each spoken line is sent to Google, either to Vertex AI (aiplatform.googleapis.com) with a Google sign-in that Hermes holds for your own OAuth client (hermes auth add creator-studio:google; the plugin never sees the token), or to generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the Gemini API key in this plugin's settings (GEMINI_API_KEY, the same variable Hermes' own Gemini provider uses), behind a spend guard (default 0.50 USD). To find speech servers it sends read-only GET requests (/v1/models, /openapi.json) to 127.0.0.1 only, on ports 2022, 5000, 5002, 7860, 8000, 8001, 8020, 8080, 8880 and 9000, plus any loopback address you set. Caption Studio runs the recognizer command you set in the plugin settings, or uploads audio to the HTTPS speech service you set (public addresses only) or to Groq (api.groq.com) with your key, only when you allow uploads; the model cannot set commands, endpoints, keys or upload consent. Programs it starts get a minimal environment (paths, locale, display/audio session and proxy settings), never your provider keys. Clip Studio runs the yt-dlp you installed (or set in the plugin settings) and makes requests to YouTube only when you give it a link: the video page and one caption track, then the audio track if you ask for speech recognition, the sections you choose to cut, and, if you ask what chat reacted to, the public chat replay of a finished stream (other people's messages and display names; kept in private plugin storage, the raw download deleted once counted, names kept only for paid messages). It never uses browser cookies or a YouTube sign-in. Recognizing a whole recording continues in a background thread inside Hermes until its pieces are done. Clips, joined videos, titles, descriptions and thumbnails are written to plugin storage. Runs FFmpeg and ffprobe, an installed speech program if you choose one (espeak-ng, flite, piper), and for screen tutorials xwininfo, xprop, xdotool, pactl and xclip; the recorder starts one detached FFmpeg worker per take, and tutorial steps click and type through Hermes computer_use, so its approvals apply. Stores projects privately in plugin storage. Nothing is published.

entries.name: creature-workshop
entries.description:
Manage your project's development lifecycle all in one place: your project.

The development lifecycle's grown more and more complex over the years. It's getting tougher and tougher to get truly polished features over the line into production. And with agentic development, the complexity is ramping more than ever.

Creature Workshop offers a one-stop shop right in your project to manage your project's entire development lifecycle, one piece at a time as it becomes relevant to you. From initial tooling setup, environment handling, and issue intake, to review, merge, testing, build, deployment, documentation, and monitoring, your project's devops should let you focus on your features instead of on the headache of pipelines or on ticking all the boxes for project readiness and change reporting. Disclosure — in a project the user lists in the approved_projects setting (empty by default; added from Settings → Plugins or the pane's Approve button, never by the agent), the workshop_* tools and the terminal pre-check run that repository's own .envrc and shell/ops scripts on the host outside the terminal sandbox, with no per-call approval and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, locale, terminal, XDG dirs plus any names in ops_env_passthrough); workshop_install can install the project's declared tools, which may use the system package manager via sudo; the pane's Explain and set-up buttons send the repository's README opening, top-level file names and matching source lines (secrets redacted) to a Hermes auxiliary model that defaults to free Nous Portal models with free OpenRouter models as fallback.

entries.name: credential-pool-switcher
entries.description: Switch between pooled provider accounts (e.g. multiple Claude logins) from chat (/switch), CLI, the agent, or a desktop status bar chip — lists every pooled account with its priority, bench state (benched / dead) and Anthropic usage, moves any account to the front of the rotation, refuses unsafe switches (dead logins, env:-fed API-key entries), verifies the new order afterwards, offers plan/dry-run previews, and guides account setup (`/switch setup`, after-install note, status bar chip with copyable `hermes auth add` commands). A pre_tool_call hook escalates every model-initiated real switch to the human-approval gate (list/plan stay direct), so a prompt-injected turn cannot silently redirect which account gets billed. Disclosure — reorders your Hermes credential pools through the pool's own move_entry (the call behind `hermes auth priority`), and Hermes asks for approval before each switch the model starts; the optional usage view calls Hermes' public agent.account_usage.fetch_account_usage(read_only=True) with each usable pooled Anthropic OAuth token, which sends it to api.anthropic.com to read that account's own usage; the plugin never reads or writes auth.json itself and never refreshes or stores tokens; its desktop chip polls `hermes credential-pool-switcher status --json` and runs `hermes credential-pool-switcher switch <label>` when you click an account.

entries.name: crew
entries.description: One /crew message becomes verified work on the kanban board. Disclosure — install.py creates four crew-* profiles cloned from your chat profile (including its .env provider keys and memories), deletes non-crew skills in them, updates crew in other profiles and on Linux starts a loopback dashboard service (127.0.0.1:8799, transcript excerpts; --publish serves it to one tailnet login), restarting it when an upgrade changes the plugin code; it never approves shell hooks itself, but on a terminal offers (y/N) to open each profile's Hermes so Hermes asks for hook consent, first revoking approvals whose hook script changed; on native Windows the service and the optional nightly cron are skipped and the dashboard is started by hand, and proofs run in Git for Windows's bash; a Crew tab in the Hermes dashboard and a native Crew page in Hermes Desktop build that board inside the Hermes backend, including its transcript excerpts, each live card's step count and last tool name, and its acknowledge, Unstuck, Retry, Proof and Stop actions, under /api/plugins/crew/ to anyone with dashboard access; a detached coordinator makes read-only model decisions and runs card proof commands unattended with a scrubbed env, flagged or changed proofs only after the owner answers /crew-proof; card reports (with longer proof-command and summary excerpts) and questions are sent to the originating chat via hermes send, each linking its ticket id to the card on the dashboard (<dashboard>/crew?card=<id>); agent-written per-role lessons are injected into later crew turns.

entries.name: crontab-ref
entries.description: @crontab: context references that explain a cron expression for the model: @crontab:"0 9 * * 1-5" (or a shortcut such as @crontab:@daily) attaches a plain-words reading ("At 09:00 on Monday through Friday."), each field on its own row, whether Hermes's /cron takes it as a cron expression (shortcuts, ? and 5#3 are not), its next five runs in Hermes's timezone setting worked out the way cron/jobs.py computes next runs, and notes on day of month OR day of week, * in the minute field, steps that do not divide the hour or day, days 29-31 and 7 as Sunday; the TUI and Desktop composer suggest examples and preview an expression as you type it. The reading comes from croniter, the library Hermes's scheduler uses. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, the system clock and Hermes's timezone setting (HERMES_TIMEZONE, else timezone from the loaded config through hermes_cli.config), using croniter (already installed with Hermes) and Python's standard library; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read, no cron job created, changed or run; the @crontab: reference and its explanation become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @crontab: reference provider.

entries.name: crowdcode
entries.description: Cloud agents with their own wallets. Create CrowdCode agents owned by this install's Base wallet (no sign-up or API key), fund them with USDC, give them tasks that buy x402/MPP services or deploy paid services of their own, list and download the files they produce, and withdraw the earnings. A pre_tool_call guard sends every money-moving call (create, fund, task budget, withdraw, transfer) to Hermes's approval prompt by default and blocks spending above a daily cap; unattended runs are denied. Disclosure — Network calls go to crowdcode.app (agent creation is paid by x402 on Base; owner requests are signed) and to a Base RPC to read the wallet's USDC balance. The wallet's private key is a declared secret kept in Hermes's credential store. Agent creation, funding, task budgets, withdrawals and transfers spend real USDC; each goes to Hermes's approval prompt by default, spending above a daily cap is blocked, and unattended runs are denied. crowdcode_download writes files only when asked, into ./crowdcode-files/<agent>/ or another folder inside the session's working directory, never overwriting; a folder outside it needs approval first, and paths refused by Hermes's file-safety policy, HERMES_HOME and autostart/service folders are never written.

entries.name: crucible
entries.description: Adversarial research and code audits. Proposer agents commit quoted claims, attackers try to break them, a blind referee checks every quote against its source and re-runs every proof of concept in a sandbox, and you get a map of what survived and what was held back. Disclosure — Crucible runs spend tokens on your configured model through parallel subagents (each run has a USD cap). Research mode fetches the web pages its agents cite directly from your machine (public addresses only), plus NCBI PubMed and OpenAlex for papers. Code mode copies the repository you name into the plugin's data folder and gives its subagents the file and terminal tools on your terminal backend. Proofs of concept are re-run only in a network-less, read-only Docker container (image python:3.12-slim by default, pulled if missing). The optional guard mode (`/crucible guard on|strict`, off by default) rewrites the agent's answers to flag unsupported claims. Run records stay local under the plugin data folder. No telemetry.
entries.title: Crucible
known_issues: A full run takes a few minutes and spends your model's tokens; each run has a USD cap.
Code mode's agents run commands through your terminal backend: audit untrusted repositories with terminal.backend set to docker.
Some providers refuse security-audit agents; set the plugin's agent_model to a model that accepts the work.

entries.name: crystallize
entries.description: Spend less on repeated work in Hermes chats and cron jobs, without making your model think less: trims repeated context and tool output in chats, and lets a cron job skip its AI run when its input has not changed, with local receipts showing what each change saved. Disclosure — reads Hermes session costs, user-message counts and final cron answers (state.db, read-only), cron outcomes and job definitions (cron/executions.db, cron/jobs.json) and your config and rate cards; looks up public model prices from the active route's /models endpoint and models.dev once a day with no credentials or chat data (off with hermes crystal prices --lookup off); the optional helper, compare and check features make paid model calls through your own Hermes route; cron tuning, promote and undo run hermes cron CLI commands that edit the chosen job, choosing a helper model or deferring tools runs hermes config set (auxiliary.crystallize_chat, tools.tool_search.defer), and generated pre-run wrappers, drafted snapshot scripts (which replay the job's recorded shell commands and URL reads) and approved snapshot scripts are written under scripts/crystallize/, scripts/crystallize-drafts/ and scripts/crystallize-native/ and run as ordinary cron scripts once attached; in CLI and TUI chats posts one short status line after each turn with ctx.post_message (never on Desktop or messaging platforms; off with /crystallize line off); stores captured tool results, cache entries and receipts in its plugin-data folder; no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update.
entries.title: Crystallize
known_issues: Live savings at unchanged reasoning are measured on Nous and OpenAI Codex, with small samples and synthetic fixtures; other providers are untested. Hand-offs cost more in live tests and are off by default.
Frozen fixture checks do not prove semantic equivalence or universal provider coverage.
Automatic nested tool execution and pre-run/no-AI replay of learned tool plans are unavailable on the audited SDK; explicit tool mode returns pending normal-host-tool plans.
Configured/declared routes have unverified authentication and availability. User rate cards and public provider quotes are estimates, not billing evidence.

Optional native Python snapshot sources require explicit source approval, and a job that delivers needs confirmation that an unchanged run sends nothing; copied code/imports run with ordinary cron permissions, and host text trimming/redaction still apply.

entries.name: ctrlall
entries.description: Drive ctrl+all on your Mac from any Hermes conversation: launch and steer multiplayer coding-agent chats on the engines you already pay for (Claude Code, Gemini, opencode), read transcripts and the team inbox, and review git status and diffs. The plugin calls the ctrl+all daemon's authenticated loopback RPC; the daemon owns every permission gate (plan / ask / auto-edit / full-auto modes, engine boundaries, project fencing). Disclosure: network calls go only to the configured daemon URL (default loopback 127.0.0.1:9931) - no third-party endpoints, telemetry or analytics; the daemon token is read through Hermes's secret scope (CTRLALL_DAEMON_TOKEN), never from ~/.ctrlall, .env files or any other credential store; ctrlall_chat_create, ctrlall_chat_send and ctrlall_chat_mode start or steer real coding-agent turns on your Mac under the daemon's permission mode; the plugin reads no files, runs no shell commands and starts no background processes; Python standard library only; no self-updater. Creating a chat in, or switching a chat to, auto-edit/full-auto requests Hermes human approval through a pre_tool_call hook before the tool runs.

entries.name: ctx_checkpoint
entries.description: Memory provider that archives the direct user/assistant transcript into a ctx knowledge store before every compaction, deterministically and with no LLM in the path, and hands the resulting block IDs to the compaction summary so the exact wording stays recoverable. Set up from the Desktop/Dashboard memory form or `hermes memory setup ctx_checkpoint` (ctx URL and API key, no YAML editing; the Desktop form and the terminal setup test the connection before saving a changed URL or key); checkpoint limits and memory switches sit under Settings → Plugins; over MCP, `hermes memory status` tests the connection and shows the last checkpoint; compaction thresholds stay Hermes' defaults, which suit 1M-token windows. Best-effort by default; with compression.checkpoint_required (the operating mode the Desktop form and the terminal setup offer) it uses the fail-closed pre-compress checkpoint contract (#94639) and blocks compaction until the checkpoint is durable. Optional memory layer (`memory: true`, off by default): recall before each turn, ctx_query/ctx_store/ctx_search/ctx_get tools, a mirror of MEMORY.md/USER.md, fact extraction from compacted turns, session digests and a bundled `ctx-memory` skill, over the same ctx server. Disclosure — the turns about to be compacted (tool results and system prompts excluded; the ctx key the server entry signs in with and credentials in known shapes are masked, while unnamed values, plain-word passwords, card numbers and IBANs pass) and, with the memory layer on, the mirrored memory entries, extracted facts and digests (all redacted the same way) are written through Hermes' MCP dispatch to the ctx server you configure in mcp_servers; setup, when you run it, writes memory.ctx_checkpoint and that mcp_servers entry to config.yaml and the API key to .env as CTX_API_KEY, and compression.checkpoint_required only when you change the operating mode (turning it on needs a passing connection test; otherwise nothing is written); the connection test is Hermes' own MCP probe of that same entry; the plugin never writes compaction thresholds, holds no credentials of its own unless you opt into transport: rest (CTX_KEY in .env; that client redacts the key from every error text it produces and follows no HTTP redirect); to mask the ctx key it reads, through Hermes' config and env lookups (.env included), the key in that mcp_servers entry's Authorization or X-Context-Key header and CTX_API_KEY, and uses them for nothing else; of the other mcp_servers entries it reads only the names and enabled flags, to refuse one whose tool names would collide with its own; it makes no other network calls and has no telemetry; it reads state.db read-only, records the outcome of the last checkpoint and the checkpoint head ID of up to 512 recent sessions in HERMES_HOME/ctx_state/checkpoint-status.state (plus a lock file) and, with the memory layer on, keeps small dedupe state files there; once a session has a checkpoint, its system prompt carries a short pointer to it (head ID, its title and the read tools' names; no transcript text), also with the memory layer off; it imports the core modules agent.memory_provider, agent.redact, agent.secret_scope, tools.registry, tools.interrupt, hermes_constants, utils, hermes_cli.config, hermes_cli.mcp_config (the private _probe_single_server behind `hermes mcp test`) and plugins.memory.config_schema (the Desktop memory form).

entries.name: ctx_handover
entries.description: Close the lid, the session goes on: ctx_handover moves a running Hermes session, with the conversation and the project folder it works in, from one machine you own to another and back. `/handover to server` sends it after work, `/handover take` brings it to the laptop, and `--continue "task"` lets the agent keep working on the server if you allow it there; without a connection, `/handover export` writes one file you carry over. The conversation is copied message by message and checked with hashes on both sides, git projects keep branches, stash and uncommitted work, nothing at the destination is overwritten, and the session on the machine you left is retired only after the other one confirms. Works without ctx. Not the core /handoff. Disclosure — talks only to the gateways you pair (HTTPS; plain HTTP only on loopback or with --allow-insecure); no third-party services, telemetry or update checks. Transcript, tool outputs and working files travel unredacted and handover files are unencrypted; workspace .env files, keys and credential folders stay unless released per path with --include-secret, and Hermes' own credentials always stay. A paired device can take this profile's sessions (pull right) or write sessions and project copies under allow_roots (push right) through Ed25519-signed routes behind the dashboard sign-in. Stores the peer's dashboard token or Basic login, which opens that peer's whole dashboard, and an identity key in the profile .env through Hermes' secret routes. Runs git without a shell and with an allowlisted environment, --version probes of developer tools, and with --continue plus allow_remote_continue one `hermes chat --resume` turn that never starts while approvals are off. One model call per handover (refine: off disables it). The complete list is in the README and docs/security.md at the pinned commit.

entries.name: ctxprune
entries.description: Shrinks tool results before the model reads them, without dropping content: runs of identical lines are counted, JSON record lists with nested values (typical MCP results) become rows on hosted models, read_file/terminal JSON wrappers are unescaped, and every structural rule is kept only if it decodes back to the exact original. patch/edit/memory/todo results are never touched. On claude-opus-* models, an llm_request middleware turns a tool result that repeats an earlier one in the same request into a reference to it. Fails open: on any error or past a 2 s budget Hermes gets the original output. Disclosure — stdlib Python only; no network calls, no shell commands, no child processes, no credentials, no telemetry; rewrites tool results before the model sees them and, on claude-opus-* models, edits repeated tool results in outgoing requests into references; writes a small state store (first-render pins so already-sent results keep their bytes and the prompt cache stays valid, plus a registry of its own outputs) under ~/.cache/ctxprune or $CTXPRUNE_STATE in a 0700 directory shared by all Hermes profiles, and reads only that store and its optional ~/.config/ctxprune/settings.json; CTXPRUNE_OFF=1 disables it.

entries.name: cua-spaces
entries.description: Cua's own plugin: runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live, as a terminal backend (`hermes config set terminal.backend cua`). On Hermes 0.22.3 and later, Bot Desktop, computer_use and the browser follow the terminal into the Space too (needs the `cua` command). Disclosure — installs the `cua` Python SDK (>=0.5.0,<0.8); every command the agent runs, every file it touches, and (on 0.22.3+) every screen, click and page the agent drives go to the Space: on this machine for a local Space, or on Cua's cloud (cua.ai) or a machine you name, using the sign-in `cua auth login` saved (the plugin never reads or stores a token, and keeps CUA_API_KEY/CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN out of the Space). Windows Spaces run Hermes's tools in Git Bash, like Hermes on a Windows PC: if the Space lacks Git for Windows or Python, the plugin installs them inside the Space (pinned official installers checked against SHA-256, `winget` fallback) and adds `C:\c`-style drive aliases there. The optional `desktop` setting installs a desktop stack (VNC, Chromium, agent-browser, cua-driver) inside a Linux Space with sudo there. Nothing is installed on this machine. With the default `space: create` it makes a fresh Space per session and deletes it when Hermes finishes (`delete_on_exit`); because that Space is a disposable sandbox, Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends. A Space you name is never deleted and keeps the prompts.

entries.name: culprit
entries.description: git bisect for your agent. Records a snapshot after every tool call that changes a file, then binary-searches those snapshots with your test command to name the exact step that broke it, with its diff, and can undo only that step while keeping every later change. Works as /culprit, as `hermes culprit`, and as tools the agent can call. Disclosure: no network and no telemetry; runs git against a private object store under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/culprit/ (the project's own .git is never read or written) and stores unencrypted copies of the working folder's files there, honouring .gitignore and always skipping .env files, keys, credential folders and dependency folders; keeps each step's tool name and the first 100 characters of its path or command with token-like values masked on a best-effort basis; during a search it runs the given test command through the system shell in temporary copies and deletes them; git and the test command get an explicit minimal environment (PATH, home, temp and locale variables, plus the names the user lists in pass_env), never the Hermes environment; revert writes only the files in the reverted step's diff and refuses when later edits conflict; model-initiated culprit_bisect and culprit_revert go to Hermes's approval prompt, which shows the exact command (masked) or the step, with a rule key derived from it, and fail closed in unattended runs; /culprit typed in the CLI or Desktop runs directly, and on messaging platforms it is read-only (steps, show, help) unless the owner sets allow_remote_commands; no background processes; nothing is pruned automatically (/culprit clear deletes a project's data).

entries.name: cursor-acp
entries.description: Use your Cursor subscription models (Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Composer 2.5, GPT-5.6, Grok) inside Hermes Agent via the Cursor CLI's ACP server (`agent acp`). Install with one command (`npx hermes-cursor-acp`) or `hermes plugins install cursor-acp`. The plugin rewrites `.cursor/cli.json` in an empty private workspace every run with a deny-all list (`Read`, `Write`, `Shell`, `WebFetch`, `Mcp`) to prevent Cursor's native CLI tools from accessing host files. It includes a custom extractor that recovers both flat `{"name", "arguments"}` and inline `<tool_call>` blocks that standard regex bridges drop, retries on concurrent `set_model` calls, and reports `usage=None` so Hermes proactive context compression functions correctly. Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Hermes tool schemas and tool results to Cursor through your locally installed, signed-in Cursor CLI (`agent acp`); Cursor's own tools are fenced by a deny-all `.cursor/cli.json` that the plugin rewrites in a private workspace under `$HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-acp-workspace` on every start (a differing existing file is backed up to `cli.json.bak`), and Hermes executes every tool call under its own approvals.

entries.name: cursor-provider
entries.description: Cursor model provider using the official proprietary Cursor SDK. Disclosure — uses Cursor's proprietary cursor-sdk (PyPI, bundled binary bridge on loopback) with the user's CURSOR_API_KEY; sends the full conversation, tool schemas/results and images (HTTPS URLs or base64) to Cursor; keeps private per-session SDK workspaces under HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-sdk. Cursor built-in tools and MCP are requested off and Hermes keeps tool execution and approvals; native custom tools are opt-in (default off) with an inert executor. Plan-only exhaustion and rejected model parameters are terminal and fail closed without fallback. The SDK passes a loopback tool-callback token on the bridge argv (not the API key) and copies the gateway environment into the bridge process.

entries.name: cursor-sdk
entries.description: Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Hermes's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Hermes support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (`npm ci` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR_API_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.
known_issues: Experimental: included subscription billing and live permission equivalence are not verified.
Node 22.13 or later and Git are required. Install the pinned npm dependencies in the plugin directory.
Text-only, buffered responses. Model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery.
SDK workspaces and conversation state remain under the installed plugin's runtime directory.
Uses 3 private Hermes helper imports, disclosed in the README and entry PR.

entries.name: cursor-subscription-directsdk
entries.description: Experimental model provider that runs Hermes turns on your Cursor plan through Cursor's official Python SDK (cursor-sdk), with Cursor Auto offered as `cursor-auto`, and Hermes tools registered as native Cursor custom tools: each tool callback parks until Hermes has executed the call under its own approvals, then the same Cursor run continues, so parallel calls arrive as one batch and tool rounds keep the model's native context and prompt cache. `hermes auth add cursor-subscription-directsdk` runs Cursor's official browser sign-in with Cursor-side persistence off and stores the minted, revocable 90-day user API key in Hermes' credential pool (CURSOR_API_KEY also works). Disclosure — sends the full conversation, Hermes' system prompt, tool schemas, tool results and user images to Cursor with your key; installs cursor-sdk 1.3.1 from PyPI (hash-pinned, about 200 MB, includes Cursor's bundled node bridge) into the plugin's own .venv and runs it as a long-lived sidecar (one per Hermes profile) that starts that bridge on loopback, with an environment rebuilt from an allowlist (PATH, HOME, locale, TLS/proxy, display variables for sign-in, its own CURSOR_SUBSCRIPTION_*), so no other Hermes keys or tokens reach Cursor's code; Cursor's built-in tools are disabled (tools=["mcp"]) and agents get no MCP servers or Cursor settings sources, and local Cursor agent state lives under $HERMES_HOME/cache/cursor-subscription-directsdk and is deleted when each conversation closes.
entries.title: Cursor Subscription (DirectSDK)
known_issues: Cursor's own agent harness prompt (about 10-15K tokens) precedes Hermes' system prompt, which is delivered in the first user message; the SDK has no system-prompt override.
Cursor reports usage per run, not per model call, so per-call usage and cost show n/a; spend appears on the Cursor dashboard under the SDK tag.
Images inside tool results reach the model as [image] text; temperature, top_p, stop and max_tokens are ignored.

entries.name: custodian
entries.description: Autonomous operations monitor for a Hermes install: scans gateway logs, cron jobs, skill journals and agent data directories, classifies findings against a 27-fingerprint registry, auto-repairs Tier 1 problems, escalates the rest, and keeps an append-only issue ledger. Ships /custodian (status, scan, issues, repair, verify, schedule, confidence, init, escalation-runner), four scan/health tools and a grid dashboard. Disclosure — reads gateway logs, cron job state and per-skill journal files under HERMES_HOME to build its findings, and writes repair actions and an issues ledger back there; it performs no network I/O and holds no credentials. Disclosure — /custodian init registers 3 recurring agent cron jobs (deep scan 4×/day, cron-health 4×/day, escalation runner every 30 min on weekdays).

entries.name: customs
entries.description: Plants fake credential files on your machine and blocks a hijacked agent the moment a tool call reaches for one, before the tool runs. It also redacts its own fake values from tool results and from the request to the model provider, reads local scripts before they run, and asks for approval when an upload follows a credential search and packaging. Disclosure — plants fake credential files (mode 600, never over an existing file, inside a Git repository only at paths Git ignores) under the home folder, including ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, when the user runs /customs plant, blend or add, and keeps its own state in its plugin data folder; it only recognizes its own bait files and fake values and does not find or protect real credentials. Its hooks read every tool call's arguments and results and every outgoing model request, block or send to Hermes approval the calls that touch bait or carry a fake value, redact fake values from tool results and model requests, and after a block require approval for network actions in that session until /customs unlock (on by default). It reads the local scripts a command is about to run (up to 8 files, 512 KB each) and, during /customs blend, folder names under the home folder, and runs git check-ignore when planting inside a Git repository. No network calls by default; with alert_target set, alerts go out through hermes send on the user's own Hermes messaging route and carry the rule, the bait file's path, the likely source and a masked preview of the call (first 200 characters).

entries.name: cut-sprite-sheet
entries.description: pixel art sprite sheet cutter. png to tileset splitter. cut pixel art into game tiles. sprite sheet from pixel png. 2d walk cycle sprite sheet. tileset cutter for pixel art. split png into sprite sheet. shore tiles tileset tool. pixel art walk cycle sheet. png sprite and shore tiles. Cuts a pixel-art png into frames. Tools: inspect_grid, slice_grid, place_kit for a 2D game. Disclosure — The png stays on this computer. Nothing is sent. No API key. No daily cap. A gateway room can call the tools. Stop them with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. One approval on one line via pre_tool_call. Choosing always covers only the same call when a person is present and the plan does not delete a file. That choice adds one plugin_rule:<tool>:<16 hex> line to command_allowlist in config.yaml. That line stays after the plugin is removed. The plugin itself refuses cron, hermes -q, webhook, msgraph_webhook, the API server, and the plugin host, even after always, so the same call still writes nothing there. A turn with no person and no gateway writes nothing, even after always. A plan that deletes a file asks on every call. An oversized line writes one list file, <stem>.paths.txt beside the png. A failed check writes nothing. Hermes yolo and approvals off skip that prompt when a person is present. cron, -q, and unattended sessions default to deny. A sprite writes <stem>.spriteframes.tres, <stem>.png.meta, <stem>.png.import, and <stem>.slice.json beside the png, and, unless emit_scene is false, <stem>_stage.gd and <stem>_stage.tscn. A tileset writes <stem>.tileset.tres, <stem>.png.meta, <stem>.png.import, <stem>.slice.json, and <stem>.<name>.asset plus <stem>.<name>.asset.meta for each tile. A tight tileset also writes <stem>.extruded.png and <stem>.extruded.png.import, and writes <stem>.extruded.png.meta in place of <stem>.png.meta. place_kit writes the sheet png, <stem>_tiles.png, those sidecars, the stage, and project.godot only when that file is missing. Those project files stay after uninstall. The always line stays in config.yaml. The skill index line stays only while the plugin is enabled. Empty, unknown, or a restrictive license is not written. Unknown text is copied and next warns. CC-BY-SA is copied and next names share-alike. No license chunk still writes and next says no rights are attached. Import once or play fails: godot --headless --editor --quit --path <project>. No solid-color box and no sound effect. Does not launch Godot or Unity. Play may write app-userdata. That folder stays. Uninstall leaves no cron job. Linux is untested. Unity editor 6000.6.6f1 on macOS kept the walk-sheet fileIDs after a reopen.

entries.name: cutout
entries.description: Cutout returns one transparent PNG. Disclosure — on first use downloads the u2netp background model (about 4.6 MB) from rembg's GitHub release, checks its sha256 and keeps it in HERMES_HOME/models/cutout; the photo is processed on your machine and never uploaded. Each write asks for approval and creates one new PNG in any folder you name without overwriting an existing file. On chat platforms that can show files the reply gains a MEDIA line for that PNG. Enabling installs rembg and onnxruntime.

entries.name: cutroom
entries.description: Local-first video editing studio: edit a talking video by deleting words from its transcript, style it for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, TikTok or YouTube (animated word captions, face-tracked or blurred reframing, punch-ins and transitions, supplied music ducked under speech, platform loudness), find clips in long recordings, preview with automated quality checks, approve, then export the final, a cover, chapters and a local delivery package. Ships a Hermes Desktop Studio page, three agent tools for projects and background jobs (no approval tool: only a person can approve a final export) and a CLI. Requires FFmpeg/ffprobe on PATH; speech, vision and segmentation need optional Python packages and local model files. Disclosure — reads only the local media paths it is given and launches local FFmpeg/ffprobe and a Python worker subprocess with a minimal allowlisted environment (provider API keys and tokens are not forwarded); the worker interpreter comes only from CUTROOM_PYTHON, the plugin's bundled .venv or Hermes' own interpreter; projects, renders and reports are written only under its own workspace in the Hermes home and never overwrite sources or existing outputs; models are never downloaded automatically, and `cutroom setup-models --confirm-downloads` fetches pinned files from storage.googleapis.com (MediaPipe) and huggingface.co (faster-whisper) with SHA-256 verification. Two optional Studio actions run only from a person's click in the Desktop page, never from agent tools: Send to the cloud runs the person's own rclone CLI with its own configuration (Cutroom never reads rclone's config or tokens) to copy an approved export into a new folder on a remote the person chose, such as Google Drive; Record with OBS talks to OBS Studio's WebSocket server on a loopback address only, with the OBS password the person typed into the plugin's Desktop settings (stored by Hermes Desktop on that computer, sent only with OBS requests, never written to projects or logs). In chats on messaging services, finished renders are not shared automatically; the agent is told to ask first. No telemetry, no API keys, no self-update. Approval records a person's decision in the Desktop Studio page; it is a workflow record, not a security boundary against other code running as the same user.
entries.title: Cutroom
known_issues: Requires FFmpeg and ffprobe on PATH with libx264 and AAC support.
Speech, vision and segmentation need faster-whisper, MediaPipe and OpenCV in the runtime interpreter plus local models (see cutroom doctor and cutroom setup-models).
The older plan tools (cutroom_draft, cutroom_review, cutroom_render) are off in chat by default; set the plugin option legacy_tools to true to offer them.
Hooks, storyboards, clip scores and post text are extractive drafts from the transcript, not generated writing; gaze/mouth results are review-only heuristics.
Send to the cloud needs rclone installed with a configured remote; Record with OBS needs OBS Studio with its WebSocket server turned on.
In a Hermes profile other than the one the gateway started with, loading a video into the Studio player is slow (about 0.8 MB/s measured).
Output filesystems must support hard links (NTFS, ext4, APFS); FAT/exFAT is not supported.
Verified primarily on Windows; Linux and macOS have had less testing.

entries.name: cybopal-one-devkit
entries.description: Unofficial, not made or endorsed by CyboPal. Drive a CyboPal ONE (a 27-inch 4K screen on a 6-DOF robotic arm with the Pauli companion display) from Hermes: follow, posture presets, exact poses, gestures, both screens (markdown, pictures and videos), both cameras and an emergency stop; design new actions on the simulator and save them to run unchanged on the hardware. Works today against the open source CyboPal ONE DevKit live simulator. Disclosure — sends HTTP commands, screen text and any picture or video file the agent is given (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/MP4/WebM, up to 64 MB, checked by content) only to the device_url setting (default http://127.0.0.1:5000), never following redirects or environment proxies; saves camera pictures (newest 30) and saved routines in the profile's plugin-data/cybopal-one-devkit; moves physical hardware when device_url points at a real CyboPal ONE (allow_motion off refuses all motion, and only the person's /cybopal resume command can release an emergency stop).

entries.name: daak-duffy
entries.description: Autonomous background task queue (DAAK Duffy / Duet Do-For-You worker) with Human-in-the-Loop approval gates (duet_queue tool, /duffy and /duet commands), Ruflo multi-agent swarm orchestration (ruflo_swarm tool), and multi-model Antigravity CLI quota fallback worker (gemini-3.8-flash-high -> claude-sonnet-5-5-high -> gemini-3.1-pro-high -> claude-opus-5-5-high -> gpt-oss-120b-medium). Disclosure — when the optional background worker or the ruflo_swarm tool is used, the plugin runs the locally installed agy or ruflo CLI under its existing sign-in (counting against the user's subscription) with the Hermes process environment; the worker you start with `python3 -m daak_duffy worker` serves a token-protected dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8899; the plugin never reads, copies, links, or modifies any OAuth token files, keychains, or .env secrets.

entries.name: dafeiyu-companion
entries.description: Companion features for a Chinese-speaking persona bot (大肥魚 / Dafeiyu) on Discord: reaction stickers chosen by deepseek-flash before each reply is sent, an offline Chinese internet-meme wiki (search_meme_wiki), joke seeds, a persona reminder and per-feature switches (companion_switch). Disclosure — on every reply on an enabled platform (Discord by default) the user message (up to 500 characters) and the reply (up to 2,000) are sent to api.deepseek.com; an optional, user-configured embedding endpoint receives sticker captions and reaction text. Reads and writes <HERMES_HOME>/companion-data/ and <HERMES_HOME>/config/companion.json, outside the plugin directory. A setup script (fetch_sources.sh, run by the user, never by the plugin) downloads about 320 MB of sticker images and a meme database from GitHub at pinned versions; every downloaded file is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before it is unpacked, run or moved into place, and Node.js runs once on the checked upstream jokes.mjs to extract the joke seeds. The sticker packs are non-commercial fan works and are not redistributed by this repository. No shell commands at runtime; one short-lived background thread builds the embedding index when that mode is on.
entries.title: Dafeiyu Companion
known_issues: Prompts, injected text and sticker captions are in Chinese; the plugin is built for one persona.
Run fetch_sources.sh after installing; without the downloaded data the features log an error and stay silent.

entries.name: data-saver
entries.description: A mobile-data budget for Hermes. A pre_tool_call hook forecasts how many megabytes a terminal command will download before it runs (pip/uv with dependencies, git clone, docker pull, Hugging Face, ollama, curl/wget) and sends anything over the daily or monthly budget to Hermes's own approval prompt, or blocks it in enforce mode. Execution middleware meters the real bytes each tool call and model request used from the OS network counters into a local ledger; a lean mode trims web results when the budget runs low. Tools: data_usage, data_forecast. Command: /datasaver. Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon entry. Disclosure — forecasts send read-only metadata requests (package, repo, image or model name only; no credentials) to pypi.org, api.github.com, auth.docker.io, registry-1.docker.io, huggingface.co and registry.ollama.ai, and one header-only request to a URL named in a curl/wget command, before the command reaches the approval prompt; that URL and every redirect hop are probed only when Hermes' is_safe_url accepts them and every address they resolve to is public. The ledger (<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/data-saver/data.db) stores time, tool name, bytes and the first 300 characters of the command or URL (including any token written into it), locally. In lean mode it shortens web_extract and web_search results. Network counters are system-wide, so other apps' traffic during a tool call is counted. No telemetry, no shell commands, no background process.

entries.name: data-wrangler
entries.description: Deterministic tools for local tabular data — the counting a model should never guess at. table_profile computes an exact profile of a CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL file (row and column counts, inferred types, null counts and percentages, distinct counts, min/max/mean/median, top text values, duplicate-row and empty-row counts). table_query runs one read-only SQL query over the file in SQLite (table `data`): writes are refused up front and again by a connection authorizer, results are row-capped with the total matched count always reported, and a 10-second query budget applies. table_clean writes a cleaned copy — snake_case headers, trimmed cells, fully-empty rows dropped, exact duplicates removed (optionally on a subset of columns) — and returns a full change report; the input file is never modified. A bundled data-tables skill teaches the profile → query → clean → verify workflow. Python standard library only (csv/json/sqlite3): no dependencies, no configuration, no credentials. Disclosure — Reads local CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL files named in a tool call (Hermes' read blocklist applies), and `table_clean` writes one cleaned copy to a model-chosen path (Hermes' write denylist applies, and approval-gated paths are refused); no network calls, no shell, no state kept.

entries.name: data
entries.description: An agentic report page. Open an Excel workbook, a CSV or a JSON file and Hermes finds the story: it suggests a headline and a handful of charts, and you accept the ones you want onto the page. Every number on a chart is computed from your rows; the model picks columns and wording, never figures. Ask about the table or about one chart and an agent answers with a chart and its sources. Split a chart by a second column, point at any mark and list the rows behind it, export the report as a web page, Markdown or SVG. Once you allow it, any chat can read your reports and propose charts. Disclosure — Find the story starts a hidden Hermes session told to use no tools (your Hermes tools stay available to it, stopped after 2.5 minutes or 6 tool calls), which sees column summaries, grouped totals and the first eight rows, never the whole table; Ask starts a hidden session that uses your Hermes tools and reads third-party web pages, stopped after 4 minutes or 24 tool calls; approval prompts inside these sessions are denied; open and export go through the system dialog and the plugin's own backend, which reads workbooks with the Python standard library and refuses paths inside the Hermes home folder; a CSV or JSON file dragged onto the page is read in the page; reports live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy of the columns, charts and first 400 rows under plugin-data/data/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Hermes profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; with the Sheets or Whiteboard plugin installed, a click hands a table or chart remarks to that page through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; no telemetry, no credentials, no shell commands or background processes of its own. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: day-panel
entries.description: A Today page in Hermes Desktop, plus hermes day show and check, built from sections you list in a YAML file: any program that prints JSON (your tracker, a script of yours), your open GitHub pull requests and review requests through gh, one read-only tool of an MCP server you already configured, and your AI providers' limit windows from hermes usage. Items can carry a colour, a progress bar and a relative time; the page follows the Desktop theme. Ships a demo page that needs no login or network. Read-only and no model calls; merging a pull request from the page is off by default and needs a preview and a confirmation pinned to the head commit. Disclosure — runs the programs your sources file names (no shell), plus gh and hermes usage, as your user with your existing logins; calls a configured MCP server's tool only when the server marks it readOnlyHint, in a child process that imports three undocumented Hermes MCP modules (there is no public seam for this yet); reads only the sources file; writes nothing to disk; logs carry section names and exit statuses, not source output. No credentials stored, no telemetry.
entries.title: Today (day panel)
known_issues: The mcp_tool source imports undocumented Hermes MCP internals (discover_mcp_tools, _tool_is_read_only, mcp_prefixed_tool_name); a Hermes release can break that one source until the plugin is updated. The other sources do not use them.
Under plugins.isolation: host the hermes day terminal command is not available (Hermes skips plugin CLI commands in the host); the Desktop page still works.
The Desktop half ships disabled, like every plugin's: turn it on in Capabilities → Plugins.

entries.name: de-law
entries.description: German federal law, EU law and German federal court decisions for Hermes Agent: read one section or article (§ 203 StGB, Art. 6 DSGVO, Art. 50 AI Act) in the source wording with version status (Stand), gazette reference and a ready source line, search the index of federal laws, list a law's sections, and find and read published decisions of BVerfG, BGH, BVerwG, BFH, BAG, BSG and BPatG. Legal texts, not legal advice. Disclosure: sends HTTPS GET requests only to www.gesetze-im-internet.de (law folder names, the daily index, weekly abbreviation lists), www.rechtsprechung-im-internet.de (the daily index, document ids of decisions you read) and publications.europa.eu (CELEX numbers, text language, one SPARQL query per act listing its consolidated versions); section numbers and search words are not sent, because whole laws are downloaded and searched locally. Public sources, no key. Writes public legal texts and indexes (JSON with ETag, Last-Modified and fetch time; no questions, no session data) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/de-law/cache, capped by the cache_max_mb setting (default 200 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 25 s timeout, 40 MB response cap. rechtsprechung-im-internet.de sends a tdm-reservation header; the plugin fetches its index and single decisions on request only, and case_law: false turns that source off. No hooks, no cron jobs, no background processes. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

Disclosure: sends HTTPS GET requests only to www.gesetze-im-internet.de (law folder names, the daily index, weekly abbreviation lists), www.rechtsprechung-im-internet.de (the daily index, document ids of decisions you read) and publications.europa.eu (CELEX numbers, text language, one SPARQL query per act listing its consolidated versions); section numbers and search words are not sent, because whole laws are downloaded and searched locally. Public sources, no key. Writes public legal texts and indexes (JSON with ETag, Last-Modified and fetch time; no questions, no session data) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/de-law/cache, capped by the cache_max_mb setting (default 200 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 25 s timeout, 40 MB response cap. rechtsprechung-im-internet.de sends a tdm-reservation header; the plugin fetches its index and single decisions on request only, and case_law: false turns that source off. No hooks, no cron jobs, no background processes. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session. This plugin registers tool(s): de_law_get, de_law_search, de_law_toc, de_case_search, de_case_get. Requires Hermes >=0.22.2.

entries.name: dead-drop
entries.description: Autonomous agent-to-agent messaging across teams. Keep work moving with larger private mailboxes and durable delivery recovery. Disclosure — when you enable it (`active: true`), the model can send messages of up to 4000 chars, without a per-call Hermes approval, to the peer agents you list. Each message is committed, with your configured scope, to the private GitHub repository you name, readable by everyone with access to that repo, using the `DEAD_DROP_GITHUB_TOKEN` you store in Hermes. Sends are capped by `max_messages` and the deadline. Peer messages are fed back to the model as untrusted text. An optional cron job (`wake_enabled` plus the exact `wake_job_id`) can read and answer peer questions unattended. Requires Node.js 22+, which runs only the bundled engine, with a minimal environment.
entries.title: Dead Drop
known_issues: Requires Node.js 22+ and a GitHub mailbox credential stored through Hermes.
Unattended exchanges require available peers and separately authorized host schedules.

entries.name: deadline-guard
entries.description: Deadline governance for Hermes. Reads a local Markdown deadlines table and exposes check_deadlines, next_founder_steps, propose_status_update, and deadline_guard_cron: commitments are bucketed overdue / 24h / 72h / 7d, founder-gated next steps are surfaced before they go critical, and a status can never be recorded as 'submitted' without an http(s) receipt URL - the proposal comes back unapplied for a human to confirm. Ships a daily-check automation blueprint (08:00 cron) and a bundled deadline-guard skill. Validated on Hermes 0.23.0: hermes plugins validate --install-deps exit 0, all 15 checks pass; 47 tests pass. Disclosure - stdlib only, no network calls, no model calls, no telemetry; reads only the configured local deadlines file (config deadlines_path, default examples/hackathon-deadlines.md); writes nothing itself. entries.description: deAPI backends for image_generate, video_generate, text_to_speech and speech-to-text: text-to-image, image editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, speech with preset voices (Kokoro, Chatterbox, Qwen3-TTS) and transcription of voice messages (Whisper Large V3) on deAPI's native API, with models, limits, voices and defaults from the key's live model list. Each backend is used only when selected (image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider, tts.provider or stt.provider set to deapi). Disclosure — prompts, source images, the text Hermes asks it to speak, the recordings Hermes asks it to transcribe and the deAPI API key (DEAPI_API_KEY) are sent to api.deapi.ai; source-image URLs are downloaded by the plugin through Hermes's SSRF-guarded client, and a local source path is read in full only when its header is an image header (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP); every generation, spoken reply and transcription is billed to the deAPI account with no Hermes approval prompt; generated images and videos are written under $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/ through Hermes's helpers, and speech to the output path Hermes supplies, after downloading results from deAPI's result URLs through the same SSRF-guarded client without the key; the model list is cached in memory only; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes, extra dependencies or self-updates.

entries.name: deepseek-web-tools
entries.description: DeepSeek's server-side web tools as one Hermes tool: the model searches, opens pages and checks facts inside a single call, then answers with structured citations. thinking is opt-in (the server default is on and bills up to ~20 searches), and page text is never returned - use web_extract when you need the content. It can also ask the question over local documents (PDF/Office/text/image, up to 3 per call): each file is uploaded to the DeepSeek Files API first and referenced by id, because the vendor refuses documents inside a chat request. Disclosure — each web_research call sends the query, any URLs and image URL the model passes, and the bytes of any local file named in files (up to 3, any readable PDF, Office, text or image file the model picks, uploaded without a separate prompt), to api.deepseek.com with your DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; DeepSeek's servers search and open those pages and bill each search to your account (up to ~20 per call when thinking is on), parse the uploaded documents, and keep them - there is no delete call. No other network host and no shell commands. The plugin writes one local file: a cache of upload ids, content hashes and timestamps, no path and no file name, under ~/.local/state/hermes, mode 0600.

entries.name: defuzz-componentize
entries.description: Optional Defuzz companion for turning Python scripts into reusable components checked against saved baseline output, with 14 declarative project kits, CLI and slash commands, bundled guidance, and a Desktop settings page. Requires Python 3.13 or newer. Disclosure — Runs the baseline and test commands named in a componentize spec (`golden.argv`, `tests.argv`), and imports and calls `register()` on any plugin trees the spec lists, with your user's permissions, without a sandbox and without a Hermes approval prompt, including when started from the `/componentize` slash command in chat; nested or detached commands can outlive a cancel. It reads the chosen projects, library, specs, inputs and job evidence; creates project folders, updates kit-owned AGENTS.md blocks and .gitignore/LFS rules; saves its two settings through Hermes; and writes job evidence and locks under `<library>/.componentize/<name>/` (or `--state-root`). Libc lookup may run system utilities (ldconfig, gcc, objdump). The plugin itself makes no network calls, but the commands and plugins it runs can reach your files and the internet. Linux only; needs Python 3.13 or newer.

entries.name: deja-fix
entries.description: Stops the agent from putting back code that already failed. Every version of every file it writes in a session is fingerprinted and judged by the next test or build run, or by the user saying "still broken". An edit that would recreate a failed version is stopped once, naming when it failed and why; a second try goes through. Catches the same code reached by different edits, which Hermes' identical-call guard can't. /deja shows what is tracked. No model calls.

entries.name: delegation-receipts
entries.description: Verify what a subagent says it did before the parent reports the work as done. A "receipts" delegation backend asks every child to end its reply with a receipt (status, the files it changed, and the one command that proves the work); when a child stops, the plugin resolves and hashes each claimed path, matches every claim against the write targets that child's own tool history records so it cannot take credit for a file someone else wrote, and checks the cited command against a closed set of fixed check forms (pytest, uv run --no-sync pytest, cargo/go/npm/pnpm/yarn test), refusing a path rather than a bare name, a launcher, or inline evaluation. Host re-run is opt-in and off by default, because a hook-driven re-run bypasses Hermes' dangerous-command approval and the child's terminal backend; when an operator enables it, the command is re-run argv-style with no shell, in its own process group, with output and time bounded. Either way a verdict reaches the parent: a rejection is appended to the delegate_task result, with the failing output attached when there is one; a background child's verdict arrives on the parent's next turn instead. Every check stays in a local JSONL ledger shown by `hermes receipts`. One command per receipt, one receipt per child. Disclosure — the receipt's `verified:` command is written by the subagent being checked; host re-run is off by default, and when you enable `plugins.entries.delegation-receipts.settings.host_rerun` that command (one of pytest, uv run --no-sync pytest, cargo/go/npm/pnpm/yarn test) runs on this host with your privileges in the child's inferred workspace, outside Hermes' command approval and the configured terminal backend, and executes the project's test code and scripts, including files the subagent wrote (no shell, argv-split, filtered environment, 120 s default timeout); receipts and claimed paths are checked locally, the ledger is local at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/delegation-receipts/ledger.jsonl, and the plugin makes no network calls and holds no credentials.

entries.name: delx-recovery
entries.description: Free recovery and continuity for agents through the hosted Delx Protocol MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no API key, no OAuth, no payment), with the delx-recovery-first-hour workflow skill bundled: triage an error loop or lost context, resume a prior session, capture state and context memory, seal a Continuity Capsule (goal/done/next/blockers/refuted) before compaction so the next session resumes warm, and turn failures into a recovery plan. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); Hermes runs no code from it. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call, including the free-text problem description sent by public triage, goes to the remote server at api.delx.ai. Public triage needs no credential; private continuity uses a free agent credential returned at registration and passed as a tool argument. What the agent chooses to store (state, memory, capsules) is retained by Delx under its privacy policy, so do not send secrets. Requests carry ?src=plugin for channel attribution. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The hooks/ shell scripts in the directory are opt-in Claude Code hooks that Hermes does not load.

entries.name: desensitize
entries.description: Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.

entries.name: desktop-inbox
entries.description: An Inbox pane for Hermes Desktop. Cron jobs, scripts and webhooks file items (Read, Answer, Decide, Do, or your own types) as Hermes-started Desktop conversations, each with one clear ask. The pane is a keyboard-driven triage queue (snooze, undo, OS notifications) that also lists what waits on you elsewhere: chats with a pending question, blocked or triage kanban cards, and failing cron jobs (one click files a Fix item). Items close themselves when the kanban card they started is done. Disclosure: reads state.db, cron/jobs.json, cron/output and every kanban.db read-only; changes sessions only through public SessionDB methods (title, folder, archive state, hiding an item's opening message, its first Hermes message); writes its own files in the inbox folder; runs `hermes chat` once per new item (one model turn), `hermes kanban archive` when you archive a card from the pane, and `gh api user` once when the webhook needs your GitHub login; the optional webhook listener (off by default) binds 127.0.0.1 only, refuses posts until its token or GitHub secret is set, and refuses browser (Origin) requests; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

entries.name: detonator
entries.description: Security testing sandbox for Hermes plugins and MCP servers: detonate a plugin or MCP server you did not write before you install it, and see whether it steals keys, phones home, runs shell commands or plants persistence. Test any catalog plugin by name (/detonate <name>, no commit SHA needed), any GitHub plugin by its link, or an update before you apply it (/detonate update <name>). After you approve the run, Detonator fetches the plugin at an exact commit and loads it inside a disposable Docker container (no network, read-only, non-root, all capabilities dropped) with a throwaway Hermes home full of decoy keys, drives its hooks and tools, jumps the clock to wake time bombs, and reports what it actually did: credential theft (even disguised or split up), network attempts, shell commands, persistence, prompt injection, tool poisoning, monkeypatching. A full test also watches from outside the plugin's container (a system-call tracer and a fake internet), so a plugin that hides from the inside monitor or fakes a clean result is still caught; a quicker inside-only test is offered, and every report says which test ran. MCP servers (/detonate-mcp <name>) are run the same way, acting as Hermes: every tool is listed and called, then the server is restarted with its clock 400 days ahead, catching poisoned tool descriptions, rug pulls, time bombs, hidden email recipients, sampling abuse and key theft. A malware and supply-chain safety check you can run in seconds, with deterministic rules, a plain-language reason and MITRE ATT&CK / ATLAS IDs per finding; advisory only, a clean run is evidence, not proof. Disclosure — requires Docker; runs git (fetches the target repo over the network) and docker on your machine, only after you approve each run (git ls-remote finds a repo's newest commit when you give no commit). One-time image builds pull a digest-pinned python:3.11-slim (and, for MCP, a digest-pinned node image) and install strace from Debian's signed package archive. For /detonate-mcp it reads only the named mcp_servers entry through Hermes's own config reader (a key written directly into that entry is flagged in the report with only its first four characters shown), and downloads the server's npm or PyPI package in a separate locked-down container (install scripts off, wheels only, runs as your user); package code runs only in the sandbox. That download uses your own proxy settings and certificate bundle if you have them, never host networking (a proxy on localhost is reached through a one-port relay). To read HTTPS the fake internet makes a short-lived test certificate for each run that only the sandbox trusts, never your machine. A full test starts two extra short-lived monitor containers next to the sandbox: the tracer gets the SYS_PTRACE capability, the fake internet NET_ADMIN and NET_BIND_SERVICE; the plugin's own container keeps all capabilities dropped and reaches only the fake internet, never the real one. It refuses to run unattended; writes reports under its own plugin-data folder; never reads your .env, auth.json or Hermes credentials.

A full test starts two extra short-lived monitor containers next to the sandbox: the tracer gets the SYS_PTRACE capability, the fake internet NET_ADMIN and NET_BIND_SERVICE; the plugin's own container keeps all capabilities dropped and reaches only the fake internet, never the real one. It refuses to run unattended; writes reports under its own plugin-data folder; never reads your .env, auth.json or Hermes credentials. This plugin registers tool(s): detonate_plugin, detonator_report. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0.

entries.name: devin
entries.description: Delegate coding tasks to the Devin CLI, on your computer or in Devin Cloud, with live progress cards and change review in Hermes Desktop. Every launch goes through Hermes approval; Cloud runs need a separate Cloud-managed-permissions confirmation. Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Hermes does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Hermes approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Hermes prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Hermes provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.

entries.name: devkit
entries.description: One managed home for agent drafts: a per-session scratchpad of named buffers the agent edits in place instead of writing a new temp file per revision. Buffers live under plugin-data/devkit/, open in the Desktop code viewer, are promoted to real files only through write_file, and are removed when their chat is deleted. A Scratchpad tab beside Files groups chats by date like the chat sidebar; click a chat to open it, click a file to view or edit it in a workspace tab, and delete or clear drafts. Disclosure — adds a short placement rule (about 120 tokens) to each turn's user message; reads state.db read-only once an hour from a background thread to find deleted chats, and also removes folders idle longer than idle_days (default 90) using its own stamps; deletes only its own folders under plugin-data/devkit/; no network calls, credentials or third-party services.
entries.title: Scratchpad (devkit)
known_issues: scratchpad action=open needs the Desktop window bridge on the session gateway (NousResearch/hermes-agent#138917); on v0.22.1 open reports 'The preview pane is only available in the Hermes desktop app'. Every other action works.
The agent may not always pick the scratchpad on its own (the model chooses its tools). If it writes a loose file or pastes code instead, ask it to use the scratchpad.

entries.name: devtune
entries.description: DevTune through its official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://devtune.ai/api/mcp): what AI answer engines say about a product and who they cite instead, AI crawler and referral traffic, the ranked queue of fixes with briefs and drafts, before/after results for shipped fixes, and Agent Picks (which tools coding agents pick when asked to add a capability). Bundles two skills, devtune and agent-picks, that pick the right tool for each question and report rates in the units DevTune measures them. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code, hooks or background processes; every tool call goes to devtune.ai with the user's own project API key (DEVTUNE_API_KEY, sent as a bearer header), and the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Some tools change project data or spend DevTune credits (briefs, drafts, agent runs, Agent Picks tests); the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every MCP tool not annotated read-only and refuses those tools in unattended runs, and paid Agent Picks tests also need a quote the user approves. When the MCP tools are unavailable, the bundled skills tell the agent to call DevTune's REST API (devtune.ai/api/v2) from the shell with DEVTUNE_API_KEY, where writes and credit spends are gated only by the skill's ask-first instructions, not by Hermes approval; with no DevTune account, they tell the agent to follow devtune.ai/auth.md to register one with the user's email and use the claimed access token.

entries.name: dexio
entries.description: Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use; and a Hermes Desktop pane showing which pages the agent recalled and wrote and what your other agents changed. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. The provider uses the standard library only, the pane's backend uses the FastAPI that Hermes ships, and neither starts threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO_API_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step; while the Desktop pane is open, its backend (loaded only with dexio in plugins.enabled) asks the same server for the wiki's recent changes, name, page count and page titles, cached 8 to 60 seconds; the last 200 recalls and tool calls (search text cut to 160 characters, page paths and titles, notes and errors) are kept in $HERMES_HOME/dexio/activity.jsonl and pushed to Desktop windows connected to the same Hermes, never uploaded.

entries.name: diaktoros
entries.description: Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, a `diaktoros/review` check run or commit status at each open loop PR's head, a repository ruleset requiring that check when you run `protect`, a GitHub App's webhook URL and secret when you run `app-webhook --set`, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts or, opt-in, when a loop PR falls behind, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; an opt-in approval by the adjudicator's account when it rules for the fixer, dismissing the change request it overruled; an opt-in one-time rerun of the failed CI jobs at the default branch's head when a failure looks like a flake, as a maintainer login whose token you provide, never a seat's; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files or GitHub App private keys you provide (for an App, the host signs a JWT, with Python's cryptography package or else the openssl command, and mints a short-lived installation token for that one repository); its create-apps command opens your browser and runs a one-shot server on 127.0.0.1 for GitHub's App-manifest flow, then writes each new App's private key (mode 0600) to a directory you choose (by default under the Hermes home); edits Hermes's webhook_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose and prunes its own older default-named archives (10 kept unless set), and restore first backs up the live install, then writes an archive back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices and an optional weekly report to the chat you name; opt-in shadow reviews spend a second profile's model tokens on reviews that are recorded but never posted; an opt-in change proof runs the tests a PR adds or changes inside the same bubblewrap sandbox, on the merge base and at the head, before each review; its optional Desktop page and local dashboard API read loop state and can re-arm a failed run as `hermes dk retry` would, and, after an explicit confirmation, pause or resume a loop's hooks, escalate a PR, cancel a queued or running run, or declare or waive an issue dependency (a local record), and doctor compares the installed commit with the plugin's latest GitHub release (read-only); deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.
