entries.name: dial-a-hermes
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from any phone with no data: a USSD gateway platform (Africa's Talking-compatible callback) with 182-char paged replies, a 'thinking, press 1 to check' flow for long turns, keypad exec approvals (1 Approve / 2 Deny, full command shown first, Hermes's own approval flow), clarify answers, optional SMS of the full reply, English/Nigerian Pidgin menus and a local feature-phone simulator. Owner-only phone allowlist, fails closed. Disclosure — opens a local HTTP listener (default 127.0.0.1:8095) for POST /ussd/<secret-token> and GET /health, plus a loopback-only simulator page when USSD_SIMULATOR=true; Africa's Talking does not sign callbacks, so the secret token in the URL is the boundary; outbound calls only when USSD_SMS_MODE=africastalking, to api.africastalking.com / api.sandbox.africastalking.com (reply text and the owner's number); stores per-phone language choice in the plugin data folder; no telemetry.
entries.title: Dial-a-Hermes (USSD)
known_issues: Needs a public HTTPS URL (tunnel or reverse proxy) and an Africa's Talking account (free sandbox) for real phones; the bundled simulator works locally without either.
USSD gives each callback about 10 seconds and a session about 3 minutes; longer agent turns continue in the background and are read with "1 Check again" or by dialing back.

entries.name: dike
entries.description: Diké: checks the article citations of Chilean law in a legal brief against a sealed, hash-identified local copy of 25 statutes (Ley Chile), and refuses to certify what it cannot prove. Each citation comes back verified, with its identifier, source URL and text SHA-256, or unverified with the engine's reason (AMBIGUOUS, UNRESOLVABLE). Three tools (dike_verificar_citas on text or a .md/.txt/.docx path; dike_leer_articulo and dike_buscar_corpus, read-only on the corpus), two commands (/dike-verificar, /dike-estado) and two skills. Text in English, Spanish optional; statute text and engine codes stay in Spanish. Not legal advice: it never certifies that a provision supports an argument, nor that a dated copy is today's text. The opt-in Desktop page adds a Case Writer (a brief editor where only the engine can mark a citation verified, a pseudonymization step you control before any text leaves, and a chat about the brief in your own Hermes gateway), a read-only 3D map of the sealed corpus and a versioned case board; a Dashboard tab and a backend at /api/plugins/dike serve them. Disclosure — the vendored Diké engine runs in a child process (same interpreter, no shell, minimal environment without agent credentials), inside bubblewrap without network when it is available and in a declared degraded mode when it is not. entries.name: disko
entries.description: Run and steer a disko AI DJ set on your Mac from any Hermes chat. disko's model picks each next track and beat-matches the mix; this plugin launches it on a music folder or a Spotify playlist, starts the set, steers the energy, asks for a different next track, pauses and stops, through ten tools, a /disko slash command and a hermes disko CLI that need no model turn, and a pre_llm_call hook that tells the agent what is playing while a set runs. Standard library only. Disclosure — talks only to disko's local control socket (~/.disko/control.sock), which disko restricts to the same macOS user, so no token is used; reads ~/.disko/install.json (disko's folder and Python path, written by disko; not a credential) to find disko, and reads no token or credential file. No third-party network calls (an optional control_url, set by the user, is contacted over plain HTTP with a token from Hermes's secret store). disko_launch starts disko as a background process with a fixed command (no shell) and a minimal environment (none of Hermes's API keys) that keeps running after Hermes exits and logs to the plugin's data folder (a Spotify playlist is passed only as `liked` or a playlist id; disko, not the plugin, then uses the user's own Spotify sign-in, and only if the user turned Spotify audio on in disko themselves); disko_start plays music out loud on the Mac. While a set runs, one line of track names is added to each message and reaches the model provider. Requires disko (github.com/emirkaan5/disko) on macOS. No telemetry.

entries.description: Quotes for trades businesses (plumbers, electricians, HVAC): describe a job in words or a voice note and Docket prices every line from the owner's own price book with a deterministic engine (the model only picks item codes; it never writes a number). entries.name: docs-drift
entries.description: Checks that the README and Markdown docs still match the code after the agent edits files. When a write_file or patch call leaves the docs naming a command-line flag, environment variable, default value, npm script, make target or file that the code no longer has, the tool result gets a docs_drift block with file:line on both sides, in the same turn. When an edit adds a flag or environment variable that no doc mentions while the docs document its siblings, the result says so and says where the siblings are documented. Fixing the doc reports the finding as resolved, and the agent is reminded once before it finishes if drift from this session is still open. Also adds a docs_drift_scan tool (whole repository or changed files only), docs_drift_explain (the evidence behind one finding), a /drift command and a python -m docsdrift command line for CI. Deterministic and offline: Python standard library only, no model call, no network, no API key. Markdown and MDX docs only. Disclosure — to do its job the plugin runs git (ls-files, status, cat-file blob, diff --cached --name-only, check-ignore, config --get-regexp; none of them writes) in the repository being edited, with options that keep that repository's git config from starting a program and with an environment that carries no API key, and reads that repository's text files and .git/config. It does not follow a link out of the repository, does not open .env or key files (templates such as .env.example are read), writes nothing to disk, makes no network request and sends no telemetry.
entries.title: Docs Drift
known_issues: Reads Markdown and MDX docs only; reStructuredText, AsciiDoc and docstrings are not checked.
The hooks watch write_file and patch. A file changed by a terminal command is seen at the next watched edit or by an explicit docs_drift_scan, not when the command runs.

The first scan of a very large repository can take longer than the 8 second hook budget (measured: 52 s for the first scan of the Hermes Agent repository). That edit is then not checked and the agent is told so once per session and repository; run docs_drift_scan or /drift for the full result.

A repository that ships docs for other tools (vendored skills, exported documentation sites) gets false reports from whole-repository scans; set ignore_paths for those directories. The edit hooks report only findings that an edit introduced.

Whole-repository scans of repositories the rules were not tuned on were mostly wrong in the author's measurement: with the shipped checks, 15 findings from the default checks, 2 of them true, and 48 from the opt-in checks, 2 true, on 12 repositories scanned once and not tuned on afterwards. The README has the numbers per round and the causes.

In 106 recorded sessions with two real models (glm-5.3 and qwen3.8-27b) the plugin changed the outcome for one model and one kind of request only: glm-5.3 asked to add a flag. There the docs ended up consistent in 10 of 10 sessions with the plugin and 2 of 10 without on the author's own example project, and in 5 of 5 against 1 of 5 on encode/uvicorn. For renames, removals and changed defaults, and for qwen3.8-27b on both of its requests (an added flag included), the docs ended up consistent with and without the plugin: those models search for the name and update the docs by themselves. The reminder before the end of a turn was never triggered by a real model; it is exercised by a scripted session and unit tests.

A rename done over several edits is reported only when no non-doc file contains the old name any more. A whole-repository scan does not treat a variable whose name starts with an underscore, or one that click or typer binds with envvar=, as an environment variable of the program; the edit hooks, --since and /drift --changed report such a name when an edit removes it, a change covered by unit tests and two manual checks only, not by the real-model sessions.

The tests run in the repository's CI on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14, and the plugin is validated, installed and run through two scripted sessions on Linux in two pinned Hermes checkouts (the commit the recorded sessions used, and upstream main as of 2026-11-10 17:13 UTC). The real-model sessions and the precision measurements were run on one Windows 11 machine only.

The repository being edited is treated as untrusted (its git config, its links, the text of its files); SECURITY.md lists what is turned off and the tests behind it. Limits: this was tested with git 2.43, 2.54 and 2.56, not with older versions; a hard link to a file outside the repository is read like any other file; Python cannot interrupt a regular-expression search, so the 8 second hook budget is checked between files and between git calls, not inside one search.

entries.name: dome-relay
entries.description: Escalate a task to another established agent through an always-on callback relay and read the result back in the conversation that sent it. Registers jobs with tools dome_relay_escalate, dome_relay_status, and dome_relay_cancel; a worker polls the relay; the relay (not this plugin) wakes a Grok Bot executive. Disclosure — sends each escalated job (task text, target name, optional https reference links) to the HTTPS relay you configure in `relay_url` (no default host; you deploy the relay from this repo's `relay/` folder), which forwards it to your Grok Bot webhook and spends Grok Bot usage on each successful wake; the model can queue a job without an approval prompt, and jobs leave the machine only while you run `hermes dome-relay worker` (a long-running poller you start yourself); stores job metadata and results in the active profile's plugin-data database; its only secret is DOME_RELAY_KEY, read through Hermes secret scope and sent only to that relay; optional settings (off by default) add finished results from the relay to the next turn's context.

Disclosure — sends each escalated job (task text, target name, optional https reference links) to the HTTPS relay you configure in `relay_url` (no default host; you deploy the relay from this repo's `relay/` folder), which forwards it to your Grok Bot webhook and spends Grok Bot usage on each successful wake; the model can queue a job without an approval prompt, and jobs leave the machine only while you run `hermes dome-relay worker` (a long-running poller you start yourself); stores job metadata and results in the active profile's plugin-data database; its only secret is DOME_RELAY_KEY, read through Hermes secret scope and sent only to that relay; optional settings (off by default) add finished results from the relay to the next turn's context. This plugin registers tool(s): dome_relay_escalate, dome_relay_status, dome_relay_cancel; hook(s): pre_llm_call, post_compaction; requires env var(s): DOME_RELAY_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0.

entries.name: doorman
entries.description: Wake-on-LAN doorman for sleeping inference backends. When an API request targets a host from a config-driven host map that is asleep, Doorman broadcasts a UDP magic packet, waits a bounded time for the inference port to accept a connection, then holds a per-request keep-alive (one packet per interval) for the life of the request, released on completion or on a terminal error; hosts that answer are left alone and no packet is sent. If the turn is cancelled (/stop), a lifecycle hook releases every live hold so the host is not woken for a request nobody is waiting on. Pure Python, no dependencies, config re-read per hook fire. Disclosure — sends UDP magic packets and TCP connect probes to the local hosts listed in its own `doorman:` block in config.yaml only, never to third parties; the keep-alive runs on one background daemon thread per plugin instance, with holds bounded by a leak cap (default 7200s) and torn down on completion or turn cancellation; no telemetry, no shell commands, no credentials or secrets, no self-updating code.

entries.description: All-in-one solution for controlling DOSBox apps with your agent. Self-contained DOSBox-automation with built-in MCP server, registers in Hermes and exposes 55 tools via the dosbox-full-auto skill such as vision based mouse movement, live process memory reading and more. entries.name: dosbox-mcp
entries.description: Drive a DOS machine from the agent through dosbox-automation's own MCP bridge: type and press keys, read the screen, take screenshots, record video and audio, run Lua scripts inside the emulator, read and write its memory. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only: it starts the bridge with uvx dosbox-mcp==0.2.4 from PyPI and bundles one usage skill. Disclosure — runs `uvx dosbox-mcp==0.2.4` (dosbox-automation's own bridge from PyPI) as a local stdio MCP server that talks only to the separately installed dosbox-automation emulator on 127.0.0.1, using the API token the emulator writes to its own config folder (read-only); its tools type keys, read the screen, take screenshots and recordings into the emulator's capture folder, run Lua scripts inside the emulator and read/write the emulated machine's memory, CPU registers and I/O ports; a Lua script or a direct REST call (session_info hands the agent a curl example and the token file location) can write an audio recording to any non-system path and use API routes beyond the bridge's capability mode; `bridge_start` launches the emulator binary named in the bridge's human-edited config and `bridge_setup` changes only the headless and protocol settings; host folders reach DOS only through MOUNT below the emulator's `mount_allowed_bases`; no telemetry, no accounts.

entries.name: dossier
entries.description: Sourced, dated, refreshable dossiers on organisations and people in a professional capacity, framed for the meeting you actually have: interview, sales call, partnership, due diligence or supplier review. Every claim keeps a verbatim quote, a source URL, a publication date and a retrieval date; conflicting sources print as contested instead of being resolved, a figure the sources do not agree on is filed as unconfirmed rather than quoted, and a refresh reports only what changed since the last snapshot. Renders an A4 PDF, HTML, a chat card and a Desktop page, and ships an automation blueprint for scheduled refresh. Disclosure — makes outbound HTTP requests to the entity's own site and the pages it links to, to whatever hosts your configured Hermes web search backend returns, to api.github.com / github.com, and to www.sec.gov / data.sec.gov (SEC EDGAR); ABN Lookup (abr.business.gov.au) and Companies House (api.company-information.service.gov.uk) are contacted only when their credentials are configured; non-public addresses are refused; dossiers on people and organisations are stored under the plugin's data directory until you delete them with /dossier forget or the Desktop button.

entries.name: draft-cards
entries.description: Email and chat-message drafts as reviewable cards in the Hermes Desktop chat. The agent's draft_card tool stores each draft and its revisions; the card shows recipients, subject and body, highlights the words each revision changed (removed text on demand), supports inline editing, and offers Copy and Open in Mail. The plugin never sends anything: pressing Send records approval of that exact version and posts it to the chat, then the agent sends it with the user's existing mail or messaging tools and reports the outcome with draft_card_status. Disclosure — stores draft text (recipients, subject, body, versions) in the profile's plugin-data/draft-cards/drafts.db (the 500 most recent drafts are kept); the desktop half appends one scoped stylesheet, removed on disable; no network calls, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

known_issues: After installing, switch on the Draft Cards desktop half in Capabilities → Plugins, then start a new chat so the agent sees the draft_card tools.

entries.name: dreamer
entries.description: When Hermes goes idle, it dreams. A native plugin that watches for idle windows (default: 15 min idle, at least 12 h between dreams) and replays the day's session residue - tool traffic, dead ends, unfinished threads - into a short narrative dream generated by the LLM, graded light or deep by sleep distance and stored in a local dream journal (title, symbols, mood, dream_type). Up to 1-3 actionable insights are distilled from each dream and injected into the next fresh session as a [DREAM RESIDUE] block, so recurring issues (stale tasks, stuck PIDs, untested regressions) surface where they can actually be handled instead of dying silently between sessions. Tools: dream_now (dream on demand), dream_journal (read past dreams), dream_status (enabled/last-dream/idle state). Hooks: one pre_llm_call hook that injects the pending dream residue - and only it - into a new session's context. Disclosure — a background thread started at load (on by default; `enabled: false` stops it, but the `dream_now` tool and the session-start injection still work until the plugin is disabled) reads this profile's `state.db` read-only every 15 minutes. After 15 idle minutes, and at most once per 12 hours, it sends recent user messages and tool-error fragments from every session on the profile (all platforms and chats) to your configured model through `ctx.llm`, unattended. It injects the resulting dream digest (up to 2000 chars) into the first turn of the next new session, whichever chat starts it. Dreams are stored under `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/dreamer`. No network calls of its own.

No credentials, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-updating.

entries.name: dress-rehearsal
entries.description: Rehearse a task before it touches anything: /rehearse on, then give Hermes the job. Reads run for real; every side effect (file writes and edits, modifying shell commands, messages, schedules, any tool not on a read-only list) is recorded into a numbered script instead of running. /rehearse shows the script with diffs and risk flags, /rehearse drop strikes steps, /rehearse go replays the kept calls exactly as recorded with no model in the loop, in the folder they were rehearsed in, stops at the first failure (resumable) and refuses any file that changed since the rehearsal. Disclosure — hooks pre_tool_call (blocks and records side-effecting calls only while armed) and pre_llm_call (a short rehearsal note only while armed); one slash command; stores one script per profile, including tool arguments, in its plugin state; on /rehearse go dispatches the approved calls, plus read_file on files it is about to overwrite, through Hermes's tool registry, where Hermes's own approval and write guards still apply but other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks do not run; read-only git commands still honour the repository's own diff.external/textconv config while armed; no network calls, no subprocesses, no dependencies.

entries.name: dropstation
entries.description: Turn private local folders into Hermes inboxes with standing tasks. Drop a document or image to get a Markdown reply and a durable processing receipt. The adapter polls the configured owner-private spool and uses its filesystem permissions as the inbound authorization boundary. Its events skip messaging allowlists and pairing. Snapshots, reports and receipts are stored locally. The configured Hermes provider processes the source contents. Disclosure — every supported file written into a configured inbox folder starts an unattended Hermes turn with that lane's task; the platform is trusted_inbound, so these events skip messaging allowlists and pairing and the folders' owner-only 0700 permissions are the only gate. The file's contents go to the configured model provider, and unless platform_toolsets.dropstation is set (the example config sets it to []) the turn gets the default core toolset, terminal and file tools included; commands that need approval cannot be approved from the inbox and are not run. Snapshots, receipts and reports are stored under the configured root.
entries.title: Dropstation
entries.capability_summary: dropstation (community, maintained by satiricalguru) Turn private local folders into Hermes inboxes with standing tasks. Drop a document or image to get a Markdown reply and a durable processing receipt. The adapter polls the configured owner-private spool and uses its filesystem permissions as the inbound authorization boundary. Its events skip messaging allowlists and pairing. Snapshots, reports and receipts are stored locally. The configured Hermes provider processes the source contents. Disclosure — every supported file written into a configured inbox folder starts an unattended Hermes turn with that lane's task; the platform is trusted_inbound, so these events skip messaging allowlists and pairing and the folders' owner-only 0700 permissions are the only gate. The file's contents go to the configured model provider, and unless platform_toolsets.dropstation is set (the example config sets it to []) the turn gets the default core toolset, terminal and file tools included; commands that need approval cannot be approved from the inbox and are not run. Snapshots, receipts and reports are stored under the configured root. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: macos, linux. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0.

entries.name: ds4
entries.description: Run DeepSeek, GLM and Qwen models locally with DwarfStar (ds4), an inference engine for Apple Silicon. Turnkey from Hermes Desktop: one button installs the engine, downloads the model that fits your Mac and makes it your default; the server then starts with your first message and stops when idle. Unofficial. Disclosure — The one-button setup downloads a prebuilt ds4-server engine (about 1.7 MB) from this plugin's own GitHub release, built from antirez/ds4 by the repository's attested GitHub Actions workflow and checked against a pinned SHA-256, and downloads models of 86 to 366 GB from Hugging Face at pinned revisions; it runs ds4-server on 127.0.0.1 while Hermes uses it (with no authentication, so other programs on this Mac can reach that port), keeps ds4's prompt cache (which contains your prompts) under the plugin's data folder until you clear it, and sets the chosen model as your default.
entries.title: DwarfStar (ds4)
known_issues: The managed runtime needs Apple Silicon and 64 GB of memory or more (96 GB for the default model).
The model-provider client requires in-process plugin execution (plugins.isolation host is not supported).
Hermes keeps plugin data on uninstall; use Storage -> Remove everything first to free the models.

entries.name: dsers
entries.description: DSers multi-platform dropshipping plugin for dropshippers, combining eight bundled workflow skills with a remote MCP connection for supplier discovery, product sourcing, listing editing, product publishing, profit and pricing, store management, supplier mapping, order fulfillment, and shipment tracking. The DSers ecosystem includes AliExpress, Alibaba.com, 1688, DVAN, Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, eBay, TikTok Shop, Amazon, Walmart, BigCommerce, Squarespace, Square, Ecwid, Magento, SHOPLINE, Jumpseller, Big Cartel, Cartpanda, Genstore, and LPQV; available operations depend on account and channel access. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugin with eight bundled skills and remote MCP configuration, with no native registered tools. Hermes v0.22.5 requires manual native OAuth connection setup. A DSers Advanced, Pro, or Enterprise subscription is required. Tool arguments and results are exchanged with ai.dsers.com; Hermes manages OAuth credentials. Remote tools include write operations, among them supplier-order placement that spends money through the user's DSers account, pricing changes and listing publication; the package and the documented native entry mark the server untrusted, so non-read-only calls are subject to Hermes's tool approval settings. The remote tool set can change independently of the pinned package. Removing the plugin alone leaves the native MCP connection.
entries.title: DSers — Multi-platform Dropshipping
known_issues: On Hermes v0.22.5, configure the native OAuth connection as documented in the README; installation and enablement alone do not complete setup.
Disabling or removing the plugin alone does not remove the native MCP connection or its cached credentials; the README documents full removal.

entries.name: dsh-pet
entries.description: Desktop pet for Hermes: runs the upstream dsh-pet standalone pet (Node + Electron window), maps session/tool activity onto its work status, and adds start/stop/uninstall commands. This entry points at a fork of PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet (MIT, copyright PC2005-cloud): upstream owns the pet runtime, the animation assets and the DSH plugin; the fork adds only the hermes/ adapter, and the pinned dsh-pet@0.4.7 runtime is the unmodified upstream npm package. Catalog installs fetch that runtime on first start (~80 MB, one time) with npm ci from a bundled lockfile (98 packages at exact versions with sha512 integrities), and dsh-pet downloads Electron (~350 MB) unless a local copy is reused. The child process runs with a minimal environment (PATH/temp/user dirs plus DSH_HOME); no inherited Hermes environment or provider keys. The pet listens on 127.0.0.1:3080-3089 and keeps its data in the plugin data directory. Disclosure — on first start this plugin runs `npm ci` with its bundled lockfile (dsh-pet@0.4.7 and 98 exact, integrity-checked packages from registry.npmjs.org, install scripts off) into its plugin data directory, and the pet downloads Electron 43.3.0 (~350 MB) from npmmirror.com (override: DSH_PET_ELECTRON_MIRROR); when the gateway runs it starts a Node/Electron pet process automatically (turn off with `autostart: false`) under a minimal environment without Hermes's provider keys, which listens on 127.0.0.1:3080-3089 with a per-run token and receives only a short status line: the current item of the agent's todo list (cut to 40 characters) or, while a tool runs, a one-line description derived from the tool and its main argument (command name, file name, web host, search text or subagent goal, cut to 20 characters) — never the full tool arguments or message text; the pet's optional chat feature sends your chat messages to the AI endpoint and API key you configure in the pet's settings; Electron userData is shared at %APPDATA%\\dsh-pet-electron-helper.
entries.title: dsh-pet
known_issues: Windows is the only verified platform; macOS and Linux are untested.
First start downloads ~80 MB of runtime and ~350 MB of Electron; on slow networks it looks hung — the launch log shows progress.
Electron userData is shared with a DSH install (%APPDATA%\dsh-pet-electron-helper); settings and chat memory are not.

entries.name: dsh
entries.description: Drive DeepSeek Harness (dsh) agents from Hermes: one-shot headless runs and live ACP sessions with per-turn cancel, permissions, model config, parallel fanout, and resumable sessions. Disclosure — runs the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) CLI you install yourself (npm `@deepseek-ai/dsh`, not covered by the pinned commit) as a separate agent with its own shell and file tools in the directory the model picks, outside Hermes' terminal sandbox and under dsh's own sandbox and approval rules (letting dsh grant its own escalations asks you first); your DeepSeek/OpenCode key is passed to it from Hermes' secret store, and dsh sends your tasks and files to the model provider configured in its profile.

entries.name: duty-board
entries.description: Read-only dashboard tab and model-free /duty and hermes duty summaries for waiting conversations, unanswered messages, running turns, undelivered background results and failing cron jobs. Supports all 17 dashboard languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/state.db with SQLite mode=ro (sessions, messages, turn leases, async delegations, goals) and reads cron/jobs.json and gateway_state.json; writes only HERMES_HOME/duty-board/dismissed.json for dashboard dismissals. Chat requires in-process Hermes 0.21.7+ and a configured owner; shared-chat summaries default to counts only. No network calls, no model calls, no credentials, no background processes.

entries.name: dynamoi
entries.description: Music promotion for independent artists through Dynamoi's hosted MCP. Make free Smart Links, review Spotify and YouTube campaign results and audience analytics, check platform connections, prepare campaign drafts and apply for optional distribution. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json) with four music-promotion skills; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure: every tool call goes to dynamoi.com, signed in as the user; the first connect opens a browser sign-in and mcp-remote stores the OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. The tool list comes from Dynamoi's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Write-capable tools can change the signed-in Dynamoi account (Smart Links, team, artist setup, campaign drafts, distribution applications); the server is declared untrusted so Hermes asks before every write-capable call. Campaign launches, budget changes and checkout are not exposed.

entries.name: eachlabs
entries.description: Generate and edit images, video, music and voice with each::labs models, and run each::labs workflows, through each::labs' hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with 12 skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to each::labs' MCP server at mcp.eachlabs.ai, signed in as the user. Runs are paid and billed to the organization chosen at sign-in, and the server added with `hermes mcp add` runs them without a Hermes approval prompt unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the eachlabs entry under `mcp_servers` in config.yaml. Prompts and file URLs the user passes are sent to each::labs and to the model providers it routes to. The tool list comes from each::labs' server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add eachlabs --url https://mcp.eachlabs.ai/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`, then `hermes mcp login eachlabs` if no browser opened. Needs Hermes Agent 0.23.2 or later. Hermes enables all each::labs tools, and `hermes mcp configure eachlabs` keeps only some. The package bundles no mcp.json, so the plugin alone has no server.

entries.name: earnfi
entries.description: Work, Money & Execution Layer for Hermes — hire humans and agents, fund real-world work via x402, escrow, and receipts across Solana, Base, NEAR, and OKX X Layer. Disclosure — Crypto payments: connects to EarnFi's hosted MCP server at app.earnfi.fun, whose tools create paid jobs, fund escrow, settle x402 payments and withdraw USDC on Solana, Base, NEAR and OKX X Layer. The server is declared untrusted, so every write or payment tool asks for Hermes approval, with no spend cap by default. `earnfi_sign_x402` signs an x402 payment locally with the user's dedicated wallet key only after a Hermes approval prompt showing network, amount, asset and payee. Optional Node setup scripts install exact-pinned npm packages (with install scripts disabled) and create dedicated wallet keys that the user stores in the plugin's secret settings.

entries.name: effortless-hermes
entries.description: Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt: a fast judge (Jev/TypeSafe, a local OpenAI-compatible model, or any custom API) reads the next message once per turn and rewrites the request's reasoning effort before it ships — easy questions run cheap, hard jobs get high. Port of effortless for Claude Code. Disclosure — sends the next message (≤4000 chars) plus a short recent-conversation excerpt (≤1600 chars) to the configured judge endpoint (default api.typesafe.ai for Jev; a local or custom OpenAI-compatible API otherwise), solely to pick the effort; the optional model_map setting (off by default) also switches the turn's model to the one you map to the verdict; keeps recent per-turn token counts in its own plugin state; no telemetry; secrets resolved only through Hermes' secret scope; stdlib-only, no pip dependencies.

entries.name: egress-guard
entries.description: Automated output vetting for AI agents. Policy-driven guard for what leaves the agent. A pre_tool_call hook redacts credentials in tool arguments and sends shell commands that upload data to non-allowlisted destinations (curl/wget uploads, scp/rsync, cloud copies, gist create, git push to a URL, python/node upload one-liners) to Hermes's approval prompt, showing a masked preview of the command (fail-closed when nobody can approve). transform_tool_result and transform_llm_output suppress small counts in tables, including complementary cells and percentages so hidden values cannot be recovered (statistical disclosure control). Presets, an optional strict network mode, and a /guard command (status, report, dry-run check). Disclosure: no network access, subprocesses or tools; reads its policy from EGRESS_GUARD_POLICY, ~/.hermes/egress-guard.yaml or the bundled default, and its own audit log for /guard report; appends masked audit lines (never raw values) to ~/.hermes/egress-guard/audit.jsonl; never auto-approves.

entries.name: eksis
entries.description: Social media scheduling for an eksis workspace: draft, schedule, approve and publish posts to Instagram, Facebook, Threads, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Pinterest, Google Business Profile and DEV, answer comments and direct messages, run comment and DM automations, and read analytics. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, Streamable HTTP mcp.json, one skill), submitted by eksis, which runs the service. Disclosure: no local executable code; every tool call goes to the hosted MCP server at https://api.eksis.io/mcp and needs an eksis account (the Free plan works). Sign-in is Hermes native MCP OAuth through a `mcp_servers.eksis` entry with `auth: oauth` (Agent Plugins v1 has no auth field), and Hermes stores and refreshes the tokens. Write tools publish to the social accounts connected in the user's workspace, send comment replies and direct messages, delete posts, comments and media, and change automations and AI agents; the package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before every call that is not annotated readOnlyHint. To upload a local file the skill has the agent run the curl PUT that create_media_upload returns. Workspace data, comments, messages and analytics returned by the tools reach the user's model provider. The remote tool list can change without a new pin of this package. No telemetry, no background process, no self-update.
entries.title: eksis
known_issues: The portable mcp.json cannot complete OAuth. Add mcp_servers.eksis with url https://api.eksis.io/mcp, auth: oauth and trust: untrusted to config.yaml, then run hermes mcp login eksis and hermes mcp test eksis. A config.yaml entry replaces the package's, so keep trust: untrusted in it to keep the approval prompt.
Posts, replies, direct messages and automations act on the user's real social accounts, and calls count against the eksis plan's daily request quota and monthly post limit.

entries.name: elcaro
entries.description: Runtime prompt-injection defense and tamper-evident flight recorder. Every tool result is scanned before it reaches the model by a deterministic detector taxonomy (sub-10 ms, fully local, vendored — no network by default); quarantined content is replaced in place with a signed [CONTENT QUARANTINED] notice via transform_tool_result, and tool-call arguments (write_file, terminal, memory) are scanned for smuggled payloads via pre_tool_call. Beyond content, a kernel gate: a quarantine taints the session, and while tainted credential-path reads/writes and instruction-file writes are refused, network egress and outside-workspace writes escalate to the approval gate — tool_call, execute_code and process_manage are evaluated as the action they really make, and taint propagates into subagents via subagent_start. A canary-baited decoy credentials file (ELCARO-DECOY-* marker) forces a deterministic 1.0 quarantine on exfiltration; canary provenance edges record an injection propagating between scans; every verdict lands in a hash-chained, Ed25519-signed threat log with a Desktop pane (chain-verified badge, honeypot status, propagation rows, signed-receipts drawer), a /elcaro slash command (status / calibrate / verify / explain), and a `hermes elcaro` CLI. Two on-demand tools close the loop input scanning can't: elcaro_lint_response flags concealed-compromise artifacts in agent output (canary echoes, text-channel tool calls, tracking pixels, secrets — caught 148/152 compromised transcripts in the public 24-task IPI benchmark), and elcaro_harden_prompt returns a hardened system prompt plus a gullibility score. Engine validated on that benchmark: 22/22 attack tasks flagged (regression coverage, not held-out proof). Disclosure — scanning is fully local by default: the vendored engine's env-driven LLM second passes (api.openai.com, inference-api.openserv.ai and others) and its Postgres canary registry are built disabled; scanned tool-result text leaves the machine only when the user sets the optional `api_url` hosted lane, which POSTs it there with the optional `ELCARO_API_KEY`; the optional `ELCARO_SIGNING_KEY` is read from the profile secret store; it writes only to its plugin data dir (threat-log.jsonl, decoy-marker.txt, and a bait service-credentials.env decoy it never reads); a quarantine taints the session so credential-path and instruction-file writes are refused and network/outside-workspace actions escalate to Hermes approval (nothing auto-approves); Python deps pydantic, cryptography, httpx; no core overrides.

entries.name: elevenlabs-music
entries.description: ElevenLabs Music for Hermes: describe a song or paste your lyrics and Hermes writes, generates and sends the track, 3 seconds to 10 minutes, vocals or instrumental. It can redo one section, extend or loop a song, split it into stems (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other) and score a video. Long songs finish in the background and arrive in the chat. Bundles a music skill (prompting, composition plans, edit recipes) and, in Hermes Desktop, an inline music card with synced lyrics, format downloads and a music library tab. Model, audio format and endpoint are plugin settings. Disclosure: uses your ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, the same key as Hermes's ElevenLabs voice; needs a paid ElevenLabs plan, and a restricted key needs the Music permission); compose, plan, upload, stems and video calls are paid generations billed to your ElevenLabs account by length (drafting a plan and listing finetunes are free). Only the prompt or plan, its parameters and any file you name are sent, to api.elevenlabs.io (or the data-residency endpoint you set); with store_for_editing on, ElevenLabs keeps generated songs so they can be edited later. Files are written to cache/generated/audio under the Hermes home and never overwritten. One Python dependency (httpx, already part of Hermes).

entries.name: elm
entries.description: Local, reviewable long-term memory. You save notes (or approve notes the model proposes) and matching notes are recalled automatically. Off until the owner turns it on from a terminal: for all Desktop/TUI/CLI chats at once (`hermes elm auto on`, notes shared across chats; any chat can opt out with `/elm private`) or per chat (`hermes elm grant`). The model can never turn it on. Works as a general plugin or in the memory slot (`memory.provider: elm`, with the recall indicator; `hermes memory setup elm` offers auto mode). Optional memory-aware delegation backend (`delegation.backend: elm`): you name agents (models or profiles) and ELM routes subagent tasks to the one that did best on similar earlier tasks. Disclosure — no network calls, dependencies, telemetry, self-updater or background daemon of its own. Data stays in the profile's plugin-data/elm SQLite file. Recalled notes are added to the current message and so reach your model provider; in auto mode notes saved in one chat are recalled in your other chats (never in messaging, cron, subagent or ACP chats). Two optional, per-chat opt-in features make model calls through Hermes's auxiliary model slots: a search planner (query text only) and an organizer (selected captured text). Opt-in capture stores finished turns as plain text locally. Routing stores agent names, up to 12 plain-word goal keywords, success and duration (no task or result text), only for chats with ELM on, scoped like notes. Deleting a chat deletes its chat-only notes, captures and routing history (shared notes stay). `hermes elm sessions` reads the profile's session list to help pick a chat ID.
entries.title: ELM
known_issues: Preview. Recall is keyword-based (no embeddings); ask with words that appear in the note.
ELM is off after install. Turn it on with `hermes elm auto on` (all chats) or `hermes elm grant` (one chat).
Memory-aware routing needs the plugin enabled (`hermes plugins enable elm`), not only `memory.provider`.
Tested on Windows 11 and Linux; macOS not yet tested.

entries.name: emailfig
entries.description: Work in your EmailFig email marketing account through EmailFig's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://emailfig.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check campaign and automation results, look up and update contacts, lists and tags, add images, and draft campaigns that you review and send in EmailFig. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to EmailFig's hosted server (emailfig.com) and acts on the EmailFig account the user approved at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. The server cannot send, schedule or delete a campaign; the only email it sends is a test of a draft to the user's own address, though adding someone to a double opt-in list emails them a confirmation and adding or tagging a contact can start the account's automations. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores the OAuth token under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: embargo
entries.description: Embargoed news stays embargoed. When your agent reads 'EMBARGOED UNTIL <time>', tool calls that carry that text are blocked until the clock passes; a live countdown stamp shows what is held, and the hold lifts by itself. Disclosure: hooks pre_tool_call (blocks matching calls; fails closed while an embargo exists), post_tool_call and pre_llm_call (detect embargo headers in files read and messages), transform_llm_output (adds the card); stores label, lift time, file paths and hashed 6-word fingerprints plus hashed headline names and figures, never the raw release text (the one-line label, up to 80 characters, is plain text), in its data folder. Your model provider still sees the text you share; this is a send guard, not a privacy filter. Catches copies, quotes and reworded posts that repeat the headline names and figures; not a full paraphrase detector. Standard library only; it makes no network or model calls and reports nothing anywhere.

entries.name: emotion-chip
entries.description: Your Hermes agent decides how to say it: the sighs, whispers and pauses it writes, voiced by ElevenLabs or Fish Audio. It writes its own delivery into the text it speaks, a small score in square brackets (a sigh, a whispered line, a pause, a warm and amused tone), and Emotion Chip renders exactly that for ElevenLabs v4 or Fish Audio (s2.1-pro, Drama 3), each in its own dialect, adding nothing the agent did not write. With voice replies on in a chat (/voice on), the chip tells the agent when Hermes will read its reply aloud, so the agent can say it itself, score included, instead of Hermes reading the plain text (not on Discord). Registers the emotion-chip speech provider, a delivery guide in the system prompt, the emotion-chip-voice skill, the emotion-chip-report-problem skill (guides the agent through a bug report and posts nothing without the user's yes), the /chip command (status says whether the chip can speak and what to fix; why, quiet, register) the hermes chip command, which shows offline what each engine receives for any score, and two agent tools: chip_status (read-only) and chip_preview (offline). CC0 emotion data and pre-registered evaluations ship in the repository. Disclosure — with backend: eleven it sends your ElevenLabs API key, the rendered text, the model id, voice id, voice settings, an optional seed and, on v4 models, up to three earlier request ids from the same session (kept in memory for two hours) to api.elevenlabs.io over HTTPS; these are paid requests billed to your ElevenLabs account. The key is read at each call through the profile's secret scope and never stored. With the default backend: fish it sends nothing itself: it hands the rendered text to the Fish Audio plugin in the same process (which must be installed, enabled and signed in), and that plugin sends it to Fish Audio under its own disclosure and bills your Fish account; the chip reaches it through Hermes's speech-provider registry and imports its tag adapter. In every guide mode it registers the emotion-chip-report-problem skill, which is text only: the plugin sends and writes nothing for it, and the skill has the agent publish a report only after the user approves the exact text. With guide_mode: generate (the default) it registers the emotion-chip-voice skill, and while it is the speech provider it adds a delivery guide of up to 4,000 characters to the system prompt and registers pre_gateway_dispatch (described next). With guide_mode: generate it also registers two agent tools. chip_status reads the plugin's settings, Hermes's tts configuration and this session's last authored register and reports them; it sends nothing and changes nothing. chip_preview renders a score offline and returns the text each engine would receive and the cues it would drop; no synthesis, no network, nothing written. While the chip is the speech provider, each successful text_to_speech result gains an emotion_chip entry of at most 600 characters (the dialect, the agent's cue words, drops and notes); it stays in the conversation and is sent nowhere. The pre_gateway_dispatch hook: for each incoming message it asks the gateway whether it will read the reply aloud and keeps that answer in memory under the chat and message id (at most 256, never used after 15 minutes), used once to add one line to that message's turn; it never skips or changes a message, and registering the hook routes webhook and relay deliveries through Hermes's hooked ingress path. When another speech provider is selected, its tool_request middleware rewrites text_to_speech text containing a bracket for that provider (the Fish dialect on Fish S2 and Drama 3 models, or the ElevenLabs dialect on a v3/v4 model; for any other provider or model, including Hermes's default Edge, Fish S1 and ElevenLabs on older models, standalone bracketed words are removed as cues, a bracketed Step 2 too, while the words inside spans, numeric references such as [1] and code such as an array index stay), leaves command providers alone and records nothing. With signals on (off by default) it adds a dated situation line of up to 200 characters to the turn and, when a tool call fails, to that call's result. It reads Hermes's tts configuration (read-only) to pick the dialect, model and voice. It writes under the profile's plugin-data/emotion-chip/ only the generated skill and, unless delivery_log is off, delivery.jsonl (time, session id, sender id, platform, model, dialect, rendering group, cue words, parameters, kinds of drops and character count, never the spoken text), moved to delivery.1.jsonl at 5 MB so at most about 10 MB is kept; Hermes keeps its per-session state (task counters and timestamps, the ids of the last 16 tool calls counted, session keys, the messaging sender id and platform, the last situation and register lines, the quiet switch; the 50 most recent sessions) in the plugin's own namespaced folder under plugin-data/. known_issues: Full cues reach the voice on the text_to_speech tool path, and in chats with voice replies on, where the agent says its reply itself. Not on Discord, where Hermes plays its own reply in voice channels. entries.name: empiriolabs-media
entries.description: EmpirioLabs AI backends for Hermes' image_generate, video_generate and text_to_speech tools (backend `empiriolabs` for image_gen.provider, video_gen.provider and tts.provider): image generation and editing, text-to-video and image-to-video, and text-to-speech, with models and voices from the live EmpirioLabs AI catalog. Submitted by EmpirioLabs AI. Disclosure: registers three backends and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); when one is selected and its tool is called, the prompt, source images or text to speak go to https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1 (or EMPIRIOLABS_BASE_URL) with EMPIRIOLABS_API_KEY, read through Hermes' secret scope, and each call is billed to that EmpirioLabs AI account with no Hermes approval prompt; it reads the model catalog (GET /v1/models), polls GET /v1/jobs/{id} while a generation runs (videos up to 15 minutes by default), downloads the generated files from the returned URLs into Hermes' cache (the key is never sent to them), and reads a local image file only when the agent asks to edit one.

entries.name: emporia
entries.description: An open network for AI agents: Hermes agents meet other agents on relays — a signed feed, rooms, sealed DMs the relay cannot read, games, labs tied to code repos, and a season of quests. Testnet only; the relay holds no money. Disclosure — Crypto: agents can hold EVM/Solana wallets and pay in USDC over x402/Tempo (testnet by default; mainnet only after the person runs `emporia wallet mainnet`), with per-payment and daily caps; on testnet a Hermes approval is asked above a set threshold, and on mainnet every payment asks for Hermes approval and is refused in turns another agent or the rounds job started. The agent's posts, sealed DMs, game moves and declared model name go to the relay you choose; setup has no default relay. `hermes emporia setup` fetches Emporia's runtime from github.com/wujitsana/emporia at a pinned commit, installs its locked Python packages from PyPI, creates an agent profile, writes `mcp_servers.emporia` and settings into that profile's config.yaml and .env, and adds a Hermes cron job that runs unattended agent turns (every 4 hours unless you pick another interval in setup). The gateway runs a long-lived bridge process to the relay, and the dashboard starts a local console process on a Unix socket. Optional password-manager key sources run that vendor's CLI with a token kept in the profile's settings.
entries.title: Emporia
known_issues: Tested on Linux. The dashboard console uses a Unix socket, so Windows is not supported.

Keys in a password manager: the recommended way is the signer reading them (emporia signer add NAME --key-source 'ROLE=cmd:op read op://...'), with the vault token in the signer's folder, never the agent's. An agent-side cmd: key source still works but is not recommended: it runs the vendor CLI with an access token kept in the profile's settings, not through Hermes's secret sources (a Hermes unlock lasts one chat session; an agent signs unattended).

entries.name: emporium
entries.description: Hermes opens a shop: sell this agent's skills to anyone (people, scripts, other agents) for USDC per job over x402, paid only on delivery. A new gateway platform takes paid HTTP jobs, verifies the payment before work starts and settles it on-chain only when the result is ready, so a failed, timed-out or abandoned job costs the buyer nothing. Each job runs in its own session that loads only the toolsets its service sells, behind a tool lock and a per-job tool cap. Every job is metered (model calls, tokens, and its inference cost from Hermes's own session pricing), so /shop and the dashboard show sales, AI cost, profit and margin. Services can subcontract part of a job to owner-pinned shops, paid out of the job's own price. Hermes can also hire other shops, after checking their receipts on-chain, within a per-job ceiling, a daily budget and its approval gate. Adds a storefront page, /shop, `hermes emporium`, a dashboard tab, and stress and robbery benches. Disclosure — while the gateway runs the shop listens on host:port (default 127.0.0.1:9402) and calls the configured x402 facilitator (default x402.org) to verify and settle payments, and a JSON-RPC endpoint (default the network's public one) to check payments on-chain; the hire tools call the shop URLs the agent is given (public addresses only, unless the owner lists a private shop in buyer_allow_hosts; link-local and metadata addresses never) and the network's RPC; the optional EMPORIUM_BUYER_KEY (read via the secret scope) signs USDC transfer authorizations for hires and subcontracts within the owner's limits; a SQLite ledger of job metadata (never inputs or outputs) is kept under plugin-data/emporium/, and each job is a session in the shop profile's Hermes history. The shop refuses to open on a profile whose memory, persona or project context files would reach buyers' jobs unless the owner sets allow_unsealed_profile, and `hermes emporium init` turns built-in memory off on the shop's own profile (never the main one).

entries.name: enchanted-composer
entries.description: Draft enhancement, reusable prompt libraries, undo/redo, and owner-bound full-duplex voice for Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — Derived from hermes-live-voice by Synero (itself derived from hermes-talk) and prompt-enhance by apoapostolov (both MIT; notices preserved). Starting voice captures microphone audio. The Codex-subscription lane spawns the official codex app-server CLI under its own login with a minimal environment; through it the captured profile's SOUL.md (up to 4,000 chars), the list of installed skills and enabled tools, and Hermes task results go to OpenAI. The API lane runs only when COMPOSER_REALTIME_OFFER_URL is set: it posts the SDP offer to that https URL with COMPOSER_OPENAI_API_KEY, or the profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, as a Bearer token (redirects refused). A user-configured wss:// bridge receives microphone audio, chat/profile identifiers and task results. Spoken requests the voice model delegates run as Hermes agent turns with tools in the chat where voice started; runs that need approval are stopped, not approved. Settings and usage totals are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/enchanted-composer/. No telemetry, no self-updater, no Codex OAuth-file reads.
entries.title: Enchanted Composer
known_issues: Codex subscription authentication is managed with `codex login` outside Hermes; the plugin does not read or write Codex OAuth files.
Full two-sided persistent voice history and a phone voice client are not included in version 0.2.7.

entries.name: engagements
entries.description: Hermes is a powerful tool for shipping work to clients, no matter the industry or vertical. Engagements gives it a client notebook: each client and project is a plain Markdown record on your machine. Add a client or project from the Clients page or by pasting notes in any chat, approve the draft, and every agent working for that client can look up who to contact, how they like to work and where the files live. The agent keeps the record current with a dated source for every change. The Clients page works in Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard; it shows records but never edits them, and its Add buttons only start the chat that drafts one. Disclosure: local files only, no network requests, no telemetry, no shell commands, no background processes and no stored credentials. Reads and writes Markdown records under the library folder you choose (default is the profile's plugin-data folder), and reads the session's working directory, id and surface to link a chat to a project. Installs PyYAML 6.x.
entries.title: Hermes Engagements
known_issues: Client scoping organizes context. It is not isolation between clients; use a fresh session per client when confidentiality matters.
Runtime evidence is from Linux. Windows reads and writes are covered by native CI only, and macOS has not been exercised.
Messaging gateways and Hermes Desktop SSH remote mode are not verified.

entries.name: enhance-prompt
entries.description: A sparkle beside Send that rewrites the composer draft in place without sending it, in a voice you pick under Settings > Plugins > enhance-prompt (brief, structured, concise, detailed, questions, verify, or your own words), deepening it into a clarifier, a task list, then a phased plan on further clicks, with a one-click discard back to the original. Also registers the `/enhance` slash command and the `enhance_prompt` tool for the same rewrite from the agent, in the same voice. Draft read and write go through `host.composer`, so `@file` and `/command` chips survive. Disclosure — every click runs one stateless `llm.oneshot` call on your own gateway with the focused chat's model (the plugin's `enhance_prompt` auxiliary task, reasoning off, when no chat is focused), followed by a second short call to score the result, so it spends your model credits. It is not an agent turn: no tools run and nothing is written to a session you cannot see. Only the draft and the chosen voice's instructions are sent; the voice setting is read from your own gateway with `plugins.manage list`. It overrides no model, sends nothing to a third party, never sends the composer message, and carries no telemetry, no credentials and no self-update.
entries.title: Enhance Prompt
known_issues: The Desktop half needs a Hermes build with the composer draft API (`host.composer`); on an older Desktop the sparkle reports that an update is needed.
One model call per click, and the score is an extra call. Cancel stops the client-side wait only — the in-flight call may still finish.

Uses the chat's model; there is no separate model setting. Switch the chat model first to enhance with another one. `/enhance` and the tool use the `enhance_prompt` auxiliary task, which has reasoning off by default.
The voice shapes only the first click and `/enhance`; the task-list and phased-plan clicks and the score keep their own shape. A saved voice this version does not know falls back to `brief`.
Not a fork of `prompt-enhancer`: this one is a separate plugin with an agent tool, a slash command, three deepening stages and a scorer.
0.8.0 folds in the voices from the author's separate Prompt Lab plugin, which is not listed.

Disclosure — every click runs one stateless `llm.oneshot` call on your own gateway with the focused chat's model (the plugin's `enhance_prompt` auxiliary task, reasoning off, when no chat is focused), followed by a second short call to score the result, so it spends your model credits. It is not an agent turn: no tools run and nothing is written to a session you cannot see. Only the draft and the chosen voice's instructions are sent; the voice setting is read from your own gateway with `plugins.manage list`. It overrides no model, sends nothing to a third party, never sends the composer message, and carries no telemetry, no credentials and no self-update. This plugin registers tool(s): enhance_prompt. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0. Known issues: The Desktop half needs a Hermes build with the composer draft API (`host.composer`); on an older Desktop the sparkle reports that an update is needed.; One model call per click, and the score is an extra call. Cancel stops the client-side wait only — the in-flight call may still finish.; Uses the chat's model; there is no separate model setting. Switch the chat model first to enhance with another one. `/enhance` and the tool use the `enhance_prompt` auxiliary task, which has reasoning off by default.; The voice shapes only the first click and `/enhance`; the task-list and phased-plan clicks and the score keep their own shape. A saved voice this version does not know falls back to `brief`.; Not a fork of `prompt-enhancer`: this one is a separate plugin with an agent tool, a slash command, three deepening stages and a scorer.; 0.8.0 folds in the voices from the author's separate Prompt Lab plugin, which is not listed..

entries.name: enterprise-pathfinder
entries.description: Routes SAP questions to documented sources and reads official references on request. Parses OData metadata, tests contract claims and checks evidence before saving SAP skills. Disclosure — pre_tool_call checks skill writes and can block tool calls involving plugin data paths or direct SAP skill writes. post_tool_call records skill evidence links and transform_tool_result labels Hermes web results and records relevant page reads. pathfinder_read starts HTTPS GET requests at official or standards sources and checks the final URL. Set network to off to disable it. pathfinder_inspect reads any local file path the model names (up to 5 MB) and parses it as OData metadata. Parsed contracts, hashes, lab results, source metadata, skill evidence links and downloaded documents are stored under plugin-data/enterprise-pathfinder. Pathfinder does not read credentials or call SAP systems or APIs.

entries.name: entropicmem
entries.description: Durable local memory for Hermes agents: SQLite FTS5 facts with cited, explainable recall; a Markdown vault with knowledge-graph export and an interactive visual graph; and turn-prefetch context injection with reason tokens. Write policy auto-redacts high-confidence secrets at write time (other PII types are warn-only findings) and stored-content injection screening flags and warns on recall and prefetch payloads (flag-and-warn, fail-open by design, not a blocking filter). Includes a 38-command CLI, destructive-op gates with automatic backups, and an append-only audit log. Disclosure — all memory data (vault markdown, memory.db, index.db, backups) stays local under HERMES_HOME/entropicmem/; a shared publish DB defaults to HERMES_HOME/entropicmem-shared/. The CLI init command appends ENTROPICMEM_* settings to HERMES_HOME/.env (append-only). Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) does it either download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co on first use (optional sentence-transformers extra) or send memory text to a user-set ENTROPICMEM_EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL; memory formation is off by default (formation.mode: off) and, when enabled, and for the CLI ingest command's LLM pass, sends conversation or document text to the user's active Hermes model through ctx.llm or, outside Hermes, to a user-set ENTROPICMEM_LLM_BASE_URL; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML is self-contained: D3 and marked are vendored and inlined at export, so it renders over file:// with no network (only Google Fonts load from fonts.googleapis.com, with a system-font fallback offline); CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem_profile (action=patch) edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.

entries.name: eol
entries.description:
Live end-of-life and support status for 480+ products (languages, OSes, databases, frameworks, cloud services) from endoflife.date, so the agent stops answering support dates from memory. Reads and writes geol (.geol.yaml) stack files.

- eol_search: find a product's identifier from a name, alias, category or tag; list categories and tags
- eol_product: every release cycle with release date, LTS, end of active support, end of life, latest patch, and the product's purl/CPE identifiers
- eol_check: check many components at once, by product+version, purl (e.g. from an SBOM) or CPE, today or at any date: supported / security-only / eol, days left, newer patch, LTS-aware upgrade target, maintained cycles
- eol_stack_check: check a .geol.yaml with geol check --strict rules (skip, manual_eol, lts_strategy, lts_grace_days, always-latest)
- eol_stack_file: generate a .geol.yaml from the components found in a project; the agent writes it with write_file
- pre_llm_call hint: when a message is about versions, upgrades or security fixes (local keyword match), one line is added to that turn pointing the model at the eol_* tools, so it checks instead of answering from memory; off with the context_hint setting
- Complements CVE scanners such as Patch Sentinel: they ask "am I patched?", this asks "is this version still supported by its vendor?"

Disclosures
- Network: HTTPS GET to endoflife.date/api/v1 when a tool is called; only product names are sent (plus fetching the public purl/CPE mapping tables).
- No file access: stack files are passed in and returned as text; writing goes through Hermes' write_file and its approvals.
- No credentials, no shell commands, no background processes; 6-hour in-memory cache only.
- The pre_llm_call hook only reads the current user message, matches keywords locally and appends a fixed note; it sends nothing anywhere.
- Stdlib only, no Python dependencies (YAML via Hermes' public hermes_yaml helper).

entries.name: epistemic-harness

entries.name: epoch
entries.description: Calibrated time estimates on the Hermes Kanban board: when a worker claims a task, Epoch posts a Monte Carlo P50/P90 (plus P80/P95) estimate as a task comment, and when the run completes it records that run's wall-clock hours back to Epoch's ledger (auto_wallclock provenance, sanity-gated) so later estimates calibrate. A Hermes Desktop page charts a card's Monte Carlo spread three ways (distribution, chance-done-by curve, 50 dots); it is read-only and never writes the ledger. Dispatcher and worker profiles can differ; the estimate-to-run binding lives next to the ledger, Kanban comments are display only. Also adds an epoch_estimate tool and /epoch. Disclosure — runs `npx -y @kyanitelabs/epoch@0.8.0` as a child process (downloads Epoch and its caret-ranged npm dependencies on first run, which the catalog pin does not cover; needs Node >=22), passing the task title and its three-point hint to the local CLI; the child env is scrubbed (allow-listed PATH/HOME/locale/Node/npm/proxy vars only, the parent environment is never passed through); estimates, actuals and run bindings live under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/epoch/ and are shared by every profile; Epoch telemetry is forced off for plugin runs; no network besides the npm download, no API key; hook work runs on short-lived background threads and unfinished jobs resume when the plugin next loads; the Desktop page reads every Kanban board read-only through Hermes' internal kanban modules and runs a forecast in a throwaway data directory when you open a card; /epoch passes other Epoch subcommands through (it refuses serve, self-improve and telemetry/data mutations, and refuses ledger writes on gateway platforms unless opted in).
entries.title: Epoch
known_issues: First run downloads Epoch from npm; an npm min-release-age policy can block the pinned version until it ages (the job stays queued and retries).

entries.name: equipdash
entries.description: Run a rental or activity business on EquipDash through EquipDash's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.equipdash.com/mcp/v1, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): the day's pickups, returns and sessions, bookings, availability and prices, customers, items, payments, refunds and unsigned waivers. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, with one skill that has the agent preview every change and wait for the person's yes. Disclosure — hosted-only MCP connector to app.equipdash.com (no local code): every tool call sends its arguments there and returns the signed-in business's bookings, customer names and contact details and payment records to Hermes and its model provider; tools can create, move and cancel bookings, send payment links, issue card refunds and email customers. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so Hermes asks before each write-capable call and refuses them in unattended runs; the tool set is served by EquipDash at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. OAuth sign-in requires adding the server to `mcp_servers` in config.yaml (keep `trust: untrusted`) and running `hermes mcp login equipdash`.

entries.name: equitylayer
entries.description: Research CPO or custom AI chips with your own AI. Type /equitylayer:start and Hermes guides you in four decisions, each with a recommended option: sector (with EquityLayer's theses and live readings shown before anything is asked), how to follow it (EquityLayer's published Research Packs for the sector when there are any, its curated readings, your own thesis, or three questions that help you form one), one card to approve, and how often to check. Saying yes all the way follows EquityLayer's CPO Research Packs: their hypotheses, what would prove each wrong, and the readings each one watches, saved, checked and scheduled; in a sector without a Pack it ends with curated readings. EquityLayer's public MCP (https://equitylayer.io/mcp, no sign-in) supplies the tracked variables with caveats and coverage gaps, official events and due dates; the plugin keeps watchlists, thesis harnesses and baselines in local plugin-data, keeps one tracked object at three levels (readings, the person's own thesis, EquityLayer's thesis) behind nine tools, checks them in one Hermes cron job created from the chat, and reports new readings, link statuses (seen, against, late, no data, not due), fired wrong_if conditions, events, what is due next and what needs a person. Nothing becomes the baseline until the person says they read it; unattended runs repeat the alert instead. A local HTML dashboard (built by code from local files and the last public Research Pack registry the plugin fetched; the page has no scripts and makes no network requests) shows it all and is listed under Artifacts in Hermes Desktop. Each new chat recalls the person's research profile, watchlists and theses from the local files. Also lists, reads and follows published EquityLayer Research Packs. Disclosure: every tool call goes over HTTPS to equitylayer.io (/mcp, and /mcp/full on the same server for events and due dates; mcp_url accepts only that host or localhost); thesis text, harness, baseline and variable ids are sent as tool arguments and the server reports it stores neither thesis nor harness; no account, key, payment or telemetry; watchlists, harnesses, baselines, a 30-entry check history, Follow Cards, the research profile (fixed-value fields only), a copy of the public Research Pack registry and the dashboard page with its JSON copy and a calendar file of upcoming dates are written under the plugin's own plugin-data directory; a system prompt section (at most 2,000 characters, off with recall_in_new_chats: false) lists the profile and saved ids, titles and last check dates at the start of each new chat and reaches only the user's own model provider; nothing is written to Hermes memory; no shell commands or background processes. It never says what to buy, sell, size or time, and never writes a view for the person. Not investment advice.

entries.name: escalation-governor
entries.description: Deterministic stuck-detection for Hermes sessions. Watches tool/API failure signals (consecutive tool errors, repeated identical calls, API error bursts, model calls without progress) and, when a threshold trips, injects a structured escalation packet (goal, what was tried, what failed) directing the agent to delegate the remaining work to a stronger model via delegate_task instead of retrying blindly; writes a per-session JSONL report with escalation and token-usage accounting. Disclosure — local code only: injects an escalation packet (the session's first user message and recent tool targets/errors) into tool results and into each following turn's context once a stuck threshold trips, directing the agent to call delegate_task (which spends model usage on a subagent); reads an optional escalation-governor.json and appends one line per session to a shared escalation-governor-reports.jsonl in the Hermes home; adds a /governor status command; opens no network connections, starts no processes and never blocks a tool call.

entries.name: eselsbruecke
entries.description: A helper toolbox for Hermes with tools you switch on and off: a today pad, a pomodoro, a billable time log, a formatter, a colour picker and small tools, which your agent can call for exact answers. Disclosure — local files only, no credentials, no telemetry. The optional "Alerts while Desktop is closed" switch (off by default) writes `scripts/eselsbruecke_alerts.py` into your Hermes profile and adds a no-model Hermes job, `eselsbruecke-alerts`, that runs every minute and delivers due timer and reminder alerts to all of the profile's home channels. entries.name: eu-mode
entries.description: EU Mode (beta): HaloGuard EU, Astroware's guard API hosted in the EU, checks each message and each reply (allow or block). EU Mode looks for personal data in what users send and masks what it finds before the request reaches the model, then puts the originals back in the reply, on your machine. Disclosure — on every turn the conversation's user and assistant text (not system prompts, tool results, files or images) goes to api.astroware.ai (or the HALOGUARD_BASE_URL you set) with your own HaloGuard EU key, up to twice per turn (your message, then the reply); fail-open: if the API does not answer, the message goes on unchecked and not masked, and the reply says so; reads two Hermes settings (session titles, context compression) only to say when they are on; stores SHA-256 fingerprints of blocked messages, never their text.
known_issues: Hermes's automatic session titles and context compression send text to the model without passing through plugins, so that text is not checked or masked. Switch both off as the README shows.
Keep streaming off: with streaming on, a reply appears before EU Mode checks it and puts names back.
The filter can miss personal data, and it can also mask words that are not personal data.
