entries.name: evalroute
entries.description: Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a `claude -p` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES_YOLO_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single_query_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from_lane, to_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max_turns value and harness name the arm ran under and, since evalroute 0.10.0, whether the arm was an explore draw and which default arm it replaced (arm ids only). Disclosure — since evalroute 0.10.0, setting evalroute.explore.fraction in config.yaml (or EVALROUTE_EXPLORE) makes that fraction of routes recommend the lane's runner-up arm from the bundled explore table instead of the default arm (and "hermes evalroute dispatch" then runs that runner-up model), marked on the route card; off by default. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute[encoder]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. Disclosure — since evalroute 0.11.0 the route card and the local ledger row record the harness the caller names (--harness or EVALROUTE_HARNESS), and evalroute.explore.arms in config.yaml lets you declare your own runner-up arm per harness and lane. "hermes evalroute record" appends outcome rows, with any unit id and trace path you pass, to the local ledger; "hermes evalroute compare" reads only the local ledger; "hermes evalroute diagnose" (run by hand only) reads the trace files your ledger rows point at and writes excerpts of them, which may contain your conversation text, to a local directory you name, and calls no model and fetches nothing. contribute never uploads unit ids, trace paths, or rows on your own local: lanes. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute with its hub and decide extras (evalroute[hub,decide]>=0.11.0,<0.12, which add huggingface_hub for sync, contribute and install-encoder, and gonogo-eval for compare), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation.

entries.name: event-read
entries.description: Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list_events and read_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV_USER and CALDAV_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. On Hermes 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host a no-argument list_events still returns the next 7 days and does not record uids. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch reads cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Hermes 0.21.6). The printed cron line uses ctx.profile_name. The file write still uses Hermes's write guard. An update can stop the watch if that guard moves. These reads do not ask for approval and do not register a hook. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.

entries.name: eventforge
entries.description: Proxy the local EventForge control plane into Hermes with approval-gated tools and verified-event context. Disclosure — Each turn, adds up to 8 new signature-verified events from the EventForge control plane (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`) to the prompt, as bounded excerpts marked untrusted. `ef_listen_for_webhook` asks the plane to ensure a provider relay, which may open a public tunnel under the plane's own configuration. With `auto_start` on (default off), an interactive session starts the repository's `eventforge-standalone.cjs` with node and a minimal environment when the plane is down. Approving or rejecting actions and forge drafts, and spawning plane subagents, go through Hermes' approval prompt.

entries.name: evm-token-inspector
entries.description: Inspect any EVM token contract before interacting with it: name, symbol, decimals, total supply, owner/renounced status, EIP-1967 proxy detection, and the DEX V2 pair plus liquidity reserves — one tool, evm_token_check, on BSC, Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum. Read-only; public JSON-RPC only, no API key, no signing, no credentials. Disclosure — read-only: the evm_token_check tool sends the contract address in standard JSON-RPC read calls (via the system curl binary, falling back to Python urllib) to fixed public RPC endpoints (bsc-dataseed.binance.org, bsc.publicnode.com, rpc-bsc.48.club, bsc-dataseed1.ninicoin.io, ethereum.publicnode.com, eth.drpc.org, eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, mainnet.base.org, base.publicnode.com, arb1.arbitrum.io, arbitrum.publicnode.com); no keys, no signing, no transactions. It does not detect honeypots or hidden taxes; it reports on-chain facts (owner, proxy, pair, reserves) for the user to judge, and is not financial advice.

entries.name: exam-desk
entries.description: Practice exams inside Hermes Desktop. Add a paper by asking (Hermes finds an official paper or drafts one to the same pattern), sit it on a server-side timer in Assisted mode beside the chat or in Mock mode, get it scored per question with negative marking and a section split, and review every miss into a one-click drill paper. Disclosure — papers, attempts and evaluations are stored only in the plugin's own data directory, and a paper's figures are served from there by the plugin's own API (one question's figure at a time, never leaving the gateway). Sourcing uses the agent's web tools and AI review uses the agent's configured model, so both go to whatever services the user already configured. The plugin makes no network calls of its own except that the Desktop page loads any http(s) figure URLs a paper contains straight from those hosts when the paper is opened. It runs no shell commands of its own (its skills have the agent run the bundled pack validator/installer scripts), stores no credentials and has no self-updater. Assisted mode feeds the current question to the chat model during a sitting; the answer key never leaves the server until the attempt is submitted.
entries.title: Exam Desk
known_issues: AI review needs plugins.isolation set to in_process; under host isolation evaluation returns 503.
Sourcing a paper needs the agent's web tools; without them, papers are written by hand.

entries.name: exfilbar
entries.description: Per-file transfer routes for Hermes: you list which workspace paths may go to which hosts, and a pre_tool_call hook blocks recognized uploads from terminal and execute_code that leave those routes (curl, wget, scp, rsync, nc, socat, ssh, sftp, mail, HTTPie, git push by opt-in, Python requests/httpx/urllib and more). Protected globs (default private/**, *.env) are never routed. Desktop page shows your routes and an allowed/blocked feed per session; /exfil check explains a dry run. Disclosure: static recognition only, not an egress sandbox; scripts, browser and MCP tools and sibling-hook modifications can bypass it, and unresolved recognized transfers block by default. Stores bounded transfer metadata (paths, scheme and host, decision) and a routes summary in its own plugin data folder; never reads file contents or full commands. No network calls, subprocesses, credentials or telemetry.
entries.title: Exfilbar
known_issues: Static recognition of a bounded command and Python subset; not an egress sandbox or DLP. Uncovered tools (browser, MCP, messaging) and later sibling-hook argument changes can bypass it.
Unresolved recognized transfers block by default (block_unresolved: true), and commands over the parse budget block; both can reject legitimate work.
Paths resolve lexically against the working directory; symlinks are never resolved.
Tested on Hermes v0.23.0 at 2bd378ed1b8d6bf2192cb26e0a55ff3091e6bd19 with Desktop built from source; the floor does not establish later compatibility.

entries.name: exoself
entries.description: An unchosen temperament for every Hermes profile: on the first load it draws one seed into the profile's home and renders it into SOUL.md inside a managed block, then records one experience event per turn and refreshes that block. Two profiles get two different agents, a second load never redraws, and no tool draws a seed. Disclosure — writes $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md (its own managed block only) and $HERMES_HOME/.exoself/, and reads the turn's ask from pre_llm_call in memory to form the event line, which is hashed into the state chain and never stored as text. No network calls, credentials, subprocesses or telemetry; uninstalling leaves the certificate and the block in place.

entries.name: factkit
entries.description: Semantic recall for the built-in holographic memory provider. It reads the provider's store read-only and keeps its own embedding vectors in a separate plugin database (never writing into holographic's tables), adding an embedding-based recall block before each model call, history-aware dedupe so a fact already shown in the conversation is not injected twice, and embedding re-ranking of fact_store search results. Writes are never automatic: conflict, duplicate and TTL actions stay explicit review/apply operations. No core files are patched and the plugin never self-updates. Disclosure - the current user message and the stored fact text are sent to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint configured in the plugin's config (default http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1); point it at a remote host only if you accept that. The endpoint key is read through Hermes' secret scope, never written to the process environment. entries.name: factledger
entries.description: A typed-facts ledger with structural truth — the agent records durable facts (prices, statuses, limits, decisions, capabilities) once and search/show them whenever they matter. For every (scope, subject, predicate) exactly one row is active; a new value closes the previous one (valid_to + superseded_by) instead of overwriting it, so contradictory versions never coexist and history is the audit trail. The full ledger stays queryable on demand, separate from the character-budgeted memory view that is injected every turn. Requests are facts with a lifecycle (task.<verb>): "done" cannot be written without evidence, and an overdue task with a newer fact on the same subject is flagged instead of being presented as still live. Topic recall reports when a term also appears outside the matched subject, so a brief never looks complete by omission. Tools: add, show, search, history, compile, stale, export, check, stats, plus factledger_standalone for the full CLI (brief, topics, audit, tasks, merge-subject). Local-first TSV store, stdlib only, no network, no credentials. Disclosure — none: no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no credential access; every tool reads or writes only the local ledger file.

entries.name: fail-shrink
entries.description: When a pytest, jest, vitest, cargo test, go test, tsc, ruff, or eslint summary line shows, the result is a short block with that place and the same exit code. No summary line, or a poll with only output_preview, stays as Hermes returned it. Disclosure — rewrites long failing pytest/jest/vitest/cargo/go test/tsc/ruff/eslint terminal output into a short block and saves the full (ANSI-stripped, redacted) log under plugin-data/fail-shrink, keeping the newest 40 logs (32 MB) until the plugin data is deleted; the fail_full tool reads those saved logs only, makes no network calls and runs nothing, and is enabled on every platform, so anyone who can message the agent can ask it to read them.

entries.name: fast-chat
entries.description: One-command Fast startup for Hermes CLI/TUI until built-in startup gets easier. Disclosure — `hermes fast-chat` runs the Hermes executable (or the one given with --hermes-bin) without a shell to bootstrap the gateway and may start a long-running gateway that keeps running after it exits; on Hermes releases without `gateway attach` it obtains a single-use session ticket over the local same-user gateway control socket; it reads the active profile's model, fallback-route and display settings from config.yaml (never inline keys) and, when no --model is given, tries the configured fallback routes until one accepts Fast, so the session can open on a different provider/model; sessions it creates (including empty ones left by refused routes) use the Fast/ultrafast service tier, which can cost more with the provider; no telemetry, no credential reads.
entries.title: Hermes Fast Chat
known_issues: Disclosure: runs the selected Hermes executable without a shell; may leave a Gateway running and saves new sessions. Fast/ultrafast may cost more.

Disclosure: reads active-profile configuration and, on legacy versions, its socket pointer; uses authenticated Gateway WebSocket / same-user control socket. Connection grants stay in memory; no provider credential-store reads, telemetry, self-updates, or approval bypass.

Verified on macOS; Linux has not been tested against a live Gateway. Windows is not included in this listing.
Legacy bootstrap depends on the same-user Gateway control protocol; incompatible Gateway contracts fail at launch.

entries.name: fatetell
entries.description: BaZi (Four Pillars) charts, the Chinese almanac and the charts saved in a FateTell account, computed by FateTell's hosted MCP server, plus a skill on reading the results. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with a skill and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP; no local executable code. Disclosure — hosted MCP server at https://mcp.fatetell.com/mcp (remote tool list not covered by the pin); the server calls no language model; cast_bazi_chart and get_almanac work without an account and send a birth date and time, IANA time zone, gender, hemisphere and optional longitude (no place name); the other seven tools need a FateTell account (four of them an active membership) and Hermes native MCP OAuth (`mcp_servers.fatetell` on https://mcp.fatetell.com/login/mcp with `auth: oauth`, then `hermes mcp login fatetell`; through the bundled mcp.json alone those tools answer 401), authorization server https://auth.fatetell.com, Hermes stores the OAuth tokens; create_saved_chart is the only write tool: it adds a chart to the user's account from a display name, gender, birth date and time and a birthplace name, and cannot edit or delete charts; the package marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before that call; birth data, saved charts and account details returned by the tools reach the model provider.

entries.name: faultline
entries.description: Local API flight recorder for debugging HTTP services with Hermes. The agent starts a loopback reverse proxy in front of your service, captures every request and response (auth headers and secret JSON fields redacted before storage), learns an OpenAPI 3.1 contract from healthy traffic and flags drift (type changes, missing fields, 5xx, latency regressions), injects chaos faults (429/5xx, latency, truncated JSON), and after a fix replays the exact failing request to prove 500 -> 200. Ships six tools, a tool_execution middleware, /faultline and `hermes faultline` commands, a bundled skill, a Faultline tab in the web dashboard, and a Hermes Desktop studio page, waterfall pane, status chip and inline ::faultline-trace card. Disclosure — the proxy listens on 127.0.0.1 only and forwards to the target_url you give it (normally local; any http(s) host is accepted except literal link-local, cloud-metadata and reserved addresses and the cloud-metadata hostnames, and the URL may not carry a query, fragment or credentials); replay re-sends captured requests to the upstream they were recorded from only (the agent cannot choose another host), resolves it first and refuses link-local and cloud-metadata addresses, reaches loopback/private targets only when the owner enables the allow_local_replay setting (off by default), and replaying a POST repeats its side effects; captured traffic, contracts and chaos rules are stored in SQLite under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/faultline/; each running proxy is a daemon thread in the Hermes process; no telemetry, no other network calls, no credentials read, no shell commands, no Python dependencies.
entries.title: Faultline
known_issues: Replay against a local service needs the owner setting allow_local_replay: true (off by default). faultline_simulate's built-in service is exempt because the plugin starts it itself.
Redacted auth headers are not replayed; pass fresh ones with faultline_replay(override_headers=...) for authenticated endpoints.
Compressed (gzip/br) response bodies are proxied untouched but stored as a placeholder, so schema drift is only learned from uncompressed JSON.
Chaos rules persist in the database and apply to every running proxy until removed.
Both halves ship opt-in: enable the agent half (hermes plugins enable faultline, then restart the gateway) and flip the Desktop switch in Capabilities -> Plugins.

entries.name: faxforagents
entries.description: Fax preparation, quotes, approved sending, delivery status, cancellation, and inbox reading. The portable package starts faxforagents-mcp 0.4.1 through npx and sends data to api.faxforagents.com. MCP also exposes guidance, capabilities, balance, document previews, review requests, and billed extraction. Write-capable calls use the Hermes untrusted gate. Live sends require quote-bound approval or an allowing delegated policy and spend wallet funds. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned faxforagents-mcp 0.4.1 from npm through npx and runs it as a local child process with only FAXFORAGENTS_API_KEY from your profile; it sends the documents, destination numbers and fax requests you or the agent give it to Fax for Agents' API (api.faxforagents.com) and reads received faxes and their extracted text from it. The server is marked untrusted, so every write-capable call asks first; live sends and paid extraction spend your prepaid wallet, and a delegated policy you set in the Fax for Agents dashboard lets a live send go out without its quote-bound human approval. The tool list comes from the npm package, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. The README's optional workaround for a Hermes OAuth login stall edits a core file (tools/mcp_oauth.py) by hand.

entries.name: feishu-new-topic
entries.description: Feishu/Lark only: a message starting with `#new ` (or the spoken phrase 开启一个新话题) opens a new Feishu topic on that message, which Hermes turns into a new session — a second lane, while the session that was already running keeps running with its turn untouched. That is the difference from `/new`, which interrupts the running turn and clears the conversation. Inside a topic the trigger is stripped, because Feishu topics do not nest; if topic creation fails the message is dispatched normally with a note. Disclosure — Feishu/Lark only. Hooks `pre_gateway_dispatch` (runs before gateway auth) and checks the sender itself with the gateway's authorization probe; unauthorised senders, in-topic messages and cached duplicates cause no calls. For an authorised `#new` message it makes two Feishu OpenAPI calls through the receiving bot's own client (messages/{id}/reply with reply_in_thread, retried up to three times, then messages/{id}/delete of the one-character placeholder), sets the message's thread id so Hermes routes it to a new session, and strips the trigger from the text. Reaches gateway/adapter internals (`_is_user_authorized_for_source`, `_delivery_adapter_for`, the Feishu adapter's `_client` and `_run_blocking`), so a core refactor can stop topic creation (the message is then dispatched normally with a note). Keeps a 40-entry message-id → thread-id dedupe map in plugin state. Appended notes are Chinese-only. Requires plugins.isolation: in_process.
entries.title: Feishu New Topic
known_issues: Feishu only: the plugin is a no-op on every other platform.

Requires plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under host isolation the hook receives a placeholder gateway, so the plugin cannot resolve the receiving bot or the sender's authorization and does nothing.
Topics do not nest: sent inside a topic, the trigger is stripped and the message stays in the current session.
In a group, @-mentioning someone else alongside the bot makes the adapter prepend a [Mentioned: …] hint, so the trigger no longer starts the text and does not fire.
The notes the plugin appends (empty-body placeholder, in-topic note, failure notes) are Chinese-only, whatever language the user writes in.

If Feishu processes the reply but every response is lost, the plugin never learns the thread_id: the message falls back to the current session and the server-side topic can be left orphaned. Retries reuse one request UUID, which makes a duplicate topic unlikely but cannot resolve that ambiguity.

Reads gateway/adapter internals (_delivery_adapter_for, the adapter's _client and _run_blocking). They exist in Hermes 0.22 and are used by bundled plugins, but a Feishu-adapter refactor can break topic creation — the message is then dispatched normally with a note, never dropped.

entries.name: ficelle
entries.description: Model provider for Ficelle, a local OpenAI-compatible router that fails over between free models of the providers you add keys for (not unlimited free access). Disclosure — only when the user selects Ficelle in hermes model and confirms (default no): downloads Ficelle's official bootstrap from an immutable TheBlueHouse75/ficelle-open-core commit, verifies its pinned SHA-256 and runs it with a Python outside Hermes; the bootstrap installs Ficelle Core (SHA-256-pinned wheel from the official GitHub release) into ~/.local/share/ficelle/venv with state and provider keys in ~/.ficelle, links the ficelle commands into ~/.local/bin, and creates a long-running loopback service (LaunchAgent or systemd --user unit, 127.0.0.1:8646) that keeps running after Hermes exits and updates through Ficelle's own updater, outside the plugin; sends one test request to that service; then sets FICELLE_API_KEY (a non-secret local value, only when unset) in the profile's .env and the profile's default model through Hermes helpers. The plugin never asks for, reads or stores provider keys; removing it does not uninstall Ficelle.
entries.title: Ficelle
known_issues: Setup needs an interactive terminal (hermes model); under plugins.isolation host it stops before installing anything.
On Debian or Ubuntu, install python3-venv before selecting Ficelle.
Routing needs at least one provider key stored in Ficelle (ficelle set-key); until then setup stops at Setup required and leaves Hermes unchanged.

entries.name: field-academy
entries.description: The School of Hermes. Hermes will sometimes tell you it saved something when it didn't, and Field Academy teaches you to catch that. In Foundations you work through 11 missions in a throwaway copy of Hermes with one thing quietly broken: you do a real job, say how you think it went, then look at what Hermes actually wrote to its files. After that come 34 missions on five trails in your own Hermes, each trail ending with a Field Record of your work. New in 0.9: Foundations and the trail map. Independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls of its own and no telemetry; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill. It creates and deletes practice profiles (named academy-practice) through Hermes, which copies your provider sign-in into each; Field Academy never reads .env, auth.json or other sign-in files. Before a practice profile's first chat it writes allowlisted settings, memory, a sample skill and sample files into that profile only, and may turn on its memory or skill write-approval setting; it never changes approvals.* or the command allowlist, and never writes your own profiles. Some missions add a filesystem connector (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, pinned) that Hermes downloads with npx, and scheduled practice jobs that, once repaired, run hourly on your model provider until you pause them. AI help (on by default) sends mission text, your answers and key-scrubbed practice excerpts to your own model; the in-chat practice offer (pre_llm_call, interactive sessions only) is off until you turn it on. It reads a file you name (UTF-8, max 5 MiB); on the Guide path it reads Hermes's run-history database read-only, jobs.json and up to 25 log files; progress, practice labs and Field Records stay in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/.
entries.title: Field Academy
known_issues: Live-tested on macOS only. Linux and Windows run the same code and tests, but nobody has walked a mission there in Hermes.

Only the author has walked Field Academy in Hermes; nobody else has finished a trail yet. Walked live on Nov 11, 2026, on Hermes 0.23.1: Foundations mission 3 (Save a fact to memory and check it stuck) end to end, with AI help on Claude and the practice chat on the OpenAI route, and its Field Record saved and checked with shasum. In the connector mission, the practice chat was refused access outside its folder. Every screen was also checked in a test harness.
A repaired practice job runs every hour on your model provider until you pause it or delete the practice profile. Field Academy doesn't pause it for you.
The Field Record is self-issued. Its manifest shows a file changed after saving, but someone who edits the files and the manifest together can fake a pass.
Practice chats get Hermes's own file and terminal tools as any profile does. Hermes's file tools refuse to read sign-in files; a terminal command follows your approval settings.
The peak names drawn on the banner art are small and hard to read; the trail map below names every trail at full size.

entries.name: field-from-above
entries.description: Free Sentinel-2 NDRE and terrain context for a Polish parcel or any point via GUGiK ULDK/NMT and Earth Search STAC. Disclosure — requested parcel IDs or coordinates (as bounding boxes) are sent to uldk.gugik.gov.pl, earth-search.aws.element84.com and services.gugik.gov.pl, and Sentinel-2 band files (up to 400 MB each, several per new scene) are downloaded from sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com into a raster cache capped at 2 GB under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/field-from-above, where the PNG maps are also written; no credentials, shell commands or background processes are used.

entries.name: fieldkit
entries.description: Offline observation forms for Hermes. Describe your work in a Hermes chat and Hermes drafts the forms, then publishes them as a workspace after you approve. Fill them in on a phone with no signal (installable PWA served by the Hermes dashboard: answers, photos, voice notes, GPS and signatures), and sync entries and files back to Hermes when online, with duplicate protection and conflict review. Hermes reads the synced entries and files through 12 tools and analyses them with its own tools when asked. FieldKit never calls a model. Disclosure: the plugin backend makes no third-party calls; the phone app downloads optional translation and OCR packs from huggingface.co and cdn.jsdelivr.net only when the user installs one.

entries.name: film-suite
entries.description: A film studio inside Hermes: write the script, make pictures and video takes on your own GPU through ComfyUI, cut them to music and render the film, with Hermes working in the same project on every page. The bundled Sample film needs no model: open it, change the cut and render an MP4. Disclosure — runs ffmpeg and ffprobe, and the optional analysis engines you install, each with a minimal environment; talks to a ComfyUI on this machine (127.0.0.1:8188, then 127.0.0.1:8000) or at the address set in Hermes Settings › Plugins › Continuo (FILM_SUITE_COMFY_URL overrides it), where prompts and pictures are sent; after 10 minutes without its own work it asks that ComfyUI to free its graphics memory (0 = never, same page); fetches LoRA lookups and previews from Civitai when you ask and style thumbnails from Krea when a style board you open has none cached; the optional engine installers download hash-locked packages from PyPI and PyTorch, a Python runtime through uv (releases.astral.sh), and model files pinned by revision and sha256 from Hugging Face, GitHub and JKU; reads and writes only the folders you approve, plus its own data under the Hermes home and a local cache folder; keeps a per-profile receipt key; treats a request from this computer to its plugin page in the Hermes desktop app as you, after Hermes has authenticated it; no telemetry.

entries.name: fine-print
entries.description: Shows where Hermes silently shrinks, cuts, swaps or hides what the model sees. When a turn ends in which a limit bit and no follow-up by the model was seen, the user gets one card with before/after numbers and the fix (a `hermes config set` command, a workaround, or "hardcoded in v0.23.0"): a web page cut to head and tail, an image downscaled 4x or more, a search page that stopped at 50 with no "more" flag, a failed search backend swapped for the keyless tier, a file read whose lines were all cut at 2,000 chars, terminal output of which under half was kept, a tool result replaced by a 1,500-char preview, a context compaction, loaded images that the request no longer carries, an attached image that reached the model as a helper model's description, a pinned context window that is not in force, a sixth URL that web_extract never requested, a workbook read up to row 5,000 with its hidden sheet skipped. The model gets one short note inside the tool result only where Hermes itself tells nobody. `/limits` shows the session's hits, explains 81 catalogued limits of v0.23.0 (`/limits explain <id>`), replays the same detectors and card policy over your own history (`/limits report`, or `/limits report html` for one self-contained page) and lists every detector with its status (`/limits self-test`): 16 are verified (on real history, or in a live session for limits that leave no stored row) and may raise cards, 19 are fixture-only and only log. Disclosure — no LLM calls, no network, no Python dependencies, no tools, no middleware. Reads tool results in memory through hooks (failed calls included) and, by structure and size only, each request's message lists and the user message of a turn (image parts, Hermes's own placeholder and image notes); keeps a metadata-only ledger (sizes, counts, a URL host or file basename, hashes) in its plugin-data directory. Adds one `_fine_print` key or first line to a tool result for limits where core tells nobody (never on failed calls, images, write_file, patch or skill_manage; `/limits notes off`), and a section of under 1,000 chars to the system prompt of new sessions (`/limits sheet off`). Reads outside its own data, read-only: the profile's session database for `/limits report` (aggregates only; the FINE_PRINT_STATE_DB variable can name another copy), the .xlsx/.docx file that read_file just extracted (to count rows, sheets and tables), and the Hermes config. Writes one file only when asked (`/limits report html`, into the profile's cache folder). Posts one notice per turn into the chat in the CLI and the TUI (in Desktop 0.23.0 the notice call was refused in my check; there the hits are listed by `/limits`); off on messaging platforms by default.

entries.name: finix
entries.description: Age-encrypted profile backups with verified cloud readback and offline extraction; automatic recovery is unavailable. Disclosure — Finix copies your whole Hermes profile, including `.env`, `auth.json`, `config.yaml`, session databases and memories, encrypts it with age to a recipient key you generate, and uploads it to your Google Drive (Hermes-managed `finix:google` OAuth, drive.file scope) or an rclone remote you configure; it runs scheduled backups in the background once you enable them, needs the separately installed `age` and `age-keygen`, and anyone holding the recovery key can read every secret in those backups, so keep the key off the backup host.
entries.title: Finix
known_issues: Experimental beta. Automatic default replacement and named-profile import/activation are disabled pending a supported public recovery contract. Retained journals are not replayed.
Google Drive uses only the declared Hermes-managed finix:google client with drive.file; owning-profile client configuration and consent are required. The Workspace skill backend is removed.
Current Linux CLI/Desktop cloud backup and externally orchestrated cold data recovery are verified; current native Windows GUI/cloud and unrestricted historical-suite acceptance are not claimed.
Requires separately installed age and age-keygen. Keep independent backups and the recovery key off the backup host.

entries.name: fiscalisto
entries.description: Mexican electronic invoicing (CFDI 4.0) and SAT taxes through Fiscalisto's hosted MCP server (https://fiscalisto.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with per-company grants and read / draft / stamp scopes, no keys in config): search issued and received CFDI, draft, stamp, email and cancel invoices, payment receipts, credit notes, advances, payroll receipts, the month's VAT and ISR estimate, SAT 69-B supplier checks, and SAT documents (constancia, opinión de cumplimiento, buzón tributario). Bundles an English overview skill and thirteen Spanish workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only; OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure: every tool call goes to fiscalisto.com and acts on the companies the user approved, with their own role; stamping registers a CFDI with the SAT through Fiscalisto's PAC and uses a stamp from the user's plan, and the server refuses a stamp or cancellation without a confirmation token from a preview. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in opens a local callback port and stores OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. No telemetry. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: fish-audio
entries.description: Your agent speaks and listens with Fish Audio: expressive voices in 80+ languages, voices you design from a sentence, and live word-by-word dictation. The official Fish Audio plugin: Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop and word-by-word live dictation captions (stt.streaming: true); streaming and live dictation need Hermes 0.21.6 or newer, and on 0.21.5 replies use whole-file speech and dictation is transcribed as a file. Adds the fish_speak, fish_voices, fish_transcribe, fish_settings, fish_account and fish_pronunciations tools, /fish and hermes fish commands (including /fish setup, a checklist that ends by offering a spoken sample with /fish preview), and six skills. Also: voice auditions (up to four voices reading your passage), replies as a voice note or an audio file, long-form chapter narration with a resumable manifest, translate-and-voice for clips with several speakers, saved voice names in any script, editing your own voices on Desktop, and hermes fish speak, transcribe, voices and balance with --json for scripts. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to Fish's native realtime speech-to-text at api.fish.audio (transcribe-stream-1, Preview) while you speak, billed $0.36 per hour of open session, per second, including silence; a session opens with the first audio and closes once Fish confirms the last words (the plugin stops waiting after 15 seconds), or 30 seconds after the last audio of a cancelled recording; if a live session fails or returns no text, Hermes transcribes the recording as a file instead, a separate billed request; the live_transcription: compat setting uses Fish's older realtime endpoint instead, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model (free through 30 November 2026), whose requests Fish may use to improve its models; when no model is set and your Fish wallet shows no API credit, free credit or past top-up, the plugin uses that free model (allow_free_model: false turns this off). The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH_API_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples, cover images and recordings it uploads must be regular audio or image files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page, the /fish and hermes fish commands and the fish_settings tool can set or reset the profile's Fish model, voice and reading speed and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config, so the agent can choose its own voice under the same rules; fish_pronunciations sends the pronunciation dictionary names, descriptions and rules you ask for to api.fish.audio (dictionary management is free; speech that uses a dictionary is billed as usual), can store up to three dictionary references as the profile's default in its config, and deleting a dictionary or a version goes through Hermes's approval gate; /fish setup lists what the profile still needs without a Fish call and reads the key only through the secret scope; auditions are one billed clip per voice; the Desktop editor sends the title and description you type for your own voice to api.fish.audio; hermes fish speak --out copies the audio and subtitles to the path you give and refuses to overwrite a file unless you pass --force; fish_speak output_path copies them to a path the agent gives, never overwrites a file, and refuses paths Hermes's write guard protects; on operator-managed agents a cloned or saved voice gets a saved name in the profile config automatically; the long-form skill saves chapter files and a manifest in the folder you choose, with the agent's own file tools; /fish preview with no voice plays a short billed sample in the profile's voice; fish_account reads the Fish wallet like /fish balance and estimates costs from a dated price table without a network call; /fish use and hermes fish use also make Fish the speech provider when none is set, and given a voice title they search your own Fish voices for it, and hermes fish login sets the speech and transcription providers when they are unset or you confirm. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. When you ask for a voice that fits the agent, the voice-studio skill reads the agent's SOUL.md or persona and sends Fish a one- or two-sentence voice description, never the whole persona. Includes a report-a-problem skill: when you report a problem with Fish Audio, the agent runs hermes fish doctor --no-synth, /fish status, hermes --version and hermes plugins list --json, reads recent Hermes log lines that mention Fish, searches this plugin's GitHub issues for a few key words, drafts a bug report and files it to this plugin's repository as a public GitHub issue or comment with your gh login only after you approve the exact text; reports leave out keys, credit amounts and voice ids not confirmed as public library voices, and security problems go to the repository's private advisory form instead. No telemetry.
entries.title: Fish Audio
known_issues: Hermes's text normaliser alters <|speaker:N|> markup and Drama 3 closing tags such as </whisper> on the plain text_to_speech path; use fish_speak for multi-speaker speech and Drama 3 word tags (NousResearch/hermes-agent#133131).
An empty API key field in Settings is hard to see, worst in the dark theme; a fix is proposed (NousResearch/hermes-agent#138994).

In Hermes Desktop voice conversations, part or all of a reply sometimes goes unspoken because Desktop stops passing it to speech mid-turn; this affects every speech provider, and fixes are proposed (NousResearch/hermes-agent#129305).
Under plugins.isolation: host the hermes fish terminal command is unavailable and voice replies use whole-file speech instead of streaming; /fish, the tools and both providers still work.

entries.name: fitbit-mcp
entries.description: Read the user's Fitbit activity, heart rate, sleep and body data through the local fitbit MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Fitbit. Runs the `fitbit-mcp-unofficial@0.7.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official Fitbit Web API. The user creates their own Fitbit developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.fitbit-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to Fitbit's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Hermes credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.hermes/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: fitbit_profile_update (local profile only); fitbit_exchange_code (stores OAuth tokens locally); fitbit_revoke_access (revokes the Fitbit grant and deletes local tokens). The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

entries.name: fixmyscan
entries.description: Turn scanned books (PDF or DjVu, up to 1,000 pages) into clean, searchable PDFs for Kindle, Kobo, reMarkable and tablets through FixMyScan's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.fixmyscan.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE, no keys in config): crop pages to the text, straighten them, make them sharp black and white or greyscale, split two-page spreads and add a searchable text layer, then return a download link. Bundles the fixmyscan workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to FixMyScan's server at mcp.fixmyscan.com, signed in as the user through FixMyScan's OAuth sign-in, and counts against that account's FixMyScan allowance or plan. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. fix_scan uploads the user's file or downloads the public link they give; files are deleted 24 hours after a book is ready. Write-capable tools: fix_scan and create_upload_link (start a book), cancel_scan and delete_scan (stop or delete one of the user's books). Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. The package marks the server untrusted. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add fixmyscan --url https://mcp.fixmyscan.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401 on tool calls.

entries.name: flashdata-plugin
entries.description: Web search with Google Search; Google News, Google Images, Google Shopping, Google Video Search and Google Places for research. Use YouTube Search or YouTube Extended Search; retrieve YouTube metadata, YouTube transcripts, YouTube captions and YouTube channel data; get YouTube autocomplete; inspect YouTube trainability as license-label metadata, not training permission. YouTube downloads deliver media to your own storage. One hosted MCP connection and 15 task Skills; bring your own API key and paid FlashData Credits. Disclosure — Connects to FlashData's hosted MCP service (data.flashdata.dev) with your own FLASHDATA_API_KEY; every search, YouTube read or download spends your paid FlashData Credits, and Hermes asks before running only the tools the server does not mark read-only, so most paid searches run without a prompt. The YouTube download tool sends the storage bucket and storage access credentials you supply to FlashData, and those values stay visible in the chat history.

entries.name: fledge
entries.description: Skills have to earn their wings. Before Hermes saves or rewrites a skill, Fledge checks what actually happened in the run it learned from (tools still failing when the turn ended, a failed or interrupted turn, the user correcting the agent in the next message, /undo or a /rollback restore right after, denied approvals), using only facts Hermes reports through hooks: no model grades the model. A save learned from a bad run is held in Hermes' own skills pending queue with the reasons (review from any chat with /fledge pending|diff|approve|reject, or /skills pending in the CLI); a foreground save after errors goes through Hermes' approval prompt, and unattended runs queue instead of waiting. New and rewritten skills start on probation: clean real runs graduate them, repeated bad runs ground them, and a save from a run the user corrected right after is grounded at once; a grounded skill Hermes created on its own is archived (hermes curator restore brings it back), skills the user asked for are only reported. Skills the user edited by hand are fingerprinted, and autonomous rewrites or deletes of them become proposals in the same queue (optionally Hermes' content lock). Modes: enforce, watch (records only), off. Disclosure — nine hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_session_end, on_session_finalize, on_session_reset, on_skill_lifecycle, pre_command, post_approval_response); pre_tool_call blocks or asks for approval on skill_manage only and lets the write through on its own errors (a write already queued for review stays held); reads hook payloads (tool statuses and error text, the first 280 characters of the next user message) and skill folders to fingerprint them; writes its own SQLite under each profile's plugin-data/fledge (skill names, fingerprints, verdict reasons, session/turn ids; reasons quote the matched correction phrase and up to 80 characters of a tool error, hold summaries the skill's one-line description; no other message text, no skill bodies), held writes into pending/skills/, and archives grounded agent-created skills into skills/.archive/; calls tools.skill_provenance, tools.write_approval and tools.skill_usage (the functions behind /skills pending and hermes curator archive/lock) because no public seam exists yet, each guarded; no network, no model calls, no credentials, no shell commands, never approves anything. Needs plugins.isolation in_process to tell background-review writes from foreground ones. Measured on 2026-11-10: 153 tests passed on Python 3.14 and 3.11; `hermes plugins validate` passes on Hermes 0.23.1, 0.23.0 and 0.22.7 with only the private-import warnings above; live sessions with a real model in isolated HERMES_HOMEs (bad-run hold, approve onto probation, grounding after a correction, hand-edit proposal and approval prompt, watch mode, 13 clean writes with 0 holds, fail-open under a locked database) in VALIDATION.md, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-11-05.txt and tests/profiles-2026-11-10.txt.

entries.name: fleet-policy
entries.description: For administrators who pin settings through the managed scope: records what each agent role really sends to the provider (model, reasoning effort, service tier, plus the tier the provider says it served) next to the managed-scope state and the effective config (`hermes fleet-policy status --json`); measures cron cost per job — runs, empty runs, $/day, gate present (`crons --cost`); and `watch`, a generic wake gate for cron scripts that replays one read tool on an MCP server and wakes the agent only when new item ids appear (stock `wakeAgent` gate, no LLM call otherwise). entries.name: flightdeck
entries.description: Live air-traffic control for your agents and model servers — which agent holds which local GPU slot, who's queued, plan usage on cloud lanes, and opt-in capacity-aware subagent placement. Disclosure — records LLM request metadata (ids, profile, session, model, provider, base_url, timings, token counts, finish/error status, a clipped error message and a subagent's goal text; no prompts, message text, tool arguments or credentials) from every profile into one machine-wide SQLite file at <hermes root>/plugin-data/flightdeck/requests.db; reads every profile's config.yaml (provider base URLs, model names and its own settings only; the files can contain api_key values, which it never extracts, stores or sends) and every profile's state.db (session titles, read-only); sends GET-only metrics probes to declared model servers or to auto-discovered private/loopback provider URLs on each poll; the Desktop page reads plan usage through Hermes's model.options RPC; opt-in capacity routing (off by default) changes which local server delegate_task subagents run on.
entries.title: Flightdeck
known_issues: Cloud lanes are Hermes-observed only: providers do not publish server load, so cloud numbers cover this machine's Hermes traffic, not the provider's fleet.
Plan usage on cloud cards depends on the provider's usage hook and can be briefly unavailable; it is shown as unavailable, not as zero.

Capacity routing is opt-in and local-only: it requires route_delegation: true and delegation.backend: flightdeck, and only inner_backend: default is supported; any other inner_backend reports routing unavailable and refuses to arm.

entries.name: flightlog
entries.description: Flight recorder for Hermes. Records every tool call, model call, subagent and approval to local SQLite and flags runs that finish green but went wrong: tool errors the answer hides, loops, token spikes and effort collapse against each cron job's own baseline, failed subagents behind a "done", and "tests pass" claims with no passing check after the last edit. Flagged runs get a short incident report, a footer on the reply, per-step timelines in the CLI, dashboard tab and desktop page, and an opt-in loop tripwire that hands the 5th repeat to Hermes's own approval prompt. Disclosure — local only: no network calls, subprocesses or background services beyond one in-process SQLite writer thread; stores short redacted previews of every tool call's arguments and result in $HERMES_HOME/flightlog/flightlog.db (pruned after 30 days); flagged runs' redacted evidence goes to your configured model via ctx.llm for the incident report; appends a footer to agent replies when a run is flagged, and by default (break_silence) makes a flagged [SILENT] cron job post that note instead of staying silent; the opt-in loop tripwire registers a pre_tool_call hook that sends the 5th identical call to Hermes's approval prompt.

entries.name: flota
entries.description: Run delegate_task subagents on your own machines over SSH (delegation.backend: flota). Flota wakes the chosen machine (Wake-on-LAN, a relay host on its LAN, any command, or the machine's own wake timer), falls back to another machine if it does not come up, and suspends it after its last subagent, never a busy one (the model cannot force it). The agent tool checks and wakes machines; asking it to suspend or power one off is opt-in and every such call goes through Hermes' approval prompt. `hermes flota setup user@host` detects OS, MAC, broadcast and how the machine can sleep; `doctor` prints fixes; `uninstall` undoes it; fleet pairing with two codes (public keys only); a fleet map page for Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard. Python standard library only. Disclosure — runs ssh to the machines you configure and your own wake/sleep commands, sends Wake-on-LAN packets on your LAN, can run `sudo -n` for one fixed wake-alarm command only if you allow it, creates an SSH key pair without a passphrase (`~/.ssh/flota_ed25519`) when you have none and adds that public key to a ship's `authorized_keys` at pairing as an ordinary login line with no `command=` or `restrict` options, creates `flota-<machine>` Hermes profiles with `terminal.ssh_sync_files: false`, lets the agent suspend or power off a machine only if you turn on `agent_power_actions` and approve each call, and keeps auto-sleep timers in the gateway process; no third-party network calls, no telemetry.
entries.title: Flota
known_issues: Only one delegation backend is active at a time; delegation.backend: flota replaces any other delegation route.
Auto-sleep timers live in the running process, so auto-sleep needs a long-lived gateway.
Hermes routes the tasks of one delegate_task call sequentially, so a slow wake delays the later tasks of that batch.
Hooks carry no route, so subagents are matched to machines by calling thread plus goal text; identical goals for different machines from the same thread can still be mixed up.
Plain Wake-on-LAN needs the Hermes host on the machine's LAN; use wake: wol_via, wake: command or wake: timer across networks.
The hermes flota sleep/off CLI and the dashboard see busy machines only while a gateway is running (it publishes busy counts to a state file); without one they cannot tell.
One busy-state file per profile: a gateway and a separate chat session running subagents at the same time overwrite each other's counts.
A machine with wake: timer cannot be woken on demand; a task for it waits only if its own alarm is due within wake_timeout.
macOS and Windows ships are experimental and untested on real hardware; wake: timer is unit-tested only.

SSH file sync is still on: Flota sets terminal.ssh_sync_files: false in its machine profiles, but Hermes does not read that key until core issue #148726 is resolved (PRs #148791, #145271), so a subagent on a Flota machine copies this host's ~/.hermes files there and tars the machine's ~/.hermes back, slow on a machine with its own Hermes install. hermes flota doctor warns about it.

The agent tool's sleep and off actions are off by default (agent_power_actions); when turned on, each call needs the user's approval, so unattended runs (cron, no gateway) cannot use them, and the change reaches the model in new sessions.
hermes plugins validate warns about private core imports (profiles, cron jobs, atomic config write); a core release can break them.

entries.name: flower-shop
entries.description: An AI business operating workspace inside Hermes Desktop for a small flower shop: a business manager plus sales, inventory, production, finance, and logistics agents work from one SQLite record of orders, stock, production, deliveries, and money. Agents propose, the owner approves - order confirmation, stock receipts, adjustments, wastage, payments, and expenses create a pending approval decided by the owner from an inline chat card or the Approvals inbox (an opt-in chat relay, off by default, still confirmed through Hermes' approval prompt). Includes Overview, Orders, Inventory and recipes, Production board, a read-only low-poly 3D Shop Floor fed by live production state, Delivery, Finance estimates labelled as estimates, an AI Team page, and a guided setup with removable demo data. The repo also ships an optional matching Hermes skin (a light and a dark variant) that the setup offers but never applies on its own. Not flower-specific: the same shape - one record of what was ordered, stocked, made, shipped and paid, agents that propose, an owner who approves - fits any small physical business. Disclosure - all business data stays in one local SQLite database under the Hermes plugin-data directory; the plugin makes no network calls, stores no credentials, runs no shell commands, and sends no telemetry. Not an accounting ledger: finance figures are operational estimates plus recorded payments and expenses. Single shop, single user; no WhatsApp parsing, no bouquet canvas, no multi-branch support. Disclosure — all business data stays in one local SQLite database under the Hermes plugin-data directory; the plugin makes no network calls, stores no credentials, runs no shell commands and sends no telemetry; choosing its theme copies two bundled skin files into the Hermes skins directory and reads the active skin setting, and the skin switches only when the owner clicks; assistant profiles are created only when the owner clicks Create on the Desktop team step; design references must be image files in the plugin's uploads folder, which the local dashboard serves; approving from chat is off by default and, when turned on, every decision still goes through Hermes' approval prompt. Finance figures are operational estimates plus recorded payments and expenses, not an accounting ledger; single shop, single user.

entries.name: flowlight
entries.description: Watch public wallets and draw live on-chain money flows as glowing arcs. Read-only. Uses public NEAR, Blockscout, and RPC endpoints. When Intents Pay is installed, reads its invoice ledger and may GET 1-Click /v0/status. Never signs or sends transactions and never handles keys. entries.title: Flowlight
known_issues: Base and Arbitrum Blockscout often answer HTTP 403 from datacenter networks. Flowlight falls back to public JSON-RPC logs for major tokens and says so.
A busy address is summarized over the largest recent slice that fits the time budget, not every transfer in the requested 24h.
purefile1686.near had no fungible or native transfers in the public recent history during the 10 Nov 2026 live run. The node still draws.
Intents Pay is optional. If its ledger is missing, Flowlight reports that no Intents Pay invoices were found and keeps working.
The gold paid burst in the demo fixture is labeled DEMO FIXTURE. It is not a live settlement.

entries.name: flowsery
entries.description: Privacy-first web analytics through Flowsery's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.flowsery.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): visitors, sessions, bounce rate, time series, real-time visitors, breakdowns by page, referrer, channel, campaign, country and device, goals and revenue attribution, single visitor journeys, and the bugs and UX problems Flowsery found in session recordings. Bundles the flowsery workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Flowsery's hosted server (mcp.flowsery.com) and acts on the user's Flowsery account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Most tools are read-only; track_goal and track_payment record goal and payment events in the user's analytics (no money moves), delete_goals and delete_payments permanently remove those events, and update_issue_status changes an issue. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: fluent
entries.description: Your agent becomes fluent in any program: checks the agent's terminal commands against the real --help and man pages of the programs you adopt, before they run. A long option the installed version doesn't have is stopped with the closest real one (--crf → -crf, --ammend → --amend), and subcommands it classifies as destructive (gh repo delete, docker image prune, rsync --delete) go to Hermes's own approval prompt. Adds /fluent (adopt, show, forget, undo, mode), an @cli:<program> context reference and a dashboard tab that draws the agent's tree (a branch per program, a fruit per error caught). Tested on 333 real valid commands (0 blocked) and 22 typical mistakes (22 caught), including the tar macOS ships. Disclosure — /fluent adopt <program> runs that program on the host (not the terminal backend) with --version/-version/version/-V and --help/-h/help, plus <command> --help per subcommand only when the help carries a git, Go/cobra, argparse or click marker (git: --list-cmds and <command> -h; ffmpeg: -h full; curl: --help all; git filter-branch is never run): no shell, closed stdin, empty temp cwd, own process group, filtered environment (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, TMPDIR, XDG dirs; no keys or tokens), 5 s per call, about 25 s per program; a program that ignores those arguments runs normally. It reads man pages and terminal.backend from config.yaml; in block mode (default) pre_tool_call vetoes commands with options the installed program lacks and escalates destructive ones to Hermes's approval prompt with a per-subcommand rule key, never approving anything (unattended runs follow Hermes policy, default deny); posts one-line notices; writes only under its plugin data directory; makes no network, model or telemetry calls.
entries.title: fluent
known_issues: Only acts on the local terminal backend and on long options of commands it read with high confidence; it trusts the binary on Hermes's own PATH, so a different copy on a session PATH (venv, nvm, direnv) can be judged against the wrong help.

Risk classes are name and help-summary heuristics that only add prompts: many destructive forms are not asked about (git stash drop, gh api -X DELETE, rsync --delete-excluded), and its copy of Hermes's own patterns can drift, so a command may occasionally be asked twice.
In cron and other unattended runs, commands fluent flags as destructive are refused under Hermes's default approval policy; use /fluent risk off or approvals.cron_mode for jobs that must delete.
Live adoption progress and 'fluent caught' notices need the in-process gateway (default plugins.isolation). Tested on Linux; Windows is untested.

entries.name: fluxer-platform
entries.description: Fluxer messaging with reliable replies, attachments, rich cards, read-only guild tools, and opt-in threads and experimental voice. Connects to Fluxer and configured speech services; optional voice runs background Python processes and reads configured local context and session data. Disclosure — Reads Hermes's own session store (state.db, read-only) to name Fluxer threads after session titles; its four model tools read Fluxer channel messages, search results, guild members and the guild audit log through the configured Fluxer API (api.fluxer.app or FLUXER_BASE_URL), limited to the home guild unless FLUXER_TOOL_SCOPE=global. Optional voice (off by default) runs background Python processes, reads a configured context file and session database, runs a user-configured local speech-to-text command through the shell, and sends voice audio and reply text to the speech services you configure: api.x.ai, api.groq.com, api.elevenlabs.io, or a Kokoro endpoint you set (FLUXER_VOICE_KOKORO_URL).

entries.name: focus
entries.description: Cognitive context engine for Hermes Agent. Intercepts turns before inference, extracts true intent and entities, prioritizes repository governance, selectively ingests memory, and injects winning skills in a single step with zero KV-cache mutation. entries.name: foreman
entries.description: A green check the agent did not rig. A deterministic gate (no model, standard library and git) blocks git commit, git push and gh pr create when the change skips, deletes or moves tests, weakens what the check runs, bypasses hooks or carries a secret, and always blocks an agent-run gh pr merge; an optional second model reviews what rules cannot see, such as a loosened assertion. /foreman shows each pull request with a verdict and merges only on your command; a Desktop panel shows where each change is. Disclosure — runs read-only git in your repository; runs the GitHub CLI only on /foreman commands (merge and reject write to GitHub after your confirmation) and model calls only on /foreman commands or, with auto_review: finish, inside the agent's turn; notifications are off until you turn them on; no telemetry, no credentials, no network calls of its own. Full disclosure in the README.

entries.name: foresee
entries.description: Let AI assistants shop for home and auto insurance: compare instant quotes across every carrier. Connects to the hosted Foresee MCP server (Streamable HTTP at agents.go-foresee.com), with three workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package (hosted MCP server plus three skills), no Python and nothing runs locally; the vendor is Foresee Insurance Services, LLC (go-foresee.com). Every quote request sends the profile the user gives in chat (ZIP, age or date of birth, vehicles, drivers, driving record, home details) to agents.go-foresee.com with no account or API key. The live_carrier_quotes tool additionally sends the user's identity (name, date of birth, street address, email, optionally phone and driver's licence number) and, after the user's in-chat consent recorded verbatim, Foresee's agents submit those details to the selected insurance carriers, who may run a soft credit-based insurance score pull and contact the user. Foresee does not take payment or bind policies.

entries.name: forgebox
entries.description: Try-then-commit Git worktree workflow for Hermes Agent. Snapshots dirty repositories and journals tool calls. Best-effort hooks redirect known file paths and command working directories; shell command text is unchanged. This is not an OS sandbox and does not contain shell writes or external side effects. Review and apply changes explicitly with forgebox apply or the dashboard/Desktop panel, or discard the worktree. Requires Git on PATH. Disclosure — redirects the agent's file-tool paths and terminal working directories into a git worktree under `<repo>/.forgebox/` while a session is active and blocks file-tool paths outside that repo (shell command text is not rewritten, so this is not a sandbox); applying copies the reviewed worktree changes into your real checkout and can create a git commit, which runs your repository's own git hooks.

entries.name: forgebruecke
entries.description: A bridge between Hermes and your self-hosted Forgejo: Hermes works as its own account, writes follow Hermes' approval setting, and a desk in Hermes Desktop shows the pull requests that wait for you. Disclosure — Talks only to the Forgejo address you set, as a separate Hermes account whose token you provide; the optional personal write token is used only for the desk's Merge and Comment buttons on your click, and is available to Hermes. Per-repo flows run a background loop in the gateway that reviews new pull requests by starting `hermes -p <reviewer profile> chat` processes, which send each pull request's title, description and diff to that profile's model provider and post the verdict as a comment. The "Create a reviewer profile" button clones your profile (config.yaml, SOUL.md and every key in .env) into `forgebruecke-reviewer`, then removes its memories and the two Forgebrücke tokens through `hermes` commands. The optional mention channel, once enabled in the profile, answers Forgejo mentions from any commenter on repos where mentions are on. The git credential helper setup prints `git config --global` lines for you to run.
entries.title: Forgebrücke
known_issues: Needs a Forgejo account for Hermes, added as a collaborator on each repo, with a token for read:notification, write:issue, write:repository and read:user.
A new setup only previews writes. Switch on "Let Hermes write" in Settings, Plugins, Forgebrücke.
With Hermes on a server, install the plugin on the Desktop computer too, on the same version: Desktop loads the desk from its own computer.

Disclosure — the skills use Fotor's hosted MCP service (mcp.fotor.com), which you add separately with OAuth; image, video and audio jobs spend credits on your Fotor account, and local files you ask it to use are uploaded to Fotor's storage. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.23.1.

entries.name: found
entries.description: FOUND, the AI SDR for LinkedIn and email, through FOUND's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.foundtofind.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): warm leads found from buying signals with the reason for each, pipeline and campaign numbers, account research, new companies and the right contact at a company, work emails, drafted messages, lists, and paused campaigns with their sequences. Bundles the found-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to FOUND's hosted server (app.foundtofind.com) and acts on the user's FOUND account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Some tools spend FOUND credits (FOUND states they quote the price first and spend only on a confirming second call), and FOUND states campaigns created from Hermes start paused; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: frame
entries.description: Frame, a verification-driven security agent: scans source for vulnerabilities (SQL injection, command injection, XSS, path traversal, SSRF, deserialization and more) by taint analysis whose paths Z3 checks, in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, C# and C/C++; verifies fixes; records baselines; generates verified fixes; and answers engine queries (entry points and whether they are protected, data flows, callers, the guards on every path to a line). Bundles a frame:frame skill for security reviews. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: the server runs locally as `uvx --from frame-mcp==0.3.0 --with frame-security[scan]==1.1.7 frame-mcp` (Apache-2.0), fetched from PyPI on first run, so the PyPI packages are not covered by the pinned sha; needs uv. It reads the files it is asked to scan; write_baseline writes the named baseline file and fix writes files only with in_place. Plain scans make no network calls; scan with ai or hunt_authz, fix and exploit send source code to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint the user sets in FRAME_LLM_BASE_URL / FRAME_LLM_MODEL / FRAME_LLM_API_KEY (passed through only when set), and exploit sends requests to the target the user names. The engine_* tools keep one frame query --serve process per project. No telemetry. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before write_baseline, fix and exploit and refuses them in unattended runs; every other tool is annotated read-only. Tool-call timeout raised to 1800 s for large scans.

entries.name: freebusy
entries.description: Books meetings over email or chat from free or busy time only, with any CalDAV calendar and any IMAP/SMTP mailbox; every slot is held before it is offered. Disclosure — Fixture mode is the default: no network calls, demo data only. Connectors mode, switched on by /freebusy connect once its test passes, talks only to the CalDAV, IMAP and SMTP servers the owner sets up (https/TLS only, private and loopback addresses refused), plus one unauthenticated check of the owner's email domain for /.well-known/caldav during setup; app passwords are typed in a terminal and kept in the system keychain, never in config or chat. In that mode it reads only busy times, writes holds and bookings to the one calendar the owner picks (or a local feed file), reads only mail addressed to its agent address, and sends scheduling replies, invites and owner notes by SMTP without a per-message prompt, within the owner's groups, tiers and its own policy gate. Holds, settings and a redacted audit log stay in its data folder; a short scheduling context is added each turn. pre_tool_call gates its own actions, and other plugins' mail and calendar tools only with vet_other_tools. post_gateway_admission answers only admitted chat senders the owner lists in chat_contacts; everyone else reaches the agent as usual. Reminders are owner-only cronjob_manage jobs. Google adapter inert until 0.4.
entries.title: Freebusy
known_issues: CalDAV and IMAP/SMTP are tested against local Radicale and GreenMail servers and recorded provider replies, not yet against iCloud, Fastmail, Zoho or Nextcloud themselves.
Travel buffers read locations only on fixture data; the CalDAV adapter does not read locations yet.
No background mail watcher: /freebusy check runs one pass, and the owner can schedule it with Hermes cron.

entries.name: freeze
entries.description: Let Hermes do a task once, then replay it without the model: /freeze turns the last turn's tool calls into a checked workflow (bindings, loops over lists, and model-worked values compiled into Python that must reproduce the recording exactly), and hermes freeze run repeats it with 0 model calls, stops on drift, never overwrites a file you edited, and hermes freeze schedule makes it a no-agent cron job. Disclosure — hooks record each turn's task, tool arguments, tool results (truncated at 256 KB), final answer and token counts in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/freeze/data.db, pruned after 14 days (at load and at most hourly while recording); /freeze makes model calls through your active model (one per compiled step, at most 3 attempts) and sends the task, shortened tool results and the recorded value; replays repeat every recorded tool call except clarify, todo, memory, delegate_task, session_search, skill tools, vision/image/speech tools, mixture_of_agents, cronjob_manage, send_message and tool search (so terminal, file, execute_code, browser, MCP and plugin tool calls are re-run) through Hermes' own tools and Hermes' approvals (unattended runs follow approvals.cron_mode, default deny), and run model-compiled code with no Hermes approval in a separate python -I process with static and runtime module allowlists, no environment variables beyond PATH, and a 10 s timeout; /freeze run starts hermes freeze run as a child process, --fallback agent starts hermes chat; schedule writes <HERMES_HOME>/scripts/freeze-<name>.sh and creates a cron job with hermes cron create --no-agent that reports drift and stops (only with --fallback agent does it start hermes chat on drift, which costs model calls); no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.
