entries.name: freight-reconciliation
entries.description: Payer-side freight reconciliation: import carrier bills and trip ledgers into a deterministic local core (SQLite, WAL, no cloud), re-calculate against contracted rates and produce evidence-linked difference lists for human review — 14 MCP tools over uvx stdio (engine pinned to the immutable commit e8cd259c, release v0.4.1), with 3 bilingual workflow skills bundled. Never approves payments, sends messages or writes back to ERP/TMS; final confirmations route through a local admin page the model cannot reach. entries.name: freshdesk
entries.description: Generic Freshdesk API v2 tools for Hermes Agent. Unaffiliated community connector, not a Freshworks product. Disclosure — calls the account's native Freshdesk HTTPS origin with profile-scoped secrets FRESHDESK_DOMAIN and FRESHDESK_API_KEY; downloads an attachment into the Hermes cache only from that ticket's own attachment hosts; the five write tools (private note, create ticket, public reply that Freshdesk emails to the ticket's requester, time entry, status/priority update) escalate to Hermes human approval and fail closed when no person is present. No third-party dependencies, shell commands, telemetry, or self-updater.

entries.name: freshness-sidecar
entries.description: Notes bound to a source file: before every turn each note's file is re-hashed, so the agent is told a fact is STALE (or MISSING) the moment its file changes, instead of confidently repeating an outdated value. /fresh add|list|check|forget works from the CLI and messaging gateways without the model; a freshness_note tool exposes the same actions to the model. Runs alongside any memory provider (does not take the memory.provider slot). Disclosure — reads explicitly registered local files within the session's workspace to compute bounded SHA-256 checks (1 MiB cap; symlinks, files outside the workspace and credential-looking files are refused). Stores note text, paths and hashes in profile-scoped plugin data. Selected notes and status snapshots are added to the user turn sent to the configured model and persist in Hermes history; forgetting a note stops future recall but does not erase copies already in history. FRESH means matching bytes, not verified truth. No network calls, subprocesses, background services, credential access or self-update.

entries.name: frihet
entries.description: Official Hermes Agent integration for Frihet — discoverability, setup, diagnostics, and operating guidance for the Frihet MCP. Zero duplicated tools; the canonical Frihet MCP surface stays in @frihet/mcp-server and the remote endpoint https://mcp.frihet.io/mcp. Disclosure — /frihet setup and /frihet doctor send an unauthenticated MCP initialize to mcp.frihet.io (or FRIHET_MCP_URL); /frihet doctor also makes one read-only list_invoices call through Hermes's MCP client once you grant plugins.entries.frihet.mcp_allowlist; /frihet brief uses get_business_context, list_invoices, list_quotes, list_expenses, list_clients, and list_client_activities through the same MCP client to display business data in the current session, without writes; reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml only to check that an mcp_servers.frihet block exists; the pre_tool_call hook prompts before Frihet MCP calls it classifies as irreversible or unknown, but reads and draft-first creates pass without a prompt unless the server sets trust: untrusted.

entries.name: fusen
entries.description: Fusen (付箋, Japanese for sticky note) are notes pinned to conversations: one editable body shared by every chat it is pinned to, handed to the model only when its view is stale, and rewriteable only when you allow it — by default Hermes can merely propose a rewrite, and you apply or dismiss it.
entries.title: Fusen
known_issues: The composer banner follows the focused chat, not the split tile it renders in; the panel is the reliable place with split panes.
A note armed for "new chat with this note" can land on a different chat if you switch and never send in the draft.
Sidebar grouping by note and a per-row context submenu need core seams that do not exist at HEAD, so neither ships.

entries.name: gadget
entries.description: Talk to your Hermes from small ESP32 devices with a screen, microphone and speaker: hold a button, ask, and hear the answer. Adds a gateway platform where each device is a chat, plus tools to list devices, show a card on a screen and run device actions (LEDs, relays). Disclosure — the gateway listens for devices on a WebSocket port (8765, all interfaces by default; plain ws:// unless tls_cert/tls_key are set). New devices need a Hermes pairing code unless listed in GADGET_ALLOWED_USERS; GADGET_ALLOW_ALL_USERS skips pairing (development only). A paired device answers the agent's command approvals for its own chat (allow once or deny), within Hermes's approval timeout. The first approved device becomes the platform's home channel by default. Session hooks feed a dashboard on paired devices with each agent session's platform, a short id and its state (idle, busy, waiting for approval); a device that can switch profiles also sees the offered profiles' sessions. Optional profile switching (off unless `profiles` is set in the default profile's gadget config) lets a device paired on the default profile talk to the listed profiles; each profile approves the device through its own pairing flow (the device shows the `hermes -p <profile> pairing approve` command), the plugin writes nothing into other profiles, and revoking the device in the default profile sends it back there. A paired gadget that draws faces gets the answering profile's face: its `gadget-face.bin`, or its Hermes avatar (`assets/avatar.*`) converted with Pillow when installed; the plugin only reads these files, and `profile_faces: false` turns this off. `platforms.gadget.extra.stt_language` sets the transcription language of gadget recordings through the `pre_transcription` hook; other platforms' audio is untouched. Spoken replies that are not WAV are converted with the local ffmpeg; Opus reply audio uses the host's libopus when installed (loaded with ctypes, not bundled). `hermes gadget update --latest` downloads firmware from this repository's GitHub releases, checks size and SHA-256 against the release manifest (files carry build provenance attestations) and sends it to the device. A device that advertises `camera.capture` returns stills that are saved as PNGs under `~/.hermes/gadgetpix/` and kept until removed by hand. A Hermes Desktop page (`desktop/plugin.js`, plugin SDK only) runs a gadget in the window that connects to the local gateway as a device of its own: its device key, and the gateway access token when one is required, are kept in the page's plugin storage, it pairs like any device, and it uses the microphone only while its talk button or Space is held. The plugin's dashboard routes, behind the dashboard's login, can approve the pairing code a device is showing and send a card or run an advertised action on a connected, paired device; the requests pass through files under plugin-data/gadget/desk/. gadget_play plays audio on a device's speaker: a local file only from Hermes's audio cache and the folders in `play_dirs`, or an http(s) URL fetched under Hermes's URL safety policy (private and internal addresses refused, every redirect checked), decoded by the local ffmpeg, which is given no network or file access of its own and reads audio containers only; playback stops after `play_max_minutes` (60). Interpreter mode (`hermes gadget interpret` or gadget_interpret) translates what two people say on a device: the plugin transcribes each recording, asks the model for the translation through Hermes's plugin completion API with no tools, and speaks it; nothing reaches the agent or a session, and no transcript is kept. Widgets set with `hermes gadget widget` or gadget_widget are kept under plugin-data/gadget/. `hermes gadget diag <device>` and the dashboard's Save diagnostics report ask a connected device for its report and save it with the gateway's last 500 Gadget log lines, as a text file: from the CLI to `--out` or the current folder, from the dashboard as a browser download. `hermes gadget bot-chat` hands requests to the gateway through files under plugin-data/gadget/bot-chat/ and reads the profile's session store read-only. Messages and cron output sent to a device outside a turn are spoken on devices that speak replies. Otherwise writes only under plugin-data/gadget/. Uses Hermes's own STT, TTS and image cache; no telemetry. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: gambit
entries.description: Play chess in a Hermes terminal or Desktop pane, understand mistakes, and replay or practice public Chess.com and Lichess matches. Disclosure — runs a locally installed Stockfish executable (the path you set in plugin settings, or one found on PATH) as a subprocess that inherits Hermes' environment; fetches public games for a username you enter from api.chess.com and lichess.org; uses your configured Hermes model for each opponent move; and in Coach mode the Desktop pane automatically sends coaching requests into the bound chat when it is idle, each starting a model turn.
entries.title: Gambit for Hermes
known_issues: Requires a separately installed local Stockfish executable; it is not bundled or downloaded automatically. Hermes Desktop is optional for the graphical pane.
The standalone terminal board requires an interactive terminal with Python curses support and uses a separate Gambit session in the active profile.
Hermes skips standalone CLI command registration with plugins.isolation set to host; /chess remains available in a Hermes conversation.
Slash shortcuts return direct board or local engine evidence; use ordinary chat or the standalone coaching pane for model explanations.
Full-match recap completion is announced through Desktop only. CLI/TUI chat can retrieve the result on a later request; the standalone dashboard has no summary command.
Imports completed public standard-chess games only; source publication delays and rate limits may apply. Chess.com Bot and Coach games are unavailable through public username lookup.
Uses the configured Hermes provider for moves and coaching; normal provider usage applies, and legal engine fallback is labelled when used.
The 60-second deadline covers board replies; separate explanations have their own provider response time.
Verified platform scope is macOS only; Linux, Windows and another physical computer have not been verified.

entries.name: game-editor
entries.description: In the Godot 4 project open in your editor, it places assets into the scene, plays the game, and the next plan fixes each error from its file and line. Disclosure — Needs Godot 4.7 or later, the Godot AI 4.x add-on, and uv. The first start downloads godot-ai==4.3.0 from pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org. There is no API key. The editor is reached only on 127.0.0.1. A server this plugin starts sends no telemetry. The add-on follows godot_ai/telemetry_enabled (on by default) and can send usage to godot-ai-telemetry-v2-pudmurzsnq-uw.a.run.app. plan_change sends only the session list. apply_plan asks once. A plan that deletes, overwrites, drops unsaved work, writes outside the project or runs code it wrote is not made when what is lost exceeds 1,700 characters, and otherwise runs only after confirm_risky_plan. Play and tests ask once and run the project's code. Tools are on by default on every surface, including the gateway, so anyone who can message Hermes there can ask and approve. This plugin keeps no user list of its own. Cron, hermes chat -q and unattended runs decline. Data stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-game-editor-<id> after removal. Stop with hermes plugins disable game-editor, or hermes tools for one surface. macOS only. The studio plan step writes res://studio/ files and, with no editor open, a project under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor/studio-project, and runs headless Godot on code it wrote; each test, web export and recording needs confirm_risky_plan. studio import_asset copies a .glb, .wav, .ogg or .mp3 file of up to 64 MB from any absolute path the plan names into res://studio/imports/. studio web downloads the 1.3 GB Godot 4.7.2 export template from github.com once, only after its sha256 and sha512 match, keeps it in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor/export-templates, and serves the Web build on 127.0.0.1 only; it never uploads. Headless studio steps delete files that appear in the project outside studio/ and build/ while Godot runs. The pass ledger stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/game-editor after removal.

entries.name: game-lab
entries.description: Game Lab combines ModLab, Game Localization Studio, Sprites and experimental Playtest Pilot. ModLab works on a private game copy and invokes separately installed tools; localization drafts and exports RPG Maker MV/MZ text and the text of Unity Mono builds (JSON text assets, script-component strings and Assembly-CSharp string literals; patched copies of changed files only, the game folder is never written); localization companions estimate width and row budgets, merge and audit translation data, and proofread English; Sprites inspects and previews character sheets. Playtest Pilot uses approved X11 input, captures screen pixels within the selected window, stores private evidence frames and returns reduced previews and optional local OCR hints; for a failed check it can build a short captioned MP4 from those frames with your FFmpeg, or cut one from a recording file you point to (that asks for approval). On first use ModLab reads Steam's library list and app manifests to find installed games, lists the files in the chosen game folder, runs read-only hardware checks, and asks which modding route to use. It never fills a disk: a free-space reserve, a total cap, pruning of old revisions and a confirm-first cleanup tool. The Universal Modder and REA programs are the ones you set in the plugin settings or find on PATH (the model cannot name a program), and each toolkit call and each playtest check asks for your approval. Every program it starts gets a minimal environment, never your provider keys. The plugin makes no network calls of its own. Disclosure — Playtest Pilot sends synthetic key presses and clicks to the X11 window you select (via xdotool and Hermes computer_use, each check or batch approved), captures that window's pixels and stores evidence frames in the plugin's data folder; ModLab reads your Steam library and app-manifest files to list installed games, copies the game folder you choose into plugin data (with a disk cap), Game Localization Studio reads the RPG Maker data file or Unity game folder you point it at and copies the files that hold text into plugin data, writes a JSONL units file into the draft folder, and reads translations back from the JSONL file path named in the tool call (absolute path; symlinks, credential folders and the Hermes home are refused); and, after your approval of each call, runs the Universal Modder / REA programs set in the plugin settings or found on PATH.

entries.name: gameforge
entries.description: Game development toolkit: sound effects, music loops with MIDI, NPC voices, pixel-art sprite sheets and autotiling tilesets, low-poly and AI 3D models (.glb); 4 playable web genres (topdown, platformer, arena, roguelike), Godot 4 and Unity builds; headless Blender and Unreal pipelines; an automated playtester that plays each genre and reports crashes, stuck spots and boring stretches; one-click PWA, itch.io, single-HTML and Capacitor export. Offline by default. Disclosure — runs local Chrome/Chromium for playtests, and Godot, Unity, Blender, UnrealEditor-Cmd, ffmpeg, xvfb-run or butler only when a call asks for them; blender action=script runs a bpy file the caller names. Network only when asked: fal.ai, Tripo or Meshy (FAL_KEY / TRIPO_API_KEY / MESHY_API_KEY, prompt and image sent), ElevenLabs (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, SFX prompt), Edge TTS when edge-tts is installed (dialogue text), Godot export templates from GitHub (~1 GB, target=godot_templates), itch.io via butler (target=itch with an explicit itch_target). Writes only inside the game project directory, plus a temporary browser profile. No telemetry.

entries.name: gbrain-pointer
entries.description: Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (`gbrain serve --http`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of `[source:slug] title` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN_POINTER_ALLOW_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.

entries.name: gemini-live
entries.description: Full-duplex Gemini Live voice calls in Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard. The voice takes the profile's name and hands real work to your Hermes agent while you keep talking. It can steer running jobs, threads, bot chats and subagents, use the profile's MCP tools, recall memory and past conversations, set and read iPhone alarms, timers and reminders through hermes-mobile-device-access when a phone is paired, and report back when work finishes. Read-only local commands need three layers to agree: hard rules, a safety review and a contained run; files are read only from the workspace folder, /var/log and a few plain system files. When a job needs approval, the voice says so and Approve and Deny buttons appear; the voice model can never answer one, and spoken approval is opt-in. With the AirPods Approvals plugin, a nod or shake answers it too. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it from the client to generativelanguage.googleapis.com on a single-use ephemeral token; the Gemini key stays on the Hermes backend, read through Hermes' secret scope. Gemini also receives the voice's instructions, tool results, and, unless share_chat_context is off, the open chat's title and recent messages. On Gemini's free tier, Google may use this content to improve its products. Delegated work runs as a normal Hermes turn with that profile's tools and approvals. The iPhone tools call that plugin directly, within the access granted in the Hermes Agent app, and send alarm and reminder details to Gemini; turn them off with phone_tools. The opt-in readonly_shell and system_checks settings, both off by default, run bounded commands on the Hermes host. No telemetry and no background processes.

entries.name: gemini-media
entries.description: Google Gemini image (Nano Banana) and video (Gemini Omni) generation backends for image_generate and video_generate, in one plugin built on the google-genai SDK. Image: text-to-image and reference-guided editing (up to 14 images). Video: text-, image- and reference-to-video with native audio. Model picker comes from the key's live models.list. Disclosure — prompts, reference images and the Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY, falling back to GOOGLE_API_KEY, the key Hermes's own Gemini chat provider uses) are sent to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; reference-image URLs are downloaded by the plugin (public hosts only, redirects re-checked) and a local reference path can be any image file the user can read (accepted only after a magic-byte check); generation is billed to the API key's Google project; writes generated media under $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/ and a model-list cache (key hash only) under $HERMES_HOME/cache/gemini_media/; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates. Installs google-genai.
known_issues: The Gemini Omni video endpoint stalls intermittently; calls are bounded by a wall-clock deadline (default 300 s) and return error_type timeout.
Video input (editing, extending, reference videos) is not supported; API-key authentication only.

entries.name: geo-analyzer-mcp
entries.description: Self-hosted MCP server for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): audit how AI crawlers see a site (robots.txt rules for 16 known AI crawlers, live HTTP access for the 14 that send a user agent, WAF/bot-challenge detection, content parity, SPA-shell detection, indexability, JSON-LD, sitemap, llms.txt), track AI visibility and citation share-of-voice across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and optionally Perplexity with stable query variants, score brand sentiment and the AI claims that contradict your ground-truth facts, and turn the result into a prioritised action plan with Markdown and HTML reports. Runs entirely on your own machine; MIT licensed. 12 MCP tools (page_audit, ai_visibility, sentiment, full_analysis, get_job, get_run, list_runs, get_trends, compare_runs, list_projects, get_project, server_status) plus a bundled skill that teaches the agent the list-projects → run → poll → report workflow and the dry_run cost guard. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Disclosure — the MCP server runs locally as a stdio child process that uvx launches: it builds the installed plugin directory into a throwaway environment on first run and downloads the package's Python dependencies from PyPI; the engine API keys you supply (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, optionally PERPLEXITY_API_KEY) are read by the server from your own ~/.geo-mcp/.env file in plain text (the installer also drops an empty .env key template next to the plugin manifest, which the server does not read), are sent only to those providers, and are not read from Hermes' own secret store; project presets are read from ~/.geo-mcp/projects.yaml; every visibility or sentiment run sends your queries and company facts to the AI engines you enabled, and full answers, citations and reports are stored under ~/.geo-mcp/; the page audit fetches the URLs you name plus that origin's robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt, behind an SSRF guard that refuses private, loopback, link-local and other reserved targets; a full analysis costs real provider credits, so use dry_run and the per-run query cap to bound spend; the optional Docker/HTTP mode serves the same tools over bearer-token HTTP on localhost (it refuses a non-localhost bind without GEO_MCP_TOKEN) and can be placed behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, which exposes the run API to the internet if you do that; an optional GEO_WEBHOOK_URL posts a run summary to a webhook you configure; no telemetry and no account with the plugin author.
entries.title: GEO Analyzer MCP
known_issues: Needs uvx on PATH and Python 3.11+: the server is built into a throwaway uv environment on first launch.

The first launch builds the package and its dependencies, which can exceed Hermes' 60-second MCP connect timeout; if the geo tools are missing in your first session, start a second one and they appear.
Engine API keys are read from your own ~/.geo-mcp/.env (create it with `geo-mcp init`), not from Hermes secrets.

The install does not put the `geo-mcp` command on your PATH: write ~/.geo-mcp/projects.yaml and ~/.geo-mcp/.env by hand, or run `uvx --from git+https://github.com/clance1/geo-analyzer-mcp geo-mcp init` once.

The JS-render comparison (page_audit render_js) needs the optional `render` extra (Playwright plus a Chromium download); a plain install ships the base package, so that check reports itself unavailable.

entries.name: ghost-run
entries.description: Dry-run mode for Hermes Agent. With /ghost on, file writes, patches, deletes and terminal commands are redirected into a throwaway copy of the working folder, and network-touching tools and commands are blocked. Review the diff in the system browser (hermes ghost ui; the Desktop pane only opens that page), then optionally run one configured Verify command in the ghost (Pass/Fail banner; Apply stays human), then apply selected paths or discard. Commands: /ghost on|off|status|verify; hermes ghost diff|apply|discard|ui|verify. Disclosure — copies the working folder into a temp sandbox (reflink, then copy; never a hard link) and runs the agent's terminal commands on the host with the working directory set to that copy; only literal absolute paths under the real folder are rewritten, so a command naming ~, $HOME or another absolute path still acts on the real disk, and MCP or other plugin tools are not redirected; Ghost Mode is process-wide, so in a gateway it covers every chat in that process; writes session state under the Hermes home from hermes_constants.get_hermes_home() (then HERMES_HOME, then ~/.hermes), in ghost-run/; "apply" writes the chosen changes back to the real folder only after a person presses Apply or runs /ghost apply, and that copy does not pass through Hermes' file-write denylist; /ghost apply and hermes ghost apply with no paths apply every current change and can copy a named path that is in the ghost tree even if it is not in the diff; the review page never auto-ticks HIGH-risk files and asks to confirm any it names; hermes ghost ui binds 127.0.0.1 only, checks Host, requires a per-session token sent in the X-Ghost-Run-Token header (query-string tokens are ignored), sends no CORS headers, and POST /api/apply accepts only a non-empty list of paths that are all in the current diff; Verify runs one command taken from GHOST_RUN_TEST or the project's .ghost-run-test on the host inside the ghost copy, only after you approve that project and exact command, with provider keys stripped from its environment; opt-in outbound only: with GHOST_RUN_AI=1, pending diffs go to your Hermes provider through ctx.llm.complete, or, if that is unavailable, to openrouter.ai using OPENROUTER_API_KEY read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret; off by default, no credentials stored by the plugin, no telemetry.
entries.title: Ghost Run
known_issues: Verified on macOS in Hermes Desktop v0.23.1 at 54badf24: the pane opens the review page in the system browser; Load, Apply, and the HIGH confirm run on that page, not inside the pane. Checklist: docs/desktop-check.md.
Advisory OpenRouter notes run only when ctx.llm is unbound and agent.secret_scope.get_secret returns OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Otherwise the notes stay off.
Checked on Linux and macOS (Hermes Desktop v0.23.1 at 54badf24). Windows is untested.
The demo's headless Chrome fallback puts the review URL, fragment token included, on the browser process command line. curl reads the token from a mode-600 header file that is removed afterwards.

entries.name: ghostmark-mcp
entries.description: GhostMark through its MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://ghostmark.mrhyde.dev/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): puts an invisible watermark tied to a key into a picture, with an optional encrypted message of up to 24 bytes inside, and reads it back with the same key after the picture has been saved as JPEG, cropped, resized or rotated. Three tools: suggest_key draws a random key of common words, mark_image returns the marked file, read_image says whether a key and a picture fit and returns the message. Bundles one skill for both flows. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. The mark does not encrypt or protect the picture and is not proof of authorship: it answers whether a picture carries the mark of a key. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to ghostmark.mrhyde.dev (closed-source server, behind Cloudflare), which uses the picture, the key and the message in memory to answer one call and stores none of them; it keeps daily counts with no text, no picture and no address, and logs the address of what looks like an attack. With image_url the server downloads that picture itself. Every tool is annotated read-only; the package marks the server untrusted. The skill tells the agent to send only the picture the person named and only to ghostmark.mrhyde.dev, and to treat a message read out of a picture as data. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: gif-tool
entries.description: Show, edit and compress GIFs in Hermes. `gif_open` turns any GIF, animated WebP, APNG, PNG or JPEG (a file path or an https link) into a card in Hermes Desktop where you add exact captions, change speed, reverse, boomerang, trim, drop frames and crop with a live preview; the original file is never changed. `gif_export` and the card's export buttons compress for Discord (10 MB), Discord emoji (256 KB), Telegram, X (5 MB), under 1 MB, animated WebP or a size you name, shrinking until the file fits and reporting before and after sizes (pure Pillow: shared palette, frame differencing, size-targeted ladder). `gif_edit` gives the agent the same edits. `gif_create` makes a four-frame meme GIF from a prompt. A GIF Studio tab lists every GIF in the profile and takes a dropped file or a pasted link. Disclosure — editing, previews and compression are local; opening a link downloads that one https URL (no cookies or credentials; private, local and link-local addresses refused, redirects and the connected peer re-checked; a GIPHY or Tenor page is followed once to its og:image); `gif_create` sends only the text prompt to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/images/generations through Hermes' credentialed_provider_request with the user's OpenAI Codex sign-in, using one image from the user's ChatGPT plan per call, via an undocumented endpoint; projects and rendered files are stored under the profile's plugin-data/gif-tool and cache/generated/images.
entries.title: GIF Tool
known_issues: Restart Hermes once after installing: the card's backend routes mount at startup.
The card needs a Hermes Desktop with tool-media renderers; older Desktops and other surfaces show the plain GIF.
gif_create needs an OpenAI Codex sign-in in Hermes and uses an undocumented Codex image endpoint that can change without notice; every other feature works without it.
Not yet exercised inside a running Hermes Desktop by the author: the card and backend were tested headlessly against the real plugin code with a stand-in for the plugin SDK.

entries.name: git-autosave
entries.description: Lightweight local alternative to directory checkpoints for Git projects. Before a mutating tool call it saves the affected repository's working state to a private local shadow ref (refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>, with reflog) through a private index, or copies the single existing file outside Git; `hermes autosave find` and `restore` recover a pre-edit version. Disclosure — runs each backup in a short-lived child process killed at the hook deadline, which runs local git subprocesses in repositories the agent touches (hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor and lazy fetch disabled); writes shadow refs/reflogs and short-lived private index files into those repositories' .git and unencrypted file copies into its plugin-data directory; never changes HEAD, branches, the real index or the working tree and never pushes; skips credential stores (.env, auth.json, .ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and dependency directories; `hermes autosave sweep` reads the session database read-only and is scheduled by the user; no network, no background or long-lived processes; it observes only and never blocks or approves a tool call.
entries.title: Git Autosave
known_issues: One V4A patch that moves a symlink and then updates the moved path can miss the edited file on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems; commit first or send the Move and the Update as separate calls.

entries.name: git-gui
entries.description: Read-only graphical git client for Hermes Desktop: the repository of the chat you are in becomes a lane-colored commit graph, as a compact right-sidebar pane and as a full three-column page (BRANCH / TAG | GRAPH | COMMIT MESSAGE) with draggable widths, ref chips, author and age on every row; clicking a commit opens a drawer with the full message, author/committer, clickable parents, changed files (Path or Tree) and a unified diff per file, and history loads 500 commits at a time as you scroll. Nine locales with RTL support. Disclosure — reads only: the Desktop half registers a page, a right-sidebar pane, a sidebar nav row and two palette commands through the plugin SDK, and the Python half is a read-only API mounted at /api/plugins/git-gui/ that runs the local git executable as a subprocess in the session's working directory (rev-parse, for-each-ref, log, show, diff; GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, 15 s timeout, no fetch/checkout/index or ref writes). entries.name: git-hook
entries.description: Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT_HOOK_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT_HOOK_ROOTS (default PROJECTS_ROOT, "*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. A branch whose direct push the remote refuses on policy grounds (branch protection, a PR-required ruleset) is never committed to again: the hook drops its own unpushed commit, leaves the edit staged and dirty, and reports it once.

entries.name: git-review
entries.description: Git review pane for Hermes Desktop: every changed file of the agent's last turn, uncommitted, staged or unstaged work, the branch since it left the default branch, or any selection of commits, in one scroll, unified or split, with syntax colours; cites changed lines into the composer as @line: references; and stages, unstages, discards, commits, pushes and opens pull requests from the pane. Disclosure — reads run git subprocesses (rev-parse, status, diff, log, show, cat-file, ls-files, for-each-ref, branch, remote, rev-list, merge-base, symbolic-ref, hash-object) with timeouts and output caps, external diff and textconv drivers disabled. Writes run only when the user clicks: git add, restore, reset, rm, commit and push, on paths validated inside the repository; discard asks first in Desktop's confirmation dialog and deletes only the untracked files it names. By default hooks are skipped and any write that would run a program named by the repository's own config (filter drivers, signing, SSH or credential commands) is refused; the run_repo_programs setting allows them, and the read_only setting hides and refuses every write. Network use: push to the branch's own name on its remote, and the user's own gh or glab CLI for the PR/MR badge and for Create pull request; the plugin itself makes no network requests. Generate commit message sends what the commit will contain and recent commit subjects to the focused chat's model through Hermes's commit_message one-shot template, only when clicked. It reads files and history inside authorized repositories only (the focused workspace, configured repos/roots and the latest agent selection), this profile's config.yaml, and the cwd column of the sessions table in state.db (read-only); it writes $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/select.sqlite3 (agent selection requests), $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/git-review/turn-snapshots/ (Last agent turn snapshots: the working tree's tracked and non-ignored untracked files as git objects, written with git add -A and write-tree against a throwaway index and an object store in that directory, never the repository's; newest 16 kept, three days max), Desktop plugin storage (display settings, turn baselines) and, through the actions above, the user's repository. While the pane is open it polls the local backend every 3 s (agent selections) and 5 s (live diffs); the status-bar count and the commit box's branch state refresh every 15 s; no background processes, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: glance
entries.description: Hermes can't call a UI change done until it has looked. Glance screenshots the running iOS Simulator (or Android emulator) right before the agent's first UI edit, diffs it against the screen after the edit, and the pre_verify hook sends the agent back when the edit changed nothing, crashed to an error screen, or left the screen blank. On PASS the agent sees the before/after image, so it can catch a button that vanished. Desktop draws the result as a before/after slider. Disclosure — runs xcrun simctl (list, io screenshot) and adb (devices, exec-out screencap) as subprocesses; adb devices starts adb's own server if it is not running; on PASS calls Hermes' vision_analyze on the compare image through ctx.dispatch_tool, which is one auxiliary vision model call when the main model is text-only; appends the compare image to the agent's final reply as a MEDIA attachment, so on messaging platforms the screenshot is sent into that chat; writes screenshots and check records under plugin-data/glance and does not prune them; no network calls of its own, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: glassbox
entries.description: A contained, auditable terminal backend for macOS. Select it with `hermes config set terminal.backend glassbox` and every terminal, execute_code, read_file, write_file, patch and search_files call runs under a generated Seatbelt profile: the system stays readable, the workspace is writable, the rest of the user's home is hidden, the home directory itself is never used as the workspace, and network access is off by default. The kernel-refused reads, writes and network attempts are recorded in a local audit log, so "what did the agent try to touch?" is answerable: `hermes glassbox report` (text or a self-contained dark HTML timeline), `/glassbox status|verify|report|profile`, the glassbox_report / glassbox_policy / glassbox_verify tools, a containment self-test (`hermes glassbox verify`: workspace read/write, home read/write denial, child-process confinement, parent traversal, network denial, secret-env filtering) and a one-command demo (`hermes glassbox demo`). A pre_tool_call preflight turns file-tool denials into an actionable error with the exact `hermes config set` line to allow a path, instead of the masked empty read a `2>/dev/null` shell probe would otherwise produce. Settings: network, allow_home, workspace_writable, read_paths, write_paths, deny_paths, audit — apply to the next command, editable from the Desktop Plugins tab. Disclosure — macOS only; runs the agent's shell and file-tool commands on this Mac as the same UNIX user under /usr/bin/sandbox-exec (an OS kernel sandbox, not a VM or a separate UID; it does not defend against a kernel exploit, and system mach services other than Apple Events and LaunchServices stay reachable); osascript, open, security and launchctl are blocked by path, and Apple Events plus LaunchServices mach services are denied; the home directory is never used as the workspace and shell startup files and ~/Library/LaunchAgents are always write-denied; the generated profile, a private scratch home/tmp area and the audit log live under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/glassbox/ (the audit stores command text truncated to 2000 chars, cwd, exit code, duration, blocked paths and a short output excerpt only when something was blocked — local only, capped at 4 MB with one rotation, never uploaded, `hermes glassbox clear` deletes it); reads the workspace and any extra read_paths/write_paths the user configures; runs two `git config --global --get` calls to copy the Git author name/email into the sandbox environment because ~/.gitconfig is hidden; provider keys, tokens, passwords and SSH agent sockets are filtered from every sandboxed child environment; the containment self-test writes and removes canary files in the home directory; no network calls of its own, no background processes, no telemetry; Seatbelt is marked deprecated by Apple but shipped and functional on current macOS — if a future macOS drops sandbox-exec the backend reports unavailable instead of running unconfined.
entries.title: Glassbox
known_issues: Seatbelt is a deny-by-default OS sandbox, not a virtual machine: commands run as the same user, and the plugin does not defend against a kernel exploit or against a process the user deliberately launches outside the sandbox.
Commands that need network (package installs, git push over HTTPS) require `network: true` or a local mirror; SSH agent sockets and ~/.ssh are never passed in.

entries.name: glasses-platform
entries.description: Your own Hermes agent on your smart glasses and other devices: it sees what you see, answers by voice, and taps you on the lens when something is due. A gateway platform that adds glasses as a channel, with short spoken-style replies to the device that asked, camera photos (requested when you ask what you are looking at, or taken by the agent with its glasses_capture_photo tool), voice in and out through Hermes's own speech settings, streamed replies for heads-up displays, approval and clarify prompts on every device (approval cards with buttons, or a spoken yes or no), and cron and heartbeat pushes to all of a user's devices, kept for offline devices across gateway restarts. Also connects Even Realities G2 glasses (an Even Hub app you pack yourself), ESP32 voice boxes running the open-source xiaozhi firmware, the Omi pendant (real-time transcript webhook) and Pebble watches (the open-source Bobby app); devices that cannot keep a socket open (an Apple Watch through a Siri Shortcut, scripts) use an HTTP route. Pair a device with `hermes glasses pair` (QR code) or try it from the terminal with `hermes glasses try`. Speaks the bridge protocol of the community hermes-glasses iOS app (v0) and a richer v1; a simulator, JavaScript and Python clients and a conformance kit are included. Disclosure — opens an unencrypted listener on all interfaces (port 8765: WebSocket /voice, /xiaozhi and /bobby/<token>/query; HTTP /turn, /pending, /approval, /xiaozhi/ota/<token>, /omi/<token>/transcript and /bobby/<token>/quota) that refuses to start without a device token (use Tailscale or a TLS proxy off your home network; Omi's servers must reach the webhook over the internet); each device token, sent in a header, query or URL path, gets full agent chat as its user, bypassing the gateway allowlist, including answering approval prompts and clarify questions; `hermes glasses pair` writes device tokens to the profile .env, and the xiaozhi OTA reply gives the box its WebSocket address with its own token; with Omi, transcripts come from Omi's servers and answers go back through them; the agent can take a glasses camera photo at any time during a glasses conversation and photos are also captured automatically on visual keywords (auto_capture: off disables that), saved in Hermes's image cache; recordings and spoken replies use Hermes's own stt/tts settings, so a cloud speech provider receives the audio or text; pushes for offline devices are kept in $HERMES_HOME/glasses/outbox.json (owner-only); Omi transcript segments are held in memory until the session has been idle for ten minutes (the newest 256 per session); the device's new-session button answers Hermes's /new confirmation for that user; it runs a local ffmpeg (no shell) only to convert audio; no outbound network calls of its own and no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes Glasses
known_issues: Preview: proven against the bundled simulators and a real Hermes gateway with real models (the G2 app in the official Even Hub simulator, Pebble with a Bobby-protocol client); not yet tested on real glasses, watches, voice boxes or an Omi pendant, or with the iOS app on a device.

Each device needs a companion app or firmware that speaks one of its protocols: the community hermes-glasses iOS app in bridge mode, the bundled G2 app, xiaozhi firmware, an Omi app webhook or the Bobby app.
Without a terminal, install with --yes-deps (it needs aiohttp and qrcode); otherwise the plugin installs but stays disabled.

Known issues: Preview: proven against the bundled simulators and a real Hermes gateway with real models (the G2 app in the official Even Hub simulator, Pebble with a Bobby-protocol client); not yet tested on real glasses, watches, voice boxes or an Omi pendant, or with the iOS app on a device.; Each device needs a companion app or firmware that speaks one of its protocols: the community hermes-glasses iOS app in bridge mode, the bundled G2 app, xiaozhi firmware, an Omi app webhook or the Bobby app.; Without a terminal, install with --yes-deps (it needs aiohttp and qrcode); otherwise the plugin installs but stays disabled..

entries.name: glide
entries.description: Kevin Rajan's Hermes frontend for Tern, built on alt-glitch/hermes-tern (MIT) and carrying about 890 commits of its own. One install gives `hermes tern`, which draws the chat as native Tern UI, plus `/glide`, a guided setup that makes Hermes learn from you and run more of its work locally. Added over the original: charts from Markdown tables, OpenUI and ephemeral-ui answer cards, 3D artifacts beside the chat, written artifacts and session links, LSP diagnostics cards, live wait tiles for subagents, fork-a-session panes, /rewind, /undo and /tree, native /settings and a /models provider hub, a Vim composer, a command palette and shortcut preferences, queue-or-steer busy input, opt-in live voice with helper lanes beside the thinking orb (role, model and real state from a local lane broker), a work dock, a thinking-orbs indicator, frontend channels (`hermes tern --channel`), and tool cards that report refusals, truncation and partial failures instead of hiding them. `/fleet` (with `/hosts` and `/portfolio`) shows read-only cards of local hosts, agents, GPU/CPU gauges, k3s pods and open issues and pull requests for named repositories; `/intel` shows read-only local intelligence (hill-climb results, skills, memory, failures, traces). Inactive on released Hermes: Tern browser blocks, image delivery across hosts, plan review with a todo HUD, native /btw side questions and read-only MCP/SSH report sheets need plugin gateway methods (`ctx.register_gateway_method`) that released Hermes does not have yet; they turn on when it does. Glide guards two scarce resources: your attention and the agent's context window. `/glide focus` shows your current phase, next deep-work window and usual stop time, learned from your own local session timestamps (or from z0intelligence's `circadian` and a loopback Flowkit flow estimate when installed); a deep-work block holds non-critical agent notifications and approval asks for one digest at the end while critical ones still pass, and one wind-down card saves a resume note for the next session. `/glide` (also `hermes glide onboard`) is a chain of approve cards: detect the machine and local runtimes (and z0intelligence if installed); build a corrections memory from your past local sessions (your messages that start "no,", "actually," or "correction:") and quote up to three matching corrections into each new turn through a pre_llm_call hook, using deterministic BM25 with no embeddings or model calls; a skill router catalog; a measured CPU hill climb whose referee says KEEP, REVERT or INCONCLUSIVE; offload of small tasks to an installed Ollama model with estimated savings; and an optional Taste board pane beside the chat. Disclosure — Derived from hermes-tern (alt-glitch/hermes-tern, MIT). Network: GitHub's API with the optional GITHUB_TOKEN (and GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN only to the Enterprise hosts the user lists) for the pull request view, and through `gh` for /fleet repository cards; the user's own auxiliary model for live process and table charts; the frontend downloads image URLs from tool results and public 3D-model URLs it shows beside the chat, refusing private, loopback and link-local addresses on every redirect hop; /glide taste talks only to a loopback Taste Atlas server (127.0.0.1:8789 by default); /glide focus reads a Flowkit server (127.0.0.1:8787 by default, GLIDE_FLOWKIT_URL overrides) if one answers; live-voice helper lanes poll only a loopback lane broker (127.0.0.1:8791 by default) and stay off unless you name its token file in the plugin's lanes_token_file setting; no telemetry. Commands: runs the `tern` CLI to open files and splits, `open`/`xdg-open` for http(s) links the user clicks, and `!cmd` shell commands the user types in the composer; /glide runs `nvidia-smi`, `ollama list`/`ollama run` and, if installed, `z0int doctor --json` and `circadian show --json`, each only on an approved step, and while corrections are on it runs z0intelligence's corrections reader on every turn; /fleet runs `ps`, `nvidia-smi`, `tailscale status --json`, read-only `kubectl get`/`describe` and `gh issue list`/`gh pr list`, and /intel reads local snapshot files; every child gets a timeout and a minimal environment plus only that tool's own credentials (gh token, KUBECONFIG), never provider keys; the hill climb runs a local CPU benchmark; nothing is installed or downloaded. Tools and prompt: when the user grants `tools.override` in the profile it replaces Hermes's browser tools with a Tern-pane browser (needs plugin gateway methods); it adds system-prompt sections for pull requests and answer cards and, once turned on, quotes up to three of the user's past corrections into each turn. Reads outside its data: the profile's Hermes session database, read-only (local sessions only; cron, delegated and hidden sessions skipped), the session's background-process output, and for /fleet and /intel read-only local workspace and z0intelligence state files and /proc. Writes only under the profile. Install this or hermes-tern, not both: both register `hermes tern`.

entries.name: global-business-culture
entries.description: Cross-cultural business intelligence: country culture briefs and home-vs-host gap analysis computed from bundled Meyer, Hofstede, GLOBE and Lewis data. Three deterministic tools (culture_brief, culture_gap_analysis, culture_countries), a /culture command and a bundled practitioner-playbook skill. 57 economies offline, no dependencies, no network, no env vars — the gap analysis ranks the exact scale distances between two cultures, names the misread each gap produces and prescribes adaptation moves. Deep ASEAN/frontier coverage (Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar flagged as extrapolated from GLOBE-cluster neighbours).
entries.title: Global Business Culture
known_issues: Scale positions are approximations distilled from the published frameworks (Meyer, Hofstede, GLOBE, Lewis), not measurements; countries not in the original datasets are extrapolated from cluster neighbours and flagged in tool output.

entries.name: glorya
entries.description: Ask Hermes for an ad and get the finished file back in your chat. Glorya makes on-brand image ads, video ads, landing pages and websites, and launches ad campaigns on Meta, Google Ads and TikTok. The plugin follows each job in the background: one progress message that updates, Glorya's questions asked in the chat (answer in words or with /glorya answer buttons), and the finished videos and images sent back as attachments. Also /glorya commands that run without the model, weekly image and video ad blueprints, and a Glorya Studio tab in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — needs a Glorya account with an active plan and uses its credits; campaigns spend real money from your ad account, so a pre_tool_call hook sends every create_campaign and publish_site call through Hermes' approval prompt (rule keys glorya:campaign and glorya:publish), and /glorya campaign and /glorya publish ask before they act. Tool calls go to platform.glorya.ai through Hermes' own MCP client (mcp_servers.glorya, auth: oauth; Hermes holds the token and signing in runs Hermes' manage_connections flow), and the plugin calls that server with ctx.call_mcp (mcp_allowlist). Finished files are downloaded over https from the links Glorya returns into plugin-data/glorya, which also stores job ids, titles and chat session keys (pruned after 30 days). With allow_gateway_injection it starts one agent turn per finished job to attach the files. One background thread per followed job, at most 8. hermes glorya setup runs only hermes plugins enable and hermes config set, each after a yes. Reads gateway.session_context.get_session_env and tools.mcp_tool_discovery.mcp_servers_not_connected. No telemetry.

entries.name: gmail
entries.description: Hermes Desktop Gmail mailbox UI for search, reading, and thread inspection, with preview-confirmed send, reply, archive, trash, and label changes. Uses the active profile's existing Google Workspace OAuth setup; email is sensitive external content. Gmail actions and data access require user review and configuration. Disclosure — reads the active profile's Hermes Google Workspace token (google_token.json, refreshed in memory only) and calls the Gmail API; opening an unread message marks it read, other send/trash/label changes go through a confirm step (one setting can skip every review dialog, and then the prepare ticket, account/profile binding, exact snapshot validation and readback verification still run); remote email images load only after the user allows them. Attachment metadata listing and bounded read-only attachment download (25 MB cap) are profile/account-scoped.

entries.name: gmi-image
entries.description: GMI Cloud image generation and URL-based image editing as an image_gen provider (image_gen.provider: gmi-image). Maps Hermes aspect ratios onto each model's own schema, so seedream, gemini-image, gpt-image and luma models share one backend. Disclosure — sends prompts, the optional image URLs and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Hermes secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every generation spends GMI credits with no Hermes approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model). The result is downloaded from the URL GMI returns into the Hermes image cache; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies.
entries.title: GMI Cloud image generation
known_issues: Image inputs must be public http(s) URLs; local files are refused.
Live-tested with seedream-5.0-lite and luma-uni-1.1. gemini-2.5-flash-image edits returned upstream errors from GMI during testing. GMI limits some models per day and the error says when it resets.
Shares one client module with gmi-video and gmi-speech from the same repository; each plugin carries its own byte-identical copy.

entries.name: gmi-nexus
entries.description: Adaptive intelligence layer for Hermes Agent over the live GMI Cloud model catalogue. A goal is understood, planned into steps, and each step is routed to the model that suits it from the catalogue read live at runtime, so a retired model stops being routable and a new one becomes routable without a code change. Results are evaluated against each step's own criteria, a failure is recovered on a different model with bounded retries, the verified outcome feeds the routing statistics, and the report says what ran, what it cost and what failed. Ships a vision module for screenshots and before/after comparison, a benchmarking arena whose results feed the router, a Dev Agent that writes and tests code through Hermes' own tools, and a creative engine for image, video and audio generation and editing. Also ships a web dashboard tab. No third-party dependencies; the key is read through Hermes' secret scope; a per-run ceiling, a rolling daily ceiling and an approval threshold are enforced before any request is submitted. Disclosure — Sends goals, prompts, files and images you or the model name, plus screenshots captured through Hermes' computer_use tool, to GMI Cloud (api.gmi-serving.com, console.gmicloud.ai) for paid inference and generation billed to your GMI account. Spend at or above approval_threshold_usd, or with no published price, asks for approval in Hermes' own prompt, under per-run and daily caps. Vision downloads model-supplied public image URLs on your machine before sending them. The Dev Agent writes files and runs test commands through Hermes' write_file and terminal tools.
entries.title: GMI NEXUS
known_issues: Needs a GMI Cloud account and API key. Catalogue reads are free, but inference and generation are billed by GMI Cloud at the model's published rate.

entries.name: gmi-sandbox
entries.description: GMI Cloud Sandbox terminal backend: Hermes's terminal, file and code tools run inside an ephemeral cloud sandbox created from a ready template you provide (`hermes config set terminal.backend gmi_sandbox`). Commands are polled to completion and cancelled on interrupt; truncated output is reported as a failure. Disclosure — community plugin, not a GMI product. With `terminal.backend: gmi_sandbox`, every terminal command, file path and file content the agent handles goes to console.gmicloud.ai and the GMI sandbox data plane with your GMI_SANDBOX_API_KEY (read per sandbox through Hermes secret scope), tagged with the plugin name and the Hermes task id. The first terminal call creates a billed sandbox with no Hermes approval prompt, and a crash can leave it running until its lifetime (default 900 s, renewed per command) expires; the plugin creates and deletes only its own sandboxes. Not yet verified against the live GMI service (offline tests only).
entries.title: GMI Cloud Sandbox
known_issues: Live sandbox execution, file operations and cleanup have not been verified against GMI; this entry is pinned after offline tests only.
The template must provide bash, python3 and any development tools your tasks need; Hermes's generic resource knobs do not resize the sandbox.
Persistent container mode and per-task image overrides are refused.
Command stdout and stderr are concatenated after completion, so their interleaving is not preserved.

entries.title: GMI Cloud speech synthesis
known_issues: No streaming synthesis and no Opus voice-note conversion; the file format is whatever the model offers.
Live-tested with minimax-tts-speech-2.6-turbo. GMI prices speech per 1k characters on some models and per character on others, so the plugin shows GMI price text and never totals it.
Shares one client module with gmi-image and gmi-video from the same repository; each plugin carries its own byte-identical copy.
entries.capability_summary: gmi-speech (community, maintained by zkasuran) GMI Cloud text-to-speech as a tts provider (tts.provider: gmi-speech). Picks the voice, speed and output format parameters from the chosen model's schema and writes a file whose extension matches the real format; music models are excluded. Disclosure — sends the text to speak and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Hermes secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every synthesis spends GMI credits with no Hermes approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model). The audio is downloaded over HTTPS from the URL GMI returns and written to the output path Hermes supplies; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies. This plugin requires env var(s): GMI_API_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: No streaming synthesis and no Opus voice-note conversion; the file format is whatever the model offers.; Live-tested with minimax-tts-speech-2.6-turbo. GMI prices speech per 1k characters on some models and per character on others, so the plugin shows GMI price text and never totals it.; Shares one client module with gmi-image and gmi-video from the same repository; each plugin carries its own byte-identical copy..

entries.name: gmi-video
entries.description: GMI Cloud text-to-video and image-to-video as a video_gen provider (video_gen.provider: gmi-video). Reads each model's live schema, so duration, resolution, aspect ratio and audio options use the values that model accepts. Anything it lacks is dropped and reported. Disclosure — sends prompts, the optional image URLs and your GMI_API_KEY (read per request through Hermes secret scope) to console.gmicloud.ai; every generation spends GMI credits with no Hermes approval prompt (GMI shows its own price per model, and most video models bill per second). The result is downloaded from the URL GMI returns into the Hermes video cache; the model catalog is read live and cached in memory for one hour. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, self-updates or extra Python dependencies.
entries.title: GMI Cloud video generation
known_issues: Reference images are not supported and are reported as dropped. Image-to-video takes a public http(s) URL.

Live-tested with Minimax-Hailuo-02 (text) and Minimax-Hailuo-2.3-Fast (image). Kling-Text2Video-V1.6-Standard answers that model_name is required, a parameter its schema does not list, so it is not a default.
Shares one client module with gmi-image and gmi-speech from the same repository; each plugin carries its own byte-identical copy.

entries.name: gnani
entries.description: Gnani Prisma transcription and Timbre speech synthesis for Hermes voice notes, live dictation, and voice replies. Registers one native STT provider and one native TTS provider. Sends selected recordings, live audio, optional transcription hints and speech text to api.vachana.ai over HTTPS or WSS. GNANI_API_KEY is resolved through the active Hermes profile. Batch can transfer audio and fetch results through Gnani-issued signed S3 links without the API key. The plugin uses the locally installed ffprobe executable for compressed media inspection, writes requested speech output, and runs a bounded worker during live transcription. Gnani bills the active account. No telemetry. Independent community integration. Disclosure — sends the recordings you transcribe, live microphone audio, optional transcription hints and the text to speak to Gnani (api.vachana.ai) using your GNANI_API_KEY, billed to your Gnani account; long recordings are uploaded and transcripts downloaded through Gnani-issued signed Amazon S3 links; runs your installed ffprobe to measure compressed recordings; requires Python 3.14.
entries.title: Gnani AI Speech
known_issues: The documented presigned upload creation route returned HTTP 404 during testing. Use FLAC or split recordings above 10 MB into smaller files.
Select STT in config.yaml on Hermes v0.23.2.

entries.description: Quantitative claim verification, statistical comparison, and evidence-qualified conclusions. Disclosure — with the optional `automatic_check` and `jev_remote` settings both turned on, sends the checked claim and aggregate evidence counts to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai) with your OpenRouter key for an advisory score, which may incur charges; `automatic_check` alone holds response streaming and may append a note to the agent's final reply.

entries.name: go-whatsapp
entries.description: Outbound WhatsApp tools through GOWA: registers GOWA's native MCP server and adds device listing, pairing, and removal. Setup can connect an existing server or explicitly install pinned GOWA v9.9.0 as a loopback-only authenticated native user service on Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64, or Windows x86_64; credentials are read from the active Hermes profile. Disclosure — agents can send messages and mutate WhatsApp state through the linked account; session databases grant account access. An opt-in, direct-text watch injects one selected account/chat into its existing Hermes session, with WAIT/REPLY/REPORT guidance and a best-effort five-minute inactivity follow-up. Requires a signed route, separate injection permission, and in-process execution. Listening does not authorize replies. No webhook configuration.

entries.name: goalpost
entries.description: Stops an AI agent from making tests pass by weakening the tests. Before a test-file edit or a test command that hides failures runs, Goalpost reads the change and blocks it: adding a skip or xfail marker, deleting a test, removing an assertion, or appending "|| true", "--exit-zero" or "--no-verify". The agent is told why and steered to fix the code. Text-based and model-free, with a local ledger of every decision; mode is block, warn or off.

entries.name: godot-studio
entries.description: Headless Godot 4 workflows for the agent game studio — godot_headless_check (script/resource validation via godot --headless, no editor needed), godot_export (CI builds from named export presets, e.g. a Web build a playtester agent can load), godot_builds (export presets + artifact state: exists/size/modified — gallery data for re-export decisions and attaching fresh builds in chat), godot_setup (read-only install-state report for Godot/godot-ai/uv with the exact registration path). Complements the hi-godot/godot-ai MCP editor bridge by covering the verification and export leg of the loop; bundles the godot-studio skill teaching edit → verify → export → playtest. Ships an optional desktop half (unified package): a Godot version statusbar chip and a builds gallery pane backed by its own read-only dashboard API; opt-in, degrades gracefully when the backend is off. Tools register only when a Godot 4 binary is present (check_fn). Disclosure — runs shell commands (godot --headless against the caller-targeted project; read-only godot --version in the desktop backend; read-only hermes mcp list in godot_setup); godot_headless_check and godot_export execute the target project's own GDScript (autoloads, main scene, export plugins) with no approval prompt — point them only at projects you trust; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no background processes; exports write only inside the target project (the output path is resolved and confined to the project directory, existing files that aren't known export artifacts are never overwritten, and the default is the preset's own export_path from export_presets.cfg); the desktop backend reads export_presets.cfg and artifact metadata inside the project path the user configures in the pane.

entries.name: godseye
entries.description: Eye Of Hermes (EOH) puts a live 3D globe beside your Hermes chat that the agent can fly, read, annotate and watch. It is built on God's Eye View (bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view, MIT). Eleven composable tools (godseye_view, godseye_query, godseye_layers, godseye_feeds, godseye_annotate, godseye_nav, godseye_track, godseye_scene, godseye_watch, godseye_capture, godseye_admin) work on public data (aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, fires, weather, infrastructure and public SDR receivers) and drive the pane in Hermes Desktop and the Webapp. The agent can fly to a place and switch the visual style (night vision, thermal, noir and others); answer "what am I looking at" from the camera, the open pin or your last click; search for places and pin them with research drawers and an attached YouTube or X clip; measure distances and areas and draw walk, bike and drive routes and reach isochrones; compare imagery before and after with Esri Wayback and replay earthquakes and fires on a time slider; walk a route in Street View; follow a public aircraft, ship or satellite by its identifier; play Director camera scenes; leave area watches that report new items on the next chat turn; and save an investigation as an HTML or Markdown report, GeoJSON or KML. The Overlays sidebar lists pins, routes, areas, watches and scenes and imports or exports eoh.overlays.v1 JSON. HUD summaries use your Hermes model (ctx.llm), not OpenAI. Use it for situation briefs on a region, place and travel research, checking a fire or an earthquake, and any answer that is clearer on a map. To start, you need Hermes 0.23.0 or newer, Node 24 or newer (God's Eye View documents 24.14 or later, or 26.x) and a running God's Eye View checkout; the public SDR layer needs gods-eye-view main at or after b361a25. Run hermes plugins install godseye, hermes plugins enable godseye and hermes plugins doctor godseye, open the Eye Of Hermes pane, and start a new chat. Try "Fly to Tokyo and switch to night vision" or "Any earthquakes above magnitude 5 in the last day?" (data questions work with the pane closed). The bundled skill is godseye:godseye-analyst. Photorealistic 3D tiles need CESIUM_ION_TOKEN, live ships need AISSTREAM_API_KEY and fires need FIRMS_MAP_KEY; the Google Maps, Mapillary and TomTom keys are optional. Set them as Hermes secrets. Named-person search, face recognition and tracking of individuals are refused. Disclosure — processes: starts one node MCP child from your God's Eye View checkout, plus git rev-parse, node and systemctl --user children, all with a minimal environment. godseye_admin app_start, app_stop, app_restart and rebuild require confirm=true, are refused inside batch, may run systemctl --user on gods-eye-view.service, start Node on the checkout's vite.js, or run npm run build:panel in the checkout, and refuse a foreign listener. Disclosure — background work and prompt: runs loopback-only HUD bridge (127.0.0.1:18791) and live relay (127.0.0.1:18792) threads gated by a random token stored 0600 in plugin-data; registers a godseye.live-globe system-prompt section and ships the godseye-analyst skill; a pre_llm_call hook may add a short map line and queued watch alerts, whose feed titles are passed as quoted third-party text; an active area watch polls USGS, NASA FIRMS, OpenSky (falling back to api.adsb.lol when OpenSky fails), the local app, or Overpass/Nominatim from a daemon thread. Disclosure — network: place search, routes, isochrones, Wayback metadata and pin research call public services (Nominatim, Overpass and public Overpass mirrors, OSRM, Valhalla, Esri, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wikimedia and venue sites), and private-LAN service URLs are refused. Feed tools, including fire_check, and godseye_query op=sdr_receivers talk to your God's Eye View app, which itself fetches public third-party data feeds and the public SDR receiver directory. Disclosure — credentials: all provider credentials are declared in plugin.yaml requires_env and read only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret; no plugin dotenv reads, key-file installation or process-wide credential mutation. Browser-facing credentials are written only to gitignored mode-0600 runtime config, and server-only secrets never enter the pane. Disclosure — files and pane: overlay import and export stay under plugin-data/godseye/overlays and are not uploaded, and credential-named files are refused for import. Opening a pin drawer that has a clip loads a www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed or platform.twitter.com/embed iframe inside the sandboxed frame. Pane link opens and Ask Hermes run only after a click on the pane's confirm bar. The pane backend adds a base tag, an opt-in UI flag, a Cesium worker shim, the overlay sidebar and Director bridge scripts, and the live agent script inside the sandboxed frame only.
entries.title: Eye Of Hermes (EOH)
known_issues: Full UI in the pane and the in-app HUD via Hermes need two opt-in God's Eye View patches (shipped in patches/, upstream PRs #1571 and #1572); stock upstream gets the globe-only pane.

entries.name: gogogoogle
entries.description: Hand bulk work to Google Antigravity's agy CLI as a worker agent on your Antigravity quota while Hermes keeps its own model, then have a fresh agy conversation verify the result against the real files and git diff. Roles do, research, review and visual-review (judges image files the task names in the workdir); background jobs; resume after timeout; a verifier chain that skips models out of quota until their reset; a git check that fails read-only runs that changed files; per-run stats. Disclosure — Each `antigravity_delegate` call asks for Hermes approval. `do` runs start agy with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so agy can run shell commands and change files outside the workdir. Research, review, visual-review and verification runs deny writes, shell and non-Playwright MCP through agy session rules, which are not an OS sandbox: agy can still read files outside the workdir, and its headless browser (isolated profile) can reach your local network. Task text, files agy reads and a diff excerpt go to Google on your Antigravity account. Writes run logs and job records under the plugin data directory. Experimental, off unless configured: `antigravity_remote_review` sends one review-only task over the system `ssh` client (using your SSH agent and config; the plugin reads no key) to a second Windows machine you set up, where agy runs on that machine's Antigravity account. Tested on one Windows-to-Windows pair only.
known_issues: Requires agy and an authenticated Antigravity account; runs use that account's quota.
Hermes approval policy and other installed plugins can affect the approval boundary; see README.
Research and review permission rules depend on agy behavior and are not an OS sandbox.
Git checks can miss ignored, untracked or binary content changes and do not revert edits.
After a plugin restart job state may be unknown and a subprocess may still be running.
Hermes' CLI approval panel can truncate a long task; the prompt shows task length and hash so truncation is visible.
Research/review rules block writes and shell commands (tested on agy 1.5.1 and 1.5.2) but not reads outside the working directory; blocked actions are listed in the result.
Developed and tested on Windows 11 only. Elsewhere a timed-out run ends agy itself but not necessarily its child processes.

Research, review and verification can use agy's Playwright browser (headless by default; setting browser_mode: headless, visible or off). Page text is untrusted. Playwright tools that run code, type or upload files are denied and every other agy MCP server is denied, but a Playwright tool a later release adds stays allowed until listed. The browser can reach your local network.
The plugin points the browser's snapshot files at a temp folder; an older setup may still leave a .playwright-mcp/ folder in the working directory, which the change check ignores.

Remote review (experimental, only when remote_workers is set): tested on one Windows 11 to Windows 11 pair, review only. Not a sandbox: agy on the worker can read files outside the remote folder. The SSH forced command and spool permissions are documented, not enforced by the plugin. An UNKNOWN or TIMED OUT result does not prove the work stopped; nothing retries automatically.
Without a configured worker, validation warns that antigravity_remote_review is declared but not registered; that is expected.

Known issues: Requires agy and an authenticated Antigravity account; runs use that account's quota.; Hermes approval policy and other installed plugins can affect the approval boundary; see README.; Research and review permission rules depend on agy behavior and are not an OS sandbox.; Git checks can miss ignored, untracked or binary content changes and do not revert edits.; After a plugin restart job state may be unknown and a subprocess may still be running.; Hermes' CLI approval panel can truncate a long task; the prompt shows task length and hash so truncation is visible.; Research/review rules block writes and shell commands (tested on agy 1.5.1 and 1.5.2) but not reads outside the working directory; blocked actions are listed in the result.; Developed and tested on Windows 11 only. Elsewhere a timed-out run ends agy itself but not necessarily its child processes.; Research, review and verification can use agy's Playwright browser (headless by default; setting browser_mode: headless, visible or off). Page text is untrusted. Playwright tools that run code, type or upload files are denied and every other agy MCP server is denied, but a Playwright tool a later release adds stays allowed until listed. The browser can reach your local network.; The plugin points the browser's snapshot files at a temp folder; an older setup may still leave a .playwright-mcp/ folder in the working directory, which the change check ignores.; Remote review (experimental, only when remote_workers is set): tested on one Windows 11 to Windows 11 pair, review only. Not a sandbox: agy on the worker can read files outside the remote folder. The SSH forced command and spool permissions are documented, not enforced by the plugin. An UNKNOWN or TIMED OUT result does not prove the work stopped; nothing retries automatically.; Without a configured worker, validation warns that antigravity_remote_review is declared but not registered; that is expected..

entries.name: goneby
entries.description: Retroactive project memory for LLM agents. Captures every turn into an encrypted per-project write-ahead log (zero tokens during work), then at project close walks the log backward from the shipped product — the oracle — keeping only entries that verifiably contributed; survivors are embedded (MRL-truncated) and stored in Valkey or Qdrant for semantic search in later sessions. General plugin: coexists with any memory provider instead of replacing it. Disclosure — On by default, GoneBy records every chat turn of each project (your messages, the assistant's replies and tool output text) into an encrypted log under your Hermes profile's plugin-data folder. When you close a project, it sends the log to your configured model to choose which entries to keep, sends the kept text to the embedding endpoint you configure (default localhost), and stores it unencrypted in your Valkey or Qdrant database (default localhost). Turn capture off with the `auto_capture` setting or `/goneby gate off`.

entries.name: googlehome
entries.description: Google Home / Nest speaker as the mouth of a Hermes profile: replies are cast over the Cast v2 protocol with zero third-party dependencies, voice arrives from the host microphone through Hermes STT, and one speaker keeps one conversation. known_issues: The speaker's own microphone cannot be used; voice input comes from the host machine's microphone through Hermes STT.
Casting takes the speaker over and interrupts whatever it is already playing.
