entries.name: greenlight
entries.description: Greenlight is a Hermes Agent plugin that puts you in control of xStocks trading. Hermes can prepare a trade, but nothing is sent until you approve it. Ask for a trade and Greenlight shows what you pay, what you get, the fees, a simple risk check and your daily limit in a Hermes Desktop window. Only after you approve do you get a link, or a QR code for your phone's wallet, to confirm the trade in your own wallet, so Greenlight never holds your keys or funds. Approve in the Hermes Desktop window or with /greenlight in the terminal and chat apps. Optional daily and per-trade limits, a stock allowlist and a price-change tolerance. Every decision is kept in a tamper-evident history. Includes a no-wallet practice trade. Disclosure — crypto (Solana xStocks trading): talks to api.xstocker.com and xstocker.com, sending the wallet address, stock, amount, side and pay token for each quote and transaction signatures for status checks, through the official xStocker SDK (bundled unmodified in vendor/agent-sdk and used when Node.js 18+ is installed) or, without Node.js, directly over the same public HTTPS endpoints with Python's standard library; nothing is installed or downloaded at runtime and the plugin never updates itself; with Node.js, a short-lived node process per price request with a fixed command (node sdk-bridge.js), no shell and never an AI-chosen command; trades are released only after the user approves in the Desktop pane or with /greenlight approve (any user allowed to use that chat can run it) and are signed in the user's own wallet; writes only to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/greenlight/ (or GREENLIGHT_DATA_DIR if set); reads no credentials; no telemetry; no Python dependencies; Node.js is optional.

entries.name: greyridge-token-safety

Its verdict is a heuristic, not financial advice.
known_issues: Base chain only; DEX buy/sell tax is not measured (only transferTaxBps). Free preview is rate-limited; unattended use needs the paid x402 route ($0.01/call).

entries.name: grok-bot-twin
entries.description: Try Hermes without leaving Grok. Gives each Grok desktop-app bot a Hermes twin profile and a Desktop Twins page (conflicts, restore points); `hermes twin demo` needs no Grok account. Name and description changes reach the twin in seconds; instructions are pasted by you or imported from the setup export the bot writes about itself (routines arrive paused, connectors as names only, its memories are dropped); skills travel through optional guided skill sync (a sync bot in your own Grok account); a bot's Grok memory and model setting are not copied. Several new twins are finished in one sheet: one model for all of them (model servers already set up in Hermes listed first) and each twin's instructions from its own setup export, picked up from Downloads, a dropped file or skill sync's shared folder; optionally Hermes does the Grok part with computer use, asking before every step. Optional and off by default: the same twins on your other Hermes computers (macOS, Linux, Windows), linked once with a short code, with settings that follow by a fixed allowlist, skills, routines and end-to-end-encrypted memory each behind its own switch, and requests from one of your computers to a twin on another. Unofficial; not affiliated with xAI. Disclosure — Runs the user-installed external botport CLI (never bundled or downloaded; before it is ever run it is checked against the release SHA-256 digests shipped with the plugin or with `gh attestation verify` against hudsonwa/botport's release workflow, and its digest is pinned; `hermes twin setup --allow-unattested` is a recorded opt-out), plus `gh` (for that check only) and `hermes cron` (resume and pause on "Move routines to Hermes", create --paused when importing a setup export), each with a minimal environment; while the new-twins sheet watches for setup exports (at most 15 minutes, every 4 s) the plugin lists your Downloads folder (that folder only: names, dates, sizes) and reads new .json, .txt or .md files of at most 2 MB there and, with skill sync set up, in the shared folder's exports/ (nothing moved or deleted; only digests are kept); it writes the model you choose into each twin profile's config.yaml; via botport it reads the Grok desktop app's bot list and the selected bots' local transcript files (capped, parsed for routine changes only) and writes the twin Hermes profiles it manages; the plugin writes plugin-data/grok-bot-twin/, its own marked blocks in twin profiles' SOUL.md, plugins.enabled, a copy of itself and the allowlisted settings in each twin profile, a note per removed twin in profiles/.deleted/, and, only with their switches on, twins' skill files, memory files and cron jobs; botport keeps one owner-only key file per twin; it runs one background metadata-check/sync thread (default every 60 s) and one Grok-folder watch once a session starts, plus threads for the sharing features only while they are on; it sends no telemetry; it calls Hermes' internal skill scanner (tools.skills_guard, fail-open) for the demo's skill preview. An optional pre_tool_call hook is active only for 30 minutes after you start "Let Hermes do the Grok part" and tick that you approve each step: it makes Hermes ask before every computer_use step and refuses other apps, other chats and other typed text; pictures of the Grok window then go to that chat's model provider. Network: none unless you switch on sharing; then the computer with the Grok app listens on ONE private address (its Tailscale address, else its home-network address; never all interfaces or a public one; TCP 18777) and your linked computers connect only to that address; linking proves a one-time 12-character link code (SPEKE; the code never travels) and every later call and answer is signed with a per-computer key; plain HTTP, encrypted by Tailscale on Tailscale, readable but not forgeable on a plain home network, except a twin's memory, which the plugin encrypts end to end. Besides that, the plugin connects only to the model servers already set up in your default Hermes config.yaml, with one `GET <base_url>/models` each (at most 6, no key sent) when the new-twins sheet lists models; it never downloads a model (only `gh` reaches GitHub, for the attestation check). A request from another of your computers (off on each computer until switched on there) runs as one ordinary Hermes chat turn of that twin, under that computer's own approval rules; a step that needs approval waits on that computer unless you chose there to let your own linked computers approve. An optional background helper (a launchd agent, systemd user unit or scheduled task of your own account, set up with launchctl, systemctl or schtasks; never root or SYSTEM) keeps a linked computer following while Hermes is closed.
entries.title: Grok Bot Twin
known_issues: Real twins need botport v0.2.1 on the Mac that has the Grok desktop app; you download it yourself (the Twins page opens the release file for your computer) and the plugin verifies it before it is run. Without it only the sample works. botport has no Windows build, so a Windows computer can link to your Mac but cannot share.

Sharing between computers is signed, not encrypted by the plugin: on Tailscale it is encrypted by Tailscale; on a plain home network someone on that network can read twin names, descriptions and the settings that follow, the persona included (and skills, routines, and requests and answers, where you switched those on) but cannot change them. A twin's memory is the exception: the plugin encrypts it between the two computers.

A linked computer finds the sharing one by the address in the link code. If a home-network address changes, unlink and link again (twins come back with their chats). Tailscale addresses do not change.

From the Grok desktop app's local files, botport opens only the bot list and the selected bots' transcript files; those hold no instructions, skills, schedules or connections. Instructions are pasted by you or imported from the setup export the bot writes when you ask it (routines then arrive switched off, connections as names only); skills can travel through optional skill sync, whose Grok half was tested against botport in a pretend box with invented bots, not inside a Grok account; a bot's Grok memory and Grok model setting are not copied. Between your own computers skills and settings follow one way, from the Mac with the Grok app, and a connector must be set up on each computer (only its name follows).

Staying up to date while Hermes is closed is a terminal command (`hermes twin background on`), not a button. The Twins page was clicked through on macOS only; Linux (Omarchy, no other distribution) and Windows were tested with the terminal commands.

Finishing several twins at once was tested with invented bots and setup-export files, not inside a Grok account; whether a bot also saves its export into skill sync's shared folder when asked is not verified, so Downloads and drag and drop stay the default.
Under plugins.isolation: host, Hermes skips plugin CLI commands, so `hermes twin` is unavailable; use `/twin` or the Twins page in Hermes Desktop.

Disclosure — Runs the user-installed external botport CLI (never bundled or downloaded; before it is ever run it is checked against the release SHA-256 digests shipped with the plugin or with `gh attestation verify` against hudsonwa/botport's release workflow, and its digest is pinned; `hermes twin setup --allow-unattested` is a recorded opt-out), plus `gh` (for that check only) and `hermes cron` (resume and pause on "Move routines to Hermes", create --paused when importing a setup export), each with a minimal environment; while the new-twins sheet watches for setup exports (at most 15 minutes, every 4 s) the plugin lists your Downloads folder (that folder only: names, dates, sizes) and reads new .json, .txt or .md files of at most 2 MB there and, with skill sync set up, in the shared folder's exports/ (nothing moved or deleted; only digests are kept); it writes the model you choose into each twin profile's config.yaml; via botport it reads the Grok desktop app's bot list and the selected bots' local transcript files (capped, parsed for routine changes only) and writes the twin Hermes profiles it manages; the plugin writes plugin-data/grok-bot-twin/, its own marked blocks in twin profiles' SOUL.md, plugins.enabled, a copy of itself and the allowlisted settings in each twin profile, a note per removed twin in profiles/.deleted/, and, only with their switches on, twins' skill files, memory files and cron jobs; botport keeps one owner-only key file per twin; it runs one background metadata-check/sync thread (default every 60 s) and one Grok-folder watch once a session starts, plus threads for the sharing features only while they are on; it sends no telemetry; it calls Hermes' internal skill scanner (tools.skills_guard, fail-open) for the demo's skill preview. An optional pre_tool_call hook is active only for 30 minutes after you start "Let Hermes do the Grok part" and tick that you approve each step: it makes Hermes ask before every computer_use step and refuses other apps, other chats and other typed text; pictures of the Grok window then go to that chat's model provider. Network: none unless you switch on sharing; then the computer with the Grok app listens on ONE private address (its Tailscale address, else its home-network address; never all interfaces or a public one; TCP 18777) and your linked computers connect only to that address; linking proves a one-time 12-character link code (SPEKE; the code never travels) and every later call and answer is signed with a per-computer key; plain HTTP, encrypted by Tailscale on Tailscale, readable but not forgeable on a plain home network, except a twin's memory, which the plugin encrypts end to end. Besides that, the plugin connects only to the model servers already set up in your default Hermes config.yaml, with one `GET <base_url>/models` each (at most 6, no key sent) when the new-twins sheet lists models; it never downloads a model (only `gh` reaches GitHub, for the attestation check). A request from another of your computers (off on each computer until switched on there) runs as one ordinary Hermes chat turn of that twin, under that computer's own approval rules; a step that needs approval waits on that computer unless you chose there to let your own linked computers approve. An optional background helper (a launchd agent, systemd user unit or scheduled task of your own account, set up with launchctl, systemctl or schtasks; never root or SYSTEM) keeps a linked computer following while Hermes is closed. This plugin registers tool(s): twin_status, twin_recent, twin_ask_machine; hook(s): pre_llm_call, on_session_start, on_session_end, pre_tool_call. Platforms: macos, linux, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7. Known issues: Real twins need botport v0.2.1 on the Mac that has the Grok desktop app; you download it yourself (the Twins page opens the release file for your computer) and the plugin verifies it before it is run. Without it only the sample works. botport has no Windows build, so a Windows computer can link to your Mac but cannot share.; Sharing between computers is signed, not encrypted by the plugin: on Tailscale it is encrypted by Tailscale; on a plain home network someone on that network can read twin names, descriptions and the settings that follow, the persona included (and skills, routines, and requests and answers, where you switched those on) but cannot change them. A twin's memory is the exception: the plugin encrypts it between the two computers.; A linked computer finds the sharing one by the address in the link code. If a home-network address changes, unlink and link again (twins come back with their chats). Tailscale addresses do not change.; From the Grok desktop app's local files, botport opens only the bot list and the selected bots' transcript files; those hold no instructions, skills, schedules or connections. Instructions are pasted by you or imported from the setup export the bot writes when you ask it (routines then arrive switched off, connections as names only); skills can travel through optional skill sync, whose Grok half was tested against botport in a pretend box with invented bots, not inside a Grok account; a bot's Grok memory and Grok model setting are not copied. Between your own computers skills and settings follow one way, from the Mac with the Grok app, and a connector must be set up on each computer (only its name follows).; Staying up to date while Hermes is closed is a terminal command (`hermes twin background on`), not a button. The Twins page was clicked through on macOS only; Linux (Omarchy, no other distribution) and Windows were tested with the terminal commands.; Finishing several twins at once was tested with invented bots and setup-export files, not inside a Grok account; whether a bot also saves its export into skill sync's shared folder when asked is not verified, so Downloads and drag and drop stay the default.; Under plugins.isolation: host, Hermes skips plugin CLI commands, so `hermes twin` is unavailable; use `/twin` or the Twins page in Hermes Desktop..

entries.name: grokbot-staff
entries.description: G.I.M.F. (Grok is my friend): a chief-of-staff and specialist team inside Hermes (chief, research, design, writing, product, engineering — or a team you configure), plus an optional fail-closed bridge that hands long-running work to your own Grok Bot. Local staff answers with your current Hermes model via ctx.llm. Slash commands /staff and /grokbot, a staff delegation backend for delegate_task, a bundled skill, and a Desktop pane for the roster, pending handoffs and recent jobs. The bridge does not call any Grok Bot API (there is none); it POSTs a JSON handoff to a webhook URL you set and/or writes handoffs/<id>.json in a folder you set, then collects results/<id>.json|.md|.txt or a pasted answer. Not an importer and not Grok Bot calling Hermes — Hermes delegating to Grok Bot. Disclosure — Answers staff tasks with your current Hermes model through ctx.llm whenever a staff tool or slash command runs. When grokbot_delegate runs, POSTs the task as JSON only to the webhook URL you configure (stored as the GROKBOT_STAFF_WEBHOOK_URL secret; https only, http allowed for localhost; redirects refused) and/or writes handoffs/<id>.json in the inbox folder you set, then reads results/<id>.json|.md|.txt from that folder (symlinks and files over 2 MB ignored) and returns that text to the agent. A specialist you map to a Hermes profile makes the `staff` delegation backend run delegated tasks as that profile, with its credentials. Job tasks, answers and collected results are stored in the plugin's own data folder. The Desktop pane polls a read-only /overview dashboard route every 10 seconds. No shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: groq-provider
entries.description: Groq as a Hermes model provider (`--provider groq`, or Groq in `hermes model`): reasoning effort is sent in the form each Groq model accepts, so gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b work (through a custom endpoint, Hermes 0.21.5 sends them a value Groq rejects with HTTP 400), and the model list leaves out Groq's speech-to-text, text-to-speech, prompt-guard and 4K-context models that Hermes cannot run. Not affiliated with Groq. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' own client with GROQ_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: grounded-recall
entries.description: Before every model turn, searches your existing markdown notes (plain folders or an Obsidian vault), this profile's recent sessions and, opt-in, secret-manager item titles (never values), then injects a capped evidence block where each hit is labelled CURRENT, UNVERIFIED or HISTORICAL by freshness, plus a rule to search before answering "it doesn't exist / I have no access / I don't know". Every injection is logged per profile. No new memory store, works alongside any memory provider. Disclosure — on every turn reads the configured markdown folders, key-facts file and this profile's session store (state.db, read-only) and injects matching excerpts into the prompt; writes an audit log under the active Hermes home; when secret-title search is configured it runs the user-configured secret-manager CLI in the background with a minimal environment (plus the variable names listed in `secret_titles_env`) and keeps only item titles; when the optional semantic re-rank is enabled it sends the user message and candidate note excerpts to the user-configured embeddings URL.
entries.title: Grounded Recall
known_issues: With no roots configured it only searches sessions; add a notes folder for useful results.

entries.name: grounder
entries.description: Grounder as the web_search and web_extract backend: each search is one call to one search provider, plus the live-data APIs (scores, prices, odds, flights and more) as you set each one, and returns one list of licensed results, each uncut. Free searches need no account. Connect a Grounder search key or `hermes auth add grounder:grounder` for more. While Grounder is the web search backend, `/search` (the plugin's only command; on Slack, `/hermes search`) opens a menu that chooses how Grounder searches, in three modes: Grounder optimized (the default), a Grounder preset (Fast, Cheap, Live, Deep, Code or Balanced) or Grounder direct (one provider you pick, and what it finds is what you get, even nothing), and sets each live-data API to Every call, Never or Grounder decides (the default), in every mode, and saves that choice on the Grounder account, the one setting grounder.net's Routing page also shows. A web_extract returns each page's text, read for the question of the search that found it, or the user's latest message when no search did. Adds grounder_search, for Grounder's own search options, and grounder_list_providers. Disclosure — each web_search query and web_extract page address is sent to api.grounder.net, passed on to the search provider and live-data APIs that answer it and to the service providers that help run a search, and kept under your Grounder account indefinitely (a free search has no account); when the model reads a page no Grounder search returned, your latest chat message (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as the ranking query; /search reads and writes your saved search setting on your Grounder account; with GROUNDER_X402_PRIVATE_KEY set (unset by default), a free search Grounder answers with an x402 payment request is paid from that wallet in USDC on Base to the payee Grounder names, at most GROUNDER_X402_MAX_PER_SEARCH US dollars a search (default 0.05) with no total limit beyond the wallet's balance and no approval prompt (scheduled and unattended runs included), the wallet's key kept in the profile's .env in plain text, and a search with a search key or a sign-in is never paid from it; usage context is off by default, and only after `hermes config set web.grounder.share_usage_context true` and a restart does a search also carry two random session and prompt tokens and the name of the model that asked; the first load in a profile makes Grounder the web_search and/or web_extract backend only where none is chosen yet, and writes Grounder's public OAuth client id to the profile's .env when no search key is set; answers that used Grounder get a Sources list and a "Searched with Grounder" line appended.
entries.title: Grounder
known_issues: /search is registered only while Grounder is the web search backend; a switch made in hermes tools takes effect at the next start

Usage context (the model's name and two random session and prompt tokens on each search) is off by default. hermes config set web.grounder.share_usage_context true, then restart Hermes, turns it on and registers the post_api_request hook

With no search key, the first load writes the public GROUNDER_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID to the profile's .env, which `hermes auth add` needs for the sign-in and which keeps Hermes's web tools on while Grounder is a selected backend
Signing in before Hermes has started once needs the client id first: hermes config set GROUNDER_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID https://api.grounder.net/oauth/clients/hermes-agent. A search key needs no client id
An account gets 50 free searches a day. Past that, searches use credit bought on the account

entries.name: gsc-magic
entries.description: Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Google Analytics 4, IndexNow and Core Web Vitals through GSC Magic's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.gscmagic.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): search analytics, URL inspection, sitemaps, GA4 reports, CrUX and PageSpeed, plus finished SEO reports (quick wins, traffic drops, content decay, cannibalization, CTR outliers, brand split, index health, Google vs Bing) with optional PNG charts. Bundles the gsc-magic workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to GSC Magic's hosted server (mcp.gscmagic.com) and reads the user's own connected Google, Bing and GA4 accounts; calls count toward the user's GSC Magic plan and are logged (tool, site, status, time) for 30 days in the user's dashboard; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Write tools (sitemaps, site management, Bing URL submission, IndexNow) work only on paid plans with write mode turned on, and the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Hermes's connect timeout instead of hanging. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with hermes mcp add gsc-magic --url https://mcp.gscmagic.com/mcp --auth oauth (or a token header) and keep the skill.

entries.name: guild
entries.description: Shared skill library for a team's Hermes agents, or for one person's machines and profiles, kept in a git repository the team controls. A skill an agent saved is scrubbed of API keys, home folder paths, e-mail addresses and private IPs, pushed as a proposal branch, and merged only after a teammate approves it from the CLI, TUI or Desktop. Each member's agent then loads approved skills read-only. If an agent tries to edit a team skill, a pre_tool_call hook refuses the edit and tells it to use guild_propose. Hermes Desktop gets a Guild page to review diffs and approve or decline. Commands: `hermes guild init|join|propose|review|show|approve|reject|revert|log` and `/guild`. Disclosure — runs local `git` subprocesses (repository hooks disabled, no terminal prompts, only the environment variables git and ssh need) that fetch from and push to the remote you configure, using your existing git credentials; contacts nothing else and stores no credentials. Only the files of a skill you propose, or that your agent proposes after the approval prompt, leave the machine, with your member name in the commit. Optional background sync at session start (auto_sync_minutes, default 15, 0 turns it off); a sync moves a local skill identical to the team copy, or your own accepted proposal, into the plugin's backups folder. In a solo guild proposals are committed straight to main with no review. `init` and `join` add the library folder to the profile's skills.external_dirs and `leave` removes it. The write check reads tool arguments and does not inspect execute_code. The reviewer list is enforced by the plugin only; use branch protection on the git host for a server-side guarantee.

entries.name: habits
entries.description: Habits gives Hermes reflexes: the tool calls and small decisions it repeats, grouped into one file of steps that runs with no model turn between the steps (the advanced llm step is the one exception); decisions go to a small typed model (Jev). "Is Hermes OK?": 41 s when Hermes works it out, 2.7 s when the reflex answers with its six checks (medians of real chats, 10 November; the fast path needs your yes and a Jev key). A reflex has four kinds of step (do, check, ask, use) and ends done, or handed back with what is left. The dream re-reads the history Hermes already keeps, with no model call, and proposes reflexes for what comes back. A reflex acts on its own only after your yes, with two exceptions named below. Try without a key: hermes habits run hermes-health. Disclosure — hooks read each user message, reply and tool call; the dream reads Hermes's local session history (read only, 60 days) at most once a day (dream: manual stops it) and calls no model. Learning defaults to suggest: nothing is practised or run for you until you say try; learning: auto lets learned reflexes act with no question. A list of your reflexes (2,400 characters at most) is added to the system prompt, and Hermes may run any shipped example by name without a yes, for real (six only read; tidy-downloads moves files inside ~/Downloads). An automatic request habit can answer a message itself, without a model call, and a habit that starts on its skill runs when Hermes loads that skill. A read-only request habit you explicitly asked for starts automatic at once. Reflex commands run through Hermes's own terminal and tools under Hermes's approval rules. hermes-health sends one HEAD request to github.com and reads ~/.hermes gateway state, logs and disk use; other examples reach api.github.com, hn.algolia.com and the pages you or Hermes name. With TYPESAFE_API_KEY set, decision questions go to TypeSafe Jev (api.typesafe.ai), else to your own Hermes model. Once a message habit exists, each non-slash message of 2,000 characters or less goes there with your habit names and descriptions, and a reflex's ask steps send the text the reflex read (file names, page text). Saving a scheduled habit (every 5 minutes at most often) writes $HERMES_HOME/scripts/habits-<name>.sh and a Hermes cron job at once, before any yes, and is refused inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true; hermes habits cleanup removes every habits-* job and script. Runs and traces are stored unencrypted in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/habits/. No telemetry. Private Hermes imports are read-only, each with a fallback (docs/SAFETY.md §10).
entries.title: Habits
known_issues: Without a TypeSafe Jev key, steps that ask a question go to your Hermes model, slower, and those runs do not count toward your yes: a reflex with such a step stays learning.

Measured on one user's install, with one cheap model and one decision model (Jev); 14 of 20 request wordings never seen before were recognized, the others go back to Hermes. The headline figures are from the builds of 10 November; an earlier build of 11 November (aad995e) was tried in 229 simulated turns on throwaway Hermes profiles (docs/BENCHMARKS.md); the fixes made after it are covered by tests and by one short pass of 9 real turns on the last build.
The guard and the dream's exclusion of secrets are word-and-shape checks, not proofs; docs/SAFETY.md lists what they do not see.
With permissions: hermes, Hermes does not ask about every deletion: on Hermes 0.23 a plain rm of one file is not flagged. Set permissions: strict to make the plugin refuse deleting commands.
The dream proposes fixed actions only, and few real actions are local reads, so most practice counts that an action came back, not that a result matched.
What the dream gives on day one is a list of repeated gestures and proposals; the saving comes once reflexes are assembled or made by asking. No gain from a dream-born reflex has been measured yet.
The start on a loaded skill worked 2 of 2 on a real Hermes (11 November); a real MCP server: not tried.
A scheduled habit's cron job exists from the save, before any yes; run hermes habits cleanup before you uninstall.

entries.name: harness2
entries.description: The Harness^2 self-improvement loop for Hermes profiles. The plugin edits the files that shape the agent (system prompt + config overlay + skills) for a class of work. A harness is that set of files. It runs a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose cycle over isolated probe sessions. A contrastive cycle runs each edit against the unedited base. A probe is a fresh one-shot agent session under one harness. After the cycle, the plugin saves the lessons that the evidence supports. It saves them in a per-profile improvement library. The library is what future tasks read before editing. After each round, the promote stage writes a carry-over report. The report shows what the banked harness changed and what to apply to the live profile. A banked harness is the saved harness from a finished round. A live profile is the profile you use day to day. The user applies it. The plugin never writes the live profile. The fixed machinery (profile materialization, probe runs, structural gate, library) is tools. The judgment stages run in the host session under bundled skills that point at the verbatim stage prompts from arXiv:2610.14224. Disclosure — runs `hermes profile create --clone` and one-shot `hermes -p harness2-<task>-<probe> chat` subprocesses; each probe is a full agent session with the profile's tools (web included), billed to your configured model, with a per-probe time limit (900 seconds by default). It creates and deletes probe profiles named harness2-*, each cloned once from the active profile (configuration and .env under Hermes' own clone policy), and sets only an allowlisted set of overlay keys on them through `hermes config set` while pinning approvals to smart mode with single-query and cron runs denied, subagent auto-approve off and secret redaction on. It writes only its own plugin data and the probe profiles, never your live profile, and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: harnmem
entries.description: Cross-harness long-term memory for Hermes: injects a byte-stable memory snapshot each turn, exposes harnmem_write/search/read/forget/status tools, and can extract new memories when a session ends. Memories are plain Markdown under ~/.harnmem, shared with the pi, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, DSH, Grok, Cursor and omp adapters; the engine itself never opens a network connection. Disclosure — with auto-extract enabled the plugin sends the session transcript to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure, runs a local Node.js child process for every memory operation, and spawns a short-lived detached extractor at session end. The extraction key is read through Hermes' secret scope; the plugin collects no telemetry.
entries.title: HarnMem
known_issues: Extraction needs a plain OpenAI-compatible endpoint; gateways that require proprietary headers are not supported yet (custom headers are a follow-up shared with the CLI).

entries.name: hashference-provider
entries.description: Hashference as a Hermes model provider (`--provider hashference`, or Hashference in `hermes model`): open and frontier models on one balance, funded by mining, QUAI, Qi or staking. Each model's real limits come from Hashference's catalog: the hosted models accept 98,304 input tokens inside a 163,840-token window and cap output at 8,192, so Hermes compresses before an oversized-input refusal; models that cannot call tools are left out of the model list. Disclosure — model provider; chat requests (full prompts) go to https://hashference.com/v1 (or your configured base_url) using HASHFERENCE_API_KEY read by Hermes; the plugin itself only sends an unauthenticated GET of the public model catalog (/v1/models), cached ten minutes.

entries.name: hathor-catchup
entries.description: Check a child's vaccination card against a sourced national schedule (Egypt, Sudan, Syria, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Eritrea, South Sudan, WHO) and get the missing doses and a dated catch-up plan. entries.name: headroom
entries.description: Keeps Hermes alive on small machines (1-4 GB VPS, Raspberry Pi). Heavy terminal jobs (package installs, builds, test suites, compilers, browsers, nested agents) wait for a machine-wide slot and enough free RAM, run inside their own memory-capped systemd --user scope with a raised OOM score, get single-worker flags where a stable one exists (jest --runInBand, pytest -n 0, make -jN, cargo -j N, Node heap cap), and are stopped by a watchdog if the host nears OOM or Hermes' own cgroup starts stalling. Hermes stays outside the scope, and the tool result tells the model the cap, the peak and whether the kernel killed the job, so it retries lighter. Adds headroom_status, /headroom and hermes headroom status|events|explain|selftest. Disclosure — Linux only for enforcement; runs busctl --user (StartTransientUnit, AttachProcessesToUnit) and systemctl --user kill/reset-failed for its own headroom-*.scope units with a reduced environment (PATH, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS), plus one sleep placeholder process per isolated job; reads /proc meminfo, PSI and stat/status/cmdline/cgroup of the user's own processes and cgroup files of its scopes and Hermes' cgroup; raises oom_score_adj of job processes; kills only processes inside its own scopes (or a tracked job's process group without systemd) when the watchdog fires; rewrites heavy commands before approval so the approved command is what runs; writes events to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/headroom/events.jsonl and slot locks to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hermes-headroom (or an owner-checked hermes-headroom-<uid> directory in the system temp dir); no network, no telemetry, no credentials; reads tools.interrupt.is_interrupted (guarded) so /stop cancels a queued command.

entries.name: heartbeat2
entries.description: Give your agent a working life between your messages. Put it in charge of something and it keeps working on it on its own time. A role is a standing responsibility with a charter, a notebook the agent keeps between turns and a rhythm it sets itself, and it doesn't expire on a timer. Turn on own time and the agent gets regular turns of its own: it looks at its desk (its roles, what's due, what it noticed, the budget left) and decides what to do. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) can also arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Hermes event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions) that cost no model call until something changes. Every wake is a turn in the same conversation, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Quiet work counts: a silent turn that makes progress is real work, and only wakes that keep finding nothing to do slow down, then pause and ask once. The guardrails are budgets you set: turns per day, an optional daily cost limit, turns per role, messages per day, the unanswered mute and quiet hours. They hold back messages and spending, not initiative, and the agent can tighten its own limits but never widen yours. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps, and a watcher you ask for keeps sending its alerts while the unanswered mute is on (quiet hours and the daily message cap still hold them); HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire. It delivers to messaging-gateway DMs by default (group and topic chats too when dm_only is off), and to Hermes Desktop and TUI chats on Hermes 0.23 or later, where a wake waits while the app window is closed (after a short grace in which Hermes may still run it unseen); it needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow_gateway_injection: true. Ships the plugin skill `heartbeat2:heartbeat2-report-problem`, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — wakes, watchers, roles and own-time turns run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes, watchers and roles itself unless you set agent_can_create to ask_first or no; roles have no expiry, and a role can bring forward a follow-on role it names (handoff_to) in the same chat, within that role's usual limits, and the follow-on role receives the handing-off role's title (or note) and a summary of up to 500 characters as work input; the agent's recurring wakes, roles and watchers keep running turns during quiet hours, while the unanswered mute is on and after the daily message cap (only their messages are held; what a watcher found is passed on in one report-back turn per chat once messages can be sent, or with your next message), up to the daily turn cap and the optional daily_cost_limit_usd (no cost limit by default); keep-warm (off unless you send /pulse warm on in a chat) runs a short silent turn on that chat's model just before its prompt cache expires, while you have written there within keep_warm_idle_hours (12 h by default), billed like any message but outside the daily turn cap and daily_cost_limit_usd; own-time turns (off by default, own_time_hours) run without an assigned task; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, unless you name one for an allowed command in probe_command_env) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote <url>` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Hermes blocks from reading; in Desktop and TUI chats Hermes still shows a silent turn's text in the app window, and with notify_via set (blank by default) a wake held for 10 minutes on a closed app window sends one short notice per wait through the plugin it names (how many wakes wait, since when, the profile and app; no titles, notes or payloads), delayed by quiet hours and counted toward the daily message cap; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.
entries.title: HeartBeat 2.0
known_issues: A wake turn that fails at the provider shows Hermes's own failure notice; the plugin cannot suppress it (NousResearch/hermes-agent#136749). HeartBeat 2.0 backs all wakes off until a model call on the profile succeeds.

notify=false silences the final reply; platforms that show tool progress by default (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix) still show a progress bubble per wake turn unless display.platforms.

.tool_progress is off (quiet injection requested upstream: NousResearch/hermes-agent#136825).

Delivers to messaging-gateway chats (DMs by default, group and topic chats too when dm_only is off) and, on Hermes 0.23 or later, to Desktop and TUI chats, where a wake waits while the app window is closed (after a short grace in which Hermes may still run it unseen) and Hermes still shows a silent turn's text (NousResearch/hermes-agent#156465). CLI, API-server (NousResearch/hermes-agent#156466) and cron arming are refused.
When Hermes falls back to another model during a wake turn, its model-fallback notice is posted to the chat, even for a wake that stays silent (NousResearch/hermes-agent#137738).

keep-warm (off unless you send /pulse warm on in a chat) runs a short silent turn on that chat's model just before its prompt cache expires, while you have written there within keep_warm_idle_hours (12 h by default), billed like any message but outside the daily turn cap and daily_cost_limit_usd; own-time turns (off by default, own_time_hours) run without an assigned task; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, unless you name one for an allowed command in probe_command_env) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and `git ls-remote ` / `gh -R` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url_allow_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Hermes blocks from reading; in Desktop and TUI chats Hermes still shows a silent turn's text in the app window, and with notify_via set (blank by default) a wake held for 10 minutes on a closed app window sends one short notice per wait through the plugin it names (how many wakes wait, since when, the profile and app; no titles, notes or payloads), delayed by quiet hours and counted toward the daily message cap; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry. This plugin registers tool(s): pulse; hook(s): pre_gateway_dispatch, gateway_platform_event, pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, post_api_request, transform_llm_output, on_session_end, agent_loop_stopped, on_session_reset, kanban_task_completed, kanban_task_blocked, on_kanban_worker_exited, subagent_start, subagent_stop, api_request_error. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6. Known issues: A wake turn that fails at the provider shows Hermes's own failure notice; the plugin cannot suppress it (NousResearch/hermes-agent#136749). HeartBeat 2.0 backs all wakes off until a model call on the profile succeeds.; notify=false silences the final reply; platforms that show tool progress by default (Discord, WhatsApp, Matrix) still show a progress bubble per wake turn unless display.platforms.

.tool_progress is off (quiet injection requested upstream: NousResearch/hermes-agent#136825).; Delivers to messaging-gateway chats (DMs by default, group and topic chats too when dm_only is off) and, on Hermes 0.23 or later, to Desktop and TUI chats, where a wake waits while the app window is closed (after a short grace in which Hermes may still run it unseen) and Hermes still shows a silent turn's text (NousResearch/hermes-agent#156465). CLI, API-server (NousResearch/hermes-agent#156466) and cron arming are refused.; When Hermes falls back to another model during a wake turn, its model-fallback notice is posted to the chat, even for a wake that stays silent (NousResearch/hermes-agent#137738)..

entries.name: heats
entries.description: Your tests, not the model, decide when a fix is done. A pre_verify referee runs the repo's check when the agent edited code and is about to finish, and sends it back with the real test output if the check fails. When one attempt is not enough, heats_run races N attempts in separate git worktrees (subagents launched through the public lifecycle API, kept inside their worktree by a tool_request middleware); failing attempts are restarted with the measured output, attempts that edit tests cannot win, and the winner is applied with one call. Desktop pane with live lanes and an Apply winner button. Disclosure: the referee runs your check command in your checkout after code edits, only in repos you approved with /heats trust (none by default; it will not run a check whose defining files the agent edited in that turn); heats_run asks for your approval before running a model-supplied or untrusted check; checks get a minimal environment (no provider keys); races create and remove git worktrees and branches under <repo>/.heats/, run the check in each worktree (never for an attempt that edited what the check runs) and launch N subagents on your delegation model (cost scales with N); saves reports and patches under plugin-data/heats; Desktop routes under /api/plugins/heats/; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: hebe-longevity
entries.description: Personal Longevity Intelligence for Hermes, built on Insilico Medicine's open PLSI toolbelt (MIT). Reads nine routine blood markers from a confirmed CSV or typed panel, calculates Blood PhenoAge, shows trends and formula drivers across blood draws, and drafts safety-screened research plans challenged by a separate model call before only the user can start a plan. Includes a Hebe page and optional theme in Hermes Desktop plus a chat result card. Disclosure — PhenoAge, trend and local HTML reports make no network or model calls. The Desktop page loads Cormorant Garamond and Montserrat from Google Fonts (falls back to system fonts offline). Planning tools run a pinned subset of the PLSI CLI as a child process of Hermes' Python with fixed argument lists (no shell) and a minimal environment, and query PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA, RxNav (NIH), doi.org or Evipedia with topic queries and plan action names only. The challenger runs through Hermes' own auxiliary LLM task (auxiliary.hebe_challenger); Hermes itself sends chat and tool outputs to the user's configured model. Data is stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hebe-longevity. No telemetry, self-updater or background daemon. Research prototype, not medical advice.
entries.title: Hebe Longevity
known_issues: Research and educational prototype; not a medical device, diagnosis or treatment recommendation.
Requires PLSI's Python dependencies (pydantic>=2,<3 and PyYAML>=6,<7), which Hermes installs on confirmation.
The install scanner reports a caution on unchanged upstream PLSI code (a variable named env in formula.py and pip install hints in error messages).
For an independent challenger, configure auxiliary.hebe_challenger to use a strong model different from your chat model; if that provider fails, Hermes falls back to another configured model.

entries.name: heirpros
entries.description: Estimate the research hours for a US probate heir search (locating missing and unknown heirs for an estate) through HeirPros' free MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://heirpros.com/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): hours from the number of known and estimated unknown heirs (1.5 base hours + 1 per heir, the same formula as the heirpros.com calculator), plus general information about HeirPros' heir search service. Hours only, no pricing. Bundles the heir-search-estimate skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to heirpros.com, run by HeirPros, which does not store or email what is sent. Both tools are annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes would ask before any tool that is not. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: helm
entries.description: A redesigned Hermes Desktop. A Desk home page (greeting and crew status, a prompt that hands work to any bot, Continue, Needs you, Today's scheduled jobs); pending tool approvals and questions from every bot's live chats answered in one place, on the Desk and in a sidebar pane, only on your click; a Session pane with the focused chat's live task plan; a themeable redesign layer across the app (three bases, seven accents, type, corners, density) on a Customize look page; status everywhere (titlebar, session rows, status bar); and a Bots board of rendered robots (191 Blender-rendered PNG layers) that become each bot's Hermes avatar. Disclosure — desktop half uses only Desktop SDK areas and public gateway calls the app itself makes: host.profiles.list and host.listPersistedSessions (held in memory), session.active_list, approval.pending, session.history (the focused chat's plan), cron.manage action list only (never adds, pauses or removes a job), host.onEvent for approval/clarify/todo events; approval.respond and clarify.respond only when you click Approve, Allow session, Deny or Send; profiles.create only from New bot; host.restartGateway only from the restart button on the flat-robots notice; with "Robots as Hermes avatars" on (the default) it checks each bot's avatar once a minute (profiles.get_asset) and sets a robot with profiles.set_asset on any bot with no avatar or with Bot Mode's 160 px face, replacing Bot Mode's face each time it returns, and leaves other images alone (an uploaded image exactly 160 or 256 px wide is mistaken for a generated one); sends a chat message only from the Desk prompt on Enter or Send. The theme layer is the SDK theme customCSS and selects the app's data-slot names in CSS only (validate warns on these selectors); JS never queries, observes or edits app markup. Writes its own ctx.storage and, when changed in its settings, the app's sessionListDensity and chatTextScale. The dashboard half is a read-only FastAPI router serving the bundled PNGs (fixed-pattern names, no writes, no Hermes internals imported). The agent half registers nothing. No third-party network calls, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-updater. tools/render/ holds the Blender source that produced the PNGs (not run by Hermes).
entries.title: helm
known_issues: The robot renders come from the plugin's dashboard half, which mounts when the gateway starts; until one Hermes restart after install the Bots board shows flat SVG robots.
The theme layer's CSS targets data-slot names the app ships; if a Desktop release renames one, that rule stops applying and the palette alone remains.
Verified by hand on macOS (Apple silicon). Linux and Windows run the same code but were not exercised.

entries.name: helper
entries.description: Desktop page for people who are new to Hermes: a Dashboard with nine set-up cards (what each thing is, the steps from the Hermes docs, a button to its place in Hermes) and Helper, a small character with its own conversation window that answers questions about Hermes in plain words, from lines checked against the Hermes docs. Disclosure — reads, through Hermes's read-only Desktop calls, whether a model is ready and its name, the list of profiles and each profile's skills, the connected chat apps, and the main profile's chat list (with previews, only to tell whether a first chat exists); in Helper's set-up conversation it also reads the main profile's SOUL.md text and the list of scheduled jobs; never reads .env, auth.json or config files. When its fixed rules are not sure of an answer it sends the typed message, the last few lines of the Helper conversation and chunks of the Hermes docs to the person's own configured model (llm.oneshot), and once per set-up conversation it sends a fixed "Reply with exactly: OK" check when a model is set; both spend their model credit; no tools run and nothing is saved to their chats. Keeps a name, a few answers, the Done marks and the last 50 lines of the Helper conversation as plain text in Desktop plugin storage, shared by all profiles on the computer and not removed on uninstall. Only when the person presses its buttons, 'Do it for me' runs Hermes's own importer (hermes import-agent <agent> --dry-run, then hermes import-agent <agent> --yes, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenClaw only) and, if the importer is missing and the person agrees, hermes plugins install agent-importers --enable; no other command can run and the model cannot write one. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no self-update. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js, no __init__.py): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: herd
entries.description: Keep one Hermes across every machine. Settings, skills, memory and SOUL.md follow the user between devices, while each machine keeps what belongs to it — Docker paths, ports, bot tokens. `config.yaml` is merged per key against a stored base, with machine-bound paths resolved locally before any comparison, so a pull cannot delete the section the machine is running on. API keys never sync: herd does not open `.env`. The store is encrypted with a key stretched from a recovery code before anything leaves the device; every pull leaves a restorable backup and `hermes sync undo` puts it back, removing files the pull added. Ships a per-device manifest store over any folder or git remote, three agent tools (`sync_status`, `sync_diff`, `sync_now`), session hooks that pull at start and push at end in interactive sessions, and a `hermes sync` CLI. Pairing is one command that prints a 20-character code, valid once for 15 minutes, written as a sealed `pairing.json` in the store folder. A machine that can see that folder reads and deletes it. The file is not pushed to a git remote, because it wraps the recovery code and would remain in history after deletion; a machine that only has the git remote joins with `hermes sync join <git-url> --code HERD-…`. Disclosure — reads the profile's config, memory, SOUL.md and skills and writes the ones that changed; credential-named keys in config.yaml and `mcp_servers.*.env`/`headers` stay on each machine; never reads `.env`, `auth.json` or `state.db`; in interactive sessions the session hooks pull and apply other machines' settings, skills, memory and SOUL.md at session start and push at session end without a prompt (turn off with `auto_pull`/`auto_push`); `sync_now` asks for approval and is blocked under cron and other non-interactive sessions, where the hooks also skip; cron jobs sync only on machines paired with `--cron`; the store is any folder or git remote the user names, and nothing is sent anywhere else.

entries.name: hermagotchi
entries.description: Co-op virtual pets for Hermes: raise a pet, fight deterministic async battles, earn Bits, unlock cosmetics up to mythic tier, climb a seasonal leaderboard, and chat, DM, challenge and taunt other players in a native pane in the Hermes web app and Desktop (Habitat, Battle, Shop, Leaderboard and Social tabs plus a persistent lobby rail). Only when the owner sets the network_enabled plugin setting do they act on the real game server, using the device session the pane paired; that state persists server-side. hermagotchi_status health/me report the active backend. Agent autonomy (autonomy-gated game actions such as practice battles) and agent chat need their own settings and are off by default; the agent can never buy items, and pet care/adopt are not gated by the autonomy setting. The network, autonomy and chat settings can also be switched on by the HERMAGOTCHI_NETWORK_ENABLED, HERMAGOTCHI_AGENT_AUTONOMY_ENABLED and HERMAGOTCHI_AGENT_CHAT_ENABLED environment variables. Network traffic goes over HTTPS only (plain HTTP is refused except loopback) to the game API base URL the user configures (the optional hosted API at api.hermagotchi.rizz.click run by the maintainer, or a self-hosted server from docs/deploy). It sends pet, battle, shop and social actions and, if agent chat is enabled, lobby messages, DMs and taunts, which that server stores; other players' messages come back to the agent marked as third-party text. Online, hermagotchi_status op=pair refuses user_code/revoke_device_id (unsupported_online); approve and revoke stay human pane actions so lobby/DM prompt injection cannot attach a stranger's device. The dashboard tab renders with the dashboard SDK's React and authedFetch, used only for same-origin plugin asset and API routes; the Desktop pane uses ctx.rest only (no remote code, no host-token access). entries.name: hermeneus
entries.description: Live translation for Hermes. Hermeneus captures the audio playing on your Mac, so it works with any app that plays sound. Examples are YouTube, Twitch and X Spaces in the browser, Discord, meeting apps and podcast apps. Verified on real audio: YouTube live in Google Chrome. Captures the audio playing on your Mac (one app, or all system audio except Hermeneus) through a Core Audio process tap on macOS 14.2+, transcribes it with ElevenLabs Scribe v3 Live, translates each line with your own Hermes model and shows live subtitles in a Desktop pane, a floating overlay above other apps, the terminal (hermes hermeneus run), /translate, or an opt-in 127.0.0.1 page for OBS; spoken translation with ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 is opt-in, and language, mode, voice, output and source change while a session runs. Listening covers 100 languages and speaking covers 32. Disclosure: streams the captured audio to ElevenLabs (wss://api.elevenlabs.io) with your ELEVENLABS_API_KEY while a session runs (it stops sending after about 10 s of digital silence and resumes with the first sound), and sends the translated text there too when spoken translation is on; lists your account's voices with GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v2/voices (voices command and the pane's voice picker); sends each committed line plus up to 3 earlier lines (context_segments, 0 to 10) to your configured model through ctx.llm under its own auxiliary task, live_translate (doctor --test-model sends one tiny extra request); /translate start and /translate set --source are refused from chat platforms unless allow_remote_start is on (default off); needs the macOS System Audio Recording permission for the app that runs Hermes (Microphone for the fallback); the setup's Allow system audio and Check again, the doctor, and the pane's Doctor tab every time it opens, play a 440 Hz test tone for about half a second through a short-lived player subprocess, on BlackHole or VB-Cable when installed, otherwise quietly on the default output while the tap mutes it (--no-audio-check skips it); the process tap runs one capture worker subprocess per session with a minimal environment, stopped with the session, on unload and at exit; the floating overlay is a separate Python process while it is open, with the same minimal environment, and keeps six files under plugin-data/hermeneus/overlay/: lock, settings.json, theme.json, positions.json, positions.json.lock (empty, locked while positions.json is written) and overlay.log; positions.json is written through a short-lived .positions-*.tmp file in the same folder, by the overlay and by the process that serves the pane's overlay routes; the pane's first-run setup writes plugin-data/hermeneus/setup.json (the last audio check result, no audio, no key) and audio-check.running while that check captures (removed when it ends); settings.json, theme.json and setup.json are each written to a short-lived .tmp file beside them and renamed over the file at once; settings you change (in the pane, in Settings or with hermes hermeneus overlay-page) are saved by Hermes in its config.yaml; one session at a time on its own thread, reached through a Unix domain socket (mode 0600) under its plugin-data; no TCP port unless you turn on the overlay page, which listens on 127.0.0.1:47821 (overlay_page_port) only, behind a per-session token and a Host check; runs /usr/sbin/system_profiler SPAudioDataType and /bin/ps (read only, absolute paths, argument lists, minimal environment) to check audio routes and name the app in the permission message, and /usr/bin/open with the System Settings privacy address (x-apple.systempreferences:...Privacy_ScreenCapture) when you press Open System Settings in the setup, which changes nothing; the fallback reads a virtual device (BlackHole 2ch or VB-Cable) that you install yourself, never bundled or downloaded; subtitles stay in memory (last 200 lines) and no audio or transcript is written to disk; no telemetry. Platform status: macOS is tested on real audio; Windows support is implemented and reviewed against documentation, not yet run on a Windows machine, so this entry lists macOS only (Windows preview: docs/windows.md).

entries.name: hermes-9router
entries.description: Dashboard tab for a 9Router gateway configured as the `9router` custom provider: groups the router's models by route prefix, shows the last test result for each model, the `/models` response time and, with the optional admin password, connection health and cooldown counts. A Test group button retests one group at a time. Routing and load balancing stay in 9Router. Disclosure — calls only the 9Router URL from `providers.9router` in config.yaml; a group test sends real chat/completions requests (max_tokens 16, at most 25 models per press, never in the background), so it can spend credits or quota; the optional admin password logs in to 9Router's admin API and only connection name, provider, active state and test status reach the page; secrets are read through Hermes get_secret and not stored; results are kept in $HERMES_HOME/hermes-9router.json. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-action-bar
entries.description: A selection bar for Hermes Desktop with two kinds of action. Select text in a chat and a small bar appears: Reply, Ask, Explain, Summarize, Fact-check, Copy. Reply keeps the quote and one comment as a card above the composer; the cards go in front of your message as Markdown blockquotes when you send, so several passages each get their own comment in one message. Ask, Explain and Summarize open an answer card next to the highlight, with follow-up questions: the answer does not enter the chat and the agent does not see it, unless you click Send to chat, which puts it in the composer without sending. Fact-check is a template for the agent: it saves the quote as a reply card with a ready request to verify it, and calls no model. Actions are a label, a prompt and a place (answer card or agent), editable on a settings page, with an optional research set. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks or env vars. Disclosure — reads the text you highlight (window.getSelection) in Hermes Desktop; an answer card (Ask/Explain/Summarize, or any action you set to answer in a card) sends the selected text (up to 6000 characters), up to 4000 characters of surrounding text and the card's earlier turns to your configured model through Hermes' stateless llm.oneshot request (the open chat's model, else the auxiliary model) and writes nothing to the session; Reply, Copy and an action for the agent (Fact-check by default) send nothing; a composer middleware prepends pending quoted replies to your next message; links in answers open in your browser only when clicked; no other network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-adaptive-effort
entries.description: Choose a separate scorer to set the reasoning effort of each Hermes request. Disclosure — off by default; when a mode is enabled (or on an explicit `/hae probe`), sends the latest user message (or the parent-written subagent goal), truncated to 4000 characters, plus any configured guidance to the scorer you select (TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenAI Decisions, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Workers AI, Nace at console.nace.ai, a seventh scorer — a local Ollama endpoint that needs no key — or a custom URL) using that service's key, or with no key at all for Ollama (local only) and for an unauthenticated custom endpoint; by default an enabled mode also sends up to 4 earlier user/assistant text messages (1200 characters each, up to 6 when configured; never on subagents or `/hae probe`) and a separate yes/no continuation question to the same scorer on each turn (set `dialogue_context_messages` or `continuation_downgrade_votes` to 0 to stop this), and an opt-in setting can also send the target model identity. The prompt stays on this machine only when the Ollama endpoint is local: this plugin cannot vouch for a remote address an operator types. Named effort vocabularies cover the fifteen exact `openai-codex` `codex_responses` ids, the exact `commandcode` `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` route and the OpenCode Go `chat_completions` routes, including five newly measured ids (`hy4-flash-free`, `qwen4-max`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `longcat-2.0`, `iceman-contributor-free`); `allow_none` is opt-in and changes nothing today (no dynamic route's ladder declares `none`). `adaptive_effort_routes` is an operator opt-in that trades the prefix cache for per-turn effort on a chosen registered route. `/hae cache` reports seven-day per-route counters of effort-attributable cache loss; that store keeps no prompt text, session ids or request ids. `/hae` output is localized in French, German and Spanish on the Hermes core surface with an English fallback; the Desktop surface stays English. In Hermes Desktop it also sets the focused chat's session reasoning selector through the gateway `config.set` API after each applied change, and it keeps a prompt-free effort-change history (64 changes × 64 conversations), per-conversation mode overrides (at most 256 conversations) and per-route cache verdicts built from provider token counters (at most 128 routes) in its plugin data directory.
entries.title: Hermes Adaptive Effort
known_issues: Per-level effort intensity, cache, cost and quality remain unmeasured: the new OpenCode Go levels were checked only as HTTP-accepted (one 200 per level), not as distinct reasoning intensity.
The Ollama scorer had no live call in this release, so `logprobs` support on a given build is unverified; the prompt stays local only when `ollama_endpoint` is local.
Nine OpenCode Go ids return 403 model-access-disabled and `longcat-2.5-free` 429, so their effort vocabulary is unknown, not empty.
`allow_none` changes nothing until a dynamic route's ladder lists `none`.
The French, German and Spanish catalogs were machine-generated locally and hand-corrected, but not read by a native speaker; the Desktop surface stays English.

entries.name: hermes-agent-radio
entries.description: A 24/7 radio station about Hermes Agent and open-source agents, written, fact-checked and voiced by agents, inside Hermes. Desktop gets a player bar under the composer that lifts into a panel, a full player page, a status-bar dot and a detachable pop-out window. Your agent gets eight tools and a /radio command to see what is on, read the guide and sourced show notes, browse stations and songs, request songs, vote in the weekly chart and send the hosts a question, topic or roast; a human producer reads every one before anything airs. Disclosure — the tools make HTTPS calls only to the configured station (default hermesagentradio.com, run by the plugin's author; plain http is refused except for localhost) and send what the agent submits (question/topic/roast/track text, song ids, votes) plus an optional sender name and an anonymous random listener id stored in the plugin's data folder. The Desktop half shows the station's own player page and audio stream, loaded live from hermesagentradio.com (or a self-hosted station set under Settings, Plugins), in the Desktop SDK's sandboxed frame. No hooks, context injection, shell commands, background work, credentials, telemetry or self-updater; Python standard library only.

entries.name: hermes-android
entries.description: Remote Android device control for Hermes Agent: 58 android_* tools (read screen, tap/type/swipe, open apps, camera, screenshots & screen recording, files, notifications, microphone streaming, media, clipboard, SMS/calls, Health Connect) plus a companion Android bridge app (Kotlin/Compose). The phone dials out to a relay you host — works behind NAT, no port forwarding, no VPN. Chat and media are end-to-end encrypted with a Double Ratchet (the relay sees only ciphertext); device commands travel over your own TLS-authenticated relay. Disclosure — drives a paired Android phone (screen reading and input, camera, microphone, files, notifications, clipboard, SMS/calls, Health Connect) through a relay the plugin starts inside Hermes (localhost by default; a non-localhost bind requires TLS or an explicit ANDROID_RELAY_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1); SMS, calls, file deletion, intents/broadcasts, APK install and relay setup go through Hermes' approval prompt (cron follows approvals.cron_mode, other unattended runs refuse); chat and media are Double-Ratchet end-to-end encrypted, but device commands are protected only by the relay's TLS when configured.

entries.description: Three terminal games inside the terminal Hermes already runs in: chess against the model Hermes is using, a side-view kart racer, and Chrome's dino wearing the Hermes cap. entries.name: hermes-arena
entries.description: A pixel-art platform fighter that runs inside Hermes Desktop. Four fighters, two stages, and three ways to play: against a CPU, with a second player on the same keyboard, or online through Find a match or a room code. Online play connects the two computers directly. Disclosure — online play connects to the public PeerJS signaling server (wss://0.peerjs.com) and Google's STUN server (stun.l.google.com), then opens a direct WebRTC connection that shows your IP address to the other player; the game page loads Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) into the Desktop window each time it opens. No chats, Hermes data or credentials are sent.
entries.title: Hermes Arena
known_issues: Online play is a direct connection between the two computers, so the other player can see your IP address. The online screen says so before you connect.

entries.name: hermes-ark
entries.description: Encrypted, versioned backups of your whole Hermes — memory, SOUL, skills, config, cron, sessions and every profile — with item-level restore. Snapshots happen automatically before every memory/skill write and after sessions; a health guard tells the agent (and you) when memory or skills suddenly shrink, with the exact /ark restore command that undoes it. Off-site copies to any S3-compatible storage (AWS, R2, B2, MinIO) or a folder, new-machine recovery (hermes ark pull), and hermes ark verify to prove every snapshot restores. AES-256-GCM, deduplicated, retention pruning; a Hermes Desktop page with timeline, diffs and one-click restore. Self-defense: a prompt-injected agent cannot prune, delete, reconfigure or switch off Ark. Commands: hermes ark …, /ark …; tool: ark_checkpoint. Disclosure — reads the Hermes home and its profiles; Hermes credential files (.env, auth.json, vault, pairing, browser logins, Webapp session token) are never read, captured or restored; ARK_PASSPHRASE and the S3 keys come only through the secret scope and are never stored. Writes snapshots to the configured repository folder (default $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-ark/repo) and restores into the Hermes home only on an explicit user command or Desktop confirmation (the agent has no restore tool). tool_execution middleware on every tool call: snapshots before memory/skill writes and adds a note when the guard fires; refuses tool calls that would delete, rewrite or reconfigure Ark's backups or settings or disable it (allow_agent_admin lifts this); raises a tamper alarm when Ark is changed anyway, and never writes back settings, enabled state, secrets or its own plugin files — the user's changes always stick. The only repair is Ark's own repository key file after an agent tool call deleted it. Background threads: periodic snapshot/auto-push after sessions, and a 10-second watchdog in the agent process that stops when the plugin is disabled or unloaded. Network only to the user-configured S3 endpoint (HTTPS; plain http only for localhost). No subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-updater.

entries.name: hermes-asgard
entries.description: Twelve Norse gods carved in runestone and wood: Odin, Thor, Freyja, Loki, Frigg, Baldur, Tyr, Heimdall, Hel, Skadi, Freyr and Bragi, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named asgard-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-atlas-evolution
entries.description: Self-improvement and care for a whole Hermes home: turns tool failures that keep coming back into short lessons the agent reads, measures them and retires the useless ones; scores daily progress (Evolution index); runs Hermes' own doctor checks per profile offline; points out conflicting, duplicate or never-loaded plugins, unused skills and memory repeats; and vetoes agent commands that would take Hermes down. Terminal menu (`hermes evolution`) and a dashboard tab. Disclosure — No network access of its own and no telemetry; the reflector (on by default, at most 6 calls a day) sends redacted tool-error excerpts to the model you configured, through Hermes. It reads, read-only, every profile of the Hermes home (config.yaml, state.db, logs/agent.log, MEMORY.md/USER.md, skills, cron jobs, plugins and their install records), /proc, the hermes* systemd units and apt/dpkg state. It injects a lessons section into the system prompt and your own chat turns and registers a pre_tool_call guard. By default (Assist mode) it changes only one thing on its own: an entry repeated word for word between MEMORY.md and USER.md (a backup copy is kept). In Auto mode, which you turn on, it also acts unattended in every profile that has not opted out (`fleet_managed: false`): it runs Hermes' own commands (`curator lock`, `plugins install` of itself by catalog name, `pm gc` weekly), moves failed plugin installs into its own trash for 30 days, and can rewrite and start a broken gateway systemd user service; every change except `pm gc` can be undone. Child processes never inherit YOLO or auto-approve variables. The owner-run `evolution system upgrade` runs apt as root and keeps a root-only snapshot of /etc.

entries.name: hermes-atoll
entries.description: Native Hermes Agent plugin that runs the local Atoll notch monitor for Hermes session and turn status on macOS. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts a detached Node daemon on every Hermes session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. hermes notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Hermes's npm ci prompt. Run hermes notch stop before removing.

Starts a detached Node daemon on every Hermes session that reads state.db read-only and sends session titles, model/profile/token stats and a ≤96-char redacted preview of your latest request to the third-party Atoll notch app over localhost. hermes notch setup clones and builds the author's Atoll fork (github.com/himanusia/Atoll at a pinned commit, not reviewed here) with Xcode and installs an unnotarized app to ~/Applications. Node deps install via Hermes's npm ci prompt. Run hermes notch stop before removing. This plugin hook(s): on_session_start. Platforms: macos.

entries.name: hermes-attention
entries.description: Repeating desktop alerts for pending approvals and questions, with sound signals, custom audio and optional cached speech. Disclosure — Optional speech generation sends the alert phrase you type (never conversation content) to your configured Hermes TTS provider, or to Microsoft Edge TTS when you pick a specific language, and may incur provider charges.
entries.title: Hermes Attention
known_issues: End-to-end Desktop playback was verified on Windows; macOS/Linux playback has not been verified end to end.
Automatic TTS uses a Hermes internal helper and may need adjustment after host updates; explicit language selection uses Edge TTS.
Optional TTS sends the entered text to the configured provider or Microsoft Edge TTS and may incur provider charges.

entries.name: hermes-audio-api
entries.description: OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions and /v1/audio/speech endpoints backed by Hermes' configured STT and TTS providers. Disclosure — opens an HTTP listener (127.0.0.1:8643 by default) that starts with the gateway as soon as a key exists, protected by a bearer key (AUDIO_API_KEY, or the API server's API_SERVER_KEY when reuse is on, which is the default); uploaded audio and requested text go to whichever STT/TTS providers Hermes is configured to use; runs ffmpeg when it must convert the output format; calls Hermes' internal transcription and TTS helpers, which are not a stable plugin API.
entries.title: Audio API
known_issues: Calls Hermes' transcription and text-to-speech helpers, which are outside the documented plugin API; tested against 0.23.0 and main.
Listens on its own port because plugins cannot add routes to the built-in API server.
