entries.name: hermes-australian-legal
entries.description: Experimental public prototype for synthetic evaluation. The behavioural benchmark and qualified legal review have not been completed. Prepare Australian deal questions for counsel using dated regulatory sources. Reads selected Commonwealth instruments from a separately cloned local Git corpus, retains compilation commits and caveats, refuses dates outside recorded coverage, checks review prerequisites, calculates explicit hypothetical earn-out scenarios, and checks literal quotations. Preparation for counsel, not legal or tax advice. Disclosure — bounded local Git subprocesses, no shell; reads committed objects and metadata in the operator-selected corpus. No plugin network calls, credentials, telemetry, automatic updates, persistent matter writes or background jobs. The host model can receive supplied clause text and returned source excerpts. Approval fields are user attestations, not authenticated counsel approval or a host-wide permission gate. Quote matching does not verify source authenticity or legal support. The inspected corpus records selected Commonwealth instruments only and ends on 2026-09-01; it does not establish current law, Acts, case law, State law, tax or transaction-specific applicability.
entries.title: Australian Deal Preparation
known_issues: Synthetic evaluation only; paired model benchmark and qualified legal review pending.

entries.name: hermes-auto-titler
entries.description: Topic-aware session title tracking for Hermes Agent. Hermes generates the first title by default; AutoTitler follows conversation changes and session close without changing the host title-generation switch. Disclosure — sends excerpts of each conversation (sampled user turns, short assistant replies, compaction summaries) to your Hermes title-generation model in the background, also for up to 200 recent untitled sessions at startup; needs plugins.entries.hermes-auto-titler.llm.allow_task_override (or allow_provider/model_override for a custom route). 0.3 no longer edits config.yaml, but users upgrading from 0.2.x keep auxiliary.title_generation.enabled=false until they re-enable it (/autotitler status shows the fix).

entries.name: hermes-autonomous
entries.description: Proactive follow-ups: reads the recent conversation, finds things worth returning to (care / utility / risk / curiosity) and comes back at the right moment — a check on the weather before a trip, the price of something bought yesterday, or just "did your throat get better?". Event-driven rather than a daily digest: a cheap no-LLM gate runs on the cron tick and only wakes the agent when something is actually due. Sending goes through followups.py send, which enforces the 90-minute cooldown, the 23:00–08:00 quiet window, muted categories, at most three items and six lines per message, and records the receipt immediately. Disclosure — it reads the Hermes session database (~/.hermes/state.db) read-only: only sessions owned by the configured owner, DMs by default, with group/thread/forum/channel sessions (including other members' messages) only after setup --include-groups; it reads the cron job store (~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json) read-only when doctor or setup runs, and writes only its own plugin-data directory (mode 0600). The install step copies two helper scripts into ~/.hermes/scripts/; doctor --fix edits only this plugin's own cron job via hermes cron edit and never creates or deletes jobs. During a review the agent runs the plugin's helper through its terminal tool, and followups.py send delivers the DM with hermes send; the optional offline scripts/decide.py calls hermes -z. No credentials are read and there is no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-axiom-agent
entries.description: Adds the nine-article Axiom Doctrine as pre_llm_call context (compact form capped at 1800 characters, full at 4000, owner additions separately at 800) and a /doctrine command that reports, per article, whether a matching enforcer plugin (standing, hermes-axioma, tripwire, handydandy, hermes-gatekeeper) is loaded and enabled. Enforces nothing itself: no tools, middleware or approval hooks, and ENFORCED means an enforcer is loaded and enabled, not verified coverage. Reads an optional owner additions file and only the top-level name line of user-plugin manifests, without following symlinked files; makes no writes, network, subprocess or model calls. No Python dependencies.
entries.title: Axiom Agent
known_issues: Installed state covers user-plugin manifests under HERMES_HOME/plugins; an inactive pip or bundled enforcer shows as not found (a loaded one is detected through ctx.has_plugin).
Doctrine text is advice to the model, not a control. Install and enable the enforcer plugins for enforcement.

entries.name: hermes-axiom-coach
entries.description: The Hermes side of an open-source coach app, its free self-serve plan and the Lite fitness calculators. Three local tools (axiom_lite_split for a starting training week, axiom_lite_macros for Mifflin-St Jeor calorie and macro targets behind a five-question health screen where any yes returns no numbers, axiom_lite_cardio for MET-based session estimates) ported from the Lite app's TypeScript engines and parity-tested against 3,580 exported cases; every result carries a general-education, not-medical-advice line. Four bundled skills: coach-desk (read-only pass first, every send drafted and waiting for the coach), my-plan (work your own plan; never answers the health screen), deploy (walks the app's SETUP.md) and lite. `hermes axiom-coach setup <site>` and /axiom-coach print the steps to connect Hermes's built-in MCP client to the app's own OAuth connector with trust: untrusted, so app writes ask first. Disclosure — registers three local calculator tools, four read-only bundled skills, a /axiom-coach slash command and a `hermes axiom-coach` CLI subcommand; no hooks or middleware; reads only its own SKILL.md files at load; writes no files, edits no config, stores no tokens, reads no credentials or environment variables, and makes no network, subprocess, shell or model calls; the setup command only prints commands for the user to run, and the coach app's own tools come from Hermes's built-in MCP client, which the user configures and signs in themselves.
entries.title: Axiom Coach
known_issues: The coach-desk, my-plan and deploy skills need a running copy of the open coach app; without one only the Lite tools and the deploy skill are useful.
Lite results are estimates for general education, not medical advice, and are not saved or synced.

0.1.0 named its Lite toolset like the connector its setup steps add, which hid the app's tools from model sessions; fixed in 0.1.1 (toolset axiom-lite). Observed on 0.1.1: a full OAuth sign-in, an app tool call, and a model-driven coach-desk session on a demo workspace.
Not observed for this release: a my-plan session with a self-serve member sign-in, and an app write through Hermes's approval prompt.

entries.name: hermes-axioma
entries.description: Inline signal color in the agent's normal reply. The agent marks the few phrases that deserve a second look (stop, caution, go, whisper) and the plugin renders them per surface with color, a style cue and a word, never color alone: Desktop through KaTeX color, CLI/TUI through truecolor ANSI, Telegram/Discord/Slack as bold plus the word, SMS and email as the word only. Green renders only when a tool call Hermes reported as successful in this session backs it; a rarity budget caps marks per reply; in completed replies Axioma transforms, malformed tags in prose are removed when a recognized tag is present; malformed-only replies, preserved code and raw tags during streaming can still show brackets. A color-vision-safe palette and a style-and-words-only mode are one setting away. Secondary: an advisory card (intent, light, signal, question) staged before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls and shown through Hermes's own approval prompt. Each card and notice carries a short card code (a keyed hash of the exact text shown, the tool, its arguments and the card id), logged when shown and again with the answer; /signals verify <code> reports in plain words whether what was staged, shown and answered line up (spec section 5.6, shown equals staged). New in 0.4.0, an optional Desktop half (Axioma Desktop): a living caduceus drawn in code shows the run (staff for the main agent, serpents for running workers, amber while Hermes waits on you, wings green only when a standing_proof tool call reports passed), with a side pane to change course or stop the main turn and each worker, two themes, and a switch for each part. New in 0.5.0, Axioma Charter: the axioma_charter tool and /charter command ask ten plain-English questions about what the agent may do and compile the answers into a readable CHARTER.md and a matching settings block for the owner to review and paste; it applies nothing itself. New in 0.6.0, two optional Desktop additions: an inline advice card the model may write in a reply on the Desktop surface only (light, one-sentence signal, who is affected, a question, and Hold / Go ahead buttons that only send that short reply to the same chat), and a small Axioma light on kanban board cards showing the worst advice recorded for that card's work. Advisor, not a gate: it never blocks, approves or executes anything. Disclosure — before configured send/spend/spin/scrub tool calls (by default send_message, email/post/publish tools, payment/checkout tools, cron and kanban creation, delegate_task, terminal deploy and git push/gh pr commands, and terminal rm/mv when no workspace is configured) it escalates the call to Hermes's own approval prompt with an advisory card, using a fresh rule key each time so remembered Session/Always approvals never skip later prompts; under cron and other unattended runs Hermes's approval policy (default deny) then refuses those calls; it never auto-approves or executes anything, makes no network, model or subprocess calls, reads credentials only as presence checks through agent.secret_scope, adds a short markup guide to the system context through pre_llm_call, rewrites the agent's reply text to render the marks, and writes metadata, salted span hashes and keyed card-code digests (no message bodies) to an owner-only SQLite file plus a separate owner-only key file under its own plugin data directory. Optional operator-configured preflights probe file-presence metadata for required SKILL.md paths under external skill roots and lstat metadata for external device-lock paths; the policy resolves configured workspace/output roots and candidate remove/move paths, including symlinks, for containment checks, without reading those files' contents. Pasted-card verification optionally imports undocumented gateway.platforms.base_exec_approval text helpers and agent.i18n.t behind one compatibility function to recognize localized host framing, falling back to built-in English text if they are absent or change; it neither inspects approval state nor overrides approval. The optional Desktop half registers a right-side pane, a status-bar item, two themes, three palette commands, a settings page and a full-window canvas drawn over the app at low opacity (7-24%) with pointer events off; it subscribes to all gateway events but uses only event types, worker id/goal/status/tool-count/tool-name fields and the passed boolean of a standing_proof result, never message text; on a button press it calls session.steer, session.interrupt, subagent.steer or subagent.interrupt with the text the user typed; it keeps its on/off switches in local plugin storage and makes no network or model calls. The axioma_charter tool and /charter command write two local files, CHARTER.md and charter-settings.yaml, in a charter folder inside the plugin's own data folder and read them back; they make no network or model call, never edit config.yaml or any profile, and apply nothing. The card-code key must be owner-only; if its permissions cannot be confirmed, durable verification is refused.
entries.title: Axioma
known_issues: Axioma 0.6.0 Desktop additions (inline card, board lights): checked by the repo's stubbed-SDK Desktop checks and Python tests, and the Desktop contracts were read in v0.23.0 reference sources; the requires_hermes >=0.22.5 floor is agent-side history only and these Desktop APIs were not verified on v0.22.5. A live Desktop run of the card buttons and the board-lights route is reported in the pull request when observed.

Axioma Charter: compile, show and the pasted settings block were checked through the real plugin loader in a test profile; a model has run the ten questions with a person once from the installed question list and compile code, and has called the registered axioma_charter tool in a live session (the show action); a full interview through the registered tool with a person was not yet observed. The Charter does not read the owner's current settings, so it cannot show a merged result: the owner adds the rules by hand. Charter rules match exact text: an item over 6 words is refused unless it is in double quotes, and a shorter description of a situation still compiles into a rule that never fires. Charter files are refused when the plugin data folder or charter folder is a link, not owned by the user or open to other users; the Hermes plugin-data base folder above them is trusted.

Axioma Desktop: checked on Desktop v0.23.0 with the built-in demo (labelled fake events) and, on real events, a steer of the main turn, a delegated worker shown as a serpent row, a steer of that worker and a stop of that worker, all sent from the pane; Stop on the main turn was not yet observed, and the 0.22.5 floor comes from reading the SDK source at that tag, not from a run on 0.22.5. The background drawing stops at the plugin's own pane only while that pane's tab is showing. Closing the plugin's only pane tab switches the Desktop half off (host behavior); use the pane switch in settings instead.
Signals are written by the model. A model that ignores the markup guide produces plain replies; nothing breaks, nothing is colored.

Desktop color uses KaTeX inline math. Where the span or the reply would confuse Desktop's math parsing (code, links, stray $, characters KaTeX cannot draw), the phrase falls back to bold plus the word. Details in docs/HOST-GAPS.md.
SCRUB detection for advisory cards is best-effort shell parsing: an unparsed remove/move is capped at CAUTION, and removes inside bash -c, eval, ssh, docker exec or scripts are not seen.
Hermes shows only the first plugin's approval text, so when Axioma's card comes first another plugin's description is not shown (the human is still asked).

Charter files are refused when the plugin data folder or charter folder is a link, not owned by the user or open to other users; the Hermes plugin-data base folder above them is trusted.; Axioma Desktop: checked on Desktop v0.23.0 with the built-in demo (labelled fake events) and, on real events, a steer of the main turn, a delegated worker shown as a serpent row, a steer of that worker and a stop of that worker, all sent from the pane; Stop on the main turn was not yet observed, and the 0.22.5 floor comes from reading the SDK source at that tag, not from a run on 0.22.5. The background drawing stops at the plugin's own pane only while that pane's tab is showing. Closing the plugin's only pane tab switches the Desktop half off (host behavior); use the pane switch in settings instead.; Signals are written by the model. A model that ignores the markup guide produces plain replies; nothing breaks, nothing is colored.; Desktop color uses KaTeX inline math. Where the span or the reply would confuse Desktop's math parsing (code, links, stray $, characters KaTeX cannot draw), the phrase falls back to bold plus the word. Details in docs/HOST-GAPS.md.; SCRUB detection for advisory cards is best-effort shell parsing: an unparsed remove/move is capped at CAUTION, and removes inside bash -c, eval, ssh, docker exec or scripts are not seen.; Hermes shows only the first plugin's approval text, so when Axioma's card comes first another plugin's description is not shown (the human is still asked)..

entries.name: hermes-baikal
entries.description: Read, search and (opt-in) edit events and todos on a Baïkal or other CalDAV server, with recurrence expansion and free/busy. Disclosure — sends every request to the https URL in BAIKAL_CALDAV_URL (plain http only for localhost) with BAIKAL_USERNAME and BAIKAL_PASSWORD read through Hermes, follows no redirects and ignores proxy variables; only the six read tools register unless the plugin setting allow_write is true, and with it the agent can create, change, complete and permanently delete events and todos, visible to everyone sharing those calendars; the tools are offered on every surface where the baikal toolset is enabled, gateways included, so anyone allowed on your gateway reads your calendar; event text written by other people reaches the agent as tool output; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Baïkal or sabre/dav.
entries.title: Baïkal (CalDAV)
known_issues: Write tools (create, update, complete, delete) register only after `hermes config set plugins.entries.hermes-baikal.settings.allow_write true` and a new session

When the server cannot expand recurring events (Baïkal returns HTTP 500 if a calendar's calendar-timezone is a bare TZID, which its web admin sets), the plugin expands them itself; rules using BYSETPOS, BYWEEKNO, BYYEARDAY or sub-daily frequencies come back as the stored series with an expand_error note
Events with per-occurrence overrides can be read but not edited, editing a recurring event changes the whole series, and completing a recurring todo is refused

entries.name: hermes-band
entries.description: Compose and render original music on your own machine — an arrangement is data (tempo, key, chords, parts) rendered to exact-length wav and mp3. entries.name: hermes-board
entries.description: A Miro-like board the agent draws with its own tools and you edit in a desktop pane, both sides working on one JSON document. board_apply builds a whole diagram in one call from ordered ops (nodes, edges, free lines, groups, notes, captions, layered auto-layout, bus trunks); board_render writes a PNG for chat or the interactive HTML editor; board_watch reports your own pane edits back to the agent. The pane docks beside the conversation with the same editor, saves your edits, and takes agent updates live. Disclosure — board_render shells out to a headless Chrome/Chromium already on PATH (nothing is downloaded; private temp profile, sandbox kept unless running as root) for PNG and self-test rendering; boards live in ~/.hermes/board/ shared across profiles (HERMES_BOARD_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_RENDER_DIR / HERMES_BOARD_WATCH override); serves /api/plugins/hermes-board/ on the plugin host; reads this profile's state.db read-only to find the session board_watch should wake; no external network calls and no stored credentials; board_watch's wake into a messaging chat additionally needs plugins.entries.hermes-board.allow_gateway_injection: true.

entries.name: hermes-body
entries.description: Hermes Body turns a phone into a first-class Hermes channel: a private camera-and-voice page streams frames and speech transcripts into the gateway, and the full agent answers out loud and can act with any tool. Disclosure — the plugin runs a local HTTP/WebSocket server (default 127.0.0.1:8788, token-gated) that serves the phone page and receives camera frames, speech transcripts and recorded voice clips; it stores the pairing token (0600) and the newest 50 received frames and voice clips in the plugin data directory; frames reach the configured model provider the same way any photo attachment does, and voice clips go through Hermes' configured speech-to-text like any voice note; it opens no outbound connections of its own and sends no telemetry; the page must be served over HTTPS (Tailscale Serve or another proxy) for browser camera and microphone access.

entries.name: hermes-borealis
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop theme with a live dithered landscape behind the window: aurora curtains over mountain ridges and a mirroring lake by night, a two-ink pink and teal dawn by day. Install once, then switch with /skin borealis. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers one theme through the plugin SDK, and its stylesheet restyles parts of Desktop's own UI (tabs, composer, sidebar edge and background, wordmark colour) and clears the window's field backgrounds only while the theme is active, and the scene fades back behind text. While active it also adds one canvas behind the app and draws the scene on it with WebGL, watches the root element's theme, mode and accent attributes to show, recolour or remove that canvas, reads the pointer's horizontal position to slide the ridges, and reads the system clock to draw the moon in its current phase. No images or fonts; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks. The repo also ships borealis-cli, a still terminal skin for the CLI and TUI, installed separately by copying one YAML file into ~/.hermes/skins/.

entries.name: hermes-bot-hq
entries.description: Desktop fleet page plus a per-bot Home (status, metrics, alerts, tasks, routines, buttons) published by the bot as JSON. Disclosure — reads each local profile's home files, can run a declared cron routine from the UI on that bot's profile and credentials, and opens chat, a path, or a URL the bot declared; send_prompt buttons send the shown prompt into the bot's Bot Chat. Bot-declared run_action buttons run a script from the bot's home/actions/ folder: a script runs only after the user approves that exact file (SHA-256), is re-approved if it changes, and is limited to 30s and to that folder, but it runs as your user with the Hermes backend's full environment, including provider keys loaded for the profile Hermes was launched with. Approvals are kept under the Hermes root in bot-hq/approvals/. The `hermes hermes-bot-hq setup` command (asks first unless --yes) links the plugin into every profile's plugins folder and enables it there. No database, signup, or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-browser-extension
entries.description: Connects Hermes to the separately installed Hermes Browser Extension for user-shared page context, opt-in control of explicitly attached browser tabs, and opt-in background task tabs that a local gateway chat opens in its own Chrome tab group. Full browser control requires Chromium; Firefox supports chat, page context and restricted control. Serves authenticated routes on the Hermes API server and stores bounded redacted receipts and screenshots in profile-scoped plugin data. Disclosure — when Background task tabs is turned on in the extension, any chat of that Hermes profile, including messaging-platform chats, can open, read and act on pages in background tabs of your signed-in Chrome; leave it off unless you want that.
entries.title: Hermes Browser Extension
known_issues: Install the browser extension separately; this entry installs only the Hermes-side plugin. The API server must be enabled, and gateway routes load at startup.
Remove the older hermes-browser-companion plugin before installing this renamed plugin to avoid duplicate context-tool registrations.

On a multiplexed gateway, Hermes Control and plugin status for a named profile need Hermes to serve that profile's own plugin routes under /p/<profile>/api/plugins/ (#147703); until then use the default profile there. Host-isolated plugins cannot register the API-server routes.

entries.name: hermes-call-ledger
entries.description: Per-call cost ledger for Hermes Desktop: every model call Hermes makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Hermes' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post_api_request, post_auxiliary_call, api_request_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO_PAT read through Hermes's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from hermes-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

entries.name: hermes-call-me
entries.description: Hermes phones its owner through CALL-E before a risky action, when it is stuck, or when it finishes: call_for_approval, call_for_help and call_report each place one real phone call, the owner says a PIN the plugin compares (an approval also needs a one-time code read on the call and repeated back), and a wrong PIN, wrong code, no answer, busy, silence, an unclear reply or a timeout is never approval; an optional pre_tool_call guard blocks deploy/delete/payment-style tools until a single-use approval is on file. Disclosure — Each call_for_approval, call_for_help or call_report places a real phone call billed to your own CALL-E account, and the model decides when to call, within a one-at-a-time limit and a daily cap of 8 by default. The action summary, issue or report text the model writes, your phone number, a one-time code and the call task go to api.heycall-e.com, which handles the call audio and transcript. Call records and transcripts, with spoken digits redacted, are stored in the plugin's data folder. A tool call can block for up to 180 seconds by default (600 max) waiting for you to answer.

entries.name: hermes-canvas
entries.description: Your agent's plan, wired to its real work. The agent draws its plan as hand-drawn boxes in a Desktop pane next to the chat. Each box is bound to files and a check command: hooks mark a box doing when the agent writes one of its files, and done or failed when its check command exits. The user steers the running build on the canvas: answer a question box, link boxes, leave a note (it reaches the subagent that builds the box), remove a box (its next write is blocked), add a drift write to the plan, replay every revision. Disclosure — hooks read tool arguments and results (file paths, terminal commands and their output); canvas documents, revisions and user edits are stored in this profile's plugin database; pre_tool_call blocks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls that would write files of a box the user removed, and nothing else; canvas edits and a short plan summary are added to the model input (pre_llm_call, transform_tool_result); pre_verify keeps the agent working while one of its boxes is failing, capped by agent.max_verify_nudges; the inspector diff runs read-only git (rev-parse, cat-file) in the canvas project folder and reads the files a box wrote there, up to 512 KB each; serves /api/plugins/hermes-canvas/ on the plugin host; never writes project files; no network calls, no credentials, no background processes, no self-update.

entries.name: hermes-chan
entries.description: A chibi desktop companion who walks around your screen, reacts to Hermes, and does its computer-use clicks and typing. Disclosure — on first run builds its Rust overlay from source with cargo (downloads the crates pinned in Cargo.lock from crates.io, several minutes; needs a Rust toolchain) and then runs it as a long-lived always-on-top desktop window that Hermes restarts on crash; the build and the overlay get a minimal environment without your API keys; with computer_use.backend: hermes-chan it performs real mouse clicks and keyboard input through the core computer_use tool; its mischief setting (on by default) visually glitches and, after 20 s of user inactivity, moves or shakes the active app window; optional heartbeat/watch modes (off by default) send the active window title and a screenshot to your current model; its chat bubble injects your typed messages into the local chat only after you allow plugin injection; the desktop-tidy tools move files on your Desktop into a "Hermes-chan Tidy" folder after you approve each run and each undo in Hermes's approval prompt (journaled, undoable); no network calls besides the cargo build, no credentials read.
entries.title: Hermes-chan
known_issues: Linux needs X11 or XWayland; on Wayland she only sees and acts on X11/XWayland apps.
macOS window move/track uses osascript/System Events (tens of ms per call), so window pranks are gesture-cadence, not per-frame smooth.
The overlay is built from source on first run; without a Rust toolchain the plugin runs headless (tools/hooks only).

entries.name: hermes-chat-share
entries.description: Share Hermes Desktop conversations as long PNG screenshots, self-contained HTML, Markdown, JSON, or PDF — per-turn selection with gutter drag range-select, search, collapsing and share-scope control; light/dark theme override with syntax-highlighted code; remembered export preferences; session info (model, thinking level, cache hit, tok/s, Hermes version) in every export header and footer. The Hermes Desktop counterpart of dsh-share. Disclosure — makes no network calls; reads the conversation you share through the gateway's session.history / session.usage RPCs and the session.info gateway event, plus the session list for titles; writes to the clipboard or downloads a file only when you trigger an export. HTML exports keep the conversation's image and link URLs, which load when the file is opened.

entries.name: hermes-chronos
entries.description: Time-travel filesystem checkpoints, approval-gated rollback, and a scrubbable Desktop timeline for Hermes Agent. Disclosure — Snapshots the whole working directory, untracked files such as `.env` included, into a shadow git repo at `<workspace>/.hermes/chronos/` before each file-editing or shell tool call. Rollback overwrites workspace files and by default deletes untracked files missing from the snapshot. The model's rollback asks for approval first, but `/chronos`, the dashboard API and the Desktop pane restore without a prompt.

entries.name: hermes-cinema
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop pane that edits and exports real video with your own FFmpeg — timeline, text, colour, speed, seven transitions — and carries a cinematic engine inside that writes the voiceover first and times every camera move to it. No account, no upload, no watermark, no telemetry. Disclosure — the pane starts a local video service on 127.0.0.1 protected by a per-install token and runs your own FFmpeg and Python helper scripts on your machine; with no keys set it makes no network calls, while optional providers you turn on send prompts or narration text to image.pollinations.ai, Microsoft edge-tts, Google Gemini, ElevenLabs or a custom HTTPS endpoint you configure, and the cinematic font step downloads fonts from GitHub.

entries.name: hermes-cloud-file-manager
entries.description: Your agent's server files, as easy as local: drag in whole folders, preview, and review every edit before Save, in Hermes Desktop. Browse, search and sort by date, see which files are new or updated since you opened a folder, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, preview its images, PDFs and code files, download a file, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you press Save in the review, which shows the line diff for files up to 20,000 lines), drag files into the chat or add them with Add to chat (also right after an upload), draft a rename, move or delete request to the agent in the chat box with Ask agent (you check it and send it yourself), import files from the agent's own Google Drive, hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading, and open, preview, download or add to chat a file the agent hands you as a card in its reply. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Ships one plugin skill, hermes-cloud-file-manager:cloud-file-manager-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders: the configured roots, else terminal.cwd, TERMINAL_CWD or MESSAGING_CWD, else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists, sorts and searches those folders, reads the files you open or preview (Markdown and .txt files up to 1 MiB in the editor; the first 1 MiB of other code and text files; images and PDFs up to 10 MiB), creates folders, and writes uploads, Drive imports and editor saves (staged as hidden .cfm-* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It has no delete action: it removes only its own .cfm-* staging files and folders (aborted ones, and stale ones over a day old) and, when an upload or import fails to publish, the empty file it had reserved for it. It never follows links out of those folders, and its file API never exposes the agent's Hermes home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Download, drag and Add to chat use Hermes Desktop's own authenticated file download and @file/@folder references; the plugin adds no route for them. Ask agent only types a drafted request with @file/@folder references into the chat box; it never sends it, and the plugin itself still has no rename, move or delete action. Desktop listens for the agent's tool-completion events to refresh the open folder, and its Desktop windows pass each such event's type and agent to one another in the app (a BroadcastChannel; nothing leaves the machine). In Desktop chats only, it adds a short section to the agent's instructions that names the shown folders (at most ten, as configured) and explains the ::cloud-file{path=...} card; it carries no file names or contents. A card's path goes only to a read-only lookup route under the same folder and Hermes-home guards as a listing; a path outside the shown folders is refused. Each write names the folder it started in, and the gateway refuses it if Settings have since changed which folder that is. Apart from Desktop's calls to the gateway and the report skill's GitHub requests, its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's Hermes home, else the copy bundled with Hermes) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys, buffering their output in the gateway's temp directory. The plugin never reads the Google token itself, but those scripts (setup.py --check for the sign-in check, google_api.py drive for listing and download) refresh the agent's saved Google token (google_token.json in its Hermes home) when it has expired, as they do when the agent runs them. While Desktop is open it re-checks the plugin and Drive sign-in about once a minute. The report skill runs hermes --version, hermes plugins list and hermes logs (filtered to this plugin), may save its search words, title and draft as local files, and searches electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager issues with gh or a web tool before drafting; it posts a public issue or comment there only after the user approves the exact title and text.
entries.title: Cloud File Manager
known_issues: In a split layout with two agents' chats side by side, a drag started while one agent's chat is in focus can be dropped into the other agent's chat; the reference then names a path on the wrong machine (no file moves between agents). Use Add to chat, or focus the target chat before dragging (electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager#55).

entries.name: hermes-cobrowse
entries.description: Real-time multi-window spatial co-browsing canvas and interactive human-in-the-loop web automation for Hermes Agent via a localhost web studio with CDP screencasting, 8-way window resizing, Inspector telemetry, and 2FA handoff. Disclosure — launches headless Chromium with a minimal sanitized env and runs a token-authenticated localhost server on 127.0.0.1:9876+ with Host/Origin checks; blocks local files and private/link-local IPs by default across redirects, redacts password/OTP values in DOM state, executes agent-supplied JS via cobrowse_eval_js, reads no local credentials, and sends no external telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-codex-resets
entries.description: Know the moment OpenAI resets your Codex usage limits. A status-bar chip counts the time since the last reset; when a new one lands, a small card rises out of it (chip-only while you type), with a history page of every reset. Disclosure — polls the public codex-resets.com API every 60 s and loads fonts from Google Fonts; sends nothing about you or your sessions.

entries.name: hermes-colab
entries.description: Run Python scripts and Jupyter notebooks on Google Colab GPUs (T4 free tier, L4, A100, H100, TPU) from chat: Hermes assigns the runtime, uploads the code, keeps it alive, streams progress and GPU use, syncs outputs and checkpoints home while the job runs, resumes on a fresh runtime from the last checkpoint when Colab reclaims one, and reports back to the chat that started it; a Desktop page shows live runs with cancel and resume. Disclosure — needs the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app, Colaboratory scope) signed in with hermes auth add hermes-colab:google; Hermes attaches the token to colab.research.google.com only. Uploads the run's files (hidden files and folders, symlinks, hard links, virtualenvs and common credential files excluded; the home directory, HERMES_HOME and credential folders are refused as code or output folders) to the user's Colab runtime and executes them there with a small stdlib runner that pip-installs the run's requirements; runtimes consume the account's Colab compute units and are released when a run ends; a daemon thread supervises active runs (one per profile, lease-protected; with no active run it only reads the run store every 30 s); run records live in the profile's plugin data directory; a pre_llm_call hook adds a finished run's one-line summary to the starting chat's next turn.

Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7.

entries.name: hermes-committee
entries.description: A committee of AI models for hard decisions. You set the seats (each with its own role and model) and a chairman; the seats answer independently, rank each other's answers blind, debate the points they disagree on, and the chairman writes a decision with confidence, dissent, role-fit notes and next actions with owners. Evidence files (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, text, photos, and source code with numbered lines) go to every model as cited [E1] passages; optional Research first searches the web once through Hermes's own web tools and adds checked [W1] passages before the seats start; in the source review the user can add a missing link or search. Time and budget limits with a mid-run ask to extend, follow-up runs, saved committees, a live Desktop page (Brief, Convene, Decision) and a Markdown + PDF report. Disclosure — one run makes several calls through ctx.llm to each seat's and the chairman's model on your existing Hermes providers (typically 2-4 per seat plus 1-3 for the chairman; an estimate and a budget cap are shown before it starts; clerical steps ask for low reasoning, answers and the verdict for medium); with Research first on, the question (never file contents) goes to the web search provider set up in Hermes and up to 8 pages (14 on the Thorough setting) are read through web_extract; a link or search the user adds in the source review is read or searched the same way; evidence files the user picks or names in chat are read and their text is sent to every participating model (paths named in chat inside the Hermes folder or matching known credential files are refused); runs, reports and evidence copies are kept under the plugin's data directory; the Desktop page's Convene button starts a new Hermes chat in the background to run the committee; a run uses worker threads inside Hermes and no background process outlives it; pricing reads Hermes internal pricing tables; no credentials read or stored; no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes Committee
known_issues: Each run makes several model calls on the providers you assign (shown as an estimate before it starts, with a budget cap, default $2). Subscription routes count $0 toward the budget; unknown API prices are not treated as free and can be entered by hand.
Research first needs a web search provider set up in Hermes. Without one, the run goes on from your own evidence and says why.

Pricing and billing detection read Hermes internals (agent.usage_pricing, and the provider table in hermes_cli.auth for how each provider is signed in to; provider setup only, never saved logins or credentials), all fail-soft; if those move in a future release, cost shows as unknown rather than wrong.

entries.name: hermes-compute-priority
entries.description: Keeps the Hermes process that serves a connection ahead of the isolated turn workers it spawns: every `tui_gateway.compute_host` worker owned by the same user is deprioritised within two seconds of appearing - niceness +10 by default on Linux and macOS, the BELOW_NORMAL or IDLE priority class on Windows - and nothing else is touched unless extra rules are opted into. Disclosure - it reads process metadata only: /proc/<pid>/cmdline and /proc/<pid>/ ownership on Linux, psutil on macOS and Windows; it only ever LOWERS the priority of processes belonging to the same user, never raises one, never signals, stops or kills anything, opens no socket, writes no file, reads no credential and uses no privilege, and it is a no-op where turn isolation is off or where psutil is missing on macOS or Windows (a read-only /status route says why). Backend only: no tool, no hook, no middleware, no dashboard tab.

entries.name: hermes-continuity-capture
entries.description: Records Hermes lifecycle events (session, subagent, and kanban task) as Continuity schema-v2 events in a local SQLite spool under the plugin data directory, and can forward them to a NATS/JetStream server you run yourself. Disclosure - binds nine lifecycle hooks and writes SQLite (spool_path defaults to spool.db in the plugin data directory, 90-day retention, periodic sweep; the file grows with event volume); free-text fields (prompts, tool results, args, summary, reason, tool_call_history) are always dropped before the INSERT and only their length is kept (there is no setting that keeps them). The optional NATS password is read from the environment variable HERMES_CONTINUITY_CAPTURE_NATS_PASSWORD, never from config.yaml. Delivery is opt-in: the default publish_mode is spool-only (nothing leaves the host); in core/jetstream mode a background thread publishes to your own NATS endpoint using the bundled standard-library client, and failed deliveries stay as error rows and are retried. Only the NATS server itself is external - it is not part of this plugin. Inactive until an operator enables it. Disclosure — binds nine lifecycle hooks and writes a SQLite spool (default spool.db in the plugin data directory, 90-day retention sweep) holding event type, profile/agent id, host FQDN, process id and start time, session/subagent/task ids and tool names; prompts, tool args/results, summaries, reasons and tool_call_history are always dropped before writing and only their lengths kept. Default publish_mode is spool-only (nothing leaves the host); in the opt-in core/jetstream modes a background thread sends those events to the NATS server you configure in nats_url (default 127.0.0.1) using the bundled standard-library client, and unless nats_tls is on or the URL uses tls:// (TLS is off by default) the NATS user and password travel in plaintext.

entries.description: HermesCRM is a working CRM for Hermes Desktop. Manage contacts, companies, deals, events and follow-ups in the same workspace your Hermes agent uses. entries.name: hermes-custodian
entries.description: Local, read-only security-posture monitor for the machine a Hermes agent runs on (Linux, macOS, native Windows): scoped file and permission baselines, evidence-backed findings and a change history, a first-run terminal setup, an optional background monitor and an on-demand authenticated loopback dashboard. Registers four read-only tools (warden_status, warden_findings, warden_changes, warden_scan). Disclosure — reads: regular files and metadata under paths the user approves in setup; Hermes profile config metadata (model, provider, plugin and MCP-server names) only after explicit consent; credential files (.env, auth stores, keys), memory, chat history and SOUL are never opened (metadata only) and only .py/.md files are content-hashed; symlinks and reparse points are not followed. Runs: a foreground or per-user background monitor (systemd user service, LaunchAgent or Task Scheduler task) only when the user starts or installs it; fixed argument-array subprocesses with timeouts, explicit command-specific minimal environments and no shell (systemctl and apt list --upgradable; launchctl and softwareupdate -l; schtasks and a fixed PowerShell Windows Update query); update detection installs nothing; a Linux-only root security-update plan/apply is a separate terminal command with typed confirmation that the AI tools and dashboard cannot reach. Network: no telemetry and no model calls; the dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 only behind a username/password session (scrypt, signed cookie, exact Host and Origin checks); native OS update queries may contact the OS vendor's update service. Stores: paths, fingerprints, findings and the hashed dashboard login in a private per-user state directory; never credential contents. No self-updater, no approval or confirmation arguments for the AI, no root shell. Not an antivirus or EDR: same-user software can change its configuration. Native tests pass on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11-3.14 at the pinned commit.

entries.name: hermes-dpapi-secrets
entries.description: Resolve Hermes environment variables at startup from a single secret file encrypted with the Windows Data Protection API, instead of keeping provider keys in plaintext in .env or auth.json. Config is secrets.dpapi.map, an ENV_VAR -> store-name mapping (bare names or dpapi:// names) plus an optional file path (default <HERMES_HOME>/secrets.dpapi). The file is one DPAPI blob keyed by the current Windows user profile, so it is unreadable by another Windows account and worthless off the machine; it is written by the bundled CLI (python -m hermes_dpapi_secrets set NAME, value read from a prompt or stdin, never from argv) and only read at runtime. Mapped names that are missing or empty are skipped with a warning; a file that is not ours, a blob this user cannot decrypt, or a payload that is not a flat string map is reported as an error with nothing injected. Disclosure - this source decrypts a file for every Hermes process that enables it: resolved values become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, exactly like .env entries, so anything that can read that environment can see them. User-scope encryption only (the machine-wide flag is never used and is not exposed), and the at-rest protection is a bar for backups, cloud sync and dotfiles, not a boundary against code already running as the same user. Stdlib-only (ctypes): no Python dependencies, no subprocesses, no network calls, no self-update. Windows only. Applying fetched values stays the orchestrator's job; the plugin never writes os.environ itself. entries.name: hermes-drawbridge
entries.description: Give your remote Hermes agent limited access to folders on your device. Disclosure — the Desktop component sends the contents and names of files in the folder you share (up to the configured read limit) to the Hermes backend serving that chat, so they reach chat history and the model provider; with Create/Update enabled the agent can propose whole-file writes that Desktop applies after you approve the diff in the chat, and "Allow this session" lets later edits in that share apply without a further prompt until the share ends; no deletes, no network calls beyond your own Hermes connection.

entries.name: hermes-dreaming
entries.description: Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Secrets and instructions are screened by the dream's own rules plus a verbatim copy of the holographic plugin's screen (scripts/holo_screen.py, MIT, same maintainer), applied to stored facts and human messages before anything reaches memory, the report or the model. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — by default the scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro; with holographic >= 0.15.0 including its fact_versions/fact_confirmations tables, to say who stands behind a fact); they also read Hermes config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db_path/scope/cron_writes/min_trust_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror_memory_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote_from). An optional cloud judge (judge in dreaming.json, off by default; off, its code is not even loaded) may, once the owner enables it, send for each mention the rules counted the fact's text and that person's own words (no reply quote, link, id, sender or time; names inside the text may be included; screened for secrets and instructions first), only from the chats, sources and chat stores the owner lists, over HTTPS to the providers the owner lists, in the owner's order: OpenRouter's Decisions API (model typesafe/jev-1.14, Jev by TypeSafe; the data reaches OpenRouter and TypeSafe) and/or OpenAI's Decisions API (model gpt-6-luna); when the first gives no usable answer the same pair may reach the next. A verdict can only remove a counted mention — from promotion, confirmation, fact decay, "said again" after a rejection, the selection of new facts and conflicts, and evidence. Keys OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY are read from the environment or, since Hermes withholds these provider keys from cron scripts, straight from their own line in $HERMES_HOME/.env; the judge's calls are billed to those keys. It keeps a 90-day verdict cache and a 90-day local journal of the pairs sent in $HERMES_HOME/cache (the journal is deleted on nights the judge is off); the nightly spending cap ($0.05 by default) is soft; data already sent cannot be recalled and falls under the providers' retention terms. The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $HERMES_HOME/scripts, seeds $HERMES_HOME/dreaming.json and, through Hermes' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files, judge files and diary without them, deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text) and deletes the set-aside copies of its own broken state files; with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $HERMES_HOME/cache and a diary to $HERMES_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact_store (with holographic >= 0.15.0 marked said or inferred; with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact_store update. Since 3.4.0, with holographic >=0.19.0 and profile scope, it also reads fact_merges and current version ids to propose disjoint duplicate pairs. It saves immutable proposal numbers, both full texts, version ids, origins, keywords and the provider database path in cache/dream-proposals.json; open proposals expire after 180 days and closed ones are removed after 30 days. Full pair texts are included in the agent report and therefore reach the configured agent model. Old facts are merged by fact_store only after the adult memory owner approves the exact proposal; the response checks the database and uses expect to refuse changed versions. Scheduled extraction may merge only a newly added paraphrase from its own session into an existing fact, never old facts from other sessions. The scripts themselves still open the fact store read-only. The sweep also cleans the state of merged copies and archives their hashes so a later forget can remove older untagged diary copies; merging itself does not erase the diary. No new credentials, network providers or tools are introduced. Version 3.4.2 clarifies that forget cleans the store and the skill's own files; Git history, external database dumps, system backups and Hermes session history require separate cleanup. Reports distinguish a successful store deletion from a retained external copy and do not promise that retrying removes a documented history boundary. Version 3.5.0 adds explicit cron maintenance: known stock prompts are synchronized while custom prompts are preserved; --update-existing applies only explicitly supplied settings and --job-id scopes the entire operation. cron.expected_roles controls desired creation without pausing existing jobs. --upgrade validates the request before copying gate scripts and updating cron through public APIs, then checks the result. Checks expose paused jobs, execution modes, missing roles and duplicates; no automatic activation or job deletion. --inherit-model explicitly clears both model and provider pins. The public cron update API has no CAS; avoid concurrent configuration edits during installation. Version 3.6.0 adds opt-in read-only task-outcome summaries and recorded memory-attempt explanations from holographic >=0.20.0 (experience_schema=1). It reads bounded attempt/version references and agent-reported outcomes; usefulness does not change truth, trust, ranking or MEMORY.md. It makes no new model or network calls and keeps no second correction-text cache. Explicit --memory-store must be in chat_stores.promote_from; stores are never joined. task_outcomes: true adds only summary counts to the ordinary nightly result and creates no extra wakeup. Missing capability is reported as unsupported, not as a successful empty journal. Human corrections reported by the agent are not authenticated human confirmation. Version 3.6.1 reuses parsed numbers within a bounded in-memory nightly cache, reducing repeated work without changing contradiction rules. Version 3.6.2 copies the cron gate scripts atomically (an interrupted install keeps the previous gate) and names any cron job the installer refuses to change with the fix. Version 3.7.0 keeps the whole-store duplicate search within its nightly budget on large stores (it also narrows candidates by the numbers and names the pair rule requires; the rule still decides every pair) and names the store in task-outcome summaries. Version 3.7.1 derives each message's data once per nightly pass, with memory bounded by corroboration.memory_mb (default 256 MB; above it data is rebuilt on demand, never changing decisions). Version 3.7.2 makes the quarantine screen about 40× faster on long messages with byte-identical decisions (re-vendored holographic screen 0.22.1). Version 3.7.3 fixes an install-time scanner false positive in that screen's start list (3.7.2 was refused by hermes plugins install) and runs hermes plugins validate in CI. Version 3.7.4 changes no behaviour: the vendored holographic screen is copied whole and checked before it is written. Version 3.8.0 no longer promotes an agent's conclusion nobody confirmed (holographic origin inferred) to MEMORY.md by any corroboration route; people repeating it offer it for confirmation instead, and stores without origins are promoted as before; --explain says why, and --memory-explain keeps the provider's count of candidates that changed before the record. Version 3.8.4 keeps, for each memory entry, hashed word stems and numbers plus a 60-character preview (none for an entry with a secret) in the loss-guard snapshot in $HERMES_HOME/cache, so an entry the agent compressed, reworded or merged is no longer reported as lost; the alert names lost entries by that preview. Version 3.8.5 has the nightly agent change memory entries with the memory tool's patch (Hermes 0.22 removed replace; replace remains only as the fallback for Hermes 0.21), counts a patch staged in the pending/memory approval queue as waiting, and compares a lost entry only with entries the night wrote (also across a split, with numbers compared as numbers); for an entry of fewer than two word stems the snapshot also keeps hashed stems of its short words or, for one with no words and no secret, hashed character trigrams; state files with a UTF-8 BOM are read. Version 3.8.6: install.py --check counts a judge key only from its own line in $HERMES_HOME/.env, the one a cron script can read, and names DREAM_* variables set only in the terminal it runs in, compared with their lines in that .env (a DREAM_* value may be printed, a key never is); it and a new read-only dream.py --nightly-status read the dreaming jobs' next_run_at in cron/jobs.json to say when Hermes will not fire them (a gateway that is down, a job paused or with no next run). The nightly prompt never patches through another entry's whole text and keeps an absorbed entry when a merge fails; the loss-guard snapshot also keeps hashed full dates and each entry's hashed head key. No new credentials, network calls, tools or writes. Versions 3.8.7-3.8.12 (fixes from a code review): a rejection no longer silences a newer number, time, weekday, month or name of the same fact; a changed number is no longer taken as already in memory; a time written with a dot is not a date; a date without a year takes its year from the day the fact was stored; a fact store that cannot be read costs the night its facts, not the whole pass (alert fact_store_unreadable); a voice reply corroborates; database paths are opened as read-only file URIs (a '#' in a path no longer opened another file for writing); a broken extraction cursor restarts at the current time instead of handing old messages over again; the judge reads $HERMES_HOME/.env as python-dotenv does. A memory-loss alert, with the 60-character previews that name the lost entries, is now kept in the dream's seen state in $HERMES_HOME/cache until an agent turn answers it, and the forget sweep removes a forgotten fact from those previews too, and from the loss-guard snapshot's previews (3.8.9). 3.8.9 also ends a reply quote with a ']' inside it at its closing quote mark, so the agent's quoted words no longer corroborate a bare 'ok'; reads a generic source's epoch given as a string or in micro-/nanoseconds (microseconds used to end the pass) and day-first dotted dates; and does not archive diary sections twice after a rotation cut halfway. 3.8.10 reads a voice transcript with a bracketed annotation ('[music]') whole, and its tests no longer write into a real Hermes home. 3.8.11 carries holographic 0.30.1's screen (was 0.25.3's): it holds secrets and look-alike-letter instructions the old copy missed, and takes keys to a flat for an errand. 3.8.12 holds a card number, a PIN or CVV and a password with no separator before the value, and an agent's own conclusion people seem to say again is no longer confirmed by the agent: it asks the person (new section confirm_ask; the call is made only on their yes). No new credentials, network calls, tools or writes outside the dream's own files.
known_issues: Duplicate detection is a heuristic for questions, not proof that facts mean the same thing. Old facts require the owner to approve both complete texts. This section is disabled without holographic 0.19.0, outside profile scope, or when the provider database cannot be verified; a merge has no automatic unmerge.
Cron maintenance requires a single configuration writer; the public cron update API cannot atomically reject every concurrent manual edit. A paused job may already have an execution in progress.

entries.name: hermes-droid
entries.description: Turn physical Android devices into automated hardware testbeds and QA companion nodes for Hermes Agent — wireless MQTT APK deployments, Logcat crash diagnostics, and screen captures. Disclosure — gives the agent control of a paired Android phone: it can run device shell commands, send SMS, place calls, reply to notifications, install APKs and toggle radios (each behind a Hermes approval prompt and refused in cron runs), and without a prompt it can read SMS, contacts, notifications, recent photos, location, take camera/screen captures and pull device logs. Commands travel over the MQTT broker you configure (loopback by default; TLS and credentials required for remote brokers), and the companion app trusts any client that can publish to its command topic on that broker.

Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.19.0.

entries.name: hermes-ego
entries.description: Hermes Ego reads and saves pages in the user's ego(lite) browser through a loopback MCP relay (Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8767/mcp). The Mac daemon and the relay are installed separately, the same split as local-mcp; this package does not start, embed, or update them. Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Derived from hermes-tabs (relay code); talks only to a separately installed loopback MCP relay at http://127.0.0.1:8767/mcp with bearer EGO_RELAY_TOKEN from the Hermes profile (a remote Hermes host needs an SSH local forward); a long-running relay and a Mac daemon, installed separately, run the ego CLI against the user's logged-in ego(lite) browser, so pages that session can open are readable; ego_save_page_markdown writes markdown under the relay's configured save root (for example an Obsidian vault) and downloads third-party page images, some in a background pass after the tool returns; the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every relay tool, reads included, and refuses them in unattended runs. No telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Hermes Ego
known_issues: The Mac daemon and ego(lite) are installed separately and are not part of this package. The daemon needs macOS. A remote Hermes host reaches the relay through an SSH local forward to 127.0.0.1:8767. The relay stays on loopback.
Page images may finish in a background pass after ego_save_page_markdown returns. images_pending counts what is left. There is no second MCP response for that pass.
Relay tools do not set readOnlyHint. trust untrusted asks before every tool on this server, including ego_status and ego_get_page_text, and those calls fail closed in cron and other unattended runs.
A hand-written mcp_servers.ego entry replaces this package's server, including trust, unless that entry sets trust: untrusted.

entries.name: hermes-entity54
entries.description: Role-based authorization for Hermes Agent: OWNER, ADMIN, USER, GUEST roles, default-deny, per-tool and per-bot scoping, tamper-evident receipts, governed Linear issue creation, and versioned policy sync. Disclosure — a local Node MCP server whose principal is one static identity per profile (OWNER by default), so everyone who can talk to that profile acts as that principal; its roles govern only its own eight tools, not Hermes tools. `entity54_linear_create_issue` creates issues on api.linear.app with your LINEAR_API_KEY without a Hermes approval prompt; it needs a one-time `npm ci --omit=dev` in the installed `server/` directory and a manual `node scripts/setup.mjs` run that writes the signing keys to a local env file you copy into the profile `.env`.
entries.title: HERMES ENTITY54
known_issues: Requires Node 22+ and a Hermes Agent install that supports Agent Plugins 1.0.0.
After install, run npm ci --omit=dev once inside the installed plugin directory (server/) to install the MCP server dependency.
Live Linear transport needs a LINEAR_API_KEY; without it Linear calls fail closed as not configured. A mock transport is available for demos and tests.

entries.name: hermes-federated-search
entries.description: Federated web search backend (provider name `federated`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key `ranker`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (`type` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (`reasoning_effort=off`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.hermes-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).

entries.name: hermes-field-notes
entries.description: Field notes for a Hermes install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each hermes update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Hermes core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN from env or ~/.hermes/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.hermes/field-notes), ~/.hermes/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.hermes/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.hermes/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no_agent cron job only when the user runs install_cron.py (it reads ~/.hermes/installs/*/facts.json to find Hermes' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.hermes/.env), else local.

entries.name: hermes-finance
entries.description: Personal-finance tools over your own local hermes-finance database: spending, budgets, transactions, net worth, bills, loans, investments, cash flow, goals and categorization rules (read-only), a bank sync on request, and four writes (file a transaction, add a rule, set a budget cap, track a bill) that each wait for your approval and are blocked under cron and other unattended runs. Needs a separate trusted app checkout prepared with Python 3.12 and `uv sync`, set as HERMES_FINANCE_APP_DIR. Disclosure — reads open the separate hermes-finance app's SQLite database outside the plugin directory, and the plugin imports that app checkout's code into the Hermes process, so it runs whatever that checkout contains, not the catalog pin. `finance_sync` runs the app's sync, which calls Plaid with your optional Plaid keys and fetches security logos from financialmodelingprep.com (ticker symbols leave the machine). `hermes finance completion`, started by the app's Ask panel, sends that conversation and your finance results to your profile's own model. The opt-in report jobs (`hermes finance crons plan/apply`) write profile-owned entry scripts and run the app on a schedule. They call Plaid and, with a live read-only key, Alpaca (GET-only); they look up car and home values through NHTSA, Wikimedia/OpenStreetMap and, only if you switch them on, Carfax (in the local Chrome at 127.0.0.1:9222) and Redfin. The daily job's agent applies transaction categorizations through the app's own CLI without a per-change approval card. The four approval-gated writes stay blocked in cron. Nothing moves money or places trades. The optional Plaid and Alpaca keys are read through Hermes's secret scope only; the plugin opens no key file. Installing starts no server, sync or job. No telemetry, no update check, no Python dependencies in Hermes.

known_issues: Needs a trusted hermes-finance app checkout prepared with Python 3.12 and `uv sync`; set HERMES_FINANCE_APP_DIR to it.

entries.name: hermes-fleet-connector
entries.description: Owner-approved universal phone pairing and bundled read-only Live Operations reporting for selected Hermes profiles. Disclosure — paired phones get broad fleet:operator access over the internet, including cron jobs (unattended runs), Kanban task dispatch and media reads, and see live session titles/previews and subagent goals from the profiles you select for reporting; any messaging account you make an owner (with a one-time claim code from `hermes fleet claim`) can create pairing links and approve phones from a private chat, so that account's security is your host's security. Runs an explicitly activated background connector/reverse proxy behind your HTTPS origin and may launch a local Hermes backend; legacy QR flow opens a private local browser. Keeps an owner-only control socket in the system temp directory, plus pairing/owner state and shared local snapshots; reads selected profiles' session registries through private read-only imports. `hermes fleet reporting configure --apply` edits the selected profiles' config.yaml (with a backup). Local idle/retirement maintenance is explicit and not exposed to phones. Reporting adds no control power.
entries.title: Hermes Fleet Connector
known_issues: Native platform/auth-provider operation requires plugins.isolation: in_process; host-isolated and mixed/multiplexed reporting contexts fail closed. Isolation is never downgraded.

macOS local acceptance includes existing phone pairing continuity and nine healthy idle reporting processes; Linux and other runtime/OS results are separate CI evidence. Active agent/delegation acceptance is not claimed.
Private read-only Hermes registry imports can break on future releases. Validator retains a service caution and private-import warnings; no core runtime override is detected.

Trusted HTTPS origin reachable from host and phone is required. Legacy QR display additionally requires qrencode and an authenticated GUI/browser; terminal approval-code pairing does not require Telegram. Native Windows is unsupported; WSL browser display is experimental.

entries.name: hermes-gatekeeper
entries.description: Gatekeeper enforces rules the owner configures; not legal advice and not a compliance guarantee. A deterministic pre_tool_call gate for recognized outbound sends: literal `hermes send` and `imsg send` terminal commands (including terminal calls made from execute_code), and a send_message call if one ever traverses the hook, are checked in full. Hermes registers no model-callable send_message tool. Other tools whose names look like a send (connectors__*, mcp tools, plain names, and a cronjob_manage create/update/run with a delivery target) are not parsed: they only require owner approval, because consent, STOP and quiet hours cannot be checked for them. Browser and computer-use driving of an app and scripts that send through a subprocess are not inspected. Rules: absolute suppression, per-channel consent and recipient-local quiet hours (block), and native Hermes approval requests for unanswered threads, minimum gaps and unapproved wording (the host auto-approves these under --yolo, approvals off and hermes -z). Uses the public post_gateway_admission hook to record observed STOP keywords and DM replies (excludes control, approval, steering and slash-command traffic). Reads tool arguments, results and normalized inbound snapshots; writes only profile-local SQLite (owner-only permissions) with recipient/thread hashes, message SHA-256, decision metadata, consent source/date, timezone/region and owner template variables. No raw message-body log; hashes are not anonymity. No network, subprocess, model calls, telemetry, credential reads, external file scans or core patches. Invalid settings or storage errors block recognized sends. Disclosure — gates only the outbound sends it recognizes (literal `hermes send` / `imsg send` terminal commands and send_message calls) and asks owner approval for other send-looking tools; a whole-message STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END or QUIT from any admitted gateway sender silently suppresses that sender and is consumed without reaching the agent or getting a reply; a storage or inbound-observation failure blocks every recognized send until the owner repairs records and reloads; writes only a profile-local SQLite ledger of hashes and decision metadata, with no network, subprocess or credential access.
entries.title: Gatekeeper
known_issues: Not an egress firewall. Send-looking connector/MCP/plain tools and cron deliveries get an owner-approval request only; consent, STOP and quiet hours are not checked for them, and a differently named sender is not seen (add extra_send_tool_patterns).
Browser/computer-use driving of an app, scripts sending via subprocess or python -c, direct delivery and later argument rewrites are not governed.
The agent-visible send path is the terminal tool; Hermes has no model-callable send_message tool.
approve rules, including unrecognized-send-tool escalation, are host-owned: --yolo, approvals.mode off and hermes -z auto-approve them; block rules still apply.
Inbound hook omits control/approval/steering/slash traffic; manually record unseen optouts/replies.
No address-book or alias/group-membership resolution; use stable target identities.
