Other tools whose names look like a send (connectors__*, mcp tools, plain names, and a cronjob_manage create/update/run with a delivery target) are not parsed: they only require owner approval, because consent, STOP and quiet hours cannot be checked for them. Browser and computer-use driving of an app and scripts that send through a subprocess are not inspected. Rules: absolute suppression, per-channel consent and recipient-local quiet hours (block), and native Hermes approval requests for unanswered threads, minimum gaps and unapproved wording (the host auto-approves these under --yolo, approvals off and hermes -z). Uses the public post_gateway_admission hook to record observed STOP keywords and DM replies (excludes control, approval, steering and slash-command traffic). Reads tool arguments, results and normalized inbound snapshots; writes only profile-local SQLite (owner-only permissions) with recipient/thread hashes, message SHA-256, decision metadata, consent source/date, timezone/region and owner template variables. No raw message-body log; hashes are not anonymity. No network, subprocess, model calls, telemetry, credential reads, external file scans or core patches. Invalid settings or storage errors block recognized sends. Disclosure — gates only the outbound sends it recognizes (literal `hermes send` / `imsg send` terminal commands and send_message calls) and asks owner approval for other send-looking tools; a whole-message STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END or QUIT from any admitted gateway sender silently suppresses that sender and is consumed without reaching the agent or getting a reply; a storage or inbound-observation failure blocks every recognized send until the owner repairs records and reloads; writes only a profile-local SQLite ledger of hashes and decision metadata, with no network, subprocess or credential access. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, post_gateway_admission. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5. Known issues: Not an egress firewall. Send-looking connector/MCP/plain tools and cron deliveries get an owner-approval request only; consent, STOP and quiet hours are not checked for them, and a differently named sender is not seen (add extra_send_tool_patterns).; Browser/computer-use driving of an app, scripts sending via subprocess or python -c, direct delivery and later argument rewrites are not governed.; The agent-visible send path is the terminal tool; Hermes has no model-callable send_message tool.; approve rules, including unrecognized-send-tool escalation, are host-owned: --yolo, approvals.mode off and hermes -z auto-approve them; block rules still apply.; Inbound hook omits control/approval/steering/slash traffic; manually record unseen optouts/replies.; No address-book or alias/group-membership resolution; use stable target identities..

entries.name: hermes-gauge
entries.description: Context gauge — a live ring/dash showing how full your agent's context window is, per session and topic, with a desktop plugin, a memory optimizer (levels lean/standard/roomy, skills grouped by source and category) and tools (gauge_check, gauge_report, gauge_set_window, gauge_render, gauge_action, gauge_setup). entries.name: hermes-gemini-live
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Hermes. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — hermes_task starts, hermes_tasks reads the call's task board, and hermes_task_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Hermes needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI_API_KEY from the Hermes home's .env; delegated work runs as a Hermes run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api_server and API_SERVER_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.

entries.name: hermes-gensyn-delphi
entries.description: Seven read-only tools. Disclosure — Seven read-only tools for Gensyn Delphi prediction markets; no funds move and nothing is signed or sent. Needs Node.js 20.18+ and a manual `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in the plugin folder (installs the pinned @gensyn-ai/gensyn-delphi-sdk and its locked npm deps) before the tools work. Runs a local Node subprocess per call (25 s deadline, not a sandbox). Sends your DELPHI_API_ACCESS_KEY only to delphi-api.gensyn.ai (testnet) or api.delphi.fyi (mainnet); history and quotes read api.goldsky.com and gensyn-testnet/mainnet.g.alchemy.com without the key, and quotes use a throwaway in-memory key the SDK requires. Tools are on for every surface by default, including messaging gateways, where anyone admitted can run these reads on the owner's key (rate limit 30 requests per minute per process); disable per surface with `hermes tools`.

entries.name: hermes-gensyn-ree
entries.description: ree_validate_receipt, ree_verify_receipt, ree_infer. Validate does not re-execute and does not stand behind text_output, finish_reason, token_count, model.name, or ree_version. Verify re-executes on CPU. Infer runs one of three small models and writes one receipt. Disclosure — Starts containers from the local image gensynai/ree:v0.8.0 (pinned by digest) and never pulls it; running docker pull yourself is consent to the REE-Binary-License. ree_verify_receipt and ree_infer mount ~/.cache/gensyn and ~/.cache/huggingface read-write (a Hugging Face token file stored there is visible to the container; no token is passed in the environment), may download Hugging Face weights for any model a receipt names, and their container network is not limited to Hugging Face; they ask for Hermes approval on every call and refuse under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended runs, host isolation, or when nobody is present to answer. ree_validate_receipt runs with network none, does not ask, and returns no receipt text. Any person admitted to one of your gateways can call these tools and approve containers on your Docker daemon; disable per surface with hermes tools. Choosing "always" adds one config.yaml allowlist line per call and never covers the next call. New receipts and temporary work files are written under ~/.cache/hermes-ree; nothing is stored under HERMES_HOME. The container is not a hostile-code sandbox. No cron is created.

entries.name: hermes-genui
entries.description: Generative UI for Hermes Desktop and the Hermes Webapp: the agent answers with interactive blocks drawn inside the chat reply (charts with hover cards, KPI cards, sortable tables, day-by-day plans, photo strips, calculators with sliders and live charts, forms, checklists that keep their ticks, weather and Up next cards, and step-by-step explainers with flow diagrams, simulations and a 3D layer stack). Since 0.3 it also keeps pages in the sidebar: a Today page kept by a personal assistant the user sets up, which tracks bills, renewals, orders and replies owed from mail and calendar until each is resolved (it never sends, pays, replies or deletes), and dashboards drawn from the user's MCP servers and tools that can be kept as pages and refreshed. The model sends data only (JSON blocks, never HTML, scripts or SVG); the plugin validates every block and draws it with its own components, in the app's theme. Telegram, the CLI and other chat apps get readable Markdown instead. Ships sixteen recipe skills (hermes-genui:trip-planner, compare, explain, dashboard, personal-assistant and more). Disclosure — network calls only when the model uses a tool or a page the user made is open, carrying the model's search words, a ticker or a city: market prices from Yahoo Finance (query1.finance.yahoo.com); weather and place lookup from Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com, geocoding-api.open-meteo.com); photos from the Wikimedia Commons and Openverse APIs, from Unsplash or Pexels only when the user adds that key, from Tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set (including one already set for Hermes's own Tavily web search), from the user's configured web search, and from the head (at most 256 KB) of the top result pages; each photo host is contacted briefly to check the picture loads (https only, public addresses only, DNS pinned, redirects re-checked). Scheduled jobs — created only when the user asks, as ordinary Hermes jobs they can see, pause and remove (a job the user removed or rescheduled is put back only if they say yes): the assistant's check (every 30 minutes; new mail and calendar entries, read through the user's own MCP server or a built-in sample mailbox, go to the profile's model), an optional ideas job (web search only, no mail tools; it gets a few plain words per item) and one refresh job per kept dashboard (it repeats the recorded read-only tool calls and sends their results to the profile's model). The plugin starts these jobs with Hermes's own CLI (hermes cron run) when the user presses Refresh or new items need ideas. The plugin's 'No scheduled jobs that send data to the model' setting (plugins.entries.hermes-genui.settings.local_only, also in Desktop's plugin settings) turns the real-mail assistant, ideas and kept dashboards off for that profile, including jobs made before it was switched on. Stored under the profile's plugin-data/hermes-genui/ folder: boards as JSON, the assistant's settings and tracked items (titles, dates, amounts, senders, short facts, never mail text), kept dashboards with their recorded calls, and the Today layout; with the sample mailbox one small script is written to the profile's scripts/ folder and removed when the assistant is stopped. A recipe the user asks to save becomes a profile skill through Hermes's own skill_manage (write approval applies); no telemetry and no account. Adds a short drawing rule to the system prompt and, in Desktop only, a one-line reminder next to messages that ask for something visual, steering answers to blocks instead of Hermes's ::preview widgets.
entries.title: Hermes GenUI
known_issues: Turn off tool search for the profile (hermes config set tools.tool_search.enabled off): with it on, large boards often fail inside the search bridge.
A Desktop that connects to Hermes on another machine needs the drawing half installed in that Desktop too (Capabilities → Plugins → Install from Git).
In the Webapp, switch the plugin's Desktop half on once in each browser and at each address (Capabilities → Plugins); the choice is kept per browser.
With the plugin in two or more profiles, install it in the default profile too; otherwise Hermes Desktop can keep reloading it.
Today and kept dashboards were built and tested on Hermes 0.23.1.

entries.name: hermes-ghost-call
entries.description: A real-time AI assistant on your own phone calls. You stay on the line; Hermes listens and streams one-line hints to your page and chat (what they just offered, what to ask next), knows your private target without ever saying it, plays a hint in your earpiece on one tap, and posts a summary with what was agreed and a draft confirmation message when you hang up. Works with two browser links, a real phone line through your own Twilio account, or any call on speaker. Disclosure — streams live call audio of BOTH parties to OpenAI (realtime transcription at api.openai.com, plus hint, earpiece-TTS and summary models) and stores text transcripts (on by default; `store_transcripts: false` turns it off), hints and summaries in plugin data (SQLite); the other party is not told by the plugin that the call is transcribed, and call-recording consent law is the user's responsibility; runs a FastAPI bridge (`hermes ghost serve`, 127.0.0.1:8766 by default) that you must expose publicly at PUBLIC_BASE_URL (e.g. a tunnel), protected by one-time link tokens and Twilio signature checks; Twilio mode places paid calls through your own Twilio account to numbers the model may choose, but only numbers on your HERMES_GHOST_TEST_ALLOWLIST (empty = no dialing; HERMES_GHOST_ALLOW_ALL=1 lifts it) and never emergency/premium numbers, without a Hermes approval prompt; Hermes speaks on the call only after you type `/ghost intervene allow`, and then first says it is an AI.

entries.name: hermes-github-mentions
entries.description: Run approved GitHub mentions as Hermes tasks and reply in the original thread. Polls GitHub's API in a gateway worker and sends signed local webhooks granting terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools. Optional Discord copies and read-only Hermes session progress tracking. Disclosure — polls the GitHub notifications API every 60 s or more as the bot account, and when a GitHub user on your allowed_authors list @mentions the bot in any repository the bot can see, starts an unattended Hermes agent turn with terminal, file, web, skills and todo tools on this computer through a signed local webhook route; the mention text and the repository content the agent reads are untrusted input, and the agent acts with the bot's classic `repo` token (the same GITHUB_TOKEN Hermes' GitHub tools use). Hermes' unattended approval mode (deny by default) still governs flagged commands. `hermes github-mentions routes --apply` edits this profile's config.yaml (adds webhook routes, enables the webhook platform on 127.0.0.1). Optional progress notices read Hermes' state.db read-only; optional Discord notices post through Hermes' own Discord adapter.

entries.name: hermes-gruvbox
entries.description: Six Gruvbox themes for the Hermes Desktop app — dark and light, each in hard, medium and soft. Installing the pack writes its skins into <hermes home>/skins/ and has desktop/plugin.js contribute the same six to the app's own theme picker, with their real labels and descriptions instead of the app's hard-coded "Hermes skin". No commands, tools, hooks, middleware, credentials, network access or background work, nothing runs on a turn — it only writes its own skin files, never config.yaml, and it never overwrites a skin you edited or switches your active theme.

This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5.

entries.name: hermes-guard
entries.description: Defensive prompt-injection guard for Hermes Agent: a pre_llm_call hook scans every inbound message locally (deterministic patterns, no model calls) for Unicode smuggling, hidden instructions, special tokens, and Base64-decoded payloads; a pre_tool_call hook blocks RCE/subshell patterns, sensitive credential paths, and call-ID races. High-confidence attacks are blocked; suspicious messages are quarantined for manual review via the guard_review tool (release is manual re-send by design). Includes a Predator pattern store (human-corrected signatures), a SHA-256 hash-chained ledger, secret redaction, a live Posture Score, a 28-vector simulation arena (21 message + 7 tool-arg), and a standalone Obsidian & Gold HUD. Python stdlib + SQLite only. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials read or stored, no data leaves the machine, no core overrides, no self-updater. Phase 3 verified live on Hermes 0.21.5 (validate 13/13, doctor OK, plugins list enabled, live hook-fire test: attack blocked on both hooks, benign passed); v1.1.2 re-verified the same way (validate 13/13, live hook-fire test 19/19 through the real plugin dispatch, 168/168 tests).
entries.title: Hermes Guard
known_issues: Quarantine release is manual re-send; there is no one-click release. release/delete are owner-only slash commands (/guard-release, /guard-delete); the model tool cannot call them.
Talking about jailbreak phrases — for example, quoting one to discuss it — can be flagged, because the scanner sees the pattern, not the intent.
Very short Base64 tokens (<20 chars, or token entropy <4.0) are skipped by design to avoid false positives on ordinary words.
register() uses one register_tool(name, toolset, schema, handler) call — the single form matching the 0.21.5 signature and current Hermes alike, live-verified on 0.21.5.

Subshell patterns ($(…), backticks) are checked only for command-running tools (terminal, execute_code, shell) and are bounded to 512 chars; backticks / $(…) in write_file / read / note content are not blocked.

entries.name: hermes-guardian
entries.description: Deterministic allow/approve/block policies for Hermes tool calls, with read-only Policy Lab regression simulation and operator-reviewed policy proposals. Exact tool-name rules, explicit protected local paths, a deliberately limited shell grammar, and payload-free persistent decision audits. Unknown tools default to block; ambiguous recognized-tool arguments, invalid policy, and audit failures block. Uses the public pre_tool_call hook and native Hermes approval directives. Disclosure: reads its own settings through Hermes and filesystem metadata and symlink targets for path comparisons; writes redacted JSONL under the active profile's plugin-data/hermes-guardian directory. No protected file-content reads, enforcement-hook network calls, subprocesses, model calls, credential storage, telemetry, core overrides, or self-updater. The operator CLI optionally uses public ctx.llm structured generation, sending instructions and policy paths to the configured provider, which may charge; no separate key is required. Explicitly confirmed activation uses ctx.set_config for atomic settings updates and stores private policy backups. Offline generation is a limited exact-language template. Approval rules follow host YOLO/approvals-off and unattended-mode settings; hard block rules do not ask for approval. A policy hook, not a sandbox: intended for a trusted local POSIX backend and trusted plugins that do not rewrite arguments after inspection.
entries.title: Hermes Guardian
known_issues: No project-scoped positive permissions or Git push approval: unsupported Git commands block. Offline generation is template-based; live provider inference remains unverified.

Simulation inspects current local path metadata; it does not prove final host authorization, audit availability or execution. Stop concurrent config editors during activation; storage failure can prevent rollback.
Remote/container path namespaces, hard-link/case/mount aliases and filesystem races are not secured.
Explicitly allowed tools outside the recognized file/terminal adapters receive tool-name checks only.
Other plugins can rewrite arguments after the hook; disabled or failed-to-load Guardian provides no protection.
The 16 MiB audit limit, write failure, partial trailing record or lock contention blocks calls until repaired or retried.
Audit records describe policy decisions, not execution or final human approval.

entries.name: hermes-guests
entries.description: Share your Hermes with guests, family and teammates. They use only what you approve, from their own Telegram chat, for as long as you choose. Say it in plain words ("let Mia read the recipes and add to the shopping list until Sunday") or pick from a menu, review the card, approve, and send the invitation. Each guest gets their own Hermes profile, chat and memory, and every call they make is checked against a signed, expiring Tenuo grant before it runs. Change, extend or end access from your own chat. Disclosure — runs a maintenance task every minute while the gateway runs (renews grants, sends end-of-access notices, applies data retention and deletes ended guest profiles); runs each guest turn as a local Hermes agent process in a separate guest profile, with tool calls going through a server on 127.0.0.1 that checks the guest's grant and then runs the shared tool through the plugin tool-dispatch API, where other plugins' pre_tool_call guards do not see it; guest turns use the owner's configured model and quota (a Codex sign-in through credentialed_provider_request, API keys through the profile secret scope, handed to the guest process over a private pipe and never stored in guest profiles); creates and deletes guest profiles; once sharing is set up it answers every private Telegram message from anyone but the owner before Hermes's own pairing, so people the bot already admitted get only their scoped guest access instead of the full agent, and new people get a no-access reply instead of a pairing code; when the owner enables sharing, adds itself to an explicit Telegram tool selection; stores signing keys, grants, access records and activity in its plugin data folder; its pre_tool_call hook refuses tool calls from anyone but the owner in Telegram sessions and checks the owner's calls against an owner grant (falling back to Hermes unless require_owner_warrant is set); its pre_llm_call hook adds sharing context to the owner's Telegram turns; registers /guests and a Telegram handler for the owner and guest commands. No network calls of its own beyond Telegram and the model provider through Hermes; no telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Hermes Guests
known_issues: Telegram private chats with one owner. Group chats and other messaging apps are not supported yet.
Guests use the owner's model and quota. Guest turns support a Codex sign-in, API-key providers and local models.
Profile and process separation is not an OS sandbox. Share only tools whose effects you would accept from the guest.

entries.name: hermes-guide
entries.description: Read-only diagnostics for Hermes configuration: /hermes-doctor in-session and hermes guide in a terminal. Twelve read-only health checks (config, mcp, skills, commands, hooks, plugins, memories, sessions, storage, dashboard, update, gateway) and points to 32 troubleshooting skills, installed separately as a skills tap, for what the built-in doctor doesn't cover. Complements — never replaces — hermes doctor. Disclosure — reads config.yaml, SKILL.md frontmatter, skill bundles, plugin manifests, the shell-hooks allowlist and the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md stores read-only (the report quotes short memory snippets); the sessions and gateway scopes read the tail of logs/agent.log read-only for runaway-session and gateway websocket-disconnect signatures (session ids, model names, token counts, disconnect peers and reasons appear in the report); the dashboard scope reads the Hermes package-manager toolchain facts, the checkout's Node lock pin and package.json engines, the web UI build record and security.allow_lazy_installs read-only, and never runs node or npm; the storage scope stats $HERMES_HOME/state.db for its size only (never opens it); the update scope reads the update-lock record in the co-located hermes-agent checkout under $HERMES_HOME and probes it — owner-PID liveness, then a brief lock acquisition it releases immediately, opening the lock file writable, with a read-only fallback for a root-owned lock on POSIX (writes no content, never deletes the lock); registers one read-only plugin skill, hermes-guide:start, listed in model sessions while the plugin is enabled; /hermes-doctor and hermes guide run hermes config path as a subprocess (argument list, no shell); the default hooks check reads hook configuration, consent state and the exec bit in-process and executes nothing, while hooks --deep runs hermes hooks doctor, which executes every approved shell hook once with a synthetic payload (--fast starts no subprocess and executes no hook); /hermes-doctor and hermes guide (except with --fast or --json) also run git ls-remote once per process against the plugin's GitHub repo to print a newer-release notice (no download, no local writes), and hermes guide --update (also with --json; not with --fast) runs git ls-remote against the repo the plugin was installed from and prints the update command for this install type without running it; with opt-in proactive: true it runs the checks (including the agent.log scan and the update-lock probe) in-process at each session start/end (no hooks executed, no subprocesses, no network). The 32 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover.

entries.name: hermes-handle-it
entries.description: Handle It: your agent sits in the customer support chat so you don't have to. Hermes holds a company's live customer-support chat for you in its own browser, negotiates toward your goal for as long as it takes, and asks you before it agrees to an offer, pays, cancels or shares a detail you did not allow. Ends with the outcome and a saved transcript. Disclosure — Opens the support pages you name in a local Chromium (Playwright) with its own profile under $HERMES_HOME/hermes-handle-it, or in Hermes's own browser (with its signed-in sessions) when browser.cdp_url is set, public addresses only (every page, redirect hop and frame is checked; private, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses are refused), types messages into them on your behalf, clicks a cookie banner's reject or necessary-only button, fills a chat's pre-chat form with details from your shareable list only, and saves transcripts and screenshots there. Never reads passwords or Hermes's vault: a sign-in is made by Hermes itself. When a message mentions customer support, help desks or live chat, it adds a short note to that turn pointing the model at its own tools. For phone calls it talks to bland.ai's API with your own key (BLAND_API_KEY, read through Hermes's profile-scoped secrets), sends bland.ai your task and the details you allow to share, and places a call to a number you name only after you approve it; bland.ai's AI voice agent then speaks on the call and checks with you before agreeing to anything only when you expose its local approval bridge (127.0.0.1) through a public tunnel you set up as call_bridge_url, otherwise it agrees to nothing. With a bridge set, it sends one request to that address before each call to check that it reaches the bridge, and places no call if it does not. bland.ai records the call when you ask, and call costs are yours, billed by bland.ai. No other network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-helm
entries.description: One /helm menu in Discord or Telegram for the Hermes you run 24/7: switch MCP servers, skills and toolsets on or off, ranked by the tokens each adds to every request; resend the turns a gateway restart or crash killed; set a daily spend limit that blocks new turns; and get Discord replies too long for 8 messages as a .txt file instead of truncated. Owner-only, and menus open only in a DM. Disclosure — writes mcp_servers.<name>.enabled, skills.disabled, agent.disabled_toolsets and its own plugins.entries.hermes-helm.settings in config.yaml through one function that logs old and new values and refuses when the config is managed; stores the text of every top-level user turn, from any sender on any platform and from the CLI, for 7 days (to resend lost turns; subagent turns skipped), tokens and cost per model call, and the change log in plugin-data/hermes-helm/helm.db; writes helm-reply-*.txt into Hermes' document cache for long Discord replies; resends a lost turn with ctx.inject_message only when allow_gateway_injection is on, and Hermes re-checks the allowlist; reads some private Hermes internals (toolset resolution, pricing) behind try/except fallbacks. entries.name: hermes-honcho-plugin
entries.description: Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, add confirmed corrections or source files, and choose what Honcho learns from the chat's session. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Hermes's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. Settings changes only the focused Honcho session's learning switches (conclusions, summaries, dreams, peer card updates) and its peers' observation settings, and only after you review the changes and press Save. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-intercom
entries.description: Discover and message existing Hermes sessions within one profile using session_list and session_send. Delivery uses only the public ctx.inject_message API with attributed native notices, hop limits, per-sender duplicate detection, bounded retry identities and per-target rate limits. CLI and unknown sender surfaces are refused. Unverified routes and dormant targets that the public API cannot reach are refused; there is no private gateway transport or automatic mounting. A scheduled result confirms scheduling, not execution or durable delivery. Disclosure — lets the model list sessions in the active profile (titles, sources, working directories and routing metadata, read from `state.db` read-only) and inject attributed messages that start model/tool turns in other sessions, including other users' Discord/Telegram chats on a shared gateway, once `plugins.entries.hermes-intercom.allow_gateway_injection: true` is set; bounded by `max_hops` and per-target rate limits; restrict the `intercom` toolset to owner-only platforms on shared gateways; writes a metadata-only audit log (no message text) to `$HERMES_HOME/cache/hermes-intercom/audit.jsonl`.

entries.name: hermes-ios
entries.description: Build and visually iterate on native iOS apps in Hermes Desktop through localhost. Runs Xcode commands and a pinned preview server; known dependency security limitations are disclosed in the README. Disclosure — on approval, setup downloads an exact-pinned serve-sim (0.1.49-beta.139.1) and its locked npm tree from registry.npmjs.org into the plugin's data dir. The plugin runs Xcode/simctl commands and keeps background serve-sim preview and watchdog processes on 127.0.0.1, whose simulator stream/input/start/shutdown routes are unauthenticated to local processes (shell execution stays disabled). It reads the local Hermes config to pick its lifecycle mode. Never expose, forward or tunnel the preview port.
entries.title: Hermes-iOS-sim
known_issues: Localhost only. Never expose, forward, or tunnel the preview port. serve-sim 0.1.49-beta.139.1 requires a loopback Host and runs with shell execution disabled; simulator stream/HID routes remain unauthenticated on loopback. Localhost does not eliminate malicious-browser risks.
Requires Xcode, an iOS Simulator runtime, Node.js 20+, and npm. No minimum compatible Hermes version or independent-Mac qualification is established.
Uses the read-only undocumented worker_config_snapshot host API for lifecycle selection; host changes can break automatic cleanup.

entries.name: hermes-island
entries.description: Hermes Island: a Dynamic Island style voice window on macOS for talking to Hermes. The island_call_back tool rings it when a job is done and says the result when you answer; `hermes island status|build|setup` builds the app at the same pinned commit and points its talks at this Hermes. entries.name: hermes-issue-sync
entries.description: Two-way sync between Hermes kanban cards and Linear or Jira issues. Open issues with a chosen label in the projects you pick become cards; card status moves the issue through its workflow; a finished card posts its summary on the issue; a worker that blocks with a question gets it posted on the issue, and the first human reply there unblocks the card with the answer. Several connections (Linear workspaces, Jira sites, several projects each) run side by side, and one failing never stops the others. Desktop adds an Issue Sync panel, a status-bar chip and kanban card badges; /issues status and /issues show work from any chat. Disclosure — calls api.linear.app and your Jira Cloud site with your own API key or token (read by name through the profile secret scope, never stored); moves issues and posts comments as you, each signed "— via Hermes issue-sync", including each finished card's summary and each blocked card's question; turns the titles and descriptions of labelled issues into kanban cards, and the first reply on a blocked card's issue unblocks the card with that reply's text, so anyone who can label or comment on those issues supplies text your kanban workers act on (cards stay unassigned unless you set an assignee); runs a short background sync thread on kanban dispatcher ticks and runs `hermes kanban` subcommands to read and update the board; writes only to its own plugin data folder; no telemetry. On multi-profile gateways it binds the profile's secret scope itself through the public agent.secret_scope API until NousResearch/hermes-agent#151126 is fixed.

entries.name: hermes-jailbreak-kernel
entries.description: Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Hermes Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm_request middleware that, by default (`on`/`full` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); `slim` appends it instead, and `off` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); `/jailbreak dump off` or `HERMES_JAILBREAK_DUMP=0` turns it off. No network, no exec.

entries.name: hermes-jetstream
entries.description: NATS JetStream event bus: agents publish events (nats_publish), pull one batch (nats_fetch), and wake on subject matches — live-session watches or wake routes (config-declared or runtime-registered via jetstream_wake) with durable consumers, manual ack, an idempotent wake ledger and rate rails; an opt-in lifecycle tap mirrors Hermes events onto hermes.> subjects. Disclosure — connects only to the NATS servers in your own config (no third-party calls, no telemetry); the platform adapter holds persistent subscriptions and reconnect loops for the gateway's lifetime; token/nkey/user-pass secrets come from ${VAR} references read via the profile-scoped secret scope and a configured creds file is read from its path, never written or rotated; wake routes render event payloads into prompts that start gateway turns or fire an existing cron job (optionally under another named profile), the agent itself can add up to 16 durable wake routes with jetstream_wake that persist in plugin data across restarts (subject still limited to subscribe_allowed, no cron-job or cross-profile targets), and jetstream_watch injects matching events into the live session when allow_gateway_injection is on, so keep subscribe_allowed scoped to trusted publishers.

entries.name: hermes-jev-routing
entries.description: Per-turn model routing for the request that is about to go out. Jev reads the turn, picks the tier it deserves, and the plugin rewrites the provider request onto that model, including the reasoning level when the request carries one. Shadow by default, with notify, confirm and auto modes, a strip under the composer for the turn that was just routed, and a spend ledger. A pick on another provider is reported rather than sent, because a plugin cannot open a second provider client. Disclosure — once a routing JSON is configured, every turn (shadow mode included) sends the current message, up to 4,000 characters of recent user/assistant turns, the active model name, an estimated context size and the spend/budget snapshot to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai, endpoint overridable in that JSON), and the jev_route tool and /jev-routing route send their text the same way; in auto mode it rewrites the model and reasoning level on outgoing requests, and in Hermes Desktop the auto mode and the approve row also switch the session's model, including onto another provider (core's expensive-model confirmation is shown to the user, never answered automatically).

entries.name: hermes-jobs
entries.description: Google Calendar is the one supported backend today (scope calendar.events, one bound calendar). Bidirectional sync between Hermes cron (system of record) and that job board. discover/status are read-only; sync plans both directions and is dry-run unless --confirm on the CLI. Read-only /jobs slash command shows the 7-day agenda and pending changes; each job's last run time and status (ok/error) is written to its event as a colour and one description line, never the title. Disclosure — syncs Hermes cron job names, next-run times and last-run status (never prompts; only a prompt sha256) to one Google Calendar you bind, over Hermes plugin OAuth (`hermes auth add hermes-jobs:google`, scope calendar.events, host www.googleapis.com). Reads `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json` read-only, and the first 8 KB of each no-agent cron job's script under `~/.hermes/scripts/` only to recognise its own auto-sync job. Calendar edits change a cron job's schedule or name only when you run `hermes hermes-jobs sync --confirm`. The opt-in experimental skip writes `~/.hermes/scripts/hermes-jobs-skip-tick.py` and creates two one-shot no-agent cron jobs. The opt-in `mcp-serve` push mode polls Calendar every 60 s and POSTs signed event ids to your own gateway webhook URL.

entries.name: hermes-kame-api-rotation
entries.description: Smart API key rotation: the healthiest key for every call, each 429 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / quota refusal sized from its own evidence. Install with its companion hermes-kame-provider, which hands Hermes this plugin's rotating client through ProviderProfile.create_client (and create_messages_client where Hermes offers it); no core override. When Hermes has a fallback list, a reply whose model is busy, resting or slow moves down a ladder: the model the reply started on, then the main model (model.default), then the rest of the list; a model of the same provider answers inside the plugin on the same keys and endpoint, a model of another provider is handed to Hermes' own fallback (which walks the list), and a late reply can be raced by the next model of the same provider; nothing moves once part of the reply is on screen, and never_fall_back_to_another_model turns every switch off (the plugin reads the model and fallback_providers from config.yaml, read-only; no new network destination). Disclosure — /kame-keys add|import|split, and on start a key variable holding several comma-joined keys, write one auth.json pool row per key through Hermes' pool API after an owner-only plaintext backup (last 5 kept; switch: resolver_disabled); settings changed from /kame or the Desktop panel are saved as KAME_* lines in Hermes' .env; key-redacted, size-capped owner-only local logs (current file plus one previous), a status file, a small lifetime-counters file (replies answered and saved, requests sent per model in 24 hours, the provider's stated daily limit; no key, prompt or text) and a small model-health file (the time and the success or failure of each model's last judged outcomes, at most 7 days; no key, prompt or text) per profile; the Desktop panel reads that file and queues its settings requests through its own dashboard/plugin_api.py route (GET /state, POST /control, this plugin's plugin-data folder only); after Hermes' own fallback answered a reply, the Desktop page sets that conversation's model back to the model the reply started on with config.set --session (never --global; config.yaml is not written); while every key is resting and no fallback model can take over, chats (CLI, Desktop, messaging gateway) keep waiting with no total limit (each key's rest capped by max_hold_seconds) and cron runs give up after 300 s with the provider's refusal unless max_total_wait_seconds is set. Optional speech: where Hermes offers register_tts_provider, the plugin registers a text-to-speech provider named kame-gemini, unused until the owner sets tts.provider: kame-gemini; it sends each sentence to Gemini's own endpoint on the owner's Gemini keys, rotated like the chat's, rests a refused key as long as Google said and waits at most once, under 2 s, for a key about to come back. Optional listening: where Hermes offers register_transcription_provider, the plugin registers a speech-to-text provider named kame-gemini, unused until the owner sets stt.provider: kame-gemini; it sends the recording to Gemini's own endpoint on the same keys, rotated the same way, and when every key of the chosen model is resting it sends it to the next Gemini model of the owner's fallback list instead (only the chosen model under never_fall_back_to_another_model). Extra billed requests (chat replies only, plain API keys only - a credential Hermes records as a subscription is never raced; hedge_mode off turns them all off): a late reply, or one whose model has just answered busy (a 5xx on a key: the next model of the list is then asked beside the retry at once), may also be sent to up to two more keys of the same model (about 10% of replies, 30% in "Faster", bursts of 3), to up to two models of your fallback list on the same provider, keys and endpoint (the ones that usually answer fastest, from each model's last 20 first-word times kept on disk for seven days; one that keeps failing is left out until its retest is due; the first joins at its own usual first word when that is shorter than the reply's model's, so with a slow first model most replies send this one request more; a raced key that fails is replaced once by another key of that model), and to one more model of the list when it stays silent; a best model that is busy, or remembered as failing (its latest judged outcome failed, with at least two failures in its last ten within seven days; the reply then starts on the next model of your list, and KAME_NO_REMEMBERED_TROUBLE=1 turns this off), may be asked again beside a reply every 20 s - less often the longer it keeps failing, at most every 5 min - and that ask is heard to its first word or 30 s; a model of the list left out for its record is looked at again 10 min after its latest failure (doubling, at most 2 h): it is then asked once beside a reply that starts on the first model of the list that is not failing, at most every 20 s across conversations, and heard to its first word or 30 s (an answer clears its record); when keys keep coming back out of quota the next attempt asks 4, then 8, then up to 16 keys at once (probe_burst_max_legs); and a reply that showed a thought and then went quiet with nothing shown past its learned limit (8-20 s, at most 90 s; thought_quiet_s sets it, 0 turns it off) may be asked once more on another key of its model (the same key when it has only one) and once on the next model of your list (another key of the same model when no other model may be asked), its thoughts still shown live, the first to show text or a tool call being the answer; if those stay silent too, the reply is handed to the next entry of your list; and an answer that has begun and then sends nothing for answer_quiet_s (45 s; 0 turns it off; never while a tool the provider runs on its side is in flight) is continued with one more request. Titles and other background jobs are limited to a few requests and are stopped with a timeout so Hermes moves them down your own list; a title on a model remembered as failing, or busy, goes once to the first healthy model of your list on the same provider.

entries.name: hermes-kemet
entries.description: Twelve Egyptian gods in painted relief and gold leaf: Thoth, Ra, Isis, Osiris, Anubis, Horus, Bastet, Sekhmet, Set, Nut, Ptah and Hathor, as Hermes Desktop themes. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers twelve themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while one of its themes is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named kemet-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-lang-cs
entries.description: Czech (Čeština) language pack for Hermes Agent covering all three UI surfaces — core CLI/gateway/platforms (3,574/3,574 keys), the Ink TUI (1,443 of 1,445) and the Desktop app (5,489 of 5,611). Core keys match the English source of `main` at f65af53f28 (2026-11-15) exactly: no key upstream has since removed and no placeholder divergence, checked by flattening both sides. The remaining TUI keys are 2 whose English value is a function with branching (image plural counts), and the remaining 122 Desktop keys are 120 of the same kind (plural counts such as `cron.count`, conditional labels such as `assistant.thread.errorSwitchToModel`) plus two array values, which the pack format cannot express as one template — they are omitted so they fall back to English instead of rendering a wrong Czech form. Ships the same text as upstream PR #105503, so if that PR lands the bundled locale and this pack agree. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no network, no dependencies. Disclosure — an `__init__.py` whose `register()` is a no-op is included so the Desktop "Install from Git" flow accepts the pack (#138118); registering the pack never changes display.language, the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language cs`. Česká lokalizace rozhraní Hermes Agent.

Every translatable key exists and every value is translated against the English source of `main` at the revision this release was cut from: zero unknown keys and zero placeholder divergence on all three surfaces, and the four remaining Desktop keys are arrays/structured values a text pack cannot carry. Checked with `hermes plugins validate` and with the pack's own `tools/verify_pack.py`, which also runs as public CI on every push. Core and TUI mirror the bundled `pt` locale, registered as a real `pt-br` variant so it wins over the `pt`/`pt-BR` alias; the Desktop catalog is the original contribution (first proposed upstream in PR #92590, 2026-08-23), since the Desktop app ships no Portuguese at all. Manifest-only plugin: flat dotted YAML catalogs under locales/, no code, no network, no dependencies. Registering the pack never changes display.language — the user opts in via `hermes config set display.language pt-br`. A weekly drift workflow reports when `main` adds or drops keys; nothing self-updates. Tradução pt-BR da interface do Hermes Agent. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.name: hermes-lcm-x
entries.description: Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 16 lcm_* tools for search, recall and expansion (lcm_memory only with LCM_ENTITIES_ENABLED=1). Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from hermes-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace hermes-lcm with hermes-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — local semantic recall is on by default once its dependency companion is installed (hermes plugins install electricsheephq/lcm-x/companions/hermes-lcm-x-local-embeddings --ref <the LCM-X commit>; it carries fastembed): summaries and message chunks are embedded in-process with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 after a one-time model download, in the background, and stay on the machine. Without the companion, recall answers from full text and lcm_doctor prints the install command; on hosts with 2 or fewer effective CPUs the default answers from full text unless LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true; LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false turns semantic recall off. Cloud embedding providers (Voyage via VOYAGE_API_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama) send message text to that provider and run only with LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=true and an explicit model. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in), including a delegated subagent's turns as it runs; on gateway platforms the sender's platform user ID is recorded with each user message by default (LCM_SENDER_CAPTURE=0 turns it off), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under HERMES_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads the files Hermes saves for oversized tool results so it can store their full content, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm_status/lcm_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use. An opt-in event recorder (LCM_RECORDER_ENABLED, off by default) writes local files under HERMES_HOME/lcm-recorder (up to 20 GiB by default): what Hermes sends to LCM-X and what it returns, including conversation content, copies of lcm.db and lcm-large-outputs, session rows from state.db, and the LCM-related parts of config.yaml with credential values replaced by set/unset markers.

entries.name: hermes-lectern
entries.description: A desk you share with Hermes, inside Hermes Desktop: one dashboard of what Hermes just changed with write_file and patch, recent notes and your tasks that are overdue, due within 7 days or in progress, plus a reader and editor for an Obsidian vault. Open notes reload when Hermes edits them, and saves are conflict-safe: if Hermes or another app changes the note you are editing, your draft is kept and you can keep it, load the disk version or compare the two side by side. Editing is raw Markdown (no visual editor, graph or tabs). Tasks come from task notes (TaskNotes style, by tag or folder) and from checkbox tasks (Obsidian Tasks 📅 dates, Dataview [due:: ] fields). Once you set an attention field or tag, the ones that need you are listed too. English and Japanese UI. All file access goes through the plugin's own dashboard backend: no agent tools or hooks, no shell commands, no network calls beyond Hermes' own API. Tested on macOS; Linux is untested and Windows is not supported. Disclosure — reads the Markdown files of the vault folder you choose, plus image files inside that vault so notes can show them (hidden folders and symlinks are skipped); writes to the vault only when you save or create a note, and has no delete. Stores its settings and a SQLite search index in $HERMES_HOME/hermes-lectern, outside the vault (safe to delete; about 175 MB for a 5,500-note vault). The Desktop side listens to Hermes tool.complete events for write_file and patch to learn which notes Hermes changed, keeps the 50 most recent paths in Desktop local storage, and while you edit a note re-reads that one note through Hermes' API every 8 seconds to notice outside changes. Writes to the clipboard only when a quote cannot be inserted into a chat box. Reads and stores no credentials. Remote images in notes are not loaded (they show as links). No telemetry and no self-update. On Hermes builds that provide the preview.fileOpener area, vault notes opened from elsewhere in Desktop open in Lectern; older builds ignore it and use the normal file preview.
entries.title: Hermes Lectern
known_issues: Tested on macOS only; Linux is untested. Windows is not supported (the vault path must start with /).
The first index reads every note: a 5,500-note vault took about 40 seconds on a Mac.

entries.name: hermes-ledger
entries.description: Tamper-evident flight recorder: every tool call (arguments redacted), a SHA-256 of every result, and every approval decision are appended to a local hash-chained, Ed25519-signed log. `hermes ledger verify` walks the chain and names the first edited, deleted, reordered or truncated entry; `hermes ledger show` prints a timeline; `hermes ledger export --receipt` writes a signed receipt of one session that anyone can check with only the public key (records from other sessions appear as content-free stubs), with `hermes ledger verify-receipt` or the bundled standalone verify_receipt.py. An approval record binds to the exact call it approved. Adds a /ledger slash command, a Ledger dashboard tab with a chain-intact badge, and the skill hermes-ledger:ledger-audit. It proves the log was not changed after writing, not that the agent was honest when it wrote it (threat model in the README). Disclosure — five observer hooks (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, post_approval_response, on_session_start, on_session_end) see every tool call's name, arguments and result and every approval prompt; arguments are redacted by pattern (sensitive key names, bearer/sk- and other token shapes, PEM keys, NAME=value secrets) before writing, which is best effort; results are hashed, never stored; writes only under plugin-data/hermes-ledger/ (ledger.jsonl, ledger.head, an Ed25519 private key at mode 0600 that is never printed, and its public key); the log is never pruned; observer only, never blocks, approves, denies or changes a call; no network, no credentials read, no background processes, no shell commands.

entries.name: hermes-ledgerline
entries.description: Inspect session costs and usage in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — reads session lists, session detail, search, usage analytics and cron targets from the gateway's core REST API through the raw window.hermesDesktop.api bridge (the plugin SDK has no route to those endpoints), and runs hermes version, hermes insights and hermes send --list through the gateway's cli.exec. Only when you start them: explain and audit send the selected session's digest (tool arguments only if you tick that box) to your configured model, as a new Hermes session or a background prompt on the focused one; alerts and test messages are sent with hermes send to a messaging target you pick; scheduled reports create a Hermes cron job (one agent turn per run on the default model, delivered to the target you pick) and are paused, resumed or removed through cron.manage. Budgets, dismissed tips, scans and saved answers are kept in Hermes plugin storage on the desktop. Nothing is sent elsewhere and it exposes no tools to the model.

entries.name: hermes-lens
entries.description: Talk to your own Hermes agent through Ray-Ban Meta glasses. A platform channel for a companion iPhone app that holds a Gemini Live voice call; requests that need your data or an action become ordinary messages to your agent, and Hermes approvals appear as an Approve / Decline card that only your tap resolves. Disclosure — opens an HTTP listener (default 127.0.0.1:8795, plaintext; expose it only through a TLS proxy such as tailscale serve) where any phone holding the shared HERMES_LENS_TOKEN chats with the agent as its owner, bypassing the gateway allowlist, and resolves approval prompts with a tap; sends GEMINI_API_KEY only to generativelanguage.googleapis.com to mint single-use Gemini Live call tokens, after which the companion app speaks the agent's answers and any glasses photos you attach through Google's Gemini Live (with Google Search); `hermes lens setup` writes HERMES_LENS_TOKEN (and a Gemini key you type) to the profile .env; stores only daily call-time totals in its plugin data dir; no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes Lens
known_issues: The iPhone app is built from source with Xcode (ios/ in the repo); Meta does not yet allow glasses-toolkit apps in the App Store.
The phone must reach the gateway over HTTPS, e.g. tailscale serve in front of 127.0.0.1:8795.

entries.name: hermes-line
entries.description: A phone line for Hermes: with your approval it calls a business from your Twilio account, works the phone menu, waits on hold, then bridges you in or finishes the task, and can answer callbacks. Disclosure — Places real phone calls and sends call audio through your own Twilio account (api.twilio.com), and through xAI (api.x.ai) when XAI_API_KEY is set; every call and every released SMS code needs your approval in chat. With `enabled: true` it runs a call service inside Hermes on 127.0.0.1:8788 that you expose through your own HTTPS tunnel, plus a loopback-only tool server, and it starts one `hermes acp` process per call on a separate neutral call profile with a minimal environment. With `sms_source: adb` it reads the attached Android phone's SMS inbox. The setup check (`/line check`, `hermes hermes-line check`) runs `hermes --version` and makes read-only Twilio GET requests.
entries.title: Hermes Line
known_issues: US numbers only (geographic and toll-free); premium 900/976 and non-US numbers are refused.
Needs a Twilio account, a public HTTPS tunnel to the plugin, the Hermes gateway on the same machine, and a separate Hermes profile with no ACP toolsets for the calls (setup step in the README).

Waiting on hold was shown live on a real airline hold queue (44 min in silence, 0 phrases spoken into hold). Real agents answered on two Hilton calls, but the live-person check missed them every time; the fix is tested offline only, so detecting a real agent and bridging you in are not yet proven live.

Detecting that a live person answered is experimental: live calls produced one false detection (Delta) and three missed agents (Hilton), all fixed offline and not yet re-proven live; on restricted tasks your phone rings only after a clear yes to the live-person question, or after two human-like but unclear replies so you can judge.
Automated assistants and phone menus get only fixed phrases or keys; many real menus are left unanswered on purpose.
Callbacks from a business are tested offline only; calls forwarded from your own mobile line were answered live twice.
Grok Voice (optional xAI key) was used on one live call; barge-in and key tones on it are unproven.
Owner line mode (call your line, key a PIN) is optional, off unless a PIN is set, experimental, and not yet used on a live call.
Verification codes must arrive on a carrier phone; Twilio numbers filter one-time-code texts (error 30038).

entries.name: hermes-local-voice
entries.description: Voice memos become text on the machine that recorded them: no API key, no account, and no audio leaving the host. Capture from PipeWire or ffmpeg, run faster-whisper locally, and the transcript arrives as a note. Four tools (transcribe_audio, voice_record_start, voice_record_stop, transcribe_last) plus a speech-to-text provider registered through ctx.register_transcription_provider, so core transcribes only admitted messages when stt.provider is set to hermes_local_voice. pre_llm_call attaches the pending transcript to the turn; the legacy pre_gateway_dispatch path is opt-in and off by default because it runs before sender authorization. Ships model management (list supported Whisper sizes with disk cost and cache status, download explicitly) and a live capture path with a silence gate so ambient room tone is never transcribed. Disclosure: all processing is local. Network access happens only when the user explicitly runs the model download command, which fetches weights from Hugging Face into the Hermes model directory; no telemetry, no automatic updates, no reads outside the Hermes home and the recording paths the plugin creates. Disclosure \u2014 transcription runs locally with faster-whisper; when the user configures a loopback job server URL, audio files are POSTed to it and its reply is used as the transcript; the transcribe tool and the pre_llm_call hook read any local audio path named in the chat, and with cleanup enabled the tool deletes only recordings the plugin created; the opt-in auto_transcribe_inbound setting transcribes gateway voice messages before sender authorization; models are read from the Hermes model directory,  or , and are downloaded from Hugging Face only when the user runs the model download command; no telemetry, no automatic updates. entries.name: hermes-make-it-smart
entries.description: Canonical catalog over every Hermes profile. Reads the local state.db files, names each session "NNN [Subject] MMM [Tag] [Tag] Description · Verb", and exposes faceted filters (subject, maker, context, intention, theme, year, project) as a native Desktop page. The window is a three-column box —facet panel, vertical Session Info rail, content— and every window (Session DB, Process, New Rules) keeps its own filters and its own universe. Includes a Pending view that attributes every memory/skill approval request to the session that produced it, and a Process tab that simulates the rename, writes a mandatory backup, commits through the host's session.title API and offers one-click revert. Disclosure — reads session titles and message excerpts from the local Hermes databases on the user's machine. No text leaves the machine by default: classification runs locally, and the model path is opt-in — off unless the owner configures their own endpoint and key (the key is stored by Hermes and read with agent.secret_scope.get_secret; the plugin keeps no credential of its own) and ticks the consent box. When enabled, up to 600 characters per turn of the user's own messages go to that endpoint, with attachments and URLs stripped and sensitive values redacted first; the description it returns is written to the local database. Writes are session titles — through the cellar_rename / cellar_tag tools, or when the user presses Commit in the Process tab — always after a timestamped backup, and revertible in one click.

entries.name: hermes-make-plain
entries.description: One-click composer polish for the Hermes Desktop chat: a wand button at the right of the input box rewrites the draft in place into a clear request an AI can act on, with nothing added and nothing dropped. The layout follows the draft: a symptom report with a request stays one paragraph, separate edits get one short line each, and a draft that is already a list keeps its line count and markers. An answer longer than four times the draft is rejected with a toast, so a runaway answer never replaces the draft. Pure filler and repeated restatements are dropped, and every concrete detail is kept exactly as written: names, numbers, versions, ports, paths, file names, URLs, @-references, /commands and code. It stays in the draft's language and never translates. The message is never sent; the button spins while the rewrite is in flight, rejects an empty box before any work starts, and never overwrites a draft edited while the call is running. Disclosure: one model call per click through the llm.oneshot auxiliary route to the auxiliary.title_generation model; no other network calls, no telemetry, no analytics; reads and writes only the composer draft through the official SDK and keeps no copy of the text (plugin storage is a one-field load heartbeat); no shell commands, no credentials.

entries.name: hermes-manas-aegis
entries.description: [ALPHA] Experimental Hermes guardrail (prototype, not standalone security): pattern-based pre-tool checks that can block or rewrite some risky tool arguments, with a canary honeypot, local telemetry and a loopback HUD, plus STIX 2.1 export. Opt-in, test environments only. Disclosure — alpha guardrail: its pre_tool_call / pre_llm_call / transform hooks can block tool calls or rewrite their arguments (honeypot redirect to a decoy file, safe-flag git rewrite) and scrub tool results; serves a token-protected loopback-only HUD on 127.0.0.1 (default port 18777, off with auto_launch_hud_server: false); fetches public CISA KEV and NVD CVE feeds over HTTPS (no key) for the threat-intel panel, refreshed every 6 hours while the HUD runs; the full scan reads files under the active Hermes home (skipping .env, auth.json, config.yaml, webhook_subscriptions.json, mcp-tokens/, *.bak backups and other profiles); writes redacted telemetry and a STIX 2.1 feed under the plugin data folder; no credentials read, no telemetry sent out.
entries.title: Manas Aegis
known_issues: Alpha release: prototype guardrail, not standalone security; opt-in, test environments only.

The HUD's big KPI cards count only local activity and the plugin's internal rule/indicator count; the live CISA KEV + NVD feed appears only in the separate global-intel panel, as awareness only — the plugin does not check whether this device is affected by any listed CVE.

entries.name: hermes-maps
entries.description: A live map you and Hermes share, docked beside the chat. Hermes plots places it finds on the web with real coordinates, flies the camera, drops pins with a note and source link, and draws routes. You click a pin or circle an area and Hermes receives what you picked. Two looks: a clean flat map and a cinematic globe. No keys and no cost. Disclosure — viewing the map sends tile requests (your IP address and the area viewed) to tiles.openfreemap.org; a bundled world outline is the offline fallback. Plotting and place search send place names and search text (and the visible map bounds for a visible-area search) from this machine to photon.komoot.io, a free service with no uptime guarantee; results are kept in memory for an hour. Google Maps links and a pin's source link open in the browser only when clicked. Selections you send become chat messages and reach your model provider. Pins, routes, camera and selections are stored in Hermes plugin storage on this machine. No background processes, no telemetry, no credentials, no self-update.
entries.title: Hermes Maps
known_issues: Hermes Desktop is required: the map is a Desktop pane. The tools still save their changes without it and report delivery as queued.
Place lookup uses OpenStreetMap data through Photon. Places it does not list come back as not placed instead of getting a guessed pin, and each lookup takes several seconds.
Routes are straight lines between stops, not road routes.

entries.description: Drive Microduck, the open-source bipedal duck robot from Pollen Robotics / Hugging Face, in a MuJoCo simulation running its real trained ONNX RL policies: look through the duck's head camera, walk, turn, sit, stand, move the head, and line up and kick a ball at a goal (10 tools), with every motion gated by a pre_tool_call safety interlock (speed and duration caps, an arena geofence, a latching e-stop only a human clears with /duck clear, every blocked call logged). Ships a /duck command, a bundled skill and a dependency-free mock duck, so it runs with no MuJoCo at all. Independent community integration, not affiliated with Pollen Robotics. Disclosure — network: in sim mode, plain HTTP to the sim server you configure (default 127.0.0.1:8765, sim/server.py, a long-running process you start yourself); mock mode (default) makes no network connections. Setup: sim/fetch_assets.py, run by you once, downloads Pollen's MJCF, meshes and ONNX policies (~7 MB, Apache-2.0) from the official pollen-robotics/microduck-simulator Hugging Face Space pinned to a commit; the plugin downloads nothing at runtime. Files: camera snapshots, a blocked-call audit log and the e-stop latch under the plugin data dir. No credentials. The interlock limits this plugin's tools only; it does not stop other tools (terminal, code execution) from calling the sim server or changing the limits in config.yaml.

entries.name: hermes-mini
entries.description: A mobile-first chat app for your own Hermes agent, served from the Hermes dashboard and installable to the home screen: multiple chats, an inbox for scheduled-job results, search, bookmarks, to-dos, scheduled jobs and slash-triggered skills, live narration of what the agent is doing, a model/provider picker and approval-mode selector, profile editing, inline prompt and app-connection cards, Android share-sheet support, dictation through Hermes' speech-to-text, an optional computer view, and opt-in Web Push. Disclosure — serves a web app and routes from the dashboard behind its login (no own port); registers an in-process `hermes-mini` gateway platform for job delivery; in app chats only, adds a turn rule and job-delivery default to the prompt, appends a progress-update request to tool results during long turns, and blocks edits to its own files; reads Hermes' state.db read-only for Inbox and Search; writes the live narration line with small auxiliary-model calls on the user's provider; writes `platforms.hermes-mini.home_channel` to config.yaml once; only on explicit user action, calls Hermes' gateway methods to edit profile name/avatar, save provider API keys, or change `approvals.mode` (with confirmation before switching to Off; never auto-approves), and renders Hermes' own password/secret prompt cards (never runs sudo itself); lets the user answer an approval from a push notification; runs ffmpeg for audio metadata, `hermes gateway restart -y --detach` plus a dashboard restart from its Restart button, and, for the optional computer view's clipboard, a Tk helper and xclip; uses internal Hermes modules for dictation, the computer view, and YAML helpers, which may stop working after a Hermes update; opt-in Web Push to FCM/Mozilla/Apple/Windows push services; no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes Mini
known_issues: Tested on Android Chrome (installed to the home screen) and desktop Chrome; not yet tested on iPhone or iPad.

entries.name: hermes-mobile
entries.description: WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE_CATALOG_AFTER_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE_DELIVER_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $HERMES_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through Hermes's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through Hermes's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.

entries.name: hermes-model-switcher
entries.description: Choose models across Hermes profiles from a Dashboard tab: a per-profile picker built on host-supplied model data (SDK-authenticated GET /api/model/options), a preview of provider/model intent across every supported model-selection slot (main, delegation, auxiliary, judge, fallback, MoA, cron, plugin and specialist), and one-click apply or revert with presets. Main-slot preview shows intended provider/model, not the exact persisted diff; the exact diff is shown only after host readback. Disclosure — its apply route reads and edits the profiles' config.yaml (that is the plugin's function) through public seams only: POST /api/model/set for main and compatible auxiliary slots, and public hermes_cli.config load/save under the target home for other slots; credential presence checks use public profile-scoped secret helpers (agent.secret_scope), and profile discovery uses public hermes_constants. The plugin makes no direct third-party requests and opens no provider caches or pricing registries directly, but its browser tab does call the host's /api/model/* routes through the Dashboard SDK, and the host options route may itself initiate provider or pricing I/O even without an explicit refresh request, so reads are not guaranteed cache-only. It runs no shell commands or background processes and reports nothing. The private undo journal stores a full pre-change snapshot of each config it edits, which can contain sensitive fields including embedded credentials. Saved presets also persist reviewed change values, potentially including inline credentials or credential-bearing base URLs, in presets.json (0600) under get_hermes_home()/state/hermes-model-switcher/ (0700). The host write route has no expected-revision check: readback surfaces many foreign edits as recovery_required, but a concurrent same-key edit can be overwritten undetected and full-state deletions retain an unrelated-write race, so not every foreign edit is guaranteed to surface.
known_issues: Couples at runtime to public Hermes seams that are not stability-guaranteed APIs (the /api/model/* dashboard routes, hermes_cli.config, agent.secret_scope, hermes_constants); a host refactor can break the plugin until it re-pins. Missing upstream seams remain open: a compare-and-save write with an expected-revision check (hermes-agent #142339), a public typed write route for non-main slots (#142340), and a dry-run footprint for exact main-slot previews (#142341).

entries.name: hermes-monitor
entries.description: Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every Hermes profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls Hermes' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch_account_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, Hermes core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress.

entries.name: hermes-multiplayer
entries.description: Multiplayer Hermes. Channels, DMs, threads and a shared team room where you, up to four teammates, and each of your Hermes agents work in one place. No server to host — or one small relay when teammates can't reach each other. Disclosure — Syncs channels, DMs, threads, reactions, edits and presence with up to four teammate gateways at addresses you configure (authenticated by a shared Hermes Multiplayer secret; adds code-gated `/hermes-multiplayer/v1/pair` plus secret-protected `/hermes-multiplayer/v1/sync` and `/hermes-multiplayer/v1/ping` routes, and the same routes under the legacy `/herd/v1/` prefix, to your Hermes API server, which must be reachable by teammates), and, if you join or start a team room, sends everything it holds to the relay address you give it in plaintext where the relay operator can read it (there is no built-in relay); the `multiplayer_post` tool lets your agent post to teammates and the room without an approval prompt; with "Let my agent answer @mentions" (on by default), a chosen chat and `allow_gateway_injection: true`, a teammate's or a teammate agent's @mention starts a turn in that chat with your agent's memory and tools (at most 6 per minute, and at most 6 agent-only replies in a row per thread before a person must speak).
