entries.name: hermes-muse
entries.description: A proactive companion for Hermes: follows accepted goals (active/done/cancelled), prepares sourced research and Feed articles, maintains memory, and assembles rolling 30-day or natural-month calendar views. Read-only local Dashboard/Desktop pages show Feed, Ideas and Goals; profile selection cannot install, enable or disable Muse in any profile. One Skill, one state tool and six fixed recurring jobs; selected notices and weekly/monthly reports go to the active profile's Bot Chat and run an assistant turn there. Sources, authorization, quiet hours and actual result/delivery receipts remain distinct; partial coverage is not global availability. Disclosure: first load creates profile-local files/SQLite state and owned Cron scripts/jobs. Private/local input inbox rows retain their first 8000 characters and source identities, with associated chat/user routing IDs when present. The newest 500 remain; older rows are cleaned on later input only after both hourly/nightly cursors cover them. Unprocessed backlog can exceed 500 and has no fixed retention time. Native conversations/tool results are read separately; research records can retain returned payloads. Idempotency journals and oversized tool results stay in the profile state database without automatic expiry and may contain written content or tool output. Bounded conversation previews support full revision-checked paging. Delegates are instructed to remain read-only under inherited permissions, not sandboxed. Workers always use public delegate_task dispatch and follow the user's delegation settings; leave delegation.provider/model empty to keep the parent model. New Cron watches require cron.allow_agent_scheduling; local goal registration creates no job. Watch prompt/stop fields each allow 4000 characters; new repeating watches (interval or cron) must be at least 30 minutes apart, one-off schedules are exempt. Windows is not supported (POSIX file locks) and CI does not cover it. Background work incurs normal model/tool costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory service, core/SOUL replacement or phone/read-receipt guarantee. Native remove retains data/tasks for the documented owned-only cleanup.

entries.name: hermes-next-steps
entries.description: Clickable next steps under a Hermes Desktop reply: the agent offers two to six concrete options and one click sends that option back as the user's next message. Several options can be ticked and sent together as one turn, options a decision classifier reads as worth taking now carry a Recommended tag and start ticked, options that could damage something can carry a RISKY pill once that setting is on, a chip can explain a misleading label in a dim second line, and, with the carry setting on, options an earlier reply left unanswered follow the newest reply with an age label and a dismiss cross. The classifier is optional: with no classifier plugin loaded the chips work and are simply never marked. This edition stays inside the plugin SDK and drops the injected chip-border animation and the scroll back to an offering reply, both of which reach into the app's own DOM; the personal edition carries both. Follow-up Chips draws the same slot under a reply, so disable it before enabling this. Makes no network calls of its own. Disclosure — Derived from followup-chips (MIT). Adds a system-prompt section to every new session that tells the agent to end a choice with next-step chips on Hermes Desktop (a numbered list elsewhere), and a reply hook that rewrites the chip directive in Desktop replies; turning a prose offer into chips and carrying unanswered options forward are opt-in and change every reply when on. With a decision-classifier plugin (nerve or jev) loaded, the agent calls that plugin's tool once per reply that offers a choice. A chip sends its text as your next message only when you click it; steering a live turn with it is opt-in. No network calls, file access or credentials of its own.

entries.name: hermes-notify
entries.description: Phone notifications, questions, release progress and exact command approvals through Notify. Run `hermes notify setup` to sign in, connect the phone app, send a test and route command approvals to the phone. Disclosure — when enabled, sends model-written notifications and questions, optional release workspace data, and (when security.approval.transport is notify) each Hermes approval request's redacted command and description to the third-party Notify service (notify.belweave.ai); release Apps also go to a Cloudflare Worker you deploy yourself (uses HERMES_NOTIFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN). `hermes notify setup` signs in to notify.belweave.ai with a device code (sending a "Hermes on <hostname> (<OS>)" device label), saves the resulting 90-day NOTIFY_API_TOKEN to the profile .env and, once a phone is registered and no other transport is chosen, runs `hermes config set` to select security.approval.transport notify and transport_fallback builtin (terminal prompt when Notify is unreachable; skip with --no-approvals, undo with `hermes notify approvals off`). Phone approvals are approve-once or deny only; a phone timeout denies. Phone replies are injected into the session only when you set allow_reply_injection. Optional `hermes notify webhooks on` creates a Notify reply webhook, saves NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET to the profile .env, may run `boat host` to give the port a public HTTPS URL, sets allow_reply_injection and plugins.entries.hermes-notify.allow_gateway_injection, and then listens on 127.0.0.1 (inbound_webhook_port) for signed answer events that it re-checks with Notify before injecting the answer into the asking session as untrusted input; `hermes notify webhooks off` removes it. Runs one background delivery thread, plus a webhook listener thread when webhooks are on.

entries.name: hermes-office-desktop
entries.description: Workbench by Atlas Omnia — Open and edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Outlook for the web in Hermes Desktop. Live-tested in the automated harness and real Hermes Desktop sessions on macOS and Windows; see docs/live-evidence.md. Every edit requests Hermes approval and returns a readback/undo receipt; undo has exceptions (large Word snapshots, Excel over 10,000 cells, some PowerPoint edits and OneNote page creation), and history is lost on pane reload. powerpoint_add_speaker_notes returns Unsupported. Requires Microsoft sign-in and Upload My Add-in. A loopback HTTPS bridge on 127.0.0.1:47615-47619 (https://localhost) serves the add-in from this pinned plugin (only files listed in addin/SHA256SUMS with a matching sha256, never addin/dev), accepts only Workbench's own loopback origins (or a self-hosted addin_base's exact origin) and a user-typed single-use code, then a per-pane token; idle listeners release after ten minutes. One manual step per Hermes profile: trust the plugin's local certificate authority with the command it prints (the plugin never changes OS trust); /workbench manifest writes the add-in manifests. Earlier live runs used a private add-in site; the plugin-served default passed one live Excel run on macOS (2026-11-12) and is not live-tested yet in the other apps or on Windows. The pane loads Microsoft Office.js. Document data enters the local Hermes conversation; OneNote pages and email indexed on request persist unencrypted in brain.db. Reads are capped at 20,000 characters for Word and Outlook bodies. No Graph, credentials, telemetry, shell commands or unattended runs. Outlook reads only the open item; mail and calendar drafts are never sent or saved and recipients/attendees never changed. Image URL fetches alone use outbound HTTPS (public addresses, checked redirects, PNG/JPEG, 4 MiB); local images are restricted to allowed folders. Full disclosures and known limits: README and docs/reference.md. Not affiliated with Microsoft or Nous Research. Disclosure — Workbench serves its Office add-in from this plugin's pinned files over HTTPS on 127.0.0.1 ports 47615-47619 (https://localhost). To make that work you trust, by hand and once per Hermes profile, a local certificate authority the plugin creates. That authority can vouch only for localhost and 127.0.0.1, and its private key is stored unencrypted in the profile's plugin-data/hermes-office-desktop/tls folder, so keep that folder private and remove the trust when you stop using Workbench. The pane loads Microsoft's Office.js from appsforoffice.microsoft.com. Document and mail content you work on enters your Hermes conversation, and OneNote pages and email you index stay unencrypted in the plugin's local brain.db. Every edit asks for Hermes approval; deletes and other edits that cannot be undone have their own approval rule. Image URL fetches go out over HTTPS to public addresses only.
entries.title: Workbench by Atlas Omnia
known_issues: Windows: two Hermes profiles at once are not live-tested (port 47615 is no longer bound twice).

Requires the Hermes Desktop app (macOS 13+ or Windows) on the same machine as the Hermes gateway, or with the bridge ports 47615-47619 forwarded; the browser Webapp (webapp.enabled) preview pane cannot host Office for the web.

The add-in is served by the plugin on https://localhost: trust the profile's local certificate authority once with the printed command (manual; never done by the plugin). Live-tested with it so far: one Excel run on macOS (2026-11-12); the other apps and Windows are not yet.
Pairing follows the chat session id: after auto-compression or a /rewind fork the pane reports NotPaired and needs a fresh office_connect code.
powerpoint_add_speaker_notes is registered for schema parity but always returns Unsupported: Office.js for the web has no speaker-notes API.
hermes plugins validate warns (rule 9) about two private Hermes imports in scripts/livetest/, developer-only live-test scripts that Hermes never loads.

No third-party network, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-openready
entries.description: Prepare an open-source release candidate from a private repository and refuse to publish it: five tools (status, doctor, candidate, verify, gate) plus a pre_tool_call guard that inspects the terminal tool and blocks or escalates the publish commands it recognises - the gh, gh api and curl shapes that create a public repository or change visibility - until the owner has approved that exact candidate digest. It does not claim to catch every way to publish. No tool can push, change visibility or upload: candidate writes a local candidate directory and verify may write one packet under .openready-private/. The approval check runs the separately installed Open-Ready CLI with an allowlisted child environment carrying no Hermes provider keys or GitHub tokens. Disclosure — the tools run the separately installed Open-Ready CLI (openready_bin / openready_python from your config) as child processes with an allowlisted environment (no Hermes provider keys or GitHub tokens); openready_candidate writes a candidate directory at <repo>/.openready-candidate and openready_verify with write_packet writes one file at <repo>/.openready-private/packets/packet.json; the pre_tool_call guard inspects every terminal command and blocks, or sends to Hermes' approval prompt, the recognised gh / gh api / curl commands that create a public repository or change visibility, which is not a complete barrier (other tools, scripts or shell forms can still publish).

entries.name: hermes-osint-map
entries.description: A live situational-awareness globe in Hermes Desktop: earthquakes (USGS), disaster alerts (GDACS), natural events (NASA EONET), US severe weather (NWS), military and nearby aircraft (adsb.lol), satellites propagated live from CelesTrak elements, GDELT news incidents, about 5,000 official traffic cameras (Transport for London, with its short JamCam video clips, Caltrans, the Hong Kong Transport Department and Singapore LTA), shipping chokepoints and an opt-in live cyber-attack layer on a dithered 3D globe, with satellite orbits, aircraft tracks, a camera wall, a tour of what matters right now, day and night shading and night-vision, thermal and CRT looks, country dossiers (World Bank facts, events, headlines), NOAA space weather, markets, a feed of events, headlines and alerts, and a passive recon toolkit (DNS, RDAP, TLS, security headers, CT subdomains, CVE with CISA KEV, IP, GitHub, MAC). Seven agent tools (osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news, osint_watch, osint_show) answer from the same sources in any chat; osint_show lets Hermes fly the Desktop globe, pin places and switch layers while it answers, and the page's Brief me, Ask Hermes and dossier buttons open a chat that uses them. In Hermes Desktop, answers about a place end with a live map card. Watches check an area on a schedule and alert only on new events. No keys needed; an optional TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (plugin setting, read through Hermes's secret scope) adds equities and commodities. Unofficial; not affiliated with any data provider. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public data from fixed hosts (earthquake.usgs.gov, eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov, gdacs.org, api.weather.gov, data.gdeltproject.org, api.adsb.lol, celestrak.org, services.swpc.noaa.gov, api.tfl.gov.uk, api.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and static.data.gov.hk (camera lists), and camera stills and clips from TfL's JamCams bucket on s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, images.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and tdcctv.data.one.gov.hk, fetched only by camera id for cameras the user opens, api.worldbank.org, the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, Guardian and France 24 RSS feeds, api.gdeltproject.org (GDELT article search, only when a news query is given, which sends up to six words of the query), api.coingecko.com, and api.twelvedata.com with the key in a header when set), cached and only while the page is open or a tool is called, with a hermes-osint-map User-Agent; the optional Operator feeds layer is off until the user sets the plugin's feeds setting (or OSINT_MAP_FEEDS, read through Hermes's secret scope), then fetches only the RSS/Atom URLs the user lists, refusing a redirect to a private or internal address, and reads only the JSON digest files the user lists (up to 2 MB each, never sent anywhere), and osint_events can return those items to a chat that asks for the layer; the cyber-attack layer is off until the user turns it on and then reads threatmap-api.checkpoint.com, the undocumented feed behind Check Point's public threat map (unofficial; one stream, closed about 45 seconds after no page shows the layer); recon sends the domain, IP, CVE id, GitHub name or MAC prefix the user or agent enters to dns.google, rdap.org, crt.sh, cve.circl.lu, cisa.gov, ipwho.is, api.github.com and api.macvendors.com, and the TLS and headers lookups connect directly to the host named, refusing private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other internal addresses on every redirect, on ports 443/8443 (TLS) and 80/443/8080/8443 (headers) only; GDELT incidents are machine-coded from news coverage and labelled as such, incident titles are read from the article URL, and country-centroid locations are flagged as country-level; a watch is a normal Hermes scheduled job the user creates and can remove (named “OSINT watch · <name>”, every 15 minutes at the fastest), each check is one short model call with the user's default model plus the same public-source requests, and alerts go only to the destination the user picked (Hermes or a connected messaging channel); watch state (area, rules, the last 2,000 event ids seen, the last 20 alerts) and Hermes's latest globe scene are kept in the plugin's own state file under plugin-data; the page keeps its layer choices in Desktop plugin storage; no shell commands, no processes of its own, no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes OSINT Map
entries.capability_summary: hermes-osint-map (community, maintained by Adolanium) A live situational-awareness globe in Hermes Desktop: earthquakes (USGS), disaster alerts (GDACS), natural events (NASA EONET), US severe weather (NWS), military and nearby aircraft (adsb.lol), satellites propagated live from CelesTrak elements, GDELT news incidents, about 5,000 official traffic cameras (Transport for London, with its short JamCam video clips, Caltrans, the Hong Kong Transport Department and Singapore LTA), shipping chokepoints and an opt-in live cyber-attack layer on a dithered 3D globe, with satellite orbits, aircraft tracks, a camera wall, a tour of what matters right now, day and night shading and night-vision, thermal and CRT looks, country dossiers (World Bank facts, events, headlines), NOAA space weather, markets, a feed of events, headlines and alerts, and a passive recon toolkit (DNS, RDAP, TLS, security headers, CT subdomains, CVE with CISA KEV, IP, GitHub, MAC). Seven agent tools (osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news, osint_watch, osint_show) answer from the same sources in any chat; osint_show lets Hermes fly the Desktop globe, pin places and switch layers while it answers, and the page's Brief me, Ask Hermes and dossier buttons open a chat that uses them. In Hermes Desktop, answers about a place end with a live map card. Watches check an area on a schedule and alert only on new events. No keys needed; an optional TWELVEDATA_API_KEY (plugin setting, read through Hermes's secret scope) adds equities and commodities. Unofficial; not affiliated with any data provider. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public data from fixed hosts (earthquake.usgs.gov, eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov, gdacs.org, api.weather.gov, data.gdeltproject.org, api.adsb.lol, celestrak.org, services.swpc.noaa.gov, api.tfl.gov.uk, api.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and static.data.gov.hk (camera lists), and camera stills and clips from TfL's JamCams bucket on s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, images.data.gov.sg, cwwp2.dot.ca.gov and tdcctv.data.one.gov.hk, fetched only by camera id for cameras the user opens, api.worldbank.org, the BBC, Al Jazeera, DW, Guardian and France 24 RSS feeds, api.gdeltproject.org (GDELT article search, only when a news query is given, which sends up to six words of the query), api.coingecko.com, and api.twelvedata.com with the key in a header when set), cached and only while the page is open or a tool is called, with a hermes-osint-map User-Agent; the optional Operator feeds layer is off until the user sets the plugin's feeds setting (or OSINT_MAP_FEEDS, read through Hermes's secret scope), then fetches only the RSS/Atom URLs the user lists, refusing a redirect to a private or internal address, and reads only the JSON digest files the user lists (up to 2 MB each, never sent anywhere), and osint_events can return those items to a chat that asks for the layer; the cyber-attack layer is off until the user turns it on and then reads threatmap-api.checkpoint.com, the undocumented feed behind Check Point's public threat map (unofficial; one stream, closed about 45 seconds after no page shows the layer); recon sends the domain, IP, CVE id, GitHub name or MAC prefix the user or agent enters to dns.google, rdap.org, crt.sh, cve.circl.lu, cisa.gov, ipwho.is, api.github.com and api.macvendors.com, and the TLS and headers lookups connect directly to the host named, refusing private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other internal addresses on every redirect, on ports 443/8443 (TLS) and 80/443/8080/8443 (headers) only; GDELT incidents are machine-coded from news coverage and labelled as such, incident titles are read from the article URL, and country-centroid locations are flagged as country-level; a watch is a normal Hermes scheduled job the user creates and can remove (named “OSINT watch · <name>”, every 15 minutes at the fastest), each check is one short model call with the user's default model plus the same public-source requests, and alerts go only to the destination the user picked (Hermes or a connected messaging channel); watch state (area, rules, the last 2,000 event ids seen, the last 20 alerts) and Hermes's latest globe scene are kept in the plugin's own state file under plugin-data; the page keeps its layer choices in Desktop plugin storage; no shell commands, no processes of its own, no telemetry. This plugin registers tool(s): osint_situation, osint_events, osint_country, osint_recon, osint_news, osint_watch, osint_show. Requires Hermes >=0.22.2.

entries.name: hermes-pantheon
entries.description: Eighteen Hermes Desktop themes in dithered classical marble, one god each: all twelve Olympians plus Hades, Nyx, Helios, Selene and Medusa. Install once, then switch with /skin <name>. Matching terminal skins ship in cli/skins. Disclosure — theme-only desktop plugin: it registers eighteen themes through the plugin SDK, and their stylesheets restyle parts of Desktop's own UI (sidebar art, tabs, composer, wordmark) only while a Pantheon theme is active. It also watches Desktop's active theme: when a terminal skin named pantheon-<god> is active, it switches Desktop to that god's theme through the SDK's requestTheme. The terminal skins are plain YAML files the user copies into the Hermes skins folder by hand; the plugin does not install them or write any files. Fonts and art are bundled; no network requests, no agent tools or hooks.

entries.name: hermes-pentest
entries.description: Guided local Vite/Supabase source input discovery, fresh human approval, offline build and isolated testing with synthetic data. Populated/absent SQL controls and authenticated persisted-text XSS checks verify actual input/render paths. Reports distinguish rejected probes from failed controls and count planned versus completed same-user and cross-user stored workflows separately. Uses the provider already configured in Hermes. Also supports explicit local web/API discovery, controlled SQL injection, browser-proven reflected/DOM/stored XSS, access contracts, owner-approved localhost servers, multi-service applications and native/CLI checks. Durable budgets, supervised execution, stop/recovery, immutable evidence, fixed-build regression and reports. Disclosure — trusted Python controllers use the local Docker socket to manage exact run-owned containers; Docker targets get no host mounts, published ports or external network. Existing localhost servers are unmanaged and are tested only at origins the owner lists in `allowed_localhost_origins` (empty by default), which receive state-changing requests with the configured test-session headers. macOS supervised-local mode runs only executables the owner lists in `allowed_native_executables` (empty by default), under Seatbelt plus an RSS watchdog, not Docker isolation. Guided preparation reads the selected source and dependency trees and may fetch lockfile-verified Linux build packages from registry.npmjs.org. Guided assessments need a fresh one-shot human approval. Evidence stays in the selected profile's plugin data; no telemetry or model calls.
entries.title: Hermes Pentest
known_issues: Guided preparation currently supports Vite with an installed compatible npm cache and optional Supabase migrations. Other frameworks return setup gaps or require explicit adapters. Cached local toolchain images are required.

Guided execution requires Hermes public tool-execution middleware and all six declared hooks; missing approval integration refuses execution. Approval is one-use and bound to the exact source, runtime, plan and budget.

The v0.5.1 real-application follow-up completed all 15 selected checks: 10 data/Auth/browser contracts, 3 controlled SQL probes on a text preference-key filter and 2 same-user stored-XSS workflows. No confirmed vulnerabilities. Cross-user workflows: 0 planned, 0 completed. The earlier 3 rejected numeric-input SQL checks remain inconclusive; this follow-up does not relabel them or establish exhaustive coverage.

Source hints require model verification of route reachability and positive controls. Authenticated stored-XSS viewer proof requires a real final-document Bearer GET /auth/v1/user with its Referer; missing proof remains inconclusive. No arbitrary auth-state injection.

Localhost and supervised-local native targets are denied until the owner configures exact origins/executable paths in profile plugin settings. Plan acknowledgement flags do not grant permission. To revoke access, stop affected runs, end affected Hermes sessions, remove the entry, and start a new session. Managed sessions retain frozen settings; active attempts retain their bounded snapshot.
Bounded check catalogue, not exhaustive vulnerability coverage. Native support exercises CLI/app-bundle executables, not GUI/mobile interactions.

Managed web/Linux and browser checks require local Docker and prepared local images. Existing-localhost mode does not support HTTPS or interactive login/cookie rotation. Arbitrary Compose features are unsupported.
Existing localhost cannot be isolated or independently source-pinned. Interrupted unmanaged assessments require owner reset/new run. macOS native memory uses an RSS watchdog, not a hard limit.
MySQL/PostgreSQL timing has unit controls, but live dialect timing is unverified. PostgreSQL static dependency data flow is verified. SQLite and stacked MSSQL timing are explicitly skipped.
The local acceptance harness imports version-sensitive Hermes discovery internals, producing a validation warning. Plugin runtime registration/storage and secret access use public APIs.

entries.name: hermes-phone
entries.description: Let your Hermes agent place real phone calls for you with explicit approval. It shows a brief card and dials only after you reply "call" (or tap Call), says it is an AI in the first sentence of every call, relays mid-call questions to you in chat with a suggested answer, and reports one clean result (what was agreed, confirmation number, duration, cost) plus the transcript. Disclosure — places outbound PSTN calls through your own Twilio account (costs money; a web-phone mode needs no telephony account), streams call audio to OpenAI Realtime, runs a small FastAPI bridge that must be reachable at your PUBLIC_BASE_URL (binds 0.0.0.0 when a hosting PORT is set), and stores call logs and text transcripts in plugin data (SQLite); calls dial only after a human approval, only to numbers on your allowlist, with emergency and premium numbers blocked; card, address, ID, bank, email and phone details are shared with the callee only with per-call consent, CVV, passwords and one-time codes never; no audio recording, no telemetry, no self-updater, no credential-file reads.

entries.name: hermes-pickup
entries.description: Pick up where you left off: up to 10 cards (5 by default) of unfinished work from your recent Hermes chats, project folders and files, each with where you stopped and a one-click next step. Adapted from Herald OS by Luke (iamlukethedev), MIT. Disclosure — after explicit in-app consent (stored per profile), each Refresh reads recent chats from every profile's session store (read-only; profiles the user skips in Settings are never opened) and sends chat excerpts and metadata, project/file names and paths, git branch/changed-file names and recent commit subjects to the current profile's Hermes LLM route (the auxiliary title-generation model, main provider unless configured); runs read-only git and, on macOS, Spotlight `mdfind`; never reads document contents; writes only $HERMES_HOME/pickup/. The "Next step" button can submit a model-written prompt straight into the card's chat in one click. The optional install.sh, when asked, adds the plugin to every profile's plugins.enabled (undone exactly by uninstall.sh).
known_issues: On installs with several profiles, Hermes issue #134712 can make the Desktop backend answer Plugin not found; the page explains the fix (enable hermes-pickup in every profile, then restart Desktop).

entries.name: hermes-pilot
entries.description: Drive an autonomous Hermes Agent from a phone or tablet. Hermes Pilot turns the decisions an agent needs into one-tap review sheets and annotated screenshots, carries a one-line idea through a Quick Review interview into a spec the batch runner can execute, then files and monitors the kanban batches — with kanban, chat, terminal and usage in one installable PWA. Ships three bundled skills (quick-review, annotation, spec-architect), a Hermes dashboard tab (pairing QR, bridge status, scan directories, service control) and the PWA bridge it talks to. Disclosure — the plugin runs a local HTTP/WebSocket bridge bound to 127.0.0.1 (default port 4097), authenticated with a 256-bit token generated on first run and stored 0600 under the plugin data folder; a paired phone or tablet gets an interactive login shell on this computer through the bridge's terminal, outside Hermes' approval prompts and sandbox, plus chat, kanban and session actions through the local `hermes` CLI; it reads the kanban SQLite databases read-only; `node bin/hermes-pilot.mjs init` (run by you after `npm ci`, which installs the native node-pty module) copies three bundled skills into your Hermes skills folder and the dashboard files into your plugins folder; legacy akapen/mobile-pwa migration runs only when you confirm it, and removes old crons through `hermes cron remove`; remote access is opt-in and left to you (documented Tailscale `serve`, never started by the plugin); `hermes-pilot service install` writes a launchd (macOS) or systemd --user (Linux) unit only on explicit command; the bundled Interactive Demo is a static mock that talks to no backend; no telemetry and no third-party upload.

entries.description: A calm little garden for Hermes Desktop that grows in real time. It sits above the app like the Hermes pet, takes no layout space and can be dragged anywhere. Click a plant for a care wheel: water, prune (you choose which tip to cut, and the piece drops away), rotate, fertilize, repot, pick, sell, or ask Hermes. Four species (leafy plant, fern, cactus, little tree) grow in their own ways, pruning shapes how each one branches, and neglect only pauses them. Care earns play coins, and a small shop sells more plants and fertilizer, up to six pots. Bugs land now and then and can be shooed away. Two agent tools let Hermes check the garden and tend it when you ask. Original blue-ink artwork drawn in code. Reachable from the status bar, the command palette and the keyboard, and it speaks through the Hermes pet when one is showing. Disclosure: no network requests, no background model calls and no background processes; Ask Hermes submits one chat message only when you press it; coins are play money inside the plugin; the garden is kept in Desktop plugin storage and in plugin-data/hermes-plant/data.db; the plugin adds its own floating element to the page (Hermes has no SDK area for one) and removes it on unload, without reading or changing core markup.

entries.description: Your local markdown vault as a note graph, file tree and tabbed editor in one Hermes Desktop workspace tab, with Obsidian-style wikilinks, nested folder regions in the graph, link rewriting on rename, image and note embeds, and a ::vault chat link. entries.name: hermes-plugin-dev
entries.description: Hermes Plugin Dev: build Hermes plugins with Hermes. A plugin-development skill plus two offline tools that scaffold a new plugin and lint it against the catalog rules before you submit. The hermes-plugin-dev:hermes-plugin-development skill covers manifest v2 and strict YAML, the ctx API, all 46 hooks, capabilities and isolation, dashboard and Desktop panes, testing, release and catalog submission, and lessons from catalog reviews, with a template plugin and catalog-entry and PR-body templates. hpd_scaffold(target_dir, name) copies the hello-hermes template, which passes hermes plugins validate and doctor --ci as-is, renames it, and adds a catalog entry and PR body stub; it refuses non-empty folders and never overwrites. hpd_check(path, catalog_entry?) is a read-only lint: strict YAML, manifest rules, provides_tools against the registered tools, a security preflight, static schema token cost, and catalog entry rules (sha, image hosts, category, subdir, at most 6 screenshots). Both tool schemas together cost 190 o200k tokens. It is for anyone writing a first Hermes plugin or getting one ready for a catalog PR. To start, run hermes plugins install hermes-plugin-dev and hermes plugins enable hermes-plugin-dev, then ask: "Scaffold a Hermes plugin called weather-now in ~/code/weather-now, then check it." Finish with hermes plugins doctor <dir> --ci and hermes plugins validate <dir> --install-deps. The same skill installs into other coding agents with npx skills add mojomast/hermes-plugin-dev. Disclosure — `hpd_scaffold` creates files in any new or empty folder the model names (fixed template content only); `hpd_check` reads any folder or file the model names (read-only, never imports it); the user-run `hermes hpd check <dir> --execute` imports and runs the target plugin's `register()` unsandboxed in the Hermes process, so use it only on code you trust.

entries.name: hermes-pokemon
entries.description: A cozy pixel-art companion garden for Hermes Desktop with three starters, nicknames, fetch, berries, XP, and optional evolution through all nine starter forms. The companion keeps you company on long turns, reacts quietly to failures, to what Hermes is doing and to turns finishing in other chats, and lives through seasons with real day length and moon phases, offline showers, wild visitors it greets in character, old-friend cameos, keepsakes, milestones that leave a bench, a lantern and bunting in the garden, and a sapling that grows with the days. Reachable from the keyboard, the status bar and the command palette. Independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab community contributions; artwork is excluded from the source-code MIT license. Uses local plugin storage and read-only session activity, with no runtime network requests, credentials, backend, or model calls. Disclosure — independent fan project bundling CHUNSOFT Pokémon sprites and SpriteCollab contributions that are excluded from the MIT code license; reads session busy state and message-complete/tool-start/tool-complete events read-only (other chats contribute only "a turn finished"), focuses the composer (caret only, no text) or reveals its own pane only on a user click or command, saves a PNG snapshot to your downloads only when you click Save a snapshot, and keeps companion state in plugin storage; no network or model calls.

Independent codebase, not derived from githermes.

entries.name: hermes-proactive-radar
entries.description: Proactive assistant: follows your mail, calendar, GitHub, scheduled jobs and your own chats with the agent as long-lived tasks (trips, purchases, work items, commitments), does the legwork itself and writes to you first, on the gateway platform you choose, only when something is yours to decide. Sending email always asks; paying, booking, deploying and merging never run on their own. Disclosure — runs a scheduler task inside the gateway and delegates bounded work to 'hermes chat --oneshot' child processes (2 at a time, 100 a day by default) whose finished sessions it archives in the host session store; reaches mail and calendar only through the MCP servers or command-line tools you configure (gws, gog, the google-workspace skill's own script) and GitHub through gh, each started with a minimal environment; with Gmail push enabled, listens on 127.0.0.1:8666 (token + Google OIDC) and forwards to a host webhook route; reads the host session store (state.db), cron job outputs and the host memory provider; replies you send to its notices are passed to the chat agent with a task brief; `hermes radar setup` writes its MCP allowlist into config.yaml only after you type yes; model fallback needs the llm.provider_override / llm.model_override capabilities Hermes asks you to grant; stores tasks, bounded snippets, facts, a consent key and an audit log in HERMES_HOME/radar/ with retention limits; two optional secrets read through the host secret scope; installed disabled and in shadow mode; no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-project-stewardship

entries.name: hermes-proton
entries.description: Proton Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Drive for a Hermes Agent, through an MIT-licensed client built from Proton's own open-source Go libraries (go-srp, go-proton-api) — no Proton Bridge and no paid plan. Reads, searches and sends mail (attachments, scheduled send, labels, folders), manages calendar events and RSVPs, contacts (signed/encrypted vCards), and Drive (upload, download, move, rename, trash, public share links). Sign-in runs in a terminal via `hermes proton login` and the account password is never taken through chat; sending is refused until a recipient allowlist is set and every send is gated by Hermes's pre_tool_call approval. Disclosure — talks to Proton's private, undocumented web API over the network; stores a per-account session file (0600) holding OAuth-style tokens and the derived key passphrase (never the password) under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first load copies any sessions from the standalone client's `~/.config/protonlite` into it; reads local files you approve for attachments and Drive uploads and writes downloaded attachments and Drive files under that plugin-data folder; shells out to gpg for calendar/Drive key provisioning; `proton_schedule_followup` creates one-shot Hermes cron jobs (read-only Proton toolset) that run unattended and deliver to your home channel; no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-pushover-deliverables
entries.description: Pushover deliverables for Hermes Agent (send-only). Registers four severity-tiered cron delivery platforms — pushover-quiet, pushover-normal, pushover-high and pushover-critical (emergency: repeats until acknowledged), so a cron job picks an intent with a plain deliver=pushover-<severity> — and a pushover_send_file agent tool that delivers an image as a real Pushover attachment (png/jpeg/gif, 5 MB, magic-byte verified against the 5,242,880-byte limit), returning the Pushover request id and, at emergency priority, the receipt id needed to cancel the repeating alert. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests only to api.pushover.net carrying your Pushover app token, user key, message text and, through pushover_send_file, the bytes of the one png/jpeg/gif file the agent points it at (up to 5 MB); the pushover-critical target and priority 2 send emergency alerts that repeat on your devices until acknowledged or expired (default one hour); credentials are read only through Hermes's scoped secret route; writes nothing to disk and runs no background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-quest
entries.description: Read-only pixel-art RPG view of real Hermes Kanban and worker activity, with a live web dashboard tab and an optional native Desktop page. The Desktop page currently supports explicit local connections only; registry and SSH remote connections fail closed until a public SDK connection-lifecycle hook is available. Standalone demo data is synthetic. Disclosure — reads local Hermes data outside its own directory (kanban.db, every profile's state.db, profile.yaml, config.yaml model/effort, logs/agent.log, bot-status.json) on each dashboard poll: every /replay or /events request (about every 10 s while the tab is open) runs the bundled Python extractor as a subprocess (argument list, no shell, 30 s timeout); a background thread samples bot-status.json every 30 s (HERMES_QUEST_SAMPLER=off disables it) and writes bot-status history, checkpoint state, a lock and a random 0600 HMAC key under <hermes_home>/hermes-quest/ (not yet plugin-data); profile names and task titles are hidden unless enabled and only shown to host-authenticated dashboard sessions; the Desktop page works only on an explicit local connection; no network calls beyond the local Hermes backend.

entries.description: Codex-style quote cards for Hermes Desktop: select text outside an input and press Add to chat; the excerpt becomes a removable card above the composer while your question stays a separate draft. On send the quotes are prepended once as Markdown blockquotes (composer.middleware). Quotes are scoped per chat, several can be collected and removed one by one, a busy-agent send goes through host.composer.submit with the quote attached, and a rejected send gives the quote back. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, Python middleware or env vars. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; adds its own button element to document.body; reads the live draft through host.composer.getDraft; keeps quotes in memory only. No network calls, no credentials, no files, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-r0b0t-vibecad
entries.description: Profile-driven FDM CAD: executes trusted build123d workspace models or prepares a local single-shell STL, checks printer fit, renders depth-tested full and detail views, and writes geometry handoffs. Bambu adapters cover X2D and P2S; native process projects, live AMS binding and print dispatch are not produced. Meshy is an optional separate plugin; its paid service calls are not made by vibeCAD. CAD libraries require a separately bootstrapped Python 3.12/3.13 environment. Disclosure: reads/writes workspace files and runs trusted Python in a local subprocess. Agent execution requires approval of the final script path and bytes; direct runtime calls bypass the agent gate. The subprocess environment is minimized, not a sandbox: approved code can access files, credentials and the network. Approval binds only the top-level script. Internal Hermes approval and interrupt APIs may change and produce catalog rule 9 warnings. The plugin itself makes no runtime network calls or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-regress
entries.description: Regression tests built from your own sessions. Capture is passive: every finished turn is written as a plain JSON case holding the prompt, the model, each tool call with its exact arguments and the output it returned. Replay a case through the real agent loop with every tool call vetoed at pre_tool_call and answered from the recording, so a model, provider or config change can be measured without side effects — /regress run --model X reports pass, drift, regressed and error per case, with markdown, JUnit XML and a hash-chained export bundle for CI. Fixtures match only on identical tool and arguments; a case whose tool plan cannot be reproduced is reported as a gap instead of being answered from the wrong recording, and a replay window that never reaches the hook is marked error and stops the run rather than executing live tools. Disclosure — writes captured cases under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-regress/ (mode 0600) with the prompt, answer, tool arguments and tool results all passed through redaction first (provider keys, GitHub/Slack/AWS tokens, JWTs and inline password/token values become [REDACTED], counts recorded per case); keeps replay state in the same directory (armed.json plus an audit line per armed tool call in hook.log), scopes the replay veto to the single session that claims the armed case (only a first turn whose message exactly matches the recorded prompt can claim it, recorded from pre_llm_call), keeps that scope through a mid-turn context compression by matching the claimed task id as well as the session id, and serialises claims with a file lock, so an unclaimed window serves and blocks nobody, a late claim cannot revive a disarmed window, and other chats and cron runs are never affected, and runs the local hermes CLI as a subprocess when you ask for a replay; no network calls of its own, no telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-reliability
entries.description: Architecture-aware reliability testing for agent repositories: discover real usage datasets, generate scenarios, review them independently, execute configured targets and inspect evidence in Hermes web and Desktop dashboards. Freeze audited benchmarks and compare regressions across code changes, with baseline references for native Hermes memory. Disclosure — Sends source excerpts from the repository you point it at and sampled public dataset messages to your active Hermes model, queries huggingface.co and zenodo.org (HF_TOKEN only to Hugging Face), clones the supplied HTTPS repositories into profile plugin data, and starts a detached background worker per campaign; execution is off by default, and when enabled and approved through Hermes' prompt it runs generated evaluator tests, model-authored reference actions and the target agent (a cloned Hermes) on this host outside any sandbox, sending the target API key to your configured target base_url, while OpenHands/DeerFlow targets run in a network-disabled Docker image you build.
entries.title: Reliability Lab
known_issues: The Hermes target adapter uses version-sensitive runtime interfaces in separate evaluation workers; compatibility warnings and tested revisions are documented.
End-to-end workflows are verified with deterministic models. Live Command A target smoke and Muse scenario generation/preflight passed; a complete autonomous live campaign remains unverified.

Disclosure — Sends source excerpts from the repository you point it at and sampled public dataset messages to your active Hermes model, queries huggingface.co and zenodo.org (HF_TOKEN only to Hugging Face), clones the supplied HTTPS repositories into profile plugin data, and starts a detached background worker per campaign; execution is off by default, and when enabled and approved through Hermes' prompt it runs generated evaluator tests, model-authored reference actions and the target agent (a cloned Hermes) on this host outside any sandbox, sending the target API key to your configured target base_url, while OpenHands/DeerFlow targets run in a network-disabled Docker image you build. This plugin registers tool(s): reliability_start, reliability_status, reliability_stop, reliability_evidence, reliability_history, reliability_freeze, reliability_compare, reliability_memory; hook(s): pre_tool_call; requires env var(s): HF_TOKEN, RELIABILITY_TARGET_API_KEY. Platforms: linux. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5. Known issues: The Hermes target adapter uses version-sensitive runtime interfaces in separate evaluation workers; compatibility warnings and tested revisions are documented.; End-to-end workflows are verified with deterministic models. Live Command A target smoke and Muse scenario generation/preflight passed; a complete autonomous live campaign remains unverified..

entries.name: hermes-remote-hands
entries.description: One Hermes brain on a server, hands on your own Mac. Over plain OpenSSH (e.g. on a tailnet), with no agent, memory or model on the Mac, it adds six tools: mac_computer_use drives the Mac's screen with the same actions, element indices, hard blocks and verify ladder as the built-in computer_use (through cua-driver, in the background), while computer_use keeps driving the server's own screen in the same chat; mac_shell runs commands; mac_file, mac_patch and mac_search read, edit and search code; mac_process runs dev servers in a private tmux server. Disclosure — runs commands, reads and writes files, takes screenshots and sends input on the Mac named by the ssh_host setting, using the system ssh client and the key named in your SSH config (the plugin never reads, stores or copies keys). Every call goes through Hermes's approval gate with its own mac_* keys: commands, typed text and set_value are approved per exact text by default; credential stores, startup files, LaunchAgents, writes into .git or outside the configured project folders, and sensitive commands prompt every time; a pre_tool_call hook sends other tools' calls that mention the Mac or this plugin's code to a single-use approval; unattended runs fail closed (all of this while Hermes approvals are on, not in YOLO mode). No third-party network calls or telemetry. Background processes: an SSH ControlMaster for up to 30 s after the last call (socket under $HERMES_HOME/cache/ssh), one `ssh … cua-driver mcp` session per chat while mac_computer_use is in use, and mac_process jobs in `tmux -L hermes` on the Mac.
entries.title: Hermes Remote Hands
known_issues: Uses private Hermes internals (tools.computer_use tool/schema/cua_backend/cua_backend_session, tools.approval.request_tool_approval and check_all_command_guards) so mac_computer_use behaves exactly like computer_use. It checks them before use and fails closed with a clear message if a release renames one; re-run the plugin's self-tests after updating Hermes.

The Mac needs Remote Login, Command Line Tools (python3, used to resolve paths safely), tmux and ripgrep; projects under ~/Documents, ~/Desktop or ~/Downloads also need 'Allow full disk access for remote users'. Screen control needs cua-driver (verified 0.44.0; other versions log a warning) with its permissions granted at the Mac.
The tools appear only after the ssh_host and home settings are set. The Mac must be awake and unlocked for screen control; there is no detection of the user typing at the same moment.

entries.name: hermes-rescue
entries.description: Keeps your agent from breaking Hermes, and says what really went wrong. Refuses agent tool calls that would delete or hand-edit Hermes's own data (sessions, state.db, memories, skills, settings, profiles, keys) and names the supported command instead; sends edits to settings, SOUL.md or memory files to Hermes's approval prompt with a snapshot first (/rescue undo); and when a reply fails or quietly comes from a backup, adds one plain line per attempt with the real cause and the fix (NousResearch/hermes-agent#144562, #147620). /rescue in every surface, plus a Desktop status chip and pane. Disclosure — reads tool-call arguments (command, path, code) to decide; writes plugin-data/hermes-rescue/rescue.db (event kind, short description, up to 200 characters of the command, provider/model/status of failed model calls, Rescue's explanation; about 2,000 events kept); copies files a risky change would touch (config.yaml, SOUL.md, memories/, skills/, cron/, plugins/, state.db up to 300 MB) into plugin-data/hermes-rescue/snapshots/ before the change (newest 30 kept, so up to 30 state.db copies on disk) and writes them back on /rescue undo (for state.db only missing conversations come back, through Hermes's SessionDB export_session/import_sessions; folders are merged; only inside the Hermes folders); never opens, copies, moves or overwrites .env, auth.json or the other credential stores Hermes lists; after a failed model call that ends a turn, a short-lived background thread posts the note to the same conversation with ctx.post_message and edits it if a later attempt answers; never auto-approves (in YOLO mode Hermes itself approves the ask-first edits).
entries.title: Rescue
known_issues: The shell check follows quotes, comments, here-documents, $(…), globs, braces, cd/env -C, bash -c, xargs and find patterns (a find -regex on Hermes's folders always counts; the pattern is never run); it does not expand aliases or the scripts a command calls.
Python passed to execute_code is checked by pattern only, so Rescue asks the human there rather than blocking.
On Windows, PowerShell and cmd commands are read for deletes, moves, copies and writes; longer PowerShell scripts with their own logic are not followed.

/rescue undo for state.db only brings back missing conversations (through Hermes's own import); a conversation still there but missing messages is reported, not overwritten; the full copy stays in the snapshot.
In YOLO mode or with approvals off, Hermes approves Rescue's ask-first edits itself; the snapshot is still saved, so /rescue undo still works.
In the classic CLI without the gateway, a failed-turn note is only kept in /rescue log.

entries.name: hermes-resetwatch
entries.description: Track subscription quotas and reset times in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Hermes Python interpreter located via HERMES_PYTHON / VIRTUAL_ENV / the parent process or the Hermes installer's managed venv (HERMES_HOME/installs). Every credential read is read-only and nothing is refreshed or stored: it reads provider API keys from the process environment, the Hermes .env (through Hermes's get_secret helper, else read directly), the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden_cache.json, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source, keyed by a hash of BW_SESSION, which is never sent) and Docker s6 container env files; Hermes's saved OAuth logins (the credential pool through Hermes's read_credential_pool helper, else auth.json directly, and HERMES_HOME/.anthropic_oauth.json; for Nous plans with usage windows, the saved Nous portal login through Hermes's stored_token_account_info helper, sent as it is to the Nous portal and never refreshed); and other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins: Claude Code (credentials file, macOS keychain or Windows Credential Manager), Codex, Cursor (macOS keychain and the IDE's state.vscdb, opened read-only), Kimi, Grok, ZCode and Command Code. For GitHub Copilot (on by default) it tries COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN (through Hermes get_secret, else the process environment), then the Copilot editor's apps.json / hosts.json, then runs gh auth token (prompts disabled, 3-second limit), trying each token in turn until GitHub accepts one. For Codex, a 401 or 403 is retried once with another saved login for the same account. It sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint, presenting the vendor client's identity headers where a private endpoint expects them (Claude Code and Codex CLI user agents, the Grok CLI client headers, and for Copilot the VS Code / Copilot Chat editor headers on api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, which GitHub does not document); environment variables such as GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL (honored only for https grok.com / x.ai hosts), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and GROK_HOME change which host or file it uses. Usage results are cached under HERMES_HOME/cache/resetwatch, never tokens. It exposes nothing to the model: it is a Desktop page only.

entries.name: hermes-roam
entries.description: Encrypted, host-scoped sync of the Hermes Agent home between your own machines: an AES-256-GCM sealed bundle of the shared home (config.yaml minus host-scoped keys, SOUL.md, memories, skills) is pushed to storage you own — an S3 or Cloudflare R2 bucket, a private git repository, or a local directory — and pulled back on another machine through a plan-first, journaled, backed-up, roll-back-able install. Secrets (.env, auth.json, API keys) never sync; pulls apply only on explicit user action (the agent cannot apply by default); conflicts are detected with a signed compare-and-swap head, never merged. Every pushed version stays recoverable (hermes roam history / restore). Works across profiles and bots: one store carries every profile (each profile's identity, SOUL, memories, skills and shared config), from any profile context; a profile can be excluded per device. Opt-in, off by default: a read-only, encrypted archive of session transcripts (exported with hermes sessions export --redact) that other devices can list and read, and cron job definitions (pulled jobs land paused until hermes cron resume). Disclosure — network calls only to the user-configured store (boto3 for S3/R2, the git CLI for the git backend) and only when a roam command, tool, slash verb or session hook actually runs; the git backend also runs git as local subprocesses with an allowlisted environment, the opt-in session archive runs hermes sessions export once per profile, and hermes roam auto runs hermes config set, all as bounded local subprocesses; the shared ROAM_ARCHIVE_KEY and S3 credentials come only through Hermes's secret scope, never from files; session hooks run bounded daemon threads; no telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Hermes Roam
known_issues: The git backend is unsuitable for large homes: git hosts cap file sizes (~100 MB per file on GitHub), so keep the shared home well under ~50 MB there and use the S3/R2 backend for larger homes.

entries.name: hermes-room
entries.description: Hermes Room washes untrusted web, email, file and tool output before Hermes reads it: deterministically, with model help for semantic attacks, and with receipts you can audit. Layer 1 (always, local, stdlib-only) strips zero-width/bidi/control characters, ANSI escapes and hidden-HTML payloads, and masks leaked secrets (AWS/GitHub/GitLab/Slack/OpenAI/Google keys, JWTs, private-key blocks, password=/secret= assignments). Layer 2 runs only when Layer 1 flags something: a host-model reviewer via ctx.llm.complete_structured, your active Hermes model - no provider/model override, no extra API key - 20s timeout, 800 tokens, fail-open to Layer 1. Every change yields a local JSONL Trust Receipt (SHA-256, rule IDs, counts, reviewer verdict, never raw content): trust_receipt shows what changed, trust_report exports Markdown. Disclosure - reads only tool-output text; no network beyond the user's own provider call via ctx.llm; no shell, no background processes, no telemetry; no credentials required (requires_env is empty); writes solely to <HERMES_HOME>/hermes-room/receipts.jsonl (hashes/counts only, local); fails open, never blocks or breaks the tool loop. Disclosure — rewrites the result of every tool (web, email, MCP, read_file, terminal, skills) before the model sees it: it strips hidden HTML/control characters, deletes phrases that look like injected instructions, masks secret-looking values and adds an `[UNTRUSTED ...]` header, so files read through it may differ from what is on disk; when a rule fires it sends up to 8,000 characters of the unmasked output to your active Hermes model for review (an extra model call, up to 20 s) and may replace the result with the reviewer's re-washed text; receipts in `<HERMES_HOME>/hermes-room/receipts.jsonl` hold hashes, rule IDs and counts plus the reviewer's verdict, quoted snippets and up to 2,000 characters of its reply; no other network, shell, background work or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-ros
entries.description: Drive and observe ROS / ROS 2 robots from Hermes over rosbridge: list topics, services and nodes, read odometry, grab camera frames for the vision model, publish, call services, drive and e-stop, with every tool call gated by a pre_tool_call safety interlock (speed and duration limits, optional geofence, topic and service write allowlists, a latching e-stop, every blocked call logged). Ships a built-in mock robot (2D sim with a camera and a red cone) so it runs with no ROS at all, a bundled safety skill, and an optional read-only dashboard tab. Disclosure — network: in rosbridge mode it opens one unencrypted websocket to the rosbridge server you configure (default localhost:9090), lazily on first use; mock mode (default) makes no network connections. Files: camera snapshots, a blocked-call audit log, the e-stop latch and the last pose under the plugin data dir. No credentials. One dependency, websocket-client (already in Hermes's lock). With a real robot attached the agent can physically move it; limits default to 0.5 m/s, 1.0 rad/s and 5 s per command and are enforced on this plugin's tools outside the model, but they do not stop other tools (terminal, code execution) from reaching the rosbridge server or changing the limits in config.yaml.

entries.description: Deterministic security middleware, EVM simulation guard, and prompt injection defense for on-chain agent actions. entries.name: hermes-salespilot
entries.description: An approval-gated sales desk inside Hermes: collect companies from quoted page evidence, qualify them against your ICP, draft the first email, and send one email only after you pick "send" in the host approval prompt — then keep a customer timeline, hot prospects and follow-up dates. Sends nothing on its own, and a refusal, bounce, do-not-contact or archive stops a draft that was written before it. Eleven salespilot_* tools plus a Desktop workspace (Customers, Hot Prospects, Settings, CSV import). Disclosure — fetches the public web pages you or the agent point it at (http/https only, private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses refused); network mail traffic goes only to the SMTP and IMAP servers you configure, with mailbox credentials from Hermes secrets (SALESPILOT_SMTP_USERNAME / SALESPILOT_SMTP_PASSWORD); each email is sent only after you choose "send" in the Hermes prompt (daily cap 5); lead data lives in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-salespilot/; no telemetry.
entries.title: SalesPilot
known_issues: One mailbox per Hermes profile: several brands share the profile's single SMTP login until Hermes exposes per-instance secrets.
Reply intent is keyword-based; a reply it cannot decide opens a review item instead of guessing.
CSV import only (no .xlsx parsing yet).

entries.name: hermes-sanctuary
entries.description: Watch your Hermes Agent work: five animated characters wake up when Hermes uses their tools, in two illustrated worlds (Olympus by default, the Clearing), in Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard, in English or French. The guard barks, with a bubble saying why, on tool and provider errors, silent fallbacks to a backup model, loops (same tool, same arguments, 4 times in a turn), heavy turns, a daily budget overrun and permissions waiting for an answer; a daily journal shows turns, tools, where the work came from, tokens and estimated cost per model hour by hour, with a shareable image of the day and a sped-up replay. Disclosure — observer hooks only (they never block, change or answer anything); records tool names, turn times, platform and scheduled-task names, counters, model names with token counts, the short description Hermes gives for a pending approval (never the command) and one-letter event codes with their time for the replay (never messages, arguments, results, error texts, file paths or ids) under plugin-data/hermes-sanctuary/, files older than 2 days removed; a hash of each tool call is kept in memory for the current turn only to spot loops; read-only dashboard routes serve that activity and the plugin's own theme and images; cost is estimated with Hermes's own agent.usage_pricing module (a private import the validator may warn on); no network calls of its own, no shell commands, no background process, no secrets or .env access, no telemetry and no self-updater; the panorama runs in a sandboxed frame that receives everything by postMessage; Hermes Desktop may show native notifications (at most one per kind every 2 minutes); the daily budget is stored by Hermes Desktop or the browser.
entries.title: Hermes Sanctuary
known_issues: Hermes Desktop connected to a remote Hermes does not install the pane by itself: use Capabilities, Plugins, Install from Git with Med34000/hermes-sanctuary/hermes-sanctuary (Force reinstall if the plugin is already on the server), then quit and reopen the app.

entries.name: hermes-screen
entries.description: Pick what to watch from your own Jellyfin library using real watch history, play movies and saved scenes on your Chromecast with receiver-verified status, send YouTube links to the TV, and play camera rock-paper-scissors against Hermes. Network calls: your Jellyfin server, your Chromecast (Cast protocol, TCP 8009), YouTube on the TV, www.gstatic.com (receiver SDK), your own optional game service, and optional YouTube Data API. Listeners: a temporary expiring movie relay while something plays, and an opt-in two-container game service you deploy yourself. No telemetry. Secrets only via Hermes; no .env reads. Camera frames never leave the phone. Disclosure — while something plays, tv_play opens a temporary listener on your configured cast_relay_bind that serves only the selected Jellyfin item at a random, expiring URL; anyone on your LAN who learns that URL can fetch that one item until it expires. The optional rock-paper-scissors service you deploy yourself runs behind a public Cloudflare quick tunnel.

entries.name: hermes-security-plugin
entries.description: Check the security headers of a public URL and look up sourced penetration testing provider data through two remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no keys): check_security_headers on penetrationtestservices.com, and list_providers and get_provider on pentestcompare.com. Bundles the check-security-headers workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; the URL you check is sent to penetrationtestservices.com, which fetches it with one GET per redirect. The pts server also has request_pentest, which sends a contact request to Excession Labs and needs an agent key the plugin does not hold. Both servers are marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before any call that is not read-only. The tool set is served by the remote servers at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: hermes-security
entries.description: Security review for a local repository. The agent builds a threat model, splits the code into chunks and reviews them with parallel subagents, checks each candidate against the code and traces whether an attacker can reach it. Reports keep evidence, rejected candidates and coverage gaps, export to Markdown, JSON, CSV and SARIF, and get a Security page in Hermes Desktop. Standard, deep and diff modes; `/security` slash command and `hermes security-review` CLI. Optional "Run tests to confirm findings" writes small reproductions and runs them in a temporary copy of the repository; testing a running app needs a per-scan grant (one origin, one hour, 200 requests) that agent tools cannot issue. Apache-2.0 (parts adapted from Apache-2.0 source, see NOTICE). Disclosure — the first scan downloads a pinned osv-scanner release from GitHub (about 55 MB, refused unless its SHA-256 matches) into the plugin data folder; package names and versions go to api.osv.dev and api.deps.dev, declared runtime versions to endoflife.date (`HERMES_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CHECK=off` disables this). Test confirmation runs repository code as your user in a temporary copy with credential-looking environment variables removed; that is not a sandbox. The configured model provider receives the code under review; scan data stays in the profile's plugin data folder. With `plugins.entries.hermes-security.allow_gateway_injection` turned on (off by default), the plugin queues one "Continue security scan" message into the chat when a scan stalls, at most 3 times without progress. No Python dependencies.

entries.name: hermes-sentinel
entries.description: Deterministic runtime circuit breaker and local execution auditor. Disclosure — blocks any turn whose new user message contains a credential-shaped string; refuses the third consecutive identical tool call (including legitimate repeated polls) until `/sentinel reset`; redacts credential-shaped text in every tool result and truncates each result to 4000 characters / 100 lines before the model sees it; stores audit events (redacted 200-char argument previews) in `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/hermes-sentinel/sentinel_audit.db`, falling back to memory-only or no auditing; no network calls, subprocesses or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-seo
entries.description: Native Hermes port of Claude SEO 2.4.2: 45 SEO workflow and specialist skills, a credential-scoped hermes_seo_run tool, an isolated Python runtime, and advisory JSON-LD feedback. Derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0). Disclosure — derived from Claude SEO 2.4.2 (MIT; FLOW prompt materials CC BY 4.0); the hermes_seo_run tool starts local subprocesses in the Hermes host process, not a Docker terminal sandbox, and model-supplied script arguments may name host paths, so it can read host files (the Gemini image-edit utility uploads the named file to Google, the IndexNow utility reads a URL-list file); `hermes seo setup` downloads Python packages from PyPI within version ranges into a private environment and optionally Chromium through Playwright; audits fetch user-selected websites; separately configured providers (Moz, Bing Webmaster, Keywords Everywhere, Google APIs, Matomo, DataForSEO, IndexNow, Google Gemini) receive the data sent to them and may incur charges; skills ask before paid or mutating calls but the tool does not enforce approvals; Gemini images are saved to ~/Documents/nanobanana_generated, and other runtime state stays in Hermes plugin data storage; provider keys are read from the active Hermes profile and passed only to the script that needs them; Google OAuth workflows are disabled; no telemetry, bundled credentials, background process or self-updater.

entries.name: hermes-shaperotator
entries.description: Parametric part and assembly design for Hermes in a real CAD program. One toolset drives FreeCAD (headless, cross-platform) or Autodesk Inventor (Windows, COM); every feature reports a volume/topology delta; FEA (FreeCAD FEM + Gmsh + CalculiX) reports equilibrium, mesh convergence and an AS/NZS-aware yield safety factor, and a design sweep finds the lightest part meeting a target SF; drawings on both backends to the standard the user picks once per chat (AS 1100, ISO, ASME, DIN, BS 8888, JIS, GB), with PDF export gated on a QA check. Desktop pane: live 3D view, click a face to reference it in chat, stress map, evidence log. On Inventor, cad_native exposes 200+ inventor-forge tools (sheet metal + flat-pattern DXF, assemblies, interference, BOM, materials, mass properties, stress/modal analysis in Inventor's own Stress Analysis feeding the same evidence log). Any stress, deflection, safety factor or mass the agent quotes is checked against the analyses it actually ran, and a verification footer is appended to the reply. Disclosure — starts FreeCAD's Python as a worker process (which runs Gmsh and CalculiX) and, on Windows, can drive Autodesk Inventor over COM; cad_python runs Python inside the CAD app only after the user approves each call; reads files the user names; writes models, renders, FEA folders and exports in the session's job folder, and any write outside it (a save over a file opened from elsewhere, changed parts an assembly save also writes) goes through a Hermes approval prompt naming the path, enforced by inventor-forge at each write (Inventor's own stress-analysis reports and solver scratch go to its working folders); Inventor runs as a separate instance per chat, closed when the chat ends (left open and shown if it has unsaved work); child processes (FreeCAD worker, MCP servers, headless browser for the PDF report) get a minimal environment without provider keys; appends a verification footer to assistant replies that quote engineering figures; Inventor stress/modal analysis (no API exists) takes over the mouse and keyboard for about half a minute, only after the user approves each call; network only when the user approves installing a CAD program's add-on: Inventor's add-on, inventor-forge (MIT, same author), is pip-installed into its own environment under the plugin data folder from GitHub at the commit pinned in backends/known.json (archive checked by sha256 when git is absent) plus pywin32 from PyPI, and then runs as a child MCP server while Inventor is in use; nothing updates itself; no telemetry or credentials.

On Inventor, cad_native exposes 200+ inventor-forge tools (sheet metal + flat-pattern DXF, assemblies, interference, BOM, materials, mass properties, stress/modal analysis in Inventor's own Stress Analysis feeding the same evidence log). Any stress, deflection, safety factor or mass the agent quotes is checked against the analyses it actually ran, and a verification footer is appended to the reply. Disclosure — starts FreeCAD's Python as a worker process (which runs Gmsh and CalculiX) and, on Windows, can drive Autodesk Inventor over COM; cad_python runs Python inside the CAD app only after the user approves each call; reads files the user names; writes models, renders, FEA folders and exports in the session's job folder, and any write outside it (a save over a file opened from elsewhere, changed parts an assembly save also writes) goes through a Hermes approval prompt naming the path, enforced by inventor-forge at each write (Inventor's own stress-analysis reports and solver scratch go to its working folders); Inventor runs as a separate instance per chat, closed when the chat ends (left open and shown if it has unsaved work); child processes (FreeCAD worker, MCP servers, headless browser for the PDF report) get a minimal environment without provider keys; appends a verification footer to assistant replies that quote engineering figures; Inventor stress/modal analysis (no API exists) takes over the mouse and keyboard for about half a minute, only after the user approves each call; network only when the user approves installing a CAD program's add-on: Inventor's add-on, inventor-forge (MIT, same author), is pip-installed into its own environment under the plugin data folder from GitHub at the commit pinned in backends/known.json (archive checked by sha256 when git is absent) plus pywin32 from PyPI, and then runs as a child MCP server while Inventor is in use; nothing updates itself; no telemetry or credentials. Platforms: windows, linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7.

entries.name: hermes-shortcuts
entries.description: Share to Hermes from any iPhone or Android app, ask Hermes with Siri and hear the answer, or photograph a receipt, whiteboard or document as a task. iOS Shortcuts and Android HTTP Shortcuts call one token-protected endpoint; replies return in the HTTP response and are forwarded to your Telegram home channel (a Siri question only when it says "save the answer" or times out). Setup is three steps: `hermes shortcuts pair` prints a QR code, the iPhone "Hermes Setup" shortcut scans it into iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/hermes.json, and the shared shortcuts (which contain no token) read it. Disclosure: off until SHORTCUTS_TOKEN (32+ random chars; weak or placeholder tokens are refused) is set and the plugin is enabled; then the gateway runs an HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8645 (non-loopback bind needs SHORTCUTS_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND=true) that you expose through your own HTTPS tunnel or proxy. A single bearer token is the only authentication and every request acts as the owner. Requests run agent turns on shared, untrusted content; by default each action gets only the toolsets it needs (web, vision, plus memory for remember and cronjob for remind/ask; events get cronjob/todo only; no terminal, file, code execution, browser or MCP servers), enforced by toolsets_for_source and by a pre_tool_call hook that only acts in shortcuts sessions: it blocks any other tool, limits cronjob to create/list and makes created reminder jobs run once with no tools. `@file:`/`@url:`-style references in shared text are defanged (Hermes core would otherwise inline local files before the agent runs). Forwarded replies show URLs as code (no Telegram link previews). SHORTCUTS_TOOL_PROFILE=full opts into the platform's full toolset (then shared content can reach the terminal, directly or through cron jobs). Approvals are not bypassed. Uploads are cached in Hermes' media cache; sessions are stored in Hermes' session database; replies are sent to the configured platform's home channel. Registers the CLI command `hermes shortcuts pair`, which prints a QR code containing the server URL and SHORTCUTS_TOKEN (optional 0600 PNG; token text only with --show-token) and may query the local cloudflared metrics endpoint on 127.0.0.1:20241-20245 to find a quick-tunnel URL. On the phone the token is stored in plain text in iCloud Drive/Shortcuts/hermes.json (synced to iCloud; end-to-end encrypted only with Advanced Data Protection) or, with manual setup, inside the shortcut.
entries.title: Hermes Shortcuts (Share Sheet, Siri, Photo)
known_issues: Needs an HTTPS tunnel or reverse proxy (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, Caddy) for the phone to reach the loopback listener.
No approval buttons on this surface: commands that need approval fail or time out; use Telegram for those.
HEIC photos are rejected; the recipes convert to JPEG first.

Prompt injection in shared pages or files cannot be fully prevented by fencing; the default safe tool profile limits what it can do. `remember` stores shared content in long-term memory, which every later session (including full-tool ones) sees; use it only on content you trust.
Every shortcuts turn sees your memory/user profile like any session; a malicious page could try to make the agent put that text into a web_extract URL.

entries.name: hermes-skill-router
entries.description: Removes the always-on skill catalog from every Chat Completions request and injects a short fused shortlist instead. Ranks partly by the skills you loaded for similar prompts in past sessions. Disclosure — On Chat Completions requests this plugin removes Hermes's skill catalog from the system prompt and appends a per-turn skill shortlist as a trailing system message. Your newest message, plus up to 10,000 characters of your earlier messages, is sent to the embeddings and rerank endpoints you configure (loopback by default; any non-loopback host must use https). The query text is written to the plugin log. Its index, skill path cache, display record and learned-association database live under ~/.cache/hermes-skill-router, shared by every profile. A background heal, or the optional association backfill command, reads ~/.hermes/state.db read-only and stores normalised prompt terms. The optional interactive setup command downloads both default models from Hugging Face and starts the bundled embeddings and decider rerank servers, installing systemd user units on Linux; it runs only when you start it.

entries.name: hermes-slots
entries.description: A grimy little slot machine pet for Hermes Desktop, drawn as low-resolution pixel art. It sits in the bottom right corner above the app, like the Hermes pet, takes no layout space and can be dragged anywhere. Drag its lever down and let go, or click the machine, to spin a five by three screen for play coins. Three in a line pays across, down or diagonally on 20 lines, so about three pulls in four pay something, and a line of sevens pays 100 times the bet. Bet any whole number of coins. A piggy bank beside it keeps coins safe and pays 1% interest an hour, worked out from saved timestamps, and its panel also holds the pay table and the sound switch. Reachable from the status bar, the command palette and the keyboard. Disclosure: coins are play money inside the plugin and cannot be bought, sold or cashed out; no network requests, no model calls and no background processes; spins use the browser's random numbers and the published pay table; sound effects are CC0 clips by Kenney built into the bundle, played only after a click or key press; the game is kept in Desktop plugin storage on this machine; the plugin adds its own floating element to the page (Hermes has no SDK area for one) and removes it on unload, without reading or changing core markup.
entries.title: Slot Pet
known_issues: The machine's first position is the bottom right corner, the same place Hermes Plant starts. With both installed, drag one aside; each remembers where it was put.
