entries.name: hermes-snitchboard
entries.description: A dashboard tab that turns OpenSnitch connection evidence into plain-language findings mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, with a hash chain that makes alteration of stored history detectable. Hermes can tell you what it did and application-layer tooling can record which model requests it made; neither tells you what the machine actually connected to. The tab answers that from the firewall's own record of outbound connections and the process behind each one. It shows a summary of connections, denials, unique processes and destinations, AI traffic and unattributed traffic; an hourly coverage strip that renders a missing hour as a gap rather than as a quiet hour; findings carrying severity, confidence, the ATT&CK technique and tactic, the literal records behind the finding and one concrete next step; regular-interval destinations stated with both the benign and the malicious reading, with services on the configured expected list labelled rather than flagged; novel destinations ranked by rarity against prior runs; activity by AI process and by configured agent account; a per-run connection chart with a run that collected nothing drawn as a marked gap instead of a zero; byte volume where the firewall's connection tracking measured it; the daemon's reported state, the rules in force and open sockets; and an integrity panel that recomputes every link on request. Addresses, host names, hardware addresses, home directories and process arguments are masked by default, a deliberate control reveals them, and that control can be switched off entirely in settings. Until real runs exist the tab shows clearly labelled demonstration records built from addresses reserved for documentation (RFC 5737, RFC 3849, RFC 2606), so every panel is visible without installing OpenSnitch. Collection and viewing are kept apart on purpose: the half that runs inside Hermes never opens the firewall database, and the optional reference collector is run by the machine owner's own account, never by Hermes, which suits setups where Hermes runs under a different account from the person who owns the machine. The integrity claim is scoped deliberately: the chain attests to the order of stored records and to the digest each full record held when it was sealed, so a record that has since been trimmed keeps a shortened summary the chain does not cover, and that summary is a derived analysis aid rather than evidence. The chain makes alteration detectable; it does not prove what the network did, and anyone able to rewrite every record could recompute it. Disclosure - registers no tools, no hooks and no middleware, and needs no environment variable. Its only surface is the dashboard tab and seven GET routes served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/hermes-snitchboard/ (health, settings, runs, runs/latest, runs/{run_id}, series, verify), which require the dashboard's auth ticket. It writes nothing to disk at all. It makes no network request, opens no socket, loads no external font, script or image, executes no subprocess, no shell command and no systemd unit, starts no background process, holds no credential and no OAuth client, and sends no telemetry. It reads three things: the run records in the directory named by its runs_dir setting, which may sit outside the plugin's own data directory and which the operator chooses; a settings.json in its plugin data directory when Hermes's own settings are unavailable; and the plugin's settings from Hermes configuration through the read-only helper hermes_cli.config.load_config_readonly, with plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir for the data path. Both of those imports are guarded and fall back rather than raise. Record files are opened with O_NOFOLLOW, symbolic links in the runs directory are skipped so nothing outside it can be reached through one, no value supplied by a client ever reaches the filesystem as a path, a file is never read past the schema's size cap, and every response is bounded in both row count and serialised bytes. Record data is rendered through React element construction with no innerHTML anywhere, because process and host names from the firewall flow through that code. Python standard library only; FastAPI comes from Hermes and no third-party package is added.
entries.title: Hermes Snitchboard
known_issues: The analysis thresholds in snitchboard/config.py (beacon window and jitter bands, novelty depth, coverage tolerance, transfer thresholds, detection and aggregate caps) carry their defaults in this release. Only the twelve settings declared in plugin.yaml reach the plugin from Hermes configuration, so a threshold placed in the configuration file is dropped without warning rather than applied.
Developed and verified on Hermes Agent v0.23.0 on Fedora Linux with plugins.isolation: host. The same code runs elsewhere but no other platform or isolation mode was exercised.

Chain verification carries a 40-second budget so it stays inside the plugin host's 60-second response ceiling. On a very large history it reports that verification did not complete and gives no verdict, rather than returning a partial one.

A trimmed record keeps a shortened summary that the chain does not cover. The chain still attests to that record's position and to the digest its full form held when sealed, so the integrity panel reports how many links rest on sealed digests.

The reference collector supplies no byte counts, because the OpenSnitch database holds none, so any record it produces reports volume as unavailable. The demonstration records carry byte counts, so that panel is populated in demonstration mode only.
Account names appear in clear while home paths are masked. Masking them reaches finding text and evidence lines as well as the tables, so it is recorded as a v0.2.0 item rather than done late.
The reference collector reads connection times as naive local strings, so it must run in the same time zone as the firewall interface. The hour repeated when clocks go back is ambiguous.
OpenSnitch records connections only while its own interface is running, and its purge setting removes old rows. Both show as gaps or as runs marked no_data, never as an all-clear.

aggregates.total_connections and aggregates.dropped hold the window's counts in a collected record but repeat the daemon's lifetime counters in a demonstration record. Giving them a single meaning is a v0.2.0 item.

entries.name: hermes-standing
entries.description: Earned trust for Hermes workers. Each profile has a level (L0 read, L1 draft, L2 act, L3 trusted) that decides which tool calls need the owner's approval, and a local record of checks that held up and checks that did not. A worker can always report on its own card (block, comment, request review, heartbeat), but it cannot mark the task done on its word: kanban_complete is blocked until the task has a passing standing_proof in the same session, and Standing runs that check itself (owner-scoped file, owner-allowlisted HTTP URL, or exact owner-allowlisted read-only command). Ten clean passes raise a level (capped at L1 automatically; L2 needs the owner's explicit opt-in); one failed check lowers it; a check that could not run is logged as unavailable and changes nothing. Seeds only create new actors, so restarts never undo a demotion. /standing shows the record, /standing log the last events, and /standing set (local owner only) changes a level. Optional same-machine shared ledger for a governor and its workers, and a short score line on the task card after a completion or demotion. Disclosure — pre_tool_call returns Hermes' own approve directive for every tool call outside the profile's level (at the default L1 that includes every terminal/shell, send and unknown-tool call) and blocks kanban_complete until a Standing proof passes in the same session; a worker's block/comment/review/heartbeat calls on its own assigned card skip the Standing prompt; under cron and other unattended runs Hermes' approval policy (default deny) decides; it adds a guidance note to the model context through pre_llm_call; it never auto-approves or calls a model, and makes network or subprocess calls only for owner-scoped proofs (HTTP GET with no redirects, proxies or credentials; exact allowlisted argv, shell=False, minimal environment); it stores actors and hashed proof events in SQLite under its plugin data directory (or an owner-set db_path) and, when card_line is on, posts task-card comments through the public kanban_comment tool.
entries.title: Standing
known_issues: A passing check proves only what it checks. Standing does not judge whether the whole deliverable is right; choose meaningful checks.
Not a sandbox. Other internal hook errors fail open (logged, no directive); only the completion proof check fails closed.
At L2, shell and unknown tools run without a Standing prompt so proven unattended workers can work; recognized spend and delete/move calls still ask below L3.
Sandboxed workers cannot use host file proofs; use owner-allowlisted HTTP or command proofs instead.
Command proofs are POSIX only (Linux, macOS).

entries.name: hermes-stt-enhance
entries.description: Local speech-to-text (provider stt_enhance) with faster-whisper or opt-in sherpa-onnx Parakeet V3 and long-audio chunking, plus an optional bounded LLM pass that enhances the transcript using a custom skill, an inline prompt or the default, and keeps the raw transcript on failure. entries.name: hermes-studiotwin
entries.description: StudioTwin cloud images, environments, PBR materials, meshes, rigs, motion, sound effects and Concepts via remote MCP, with an optional Desktop media workspace. Disclosure — Sends prompts and any media you upload to StudioTwin (api.studiotwin.ai; uploads and downloads via StudioTwin's Amazon S3 and assets.studiotwin.ai) with your StudioTwin API key, and StudioTwin passes jobs to its own model providers. Generation spends StudioTwin wallet credits with no plugin spend cap; paid, upload, cancel and delete tools go through Hermes approval. The optional Desktop backend can read media-type files anywhere in your home folder (except hidden folders) for its viewers and stores downloads in its plugin-data folder. entries.title: StudioTwin
known_issues: A StudioTwin account, API key and wallet credits are required for cloud generation; prompts and authorized input media are sent to StudioTwin and its selected providers.
Paid tools use Hermes native approval. Obtain a fresh estimate for variable costs; the plugin imposes no session spend cap.
Full Desktop UI requires compatible Hermes SDK surfaces and separate Desktop enablement; remote setups need the UI installed on the client and the package and key on the backend.

Optional local processing requires backend-local Blender 4.2+, ffmpeg/ffprobe, or Node.js 22+ and Chrome/Chromium as applicable; render helpers disable Chromium's sandbox, so use trusted inputs or a separately isolated environment.

Read-only job, asset and Concept metadata replaces oversized non-URL input strings (16 KiB each; 64 KiB shared inputs budget) with a notice; malformed or excessive metadata still fails closed. Binary download limits are unchanged.

entries.name: hermes-superagent
entries.description: A resident router that dispatches and never executes, isolated workers that report only to it, team-written trigger rules, and an external watchdog that checks real progress and goal drift, plus an item ledger that keeps every task, issue and Claude Code session your sources show until it's confirmed closed. Disclosure — spawns long-running worker processes from the argv you configure, runs the outbound send, heartbeat and connector commands you configure, which read sources into its ledger, including a read-only session probe sent through the host command you configure, and, only when relaunch is turned on, types one short nudge into a stopped Claude Code session's terminal, stops or restarts its own workers, and spends tokens on the profile's model during ticks and when it writes a worker brief; on a profile set to router it drops every chat message whose sender is not on its allow list, and a webhook event from an allow-listed author starts a worker directly; the send and heartbeat commands run with the full Hermes environment. Writes its database and worker directories under the configured home, and its optional Claude Code hook logs session events to ~/.superagent/sessions. Its hooks stay inert until a profile sets a role.

entries.name: hermes-switchyard

entries.name: hermes-sysadmin
entries.description: Windows and Active Directory RMM for Hermes Agent and Hermes Desktop: users, groups and lockouts, Group Policy, RDP, Windows Server Backup, a desktop fleet and 231 vetted PowerShell scripts, all behind tiered approvals with a preview before every change, protected objects and a local audit log. Disclosure — runs PowerShell on the Hermes machine (local transport on a domain-joined Windows host, optionally as a configured account via runas /netonly) or over WinRM to one configured jump host, and from there talks to your domain controllers and the computers you target (AD, SMB, RPC, WinRM). Reads the account password only through Hermes secret scope. While the dashboard is open a background collector in the gateway refreshes read-only snapshots (setting background_collector turns it off); scheduled monitoring adds a Hermes cron job (and two launcher scripts in the Hermes scripts folder) only when you turn it on, and a cron run cannot create or remove it unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true. In permissive mode standard writes run without an approval prompt. Writes a local SQLite audit log with passwords redacted. Never reads .env or any other credential store; the opt-in monitoring cron script gets the password only if the user lists SYSADMIN_WINRM_PASSWORD in terminal.env_passthrough. No telemetry and no other network calls; the raw PowerShell tool is off by default.

entries.name: hermes-t3sidebar
entries.description: T3 Code-style session sidebar for Hermes Desktop: Input/Done/Woke badges, Pinned/Working/Snoozed/Archived shelves, unsent drafts synced across Desktops, project picker and filter, AutoTitler rename, a token/cost Usage page, and a Codex/Claude Limits page that pools accounts by plan, forecasts run-outs and wasted quota, and redeems banked Codex resets. Disclosure — The Limits page reads Hermes's credential pool and, every 5 minutes, fetches rate limits for every openai-codex and anthropic pool account with that account's own token through Hermes's read-only usage fetch (chatgpt.com, api.anthropic.com). At most hourly it lists the active Codex sign-in's banked reset credits through Hermes's signed request, and a user-confirmed button redeems one banked Codex reset. When the anthropic pool is empty it reads Claude Code's login ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude/.credentials.json) and sends that token to api.anthropic.com (/api/oauth/usage, /api/oauth/profile). An expired login is refreshed by Hermes's Claude Code resolver, which writes the new token pair back to that file. Unsent composer drafts (text and folder) are stored in the plugin's data on the Hermes host and synced to every connected Desktop. A resumed turn un-archives its session's compression lineage in state.db. The backend reads private Hermes internals (live session registry, session DB and pool-routing helpers) and can break on a Hermes update.
entries.title: T3 Sidebar
known_issues: Limits page: the backend samples every openai-codex and anthropic pool account every 5 minutes with each account's own token from Hermes's pool, through Hermes's read-only usage fetch (no refresh on 401). At most hourly it lists the banked reset credits of the Codex account Hermes currently uses, sent by Hermes with its own sign-in. No token is stored or logged.

Limits page: when Hermes's anthropic pool is empty, it reads Claude Code's login ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude/.credentials.json) to show that account's limits and plan (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /api/oauth/profile). An expired token is refreshed by Hermes's own Claude Code resolver, reached through Hermes's public usage fetch, which writes it back for Claude Code.

Unsent draft text, with its session's folder, is stored in the plugin's own data on the Hermes host so every Desktop connected to it can restore the draft; a cleared draft leaves a marker without text for 30 days.

The backend uses Hermes internals (session DB, live session registry and mutation helpers, pool account routing helpers); a Hermes release that moves them can break the sidebar, Usage or Limits page until the plugin is updated.

entries.name: hermes-tabs
entries.description: Settings page (in the language set in Hermes, nine languages; incl. which browser Hermes works in and its safety level; loosening must be confirmed in the browser) and guard rails for hermes-tabs, which lets Hermes work in individual tabs of your real, signed-in Chromium browser through an extension and an MCP relay. Disclosure — talks only to the hermes-tabs relay you configure (HERMES_TABS_RELAY, default 127.0.0.1:8766) with HERMES_TABS_ADMIN_TOKEN (paths /admin/settings and /admin/select, the latter picks the browser when several are connected); caches the last seen settings in plugin-data/hermes-tabs/settings.json and its own opt-in switch in plugin-data/hermes-tabs/options.json; the pre_tool_call hook rejects the tabs tools while switched off and, only if the user turns that switch on, blocked sites in Hermes' own browser tools and web_extract. No shell, no background processes, no telemetry.

known_issues: Needs the hermes-tabs relay and browser extension from the same repository, and the relay registered as the MCP server named tabs. The plugin alone does nothing.

entries.name: hermes-talk
entries.description: Realtime voice for Hermes through terminal, Discord, dashboard and Desktop. Disclosure — Realtime on the ChatGPT subscription uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed_provider_request (requires_auth: openai-codex); the plugin never reads, refreshes or holds a token. GPT-Live on the subscription (TALK_VOICE_MODE=live, TALK_LIVE_AUTH=subscription) starts one local `codex app-server` child per call on the Codex CLI's own login (API-key variables removed from its environment); that call uses the undocumented chatgpt.com Codex realtime endpoint, which is outside the vendor's published API terms and may change or stop working without notice. The app-server's Codex thread is ephemeral and fenced (no environment, read-only sandbox, approvals declined, apps, shell, web search, plugins, sub-agents and each configured MCP server disabled, replies only "skip"); Talk reads only the MCP server names to disable them, and each voice request costs one small Codex turn of subscription quota. Voice audio and conversation context go to the selected provider (OpenAI, xAI, Google, optionally ElevenLabs); on Desktop the voice model can list the profile's sessions, read their titles and recent messages, create sessions and queue or steer prompts into them without a per-action confirmation; spoken requests are handed to the user's Hermes agent, whose tools run under Hermes approvals. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-taskbar-badge
entries.description: Colour-coded badge on the Hermes taskbar button: a green disc for a turn finished in a session you have not opened, an amber ring while a session waits on an approval, a clarify or a password, a red triangle for a failure. Opening a session clears only that session; failure outranks waiting and waiting outranks finished. The settings page holds the three colours, a test button each, per-event overrides and a switch back to the plain grey count. Disclosure — Disclosure: the desktop half posts the current badge state to 127.0.0.1:8766 on the same machine once per event, and the Python half starts at plugin load in each Hermes process, listens on that loopback port (no token, CORS open to any origin, so any local program or open web page can also set or read the badge colour) and, from a background thread, calls the Windows taskbar overlay API or, on Linux, runs `gdbus emit` for the Unity launcher badge once a second while a badge is up; it writes `badge_bridge.log` in its plugin folder; nothing leaves the computer and no other network call is made. Where colour cannot be drawn, Chromium's grey count and the status-bar dot remain.

entries.name: hermes-teammates
entries.description: Give your agent a fixed team. You define each specialist's instructions, toolsets and model once, and the agent picks only a name: a reviewer limited to todo gets no built-in web, file or terminal tools, whatever the prompt says (built-in delegate_task children inherit the parent's toolsets). Teammates also works its own lane on Hermes' Kanban board inside the chat, where each card it finishes waits in Review, and keeps a per-profile ledger of every run's goal, status and result. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent_lifecycle API. Stock Hermes; no patched core. Disclosure — adds eight tools (teammates_roster, teammate_assign, teammate_request_changes, teammate_chain, teammate_check, teammate_wait, teammate_message, teammate_stop) and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Hermes subagents using credentials selected by Hermes from the parent, delegation settings or an operator-configured teammate route where supported. Toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write_file and patch); Hermes can add inherited MCP toolsets back unless delegation.inherit_mcp_toolsets is false. A teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where Hermes provides it, otherwise delegate_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. Optionally the roster is read from an operator-named YAML file (roster_file, relative to the profile home or absolute, so several profiles can share one); the plugin never writes it. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries, complete final results up to 256 KB of text per run, role hashes and available token receipts; no full transcripts). It does not read credential stores. Where supported in-process, subagent_start and post_api_request hooks collect token receipts for mapped child sessions. For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. teammate_request_changes reopens a lane card that is in review (Hermes reopen_review_task), adds the feedback as a card comment and starts a teammate on it again; it never completes a card either. teammate_chain creates up to eight linked cards in its lane through Hermes' kanban_create (so Hermes wakes the creating chat when a card reaches review), archives the cards it created if the chain cannot be finished, and never completes a card; a lane card's teammate receives the finished results of the cards it depends on in its launch context. The lane tools take an optional board that names an existing, non-archived Kanban board (validated before any write; the plugin never creates or recreates a board); the run records it and keeps its claim, heartbeats, review handoff and rework on that board. On Hermes builds with plugin prompt sections it adds one short paragraph (under 600 characters) about the Kanban lane to new top-level session prompts. The paragraph is rendered from its settings, carries no conversation content, and is left out without a usable teammate, for delegated children and under host isolation. It runs one in-process monitor thread per run to retain finished results and, for lane runs, keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own. Completion notices are off by default and never inject unless the operator turns on both notify_on_completion and trust_notice_routing, because Hermes cannot confirm which conversation would receive them; teammate_wait is the default. With both on, a finished run sends one line (teammate name, run ID and status, never result text) as a user message to the chat it was assigned from through ctx.inject_message, which also needs Hermes' own allow_gateway_injection consent; a run with no recorded chat gets none, and after /new, /reset or /resume the line reaches that chat's current conversation. Includes two skills: teammates-workflow, a playbook that explains the tools, the Kanban Review loop and how a teammate's model, route and reasoning effort are inherited (it adds no tools, settings or permissions); and a report-a-problem skill: the agent drafts a bug report and files it to this repository with gh only after the user approves the draft.

entries.name: hermes-teamops
entries.description: One plugin for the full lifecycle of a multi-agent Hermes team. Deploy a whole team from a blueprint (profiles, SOULs, crons, shared kanban/mesh) with `hermes teams deploy`, verify it with Deploy Guard (preflight/smoke/rollback), watch fleet status and the mesh map, catch silent cron gaps (Cron911) and dead models (Model Guard), get a daily standup digest, and broadcast decisions across teams (mesh sync). The Agent Factory is an in-plugin template generator: from a one-line spec it extends a base blueprint with a new role or scaffolds a new team, then deploys it via the same verified pipeline (fixture fallback for demos). 16 tools plus the hermes teams CLI. Local-first by default: everything runs against your own HERMES_HOME; optional `--host` ssh deploys use your own credentials, nothing is stored; `--host` copies the bundle only to your own host. Disclosure — deploying a team creates Hermes profiles and cron jobs in your HERMES_HOME; rollback deletes only teamops-prefixed profiles and files under <home>/teams/<team>/; Model Guard apply and rollback rewrite every profile's config.yaml and jobs.json; fleet and cron scans read every profile's cron store; the optional `--host` deploy copies the team bundle to your VPS over your own ssh credentials and trusts a first-seen host key; `hermes teams dashboard` runs a token-protected server on 127.0.0.1:8781; the bundled trading blueprint is paper-only by instruction, and its agents get the terminal toolset.

entries.name: hermes-teleoperator
entries.description: Keep one conversation on the gateway while switching shell, files, skills and explicitly permitted MCP tools between machines over SSH. The standalone Rust receiver needs no Hermes or language runtime. Commands have the destination SSH user's full OS authority; this is not a sandbox. Disclosure — Routes this conversation's terminal, file, process, skill and allowlisted MCP tool calls to SSH machines you configure, where the author's Rust receiver runs them with that SSH user's full authority; Hermes' dangerous-command and human-approval prompts run before each routed call, but other plugins' pre_tool_call blocks and the agent's tool guardrails do not see routed calls until core adds a seam (hermes-agent#152963). The optional `python -m hermes_teleoperator.deploy` helper downloads the receiver from the author's GitHub release (SHA256 pinned in the plugin source, build-attested) and installs it on the remote host over SSH; file transfers need approval, and gateway-local transfers stay inside a configured transfer_dir.
entries.title: Hermes Teleoperator
known_issues: Windows is unsupported. Linux is the only catalog-claimed platform; macOS binaries exist but are not execution-tested in CI.
Gateway and receiver versions must match exactly. SSH keys and verified known-host entries must already be configured.

Receiver runs with the SSH user's authority. Gateway applies Hermes' dangerous-command and human-approval gates before routing, but other plugins' pre_tool_call hooks and the agent's tool guardrails cannot see routed calls until Hermes provides a pre-execution seam (hermes-agent#152963). Browser, memory, cron and delegation do not migrate.

Remote MCP is explicit-allowlist stdio only; sampling, elicitation and interactive callbacks are rejected. Remote content search is blocked; filename search remains available. Small-file transfers are limited to 8 MiB.

Transfers require human approval scoped to the exact source, destination and move setting. Gateway-local transfers require a configured transfer_dir; deleting a gateway-local source additionally requires allow_local_delete: true.

Receiver downloads are verified against per-asset SHA256 digests committed in the plugin source for the exact release tag; SHA256SUMS is cross-checked but is not the trust root. Release assets carry GitHub build-provenance attestations. SSH key authorization remains a manual administrator action.

entries.name: hermes-templates
entries.description: Share a whole Hermes agent as one .htemplate bundle and install it from a single HTTPS link: identity (SOUL.md), config with accounts and endpoints stripped, skills, routines, MCP server definitions, memories only when the author opts in, and plugin ids. A recipe, not a clone — credentials, sessions, conversation history, logs, caches and workspace never travel. Publish puts the bundle in a GitHub repository and returns one permanent link (re-publishing updates the same URL); Install previews a link, a path or a dropped file and shows the template itself before anything is written (SOUL.md, each skill, every routine's schedule and prompt, every MCP command, risky settings such as hooks with their values). Install enforces what the packer promises on any bundle: config sanitized again (approval and consent policy — command_allowlist, hooks_auto_accept, approvals, security — is always removed and the preview shows what was removed), routines imported paused through Hermes' cron API, MCP servers set enabled: false; plugins already installed here are enabled unless --no-enable-plugins. Reinstalling the same link offers "Update v1.0.0 → v1.1.0" and keeps memories, sessions and .env. Disclosure — reads the selected profile under HERMES_HOME (config.yaml, SOUL.md, skills/, cron/jobs.json, mcp.json, memories/ when opted in) and writes a new profile directory plus its own bundles under plugin-data/; the page may read a bundle only from HERMES_HOME or the home directory, the CLI has no such limit. Network: one HTTPS GET to a URL the user pastes (HTTPS and public hosts only on the page; http, LAN and local accepted in the CLI; every redirect re-checked, 20 MB cap) and, only when the user presses Publish, the GitHub REST API to upload the bundle and download it back to prove the link before it is shown; republishing writes the file at the same public URL. Installs drop approval and consent policy (command_allowlist, hooks_auto_accept, approvals, security), import routines paused and turn MCP servers off; plugins already installed here are enabled unless --no-enable-plugins. Credentials: the optional GITHUB_TOKEN is read with agent.secret_scope under the named profile, never stored in a bundle, logged or returned. No shell, no telemetry, no self-updater.
entries.title: Agent Templates
known_issues: The Desktop half of a unified package starts disabled per browser; enable it once in Capabilities ▸ Plugins.

raw.githubusercontent.com caches plain links for up to 5 minutes per client kind, so a just-published update can briefly still serve the previous file; the result also shows the commit-pinned URL, which is immediate.
A profile named by ?profile= is only used for credential resolution; the page lists the profiles of the Hermes home it runs in.

entries.name: hermes-tenuo
entries.description:
Signed, expiring tool permissions for Hermes. Constrain tool names and arguments for sessions, cron jobs and delegated work, with local audit logs.
Disclosure — ordinary calls pass through until a warrant is configured. Set require_warrant: true to block calls without one. A configured but unloadable warrant blocks calls, and a kanban worker without a per-task warrant is blocked. Tool names and arguments are appended to $HERMES_HOME/tenuo/audit.jsonl (disable with audit_log: false). When TENUO_CONNECT_TOKEN or TENUO_CONTROL_PLANE_URL are set, the bundled tenuo SDK (compiled Rust core) streams those decisions, including arguments, to that control plane.

entries.name: hermes-themes-pack
entries.description: The 23 Omarchy stock themes (Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord, Rose Pine, Jade Horse and more) as Hermes skins, with one /theme command that switches the CLI, the TUI and Desktop together. Optionally follows the Omarchy theme. Works without Omarchy. entries.name: hermes-time-machine
entries.description: The rollback that knows what it can't undo. Incremental, time-bounded checkpoints that the agent itself can preview, restore or fork (atm_* tools, /timemachine); an approval at the point of no return (git push, npm/cargo/PyPI/gem publish, terraform apply, and MCP or plugin tools that open PRs, merge, release, send messages or deploy) that shows what becomes permanent and the exact compensation command; an effect ledger; effect memory that reminds the model of pushes it can no longer see after /rollback, /undo, /retry or compaction; and a read-only Time machine dashboard tab that shows checkpoints next to the effects no restore can undo, with per-file diffs and undo commands. Every restore takes a safety checkpoint first, so it can be undone. Disclosure — no shell commands, subprocesses, network calls, background processes or credentials; reads workspace files plus .git refs/config, package.json, Cargo.toml and pyproject.toml to capture pre-state; writes only under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-time-machine, on a rewind the workspace (replaced files go to a trash directory), and on atm_fork a new sibling folder next to the workspace; adds a restore-point note to tool results and effect reminders to the model's context; asks for approval through Hermes before every model-requested restore and before irreversible commands and tool calls, and never approves or blocks a tool call by itself; the dashboard tab adds three read-only GET routes (no restore, write or process); refuses filesystem roots, home and system directories.

entries.description: Local pixel-art town where every Hermes session is a resident and every tool call walks to a building. Passive lifecycle bridge to a loopback-only server; prompts, arguments, and output never leave the process. On start the server also reads HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.

entries.name: hermes-tripo
entries.description: Tripo 3D tools on Tripo's v3 API (openapi.tripo3d.ai). Text, photo or multiview to 3D, image edits, retexturing, splitting into parts, Smart UV, auto-rigging, preset animations, retopology, format conversion (FBX, USDZ, STL, 3MF, OBJ, GLTF) and downloads, with an inline 3D viewer in Hermes Desktop that shows whether a model is really rigged, a library pane that shows where each model came from (the steps behind it, its prompt, a jump back to the chat that made it, and one-click next steps), a local model inspector, and a status-bar chip with the Tripo balance and this chat's spend. Every credit-spending call goes through Hermes's approval prompt with its estimated cost, and a per-chat limit (a setting under Settings → Plugins, default 100 credits) makes it ask again past it. Disclosure — sends prompts and the local images or 3D model files you or the agent name (up to 50 MB; every local-file upload, free calls included, goes through Hermes's approval prompt) to Tripo's API at openapi.tripo3d.ai with TRIPO_API_KEY; saves downloaded models to $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or a folder the agent picks (never overwriting: a clash gets a " (2)" suffix), and the Desktop viewer's save button copies models into your Downloads/Tripo folder (or the folder set in its settings); keeps a local task history in $HERMES_HOME/tripo/history.json (chat id, tool, prompt, parent task, estimated cost, saved file paths; at most 2,000 tasks, never sent anywhere); the Desktop library opens local .glb/.fbx/.obj/.stl files only from inside your home folder, $HERMES_HOME/tripo/ or the viewer's download folder, and uploads nothing; the status-bar chip reads your Tripo balance every two minutes and after each Tripo tool call; no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-tube
entries.description: Take back control of what you watch. HermesTube puts your YouTube subscriptions in Hermes Desktop: tabs you make by folder, tag, channel or topic, a folder pane, a channel manager with undo, folder suggestions from your Hermes model, topic tabs it builds from YouTube search, and videos in Hermes's own player. New and still experimental: a cleanup list you approve, /tube buttons on Telegram and scheduled routines. Disclosure — the gateway fetches public www.youtube.com pages only (channel feeds and pages, uploads and Shorts playlists, video, /shorts and search pages, also in a background pass after refreshes), without login, and, for the favorites routine's Telegram message, one cover image per new video from i.ytimg.com; it connects to public addresses only and sends YouTube's anonymous consent cookie SOCS=CAI to YouTube hosts only; Desktop loads thumbnails and avatars from YouTube's image hosts and plays videos in Hermes's own embed. A separately installed Chrome extension, the only link to the YouTube account, unsubscribes only channels a person approved in Desktop or with the /tube cleanup buttons, and talks to a plugin server on 127.0.0.1 (ports 47615-47624) paired with a 6-digit code; the approve and pairing RPCs accept any client authenticated to the gateway. Organize, cleanup reasons and topic tabs send channel names and video titles to the user's model through ctx.llm, also from unattended blueprint jobs. After a button confirmation, /tube routines writes scripts to HERMES_HOME/scripts and creates cron jobs. The favorites routine sends each new video to Telegram by running hermes send with a fixed argument list; it reads cron/jobs.json read-only to find the chat and never reads the bot token. Only on a click in Desktop, Set up the extension copies the extension bundled in the plugin to a fixed HermesTube Extension folder in the home folder (refusing one it did not create) and opens the Extensions page of one Chromium browser (chosen from a closed list of those found in fixed install places; no profile is read) and the file manager with fixed argument lists and time limits; a second button only drafts a fixed help request in a new chat, which the person sends. Data in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-tube; no shell commands, credentials or telemetry; the README lists the known limits. Formerly MyTube, by the same author; not affiliated with YouTube, Google or Nous Research.
entries.title: HermesTube
known_issues: The extension is not on the Chrome Web Store: the plugin ships it built and copies it to a folder, and the person turns on Developer mode and loads that folder (Load unpacked or drag and drop) in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium, Vivaldi, Opera or Arc. Hermes and the browser must run on the same computer (with Hermes inside WSL on Windows, the folder goes to the Windows user folder and the Windows browser is used).
Reading subscriptions and unsubscribing depend on YouTube's page layout; on a mismatch the extension reports a failure and clicks nothing.

Run on macOS and, without a screen, on Debian 13 in a container. Windows (Hermes inside WSL 2, or installed natively) is covered by automated tests and a Linux container that imitates WSL, but has not yet run on a real Windows machine (Windows testers and pull requests are welcome); inside WSL the browser reaches the plugin through WSL's localhost forwarding (on by default), and natively the plugin does not hot-reload its code (restart Hermes after an update).

English and Brazilian Portuguese only. A few validation messages of the plugin's API may still be in Portuguese; routine and blueprint keys (bom-dia, favoritos, resumo-pasta, faxina-mensal, pasta-novos) are fixed Portuguese identifiers that show up in hermes cron list.

First version: reading subscriptions, unsubscribing through the extension and the youtube.com sidebar were run on a real signed-in YouTube account with the interface in Brazilian Portuguese and one to three subscriptions; /tube status, tabs, triage buttons, routine install and the morning digest were run on one real Telegram chat. The other four routine messages, /tube topic on Telegram, chat video cards, adding a channel by link, other interface languages and long subscription lists are covered by automated tests only.
The Home on youtube.com and the Extras are not part of this version; topic tabs are not re-searched on a schedule yet (refresh one by hand).

HermesTube does not use the official YouTube API: it reads public pages and clicks in the person's own browser. YouTube's Terms of Service may not allow this kind of automated access; use it at your own risk.

entries.name: hermes-tuneup
entries.description: Shows when compaction really fires on every profile and model route, flags settings that waste quota or break prompt caching, and fixes them only after you confirm, with a diff and a backup. Disclosure — reads every Hermes profile's config.yaml (and four context-length cache files) read-only, through Hermes' own loader on a temporary copy, and shows the model a redacted per-profile digest; writes a profile's config.yaml only when you type a fix and confirm it (never from cron, a group chat or an agent-launched shell), after saving a backup under that profile's backups/config; when you turn receipts on it records compaction, cache and model-use metadata (never message content) in its own plugin-data folder; imports undocumented Hermes resolver modules from one adapter file (validate shows rule 9 warnings); no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

entries.name: hermes-ui-cards
entries.description: Interactive answer cards in Hermes Desktop and the Webapp; your answer goes back as the next message. Disclosure — stores every Desktop card and the user's answers, free text typed into cards included, in the profile's plugin-data/hermes-ui-cards/ (answers.db plus the newest 500 card files; nothing expires by time and deleting a chat does not delete its entries); adds turn context for the model (card answers, confirm-card actions and commands, and a periodic Desktop hint to use cards); Desktop cards load images from https URLs the model supplies, so the image host sees the user's IP; read-only backend routes /api/plugins/hermes-ui-cards/answers and /settings; no telemetry, no credentials, no shell commands.

entries.name: hermes-ui
entries.description: A bespoke chat workspace for Hermes Desktop and the Webapp: it takes over the app's home route and replaces it with a three-column page — a rail of bots (one row per profile, each with its own conversations), the conversation itself with folded reasoning and one working line that says what the bot is doing (tool calls are not listed; a call waiting for permission still shows its card), and a right panel for files, previews and session detail. Bots can answer with a structured block that the thread draws as rich components (status cards, tables, checklists, approval prompts) instead of prose, its questions answered in the thread with buttons, a multi-select and free text; links open in the OS browser; messages written while the bot works wait in a queue under the composer and go in order, slash commands, per-bot models and a settings page come with it (a model switch is sent to config.set without the confirmation flag; when the gateway asks to confirm a costly or data-policy-sensitive switch, its own message is shown in a dialog and the flag is sent only after the user clicks Switch), and media blocks render images, audio and video inline. Disclosure — takes over the Desktop/Webapp home route by default: opening home or a session from the native sidebar redirects into Hermes UI (a palette command turns this off). Its side panel previews files that replies name (MEDIA: lines, attached-image paths) by reading them through the plugin's own backend routes, which accept any path under the profile home or the user's home directory except core-refused and credential files (.env*, auth.json, config.yaml, credentials, webhook_subscriptions.json, private keys, .ssh/.aws/.gnupg, secrets, mcp-tokens and pairing folders); those local previews stay on the device. Web images a reply links to (markdown images, MEDIA: web addresses) are loaded by the app straight from their host, with no referrer. The bots rail reads each profile's state.db read-only. Changing a bot's look (shape, eyes, colour) writes ui_meta['hermes-ui'] in that profile's profile.yaml through Hermes' own profiles.configure. No telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes UI
known_issues: The Desktop half of a unified package starts disabled per browser; enable it once in Capabilities ▸ Plugins.
On a shell that loads plugins late, the first paint can be the native home for a moment before the page takes over; the sidebar entry always opens it.

entries.name: hermes-unlimited
entries.description: Create and operate AI-native provider organizations with scoped services and Hermes tasks. Disclosure — Creates and reads Hermes Kanban tasks (run by your Hermes workers as the current profile) through the local `hermes kanban` CLI on a per-tenant board, and stores company, service, request, human-oversight time and cost records in a local SQLite file you configure; sends your JustYou session token only to a loopback JustYou validator you configure.
entries.title: Hermes Unlimited
known_issues: Experimental public core; no live billing, payment settlement or independently attested customer fulfillment. New service requests remain blocked pending separately verified execution authority; identity-only sessions do not authorize work.
Human oversight/AI recovery cost inputs are MODEL_SUBMITTED_UNVERIFIED; no independent financial value or ROI is established.
Community adapter discovery is catalog-only metadata; no external provider integration is activated or independently verified.
Company Memory recall is read-only; stored verification labels are not independently attested by the plugin.

Specialist Factory uses local plugin declarations only when Hermes does not expose a host tool registry; these are not live verified capabilities. External toolsets require an explicit host registry. No execution authority is granted.
Economic evaluation is advisory comparison of MODEL_SUBMITTED_UNVERIFIED costs against MODEL_SUBMITTED_UNVERIFIED scenario caps, not an approved budget, verified ROI, or execution decision.
Requires a configured JustYou session validator, signed Ed25519 profile bindings and provisioned tenant boards. Beta.7 ready/running tasks are not retroactively quarantined by upgrade.

entries.name: hermes-ussd
entries.description: Use Hermes from any phone, including feature phones with no internet: dial a USSD code for an instant menu, ask a question, get the agent's answer by SMS, and read long answers back page by page on USSD. Africa's Talking (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Nigeria, Malawi and more). Closed by default (allowlist), phone users get the `safe` toolset, store-first at-most-once SMS outbox, daily SMS cap. Disclosure — opens an HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1:8790 (loopback; the user exposes it through their own tunnel or reverse proxy); makes outbound HTTPS calls only to api.africastalking.com / api.sandbox.africastalking.com (SMS API), sending reply text and the recipient's number; every question and reply crosses the mobile operator and Africa's Talking as plain-text USSD/SMS; stores phone numbers and reply text in a 0600 SQLite file in Hermes plugin storage (7-day default retention, `hermes ussd purge`); runs an outbox worker and an hourly purge task inside the gateway process; Africa's Talking callbacks are unsigned, so the secret URL path is the only authentication (rotate with `hermes ussd rotate-secret`), and anyone holding that URL or spoofing an allowlisted sender number gets an agent turn with this profile's memory and the `safe` toolset (web, vision, image generation) by default; `AT_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` lets any phone start turns on the user's account; sending SMS costs money on the user's Africa's Talking account (daily cap of 200 on by default); `hermes ussd setup` writes its own AT_* values to the Hermes .env; no telemetry, no shell commands, no self-update, no binaries.
entries.title: USSD & SMS (Africa's Talking)
known_issues: Needs an Africa's Talking account. The free sandbox works for development; a live USSD code needs approval from Africa's Talking and the mobile operators.
Africa's Talking callbacks are unsigned; authenticity rests on the secret URL path.
One listener per Africa's Talking account and port (shared-ingress multiplexed profiles are not supported).

entries.name: hermes-vault-broker
entries.description: Fill saved logins from an out-of-process credential broker. The broker runs as its own system user with ProtectHome=yes, derives a KEK from a passphrase with scrypt and keeps the random data key (DEK) in checked mlock'd memory, and writes the password into the page itself over a DevTools endpoint taken ONLY from its own root-owned loopback config — the model cannot choose it, and a tab's websocket is refused unless its host:port matches. The agent sends (handle, origin) over a unix socket and gets a fill count back; SO_PEERCRED limits the gateway uid to status/list/fill while unlock/add/remove/init/lock stay with root and the broker's own uid. Exact-origin binding is re-asserted inside the tab immediately before the write. Import only accepts a JSON export the operator made themselves; the broker never opens Hermes's credential stores. An optional CDP-pipe mode lets the broker launch and own Chromium with no TCP debugging port. Linux; stdlib unittest suite; deps cryptography + websockets. Disclosure — requires running `scripts/install.sh` as root, which creates a `vaultd` system user, adds the Hermes user to its group, pip-installs `cryptography` and `websockets` into /opt/hermes-vault-broker/venv and enables a system-wide `hermes-vault-broker` systemd service; saved passwords are typed into browser pages over the Chrome DevTools endpoint configured in /etc/hermes-vault-broker/cdp.json, so any process running as the browser's user can read a filled field or take over that port; the optional unlock page (`unlock-form`) serves the passphrase form over self-signed HTTPS and the README suggests binding it to 0.0.0.0.

entries.name: hermes-vcc-engine
entries.description: Instant context compaction for Hermes Agent: builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message for recall via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads Hermes's config.yaml through Hermes's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods and on private helpers and constants in Hermes's agent.context_compressor, conversation_compression, auxiliary_client, agent_init and skill_commands modules and hermes_cli.plugins.get_plugin_commands, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing; with the opt-in only_local_models setting, compaction for a non-local chat model goes to Hermes's stock LLM summary; the /vcc chat command, available to anyone allowed to chat with the agent, switches that for hosted models for the whole profile and stores the choice in <HERMES_HOME>/vcc_state.json, the only file it writes.
entries.title: Instant Context Compactor
entries.capability_summary: hermes-vcc-engine (community, maintained by danbiocchi) Instant context compaction for Hermes Agent: builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message for recall via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads Hermes's config.yaml through Hermes's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods and on private helpers and constants in Hermes's agent.context_compressor, conversation_compression, auxiliary_client, agent_init and skill_commands modules and hermes_cli.plugins.get_plugin_commands, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing; with the opt-in only_local_models setting, compaction for a non-local chat model goes to Hermes's stock LLM summary; the /vcc chat command, available to anyone allowed to chat with the agent, switches that for hosted models for the whole profile and stores the choice in <HERMES_HOME>/vcc_state.json, the only file it writes. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.7.

entries.name: hermes-vcc
entries.description: Algorithmic (no-LLM) context compaction engine: builds summaries by deterministic regex extraction instead of a summarizer-model call — zero-token, byte-reproducible, inside the built-in ContextCompressor; compacted turns stay searchable via session_search. Disclosure — no network calls, no env vars, no secrets, no telemetry; registers no tools/hooks/middleware and reads only the turns the host passes for compaction; debug: true (default false) writes one metadata-only file $HERMES_HOME/vcc-debug.json. Derived from pi-vcc (MIT, sting8k)

entries.name: hermes-verifier
entries.description: Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your Hermes session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read_file, search_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in HERMES_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read_file/search_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY from the process environment or the host `hermes` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to Hermes's stored credentials.

entries.name: hermes-verify
entries.description: Configurable tool-risk flags, bounded local receipt metadata and held unverified-prose labels. Disclosure — prepends an "unverified agent prose" banner to every final reply (stored in the transcript), holds streaming so replies arrive only after labeling, and replaces any reply over 100,000 characters with an omission notice; the verify_claim tool fetches model-supplied public http(s) URLs (private addresses refused); flagged tool calls are logged locally and blocked only when blocking_mode is on.
known_issues: Default observation mode logs and allows; optional blocking is a heuristic, not OS containment.
Whole-output labeling and lexical source comparison do not establish factual truth.
Local receipt records are unauthenticated; action returns do not prove completion.
Host storage-helper errors can select a fallback directory that is not guaranteed to follow the active profile.
End-to-end agent stream delivery and integrated strict-mode actions are not yet qualified.

entries.name: hermes-video-editor
entries.description: Local video editor for your own footage: 45 FFmpeg tools for the agent (cut, silence removal, 9:16 reframe, captions, music with ducking, loudness, platform export and checks) plus a visual editor in Hermes Desktop with canvas, any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays and music, scenes and an English/German help. 100% local, no API key. Licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Disclosure — the Desktop page starts a local web server on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-run token) that can read and write media and image files anywhere under your home folder (and any VE_EDITOR_ROOTS); preview caches go to the system temp folder. The agent tools run ffmpeg/ffprobe on the input paths the model passes and write media, image or .srt files at the output paths it passes (replacing an existing file only with overwrite: true).
entries.title: Video Editor (local FFmpeg)
known_issues: Requires FFmpeg and ffprobe on PATH (apt install ffmpeg / brew install ffmpeg / winget install Gyan.FFmpeg).
lk_transcribe_captions is optional and needs 'pip install faster-whisper' plus a model already on disk.

The visual editor has one main video track plus any number of tracks for text, shapes, video overlays, audio and scenes; these items sit at fixed times and do not move when the main clips are cut (bundle them in a scene to move them together).
The editor preview needs H.264 or VP8 playback in the app's browser engine; editing and export work without it.

entries.name: hermes-vision-inline
entries.description: Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision_analyze handler through tool_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image_input_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Hermes private vision helpers, so after a Hermes update it may silently fall back to the normal path.

entries.name: hermes-visual-memory
entries.description: Your agent remembers what a camera saw on your desk: "what's in front of you?", "what did I take away?", "where did I last see my keys?", "what was here yesterday?". Built for a used Echo Show running Hermes Eye, with before/after pictures on its screen. Vision goes through Hermes's own model routing (its own "Visual memory" slot) or a local OpenAI-compatible model such as Qwen 3.6 in Ollama. Disclosure — off until the user turns it on by voice; the first tool call starts background threads inside Hermes: a camera loop reading one snapshot a second from Hermes Eye on the LAN (only while on), a token-protected API on 127.0.0.1:28950, and a LAN display feed (port 28951) restricted by client IP and the Home Assistant screen origin; pictures go to the vision model Hermes routes the task to (a cloud provider if that is the user's vision model) or to the local server the user sets; SQLite and snapshots in the plugin's data directory, pictures deleted after 14 days; reads EYE_TOKEN through Hermes; no shell commands, no telemetry.
entries.title: Hermes Visual Memory
known_issues: Needs a camera running Hermes Eye (an Echo Show 5 with the app from this repository).
Small metal things (keys, clips) get a different name on most looks with local models.

entries.name: hermes-vitals-light
entries.description: CPU, load, free RAM, Linux PSI CPU pressure, active sessions, running Hermes processes and round-trip time of the connected Hermes server in the Desktop status bar, plus an optional TUI card. Disclosure — the Desktop chip's backend route reads CPU/memory figures via psutil, Linux /proc/pressure/cpu and /proc/meminfo, every process's command line (only per-command Hermes process counts are returned) and the server's own loopback /api/status, and reports the server hostname to the Desktop; the optional TUI card, copied by hand into tui-widgets/, runs the same code as a long-lived `python3 -c` child of the TUI and saves its options to <HERMES_HOME>/vitals.json; no third-party network call, no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: hermes-vnc
entries.description: Computer-use backend that drives any machine reachable over VNC (RFB): the stock computer_use tool captures the remote screen and moves that machine's mouse and keyboard, so the agent can work on a second computer, a lab box or a cloud desktop with no Hermes process running on it. Select it with computer_use.backend: hermes-vnc and point computer_use.vnc.host at the target. VNC carries pixels only, so the backend runs in the screenshot lane: capture returns a PNG and no accessibility elements, element-addressed actions (click-by-element, focus_app, set_value) report unsupported_action instead of guessing, and list_apps / list_windows return empty lists rather than inventing an inventory. capture_max_width downscales each capture — vision tokens scale with the image's area, so this is the one setting that changes what a screenshot costs (measured 1920 -> 786 estimated tokens at 1024 wide on a 1600x900 desktop). It also ships an optional desktop pane that shows the remote screen while the agent works — off by default, a viewer that opens its own read-only connection and never sends input. Disclosure — connects only to the VNC server you configure (host and port) and sends it screenshots and input; RFB traffic (screen pixels, keystrokes, clipboard text) is unencrypted, so use it over a private network or an SSH tunnel; the one credential is the VNC password, read from the variable named by password_env through Hermes's secret scope and never written or logged; computer_use.vnc.host/port can also be overridden by the HERMES_VNC_HOST / HERMES_VNC_PORT / HERMES_VNC_PASSWORD_ENV process environment variables; no shell, no files written, no telemetry; one daemon thread runs Twisted's reactor, started on first connect and deliberately never stopped because the reactor is process-wide and cannot be restarted; the optional desktop live-view pane (off by default) opens a second read-only VNC connection served through the plugin's dashboard route; one dependency (vncdotool>=1.2,<2).
entries.title: Hermes VNC
known_issues: Needs a VNC server on the machine you want to drive (TightVNC, UltraVNC, TigerVNC, x11vnc, macOS Screen Sharing, or a cloud VM's VNC endpoint). Nothing is installed on the target beyond that.

Enable the plugin, do not just install it: python_dependencies are installed by `hermes plugins enable hermes-vnc`, and enabling builds a new pm environment that an already-running gateway or CLI does not switch to. Install, enable, then restart the host — otherwise the tool reports vncdotool is not installed even though the environment now has it.

Pixels only: RFB has no accessibility tree, so every action is by coordinate; focus_app, set_value and click-by-element answer unsupported_action, while list_apps and list_windows return empty lists rather than inventing an inventory.
Typing covers printable ASCII; text outside Latin-1 (Cyrillic, Greek, CJK) is refused with unsupported_text, because RFB's cut-text message is Latin-1.

capture_max_width trades click precision for tokens: click coordinates stay in native desktop space, so a downscaled frame makes the model multiply what it reads off the image. Native (0) is the default.

The optional live view holds a second RFB connection, so the target must accept more than one viewer at a time — x11vnc -shared, TightVNC, UltraVNC and macOS Screen Sharing do by default. Frame rate is set by the round trip: measured ~100 ms per frame (9.7 fps) against a local server, ~1.1 s (0.9 fps) over an SSH tunnel to a cloud host. Do not enable x11vnc -ncache with it: that measured 11-23 s per frame, twenty times worse.

Authentication is none / VNC password / Apple ARD (Diffie-Hellman) — the three a desktop server realistically asks for, macOS Screen Sharing included. A server offering only another type is refused with its own list of security types in the message, rather than hanging.

The framebuffer size is whatever the target reports, read on every capture and never cached: TigerVNC 1.13.1's Xvnc returned 675x800 on the first frame of a fresh connection and 1280x800 afterwards, and both were reported as they came.

entries.name: hermes-voice-gateway
entries.description: Answers Twilio phone calls with Hermes: caller speech is transcribed and Hermes' replies are spoken with ElevenLabs over a Pipecat pipeline. Callers get only two restricted tools (inventory search, enquiry save). Operator-approved callbacks are proposed by the agent and dialed only after a human runs /voice-callback approve. Disclosure — runs a call server on 127.0.0.1:8081 (VOICE_WEBHOOK_HOST / VOICE_WEBHOOK_PORT) that a tunnel or reverse proxy must expose to Twilio; Twilio webhooks are signature-checked and callers must be on VOICE_ALLOWED_USERS, but caller ID can be spoofed, so treat the allowlist as a filter, not authentication. Install it in a dedicated voice profile: callers talk to a normal Hermes agent that can see that profile's persona, project context and voice instructions, and calls are refused unless that profile's memory and user profile are off and no memory provider is set. Call audio goes to ElevenLabs (speech-to-text and text-to-speech) and call metadata and callbacks go to the Twilio REST API; the optional local dev pipeline also uses OpenAI. Caller enquiries are stored as plaintext in the plugin's own SQLite file under HERMES_HOME.
entries.title: Hermes Voice Gateway
known_issues: Requires pipecat-ai 1.7.0 exactly (pinned) and uvicorn; the Hermes runtime must be able to install them.
Twilio WebSocket calls have basic call control only: no transfers or reconnects. Voicemail is not detected, and full barge-in is unverified.
Twilio call-status callbacks are not wired in, so a stored callback status stays answered after the call ends; use voice_check_call_status for live state.
Caller ID is unverified. Anyone Hermes lets run slash commands can approve callbacks, so restrict command access to your operators.

In-process gateway platform only; the caller-tool policy uses some non-public Hermes internals and must be re-verified on Hermes upgrades. The Hermes profile's Voice tool selection must be set to voice_caller only (see the README), otherwise calls fail closed.

Voicemail is not detected, and full barge-in is unverified.; Twilio call-status callbacks are not wired in, so a stored callback status stays answered after the call ends; use voice_check_call_status for live state.; Caller ID is unverified. entries.name: hermes-voice-lab
entries.description: A voice you can play inside Hermes, made by a physical model of a throat, tongue, lips and nose with air pushed through them in real time: no samples and no TTS model. Drag her tongue and lips on a side-profile portrait with a live cutaway, play notes and sing lyrics from the keyboard, beatbox on pads. The agent plays her too: it speaks lines, writes songs and beats, changes her voice, and jams with you (play a phrase, pause, and Hermes sings an answer). Disclosure — local synthesis only, no network calls. Agent renders and the optional read-aloud provider run node runtime/render.mjs (the plugin's own bundled script; fixed argv, no shell, 120 s timeout) and write WAVs and projects under the plugin's data folder; Desktop export and import use only a folder the user grants. With Jam switched on, each phrase you play is sent to the focused conversation as your message. MIDI access only on request. runtime/voice_lab_engine.wasm is built from the repo's Rust source in GitHub Actions and attested; desktop/plugin.js is the esbuild bundle of src/ and inlines the same engine. Optional read-aloud provider, off unless tts.provider is set to voice-lab. No telemetry.

entries.name: hermes-vpn
entries.description: Named network exits for the agent's browser: ask it to browse from another country and it switches, then verifies by reading back the address the far end actually saw, never trusting a label. Any VPN, WireGuard config or proxy works as a local exit; gluetun containers are discovered automatically and one can be brought up on demand. VPN credentials never reach the agent, the chat or the model. Disclosure -- a root-owned helper, installed out of band by the user through a narrow exact-path sudoers rule, is the only thing that reads the credentials and writes them to a root-only file (the agent names a country, never the key), and it pulls the gluetun image pinned by digest; the helper manages gluetun Docker containers, bringing exits up and down; the plugin registers a tool_execution middleware that holds browser_* calls when no verified exit is up (the kill switch, and optional cross-provider failover); it verifies exits by calling public IP-geolocation services (ipinfo, ifconfig.co, ip2location, cloudflare); credential entry is CLI-only, with no model tool for it -- `hermes vpn provider <name> --set` (interactive) or `--from-ref`, which resolves a WireGuard config from pass/gopass or a host file host-side and never returns it to the model; opening a .onion needs `hermes vpn allow-onion`, a terminal command a person runs (no model tool) that turns off Hermes's own internal-address check so onion names resolve and restarts Hermes, and the plugin never writes that setting itself; the active profile comes from the plugin context (ctx.profile_name), not a private core import.

entries.name: hermes-wake
entries.description: Wakes the exact chat session (Matrix room, Telegram forum topic, ...) that started detached background work (systemd-run unit, PID or file) when that work ends, so the agent reports back on its own instead of the human asking "any updates?". Tools: wake_me_when, wake_list. Disclosure: runs the public 'hermes kanban' CLI (board hermes-wake, notify-subscribe --delivery-mode wake) and systemctl show; a daemon thread polls watches every 15s; stores watch targets, notes and origin ids in local SQLite under plugin-data/hermes-wake; makes no network calls of its own; adds a one-line hint to terminal output of detached commands via transform_terminal_output.

entries.name: hermes-wallet
entries.description: All of DeFi. One conversation. Hermes Wallet by CoinFello makes your agent the only DeFi interface you need: swap, bridge, lend, LP, trade perps, farm yield and automate strategy from your own CoinFello wallet. Fello, CoinFello's DeFi agent, plans and stages each step, and nothing runs until you approve your agent's transaction summary in Hermes, inside a daily spending limit CoinFello enforces. The wallet pane covers portfolio, activity, swap, send, earn, strategies and settings. Built by jacobc.eth, former Lead Managing Director at MetaMask. Sign-in is the plugin's oauth: entry (hermes auth add coinfello:coinfello, OAuth 2.1 + PKCE against app.coinfello.com); Hermes stores and refreshes the grant and the plugin never holds a token. Disclosure — crypto wallet: the agent can move funds from your CoinFello automation wallet (keys held and signing done by CoinFello's server) within the daily limit you approve on CoinFello; coinfello_execute and every coinfello_chat message go through Hermes' approval prompt, and Fello can carry out on-chain actions from an approved chat message. Talks to app.coinfello.com (which records a daily activity event per session with your account id and wallet address), LI.FI's status API (li.quest), public chain RPCs (publicnode.com and others) for swap-venue lookup, static.cx.metamask.io for token icons and Google Fonts in cards; stores non-secret wallet/card state under the Hermes home and the plugin directory; the open Desktop pane polls status and balances.

entries.name: hermes-wallpaper
entries.description: Put any image, GIF or short video from your drive behind the whole Hermes Desktop window. Pick it with the normal file dialog or drop it in, then tune opacity, blur, brightness, saturation, contrast, vignette, fit, anchor, zoom and mirroring; videos get speed, pause-when-hidden and reduced-motion controls, and a small library with an optional slideshow keeps several backgrounds. Quick controls in the status bar, a full settings page and command-palette commands. Disclosure — desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js, imports only @hermes/plugin-sdk and react): no backend, agent tools, hooks, env vars, network calls or telemetry. Picked files are copied into the plugin's own IndexedDB in the Desktop app's local profile and never leave that computer; settings use ctx.storage. While a wallpaper shows, the plugin adds its own fixed z-index -1 layer and one style tag under its own html attribute that applies Desktop's glass-mode transparent-surface rules (surface CSS variables, [data-contrib-shell] and [data-slot='sidebar-wrapper'] fills; data-glass-opaque/raised surfaces stay filled); turning it off or disabling the plugin removes all three.
entries.title: Wallpaper
known_issues: Videos play what Chromium supports: MP4 (H.264) and WebM work; HEVC/ProRes .mov files usually do not and are rejected with a message.

entries.name: hermes-walrus-memory
entries.description: Append-only memory with temporal provenance and hash-chain integrity. Corrections are appended next to the original instead of overwriting it, recall returns the exact ledger line behind any fact, and with Walrus credentials every line is also stored on Walrus Mainnet. Runs zero-config as a local tamper-evident ledger with no external Python dependencies. All file access is confined to the profile: the ledger lives under plugin-data/hermes-walrus-memory, and memory_import reads only the profile's own memories/MEMORY.md. It does not touch memory.provider, so it runs alongside the built-in MEMORY.md rather than replacing it. Disclosure - when WALRUS_DELEGATE_KEY and WALRUS_ACCOUNT_ID are set, every memory line (facts, corrections and derived rules) is uploaded to the Walrus Memory relay (relayer.memory.walrus.xyz by default) under the configured namespace. Lines are sent over TLS and sealed with Mysten SEAL at the relay before they are written to Walrus; the plaintext is not sealed on this machine. Offline that is the whole payload: no telemetry, no other network calls, and nothing is written to ~/.hermes/MEMORY.md. Without credentials nothing leaves the machine. Reading sealed blobs back requires a SEAL session, supplied through WALRUS_SEAL_SESSION or an optional WALRUS_SEAL_BRIDGE command; nothing is pulled or decrypted without one. Disclosure — when WALRUS_DELEGATE_KEY and WALRUS_ACCOUNT_ID are set, every memory line (facts, corrections and derived rules) is uploaded to the Walrus Memory relay (relayer.memory.walrus.xyz by default, or MEMWAL_SERVER_URL) under the configured namespace; lines travel in plaintext inside TLS and are sealed with Mysten SEAL at the relay, not on this machine; reading sealed lines back runs the optional WALRUS_SEAL_BRIDGE command you configure, with a minimal environment. Without credentials nothing leaves the machine.

entries.name: hermes-warden
entries.description: Bitwarden built into Hermes. Easy: a lock tab installs the Bitwarden CLI, signs you in and unlocks, no terminal; one-click copy with auto-clearing clipboard. Integrated: works in Hermes Desktop, the Webapp and any chat (9 agent tools, /warden, the Hermes display language). Safe: secrets are typed only in masked dialogs, the session key lives only in memory, and secrets leave only to your clipboard or commands you approve; the agent never sees them. Disclosure — runs the Bitwarden CLI (bw), which talks to your Bitwarden server; Have I Been Pwned is queried (5-char SHA-1 prefix) only for a password check you approve; the CLI installer uses Homebrew, npm or downloads the official Bitwarden build from github.com/bitwarden/clients (SHA-256 pinned) only when you press Install; a background broker process per Hermes profile holds the session key in memory and exits when locked and idle, and each named profile signs in to Bitwarden separately; warden_run executes the shell command you approve directly on the Hermes host (outside any terminal sandbox) with the chosen vault secrets in its environment; bw serve, which you start from the Warden tab, exposes the unlocked vault on 127.0.0.1 with no authentication to any local process while it runs; exports you approve in csv, json or zip format are written to disk unencrypted; osascript is used on macOS for host dialogs and clipboard; a pre_tool_call hook blocks the agent's terminal from running bw or reading the clipboard for 15 minutes after a secret was copied; settings (no secrets) under <Hermes home>/plugin-data/hermes-warden. No telemetry. Not affiliated with Bitwarden or Nous Research.
entries.title: Hermes Warden
known_issues: macOS and Linux only; Windows is not supported. Bitwarden Secrets Manager (bws) is not covered.

In the Webapp, browsers do not let a page write the clipboard while its tab is in the background: if the tab is not focused when the 30-second timer ends, the plugin asks you to clear the clipboard yourself.
The lock tab comes in 9 languages; only English and Brazilian Portuguese were reviewed by a person.
