A synonym is found only if the fact's keywords name it, unless the optional online search by meaning is on; facts stored without keywords (older ones, auto_extract) need `enrich`.; Arabic, Indic scripts, Indonesian, German, Turkish, Polish and Dutch are matched by scanning the facts' text: the first such search after start analyses every fact (about 1-1.5 s at 5,000 facts, 4-6 s at 20,000); stores without such facts never scan. The bundled dictionaries load on the first word of their language (Chinese about 0.2 s and 30 MB).; forget cleans the database file only: Hermes session history, `hermes backup` archives and copies other tools made are not rewritten (tools can read the `forgotten` table and clean their own copies by fact id).; rerank: on is experimental and does not raise hits. On the maintainer's held-out set it lost one target in 126 questions with embeddings off and two with them on, on questions where several facts of one kind compete, against about 40 % fewer non-target facts. Each turn waits for one rerank call: on 4 CPU threads about 120 ms median with jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual and 340 ms with bge-reranker-v2-m3, capped by rerank_timeout (3 s, lower with embeddings on so that both fit the core's 8 s prefetch budget). The suggested CPU model, jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual, is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial use only); bge-reranker-v2-m3 is Apache-2.0. The plugin ships no model. It sends no key, so a cloud rerank API that requires one (Cohere, Jina) refuses every call; it is tested with llama-server.; After the first merge the file uses history schema 2. Downgrading to a writer below 0.19.0 disables memory for that file until 0.19.0+ is restored or a pre-merge backup is used; manually lowering the schema mark is unsafe. There is no automatic unmerge. In this first release merged copies keep separate historical ids and confirmations are not pooled into the retained fact's origin counts.; memory_map.py (experimental, off unless run) writes the stored facts' texts to its output: a page or file made from it must stay behind a password and is not reached by a later forget. Its JSON format may change without a deprecation period. prefetch_clause_coverage (experimental, off) rescued no facts on one live install's history (5,081 messages) and is kept off there..

entries.name: home-3d-workshop
entries.description: Ask. It's in the box. A 3D printer as a member of the group chat (the persona is Mıstık by default; the name and the en/tr message language are settings, English by default). People in a family or team chat ask in plain words, often by voice note; the agent finds MakerWorld models through Bambuddy, scales one, or designs a part in OpenSCAD (it writes the code, renders it, looks at the preview pictures and keeps every version), slices, and queues with manual start. A print starts only with the owner's typed approval (never from a voice note); when someone else asks, the watcher passes the request to the owner with the exact command. A zero-token cron watcher follows the print; the person who asked gets a one-line start notice and, at the end, a line with a photo in the chat the request came from (groups setting: family or team tone, per-group language), and the owner gets a technical note. Notices go through a saved outbox with retries. Finished parts are tracked in a done box. The owner gets one Workshop screen in Hermes Desktop (approval card with the part in 3D, Start, Pause and Stop, queue, done box, messages, filament, setup check, design versions). Each moment a person had to step in is logged, and repeats become upgrade proposals (for example a printed tilted base for auto-eject). Works with a Bambu Lab printer managed by Bambuddy, or with a built-in simulated printer (hermes home3d demo). Disclosure — Network: only the one Bambuddy URL you set, over HTTP on your LAN. When HOME3D_BAMBUDDY_API_KEY is set, it is sent as X-API-Key, unencrypted over plain http. MakerWorld lookups and downloads go through Bambuddy; the plugin makes no other network calls. The setup check (hermes home3d doctor, the status tool's capabilities, the Workshop screen) makes read-only requests, including GET /api/v1/updates/version, /api/v1/makerworld/status and /api/v1/printers/<id>/camera/status, and never takes a photo. Writes: import, scale, design upload, slice and queue add write to the Bambuddy library and queue without a prompt, for the owner and the people in the household list (unknown senders only with allow_guests); queued items are always manual start. Queue remove only removes the asking person's own waiting items: never a job queued outside the workshop or another household member's job, not even for the owner (who can remove anything by hand in Bambuddy). Bambuddy settings are read (GET /settings/) and never changed. With Bambuddy's require_plate_clear off, Bambuddy may start its own auto-start items on a finished printer before the camera check; hermes home3d doctor warns about this. Chamber light: a tool photo or plate check switches it on for about 12 s and restores its earlier state. The cron watcher also switches it by itself for its plate checks and photos: at most once per pass (twice when a camera request fails), one photo near the end of each workshop print (other prints: one photo and plate check in one light cycle when they end), a check when a print ends, and re-checks that back off 15, 30, 60 and 120 min (at most 6) while a plate or a job waits. Approvals: start, resume and plate-clear confirm follow one rule for the agent path, /home3d and the Workshop screen. They are blocked in cron and in runs with nobody present (kanban workers, chat -q, -z, --source tool; both checks fail closed), when a safety gate fails (printer busy or offline, active HMS error, plate not judged empty, another person's job ahead, plate not confirmed after a failed print, bed hot or of unknown temperature for a plate clear), for unknown or non-owner senders, who are told that the owner approves with /home3d approve, and when the ask came in as a voice note (a typed confirmation is asked for). Voice is detected by the pre_gateway_dispatch hook, which reads only the message type and sender id of each inbound gateway message (never the text), keeps the newest few per sender in memory for 10 minutes and always returns None, and by the transcript shape of the turn text; it does not see local CLI, TUI or Desktop turns. A household member's blocked request is stored, and the watcher tells the owner once (when owner_target is set; otherwise the block tells the person to ask the owner directly). Only an owner session gets the Hermes approve prompt. The owner is any id in owner_ids, plus, while local_is_owner is true (the default), any local CLI, TUI or Desktop session and any slash command typed in the TUI, Desktop or web dashboard or run by the Workshop screen; turn local_is_owner off when others can reach the dashboard. On IRC and ntfy, where people choose their own ids, only an entry written with the platform (irc:<nick>) matches a sender. The tool handler also needs a single-use pass from that hook or from /home3d approve, so a call that skips the hook is refused, and it checks the plate with the camera right before the action. /home3d approve runs the gate and the action at once and stores nothing for later. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt in an owner session (the unattended, identity and voice rules are blocks and are not skipped). Each rule_key is unique, so always does not carry over, and each always answer adds one unused command_allowlist line to config.yaml. Stop and pause need no approval and pass no gate; who may use them is stop_policy (known: the owner and the household list, the default; anyone; owner), and the person who did it is recorded. Hook time: pre_tool_call reads only printer status and queue (at most 5 s per request, 12 s in all, never the camera), so it stays inside Hermes' 30 s hook limit; with a lower plugins.hook_callback_timeout it allows itself 0.4 of it. Workshop screen: three GET routes under /api/plugins/home-3d-workshop/ (health, overview, file), mounted only while the plugin is enabled and callable by anyone who can use that Hermes's dashboard or API; overview returns printer state, queue, requesters' names and words, groups, the done box, filament, moments, upgrades, design versions and the setup check (notice texts and setup details only while local_is_owner is on, chat targets never), reads printer status and queue on each call and runs the setup check (read-only Bambuddy requests, hermes cron list) in the background at most once every 5 minutes; file returns only design STLs, design previews and stored camera photos from the plugin's data folder; no route writes anything. The Desktop half (desktop/plugin.js, built with esbuild, three.js bundled) is off until turned on in Capabilities, calls only its own routes, the gateway's session.create (one hidden session titled Workshop actions (home-3d-workshop)) and slash.exec with /home3d commands only, polls overview every 15 s for its status-bar chip and every 5 s while the page is open, and runs printer actions as the local user through /home3d, so the owner check applies. Hermes internals: besides ctx.current_cron_execution(), the cron, unattended and origin-chat checks read non-public Hermes internals from sys.modules (gateway.session_context.get_session_env, also for HERMES_SESSION_CHAT_ID; cron.execution_identity._CURRENT; gateway.session_finite; and hermes_cli.plugins._resolve_hook_callback_timeout for the hook deadline); they are never imported or patched. A check that raises counts as cron or unattended (fail closed); a renamed one is skipped. Subprocesses: hermes send for notices (with -p send_profile when set, each stopped after send_timeout_s, default 20 s, and all sends of one pass within send_budget_s, default 45 s); hermes cron create, list and remove from hermes home3d setup and teardown, and hermes cron list for the setup check; openscad for the name-tag and label-box templates and for the agent's designs (and openscad --version for the setup check), and xvfb-run for the design preview pictures, when they are installed (one render at a time, a 180 s default time limit, a CPU-time limit, a memory cap and an STL size cap; a design may read files only from its own folder and OpenSCAD's own libraries, checked in the source and in OpenSCAD's list of the files it read). hermes home3d setup writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/home3d_watch.py and creates one hermes cron create --no-agent --script job, every 2 minutes by default (720 runs a day, no daily cap); it runs while the Hermes scheduler (hermes gateway) runs; setup --print-only writes nothing. The job calls no model, and empty output sends nothing. A failed notice is retried on later passes (backoff from 1 min to 4 h, at most 10 attempts within 24 h), then the owner is told once. The script reads HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (the plugin settings) and stays silent while the plugin is disabled or removed. The job and the script stay until hermes home3d teardown (after an uninstall: hermes cron remove and delete the script). Data stays local under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/home-3d-workshop: a SQLite database (requests with the platform and chat id they came from, jobs, household and group sender ids and names, approval requests, who stopped or paused a print, the outbox with every notice and its delivery state, done-box records with who a part is for and who picked it up, open human-needed moments, audit events), outbox.jsonl with every send attempt, camera photos, model files, designs (OpenSCAD source, STL, preview pictures and facts for every version), a watcher log and a settings snapshot without secrets (the watcher's fallback). pre_llm_call adds up to 900 characters of context (persona, speaker, printer state): for household members and the local owner on the first turn, on printing turns and on printer state changes, else one speaker line; for other senders only on printing turns; inject_context: never turns it off. The tools are on for every surface, and while the plugin is enabled its two skills add one line each to the skills index of every session. Tested on Linux with Hermes 0.22.5; the Workshop screen was run in Hermes 0.23.1 (Webapp) on the simulated printer, not yet in the Desktop app. Verified on a real Bambuddy 1.3.0 with an A1: printer status, queue, Bambuddy settings, lit photo with plate check, MakerWorld import, slice, scale, queue add and remove, and the watcher in dry run on a real print (finish and plate check). The templates, a sample design and the file-access probes are tested with OpenSCAD 2021.01 in CI; a part designed with home3d_design was uploaded and sliced on the real Bambuddy. Planned on the real printer: start, stop, pause and resume, watcher notices and auto-eject with this plugin; nothing new in 0.2.0 was run on it.
entries.title: Home 3D Workshop
known_issues: Bambu Lab printers through Bambuddy only (tested with Bambuddy 1.3.0 and an A1). The default backend is a simulated printer.

Real-printer status: status, queue, settings, lit photo with plate check, import, slice, scale, queue add/remove, a designed part uploaded and sliced, and the watcher in dry run on a real print are verified; start, stop/pause/resume, watcher notices and auto-eject with this plugin are planned. Nothing new in 0.2.0 was run on the real printer.

The Workshop screen was run in Hermes 0.23.1 (headless gateway and Webapp) on the simulated printer, not yet in the Hermes Desktop app. Its Desktop half is off until you turn it on in Capabilities → Plugins.
Since 0.2.0, stop and pause are open to known people only (stop_policy: known) and unknown senders cannot prepare prints (allow_guests: false).
Voice detection is in memory and sees only messages that reach the messaging gateway; a restart forgets recent voice notes.
Auto-eject needs your own tilted base and an end G-code preset; the plugin ships no G-code. Turn on Bambuddy's Require plate clear setting.
The watcher cron job runs only while the Hermes scheduler runs (hermes gateway).
Designing parts needs openscad (and xvfb-run for preview pictures) on the Hermes machine; without it the agent uses ready models and the scale tool only.
Tested on Linux only.

entries.name: home-dashboard
entries.description: Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Hermes Web and Desktop.
entries.capability_summary: home-dashboard (community, maintained by albertocvrrbs) Personalizable rice-style Home page with draggable, resizable glass widgets for Hermes Web and Desktop. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars.

entries.name: homeassistant-statistics
entries.description: Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access.
entries.capability_summary: homeassistant-statistics (community, maintained by goncami) Read-only Home Assistant Recorder statistics tools (ha_list_statistics and ha_get_statistics). Disclosure — each call opens an authenticated WebSocket connection to the configured Home Assistant instance using the active profile HASS_TOKEN; returned statistic metadata and values become agent tool results and may reach the configured model provider. No telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credential storage or direct database access. This plugin registers tool(s): ha_list_statistics, ha_get_statistics; requires env var(s): HASS_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5.

entries.name: homeassistant
entries.description: Home Assistant gateway platform (state-change events in, persistent notifications and cron notify delivery out) plus the homeassistant toolset (ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically.
entries.capability_summary: homeassistant (official, maintained by NousResearch) Home Assistant gateway platform (state-change events in, persistent notifications and cron notify delivery out) plus the homeassistant toolset (ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. This plugin registers tool(s): ha_list_entities, ha_get_state, ha_list_services, ha_call_service; requires env var(s): HASS_TOKEN. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.name: homelab-watch
entries.description: Your homelab, your agents and your agent's bill in one Desktop status chip: read-only checks of your router, servers, websites, a Bitaxe miner and your cron jobs with root-cause rollup (a router outage is one alert, not ten); token-free alerts through a no_agent cron job; per-day LLM token counts and API-equivalent savings (subscription, cheaper and free models; unpriced models never estimated); a Scan my network button on the Homelab page that finds devices on your own network (VPN tunnels skipped) and adds the ones you tick, six bundled skills (add-targets, diagnose with an approved-only fix handoff, watch-my-agents, weekly-report, tune-thresholds, bitaxe-advice), a first-run welcome note (a pre_llm_call hook, shown once per install), and the jev_route delegation backend, shadow by default, that sends simple subagent tasks to a cheaper model when a judge clears them. Disclosure — probes only the hosts and URLs in targets.yaml, except that the Desktop "Scan my network" button, when pressed and confirmed, pings and connects to ten common ports on every address of one private /24 the machine is on (VPN tunnels skipped) and appends only the devices you tick to targets.yaml; records token counts and model names from post_api_request, never prompt text; with alerts on, writes one script under scripts/ and creates one cron job via cronjob_manage; sends nothing off the machine by default, but with the optional TypeSafe key and delegation.backend jev_route each subagent task's goal and context (up to 4,000 characters) go to api.typesafe.ai for one judgment; no telemetry.

entries.name: honeytrap
entries.description: Catch a hijacked agent by the fake credentials it goes looking for. Honeytrap hides a realistic ops note (prod-access.md) in the agent's workspace with six decoys (deploy ref, signing key, AWS id, database URL, admin portal, license key) in shapes Hermes's redactor leaves visible, and never mentions them to the model. If one shows up in any tool call, plain or disguised (base64, hex, URL-encoded, reversed, split, zero-width or Unicode-tag smuggled, lookalike letters, or leaked in fragments across calls), or the decoy file is sent out by path (curl -F @file, cat | nc), the call is blocked (pre_tool_call), the session's outbound tools are quarantined until /honeytrap release, the chat gets an alert with the attack chain (untrusted source, decoy read, blocked egress) and an OCSF-style Detection Finding is written for your SIEM. /honeytrap plants, tests, lists incidents and switches mode; hermes honeytrap generates, rotates and removes decoys. Disclosure - writes one decoy file into the agent workspace when you run /honeytrap plant (through the agent's write_file) or hermes honeytrap init --dir/plant; stores the decoys, their placements and incidents (tool name, decoy kind, encoding, destination host, chain of tool names; never arguments or conversation text) in its own plugin data. No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials or telemetry. Disclosure — adds pre_tool_call/post_tool_call hooks that scan every tool call's arguments and results (up to 256 KB each) for its own decoys; in the default enforce mode it blocks a call carrying a decoy, blocks the session's outbound tools after a critical hit until /honeytrap release (in-memory, cleared on restart, and release lifts every session), and blocks every tool call if the guard itself errors (switch to monitor mode to recover); /honeytrap plant (through the agent's write_file) or hermes honeytrap init --dir/plant writes a decoy file prod-access.md into the chosen workspace; stores decoy values, placements and incidents (tool name, decoy kind, encoding, destination host, tool-name chain; never arguments or conversation text) under its plugin data dir; no network, subprocesses, tools, credential reads or telemetry.

entries.name: house-rules
entries.description: House rules your agent can't forget. Refuses tool calls that match your rules (a command with flags such as git push --force or rm -r, or a regex on a tool argument such as a .env path) or that leave the folders you allow. The refusal tells the agent why and to ask you; you lift a rule for the current session with /rules unlock <n>. /rule turns plain words into a rule draft as YAML and replays it on past tool calls; you paste it into the profile config.yaml yourself, the plugin never writes it. Rules apply from the next session. For an agent that forgets or ignores instructions; it is not a security boundary (scripts, aliases and indirect effects are not seen). Disclosure — no network call of its own, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry, no background task. Hook pre_tool_call reads each tool call's name and arguments and refuses matches; a refusal notice (tool name and reason, never the arguments) is posted to the conversation with ctx.post_message. /rule makes one LLM call through ctx.llm.complete_structured with the user's words, and reads the profile's state.db read-only to replay the draft (other profiles' state.db only if the user picks them). Reads its settings with ctx.get_config and the profile config.yaml read-only. Writes nothing to disk.
entries.title: House Rules
known_issues: Not a security boundary: aliases, scripts, variables and other programs with the same effect are not seen.
Rules are read once per session; config.yaml edits apply from the next session.

entries.name: household-tiers
entries.description: Per-person tool tiers for one shared Hermes bot, with a family preset for curfew, a parent alert, and a homework note: built-in owner memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) withheld from non-owner prompts; an external provider block joined after those boxes is removed; a provider block with no built-in box, and compaction's auxiliary summary, are not filtered. Disclosure — gateway access policy: blocks tool calls per sender tier through pre_tool_call (fail-closed: an unreadable household-tiers.json blocks every tool call and withholds memory from every request, owner included), rewrites non-owner model requests through llm_request middleware to remove the owner's MEMORY.md/USER.md and filter tools (external memory-provider blocks with no built-in box and compaction's auxiliary summary are not filtered), resolves non-owner URL hostnames with the system resolver to refuse local targets, sends a curfew alert through the gateway's own adapter to the chat you set in `notify`, and writes household-tiers.json and a per-person audit log under the active Hermes home; /family tier and /family forget change those files and are owner-only.
known_issues: pytest (108 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped), plugins validate, and plugins doctor were run on Hermes commit ed1afb082eb3e46cf2edae9d8f68fb67b09ee4df with uv CPython 3.11.18, 3.12.16, 3.13.18, and 3.14.10. uv sync --locked refuses interpreters before 3.14 (lock environment python_full_version >= 3.14); those runs installed that lock's wheels into each interpreter. Tag v0.22.7 (b200f5bc60e31588ba2cb60e288029c4a54ba5fa) was not re-run. requires_hermes stays >=0.22.7. CPython 3.13.18 and 3.14.10 also printed 44 DeprecationWarnings from Hermes plugins_manifest.py.

hermes plugins validate still warns on tools.memory_tool_store.ENTRY_DELIMITER in __init__.py (three sites). That constant is not on a public plugin surface. Memory files are get_hermes_home() / memories, the same path as get_memory_dir(). The plugin does not call MemoryStore._parse_entries. Measurement imports live under tests/ and are not part of plugin load.

With plugins.isolation set to host the plugin host does not forward the per-turn sender, so household-tiers fails closed (everyone is a guest) and the parent alert is skipped. Use isolation in_process for per-person tiers.

Shared sessions (a thread with thread_sessions_per_user false, or a group with group_sessions_per_user false) carry replies to other people. Non-owner tiers are refused there by default (shared_threads refuse) and asked to use a direct message.

If household-tiers.json is unreadable, tool calls are blocked and memory blocks are withheld from every request, including the owner's, and every gateway turn gets a short error reply until the file is fixed.

HTTP redirects onto the local network, and DNS names that change address between check and connect, are not re-validated. A non-owner web tool resolves the hostname once with the system resolver and does not fetch the URL. See the README known issues.

Memory stripping and tool filtering were executed on chat_completions, anthropic_messages, codex_responses, and bedrock_converse payloads from Hermes commit ed1afb08, including multi-paragraph entries joined with §. The strip stops at the memory block; the date line and runtime block stay. A kid message that quotes an entry does not refuse the turn. Gemini conversion was not executed. Relative paths use ctx.session_cwd() and os.path.realpath. Case-folding was tested with a monkeypatched normcase on Linux, not on macOS.
Desktop and TUI turns resolve to guest once the process has served a messaging turn. A turn with no sender is then guest, not the local owner.

The default user tier has no read_file or search_files. A non-owner tier that adds them may only read file_roots (default empty, so no path is allowed). The active profile home, credential directories, and browser profiles are always refused, including a search root that contains them. The named path is realpath'd. search_files also walks the directory and refuses a symlink that leaves file_roots or touches a blocked path. The walk stops and refuses past 20000 entries. A search_files path that contains a comma is checked part by part; with no comma, two or more whitespace-separated pieces are checked as well as the raw string. target is the search mode, not a path, and a missing or blank path is checked as `.`. file_roots does not apply to other tools, such as terminal.

Context compaction's auxiliary summary request does not pass through llm_request, so the summary model still sees owner memory and MEMORY PROVIDER CONTEXT. post_compaction is observer-only. On a later main request, a message recognized as a compaction handoff has built-in entry text of 8 or more characters, and memory-provider-context tags, redacted in that span. A paraphrase is not detected. That auxiliary call was not executed.

An external provider system_prompt_block() joined after the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md boxes is removed with those boxes. A provider block with no built-in box in the prompt is not located. Pieces of 8 or more characters from MEMORY.md or USER.md are redacted anywhere in an injected system section, including SOUL, AGENTS.md, and skills text when they match.

Disclosure — gateway access policy: blocks tool calls per sender tier through pre_tool_call (fail-closed: an unreadable household-tiers.json blocks every tool call and withholds memory from every request, owner included), rewrites non-owner model requests through llm_request middleware to remove the owner's MEMORY.md/USER.md and filter tools (external memory-provider blocks with no built-in box and compaction's auxiliary summary are not filtered), resolves non-owner URL hostnames with the system resolver to refuse local targets, sends a curfew alert through the gateway's own adapter to the chat you set in `notify`, and writes household-tiers.json and a per-person audit log under the active Hermes home; /family tier and /family forget change those files and are owner-only. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, subagent_start, pre_gateway_dispatch, post_gateway_admission; middleware: llm_request. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7. Known issues: pytest (108 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped), plugins validate, and plugins doctor were run on Hermes commit ed1afb082eb3e46cf2edae9d8f68fb67b09ee4df with uv CPython 3.11.18, 3.12.16, 3.13.18, and 3.14.10. uv sync --locked refuses interpreters before 3.14 (lock environment python_full_version >= 3.14); those runs installed that lock's wheels into each interpreter. Tag v0.22.7 (b200f5bc60e31588ba2cb60e288029c4a54ba5fa) was not re-run. requires_hermes stays >=0.22.7. CPython 3.13.18 and 3.14.10 also printed 44 DeprecationWarnings from Hermes plugins_manifest.py.; hermes plugins validate still warns on tools.memory_tool_store.ENTRY_DELIMITER in __init__.py (three sites). That constant is not on a public plugin surface. Memory files are get_hermes_home() / memories, the same path as get_memory_dir(). The plugin does not call MemoryStore._parse_entries. Measurement imports live under tests/ and are not part of plugin load.; With plugins.isolation set to host the plugin host does not forward the per-turn sender, so household-tiers fails closed (everyone is a guest) and the parent alert is skipped. Use isolation in_process for per-person tiers.; Shared sessions (a thread with thread_sessions_per_user false, or a group with group_sessions_per_user false) carry replies to other people. Non-owner tiers are refused there by default (shared_threads refuse) and asked to use a direct message.; If household-tiers.json is unreadable, tool calls are blocked and memory blocks are withheld from every request, including the owner's, and every gateway turn gets a short error reply until the file is fixed.; HTTP redirects onto the local network, and DNS names that change address between check and connect, are not re-validated. A non-owner web tool resolves the hostname once with the system resolver and does not fetch the URL. See the README known issues.; Memory stripping and tool filtering were executed on chat_completions, anthropic_messages, codex_responses, and bedrock_converse payloads from Hermes commit ed1afb08, including multi-paragraph entries joined with §. The strip stops at the memory block; the date line and runtime block stay. A kid message that quotes an entry does not refuse the turn. Gemini conversion was not executed. Relative paths use ctx.session_cwd() and os.path.realpath. A turn with no sender is then guest, not the local owner.; The default user tier has no read_file or search_files. A non-owner tier that adds them may only read file_roots (default empty, so no path is allowed). The active profile home, credential directories, and browser profiles are always refused, including a search root that contains them. The named path is realpath'd. search_files also walks the directory and refuses a symlink that leaves file_roots or touches a blocked path. The walk stops and refuses past 20000 entries. A search_files path that contains a comma is checked part by part; with no comma, two or more whitespace-separated pieces are checked as well as the raw string. target is the search mode, not a path, and a missing or blank path is checked as `.`. file_roots does not apply to other tools, such as terminal.; Context compaction's auxiliary summary request does not pass through llm_request, so the summary model still sees owner memory and MEMORY PROVIDER CONTEXT. post_compaction is observer-only. On a later main request, a message recognized as a compaction handoff has built-in entry text of 8 or more characters, and memory-provider-context tags, redacted in that span. A paraphrase is not detected. That auxiliary call was not executed.; An external provider system_prompt_block() joined after the built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md boxes is removed with those boxes. A provider block with no built-in box in the prompt is not located. Pieces of 8 or more characters from MEMORY.md or USER.md are redacted anywhere in an injected system section, including SOUL, AGENTS.md, and skills text when they match..

entries.name: housemate
entries.description: Hands-free Hermes in every room: old phones, tablets and laptops become room speakers through their browser. Say the wake word, ask, and hear the answer in the same room. One household conversation across rooms, the nearest device answers when several hear you, timers and alarms that ring where they were set, intercom, cards on room screens, spoken approvals, and a Rooms page in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — the gateway runs an HTTPS + WebSocket hub on 0.0.0.0:8742 (self-signed certificate made on first start; its fingerprint is shown on the Rooms page and by hermes housemate cert) and a loopback control API on 127.0.0.1:8743 with a token that changes on every start; only devices paired with a six-digit code approved on the PC are heard. Each started satellite streams its microphone to the hub continuously; the hub keeps the stream in memory and hands only the question after the wake word (or a held talk button or an open answer window) to Hermes's audio cache and the STT provider configured in Hermes; replies use the configured TTS. On first start it downloads openWakeWord v0.5.1 models (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial) from the official openWakeWord GitHub release and Silero VAD v6.2.3 from the official silero-vad repository, each pinned by SHA-256, into plugin-data/housemate/models/. It registers an optional streamed Piper voice (tts.provider: housemate-piper); when chosen, a missing voice is fetched with Piper's own downloader into Hermes's cache/piper-voices. Runs ffmpeg from PATH to decode non-WAV speech. A start-up warm-up sends one quiet tone through Hermes's STT in a side chat that the plugin's pre_llm_call hook vetoes (prewarm: false turns it off); the same hook applies spoken approve, deny, clarify and stop answers to Hermes's own cards by request id through resolve_gateway_approval_card and resolve_gateway_clarify, never auto-approves, leaves an unanswered approval to Hermes's timeout (deny), and takes only a tap for commands flagged by smart approval. The agent can speak in other rooms with housemate_announce, and /announce does the same from any chat. Writes only under plugin-data/housemate/ (SQLite with rooms, devices and SHA-256 hashes of their keys, timers; the certificate and private key; the control token), except that the Rooms page's Household / Per room switch writes platforms.housemate.conversation to config.yaml; paired device ids are set as the platform's allow_from in memory. The gateway log records the first 80 characters of spoken answers to prompts. hermes housemate bench is opt-in: it downloads about 266 MB of public-domain LibriVox audio from archive.org (SHA-1 pinned), may generate test clips with Microsoft's Edge TTS service when edge-tts is installed, and pairs a device named Bench satellite. No telemetry.
entries.title: Housemate
known_issues: The wake phrase is "Hey Jarvis" (openWakeWord's stock model). A custom "Hey Hermes" model missed our accuracy bar on non-US accents and is not shipped.
openWakeWord's wake-word models are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so the wake pipeline is for non-commercial use.
Needs speech-to-text turned on in Hermes (stt.enabled, any provider) and a text-to-speech voice.
On Hermes 0.23.0 the Rooms page uses the plugin's REST routes; the plugin RPC path for newer builds is unit-tested only. Tested in the Webapp, not in the native Desktop app.
The first answer after a gateway restart takes about 7 s.
Tested on Windows 11 with Chrome; macOS and Safari are untested.

entries.name: htmi
entries.description: Review the HTML pages your agent writes, on the page itself: comment on the exact element, chart, table row or passage; Hermes is told about new comments, reads each one with its context, makes checked edits and replies. Pages can also be published as a GitHub issue or pull request description, and comments posted there are pulled back. Adds 11 tools, a pre_llm_call notice, a pre_tool_call approval gate, a skill, the /htmi command and a Review tab in the dashboard. Disclosure — runs its bundled engine (bundle/htmi.mjs, built from the repo's src/) with Node and runs git and gh with a minimal environment that carries no provider keys; reads and edits documents only inside the current repository (comments go to .htmi/); opening a review page starts a local review server on 127.0.0.1 (token-protected writes) that keeps running in the background until /htmi stop or a restart; GitHub work uses your own gh CLI login and only this repository's origin plus repositories you list in github_repos: creating an issue or replacing or editing a description waits for your approval, and replies to comments that came from GitHub are posted there; no telemetry, no stored credentials, no other third-party services.

entries.name: huddo
entries.description: Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, edit or unsend your own messages, react, answer or close polls and forms, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.10.2, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo_app_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, and when a message contains a link it fetches that page once from this machine (public hosts only, skipped for links carrying a token or signature) and uploads a small preview image with the message; huddo_transfer (and huddo_leave with to) hands room ownership to another member, and huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar with operator: true change your paired human's display name or avatar; Hermes does not ask before huddo_send/huddo_answer/huddo_close_choices/huddo_whisper/huddo_react/huddo_edit/huddo_unsend/huddo_app_submit/huddo_download/huddo_transfer/huddo_leave/huddo_update_name/huddo_update_avatar/huddo_rename run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, and, if Hermes can schedule recurring tasks, to schedule one that does the same between turns, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; the server also tells the agent to read the remote guide at https://huddo.ai/SKILL.md before starting (vendor-hosted, not pinned), and the skills point to npx -y huddoai@latest (unpinned) for identity export and app publishing; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) and a local copy of your rooms' messages (used by huddo_search/huddo_show/huddo_files; huddo_sync fetches older history from api.huddo.ai) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry; requests to api.huddo.ai carry an x-huddo-client header (cli/mcp/<version>) that the server counts for usage statistics, with no identity or content in it. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skills tell the agent to get confirmation in your own Hermes chat before anything sensitive.

entries.name: huntapi
entries.description: Tools to read the metadata of public videos and download their video or audio, through the HuntAPI media API. entries.name: hwiki
entries.description: Markdown wiki as Hermes long-term memory: plain files you and the agent edit together (Obsidian-compatible, git-versionable), local SQLite FTS5 search with optional qmd hybrid retrieval. Inspired by the Karpathy LLM wiki. Disclosure — reads every Markdown file under the wiki folder you set (wiki_path, outside HERMES_HOME; untrusted_dirs, default raw/, excluded) and injects up to ~1,400 characters of matching excerpts into each turn; the agent appends dated notes only under <wiki>/<memory_dir> (default wiki/memory), and additions to Hermes's built-in memory are mirrored there by default (mirror_builtin_memory), so they land in a folder you may commit or sync; keeps an index at HERMES_HOME/hwiki-index.sqlite and config in HERMES_HOME/hwiki.json, and adds the wiki folder to hermes backup. Cron and subagent runs get read-only recall. No network with the default fts5 backend; the optional qmd backend runs the separately installed qmd CLI (npm @tobilu/qmd, Node ≥22), whose vector modes download local models (~0.3–1.6 GB).

entries.name: hyatlas
entries.description: HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `hermes memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Hermes's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through Hermes's get_secret and reads no Hermes credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as Hermes auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `hermes memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Nous Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. A server the plugin starts gets that key in its environment; for a server started another way (the launcher, a service) that reports "awaiting_key", the plugin (at most every 10 minutes) and `hermes hyatlas doctor` POST the key over plain HTTP to /api/v1/llm/key, only when the configured server host is this machine; the server accepts it only from a loopback address and keeps it in memory only, never on disk. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS_CONSOLIDATE_GRAPH=off disables that). Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions, recent summaries and newest facts to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS_NOW_EVERY), and, after a 30-minute pause in an owner's writes (HYATLAS_EPISODE_GAP; off disables it), up to 40 of that stretch's facts to write one episode summary. HYATLAS_RECONCILE=on (off by default) adds a second LLM call per write that sends the new facts together with similar stored ones (including those under user IDs grouped with the owner by HYATLAS_USER_ALIASES) so the model can update, replace or link them; it is meant for a local model. An optional HYATLAS_LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. Turns written while the endpoint was unreachable or before a key arrived are extracted later by a catch-up pass (every 10 minutes by default, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_EVERY; rows up to 7 days old, HYATLAS_CATCHUP_MAX_AGE), sending the same text a write would have sent. `hermes hyatlas doctor` sends one short test prompt ("Reply with the single word OK.") to the endpoint and writes, finds and deletes one test memory. When you replace or remove an entry with Hermes's memory tool, the plugin asks the local server to retire the matching memory (reversible); nothing leaves the machine. HYATLAS_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS_*), not the agent's keys. auto_start is off by default; when on, Hermes starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto_start or `hermes hyatlas start` keeps running after Hermes exits until `hermes hyatlas stop`. entries.title: HyAtlas Memory
known_issues: After enabling, select the provider with `hermes memory setup` (memory.provider: hyatlas) — installing and enabling alone does not activate memory.
The agent tools and hooks arrive through the MemoryProvider interface, not ctx.register_tool, so they do not appear in the plugin tool list.
Requires the separate hyatlas-go server binary (installed by the user); without a reachable server the provider reports unavailable and memory features degrade rather than fail.

Updating the plugin does not update the server: install hyatlas-go v5.0.0 too. A store written by an earlier version can be cleaned with the server's maintenance endpoints (see after-install.md, 'Upgrading a store written before 4.5.0').
5.0 removed share_llm_key: the plugin no longer uses Hermes's Nous sign-in. Set your own extraction key (llm_key) with `hermes memory setup`; `hermes hyatlas doctor` checks it.
entries.capability_summary: hyatlas (community, maintained by tuancookiez-hub) HyAtlas 5 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories are kept locally. Ships agent tools (hyatlas_status/search/recent/add), a `hermes hyatlas` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings are computed locally; stored memories leave the machine only in the LLM calls described below. Extraction is opt-in and uses an LLM you choose: `hermes memory setup` asks for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, model and key, and stores the key in Hermes's .env as HYATLAS_LLM_KEY. The plugin reads that key only through Hermes's get_secret and reads no Hermes credential. A plain key file named by HYATLAS_LLM_KEY_FILE also works; the server reads it on every call, so do not point it at another program's credentials such as Hermes auth.json. The server has no default endpoint and makes no LLM call until the endpoint, the model and a key are all present; while the endpoint and model are set but no key has arrived, /api/v1/status reports llm "awaiting_key". `hermes memory setup`, the repo installer and the sample launcher pre-fill a free Nous Portal endpoint and model (and setup defaults to ultra mode), but nothing is sent until a key is supplied. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters), together with up to 5 related stored facts, 3 entity pages and 5 open intentions of that owner so the model can update them instead of duplicating them. In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. Once a day per owner (HYATLAS_CROSS_SCHEMA_EVERY; off disables it) ultra also sends up to 40 of that owner's stored patterns to find up to 3 that hold across topics. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, `hermes hyatlas start/stop` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads no credentials (since 4.8.0 it no longer reads Hermes auth.json). entries.name: hybridops
entries.description: Inspect, export and import Containerlab recovery sets through an existing HybridOps runtime. Export and import are disabled by default and require Hermes approval when enabled; input and execution-contract digests prevent an approved operation from running after its files or target settings change. Disclosure - Linux only; reads operator-configured input files and HybridOps module state, then runs the configured local hyops executable with fixed argument lists and no shell. HybridOps and Ansible may connect to the configured target, run Containerlab save or snapshot commands, and write recovery data on the target and controller; import may replace the declared native lab directory after validation. The plugin makes no direct network calls, starts no background process, sends no telemetry, does not update itself, and does not install HybridOps or its Ansible collections.

entries.name: hyperactive
entries.description: Hermes, but it texts you first. Keeps your goals (life > year > quarter > week), promises both ways and decisions with review dates, and speaks first on Hermes's own cron: a daily brief, check-ins, decision reviews, nudges on stalled goals, and tap cards with a recommended answer. An unanswered card is re-asked after an hour and, only if low stakes, applied an hour later as a typed action the plugin performs itself (move or schedule its own reminder, set a goal's status); money, public and irreversible calls always wait for the person. Every message names the goal it serves and /ha why explains it. Disclosure — stores data in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/hyperactive/; on first use or `hermes hyperactive setup` writes two 4-line shims to HERMES_HOME/scripts/ and creates two recurring cron jobs: hyperactive-pulse (no-agent, no model call) and hyperactive-brief (agent mode, one model call a day through Hermes's configured model, skipped when there is nothing to brief; brief_at empty turns it off); once set up, re-creates a missing job or shim on session start; the `hermes hyperactive` CLI runs `hermes cron` subprocesses; pre_llm_call appends a few lines of due items to turns and records a card answer when the message is exactly an option; reads Telegram reactions via gateway_platform_event. No network calls or telemetry of its own; no secrets; `hermes hyperactive uninstall` removes both jobs and shims.

known_issues: A Telegram reaction answers the most recently asked card only (Hermes does not pass the delivered message id), and the reaction path has not been tested against a live bot yet.

entries.name: hyperrizz
entries.description: Hyperrizz: tell Hermes the story and watch your HyperFrames film take shape in a live review pane, then get a verified MP4. Hermes researches, art-directs, writes the scenes, builds, checks and iterates on a HyperFrames project while the pane plays the actual composition with sound, a scrubber and frame stepping. Pause on a moment, write a note and press Iterate with Hermes: the note carries the project, revision and exact frame back into the chat. Full editor opens HyperFrames Studio inside the pane (timeline, assets, code, layers, inspector), and the agent reconciles your manual edits before it rebuilds. Renders are separate, cancellable jobs; a failed build keeps the last working revision and a failed export keeps the last verified MP4. Three tools: hyperrizz_project (create, inspect, edit, restore and reconcile projects), hyperrizz_review (open the pane, exchange frame notes, hand off to Studio) and hyperrizz_produce (build, check, render, inspect jobs, cancel), plus the hyperrizz:production skill with its guides, a broadcast kit and starter templates. Use it for product promos, release announcements, music-led cuts, and restyling or rescuing an existing film. To start, you need Hermes 0.23.0 or newer, Node 22 or newer, Python 3.11 or newer and FFmpeg; Linux is the tested platform. Run hermes plugins install hyperrizz and hermes plugins enable hyperrizz, enable Hyperrizz under Capabilities → Plugins to show the pane, then ask: "Use Hyperrizz to make a 30-second film about this release. Show the live project as you work, then deliver the MP4." The first build installs the pinned npm dependencies. No API keys or hosted generation. Disclosure — processes: spawns local Node, Chromium and FFmpeg child processes with a minimal non-secret environment; runs background build, check and render workers and an optional loopback Studio sidecar (token-gated, 512 KiB capture budget, no redirects); the embedded HyperFrames Studio server listens on loopback without a token. Disclosure — code execution: project write can edit the project's scripts/*.mjs and package.json, and build, check and render run them with Node at your full privileges (no filesystem or network sandbox), the same power as file writes plus the terminal. npm downloads pinned dependencies on first build, and npm ci runs package lifecycle scripts. Disclosure — data: projects are stored in profile-scoped plugin data; the Desktop pane uses ctx.rest only; a post_tool_call hook binds projects to the host session. No credentials, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: hyprland
entries.description: Hyprland-native computer use for Hermes: grim capture, wlr-virtual-pointer clicks/drags/scroll, wtype text, and window-scoped target enforcement. No XWayland, accessibility tree, root, or /dev/uinput. Disclosure — the pointer helper is C source you build locally (`make -C <plugin>/pointer`) and the plugin runs it, or the binary named in `computer_use.hyprland.pointer_bin` / `HYPRLAND_CU_POINTER_BIN`, to inject pointer events; screenshots of the screen or the targeted window go to your model like any computer-use backend; capturing a named app focuses its window; and text that starts with `-` (or that wtype refuses) is typed by pasting through the Wayland clipboard, which overwrites your clipboard and leaves that text in it.
entries.title: Hyprland Computer Use
known_issues: The pointer helper is C source and must be built locally: make -C ~/.hermes/plugins/hyprland/pointer (catalog rule 17 forbids shipping binaries).

entries.name: hypruse
entries.description: Hyprland computer use through the hypruse CLI: controls from the accessibility tree clicked by number, typing and keys sent to one window, and a background mode where the agent works in apps on its own workspaces (99 down to 90) while your cursor, focus and workspace stay put. Select it with `hermes config set computer_use.backend hypruse`. Disclosure: the provider is pure Python with no third-party dependencies. Each action runs the separately installed `hypruse` command (0.13 or newer), or the one named in `computer_use.hypruse.command` or HERMES_HYPRUSE_CMD, as a subprocess with no shell, and that child gets only the desktop session variables and HYPRUSE_* settings, never Hermes' API keys; `hermes computer-use doctor` also runs `hypruse doctor`. hypruse clicks, types and presses keys in your live session, and a foreground pointer action moves your cursor. With the optional `computer_use.hypruse.delivery: auto`, an action on the window you are in runs on your screen. Screenshots of the targeted window, or of the focused monitor for `app='screen'`, go to your model like any computer-use backend's, and each capture file is deleted once read. It reads hypruse's state file `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypruse/cli-state.json` and never writes it. No network calls, telemetry, stored data or credentials.
entries.title: hypruse
known_issues: Needs Hyprland and the hypruse command 0.13 or newer on PATH (PyPI, AUR or Nix), which this plugin does not install. Check it with hermes computer-use doctor.
set_value is not supported: hypruse has no verb that sets a value. Click the field and type, or click the control.
Modifier keys held during a click, drag or scroll, and triple clicks, are not supported.

The pointer never works in the background: coordinate clicks, drags and scrolls need delivery_mode='foreground' on the window you are in, and right, middle and double clicks by element work only in the foreground.
som captures (marks) are sent at full size; max_image_dimension applies to vision captures only.
computer_use has no launch action: run hypruse launch -- APP with the terminal tool to open an app on the agent's workspaces, then capture(app='APP').
Does not load under plugins.isolation: host, because Hermes loads computer-use providers only in its own process.

entries.name: iacg-board
entries.description: Web dashboard tab showing the IaC Genius mission board: findings, validation evidence with tool + version, repair attempts spent/allowed, disposition and next owner. It renders the snapshot the iacg-desk service writes and never invents live state; an empty state is shown until a snapshot exists. Disclosure — read-only dashboard tab: reads the iacg-desk board snapshot (board.json/board.html) over the local Unix socket or the shared data dir, renders it in a sandboxed iframe (scripts allowed, no same-origin access) and accepts messages only from that iframe; registers no agent tools or hooks, makes no network calls, runs no subprocess, no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — talks to the local iacg desk service over a Unix socket (or runs python -m iacg_desk as a subprocess); the desk's terraform init downloads providers read-only from the public Terraform registry into a shared cache; while the plugin is enabled it refuses terraform/tofu apply and cloud write commands in every terminal call of every session, not only IaC Genius missions; approve, confirm and deliver each raise Hermes' approval prompt so a person must grant them; model-supplied tree/out paths are confined to the desk work dir and validation tools run with a secret-free environment; delivery pushes a branch and opens a pull request on GitHub with the IACG_GITHUB_TOKEN secret only after the gates pass and a human approves; no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: iacg-desk
entries.description: IaCGenius runs deterministic Terraform/OpenTofu missions on Hermes: a decision ledger asks the costly or irreversible questions before spend, freezes the agreed scope as one build-sheet hash, grounds every argument on the pinned binary provider schema, runs terraform validate / tflint / checkov / secret scan as evidence, repairs within a bounded budget, and delivers a reviewable PR whose body is the ledger. The model proposes; the toolchain decides. Disclosure — talks to a local Unix socket served by the iacg_desk desk service (or runs python -m iacg_desk as a subprocess); reads its own local.json + IACG_* config paths (not secrets); the desk's terraform init fetches providers read-only from the public registry into a shared cache; hard-refuses terraform/tofu apply and cloud write commands at pre_tool_call, and escalates approve/confirm/deliver to Hermes's human approval gate so a person must grant them (never model-self-approved); model-supplied tree/out paths are confined to the desk work dir; validation tools run under a secret-free allowlisted env; holds no cloud credentials and never changes cloud state; GitHub delivery uses a token read through Hermes's secret scope only after the gates and a human approval, then reads the commit back; the board briefing is injected via pre_llm_call on the first turn; no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: ichor
entries.description: Catches the moments you correct Hermes (a correction, /retry or /undo), pairs the rejected answer with the accepted one, scrubs secrets and personal data locally, and asks you once to keep, share or discard it with a one-letter reply. Kept pairs export as TRL preference JSONL and an Atropos environment, ready to fine-tune or run RL on your own model. Disclosure — captures your corrections (rejected and accepted answers, your feedback) into a local SQLite store in its plugin data directory after local secret/PII scrubbing, posts and edits its own card messages in the chat, and claims the bare replies k, s, d, keep, share or discard in a direct chat within 120 seconds of an open card; asks the session model for a one-word mistake label per captured pair via the optional llm.side_question capability (spends main-model tokens); makes network calls only on /ichor share, uploading scrubbed pairs to a Hugging Face dataset under the HF_TOKEN owner's account (private unless /ichor set public); the store is shared per profile, so on a multi-user gateway every allowlisted user can review, share or publish pairs captured from other users' chats.

entries.name: icon-index
entries.description: 40 free CC0 3D icons in one matching style for websites, apps, slides and videos. Browse them spinning in a Hermes Desktop pane, recolour them (8 presets or any colour) and download the result, and let the agent find an icon by meaning, return embed code (iframe, model-viewer, React, three.js) and download links, show it as a draggable 3D card in chat (::icon-index directive), or save its files into a project folder. Disclosure — the pane, chat card and icon_save fetch icon files (GLB, PNG, MP4) from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/minutechreview/3d-icons at a pinned commit; the 3D viewer is https://motion.minutechbuilds.com/icons/viewer.html shown in a SandboxedFrame (opaque origin, allow-scripts, plus allow-downloads in the pane so its Download GLB button can save a recoloured model) and it loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; icon_save writes only into the folder the agent names and never overwrites a file; search, metadata and embed code come from the bundled data/icons.json. No shell, credentials, telemetry or background work.

entries.name: idea-board
entries.description: A nightly board of things your agent can take off your plate, each tied to your own words. Code finds signals in your last 14 days of chats (things asked on several days, remind-me loops, upcoming dates, corrections, failing tools, things the agent said it couldn't reach); a model drafts ideas, a second pass critiques them, and code checks every idea (evidence ids must exist, named capabilities must be installed, links and @file/@url references you never typed are rejected). Click an idea and a new chat opens with the prompt in the composer; you press send, nothing is sent for you. Dismiss with a reason and it becomes a rule applied on every later run. Also ranks which Portal connector to add next by how many ideas it would unlock that match your chats (no model call). Desktop board and setup page plus a Python half. Disclosure — no network calls of its own and no telemetry; all model calls go through Hermes (two per run, ideation and critique, on the auxiliary task idea_board; unset it follows your main model; about 70–80k tokens for two weeks of heavy use). Reads outside its own data: state.db chats from the last 7/14/30 days you pick (scheduled-job runs, subagents, hidden and group chats skipped; only text you typed is quoted, other content is wrapped as untrusted), this profile's toolsets, MCP servers, connectors, skills, messaging platforms and scheduled jobs, Hermes's suggested cron jobs, and memories/USER.md; some of that goes to your configured model inside the ideation prompt. Three imports of undocumented Hermes internals (hermes_cli.tools_config._get_platform_tools, toolsets.resolve_toolset, cron.suggestions.load_suggestions) trigger the catalog's rule 9 warning; each has a tested fallback (tests/test_compat.py) and a public-API request is open at NousResearch/hermes-agent#149576. Stores ideas, dismissals, rules and run history in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/idea-board/data.db. A pre_llm_call hook only links a chat started from a card back to its card (no injection). Nothing is scheduled until you press Schedule it in setup, which creates one cron job (nightly, time you pick) through Hermes's cron API; that job wakes the agent for one short turn (about 30k prompt tokens, mostly cached) to call idea_board_run. No shell commands, no stored credentials, no background process of its own.
known_issues: Three undocumented Hermes internals are imported (see the disclosure); each falls back cleanly if a release moves it.
Desktop connected to a remote Hermes: install the agent half on the server, and the Desktop half from Git on the laptop (the desktop half of a remote plugin can't be read from another machine).

entries.name: ideacut
entries.description: Turns a chat brief into an editable, art-directed video: seven agent tools capture and record a public page, write typed scenes, revise them and export H.264 MP4 locally with Chromium and FFmpeg. Capture goes through a loopback validating proxy that refuses private/loopback/metadata targets. Optional narration is sent to the user's configured TTS provider; the live preview is silent. Disclosure — ideacut_capture and ideacut_record open model-chosen public web pages in your installed Chrome/Edge (headless) and can scroll, click and type into them (forms included); every connection goes through a loopback-only proxy that refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses. Scene images, clips and music may be any local file path the agent names and are copied into the plugin's data folder. Rendering runs your system FFmpeg/ffprobe. Voice-over (off by default) sends each scene's narration text to your configured Hermes TTS provider (directly via edge-tts when that provider is Edge).

Clip audio is discarded on import. Desktop/mobile capture requires separate host tools or imported recordings.

entries.name: idealphase-elevenlabs-audio-tags
entries.description: Hermes plugin that adds a few honest ElevenLabs delivery tags so speech sounds more human. It does not replace the built-in ElevenLabs voice provider, and it does not change the chat transcript. Disclosure — sends the prepared speech, voice ID, model ID, and any pronunciation-dictionary locator to api.elevenlabs.io with your ELEVENLABS_API_KEY; synthesis is billed to your ElevenLabs account. When automatic tags are on, the untagged transcript is also sent to the model configured for auxiliary.idealphase_elevenlabs_audio_tags, or your normal chat model if you did not pin one. entries.name: ikigai
entries.description: Getting-to-know-you interview and periodic check-ins that build a detailed, sourced picture of the person using Hermes. 76 questions in 11 modules with a 12-question express path (English and French). The interview runs itself: a pre_llm_call hook consumes each answer and returns the next question, so no model call is spent on it and a reply cannot drift into another topic. Every answer is stored locally with the user's exact words and a source tag (declared, inferred, corrected); guesses are held back until confirmed. /ikigai compile proposes a merge into USER.md that fits the 1,375-character limit and touches only the lines Ikigai owns (applied by the agent through the built-in memory tool, so write approval still applies), a SOUL.md draft that is never applied automatically, and detailed sheets kept outside the prompt. /ikigai show reads the profile back in the chat. Weekly 3-question check-ins and an offer to turn a thrice-repeated correction into a lasting rule. Disclosure: no network calls, no telemetry, no dependencies; reads USER.md (to show a diff) and the current turn's user message (local keyword matching to count corrections); writes only under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ikigai/ (0600 files, 0700 directory); answers tagged local-only never reach USER.md, SOUL.md or the sheets.

entries.name: imagegen
entries.description: Image studio for Hermes Desktop: generate, compose from references, edit and upscale across FAL, Nous Portal, Magnific, Vertex AI, the Hermes image providers and a local image server of your own, with a guided prompt builder, campaign grids, a gallery and a local monthly budget. It can also serve the agent's image_generate calls when picked under Tools → Image Generation. Disclosure — Each generation is billed by the provider you pick (FAL, Magnific, Nous Portal, Vertex AI or a Hermes image provider). On its screen each one starts from a button you click; the agent spends only if you pick ImageGen under Tools → Image Generation or add the optional MCP server; prompts and reference images go to that provider (queue.fal.run, fal.run, api.magnific.com, aiplatform.googleapis.com, or a Hermes image provider, including Nous Portal and a linked ChatGPT subscription through Hermes's own providers). With the optional local server address set, prompts for its models go only to that address, at no cost. Prompt writing and image reading use your Hermes model through ctx.llm. Images, history and the spending ledger are stored in plugin-data/imagegen. Optional FAL_KEY, MAGNIFIC_API_KEY, VERTEX_API_KEY, VERTEX_PROJECT and IMAGEGEN_LOCAL_SERVER_KEY are plugin secrets. An optional command line runs single or batch generations only when someone starts it, as the `hermes imagegen` subcommand. It imports some non-public Hermes modules to read the image provider registry and the FAL catalog.

entries.name: inbox-sentinel
entries.description: Watches a Gmail inbox (history polling over a read-only OAuth grant) or an IMAP mailbox over TLS, filters routine mail locally, asks your configured model whether the rest needs attention, and sends a notification through a configured `hermes send` target, with an optional reply draft for review. Never sends, labels, archives or deletes mail. IS-ScamShield, a deterministic pre-gate check, flags password-protected-PDF and undisclosed-recipients lures as POSSIBLE SCAM warnings and never drafts replies to them; over-warning is intentional, so false positives (e.g. legitimate password-protected statements) are expected. Eight toggleable modules: IS-ScamShield, IS-AttachmentGuard and IS-LinkGuard warn on lure shapes (password-protected PDFs, dangerous attachments, suspicious links); IS-NoiseFilter, IS-SenderLearning and IS-StormShield keep the channel quiet (local drops, learned rules, identical-repeat storm suppression that never hides first arrivals or security warnings); IS-Drafter drafts the optional reply (withhold rules, budgeted through the host's daily draft cap) and IS-AlertShaper formats the EMAIL ALERT text — both post-gate, both degrading to the host's previous behaviour when disabled or failing. Modules get bounded state, config and model-seam access — transport, model budgets and delivery stay host-owned. Gate and drafts run in two plugin-owned auxiliary model slots that follow the main model until pinned; daily attempt caps bound model calls. Sends one "not watching your inbox" alert a day if the mailbox can't be reached. Disclosure — runs a long-lived background poll after a session event; calls gmail.googleapis.com through a Hermes-managed gmail.readonly grant from the user's own Google Cloud Desktop client, or the user's IMAP server with a profile-scoped password; message text goes to the configured model provider; alerts run `hermes send` as a child process with the text on argv and may be stored by the destination; sender rules and counters are kept in profile plugin state; no telemetry.
entries.title: Inbox Sentinel
known_issues: Gmail needs the user's own Google Cloud Desktop OAuth client and a terminal sign-in (`hermes auth add inbox-sentinel:gmail`). In Testing mode Google expires the grant after seven days.
If the Gmail history cursor expires, the baseline is rebuilt and mail received in the gap can be missed.
Tested on macOS with Hermes v0.23.0 only. IMAP is tested against a scripted loopback TLS server, not an external provider.

entries.name: inboxapp
entries.description: Inboxapp, the shared inbox and CRM for X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp DMs, through Inboxapp's official MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.inboxapp.com/mcp): list, search and read threads; send, edit, unsend and react to messages from the user's connected accounts; update contacts (status, tags, notes, valuation, assignee); archive, assign and delete threads; manage the team's tags and statuses. Bundles four skills: inboxapp (connect and pick the right skill), triage, reply and pipeline. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Inboxapp's server at mcp.inboxapp.com, and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, so it is not covered by the pinned sha. It sends, edits and unsends real messages from the user's linked X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp accounts and can delete threads, tags and statuses; the agent gets the same access as the user in the chosen team. Sign-in is by OAuth on inboxapp.com (token kept by Hermes) or an Inboxapp API token. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only and refuses those tools in unattended runs; the skills may also read docs.inboxapp.com.
entries.title: Inboxapp
known_issues: Hermes runs OAuth for a remote MCP server only when config.yaml sets auth: oauth, which a package cannot set. Add mcp_servers.inboxapp with url https://mcp.inboxapp.com/mcp, auth: oauth and trust: untrusted to ~/.hermes/config.yaml, then run hermes mcp login inboxapp. That entry replaces the package's server, so keep trust: untrusted in it.
Needs an Inboxapp team with API v2 access, which is in private rollout; the server answers 404 for teams without it.

entries.name: incognito-private-mode
entries.description: Private mode, honestly: provider privacy flags, memory blocks stripped from main-chat requests (provenance-checked against the last 6 observed file versions, fail-closed outside that window), tool vetoes on unclassified tools, honest coverage labels, and consent-gated fenced history cleanup on close (exact-id + transcript + closed-state fences, archived chats excluded). Content-free outbound audit log (endpoints + verdicts only, local 0600). No telemetry; the plugin itself makes no network calls. Disclosed limits: auxiliary-call fan-out not stripped, MoA advisors receive the full unstripped request before private mode blocks the aggregation, provider-side retention guarantees impossible. Disclosure — after you record consent in setup, deletes closed private chats from Hermes history (state.db and session files) through Hermes' fenced session delete, run in a background cleanup thread; installs a process-wide log filter that redacts gateway, turn-context and tool-call log records while private mode is on; changes outgoing main-chat requests (provider privacy flags, memory blocks stripped) and blocks the memory, skill_manage and session_search tools; keeps a content-free audit log and hashed-id ledger in its own plugin-data directory (0600); makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: incognito
entries.description: Ephemeral clean-room chats and fail-closed RAM PII masking across CLI, TUI, Gateway, and Desktop: hides active sessions, blocks memory and skill writes, strips profile and personal memory in RAM in strict mode, masks outbound personal details before sending, zero-fills transcript and hook spill files before unlinking on close or sweep, and supports confirmed Save with reversible Undo. Disclosure — deletes the database rows, transcript files and hook-output files of chats marked incognito when you burn them, when they close, or on a sweep after their idle TTL expires (file contents are zero-filled first); the model cannot trigger a burn; Save moves an incognito chat into normal history and Undo (within the undo window) returns it to incognito; while any incognito chat is active it blocks terminal, file-read, search and code tools from touching Hermes session storage in every session on the host; with Mask personal details on (off by default) it replaces detected personal details with placeholders in messages and tool results before they reach the model and blocks sends it cannot check; adds no-retention flags (`store: false`, OpenRouter `data_collection: deny`) to outbound model requests from incognito chats; stores content-free leases, save-undo metadata and receipt hashes under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/incognito/; makes no third-party network calls.

entries.name: index-network
entries.description:
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or `hermes index login`) writes INDEX_SESSION_TOKEN and INDEX_API_URL to the Hermes env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX_NEGOTIATOR_ENV_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Hermes model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $HERMES_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX_API_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Hermes env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX_EARLY_NETWORK_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Hermes sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.
