entries.name: index-search
entries.description: Search one index you run and watch one saved query, with index_search, index_health and index_watch. It searches a Meilisearch server you run, so notes or local files can be found only after you index them there; it does not search files on disk itself. Disclosure — Sends MEILI_API_KEY as a Bearer token to your MEILI_HOST. Over plain http that key travels unencrypted, and a master or admin key is sent as given, so use a search-only key. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can search with your key. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. On Hermes 0.21.6 and later, while the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. index_watch save stores one query and prints a hermes cron create line for every 15 minutes. You run that line. A run is a model turn, and a tool call is another model request, with no daily cap. The watch covers only the first 20 hits. The job stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. This plugin does not create or remove the cron job and it does not ask. Writes use the guard in agent.file_safety. An update can stop the watch.

entries.name: injection-guard
entries.description: Prompt-injection firewall for tool output. A tool_execution middleware scans results from web, browser, file-reading and mail tools for instructions addressed to the model, redacts the matched spans, strips zero-width and bidi characters, HTML comments carrying instructions, CSS-hidden text and oversized base64 blobs, then wraps what remains in a labelled untrusted- data envelope. Fully local and deterministic: seven weighted signal families with a default threshold of six, so one strong signal or two medium signals trip it; no network calls, no API calls, and no model in the decision path. Ships a read-only injection_guard_stats tool and a /guard command, and appends one audit line per block carrying signal names and scores only — never the offending text. Embedded envelope markers are defused before wrapping, so a payload cannot close the untrusted block early. For tools listed in file_reader_tools the destructive family is exempt, because redacting a local migration or deploy script would corrupt it if the model rewrote the file; instruction-override and concealment still fire on reads. Disclosure — it rewrites tool results before the model reads them, which is the purpose of the plugin and does change the content the model receives; detection is pattern-based, so a novel phrasing that avoids every rule will pass, and the guard covers the tool path only, not text a user pastes into chat.

entries.name: injection-range
entries.description: A prompt-injection fire drill for your own agent. /drill run plants eight documents, one at a time, each carrying a test injection (plain override, hidden HTML comment, forged system message, memory poisoning, base64, reply hijack, and two delegated-task cases where you tell the agent to follow a document), gives the agent an ordinary task with each, blocks any tool call that carries a drill canary before it runs (pre_tool_call), and scores each scenario as held, neutralized by a guard, or compromised from the tool calls and model requests it observed, never from the model's own account. Use it to test a model, or a guard plugin, before you trust the agent with real documents. Disclosure — hooks see every session's tool calls and turns and return at once when no drill is running; during a drill it reads outgoing request messages to check the payload arrived (not stored), blocks canary-carrying tool calls with a neutral message, and queues one user-role task per scenario into the session that ran /drill (terminal UI only, and only with plugins.entries.injection-range.allow_gateway_injection: true; otherwise it shows the task for you to send). Ships its test injections as plain text in scenarios.py; every payload points at a per-run random token or the reserved host range.invalid, and none asks for a secret or a real file. Writes planted documents to per-scenario temp folders (deleted when the scenario ends) and the last 20 results to its plugin data folder (verdicts, the first 240 characters of each blocked call's arguments, the first 400 characters of each drill reply). No network, subprocesses, tools, credentials, telemetry, background threads or dependencies.

entries.name: injection-shield
entries.description: Injection-Shield — defends Hermes agents against prompt-injection attacks via tool outputs and untrusted content. Validates LLM responses, audits risky tool calls. Modes: audit / enforcement. Disclosure — injection-shield sees every tool call and tool result, MCP tool descriptions, each user prompt with its conversation history, and every model reply. It adds a firewall instruction block to each prompt as hook context. In enforcement mode it can block tool calls and replace suspicious tool results or model output (the default is audit mode, which only logs); with `enforce_min_severity` set it also blocks terminal, write_file and execute_code calls whose findings reach that severity while in audit mode. It writes an audit log of detected attempts to `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/workspace/05-Logs-Snapshots/prompt-injection-attempts.log`, and keeps MCP trust/integrity hash stores under `~/.hermes/profiles/default/workspace/05-Logs-Snapshots/`. When you set `INJECTION_SHIELD_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` and `INJECTION_SHIELD_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, it sends alert summaries (violation types, counts and time, no matched text) to `api.telegram.org` with your own bot token. Its dashboard/Desktop controls pane saves settings into `config.yaml` under `plugins.entries.injection-shield`. It installs no cron or launchd jobs. Disclosure — privacy-shield sees every user message, outgoing LLM request and assistant reply. Its llm_request middleware rewrites the user messages in each cloud request (current prompt, earlier turns and injected context; Ollama is exempt) to replace detected personal data with tokens, and its transform_llm_output hook puts the real values back into replies on whitelisted channels (telegram, desktop, cli, kanban by default; cron only when you opt in) and always into subagent results returned to the parent agent, which then reach the model unmasked as tool output. The token-to-value mapping is kept AES-256-GCM-encrypted in `~/.hermes/privacy/mapping.db` (restored attachments go under `~/.hermes/privacy/restore/`), and the audit trail is written to `~/.hermes/profiles/default/workspace/privacy-shield-audit.jsonl` plus a rotating log, whichever profile is running. The plugin reads its key `PRIVACY_SHIELD_KEY` through the Hermes secret scope, and the restore chat id from `PRIVACY_SHIELD_RESTORE_CHAT_ID` or your `pass` entry `hermes/telegram/chat_id`. The dashboard/Desktop Controls pane and `privacy-shield set-mode` write its settings into `config.yaml` under `plugins.entries.privacy-shield`. The optional doctor/cleanup shell wrappers under `scripts/cron/` are never installed by the plugin: if you schedule them yourself, they read the key from your `pass` store and call a `telegram-alert.sh` under `$HERMES_HOME/profiles/sysadmin/scripts/` if one exists. The plugin itself makes no network calls.
known_issues: Formal multi-agent security audit covers privacy-shield; the equivalent formal audit for injection-shield is still pending (status: triple peer review + 410+ regression tests; see SECURITY-AUDIT.md in the repo).

entries.name: inkly
entries.description: Run your eSignature and document signing workflows directly from Hermes. Inkly lets you send, track, and manage documents for eSignature. Send a contract from your saved templates, turn a PDF into a signable document, see which agreements are still waiting to be signed and send a reminder, or get the signed PDF of any completed document. Built for anyone who needs fast, simple document signing, whether it's contracts, forms, or approvals. Connects to Inkly's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.inkly.so/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles the inkly workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Inkly's hosted server (www.inkly.so) and acts on the user's Inkly account at the workspace and access level they approve at sign-in; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. send_template emails a real, legally binding document, send_reminder emails signers, and void_document voids a sent document and emails its signers; at the default Prepare level nothing is emailed until the user presses Send in Inkly. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: innernet
entries.description: One memory for every AI tool: load a project's context, answer from what was decided before, save new decisions back, and pick up where the last session left off, in the same memory Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Grok read and write. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at innernet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with CIMD and DCR); the two bundled skills load as innernet:innernet and innernet:innernet-handoff. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code, hooks, background process, telemetry or self-update. Every tool call goes to innernet.live, signed in as the user through innernet's own browser sign-in (a first sign-in creates a free innernet account); what a call carries (a project name, a question, text the user asks to save) is sent there, and what the memory holds comes back into the session context, so it reaches the user's model provider. Some tools write to the user's innernet account (save context, capture a note, write a handoff, update a task, forget on request); every write is versioned and can be read, edited or deleted on the user's dashboard. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with an `mcp_servers.innernet` entry in config.yaml (url https://innernet.live/api/mcp, `auth: oauth`) and `hermes mcp login innernet`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: innerscape
entries.description: Gentle check-ins, journaling and an Unstuck Coach with your own Innerscape server: save a mood check-in in your words, save a journal entry or park an inbox item only after you say yes to the exact text, and look back on today. When you're frozen or overloaded, the bundled unstuck skill names what's in the way, gives one next move and holds the rest. The skills never score, label or diagnose a mood. entries.name: inset
entries.description: Opens your site in headless Chromium at phone, tablet and desktop widths, inspects every page section separately (the Section Atlas) and measures overflow, clipped text, covered controls, section spill-over and failed media with DOM selectors and pixel boxes. Hermes fixes the source with its normal tools and approvals; INSET then rechecks the same URL and viewport and reports resolved, reproduced, needs review or not verified, never a pass it could not observe. Disclosure — INSET launches a headless Chromium (installed separately with Playwright) that opens any localhost/loopback port the agent asks for without an approval prompt and returns screenshots and page text to the model; other origins open only when you add them to INSET's allowed_origins setting, and private-network addresses are refused. It also runs read-only git commands in the session workspace.

entries.name: inspeximus
entries.description: Memory provider with keyed corrections you can undo. A correction retires the old value by key, so it stops being recalled, and inspeximus_revert puts the previous value back from the key alone, without anyone retyping what the record used to say. Recall before each turn returns retrieval minus what a later correction retired, so a value corrected three sessions ago cannot come back as context. Adds inspeximus_remember, inspeximus_correct, inspeximus_revert, inspeximus_forget and inspeximus_forget_me. Disclosure — installs the inspeximus package from PyPI (inspeximus>=3.27.0,<4, including its `inspeximus` command-line tools) into the Hermes environment; the provider makes no network calls and carries no telemetry: memories live in a local file under the profile's Hermes home (or a path you set), recalled memories are added to each turn's context and to the compression summary prompt, and writes made with the built-in memory tool are mirrored into the store.

entries.name: instabox
entries.description: Terminal backend that runs Hermes terminal, execute_code and file tools in an instabox cloud sandbox, paused and resumed by name per task or created per session and deleted when it ends. Disclosure — requires an instabox API key (INSTABOX_API_KEY); every command and the files the file tools touch are sent to instabox; your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files are uploaded to ~/.hermes in the box, and skill and cache files changed in the box are copied back to your machine; boxes are created, paused, resumed and deleted in the key's workspace and billed to it; persistent mode keeps one paused box per task (each gateway session is its own task), and paused boxes keep their disk until deleted; commands in the box can become root without a password, and dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the box.

entries.name: intents-pay
entries.description: Crypto invoices and cross-chain payment quotes for a NEAR account via the NEAR Intents 1-Click API. Dry quotes by default. A quote or invoice requires an explicit recipient — there is no default payee. Payable tool calls (invoices and non-dry quotes) wait for Hermes's approval prompt via a pre_tool_call hook. Never moves funds and never handles signing keys. Disclosure — payments plugin: sends quote and invoice details (amounts, recipient NEAR account, refund address, and an optional partner API key as X-API-Key) to the NEAR Intents 1-Click API (1click.chaindefuser.com by default); creating an invoice or a live quote produces a real deposit address that anyone can pay, gated by Hermes's approval prompt, a one-time confirmation token and a refusal under cron; never signs or sends funds; stores invoices in its plugin-data folder.
entries.title: Intents Pay
known_issues: Dry quotes on EVM and Solana send a public placeholder refund address so 1-Click can check the format. No deposit is created. A live quote rejects that placeholder and requires the payer's own refund address plus a one-time confirmation token.
Verification for this release used live dry quotes only. Completing a mainnet deposit address is gated and was not part of the test run.
A quote or invoice requires an explicit recipient. Payable tool calls wait for Hermes's approval prompt via pre_tool_call.

entries.name: interfaze
entries.description: Interfaze, a model built for deterministic tasks, with accurate and verifiable output in one call: web search, web scraping, OCR for images, PDFs and Word documents, speech-to-text, object and GUI detection, translation, classification and time-series forecasting through the hosted Interfaze MCP server (Streamable HTTP, API key or keyless), with seven skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the Interfaze MCP server at api.interfaze.ai, with INTERFAZE_API_KEY when it is set, or keyless without it (README). It sends prompts, search queries, URLs, text, and the images, documents and audio that the agent attaches. get_upload_url uploads local files to Interfaze storage. Interfaze stores the prompts, responses and intermediate task outputs of each call, and keeps the request ID, status, timestamp and token counts. The plugin does not send the zero data retention header (x-interfaze-zdr), so Interfaze stores the request contents. For keyless calls, Interfaze also keeps the caller's IP address and token counts. Interfaze does not use the data for model training without explicit consent. Results go into the session context and reach the user's model provider. The tool list comes from the server at run time, so the pinned commit does not cover it. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before get_upload_url. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no self-update.

entries.name: invinoveritas-receipts
entries.description: Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post_approval_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post_llm_call + on_session_end record, when a turn ends with max_iterations_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api_url) under INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max_iterations_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool_call_id/turn_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.

entries.name: iolite
entries.description: Pick an LLM that is smart enough, then cheapest, in one tool call. Set an intelligence floor or name an anchor model, and Iolite returns the few models on the cost x intelligence front, ranked toward cheaper, smarter or balanced. It answers from a catalog of 621 models bundled in the plugin, so a fresh install works offline with no setup. Adds three tools (iolite_shortlist, iolite_model, iolite_show), /iolite, a skill and a Hermes Desktop pane that plots the catalog in 3D and 2D and follows the agent's picks. Data and credits: Epoch AI ECI (CC BY), LMArena ratings (CC BY 4.0), LiteLLM prices (MIT); every answer names its sources, and catalog rows whose source names Artificial Analysis are refused. Disclosure — no network unless you set catalog_url (one https GET, no credentials added; plain http only with allow_http); a post_api_request hook records tokens per second and per-task tokens and model seconds (task ids hashed) on your machine only, never uploaded, off with measure_speed and measure_usage false; your last shortlist, your own prices and temporary .pane-*.receipt markers are kept in the plugin data directory; three local Desktop routes (/landscape, /my-prices, /pane-receipt) add no auth of their own and rely on the dashboard's loopback bind, so keep the dashboard on 127.0.0.1; no prompt text is sent to the pane; no secrets read; tool results stay in session history like any tool output.
entries.title: Iolite
known_issues: The three local Desktop routes add no auth of their own; if you expose the Hermes dashboard on a network interface they are exposed with it (they reveal your latest shortlist and accept saved prices). Keep the dashboard on loopback.
The Desktop pane starts off and the agent cannot switch it on; enable it in Capabilities -> Plugins.
Speed is measured on your own machine only and is not comparable across machines; models with no price or score are not plotted.

entries.name: iowap
entries.description: Fleet control for Hermes Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). The task watcher posts stage/final task updates into the app's chat composer with user-typed authority (fail-closed, never a broadcast; switchable + persisted, a one-time long-run hint for tasks actually claimed beyond 5 minutes) and warns about fleet anomalies (node up/down, relay reachability) under the same toggle. Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the node-cli, and the plugin makes no raw HTTP calls of its own. Node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files, and tracked task ids are stored in your Hermes home under plugin-data/iowap/. The task and fleet watcher is off by default. When you turn it on, it drafts task-event lines (task name, id and stage status, never node output) into the chat composer, or, in direct mode, which you must choose, sends them with your typing authority into the session that submitted the task or the session you configured. No third-party endpoints.

entries.name: iris-chat-channel
entries.description: Chat with Hermes through Iris Chat: Signal-like messaging using Nostr Double Ratchet end-to-end encryption, without phone numbers or signup. Iris also supports nearby messaging over local networks and Bluetooth. The native channel supports one approved contact, text replies, seen receipts and typing. Disclosure — invokes the separately installed Iris CLI and runs its background service when needed; Iris stores its own dedicated identity and message history and connects to configured message servers/transports. Plaintext requests pass through Hermes and its selected model. No telemetry, automatic software downloads, imported personal keys, or added tools. Not filesystem isolation.

entries.name: its-in-your-head
entries.description: It's in Your Head — a calm desktop instrument that shows how you work with Hermes: live tool activity (PULSE), a six-dimension working-style portrait, and drift trends, with optional opt-in directional adaptation (one bounded instruction per turn). Zero network by default; raw prompts and reasoning are never stored (derived features only). Optional local ONNX Tier-1 downloads a pinned model from Hugging Face only on explicit `/mirror engine enable`. Disclosure — no network by default; the optional local ONNX engine, enabled only by `/mirror engine enable`, downloads an Apache-2.0 embedding model (onnx-community/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2-ONNX) from Hugging Face, pinned by revision and per-file sha256, into the profile's plugin-data directory, and runs it in a Hermes-managed isolated environment (onnxruntime, CPU) as a local worker subprocess with a minimal environment, plus a small watchdog process that stops that worker if Hermes exits uncleanly. When the current profile has no portrait yet, the portrait view reads (read-only) this plugin's own data from your other Hermes profiles on the machine and shows the most recent one, labelled with its profile name. No credentials are stored, no telemetry is sent, and raw prompts and reasoning are never stored (derived features only).

entries.name: iwork-studio
entries.description: Create, edit, design and export Apple Numbers, Keynote and Pages files: designed Keynote decks from data and the user's brand kit, spreadsheet cells, formulas and formatting, Pages text and tables, exports to PDF, Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Every write is backed up, made on a copy, re-read and checked, then swapped in; any change can be undone in one call. Arabic and right-to-left text round-trip exactly. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/): a local stdio MCP server (65 tools) and a workflow skill. macOS. Disclosure — first start downloads iwork-studio==2.6.1 and its Python dependencies from PyPI with uvx (about 60 MB; built from the v2.6.1 tag by the repo's release workflow through PyPI trusted publishing; the server code is that release, not the pinned tree); Pages, exports, render checks and Keynote slide operations drive Numbers, Keynote and Pages through osascript, and macOS asks once for Automation access; it reads and writes the iWork files and export targets the agent names, anywhere on disk unless IWORK_STUDIO_ROOTS is set to fence it, and Hermes does not prompt before its write tools; it keeps backups in ~/.iwork-studio/backups (last 10 per file) and saved design kits in ~/.iwork-studio/kits; no network calls after the download, no telemetry, no self-updates.

entries.name: jev-approvals
entries.description: TypeSafe's Jev decision model as Hermes' smart-approval reviewer only: it cannot generate text and refuses every other task. Supports TypeSafe direct, OpenRouter, and configurable Jev-compatible HTTPS endpoints with optional endpoint-specific authentication; custom and aggregator routes use a plugin-owned dispatch placeholder that is never sent upstream, while TypeSafe direct still requires TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Validates typed answers and endpoint/redirect boundaries, redacts command credentials, caps oversized commands (64000 characters by default, halving to 16000 on a context-limit response) and never auto-approves a truncated command, and records bounded structured audit logs. Disclosure — each command routed to smart approval (redacted best-effort) and the operator's smart-policy text leave the machine for the configured third-party endpoint; provider or validation failures fail closed to ESCALATE.

entries.name: jev-curator
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev semantic governance for Hermes' native Curator: classifies relationships between complete skill packages, produces content-hash-bound, fail-closed consolidation plans, and locally guards background destructive skill_manage calls while Hermes retains control of backups and mutations. A profile-scoped 60-second lifecycle debounce coalesces skill changes into dry refreshes. Disclosure — no egress occurs by default; after allow_content_egress is explicitly enabled, redacted bounded skill content is sent to the configured TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or custom Jev endpoint and may spend provider credits. Automatic refreshes never apply mutations, and missing, stale, or incomplete evidence fails closed.

entries.name: jev-effort-router
entries.description: Per-turn model AND reasoning-effort routing, decided by TypeSafe Jev, which rewrites the outgoing chat_completions provider request itself via the llm_request middleware. The six measured criteria are capability slots; a built-in Ollama:Cloud profile ships, and provider_profiles maps the slots to another active provider's models. Most catalog routers decide one half — a model or an effort level; this one decides both per turn, with a measured grid, a confidence guard, per-surface policy and an audit trail that reports what was applied. Ollama:Cloud is the shipped profile; another chat_completions provider is routed only when the operator declares a profile, and the router never switches providers. Every failure path leaves the request byte-identical to a plugin-disabled run. Disclosure — sends the current user message and up to 4 previous turns to the Decisions surface selected by the key present (Requesty /v1/systemone with typesafe/jev-1.14.0, or OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13), billed to that account; credentials are read through Hermes' profile secret scope; the local audit file keeps decisions and turn identifiers, message text only when explicitly enabled; no telemetry.

entries.name: jev-judge
entries.description: TypeSafe Jev as a judgment layer — a pre-tool gate (shadow by default, enforce escalates) on terminal, write_file and patch asking destructive / exfiltration / impact (a v2 signal set — reads_secrets × sends_outbound, blast_radius, self_advocating — is one setting away), plus a jev_ask tool for typed judgments. Thresholds in code, one JSONL line per decision with the fail-open reason, fail-open on every error path. Stdlib only, no Node; no redirects, proxy env ignored, payload capped; works with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. Disclosure — each judged call sends the tool name and its redacted arguments (≤600 chars each, ≤12 args) to TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or your configured gateway, using your key; shadow mode only logs. With the default backend auto, OPENROUTER_API_KEY is used automatically whenever it is present and TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not, so tool names and redacted arguments go to openrouter.ai on your main-model OpenRouter key unless backend is set to typesafe or gateway.

entries.name: jg-provider-usage
entries.description: Provider usage in a Desktop status-bar chip, popover and full page: subscription windows, API balances, reset times and profile-scoped account state. Signed-in OAuth accounts are listed even when the chat is on another provider. Includes data-only JSON connectors with explicit destination approval, setup cards for Claude, Gemini and Z.ai, a running-agents footer with honest unknowns, and an active-account Codex banked-reset preview/confirmation. Readers: Codex, OpenCode Go/Zen, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud, Nous, Claude subscription, Grok, Moonshot, Novita, DeepInfra, Fireworks and Arcee (the last four are fixture-tested against documented response shapes, not exercised against a funded account). Stock Hermes 0.23.1 needs no core patch; Grok reads through the host when it brokers xai-oauth, or through an opt-in compatibility setting that resolves the account through Hermes' own locked resolver rather than a token file. A Settings panel renders from an allowlisted per-profile JSON spec and refetches usage on save. Usage reads use Hermes account helpers or scoped API-key access and provider HTTPS endpoints. Brokered subscription tokens stay with Hermes; opt-in xAI compatibility mode handles the token in the plugin backend for that request. Custom definitions are HTTPS GET only, approved-host restricted, with no redirects or executable code. Confirming a Codex reset spends one banked reset; refresh and preview do not. No purchase, automatic redemption, telemetry or self-update. Screenshots and demo use real plugin components with clearly labeled synthetic data, not live accounts. Disclosure — reads your own usage/credit data with vendor client-identity headers (`User-Agent: codex-cli` to chatgpt.com for Codex reset credits; `x-xai-token-auth: xai-grok-cli` to cli-chat-proxy.grok.com for Grok billing), and with the compatibility setting enabled the plugin receives the account's OAuth access token from Hermes' locked resolver and sends it only to xAI's billing hosts for that request; the usage page can read every local Hermes profile's provider usage through Hermes' profile scope; confirming a Codex reset in the page spends one banked reset; it reads state.db read-only for token totals and fetches DeepSeek's public pricing page every 12 hours.

entries.name: joust
entries.description: Races 2 to 4 coding subagents on one task, each in its own Git worktree, judges them with your tests and merges only the best patch after you approve. joust_launch provisions one detached worktree per contender under the profile's plugin-data folder (uncommitted tracked edits are mirrored and committed as the baseline) and, inside an agent turn, launches one Hermes subagent per contender through ctx.subagent_lifecycle, optionally each on its own model. A tool_request middleware rewrites each child session's file paths, V4A patch headers, search roots and terminal workdir into its worktree, and a pre_tool_call hook vetoes escapes. joust_evaluate runs the bout's test command in every worktree through the Hermes terminal tool, 1 to 7 times (Flake Shield: every run must pass, median speed, flaky contenders cannot win), scoring Correctness 60, Speed 25 and Diff minimalism 15. joust_crossfire fires each contender's new tests at every rival worktree, and survival is the first tiebreak. joust_merge applies the winner with git apply behind Hermes's approval gate, after saving a rollback patch and keeping every contender as a joust/<bout>/<contender> branch; joust_report writes a markdown bout report. Also adds /joust, the hermes joust CLI, the joust-arena skill and a Desktop half (/joust page, right pane, status-bar chip, palette command, ::joust-bout inline card). Disclosure — runs local git in the repository you name (rev-parse, worktree add/remove/prune, add -N, diff, apply, apply -R, reset, branch, write-tree and commit-tree; init/add/commit for its demo repo and the copy fallback, which copies the repository into the profile's plugin-data folder), registers worktrees in that repository's .git/worktrees until joust_merge action=cleanup, creates joust/<bout>/<contender> branches (config keep_loser_branches, default on), and writes the approved patch into your working tree. Contender subagents' file paths and terminal workdir are redirected into their worktrees, but their shell commands are not sandboxed beyond Hermes's normal approvals. Test commands (yours or the model's) run only through the Hermes terminal tool, also on a background thread when a contender subagent finishes (auto_evaluate_on_stop, default on); the CLI and dashboard refuse to judge, and only the self-contained demo uses a bounded subprocess with plugin-authored commands. Captured output is secret-scrubbed with a stdlib regex and stored, with diffs, goals and repository paths, in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/joust/joust.db (SQLite); bout snapshots are broadcast to connected Hermes Desktop windows and the Desktop half polls the dashboard API while visible. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no Python dependencies. Linux and macOS.
entries.title: Joust
entries.capability_summary: joust (community, maintained by mrnetwork0001) Races 2 to 4 coding subagents on one task, each in its own Git worktree, judges them with your tests and merges only the best patch after you approve. joust_launch provisions one detached worktree per contender under the profile's plugin-data folder (uncommitted tracked edits are mirrored and committed as the baseline) and, inside an agent turn, launches one Hermes subagent per contender through ctx.subagent_lifecycle, optionally each on its own model. A tool_request middleware rewrites each child session's file paths, V4A patch headers, search roots and terminal workdir into its worktree, and a pre_tool_call hook vetoes escapes. joust_evaluate runs the bout's test command in every worktree through the Hermes terminal tool, 1 to 7 times (Flake Shield: every run must pass, median speed, flaky contenders cannot win), scoring Correctness 60, Speed 25 and Diff minimalism 15. joust_crossfire fires each contender's new tests at every rival worktree, and survival is the first tiebreak. joust_merge applies the winner with git apply behind Hermes's approval gate, after saving a rollback patch and keeping every contender as a joust/<bout>/<contender> branch; joust_report writes a markdown bout report. Also adds /joust, the hermes joust CLI, the joust-arena skill and a Desktop half (/joust page, right pane, status-bar chip, palette command, ::joust-bout inline card). Disclosure — runs local git in the repository you name (rev-parse, worktree add/remove/prune, add -N, diff, apply, apply -R, reset, branch, write-tree and commit-tree; init/add/commit for its demo repo and the copy fallback, which copies the repository into the profile's plugin-data folder), registers worktrees in that repository's .git/worktrees until joust_merge action=cleanup, creates joust/<bout>/<contender> branches (config keep_loser_branches, default on), and writes the approved patch into your working tree. Contender subagents' file paths and terminal workdir are redirected into their worktrees, but their shell commands are not sandboxed beyond Hermes's normal approvals. Test commands (yours or the model's) run only through the Hermes terminal tool, also on a background thread when a contender subagent finishes (auto_evaluate_on_stop, default on); the CLI and dashboard refuse to judge, and only the self-contained demo uses a bounded subprocess with plugin-authored commands. Captured output is secret-scrubbed with a stdlib regex and stored, with diffs, goals and repository paths, in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/joust/joust.db (SQLite); bout snapshots are broadcast to connected Hermes Desktop windows and the Desktop half polls the dashboard API while visible. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no Python dependencies. Linux and macOS. This plugin registers tool(s): joust_launch, joust_evaluate, joust_diff, joust_steer, joust_merge, joust_status, joust_crossfire, joust_report; hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, subagent_start, subagent_stop; middleware: tool_request. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5.

entries.name: jp-address
entries.description: Splits one Japanese address into prefecture, city, town and the remainder with address_split, built on Geolonia's address data (CC BY 4.0, from the Digital Agency address base registry). Give it a Japanese postal address as written, such as 東京都千代田区霞が関2-1-2, and it returns the prefecture, city and town as separate fields. Disclosure — Each call sends at most two HTTPS GET requests, with no API key, to japanese-addresses-v2.geoloniamaps.com or the JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL you set (plain http only for 127.0.0.1 and localhost). The matched prefecture and municipality names go into the URL path; the house number, the lot and the building name are not sent. JP_ADDRESS_BASE_URL is read for the active profile on each call, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The tool is on for every surface, including gateways, and asks for no approval: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. It writes no files and creates no cron job. A point can be coarser than the town and is not a rooftop geocode, and an address it cannot place for certain comes back as ambiguous or at the municipality instead of a guess. The publisher may change or stop the free host and suggests self-hosting for commercial use. Called from Hermes with five models in a small sample of 18 sessions (see CHANGELOG.md). The skill tells the model to pass a registered address from a company record into address_split only when a tool result already returned that address. If none was returned, it says the address was not split. When level is below 3, absent lists the missing parts, and those parts are not 0. pre_llm_call adds the address paragraph only on an address question, and adds nothing on other turns. An address question is 所在地, 住所, 都道府県, 丁目, 番地, a prefecture name, or address_split called in the previous turn. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says to call address_split only with an address copied from a tool result, names the absent parts by level, and says a missing part is not written as 0. When a previous turn returned a prefecture, it says to copy that prefecture. transform_llm_output returns no string unless address_split was called and jp-charts would leave the reply unchanged. It does not match success wording. When address_split returned no prefecture, a named prefecture is removed and the reply says the address was not split. level 0, bad_args, and upstream are not described as a completed split.

entries.name: jp-charts
entries.description: Bar, line, stacked and 100% band charts as phone-sized PNGs for chat replies and reports, with Japanese text, 万/億 units and a required unit and source line. Following Japanese chart conventions, it turns a table typed in chat or read from a CSV or JSON file into a bar or line graph ready to post. Every bar, point, label and tick is read back from the finished figure and compared with the parsed data before the image is returned. Disclosure — no network calls at run time; reads a local .csv/.tsv/.txt/.json only when given its path (never hidden files or the Hermes home); writes PNGs to the Hermes image cache; a transform_llm_output hook adds a forgotten MEDIA line to replies on chat platforms and cron deliveries (setting auto_attach, on by default). The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. Installing the plugin also installs the Python packages matplotlib and matplotlib-fontja from PyPI. The PNGs are written to <HERMES_HOME>/cache/images. Removing the plugin deletes its folder only; the PNGs and those two packages stay. A transform_tool_result hook remembers value and unit pairs in the process for that session and does not change the tool result. A pre_tool_call hook blocks chart_render when a plotted number was already returned in the same session with a different unit string, including a comma-grouped number such as 1,234, and no PNG is written. pre_llm_call adds one paragraph only on a chart question, and adds nothing on other turns. A chart question is 図, グラフ, チャート, or the word chart, or chart_render, chart_validate, or chart_types called in the previous turn. Company, filing, and unrelated questions do not add it. The paragraph says to call chart_render only with numbers and the unit copied from a tool result, that 1,234 is the same integer as 1234, that a different unit blocks the chart, and not to say a chart was drawn or write 取得しました when no number was returned. transform_llm_output does not replace or delete the model's sentences. It appends one line when this turn's tool record has no figure and an area tool was called, or some tool was called on a company or filing question. The line is: Tool record: this turn returned no company, filing, address, subsidy, statute, or chart figure, so a number or a fetch claim in this reply is not from a tool result. chart_types and chart_validate are not a figure. A turn whose only area tool is address_split is left unchanged by this hook.

entries.name: jp-chatwork
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from Chatwork rooms, built on the Chatwork API: put Hermes in a Chatwork room and ask it with [To:] or a reply, like a colleague; the answer comes back as a Chatwork reply. Polls the Chatwork API (no public URL or webhook), never answers a message twice across restarts, and while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset only the token's own account can use Hermes commands beyond /help, /whoami, /new and /reset or answer approval prompts. Disclosure: talks only to api.chatwork.com with your own API token; polls every 5 s by default while the gateway runs; stores read positions and the ids of its posted messages in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json. Disclosure — while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset everyone in the rooms listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS (external guests included) can prompt the agent and use its enabled tools, with Hermes commands and approval answers kept to the token's own account; talks only to api.chatwork.com with your API token, polling every 5 s while the gateway runs; stores read positions and posted message ids in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-chatwork/state.json; logs each asker's name and account id.

entries.name: jp-corporate
entries.description: Look up a Japanese company by name or 13-digit corporate number and read its gBizINFO record, from registration to subsidies, contracts, and financials. Disclosure — sends the company names, corporate numbers and prefectures you look up only to api.info.gbiz.go.jp (METI gBizINFO) with your own GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN, read on each call; no proxy, nothing written to disk; the tools are on for every surface, so anyone you allow on a gateway spends your token; the bundled japan-company skill adds one line to every skills index; on turns that look like company talk (a 13-digit number, 法人番号, 株式会社 and other legal forms, a few listed company names, or a jp_corp call last turn) a pre_llm_call hook adds a fixed paragraph, even where the tools are off, telling the model to find jp_corp_search via tool_search before web_search, copy next_step on token_missing, and not state data or write 取得しました/確認できます that the tool did not return.

entries.name: jp-edinet
entries.description: Japanese filings on the EDINET API v2. It finds a Japanese company's annual securities report (yuho) and other financial reports filed on EDINET, and reads headline figures such as revenue and total assets from a filing. Disclosure — talks only to api.edinet-fsa.go.jp over HTTPS, and your EDINET_API_KEY rides in the URL as Subscription-Key. Each call reads EDINET_API_KEY for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. The edinet toolset is on for every platform, including gateways, so anyone a gateway admits can call these tools with your key. With CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS unset, everyone in CHATWORK_ROOMS can call them. Turn the toolset off per platform with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. There is no daily cap. The agent can call the three tools itself. A cron you add stays after uninstall until you remove it in Hermes. This plugin starts no child process and is not a sandbox. Search sends EDINET the filing date, and a download sends the document id and its type. Company name, securities code, EDINET code, and corporate number are filtered on your machine. found: false means that line is absent from that period in periods or in filing_company (CurrentYear or Prior1Year to Prior4Year), not proof the filing has no figure, and not 0. A past day's filing list can change. Lists, saved files, and a key fingerprint, not the key, stay at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/jp-edinet per profile after uninstall. Delete that directory to remove them. The plugin relies on Hermes internals for the write check and the data folder. If an update moves those parts, the tools refuse and do not call EDINET. Test files are not loaded at startup. Since version 0.1.6 it returns those five consolidated periods in periods and the filing-company six lines in filing_company. A missing line is not copied from the other series. pre_llm_call adds one of three paragraphs only on a filing question (有報, 有価証券, 連結, 提出会社, the word EDINET, securities, or consolidated) or when edinet_search_filings, edinet_financials, or edinet_save_document was called in the previous turn, and adds nothing on other turns. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. When the secret helper cannot be read, the paragraph says the helper could not be read and does not say the key is unset. When EDINET_API_KEY is unset, the paragraph says to call edinet_search_filings once with the company name only, not to invent a file date, and to copy the free-key next_step (WEEK0060, the unit, and the filing URL once a document id is known). When the key is set, the paragraph says to call edinet_financials once a doc_id is known, and otherwise edinet_search_filings with only the file dates the user wrote. Each paragraph says not to write successfully retrieved, verified, or obtained using. That ban is the same as 取得しました.

entries.name: jp-egov-law
entries.description: Japanese laws for Hermes Agent, built on the e-Gov Law API: find a law by name, abbreviation or phrase, read one article as in force today or on a given date, and check amendment history and enforcement dates, with the source credit e-Gov's terms ask for. Ask for one Japanese law article, such as Article 32 of the Labor Standards Act, and it returns the official law text with the law number and the date that version took effect. Disclosure — sends the law names, article numbers, dates and search phrases you look up to laws.e-gov.go.jp (public API, no key); no other host, nothing written to disk. Registers blueprint jp-egov-law:weekly-amendments and does not create a cron job. When you create a job from that blueprint, one model turn runs once a week (default Mon 09:00, Hermes tz or the host clock if unset, not converted to Japan). A turn that calls a tool is at least two model requests, and there is no daily cap. The agent can schedule it, and scheduling it twice creates two jobs. Silence is not "no amendment". Uninstall leaves the cron until hermes cron remove. Tools stay on every platform, including gateways (a guest can call them; hermes tools disables one). While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 load the tools and skip the blueprint. pre_llm_call adds its paragraph only on a statute question, and adds nothing on other turns. A statute question matches 法令, 法律, 条文, e-Gov, 第N条, or 条 outside 条件, or egov_law_search, egov_law_article, or egov_law_revisions called in the previous turn. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says not to call egov_law_search with an empty query or a company name, that pre_tool_call blocks that search, that no article URL is written and a URL is not guessed, and to call egov_law_article when a law and an article are named and copy source.url; the same paragraph also tells the model not to call tool_describe and not to write 取得しました or 確認できます on that turn. pre_tool_call blocks egov_law_search when the query is empty or, in title mode, does not name a statute. 条 inside 条件 is not a statute name. The block says no article URL was written and a URL was not guessed. A text-mode search and egov_law_article are not blocked.

entries.name: jp-estat
entries.description: Japanese government statistics from the e-Stat API: search tables and fetch figures such as population, households, wages, and prices, with estat_search_tables, estat_table_info, and estat_get_data. Disclosure — It needs a free e-Stat application ID, set as ESTAT_APP_ID in the .env of each profile. Each call sends your search words and table selections to api.e-stat.go.jp and puts ESTAT_APP_ID in the request URL. The ID is read for the active profile on each call. entries.name: jp-kokkai
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Posts new Diet meeting hits as metadata and the official meeting URL, with kokkai_search, kokkai_speech, and kokkai_watch. Disclosure — Talks only to kokkai.ndl.go.jp over HTTPS GET with no API key. kokkai_speech requests speech text and returns a short excerpt. Speech text is not stored. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, read a speech excerpt, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. kokkai_watch add writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/jp-kokkai-watch.py and creates one cron job that does not call a model, once a day, at the hour you pick in Hermes's own timezone. Each run costs 0 tokens and has no daily cap. Empty script output sends nothing. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch returns one pre_tool_call approve line, as does a repeat add that switches the saved job. Hermes shows it. An unchanged repeat add returns none. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt when a person is present. A cron job, hermes -q, and a separate plugin process cannot add or remove a watch even after always. A webhook or API-server turn inside the gateway is refused by Hermes unless "always" was already given for that exact add plan. plugins.isolation: host still blocks add and remove. Answering "always" on add covers only the same add plan. That choice adds one plugin_rule:kokkai_watch: line to config.yaml, and the line stays after the plugin is removed. A different add plan asks again. Remove builds a new rule key on every call, so answering always on remove does not cover the next remove, including the call that deletes the cron job. While the read-meetings skill is enabled, Hermes adds one line to the skill index of every session, including a session whose tools are turned off. The scheduled script does not run inside plugins.isolation: host, so that setting does not stop the watch. kokkai_watch run still cannot save seen speech IDs under plugins.isolation: host and says so on every run of the tool. The cron mark is cron.execution_identity.current_cron_execution (Hermes 0.21.6). The daily job is created with the public hermes cron command using --no-agent and --script. hermes cron create on 0.21.6 cannot pin a toolset, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Running add again asks, then switches a model job onto the script and clears its prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next add. An update can stop the watch if the cron mark or that command moves. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data. The script timeout is 3600 seconds unless it was changed. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Hermes 0.22.2, not in a live chat.

entries.name: jp-reinfolib
entries.description: Quarterly MLIT prices for one city, via reinfolib_quarter. Use it for Japanese real estate and property prices in one city: it returns the number of recorded sales, the median trade price and the first 20 rows for a quarter. These are transaction prices, not the official land prices published as 地価公示. Disclosure — sends your REINFOLIB_API_KEY as Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key to www.reinfolib.mlit.go.jp (HTTPS, XIT001) or the host of REINFOLIB_BASE_URL. Plain http is refused except 127.0.0.1 and localhost, where the key is not encrypted. On for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow can call it with your key, with no approval prompt, including unattended cron, yolo, and approvals off. hermes tools does not stop /jp-reinfolib. Stop the slash command with allow_admin_from, user_allowed_commands, group_user_allowed_commands, or by disabling the plugin. After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until hermes cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register_automation_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be [SILENT] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」

entries.name: jp-subsidies
entries.description: Japanese subsidy search and weekly watch, built on the jGrants public API. Disclosure — Searches api.jgrants-portal.go.jp with no API key and no daily request cap; each call waits at most 60 seconds and retries at most twice, and a result is a search match, not proof that every subsidy came back. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can call these tools and change this profile's watch, and the agent can set up a watch by itself. In a Chatwork room listed in CHATWORK_ROOMS, everyone can call them while CHATWORK_ALLOWED_USERS is unset. The tools are on for every platform, including gateways; turn them off per platform with hermes tools. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off, and its pre_llm_call paragraph is added on those surfaces too. The /subsidies command is outside hermes tools; limit it with allow_admin_from or user_allowed_commands, or disable the plugin. The optional weekly watch is an unattended cron job that runs a script with no model call and is not a sandbox; delivering it to bot-chat instead runs one model turn on the fetched text. If delivery fails after the script runs, those subsidies are already marked seen and the text stays under cron/output/. Uninstall leaves the cron job, scripts/jp-subsidies-weekly-*.py and plugin-data/jp-subsidies/ until you run hermes cron remove and delete the files. The plugin does not store the name or ID of who asked. Not tested against a live gateway, with the Chatwork plugin loaded, or for result sets of several hundred rows. subsidies_detail compares a corporation's published industry, capital, employee count, and address with the call text as characters, returns a cap only when the call states one, and does not estimate an award. pre_tool_call blocks subsidies_search unless keyword is contained in industry text copied from a tool result, including a list of industry strings. A company name does not pass, including when the industry text is contained in the company name. When industry text was returned and the keyword is not that text, the block does not say the industry was missing. The block says the search was not run, eligibility is not_claimed, and no award was estimated. A company name contained in business_summary does not pass as an industry keyword. That holds when the name field is absent and the summary is トヨタ自動車は自動車を製造する。: トヨタ自動車 does not pass and 自動車 does. transform_tool_result remembers industry text and returns nothing, so the tool result is unchanged. pre_llm_call adds its paragraph only on a subsidy question (補助金, 助成金, jGrants, or 募集) or when subsidies_search, subsidies_detail, or subsidies_watch_setup was called in the previous turn, and adds nothing on other turns. A company name alone or an unrelated question does not add it. The paragraph says to call subsidies_search only with industry text copied from a tool result, that eligibility is not_claimed, and not to estimate an award or write 対象です.

entries.name: jw3
entries.description: JW3.ai non-custodial trading inside Hermes: 12 market/risk/Diary reads, Diary propose cards, and 4 human-approved execution tools — all thin wrappers over the local jw3 CLI, which owns the PAT and enforces server-side scope, kill-switch, fee, and idempotency gates. Bundles the jw3-ops skill and /jw3-status. Disclosure — every tool call runs the local `jw3` CLI (installed separately from github.com/agnostic4321-ops/jw3-mcp-cli, not covered by the pinned sha) with a minimal env (PATH, HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, TMPDIR, JW3_*); the CLI holds the JW3 PAT and reaches JW3.ai's Supabase edge functions and the user's exchange accounts; jw3_execute, jw3_close, jw3_exits and jw3_cancel dry-run unless confirm=true, and every confirm=true call goes through a Hermes approval prompt showing the exact command before it places, closes or cancels real orders with real funds (unattended runs follow the user's approval mode; an "always" answer pre-approves only that identical command); the plugin itself holds no secrets and stores nothing.

entries.name: jwt-ref
entries.description: @jwt: context references that decode a JSON Web Token for the model: @jwt:<token> (or a quoted "Bearer <token>") attaches the header with the algorithm in words, every claim as JSON, the exp, nbf, iat and auth_time claims in UTC with how long ago or ahead they are, whether the token has expired and its lifetime, and notes on alg none, a missing or empty signature, a header that names its own key (jku, x5u, jwk), crit and duplicate names; encrypted tokens (JWE) show their header only; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a token as you type it. The signature is never verified. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's base64, json and datetime; no network (no key sets fetched), no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the token, but the @jwt: reference and the decoded header and claims become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history, so decode only tokens you are willing to share with it; register() only adds the @jwt: reference provider.

entries.name: k6pane
entries.description: Local load testing with Grafana k6 from chat. Three tools: k6pane_doctor (checks the k6 install and limits), k6pane_run (writes and runs a k6 test from a URL or a multi-step request flow with smoke, load, stress, spike, soak, constant or fixed-arrival-rate profiles, or runs your own k6 script) and k6pane_report (lists, reads and compares stored runs and flags latency, throughput and error regressions). Each run returns pass, fail, invalid (the requested load was never actually applied: dropped iterations, achieved rate short of target, or timeout) or error, with RPS, error rate, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and a per-endpoint breakdown. Bundles the k6pane:load-testing skill. Targets are limited to localhost and private networks unless the user lists a host in the allowed_hosts setting; link-local and cloud metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, fd00:ec2::254) are refused unless the exact host is allowlisted, and k6 is fenced with --blacklist-ip to exactly the validated IPs, so redirects, DNS rebinding and runtime-built URLs cannot reach anything else. VU, duration and request-rate caps reject oversized tests. One run at a time. Disclosure — runs the user's local k6 binary as a subprocess (never through a shell); sends load-test traffic only to the validated targets; resolves target hostnames via DNS; k6's anonymous usage report is disabled; no other network calls, no telemetry, no update checks. Writes each run (generated script, k6 summary, k6 log, parsed result, all redacted) under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/k6pane/runs plus a run.lock file. Reads only k6 scripts the user points it at. Custom script/script_path tests are JavaScript that k6 runs directly on the host, outside the Hermes terminal sandbox and approval prompt, and k6's open() can read local files. Credentials: optional K6PANE_SECRET_<NAME> values, resolved per profile through agent.secret_scope.get_secret only when a test references ${secret.NAME}, passed to k6 through an inherited pipe (never disk or argv) and redacted from every stored file and tool result; k6 runs with a scrubbed environment. Standard library only, no Python dependencies; requires the k6 binary (not bundled).

known_issues: Requires the k6 binary on PATH (or the k6_bin setting); k6pane_doctor prints the install command. Tested with k6 v2.3.0.
Secrets use k6's file secret source over an inherited pipe, which needs macOS or Linux; Windows is not supported.

entries.name: kaggle-competitions
entries.description: Track Kaggle competitions from your agent: live submission status, score history, personal-best watch, leaderboards, and new-score watch. Four agent tools over the Kaggle CLI (submissions, score history, watch for new results, leaderboards), a desktop pane, a full web page with sidebar nav, and a dashboard API route. Multi-competition - track any number of slugs via config. Auth resolves KAGGLE_API_TOKEN through Hermes's secret scope (declared secret in the manifest) or lets the CLI read ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json; child processes get a minimal explicit environment; the token is never logged or echoed. entries.name: kairos
entries.description: The god of the opportune moment, now working for Hermes. It waits for a clean stopping point to offer a short break or a wind-down at the bedtime you chose, saves your place so stopping costs nothing, and reports only what your data supports. Disclosure — reads Hermes's own session store (state.db, read-only: message timestamps, roles and tool names, no message text) to chart when you work; `sleep_import` reads the sleep export file you or the agent name (CSV, Gadgetbridge SQLite, Xiaomi folder), and `kairos_wearable` calls only MCP servers you list in `plugins.entries.kairos.mcp_allowlist`; adds short blocks to the conversation through `pre_llm_call` (wind-down nudge, break suggestion, the opt-in pomodoro offer, and once per new session the handoff note the agent saved when you last stopped, kept in the plugin's data folder), never into cron or subagent turns; `on_session_end` records, with the pomodoro on, when each turn ended, whether it completed, and its tool-call count (timestamps and counts only, in the plugin's own database); the optional quiet-hours guard can require approval for or block destructive terminal/file/code tool calls during hours you set.

entries.name: kanban-empowered
entries.description: A redesign for the Hermes kanban: per-board project status, a dashboard that explains what is really happening across your boards, a live summary of what each agent is doing right now, a chain view that shows where a block starts, and a fast way to answer what the kanban needs from you, by Telegram or Desktop. Cards waiting on a person get a structured ask, reminders and an escalation; cards held by guards or parked by host failures are reported or undone within a budget. No card stays silently stuck. Disclosure — a coordinator runs inside the gateway's kanban dispatch tick (coordinator profile only, leader lock, no extra process); it reads every board's kanban database and metadata through Hermes' kanban functions and writes only through them (comments, unblocking a waiting card when its owner answers, undoing an infrastructure park, reassigning a card on the release command); its SQLite state lives under the coordinator profile's plugin-data/kanban-empowered and is read by the plugin in every other profile, and its doctor command reads every profile's config.yaml read-only; it consumes Telegram replies from the configured owners to its own messages before they reach the agent, except that an owner's answer to a card a worker cannot run is rewritten into an instruction (card title, assignee and the owner's answer) and passed on as a normal turn to the Hermes session of that same chat, reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (the gateway's bot) only through Hermes' secret scope, and, apart from the auxiliary model below, calls only the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage, editMessageText, pinChatMessage to the configured owner chats, one pinned panel; never getUpdates) plus Hermes' own IPv4 fallback path (DNS-over-HTTPS lookups of api.telegram.org at dns.google and cloudflare-dns.com); to show what a running card is doing, the Desktop backend reads that worker's recent session from its profile's state.db read-only (what the agent wrote, including reasoning, and tool names; never commands or tool output), redacts secrets and sends it to the Hermes auxiliary model the user configured, only when the session changed and at most once a minute per card; when the user asks to explain a project's blocks, it also sends that project's waiting cards (titles, block reasons, options and counts, already redacted; no sessions, comments or command output) to the same auxiliary model; no shell commands and no telemetry; imports private Hermes kanban, i18n, profile, plugin and Telegram-network modules (listed in its README); ships an optional core patch adding kanban veto hooks that the user applies by hand to the Hermes checkout (the plugin never applies it, and `hermes update` drops it), and registers kanban_pre_claim only on a Hermes build that exposes it.

entries.name: kanban-gantt
entries.description: One board, four views, and each answers a different question: List says what the work is, Timeline says when it happened, Graph says what hangs off what, and the Whiteboard lays the same cards out as a spatial plan you can arrange, frame and link by hand. The Graph view draws a card per task and an arrow per dependency, laid out top-down by longest path (or left to right, by status, or as a compact grid), with a transitive reduction that counts the arrows it implies instead of hiding them, links you draw, move and delete where they are drawn, and a click that lights the whole upstream and downstream lineage of a task. The Timeline renders any board as real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a period selector from 6 hours to 7 days. The List view trades the bars for a dense table — task, assignee, status, last activity. Quick scopes (Running, Blocked, Open, All) narrow the board in all three views alike, and a lineage switch widens any of them to what leads to the selection and what follows it. Tasks are created from the page (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parented by drag & drop or from the drawer, and moved between boards with their children; any task with files carries a paperclip, its files listed on demand — the board payload carries only a count — and previewed by type (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or downloaded. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Since 1.10 the header keeps its reading controls on one row — scope chips, a segmented period selector that zooms the Timeline and filters the other views, and the search — while the camera is a single floating bar (−, zoom, +, Fit) shared by the Timeline, the Graph and the Whiteboard, with the Fit state lit in the accent colour and the Graph's footer counting the cards in scope. Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create boards, optionally defaulting to a project's repo folder; create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; change a task's model, provider and reasoning-effort override; reclaim a running task, which releases its worker claim and resets its failure count; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download; read a task's worker log from the kanban worker-log folder); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN_GANTT_WS=0; no third-party network.

entries.name: kanban-stream
entries.description: Live-stream Hermes kanban worker activity to a Telegram ops channel: one edit-in-place message per task with rolling tool-call history, elapsed timer, tokens/sec, thinking indicator, and a pinned final state (done/blocked). Mid-task steering via task comments — /steer from Telegram through the bundled companion daemon, or straight from the board. Ships disabled by default; needs a dedicated ops bot (KANBAN_STREAM_BOT_TOKEN + KANBAN_STREAM_ALLOWED_USERS). Outbound calls go only to api.telegram.org; reads the kanban DB read-only; no telemetry, no self-update. Disclosure — sends kanban task titles, summaries and tool names with command/path snippets to the Telegram chat you configure via your own bot; the optional steer daemon posts allowlisted Telegram users' /steer text as task comments that reach the running worker.

entries.name: kanban-task-threads
entries.description: Give every Hermes kanban task a live Discord forum thread with a rewritten status card and append-only event log. Disclosure — sends task and lifecycle data to the configured Discord webhook (no host allowlist). Cards and event replies use built-in or operator-configured templates and may include identifiers, titles, status, assignment, branch and workspace metadata, relationships and blocking details, comments, event actors, reviewers, reasons, summaries, and configured dashboard links; the comment excerpt length is configurable. Fixed prerequisite announcements additionally send the prerequisite task ID, title, assignee, and up to 140 characters of its body and are not template-configurable. The absolute workspace path is off by default and requires explicit opt-in. Reads the kanban database read-only and stores thread mapping state under <kanban_home>/kanban/plugins/kanban-task-threads/. With an optional existing publisher-profile Discord bot token, reads forum and thread metadata; creates or repairs managed status tags and emojis; replaces applied tags on plugin-managed threads; renames threads; and archives or unarchives them. Discord fetches webhook avatars from the configured HTTPS asset origin. Disclosure — the avatar asset origin defaults to the author-hosted https://diegomarino.github.io/kanban-task-threads (disable with avatars_enabled: false). With the bot token the periodic metadata audit also lists the guild's active threads (filtered to the forum) and may rewrite the forum's available-tag list to add the 11 managed status tags (requires Manage Channels).

entries.name: kanzo-board
entries.description: Your Kanzo kanban board (github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo) as a Hermes Desktop sidebar page. The page runs the board's own web UI from the user's running board inside SandboxedFrame, with a bridge that routes the frame's requests, storage, confirm() and links through the plugin. When no board answers, the page offers to install the official Kanzo release, start it, or join a shared board; a bar offers to add Kanzo's MCP server so the agent can work on the board. Disclosure — backend routes under /api/plugins/kanzo-board/ proxy requests to the configured board (127.0.0.1 on Kanzo's port from $KANZO_HOME/config.toml or ~/kanzo, or the board_url setting); paths are limited to that board. Only on a user click: downloads one file from github.com/emanuele-em/kanzo releases, checked against a SHA-256 pinned in the plugin, and writes the kanzo program to $CARGO_HOME/bin or ~/.cargo/bin (never over an existing one); runs `kanzo service install` (a login service), `kanzo --no-open` (detached, log in plugin-data/kanzo-board/ in the active profile's Hermes home), `kanzo join <address>`, and `hermes mcp add kanzo` (adds an mcp_servers entry with all of Kanzo's tools, including delete_task, enabled without per-call trust prompts). Runs `kanzo --version` for the status screen. Every kanzo process gets a minimal allowlisted environment (PATH, home/temp, KANZO_*, CARGO_HOME, XDG_*, locale, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, proxy and Windows system vars), never Hermes' API keys; only `hermes mcp add` inherits Hermes' environment. Reads Hermes' config read-only. The page loads the board's images and translation file directly from the board. Kanzo has no login. No telemetry, no update check.

known_issues: Turn on both switches on the Kanzo Board row in Capabilities → Plugins (Agent for the backend, Desktop for the page), then restart the gateway.
Shows Kanzo's current web UI (0.4.x) through a bridge; a Kanzo release that rebuilds its page may need a plugin update.

entries.name: kareverse
entries.description: Elder care at home in Bangalore, India, from Hermes through Kareverse's public MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.kareverse.com/mcp, no sign-in): search services and prices, read a service's details, the monthly Care Plan, service areas and care guides, and send a callback request to the Kareverse team. Bundles one skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to www.kareverse.com, operated by Kareverse; submit_enquiry sends the name, phone number and details the user provides to Kareverse so the team can call back, requires consent: true, and the package marks the server trust: untrusted so Hermes asks before it runs. The other six tools are read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: kata
entries.description: Learns the multi-step tool routines your agent keeps repeating across conversations and, only after you review and approve each one, compiles it into a single deterministic tool that runs its steps without model round-trips in between. Proposals show the steps, data flow between them, permissions, input and output schemas, per-step side effects and a twelve-check offline validation (exact replay of recorded runs, held-out fit, injected failures and timeouts, secret scan, tool schema fingerprints). Approve, reject, disable, roll back and inspect run traces from /kata, `hermes kata` or a dashboard tab. Disclosure — records tool names, arguments and results (first 64 KB, secret-named keys and common credential formats redacted) plus model request timing and token counts to a local SQLite file under its plugin data directory, kept for 30 days by default; registers tools only after explicit approval and executes their steps through ctx.dispatch_tool; katas whose steps have external or unclassified effects escalate every call to Hermes's own approval prompt with a fresh rule key, so remembered approvals never repeat them and unattended runs follow Hermes's approval policy; side-effecting steps are never retried; makes no network, model or subprocess calls of its own.
entries.title: Kata
known_issues: Approved katas are registered as additional kata_<name> tools at runtime; they are not listed in provides_tools because they do not exist until you approve one.
Routines are linear. Branching on a result stays with the agent.
Values inside free-form text output cannot be referenced; they become inputs instead.
