entries.name: katara
entries.description: Katara memory provider — recalls facts and Brain/Wiki knowledge from your Katara organization before each turn, with katara_recall / katara_entity / katara_remember / katara_forget tools and mirroring of Hermes's built-in memory writes, over Katara's MCP memory API. Maintained by Katara. Disclosure — network calls only to the configured Katara MCP endpoint (mcp.katara.ai by default) with the profile's KATARA_API_KEY as bearer token (read through Hermes secrets, never from files; redirects are not followed); every non-trivial prompt is sent as a recall query (auto_recall, on by default); entries Hermes adds or replaces in its built-in MEMORY/USER stores and facts saved with katara_remember are written to the Katara Brain with world visibility, readable by every agent connected to it (mirror_memory_writes, on by default); no transcripts uploaded, no telemetry, no shell commands, no background daemons (short-lived threads for mirroring); stores only $HERMES_HOME/katara/config.json.

entries.name: keepvoice-hermes
entries.description: Start a KeepVoice voice-cleanup job from an authorized upload, track creator review and approval, and release the final video only for the approved revision. entries.name: keryx
entries.description: Outbound phone calls from your own phone. Hermes writes a brief and calls place_call; after you approve (every call, single use), your phone dials over Bluetooth hands-free through PipeWire's telephony API, the plugin plays an AI-disclosure line, and a realtime voice model (OpenAI Realtime or GPT-Live) holds the conversation, asking you mid-call when it needs a decision. The outcome, details and transcript go back to Hermes; /calls lists recent calls. Guardrails in code: emergency, short-code and premium numbers blocked, quiet hours, hourly rate limit, hard 5-minute cap. Linux only (PipeWire >= 1.4, a paired phone). Disclosure — places real calls on the user's SIM; call audio streams to OpenAI (wss://api.openai.com realtime or live sessions) plus OpenAI TTS for the disclosure line and, for GPT-Live, one Responses request per call; runs busctl, pw-dump, pw-record, pw-play, pw-link, pw-cli and espeak-ng; audio processes and two temporary virtual PipeWire nodes exist only during an approved call; stores a call log (and recordings only if `record: true`) under plugin-data/keryx; reads OPENAI_API_KEY through Hermes secrets only.

entries.name: kestra-oncall
entries.description: Puts Hermes on call for Kestra. When an execution in an allowed namespace fails, Hermes reads the failed task, its error logs and what changed since the last good run, proposes the smallest fix to the flow and asks you in chat. After one approval it saves the fix as a new flow revision, replays the failed execution from the task that failed (tasks that already succeeded are not rerun), follows the replay and checks the result. A failed replay restores the previous revision if the flow is still at the fixed one. Kestra Pause tasks become chat questions you can answer from any Hermes surface. A Kestra on-call dashboard tab and Desktop pane list incidents, proposals and pauses (read-only). Disclosure: network: only the Kestra URL you configure (kestra_url, HTTPS required except for loopback and explicitly allowed private hosts), with the Kestra credentials you give Hermes (KESTRA_USERNAME and KESTRA_PASSWORD or KESTRA_API_TOKEN, read through Hermes secret scope). No other host, no telemetry. Writes to Kestra: a flow update, a replay, a rollback to the previous revision and resume or kill of a paused execution. Each needs a person: the typed command /kestra apply <id> <hash> (the hash must match the stored proposal) or Hermes's approval card for the two write tools with the whole stored diff, bound to the proposal hash. Diffs too long to read in full are refused. The write tools refuse in webhook, cron, single-query and unknown surfaces and the model-driven path refuses while Hermes approvals are bypassed. Fails closed: an empty namespaces setting allows nothing and protected_flows are diagnosis-only. Stored data: incidents, flow sources, error logs, task outputs, diffs, proposals and decision records in the plugin's profile-scoped SQLite database. Data sent elsewhere: the tools return flow sources, error logs, task outputs and execution inputs to the model, so they go to the profile's LLM provider. The dashboard routes under /api/plugins/kestra-oncall only read and show diffs and logs to anyone who can open the Hermes dashboard. hermes kestra-oncall setup --apply adds one named webhook route to config.yaml and never deploys a Kestra flow. Anyone holding WEBHOOK_SECRET can start a read-only model run against your Kestra. AI-assisted implementation.
entries.title: Kestra On-Call
known_issues: Kestra has no compare-and-set on flow updates, so the check-then-write window is narrowed by a fresh re-read and a read-back, not removed.

Slash-command writes are typed approvals (/kestra apply <id> <hash>) because ctx.dispatch_tool does not run pre_tool_call hooks on Hermes main or v0.23.0 and a plugin command has no way to raise an approval card in a chat.

Model-driven writes are refused while Hermes approvals are bypassed (--yolo, /yolo, approvals.mode: off). The check imports tools.approval.is_approval_bypass_active, which hermes plugins validate reports as one non-public import.
Built for plugins.isolation: in_process (Hermes's default). Host isolation skips CLI registration and was not tested.
Tested on Kestra 2.0.9 only. A failed Loop cannot be replayed on that version and a failed Subflow is diagnosis-only.
The end-to-end run used Hermes main at c3354ea. On v0.23.0 scenarios S1, S1b, S2 and S3 passed, as did validate, doctor and the live plugin test.

entries.name: keychain
entries.description: Keep Hermes provider credentials in the macOS login keychain instead of plaintext .env. Registers a SecretSource (secrets.keychain), so startup resolution runs through Hermes's own orchestrator, after ~/.hermes/.env loads and before credentials are read — the same path the bundled Bitwarden and 1Password sources use. Bindings are explicit (secrets.keychain.env: ENV_VAR: keychain-account) or discovered from an index the plugin keeps inside the keychain, so `hermes keychain put NAME` is the whole setup. Adds keychain_status (vault-backed vs still-plaintext inventory; names, lengths and outcomes only), keychain_migration_plan (report-only: lists candidates and returns the exact `hermes keychain migrate ...` command; writes nothing) and keychain_audit (fetch/migrate trail), plus a `hermes keychain put|ls|rm|test|migrate|status|audit` CLI. Migration is operator-only in that CLI: it stores each value, verifies it by readback, backs up .env (0600), then removes the variable through hermes_cli.config.remove_env_value() — the `hermes config unset` path, so core's .env lock and its refusals for package-managed installs and admin-managed keys still apply. Disclosure — reads and writes generic-password items in the user's login keychain through /usr/bin/security called by absolute path (service `hermes` by default); no network calls and no third-party service, nothing leaves the machine; the index of stored names lives in a keychain item (`hermes!index`) and the audit log in <hermes home>/plugin-data/keychain/audit.jsonl; the only .env write is the operator-run `hermes keychain migrate` described above; the agent-facing tools write nothing; a locked keychain or denied ACL is a warning, never a startup block; a stored value is passed on argv for the single `security add-generic-password` call (visible to same-user processes for that moment) while reads, the once-per-process hot path, never put a value on argv. macOS-only, no Python dependencies, no env vars.

entries.name: kfchow-llm-value-router
entries.description: Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI_API_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS_API_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.

entries.name: kimchi-acp-provider
entries.description: The Kimchi coding harness (kimchi.dev) as a Hermes model provider over ACP stdio — spawns kimchi --mode acp keeping the harness's permission prompts on (YOLO opt-in via KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo"), the harness owns its own auth, and completed tool calls surface as inline bullets in the reply. Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (`kimchi --mode acp`, overridable with KIMCHI_ACP_COMMAND / KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. The harness calls kimchi.dev with its own stored login and runs its own shell, file and web tools. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI_ACP_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI_CONFIG_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes.

entries.name: kin
entries.description: Gives Hermes Desktop a face. Pick one of thirteen original characters, six 3D busts and seven 2D cartoons, each with its own voice. It watches your sessions, frowns when a step fails, and grins when a turn finishes. An optional overlay adds a plain-English task drawer, voice input, and one-click screen diagnosis. Disclosure — the optional overlay is a separate Electron app you install with npm and run yourself. It reads Hermes's state.db (read-only), processes.json and the latest terminal output to draw its task drawer. When you click it, it captures the active window or terminal with the OS screenshot tool, OCRs it with tesseract, and submits that text to Hermes as a prompt. Switching persona runs `hermes config set` for tts.openai.voice and voice.gpt_live.voice, which changes Hermes's TTS voice everywhere. While the overlay runs, the first 280 characters of each reply are spoken through Hermes's configured TTS provider, and opt-in mic audio is transcribed by local whisper.cpp or Hermes's configured STT provider.

entries.name: kinocut
entries.description: Guardrailed local video editing: Kinocut's MCP server plus two workflow skills (editing and short-form repurposing). Trim, caption, reformat and check quality with local FFmpeg. Portable Agent Plugins v1 configuration and skills, no plugin code. Requires uv and FFmpeg on PATH; launches uvx kinocut==1.16.4 over stdio. First launch downloads Kinocut and dependencies from PyPI. URL inputs download the requested media; font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub. Explicit Revideo dependency installation runs npm ci and may download renderer dependencies. Local FFmpeg editing and color grading need no account or API key. Kinocut's optional vision calls default off and require explicit configuration: legacy product descriptions use an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, while sampled-frame QC uses Anthropic. The README explains how to use the host's image model instead, including local models. Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry default off. Unverified Hyperframes browser previews and Docker renders require explicit telemetry consent. Hyperframes capture/snapshots disable implicit model analysis. These controls are not a network sandbox; see the plugin README for configuration and remaining network use. Disclosure — launches `uvx kinocut==1.16.4` over stdio, which downloads Kinocut and its dependencies from PyPI on first launch; edits and writes local video files with FFmpeg; URL inputs download the requested media, font and model-weight features fetch assets from GitHub, and an explicit Revideo install runs `npm ci`; optional vision features (off by default) send selected images or sampled frames to an Anthropic-compatible endpoint or Anthropic; Revideo and Hyperframes telemetry stay off unless the operator enables them.

entries.name: kleos
entries.description: Kleos, the AI marketing team for small businesses, through its hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.getkleos.ai/mcp; OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, signed in with the user's own Kleos login; no keys in config). Thirty-one tools: list businesses, read the month's calendar and open slots, plan the next 30 days, draft a post or a blog article in the business's voice, save a post in the user's own words, list and approve drafts waiting for review, schedule an approved post to a connected channel, report results (posts published, impressions, clicks, leads) and whether ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and Perplexity recommend the business, read the tracked AI questions, buyer searches and competitor pages, read and record product updates, read and confirm the buyers' day-to-day topics, and the planning writes the Kleos director uses (a calendar entry with its reason, a slot brief, a tracked question, a competitor, a note). Bundles one skill (kleos) that says which tool fits which task and that nothing is published without the user asking. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, and the optional OAuth sign-in, goes to app.getkleos.ai (New Odyssey), authenticated with the user's own Kleos OAuth login or an optional KLEOS_API_KEY sent as a bearer header; drafting, planning and AI-visibility checks spend the workspace's plan allowance, and approving or scheduling publishes to the business's connected channels (approve_draft can publish when the business has auto-publish on). The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before any tool not annotated read-only and refuses those in unattended runs; the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: klieg
entries.description:
Motion design for Hermes. klieg_motion lets the agent author a scene - kinetic type, transitions, lower-thirds, logo stings, loops, explainers - as a declarative spec, a template, or raw HTML+GSAP, and render it to MP4/GIF locally with no API keys; rendering is deterministic (seek + screenshot per frame) so motion is smooth, and each render is a detached job verified by its artefact. The same job engine drives Blender and other DCC hosts (Houdini, Nuke, Cinema 4D, After Effects, Resolve) behind one adapter interface: probe what is installed, run scripts inside the host, render frame ranges as resumable jobs that survive the agent's shell. A job is only "done" when its artefact is newer than the job started - klieg_jobs verify compares mtime and the promised frame count, so a render that dies at frame 3 of 288, or emits frames from a blend that failed to rebuild, cannot report success. klieg_plan resolves a pass without running or writing anything. One GPU, one render: a second request queues behind the holder, queue=false refuses, and killing the holder dispatches the next job. klieg_publish encodes with explicit BT.709 conversion and colour tags, including mid-sequence and gapped frame sets. Built-in gates (flash, loop, stats, safe_band) measure any frame set with numpy/Pillow, no DCC required. klieg_ledger seals a finished job's provenance - scene, script, every frame, colour manifest, encode - into sha256 commitments and checks it for drift later. Children get a 13-variable environment allow-list, never os.environ, and key/token/secret names are dropped and recorded.
Disclosure - klieg_run, klieg_track and klieg_gate script=... execute model-authored Python inside the host application with the user's privileges; klieg_motion render/preview executes model-authored HTML+JavaScript in a headless browser (playwright/chromium) and spawns ffmpeg. All are approval-gated per action (read-only actions of mixed tools pass free); unattended runs fail closed. Klieg is not a sandbox: an approved script or scene is arbitrary code, and a malicious scene file executes when the host opens it. Outputs are refused under system and credential paths. The flash gate is a screening approximation, not a certified Harding test; the ledger detects drift but is not a signature. A live session bridge into a running Blender is available through klieg_session; other hosts remain batch-only. After Effects and Resolve are reported present-but-unsupported rather than faked. Motion rendering requires playwright + a chromium headless shell (reported as data when absent). Built with AI assistance (Hermes Agent); author-reviewed and tested. Disclosure — klieg_run, klieg_track, klieg_gate with a script and klieg_session eval run model-written Python inside Blender or another installed DCC app with your user privileges, and klieg_motion runs model-written HTML and JavaScript in a headless Chromium (playwright, sandbox off) and spawns ffmpeg; each of these, plus renders, encodes and job kills, asks for approval first and fails closed in unattended runs. Opening a scene file in the host app can run code stored in it. Detached render jobs keep running after the agent's shell exits. Job logs, scenes, the taste model and ledger live in the plugin's data folder.

entries.name: klipper-print-watch
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Built on the Moonraker HTTP API. Cron reports klippy_shutdown, complete, error, paused (after printing), cancelled, stalled. Disclosure — Talks to the one Moonraker URL you set. Over plain http on a LAN, MOONRAKER_API_KEY is sent unencrypted. While a person is in the session, pause, resume and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Hermes shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt. Choosing always adds one config.yaml command_allowlist line. For pause and resume, answering "always" covers only the same action at the same Moonraker origin, and only while a person is in the session. Cancel asks every time. Its rule_key changes on each call, so a saved always line does not approve the next cancel. It does not move the printer in cron, hermes -q, webhook, or plugins.isolation: host. cron, hermes -q, and unattended sessions default to deny, and this plugin also refuses the move after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a move and approve it. A different action or origin asks again. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. schedule writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/klipper-print-watch.py and creates the job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. Running schedule again switches an existing job with hermes cron edit --script --no-agent and clears the stored prompt. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until that next schedule. On that leftover turn, pre_tool_call allows klipper_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool name. A deferred tool named inside tool_call is checked under that inner name. Pause, resume, and cancel stay refused on it. Removing the plugin leaves the script job. Run unschedule first, or hermes cron remove after. The scheduled script does not call the vision model. vision_check, off by default, still applies when klipper_watch itself runs on a cron turn, and it does not cancel the print. The plugin host cannot run that tool watch. The scheduled script is started by Hermes cron, so plugins.isolation: host does not stop it. Not tested on real hardware.

entries.name: kokoro-tts
entries.description: Local Kokoro-82M text-to-speech on Apple Silicon (MLX) and Linux (PyTorch on CPU): adds the kokoro-mlx speech provider (tts.provider: kokoro-mlx) with sentence-by-sentence PCM streaming for voice mode, read-aloud and text_to_speech, an optional voice per language that switches per sentence between Brazilian Portuguese and English (tested by the author) and Italian (not yet tested by the author), and an optional dictionary of English words a non-English voice pronounces in English without changing voice; plus hermes kokoro install, status, restart, voices, say, words and uninstall. Disclosure — hermes kokoro install creates a separate Python 3.11 environment with uv (about 1.1 GB on macOS or 1.3 GB on Linux from PyPI, plus spaCy's en_core_web_sm wheel from its GitHub release and, on Linux, the CPU-only torch wheel from download.pytorch.org, both pinned by SHA-256), downloads the model at a pinned revision from Hugging Face (mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16 on macOS, hexgrad/Kokoro-82M on Linux, about 340 MB), and installs a background service that keeps a local server running (a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux, both named dev.hermes.kokoro-tts). The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (it refuses other addresses), runs offline, and does not log the text; the text to speak goes only to that local server, bypassing any proxy settings. entries.name: kokpit
entries.description: A personal cockpit for Hermes Agent. When a session produces something, Kokpit leaves a short card and receipt in plain Markdown that Hermes, Claude Code and Codex all read, so the next session picks up where the last one stopped. It also captures notes and todos from any Hermes chat, gives a morning brief, and runs a night pass whose proposals quote their exact source lines. Local, stdlib only. Disclosure — Adds notes from your Kokpit Markdown vault (threads, last session card, latest receipt, related notes) to each turn's context; by default writes a session card and receipt into the vault when a session captured notes or wrote files (listing the paths written); its tools let the agent append notes, tasks, journal lines and accepted idea files to the vault without a prompt and read the Kokpit app's SQLite database read-only; optional settings, all off by default, run the night pass in a background thread at session start (`night_auto`), send up to 10 vault files to your configured model (`night_model`), and run `systemctl --user is-active` for units you list (`server`).

entries.name: kosa8
entries.description: Terminal backend that runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools in a kosa8 Cloud sandbox (a microVM with its own kernel) instead of on the Hermes machine. Select it with `hermes config set terminal.backend kosa8`. Disclosure — every command, file read and file write is an HTTPS call to the kosa8 Cloud API (https://api.kosa8.com by default, or the configured base_url) and runs inside the remote sandbox; the plugin runs no shell on the Hermes machine and reads no local files beyond its own config. One stored credential, the kosa8 Cloud API key (KOSA8_API_KEY), read through Hermes's secret scope. kosa8 Cloud is a paid service (plans from $29 a month); sandboxes count toward the account's plan, sleep after the configured idle time and can be given a lifetime (ttl). No telemetry.

entries.name: kubernetes
entries.description: Write one namespace in cluster.json to approve the scope, then use four reads: list pods, get one pod, list events, and read logs. Kubernetes is a registered trademark of The Linux Foundation. kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 is the GitHub release binary. The plugin downloads kubernetes-mcp-server-<os>-<arch> from https://github.com/containers/kubernetes-mcp-server/releases/download/v0.0.68/ into the plugin data directory, checks the sha256 against constants taken from that release's GitHub asset digest, and starts that file. MCP initialize and tools/list are answered before that download. A partial download is kept and continued with HTTP Range. A mismatch, including a file that was already there, is refused. read_only is true, toolsets stay core, and only pods_list_in_namespace, pods_get, events_list, and pods_log are enabled. Helm is not offered. Secret, ConfigMap, and ServiceAccount are denied. configuration_view is not listed. prod, production, live, and prd names are refused unless allow_production is true. Public and link-local hosts are always refused. The host must be local, and DNS is not resolved. readOnlyHint is true, so no approval card is shown. Before the call, name the namespace, the object, and that it only reads, because status, events, and logs reach the model. This plugin does not create a cron job. Disclosure — reads the kubeconfig you name in cluster.json (read-only) and sends its token only to that kubeconfig's API host (plain http sends it unencrypted); on the first tool call downloads the kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68 GitHub release binary (~90 MB) into the plugin data directory, refuses it unless its sha256 matches the pinned release digest, and runs it as a subprocess (a file swap between the check and the start is not fully excluded); pod status, events and logs reach the model, with password-like env values and last-applied-configuration redacted; no HTTP proxy is used; gateway users can call these read tools with that kubeconfig; stop with hermes plugins disable kubernetes or hermes tools disable mcp-kubernetes.

entries.name: kumi
entries.description: Kumi puts Hermes inside Ableton Live, REAPER and Renoise: it hears your mix, makes changes you can undo, and turns your samples into new sounds. Disclosure — after you approve setup, downloads the Kumi release this pin names for your platform (27–35 MB, SHA-256 checked) from github.com/user1303836/kumi/releases into HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/kumi/ and installs Kumi's part in your DAW (Live's Remote Script with its Kumi Ears device, a REAPER extension or a Renoise tool) at paths you approve; a newer release comes only with a new catalog pin. Runs Kumi's runtime and DAW bridge as local child processes on loopback that stop with the chat or after idling. Reads the open DAW project, the sample folders you list, HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/audio, VST3 metadata in the standard plug-in folders and, after you approve, an existing Kumi's DAW connection files. Writes the Max for Live devices, presets and wavetables you ask for as new files in Live's User Library, copies your saved project beside it before some changes, and, using an existing Kumi's installation, keeps a write lease and listening renders in its folder. Runs a DAW script you ask for with the DAW's access to your computer (asked first, with its code). Plays the project only for a listen or play you ask for. Sends FOCUS notes and measurements to your Hermes model, and with listen_interpretation on, a small band-energy image to the auxiliary model. Mirelo (paid, off by default): only with your key and a credit cap above 0, approved prompts and audio go to api.mirelo.ai and the transfer hosts it names. No telemetry.

entries.name: lahja
entries.description: Arabic dialect speech-to-text (provider lahja), fully local: a dialect fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo on whisper.cpp keeps Levantine, Gulf, Egyptian, Iraqi and Maghrebi speech as spoken instead of rewriting it as formal Arabic (WER 29% vs 41% for stock turbo with the same VAD, across 13 dialects), Silero VAD always on plus a filter for subtitle-credit hallucinations («ترجمة نانسي قنقر»), per-note language routing that never forces a non-Arabic language (English, including accented English the dialect model writes in Arabic letters, goes to a stock Whisper model you choose), and corrections taught once with /stt-fix. Disclosure — audio is decoded locally in a temp dir deleted after each call; nothing is uploaded. Network only in `hermes lahja setup`, which downloads commit-pinned, SHA-256- and size-checked model files from huggingface.co (redirected to its *.cdn.hf.co CDN); the dialect model is a community ggml mirror (JoaoZaokk) that bench/convert.sh reproduces byte for byte from oddadmix's official weights. Runs ffmpeg (local files only) and whisper-cli with a fixed argv, no shell, one deadline per note, at most max_parallel at once, and a minimal environment (PATH, LANG, LC_ALL, TMPDIR, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) without Hermes' variables. Reads the audio Hermes passes, its own model files, and an optional other_languages_model .bin you configure. Writes model files and the two phrases of each /stt-fix correction to its plugin data dir; corrections apply profile-wide and any user the gateway admits can add one (control/invisible characters refused, max 500). No audio or transcripts stored; no tools, hooks, background processes, telemetry or credentials.

entries.name: lane-keeper
entries.description: Keeps your agent on a few active lanes (current commitments): new ideas the user mentions are saved as dormant markdown lanes instead of quietly becoming work, only the user can promote one (/lanes promote, cap-aware, forces choosing what to park), and stale or over-cap lanes are called out once. Status lives in a registry in the plugin's own data, so editing a lane file can't promote it; the hermes lanes CLI is read-only. Disclosure — no network calls, no subprocesses, no LLM calls of its own, no telemetry, no background work; one declared Python dependency (pyyaml>=6,<7); never reads credential stores; reads/writes *.md files in lanes_dir (default <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/lane-keeper/lanes, or a top-level folder the user configures) and <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/lane-keeper/registry-<hash>.json (statuses, stale notices given, ≤300 session fingerprints); sends to the model provider a rules section plus active lane titles/next actions and up to 15 dormant titles once per session in the system prompt, and a one-line note in the user turn only when lanes change; its pre_tool_call hook reads tool names/arguments to block agent writes to lane data, status-changing CLI calls, Lane Keeper settings changes and disabling the plugin, and stores nothing.

entries.name: language-lock
entries.description: Your agent answers in your language, and stays there (hermes-agent#130117). Learns your language from your recent messages or a setting, detects each reply's language without a model (20 languages, by script and common words, ignoring code and links), and after a reply drifts tells the agent to switch back on the next turn. Asking for a translation on purpose is respected. /lang shows drifts caught and corrected. No model calls, nothing stored.

entries.name: laso-finance
entries.description: Spend USDC in the real world from Hermes: prepaid cards, gift cards, push-to-card, Venmo/PayPal and bank payouts, through the Laso Finance API. Native plugin, standard library only. Sign-in is the OAuth device flow (link and code handed to the human, approved on any device), so there is no key to paste and it works over SSH and the messaging gateway. Every tool that moves money or mints a credential goes through the Hermes approval gate first. Disclosure — the tools move real funds from the user's Laso account and agent wallet; 25 money-moving or credential-minting tools ask for Hermes approval first, but approvals.mode off / yolo, or approvals.cron_mode/unattended_mode approve, let them run without a prompt; laso_buy_with_saved_card is not prompted in Hermes (Laso requires a passkey approval on the holder's device before an order), and laso_move_agent_wallet_funds moves USDC between the agent wallet's own Solana and Base sides (0.075% fee) without a prompt; all traffic goes to laso.finance only; the approved key is saved as LASO_API_KEY in the profile's .env and removed when Laso rejects it.

entries.name: last-price
entries.description: Lets Hermes haggle with buyers in chat while the plugin, not the model, owns every price that leaves. You set an item's floor from your terminal; it stays in plugin state and never reaches a model, tool result, prompt or log. Every deal reply is held and checked, and one offering less is rewritten before anyone sees it; a buyer who offers or accepts a price the plugin would take is closed at their own number; deal sessions can use only Last Price's three tools (plus Hermes's tool-search bridge, whose calls are checked the same way). Includes hermes lastprice duel --vs-prompt, a side-by-side against a seller with the floor in its prompt (inside Hermes, in the 48-duel bench of version 0.1.1: that seller sold below the floor in 10 of 48 duels; Last Price in 0), and hermes lastprice challenge, a public 'buy it below my floor' Telegram challenge. Disclosure — buyer messages and Hermes's draft replies go to your model provider, as in any Hermes chat; a rewrite of a too-low draft goes to the same model (it sees the buyer's message, the draft and the current counter, never the floor). In a duel or bench, the buyer model (your own model, or the one you name with --buyer) receives the buyer's instruction and the whole conversation so far, the seller's replies included. duel and bench start hermes chat child processes in your terminal (no --yolo; with --ignore-rules and --source tool, so your own rules and memory stay out and the duel sessions stay out of your session list): the Last Price seller gets Last Price's three tools only; the stock seller gets Hermes's todo toolset plus every plugin toolset your profile turns on by default, and its system prompt carries the duel item's floor, which by default is a demo item's throwaway floor, never one of yours unless you pass --item <id> --real-item. Hermes saves that prompt with the stock session in state.db; each duel deletes its stock session when it ends (hermes sessions delete), and the stock seller's replies stay in Hermes's 7-day deletion tombstones and in Last Price's duel records (and the deleted bytes in state.db's free pages until hermes sessions optimize). hermes chat starts Hermes's background gateway when none is running; a duel or bench that started it stops it when it ends. challenge start and shop on run only in a profile with memory off (memory.memory_enabled and memory.user_profile_enabled false, no memory.provider; read with hermes config get, and refused if unreadable), so strangers never chat with an agent that knows you: run them from a dedicated profile (hermes -p shop ...) with a neutral SOUL.md. challenge start changes six Hermes settings through hermes config set (Telegram open access, a Last-Price-only Telegram toolset, owner-only slash commands) after reading their earlier values one by one with hermes config get (it reads no .env and parses no config.yaml), and challenge end restores all six. Floors are stored as plain JSON in plugin state: hidden from the model in deal sessions, readable on your machine by you and by any agent you give file tools to. No payment provider is called in 0.1.x, no telemetry.
entries.title: Last Price
known_issues: Pay links are placeholders in 0.1.x (no payment provider is called).

Telegram and WhatsApp deal chats (hermes lastprice shop on <platform>) and the Telegram challenge (hermes lastprice challenge) are unit-tested; no live messaging run yet, so the live runs so far are terminal duels and benches.

entries.name: lastgood
entries.description: LastGood records which of your preset checks passed on which tested state, and what restoring files will not undo. Checks you choose (file opens, words present, files exist, page loads) run after write_file or patch in an opted-in project, and on demand via /lastgood and /blame. Results are PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN, with a content fingerprint so changed files mark old results stale. Blame shows the first failing step and bounded configured-string presence deltas, not the cause. A ledger lists recognised tool calls a file rollback will not undo, without storing their arguments. Disclosure — the optional url_loads check fetches the http(s) address set in the project's lastgood-config.json (loopback and public hosts; link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused, including after redirects; private ranges only when you turn on allow_private_urls). The lastgood_setup tool refuses page checks, but the agent's own file tools can still edit lastgood-config.json, so leave allow_private_urls off unless you trust what the session writes.

entries.description: Track parcels and ocean containers across 549 carriers and compare USPS, UPS and FedEx rate quotes between US ZIP codes, through the hosted lastscanned Streamable HTTP MCP server plus one workflow skill. entries.name: launch-desk
entries.description: Built something? Ask Hermes to prepare the launch, based on what posts.design learned from launches that worked: ideas from three real launch posts like yours, a post in your own words checked in code for slop, a share card from your own screenshots, colours and logo, and with /launch film a 14-second launch film in your brand plus a checklist so you don't post a sloppy video. You approve a preview first, then get the text, the card and a link that opens X with the post filled in. Disclosure: one posts.design search per run through your own posts MCP server, a fetch of your product site, brand kit and packs stored locally, two check-ins scheduled only if you say Yes, an optional Hermes Desktop page (off until you turn it on) whose read-only backend, served while the plugin is enabled, reads your packs and the times of the check-ins it scheduled, a launch film made only when you ask with /launch film, rendered on your machine by the renderer you set up (a configured command or HyperFrames on PATH) with HyperFrames telemetry off (Launch Desk downloads nothing itself; HyperFrames may download its own headless Chrome on its first render), plus posts.design's free playbook list and, on Pro, one playbook read (1 credit) the first time and again only when posts.design updates it, and nothing is ever posted; see the README for the full list.

entries.name: launchspy
entries.description: Spy on the ads and funnels of the top coaches and course creators through LaunchSpy's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://launchspy.io/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): search creators by niche and country, see who is scaling and how they run ads, read their Meta ads with run dates and EU reach, pull the longest-running ads of a niche, find and take apart their funnels (steps, builder, pixels, payment stack, pricing), size a market by niche and country, and check what is known about any domain. Bundles six workflow skills. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to LaunchSpy's hosted server (launchspy.io) and acts on the user's LaunchSpy account; each tools/call uses one credit (a free account gets 50 trial credits, once; paid plans include monthly credits); the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. All ten tools are annotated read-only and the server is marked untrusted. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth.

entries.name: laya-oneshot
entries.description: Ask typed questions about a piece of text — yes/no, pick one of N, a score on a scale — and get probabilities back in about a second, from an open Laya model that is not running. Loads the checkpoint, answers, exits: no server, no port, no resident memory, no API key. Runs the model locally or on another machine over ssh, so a laptop that is otherwise off answers one call and goes back to sleep. Ships four question sets (triage, email, guard, router) and accepts your own. Disclosure — the text you decide about is sent to the model host, which is either this machine or an ssh host you configure in laya-oneshot's own config; on first use the laya-mlx runtime downloads the Laya checkpoint (~2 GB) from Hugging Face. The model is a ~400M encoder, not a language model: do not use it for multi-step reasoning.

entries.name: layersift
entries.description: Exact, local reading of saved container images: docker save and podman save tars (classic and Docker 25+ layouts) and OCI image archives, including multi-platform indexes and gzip, bzip2 or xz compression. image_summary says where the size goes: each layer with the Dockerfile instruction that made it, the final filesystem size, bytes still shipped after a later layer deletes or overwrites them (which layer added them, which removed them), caches and archives left behind (apt lists, apk/yum/dnf, pip/uv/npm/yarn, Go and Cargo caches, temp directories, .git, compilers) with the fix, and the biggest directories and files; image_layer opens one layer; image_compare compares two images before and after a Dockerfile change. Standard library only: no network, never runs docker or contacts a registry, no credentials, no subprocess, never extracts to disk, no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local image archives you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.
entries.title: Layersift
entries.capability_summary: layersift (community, maintained by rodricksz4h5) Exact, local reading of saved container images: docker save and podman save tars (classic and Docker 25+ layouts) and OCI image archives, including multi-platform indexes and gzip, bzip2 or xz compression. image_summary says where the size goes: each layer with the Dockerfile instruction that made it, the final filesystem size, bytes still shipped after a later layer deletes or overwrites them (which layer added them, which removed them), caches and archives left behind (apt lists, apk/yum/dnf, pip/uv/npm/yarn, Go and Cargo caches, temp directories, .git, compilers) with the fix, and the biggest directories and files; image_layer opens one layer; image_compare compares two images before and after a Dockerfile change. entries.name: lazy-plugin
entries.description: A dashboard page in Hermes Desktop where you describe a plugin and watch it get built. Say what you want — or start from a skill the agent wrote, or a job that runs on a schedule — and your own agent drafts the plan in a chat turn you can read, the code comes from four fixed templates, and the page shows a receipt: plan, files, validator result, and a real try-out of every tool (purrs, needs a key, blocked upstream, held back, half-built, broken — with the exact failing line). The build never runs what it wrote: the try-out is your click, a key only travels to a public https host, and a file tool stays inside its own data dir. Nothing installs itself, and publishing is a SHA-pinned catalog PR you send. Also callable as lazyplugin_create from any conversation. Disclosure — the Desktop "try it" button runs every generated tool for real on your machine (generated `command` tools execute the drafted argv; declared keys are only sent to public https hosts named in the code, never Hermes' own keys), and "publish" uses your `gh` login to create a public GitHub repo for the generated plugin and open a pull request to NousResearch/hermes-agent in one click; builds from `lazyplugin_create` never run generated code.

entries.name: lazybird
entries.description: Lazybird text-to-speech as a Hermes voice provider (tts.provider: lazybird), driven by the Lazybird v2 API. tts.voice takes any voice id from the Lazybird voice library or a voice you cloned or designed in your account (defaults to the official Elyssia voice), and tts.speed is passed through. The API returns MP3, which Hermes converts for Opus voice notes on messaging platforms. No new Python dependencies: the plugin posts with httpx. Disclosure — sends the text being spoken, the chosen voice id and speed, and your LAZYBIRD_API_KEY (header X-API-Key) to api.lazybird.app; synthesis is billed to your Lazybird account's characters; generated audio is written to Hermes's audio cache; no tools, hooks or middleware; no telemetry. Not implemented: realtime streaming (voice-mode replies are spoken sentence by sentence) and voice listing.

known_issues: Output is always MP3; a request for another format gets an .mp3 file.

entries.name: ld-workbench
entries.description: A new tool for high school debate students. Build a Lincoln-Douglas case with a coach, run a full timed round against an AI opponent, answer Extemp questions out loud, and study great speeches. You speak on a real clock that starts when you do. A practice judge writes a full ballot after every round and quotes your own lines back to you, and you can play each one back from your own recording. Try an answer twice and see what got better. Ballots are kept, and the habits that keep costing you are counted across them. Rhetoric lessons mark the figures in famous speeches. The coach asks questions first and writes nothing into your case until you press Add. In any Hermes chat, /debate gives you today's question. New in 0.2: Extemp answers spoken on a real clock, a Rhetoric room, a Ballots page that counts your habits across rounds and shows which way each is heading, and a Start here guide to the four rooms. Disclosure — an independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Nous Research, the National Speech & Debate Association, AllSides or any news outlet. Registers a Desktop page, a dashboard API, the /debate command, two read-only agent tools (debate_record, debate_today; both refuse in scheduled jobs), three model rows and a debate-coach skill; no hooks, middleware or env vars. The microphone opens only while you press Start speaking. Recordings, transcripts, cases, ballots and your extemp file stay in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ld-workbench/, with delete buttons in Settings. Takes go to Hermes's speech-to-text (a cloud provider gets a take only when you press Transcribe now on it) or to the plugin's own speech model, downloaded from huggingface.co (about 145 MB) only on a press. Pressing Hear it sends the AI opponent's or coach's speech text to the text-to-speech voice set up in Hermes. Its own network calls start on a button (Pull headlines: Google News RSS and outlet feeds, https only; Get up to speed: up to 4 public pages from your Hermes web search; a link you save, http or https), public addresses only, with time and size caps. Model calls go to your own Hermes model; with coach examples on, one runs in the background after each 60-second answer. Uses one private Hermes import (tools.voice_mode.transcribe_recording), guarded with a local fallback. No credentials, telemetry, background jobs or self-updates.
entries.title: Debate Workbench
known_issues: Tested on macOS. Windows and Linux are untested.
plugin.yaml declares Hermes 0.21.6 or newer, but 0.2.0 was run live only on Hermes 0.23.1 (Nov 11, 2026).
The judge and the coach are an AI on the model you chose in Hermes. Their points are practice feedback, not a real judge's.
Hermes's speech-to-text returns no word times, so exact line playback and the answer-in-the-first-10-seconds measure work only with the plugin's own speech model.

Transcription imports tools.voice_mode.transcribe_recording, which is not in Hermes's public plugin API. It is guarded and falls back to the plugin's own faster-whisper, so a Hermes release that moves it can turn off Hermes-backed transcription.

To open at once, the page keeps a copy of its last answers (each under 200,000 characters, with secret-looking values removed) in the plugin's own Hermes storage, and shows it until the backend answers.
Start or stop speaking has a keybind with no default key; set one in Keyboard settings.

entries.name: leadpoet
entries.description: Send your website and get customers. Hermes finds verified contacts at companies showing a buying signal, writes emails where every personal line shows its source, lets you approve from your phone, and brings replies back to chat. The first look at who buys from you needs no account. Disclosure — calls the Leadpoet API (leadpoet.com) with your LEADPOET_API_KEY: it can spend Leadpoet credits on contact searches, create and launch email campaigns to third parties from your connected inbox, and send replies, each only after you type the approval code shown under the exact content; it reads public pages of your site and your prospects' sites and sends that text and prospects' replies to your configured Hermes model; the optional `hermes leadpoet watch` cron check runs with no model, launches campaigns you already approved and approves matching drafts unattended; contact details and drafts are stored in the plugin's data folder.

entries.name: lean-mode
entries.description: Cheap-model subagent (quick_run) with a dollar cap, auto-escalation when the cheap model fails, and an honest cost receipt. Each child call starts with 4-10k prompt tokens vs the parent's 100-300k. Per-run budget cap (soft, stops within one call), watchdog timeout, escalation to the parent model, a restricted toolset (no delegation/memory/skills/clarify/cronjob), and a JSON audit logged to plugin-data/lean-mode/runs.jsonl. Requires the operator to configure lean: in config.yaml with a cheap model, parent model, prices and presets. Tested on Hermes v0.23.0. MIT licensed. Disclosure — the model can start cheap-model subagents with quick_run and may set the model id, budget and timeout per call; the dollar cap is soft, works only for models priced under lean.prices, and is off by default. When the parent's toolsets cannot be narrowed, and on every escalation, the child runs with all of the parent's toolsets (skills included) on the parent model. Run metadata (tokens, cost estimate, model, child session id, result hash; no message content) is logged to plugin-data/lean-mode/runs.jsonl. No network calls, shell commands or credentials of its own.

entries.name: learning-workbench
entries.description: Study with Hermes in a Desktop pane: a short diagnosis, a route of 2–7 steps you can rename or skip, then one lesson and exercise at a time, answered in your own words. The plugin keeps the record honest: answer keys, rubrics and hints are frozen before you answer, only you can submit an attempt (the agent's six tools propose and read), every check must quote your words and the quote is verified, and each attempt is labelled unaided, after feedback, after hints, after help in chat or after a revealed solution. Drafts and attempts survive restarts and compaction, a contest keeps the earlier verdict, and a study exports as a Markdown record. /study covers the CLI and messaging. Disclosure: studies are stored locally in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/learning-workbench/ (SQLite) until you delete them, including after uninstall; while an exercise is open in a chat, the pre_llm_call hook adds a short reminder with that exercise's question to the turn's user message and records that the turn happened (not its text); chats without an open exercise are untouched. No network calls of its own, no credentials, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. Verdicts use the user's configured model.

known_issues: The Desktop pane is opt-in: after installing, turn it on under Capabilities → Plugins → Learning Workbench.

entries.name: leash
entries.description: Lean OWASP Top 10 pentest toolkit run by the agent against your own dev app: scope-gated recon (TCP scan, same-origin crawl), multi-identity access-control testing with canary-based leak detection, parameter fuzzing, security-header audit and an evidence ledger that turns findings into a plain-language report grouped by OWASP category. entries.name: leitmotif
entries.description: Hear what your agent is doing. Every tool call becomes a short musical motif from a pure-Python synth, so reads, writes, shell commands, loops (the motif repeats and climbs), error streaks (dissonant, sinking), pending approvals (a heartbeat, then a distinct still-waiting cue until you answer) and finished turns (a V-I cadence) are audible without watching the screen; also a non-visual status channel for blind and low-vision developers. Modes full / ambient / alerts-only, themes studio / arcade / zen, and /leitmotif export saves a session as WAV, MIDI and a piano-roll SVG. Disclosure — observer-only hooks, never blocks or approves anything; starts the OS audio player (afplay, pw-play, paplay or aplay) as a short-lived subprocess per sound, or uses winsound on Windows; keeps tool names and argument hashes in memory only; caches rendered notes and writes exports in its plugin data directory; no network calls, no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: lemma
entries.description: An AI-scientist plugin that audits what your agent reads. Paste or mention a paper link and the ambient pre-LLM hook offers an audit unprompted; six tools (quick_audit, audit, doctor, status, judge, improve) extract testable claims, generate and run honest audit scripts behind a mandatory positive control, and render verdicts — supported, falsified, inconclusive — over an append-only evidence trail. The Desktop Audit Room pane shows live runs (stage, attempts, trace tail) and self-distrust flags (verify_gain) when a post-feedback flip to supported needs eyeballing. Everything stays local under plugin_data_dir. Disclosure — paper text and audit prompts go to your configured LLM provider (Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set via OPENAI_BASE_URL); papers are fetched from arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org and openreview.net; LLM-written audit scripts run inside a sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS: no network, workdir-only writes, minimal env) and are refused where no sandbox exists unless you turn on the plugin's `host_exec` setting, which runs them on the host without isolation; `lemma_audit` and `lemma_improve` run as detached background processes; a pre-LLM hook adds an "offer an audit" hint when a paper link appears in the conversation; all artifacts stay under the plugin data directory.

entries.name: leonardo
entries.description: Leonardo.AI video generation backend for video_generate: Motion 2.0 text-to-video and image-to-video through the Leonardo REST API, using only the Python standard library. Disclosure — the prompt and any reference image URL are sent to cloud.leonardo.ai and the finished clip is fetched from cdn.leonardo.ai, authenticated with your LEONARDO_API_KEY, which the plugin reads through Hermes's secret scope and never from a file or the ambient environment; generation is billed to your Leonardo API token balance (about 200 tokens per 5-second clip, purchased separately from a Leonardo web subscription); the job is polled in-process with a bounded wall-clock deadline, and the token cost is reported back but no budget is enforced, so an unattended run can spend your balance; no telemetry, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials and no self-updates. entries.name: lethe
entries.description:
Take one chat off the record with /lethe: nothing reaches memory, your profile or skills, the transcript is deleted, and a river shows every write it kept out.

Use an external memory provider? Copy this into a Hermes chat and replace <PROVIDER> with yours:

Extend my local Lethe plugin (~/.hermes/plugins/lethe) so off-the-record chats also skip my <PROVIDER> memory provider's per-turn sync, session-end extraction and save tools when store.is_on(session_id) is true. Show me the diff, add a test, then run hermes gateway restart. Disclosure — Deletes the off-the-record chat's transcript (and its compression chain) from Hermes's session database via SessionDB.delete_session when the chat ends, on /lethe-end or /lethe-forget, or from the Desktop panel's Delete transcript now (unless keep_transcript is on); while on, it blocks memory, user-profile and skill writes plus provider tools whose names look like saves, and adds a fixed off-the-record note to each turn's context; external memory providers' per-turn sync is not blocked.

known_issues: External memory providers (memory.provider) are not covered out of the box. Show me the diff, add a test, then run hermes gateway restart."
The end-of-chat receipt can't print at /exit in the CLI/TUI yet (the shared gateway drops plugin end-of-session messages); use /lethe-end first. The transcript is deleted either way.
In a brand-new Desktop chat, typing /lethe first hits Hermes's "Submission destination changed" error; use the panel's Start off the record.

entries.name: letsfg
entries.description: Search and book real flights and hotels through the hosted LetsFG MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the letsfg travel-booking workflow skill bundled: fares across airlines and the major travel sites, flexible dates, destinations in a region, bookable hotel rates, then book, follow and stop bookings. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at letsfg.co/mcp. Booking tools act on real money: a booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account (captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, released if it fails); per LetsFG, a booking, paid extra or hotel cancellation starts only when the user presses Approve in an e-mail from LetsFG, never from the conversation, and Hermes itself does not prompt before these tools unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the letsfg MCP server. Card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co, never in the conversation. Traveller details given for a booking (name, date of birth, gender, passport, contact, address) are sent to LetsFG and saved on that account. The server and its OAuth sign-in are added with `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`.

known_issues: Sign-in needs one extra command after install, because a portable plugin cannot declare an OAuth MCP server: hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300

entries.name: letterpress
entries.description: Drop in your PDFs, Word files and text, and Letterpress turns them into a finished deck, one-pager, graphic or audio brief in your own brand. Pick from three deck designs (Editorial, Data board, Statement), mix slides between them, and revise any slide by asking in plain words. Ask questions of your sources and get answers that cite the paragraph. Numbers and quotes are checked against your sources before export, and a Source notes PDF sets each one beside the sentence it came from. The check covers numbers and quotes, not claims or framing, so read the headlines yourself. Five built-in brands, or make your own. Independent community plugin, not made or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — Sends source text (secrets redacted by Hermes), questions, briefs and pictures of draft slides to the user's own Hermes model (auxiliary task "Letterpress writing") and audio scripts to the user's Hermes text-to-speech provider; fetches only web addresses the user enters, through Hermes's SSRF-safe client or the user's web_extract tool; starts a headless Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave child process (path from LETTERPRESS_BROWSER or IMPRINT_BROWSER, install folders or PATH) with only a minimal environment to render exports with network blocked and, on macOS/Linux, to view up to four pages of a user-named website through a public-address-only proxy on 127.0.0.1; runs sips on macOS; on first start copies its own earlier data from $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/imprint/ when that folder holds this plugin's database, without changing it; writes only under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/letterpress/ (or LETTERPRESS_DATA_DIR / IMPRINT_DATA_DIR) and to paths picked in the save dialog.
entries.title: Letterpress
known_issues: The three designs, and PDF or image export of a designed piece, need Google Chrome, Chromium, Microsoft Edge or Brave, found in the usual install folders, on PATH, or at the path in LETTERPRESS_BROWSER. Without one the Designs screen says so and the Template version still works. The lookup has been run on a Mac; on Windows and Linux it is covered by tests only.
Build from a website looks at the site in that browser on macOS and Linux only. On Windows it still reads the site's colors and fonts, but writes no style brief.
A three-designs run takes several minutes on a small model.
Updating the plugin while Letterpress is working reloads its page, and an outline in progress loses its place on screen.
In the light theme, placeholder text and buttons that aren't ready yet are pale.
Audio needs text to speech turned on in Hermes; without it the script is made and can be exported.
Reading a logo or brand sheet needs a model that can see images.
The source check proves a number or quote is in your sources, not that the source is right.
The check covers numbers and quotes, not claims or framing: a sample deck headlined "adds a site" passed 19 of 19 when its sources said "proposes".

entries.name: lfg-alarm
entries.description: Put a real alarm on your phone from Hermes, and on your friends', family's or community's phones, ringing together: for a time, an event, a post, a stream going live, a token price, or anything that can call a link. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), with one workflow skill bundled. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code. Every tool call goes to LFG Alarm's MCP server at mcp.lfg.gm, signed in as the user through LFG Alarm's sign-in. Alarm titles, times, notes, links and the people added are sent there, and what the tools return, such as the user's alarms and friends, enters the session and reaches the user's model provider. Tools make, change and delete alarms and can ring every phone on an alarm the user made. The tool list comes from LFG Alarm's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add lfg-alarm --url https://mcp.lfg.gm --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. That command replaces the package's server entry and its trust setting, so the README's next step sets it again: `hermes config set mcp_servers.lfg-alarm.trust untrusted`.

entries.name: lifeboat
entries.description: Rescue what a sweeper bot left behind in a drained EVM wallet: claims, unstakes and transfers in one EIP-7702 transaction paid by a fresh operator, sent only after you approve the exact text. Disclosure — moves funds on-chain: signs EIP-7702 delegations with the private key of the already-drained wallet (LIFEBOAT_VICTIM_KEY, read through the Hermes secret scope) and sends transactions from fresh operator wallets whose keys it generates and stores sealed under its plugin data directory; sending is off until LIFEBOAT_ENABLE_EXECUTE=1, every send needs a per-transaction Hermes approval prompt, and it refuses to send in yolo mode, with approvals off or in unattended runs (cron, -q, webhook, API); assets go only to LIFEBOAT_SAFE_ADDRESS; sends the wallet address to the public RPC of each supported chain (scan with no chain list queries all of them; override per chain with the `rpc` plugin setting) and to each chain's public Blockscout API for the balance scan and sweep history; reads Hermes' private approval-mode functions to detect unattended runs (fails closed); no telemetry, no background threads.
known_issues: Runs only for a wallet with a sweep on record (gas that arrived and left again within five minutes, at least twice). There is no switch to turn this off.
After a rescue the wallet stays delegated to the batch contract and the leaked key still controls it. Never use that wallet again.
On seven chains the explorer cannot be read by scripts, so the scan lists only the native balance there and you name the tokens yourself.

entries.name: lightkeeper
entries.description: An Obsidian-compatible map of how your codebase works (modules, flows, integrations, platform traps, decisions), kept outside the repo and kept honest by hooks: a primer on the first turn, pointers to the notes that own what you are asking about or editing, and a reminder through the verify gate when code moved but the map did not. Eight lightkeeper:* skills carry the procedures (init, seed, tidy, trace, release, knowledge-vault, vault-sync, vault-tidy); the vault CLI (find, check, sync, status, log, export) works from any shell. Not a memory provider. Disclosure — each hook runs python3 on the plugin's own scripts as a synchronous subprocess with a 10 s timeout (on every user message, after every write_file and patch, at the verify step and at session end), and those scripts run read-only git commands (rev-parse, remote get-url, worktree list, ls-tree, status, log) in the session's checkout and in the vault folder; the session primer and prompt hints put text from the vault's notes into the model's context; the hooks read the vault registry ~/.claude/vaults and the vault folders it lists, and write only inside the vault (_meta/index.json), a small per-session state file in the system temporary directory ($TMPDIR), and the plugin's own data directory; the init, seed, sync, tidy, trace and release procedures run the vault CLI through the terminal and commit to the vault's own git repository, and vault init appends the vault to ~/.claude/vaults and, only when you pass its opt-in flags, copies a vault launcher to ~/.local/bin (--install-cli), installs report-only post-merge and pre-push hooks in your code checkouts (--git-hook), or adds a post-commit hook that pushes every vault commit to the remote you name (--backup-remote); vault export writes an HTML map that loads d3 7.9.0 from cdnjs.cloudflare.com when opened; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no dependencies beyond Python 3.9 and git. Silent until a vault covers the session's working directory.

entries.name: ligis
entries.description: Verify that a payee holds a live, third-party-issued, revocable on-chain capability credential before your agent pays them. Hermes agents pay other agents, and the destination address comes from the HTTP answer asking for the money — nothing in the x402 flow ties that address to anything the payee has proven about itself, which is the gap ERC-8478 states in spec form. ligis reads the credential registry directly over read-only JSON-RPC and answers the question the payment flow leaves open: is this counterparty entitled to this? Five tools (ligis_check_capability, ligis_capability_hash, ligis_verify_payee, ligis_verify_payment, ligis_chains) plus two surfaces: a pre_tool_call gate that intercepts payment-shaped tool calls and escalates to Hermes's approval prompt when the payee cannot be credentialed, and a transform_tool_result hook that annotates an x402 402 challenge with the payee's credential verdict before the agent signs. The registry lets anyone issue a credential for any subject, so a live credential only counts when a trusted issuer signed it: the operator's trusted_issuers setting is the sole root of trust — tool arguments can narrow it, never widen it — verified on-chain with isCapableFromIssuer. Before its first read the plugin probes eth_chainId and eth_getCode on the registry address, so an endpoint serving the wrong chain or an address with no contract reads as unknown rather than an answer. A capability is indexed by the keccak-256 hash of its name, so the same capability resolves to the same bytes on every chain. No key, no hosted service, no secret scope. Disclosure — makes read-only HTTPS JSON-RPC calls to fixed public testnet RPC endpoints (https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz for monad-testnet, https://atlantic.dplabs-internal.com for pharos-atlantic); the RPC operator sees the caller's IP address and the queried registry, subject and issuer addresses; it holds no keys, signs nothing, sends no transactions, reads and writes no files, runs no background processes, and has no telemetry. A credential counts only when its issuer is in the trusted_issuers setting; with none configured every credentialed payee is escalated. The pre_tool_call hook escalates to Hermes's approval prompt, and --yolo and approvals.mode: off auto-approve those escalations while cron follows approvals.cron_mode; set mode: enforce to block outright. If the registry cannot be read, or a payee does not fit the hook's time budget, the call is not gated.

entries.name: limbic
entries.description:
Local long-term memory for Hermes agents: facts and preferences stay on your machine in one SQLite file with bundled embedding and natural language inference (NLI) models, decaying and reconsolidating organically with use and abstaining rather than guessing. No LLM calls.

Disclosures
- Network: ~1.0GB of pinned, sha256-verified ONNX models download from huggingface.co on first session start (Arctic 2.0 L int8 ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI ~430MB). Optional spaCy models pip-install ~14.5MB from spaCy's GitHub releases — version not hash-pinned.
- Local files: everything lives under HERMES_HOME (limbic.db, backup VACUUM snapshots) except the model cache ~/.cache/limbic, which is pruned at every model load — files not in the pinned manifest are deleted, so never point cache_dir at a shared folder. Memories at trust zero are deleted.
- forget: user-scoped two-step (list candidates, pick one) that appends a hash-only receipt (sha256, length, user id, fact id) to limbic.db.deletions.jsonl beside the database.
- Agent surface is exactly remember, recall, forget — no shell commands, no background services, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: lineage
entries.description: Provenance for everything the agent produces: every file Hermes writes gets a receipt (what it was made from — files read, pages fetched, searches run — by which tool call, model and agent, with SHA-256 hashes) and a Desktop page draws the graph back to the sources, with observed / evidenced / inferred links labelled, never blended. Verify a file and its sources against recorded hashes; export Mermaid/DOT. Disclosure — hooks only (post_tool_call, pre/post_llm_call, post_api_request, api_request_error, post_auxiliary_call, subagent_start/stop, on_session_start/end); no tools, middleware, LLM calls or credentials; runs no commands. Hashes files the agent read or wrote and files named in terminal commands (credential files such as ~/.ssh and .env are never opened), scans files the agent wrote (bounded text scan) and stats the working tree once after terminal/execute_code calls; receipts only for files the agent produced. Writes under plugin-data/lineage/ (SQLite, install.key) and, on request or with sidecar: true, <file>.receipt.json beside artifacts. Stores redacted, bounded previews of prompts, tool arguments and results (store_previews: false keeps ids and hashes only). Network only on an explicit `verify --refetch` (GET to the recorded source URLs, public hosts only; redirects are followed only to public hosts). No telemetry.

entries.name: linear-digest
entries.description: Schedule a model-free morning list of open Linear issues assigned to you, with linear_digest. Disclosure — LINEAR_API_KEY is read from this profile on each request and sent as the Authorization value with no Bearer prefix, as up to ten HTTPS POSTs to host api.linear.app path /graphql; redirects are not followed and proxies are not used; nothing is downloaded at run time and the schema file shipped here is about 1.3 MB; the tool and the script are read-only; archived issues are left out; tools are on for every surface, including gateways, so anyone you allow there can call linear_digest with your key, and hermes tools turns a surface off; schedule writes a no-agent cron at 08:00 delivered to local, empty stdout sends nothing, and there is no daily cap; unschedule removes the saved job, while the script stays only when another job is also named linear-digest; a leftover job is removed with hermes cron remove, and that command leaves the script file; settings stay in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/linear-digest; the skill linear-issues is registered with the tool; bot-chat puts the list into another model turn and that turn is not model-free; an http loopback LINEAR_DIGEST_REHEARSAL URL receives the key in clear text, and any other value fetches nothing.

entries.name: lingua
entries.description: A language learning trainer for Hermes Agent: plenty of plugins give the agent a memory, Lingua gives the user one. Build vocabulary decks (one per language) and Hermes quizzes you in chat, grades your recall honestly (again, hard, good, easy), and schedules each card with SM-2 spaced repetition, the algorithm behind Anki, so words return right before you forget them: a good card comes back in 1 day, then 6, then stretches by its ease factor, and a failed card returns in about 10 minutes. A pre_llm_call hook nudges you at the start of a session, or when you mention practice, whenever reviews are due. Six tools (lingua_add, lingua_due, lingua_grade, lingua_list, lingua_remove, lingua_stats), a /lingua slash command (including one-command French and Spanish starter decks of 20 essentials each), and a bundled lingua-learning skill that teaches the agent to quiz one card at a time and never reveal an answer early. Decks live in a local SQLite database in the active profile's plugin data directory. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only files touched are the plugin's own SQLite database and its bundled starter deck.

entries.name: linkedcamp
entries.description: Plan, build and run LinkedIn and email outreach in LinkedCamp through LinkedCamp's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.linkedcamp.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in with the account's API key, no keys in config): campaigns, audience search URLs, multi-step sequences, leads, unified inbox and AI-drafted replies, sending-account health, analytics, reply agents, and agency sub-accounts. entries.name: liquid-inference-provider
entries.description: Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a Hermes model provider (provider id `liquid`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set `model.default_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model `liquid.auto`) and the model list go through Hermes's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID_BASE_URL) with LIQUID_API_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. entries.name: listeningkit-log
entries.description: Your agent, working your DMs the way you would. Ask Hermes who is waiting on a reply across X, Discord, Slack, Instagram and Reddit, read the whole thread, and get a draft in your own voice that sends only after you approve it. A log tab in the dashboard shows who is waiting, every account's session and today's sends against its daily limit. LinkedIn support is currently limited to a session-status check. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) plus a dashboard tab. Disclosure — starts the separately installed logMcp executable as a long-running stdio process; log makes network calls directly to the social platforms the user signed into and reads account sessions, cookies and message history from its own ~/.logCli data directory. Write tools can send replies, DMs and posts, and can like or follow as the user's account; the server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks for approval. The dashboard tab's backend reads, read-only, log's session.json, governor_state.json and synced X inbox (inboxSync.json, including message previews) under ~/.logCli; it makes no network call, runs no command, writes nothing and never reads cookies. The optional router hook (logHooks, a pre_llm_call hook that passes each prompt to log's own hook script before each model call) is a separate native plugin installed by log's own plugin pack or `log launch --setup`, not by this entry. Some skills link to services log works with (treg, Memelord, Inworld, Fish Audio) through ListeningKit referral or affiliate links; each such skill and the README say so. The MCP tool set comes from the user's installed log version at runtime and is not covered by this plugin's pinned commit.

entries.name: lithermes
entries.description: Adds lit to Hermes Agent so a request is planned, built with tests and recorded checks, reviewed, and closed with a handoff note. 40 skills. MIT. Disclosure — adds per-turn workflow context and output marks through Hermes hooks (including a ⛔ LIT: not done line when a reply claims completion while a goal's gate is closed or a lit session never opened one, and a pre_verify hook that asks the agent to keep going while the gate is closed) and writes its plans, goals, test baseline, handoff cards and run state under the workspace's .hermes/lithermes/ (default-on knowledge capture, opt-out: LITHERMES_WIKIFY_CAPTURE=0); after every terminal command it appends a signed note there with a redacted 100-character preview of the command and its exit code, and when a goal is open it reads the workspace's git state (rev-parse, ls-tree, ls-files) and scans its test files; keeps a per-install signing key at ~/.hermes/lithermes/litgoal.key; a new session reads other sessions' goal files in the same workspace to offer a resume (LITHERMES_GOAL_RESUME=0 turns it off); a read-only dashboard route, limited to folders inside the home directory and sending no CORS headers, feeds a Hermes Desktop goal pane; /lit-adhd reads recent Hermes session titles, asks and tool names from ~/.hermes/state.db read-only with the sqlite3 CLI; /lit-hijack downloads the URLs and files you name (web pages, PDFs, X posts via api.fxtwitter.com, git clones of github.com repos and gists) into the workspace; bundled skill runtimes install from their own lockfiles when a skill asks; the processes the plugin starts (git, node, a prose detector, pdftotext) get an allowlist environment without provider keys; reads Hermes internals read-only (context compressor, config defaults, model metadata, command registry, working-folder helpers), which can break on a Hermes release.
