entries.name: live-translate
entries.description: Real-time speech-to-speech translation on your own computer: anyone speaks in any language and you hear them in yours, in their own voice, about 2-3 seconds behind. Hears ~100 languages (Qwen3-ASR + Whisper), translates between 201 (Qwen3.5-4B, a local server, a subscription, or the model Hermes already uses through ctx.llm), and speaks with the speaker's cloned voice in 23 languages and natural voices in 600+. One-way, two-way conversations and meetings/streams through a virtual audio device (Zoom, Meet, Teams, Discord, OBS, with OBS closed captions viewers can switch on); echo cancellation, background voices ignored, several speakers each with their own language and voice. Tools translate_start/stop/status/languages, /translate, hermes translate setup|start|file|serve|languages|devices, and an agent skill; optional desktop tray app (separate download). Disclosure — while translating it listens to the microphone or audio input you choose and plays to the output you choose; it never starts from a chat app or a scheduled job unless you enable allow_remote_start. Voice cloning uses a 5-second sample of each speaker on this computer, except with ElevenLabs voices, which upload each speaker's sample to ElevenLabs to create a cloned voice in your account that is deleted when the speaker changes or translation stops; temporary local copies are deleted when the session stops. Each session's captions are saved to plugin-data/live-translate/sessions/*.jsonl. hermes translate setup builds a separate Python environment with uv (plus three voice-model environments on Windows/Linux) under plugin-data/live-translate, installs packages from PyPI, PyTorch's index (Windows/Linux) and llama.cpp's prebuilt-wheel index (abetlen.github.io), installs uv from PyPI into the plugin's data folder if it is missing, and downloads 6-9 GB of model weights pinned to exact commits from their official Hugging Face repos into the standard Hugging Face cache. While translating it runs the engine and voice-worker processes (stopped on Stop or when the session that started them ends) and a local server on 127.0.0.1:7865 only, protected by a token kept in an owner-only file under plugin-data/live-translate, a Host check and an Origin check. No network while translating with built-in or local models; a cloud model or voice you choose receives the session's text or audio with your key, read only through Hermes's secret store. No telemetry. Licences: Apache-2.0/MIT models by default; OmniVoice (best preset) is CC-BY-NC-4.0; on CPU-only machines Kokoro uses espeak-ng (GPL-3.0).
entries.title: Live Translate
known_issues: First setup downloads 6-9 GB of models and builds its own Python environments; run hermes translate setup once (or press Set up in the app).
Real-time voice needs Apple Silicon or an NVIDIA GPU; on CPU-only machines captions come first and the voice follows with a delay.
Under plugins.isolation: host the hermes translate terminal commands are not available (Hermes skips plugin CLI commands in the host); the tools and /translate still work.

entries.name: live-video
entries.description: Give Hermes eyes in a live voice conversation. Point your phone at the room, talk normally, and the agent answers in duplex voice whilst the camera streams: ask what it can see and it answers from the current frame; ask to be told when something comes into view and the relay checks the frames for 90 seconds, verifies a sighting against the held image before claiming it, and says it once. The six-action tool starts the relay, hands you the URL to open, reads a session's transcript back to the agent, and replays what it saw — measured first-token latency was 0.57 s and 1.03 s across two turns on a modest VPS. Disclosure — audio and camera frames stream from your browser to a relay this plugin starts on port 8098 (loopback by default; a LAN bind is opt-in and protected by a token minted per start), and from there to generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Gemini Live, which also answers watch checks) using GEMINI_API_KEY read from Hermes' secret scope; `start` spawns `node server.js` from the plugin's own directory as a background process, which spawns a Python frame-change tracker (numpy, Pillow, torch); the tool reads the relay's transcript.log and server.log back to the agent; watch verification spends the key's quota. No telemetry, and the key is never written to disk.
entries.title: Live Video
known_issues: The frame tracker is a change detector, not an object detector: with the heartbeat disabled it can miss a small object arriving in an otherwise still scene.
The verifier takes 3–7 s per look, so a sighting is voiced a few seconds after it appears; one watch window at a time, 90 s by default.
Windows: the relay path is exercised there (spawn, health, tree kill), but not yet through the Hermes plugin loader.

entries.name: livetalk
entries.description: Realtime duplex voice chat with the Hermes agent — a composer mini-bar for the Hermes desktop app. The voice model answers small talk itself and delegates real work through a declared `talk` tool to a dedicated Hermes agent session (acknowledge-first, context-first routing); the answer is spoken back in one of the 30 documented HD prebuilt voices. Native config_schema settings (provider, live model, voice, transcription languages, spoken-answer detail, transcript/log visibility). Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live WebSocket and the user's key (requires_env GOOGLE_API_KEY); the desktop UI only talks to localhost. No Hermes agent tools registered; dashboard tab hidden. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GOOGLE_API_KEY (or GEMINI_API_KEY) from the environment; input/output transcripts are held in backend memory for the session, and a Gemini session-resumption handle is written to .resume.json inside the plugin's install directory. Formerly gemini-live-bridge — renamed for a provider-neutral roadmap; the old repository URL redirects.

Hooks-only (no agent tools). Disclosure — Adds approval prompts to tool calls by default (balanced mode): every MCP, connector or other-plugin tool, memory and skill writes, file reads outside the working and temp directories, and network-capable terminal/code commands go to Hermes's approval prompt; strict mode blocks them instead, and opt-in enforced fleet mode blocks all tool calls until the served model name matches the admitted one. entries.name: llmapi
entries.description: LLM API (llmapi.ai) as a Hermes model provider (`--provider llmapi`, alias `llm-api`, or LLM API in `hermes model`): Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen and more on one key, each on the API it works best on. Claude runs over the Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' prompt caching applies), GPT-5 and later over the Responses API, everything else over Chat Completions. The picker lists LLM API's tool-capable chat models with 64K+ context from its public catalog, which also supplies context windows, image input, per-model reasoning levels and list prices; catalog aliases resolve in /model. Gateway errors (out of credits, spend caps, model not allowed for the key) map onto Hermes' fallback instead of a key rotation; /usage shows the credit balance and monthly cap; per-request cost is the billed amount when the gateway reports it, else a list-price estimate. Maintained by LLM API. Disclosure — none

entries.name: llmslim
entries.description: Context engine that compresses older tool output and turns locally with LLMSlim instead of asking a model for a summary: no LLM call, deterministic output, and the start of the prompt is sent unchanged, so prompt caching keeps working. entries.name: llmux
entries.description: Compare Surplus Intelligence, Antseed and Solid offers in the Hermes composer, then route through one local provider by price, speed or balanced policy. Includes seller trust signals, explicit mid-chat switching, cached market data and a local usage ledger. Disclosure — Loading the plugin starts a detached local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8378 (LLMUX_PORT) that keeps running after Hermes exits and holds this profile's Surplus/Solid API keys (set LLMUX_AUTOSTART=0 to run it yourself); every chat sent through the llmux provider is forwarded in full to the seller it picks on Surplus Intelligence (api.surplusintelligence.ai), Solid (accounts.solid.xyz) or your local Antseed buyer (127.0.0.1:8377), where third-party marketplace sellers may serve it and bill your account with no spending cap; it also polls those marketplaces for prices in the background and keeps a market cache and proxy log under your Hermes home.
entries.title: LLMUX
known_issues: Installed-Desktop mid-chat switching and a real paid reply/ledger row have not yet been verified. Automated card interactions use a simulated SDK host.

Inference is billable at the selected seller with no hard spending ceiling. Cross-source failover is off by default; LLMUX_ALLOW_FAILOVER=1 permits additional potentially billable attempts after upstream failures.

Marketplace keys resolve through agent.secret_scope.get_secret. Each proxy port is bound to one profile/configuration; mismatches fail closed. Antseed-only operation without any marketplace key is not supported. Solid prices are a dated manual table; speed and trust are unpublished.
Trusted view excludes explicit marketplace untrusted signals, but still includes sources with no published trust verdict. Lists are ranked shortlists, not every marketplace seller.

Starts a detached loopback proxy which can outlive Hermes. It reads configured marketplace credentials, sends inference context to the selected upstream and writes proxy logs, public market-cache snapshots and a local usage ledger. The ledger is off by default and enabled only with LLMUX_TRACK_USAGE=1.
Default upstreams are api.surplusintelligence.ai, accounts.solid.xyz and the optional Antseed buyer proxy at 127.0.0.1:8377. Base URLs are configurable.

entries.name: load-lock
entries.description: A machine-wide load broker for coding agents: Hermes, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor and any MCP client share one heavy-work budget, so builds and test suites take turns instead of thrashing the machine. 19 load_lock_* tools (acquire, queue, offers, honest waits, background jobs that release their permit on exit, machine inspection), a policy brief at session start, a Load Lock dashboard tab, and a Desktop pane, status-bar chip and palette command. Disclosure — every tool shells out to the local load-lock CLI (Node >= 20, installed separately with npm), which auto-starts a per-user background daemon on a Unix socket with state in ~/.local/state/load-lock; load_lock_run_with_permit runs the command the agent passes on this host in its own process group, only when Hermes's terminal backend is local (it refuses under docker, ssh, modal and other sandboxes, resolving the backend via tools.terminal_scope and config), and a pre_tool_call hook sends any command Hermes's dangerous-command detector flags (imported from tools.approval_detection) to the same approval gate as the terminal tool; every child process (CLI, daemon, jobs) gets an allowlisted environment without provider API keys, plus any names the user lists in env_passthrough; machine inspection reads CPU, memory, load and cgroup limits; the optional auto_install setting (off by default) fetches the pinned npm package with npx, a network call to the npm registry; background work: the daemon, a heartbeat thread and job registry in the plugin process, and one idle `load-lock events --follow` tail in the process serving the dashboard; no telemetry, no credentials, no other network calls.
entries.title: Load Lock
known_issues: Needs the load-lock CLI >= 1.7.1: `npm install -g @aron98/load-lock@1.7.1` (Node >= 20). Without it every tool returns a clear error; the auto_install setting (off by default) can fetch the pinned version with npx instead.
The Desktop pane and status chip ship disabled, like every Desktop half: turn them on once under Capabilities ▸ Plugins.
Windows has a named-pipe transport that is unit-tested but not yet verified on a Windows machine.

entries.name: loaded-skills-indicator
entries.description: Status-bar chip, popover and dockable pane showing which skills are read into the active Hermes Desktop conversation's context: full bodies bold with an accent dot, compression-pruned ones ghosted, never-loaded ones not listed. A second pane view lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions and a loaded marker, and clicking a skill drops /<skill> into the composer for you to send (it never submits). A small local backend reads the profile's state.db read-only to tell a live skill body from a [SKILL_PRUNED] marker, and reads SKILL.md frontmatter for the descriptions. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no writes. Disclosure — the local backend opens state.db read-only for the requested session in this profile, the default root and, as a fallback, every other profile's state.db, and returns only skill names and load state; it reads SKILL.md frontmatter under the Hermes skill directories and makes no network calls or writes.

entries.name: local-business-leads
entries.description: Build local business lead lists from chat: any niche and city from Google Maps (12 countries), plus Yellow Pages US and Canada, BBB profiles, and dentist, contractor and restaurant lists with phone, website, address, hours, rating and business email. Four workflow skills (find leads, list cleanup with email validation and CSV export, BBB trust check, cost estimate) drive eight Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of an Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.0015 to 0.05 per row plus up to USD 0.019 per run). Search terms and places, and any email addresses the user asks to validate, are sent to Apify; the Actors read public business listings and the businesses' own websites, and the results are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Results are business contact data, and outreach with them must follow the marketing laws that apply to the user. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Hermes runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `hermes mcp add business-leads --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Hermes asking before each paid run. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with Google, Yellow Pages or BBB.

entries.name: local-fleet
entries.description: Your local inference fleet, operated from Hermes Desktop: routing across your own boxes (DGX Spark / GB10, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, clusters behind one endpoint). Probes each box, makes the least busy healthy one the primary model, falls back to smaller models on smaller boxes, then to your cloud model, and switches back when a box recovers. Why-this-box inspector, flight recorder, outage rehearsal, drift detection, readiness, savings with its working, doctor. Optional: subagents across boxes (delegation backend fleet), side tasks on the fleet (auxiliary.<task>), keep the routed model loaded, private inference (primary, fallback chain, side tasks and subagents held to your boxes, failing rather than using cloud; not air-gapping). Writes model.*, fallback_providers, and on request delegation.backend and auxiliary.<task>; private on removes non-local fallback entries and puts them back on off; hermes fleet restore puts the primary back. Network: HTTP only to the boxes you register. Observer hooks record per-call endpoint, model, tokens and duration (never content) in its data dir. Never moves a primary that holds an inline API key and never copies a key into its data. Read-only tools plus a model pull from the Ollama library that Hermes asks you to approve; no remote command execution. Disclosure — Once you opt in, Local Fleet rewrites `model.*` and `fallback_providers` in your config.yaml (and, on request, `delegation.backend` and `auxiliary.<task>`) to route Hermes to your own inference boxes; it sends HTTP only to the boxes you register, records per-call endpoint, model, tokens and duration (never content) in its data dir, and asks for approval before every model pull.

entries.name: local-hands
entries.description: Remote brain, local hands: Hermes runs on your server while terminal, read_file, write_file, patch, search_files and execute_code run on your own computers, through a one-file, stdlib-only daemon that dials out to the Hermes host over key-pinned TLS and asks you before acting (per conversation, per command, or never). Pair several machines and let the agent switch between them and the host with the hands tool; each keeps its own working directory. Answers #18715 and #1855 on the public terminal-backend surface. Disclosure — starts a long-running detached hub process on the Hermes host that listens on all network interfaces on a TCP port (default 0.0.0.0:7717, self-signed TLS, so clients use ssl.CERT_NONE plus a SHA-256 public-key pin) once the hands backend runs its first command or you run `hermes hands up` / `pair`, and serves the daemon source hands.py over HTTPS on that port (no self-update); runs shell commands sent by the Hermes host on each paired machine under the user's account (not a sandbox); with the 'brain' target on (the default) the agent can also switch its terminal to the Hermes host itself, through Hermes' local backend; command output returns to Hermes and so to the model provider; writes TLS key and certificate, devices.json (token hashes only), audit.jsonl and hub.log under plugin-data/local-hands/, and ~/.config/local-hands/ on each machine; adds one short context line to a turn when the active machine changes; Hermes dangerous-command approvals stay on; no telemetry, no third-party service, no credentials read from files.
entries.title: Local Hands
known_issues: The hands daemon runs on macOS, Linux and WSL (bash and Python 3.8+); not on native Windows.
The active machine is chosen per conversation (each gateway chat keeps its own; the CLI is one conversation) and is kept in memory: a chat returns to the default machine when Hermes restarts.

Hermes and its hub talk through a Unix socket: where the operating system forbids those (some sandboxes and seccomp profiles) no machine can be reached, and the hands tool, hermes hands doctor and the command output say so.
Environment variables and skill files are not sent to the machine; browser and computer_use tools still act where Hermes runs.
After a cd, Hermes may resolve relative write_file/patch paths against the machine's workspace rather than the new directory; absolute paths are exact.
Needs plugins.isolation in_process (the default): Hermes cannot hand a terminal environment across the plugin-host boundary.

Imports tools.environments.base (BaseEnvironment, EnvironmentConnectionError), the base class every terminal backend subclasses, tools.environments.local (LocalEnvironment), which runs commands sent to the 'brain' target with core's credential-stripped environment, and hermes_cli.plugin_session (session_key), which tells which conversation a hands tool call belongs to (guarded: without it the active machine is process-wide, as in 1.0.0); hermes plugins validate reports the three as private-import warnings.

entries.name: local-mcp
entries.description: Mac apps for Hermes through a separately installed LMCP app: Apple Mail, Microsoft 365 mail, Calendar, Teams, Slack, OneDrive, Office files, a logged-in browser and the terminal, with a skill for scoping tools on unattended jobs. entries.name: local-scout
entries.description: Local privacy and safety layer for Hermes. Detected sensitive data (e-mails, phones, cards and CVVs, IBANs, SSNs, PESEL numbers, addresses, API keys, and passwords, 2FA codes and PINs without a known format; person names in prompts when turned on) is replaced with one-way placeholders on your machine before Hermes sends a request to a model: user prompts, file and terminal output, MCP tool results, tool-call arguments and auxiliary calls such as title generation, in CLI and gateway sessions. Also flags prompt injection in what the agent reads (flagged, not blocked), offers optional calibrated local triage, an optional basal method through a basal engine you run locally, and local Insights. Disclosure — enabling the plugin turns on masking of the data above on a fresh profile (person names are off until you choose `/scout names basic|deep`); `/scout` in a local chat or `hermes scout` shows and changes settings, `/scout masking off` turns it off and the choice persists; from messaging gateways `/scout` only shows status. With masking on it rewrites outgoing model requests on supported paths (auxiliary calls best-effort), tool-call arguments and tool/terminal/MCP results to replace detected data with one-way placeholders, adds a short system-prompt section and a `masking` skill telling the model to keep placeholders, appends a LOCAL_SCOUT_ALERT line (categories only, never values), adds a one-line note under a reply naming the data types detected (never values; `/scout note off` hides it), optionally (off by default, `/scout numbered on`) numbers names, e-mails, phones and addresses so equal values share a token within a profile and process — nothing is restored and only salted digests are kept in memory, passes images and other non-text content through unscanned, and replaces a user message (or, if the whole scan fails, the entire request) with a withheld notice unless you set `scout configure --guard-mode open` for that profile; it stores no prompt contents or detected values, saves explicit settings locally and writes Insights counters only when Insights is on; local answers and learning are opt-in; a name in the first message of a Discord thread can appear in the Hermes thread title; with the optional answer grant it answers confident triage tickets locally and makes no main model call for them; the optional basal engine is reached on loopback only and receives unmasked candidate lines for password checks; it reads the profile config.yaml (title-generation setting only) and the history/dataset files you name in the CLI; state stays in its plugin-data directory, apart from export files you name in the CLI and a launcher link in the user cache directory; no other network calls, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials.

entries.name: local-system-one-hermes
entries.description: Local System One observes selected Hermes decisions through a separate local sidecar. Installation defaults to OFF; the first Shadow enables Search only. Shadow does not change provider requests. The default loopback sidecar uses a private per-profile token; processes owned by the same user may access it. Search can send a bounded task and recent context to the sidecar. Other Gates require opt-in and may send bounded response or failure context. A remote HTTPS sidecar requires explicit configuration and receives no local token; remote-sidecar security is outside this pilot's verified support. Canary request changes require separate explicit acknowledgement; production Canary has not been authorized or accepted in this pilot. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar; installs with mode off. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task (up to 4000 chars) plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow (opt-in) may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata; Completion Gate (opt-in) may POST the task plus the final result (up to 6000 chars); Retry Gate (opt-in, post_tool_call) sends only typed tool-failure metadata, never tool arguments or output. The default sidecar is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787, authenticated with a private per-profile token read from ~/Library/Application Support/Local System One/profiles/<profile>/access-token after an identity handshake; a remote sidecar requires allow_remote_sidecar plus HTTPS and receives no token. The plugin persists decision metadata, not raw task or response text, and imports Hermes' private kanban modules read-only to resolve a kanban worker's task. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode, are removing web_search/web_extract tools for audited no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning_effort on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.

entries.name: loci
entries.description: Local models on your Mac for file summaries, document extraction, folder search, audio transcription and batch processing alongside Hermes. Disclosure — connects to the separately installed Loci Mac app's local MCP server (127.0.0.1:5624) using the token Hermes reads from Loci's discovery file (~/Library/Application Support/LociRust/agent-api.json); the live tool set is served by the app and is not covered by the pinned sha. Loci tools read the files and folders you authorize, write extraction outputs, keep a persistent local search index, and can download models; the setup skill can guide downloading and installing the Loci app (askloci.ai DMG, SHA-256 pinned). The server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before write-capable tools and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: locksift
entries.description: Exact, local review of dependency lockfiles: npm package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock (v1 and Berry), uv.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, Cargo.lock, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock and go.sum. lock_diff compares two versions of a lockfile (a branch against main) and returns the dependency changes instead of thousands of lines of churn, with supply-chain signals per installed copy: a source that moved (registry to git or URL, another registry host, a different tarball or commit at the same version, an alias or patch that changed, a tarball that belongs to another package), checksums changed, removed or weakened, new install scripts, new registries. lock_summary gives counts, packages at several versions, non-registry sources and install scripts; lock_why shows the dependency chains that pull a package in. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs git or a package manager), no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local lockfile paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.

entries.name: locus-codegraph
entries.description: Rehearse a Python refactor before making it, and catch missed callers when you do. @whatif:<symbol>(<new parameters>) or the locus_rehearse tool binds every statically proven caller against a proposed signature before any file is edited and lists which call sites would break and why. After an edit, the same check appends caller locations, binding errors and, for a renamed keyword, a caller patch to review to the editing tool's result. Covers functions, class constructors, static and class methods, methods on locally constructed instances, and calls inside the edited file, through direct and module-qualified imports, aliases and static re-exports. Receivers whose type is not in view (self, parameters, attributes), decorated callables and dynamic bindings are not checked; other supported languages receive structural indexing only. One local index also powers five tools, @sym:/@impact:/@hotspots: references, /locus commands, and Web Dashboard and Desktop caller inboxes. Suggested tests and impact scores are static heuristics, not execution coverage; no alert or predicted break is not proof of safety. Disclosure: reads supported workspace source subject to exclusions and size caps, rejects symlink escapes, and stores structure, call shapes, and drift history in profile-scoped SQLite. Expands explicit references and adds diagnostics and proposed patches to editing-tool results and the configured model's context. Does not modify workspace source, apply patches, or run tests. No external network requests, credential access, shell subprocesses, background daemons, or additional runtime packages.

entries.name: logmine
entries.description: Exact, local intelligence over large text log files. log_summarize mines the file into recurring message templates (masking numbers, IPs, UUIDs, hashes, quoted strings and timestamps so near-identical lines collapse into one ranked pattern with an exact count), plus a level histogram and the detected time span; log_grep is regex search with line numbers and grep-style context; log_timeline buckets events per minute/hour/day to find spikes. Streamed, so a log too big to fit in the model's context still works. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no background processes, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local log path you pass it (read-only).

entries.name: look-at-this
entries.description: Instant active-window, region-snip, and UI-context capture for Hermes Agent and Hermes Desktop. Global OS hotkeys (Ctrl+Alt+L / Ctrl+Alt+S on Windows), interactive window-hover/crosshair snipping, live window picker with thumbnails, composer preview banner, and ephemeral single-turn vision injection. Runs an in-process Win32 RegisterHotKey listener thread and a lazy headless PowerShell UIAutomation reader on Windows, spawns an isolated Win32 GDI overlay subprocess only during interactive snips, mounts authenticated local routes under /api/plugins/look-at-this/*, injects queued captures via pre_llm_call and llm_request, and stores transient state and temporary PNGs under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/look-at-this/ (data.db and shots/, deleted in post_llm_call, on_session_end, /look clear, or after a 5-minute TTL). Zero third-party Python dependencies and zero outbound network requests. Disclosure — the model can call lat_grab to screenshot any open window or screen region (password managers and private browser windows are refused) and the image, window text, URL and selection are sent to your model provider; on Windows it runs a background global-hotkey listener and a PowerShell UI Automation reader for as long as Hermes runs.
entries.title: Look At This
known_issues: Unified git plugin note: Hermes Desktop enables the Agent half on install while the Desktop UI half starts disabled by default — toggle "Look At This" ON once in Settings -> Capabilities -> Plugins -> Installed to activate the composer preview banner, '+' attachment items, status-bar chip, and global hotkey session routing.

Secret redaction (default_redact / /look redact) masks sensitive patterns in text fields (title, URL, selected text, and UI highlights/tree) only; it does not blur or alter pixels inside the attached screenshot PNG.
On Windows, User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) prevents a normal medium-integrity Hermes process from capturing or inspecting windows running elevated as Administrator.

System-wide global hotkeys (Ctrl+Alt+L / Ctrl+Alt+S) use Win32 RegisterHotKey on Windows. On macOS and Linux, use in-app shortcuts (Mod+Alt+L / Mod+Alt+S / Mod+Alt+W), the composer '+' menu, or /look; macOS requires Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions, and Linux uses grim + slurp (Wayland) or imagemagick + wmctrl (X11).

entries.name: look
entries.description: Ask about pages and use guarded Chrome actions. Apple Silicon macOS beta with broad debugger access and optional local voice and eyes. Disclosure — Look runs its own Chrome profile (~/.cache/look/chrome-profile) on a loopback DevTools port and sends your questions and captured page evidence to your configured model. Model-requested navigation and link clicks refuse private, loopback and metadata hosts only before navigating (redirects and DNS rebinding are not contained; the owner setting allow_private_network turns the check off). `/look actions allow-all` skips Look's own action review for the bound conversation. When TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set (early_highlight is on by default), your spoken question and pointer structure, plus page text if highlight_include_page_text is on, go to api.typesafe.ai. Setup downloads checksum-pinned NVIDIA NeMo-Speech native libraries, Hugging Face speech models and MediaPipe WASM into ~/Library/Caches/Look and ~/.cache/look.
entries.title: Look
known_issues: Requires Apple Silicon, native arm64 Python 3.11–3.14, Chrome, one display and an in-process local Hermes session with input permission.
Eye tracking is experimental. Real-camera accuracy and screen-reader compatibility are unverified. English-first voice and UI.
Questions and page evidence reach the configured model. Optional TypeSafe scope requests can add costs.
Explicit allow-all skips Look action review for requested actions. Chrome sign-ins, model caches, calibration and Hermes/provider history survive plugin removal.
Gallery shows fixture-backed UI captured before v3 integration, with scripted answers and no provider inference. Not native Chrome consent or a fresh install.

entries.name: loshify
entries.description: A Spotify curator that knows you: it learns your taste from your listening and your reactions, builds playlists with a reason for every track, and remembers what you loved and what you never want again. Desktop remote with 👎 👌 ❤️, rotations, and a chat curator. Connect in about two minutes; the Desktop card walks you through it one step at a time with copy buttons, and the agent walks the same steps in chat. First install with hermes plugins install iHeavyShoes/loshify --enable (once listed, hermes plugins install loshify). Then in Hermes Desktop open Capabilities → Plugins and turn on Loshify's Desktop switch (the Desktop half starts off and config.yaml does not turn it on). (1) Open developer.spotify.com/dashboard and press Create app. (2) App name Loshify, Redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:43828/callback, tick only Web API, Save. Your own key to Spotify; 127.0.0.1 means this computer, nothing leaves it. (3) Add yourself under User Management (new Spotify apps only let in listed accounts). (4) Paste the Client ID into the Loshify card; it is saved in the plugin's setting. (5) Run hermes auth add loshify:spotify once in a terminal (Windows: Start → PowerShell) and press Agree. (6) The card checks with one real call to Spotify and turns green. Disclosure — data is stored locally in plugin-data/loshify/data.db, and the Desktop setup card saves your Spotify Client ID into this profile's .env through Hermes's own settings writer. The plugin calls Spotify API and accounts hosts, and the Desktop loads Spotify image CDN artwork. Hermes sends taste facts (artist names, track titles, and notes) to your configured model provider for portraits and picks. The plugin never sees a token. Edits or removes tracks only from playlists Loshify created. Playback control needs Spotify Premium. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: lowrouter
entries.description: LowRouter as a Hermes model provider (`--provider lowrouter`, or LowRouter in `hermes model`). The picker shows the `auto/` chat models with tool calling and 64K+ context, plus the user's own `alias/` models, instead of every ID from /v1/models. Context windows come from LowRouter's catalog instead of Hermes' 256K fallback, and /usage shows the credit balance in euros. LowRouter bills in EUR, so the plugin reports no USD cost and Hermes shows it as unknown. Maintained by LowRouter. Disclosure — registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and LOWROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.lowrouter.ai/v1 (or the configured model.base_url) through Hermes' client, and LowRouter forwards each request to the host serving the model. The plugin's own requests are GET /v1/models (cached for an hour per key and base URL) and GET /v1/credits on /usage, to the same base URL with the same key, through Hermes' open_credentialed_url. No files read or written, no processes.

entries.name: lumina
entries.description: Protects the private documents in your Apple Photos library, on-device. A privacy check-up finds passports, payment cards, passwords and ID documents; Safe Send makes a redacted copy and re-reads it to prove nothing sensitive remains; Leak Guard, a pre_tool_call hook, blocks any Hermes tool call that would send a raw image of an ID document off the Mac. Also searches photos by person, place, scene or text in the image, lists expiry dates, creates albums and renders memory videos. Disclosure — macOS only; reads the Apple Photos library database and image files (needs Full Disk Access) through osxphotos; creates albums in Photos via AppleScript (photoscript) only when asked; runs Apple Vision text recognition locally and the local sips and ffmpeg binaries; the pre_tool_call hook inspects every tool call's arguments and reads image files they name; a transform_llm_output hook edits Hermes's replies (adds photo-grid/redaction cards or MEDIA lines, removes MEDIA lines for images that look like ID documents and Lumina file paths); exported photos, redacted copies and memory videos are written to the plugin's data folder and, on messaging platforms, delivered through Hermes's MEDIA lines to that chat service; the lumina_redact tool accepts any image file path on the Mac; recognised text is cached in the plugin's own data folder; Lumina makes no network requests of its own, stores no credentials and has no telemetry. Text of matched photos (snippets, or full text of up to 5 photos when asked) is returned to the model.
entries.title: Lumina
known_issues: macOS only. Hermes (or the terminal running it) needs Full Disk Access to read the Photos library; album creation asks for Automation permission for Photos.

Text search, expiry and the privacy check-up rely on the text Apple Photos has already recognised; photos added in the last few days are read directly, a few seconds at a time, and a partial result says so.
Leak Guard catches the common routes (image paths in terminal, code, browser and message tool calls) and is not a guarantee against a determined attacker. LUMINA_LEAK_GUARD=off disables it.

The check-up reports four kinds (passports, payment cards, passwords, ID documents) and prefers missing a document over a false alarm. Tested on a small library; very large libraries are not yet measured.
Memory videos use ffmpeg when installed and fall back to an animated GIF.

entries.name: lusor
entries.description: AI agents on real phones through Lusor's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE): list your phones, run a task on your own iPhone or Android or a Lusor Phone in the cloud and read the result, answer the agent's questions, read the screen, tap, type and swipe, and install catalog apps. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to mcp.lusor.ai, signed in as the user through Lusor's OAuth sign-in, and counts against that workspace's Lusor plan. Tool results, including screenshots and screen text, enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Signing in gives 14 tools: list_phones, get_phone, run_task, get_task, list_tasks, reply_to_task, stop_task, get_screenshot, get_screen_state, phone_action, install_app, list_app_installs, remove_phone and wipe_phone. Write-capable among them: run_task (uses credits, and phone minutes on a Lusor Phone), phone_action, reply_to_task, stop_task, install_app, remove_phone and wipe_phone (erases a Lusor Phone; confirmed by typing its name). add_phone (buys Lusor Phones after a price quote), search and execute need an API key instead of sign-in. The package marks the server untrusted, but the required sign-in step writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds trust: untrusted to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Lusor's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add lusor --url https://mcp.lusor.ai/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: lydite
entries.description: Hand a GitHub issue and the command that proves it done to Lydite from the chat. Claude Code workers do the job, Lydite replays your proof itself, and a pull request comes back with a receipt (cost, workers, retries, the commit that was reviewed and replayed, and what was not replayed). Also hands Hermes the lessons Lydite keeps for a repository, read-only, has Lydite check a plan file before a launch, and turns a hermes-security findings export into one Lydite plan per finding you choose (prove it by a failing test, then fix it). Disclosure — after your approval of each launch (the prompt shows the repository, work, exact proof command or, for a plan, its header proof (cut if long) and SHA-256, profile and target branch; a value holding a control or formatting character, and a plan in which a task carries its own proof, are refused before any prompt; "always" covers only that exact request: repo, profile, issue or objective, target branch, dry run or launch, and proof or plan bytes), starts the already-installed `lydite` binary (argument list, no shell) as a detached background process with a closed environment list plus the provider key you set; Lydite runs git, gh and Claude Code on the host with your GitHub login; under a `mur = exige` profile (the default) the workers' commands run in Claude Code's sandbox and srt replays your proof inside the wall, `mur = natif` does the same with Lydite's own bubblewrap wall in place of srt, and one of the two is required for `--issue` and for a plan written from a findings report; under a profile you accepted with `mur = demande` the workers' commands may run outside the sandbox and see the provider key, and your proof is replayed directly on the host; it reaches GitHub and the model provider of its profile; the status, lessons and plan-check tools run the binary without approval, as does the read-only wall check (`lydite profil`) before a findings plan's prompt; the findings tool starts nothing; reads the plan file, the repository's `.agents/skills` lessons and the findings report you name, and writes the plans of the findings you choose under the plugin's data folder; no telemetry.
entries.title: Lydite
known_issues: Linux only: Lydite's sandbox wall holds there.

Needs the lydite binary of the same release as this plugin (attested release of github.com/aoricloud/lydite), Claude Code, gh and srt installed (bubblewrap and lydite-reseau instead of srt under mur = natif), and a Lydite profile accepted by a human.

Some names are still French: three tool names (lydite_lancer, lydite_etat, lydite_lecons), the plugin settings (binaire, profil, cle_nom, cle) and a few lines Lydite writes, such as impossible (déclarée). Lydite's commands have English words, and its usage and the lines about the pull request and CI are in English; pull request receipts are in English. The progress lines of a launch are still in French.

entries.name: manyhands
entries.description: Identity, memory and permissions for every person who talks to one Hermes bot. A gateway is a single-operator agent: the platform already carries sender_id and platform into every turn and nothing acts on it, so everybody in a group or a household shares the same memory, the same tools and the same approval authority. manyhands acts on it. Roles (owner, member, guest, blocked) are resolved from the platform event, never from message text, and applied as three states per tool: allow runs, ask parks the call under a four-character code and sends it to the owner's own DM, and everything else is refused with a message that names only the asker's own role. `/many approve CODE` opens a one-shot grant bound to that person and that tool, spent by the next call and expired on silence — only a human typing the slash command can approve, and nobody can approve their own ask. The operator's own MEMORY.md and USER.md blocks are withheld from everybody else's system prompt and replaced with a card about that person, because "everyone gets their own Hermes" has to include not handing a stranger your notes; each person also gets their own facts, their own token budget, and `/many pause`. Six tools (whoami, people, remember, recall, share, audit — `people` is read-only: a roster change is a human-typed verb, never a tool call) and `/many` (roster, invite, claim, add, role, tools, budget, audit, approve, deny, pause) whose owner-only verbs stay owner-only because a command's identity comes from the platform event too, so a stranger typing in the owner's own chat session is still a stranger. Identity fails closed: a session with no human turn on it — a restart, a subagent, a tool driven from the gateway socket — gets the guest allowlist, not the owner's, and a tool call in a session more than one person has spoken in is attributed by the task id the host dispatches with (or refused, never guessed from the last speaker). Every turn, tool decision, refusal, escalation, approval, spent grant and token count is an audit row you can read back. Disclosure — hooks, one middleware, six tools, the `/many` command and the `manyhands` approval transport, no other capability. pre_llm_call resolves the sender from the platform event, records the session and turn to person map, redeems `join CODE` invites and appends that person's facts to their turn; pre_tool_call applies the role to the tool allowlist, parks asks, spends grants and fails closed; post_api_request records token usage per person; an llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing provider request for non-owners, removing the operator's memory blocks and injecting the person card. One SQLite file under plugin-data/manyhands (people, facts, shared facts, invites, approvals, sessions, settings, audit) holding sender ids as platform:sender_id, roster names you set, the facts people store and the audit trail; `/many remove` deletes a person and their facts. Reads no other file on disk, runs no command, makes no network call, imports nothing outside the Python standard library and calls no model. Approval prompts are delivered through the host's own gateway injection into the owner's DM, which the host records as a turn in that chat.
entries.title: manyhands
known_issues: Identity is only as good as the platform event, and a call that carries none fails closed: a session that never had a human turn on it, a subagent, and a tool called from inside `execute_code` (the host passes an empty session id there) all get the guest allowlist rather than the owner's. Set `unknown_session_policy: operator` if every caller on your machine is trusted. Machine-generated turns are recognised by a marker AND the absence of a sender, so a cron prompt is the operator's while a guest who types `[cron]` stays a guest.

DM routing is Telegram-shaped: a private chat id is the user id, so the approval prompt reaches that chat. Other platforms need their own DM resolution; the prompt fails closed there rather than guessing, which means asks are denied until a code is minted another way.

The operator's own memory is withheld by removing the two built-in block titles (MEMORY, USER PROFILE). A block rendered by a third-party memory provider is not removed, so run manyhands without one if that matters to you.

A plugin escalation cannot use Hermes's approval-transport seam: request_tool_approval routes it through _ACTION_GATE, which is built with transport=False. manyhands parks and DMs the ask itself and leaves the registered transport to the dangerous-command prompts that do consult it.

The approval prompt arrives as a plugin-triggered turn in the owner's chat (inject_gateway_message), so each prompt costs one turn in that conversation; keep approval_timeout_s honest so a stale code cannot sit there long.
entries.capability_summary: manyhands (community, maintained by PhiBao) Identity, memory and permissions for every person who talks to one Hermes bot. A gateway is a single-operator agent: the platform already carries sender_id and platform into every turn and nothing acts on it, so everybody in a group or a household shares the same memory, the same tools and the same approval authority. manyhands acts on it. Roles (owner, member, guest, blocked) are resolved from the platform event, never from message text, and applied as three states per tool: allow runs, ask parks the call under a four-character code and sends it to the owner's own DM, and everything else is refused with a message that names only the asker's own role. `/many approve CODE` opens a one-shot grant bound to that person and that tool, spent by the next call and expired on silence — only a human typing the slash command can approve, and nobody can approve their own ask. The operator's own MEMORY.md and USER.md blocks are withheld from everybody else's system prompt and replaced with a card about that person, because "everyone gets their own Hermes" has to include not handing a stranger your notes; each person also gets their own facts, their own token budget, and `/many pause`. Six tools (whoami, people, remember, recall, share, audit — `people` is read-only: a roster change is a human-typed verb, never a tool call) and `/many` (roster, invite, claim, add, role, tools, budget, audit, approve, deny, pause) whose owner-only verbs stay owner-only because a command's identity comes from the platform event too, so a stranger typing in the owner's own chat session is still a stranger. Identity fails closed: a session with no human turn on it — a restart, a subagent, a tool driven from the gateway socket — gets the guest allowlist, not the owner's, and a tool call in a session more than one person has spoken in is attributed by the task id the host dispatches with (or refused, never guessed from the last speaker). Every turn, tool decision, refusal, escalation, approval, spent grant and token count is an audit row you can read back. Disclosure — hooks, one middleware, six tools, the `/many` command and the `manyhands` approval transport, no other capability. pre_llm_call resolves the sender from the platform event, records the session and turn to person map, redeems `join CODE` invites and appends that person's facts to their turn; pre_tool_call applies the role to the tool allowlist, parks asks, spends grants and fails closed; post_api_request records token usage per person; an llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing provider request for non-owners, removing the operator's memory blocks and injecting the person card. One SQLite file under plugin-data/manyhands (people, facts, shared facts, invites, approvals, sessions, settings, audit) holding sender ids as platform:sender_id, roster names you set, the facts people store and the audit trail; `/many remove` deletes a person and their facts. Reads no other file on disk, runs no command, makes no network call, imports nothing outside the Python standard library and calls no model. Approval prompts are delivered through the host's own gateway injection into the owner's DM, which the host records as a turn in that chat. entries.name: mapdesk
entries.description: A GIS workspace inside Hermes Desktop. Import GeoJSON, CSV, KML/KMZ, GPX, XLSX, zipped shapefiles and bounded public ArcGIS layers; style, query and select layers; run geodesic buffer, dissolve, clip, centroid, hull and points-in-polygon analysis; export GeoPackage, shapefile, KMZ, GeoJSON, CSV and PNG, from chat or from the map pane. Works with no account on a keyless OpenFreeMap basemap; a public Mapbox token is optional. Disclosure: the map pane loads version-pinned, SRI-checked MapLibre GL JS (unpkg) or Mapbox GL JS, and basemap tiles from OpenFreeMap, Esri ArcGIS Online (satellite), the Terrarium elevation set on Amazon S3 (terrain) or Mapbox (billed to your token). ArcGIS imports contact the source you choose, and geocoding a CSV by an address column in the pane sends those addresses to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Layers stay in the profile's plugin data folder. No telemetry, no self-updater, no shell commands.

entries.name: maqami-travel
entries.description: Search hotels (3M+ hotels) and flights worldwide on MAQAMI, read hotel details and reviews, then send the customer a secure checkout link on book.maqami.co, through the official MAQAMI Travel MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.maqami.co, no account or key), with the maqami-travel-booking skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — connects to the hosted MAQAMI MCP server at mcp.maqami.co (no key); its tool list is defined by that server, not by the pinned repo. The tool arguments the agent sends go to it: destinations, dates, guests, lead-guest nationality and currency, plus booking ID and email for lookups, amendments and cancellations. Prebook (hotels) and verify (flights) hold a real rate, and the amend and cancel tools change or cancel real bookings (late or non-refundable cancellations are still charged); the skill tells the agent to show the details and get a clear yes before each prebook, amend or cancel. Customers pay only on book.maqami.co; no tool takes card or passport details.

entries.name: marcora
entries.description: Brand context, marketing blueprints, content creation, grounding, and GTM planning through Marcora's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.marcora.ai/, OAuth 2.1 PKCE or Bearer API token). Bundles the marcora-mcp workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Marcora's hosted server (mcp.marcora.ai) over HTTPS and acts on the user's Marcora workspace under their own role; the 63-tool surface (32 read-only, 31 non-read-only, 15 destructiveHint: true) is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Non-read-only tools create or update workspace records, send team invitation emails (invite_user), publish share links (create_external_share), or spend team Marcora Studio Credits (create_content with instructions, produce_plan, create_blueprint_draft, create_project with project_brief_instructions, ask_content_assistant, check_content_grounding, trigger_health_audit_scan, convert_markdown_to_word_doc at 2 credits/conversion, and run_workflow). run_workflow starts a server-side automated agent session using Marcora tools and the user's connected third-party apps (allowed_tools is a prompt instruction to the runner, not a separate permission check), workflows that are Active with an On schedule run on Marcora's server-side scheduler independently of the local client, and ask_content_assistant runs an asynchronous background AI assistant that may edit a document in place. The package marks the server untrusted (timeout: 180), so Hermes's host policy prompts before client-initiated calls to tools the server does not mark read-only, though neither Hermes trust nor advisory MCP annotations prevent server-side scheduled workflow runs or background agent actions once started or activated on Marcora.

entries.name: margin
entries.description: Comment @hermes on highlighted text in Google Docs, Slides or Sheets and Hermes answers in the comment thread. A gateway platform: each Drive comment thread is its own Hermes session with the document text and the highlighted text as context; follow-ups in the thread continue it, Hermes's status reply is edited in place into the answer, and replying "apply" replaces the highlighted text with the proposed wording (Docs and Slides, only when the text occurs exactly once). Watch files with /margin watch or hermes margin watch. Disclosure — sends the text of each watched file (up to MARGIN_MAX_DOC_CHARS, default 60,000 characters), the highlighted text and the comment thread to the user's configured model provider at the start of each thread; signs in with the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client through Hermes (`hermes auth add margin:google`, scopes drive, documents, presentations) and calls only www.googleapis.com, docs.googleapis.com and slides.googleapis.com through credentialed_provider_request, never holding the token; polls Drive comments.list every 10 s per watched file from a background loop inside the gateway; posts and edits its own comment replies and edits document text only on an explicit "apply" reply; by default only the signed-in Google account can trigger it (MARGIN_ALLOWED_USERS / MARGIN_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widen that); stores the watch list, poll cursors, handled comment ids and per-thread highlighted text and last proposal in Hermes plugin state under HERMES_HOME (no document text, no credentials); no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Margin
known_issues: Needs the user's own Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app) with the Drive, Docs and Slides APIs enabled; sign in once with hermes auth add margin:google.
Google may show an unverified-app warning for a personal OAuth client in testing mode, and testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
Polling, not push: replies arrive within about one poll interval (10 s) plus model time.

entries.name: mariadb-dev
entries.description: Work with MariaDB from Hermes: 85 skills on MariaDB SQL, functions, schema management, REST services, connectors and migration from MySQL, plus the native mariadb-shell MCP server (run SQL, inspect schemas, dump/load/copy data, deploy local sandbox servers, manage REST services). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — the MCP server is the local mariadb-shell binary, started by scripts/mariadb-mcp-launcher.sh. If no mariadb-shell of the required version (26.11.2) or newer is on PATH or in ~/.local/bin, the launcher downloads the official installer from a fixed github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-shell commit and installs exactly release v26.11.2 into ~/.local/share/mariadb-shell, linked into ~/.local/bin. The package is verified against scripts/mariadb-shell-v26.11.2.SHA256SUMS, committed at the pinned sha; a mismatching package is refused. When the agent sets up a REST service, the MCP server installs exactly mariadb-restd release v26.11.0 the same way, verified against scripts/mariadb-restd-v26.11.0.SHA256SUMS. The launcher reads no GitHub credentials and sends none. Tools run SQL against the databases the user registered with mariadb-shell, whose passwords stay in mariadb-shell's own OS secret store and never pass through the agent; the sandbox tools download and run local MariaDB server instances. No telemetry.

entries.name: mariadb-guard
entries.description: Companion to mariadb-dev; install it together with mariadb-dev, whose MCP server it redirects to. A pre_tool_call hook that blocks the agent from running the mariadb/mysql command-line clients (and similar) for what the mariadb MCP tools do, so no database password reaches a command line, plus a short system-prompt rule saying so. entries.name: market-search
entries.description: Live market data for Hermes through the market-search MCP server: Kalshi and Polymarket odds, Fed rate-path probabilities, stocks, ETFs, options, futures curves, corporate and government bonds, FRED macro, Treasury auctions and fiscal data, SEC filings by section and XBRL, insider trades, short interest, CFTC positioning, and Fed, ECB, BOJ, BOE and BIS data, all on one timeseries axis. 25 data tools plus report_issue, no API keys, no account. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) with one skill that maps questions to tools. Disclosure — the stdio server is started by scripts/launch.sh, a readable shell script: it runs an already-installed market-search binary if one is on PATH, in ~/.local/bin or ~/.cargo/bin; otherwise it downloads the v0.6.2 release binary for the user's OS from this repository's own GitHub release (github.com/efoltyn/market-search, the upstream project), checks it against a SHA-256 written in the script, refuses to run it on mismatch, and caches it under ~/.cache/market-search/. The release binaries are built by the repository's public release workflow and carry GitHub build attestations. No self-update: the version and checksums change only with a new pinned commit. The 25 data tools make read-only HTTPS requests from the user's machine directly to public data sources (Yahoo Finance, Kalshi, Polymarket, FRED, SEC EDGAR, FINRA, US Treasury, NY Fed, the Federal Reserve Board, Cleveland Fed, OFR, CFTC, BLS, BEA, Census, Nasdaq, CBOE, CNBC, Kraken Futures, Binance, Hyperliquid, Deribit, the ETF issuers State Street, iShares, Direxion and ProShares, ECB, BIS, BOJ, BOE, EIA); most are GET, and queries to FINRA, Hyperliquid and Polymarket's order-book endpoint are POST. No data request goes through a server of the author's. If the user runs an Interactive Brokers gateway on the same machine, IBKR: tickers and the ibkr options provider read prices through it. One tool, report_issue, sends the developer a note when a tool errors or returns a wrong number: what the agent wrote (message, tool name, arguments, error text) plus the market-search version, OS and client name, by HTTPS POST to the developer's inbox on tell.dev, a service the author runs. It is sent only when the agent calls the tool, and Hermes asks the user first because the package marks its server untrusted and the tool is not read-only. Setting MARKET_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=off removes the tool. finance_log keeps a local hash-chained record of tool calls in the user's data directory. The server runs only the tools it lists and refuses any other name; none of them places an order or moves money. The binary's command line, which the plugin does not call, has a finance ibkr command that can read an Interactive Brokers account and place or cancel orders through a local gateway. Every tool carries a title and annotations (24 read-only; finance_log writes its local log; report_issue sends a note). No telemetry: nothing is sent automatically. Not financial advice.

Disclosure: creates and edits real ad campaigns that spend your ad budgets; every write is a separate approval-gated operation and the skills instruct confirm-before-spend, but that is enforced by the skills and the server's approval flag, not by Hermes. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.20.

entries.name: marsell
entries.description: Run Marsell, an AI for marketing, sales and content creation, from Hermes through Marsell's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://getmarsell.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): read what Marsell planned, made and found for each project, answer the decisions waiting for the owner, read and update the brand, plan posts and other work, make pictures and films, run series, and check results and token balances. Bundles the marsell workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Marsell's hosted server (getmarsell.com) and acts on the user's Marsell account with their current role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Tools that write change the owner's Marsell projects, and answering a waiting card in the owner's name can publish, send or spend as the chosen option says. Tools that make pictures, films and voice-overs, and some others such as research and page changes, spend Marsell tokens from the owner's plan; each says so in its description and asks the agent to give the price first. Ad spend needs the owner's approval in Marsell: an ad spends nothing until someone allowed to spend presses Start on its card there. Mission tools give the agent messages Marsell wrote for the owner's own Reddit, X or LinkedIn accounts, to send word for word from a signed-in browser, only where the owner said yes to that in Marsell. Upload tools give the agent a one-time address and a curl command that sends files from the user's machine, such as a logo or voice recordings, to Marsell. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port the first time a tool needs the account and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package has no telemetry and no self-updater. It marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: max-platform
entries.description: MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (*.max.ru, *.oneme.ru, *.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX_AUTO_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.

entries.name: mayar
entries.description: Read and manage a Mayar (mayar.id, Indonesian payments platform) account through Mayar's official hosted MCP server: balance, invoices, installments, payment links and products, customers, transactions, memberships, credits, coupons, webhooks, reviews, QRIS and license codes. entries.name: mcp-pin
entries.description: Hold MCP tools whose definition changed since you approved them. Fingerprints every MCP tool's description and parameter schema as Hermes registered it; if a server later changes a tool (a rug pull, instructions hidden in a description, a new parameter) or adds a tool to a pinned server, the new definition is hidden from the model (tool list, tool_search catalog, tool_describe) and calls to that tool are refused until the owner reviews the full change with /mcppin diff and approves exactly that definition with the code it shows. Works with tool_search on or off and with every provider wire format (not the Codex app-server runtime, where Codex calls MCP servers directly). Fails closed: an unreadable or deleted pin file withholds MCP definitions and refuses MCP calls. Disclosure — llm_request middleware rewrites only held MCP tool definitions in the outgoing request (their tool entry or tool_search catalog line); tool_execution middleware rewrites only tool_search / tool_describe / tool_call results that carry a held definition; pre_tool_call may block a call to a held MCP tool (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system); registers /mcppin; reads only its own settings, MCP tool definitions from the tool registry, the per-message session identity, and Hermes's allow_admin_from / group_allow_admin_from lists through the gateway config loader when an approval is attempted from a chat; writes pins.json and a transient lock file (MCP tool names, descriptions, parameter schemas, timestamps, approver) in its plugin data directory, and its own store_id setting (a random id that lets a deleted pin file be detected); no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credential reads, no self-update. Not a sandbox: an approved tool keeps its normal reach.

entries.name: mcp-serve
entries.description: Run Hermes as an MCP server: `hermes mcp-serve` lets any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex) list and read your messaging conversations, poll live events, send messages and answer approvals over stdio. `--tools` (off by default) also exposes Hermes' web, vision, image generation, skills and TTS tools; terminal, file and kanban tools are never exposed. Formerly built into Hermes core as `hermes mcp serve` (MCP clients change their args to ["mcp-serve"]). Disclosure — the connecting MCP client reads the active profile's conversation history (state.db) and can send messages as your connected platform accounts; with `--tools` it also runs Hermes tools under your configured provider credentials, which can spend provider credits. The plugin itself makes no network or model calls beyond those tool calls and sends.

entries.name: mdvault
entries.description: Memory provider that treats a folder of Markdown notes as the agent's long-term store: BM25 retrieval with CJK bigrams over an in-memory index, relevant notes injected before every turn (prefetch), four tools (mdvault_search, mdvault_note, mdvault_recent, mdvault_remember), built-in memory writes mirrored into a human-readable vault note, a `hermes mdvault` CLI and a dashboard config panel. No network, no database, no dependencies; the store is plain .md files the user can edit, git and back up. Disclosure — reads only the configured vault folder (file symlinks skipped, excluded directories ignored), writes only inside that folder (new notes with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, plus the ownership-marked mirror note), no telemetry, no self-updater, no background process, no subprocesses. The vault itself lives outside $HERMES_HOME, so `hermes backup` does not copy it.

entries.name: mediarag
entries.description:
Local, offline semantic search across your documents, notes, images, audio and subtitles: one index you query by meaning from Hermes or any MCP client, with snippets, timestamps and thumbnails from PDFs, Office files, photos and recordings.

Disclosure —

- Downloads about 480 MB of EmbeddingGemma-2 ONNX model weights from Hugging Face at a pinned revision on first setup; offline after that.
- Reads the folders you point it at, outside the plugin directory.
- Runs pandoc, pdftotext, ffmpeg and curl from PATH; ffmpeg samples video files at 0.5 frames per second (first 240 frames) into its local cache to index them.
- Fetches the http(s) URLs you add, from public hosts only, re-checked on every redirect.
- Runs source adapters as local subprocesses; the optional Raindrop and Notion adapters send RAINDROP_API_TOKEN to Raindrop's API and NOTION_TOKEN to api.notion.com.
- With MEDIARAG_AUTO_BOOTSTRAP=1, the standalone MCP launcher installs its Python environment from PyPI, about 1.7 GB.

entries.name: meeting-ai
entries.description: Meeting.ai records your meetings and writes the notes; this plugin gives them to Hermes, so Hermes works from what was actually said. Meeting.ai records in person or on Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams, from web, mobile, or desktop. Hermes recalls past decisions and open questions, prepares your brief or deck, and turns a meeting into the work you need: a follow-up with decisions, owners, and next steps, a PDF of the minutes, a PowerPoint deck, or a Visual Note. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Meeting.ai's hosted server (mcp.meeting.ai) and acts on the user's Meeting.ai account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Recording, Visual Notes and image and audio generation use the user's Meeting.ai Coins, the usage credits that come with a Meeting.ai plan or a Coin pack; generation sends the supplied text to third-party AI providers. The package sends no telemetry, but the Meeting.ai server records each MCP call (tool, outcome, user, workspace and client identifiers) for product analytics; this is part of the hosted service. The notetaker joins live calls as a visible participant, and a share link shows the notes and, by default, the transcript. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; the sign-in must finish within about 55 seconds. The package marks the server untrusted, so by default Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: meeting-copilot-live
entries.description: Read-only meeting answers with cited project evidence. Disclosure — explicit answers send bounded transcript, selected project snippets and (when enabled, or in all-projects and web-fallback answers) prior-session snippets through the configured Hermes default and its host routing/fallback policy, or selected OpenAI/OpenRouter/Meta (api.meta.ai) APIs; optional Meta ASR sends audio to api.meta.ai and Google preview ASR to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; optional web queries leave through host search; reads selected project files, read-only session SQLite and attached Meetily recording files; readiness, permission setup, capture and explicit synthetic-audio tests launch native/worker child processes; capture/readiness/test workers use minimal environments; Google preview keeps a counts-only allowance ledger in ~/.meeting-copilot shared across profiles; separate macOS setup installs SHA-256-pinned PyPI wheels and compiles/signs native helpers; explicit local-model preparation may download public Whisper weights; clipboard exports may contain confidential context.
entries.title: Meeting Copilot
known_issues: Developer preview: one generated 38.4-second fixture verified local Whisper and Google; not a general accuracy benchmark or proof of live system audio, diarization or sustained capture. Live OpenAI/OpenRouter responses remain unverified.

Google preview is explicitly selected, limited to 60 seconds per source and four shared stream attempts. Local $1-per-stream reservations are not actual charges or a guaranteed bill cap; final-tail completeness is unconfirmed. Source labels are not speaker identities. Free-tier audio may improve Google products.
macOS audio preparation targets Apple Silicon, preinstalled CPython 3.12 and the macOS 26 SDK; rerun it after runtime updates. Native Windows readiness remains unsupported and fail-closed.
Missing request-bound secret scope fails closed. Follow Hermes default requires a genuine same-profile in-process facade; isolated/remote routes are unsupported and no core credentials are copied.
Overlay recording exclusion is best effort. Hide it and verify it is gone when it must not appear.

entries.name: meetstream
entries.description: Hermes in Meetings, from MeetStream: Hermes joins Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams calls as a visible bot that records and transcribes them, answers questions people type in the meeting chat (while the gateway runs), and does the follow-up work from the transcript. Disclosure — talks only to the MeetStream API at https://api.meetstream.ai with the user's own MEETSTREAM_API_KEY: the tools call it when used; while the gateway runs, the meetstream platform lists the account's bots of the last day every 120 seconds (at most 4 pages) and, for each Hermes bot in a call, reads its chat every 5 seconds and its status every 30 seconds. It sends meeting links, the bot name, the join message and the agent's chat replies, and receives bot status, meeting chat and transcripts. Meeting-chat senders are identified by display name, which participants choose: the gateway admits nobody until MEETSTREAM_ALLOWED_USERS lists them, and every turn from meeting chat is limited to web_search/web_extract (the adapter pins the platform's toolsets to [web, no_mcp], and its pre_llm_call/pre_tool_call hooks block every other tool, including other plugins' tools, in those sessions; always on). The hooks only read session_id, task_id, platform and tool_name. MeetStream bills bot time and transcription to the user's account. No files written, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: memex8
entries.description: Self-hosted vector memory (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) with auto-discovered knowledge realms, semantic search across conversations and ingested documents, and a slumber pipeline for memory consolidation. v1.2.0 adds private-span redaction before capture, compact retrieval with ordered batch get, scoped chronological timeline, user-certified memory protection, and recoverable consolidation/dedup archives. v1.1.0 added optional per-session injection dedup with char-budget gate, decision/evaluation memory-type promotion (slower decay for load-bearing turns), prompt-injection sanitization on read, configurable system-prompt template, export/import memories as JSON, and a /memex8 slash command. entries.name: memory-bridge
entries.description: Read-only, permission-aware search and reading over an operator-approved folder of Markdown notes, such as a team's shared agent memory. Two tools, memory_bridge_search and memory_bridge_read. Each calling profile's policy.json (in its plugin-data directory) sets the memory root and allow/deny patterns; the model can only ask questions and cannot widen access. Cron and delegated subagents are refused unless the policy opts in. Standalone tool plugin, not a memory provider. Disclosure — reads Markdown files under the operator-configured root, which is outside the plugin's own data, and returns snippets and file text into the model's context (sent to your model provider). On macOS it reads file ACLs through the system C library (ctypes). No network calls, shell commands, background processes, credentials, telemetry, writes or Python dependencies. Logs short refusal reason codes only. Imports the undocumented agent.delegation_context helper for subagent detection (rule 9 warning) and fails closed if it moves.
