entries.name: memory-shaper
entries.description: Keyword-index memory for Hermes: a small resident index of 'keyword keyword -> file.md' routing lines stays in the system prompt while verbose topic files stay on disk and are read only when the conversation touches their keywords. Retrieval is done by the model reading a literal index — no embeddings, no vector store, no retrieval service. Disclosure — a pre_tool_call hook and a tool_execution middleware refuse a non-memory tool's write to the memory index across the recognised write vectors (write_file, patch, shell redirects, tee, sed -i; best-effort against arbitrary shell indirection) and refuse malformed index lines with a fix message rather than fixing them silently (including the keyword count: an entry outside the documented 5-20 keywords is refused, and the ASCII arrow is refused on every code path), while read-only commands and reads through a pipe always pass so the agent can audit the file it maintains; the same guard refuses any memory-tool remove, replace or patch whose old_text lands inside the index header, because on the stock store the whole preamble is a single §-joined entry and such an edit would rewrite or delete every header line at once; a documented escape hatch lets a scripted rewrite proceed when the sentinel file $HERMES_HOME/state/.dynmem_rewrite_approved exists or DYNMEM_ALLOW_REWRITE=1 is set. Beyond $HERMES_HOME/memories/, the guard reads one thing: when a shell command invokes python3 on a script file, it opens that script (and the execute_code payload is already in args) to check whether the code would write the index; no file content is retained or sent anywhere. The repo also ships an optional core patch (scripts/patches/0001-flat-memory-separator.patch, changes tools/memory_tool_store.py) that the plugin does not need and never applies; a user who applies it by hand must re-apply it after every Hermes update. No network calls, no subprocesses, nothing spawned in the background. The pre-1.8 MEMORY_SHAPER_* variable names and the .memory_shaper_rewrite_approved sentinel are still accepted, so the rename cannot strand an existing install. A second hook pair (pre_llm_call + transform_llm_output) appends, only when the plugin's own setting plugins.entries.dynmem.settings.memcheck.enabled is true (off by default; MEMCHECK_DISABLED=1 is a one-process kill switch), a hidden tagged self-report to the first four user messages of a session asking which memory files were read, which were nearly read, and whether the routing turned out wrong; on Hermes 0.22.6 and later the transform hook is registered with hold_stream so the tag never streams to the user (older releases show it while the reply streams), the tag is stripped before the reply is stored or shown, every claim (filename, keyword, quoted fact) is checked against the index and the topic file body, and it is skipped on cron, subagent, one-shot and batch runs. That hook keeps per-session state under $HERMES_HOME/state/memcheck/: state.json holds the last four user messages and the last verdict, samples.jsonl appends one record per checked turn (the tag fields plus the first 400 characters of the user message) and rotates at 5 MiB, keeping one previous window as samples.jsonl.1; nothing leaves the machine. A third pre_llm_call hook adds one setup question to the first turn after install (fewer requests or fewer tokens), asking the agent to record the answer with hermes config set plugins.entries.dynmem.settings.profile, then adds a one-line mode reminder once per session; it skips cron, subagent, one-shot and batch runs and keeps only the asked time and the last 50 session ids in $HERMES_HOME/state/dynmem/billing.json. Separately, the plugin writes one line of its own: when MEMORY.md already looks like a dynmem index (an arrow entry or the template line), it inserts or refreshes a single '# All memories are located in: <absolute path>' header line, atomically, with one backup slot under $HERMES_HOME/state/, and DYNMEM_NO_PATH_HEADER=1 disables it; a stock-store or prose MEMORY.md is never touched.
entries.title: Dynmem (keyword index)
known_issues: The routing rule from skill/ (or an equivalent line in your personality file) is part of the setup: stock Hermes injects the index with no instructions, so without the rule the agent still finds the right file, but by brute-force filesystem search which does not scale.
entries.capability_summary: memory-shaper (community, maintained by ockentap) Keyword-index memory for Hermes: a small resident index of 'keyword keyword -> file.md' routing lines stays in the system prompt while verbose topic files stay on disk and are read only when the conversation touches their keywords. Retrieval is done by the model reading a literal index — no embeddings, no vector store, no retrieval service. Disclosure — a pre_tool_call hook and a tool_execution middleware refuse a non-memory tool's write to the memory index across the recognised write vectors (write_file, patch, shell redirects, tee, sed -i; best-effort against arbitrary shell indirection) and refuse malformed index lines with a fix message rather than fixing them silently (including the keyword count: an entry outside the documented 5-20 keywords is refused, and the ASCII arrow is refused on every code path), while read-only commands and reads through a pipe always pass so the agent can audit the file it maintains; the same guard refuses any memory-tool remove, replace or patch whose old_text lands inside the index header, because on the stock store the whole preamble is a single §-joined entry and such an edit would rewrite or delete every header line at once; a documented escape hatch lets a scripted rewrite proceed when the sentinel file $HERMES_HOME/state/.dynmem_rewrite_approved exists or DYNMEM_ALLOW_REWRITE=1 is set. Beyond $HERMES_HOME/memories/, the guard reads one thing: when a shell command invokes python3 on a script file, it opens that script (and the execute_code payload is already in args) to check whether the code would write the index; no file content is retained or sent anywhere. The repo also ships an optional core patch (scripts/patches/0001-flat-memory-separator.patch, changes tools/memory_tool_store.py) that the plugin does not need and never applies; a user who applies it by hand must re-apply it after every Hermes update. No network calls, no subprocesses, nothing spawned in the background. The pre-1.8 MEMORY_SHAPER_* variable names and the .memory_shaper_rewrite_approved sentinel are still accepted, so the rename cannot strand an existing install. A second hook pair (pre_llm_call + transform_llm_output) appends, only when the plugin's own setting plugins.entries.dynmem.settings.memcheck.enabled is true (off by default; MEMCHECK_DISABLED=1 is a one-process kill switch), a hidden tagged self-report to the first four user messages of a session asking which memory files were read, which were nearly read, and whether the routing turned out wrong; on Hermes 0.22.6 and later the transform hook is registered with hold_stream so the tag never streams to the user (older releases show it while the reply streams), the tag is stripped before the reply is stored or shown, every claim (filename, keyword, quoted fact) is checked against the index and the topic file body, and it is skipped on cron, subagent, one-shot and batch runs. That hook keeps per-session state under $HERMES_HOME/state/memcheck/: state.json holds the last four user messages and the last verdict, samples.jsonl appends one record per checked turn (the tag fields plus the first 400 characters of the user message) and rotates at 5 MiB, keeping one previous window as samples.jsonl.1; nothing leaves the machine. A third pre_llm_call hook adds one setup question to the first turn after install (fewer requests or fewer tokens), asking the agent to record the answer with hermes config set plugins.entries.dynmem.settings.profile, then adds a one-line mode reminder once per session; it skips cron, subagent, one-shot and batch runs and keeps only the asked time and the last 50 session ids in $HERMES_HOME/state/dynmem/billing.json. Separately, the plugin writes one line of its own: when MEMORY.md already looks like a dynmem index (an arrow entry or the template line), it inserts or refreshes a single '# All memories are located in: <absolute path>' header line, atomically, with one backup slot under $HERMES_HOME/state/, and DYNMEM_NO_PATH_HEADER=1 disables it; a stock-store or prose MEMORY.md is never touched. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call, transform_llm_output; middleware: tool_execution. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.2. Known issues: The routing rule from skill/ (or an equivalent line in your personality file) is part of the setup: stock Hermes injects the index with no instructions, so without the rule the agent still finds the right file, but by brute-force filesystem search which does not scale..

entries.name: memory-shield
entries.description: Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Hermes' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Hermes' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre_tool_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session_context) and whether the run is Hermes' unattended review (tools.skill_provenance.is_unattended_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Hermes' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted_chats, and once trusted_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.
entries.title: Memory Shield
known_issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host the plugin cannot see the current chat, sender or Hermes' review marker, so it judges every call like a direct chat and the group chat and background review protection does not apply.
Covers Hermes' built-in memory tool (USER.md, MEMORY.md) only, not the tools of memory provider plugins such as Honcho or Mem0.

Without trusted_users every direct chat counts as the owner: whoever can message the agent directly may add facts to the owner profile and correct them (not delete them) until the owner's id is listed.
Spotting USER.md and MEMORY.md edits made through terminal and execute_code is best effort: a path built some other way, or a command run from a script file, can get through.

terminal and execute_code calls are read up to 16,384 characters. A longer call that contains the word memories, USER.md or MEMORY.md (any case, quotes ignored) is refused even when it only reads them; a longer call that contains none of them passes without being read.

entries.name: memorybank
entries.description: Memory Bank - unlimited local long-term memory for Hermes as a knowledge graph; adding a new memory never fails for lack of room, relevance-gated recall, an index of past sessions and skills, a live network view and a usage meter. Disclosure — keeps excerpts of your conversations, MEMORY.md/USER.md and skill text in a local unencrypted SQLite bank under the profile's plugin-data folder, and on first run indexes past session history from Hermes' state.db (opened read-only); when the built-in memory tool refuses an add because MEMORY.md or USER.md is full, it stores the entry in the bank and reports the save as successful; `hermes memorybank ui` runs a token-protected viewer on 127.0.0.1 and opens it in your browser.
known_issues: Works on Windows and macOS (developed and tested on Windows, installed and used on Macs); Linux has not been tried.
A replace that makes an existing MEMORY.md / USER.md entry longer than the room left is still refused by Hermes; only new entries (adds) are rescued.
Keeps excerpts of what you typed in each conversation (and skill text) in a local, unencrypted SQLite file.
The network view animates (about 30 frames a second) while it is open and visible; it stands still under the system's reduced-motion setting and in a hidden window.

entries.name: memrack
entries.description: memrack is one memory provider that hosts a rack of backends behind one search and one write tool, with agent-side routing (cards advertise best_for/limits per backend; no LLM judge at write or read — no auto mode): base-db is the stdlib SQLite floor (atomic facts per row, FTS5 bm25 rank, hash-dedupe idempotence, per-entry heat counters, pointer directory), wiki (read-only whole-page search via a stdlib mtime index), state-episodic (READ-ONLY over the canonical Hermes session log in state.db, default on — turns are never copied), and vec (opt-in autonomous document backend: its own chunk store, an ingest tool and CLI (hermes memrack vec add; md/txt/pdf via the optional pypdf dep), semantic knn recall with vec:<source>#chunk reading refs — no automatic ledger harvest; nothing is embedded that was not ingested). memrack_search fans out over every active backend (parallel, per-backend timeout, budget) merging with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF k=60), per-target collapse, deterministic tiebreak; every answer carries a lean rack_status slot (per-backend modes + participation) and card prose on membership delta. Catalog providers dock manifest-first: isolated probe, draft card with human review, mirrored tools under the memrack__<provider>__<tool> namespace (collision fail-closed), uninstall grace (park now, card cleanup after a retention window), and docks receive turns or transcripts only via recorded per-card gates (forward_turns / forward_transcript, default OFF). Tools: memrack_search, memrack_write, memrack_status, memrack_import, memrack_dock, memrack_card_review, memrack_vec_add, plus hermes memrack status|report|export|import|vec add. Config: desktop pane via a declared config_schema (membership toggles, force-backend, top_k, fanout timeout, prefetch budget, vec keys, uninstall retention) and config.yaml plugins.memrack — dual-store bridge. Disclosure — memrack keeps its facts store, vector index and routing log locally under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/memrack/ and opens the Hermes session database read-only; nothing leaves the machine by default. When you enable the optional vector backend, queries and ingested document text are sent as plain text to the embedding endpoint you configure (a local Ollama host by default, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set, with the API key read from the Hermes secret scope).
known_issues: The wiki page engine uses a deterministic AND-gate scorer rather than bm25 (facts and session history rank with bm25); hybrid retrieval is per-backend engines + RRF merge.
vec is opt-in and needs sqlite-vec plus a reachable Ollama host; without them its card degrades with a visible env_gap note and the rack answers fts only.
The vec corpus holds only what was ingested (no automatic ledger harvest); PDF ingestion is text layer only (no OCR).
Membership toggles act on the NEXT search of a running session (tool paths live; the injected context channel follows the session).
Auto-enable at activation defaults OFF — no storage backend gets enabled without an explicit toggle.
memrack_import is a one-shot migration job per profile (idempotent via hash-dedupe), not a standing cron.

entries.name: memtomem-memory
entries.description: Memory provider backed by memtomem: on eligible user turns (not greetings or slash commands) it asks memtomem for the notes most relevant to the message, through Hermes's own connection to a memtomem MCP entry, and injects what returns within its time budget as context, without a model tool call. Optionally (mirror_writes, off by default) it also copies what Hermes's built-in memory tool adds, replaces or removes in MEMORY.md / USER.md into memtomem. Needs Hermes with MCP support, memory.provider: memtomem-memory, the grant plugins.entries.memtomem-memory.mcp_allowlist: [memtomem], and a memtomem MCP entry with trust: full running memtomem 0.6.8 or later (0.7.8 or later for mirroring): the memtomem catalog plugin, or your own mcp_servers.memtomem. Disclosure — each recall sends the turn's full message as the search query to whatever server that entry connects, local or remote; with mirroring on, each added, replaced or removed entry's text is sent too (a replace or remove also sends the full text of the entry it changed), and memtomem keeps the accepted ones in its database and renders them into a hermes-mirror/<profile hash>/<target>.md note that every profile on the same store can recall (a removed entry keeps only its key; an entry matching a memtomem privacy pattern is refused). It shares that entry's connection, call queue and circuit breaker with the model's memtomem tools. It starts no server, reads no credentials and uses the standard library only.

entries.name: memtomem
entries.description: Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem[onnx]==0.7.12, with huggingface-hub held at 1.20 or later) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session, with PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 so it loads no .env file and HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1 so its Hugging Face downloads neither open a saved Hugging Face login nor use HF_TOKEN. It reads the directories you ask it to index and watches its configured index roots while it runs. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine on its own; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking, search webhooks or scheduled maintenance jobs that run without a tool call and can send stored notes to the configured LLM, its fetch action downloads a URL on request, and turning reranking on through mem_do (rerank.enabled) loads the configured reranker at once, downloading the default local model from Hugging Face when it is not cached. The server runs as your user and is not confined to ~/.memtomem: actions that take a path (indexing, ingest, import) read it wherever you can, context_detect and context_diff read other coding agents' instruction files, skills, hook settings and MCP configuration, and its own writes, mostly under its configured memory and project directories, can follow existing directory links out of them and include runtime files such as locks under the system temp directory. Since 0.7.9 the context-gateway writes into other agents' files are not on MCP (the mm context CLI and the web UI keep them), and export bundles go to ~/.memtomem/exports/; see the README's "Files outside memtomem's own data".

entries.name: mentionagent
entries.description: Run link building outreach through MentionAgent's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mentionagent.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): review the outreach drafts MentionAgent wrote, send the batch, answer publisher replies, close placements, and change campaigns in plain English, across every site in the user's account. Bundles the link-building-outreach workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to MentionAgent's hosted server (mentionagent.ai) and acts on the user's MentionAgent account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. approve_batch and send_reply send real email from the user's sending inbox, and trigger_run and draft_reply spend MentionAgent credits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: merageo
entries.description: How often ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini mention a website, through meraGEO's official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://merageo.com/api/mcp/agent, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with the user's meraGEO account, scope geo:scan, no keys in config): read the latest AI visibility report for a domain (0-100 score, per-model mention counts, top issues), request a new scan, check scan status. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Setup after install and enable: add an mcp_servers.merageo entry to ~/.hermes/config.yaml with url https://merageo.com/api/mcp/agent, auth: oauth and trust: untrusted (required; hermes mcp login fails without auth: oauth, and this entry replaces the package's, trust included), then run hermes mcp login merageo. entries.name: meridian
entries.description: Finds and verifies the implicit state machines hiding in a codebase; enforces the accepted ones in CI. Meridian discovers status/state fields, anchors every state and transition to file:line (Python AST; TS/JS lexical, unguarded), flags unreachable and dead states, and gates on a human-reviewable .meridian.yaml spec (check exits 1 on violation, 2 when nothing is enforced). Every check event is appended to a SHA-256 hash-chained log for audit. No model calls, no network, no dependencies beyond stdlib. Disclosure - post_tool_call observes tools whose names contain write/edit/patch/replace/create/editor and re-runs the local analyzer only when a .meridian.yaml governs the repo (advisory; never blocks or approves); the ledger under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/meridian/ stores event names, machine ids, aggregate counts and repository/spec/report paths (never verdicts, never file:line anchors, never file contents); its chain is unkeyed SHA-256, so it detects edits but can be recomputed by anyone with write access; no telemetry; no background processes. Disclosure — post_tool_call observes tools whose names contain write/edit/patch/replace/create/editor and re-runs the local analyzer only when a .meridian.yaml governs the repo (advisory; never blocks or approves); meridian_spec accept and meridian_report out_file write only inside the agent's working directory (refused at /, $HOME or its parents, or the Hermes home) and never through symlinks; the ledger under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/meridian/ stores event names, machine ids, aggregate counts and repository, spec, report and edited-file paths (never verdicts, never file:line anchors, never file contents) in an unkeyed SHA-256 chain that detects edits but can be recomputed by anyone with write access; no telemetry, no network, no background processes.

entries.name: mindgraph
entries.description: MindGraph typed knowledge-graph memory: bounded per-message recall, durable transcript/delegation capture and built-in memory mirroring, and the mindgraph-mcp general tool surface. Disclosure — tool calls, recall, capture and mirrored memory go to the MindGraph API (api.mindgraph.cloud, or MINDGRAPH_BASE_URL) under MINDGRAPH_API_KEY; automatic capture (default on; MINDGRAPH_AUTO_CAPTURE=off disables it) sends completed-turn user/assistant text and available participant ID/name/bot metadata, plus parent delegation task/result/child session ID, for extraction; other tool calls and outputs are not captured. Undelivered text and native memory operations rest in the profile directory (mindgraph/capture.db, mode 0600), are deleted on delivery, and transcript receipts are kept 30 days; background threads retry delivery. Native memory add/replace/remove changes are mirrored even with transcript capture off; replacements save new before forgetting old. Recall (MINDGRAPH_RECALL=off disables it) sends current-message content words and previous-message terms for subjectless follow-ups. Tool calls first send name, action and target node UIDs to the server governance check (MINDGRAPH_GOVERNANCE=off skips it). Automatic writes run only in the primary agent, except required compression checkpoints capture snapshots in any context. Ordinary turn/delegation capture requires plugins.isolation: in_process; isolated host mode reports that capture limitation while keeping recall, tools, native mirroring and required checkpoint snapshots. Queue overflow rejects new capture without evicting accepted evidence; v1 upgrades may replay previously delivered rows at the first required checkpoint. No telemetry, plugin-spawned separate processes or credentials stored outside Hermes.

entries.name: mistral-vibe
entries.description: Direct Mistral Vibe subscription access — browser PKCE login, dedicated credential pool, account-visible catalog discovery, relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models and mistral-large-4 (low/medium/high). Disclosure — unofficial, not affiliated with Mistral. "hermes auth add mistral-vibe" runs a browser PKCE sign-in against Mistral's Vibe console endpoints (console.mistral.ai/api/vibe/*) and stores the returned API key in the Hermes credential pool (auth.json, slice mistral-vibe), or uses MISTRAL_VIBE_API_KEY. Prompts and model listing go only to api.mistral.ai/v1. Vibe subscription coverage of API use is not guaranteed and may bill as pay-as-you-go. Logout clears the local pool but does not revoke the key remotely.

entries.name: mixar
entries.description: Mixar's own desktop MCP server over stdio, with a Mixar workflow skill: build and edit 3D scenes, generate models, textures, rigs and animation with AI, render, and export game-ready assets for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Requires Mixar 4.2.1+ on macOS, Windows or Linux, signed in with Connect MCP turned on, on the same computer as Hermes. Disclosure — runs the launcher the installed Mixar app writes at ~/.mixar/connector/mixar-mcp (%USERPROFILE%\.mixar\connector\mixar-mcp.cmd on Windows), which reads Mixar's own files under ~/.mixar/; tools execute arbitrary Python inside Mixar with your privileges; a tool call can start the installed Mixar app, which stays open after Hermes exits; calls go over loopback to Mixar, which forwards them to api.mixar.app under the signed-in account; generation prompts and reference images go to the AI provider running the chosen model; Mixar's backend keeps diagnostic records of MCP tool calls (inputs and results) and deletes them within 30 days; AI generation and create_layered_material spend Mixar credits, declared to Hermes as cost ranges with a 500-credit spend limit per chat; the plugin stores no credentials, ships no binaries, sends no telemetry and never updates itself; the optional MIXAR_MCP_LAUNCHER variable makes it run the program it names; at install Hermes looks for Mixar (macOS: Mixar.app in /Applications and ~/Applications; Windows: the installed-apps entry or %ProgramFiles%\Mixar; Linux: a mixar command on PATH or Mixar's launcher) and refuses the install when it is missing or, on macOS and Windows, older than 4.2.1.

entries.name: mnemos
entries.description: A memory of the agent's own. It keeps what it decides to keep, in its own words, wakes with it at the start of every session, and with each message the few memories that bear on it come back to it; nothing is written from a conversation on its own. Memories fade unless used, and before one is gone the agent is asked what it taught. What you ask it to always remember never fades. Hermes's MEMORY.md and USER.md stay on, and what the agent writes there is kept too. Each profile is its own agent with its own memory, one SQLite file on this machine that stays when the plugin is removed. No key or account needed. Disclosure — no network and no telemetry unless you choose it: deep_maintenance with a provider chosen for Mnemos (MNEMOS_LLM_PROVIDER, openrouter or openai) sends memory text to that provider during upkeep, and MNEMOS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=gemini sends the words of memories and questions to Google; keys are read only through agent.secret_scope, never from a file; the memory lives outside HERMES_HOME, in ~/.mnemos/hermes.db or ~/.mnemos/hermes-<profile>.db, with settings in $HERMES_HOME/mnemos.json, and Mnemos reads ~/.mnemos/config.json and Hermes's config.yaml; what the agent marks shared goes to ~/.mnemos/shared-memory.db, readable by every Mnemos agent on the machine; upkeep, when due, runs in a short-lived child Python process that exits when done, and nothing is scheduled; mnemos_page serves a page on 127.0.0.1 (a port the system picks, a fresh path, this machine only) until Hermes stops; it also shows the other agents whose memory Mnemos keeps in ~/.mnemos, and there the person can correct or let go of a memory, or leave a note, for any of them; the system prompt carries Mnemos's rules for keeping a memory and the agent's wake; on first start it raises the process's open-file limit to 4096 if lower.
entries.title: Mnemos
known_issues: If you connected Mnemos before with `mnemos connect hermes`, install with --force, which replaces the folder connect wrote. The agent keeps its memory and its settings.

entries.name: mnemoverse
entries.description: Persistent memory for agents, shared across tools: save preferences, decisions and lessons and recall them later by natural-language search; rating a recalled memory as helpful or misleading re-ranks what comes back next; shared rooms let several people's agents work from one memory. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) pointing at the hosted Mnemoverse MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR); the bundled skills load under a namespaced name. Disclosure — hosted-only connector; Hermes runs no code from the package (scripts/ holds the repository's own CI checks). Every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.mnemoverse.com (authorization server auth.mnemoverse.com, browser sign-in on console.mnemoverse.com); memories the agent writes are stored in the signed-in user's Mnemoverse account, and recalled memories are pulled into the session context. OAuth tokens are held and refreshed by Hermes, never by the package. No telemetry, background process or self-update code.

entries.name: mock-review
entries.description: Review boards for UI mockups and plans. The agent builds a board from a decisions.json file and your prototype pages; you open it on desktop or phone, mark each decision approve, change or skip, pin comments on the mocks and press Send, and your agent wakes up with the feedback as a markdown digest. Plan boards add question cards and one footer button, Build, which stays locked until nothing is open and then wakes the agent with the approved plan; mocks carry working controls by default (`interactive_elements`). A design profile bound to a project is enforced: a round with off-profile colours or fonts is refused unless `--off-brand` gives a reason. 2.0 adds people: there are no passwords; the board server has accounts, single-use invites (`hermes mockreview invite`), per-review roles (viewer, commenter, reviewer) and one share link per review whose guests never wake Hermes. Pins are threads with replies, resolve and `@Hermes` mentions, and a round exports as PNG, PDF, HTML or Markdown. here.now hosting is removed; `hermes mockreview migrate` converts old here.now reviews to local or tailnet. 2.1 makes `@Hermes` work: an owner's or reviewer's `@Hermes` comment wakes Hermes, which replies in the thread, resolves it, or patches the anchored block in place when the comment asks for it (three new tools: mock_review_list_comments, mock_review_reply, mock_review_resolve); a guest, an agent token or a wake-off board never wakes anyone. Hermes Desktop gets a Mocks tab that lists reviews, shows a round read-only and deletes; commenting stays in the browser. Boards open in a flatter inline layout by default (`layout: cards` keeps the 2.0 look). 2.2 shows live which pins Hermes is working on (a pulsing red dot on the pin, a working chip on the block and a count in the header). 2.3 keeps resolved pins on the board (`hide_resolved_pins` hides them) and wakes the chat a board was made in on every messaging platform Hermes hosts, Hermes Desktop chats included; `setup` creates the wake and notice routes for every configured messaging platform. Nine mock_review tools, the `hermes mockreview` CLI and slash command, a bundled usage skill, and a stdio MCP server (`bin/mockreview mcp`) that serves the six board tools to Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode without Hermes, plus three comment tools when given a personal access token; that server starts only when you add it to such a client, and its boards do not wake an agent unless you pass `--wake`. Plain http(s) links in mocks stay clickable and open in a new tab; every other link scheme is stripped. Disclosure — when autostart is on (off until `hermes mockreview setup`), a board web server (127.0.0.1:8790 by default) and one worker thread run inside the gateway process; setting host to 0.0.0.0 shows every device on your network the sign-in page, where people join with an invite or a share link. With Hermes Desktop, the Mocks tab's backend is a plugin route (/api/plugins/mock-review/) served by the Hermes dashboard process behind the dashboard's session token; it only lists, renders and deletes reviews. Outbound calls: signed POSTs to the local Hermes webhook (localhost:8644, or the receiver you name in MOCKREVIEW_WEBHOOK_URL for the MCP server): the wake-up on Send, Build or an `@Hermes` comment, an instant acknowledgement, and a later stall notice that carries the review title and counts, never your notes; and, only when you set `cloudflare_team` and `cloudflare_audience` for Cloudflare Access sign-in, a GET of that team's signing keys at https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs. A board made in a Hermes Desktop chat is woken differently: the board server inside the gateway queues the wake prompt into that chat's own session through Hermes's plugin `inject_message` API, which Hermes allows only with `plugins.entries.mock-review.allow_gateway_injection: true`. Setup asks for that consent and sets it (with `hermes config set`) only on an explicit yes at a terminal, never under `--yes`. That turn runs with the chat's own tools, so a Desktop board is refused unless Send is gated (loopback, no public URL, no Funnel mapping, not a public board). Secrets: only MOCKREVIEW_WEBHOOK_SECRET, read through Hermes's secret scope or from the process environment when the stdio MCP server runs without Hermes; setup generates it; no credential file is read. Runs `git -C <project> rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` (read only) to match a project to its bound design profile; runs `tailscale status --json`, `tailscale serve status --json` and `tailscale funnel status --json` (read only; on macOS the Tailscale app's own binary if the symlink crashes), and, only when you run `hermes mockreview public on|off`, `tailscale funnel --bg --yes --https=<port> http://127.0.0.1:<board port>` or `tailscale funnel --https=<port> off` to publish the board on a public Funnel URL behind sign-in; from `setup` it runs the hermes subcommands `--version`, `gateway status`, `config get/set/unset`, `webhook subscribe`, `webhook remove` (only for a stale self-delivering route, after you confirm) and `plugins validate`. The opt-in `wake_toolsets` setting lets the session woken by Send use the toolsets you list (for example terminal and file), so board feedback reaches those tools; setup refuses it while the server listens beyond loopback and only prints the `toolsets` line for you to add to the wake route by hand (re-add it after every setup run). Reviews, accounts and comments are stored under $HERMES_HOME/workspace/mock-reviews. No telemetry, no update check. One Python dependency, itsdangerous; the optional crypto extra adds PyJWT for Cloudflare Access sign-in.

entries.name: model-drift-watch
entries.description: Catches silent quality drift in your model: 34 questions graded exactly against its baseline. Messages only for a confirmed drop, a changed served model, or a failed measurement. Disclosure — calls your model via ctx.llm on your bill (cap 120,000 tokens and $0.50); model_drift can start one; may fetch OpenRouter or models.dev prices; 10 code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child, not a sandbox, in unattended cron; job and script stay after removal until unschedule; no extra agent turn; questions still count on the cap; history stays in plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry; gateway users can run it at your cost; hermes tools turns it off per surface; disable stops /model-drift-watch.
entries.capability_summary: model-drift-watch (community, maintained by TakeshiTGAL) Catches silent quality drift in your model: 34 questions graded exactly against its baseline. Disclosure — calls your model via ctx.llm on your bill (cap 120,000 tokens and $0.50); model_drift can start one; may fetch OpenRouter or models.dev prices; 10 code questions, off by default, run model-written Python in a limited child, not a sandbox, in unattended cron; job and script stay after removal until unschedule; no extra agent turn; questions still count on the cap; history stays in plugin-data/model-drift-watch; no telemetry; gateway users can run it at your cost; hermes tools turns it off per surface; disable stops /model-drift-watch. This plugin registers tool(s): model_drift. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.name: model-explainer
entries.description: A Models page for Hermes Desktop, plus a button beside the chat model pill that opens it as a pop-up, built around your own model picker: choose a model to see its Hermes Index score, cost per task, context and output limits, price, abilities and your own measured speed and spend, with a score-against-cost frontier chart, and compare up to four side by side. Every value cites a source and date. Disclosure — one GET of a public JSON data file from the author's GitHub repo (raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer, main branch, so its contents can change after this pin), at most daily and only when the page or pop-up opens (can be turned off; the bundled copy works offline; the file is validated data, never code); reads model.options and the focused session's model and usage figures; writes plugin storage, and switches the chat model only when the user presses Use this model (the same config.set request as the built-in picker, scoped to the open chat). Desktop only: no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

entries.name: model-forge-desktop
entries.description: Model Forge cockpit pane for Hermes Desktop — compute targets, live engines, loaded models and hardware at a glance. Companion UI for the Model Forge plugin. Disclosure — the pane polls each compute target you register in Model Forge (plus http://127.0.0.1:8080 by default) with read-only GET requests to /v1/models, /api/tags and /system_stats to show which local engines are running, reads Model Forge's own targets file through a read-only shell command, and runs Model Forge's read-only hardware and memory probes when you open the resource view; no generation calls, no writes, no credentials, no background processes, no telemetry. Disclosure — model pulls download weights from huggingface.co or modelscope.cn on user request, and model_forge_browse queries the public huggingface.co model API for fresh listings unless fresh=false (optional HF_TOKEN / MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN pull credentials live in plugin settings, are read only through Hermes' secret route and are sent only to their own host family); shell commands are read-only hardware probes (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi) plus vendor engine installers — model_forge_install action=engine_install runs a pinned vendor installer (a SHA-256-verified install script, or a pinned git commit checked out and re-verified before setup runs) in a background job only after Hermes approval; every child process (installers, engine servers, hardware probes) runs with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR plus declared engine variables) that never carries credentials; hardware probes read local system state (GPU queries, sysfs, the Windows memory API) while remote compute targets use user-declared budgets; adding a compute target, deleting a model-storage entry, model_forge_activate with apply=true (which rewrites model.default, model.provider and base_url in config.yaml and adds a custom_providers entry), running a vendor installer, and any broker claim, swap, release or media job that would start an inference engine server process each ask for Hermes approval first; started engine servers (llama-server, vLLM) bind 127.0.0.1 only; media jobs and Maya pulls POST prompts and image bytes to user-configured endpoints; the bundled TTS helper POSTs text and base64 voice-clone reference audio to a user-configured /v1/audio/speech endpoint; background processes are the download daemon thread, approved installer jobs and approved engine server processes; no telemetry.

entries.name: model-forge
entries.description: Local models for every modality — chat, vision, OCR, image generation and editing, video, 3D meshes, music, SFX and voice. Model Forge finds your hardware (local probes; remote compute targets use the budgets you declare), shows which models fit, maps each model to the right inference engine (llama.cpp, Strata, Ollama, vLLM, ComfyUI, a user-configured OpenAI-compatible media gateway and more), pulls the model, and wires it into Hermes as a provider — so chat, image_generate, video_generate, vision and TTS run on hardware you control with no account and no API key. Six tools: model_forge_status (targets, VRAM/RAM, engines, loaded models), model_forge_browse (per-modality model catalog with hardware-fit verdicts), model_forge_target_add (register compute targets), model_forge_install (pull models through engine-native paths), model_forge_activate (wire a running chat model into Hermes), model_forge_generate_media (3D, music and SFX jobs through a user-configured OpenAI-compatible media gateway). Disclosure — model pulls download weights from huggingface.co or modelscope.cn on user request, and model_forge_browse queries the public huggingface.co model API for fresh listings unless fresh=false (optional HF_TOKEN / MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN pull credentials live in plugin settings, are read only through Hermes' secret route and are sent only to their own host family); shell commands are read-only hardware probes (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi) plus vendor engine installers — model_forge_install action=engine_install runs a pinned vendor installer (a SHA-256-verified install script, or a pinned git commit checked out and re-verified before setup runs) in a background job only after Hermes approval; every child process (installers, engine servers, hardware probes) runs with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR plus declared engine variables) that never carries credentials; hardware probes read local system state (GPU queries, sysfs, the Windows memory API) while remote compute targets use user-declared budgets; adding a compute target, model_forge_activate with apply=true (which rewrites model.default, model.provider and base_url in config.yaml), running a vendor installer, and starting an inference engine server process each ask for Hermes approval first; started engine servers (llama-server, vLLM) bind 127.0.0.1 only; media jobs and Maya pulls POST prompts and image bytes to user-configured endpoints; the bundled TTS helper POSTs text and base64 voice-clone reference audio to a user-configured /v1/audio/speech endpoint; background processes are the download daemon thread, approved installer jobs and approved engine server processes; no telemetry.

entries.name: model-kombat
entries.description: Head-to-head model evaluation: scout a task or kanban card into lanes, build a deterministic fight card (Warm-up 1pt, Main Event 2pt, Championship 3pt, sudden death) at standard, hard or gauntlet intensity, fight two models on identical prompts, and score mechanically — executed code, exact counts, numeric tolerances, phrase groups, JSON leaf equality, SQLite rows — with a per-lane Elo ladder, live arcade pane, kanban badges, and a measured best-value call when strong models tie ('equal quality — X is 18x cheaper'); a local task_stats.json remembers which tasks split the two models and demotes saturated ones. Disclosure — model calls: all fights go through Hermes' own LLM facade with a per-call model override you must enable (`plugins.entries.model-kombat.llm.allow_model_override`); pure fights make two model calls per task, capped by `max_fight_cost_usd` / `max_fight_tokens` and `max_fight_seconds`, which tool arguments can lower but never raise; agentic fights create kanban tasks assigned to your active profile with a per-task model override, which start worker agent sessions with that profile's tools and are not spend-capped; code execution: off by default and switchable only in plugin settings, and when enabled, model-written Python runs as your user in a resource-limited subprocess that is not a security sandbox; local files: reads optional project tasks from `.kombat/tasks.json` in the working directory and writes reports, history, ladder, exports and stats only under its plugin data dir; kanban: posts display cards on a dedicated `model-kombat` board and auto-closes its own stale cards there; no third-party network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads.

entries.name: model-leaderboard
entries.description: Model leaderboard for Hermes Desktop: a full /model-leaderboard page that ranks any OpenRouter model for a chosen Hermes profile — context window, prices, Artificial Analysis indices and curated SWE-bench Verified / LiveCodeBench — with per-profile criteria, six score views (cards, table, score bars, histograms, heatmap, quality-vs-cost Pareto frontier), an OpenRouter news feed (new models, price changes, promos) and a documented REST surface under /api/plugins/model-leaderboard/. Disclosure — outbound HTTPS to OpenRouter's public model API (catalogue and pricing) on a 60 s poll and a forced refresh every 10 minutes while the page is visible, and to Hugging Face's public model API (safetensors metadata, for parameter counts) on demand and cached; reads the installed Hermes profiles' own config.yaml files once, to seed the tracked list from the models those profiles declare; an index the catalogue does not publish for a variant is borrowed from its exact alias or from a published member of the same model family and shown as inherited (⤵), with no network call for that; keeps its state in <hermes home>/plugin-data/model-leaderboard/ (seeded from the JSON shipped with the plugin), which LLM_DASH_DATA / LLM_DASH_CACHE_TTL can move or tune; the optional "Auto-fill criteria" action runs on the host LLM facade (ctx.llm.complete_structured), so it spends the user's configured model tokens; prices the models at the context size each profile declares (the profile's Hermes compaction settings, or a fixed 32k-1M volume) using OpenRouter's published context-price tiers; the news feed's promotions are curated examples, labelled as such, not live OpenRouter offers; ships one read-only skill (model-leaderboard:refresh-benchmarks) whose only write is a POST to its own /benchmarks route; ships an optional harvester (scripts/harvest_aa.py) that the plugin never runs (a user or a cron does) to fill the intelligence index from Artificial Analysis, either through their free data API with the user's own ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY or, without a key, by reading their public leaderboard page once, writing the result only into the plugin's own benchmarks.json; the plugin itself makes no Artificial Analysis request, writes nothing outside its data directory, and only checks through Hermes whether the optional ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY is set, never storing, echoing or logging it.

entries.name: model-picker
entries.description: Per-turn cost classifier across three model tiers (Quick / Standard / Expert): rates each user turn from configurable best_for lists and rewrites the outgoing request's model through the llm_request middleware, biased to keep the previous tier unless the turn changes shape, with escalate_model for tool failures. Disclosure — the plugin rewrites the model field of every outgoing request for a classified session, picking between three configured model ids that must all belong to the session's own provider (a foreign-provider tier is refused and the session model stands); it makes one bounded auxiliary classifier call through the host's plugin LLM route on each classified turn (up to about 12,000 characters of recent conversation plus the prompt), reading its model ids from config.json next to the plugin, MODEL_PICKER_CONFIG, or MODEL_PICKER_* env, and falls back to the host's primary model; routing decisions, with the first 120 characters of each classified prompt, are logged to $HERMES_HOME/logs/model-picker.log; a classifier-driven tier change can ask the context engine to compact the transcript before the switch, and escalate_model replaces the next request's context with a model-written handoff summary plus the recent tail; that engine registers only when the host config sets context.engine: model-picker.

entries.name: model-router
entries.description: Profile model settings and native delegate_task routing for Hermes, with a Korean-first Desktop settings page (Settings → Plugins → 모델 및 라우팅) and a composer execution status line. A delegated task runs on the model of its task slot (design, complex code, simple code, simple verification, complex verification, computer use), each slot with optional spare models, or as an explicitly allowlisted local profile using that profile's own model, credentials and tools; with model-router-auto the agent chooses one of these routes per task. The status line shows each subagent's requested slot, the model/provider its own API calls reported (including observed spare-model switches), elapsed time, tool count and token totals; since v0.13.2 a completed profile delegation also shows the model/provider from the origin's stored delegation route report (read-only scalar metadata), and a refused, cancelled or timed-out request is settled instead of lingering as running. Its roster is bounded in-memory metadata (ids, counters, model/provider ids; no prompts, results or secrets); since v0.13.1 it survives an in-process plugin reload, but not a process restart. entries.name: modelscout
entries.description: Per-task model choice from the models you actually have, so light work stops spending frontier-model tokens and subscription usage limits last longer. A pre_llm_call hook shows a short card for each new task (tier, best-fit model from your keys, subscriptions and live models.dev pricing, and why), then routes the work to a right-sized delegate_task child, up or down tier, asks, or stays, per your defaults. Bundles the modelscout skill and a /modelscout command for settings and a measured savings report. Disclosure — reads and writes ~/.claude/modelscout-profile.json (settings shared with ModelScout on other agents), appends routed-child outcomes (tier, model, status; no goal text) to ~/.claude/modelscout-outcomes.jsonl, and reads the model inventory and catalog JSON beside it plus Hermes's own models_dev_cache.json; it opens Hermes state.db read-only to look up a routed child's model and for the savings report, which also reads Claude Code transcripts read-only. A pre_llm_call hook adds routing instructions to each new task's prompt and can steer work into delegated subagents. In Hermes the plugin code makes no network calls and reads no credentials. On Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Grok Build (not Hermes), hooks/session_start.py runs scripts/catalog.py in a detached process to fetch the public models.dev catalog weekly, sending no keys or user data (`modelscout: catalog off` disables it). The bundled skill's optional discover-models.sh, run through the terminal tool, reads provider API-key env vars (and only checks whether Azure, Bedrock or Vertex credentials are present, without reading or using them), sends each only to its own provider's list-models endpoint and fetches the public models.dev catalog. Typing `modelscout: grok setup` (in any host, Hermes included) writes Grok Build's rules file ~/.grok/rules/modelscout.md (or under GROK_HOME) and reads ~/.grok/config.toml for custom model names; later ModelScout settings commands rewrite that file only if ModelScout wrote it, and `modelscout: grok remove` deletes it. No telemetry or self-updating, and no background processes in Hermes.

entries.name: moment
entries.description: Keeps a Hermes agent honest about its own memory. Hermes injects SOUL.md, memories/MEMORY.md and memories/USER.md into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start; anything that changes those files while the session lives stays invisible to it, and the agent keeps answering from stale memory. Moment fingerprints the three house files at a session's first turn and re-checks them on every later turn (pre_llm_call); when one changed, it injects a short drift receipt — which file, its absolute path, baseline and detection timestamps, the changed lines, and the full current content for small files — so the agent answers from the present and says plainly that its memory drifted. It also provides a moment_check tool for on-demand freshness reports against the session's starting state. Disclosure — reads only the active profile's SOUL.md, memories/MEMORY.md and memories/USER.md (the agent's own house files; never credential stores); writes only its own baseline and receipt-journal state in its plugin data directory (plugin-data/moment); the hook only adds context and never blocks or modifies a turn; no network, no shell, no subprocess, no telemetry; Python standard library only, zero dependencies.

entries.description: Write, run and repair Momentic end-to-end tests for web (Chrome) and iOS/Android (simulators and emulators), and run Mo bug bashes that file each bug with a Momentic regression test. entries.name: money-rules
entries.description: Money rules for Hermes: pay, split, sweep and alert on USDC from your own Solana wallet, under rules you set in chat. You sign one capped USDC allowance (SPL approve) to a local helper key; USDC stays in your wallet until a rule pays, and every new rule waits for /money approve. Every payment started from chat goes through the Hermes approval prompt, and the relay fee is capped on the client (max_fee_usd, default 0.05). Rules fire on a schedule, when USDC comes in, or when a balance crosses a line. Gasless: a relay pays the Solana fee for a small USDC fee in the same transaction and only co-signs connect, revoke and pay. Disclosure — Crypto: moves USDC from your own Solana wallet through a local helper keypair (stored in plain JSON, mode 600, under the profile's plugin-data/money-rules) that you allow, with one SPL approve you sign on hermes-money-rules.vercel.app, to spend up to a cap you choose; every payment the agent starts asks in the Hermes approval prompt, and new rules and held payments wait for your /money approve, but approved rules (scheduled pay, incoming splits, sweeps of everything over a kept amount) then run unattended from a background thread that polls every 30 seconds while Hermes runs, up to a local daily limit (default $100/day, relay fees included); every payment is co-signed by the author's relay at hermes-money-rules.vercel.app, which takes a USDC fee in the same transaction, capped by your max_fee_usd setting (default $0.05, plus up to $0.60 for each recipient that has no USDC account yet); wallet reads go through that relay's RPC proxy unless you set rpc_url; /money revoke zeroes the allowance on-chain; no telemetry.

entries.name: mood
entries.description: A tiny evolving mood for Hermes, built for slow local models. Tracks mood, rapport and three slow-moving traits (warmth, playfulness, directness) that change with keyword rules on what the user writes and drift back to neutral over hours, then appends one ~30-token line to each user message through pre_llm_call, so the system prompt and its cache are never touched. Adds a /mood command (show, reset, on, off). Disclosure — makes no model calls, no network I/O, runs no shell commands and holds no credentials; reads the text of each user message and reads/writes only its own plugin-data state file (state.json, per profile).

entries.name: morph
entries.description: One adaptive workspace across the applications you use, with human-approved, verified actions: an approval gate between the agent and the APIs it can write to. Connect a GitHub repository (`hermes morph connect github owner/name`) or any service that publishes an OpenAPI document, and MORPH learns from the schema what can be read and what can be safely changed. The agent gets tools to read and to propose; it has no tool that approves and is never given the token an approval needs. A human approves each change in the dashboard, seeing the exact before and after; MORPH writes it, then re-reads the record from the API and reports it verified only if it matches what was promised. Only operations with a checkable effect are offered — for GitHub issues: close, close as not planned, reopen, set labels, set title, assign, unassign. The dashboard has five views (Workspace, Connections, Approvals, Activity, Context) and composes tables, boards and charts over the connected data from a goal stated in plain language. Every proposal, approval and result is kept in a hash-chained audit log. Disclosure — MORPH makes outbound HTTPS calls to the services the operator connects, including api.github.com when a repository is connected (loopback only with an explicit opt-in; private, link-local, reserved and cloud-metadata targets are refused, redirects are never followed, and the address actually dialled is validated at connect time); it stores its connection list, workspaces, pending proposals, read cursors and the audit log in its own plugin-data directory; it reads bearer tokens through agent.secret_scope by environment-variable name and never logs, stores or returns them; it calls the host model through ctx.llm for interface planning with a deterministic offline fallback, and sends the model schema only, never a record value. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating code. Ships three workflow skills and an optional offline sandbox of three loopback services (`hermes morph connect sandbox`, started only by `hermes morph up`) so the whole loop can be tried with no account and no key.

entries.name: motion-studio
entries.description: Creation-first media studio for Hermes Desktop. Quick Create turns a chat request into sound effects, images, voice or video takes you can play, compare, keep and download; Production collects chosen takes and imported files into a project and exports them. Image, voice and video come from Hermes' own image_gen, tts and video_gen tools; sound effects generation is unavailable outside the author's pinned Stable Audio setup; imported sound effects remain supported for review and export. Disclosure — downloads finished media only from the provider URLs Hermes' image_gen/tts/video_gen tools return (x.ai, openai.com, oaiusercontent.com, fal.media, fal.run, deepinfra.com, krea.ai; no proxies, cookies or credentials, same-host redirects only); runs ffmpeg/ffprobe to check imported and generated media, nvidia-smi to report GPU use, and the author's pinned local audio engine, each with a minimal fixed environment (no inherited credentials or provider keys); reads Hermes' generator output cache read-only (secret and hidden files refused), checks only whether provider API keys are set through Hermes' scoped secret API, and reads installed Hermes provider source files to list available methods; stores projects and takes under the profile's plugin data directory; saved takes are kept, not deleted. No telemetry.
entries.title: Motion Studio
known_issues: Open Motion Studio from a chat in the motion-studio profile: the panel works with the focused chat. If it says the chat is not connected, click Connect.
Image, voice and video need the matching Hermes tool enabled with a provider. Paid or unknown-cost methods ask before running.

Sound effects generation is unavailable outside the author's pinned Stable Audio setup; this release cannot configure another user's wrapper. Imported sound effects remain supported. Music generation is not available yet.
Tested on Linux and Windows Hermes Desktop. macOS has not been tested.
Saved takes and projects cannot be deleted from the app yet.

Hermes' security scan rates the package caution because it runs media tools (ffmpeg/ffprobe) on file descriptors and includes subprocess and setup helpers. A catalog install at the reviewed pin accepts that rating without a scan prompt; an install from the bare Git URL asks for confirmation.

entries.name: mqtt
entries.description: MQTT as a Hermes platform: one authenticated broker connection, per-topic routing (deliver, agent, job, drop) and JSON replies published outside the consumed namespace; ships its own standard-library MQTT 3.1.1/5.0 client over TCP or TLS (verified by default, optional private CA/mTLS) with keepalive, reconnect and opt-in burst coalescing, and drops unmatched topics. Disclosure — holds one outbound broker connection and its reconnect loop, reads the MQTT username/password through Hermes's scoped secret route and optional TLS files at operator-provided paths, and enables trusted_inbound (the broker's authentication is the trust boundary): any publisher the broker's ACL admits can start agent turns, and on topics you map to deliver or job it can post text to the chat you name on another connected platform or run the cron job you name, while payload text can never issue gateway commands; job and cross-platform delivery go through Hermes internals (tools.cronjob_tools, the gateway runner), so a Hermes update can disable them; no telemetry, no shell, no writes.
entries.title: MQTT
known_issues: Intel Macs are not tested or supported (CI covers macos-latest, which is Apple Silicon).
trusted_inbound is on: every publisher the broker's ACL admits can start agent turns, so scope the broker account to the subscription filter and reply topic.

entries.name: ms-decision-provider
entries.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 (Azure AI Foundry System One) decision provider for bounded agent decisions. Registers typed-decision tools (decision_noul, decision_choice, decision_score, decide) that preserve full probability distributions, plus an opt-in pre_tool_call hook that requests human approval for known-risk calls without sending their arguments to Azure. Disclosure — the four decision tools send the caller-supplied state/questions text to the Azure Foundry endpoint you set in AZURE_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL (nothing is sent while it is unset); with MS_DECISION_GATE=1 the pre_tool_call gate sends only a coarse operation label for known-risk tool calls to that endpoint and routes them to Hermes's human approval prompt (MS_DECISION_GATE_MODE=block hard-denies instead); the labelled eval corpus under tests/ contains literal destructive commands as should-refuse examples.

entries.name: mulligan
entries.description: Counterfactual replay for Hermes: record a run, rewind to any step, edit one tool decision, replay forward in a fresh child session, and diff the branch against the original. Replay-to-point reproduces the recorded steps with zero provider calls and zero tool side effects; the branch runs live with normal approvals. Uses llm_execution, tool_execution and tool_request middleware, pre/post_tool_call hooks and ctx.subagent_lifecycle.launch; stdlib only, no dependencies. Stores append-only JSONL traces (prompts, tool arguments and tool results) under $HERMES_HOME/replay-traces/. Disclosure — while enabled it records every session automatically (full model responses, tool arguments and tool results, and the last user message) as append-only JSONL under $HERMES_HOME/replay-traces/, which are sensitive, not rotated and persist until you delete them; mg_play launches a child session whose live tail spends provider tokens and runs tools with normal approvals; no network calls, no credential access, no shell execution, no self-update, and no approvals are bypassed or auto-answered.
entries.title: Mulligan
entries.capability_summary: mulligan (community, maintained by onyebuchidaniel60) Counterfactual replay for Hermes: record a run, rewind to any step, edit one tool decision, replay forward in a fresh child session, and diff the branch against the original. Replay-to-point reproduces the recorded steps with zero provider calls and zero tool side effects; the branch runs live with normal approvals. Uses llm_execution, tool_execution and tool_request middleware, pre/post_tool_call hooks and ctx.subagent_lifecycle.launch; stdlib only, no dependencies. Stores append-only JSONL traces (prompts, tool arguments and tool results) under $HERMES_HOME/replay-traces/. Disclosure — while enabled it records every session automatically (full model responses, tool arguments and tool results, and the last user message) as append-only JSONL under $HERMES_HOME/replay-traces/, which are sensitive, not rotated and persist until you delete them; mg_play launches a child session whose live tail spends provider tokens and runs tools with normal approvals; no network calls, no credential access, no shell execution, no self-update, and no approvals are bypassed or auto-answered. This plugin registers tool(s): mg_list, mg_inspect, mg_rewind, mg_edit, mg_play, mg_diff; hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call; middleware: llm_execution, tool_execution, tool_request. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0.

entries.name: multi-telegram
entries.description: Run an arbitrary number of Telegram bot identities through one Hermes profile and agent. Each bot has its own token reference, display identity, allowlists, role prompt, welcome message and session policy; replies always leave through the bot that received the triggering message. Optional shared-session groups continue one stored Hermes transcript for the same external chat/user/topic. Disclosure - long polling to the Telegram Bot API uses one bot token per bot, read from the active profile's secret scope via a per-bot token_env; no telemetry, subprocess, self-update or core overrides; authorized inbound attachments are cached through Hermes; non-secret status and proactive routes are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data. Transcript isolation is not memory isolation: MEMORY.md, USER.md, session_search and tools are profile-wide; use separate profiles or restrict toolsets for hard isolation. Webhooks, inline clarify/approval keyboards and out-of-process cron delivery are not implemented. Disclosure — runs one Telegram Bot API long-poll connection per configured bot, using a per-bot token read from the active profile's secret scope by its `token_env` name (optional operator-set proxy / custom Bot API base URL); inbound messages from allowlisted senders (deny-all by default; `allow_all_users` makes a bot public) reach this profile's one agent, whose memory, USER.md, session_search and tools are shared by every bot unless per-bot `toolsets` restrict them; attachments are cached through Hermes and status/route files are kept under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/multi-telegram; may lazily install Hermes's own `telegram` extra through Hermes's package manager; adds a token-redacting filter to the process's root log handlers.
entries.title: Multi-Telegram
known_issues: Long polling only; webhooks are not implemented.
Inline clarify/approval keyboards are not implemented; text fallback is used.
Out-of-process cron delivery is not implemented.
Isolated transcripts do not isolate profile memory, USER.md, session_search or tools; use separate profiles or restrict toolsets.
Telegram DM topics are unverified.

entries.name: multiverse
entries.description: Best-of-N for coding agents, with real checks. multiverse_race makes one git worktree per attempt (2 to 6) from the same base (HEAD, or the uncommitted working tree through git stash create), starts one delegate_task subagent per worktree with its own approach, pins each subagent to its worktree (pre_tool_call rewrites terminal workdir, file paths and V4A patch paths, and blocks access to the other worktrees and nested delegation), runs the same check commands in every worktree, ranks them by checks passed and then by the smallest real diff, and multiverse_adopt applies the winner with git apply. With delegation.backend: multiverse, each attempt can use its own model and provider. Hermes Desktop: a live race board pane (each attempt's status and tool-call count, then checks passed, diff and the winner), a status-bar chip while racing, and a toast when judging ends. Disclosure — no network calls of its own, no credentials, no telemetry, no background threads. Runs git (rev-parse, stash create, worktree add/remove/prune, add -A inside the worktrees, diff, apply), mkdir, rm -f of its own .patch files and rmdir, plus your check commands, through the Hermes terminal tool, so approvals and the configured terminal backend apply. Creates worktrees next to the repository in .<repo>.multiverse/<run id>/. Starts subagents through delegate_task, which uses your configured model(s) and costs tokens per attempt. Stores run metadata (goal, checks, worktree paths, scores, the last 1500 characters of each subagent summary) in its plugin state under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data. Sends plugin.multiverse.run snapshots (goal, checks, per-attempt label, model, approach, status, tool-call count, scores and diff stats; no subagent text) to Desktop windows attached to the same Hermes process, at most once a second while attempts run; the desktop half keeps the last 10 runs in Desktop plugin storage.

entries.name: munin
entries.description: Munin meeting notes for Hermes Agent: ask what was decided in your last meeting, get a follow-up with every action item checked against the transcript and cited by meeting id, line id and clock time, and search who said what across meetings, through the hosted Munin MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and DCR) with two workflow skills bundled (munin-followup, munin-recall). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no plugin code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at app.muninlabs.ai; meeting notes, transcript lines, titles and people's names from the user's Munin account are pulled into the session context. On Munin's consent page the user picks a read-only or an editable connection; an editable one lists the server's two write tools (set_speaker renames a speaker in one meeting, import_meeting saves a meeting from another app). The package declares the server untrusted so Hermes asks before any write-capable call, but the `hermes mcp add munin --url https://app.muninlabs.ai/mcp --auth oauth` config entry that OAuth requires replaces that setting unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it (the README shows how); then `hermes mcp login munin`, since the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401. No local code, no hooks, no env vars, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: music-listener
entries.description: Listen to an MP3/FLAC/WAV by reconstructing every instrumental track, the vocal melody, pitch contour and time-aligned lyrics into a multi-track MIDI, MusicXML score and a compact structural JSON. Runs a heavy audio/ML stack (Demucs htdemucs_6s 6-stem separation, Spotify Basic Pitch polyphonic transcription, librosa pyin f0, faster-whisper lyric alignment) inside its own isolated Python 3.11 venv so Hermes' core runtime is never touched. The listen_to_music tool accepts an audio path and returns artifact paths (full_score.mid, full_score.musicxml, score_summary.json) plus tempo, key, per-track note counts, 8-bar section descriptors and synced lyric words — a compact structural summary so the agent reasons over the song without loading thousands of raw MIDI events. A /listen slash command and the music-listener:music-listener skill (pretty_midi/music21 recipes for bar queries, motifs, transposition and re-harmonization) round out the working surface. The worker prints progress to stderr and only compact JSON to stdout. Security: no shell=True (argv-list subprocesses), sanitized output paths, no credential reads, no network ports, a 60-minute worker cap; its only outbound traffic is official Demucs/faster-whisper model-weight downloads. Proven end-to-end on a real 2:46 commercial track (Imael Angel - "Bad Times"): 7 named MIDI tracks, valid MusicXML, 100 time-aligned lyric words. See https://github.com/JPeetz/music-listener#readme. Disclosure — after install you run the plugin's install.sh, which builds a Python 3.11 venv inside the plugin folder and downloads about 1-2 GB of packages (torch, Demucs, faster-whisper); the first transcription downloads Demucs and faster-whisper model weights from their upstream hosts; listen_to_music reads whatever audio path the agent passes and writes stems and scores under transcriptions/ in the agent's working directory (or the configured output_dir), running a CPU/GPU-heavy worker for up to 60 minutes per call.
entries.title: Music Listener
known_issues: On Intel-mac CPU-only hosts, torch must stay at 2.2.2 and torchcrepe's full.pth CPU inference hangs; the worker uses librosa pyin behind a 30s watchdog as its reliable f0 path. Memory-ordered stages keep whisper from OOMing 16 GB hosts.

entries.name: muster
entries.description: See what your AI helpers are actually doing. Every worker hermes starts shows up live in one pane: working, stuck (silent too long), failing on repeat, or gone (hermes crashed). Stop a stuck one or send it a message with one click. Start your own helpers with muster_fanout. /muster-digest reports status, spend and the decisions you need; scheduled Fleet watch + Morning report blueprints speak up only when something needs you. No network, no setup.

entries.name: myeline
entries.description: Myeline is a remote MCP memory server: every memory is a single fact with its source attached, AI proposals land in a human review queue, and removing a fact takes a written reason kept in an audit log. One retraction stops a stale fact in every connected assistant at once. Maintained by Sandbox Group, the Myeline vendor. Disclosure — registers the vendor-hosted remote MCP server cortex.myeline.si/mcp, signed in through Hermes's remote MCP OAuth with your own Myeline account; the queries and facts the model sends in Myeline tool calls are stored and processed on Myeline's servers, and the server defines its own tool list, which can change without a new catalog pin.

entries.name: myfolks
entries.description: Persistent, exact memory about the people in your life. myfolks, /myfolks or /contacts saves and returns details word for word, with when and where each was saved; saving and recall never call a model. Plain words (remember, fix, forget, undo), a Desktop page to search, add, edit, delete and undo, vCard and CSV import, and optional Google Contacts sync. Encrypted SQLite store (AES-256-GCM) in the Hermes folder. Owner only by default, group chats refused, optional per-person sharing (read or add). Disclosure — no network calls until the owner runs myfolks sync; after that Hermes calls the Google People API (people.googleapis.com, contacts.readonly) for the plugin through its declared oauth client (signed in with hermes auth add myfolks:google, token stored and refreshed by Hermes, never given to the plugin), on each sync and automatically at most every 10 minutes when a save or lookup names someone not yet stored, until myfolks sync off. Replies sent over a messaging platform pass through that platform. AI access is off by default; when turned on, the details it needs are sent to the configured model provider. Hooks: pre_gateway_dispatch answers the owner's (and listed shared people's) MyFolks messages in chat apps before the session sees them; pre_llm_call stops a MyFolks command from reaching the AI; pre_tool_call blocks AI tools that directly name its files. Other messages get an in-memory text check only. Stores its own device key in a file only the user can read, or in the OS keychain when Python's keyring package is available.
entries.title: MyFolks for Hermes
known_issues: Google sync needs your own Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app, People API on), set as MYFOLKS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and MYFOLKS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET; file import needs nothing.
Tested in Telegram, the Hermes terminal and Hermes Desktop. Other chat apps and Windows are untested.

entries.name: myradio
entries.description: Hermes DJs your own myradio station. /radio shows a now-playing card, plays a song by title and sends song requests to the station's music maker, all without a model turn. The agent gets 12 tools to read the station, search the library, plan the queue, write the DJ's lines and ask for new songs, plus the myradio:dj skill and the myradio:dj-shift blueprint for unattended DJ shifts. Going live and deleting audio are not agent tools. Disclosure: each tool call starts myradio's own MCP adapter as a short-lived child process (no shell, small environment without API keys); that adapter reads the station's control.token from its data folder (~/.myradio by default) and talks only to the station on 127.0.0.1. /radio request makes one completion with the user's configured Hermes model (Hermes 0.23+). No other network calls, no files written, no background process, no telemetry. Needs a running myradio station.
