entries.name: myswarm
entries.description: Discover, visualize, sanitize/export, and import community agents.md swarm configurations. Outputs abbreviated agent/persona/goal tables, renders ASCII topology diagrams (.svg and .png images + portable 7-bit copy-paste ASCII symbol blocks), generates rich themed swarm illustrations across 12 curated signature themes and orthogonal intensity levels (understated, normal, overstated) via Hermes default model and image_generate, exports sanitized agents.md files, and imports/reverts shared configs with on-screen file preview and best-effort import warnings; every import/revert asks for approval. Disclosure — myswarm_import/myswarm_revert replace the workspace AGENTS.md/agents.md (a file Hermes loads into every session's system prompt) after a Hermes approval prompt; choosing "always" approves all later imports. The import security check is a best-effort regex + model warning, not a security boundary — only import files you trust. Swarm file contents are sent to your configured model for parsing and PII scrubbing (also best-effort; review exports before sharing), and myswarm_visualize_image calls your configured image_generate provider (may cost credits). Adds a ~2.8k-character MySwarm guidance section to every session's system prompt. Writes myswarm-ascii.svg/.png and .md exports into the current folder (exports may overwrite an existing .md file there), plus a .agents.md.myswarm.orig sidecar, and keeps import backups under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/myswarm/.

entries.name: nachalo
entries.description: Pair Hermes agents end-to-end from six spoken words (CPace + X25519 + ML-KEM-768) and catch a man in the middle with four safety words; the agent only drafts, a person sends. Disclosure — talks to a relay (ntfy.sh by default or your relay_url, plus whichever relay each paired peer chose) that sees topics, IP addresses, timing and fixed-size encrypted frames, never contents; while a peer is active a background thread in the gateway holds an HTTPS subscription to it; peers, inbox, drafts and an audit log (no words, no keys) live in the profile's plugin-data/nachalo, and channel state is sealed with NACHALO_STORE_KEY, which the plugin creates once in the profile's .env with save_env_value and reads through the secret scope; pairing is human-only, peer messages are held and never start turns or tool calls (each turn the agent is told only how many are waiting and from which peer names, and reads them as untrusted content with nachalo_inbox), sending needs a person who sees the exact text and does not rely on approval modes, and cron or -q runs never pair or send; a pre_tool_call hook blocks agent terminal calls that drive the nachalo CLI or its data; the native code ships in the nachalo wheel on PyPI with provenance attestations; the protocol and channel are unaudited drafts.

entries.name: nachos
entries.description: Durable memory and context compression for Hermes Agent with local SQLite or flat-file storage. Disclosure — replaces the memory provider (memory.provider: nachos) and, only when context.engine: nachos is set, the context engine; the provider injects a system-prompt block telling the agent to use the nachos_memory_* tools and keep built-in memory disabled; opt-in semantic ranking either runs a separately installed nachos-embeddings CLI or sends the turn query plus memory titles/summaries to api.openai.com with OPENAI_API_KEY; all storage is local under $HERMES_HOME/nachos/.

entries.name: nagaai
entries.description: NagaAI as a Hermes model provider (`--provider nagaai`) over the OpenAI Responses API: one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, MiniMax and other models, paid from a prepaid NagaAI balance. The /model picker lists the chat models that accept tool calls on the Responses endpoint, read from the public GET /v1/models catalog, with a short built-in list when it is unreachable. Disclosure: registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, middleware, commands, background work or file access). Prompts, tool schemas and results go to https://api.naga.ac/v1 through Hermes' own client with NAGAAI_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself makes one request, GET https://api.naga.ac/v1/models without the key, and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: neocore
entries.description: One memory for every AI harness you use: your own Hermes conversations (CLI, desktop, and direct messages from the ids in `owners`) share the NeoCore memory that Claude Code and Codex use on the same machine (`neocore setup`), or your own NeoCore memory server (`neocore connect`). Before each turn, dated verbatim excerpts and facts are recalled with zero model calls (BM25 plus a local bge-small embedding model); on a machine with an NVIDIA graphics card or Apple silicon, NeoSift, NeoCore's own 32M relevance model, keeps only the ones that help. Groups and anyone else who messages the agent keep a separate memory per chat. In the owner's conversations the provider adds neocore_search, neocore_open, neocore_timeline, neocore_facts, neocore_profile and neocore_remember; elsewhere neocore_search and neocore_forget. Disclosure — the owner's turns are stored in ~/.neocore (or $NEOCORE_HOME), one memory shared by every Hermes profile on the machine, or sent to the memory server that machine was connected to; other chats are stored in $HERMES_HOME/neocore/memory.db. Text is stored after Hermes's and NeoCore's secret scrubbing. After the owner's turns, at most once every 5 minutes, a detached `neocore sync` process indexes the memory and, if that memory is set up with a background model (the one named in its config, else the first installed of the Hermes CLI, on the model and provider set up in Hermes, with no tools, rules or memory, one turn and a tool session kept out of session lists, then the Codex or Claude Code CLI; `neocore doctor` shows which, or none), sends recent turns to it to form dated facts and a short briefing, as NeoCore does for Claude Code and Codex; on such a machine it also reads Claude Code and Codex transcripts, as their own NeoCore hooks do. Recall itself never calls a model unless the optional hosted relevance filter was chosen at setup. With dense_recall on, the first start downloads bge-small-en-v1.5-onnx-Q (three files, about 65 MB) from huggingface.co/Qdrant, each refused unless its SHA-256 matches the hash pinned in neocore-memory. With neosift: auto (the default) and a graphics card, it installs NeoSift once in a background thread into ~/.neocore/sift: a Python venv with torch (download.pytorch.org) and transformers from PyPI within version bounds, about 2-3 GB, plus the pinned model (about 120 MB, SHA-256 checked) from the NeoCore GitHub release, switched on only if a speed check passes; it runs a local scoring server on 127.0.0.1:8796 that keeps nothing. shared: off keeps Hermes on a memory of its own; neosift: off disables NeoSift. No telemetry. Subagent, cron and flush contexts never write. Programs it starts (the detached sync, the Hermes, Codex or Claude Code CLI, the NeoSift server) get a minimal environment without Hermes's provider keys (the Hermes CLI reads its own); only a key the NeoCore config itself names is passed.

entries.name: nerdit
entries.description: Hermes puts what it builds online on its own machine and keeps it alive. nerdit_ship deploys a folder to the local Nerdit engine (open source, Docker), waits until it is healthy and returns its URL, with the engine's diagnosis on failure. nerdit_share gives an app a hosted https URL, private by default and public only after the user confirms. A pre_llm_call hook tells the agent when one of its apps is failed, degraded or restarting, once per outage and with no model polling; /apps answers with the status of every app without a model call; the nerdit:watch automation blueprint checks the apps on a schedule, restarts what a restart fixes and reports. Two bundled skills (ship, rescue). Disclosure — requires the Nerdit engine and Docker on the same machine. Each call starts the engine's own `nerdit mcp` process over stdio (fixed argv, no shell; the outage check at most once a minute) with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONTEXT, NERDIT_*; none of Hermes's provider keys) and acts with the rights of the user's nerdit CLI token, an admin token unless the user scopes it; the plugin never reads or stores that token. The engine zips and builds the folder the agent names. nerdit_call reaches every engine tool by name; only read tools and restart_service run directly, and every other engine tool, plus public sharing, goes to the human approval prompt. A pre_llm_call hook adds app status and a pointer to nerdit_ship to the agent's context. The plugin makes no network call and has no telemetry; sharing an app outside the machine goes through the optional Nerdit Cloud account.

entries.name: nerve
entries.description: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system for Hermes Agent with provider-neutral Jev, Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and Liquid D1 Reflex backends, evidence-backed Kanban supervision, context governance, token-budget trajectory control, and durable SSH workers. Disclosure — the default Reflex backend is hosted Jev; with the default settings (enabled / admission_enabled on) each turn's user prompt (up to 12k characters) and redacted tool/result previews are sent to the configured Jev provider (OpenRouter Decisions / TypeSafe Jev) using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY, spending your credits on every turn. Laya, OpenJev, SystemOne, and D1 can be configured as local/self-hosted backends. The Operator/Lean/Marie Kondo/Fat Cat presets (Operator is what `nerve setup` / the control panel picks for new homes) rewrite each outgoing model request to trim deferred tool schemas and skill descriptions to the current task, which can change the prompt-cache prefix between turns. The operator-only `nerve ui` control panel (127.0.0.1, per-run token) can replace the installed Nerve plugin with a local source checkout and run `hermes plugins validate/enable`, and, after an explicit confirmation, can create a Python venv under HERMES_HOME, pip-install Laya or PyTorch/transformers from PyPI, download model weights, and start a long-running localhost model server (D1 runs Hugging Face `trust_remote_code` model code). The operator-only nerve setup CLI can copy a local HermesContextBus checkout into HERMES_HOME/plugins/hermes-context-bus and runs hermes plugins enable/disable for that plugin when a profile is saved; the model cannot trigger any of this.

entries.name: netease-cloud
entries.description: NetEase Cloud Music (网易云音乐) mini player in the Hermes Desktop status bar, in the spirit of the built-in Radio plugin: a compact themed popover with Now Playing (cover + scrolling synced lyrics with the current line highlighted), search for songs and playlists, daily picks / recommended playlists / Personal FM, favorites (heart / Liked Music), browsing and in-panel playback of your own playlists, play/pause/skip/progress/volume with outline-style controls, loop modes (list loop, single loop, shuffle), plus a mini control cluster on the status bar itself with a like/unlike heart, prev/next transport, a live audio-spectrum dot visualiser driven by the Web Audio analyser, and a vinyl-record Now-Playing visual whose articulated tonearm drops on the record while playing and parks off it when paused (v0.5.0). Also offers phone-number + SMS verification-code sign-in as a second login method. Desktop-only UI (desktop/plugin.js on the plugin SDK surface) plus a local FastAPI backend (dashboard/plugin_api.py) that implements NetEase's weapi/eapi request signing (AES-CBC/ECB + RSA) with the Python standard library only — no build step, no extra Python dependencies. Disclosure — unofficial NetEase Cloud Music client: the backend calls only NetEase hosts (music.163.com, interface3.music.163.com, and the p*.music.163.com CDNs for covers and audio) using NetEase's own web/PC client identity (Chrome User-Agent, music.163.com Referer/Origin, eapi os=pc/appver headers, x-os/x-login-chain-id QR-login headers with a locally generated anonymous browser-style cookie set; SMS verification-code login calls NetEase web endpoints /api/sms/captcha/sent and /api/w/login/cellphone with the phone number you type); after you log in, your NetEase session cookie (MUSIC_U) is stored in the plugin's own data/cookie.json and sent only to NetEase hosts, and 'Log out' deletes it; while logged in it reports each played track to NetEase (feedback/webenergy play history) and the heart button likes/unlikes songs on your account; no other third-party services and no telemetry; QR and SMS sign-in may be blocked by NetEase risk control (the panel then surfaces a one-click button to NetEase's official account-verification page); pasting the MUSIC_U cookie remains the documented fallback; VIP songs stream through your own VIP session.
entries.title: NetEase Cloud Music
known_issues: QR and SMS sign-in can be blocked by NetEase risk control (「检测到当前设备环境异常」/「安全风险」); the panel then shows an 打开验证页面 button for NetEase's official unblock page, or paste the MUSIC_U cookie on the 账号 tab instead (README has a 3-step Chinese guide).
Playlists load the first 1000 tracks; the panel shows the real total (e.g. 共1859首·显示前1000).
Audio quality follows your NetEase account (VIP → higher bitrate); the plugin requests exhigh and falls back to standard.

entries.name: netplane
entries.description: Install, configure and operate a self-hosted Headscale control plane from Hermes. netplane_setup previews a configuration and, after approval, installs the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB on a fresh Debian 12+ or Ubuntu 22.04+ systemd host (amd64/arm64). Installation runs on the Hermes host, requires root or noninteractive sudo, refuses existing deployments, and verifies the package SHA-256. It configures SQLite, MagicDNS, embedded DERP/STUN, local admin gRPC, and either Let's Encrypt HTTPS or a loopback backend for an existing reverse proxy. It starts the system service, creates the first user, and saves a 90-day API key and connection settings through Hermes's active-profile APIs. netplane_status reports health, netplane_nodes lists devices, and netplane_preauth lists metadata without stored join secrets or creates an approval-gated, single-use-by-default join key with a 1–168 hour lifetime. Desktop includes setup preview/confirmation, health, nodes, join keys and confirmed node expiration, with a FastAPI backend. Management requires NETPLANE_APIKEY; setup works before a key exists. Bundled protobuf stubs use pinned sources and a compatible toolchain. Disclosure — the netplane_setup tool (after Hermes approval) and the Desktop pane (after confirmation) install the pinned official Headscale v0.29.6 DEB as root through noninteractive sudo on the Hermes host, downloading it from GitHub (SHA-256 verified) and possibly contacting configured APT repositories; it writes /etc/headscale, /var/lib/headscale and a systemd drop-in, and enables a persistent headscale service that in Let's Encrypt mode listens publicly on TCP 80/443 and UDP 3478 (admin gRPC and metrics stay on loopback); Let's Encrypt receives the chosen domain and email; setup saves a new 90-day Headscale API key as NETPLANE_APIKEY in the active Hermes profile; management reads credentials only from Hermes and uses TLS with system trust off-host; approved join-key creation returns the key into the chat; status runs systemctl is-active headscale and tailscale serve status; no telemetry and no automatic software updates.

entries.name: network-xray
entries.description: Compare DNS, TCP, verified TLS and HTTP HEAD captures of one URL from two machines, find the first observed difference and export a local evidence report. Read-only and local-first, with native agent tools, a Desktop workbench and a stdlib-only portable collector for the second machine. Disclosure — the network_xray_probe tool, the CLI and the Desktop page connect from the Hermes machine to a URL the model or user names, including private and loopback addresses (link-local, multicast and unspecified are refused): DNS, TCP, verified TLS and one HTTP HEAD request, with no query, credentials, redirects or body, run in an isolated Python child with a minimal environment; it saves the target, resolved IPs, certificate fingerprint and the server/content-type headers under the profile's plugin-data/network-xray/ folder, and imported bundles from a second machine are unauthenticated; no telemetry.

entries.name: neural-mesh
entries.description: Bi-temporal long-term memory for Hermes: point-in-time recall (mesh_asof answers what was true on a date, not only what is true now), supersession instead of overwrite so a corrected fact keeps its history, hybrid dense + lexical retrieval, a poisoning quarantine, an injection floor measured on a 15-family ablation, and a tamper-evident provenance ledger (mesh_verify, mesh_provenance) that names what its verdict rests on: which anchor file it was judged against, or plainly that it had none. Disclosure — this is a Hermes MemoryProvider (`memory.provider: neural-mesh`). It stores user turns, pre-compression and session-end message extracts, and mirrored MEMORY.md/USER.md writes in an unencrypted local SQLite file at `<profile>/neural-mesh/mesh.db`, so credentials do not belong in it. The provider makes no network calls and needs no API key. The repo also vendors unused upstream modules with LLM/chain HTTP clients that the provider never calls. It ships no compiled binary (the Rust extension is not vendored, so retrieval runs the pure-Python path).
entries.title: NEURAL_MESH
known_issues: The memory store is plain, unencrypted SQLite inside the Hermes profile — anything it remembers is readable by anyone with filesystem access to that profile, so credentials do not belong in it.
The upstream Rust resonance extension is not shipped (catalog rule 17), so retrieval uses the pure-Python path; mesh_stats reports resonance_backend: python rather than rust.
Automatic context injection is held to a measured 0.25 score floor, so a weakly-matching memory is deliberately not injected. Use mesh_recall (0.05 floor) when you want a wider net.

Tamper-evidence needs an anchor outside the store. Out of the box the ledger anchor lives in the same SQLite file, so an attacker who can write that file can delete the anchor along with the entries it protects; pass mesh_verify an `anchors` path (or set NEURAL_MESH_ANCHORS) to a file outside the store to make a clean truncation detectable. Until then mesh_verify says so in its verdict rather than implying the stronger guarantee.

Superseding a memory that does not exist is reported in the tool reply rather than failing the write, so a correction naming a bad id is stored as a new fact — and the reply says so instead of silently leaving two contradictory values current.

entries.name: neuralmind
entries.description: Code memory on every Hermes turn, with no tool call. Before the model runs, the plugin looks the user's message up in a local NeuralMind index of the project and appends the matching files and symbols (with line numbers), the code linked to them in NeuralMind's synapse graph, and decisions recorded in commit trailers. A session's first turn also gets a recap of the previous session in that project. The plugin is a stdlib-only shim around the separately installed NeuralMind CLI: install NeuralMind 4.9 or later yourself (`pipx install neuralmind`, `uv tool install neuralmind` or `pip install neuralmind`) and run `neuralmind build` in the project; in any other directory it does nothing. Not a memory provider: it registers no `memory.provider` and runs beside whichever one is configured. Disclosure — runs `neuralmind _hook <action>` as a child process once per turn (twice on a session's first), once for each file a write_file or patch call wrote, and once for each read_file of a file inside the project; each call is stopped after NEURALMIND_HERMES_TIMEOUT seconds (default 8) and the turn goes ahead without its context. A session's first turn can leave a detached NeuralMind process running after the hook returns, which writes the project's graph cache or, on a large synapse store, runs the decay tick and memory export, then exits. NeuralMind runs read-only git queries in the project (rev-parse, ls-files, log, diff --name-only). Reads the project, and reads and writes its .neuralmind/ directory, including each session's prompts (secret-redacted and truncated) and the paths of the files it edited, for the recap. On a session's first turn it copies .neuralmind/SYNAPSE_MEMORY.md into Claude Code's memory directory for the project (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/) when that directory already exists. The added context is part of the user message, so it is sent to the model provider with that turn and stays in the session history. The plugin makes no network requests and NeuralMind sends no telemetry; NeuralMind downloads its embedding model once when it has no cached copy, normally during `neuralmind build` (ChromaDB's all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX archive from chroma-onnx-models.s3.amazonaws.com, SHA-256-checked, cached in ~/.cache/neuralmind/). Subagent and cron turns are skipped. MIT.
entries.title: NeuralMind
known_issues: Needs NeuralMind installed separately (`pipx install neuralmind` or `uv tool install neuralmind`) and the project built with `neuralmind build`. Without both, the plugin loads and adds nothing.

Installed from the catalog, the plugin runs the `neuralmind` command on Hermes's PATH. If that PATH doesn't include it (a gateway run as a service, Hermes Desktop) or finds an older NeuralMind, run `neuralmind install-hermes-plugin` once: on a plugin Hermes installed, it only records the interpreter in the plugin's config.json and leaves the code alone.

entries.name: neuralwatt-provider
entries.description: Neuralwatt as a Hermes model provider (`provider: neuralwatt`). The /model picker lists Neuralwatt's live catalog with real context windows, and Hermes's reasoning setting is sent as `reasoning_effort`. Each turn gets a cost estimate from Neuralwatt's published energy figures, and /usage shows credits, daily free energy, this month's spend and 30 days of energy and carbon. Works alongside the `neuralwatt` tools plugin. Not affiliated with Neuralwatt. Disclosure: registers one model provider and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat goes through Hermes's own client to https://api.neuralwatt.com/v1 (or NEURALWATT_BASE_URL) with NEURALWATT_API_KEY, read through Hermes's secret scope. The plugin itself sends GET requests to that API's /models, /quota and /usage/energy, and to Neuralwatt's public energy price table at portal.neuralwatt.com. It sends the Hermes session id as `metadata.conversation_id`, which Neuralwatt stores as a hash. It writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: neuron-steer
entries.description: Neuron steering for Hermes Agent, implementing Nous Research's own Contrastive Neuron Attribution (arXiv:2605.12290). Find the sparse MLP neurons that distinguish two behaviors with forward passes only, save them as named circuits, then scale or ablate those neurons at inference to steer a local model, plus a dose scan that maps where the behavior turns on before output quality breaks. Disclosure — loads local Hugging Face models with torch on this machine; when a tool call sets allow_download (the model can set it) or NEURON_STEER_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD=1, it downloads the named model from huggingface.co, which can be several GB.

entries.name: nextcloud-talk-platform
entries.description: Nextcloud Talk platform adapter for Hermes Agent, in two modes behind one plugin: a webhook bot (Nextcloud Talk Bot API, HMAC-SHA256 signed, with an explicit body-size cap and a nonce-replay cache ahead of payload parsing) and a real Nextcloud user account (app password, long-polling the Chat REST API, with federation-invite support, per-room mention/watch/free modes, and an agent-to-agent loop guard plus active-listening context for multi-agent rooms). Mode is picked automatically by which credential is configured. No extra SDKs -- aiohttp for bot mode, httpx for user mode, both already Hermes dependencies. Disclosure — Connects to your Nextcloud server either as a Talk bot (HMAC-verified webhook listener, 127.0.0.1:18797 by default) or as a real Nextcloud user with an app password (long-polls the Chat API and auto-accepts federation invites only from NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ALLOWED_INVITERS); in user mode, unanswered room messages from allowed senders (up to 40 per room by default) and, for rooms listed in NEXTCLOUD_TALK_ROOM_MODES or with room_rules_all_rooms on, the room description are added to the agent's next turn in that room.

entries.name: nexus
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Hermes and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Shared rooms are handled by observation, not by chat type: a room turns shared as soon as a human other than the owner has written in it, bots never count, and recall, the tools and the graph then serve public memories only. A memory whose text sat in a legacy `text` field still reaches the injected block (the block falls back from `content`), and a short state fact marked by the write gate (a version, a count, an amount) needs 12 characters instead of 40, so "Hermes version: 0.23.1" is no longer filtered out. The write gate recognises state values: a long text stores unchanged but comes back with a hint to keep the value as its own short fact, no second write, no automatic extraction. The owner is identified per platform through owner_user_ids. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Hermes config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to Hermes's own default model through local Ollama; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS_EMBED_IN_HOST=1), the plugin starts `nexus-memory serve` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon that sends memory text to the Ollama endpoint at 127.0.0.1:11434 or NEXUS_OLLAMA_BASE under the model named by NEXUS_CONSOLIDATION_MODEL, nexus-memory.consolidation_model or Hermes's model.default, which can be an Ollama cloud model), and the service keeps running after Hermes exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Hermes config.yaml, and the opt-in recall reranker (nexus-memory.rerank or NEXUS_RERANK=1) defaults to sending each query plus up to 20 memory snippets to that same endpoint using the provider API key it reads from config.yaml; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml, and opens Hermes's state.db read-only for the session's chat type when the host reports no message author; the shared-room rule records the owner id in <hermes_home>/nexus/config.json (taken from the first gateway user when owner_user_ids is unset) and shared chat ids with a hashed author id in <hermes_home>/nexus/chat-sharing.json; a keyword (SQLite FTS5) copy of memory text and metadata, private memories included, in <hermes_home>/state/nexus-fts.db (or NEXUS_FTS_DB); state, daily backups, a write log without private content and the plugin's own service key (agent_keys/hermes.key, 0600, obtained once from the local service's loopback-only /enroll) under ~/.nexus-memory; the per-turn recall block holds at most three entries and leaves out `session` and `entity` hits. Every recall writes one line to ~/.nexus-memory/logs/read-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (timestamp, agent, hit count, memory ids, a hash of the query, never the query or memory text; rotated after 90 days, and a failed log never fails a recall). The write gate recognises dictated residue (filler words, word repeats, no closing punctuation) by five weighted signals and stores it as `session` instead of `rule`, word for word; a rule confirmed at a terminal is left alone; opt-in NEXUS_UPDATE_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt. At session end the plugin reports that session's failed tool calls (tool name, up to 2,000 characters of error text each, at most 50, and the session id; never the conversation) to the Nexus service's POST /events at 127.0.0.1:9122 or NEXUS_SERVICE_URL with its service key, where they are journaled in ~/.nexus-memory/events and the nightly learning may turn a failure that recurs across sessions into a stored lesson; NEXUS_REPORT_INCIDENTS=0 turns this off.

entries.name: ngrok-ai-gateway
entries.description: The ngrok AI Gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider ngrok`, or ngrok AI Gateway in `hermes model`): one access key for all your model providers, with failover. The model list comes live from your gateway, and gateway errors (unrouted model, access-policy and upstream-key failures, out of credit) map onto Hermes' fallback instead of a generic error. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests and the model list go to https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1 (or NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with NGROK_AI_GATEWAY_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: night-shift
entries.description: An on-call engineer that never sleeps. Alerts trigger a read-only investigation, a human approves the fix with one tap in Slack, and Night Shift runs it, proves recovery, and writes the runbook as a skill so the next incident is recognised. Disclosure — runs read-only shell diagnostics during an incident, and after a listed human approves it runs the approved commands through the terminal tool without a second Hermes prompt (optionally over the configured ssh prefix). Destructive commands are refused at proposal time. Sends container logs, status and database activity to the model provider. Calls Prometheus at the configured URL and Slack through the user's Hermes Slack app. Writes runbook skills through skill_manage and keeps incident state in plugin state. No telemetry, stores no credentials.
entries.title: Night Shift
known_issues: Diagnostics assume Docker. docker_host_prefix, deploy_history_command and db_check_command cover other setups, but only local Docker has been tested end to end.

Slack buttons need plugins.isolation: in_process (the default), because they use native Slack handlers. /nightshift approve (two steps: it shows the exact commands, then runs them on a confirm code) works in either mode.

entries.name: nightshift
entries.description: Hermes takes the night shift on your ML training runs: Nightshift watches a run's metrics (stdout, JSONL, CSV or TensorBoard), catches NaN, loss spikes, divergence, out-of-memory crashes and stalls, recovers the run within a playbook you approved (roll back to the last healthy checkpoint with a lower learning rate, or restart with half the batch), and pushes the chart to your phone. Desktop pane, dashboard tab, /nightshift, hermes nightshift and a morning-report blueprint. Zero runtime dependencies. Disclosure — the agent can only propose a training run; after your explicit approval (/nightshift approve in chat or the Approve button; there is no CLI approve) it launches the approved command as a long-running background process from a background thread that starts with Hermes, with a minimal environment (no Hermes keys unless you name them in env_passthrough, shown on the approval card), and may stop or restart that process group, re-rendering only the approved command with the playbook's parameters (lr, batch size, grad accumulation, checkpoint path) within an intervention budget; it signals only process groups it started (start-time checked, never a run it cannot verify), reads the log, metric and checkpoint paths you or the agent give it, runs nvidia-smi and ps, stores run data in its plugin data folder and alert charts in Hermes's image cache, makes capped LLM calls on your configured model with a redacted log tail on critical incidents, and sends alerts through Hermes's own `hermes send` to your messaging platform; no network calls of its own.

entries.name: nine-balance-widget
entries.description: Nine AI provider balances in one desktop widget — live balance/usage and quota reads, token-based spend estimates with off-peak price windows, drop alerts, and an anime mascot per provider with rotating flavour lines (DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok). Fully English UI. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Keys are entered in the widget's settings page and stored in plugin-scoped storage; the widget only calls those providers' official APIs. Ported from MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget (MIT). Disclosure — API keys you enter in the widget's settings are stored in plaintext in Desktop plugin storage (not Hermes' secret store); while the widget is on, the Desktop renderer polls the balance/usage endpoint of the provider matching your current model every 60 s with that provider's key (api.deepseek.com, api.minimaxi.com / api.minimax.io, open.bigmodel.cn / api.z.ai, api.moonshot.cn / api.moonshot.ai, api.kimi.com, token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com, api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com with the key in the URL, api.x.ai); each key goes only to its own provider; draws a floating widget over the app window.

entries.name: ninsei
entries.description: Rooms where you and your Hermes agent hang out with other people and their agents. Play games the agents host, build small web toys together and message friends privately. No server: rooms run on free public Nostr relays. Disclosure — Rooms, reactions, edits, room details, shared toys, your interest card, picture, portrait and face are signed and posted to public Nostr relays (nos.lol, relay.primal.net, nostr.mom, relay.snort.social, relay.damus.io by default), which may keep them forever; private messages are NIP-17 encrypted but relays see your key, timing and IP. Your room agent is a separate tool-less model call (no Hermes memory or tools) that strangers in a room can trigger against your daily token budget; its personality can be imported from any local Hermes profile's SOUL.md when you choose to, and whatever you keep there can surface in its public replies. The "Your Hermes" private line is a local gateway platform registered with trusted_inbound=True that switches itself on once Ninsei has data in the profile: it reaches your full Hermes agent (tools, memory) from rows in Ninsei's 0600 SQLite file, so any program running as your user that writes that file is treated as you (turn it off with gateway.platforms.ninsei.enabled: false). Five observe-only hooks run in every chat and record only step counts for toy builds you accepted. Stores two Nostr keypairs and decrypted private messages unencrypted in that SQLite file.
entries.title: Ninsei
known_issues: Rooms are public: messages, reactions, edits, room details, shared toys, your interest card, your picture, portrait and face are signed and posted to public Nostr relays, which may keep them forever.
Editing or deleting a message doesn't erase it. The earlier text stays on relays, and a delete is a request that relays and other apps may ignore.

Private messages hide their text, but relays see your key, when messages arrive and your IP address, so they may guess who your friends are. As of 2026-11-07, relay.damus.io accepts private messages but won't hand them out, so they arrive through the other relays.

A room code or invite can name up to three relays. Ninsei lists the ones you don't use and connects to them only after you press Add and look again; connecting to a relay shows it your IP address. Invites come from friends only and carry a room id and relays, never text.

A shared toy can't fetch from the web, but it can open a WebRTC connection, which no browser policy blocks today, and that reveals your IP address and can carry data out. It can also open a web page inside its own frame, which can see your IP address too. Ninsei closes a toy that does this in the usual ways, though one built to beat the check can still show a page. Toys run only after you press Run.
A stranger's text can still get an agent to say something wrong in a room under its owner's name. It can't make the agent act, because room agents have no tools.
In the browser Webapp, Ninsei's Desktop switch starts off: turn it on in Capabilities, Plugins, Ninsei. On iPhone with Hermes 0.23.0 that page crashes in Safari (Hermes issue #148538).

Stores two Nostr keypairs, decrypted private messages, the friend list and other people's pictures unencrypted in an owner-only (0600) SQLite file in the plugin data folder. Uses your configured model up to the daily budget you set.

Registers a local gateway platform with trusted_inbound=True (its only sender is the Ninsei page, through the plugin's own SQLite file), which turns itself on once Ninsei has data in the profile. Five observe-only hooks (they return None) run in every Hermes chat and store nothing from other chats. Full list in the README.

entries.name: no-cap
entries.description: Receipts for agent claims. No Cap checks the claims in each final reply (tests pass, pushed, merged, deployed, file written, URL live, SHAs, counts; English plus Chinese, Thai and Spanish for tests, push, merge and deploy) against the tool calls the agent made, with no extra model, and appends a footer: 🧾 NO CAP when a tool call proves the claim, 🧢 CAP only when one directly contradicts it (exit code, test counts, push ref, PR state, or a claimed SHA or branch that does not exist in the session's repo), and an opt-in 🤔 NO RECEIPT. A claim about earlier work can cite an earlier turn of the same session. A green run after the agent changed the suite in that turn (deleted, moved, skipped or deselected tests, a conftest or runner-config filter, PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-k) no longer earns 🧾 for "all tests pass": it gets a visible 🤔 naming the change, and 🧢 only when an earlier run named the removed test as failing and the reply doesn't say so. /cap makes the agent prove or retract its open claims and re-scores the next reply; /capscore keeps a per-model honesty board, a scorecard and an A/B compare card; /nocap verdict draws a session verdict card; strict mode uses pre_verify to send a coding turn back, at most twice. Surfaces: a Cap Board dashboard tab (agents, models and skills ranked live; this profile only unless you opt in to a team view), Hermes Desktop receipt chips and a Receipts popover, opt-in Discord embed + buttons, and Cap Coach, which drafts a rule from repeated caps and injects it only after you approve it. Opt-in Obsidian lessons (0.3.0): each 🧢 becomes a redacted line in that agent's note in your vault and, once per agent and pattern, a mistakes-board note (Agent Black Box format); with obsidian_learn the agent's own repeated cap patterns come back as built-in rules at the start of its turns. entries.name: no-manual
entries.description: Furniture with no instructions? Send photos and Hermes finds the official manual, turns your disassembly photos into a manual in reverse, or works out flat-pack assembly (closets, bookcases, cabinets) from the parts, then coaches you step by step and checks a photo of each step. Steps arrive as images in chat; Hermes Desktop shows an interactive 3D step viewer. Never generates instructions for children's furniture or anything people sit, sleep or climb on. Disclosure — photos you add are sent to your own configured model provider through Hermes (ctx.llm) to read panels, labels and step photos; image and PDF paths the model passes are read from anywhere on disk (images and PDFs only) and copied into the plugin's folder, and `recent` mode picks up images from Hermes's shared inbound image cache (<HERMES_HOME>/cache/images, cache/documents/native-inputs) from the last 30 minutes, which on a multi-user gateway can include another chat's upload; manual PDFs found by Hermes's web search are downloaded over https (max 30 MB, public hosts only); photos, manual pages and generated images are stored in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/no-manual/ and deleted with /nomanual delete; the Desktop half bundles three.js (source in desktop/src/); no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no credentials stored.

entries.name: nomads-planner
entries.description: Nomads.com for Hermes: read your own trips and favorite cities, look up curated city and country facts (monthly costs, rent, internet speed, weather, safety and other 0-5 scores), list upcoming in-person meetups, and build a next-stay brief in one call that joins your current and upcoming stays, unplanned gaps, city facts, meetups inside each stay's dates and your past visits, with deterministic comparisons (cheapest, fastest internet, safest). Native plugin: 7 read-only tools, a /nomads slash command and a bundled planning skill. City, country and meetup tools work without an account; trips and favorites need a free personal key from https://nomads.com/settings, read through Hermes' secret scope. Disclosure — makes HTTPS GET requests to https://nomads.com/api only (sending your username and personal key in the Authorization header for trips and favorites); no writes, no other hosts, no files read, no background processes, no telemetry; public city data is cached in memory for 10 minutes. Not affiliated with Nomads.com.

entries.name: nostr-vpn
entries.description: Private mesh networking through the separately installed nvpn CLI. Instruction-only skill; connects to relays and peers and starts a persistent daemon. Tunnels need elevated host networking privileges. Disclosure — instruction-only skill: the agent runs the separately installed nvpn CLI in the terminal (installed by the user, or by the agent from the project's latest GitHub release or an unpinned `cargo install nvpn`), which creates local device keys, connects to Nostr relays and peers, starts a persistent daemon that with elevated privileges creates tunnel interfaces and routes, and on an admin host can approve devices into the user's private network.

entries.description: Nostr platform adapter for Hermes, backed by the local Hermes Nostr Gateway daemon: NIP-17 and NIP-04 DMs, kind-1 mentions and feeds, Concord channels and Marmot groups arrive as one message stream, with reach and authority decided by the gateway's policy. entries.name: ntfy-approval
entries.description: Answer Hermes' approval prompts from your phone: once selected with security.approval.transport: ntfy, each dangerous-command prompt arrives as an ntfy push notification with Approve once, Approve for session and Deny buttons, and no answer still means deny. Disclosure — once selected, anyone who can read the ntfy topic can approve dangerous commands (the one-time answer codes are in the notification), so on the public ntfy.sh default the topic name is the only secret and NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN is optional; each pending approval publishes Hermes' reason, the redacted command (unless send_command is false), the non-default profile name and one-time answer codes to the configured ntfy server, then reads <topic>-reply and deletes the notification; any failure or timeout is a deny; reads NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC/NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN from the profile .env, never puts the token in a notification, follows no redirects, writes no files and starts no processes.

entries.name: numogram
entries.description: Hermes debugs ESP32 firmware on real hardware. It watches the board's serial port, maps crash addresses to source lines from the ELF, fixes the code, builds with idf.py and flashes with esptool, then reads the log to confirm the fix. A crash wakes the session on its own. Also checks firmware GPIO use against a KiCad netlist (swapped signals, strapping, flash and USB pins) and audits chip security read-only. NUMOGRAM_PORT=virtual runs an emulated ESP32-C3 in Espressif's QEMU, so it works without a board. Disclosure — board_build and board_flash go through Hermes's approval prompt (a pre_tool_call hook, one approval rule per tool) and are blocked when nobody can answer; a build runs ESP-IDF's export.sh, idf.py and the project's own CMake and Python scripts and writes the build directory it is given. Runs esptool, espefuse summary (read-only; the plugin has no eFuse write) and, for the virtual board only, Espressif's qemu-system-riscv32 with networking off, always with fixed argument lists, and each child gets an environment allowlist (PATH, HOME, locale, ESP-IDF variables), never Hermes's keys or tokens. Background: a serial watcher thread while watching is on, and a QEMU process for the virtual board that stops when Hermes exits. Network: none beyond loopback (unauthenticated) to its own macOS USB bridge or virtual board, or the socket:// address set in NUMOGRAM_PORT. Reads the project, build, ELF and netlist paths it is given; writes its own state only under the active Hermes profile's home (get_hermes_home() / numogram). Serial output is passed to the model as untrusted data; wake-up messages are built from fixed text and validated hex. The bridge and virtual board drop eFuse write commands. No credentials, no telemetry.
entries.title: numogram: Hermes debugs your ESP32
known_issues: One board at a time. Building and flashing need an ESP-IDF project; board_build needs ESP-IDF where Hermes runs.

Tested end to end on an ESP32-P4 over USB-Serial/JTAG and on the emulated ESP32-C3. Other chips use the same paths but are untested on hardware; crash parsing on Xtensa chips (ESP32, S2, S3) is untested.
The macOS bridge supports boards on the chip's own USB-Serial/JTAG port, not boards behind a USB-UART bridge chip.
The virtual board needs Espressif's qemu-system-riscv32 (idf_tools.py install qemu-riscv32).

entries.name: nurse
entries.description: Supervisor-aware service management for a Hermes host. Reads pm2 and systemd into one table, triages a failing service's own logs into a ranked diagnosis (OOM via SIGKILL/exit 137, port already in use, missing env var, crash loop measured as restarts per hour rather than uptime, bad exit code, dependency unreachable), and repairs it through one guarded surface. Disclosure — service_repair changes supervisor state: it restarts, starts, stops, reloads or resets a named pm2 process, or restarts, starts, stops or reset-fails a systemd user unit, behind an allowlist of verbs, a confirm plan-then-act step, a persisted per-service cooldown ledger, a refusal to restart a service already crash-looping, and a pre_tool_call hook that escalates every state-changing call to Hermes' own human-approval prompt. It shells out to `pm2` and `systemctl`/`journalctl` as the invoking user, so it can only act on services that user already controls; it reads their log files (including pm2's rotated siblings) and writes a small JSON snapshot and cooldown ledger under plugin-data/nurse. No network I/O, no credentials, no elevated privileges.

entries.name: nvidia-switchyard
entries.description: Automatic inference routing between local and cloud models, escalating tasks only when needed. With Verification-Gated Routing (VGR), each turn is tried on the local model, checked, and escalated to the cloud model only when the check fails. Either model can be any URL or a third-party model provider set up in Hermes; each provider's terms and conditions apply. Presets are selectable as switchyard/<preset> models, with a Desktop page and dashboard tab showing each decision live. Disclosure — installs nemo-switchyard from PyPI; runs a loopback sidecar on 127.0.0.1:4110 that keeps running after Hermes quits (`hermes switchyard stop`), and Open in browser starts Hermes's web dashboard; reads every model request and response to route it, and adds to each tier's system prompt the model-specific guidance Hermes gives that tier's model; for a provider tier it takes that provider's credential (sign-in tokens included) from Hermes on each call and sends it only to that provider; stores a generated sidecar token and any tier API keys in Hermes's .env through Hermes's config API; setup makes switchyard/<preset> the default model and sends titles and smart approvals to the local model; copies its provider profile to <HERMES_HOME>/plugins/model-providers/switchyard/ on load; logs and routing records stay in <HERMES_HOME>/switchyard/; after removal it restores the replaced models, stops its sidecar and deletes its provider copy; it never rewrites saved conversations. No telemetry.

entries.name: nyx-wiki-recall
entries.description: Attach short wiki glimpses chosen by a decision model, and write a daily Markdown transcript of every turn. A local Markdown wiki (starter layout shipped) is scored per message through OpenRouter's Decisions API; matching glimpses are injected before the model answers, and wiki_read opens the full article. Transcripts are written by the plugin itself into HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/nyx-wiki-recall/ with no extra setup (transcript = yes and finalize = yes are the shipped values). Each day runs from finalize.after to finalize.after (default 02:00). Scheduled (cron) jobs are recorded under a Scheduled job heading; only subagent turns are skipped by default. A day is finished at finalize.after the next morning. The files are what a wiki is built from. Ships Clotho's wiki-archivist skill. Default provider=no runs as a hook beside any memory provider; provider=yes can serve as Hermes's memory provider when memory.provider also says so. Disclosure — for each message that passes the skip rules (not empty, not a slash command; cron turns skipped by default), HTTPS POSTs go to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (decisions.url, default that URL; model typesafe/jev-1.13) with OPENROUTER_API_KEY (via agent.secret_scope.get_secret), carrying the recent conversation (context.turns, default 2) trimmed to message.chars (default 20,000 characters) and the titles, paths and glimpses of the wiki folders and pages being asked about (up to three requests per message, within budget.seconds); nothing else is sent anywhere and there is no telemetry. Reads the wiki folder (wiki_path), Hermes config read-only, and the gateway-bound HERMES_SESSION_* values via gateway.session_context.get_session_env; in memory-provider mode only, also opens HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only for the last 40 messages of the current session. Writes a journal and daily Markdown transcript of every turn (user messages, replies and short tool-call summaries such as terminal commands and file paths, after pattern-based secret redaction, with default file permissions) only under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/nyx-wiki-recall/ (or transcript.folder), plus suggestions, finalized.json and lock files. Deletes nothing by default; with keep.days > 0, only its own finished journal/ and suggestions/ day files. Runs one day-finishing background thread per Hermes process and one short-lived transcript thread after each reply; runs no shell commands and stores no credentials.
entries.title: NyxWikiRecall
known_issues: Install with `hermes plugins install blacksmithFF/NyxWikiRecall --no-enable` then `hermes plugins enable nyx-wiki-recall`. Hermes 0.22.5 `plugins install --enable` (or answering yes) sets memory.provider and skips plugins.enabled for plugins that register a memory provider, so the transcript and glimpse hooks never run. If that already happened, enable the plugin and set memory.provider back.

`hermes plugins validate` warns once on a private core import of gateway.session_context.get_session_env (transcript.py). That is the documented session-identity reader in Hermes 0.22.5's plugin guide; the import is wrapped and falls back to transcript.user.name if it goes away.

Cron turns get no wiki lookup by default (lookups.on_cron = no). Transcripts record scheduled (cron) jobs under a Scheduled job heading, and skip only subagent turns by default (transcript.skip.platforms = subagent).

Disclosure — for each message that passes the skip rules (not empty, not a slash command; cron turns skipped by default), HTTPS POSTs go to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (decisions.url, default that URL; model typesafe/jev-1.13) with OPENROUTER_API_KEY (via agent.secret_scope.get_secret), carrying the recent conversation (context.turns, default 2) trimmed to message.chars (default 20,000 characters) and the titles, paths and glimpses of the wiki folders and pages being asked about (up to three requests per message, within budget.seconds); nothing else is sent anywhere and there is no telemetry. Reads the wiki folder (wiki_path), Hermes config read-only, and the gateway-bound HERMES_SESSION_* values via gateway.session_context.get_session_env; in memory-provider mode only, also opens HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only for the last 40 messages of the current session. Writes a journal and daily Markdown transcript of every turn (user messages, replies and short tool-call summaries such as terminal commands and file paths, after pattern-based secret redaction, with default file permissions) only under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/nyx-wiki-recall/ (or transcript.folder), plus suggestions, finalized.json and lock files. Deletes nothing by default; with keep.days > 0, only its own finished journal/ and suggestions/ day files. Runs one day-finishing background thread per Hermes process and one short-lived transcript thread after each reply; runs no shell commands and stores no credentials. This plugin registers tool(s): wiki_read; hook(s): pre_llm_call, post_llm_call; requires env var(s): OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5. Known issues: Install with `hermes plugins install blacksmithFF/NyxWikiRecall --no-enable` then `hermes plugins enable nyx-wiki-recall`. Hermes 0.22.5 `plugins install --enable` (or answering yes) sets memory.provider and skips plugins.enabled for plugins that register a memory provider, so the transcript and glimpse hooks never run. If that already happened, enable the plugin and set memory.provider back.; `hermes plugins validate` warns once on a private core import of gateway.session_context.get_session_env (transcript.py). That is the documented session-identity reader in Hermes 0.22.5's plugin guide; the import is wrapped and falls back to transcript.user.name if it goes away.; Cron turns get no wiki lookup by default (lookups.on_cron = no). Transcripts record scheduled (cron) jobs under a Scheduled job heading, and skip only subagent turns by default (transcript.skip.platforms = subagent)..

entries.name: nyx
entries.description: Nyx: local, single-user long-term memory with no LLM on the write path. Every turn is logged verbatim and indexed (SQLite FTS5, optional embeddings); on top of that log Nyx keeps bi-temporal facts (what is true now, and what you believed on a given day), source trust (tool, delegation and bot output never becomes a fact about you), two-stage forgetting with a restorable quarantine, and secrets filtering before anything is stored, with an optional encrypted vault that hands a pasted key back to its owner only after human approval. Disclosure — memory is stored locally in ~/.neurobase (configurable); no network calls by default. Opt-in only: a configured embedding API receives memory text and queries; l3_llm sends profile, scene and recent-decision snippets to DeepSeek or OpenRouter; LLM extraction sends the sentence being extracted to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you set (default 127.0.0.1). Keys are read through get_secret. The optional vault stores secrets encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a master key in ~/.config/nyx/vault.key, or optionally in the OS keychain under Nyx's own service name; revealing one asks for approval through Hermes and is refused under cron and subagents. Adds a hermes nyx CLI (vault, doctor, scrub, repair, status). A separate opt-in companion plugin shipped in the same package, nyx-reveal, registers one transform_llm_output hook.

entries.name: oathkeeper
entries.description: An owner's oath, enforced by the machine. The owner writes standing rules once in a plain oath file (standing missions briefed into every session, never delete or modify these surfaces, always require evidence such as a backup before touching those) and Oathkeeper enforces them deterministically on every tool call: never rules block with the violated oath line cited, always-require rules block until the prerequisite evidence exists in the same session, fingerprint snapshots of sworn surfaces detect changes made outside the gate and report them on the next turn, and the oath file itself can never be modified by the agent. Every verdict is written to an append-only local ledger. Disclosure: reads tool call arguments to extract intended file actions and reads files covered by oath patterns to fingerprint them; all state is stored locally under $HERMES_HOME/oathkeeper/; makes no network calls and calls no model.

entries.name: obol
entries.description: Safe invoicing for freelancers, consultants and agencies who bill clients, from any chat Hermes runs in (tested: Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, email and the terminal). Hermes drafts invoices (also from forwarded messages via ctx.llm), sends them as Stripe payment links or as bank-transfer PDF invoices with no provider account, tracks who has paid, and adds Invoices and Security dashboard views plus /invoices in every chat. Every invoice write needs approval, with deterministic checks for prompt injection (a message can never choose the recipient), lookalike and impersonated client addresses, duplicates, unusual amounts and changed payout details; live keys are refused unless allowed, writes are refused in unattended runs, and the activity and security logs are hash-chained. Disclosure — handles payments: in Stripe mode it calls api.stripe.com with your STRIPE_API_KEY (read through Hermes's secret route) and Stripe emails your clients when invoices are sent or reminded; live keys are refused unless you turn on allow_live, and in live mode the approval prompt warns that sending or reminding emails the real client; every invoice write asks for approval and writes are refused in cron runs; forwarded messages you ask it to draft from go to your configured model; bank-transfer mode makes no network calls and prints the bank details you enter in plugin settings (stored in config.yaml) on PDF invoices; data stays in plugin-data/obol/.

entries.name: obscurify-provider
entries.description: Obscurify.ai as a Hermes model provider (`--provider obscurify`, or Obscurify.ai in `hermes model`): a privacy-focused, OpenAI-compatible API to 200+ models with zero-data-retention routes and account-number sign-up (no email). The model list leaves out decision models and models under Hermes' 64K context minimum, context windows come from the catalog, and reasoning effort is sent as `reasoning_effort`. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads); chat requests go to https://obscurify.ai/v1 through Hermes' own client with OBSCURIFY_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself only fetches the public model catalog (GET https://obscurify.ai/v1/models, no credentials) at most once an hour per process, reads and writes no files and starts no processes. Usage is billed from the user's prepaid Obscurify.ai balance; the plugin makes no payments.

entries.name: offgrid
entries.description: Chat with your Hermes agent by plain SMS, with no mobile data, through Africa's Talking, plus a USSD menu as a fallback for basic phones. Texts become normal Hermes messages on the offgrid platform, one conversation per phone number, and replies come back as a single SMS (Markdown and emoji stripped, capped at five billed segments). A safe subset of gateway commands works by text: NEW, SESSIONS, RESUME <n>, MODEL, STATUS, HELP and /retry, /stop, /title; every other slash command is refused by default. Disclosure — every question and every reply is sent through Africa's Talking and the mobile network as SMS, in plain text, and each outbound SMS segment (up to five per reply) is billed to the operator's Africa's Talking account (incoming SMS and USSD sessions may also be billed). Requires an Africa's Talking API key, a callback secret and an explicit allowlist of phone numbers; the callback must be reachable over public HTTPS (the listener binds 127.0.0.1:8080 by default, so a tunnel or reverse proxy is needed). SMS sender numbers can be spoofed: a spoofed text from an allowlisted number gets a normal agent turn with this profile's tools and memory (the reply goes to the real number), while commands that change config, approve tools or reveal other sessions are blocked and dangerous commands time out unapproved. Verified in the Africa's Talking sandbox only, not on a live carrier. Uses its own platform name and OFFGRID_* settings, so it installs alongside ussd-platform.
entries.title: Offgrid
known_issues: Sandbox only: not yet tested on a live carrier or physical handset.
Questions are dispatched by one worker from an in-memory queue, so one slow answer delays others and a crash can lose queued questions.
Texts over the per-phone rate limit or over 500 characters are dropped without a reply.
An SMS user cannot answer a dangerous-command approval prompt; it times out and the action is blocked.

entries.name: office-3d
entries.description: A live isometric office for Hermes Desktop: every profile is a person at a desk — a profile doing real work sits typing with a lit terminal screen, an online-but-idle one relaxes in the lounge with tea, an offline one leaves an empty desk with a dark monitor. Click a desk to inspect that profile (state, sessions, tokens, cost) and open its chat or latest session; a cost/tokens leaderboard ranks the profiles; plus a global Total/Working/Idle/Offline overview, a status-bar chip, a palette command with keybind, a settings page with per-profile visibility switches, and an office_status agent tool that reports the same status to the model. Desks are labelled with each profile's own display name when set. Disclosure — the backend and the tool read each profile's gateway_state.json and profile.yaml (display name only) and open its state.db read-only, running aggregate queries (COUNT/SUM/MAX over the sessions table: counts, token totals, cost, last-activity) plus one read of the default profile's in-flight async_delegations task JSON, from which only the target profile label is kept; they never read message content, system prompts or titles, make no network calls, and need no credentials. Opening a profile's latest session asks the app's own session.list RPC for that session's id (metadata only) and then opens it through the app's own openSession; no message content is read. Runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. The process-liveness check never signals the target: on POSIX it uses os.kill(pid, 0), and on Windows it opens the process with OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) and reads GetExitCodeProcess.

Disclosure: reads any Office file the agent is pointed at but writes only inside folders the user puts on the Desk (backups and receipts live in the plugin's own data dir). xlsx_recalc runs the user's installed LibreOffice (soffice, headless) on a temporary copy. The Desk page reads the session store read-only to show a workstream's chat. No network calls, telemetry, credentials or background processes. Depends on the paper-docx, paper-pptx and paper-xlsx forks. They provide the docx, pptx and openpyxl import names, so they must not share an environment with python-docx, python-pptx or openpyxl. This plugin registers tool(s): office_desk, office_inspect, office_search, docx_tracked_edit, docx_comment, docx_redline_accept_reject, pptx_inspect_formats, pptx_edit_shape, pptx_compose_decks, pptx_diff, xlsx_edit, xlsx_recalc, xlsx_diff, office_receipt; hook(s): pre_llm_call, post_llm_call.

entries.name: offpeak-bekci
entries.description: Makes Ollama Cloud's off-peak window visible and actionable in Hermes: a desktop status-bar chip shows the countdown and the queue item counts (Ollama off-peak hours: weekdays 18:00-12:00 UTC, weekends one block), a one-shot notice fires 30 minutes before the window opens, and approval is taken only from the user (`/offpeak-onayla <id,id>`) — work runs only if approved, and items never enter the queue by themselves. `/offpeak-durum` prints a readable report by default (machine-readable JSON with `/offpeak-durum json`), and `/offpeak-kur` prints the cron job it would install in full plus a `plan_hash`; nothing is installed without a hash-bound approval typed by the user, and the plugin never writes the cron store. One `llm_execution` middleware measures the call rate for Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window and ships measure-only (`kuru_kosu: true`): it records what it would delay and never delays. No network calls, no telemetry, no credential reads; the only local files it touches are the queue ledger, its own JSONL measurement log, and a read-only look at the profile's cron/jobs.json. Output language is English by default; `dil: tr` selects Turkish. Auto-delivery is host-dependent: in a classic CLI session the request enters the agent queue; on the Ink TUI / desktop-panel host the core asks for a persistent `session_key`, which the command handler does not receive, so the command prints the parameters as a single line of JSON. Injecting into a gateway additionally requires `plugins.entries.offpeak-bekci.allow_gateway_injection: true` (default off); the only in-process way to read that key is the private `gateway.session_context` module (rule 9 -> not used). Requires Hermes >= 0.22.2. Disclosure — the llm_execution middleware can sleep Ollama Cloud calls during the peak window once `kuru_kosu: false` is set (default is measure-only); it writes a JSONL measurement log and, on `/offpeak-onayla`, rewrites the user's queue file; it reads the profile's cron/jobs.json read-only (on `/offpeak-durum`, `/offpeak-kaldir` and at every session end) to count enabled queue-consumer jobs; `/offpeak-kur` and `/offpeak-kaldir` leave cron install/removal requests in the session (or, with `allow_gateway_injection: true`, inject them into the gateway) for the agent's own cron tool to act on; no network calls, no credential reads, never writes the cron store.

entries.name: oh-my-pi-terminal-backend
entries.description: oh-my-pi (omp) terminal backend for Hermes Agent: Hermes's terminal, file and code tools run each task's commands through one long-lived `omp --mode rpc` session shell on this host, with lossless output transfer past omp's inline caps. Select with `terminal.backend: oh-my-pi-terminal-backend`. Disclosure — no Python dependencies and no network calls of its own (the spawned omp CLI may reach the model provider you configured for omp): it drives the `omp` CLI you install yourself, spawns one long-lived `omp --mode rpc` process per Hermes task on this host with Hermes' command approval left on, gives that process only a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, user, shell, terminal, locale and temp vars) plus any variable names you list in the plugin's `env_passthrough` setting, spools command output, a per-env config overlay and optional stdin through private temp files in your scratch directory, and keeps a private live-observation log of the last command's text and full output under your Hermes home's `omp-live/` (0700/0600).

entries.name: oikos
entries.description: Pixel habitat page for Hermes Desktop: each of your Hermes profiles becomes a resident with its own home and routines on a 9-district pixel-art map, and live gateway activity (turns, tool use, subagents, approval prompts) shows up as residents walking to stations. Desktop-only: desktop/plugin.js uses one route, a sidebar row, a palette command and a status-bar chip through the plugin SDK; no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, backend or credentials. Disclosure: reads the profile list through host.profiles.list() (or the profiles.list gateway RPC) and keeps each profile's name, display name and description; reads the gateway, profile, focusedSessionId, activeSessionId and busy state atoms (sessions are shown by the first 8 characters of their id, no session title is read); and from gateway events uses only the event type, session id, profile tag, tool name and subagent id/index, never tool arguments, previews, results, paths, commands, message or reasoning text. World state, text the user types in Oikos and short activity labels built from tool names are kept in the plugin's own ctx.storage only. Model use is off by default; if the user opts in on the Chronicle tab, it calls the gateway RPC llm.oneshot through host.request (task "oikos_mind", no session_id; model from auxiliary.oikos_mind, else Hermes's automatic choice, which may be paid) about every 3 minutes while its page is visible. Each request carries up to six residents' names, built-in or user-typed citizen personas (Hermes profile descriptions are replaced by a fixed placeholder), mood, needs, item ids, up to 3 notes the model itself wrote, and station ids, time and weather; chat, station tasks, typed memories, profile descriptions and all Hermes session content are never sent. Spend is limited by Oikos's own estimated counters (default 10 requests an hour, about 20,000 estimated tokens a day, a reload lease), which are not a billing cap enforced by Hermes or the provider. No direct third-party network requests, shell, telemetry or self-updater; optional model requests go through Hermes and its configured provider. The bundle embeds LimeZu pixel art (Modern Exteriors, Modern Interiors, Character Generator 2.0) as base64 PNG sheets, credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; the art is not under the MIT code licence.
entries.title: Oikos
known_issues: Desktop-only. After installing, make sure the Desktop switch on the Oikos row in Settings → Plugins is on.

The optional model mind is off by default and uses the gateway RPC llm.oneshot rather than the documented ctx.llm plugin route (Oikos has no Python half), so oikos_mind is not listed in the Models settings; it was tested only against a mock gateway, and any failure falls back to the deterministic scheduler.

entries.name: olympus
entries.description: Manage your Hermes agents from one dashboard tab: every agent (profile) on one list with its status, current task and tool, helpers and a week of runs; one Needs-you queue of questions waiting on your answer, failed or overdue cron jobs, stalled or failing Kanban workers, blocked or unassigned tasks, offline gateways and looping or expensive runs, each with its action; an inspector per agent; a Live view of every open run with its subagents and their last tool; a Floor with every agent at a fixed place, moving only on recorded tool calls; a Pop out window of the roster that stays on top; and a Performance view of run success, run time, tool failures and cost per agent, each compared with the days before, with the runs behind any day a click away. Controls (pause, resume or run a cron job; answer, retry, reclaim or reassign a Kanban task) are confirmed, logged and executed by Hermes' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off. Opt-in alerts run as a Hermes no-agent cron job. Disclosure — reads Hermes' own stores read-only across every profile under HERMES_HOME (sessions and messages in state.db, cron jobs, run output and the usage ledger, the Kanban database, gateway state, config.yaml and profile.yaml, skills, the agent/gateway/error log tails and subagent live transcripts under cache/delegation/live) and writes to plugin-data/olympus/, plus `$HERMES_HOME/scripts/olympus_alerts.py` when you run `hermes olympus install-alerts`; controls (on by default, each confirmed; `dashboard.olympus.controls: false` turns them off) pause, resume or run cron jobs and answer, retry, reclaim or reassign Kanban tasks through Hermes' own dashboard and Kanban endpoints; no network calls to third-party services, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials and no self-updater; never opens a profile's .env (configured gateways come from Hermes' own helper, a private import the validator warns on); local labels, task titles, questions and message previews stay hidden unless `dashboard.olympus.expose_local_labels: true`; the Desktop page uses the plugin SDK only.
entries.title: Olympus
known_issues: A Kanban worker that has finished can read as Working for up to ten minutes, because Hermes leaves the worker's session open after the task run ends.
While a worker runs, Now shows its task but not the tool it is using.
At 390 px the confirm popup for a control can overflow its row by a pixel.

entries.name: omh
entries.description: Oh My Hermes (OMH) bridge: routing hints and role context for OMH workflow skills, per-task delegation model routing, plan todos and a status tool, a Hermes Desktop status pane (off until enabled), bounded evidence probes that keep prepared work apart from observed results, and a file-backed memory provider, a dag-ulw run keeper (omh_dag) whose nodes the parent dispatches with Hermes' own delegate_task, a data-only search planner (omh_search, no retrieval), and language-server navigation tools (lsp_definition, lsp_references, lsp_diagnostics, lsp_rename) over Hermes' own LSP service. Disclosure — omh_delegate_route writes delegation.model/provider/reasoning_effort in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml and the session hooks restore them; omh_gather_evidence runs allowlisted checks (python -m unittest with reporting flags only, python -m compileall, git diff --check, omh doctor/probe/docs/release checks) via subprocess on the host, outside any sandboxed terminal backend and without Hermes' terminal approval, in the agent working directory or below it, so it runs whatever test code that directory holds; omh_team (only with the separate OMH core package installed, which the plugin imports from the directory OMH's own installer recorded) asks once through the Hermes approval prompt for an exact list of up to 8 check commands from an accepted plan, then runs them on the host as each helper returns; omh_jev_ask posts model-supplied state and questions to api.typesafe.ai (openrouter.ai only when the operator opts in via ~/.omh/jev/settings.json) with the user's own TYPESAFE_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY, only in a turn where the user names Jev; opt-in egress_attempts (re-registers chosen core tools, needs the operator's tool-override grant) and browser_adapter (vetoes core browser_* tools) settings; the pre_tool_call hook refuses skill_manage edits and deletes of skills OMH installed; lsp_rename applies the language server's workspace edit all-or-nothing, only to files inside the session workspace root Hermes' file tools resolve (apply=false previews), and the lsp_* tools (off until OMH_LSP_TOOLS or the lsp_tools setting) drive Hermes' agent.lsp service through its private loop, answering lsp_unavailable when that seam is absent; omh_dag reads delegation.max_concurrent_children and state.db async_delegations read-only to size each ready batch and, on a Docker or SSH terminal, runs fixed read-only file and $HOME checks in that terminal without Hermes' approval prompt; the memory provider reads the profile's .env, config.yaml and pairing files to find the gateway allowlist when classifying DMs; adds system-prompt sections for delegated children and a per-model calibration block; reads session and cost metadata from state.db read-only; state lives under ~/.omh and <project>/.omh.

entries.name: omonpakari
entries.description: Considerate health context for Hermes Agent: barometric pressure (OpenWeather), a typed journal (symptoms, medications, supplements, food, notes), menstrual-cycle windows returned as date ranges, sourced absorption-interaction checks against logged times, the person's own life notes and alternatives, per-rhythm wave states (pressure, cycle, symptoms, sleep, nutrition) and long-term patterns - assembled by a pre_llm_call hook into a short quiet picture before each reply, so suggestions are weighed against the person's body and habits first. No reminders, no pestering; a quiet first word on the host's own scheduled turns is opt-in. Disclosure — Stores a health journal (symptoms, medications, supplements, food, menstrual-cycle marks, life notes) locally in the plugin's own database and adds a short summary of it as context before each reply on attended turns, including gateway turns from any approved sender in shared chats, so the configured model provider receives it and the model may repeat it to other chat participants; scheduled cron turns get it only when first_word_turns is enabled. With an OpenWeather API key and coordinates set, it calls api.openweathermap.org (key and coordinates in the request) from the pressure tool and from at most one background refresh thread per hour during user turns. No telemetry, shell commands or self-updating.

entries.name: on-brand
entries.description: Brand voice and compliance rules Hermes can't break. entries.name: onair
entries.description: Hermes inside your OBS. Control scenes, sources, recording and streaming by asking; put cards and chapter titles on stream; design animated scenes or build one from an image, GIF, video or voice line; answer questions about your screen on an overlay; mark the good moments and get the highlight reel, YouTube chapters and a draft title when you stop.
