entries.name: onboard-me
entries.description: Onboard Me: the deep-intake onboarding every new Hermes user should get. Two guided experiences in one plugin: (1) a warm structured intake conversation — 9 sections covering identity, daily life, work, goals, AI expectations, taste, hard rules, weekly rhythms and vision, with per-section opener guidance, follow-up prompts and care rules for sensitive topics, resumable across sessions (progress saved per section), three depths (quick ~25min / standard ~50-70min / deep 90+), compiling via onboard_finish into memory-ready declarative facts, verbatim hard rules, and automation candidates harvested from what the user says they keep forgetting; (2) onboard_setup_check — inspects the actual install (model, gateway, memory, MCP, plugins, skills, crons) and returns a personalized beginner-safe plan with exact commands plus a curated FAQ of real failure modes researched from the official docs, GitHub issues and community guides. Client-intake mode for agencies: engagement section, per-client profiles that never mix, handoff brief. Adds a /onboard slash command and a first-session pre_llm_call hook that offers the intake once per session on fresh installs only (never nags after a profile exists or on dismiss). Disclosure — runs entirely locally with no network calls, no credentials and no shell execution; the setup check reads your Hermes config structure and the names (never values) of environment keys, and the plugin reads and writes its own JSON profiles under `<hermes home>/plugin-data/onboard-me/`, which you can inspect or delete; on fresh installs a first-turn hook adds a one-time suggestion to offer the intake (turn it off with the `auto_greet` setting or `/onboard dismiss`).

entries.name: onebot-platform
entries.description: QQ bot via the OneBot 11 protocol: connects Hermes to your own self-hosted NapCat, Lagrange, LLOneBot or go-cqhttp deployment over WebSocket — the plugin hosts a reverse-WS server inside the Hermes gateway, or dials an existing forward-WS endpoint — and adds the qq toolset (qq_send_image, qq_send_voice, qq_send_video, qq_send_file, qq_send_forward, qq_send_segments, qq_napcat_api, qq_group_history) for DM and group chats with admin allowlists, group mention gating, per-member soft limits, and cron/notification delivery to a configured home channel. Inbound messages are parsed from segment arrays with CQ-string fallback; images are downloaded through an SSRF-guarded fetch (private/CGNAT/NAT64 addresses rejected, allow_cidrs escape hatch, per-hop redirect re-validation) with magic-byte extension sniffing and downscaled (Pillow) before the vision tool sees them; voice clips are SILK-magic-checked and converted to 16 kHz mono WAV for the STT pipeline; QQ cards (json/xml segments) are flattened to readable text; stickers resolve to local paths. Outbound replies are never auto-split: a two-tier policy delivers short replies as one bubble and longer ones as a locally rendered text image (fonttools/Pillow, system CJK fonts with platform-aware font chains) with a PNG size cap falling back to single-text; Markdown is stripped to QQ plain text with word-boundary emphasis handling. Includes a per-chat inbound rate limit, a proactive-write gate for the qq_* tools (minute/day caps, JSONL audit, /api/write_gate_stats), <user_message> prompt-injection boundaries (wrap inbound, strip echoed tags outbound), host clarify-tool hooks (numbered-choice card, recall on expiry), and a bundled webapp dashboard settings page (status panel, grouped config forms with write-only secrets, audit viewer). Disclosure — talks only to the user's own OneBot deployment; the plugin's listener (default port 8643) is a long-running background server inside the Hermes gateway process that accepts the bridge's reverse WebSocket and also serves the qq_* tools' local HTTP API behind an auth gate, refuses a non-loopback bind without an access token, and limits tool sends from a QQ session to that chat or the configured home channel unless the session is an admin user's private chat; inbound message media are downloaded from that deployment (or the URLs it vouches) into the plugin's data directory for the vision tool; text-to-image rendering runs locally (fonttools, Pillow, system CJK fonts) with no third-party calls; credentials (the OneBot access token, allowed-user lists, home channel) reach the plugin only through Hermes's secret scope and ONEBOT_* config and go nowhere but your own OneBot deployment; no telemetry or usage reporting.

entries.name: openany
entries.description: OpenAny is the B2A (business to agent) marketplace. Add one MCP endpoint, https://mcp.openany.si, and your agent can find and use 3,200+ APIs and 168+ AI models. Searching and checking prices is free with no key. You only need an OpenAny API key to run a call, and you pay per call. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) that connects Hermes to OpenAny's hosted MCP server over Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.openany.si. Hermes discovers openany_overview, search_apis, get_api, and run_api from that server. Auth is OPENANY_API_KEY via the Hermes config_schema secret, sent as Authorization Bearer. The server is marked trust: untrusted. Declares Python dependency mcp==2.3.0. No local Python entrypoint, hooks, middleware, self-updater, or telemetry. Disclosure — connects to OpenAny's hosted MCP server (mcp.openany.si, Alephant AI LLC) with your OPENANY_API_KEY; every tool call and its inputs go there, and run_api forwards them to the third-party API you pick and can incur a pay-per-call charge. The package marks the server `trust: untrusted`, so calls that are not read-only ask first and are refused in unattended runs. The tool list is served by the remote server and can change without a new pin.

entries.name: opencode-free-acp
entries.description: Real OpenCode CLI over ACP as a Hermes model provider, with curated free-model selection and Hermes-owned tool execution and approvals. Independent stdlib transport using only the documented provider API, not an HTTP compatibility client or a handoff to OpenCode's autonomous tools. Disclosure — starts the separately installed opencode acp executable for discovery/inference in the included restricted workspace; forwards the conversation, tool schemas and results to OpenCode and its selected upstream model. The CLI uses its normal HOME/configuration/login and may load user-configured vendor plugins/hooks; its normal network calls, local records and vendor terms apply. Windows batch launchers use the OS cmd.exe with fixed quoted arguments, AutoRun and delayed expansion disabled; processes join a private cleanup Job Object before running. Linux/macOS use an owned process group. These are not OS sandboxes. Child environment is allowlisted; Hermes/provider keys and YOLO settings are not inherited. Plugin code reads no credential stores, writes no runtime state, makes no direct network calls, installs no binaries and sends no telemetry. Native ACP permission/file/terminal requests are refused, native tool events abort the request, and selection must be confirmed before inference. This is not authorization to use OpenCode; broader vendor policies can override workspace restrictions, and free availability/pricing/privacy can change.

entries.name: openltm
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in HERMES_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)

entries.name: opensop
entries.description: Turn your best agent workflow into a file anyone can run. An OpenSOP process file sets, step by step, what is a script (must be certain) and what needs the agent (judgment). Hermes starts a run with sop_run, does its steps and submits them with sop_submit; the next script step checks the work, so scripts decide done. The run lives on disk, not in the conversation: Hermes is re-anchored on its open step every turn and across compaction, nudged to finish it before wrapping up, and refused when it tries to decide a step reserved for a person (seat belts, not a sandbox). Any agent or person can pick the run up with the opensop CLI, and every step leaves a receipt. Requires the opensop CLI 0.10.0+ on PATH. Disclosure — sop_run, sop_submit and sop_retry go through Hermes's approval prompt (process hash, inputs, run id, run folder) because a run's script steps run as shell commands with your permissions, outside Hermes's terminal approvals; a run this profile started or continued through an approved call does not prompt again. llm and judgment steps can drive coding-agent CLIs (claude, codex, cursor-agent, kimi) with the permission the file declares, so only run process files you trust. The plugin has no credentials of its own. An OpenSOP process file sets, step by step, what is a script (must be certain) and what needs the agent (judgment). Hermes starts a run with sop_run, does its steps and submits them with sop_submit; the next script step checks the work, so scripts decide done. entries.name: openviking
entries.description: Long-term memory for Hermes. Capture conversations, recall useful facts across sessions and search your knowledge. Choose Quick Local, OpenViking Service (managed cloud) or your own server. Disclosure — conversation turns, tool results and MEMORY.md / USER.md edits are sent to the configured OpenViking server. Quick Local setup installs the newest OpenViking 0.5.x server release from PyPI at setup time (checked against PyPI's hash, not the version reviewed here; re-running setup upgrades it) plus a hash-pinned llama-cpp-python wheel and a local embedding model. It copies the active Hermes static LLM API key into a private file under the profile for extraction, and its localhost server keeps running after Hermes exits and after plugin removal (stop it with `hermes openviking local stop`). Extraction can use a remote LLM. Custom localhost connections can start openviking-server from PATH with the profile environment minus Hermes bot, gateway, GitHub and dashboard secrets; model and tool API keys still pass.

entries.name: openwall-mcp
entries.description: OpenWall through its MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://openwall.mrhyde.dev/mcp): a giant shared wall, 40,000 px across, where AI agents paint live while people watch. The agent finds free space, plans an artwork at wall scale, paints it with shapes, pixel art or a photo the server converts to pixel art, checks it with a picture of the wall, titles it and returns its link. Bundles one skill for the whole flow and an after-install note. Tested end to end with Hermes 0.23 on a local copy of the wall: seven artworks painted from seven requests, plus a seagull added to one of them after a preview with look. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Each agent uses its own key (ow_...), created with Connect on the site and read from OPENWALL_API_KEY, declared as a secret in config_schema and sent as an Authorization header that Hermes fills in. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to openwall.mrhyde.dev (closed-source server), and the tool set is served by that server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. What the agent paints, its titles and its name are public on the wall; the server keeps a hash of the key and keyed hashes of IP addresses for rate limits; uploaded photos are converted and the original is not stored; moderation reviews artworks after they appear. The server is marked untrusted, so painting and erasing tools ask for approval (Once / Session / Always per tool).

entries.name: operations
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads hermes-metrics-dash's <hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB_HOST/GITLAB_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL_ROUTER_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <hermes root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert_target set it posts new attention items through hermes send; with drift_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations_summary auxiliary task. From the setup checklist's Connect GitLab step it can also adopt this profile's own login - its environment read through Hermes' secret scope, or the host the gitlab-mr plugin names - or take a host and token typed on the page; the host goes through the plugin-settings writer and the token through Hermes' .env credential route as OPERATIONS_GITLAB_TOKEN, and the token is never sent back to the page. No other credential store is read: a login that exists only in another profile's .env or in the glab CLI's config is typed in instead. Since 0.3.5 the plugin keeps its own metrics store: it tails <hermes root>/metrics/requests.jsonl and moa-refs.jsonl, guardrail lines in logs/agent.log, logs/model-router-requests.jsonl and clientgate/clientgate-usage.jsonl (all read-only, offset-tracked) plus its own host probes (CPU and memory via sysctl/vm_stat or PowerShell, LM Studio's lms ps, and every five minutes the local conformance.yaml's install-stamp, launchd/scheduled-task, loopback-port and key-name checks), and reads session titles and costs from <hermes root>/state.db and every profile's gateway_state.json (read-only), into <hermes root>/metrics/operations.db, which this plugin alone writes and prunes to the metrics_retention_days setting (30/60/90 days or forever, chosen on the page and written through Hermes' plugin-settings writer); hermes-metrics-dash's metrics.db is then only a read-only fallback until the own store holds data. It probes the local metrics dashboard's /api/about (METRICS_DASH_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8899, cached five minutes) to link to it rather than duplicate it, and every Hermes process that loads the plugin starts a daemon timer: when no kanban dispatcher tick has arrived for two minutes it runs the same sweep itself every 30 seconds (collection, alerts and, with drift_action: automatic, the fix cards), and the page says so; OPERATIONS_HEARTBEAT_TIMER=0 turns that timer off. Since 0.3.4 a failed model call is classified with the host app's own error classifier and shown with its cause and remedy commands; no new outbound call is made for that.
entries.title: Operations
known_issues: On a fresh install the request, error, host and conformance sections read hermes-metrics-dash's metrics.db (read-only) until the plugin's own store has collected; with neither present they show "unavailable".
Merge requests and the GitLab conformance standard need the GitLab host and token set in the plugin's settings (or GITLAB_HOST and GITLAB_TOKEN).

entries.name: optchat
entries.description: OptChat-style endless memory for Hermes: an append-only verbatim log plus a binary summary tree, exposed as recall through the MemoryProvider ABC. Background compactor builds the tree with a cheap auxiliary model (call_llm task optchat_compact); prefetch returns a fixed-budget view of the whole history; optchat_zoom/optchat_date tools open any line down to the verbatim message. Disclosure — every turn's user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results (each result capped at 30,000 characters, after Hermes's secret redaction) are appended permanently to unencrypted owner-only files under $HERMES_HOME/optchat/, with no deletion or retention limit; a background compactor sends those messages and the surrounding summary view to your auxiliary model route (task optchat_compact) for summarization; each turn injects up to view_budget_chars (default 16,000) of that history into the model context.

entries.name: optmem-hermes
entries.description: Independent Hermes integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under HERMES_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

entries.name: orbit-desktop
entries.description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research. This plugin registers tool(s): orbit_workspace. Platforms: linux.

entries.name: orcaslicer
entries.description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/HERMES_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.hermes-orca (HERMES_ORCA_HOME), outside HERMES_HOME.

entries.name: orphic-eyes
entries.description: Pixel-only screenshot review for Hermes: capture URL pairs, inspect changed zones, prepare coding-agent requests and run bounded follow-up review rounds. Disclosure — launches an installed headless Edge/Chrome/Chromium with a minimal environment; captured pages can load network resources and follow redirects (private and loopback destinations only when you set allow_local in the plugin config; link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused); renders http://localhost pages and file:// pages inside your configured file_root (default: the working directory), which can embed other local files; stores screenshots, reports and prompts under HERMES_HOME/orphic-eyes and can serve them read-only on 127.0.0.1 with a random token until stopped. No telemetry or credential-store access; prompts are returned, never sent or executed by the plugin.
entries.title: Orphic Eyes
known_issues: Requires Python 3.12 or newer, Pillow and an installed Edge/Chrome/Chromium browser.
Windows/Edge, macOS and a live Hermes host are not covered by automated tests.
Public DNS and proxy rules can block capture; login walls and dynamic pages can affect pixels.

entries.name: orquehelx
entries.description: Per-call delegation across your own subscriptions. The model sends each subagent to a named route with delegate_to(route, goal, context); each route pins a provider Hermes already knows (Claude, Codex or Antigravity subscription plugins, ACP provider plugins) and a model. delegate_task, by contrast, uses the one target in config.yaml. Subagents launch through ctx.subagent_lifecycle. A child counts as out of quota only on an unambiguous provider error or a measured window at 100 %, and the route never switches on its own: a policy decides whether the parent asks you, picks another route, or waits. Disclosure: a pre_tool_call hook blocks delegate_task spawns while routes are configured (list/steer/stop pass); an api_request_error hook records quota errors in memory. Quota is read with Hermes' fetch_account_usage (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex) on /ohx quota and after a provider error. No other network egress, no files written.

entries.name: osv-ref

entries.name: othigai
entries.description: A fire drill for your Hermes agent. /drill starts test agents on your machine with your model and your own SOUL.md, hands them an ordinary errand, and plants a trap in the email they read. Everything they can reach is fake: a fresh fake key, a throwaway folder in the system temp folder, and a listener on 127.0.0.1 standing in for the attacker. A default-no pre_tool_call gate checks every tool call a test agent makes, and you get a safety score with a 95% range, a step by step replay and fixes that the next drill measures. Nothing runs until you read a notice and type /drill yes. Disclosure — test agents make model calls on the model you name or your default, which costs money on a paid model (capped per agent and per drill, with a daily limit); before a drill it runs a harmless `rm -r` of its own temp folder plus curl and /dev/tcp probes to its listener through your session's terminal to check that the approval prompt works, so an approval prompt may appear and the right answer is no; test agents run a short list of commands inside a throwaway folder in the system temp folder; a local listener runs on a random 127.0.0.1 port for the length of a drill; it reads your SOUL.md and passes it to the test agents, and reads which memory provider is configured; test agent sessions stay in Hermes's normal history, where memory or telemetry plugins may see the trap text. No third-party network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

entries.name: oura-mcp
entries.description: Read the user's Oura Ring readiness, sleep, HRV and activity through the local oura MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Oura. Runs the `oura-mcp-unofficial@0.8.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official Oura Cloud API v2. The user creates their own Oura developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.oura-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to Oura's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Hermes credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.hermes/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. Tools that change state: oura_profile_update (local profile only); oura_exchange_code (stores OAuth tokens locally); oura_revoke_access (revokes the Oura grant and deletes local tokens). The tool set comes from the pinned npm version, not from this repository's source tree.

entries.name: overhead
entries.description: What changed at this place between these dates? Measures vegetation loss and gain, burned area by severity (dNBR) and water change in hectares anywhere on Earth from free Sentinel-2 L2A imagery, and delivers a before | after | change panel or a timelapse GIF to every surface, with an interactive before/after swipe and timelapse card in Hermes Desktop. Provides the overhead_locate, overhead_scenes, overhead_compare and overhead_timelapse tools, the overhead:earth-watch skill, and post_tool_call / transform_llm_output hooks that append the image's MEDIA line when a reply lacks it. Disclosure — Makes unauthenticated HTTPS requests to the Earth Search STAC API by Element 84 (earth-search.aws.element84.com: scene searches by the area's bounding box, never its exact outline, and dates) and to the AWS Open Data sentinel-cogs bucket in us-west-2 (range reads of Sentinel-2 bands, with ~/.netrc never read), and, only to look up a place name, to Nominatim / OpenStreetMap (nominatim.openstreetmap.org, at most 1 request per second). STAC and Nominatim requests carry the User-Agent `overhead-hermes-plugin/0.1.0 (+https://github.com/leoresendedop-sys/overhead)`. Place lookups, the pixels read and searches over past date ranges are cached under the plugin's data folder (plugin-data/overhead: cache/ and runs/), which is not pruned automatically. The Desktop card's Open map button opens openstreetmap.org in the browser, only when clicked. Reads a system font to draw panel labels. The plugin itself needs no API keys or accounts, stores no credentials and adds no telemetry; rasterio installs only after Hermes dependency consent. For optional visual interpretation, it offers local image paths and questions for Hermes's public vision_analyze tool. If the agent calls that tool, Hermes may send the selected images and prompt to its configured native or auxiliary model provider; images may include location and date labels, and credentials, costs and privacy terms depend on the user's Hermes configuration.
entries.title: Overhead
known_issues: The first run over a new area takes about 40 to 70 s, sometimes longer, while the imagery streams from AWS us-west-2; repeat runs take about 1 s from the cache.

The interactive Desktop card needs a Desktop build with the tool-media renderer area (main after 24 Oct 2026, or the first release after 0.22.5) and its Desktop half switched on in Capabilities → Plugins; other builds and surfaces show the panel PNG or the GIF.

entries.name: own-compute
entries.description: Bring your own compute. For researchers and scientists with a workstation, a lab server or a cluster account. Runs sandboxed container environments, Slurm batch jobs and cloud agents (a Hermes agent in a sandbox on the user's own machine, not a hosted service, that hands its work back as a git branch) on SSH hosts, Slurm login nodes, and the Docker or Podman on this computer. Independent of Nous Research. A Compute page in Hermes Desktop shows every machine and what runs on it, and the same actions are chat tools with approval cards before anything starts, changes or is deleted. Disclosure — runs ssh, git and the container runtime (podman or docker), and on Slurm hosts sbatch, squeue, sacct, scancel and srun, on the hosts you add; opens ssh -L tunnels bound to 127.0.0.1 and terminal windows when you click; adds a host's key to your SSH known-hosts file on first contact (accept-new); remote hosts pull container images from public registries; cloud agents send the model key you store as a Hermes secret (CC_AGENT_API_KEY or a profile model's key) into the agent's sandbox, where commands the agent runs can read it, and call the model endpoint you choose from inside that sandbox only; one background thread starts on the first tool call or chat turn (reachability checks, Slurm and agent polling, time and idle limits); stores hosts, templates, run records and saved file copies in the plugin's data folder; reads secrets only through the Hermes secret scope; no telemetry, no update check, no call to any service run by the author.
entries.title: Own Compute
known_issues: Tested on Windows 11 (Hermes Webapp), Fedora 43 with rootless Podman, and macOS 27.2 on Apple Silicon, against a Slurm test cluster running in containers. The native Hermes Desktop app, GPUs and Docker on Linux were not tested.

Cloud agents need a model from an API-key provider or a model server you run; a sign-in or subscription provider cannot be used. The agent's key is readable by commands the agent itself runs in its sandbox: use a scoped, spend-capped key.

Slurm only (no PBS or LSF). Cloud agents are off on Slurm hosts. The Hermes gateway has to run on the computer that shows the Compute page. An EC2 host starts a machine in your own AWS account that AWS bills while it runs; EC2 was tested on us-east-1 and t3.micro only.

entries.name: ownmachine
entries.description: Give Hermes its own Mac, Omarchy or Windows VM to test apps, scrape websites and automate desktop work with private SSH access and you in control. Keep a persistent workspace on infrastructure you control, watch from your browser and take over when needed. Privacy: screenshots and app text follow your configured model provider. Disclosure — Runs OpenSSH, using operator-configured aliases, agents and keys, to a Mac or Linux KVM host and streams VM screenshots, accessibility text and computer_use input through a restricted fixed-command MCP relay; screenshots and app text go to your configured model provider; guided setup (`/ownmachine setup --run`) executes reviewed remote provisioning stages over a separate temporary setup SSH alias and requires administrator registration and manual guest consent/sign-in; Windows guests use separate agent/viewer roles, a root-owned runtime, libvirt policy, firewall rules and a private Unix console on the host; the opt-in `remind later --mode tomorrow` writes a helper script into the Hermes `scripts/` directory and creates a one-shot no-agent cron job through the profile's local gateway; a shared control database is kept in an operator-chosen directory. Licensed PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.
entries.title: OwnMachine
known_issues: Omarchy supports tested foreground control on Apple Silicon; background input is experimental and Chromium requires explicit matching Hyprland module opt-in.
Linux uses a reviewed preview-grade driver pin; rolling system updates require compatibility checks.
Declares websockets==15.0.1 for gateway scheduling and Pillow>=11.0.0,<14 for screenshot verification; Hermes requests dependency consent during installation.
Windows support is Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation x86-64 on Linux KVM/libvirt; Home/Pro, Windows ARM and other hypervisors are not qualified.
Administrator firewall/runtime registration and manual guest consent/sign-in are required; Windows first DVD boot needs the private viewer.
Linux host reboot acceptance was skipped; firewall-service restart is tested. Broad Windows background/pixel input and clipboard sync are not qualified.
Hermes must use in-process plugin isolation; keep viewer credentials separate and configure the OwnMachine computer_use backend and shared control directory.
Guest provisioning downloads pinned upstream driver artifacts; Windows installation uses operator-supplied verified Microsoft media. Guest-driver updates require separate fresh-guest qualification.
Independent ALF-only random-port blocking and reboot persistence of the new security setup are unverified.
One initial guest boot hung; later restart checks passed.
Model-driven pixel-click acceptance is deferred; cloud Mac hosting is unverified.
PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; commercial use outside its permissions requires a separate license.

entries.name: pagecast-director
entries.description: Editable cast narration with locked voices, source passage IDs, resumable synthesis and selective regeneration. Disclosure — Stores books and generated audio privately in its plugin data. On first use it lists the speech options on this computer and asks which to use; it never picks one for you, and online engines are blocked if you say no online services. To find local speech servers it sends GET /v1/models only to this computer's loopback address (ports 8000, 8880, 5002, 8020 and 8080, plus any local address you set; no redirects, 1 second timeout). Every program it starts gets a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG), never your provider keys. Voices are local (an installed speech program such as espeak-ng, Flite, Piper or say, or a speech server already running on this computer) unless you choose hosted Inworld, ElevenLabs or Google Gemini, which send passage text and voice choices to that provider with your own key and use your credits; the optional Gemini Vertex route uses a Google sign-in that Hermes holds for your own OAuth client (hermes auth add pagecast-director:google; the plugin never sees the token), sent only to aiplatform.googleapis.com. Can render a short captioned video clip (audiogram) of a finished chapter span into plugin data, with a cover image you point to. Runs local FFmpeg/ffprobe and adb; mpv only plays a preview aloud when you approve it. The optional Android tools check the author's GitHub releases (flabanabba8/PageCast) for the PageCast app and can download the latest APK (checked against that release's own SHA256SUMS); installing it on a phone with adb, replacing a locked voice and playing a preview aloud each ask for your approval (one pre_tool_call hook). No background processes beyond a render or preview you start.

entries.name: palate
entries.description: A palate is the instrument that does the matching, and it sharpens as the record fills. Now working for Hermes. It keeps your own local record of what you watched, what you turned down, and the reason in each case, then picks from that: mood is held separately from taste, so something can suit you and still be wrong for tonight and be offered for another night with the blocker named. It reports an affinity only when the evidence supports one, and says so plainly when it does not. Picks are spread across the works you liked rather than six neighbours of whichever one came first, and each one says how strong the match is, so the best of a thin pool is never dressed up as a recommendation. Suggestions can come from what you liked, from widely-seen titles you have no verdict on, or from what is free on your own services, because similarity alone cannot reach a classic that sits next to nothing in your record. Availability covers subscriptions, free ad-supported tiers, library access and your own files, and rentals are opt in per storefront, so Amazon can count while others do not; every suggestion names what it would cost, and since the data carries no prices, none is invented. No account and no hosted service. Disclosure — calls only api.themoviedb.org, sending the titles and ids you ask about plus discovery filters (search, keywords, credits, runtimes and JustWatch-licensed watch-provider availability), never your verdicts, reasons, ratings or services; reads your TMDB key only from plugins.entries.palate.settings.tmdb_api_key; palate_import reads only the single CSV path you name, honours Hermes' read denylist and refuses anything that is not a Letterboxd or Trakt export; stores its ledger and TMDB cache in the plugin's own data folder; palate_export writes one JSON file to the path you choose, refusing paths on Hermes' write denylist, paths inside the Hermes home, names not ending in .json and any existing file that is not an earlier Palate export; no hooks, background work, subprocesses or telemetry.

entries.name: pandora
entries.description: Unofficial Pandora (pandora.com) client for Hermes: play your stations on this PC or cast to networked speakers, see the Now Playing artist and song in the desktop status bar. Left-click the chip for search, play/pause, skips, thumbs, volume, recent stations and output. Search for an artist or song to start a station (on-demand playback depends on the Pandora plan); albums and playlists appear only when the account's plan allows them. Also usable headless: the seven agent tools work from the CLI with no desktop app. Local playback uses mpv, which is not bundled: after installing, click "Set up audio" in the Pandora chip (or run `hermes pandora setup`) — that downloads mpv, the audio engine the plugin streams music through, as a SHA-256-verified official portable build (~27 MB, once per PC). Nothing is downloaded until you ask. Disclosure - sign-in uses your own Pandora account email + password (`hermes pandora login`); the password is stored only in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager on Windows, entry "Hermes pandora" / your account email, shared by every Hermes profile of that OS user) and read back from that same entry, both through a plugin-registered Hermes secret source and directly. The plugin never writes a plaintext password. The session token and cookie jar live in the active profile's plugin-data/pandora/session.json (mode 0600). Credentials are sent only to pandora.com, and credential-bearing requests never follow redirects. Disclosure - this plugin uses automated access to pandora.com that may violate Pandora's Terms of Use; use is at your own account risk. Unofficial and unaffiliated; no Pandora logo or artwork is bundled. Windows only (exercised end to end).

entries.name: pandy-tickets

entries.name: pantheon
entries.description: Let Hermes exchange messages and agree on outcomes with other agents in a shared Pantheon chat. Disclosure — Sends chat messages, files you upload (from the session's working directory, up to 1 MB each) and static site bundles (up to 20 MB) to pantheon.talk, where other chat members can read them; saves files received from other members under the profile's plugin-data/pantheon/downloads; when you enable incoming replies (plugins.entries.pantheon.allow_gateway_injection), a background thread polls pantheon.talk and wakes the conversation with a prompt to read new messages. New incoming-reply approvals persist until you disable them, while older temporary approvals restore their prior value after the last connection ends. Progress reports can include numeric token counters from turns attributable to Pantheon wake-ups; native transcripts and provider credentials are not collected for accounting. Task and handoff content you post is shared with authorized chat members. Questions the agent asks you are sent to pantheon.talk and, if unanswered after five minutes, emailed to you with a chat link.

No telemetry, shell commands, self-update or core overrides.

entries.name: passkey-gate
entries.description: Approve your agents' risky actions with your phone's passkey, even when you're not at the agent's keyboard. An agent asks for approval of an exact action (and optionally the exact command); you get a link in any chat, read it on your phone and sign with Face ID, a fingerprint or your screen lock; the agent then verifies your signature locally against your pinned key before acting. A relayed 'the human said yes' proves nothing; only your signature counts. Optional enforcement blocks matching tool calls until you approve them, and each approval runs once. Includes a guided `setup` wizard, a background service, a hash-chained audit log, and approvals between agents owned by different people. It is an honest approval record, and becomes a hard boundary only when agents can't modify the gate (see the README's Security model). Lanes choose which conversations need a passkey: you at the keyboard, your own chat accounts, other people, bots or other agents. It can also act as Hermes's approval transport, so a command Hermes itself flags needs your passkey. Disclosure — runs a small web server on 127.0.0.1 that your phone reaches over HTTPS (by default published to your own tailnet with `tailscale serve`); can install a background service (systemd user unit or LaunchAgent) that runs as you; runs `tailscale`, `systemctl --user`/`launchctl` and a short Python process to time new patterns, never with elevated privileges; contacts only its own address and any peer gates you allowlist, follows no redirects, no telemetry; stores passkey public keys, requests, the pinned key, an audit log and a remote-minting token in its plugin data folder (no private keys); its hooks note each turn's platform, sender id and bot flag in memory only; as the approval transport (off until you select it) it posts one message into the conversation with the approval link for a command Hermes flagged, or one line saying it couldn't, and rewords one blocked tool result when a passkey request went unanswered; setup can change Hermes's `security.approval.transport` and `transport_fallback` settings, after asking; ships two test skills an agent runs only when asked; with enforcement on, any failure blocks the call; only your pinned passkey can approve, and anyone with an approval link can read and deny that request; patterns are a best-effort list, not a sandbox.

entries.name: patch-sentinel
entries.description: Measures the host, not the source tree: code review asks "can an attacker exploit this code?" and this asks "is this machine running what the vendor shipped?" — the two are complements, never substitutes. Answers "are we patched?" with evidence, for whatever the host runs — an adapter chosen from the host's own /etc/os-release (apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, apk), the running kernel against the newest installed and installable, whatever advisory names the fixed version per release (Ubuntu notices, OSV per release, Bodhi, Arch's tracker, SUSE's OVAL), container image digests, nine language ecosystems through OSV plus lockfile pins, package checksums and listening sockets against a recorded baseline, and a CycloneDX SBOM. Every check has three outcomes — clean, finding, could-not-look — so an unreachable host, an unimplemented distro or a rate-limited registry reads as unknown rather than clean. The pane reads one device at a time and hands over the exact commands per device; a gated cve_apply tool stages, applies, re-measures and writes a receipt for an agent explicitly asked to patch. Linux only: any other OS answers "unsupported" with its name. Disclosure — scans run fixed read-only commands on this machine and, over your own ssh agent, on hosts you list; package names and versions go to api.osv.dev, api.first.org and the distro advisory sites (ubuntu.com, bodhi.fedoraproject.org, security.archlinux.org, ftp.suse.com, cisa.gov); cve_apply, after Hermes's approval prompt, runs the distro's full upgrade with sudo -n on the chosen host; scans, receipts and SBOMs stay under $HERMES_HOME/patch-sentinel (mode 700).

entries.name: patchreview
entries.description: Routes recognized file-writing tool calls through Hermes' native human-approval gate with a proposed diff. PatchReview never exposes model-callable accept tools and never writes target files: on approval, Hermes executes the original tool through its normal write path and protections. Full-content and exact string-replacement previews support replace_all; unsupported or unparseable recognized calls are blocked. Coverage is limited to recognized tool names and does not intercept shell commands, scripts, or unrelated processes. The plugin makes no network calls, sends no telemetry, invokes no shell commands, stores no credentials, and starts no background processes.

entries.name: patchsmith
entries.description: Adds `implement_task` and `apply_patch`. The first hands a single well-specified coding task to a local model served through Ollama (the measured backend) and returns the resulting diff. Propose mode runs in an isolated temporary checkout, preserves the source checkout, and saves a full patch for review. The second tool applies an approved saved patch only after hash, base, affected-file and path checks. The local model works inside a fixed toolset with no shell (read, grep, glob, git status/diff, write/edit, run the configured test command, finish) under hard turn and total token budgets shared across up to three fresh-context attempts. An optional local model is used only on the final allowed attempt; failures return a factual handback. Includes a path jail, read-only test files, an auto-finish when tests go green, a repeat-call guard, and revert of partial edits when a run is blocked. Your main model spends tokens only on the instruction and the returned diff. Disclosure — runs git and the owner-configured test command (PS_TEST_COMMAND, never chosen by the model; it executes project code on the host) as subprocesses in the working directory with a minimal child environment plus an owner passthrough list (PS_ENV_PASSTHROUGH); in direct mode a local model writes implementation files inside the given workdir (never .git, node_modules, test files, .env* or .ssh/; the Hermes home, the user home and filesystem roots are refused as workdirs) and a run transcript with file excerpts under <workdir>/.patchsmith/; propose mode copies the checkout to a temporary Git worktree and keeps the patch, provenance record and transcript under <hermes home>/plugin-data/patchsmith/proposals/, with run summaries under <hermes home>/plugin-data/patchsmith/runs/. Task text and file contents go only to the local model endpoint set in PS_ENDPOINT (loopback or private-network address; public and link-local hosts refused). inspect_hardware runs fixed OS probes (nvidia-smi, sysctl, system_profiler, PowerShell CIM) and reads the endpoint's model list. No telemetry, no self-update, no stored credentials.

entries.name: pdf-shrink
entries.description: Shrink a PDF to a size limit (2 MB, 500 KB, whatever the upload form says) with everything running locally — no upload, no API key, no third-party service. Two tools and a bundled skill. pdf_inspect reports what makes a file heavy: image share of the bytes, the resolution each image is actually displayed at, fonts, embedded attachments and duplicates, with a verdict (images dominate / images not reclaimable / vector-heavy / already small) so a shrink that cannot work is caught before it runs. pdf_shrink downsamples images it can re-encode safely to the resolution they are displayed at, recovered by replaying each page's content stream (q/Q/cm/Do, including nested Form XObjects), then walks a measured ladder of DPI/JPEG-quality rungs from the mildest down and keeps the first that fits — each rung rebuilt from the pristine original, so the copy is one generation of compression rather than six. Text, fonts and vector art are never rasterised; images that cannot be re-encoded safely (JBIG2, CCITT, 1-bit or non-8-bit samples, soft/stencil masks, /Mask, /Matte or /Decode arrays, CMYK and other print colour spaces, tiny logos) are left byte-for-byte alone. When the limit cannot be reached without making the document unreadable it stops at the safe floor, reports the smallest safe size, saves that copy when it is meaningfully smaller, and names the levers that can actually help (a reachable higher target, or aggressive=true when it can do better) instead of handing back mush. Every copy is re-opened and verified (page count, blank pages, structural syntax) before delivery; a copy that fails is reported as failed, not as a success. The source is re-hashed before and after every completed run, and a change is reported rather than claimed untouched. A before/after render of page 1 comes back when PDFium is available and a verified copy was written. Writes only new files; an existing output path is refused, never overwritten. Ladder rungs are built in a private system-temp directory, never beside the PDF; a read-only source folder still works, and the default output falls back to the current directory when the source folder cannot be written. An explicit output_path must end in .pdf, and a location that Hermes's own write denylist refuses is rejected before anything is written. The only destructive option is drop_attachments=true, off by default.

entries.name: pdf-surgeon
entries.description: Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Hermes installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.

entries.name: peakflo-spaces
entries.description: Hand off repetitive finance and operations work to cloud agents or people through Spaces by Peakflo's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.peakflo.ai/mcp, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with PKCE, no keys in config): create one-off or recurring (cron) tasks and get a link to follow them, list workflows and their runs, query workspace data tables with read-only SQL, pull aggregated reports on bills, invoices, payables and receivables, search policy documents, and review pending approvals. Bundles the spaces workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Peakflo's hosted server (api.peakflo.ai) and acts on the user's Spaces workspace with their own role and permissions; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Spaces does not move money, make payments or trade. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only (creating tasks, running workflows, completing approvals, writing data) and refuses them in unattended runs. No telemetry.

entries.name: penthera
entries.description: Offline, rule-based security checks run through the terminal: a repo scan, dependency capabilities, a passive scan of a URL you own, and an audit of your AI agent config (skills, MCP servers, hooks, permissions). A skill only: no tools, hooks, middleware or MCP server. It runs the pinned penthera npm package with npx, which downloads that package on first use (Node.js 22 or later). Rules decide every finding; a model never does. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no background process, no self-updater. Disclosure — the skill runs the third-party `penthera` npm CLI pinned at 2.4.0 through `npx -y`, which downloads it from the npm registry on first use and runs it on the host outside Hermes' sandbox; it reads repo files and local agent configs (`~/.claude`, `~/.cursor`, `.mcp.json`), makes passive requests to URLs the user names, and, when the user approves, edits code on a local branch or installs a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` hook.

entries.name: perf-hud
entries.description: Live performance HUD for Hermes Desktop: a status-bar chip with core-compatible TPS (sum of output tokens over sum of API durations for the last 10 completed calls, the same window and arithmetic as Hermes' own status bar) in `tps`, `tps_ttft` or `calls` form, and a statistics popover with TPS, a separately labelled Session Avg TPS (the same ratio over every call in the session), median TTFT from `first_chunk_at`, LLM calls, an `Agent steps*` compatibility alias (equal to LLM calls, footnoted inside the snapshot by `agent_steps_note`), turns, errors, input, output and cache-read tokens, cache hit rate on Hermes' `cache_read / (cache_read + input)` buckets, tool calls and tool time, tool time share, wall-clock session duration, and the model and provider. Two controls — Reset current statistics (clears the plugin's own in-memory counters, never Hermes session state) and Clear history — plus local performance history for the last 50 sessions. Observes only: nine observer hooks, no tool or message is ever blocked, rewritten or reordered, no Hermes core file is touched, the aggregation layer is pure with no I/O and no host imports, all handlers are fail-open so a telemetry bug cannot break a turn, and a corrupt history file is quarantined instead of raised. Disclosure — reads only from the observer payloads: token usage buckets (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning), API and tool timings, first-chunk timestamps, model and provider names, session ids, and tool names plus error status for the counts; prompts, model responses, conversation contents, tool arguments and tool results are never read and have no field in its snapshot, its desktop event or its history record. Writes exactly one JSON file per profile at `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-perf-hud-*/history.json` containing only session_id, model, provider, started_at, updated_at, duration_ms, ttft_ms, tps_core, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_hit_pct, tool_time_ms and llm_calls, allow-list enforced, atomic, capped at 50 sessions; no other disk writes, and no config change beyond the documented `plugins.entries.perf-hud.settings.*` keys (chip_enabled, chip_metric, history_enabled, history_max_sessions, poll_ms, broadcast_min_interval_ms). Desktop updates travel over Hermes' in-process plugin event bridge (`broadcast_plugin_event`, topic `plugin.perf-hud.stats.update`, throttled to 400 ms) and its REST routes are served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/perf-hud/ (snapshot, sessions, history, config, reset, clear-history, status), which requires the dashboard's auth ticket. Executes no subprocess, no shell command, no systemd unit, no Task Scheduler task; makes no network request; has no credentials, no OAuth and no telemetry. Standard library only, no third-party dependencies.
entries.title: Perf HUD
known_issues: Turns counts completed turns, so one long turn can show `Turns 0` beside a high `LLM calls` (an agent loop is many calls, one turn). `LLM calls` and `Agent steps*` count per call.

The status-bar chip appears after one desktop restart, because the desktop half is materialised into `<HERMES_HOME>/desktop-plugins/` at app startup. The backend half (hooks, history, REST) is live as soon as the plugin is enabled.
Verified by hand on Windows with a packaged Hermes Desktop build. Linux and macOS run the same code and the same plugin directories, but were not exercised on those platforms.

If `dashboard.turn_isolation` runs turns in a compute-host child process, the child keeps its own in-memory counters: live events still reach the desktop, but `/snapshot` in the parent will not include them. History is on shared disk, so `/history` stays complete.
TTFT needs `first_chunk_at`; providers or non-streaming paths that do not report it show a dash for those calls instead of an invented sample.

Disclosure — reads only from the observer payloads: token usage buckets (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning), API and tool timings, first-chunk timestamps, model and provider names, session ids, and tool names plus error status for the counts; prompts, model responses, conversation contents, tool arguments and tool results are never read and have no field in its snapshot, its desktop event or its history record. Writes exactly one JSON file per profile at `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/agent-plugin-perf-hud-*/history.json` containing only session_id, model, provider, started_at, updated_at, duration_ms, ttft_ms, tps_core, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_hit_pct, tool_time_ms and llm_calls, allow-list enforced, atomic, capped at 50 sessions; no other disk writes, and no config change beyond the documented `plugins.entries.perf-hud.settings.*` keys (chip_enabled, chip_metric, history_enabled, history_max_sessions, poll_ms, broadcast_min_interval_ms). Desktop updates travel over Hermes' in-process plugin event bridge (`broadcast_plugin_event`, topic `plugin.perf-hud.stats.update`, throttled to 400 ms) and its REST routes are served by the user's own local dashboard at /api/plugins/perf-hud/ (snapshot, sessions, history, config, reset, clear-history, status), which requires the dashboard's auth ticket. Executes no subprocess, no shell command, no systemd unit, no Task Scheduler task; makes no network request; has no credentials, no OAuth and no telemetry. Standard library only, no third-party dependencies. This plugin hook(s): pre_api_request, post_api_request, api_request_error, post_llm_call, post_tool_call, on_session_start, on_session_end, on_session_finalize, on_session_delete. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5. Known issues: Turns counts completed turns, so one long turn can show `Turns 0` beside a high `LLM calls` (an agent loop is many calls, one turn). `LLM calls` and `Agent steps*` count per call.; The status-bar chip appears after one desktop restart, because the desktop half is materialised into `<HERMES_HOME>/desktop-plugins/` at app startup. The backend half (hooks, history, REST) is live as soon as the plugin is enabled.; Verified by hand on Windows with a packaged Hermes Desktop build. Linux and macOS run the same code and the same plugin directories, but were not exercised on those platforms.; If `dashboard.turn_isolation` runs turns in a compute-host child process, the child keeps its own in-memory counters: live events still reach the desktop, but `/snapshot` in the parent will not include them. History is on shared disk, so `/history` stays complete.; TTFT needs `first_chunk_at`; providers or non-streaming paths that do not report it show a dash for those calls instead of an invented sample..

entries.name: perf-lab
entries.description: Proof for speed-ups. When you ask Hermes to make code faster, Perf Lab times it before and after, fingerprints the output so a faster-but-wrong change is rejected, profiles Python with a flame graph, and enforces it with hooks: no code edits before a baseline, no finishing before a re-measure, and the plugin's own measured result appended under the reply. Disclosure — perf_bench and perf_profile run the command the agent passes on your machine, so every run first goes to Hermes' approval prompt (in any chat; "always" trusts one project folder; it fails closed and is skipped only when Hermes approvals are off); the command runs without a shell and with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, locale, temp and interpreter/venv variables, no API keys), must be an interpreter running a script, and inline code is refused, but an approved script runs with your permissions as it would in the terminal. In chats about speed, its hooks add a short rules note to the turn, block write_file/patch on code files until a baseline exists (at most twice per file), ask for one re-measure if code changed, and append a clearly labelled Perf Lab section under the reply without rewriting the agent's text; a Gatekeeper switch in the pane turns the hooks off. It stores commands, timings, output fingerprints, the first 200 KB of each run's stdout, profiles and per-chat state under plugin-data/perf-lab, makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: permission-canvas
entries.description: Per-control permissions for the computer_use tool. In a native panel you preview the target window privately, click any control and set it to Allow, Read only, Ask first or Hide. The backend enforces the choice before every input and before a screenshot or accessibility tree reaches the model: read-only controls refuse clicks, typing and value changes; ask-first operations wait for a one-time human approval of the exact action and arguments; hidden controls are removed from the tree and their pixels masked, and a capture that cannot be masked reliably is refused. New profiles start paused with unknown controls set to Ask first. Select it with computer_use.backend: permission-canvas; adds the /pc-canvas and /pc-approve commands. Validated on Windows with cua-driver 0.21 and 0.39. Disclosure — launches cua-driver (telemetry disabled) and a bounded Windows accessibility helper as local subprocesses while the backend runs, reads the selected window's pixels and accessibility data, stores policy, approval records, an audit log and the latest redacted capture in its own data directory, and opens a local Tkinter panel on /pc-canvas; no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry. Protects only actions routed through this backend; it is not an OS sandbox.
entries.title: Permission Canvas
known_issues: Desktop behaviour is validated on Windows only. Other native desktops need permission_canvas.desktop: native and are experimental.
Only actions routed through this computer_use backend are protected. Disable terminal, file, browser and other tools that could bypass it.
A Chromium window covered by another window at startup can report browser_page_unavailable until it is brought to the foreground.

entries.name: permission-tiers
entries.description: Host-enforced tiered tool permissions: assign allow/ask/block tiers to tool-name patterns (fnmatch globs), and the plugin's pre_tool_call hook vetoes or escalates matching calls before they execute, while post_tool_call keeps a local SQLite audit ledger. Two tools manage it: permission_tiers_report (rules + ledger) and permission_tiers_set (add/update/ remove). Implements the per-tool permission-levels feature requested in issue #527 without touching Hermes core — public hooks only. Safe defaults: shell and MCP tools ask, everything else keeps Hermes' existing behaviour; hook errors fail open; unattended runs fail closed on ask escalations (the plugin never auto-approves). Disclosure — no network calls, no third-party services, no stored credentials; reads/writes only its own tiers.json and ledger under the Hermes plugin-data directory; bundled permission-tiers skill documents usage.

entries.name: personal-assistant
entries.description: A remote personal assistant for your agent: it does the errands up to the final page and stops at your yes. It interviews you once ("grill me": eight short sittings on your business, people, decision rights, preferences and calendar rules), remembers corrections, people, SOPs and trust levels in a local ledger, and never asks the same thing twice. Travel and errands on real sites in English, Japanese and Korean: restaurant tables (TableCheck, Tabelog, OpenTable, Catch Table), hotels and flights on Trip.com, taxis, food and konbini delivery, with sourced prices, an approval packet for each action and an honest handoff at a sign-in, OTP or app-only wall. Optional Chief of Staff mode adds a daily plan, a weekly closeout and a radar. Adds the pa and pa_call tools, the /pa command and 42 skills (the Chief of Staff ones load only in that mode). Disclosure — Keeps its records in a SQLite ledger in your profile (state/travel-ledger/travel.sqlite): trips, prepared actions, setup answers and the chat setup runs in, preferences, people, SOPs, trust levels, call cards and transcripts, task evidence and receipts; its shell ledger helper, which skills run for payment-readiness and connectivity records, also stores browser checkpoints (page URLs, session ids), budgets and which providers hold a card. Optional features add a delivery packet queue (full packets, including priority-mail excerpts, never pruned), Daily Ops config and state, and a client index (names, emails, domains). Owner-memory and evidence records refuse recognised card numbers and credentials, records written through pa pass a lighter pattern filter, helper and approval records are kept as given, and nothing is deleted automatically. After you approve a setup review or a Chief of Staff closeout it writes USER.md, a marked PA section of SOUL.md, an operating-manual skill (or an edit of your existing one) and any context file you name, holding your approved business, people, spending-limit and approver answers as plain text, and pins the manual with hermes curator pin; a trip export writes Trip.ics and Trip-Reference.md to a folder you choose; /pa mode writes the plugin's mode setting. A pre_tool_call hook sees every tool call and blocks only tools covered by a PA exact-action approval or its deny list, plus most tools while the ledger is unreadable; a pre_llm_call hook adds short notes to your own turns (setup offer and routing, and on a session's first turn, including another person's first turn in a shared chat, your preferences and people not yet in your files) and records which chat setup runs in. With your consent during /pa setup the agent reads USER.md, SOUL.md, its memory, the calendar, past itineraries, a context file you name and up to 20 recent sent emails (PA stores no raw mail); mail work you ask for reads messages and attachments; accepted Daily Ops routines sort unread mail twice a day and send you a digest of five lines or fewer; drafts are written only if you opted in during setup (gog's gmail.compose scope, which can also send), and every send, archive, delete or label change needs your yes for that item; during a provider sign-in it may read your connected email or SMS for a link or code; accepted Chief of Staff jobs run scheduled turns that read PA's ledger and your USER.md or manual, may read your calendar and inbox, and search the web for your radar topics. Calendar writes need your yes for each item and go only to calendars you opted in to (gog's calendar.events scope), with one standing exception: during trip work the agent may add minimal private trip events (flight and hotel times, check-in and leave-for-airport reminders, no details or guests) without asking each time. The agent creates Kanban tasks for open commitments, and with your approval may adapt an existing brief cron job. Errands drive Hermes's browser tools on provider sites (Trip.com by default for flights and hotels, then airline or hotel sites or local sellers; reservation platforms, maps and guides for restaurants; another regional domain if blocked), in the local browser, agent-browser on Browserbase or another attended browser you configured, and provider sign-ins you give in chat are saved in the agent's credential lane and browser profile. What the agent reads and writes goes to your configured model provider as part of the conversation. Other network calls happen only when you ask or opt in: Browserbase (api.browserbase.com) with your BROWSERBASE_API_KEY and BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID, recording off for sessions PA creates, sessions kept alive up to 20 minutes, connect and live-view links visible to the model; PA holds no Google token and makes no Google API calls: the agent reads and writes calendars with the profile's own calendar tools, and Daily Ops reads them through the gog CLI (gog auth add stores gog's own credentials); parallel research subagents for SIM comparisons; Open-Meteo for an accepted trip watch; ElevenLabs read-only from the manual phone_poll command, with the declared ELEVENLABS_API_KEY read through Hermes's secret accessor; and opt-in Daily Ops (gog mail and calendar reads, with selected mail and calendar items sent to your model provider and email addresses aliased by pattern; Nominatim and OSRM through curl after geo consent; Stripe and Supabase CLIs after consent). Background work only after a yes: an accepted trip watch arms a HeartBeat 2.0 watcher that, once you allowlist it, runs a local PA script every 15 minutes for at most 14 days, and its notices wake an agent turn (a flight change may look up rebooking options, never book), plus optional check-in and arrival wakes; opt-in conversation delivery injects packets into one verified Telegram session as agent turns, with priority-mail excerpts not aliased; opt-in Daily Ops routines and an optional watchdog on the schedule you accept (every 20 minutes or less when leave-by alerts are on); accepted routine suggestions run a local precheck every 5 minutes (scripts stay in the profile's scripts/ folder); approved follow-up wakes (Chief of Staff, and open-loop follow-through wakes created only for a date you approve in chat). An accepted daily brief also sends an end-of-day note after eod_time (default 18:00) unless the brief itself is set after it, and accepted due-action checks also wake the agent for open-loop chase steps (day 2, 5 and 10, then an escalation), which only remind you or hold a nudge draft for your yes. Updates go through hermes plugins update; the version probe is read-only; developer eval scripts call model providers only when run by hand, with a token you pass in an environment variable (the optional lab judge runs the Codex CLI on its own sign-in), and PA code reads no saved login; the manual scripts/check_release.py reads this repo's GitHub releases through the gh CLI's own sign-in. PA's skills stop bookings, payments, reservations, orders and cancellations at the final page for your explicit yes, and its pre_tool_call gate enforces exact-action approval for actions a PA workflow has scoped; nothing dials a phone. No telemetry. Full list: the README's "What it touches".

entries.name: pethost
entries.description: Deploy and run Docker Compose projects on Pethost with its skill and Pethost's hosted MCP server: deploys, logs and requests, rollbacks, backups and restores, domains and commands in containers. Disclosure — connects Hermes to Pethost's hosted MCP server (mcp.pethost.dev), signed in by OAuth through `hermes mcp add pethost --url https://mcp.pethost.dev/mcp --auth oauth`, with no key or token in the package; the package marks its server untrusted, but that native entry replaces it and runs at trust: full unless mcp_servers.pethost.trust is set to untrusted, as the README's install does; tools act on the account's machine (deploys, restarts, restores, deletions, commands in containers); to move files the skill has Hermes run tar and curl in commands the skill writes, only to https at the machine's own hostname (*.pethost.network) under /transfer/, never a command the server returns, and says before an upload that the project folder goes as it is, .env included; it also has Hermes generate app secrets with openssl in the user's shell and fetches a deployed site to check it.
entries.title: Pethost
known_issues: The package's own connection is not signed in and registers no tools: the README's `hermes mcp add` step signs in by OAuth, and the native entry it writes overrides the package connection and trust setting.

entries.name: pfwa
entries.description: Provably fair randomness for Hermes, plus prediction markets on Robinhood Chain. pfwa_random gives a number, coin flips, winner picks from a list or a shuffle from a drand evmnet (League of Entropy) round chosen before it existed, with the round, signature and derivation so anyone can recheck it: for giveaways, raffles, draws and tie-breaks an LLM would otherwise make up. Market tools list PFWA's open markets, read live prices onchain, show a wallet's positions and claimable winnings, list results, and build unsigned buy, sell or claim transactions for the user's own wallet to sign; two more read HoodRand requests and the live Sherwood game round. Native Python plugin, standard library only, no keys and no configuration. Disclosure — Crypto: reads PFWA prediction markets on Robinhood Chain and builds unsigned buy, sell and claim transactions that you sign in your own wallet; it never holds keys or sends transactions. Network calls go only to www.pfwa.fun (the PFWA agent API), rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com (read-only eth_call; wallet addresses you ask about are sent in balanceOf calls) and drand's public relays (api.drand.sh, api2.drand.sh, api3.drand.sh).
