entries.name: photo-to-part
entries.description: Photo to Part for Hermes: turn photos, a few measurements, or a messy 3D scan into a parametric printable part, and check the mesh locally before you print. The agent writes the solid in code, checks that it is watertight and the right size, and renders views you can hold next to the original. Six tools: photo_part_template (watertight starting shapes such as plates with holes, an L-bracket, a print-in-place hinge, thread, knurl, hex standoff, bottle cap, spur gear and strap hinge), photo_part_build (runs one local build script after Hermes approval), photo_part_validate (watertightness, shell count, size, bores, printability and spec.json dimension checks), photo_part_render (fitted views, a comparison sheet and a silhouette overlay scored against your photo), photo_part_heal (weld, fill holes and clean up a scan) and photo_part_measure (pixels per millimetre from a coin, a ruler or an ArUco/AprilTag marker). Output is STL or 3MF; a STEP solid needs CadQuery or build123d in the project environment. A millimetre value you state is never replaced by a photo measurement. Hermes Desktop 0.23 or newer can show an optional Part studio pane with the stage, photo and overlay, renders, history and file paths while a run is in progress; the six tools still install and run when that pane is unavailable. It is for makers replacing a broken clip, bracket, knob, cap or gear, printing a fit test, or turning a scan into a clean solid. To start, run hermes plugins install photo-to-part and enable it, then start a new session. Attach a photo with a coin or ruler in frame, give any dimensions you know, and ask for a printable replacement. The skill id is photo-to-part:photo-to-printable-part. Pass that exact string only to skill_view. Do not pass it to skills_list, and do not add a plugin: prefix or a slash. Disclosure — files and network: tools read and write only the paths you pass (STL, 3MF, PNG, JSON), plus progress notes in a .photopart folder inside those project folders and a pane index under the Hermes plugin-data folder. Build scripts run with a minimal environment that carries no provider keys. No credentials and no printer connection. Enabling the plugin installs its Python packages from PyPI after Hermes dependency consent. Installing CadQuery or build123d for a STEP solid downloads packages and can take several minutes. Chat photos still go to your model provider. In a session that uses the plugin, it adds short tool-call budget notes (a 40-call default) to other tools' results. Disclosure — build approval: photo_part_build asks for approval before it runs a local Python file with a timeout. Hermes --yolo auto-approves a build prompt; this plugin does not block that flag.

entries.name: physis
entries.description: Offline evidence-backed execution memory: per-repo graph context, a deterministic verify hook, and verified tool recipes that replay with zero provider calls and refuse when their tools, registry or captured files changed. An opt-in pre-reasoning packet (pre_context) and an edit-following graph (auto_observe) are off by default; the packet reads an existing index only and is skipped when the graph is stale or retrieval is weak. Two bundled Linux engines and no API key or model download; approved host commands still run with host privileges and Python entry points need an interpreter, and untracked dependencies are not replay-checked. Operator-only approval and replay; the model cannot set executable paths or trigger raw commands. Disclosure — Ships two compiled Linux x86_64 engines (bin/physis-core, bin/replant) built and attested by the repo's own GitHub workflow; operator-approved replay commands and the operator's verify_cmd run as shell commands with the user's file and network access; physis_ingest can read shell history, ~/.claude/projects transcripts, every process's command line and the browser history database only when the operator enables those sources in plugins.entries.physis.settings.ingest_sources (off by default).
known_issues: Replay freshness is partial: only captured files up to 1 MiB are fingerprinted, so a dependency outside that set can change and replay will still proceed. The check that matters is the tool registry and engine digest; the captured-file set is a floor, not a proof of sameness.

Operator-approved commands execute with host privileges. Approval is a boundary on what the model may ask for, not a sandbox: an approved command can read any file the user can read and can reach the network.
Python entry points need a Python interpreter (standard library only). The two bundled engines are native ELF binaries; no interpreter is needed for them.
Bundled binaries are Linux x86_64 only.

entries.name: pickwise-photos
entries.description: A correction tool, not an art critic: culls a folder of photos locally. Flags blurry and unrecoverable shots, labels what an edit could rescue, keeps the best frame of every burst and explains every decision. Follows a brief in your own words ("concert, dark is fine, best 30", "moody low-key shots") and learns gradually from your corrections. Treats RAW+JPEG pairs as one photo, handles folders of thousands of photos in resumable steps, and reads JPEG, HEIC and camera or iPhone RAW (DNG, ARW, CR3, NEF and more) through their embedded previews, using only Pillow and pillow-heif. On request it makes local previews so Hermes can take a visual second look for closed eyes, a blurred subject or clear composition mistakes. Disclosure — reads image files in the folder you name (any folder the agent can reach; symlinks and hidden files skipped); writes only a Pickwise/ subfolder inside that folder (copy or reversible move) or .xmp rating sidecars that never replace existing ones; never deletes, overwrites or edits photos. The dry-run-then-confirm step is a tool argument the agent sets, not a Hermes approval prompt. Stores per-photo measurements, reports, learned preferences and (only when asked) downsized previews in its plugin data folder; no network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry. A visual check sends the chosen previews to the model provider through Hermes' own vision tool. Raises Pillow's image-size limit to 300 MP for the whole Hermes process.

entries.name: picky
entries.description: Picks the best place to sleep (tonight or for your dates) and the best ride there, then sets up the reservation: real OpenStreetMap stays auto-ranked by OSRM drive time with a one-line why and backups, Uber/Bolt/Lyft options with rough fare and ETA estimates, and Booking.com/Airbnb/Expedia/Google Hotels links prefilled with dates and guests. Never books, never pays, never asks for a card: you make the final tap. Disclosure — sends the place names or coordinates you ask about to nominatim.openstreetmap.org (geocoding and a backup stay search, max 1 req/s), overpass-api.de and fallback overpass.kumi.systems (nearby OSM lodging), router.project-osrm.org (driving) and routing.openstreetmap.de (walking). When use_current_location / 'my location' is requested, also contacts ipinfo.io or ipapi.co once for a city-level approximate location (used once, never cached or stored). Returns (does not contact) www.booking.com, www.airbnb.com, www.expedia.com, www.google.com (Maps, Hotels), m.uber.com, lyft.com, bolt.eu, wa.me and www.openstreetmap.org links. No API keys, no credentials, no telemetry, no self-updater, no binaries. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

entries.name: pilot
entries.description: Give Hermes a real interactive terminal. Pilot runs commands inside a private tmux server, so the agent can drive programs that need a TTY: ssh logins, vim/nano, htop/btop, fzf, less, package installers, ncurses menus and REPLs. It types literal text and named keys, reads the pane back as plain text, and keeps sessions alive across tool calls; a human can attach to the same pane and take over. The suite exposes 24 tools for session control, scripted expect flows, scrollback search, snapshots/diffs, logging, signals, resize, health and base64 file transfer. entries.name: pinocchio
entries.description: Pinocchio is the honesty layer for Hermes Agent: it keeps the receipts for everything the agent does and holds the agent's closing claims against them. A post_tool_call hook records work evidence for every session (commands and exit codes, test runs, builds, file writes, git operations, deploys); a transform_llm_output hook extracts the checkable claims in the agent's closing message (all tests pass, the build succeeds, a file was updated, changes are committed, it is deployed) and stamps the delivered message verified, unverified, or contradicted, citing the most recent matching receipt; a pre_verify hook bounces a contradicted claim back once on coding turns so the agent re-runs the failing step or corrects the record, and an all-time nose counter tallies the contradicted claims. Two tools (pinocchio_report, the session truth table, and pinocchio_receipts, the recorded evidence), a /pinocchio command (report, receipts, nose), and a bundled pinocchio-honesty skill that teaches the agent how to earn verified stamps. No second model grades the first: verdicts are deterministic comparisons between the agent's own words and its own tool receipts, in pure Python standard library. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands spawned by the plugin, no background processes, no credentials read or stored, no telemetry; the only storage is a local SQLite database in the active profile's plugin data directory holding tool-call metadata (tool name, truncated command or target, status, exit code, timestamp) and the claim snippets it stamped.

entries.name: pinpoint
entries.description: Audit mode and Design mode for the live page in Hermes Desktop's Browser pane. Measure it with in-page audits (contrast, tap targets, alt/labels, overflow, small text), pin findings on the real elements, point at any element to inspect its live box model, typography, layout and contrast, send a pin or an instruction to the agent, and re-audit to get a score delta, a pasteable receipt and a per-pin outcome: fixed (no longer reported and the same element signature is still present; not a re-measurement), gone (element signature missing, never counted as a fix) or not rechecked (unverifiable, stays open). Disclosure - Pinpoint's desktop half runs its own audit script inside the web page open in Hermes Desktop's Browser pane, only after you allow it for that site (Desktop's per-origin consent dialog; revocable under Capabilities > Plugins). The script reads computed styles, layout, the page's visible text, and the values of the attributes id, name, href, src, alt and aria-label (plus title and placeholder when it works out an element's accessible name); it contains no cookie access and does not read form-field values, and it draws an overlay. Findings (CSS selectors, short element labels that can contain page text, measured values) are stored locally in a SQLite file under the plugin-data folder (`pinpoint/data.db`; at most 20 pages, 200 pins and 50 audits per page; entries older than 7 days are pruned). They are sent to the model only when the agent calls `pinpoint_audit`/`pinpoint_pins` or when you click Fix, Fix all high or Send in the Desktop pane (or its command-palette action); an event raised by the page itself never sends a chat turn. Pinpoint also adds a short hint to the system prompt that names its two tools. The desktop half polls the page every 0.5-1 s while pins are shown (via `executeJavaScript`) and re-audits automatically after page changes (switch off in the pane). `pinpoint_audit` blocks up to 90 s waiting for the Desktop (configurable) and returns `desktop_unavailable` when no Desktop window answers, including under cron. No network calls, no subprocesses, no shell, no credentials, no telemetry, no files written outside plugin-data; it never edits your source (the agent does, under normal approvals). Limits: verified on Windows 11 with Hermes 0.22.7 only (macOS and Linux are untested). Results are a limited heuristic audit, not WCAG certification, and fixed / gone describe what this engine observed, not a guarantee about your page. entries.name: pioneer
entries.description: An inverted search for your own work. Pioneer reads your project folder, Hermes memory and recent chats, then looks for what does not exist yet and should. Your own model writes the gaps. Code checks every citation, runs an absence check against existing tools, and scores need, originality, counterfactual value, value and durability. When an existing tool already does the job, the board says so and names it. Rounds expand into a trail, shown on a Desktop page and pane. Disclosure — reads your project folder (README, agent rules, manifests, recent commit subjects), Hermes memory files and the title and first message of your last 14 days of chats (state.db, read-only) to build its seed for your own model; model-written search queries go to hn.algolia.com, api.github.com and api.openalex.org by default (api.firecrawl.dev and the api.typesafe.ai judge only when you turn them on).

entries.name: pipefire
entries.description: Pipefire (pipefire.ai) is cold email software for agencies that sets up and runs outreach for you. This plugin connects Hermes to Pipefire's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://pipefire.ai/mcp) and adds two skills. 16 free email deliverability tools with no account or key: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI and MTA-STS checks, blacklist lookups, email header analysis, cold email and subject line scoring, sending domain ideas and DNS record generators. Pipefire customers can sign in with OAuth to read campaigns, replies, mailboxes and results. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to pipefire.ai. The free tools look up public DNS and blacklist data. Account tools see only the signed-in team's data; the plugin stores no credentials. Every tool is annotated read-only except pause_campaign, resume_campaign, create_campaign (draft only), redraft_reply and request_lead_list; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before any of them runs and refuses them in unattended runs. Sending and launching happen only in the Pipefire console. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: pit-crew
entries.description: Proactive, safety-gated car agent: live state, a "will I be ready?" planner, a background watcher and approval-gated commands, with Home Assistant, Teslemetry/Tessie, TeslaMate or a built-in simulated car. Disclosure — once you switch it live with `/car live`, Pit Crew sends real commands to your vehicle (unlock, trunk, frunk, vent, Sentry-off, honk and flash go through Hermes's approval prompt and follow your approval setting), and its background watcher polls your configured Home Assistant / Teslemetry / Tessie / TeslaMate endpoint and posts alerts to the chats you bind.
entries.title: Pit Crew
known_issues: Unlock, trunk, frunk, vent, Sentry-off, honk and flash follow the user's Hermes approval setting (asked when approvals are on; not asked when off/yolo). The Advanced 'Always ask a person' setting (require_human_for) relies on Hermes' post_approval_response hook.

Only the Home Assistant tesla_fleet profile is built from recordings of a real car (verified live on a real Model Y: status, twelve no-approval commands and all seven approval-class commands, each confirmed by the car; that run had Hermes approvals off, so the approval prompt with approvals on is covered in CI only). The BMW and Kia/Hyundai profiles are verified against each integration's source and test fixtures, not run on a real car. Home Assistant removed its BMW Connected Drive integration in March 2026 (BMW blocked third-party access), so that profile only fits an install that still has the old entities; the Kia/Hyundai profile targets the kia_uvo HACS custom integration.

Home Assistant ships the Tesla Fleet Odometer, Shift state, Speed, Tire pressure and Tire pressure warning entities disabled; enable them for the odometer, the unlock/trunk motion check and the tire alerts (/car and car_status list the missing ones).

The direct Tesla adapter (Teslemetry / Tessie) is tested with mocks of tesla-fleet-api only; no live account was available. Tesla Fleet API (own developer app) works through Home Assistant; a native Fleet-direct mode waits on a Hermes OAuth enhancement.

entries.name: pixel-hq
entries.description: Gamified headquarters for a Hermes bot fleet: a pixel office of rooms and departments that you arrange in the page (Edit layout with drag and drop, live numbers per department: members, active, blocked, average HP, XP) and a class-based sprite per profile; each bot's character card shows its configuration (model pin, skills, toolsets, MCP servers) and edits its SOUL.md with a diff preview, a second confirming click and a restorable history; XP, levels and HP are scored automatically from Kanban outcomes (completed, changes requested, gave up, timed out, hallucinated references) plus optional pass/revise/fail reviews you give from the UI or that an orchestrator records with the `pixelhq_review` tool; a live board of what every bot is doing right now (current step, last tool call, tokens/cost, sub-agents, Kanban heartbeats) with Open session, Talk to this bot and Ask for status (prepares a draft, never submits it); a leaderboard; a blocked-card triage across all Kanban boards with Answer & unblock / Retry / Comment / Archive and a 'triage run' that opens a chat with your orchestrator profile; a GPU/LLM reactor panel; an Update available notice for Pixel HQ itself; and, if you configure it, a read-only view of the bots, activity and blocked cards of other hosts (host badge, data age, stale marker), fetched from a bundled exporter that writes nothing. Works on a fresh installation: the roster is generated from your profiles, edited in the Roster tab, and settings live in the Desktop app. Disclosure — reads every profile's config.yaml (model name) and state.db read-only (session titles, current step, tokens/cost and the last tool call with its first argument, e.g. a terminal command or path, clipped to 160 characters), every Kanban board database read-only, and the reviews ledger (plugin-data/pixel-hq/reviews.jsonl, plus an optional legacy ledger path you configure); through Hermes' own calls it reads a bot's profile (profiles.describe: SOUL, model pin, skill/toolset/MCP server names) when you open its Config section and the plugin list (plugins.manage list, at most every 6 h) for the update notice; no shell commands for reading; network only to the Prometheus / model endpoints you configure (none by default); bots on other hosts through the Desktop app's own connections and, only for sources you list in `remote_sources` (none by default), read-only: one fixed `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 -T <destination> pixelhq-export` call per source without a shell and with an explicit environment, only while a snapshot is collected (the remote account's forced command runs the exporter; entries.name: plan-mode
entries.description: Plan mode for Hermes Agent: it explores read-only and writes a plan, and its edit tools stay blocked until you approve. Approval comes as a Claude Code-style card; Hermes' Codex app-server runtime and TUI /background and btw side agents are outside the block (see the Disclosure). It works on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Hermes approvals are on, every write_file and patch then gets Hermes' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo_list progress; on Telegram, Discord, Slack, Desktop and the TUI a live progress card lists the plan's steps and updates as each one finishes. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan_profile: classic), approval_card: false and surfaces without a card use Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions (say "grill me" for more, or set questions: thorough for an interview before every plan, one decision at a time), the reply names any tool call plan mode blocked (Hermes itself shows none), and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan_style, plan_profile, questions, allow_commits and plan_skill settings). When an approved plan finishes, the reply ends with one line of steps done and files changed (counts only on chat platforms); /planmode list shows the newest plans with their status, and the agent can read its own state with plan_mode(inspect) or list. Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 or newer recommended, tested through 0.23.1. On the interactive classic CLI, Hermes' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Hermes' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .hermes/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state, plus the status of up to 200 plans for /planmode list, in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. While an approved plan runs it posts one progress message through Hermes' post_message and edits it in place (progress_card: false turns it off). When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Hermes core writes a plugin_rule:plan-mode entry to command_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow_gateway_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan_once) it reads the visible reply text from post_api_request while planning and saves its <proposed_plan> block as the plan file; if another plugin holds the stream to withhold commentary, that text can include the commentary it kept off screen (plan_profile: classic turns plan_once off, unless a custom levers list names plan_once or all). On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write_once) it checks that Hermes printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.

entries.name: plan-usage
entries.description: Plan usage across providers in the Hermes Desktop status bar: a named chip per Claude and ChatGPT/Codex account in Hermes's credential pool (5-hour and weekly windows from Hermes's own usage cache via model.options, a default-account star, account-switch / all-out warnings and an opt-in 90% warning that name the next account), Nous Portal credits, and month-to-date (UTC) API spend from optional Anthropic / OpenAI Admin keys. Preferences are a Settings -> Plugins page. Disclosure — its own network calls go only to api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/cost_report and api.openai.com/v1/organization/costs, and only with the optional ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY / OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY config_schema secrets read through get_secret, with redirects refused; Nous credits come from Hermes's build_credits_view (Hermes makes the Portal request); never reads or sends a subscription token, never opens .env or auth.json; writes only its own settings in plugin-data, the shown-warning ids in Desktop plugin storage, and, on an explicit star click, the credential-pool order through CredentialPool.move_entry; no subprocesses, no telemetry.
entries.title: Plan Usage
known_issues: Claude windows at exactly 1% used can show as 100% (and warn): Hermes core reads Anthropic's utilization as a 0-1 fraction. Plan Usage shows what Hermes reports. Upstream issue NousResearch/hermes-agent#145660 (fix PRs #139916 and #145663, both open).
Usage rows are matched to pool accounts by label in pool order; give each account its own --label so two accounts are never confused.

entries.name: plansift
entries.description: Exact, local review of OpenTofu and Terraform plans before apply, from the JSON of a saved plan (`tofu show -json` / `terraform show -json`). tf_plan_summary gives exact counts per action, every delete, replace and forget with the plan's reason and the attributes forcing the replacement, drift detected outside the tool, changed outputs, failing checks and the modules and resource types with the most changes; tf_plan_changes gives an attribute-level before/after diff (JSON policies stored in strings are diffed inside), filterable by action and address and paged; tf_plan_check gates the plan on denied actions for address patterns, a change budget, drift and failing checks. Sensitive values, text under secret-like attribute names, variable values and output values are never returned. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs tofu or terraform), no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local plan file you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.

entries.name: playbox
entries.description: Collaborate with other people's Hermes agents in a private room: share a git repo, run sandboxed tasks, and keep a signed, tamper-evident history. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package wrapping the local 'playbox mcp' server, with a host/guest workflow skill. Requires the separately installed playbox binary. Disclosure — runs the separately installed `playbox mcp` binary (installed by the user from github.com/Epistetechnician/playbox releases; v0.1.0 is checksum-checked but not signed); hosting opens an iroh endpoint reachable through n0's public relays and discovery by default (`transport: local` keeps it on the LAN); a host started with a runtime (`docker`, `libkrun`, `openshell`) runs commands from invited remote members in a no-network, resource-limited sandbox on the host machine; git bundles, patches and chat are exchanged with invited members, and their text is untrusted input; keys, histories and room state are written under `~/.playbox`.

entries.name: plugin-safehouse
entries.description: Runs one local Hermes plugin inside a disposable, canary-seeded macOS profile; invokes its registered handlers and reports observed file, environment, network, process, persistence, and model-context behavior as FLAGGED, REVIEW, INCONCLUSIVE, or NO_FLAGS_OBSERVED. Disclosure — the model-callable `safehouse_trial` tool (and `/safehouse`) executes the chosen local plugin's register() and handlers without a Hermes approval prompt, inside a short-lived macOS sandbox-exec worker with a scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME, fake canary credentials and a minimal environment; the sandbox profile is allow-default with network, fork/exec, signals to other processes, LaunchServices and writes outside a temporary trial root denied, so files outside the user's home and non-LaunchServices system services remain reachable; the trial root is removed afterwards. The report returned to the model includes short candidate-controlled text (handler return values up to 300 chars, worker stderr tail up to 1200 chars) with canary tokens redacted. It imports PluginManager and calls the private _scan_directory/_load_plugin loader inside the disposable worker so the candidate registers through Hermes' real loader; this is a disclosed compatibility risk. The installed plugin makes no third-party network calls, stores no credentials, sends no telemetry, and starts no long-running background process. Optional repository-only launch scripts invoke local ffmpeg.

entries.name: plugin-scout
entries.description: A scout goes ahead, reports what's useful, and warns about trouble. Plugin Scout finds the plugins that fit how you use Hermes (each pick with its evidence), and checks: it tells you what a plugin does with your data before you install it, warns when a plugin's fine print does not fit your settings, catches plugins that clash and explains what to do. Quiet weekly note, plain-English requests, and a dashboard tab. Recommends only; never installs or enables anything. Disclosure: one network call, a GET of the public catalog index from hermes-agent.nousresearch.com (redirects to nousresearch.github.io/hermes-agent; any other address or redirect is refused), cached 6 hours. Reads, read-only, the last 30 days of session history (up to 200 sessions) to count tools used and topic keywords locally, plus Hermes memory files and the user's own (non-bundled) skill list for the same local topic matching, plus config.yaml (enabled plugins, memory provider, and settings named in plugins' known issues), other plugins' plugin.yaml and plugins/.install-metadata.json. Writes only its own plugin-data folder and plugin state. The dashboard tab adds routes under /api/plugins/plugin-scout on Hermes's own local dashboard, behind its sign-in; the only changes they make are your onboarding choices and skipped picks. Optional ai modes send topic counts and public catalog descriptions to the user's configured model; message text is never sent. No shell commands, credentials or background processes.

entries.name: plugin_foundry
entries.description: Turn a narrow plugin request into a native Hermes plugin: manifest, entry point, tool, SQLite state, tests, static scan and catalog draft. Two archetypes only: a SQLite folder watcher and a JSON API poller, each with one tool. The folder-watcher parser accepts one explicit supported file type or complete dotted suffix and refuses unsupported, composite, conflicting or ambiguous requests. A trailing period is removed only at request end or before validated supported follow-up instructions. Sentence boundaries are detected before a capitalised token or complete instruction verb, but that detection alone does not permit removal; other prose fails closed, and abbreviations without a sentence start stay inside the instruction. Writes stay under the Foundry data root, generated tests run in a minimal environment, and paths outside the root need a pre-tool approval. Provides pre_tool_call and post_approval_response hooks plus the public tool_execution middleware for trusted call IDs. Foundry itself makes no network requests. Installing or cataloguing generated code is a separate human step; nothing is auto-merged.

known_issues: Declared runtime floor is Hermes >=0.23.0. The public plugin API at 0.21.5 was audited, but runtime and approval acceptance is only recorded on v0.23.

The watcher parser intentionally rejects ambiguous or unsupported file-type prose rather than guessing. Use one explicit type, for example CSV files; arbitrary sentence wording is not supported.
Generated code is not installed, published or catalogued automatically. A human must review and install it.

entries.name: pocket-platform
entries.description: A native Hermes platform for an owner-enrolled low-bandwidth radio companion: bounded chat replies, notes and opt-in P2/R2 home-music controls. Requires a separately provisioned radio/USB bridge and a new dedicated, unrouted, in-process Pocket-only Hermes home. Model tool execution is blocked in that dedicated process; installation alone does not block unrelated tool calls. Disclosure: the adapter listens on a private local Unix socket with peer-UID and HMAC authentication. POCKET_HMAC_KEY is read through Hermes's scoped secret helper; the bridge is provisioned independently. Local request identities, notes and replay state are journaled. Optional location reads an operator-set SQLite snapshot; optional music reads approved local files through an existing loopback HTTP service. Normal chat uses the operator's Hermes model/provider and may leave the host and incur provider charges. No arbitrary model tools, shell commands, self-updater, telemetry, bundled firmware or media. The source includes bridge libraries, not a turnkey standalone radio service or handheld firmware installer. The source qualification uses synthetic provider/HTTP fixtures and does not certify this published package's physical RF or audio.

entries.description: Real-time Pokémon GO hunting inside Hermes, with a live Radar, nearby catches and raids, approved scans, and desktop alerts. entries.name: policy-backtester
entries.description: A test harness for Hermes guardrails: what a rule would break, and what it would miss, on your agents' real work. hermes backtest try replays the current profile's past tool calls through a policy, names the completed cron or Kanban jobs it would have broken and the sessions it would have caught, checks it against known calls it should stop, then starts it in shadow, which logs and changes nothing; log says when every scheduled job has run untouched, and enforce blocks or hands the call to Hermes's approval gate. Enforce refuses a policy that hasn't run in shadow, would break a job, or hasn't seen every scheduled job run. Built-in guard rules keep an agent from switching its own guard off. run, diff, suggest (exemptions pinned to each broken job's exact command and folder, never applied) and check (one call, or a cases file for CI) are the tools under it. Disclosure — reads the state.db, cron/jobs.json, cron/executions.db and Kanban board databases of the profiles a command covers, read-only (SQLite mode=ro); writes its own index (<root>/backtest/index.db, 0600) and, in profiles where you promote a policy, the policy copy, promotions.jsonl, decisions.jsonl and three plugin settings; the index and log keep tool names, arguments (file bodies replaced by a length, commands unredacted) and result status, never result bodies; in shadow or enforce mode its pre_tool_call hook checks every tool call, and enforce blocks calls or sends them to Hermes's approval prompt. No network calls, no shell commands, no telemetry.
entries.title: Policy Backtester
known_issues: Enforce is a policy gate, not a security boundary: rules see what a command says, not what it does, and code an agent writes and runs can get past them.
Enforcement runs per profile: install it and promote a policy in each profile you guard.
A backtest can't vouch for a scheduled job it never saw run; it names those jobs, and enforce waits for one completed run of each.
The install scan reports caution: the shipped policies, tests and README quote the commands the plugin exists to catch.

entries.name: polign-recall
entries.description: Recall by Polign memory provider. A new statement replaces the old one, the old one stays in the history, and memory can be read as of any earlier time, so the agent sees the correction, not just the latest value. Memories in front of each turn, extraction after it, mirroring of MEMORY.md, and five memory tools. Local database under the profile by default, or a recall serve you run. Disclosure. Each turn is sent to the extraction model named in the profile (Anthropic or OpenAI key from .env, or a local Ollama model); with no model, text is kept as written and nothing leaves the machine. On first use the recall binary downloads polign-server from dl.polign.com and checks it against a SHA-256 built into the binary. Disclosure — each completed turn (up to 4,000 characters per message) and every built-in memory write is sent to the extraction model picked from the profile's Anthropic or OpenAI key (or a configured Ollama model; set extract_model to none to keep text local), or to the recall serve named by RECALL_URL; in the default local mode the polign-recall package's bundled recall binary downloads polign-server from dl.polign.com on first use (checked against a SHA-256 built into the binary) and starts it as a detached loopback server under $HERMES_HOME/recall that keeps running after Hermes exits.

entries.name: pollinations
entries.description:
Pollinations image generation and editing for image_generate.

The picker is read live from the Pollinations catalog, so it lists whatever Pollinations publishes and follows changes without a plugin update. No key is needed for the free route, which watermarks images and throttles per IP. A Pollinations key unlocks the rest of the catalog and image editing. Paid-only models stay hidden behind a toggle that ships off. Disclosure — sends prompts and any reference images to Pollinations (gen.pollinations.ai, image.pollinations.ai); with no key the free classic route is used (prompt in the request URL, watermarked, throttled per IP). A reference image given as a URL is downloaded from that host first (public addresses only, through Hermes' SSRF guard) and a local reference path may be any image file the user can read (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, checked by magic bytes); both are then uploaded to Pollinations. With POLLINATIONS_API_KEY set, generation and editing spend the account's Pollen; the "Include paid models" toggle only hides paid-only models in the picker, a paid model set by id is still billed. Caches the model catalog and free-model list under $HERMES_HOME/cache/ and writes images under $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/images/. No telemetry, no shell, no background processes, no self-update.

entries.name: polydesk
entries.description: Agent paper-trading desk for Polymarket: research a market, quote a trade against the live CLOB order book (fills sweep real book levels, so slippage is realistic), confirm with a single-use 5-minute ticket that is re-priced at execution, then track mark-to-market P&L with automatic settlement when markets resolve. Risk limits (max trade, max % of equity per outcome, max slippage, liquidity checks), a persistent ledger, a /desk command and a bundled workflow skill. The paper bankroll can be backed 1:1 by testnet USDC in a linked Base Sepolia wallet. Disclosure — HTTPS GETs only to gamma-api.polymarket.com and clob.polymarket.com (the client refuses other hosts); when polydesk_wallet is used, JSON-RPC eth_chainId/eth_getBalance/eth_call (USDC balanceOf) to sepolia.base.org or the configured rpc_url, which receives the linked public address; stores a SQLite ledger in the profile's plugin-data/polydesk/desk.db; no keys, signing, transactions or real orders. Paper trading only; not financial advice.
known_issues: Polymarket's API is blocked by some ISPs and regions; tools then return a 'could not reach Polymarket' error instead of stale data.

entries.name: polyglot
entries.description: Live interpreter for group chats on the Hermes gateway (Telegram, Discord): an authorized user sends /polyglot on in a group, and every message from a sender Hermes admits is then translated into each other member's reading language, returned as the reply. Languages are learned from each person's first message or set with /lang; "hermes, ..." or an @mention still reaches Hermes as a normal question. Translates with the user's own Hermes model; a Sarvam AI key is optional for Indian languages. Disclosure — registers one hook (post_gateway_admission, so it runs only after Hermes's authorization) and two commands (/polyglot, /lang), no tools; in chats where an authorized user ran /polyglot on, message text from admitted members goes to the configured model provider through Hermes's ctx.llm, and, only if SARVAM_API_KEY is set, text for Indian languages goes to https://api.sarvam.ai; translations are posted back to the group as the bot's reply, and ordinary group messages in those chats no longer start an agent turn; stores each group's member languages and display names in Hermes's plugin state; no file reads, shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

entries.name: polytropos-router
entries.description: Model provider polytropos-router with one model, auto. For each turn a short classifier call picks the simple or the complex route, and the router tries that route's models in order. A local Ollama model only gets the turn when the machine has memory to spare and the request fits its context window, otherwise the turn goes to free cloud models through FreeLLMAPI. Set it up with the polytropos plugin. Disclosure — sends each turn to the upstreams in its config, which are FreeLLMAPI and Ollama on 127.0.0.1 by default, or any other OpenAI-compatible URL the user adds; the classifier sends up to 2,000 characters of the last user message to the classifier model, FreeLLMAPI's auto model by default, also when the turn then runs locally; asks the Ollama API for its version and loaded models and unloads a local model when memory runs low; reads memory pressure with sysctl on macOS or /proc on Linux; fetches stack-canary's public results from raw.githubusercontent.com at most once a day; traces are off by default and never hold message text; reads upstream keys through agent.secret_scope; no telemetry.
entries.title: Polytropos router
known_issues: Hermes needs FREELLMAPI_API_KEY for every turn on the router, also when all routes are local.
Has not been tried in a real Hermes home or on Linux yet. The end-to-end tests run Hermes v0.23.2 in a sandbox on macOS.

entries.name: popquiz
entries.description: Pop Quiz, the room vs the models: any document becomes a live quiz for the whole room in about a minute. Hermes writes the questions and the plugin refuses every question whose quote is not found verbatim in the document; people join from their phones with a QR code (no app, no account) while up to four Nous Portal models play the same questions on the same clock, with latency and cost on screen (a free preset plays models the Portal prices at $0); the report says what the room got wrong and which model understood the document best, for what cost. Disclosure — runs an aiohttp web server on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default while a quiz is up (it stops 10 minutes after the game ends); "Open to phones" (the /popquiz command, or the agent calling popquiz_control open_lan without an approval prompt) adds one listener on the machine's private LAN address (never all interfaces), plain HTTP, and from then on anyone on that network can watch the projector page (questions, source quotes, room code), join as a player and read the end-of-game report; the host page and host commands need the host token and a loopback client (with a public_url tunnel every visitor arrives as loopback, so only the token protects them); model players are ctx.llm calls on your Nous Portal account, started when the game starts (the agent can start it), paid unless you pick the free preset, capped per game by budget_usd (default 1 USD) against estimated costs, with no cap for a model the public price list does not know (a custom players entry, or your main model when the llm.model_override and llm.provider_override capabilities are not granted); in open_book mode each call carries the document text (up to 400 000 characters); if the Portal refuses a call, Hermes may retry it on its fallback chain and then on your main model and provider, and such answers are labelled fallback model; at the end of a game the report (with player nicknames typed by the people in the room) is posted into the chat as a user message, which starts a model turn; fetches the public Nous Portal model list for prices at most once a day (no key sent) and caches it in its plugin state, the only thing it writes; reads only the document the agent is given, inside the session folder or the Hermes document cache; an opt-in Desktop pane frames the projector page in the SDK's SandboxedFrame; no telemetry.
entries.title: Pop Quiz
known_issues: Tested on Linux (Ubuntu 26.04); macOS and Windows are not tested yet.
Phones must reach the host machine on the local network; guest Wi-Fi with client isolation blocks them.
Paid model players need Nous Portal credit; without it their answers are refused ($0) and the game still runs for the humans. The free preset needs no credit.
The Desktop pane was checked in headless Chromium with the same sandboxed frame, not yet inside the Desktop app.

entries.name: post-cortex
entries.description: Self-hosted long-term memory through a post-cortex daemon (https://github.com/julymetodiev/post-cortex): typed records (decisions, fixed problems, code changes) in an entity graph with local semantic search. Recalls related records from the profile's workspace before each turn, puts the user card and the workspace's project card in the system prompt, mirrors built-in memory writes as records, and adds post_cortex_search, post_cortex_record and post_cortex_context (graph neighbours and reverse dependencies of named components) plus the post-cortex:memory skill. Records and captured turns carry the author hermes:<profile>. Profiles are mapped to shared workspaces by name glob, so a team of profiles recalls each other's records. Disclosure — talks only to the post-cortex daemon at the configured URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3737; a remote daemon over plain HTTP should sit on a private network or behind TLS): each non-trivial user prompt (up to 2,000 characters) is sent as a search query, and built-in memory writes and post_cortex_record calls are sent as records; with the opt-in capture setting (off by default) each completed turn of the primary agent is sent too: the user's message (with the sender's display name when Hermes knows it), the final reply, tool names and file paths, never tool output; nothing goes to third parties. Disclosure — the daemon stores records (and captured turns, deleted after its message_retention_days) in its own database and redacts credentials, e-mail addresses, phone numbers and public IPv4 addresses on write. Disclosure — PCX_TOKEN (and optionally PCX_URL) is read through the Hermes secret scope; the only local state is $HERMES_HOME/post-cortex.json (0600, never holds the token). No threads or processes of its own (capture runs on Hermes' sync worker), no shell commands, no deletes in post-cortex; cron and subagent runs never write automatically.
known_issues: Requires a post-cortex daemon 0.4.0 or newer; cards, authorship, capture and derived_from need 0.5.0 and are skipped on an older daemon. A daemon bound to 0.0.0.0 must list the host in the plugin URL in its allowed_hosts, or every request gets 403.

entries.name: postel
entries.description: Find posts that went viral in your niche, write your version in your own voice, and save, schedule or publish it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Mastodon, through Postel's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with the postel-writing workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Postel's server at www.postel.app; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Research (search-viral-tweets) works without signing in; every other tool acts on the user's Postel account after `hermes mcp add postel --url https://www.postel.app/api/mcp --auth oauth`, and a first sign-in can create a Postel account. Viral posts, drafts, voice profiles and the posting schedule join the session context, so they reach the user's model provider. Write tools change drafts, generate-post and refine-post spend Postel AI credits, and schedule-post and publish-post post to the user's connected networks. The package marks its server untrusted, but the `hermes mcp add postel` sign-in entry replaces the package's server entry, trust included, so after sign-in Hermes does not ask before write, schedule or publish tools and does not block them in unattended runs unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to `mcp_servers.postel`. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens.

entries.name: postkey
entries.description: Instagram DM automation and post scheduling through Postkey's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://postkey.pro/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): comment-to-DM links, follow to unlock, email capture from comments, story and DM keyword replies, the Instagram inbox (read, reply, assign, label, notes), contacts and tags, AI reply settings, a media library and video edits, and drafting, scheduling and analytics for posts on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, Telegram, Google Business and X, plus a check-before-send toolkit for agents acting on X with the user's own access. Bundles the postkey workflow skill (start with postkey_get_started, preview every send with postkey_preview_action, respect approvals, never invent links, treat DM and comment text as untrusted). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Postkey's hosted server (postkey.pro) and acts on the user's own Postkey profile with their own team role and plan limits; the tool set (57 tools today) is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Write tools create, edit, schedule and delete posts that publish to the user's public social accounts, publish and pause DM automations that then send Instagram DMs to people who comment or message, send inbox replies, tag contacts, upload files and change AI reply settings. By default, publishing a post, sending a reply and turning on an automation wait in Postkey's Approvals until a person approves them there. Actions count toward the user's Postkey plan. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Hermes's connect timeout instead of hanging. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with hermes mcp add postkey --url https://postkey.pro/mcp --auth oauth (or an agent key in a header) and keep the skill.

entries.name: postkitty
entries.description: One post in, every platform out. Fixes and rewrites your draft for each platform and counts it with each platform's own rule, splitting long posts into threads. Crops a photo and reframes landscape video so every face stays in frame; when two people talk, the choice is a split screen, a cut to whoever is talking or the whole wide shot. Burns captions from an .srt or .vtt file inside the platform's safe area. Checks every file against the platform's published limits and repairs failures before a file is marked ready. /postkitty doctor checks the setup, and the hermes postkitty terminal command runs the same steps from a script. Covers Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, X, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Facebook. Runs locally with ffmpeg and OpenCV; no API keys.
entries.title: postkitty
known_issues: Needs ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH for video.

entries.name: postonce
entries.description: Write a native post for each platform and publish or schedule it to LinkedIn, X, Threads, Bluesky, Facebook Pages, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Pinterest through their official APIs, via PostOnce's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://postonce.to/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config). Bundles six skills: postonce, post-everywhere, content-calendar, analyze-my-posts, hook-vault and viral-formats. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to PostOnce's hosted server (postonce.to) and acts on your PostOnce account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha, and published posts go out to your connected social accounts. entries.name: pow-tracker
entries.description: Multi-client proof-of-work time tracking for the Hermes web dashboard — live OPEN/CLOSED timers, file-activity auto-capture, invoicing with per-entry rate overrides, and per-client SQLite billing, in a dashboard pane/tab (track / entries / tasks / invoice / rate views, updating live over a WebSocket) backed by a FastAPI plugin API the dashboard host mounts. Every client keeps its own time database inside its own folder, so billable data travels with the client folder; invoices aggregate billable time per task, exportable as CSV (PDF through an optional, lazily-imported extra); and a background auto-capture thread (per-client, off by default) opens and closes `auto` entries from file activity while you work. It has run a real multi-client operation in production since August, and no client data ships with the tree. Disclosure — registers no tools, hooks or middleware (dashboard tab + plugin API only) and makes no outbound network requests; on load it creates SQLite files outside Hermes' data dir, in the configurable clients root (default `~/Documents/Clients`): a registry at `.pow-tracker/clients.db`, a `Default` client folder, and a `.pow-time/time.db` inside every sub-folder of that root it auto-registers as a client; a background thread in the dashboard process polls every 5 s and, only for clients where you switch auto-capture on (off by default), walks that client's folder reading file modification times (never names or contents) to open and close time entries.

entries.name: ppq
entries.description: PayPerQ (ppq.ai) OpenAI-compatible model provider for Hermes — per-response cost estimation from ppq's published rate card, chat model discovery from GET /v1/models, automatic per-request Zero Data Retention opt-in, and a 3-layer picker pin strategy (user-local pins file → live top chat models from ppq's public stats dashboard → generic static fallback; generic installs never get the author's personal pins). Disclosure — model provider; PPQ_API_KEY and all prompts, tool schemas and responses go to ppq.ai (PayPerQ; terms https://ppq.ai/terms, contact matt@ppq.ai), a relay that routes requests to third-party inference partners, some outside the user's jurisdiction, and frontier providers still see prompts; usage is billed per request from the user's prepaid PayPerQ balance (funded by card or cryptocurrency on ppq.ai; the plugin itself makes no payments). Privacy protections are opt-in per request: for models badged privacyLevel 'zdr' the plugin automatically sends provider={"zdr": true, "data_collection": "deny"} so requests route only to endpoints with a Zero Data Retention policy that do not collect data (the zdr model set refreshes hourly from an unauthenticated GET /v1/models with a pinned fallback); models badged 'e2e' run inside TEE enclaves with no opt-in flag needed — enclave coverage applies to chat by default, not to image/video/audio, and true end-to-end encryption is only available via the optional local ppq-privacy-verifier proxy. Building the model picker, for any provider, starts a background unauthenticated POST to stats.ppq.ai at most hourly to fetch the top chat models; cost estimates and personal picker pins read optional local files under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/ppq/ (prices.json, pins.json) that the plugin does not create, so costs show as unknown without a price snapshot. Additional caveats: Claude Opus 4.8 with web search enabled drops the ZDR guarantee, and some Anthropic/Gemini models may override the provider routing fields (order/only/ignore).

entries.name: precedent-log
entries.description: Saves a human's answer to a blocked Kanban question as a ruling for later workers. Shows rulings and vetoes in Desktop with confirmed retirement. Disclosure — Saves human rulings under HERMES_HOME/precedent-log/ and injects matching rulings into Kanban worker prompts; in the default enforce mode it vetoes a worker's kanban_block up to twice per task when an active ruling matches, which can leave a no-edit worker's card running (set precedent_log.veto: advisory to only annotate). In calls carrying a Kanban task marker on boards with active rulings it blocks execute_code and process stdin writes (precedent_log.guard: strict extends this to every marked worker and delegated subagent), and blocks worker commands that name its store. Reads four private Hermes board/delegation helpers (read-only, no core overrides) that may break on a core update. Desktop reads and retires rulings through host-routed gateway slash RPC, possibly to a remote gateway. No network calls, shell, credentials or telemetry in the plugin runtime; the bundled demo/ harness is opt-in and spawns subprocesses and provider calls when run.
known_issues: Four private board/execution-identity helpers require catalog rule 9 review; catalog/CORE-ISSUE.md is an unsubmitted request. No core overrides.
In-process mode only; the host does not supply the tested execution context or CLI path.
Default enforce mode can leave a no-edit worker's card running after veto (B2). Core recovery/retry settings apply; no deadline. Advisory avoids this veto path.
Tested only on Hermes v0.23.0 at 2bd378ed1b8d6bf2192cb26e0a55ff3091e6bd19; the floor does not establish later compatibility.

Desktop catalog description, navigation, no-session guidance, status, page badges and confirmed retirement live-run verified with v0.4.1 in an isolated home with a fake model on Hermes source 2bd378ed, Desktop built from source; v0.4.0 also verified status click-through. entries.name: precleared
entries.description: Checks cold email against the law before it goes out: when the agent sends an email with a send tool, one of Hermes's email skills (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace) or an email API call, Precleared checks each new recipient against UK PECR and UK GDPR, US CAN-SPAM, Canada's CASL and German, French, Australian, Irish and Dutch rules; anything not cleared goes to Hermes's approval prompt (or is refused in block mode) with the rule, its source and a signed receipt. Adds precleared_check and precleared_verify_receipt tools and a cold-email-check skill. Disclosure — when the agent sends email through a send tool, an email skill (himalaya, agentmail, Google Workspace), a mailer command or an email-API call, and on every precleared_check call, the plugin sends each new recipient's address with the configured sender country, address source, pitch and optional prospect country to precleared.dev over HTTPS; Precleared keeps a signed receipt of each check that anyone holding the receipt id can open at precleared.dev/r/<id>. The optional PRECLEARED_API_KEY is read through Hermes's secret scope and sent only in the Authorization header; without a key, checks draw on a free allowance shared by everyone on the same network. Emails not cleared go to Hermes's approval prompt (or are refused in block mode), and verdicts are cached under hashed addresses in plugin state for 30 days. No shell commands, background processes or telemetry; maintained by the operator of Precleared.

entries.name: precog
entries.description: Hermes stops repeating its own mistakes: learns every terminal command that failed for an environment reason (missing module, command not found, wrong package manager, bad flag, missing path) and the command that fixed it, then fixes the same mistake before it runs again, in any session, with no extra model calls. Disclosure — reads every terminal tool call's arguments and results and stores redacted commands and short error excerpts locally in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/precog/; in auto mode (the default) rewrites a terminal command through tool_request middleware before Hermes's approval check, using a fix that already succeeded in the same project (a program or flag fix seen in two projects is applied machine-wide), and tells the model in the tool result; once per session blocks a command that already failed in the project and shows what worked, and adds a short lessons briefing to the user turn once per project; no network calls, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: preflight
entries.description: Approval dry-run gate: runs every terminal command in a disposable copy of the workspace (reflink/copy, no Docker), shows a per-file review before the exact diff, and applies only what the user approves. Disclosure — preflight is a dry-run gate, not an isolation sandbox: agent shell commands run as host processes in a copy of the workspace under the Hermes home's `sandbox/` folder, with a filtered environment and HOME pointed at the copy; its path guards are best-effort pattern matching, and scripts or commands that build paths at run time can still reach files outside the copy; `sandboxctl apply` copies the whole pending change set into the real workspace and deletes files that were removed in the copy.

entries.name: preview-text-size
entries.description: Larger or smaller text in the Hermes Desktop file preview pane: scales the rendered Markdown from 90% to 175%, independent of Chat Text Size and UI Scale, through a row in Settings → Appearance, three command-palette entries and rebindable shortcuts (⌘⌥=, ⌘⌥-, ⌘⌥0 on macOS; unbound by default on Windows and Linux, where Ctrl+Alt is AltGr). entries.name: print-job-watch
entries.description: Each watch run costs 0 tokens, and the unmanned run holds no tools. Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT_URL with your OCTOPRINT_API_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel return one pre_tool_call approve line. Hermes shows it. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt while a person is present. cron, hermes -q, webhook, and unattended sessions refuse the move, including after always. plugins.isolation: host still refuses the move. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" on pause or resume adds a permanent allowlist line to config.yaml, so a later pause or resume of that same action at the same origin runs without asking while a person is present, until you remove that line. Each cancel asks again. Answering always on cancel does not cover the next cancel. cron, hermes -q, and webhook do not use that line. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. hermes print-job-watch schedule writes HERMES_HOME/scripts/print-job-watch.py and creates one cron job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. This is the same when HERMES_HOME is HOME/.hermes and when HERMES_HOME points somewhere else. unschedule removes that job and that script in both places. The job does not call a model. Empty script output sends nothing. The script binds the profile secret scope and then reads the URL and API key, and it does not print the key. The default schedule is every 5 minutes. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. Running schedule again switches an existing job in place with hermes cron edit --script --no-agent. A job made by 0.1.x keeps its model turn until the next schedule. The create command cannot set a tool list, which does not matter because the unmanned run holds no tools. Under plugins.isolation: host, the print_job_watch tool cannot watch the printer. Set plugins.isolation to in_process. The scheduled script is not that form, so that setting does not stop the watch. The job and the script stay after uninstall until you run unschedule, which removes both. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam. A request that sent the API key is not followed on a redirect, including one that stays on the same origin.

entries.name: print-tools
entries.description: Printer-agnostic Linux CUPS printing for Hermes: queue status, files, wrapped text, and styled one-page letters. Disclosure — every print tool call sends a real job to a CUPS queue installed on this machine (local or network printer, 1-5 copies, at most 20 pages) with no approval prompt; `print_file` reads a model-chosen JPEG/PNG/PDF/TXT/MD file under your home or temp directory (20 MB limit) and sends it to that printer; runs `lpstat`, `lp`, Ghostscript (`gs -dSAFER`), the CUPS `texttopdf` filter, `fc-match` and a Pillow letter renderer as child processes with a minimal environment (no Hermes keys forwarded); no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no credentials.

entries.name: print3d
entries.description: Turn an idea, a photo of an object, or a shop listing into a sliced Bambu Studio project. The agent writes a Blender script, print3d checks the mesh (overhangs, thin walls, fits between parts, likeness to the photo), slices it and says what to fix, until it prints clean; each run also writes a 3D view the agent opens in the Desktop preview pane. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one skill and a stdio MCP server run through uvx, so Blender 4.2+, Bambu Studio and uv are required; at install Hermes looks for Blender in the standard locations (/Applications and Steam on macOS; PATH, flatpak, snap and Steam on Linux) and refuses the install without it. Disclosure — runs Blender and the Bambu Studio CLI as local child processes; Blender runs the agent-written Python with your user's permissions, outside Hermes's terminal sandbox, and the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool that runs a script or changes a job (the read-only tools still write preview images and the 3D view under ~/print3d/jobs without asking); installs Pillow and mcp from PyPI; the 3D view loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net; the optional `print3d setup` command (not needed for a catalog install) edits Hermes, Codex, Claude, Cursor and Gemini config files, with backups. Never contacts the printer; no telemetry, no credentials.
known_issues: Tested on macOS, where Blender and Bambu Studio are found automatically. On Linux, Blender must be on PATH or installed with flatpak, snap or Steam for the install to go through; set BAMBU_STUDIO_BIN if Studio is not on PATH.
Bambu Studio is not checked at install; without it, make stops at the slice step and says to install it or set BAMBU_STUDIO_BIN.
The skill folder is a symlink, so Windows is not supported.

entries.name: printsi
entries.description: Get a PDF professionally printed and delivered. 19 MCP tools: a free preflight that reads the PDF from disk (bleed, trim size, safe areas, image resolution, fonts, colour) and returns each issue with its position and fix plus the page preview as an image; quotes for printing with tracked delivery; a payment link a person pays on Stripe; order tracking and support tickets. A Hermes Desktop pane draws the page to scale with each issue marked, and shows the order's progress with a pay button. Flyers, cards, brochures, stickers, calendars, posters, banners, canvas and wall prints, mugs, bags, T-shirts and hoodies, delivered in the contiguous US. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + one skill) with a desktop/plugin.js; no Python. The stdio MCP server ships in the package as one readable, unminified JavaScript file (server/printsi.mjs, run with node; Node.js 18+ required), so nothing is downloaded at run time; its TypeScript source and a locked build that reproduces it are in the repository under source/. Disclosure — calls the printsi API (printsi-api-live.magnus-ahmad.workers.dev) and nothing else; uploads the PDF being checked or printed and sends the delivery name, address, phone and email to printsi and its print supplier; saves check previews to a temp folder the server creates; orders cost real money, but the plugin cannot pay: order_purchase returns a link and a person pays on Stripe, with the card held until the printer accepts; the server is marked untrusted and only tools that send nothing of the user's are marked read-only, so Hermes asks before every tool that uploads a file, sends an address or changes something; a tool argument can name no file except the PDF, and no folder to write to; no account is needed: on first use it mints a printsi guest key and keeps it, with order tokens, in the plugin's own data folder in the Hermes profile, and reads no other credential store; the Desktop pane only reads this plugin's own tool results (no network, no files, no tool calls) and opens printsi's payment page in the browser when the user presses the button; the skill's optional helper scripts run Chrome and Ghostscript locally and fetch segno from PyPI through uvx; no telemetry (PRINTSI_TELEMETRY=0), no update checks, no self-updating code.

entries.name: printwatch
entries.description: Control 3D printers over the local network from your agent: fleet status (temps, progress, layers), file listing, print start/pause/resume/cancel, file upload with automatic dialect packaging (printer_upload), and camera snapshots delivered into chat. Dual protocol — Anycubic Kobra printers over their built-in stock LAN Mode (clean-room reverse-engineered handshake + MQTT; no cloud, no rooting, nothing flashed) and Klipper/Moonraker over HTTP, and Bambu Lab printers over their local MQTT/FTPS interface (user's LAN access code; X1/P1/A1 family). Includes a headless slice-to-print pipeline: any raw .gcode is repackaged into the exact Anycubic .gcode.3mf dialect the stock firmware requires (header blocks, M75, uppercase-MD5 sidecar, X-ACNext slice info) and started remotely. Disclosure — connects only to the printer hosts the user configures (PRINTWATCH_PRINTERS / PRINTWATCH_BAMBU / PRINTWATCH_MOONRAKER_URL via agent.secret_scope); printer_print, printer_upload, printer_pause_resume and printer_cancel move physical hardware and ask for Hermes approval on every call (refused when no human is present); printer_upload sends a local .gcode/.3mf file the model names to the configured printer; printer_snapshot shells out to ffmpeg, and for Bambu printers the LAN access code is visible in ffmpeg's process arguments for the ~2s capture; Anycubic MQTT and Bambu FTPS/MQTT accept the printer's self-signed certificate (CERT_NONE) on the local network; no telemetry, no external services, no credentials persisted.
entries.title: PrintWatch
known_issues: printer_snapshot requires ffmpeg on PATH.
Bambu adapter verified against the documented protocol (community-verified X1C fw 01.12 wire format) plus a simulated printer; physical-printer verification pending community feedback.
Anycubic LAN Mode must be enabled on the printer (built-in settings toggle, stock firmware).
Camera snapshots work only on printers with an Anycubic camera attached; the tool fails cleanly (printer error 11401) otherwise.
Bambu RTSP snapshots expose the LAN access code in the local process argv for the ~2s capture window (ffmpeg RTSP limitation; local-only exposure, documented).

entries.name: priors
entries.description: Pay HTTP 402 (x402) APIs on credit: when the agent's wallet is short, it borrows the gap in USDG from its Priors credit line on Robinhood Chain, pays, and repays; before paying another ERC-8004 agent it reads that agent's repayment record. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables. Disclosure — payments plugin for Priors: the priors-wallet server runs the local priors-mcp command (npm @priors/mcp, installed by the user, not bundled; the README pins 0.14.1) and signs payments, loans, repayments, savings, stock and market trades and Autopay allowances in USDG on Robinhood Chain mainnet with the key named by PRIORS_KEY_FILE (or PRIORS_KEY) in the profile's .env; both servers are marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write-capable call, and where nobody can answer (chat -q, cron, the gateway without a prompt) the call is declined and nothing is paid; pay_url pays only https hosts listed in PRIORS_PAY_HOSTS when it is set (any public https host when it is not), at most max_price_usd a call, and borrows only when max_borrow_usd is given (a loan is at least the pool's minimum, 5 USDG today); a loan more than three days late can be marked defaulted, which ends the agent's record on Priors; the hosted read-only server (https://mcp.priors.trade/mcp) receives the tools' public arguments (agent ids, addresses) and counts connections by the client's runtime name only; the tool sets are served by @priors/mcp and the hosted server at runtime and are not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: privacy-xray
entries.description: Where does your data actually go? Records every outgoing model request, the main loop and side tasks such as title generation, compression and vision, as metadata only: destination host, vendor, vendor HQ country, the model vendor behind aggregators such as OpenRouter (read from the model id; the final processing vendor behind an aggregator is not visible), size and counts of detected personal data types (e-mail, IBAN, payment card, phone, IPv4, German Steuer-ID and USt-IdNr, own watch terms). /xray canary invents a fictitious person and /xray trace shows every request and local store that carried it. /xray check audits the config with a severity and the exact hermes config set fix per path; /xray fix <id> --yes applies one; a session retention hint is advice only and is never applied. /xray fix --yes and /xray find run only on local surfaces (CLI, TUI, desktop, dashboard) unless allow_sensitive_on_gateways is turned on. /xray find searches the local stores for a person, /xray report writes a self-contained HTML leak map (no scripts, no external assets) with a before and after view of two canaries; a dashboard tab shows the same page in a sandboxed frame. Not legal advice and not a compliance certificate. Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls, standard library only. pre_api_request and pre_auxiliary_call are observers; they write one metadata line per request (time, session and turn id, task, provider, model, host, vendor, counts, canary id and message fields; never message text or matched values) to HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/privacy-xray/ledger.jsonl (rotated once at ledger_max_mb, default 5 MB). The llm_request middleware is off by default (guard: false); when turned on it masks canary values and watch terms in main model requests before they are sent. Reads the merged Hermes config through load_config_readonly. /xray trace, /xray find and /xray check read outside the plugin's own data, read-only and under a time budget (scan_seconds, default 30): state.db (messages, session titles, stored system prompts, delivery queue), session files including request dumps, memories, logs, cron output, other plugins' plugin-data, paste and pending folders; output shows counts and masked snippets only. Writes config only on /xray fix <id> --yes, through hermes_cli.config.set_config_value (same code as hermes config set); never deletes files. Stores fake canary persons, last check and trace results and requested HTML or Markdown/JSON reports under its plugin-data folder. Registers the tool privacy_xray (map, check, trace, find; read-only, never changes settings), the slash command /xray and a skill that adds one line to the skills index of every session while the plugin is enabled. No credentials, no shell commands, no cron jobs, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: proactive-continuity
entries.description: Keeps your agent working through multi-step tasks without losing pending work: it continues to the next step on its own, lists open Kanban cards in each new session, gives a catch-up after idle time, and asks for approval before anything that sends, posts, pays or deploys. Glue over built-in Kanban, cron and approvals; works with any model. Disclosure — adds working rules to the system prompt; sends the agent a continue message on its own (at most 6 per session per hour, needs allow_gateway_injection on messaging platforms). The user-run `hermes proactive-continuity setup` backs up config.yaml and SOUL.md, changes approval and display settings through `hermes config set`, enables the kanban toolset, grants itself allow_gateway_injection, copies one script into the Hermes scripts folder and creates a paused cron job; uninstall reverses this. No network calls and no telemetry.
