entries.name: procgen-studio
entries.description: Image and video backend that draws with code. Your configured model writes SVG/Python drawing programs, which are rendered locally to PNG (and MP4/GIF) with the editable source and a reproducible seed saved next to each image. No image API key, STYLE.md art contracts with six presets, a critic pass with bounded redraws, local seed re-rolls and restyles, /procgen and hermes procgen commands, and a Desktop pane. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; every model call goes through ctx.llm on the user's configured provider (the procgen_draw / procgen_critic auxiliary slots when pinned); runs model-written Python drawing programs in a separate sandboxed Python process (AST import allowlist, audit hook refusing network, subprocess and file access outside the job directory, CPU/memory/file-size limits, wall-clock timeout; allow_python: false switches to SVG/pixel-only); invokes the system ffmpeg as a subprocess for video only; reads a STYLE.md from the session working directory when it has a preset:/palette: line; writes renders under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/procgen-studio/ and $HERMES_HOME/cache/generated/, plus an optional user-configured output folder; no telemetry, credentials, background processes or self-updates. Installs cairosvg (needs the system cairo library), numpy and Pillow.
entries.title: Procgen Studio
known_issues: Not for photorealism; it is built for icons, game assets, logos, flat illustrations, scenes, patterns, diagrams, low-poly creatures and motion graphics.
cairosvg ignores SVG filters (no blur); glows and soft shadows are drawn with gradients.
Output quality tracks the configured model's coding ability; small local models produce simpler drawings.

entries.name: profile-chip
entries.description: Draft-aware profile readout for the Hermes Desktop status bar. On a multi-profile or multi-gateway desktop, a fresh Ctrl+N draft shows no profile anywhere until the first message creates the stored session; this chip names the owner up front in the left status-bar cluster, using the core profile glyph and deterministic identity color (home codicon for default, soft-tinted initial tile for named profiles). Hover shows the gateway label so two gateways' default profiles never read alike; click re-reads the connection registry. Disclosure: reads profile, connection and focused-session state through the public Desktop SDK only. No agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; no network calls, filesystem access, shell, credentials or telemetry.

entries.name: profile-switcher
entries.description: The Alt+Tab gesture for Hermes profiles. Hold Ctrl+Alt and tap Tab to cycle through your profiles, release to land on the highlighted one — the same hold-tap-release rhythm as the OS app switcher. (Alt+Tab, Win+Tab and Cmd+Tab are owned by the window manager and cannot be bound by any application, so the gesture lives on ctrl+alt+tab, unclaimed by the OS and by Hermes core.) Each row shows the profile's model and most recent conversation; a working profile shows a spinner. Also opens with a single contributed keybind (Cmd+Alt+P / Ctrl+Alt+P, rebindable in the app's own keybind panel), a status-bar chip, and a palette command. The switch goes through the Desktop's own profile path, so the target profile's backend is activated and its chrome is scoped onto it. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, network calls, or stored credentials.

entries.name: project-command-center
entries.description: A board for every Hermes Project: lane, live sessions, token spend, git branch and GitHub issues and pull requests in one place, with a detail page per project. Click an issue and a session opens inside that project's folder with the issue number, title and URL already in the composer, unsent. Branch rows open a session in a worktree or after a checkout, and each session carries its own lane, so a PR climbing to review is visible where the work happens. Includes a GitHub reader with full issue and PR modals, comments, status filters and a Zed-style commit graph. Disclosure — reads your git repositories and their history, switches branches and creates worktrees under `<repo>/.worktrees/` when you ask it to from the board (refusing on a dirty tree, an in-progress merge, a branch checked out elsewhere or an existing target; git's own repo hooks run as they would in your shell), and comments on or closes issues and PRs as your authenticated gh account. Board state lives in a local SQLite file under the Hermes home. Two hooks read a terminal call's `gh pr create` output to link the PR and move the session to review, and inject one short line naming the session's own card into each turn; each has its own kill file (`auto_link.off`, `card_context.off`). Network calls go to api.github.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com, and a favicon of a homepage a project declares.

entries.name: project-manager
entries.description: Git workbench for the Hermes Dashboard and Desktop: discovers the git repositories under the folders you watch, and inspects or changes them per file — stage, unstage, diff and discard — plus commit, push, pull, branches, commits and worktrees. Disclosure — reads the watch paths from its own SQLite table (under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/project-manager) and git metadata (branch, remote, ahead/behind, commit subjects, status and diff text) from the repositories under them, and lists folder names under any path you type when adding a watch folder; file contents are read only as diff text returned to the requesting UI; the five agent tools are read-only. Writes on request only from the Dashboard/Desktop UI: git add, commit, push, stash (including stash -u before a branch switch), fetch, merge --ff-only (also as "pull all" across every watched repository), restore, clean -f, git switch, and git worktree remove (including --force and remove-all). Discard on a tracked file restores it from HEAD and drops the uncommitted edits; on a file in no commit (untracked or staged-new) it leaves the bytes on disk but nothing here can restore a version of it, and both sit behind a confirmation naming which one you are doing. The Desktop Chat button starts a new Hermes session whose working directory is that project's folder, and the project name and branch chip open the repository's remote URL in your system browser. The optional standalone server (project_manager_server.py, 127.0.0.1:9120) requires a per-run token printed to its log. No outbound network, no model call, no API keys; git fetch/push contact the remote named in the request (the UI sends the repository's own remote).
entries.title: Project Manager
entries.capability_summary: project-manager (community, maintained by AiSolve-me) Git workbench for the Hermes Dashboard and Desktop: discovers the git repositories under the folders you watch, and inspects or changes them per file — stage, unstage, diff and discard — plus commit, push, pull, branches, commits and worktrees. Disclosure — reads the watch paths from its own SQLite table (under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/project-manager) and git metadata (branch, remote, ahead/behind, commit subjects, status and diff text) from the repositories under them, and lists folder names under any path you type when adding a watch folder; file contents are read only as diff text returned to the requesting UI; the five agent tools are read-only. Writes on request only from the Dashboard/Desktop UI: git add, commit, push, stash (including stash -u before a branch switch), fetch, merge --ff-only (also as "pull all" across every watched repository), restore, clean -f, git switch, and git worktree remove (including --force and remove-all). Discard on a tracked file restores it from HEAD and drops the uncommitted edits; on a file in no commit (untracked or staged-new) it leaves the bytes on disk but nothing here can restore a version of it, and both sit behind a confirmation naming which one you are doing. The Desktop Chat button starts a new Hermes session whose working directory is that project's folder, and the project name and branch chip open the repository's remote URL in your system browser. The optional standalone server (project_manager_server.py, 127.0.0.1:9120) requires a per-run token printed to its log. No outbound network, no model call, no API keys; git fetch/push contact the remote named in the request (the UI sends the repository's own remote). This plugin registers tool(s): list_projects, get_project, list_branches, get_recent_commits, list_watch_paths. Requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.name: promise-keeper
entries.description: Tell Hermes a rule once ("never touch the prod folder", "ask me before you change migrations", "never force push"). It proposes an exact rule quoting your words; you turn it on with /promise or the Desktop panel. Every tool call is then checked twice (pre_tool_call, and tool_execution middleware on the final arguments) by deterministic code, and a block quotes you. Each rule shows what is enforced, best effort and not covered. Local only: rules in plugin data, no network, no telemetry; reads scripts, Makefiles, package.json and git config of calls it checks. Disclosure — every tool call is checked by a pre_tool_call hook and tool_execution middleware that can block it, or send it to Hermes' approval prompt, under rules the user confirmed (via /promise or the Desktop Promises panel); to judge a call it reads the scripts, Makefiles, package.json, the repo's .git/config and ~/.gitconfig the call refers to and runs `git ls-files` in the target folder; rules and a block history are stored locally in plugin-data/promise-keeper/rules.db, with no network I/O.
entries.title: Promise Keeper
known_issues: Terminal commands are read best effort: an opaque binary that writes files on its own can't be seen; code that names a protected path is blocked to be safe.
Not covered: other plugins' tools that write without a path argument, or a plugin's pre_tool_call hook that rewrites arguments after Promise Keeper's checks.
A process that obtains the dashboard session token is as trusted as the UI (a Hermes-wide limit, not specific to this plugin).

entries.name: prompt-enhancer
entries.description: A composer button for Hermes Desktop that first repairs dictation typos in the draft, then rewrites it into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape); one click back restores the original typing, and ⌥-click repairs without enhancing. ⌘-click picks the model both steps use (written to auxiliary.prompt_* in config.yaml; the prompt_repair / prompt_enhancement task slots are registered by the plugin, as current Hermes builds require). Ships three rebindable keybind actions in Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts (enhance / repair-only / enhance-with-previous-turn, unbound by default). Also ships a /enhance slash command (mobile app / Telegram / TUI: fix / raw / copy modes) and a POST /enhance HTTP door for iOS Shortcuts, running the same two templates host-side with the shared model config. Reads the session's own history (local, read-only) to build a proper-noun list for the repair step. Preserves @file and /command chips plus inline /skill references verbatim; per-session state. Multi-composer isolation: parallel sessions enhance independently and each result writes back to its own composer in real time; a result from a switched-away session applies automatically on return (never overwrites manual edits). UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

entries.name: prompt-firewall
entries.description: Community security-preview plugin that detects and quarantines selected prompt-injection patterns in tool results and evaluates risky tool actions; limited to hook/Core enforcement semantics. Disclosure — Rewrites tool results the agent sees: spans that match its injection heuristics are replaced with `[QUARANTINED:<category>]` markers, and output past its scan budget (or output it fails to scan) is withheld with a notice; may block or escalate to the Hermes approval prompt writes to protected config/instruction/credential paths, endpoint changes and commands that disable prompt-firewall; adds a fixed trust-boundary notice to every turn; to pick the approval card's language it reads `HERMES_LANGUAGE`, `display.language` and, read-only, your last few messages in the current session; appends metadata-only audit records (tool name, target path, reason) to `<HERMES_HOME>/logs/prompt-firewall.jsonl`. No network.
entries.title: Prompt Firewall
known_issues: Security preview, not a sandbox; detection is heuristic and incomplete.
Approval decisions depend on Hermes Core and can be bypassed by auto-approval settings.

entries.name: prompt-queue
entries.description: Kanban-style prompt queue for the desktop: Play drains cards one at a time into per-card target modes — new session, existing session, project, or a profile's canonical Bot Chat — gated on the global model slot, background-review completion, and context compaction. Queue/Done/Skipped/ Failed tabs, two-row target picker, markdown ingest (Windows), and a trust-aware ::enqueue directive (ask-first by default). Disclosure — Desktop pane that runs queued prompts as full agent turns (all tools the session allows) in new or chosen existing sessions, projects it can create, or a hidden per-profile "Bot Chat" session while Play is on; reads recent agent.log lines to detect background reviews and context compaction; on Windows the markdown-ingest menu runs local shell commands (mkdir, dir, certutil, explorer, and python on a small bundled reader script it writes into the chosen folder) through Hermes's shell.exec; an opt-in Auto-add setting lets ::enqueue directives in a live assistant reply queue prompts that run without a click.

entries.name: promptli-comms
entries.description: Give Hermes its own email address and phone number: a gateway platform for Promptli Comms, so people email, text or call the agent and each person gets their own Hermes session across channels, with replies sent back on the channel they used; calls are taken by Promptli's AI voice assistant, which asks Hermes for answers (or Hermes speaks every word with PROMPTLI_VOICE=agent), and the caller is always told they are talking to an AI. Disclosure — talks only to Promptli (HTTPS to api.comms.promptli.com, plus one outbound Agent Link WebSocket held open while the gateway runs, so no public URL or open port is needed); sends message bodies, call text and destination addresses or numbers to Promptli; `hermes promptli setup` saves an identity-scoped Promptli API key in the active profile's .env through Hermes's save_env_value (an organization key, if pasted, is used once to mint the agent key and never stored), and `hermes promptli mcp` adds the hosted Promptli MCP server (OAuth via `hermes mcp login`, trust: untrusted) to config.yaml; the key is read through Hermes's secret scope; a pre_tool_call hook refuses outbound Promptli tools in conversations started by people outside PROMPTLI_ALLOWED_USERS, refuses a call opening that does not say the caller is an AI and limits calls to Indian (+91) numbers to 9 AM-9 PM IST; only PROMPTLI_ALLOWED_USERS (or everyone, with PROMPTLI_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true) can reach Hermes, and their sessions get only the web and todo toolsets and no MCP servers by default; stores the Agent Link cursor, processed event ids and reply routes in plugin data (state.db); Python dependencies promptli and promptli-gateway (>=0.2.2,<0.3) carry the transport code and are not covered by the pinned sha; no shell commands, child processes, telemetry or self-update.

entries.name: proof-lens
entries.description: Verify a DRAT refutation and profile its proof depth as a Desktop pane. Pick a CNF and a trace; every accepted line is re-derived by unit propagation (RUP only), and the pane reports the empty clause's certificate depth plus a histogram of derived clauses by depth. Deletions are ignored rather than replayed (sound, strictly more permissive than a deletion-aware checker). Disclosure — reads only the two files chosen in the browser file dialog; all work runs in the renderer; no network calls, no shell commands, no stored files.

entries.name: proof-run
entries.description: Proof Run records a successful Hermes task at the tool boundary and saves it as a procedure with named inputs. A guided run tells a cheaper follower each step and checks every action before it executes; strict exact guards and checked-execution workflows remain available beside it. Disclosure — recorded tool calls, arguments and results are saved as procedures in the plugin's data folder (values matching common secret patterns are refused); during a guided or guarded run its pre_tool_call hook blocks any tool call that does not match the saved procedure; /proof run continues a run as a background task in the Hermes process; the optional workflow follower sends step prompts only to a local Ollama server on 127.0.0.1/localhost; the checked-execution workflow mode works only on a Hermes build carrying the author's hand-applied host patch (integration/hermes-checked-execution.patch) and refuses to run otherwise; no other network, no telemetry.

entries.name: proofgate
entries.description: No proof, no done. Verifies an agent's completion claims (file created, message sent, command ran, tests passed, figures quoted) against the tool evidence recorded in the same session, before the final reply is delivered. Unproven claims are flagged as unverified or withheld, fail closed, and every verdict is written to an append-only ledger stored locally in $HERMES_HOME/proofgate/. Disclosure — observes every tool call and final reply in profiles where it is enabled and stores tool arguments (sensitive-named keys redacted) and the first 800 characters of every tool result, unredacted, in append-only files under $HERMES_HOME/proofgate/ with no rotation; makes no network calls; in the default enforce mode it holds reply streaming and may append warnings to or entirely withhold a reply judged by keyword heuristics to contain unproven claims.

entries.name: proofly
entries.description: Checks an agent's claimed Base mainnet transfers against chain evidence: tx hash, receipt status, recipient, token and exact raw amount, over read-only JSON-RPC. It annotates results from the payment tools you list in its payment_tools setting and corrects unsupported "payment sent" claims in the final reply; adds the read-only proofly_verify_tx tool and the /proofly command. Disclosure — sends read-only JSON-RPC requests (tx hashes) only to the configured Base RPC endpoint (default https://mainnet.base.org), whose operator sees the hashes and your IP; replaces the results of the payment tools you list in payment_tools with its verdict and rewrites unsupported payment claims in the final reply; stores a verdict ledger (tx hash, verdict, expected and observed transfer fields, HMACs of session and turn ids, newest 300 rows) in plugin-data/proofly; registers transform_llm_output with hold_stream, so every reply in a profile that loads it is shown only after the check; no keys, signing, wallets, .env reads, shell, background processes, self-update or telemetry.
entries.title: Proofly
known_issues: Holds every reply in a profile that loads it until the check has run (hold_stream). Tool progress and reasoning are not rewritten; turn them off (display.tool_progress, display.show_reasoning) for strict use.

entries.name: proofops
entries.description: Verification for AI agent completion claims: turn "the agent said done" into a sealed receipt of what was checked, what was observed, and what passing does NOT prove. Hermes runs a declared plan of read-only checks against a live service, a deliverable or a system of record, and gets a receipt: each check's actual result, what it proves, and - printed on every receipt - what passing does NOT prove. Fourteen check types: HTTP status/JSON/body/headers, command exit codes, file and directory inventory, checksums, CSV shape, image dimensions, PDF pages/size/text, and read-only SQLite queries. Receipts are sealed with a sha256 digest and can be HMAC-signed, so editing a verdict after the run is detectable; `verify` reports valid / tampered / unsealed / needs-key. A check that could not run is reported NOT RUN - never a green tick - and the receipt carries claimable: false. Refuses undeclared origins, undeclared commands, unknown check types, and paths outside the operator's allowed_paths. Disclosure - network: HTTP GET only, against origins the plan names, resolving each host once and connecting only to the addresses it classified (every redirect hop too), refusing loopback/private/link-local addresses unless the operator allows local targets, environment proxies ignored; shell: exactly the argv a plan lists, and only when the operator also lists that command verbatim in plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_commands - there is no approval prompt inside a tool call, because there is nobody to answer one; reads: no file or SQLite access at all until the operator sets plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_paths (an unset fence is a denial, not a default), then only inside the operator's roots and the plan's, SQLite opened read-only and single-statement; storage: receipts under the plugin's own data directory containing observed values, hostname, cwd and command output; credentials: none read or stored, signing is CLI-only; no telemetry by default and no network access at import or registration; telemetry exists only as an explicit opt-in: a one-time "Send anonymous diagnostics" checkbox after the first run, framed as the feedback that decides what gets fixed next, where Enter leaves it unchecked and the refusal is remembered and the exact bytes printable via `proofops share --dry-run` sending an anonymous six-field aggregate (random install id, version, platform, run and plan counts, pass/fail/not-run counts) that `proofops share --dry-run` prints in full beforehand, with version and platform allow-listed on both client and server so no name, path or hostname can be stored; the aggregate carries pass/fail/not-run totals plus the same totals per check type from a closed set of fourteen, so the report can say what kind of thing is verified (web service, file, PDF, database) without saying whose, and is published at https://rasrobo.github.io/proofops/metrics/ Disclosure — network: HTTP GET only, to origins the plan names, connecting only to addresses it resolved and classified (every redirect hop too, proxies ignored) and refusing loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT and other non-global addresses unless the operator sets allow_local_targets; shell: only a command the plan lists verbatim AND the operator lists in plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_commands, run without a shell and with PATH/HOME/LANG plus operator-listed env vars; reads: no file or SQLite access until the operator sets plugins.entries.proofops.settings.allowed_paths, then only inside those roots, SQLite read-only; storage: receipts under the plugin's data directory, containing observed values, hostname, cwd and command output; credentials: none read, signing is CLI-only; telemetry: none from the Hermes plugin, the standalone `proofops` CLI can send an opt-in anonymous aggregate to t.sqs.chat after a one-time prompt.

entries.name: protocol-chaos
entries.description: Long-lived matters shared by all your assistants, kept on your own Protocol Chaos server (draft 0.2): Hermes sees an overview of your open matters and the details of the ones a message names, records your words after it answers and folds them into that matter's goal, limits, plan, progress and state, and a bundled skill organizes what every assistant recorded once a day. Runs beside your memory provider, not instead of it. Disclosure — each new session's system prompt (not a scheduled job's; subagent sessions included) gets an overview of open matters, up to 3,900 characters. Before each turn the plugin fetches the server's directory (cached 30 seconds) and reads, by id, up to three matters whose titles share words with the message; the message itself is never sent to the server. After each answer, a background call to the auxiliary model Hermes routes for protocol_chaos_capture (the compression model by default) receives the user's message, up to 600 characters of the previous reply, the matters' titles and states and today's date; when it decides to record, the user's words, copied verbatim, are sent to the server at PROTOCOL_CHAOS_URL with PROTOCOL_CHAOS_TOKEN, and a second call receives that matter's fields, up to six earlier words, the titles of its larger matters and parts, and the last few messages with the reply (about 6,000 characters), and the fields it returns are written to the server. Nothing else is contacted and there is no telemetry; logs hold ids, counts, times and token counts. Like any plugin's added context, the matters added to a turn are saved with it in Hermes's session history and resent on later turns. Cron and subagent turns get no per-turn context and record nothing. The bundled organizer skill runs only as a scheduled job the user creates, uses the server's MCP tools, and keeps a checkpoint at ~/.hermes/protocol-chaos/organizer-checkpoint.

entries.name: protonpass
entries.description: Proton Pass secret source: resolves pass://vault/item/field references (mapped source "protonpass") or every env-var-titled item of one vault (bulk source "protonpass_vault") into environment variables at startup through the user's own pass-cli, beside the built-in Bitwarden and 1Password sources, with a hermes protonpass setup/status/token/set/remove/sync/disable CLI. Stdlib-only, no Python deps. Disclosure — when enabled, runs the user-installed pass-cli (argv only, allowlisted env, 30 s per call), which talks to Proton's API; a personal access token or AI-agent token is read from Hermes' env and passed only to the pass-cli login child's environment (never argv); writes a 0700 session dir under cache/protonpass and a 0600 value cache (cache_ttl_seconds: 0 disables); no self-update, no downloaded binaries, no telemetry, no background process.

entries.name: prove-it
entries.description: Checks an agent's completion claims against local read-only probes before you read the reply: HEAD vs the remote-tracking ref for a push, git cat-file for a commit, a file stat for a write, observable output for tests pass. No model in the check. The footer says ✓ verified, ✗ contradicted, ⚠ could not verify, or ⏸ blocked on an approval; /proveit explain shows the claim, the probe and the raw output. Disclosure — runs local read-only git commands (rev-parse, merge-base, log, cat-file) in the repository the agent worked in this turn, with fsmonitor and ext protocols disabled and no stdin; never contacts a remote or authenticates; stats absolute file paths named in the agent's reply; makes no probe when the terminal backend is not local; stores a bounded ledger (arguments and output only for terminal, file-write, code-execution and delegation calls, truncated, secrets pattern-redacted, deleted after 7 days) plus checked claims and approval pattern/description (never command text) in plugin-data/prove-it/data.db; every probe has a 2 s timeout and the footer a 4 s budget; a plugin error never withholds the reply in footer mode; no telemetry

entries.name: proveit-tests
entries.description: Flags recognizable ways an agent weakens tests to reach green: removed or loosened asserts, skip/xfail/.only, deleted tests, expected literals rewritten to match failing output, assert True and tautologies, try/except pass wrappers, and test-runner escape hatches (pytest || true, -k "not ...", --deselect, --passWithNoTests, CI continue-on-error), and pytest config / conftest.py narrowing (addopts -k/-m/--deselect/--ignore, testpaths, collect_ignore, deselecting hooks). Net-new only: each edit is compared with the file as it was before, so pre-existing skips are not blamed on the edit. Deterministic AST + regex, no model calls. Modes: observe (default), escalate to the human-approval gate, or block on unattended/cron runs. SHA-256 receipts and a /proveit ledger. Python-strong; JS/TS coverage is heuristic and limited. Disclosure — no network calls and no model calls. Reads edited test, CI, pytest-config and conftest.py files and tool arguments to compare before/after; appends warnings into tool results; may escalate or block tool calls when configured. Ledger is written only under the Hermes plugin data dir (in-memory if none); terminal findings keep a short, secret-redacted command excerpt locally. Not a sandbox and not unbypassable: an agent can still rewrite via shell, disable the plugin, or invent new weakenings. No findings is not proof that tests were preserved.

entries.name: provenance-gate
entries.description: Flags memory and skill_manage writes that state a user decision ("the user decided ...", "用户决定 ...") without the user's own words: each such sentence needs a quote that appears verbatim in text the user typed in this session, shares key words with the decision and does not drop a negation. A patch is checked by the text it produces. Observe mode (the default) records flagged writes and `hermes provenance-gate report` lists them; block mode refuses them and tells the model how to fix the write. Measured on an independent blind set of 133 lines: precision 1.000, recall 0.694. Disclosure — two hooks (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call); keeps a local copy of the text the user types, with its sender_id and session link, and an evidence log of checked claims under plugin-data/provenance-gate (30-day default retention, `hermes provenance-gate purge`); reads MEMORY.md, USER.md and skill files to reproduce what a patch produces; no network, no credentials, never asks for approval.

entries.name: provider-status
entries.description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Hermes environment keys on exhaust, and an expired OAuth token asks for a new login. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent. Disclosure — Reads provider API keys from the Hermes .env and its own config.json and calls each enabled provider's own usage or billing endpoint; Codex and Grok sign-ins use those CLIs' OAuth client identity and user-agent, keep the plugin's tokens in its install folder, and ask for a new login on expiry. When the Discord gateway runs, the bot's Discord presence (visible to everyone in servers the bot shares) is updated every 20 seconds by default with tokens/sec, context-window use and the active provider's name with its remaining quota or dollar credit balance (model and running tool are opt-in); turn it off with plugins.entries.provider-status.settings.discord_presence_enabled: false. /pulse and the agent_pulse tool report process-wide telemetry (model, provider, current tool, quota) to anyone allowed to call them on a gateway. Writes a secret-free quota-cache.json into its install folder and reads Hermes config.yaml for the active model.

entries.name: provider-usage
entries.description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Hermes desktop status bar. Pinned providers in the bar (or the current chat's provider when none are pinned), a popover sorted by risk with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, a per-window usage chart over the whole window with burn rate and projected run-out, a yellow watch tint and an amber near-limit tint, and a desktop notification at a per-window alert level. entries.name: proving-ground
entries.description: A wiring test for your plugin stack: known, harmless test calls go through every installed plugin in a throwaway child Hermes home with the model never called, and each cell shows which plugin blocked, rewrote, changed the result, gated for approval, or passed it through. Disclosure — Runs every enabled directory plugin's own code in child Hermes processes under the system temp dir with your file permissions (approvals forced to deny, model never called, plugin settings with secret-shaped names withheld); the first warm-up copies your local Hermes runtime or, if none exists, lets Hermes's installer download about 650 MB.
entries.title: Proving Ground
known_issues: Spawns child hermes processes with throwaway homes under the temp dir; the first run copies Hermes's runtime from your local installs (no network); only without any does Hermes's own installer download ~650 MB once (up to 15 min).
Subject plugins run with your own file permissions; a call that leaves the temp dir is detected after it ran, not prevented.
A session-level /yolo toggle has no public API, so only HERMES_YOLO_MODE and approvals.mode: off are detected.
Other plugins' own network code cannot be blocked by a plugin; it would only see synthetic test data.

On macOS, Hermes's finished launchd job labels for the child homes stay listed until its next gateway start; the parent hermes process may write Hermes's own bytecode into the Hermes install; each drill child installs a process-wide audit hook (sys.addaudithook) to count non-loopback connects.

entries.name: prsn-id
entries.description: Gives a Hermes agent its PRSN ID, read live from PRSN Connect, the desktop app that keeps the agent's signing key in the computer's secure hardware. The agent knows its own PRSN ID at each session and can seal email and files with its PRSN's key. Hermes asks the human before each Seal with its own approval prompt. It also asks the human before a command or file action of Hermes's own that names PRSN Connect or its files. /prsn shows the state, and Hermes Desktop gets a status bar item. Disclosure. The plugin reads ~/.prsn-id/gateway.json, which PRSN Connect writes and which holds no token. It starts prsn-gateway-mcp, a program PRSN Connect installed, gives it a short fixed list of environment settings with none of Hermes's API keys, and talks to it over standard input and output on this computer. PRSN Connect makes the calls to api.prsnid.ai, and a Seal's link opens verify.prsnid.ai. It writes its last state to status.json in its own data folder, and, only with the server_log setting on, PRSN Connect's server log. After a file Seal it opens the Seal's page at verify.prsnid.ai in the default browser, and no other address. It makes no network call of its own, stores no credential and sends no telemetry.
entries.title: PRSN ID
known_issues: Needs PRSN Connect v0.2.1 or later on macOS and Linux, and v0.2.2 or later on Windows, running on the same computer and user account. A server with no desktop cannot run it today.
A file Seal's page opens only in the browser on the computer where Hermes runs. Through a chat platform, no working link reaches you.

With Hermes's approvals off, in yolo mode, or in a one-shot hermes -z run, Hermes asks nothing, so a Seal is made without the human's yes. An agent that can run commands can start such a run itself. The plugin's check on commands that name PRSN Connect is not a wall.

entries.name: psychopomp
entries.description: Every week, Hermes helps you write a page of your life (your Book) from what it already knows of your week: proposed as a card in the chat, added only when you approve; once a year, a year in review. Seal letters for the people you love. If you ever go silent for good, Hermes checks in, then asks your witness for a one-time code they can send on any channel, and only then carries your Book (one designed HTML file) and letters. Rehearse the whole passage in 20 seconds on a virtual clock, on the Desktop page or in any chat. Disclosure — sends weekly nudges, check-ins, a code request and (after the witness's code) the user's Book and letters to the chats the user sets, each through Hermes' own `hermes send` CLI with the text over stdin; reads every inbound gateway message before Hermes' sender check to catch PSY- codes, and consumes those messages; stores the Book and letters in plain text under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/psychopomp; runs a 30-second background ticker; no telemetry.

entries.name: pugin
entries.description: A dancing companion for Hermes Desktop that beams in while the chat you're viewing is working and beams out when its whole job is done: the reply, plus the subagents, background processes and Kanban cards that chat started. Work from other chats never counts. Click him for a list of what's running (with Stop for subagents and processes); NEED YOU!, STUCK? and DONE! callouts take you to the approval, the stalled card or the finished work. Seven characters, size, opacity, presence and reduced-motion settings. Disclosure — no network calls (all media is bundled inline), no telemetry, no shell, no credentials. While its window is visible the Desktop half polls Hermes's subagent, background-process and pending-approval lists for the focused chat every 4 s, and its backend route opens the Kanban board databases under the Hermes root (every non-archived board, shared across profiles) read-only with SQLite and returns only the cards linked to that chat. Its only actions are Stop (kills the chosen background process or interrupts the chosen subagent, after a click and a confirm click) and Open, which switches to the Kanban page and copies the card id to the clipboard. Settings are kept in Desktop plugin storage.
entries.title: PUGin
known_issues: Needs Hermes Desktop; the companion has no CLI or TUI surface.
Kanban tracking needs a Hermes with the Kanban board; without it PUGin follows the chat, its subagents and processes, and Settings says Kanban is unavailable.

entries.name: pulse-rings
entries.description: Live numbers beside your chat: a Pulses pane for Hermes Desktop with rings, bars, numbers and trends from Discord servers, GitHub, feeds, public JSON APIs, read-only MCP tools, Windows notifications and Hermes's own activity. The agent drafts a pulse; only a person can approve it, and the approval card lists every host and the hourly request budget. No model tokens to refresh. Network: GETs to discord.com, cdn.discordapp.com, api.github.com, avatars.githubusercontent.com and HTTPS hosts you approve; the builder's Find sends one query to geocoding-api.open-meteo.com or store.steampowered.com. Notification pulses read counts from the local Windows store; sender and text previews are a separate opt-in. No telemetry; background collection is opt-in. Disclosure — Approved pulses send HTTPS GETs to discord.com, cdn.discordapp.com, api.github.com (with your optional GitHub token), avatars.githubusercontent.com and any public HTTPS hosts you approve per pulse; the builder's Find sends a query to geocoding-api.open-meteo.com or store.steampowered.com. On Windows, notification pulses read the local Windows notification database (read-only), and a one-time import you start reads an old Discord Pulse plugin database read-only. Background collection is off by default.

Not yet checked by an independent security review.

entries.name: puppetmaster-learn
entries.description: Turns a Puppetmaster swarm into a Hermes skill. Puppetmaster runs durable worker jobs (swarms and flow graphs) for an agent. When a Hermes session ends, this plugin finds the swarm that finished during that session in the session's directory and, if it produced findings or a patch, writes its goal and findings (title, location, severity, failure scenario, evidence) as a skill candidate under $HERMES_HOME/skills-candidates/. entries.name: pushary
entries.description: Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native Hermes approval transport, with optional per-tool gates and a Hermes Desktop status-bar panel. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account, or to the approvers a Pushary Team route names (fails closed); the Hermes Desktop panel answers an approval this Hermes is carrying by withdrawing it on pushary.com and uses the answer only when Pushary confirms that withdrawal won; each approval is recorded owner-only in plugin-data/pushary/approvals (redacted command, choices, outcome; removed after a day); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions and wait in ~/.pushary/run/hermes-commands; when the user has turned on Pushary's encrypted conversation history and installed Pushary's helper, a background thread reads the session through Hermes's SessionDB, keeps owner-only snapshots in ~/.pushary/hermes-history (removed after 48 hours unchanged) and runs that helper (pushary-native-transcripts inside Pushary.app, or pushary-transcript-register at the owner-only path record ~/.pushary/hermes-history-helper.json that Pushary setup writes, else on PATH) with the API key so Pushary's uploader can encrypt and send them; sends session events with a machine id (~/.pushary/machine-id when present, else a hashed hostname) on every turn, the redacted command and description of each approval it carries, the redacted reason when Hermes marks a turn failed (max 200 characters), redacted gated-tool arguments and pushary_remind reminder text to pushary.com; reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Hermes.
known_issues: Updating from 0.5.9: this release reads PUSHARY_API_KEY only through Hermes. If Pushary setup or the Pushary app gave the old copy its key, save it once with: hermes config set PUSHARY_API_KEY <your key>

entries.description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers, Hermes's sudo password prompt) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. entries.name: pwn-board
entries.description: Pwn boards for Hermes: engagements and problems with a known origin, a testable goal and no known path (a foothold to reach, a privilege to escalate, a flag to capture; also flaky failures and regressions), and the workflow that takes a finished one to complete. The agent keeps a frontier of intents rooted at the board's origin, claims them (subagents too), and records findings that must cite real tool output: while a board is open every tool result carries an evidence id, and a finding citing an id no tool returned is refused. It never scores itself: the goal test is fixed at open, run through the terminal tool under normal approvals, and the plugin writes the verdict. A finished board is written up with the files as delivered, goes to the operator's review (notes the agent must answer before the next round), then to verification: an independent verifier subagent and the agent check it separately, the verifier's report held from the agent until it files its own, and the agent reconciles them for the operator to accept or send back. /pwnboard and a Desktop pane drive all of it. The board carries no offensive tooling of its own. Provenance — the fact-intent-hint board model originates in Cairn (https://github.com/oritera/Cairn, AGPL-3.0); this is an independent implementation for Hermes and contains no Cairn source. Disclosure — while at least one board is open, records an excerpt of every tool result (first and last 2,000 characters, 1,000 of the arguments, length, SHA-256) in <hermes home>/plugin-data/pwn-board/boards.db and tags the result with an evidence id (an added _evidence key in JSON objects, else a last line); uncited evidence is deleted after 14 days; pwn_board_test runs the board's goal-test command through the terminal tool (same backend and approval rules as any agent command); pwn_board_report reads the files the agent names through the read_file tool and keeps them in the database; each verification launches one leaf subagent through ctx.subagent_lifecycle with the terminal and file toolsets (Hermes's child-agent rules, backend and approvals apply), whose goal and context carry the board, write-up, delivered files and cited tool output, on the user's configured model (a memory provider, if any, is told of the delegation); with allow_gateway_injection granted, the operator's workflow moves start a turn in the board's session through ctx.inject_message; pre_llm_call adds one line per board to the main agent's current turn; a daemon thread, started on first use, polls the plugin's own database every 3 s to deliver those turns (verifiers start only inside a main-agent turn); the plugin records its own version in its database, at load only if that database already exists so loading creates no files, for the pane's build check; the Desktop pane renders write-ups, checks, reports, notes and findings as Markdown with the chat's renderer in preview mode, loading no images and running nothing; no other network calls, no telemetry, credentials, shell commands of its own or self-updater.

entries.name: qdrant-memory
entries.description: Durable native memory for Hermes with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Hermes-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant_memory_search, qdrant_memory_add, qdrant_memory_update and qdrant_memory_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; a restart-interrupted remote write stays retryable with the same request identifier, and a deterministic extraction failure is quarantined without stopping unrelated writers. Optional shared memory runs through one authenticated Owner over loopback or HTTPS MCP with provisioned device grants, fixed scopes and one writer per destination; the default stays private under a local ownership lock. scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and `migrate mem0` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — optional shared memory runs one authenticated Owner service (off by default, loopback or HTTPS MCP only, token-checked device grants with fixed scopes).
known_issues: Multi-writer Server/Cloud deployments, hybrid retrieval and a web UI are not supported.
Upgrading from a pin older than 0.5.0 changes the embedding transport rule: a non-loopback embedding endpoint must use HTTPS, or use a loopback address.
Deletion removes records and fences pending operations but is not a forensic secure erase; storage-level remnants (WAL, backups) may persist.
Embedded mode is single-writer: a second process fails closed on the ownership lock instead of sharing the store.
Extraction adds LLM latency after a turn; memory admission is not guaranteed before the host admits the provider, and pending operations replay on the next start.
Optional offline CPU embeddings need the local extra in a separate environment; the plugin manager installs only the dependencies declared in the manifest.

For optional CPU embeddings, upgrading from 0.5.4 changes FastEmbed 0.9.0 to 0.9.1 and changes the embedding fingerprint even with the same model and dimensions. Preserve the old environment and data; export and re-embed into a new profile and collection before switching. Do not directly reuse the old CPU collection.

entries.name: qdrant
entries.description: Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off | summary | verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off | minimal | verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Six opt-in hardening knobs (gate, temporal, rerank, entities, cascade, ledger), metadata filter operators, decay_scan.py and semantic_dedup.py scripts, hybrid dense+sparse RRF search, and display.level (off|summary|verbose) — all default off, so existing users see no change unless they opt in. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on, and the Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 cross-encoder or the configured rerank_model when the rerank knob is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding and reranking run on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials), last-operation status in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-status.json, and, only when the ledger knob is on, per-memory history including the first 200 characters of each stored memory in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory-ledger.db. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.hermes/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/hermes_default, ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Hermes home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate hermes_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Hermes session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.
known_issues: Windows on ARM is unsupported: grpcio, pulled in by qdrant-client, has no win_arm64 wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are supported.
Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and requires a reachable server.

md_search returns 'no markdown index yet' until you run the bundled ingest script once (python scripts/md_ingest.py, lexical only and fast; add --semantic for the embedding tier, which takes about 7 minutes for 5500 chunks on a 5-core CPU). No background process does this for you.

Running the plugin's pytest suite inside an installed copy still changes the PM dependency stamp (the .pytest_cache directory is hashed as a build input); only an upstream core change can exclude gitignored state.

entries.name: quick-eval
entries.description: Get a second opinion on any answer. /quick-eval sends your last question to other models, shows the answers side by side, and records which ones you mark good. Runs and picks go to an append-only JSONL file, and a review page (/quick-eval open: the Quick Eval page in Hermes Desktop on Hermes 0.22.3 or newer, or a browser page elsewhere; also a tab in hermes dashboard) shows each comparison and a model leaderboard. Disclosure — sends your last question (only that message) to the models you name through Hermes' configured providers; probes localhost ports 11434, 1234, 8000 and 8080 for local model servers and, the first time you name a model one of them serves, adds that server as a `providers:` entry in config.yaml; asks for the model/provider-override permission on Hermes' consent screen (`/quick-eval allow` writes it into config.yaml on older Hermes); writes ~/.hermes/evals/evals.jsonl; reads ~/.hermes/state.db read-only to show your sessions; `/quick-eval open` outside Hermes Desktop serves the review page, which includes full session transcripts, on 127.0.0.1:8765 (or a free port) until Hermes exits, locked to a random per-launch token in the opened URL.

entries.name: quota
entries.description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the hermes-quota-plugin User-Agent, caching Anthropic usage responses and rate-limit cooldowns in the Hermes root directory keyed by a token hash so profiles sharing one Claude login share them; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Hermes' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; when a Codex account is configured, each refresh also fetches public Codex reset announcements from the third-party site codex-resets.com (anonymous request, no credentials sent); the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Hermes' auth.json pool and OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check first sends Hermes' own xai-oauth access token (read via Hermes or from auth.json, read-only) to grok.com's billing endpoint with a browser User-Agent, and on an authentication failure falls back to local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux, the macOS Keychain or Windows DPAPI for the browser's cookie key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or every saved commandcode credential in Hermes' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA_API_KEY from ~/.hermes/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage, /api/balance and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Hermes' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints. The opt-in (default off) Agent Monitor reads this profile's Hermes session database and the local process list to show running sessions, spend estimates and model health, locally only.

entries.name: quotum
entries.description: A quotum seat or prepaid PAYG project as a provider, with usage and dashboard records or balance and receipts. Seat 401/402 recovery hints, opt-in advisory preflight and shared meter caching. Disclosure — seat mode sends prompts and QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY to api.venice.ai; /usage, Desktop usage, 402 guidance, optional QUOTUM_PREFLIGHT and the dashboard Seals tab send only a 16-hex sha256 handle of the seat key to quotum.org and read the seat's public record and model catalog there; QUOTUM_X_SEARCH=1 drops Hermes web_search from seat requests for Venice-side web and X search (billed per search); PAYG mode (QUOTUM_PAYG_KEY, takes precedence) sends prompts, replies and the project key to quotum.org/api/payg/v1, whose gateway processes them and bills a prepaid project balance, and the dashboard reads balance and receipt metadata from it; both modes replace Hermes' HTTP client via create_client; seats are funded by the QUOTUM crypto token; keys are read only through Hermes' profile secret scope; no telemetry, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials.
known_issues: Requires agent.secret_scope.get_secret. Hosts without that API can load the plugin, but provider actions refuse credentials and the dashboard asks for a Hermes upgrade and restart.
Both modes supply a client through create_client and require plugins.isolation in_process (the default); host isolation is unsupported.
Hermes credential pools or configured fallback chains may run before terminal provider hints. Older builds without the classification hook cannot guarantee a Hermes-level stop.
QUOTUM_PREFLIGHT is advisory and seat-only. Missing metadata skips the warning; it never switches the model or blocks inference.
Set QUOTUM_SEAT_KEY or QUOTUM_PAYG_KEY; PAYG takes precedence. requires_env is empty because Hermes has no either/or declaration. Restart Hermes and its gateway after changing modes.
PAYG intake and model availability are controlled by the gateway. Per-request x402 intake remains closed; use prepaid project keys.
Hermes' bundled Achievements page has no hook for outside achievements, so the seat's seals live in the plugin's own Seals tab.

entries.name: radio-dm-gateway
entries.description: Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC_ALLOWED_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until hermes tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until hermes cron remove. Hermes main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.

entries.name: rails
entries.description: Guardrails and decision plugin: a fast local System 1 model (d1-3B Decision Guard) decides on every turn whether the agent is only looking or changing things, flags work you did not ask for, makes code work load the matching skill and run a test before 'done', and shows every decision inline as a tag. Optional d3 vision checks the screen before a computer-use task is called done and adds decide, screen_find, screen_check and video_check tools. Disclosure — network calls only to local model servers on 127.0.0.1 (ports 8089, 8898, 8899), which receive your message, the agent's last reply, tool-call arguments, web/email tool results and screenshots; no third-party services, no telemetry, no shell commands, no stored credentials, no Python dependencies. Can hold tool calls: by default code edits and changing terminal commands are blocked until the suggested method skill is loaded, and "done" after code edits is refused until a test runs. computer_use_mode defaults to shadow (show only); set to on, it holds stand-in browsers, and clicks are not held when vision is down. computer_use_driver defaults to vision; text_first lets d1 pick a numbered element and d3 aim when it cannot, and cloud lets the model click on its own. Detected money and email actions ask d1 and are held unless d1 confidently authorizes that specific step, including when d1 is down. Detection includes cached screen targets and explicit curl SMTP requests; this is not a sandbox or exhaustive recognition of arbitrary scripts or unobserved controls. Appends a decision log to <HERMES_HOME>/logs/rails.jsonl (long tokens masked); reads the newest computer-use screenshot and media passed to its tools to send them to the local vision model; checks a sibling superpowers plugin folder for skills; short-lived daemon threads for second-opinion and prompt-injection checks. Ideas (shadow mode, decision log) credited to kerpopule/hermes-jev-skills; not a fork.

known_issues: Needs a local d1 decision server on 127.0.0.1:8089; when it or the optional d3 layers are off, Rails says so and does not fake a decision.
Built and tested on Windows.

entries.name: rainbowomma
entries.description: One Mac, one human, many agents. Each Hermes profile gets a Chrome of its own with a coloured, named window frame, its own ports, processes, clipboard and document leases in Word / Excel / Acrobat / Preview. A pre_tool_call guard refuses what would hit the human or another agent before it runs (pkill Chrome, quitting Word through AppleScript, a port or a process that isn't the agent's, the human's clipboard and Chrome profile, typing while the human types) and names the tool that does it safely; a Messages/Mail send goes to Hermes's approval gate. Idle tabs, expired document leases, apps an agent launched and orphaned servers are cleaned up at session end and on a timer. With browser.cloud_provider: rainbowomma, Hermes's own browser tools drive that Chrome. /rainbow shows who holds what; /rainbow pause stops every agent at once. Disclosure — macOS only. Starts Google Chrome for the agent (own profile folder, a DevTools port on 127.0.0.1, an unpacked theme extension) and runs osascript, ps, pgrep, lsof, ioreg, open and xcrun simctl with a minimal environment (no Hermes provider keys); stops only processes that are provably the agent's, its own idle Chrome, and an Office app an agent launched and left empty. Keeps one guard helper process per profile and a housekeeping timer thread while Hermes runs. Writes its state under ~/.rainbowomma (registry, leases, a receipts log, Chrome profiles, temp copies for Word conversions); conversion outputs go only into the source document's folder, and rainbow_save_document saves in place a document the agent itself opened. When one Hermes process serves several profiles it prefixes the agent's shell commands with `export RAINBOW_AGENT=…` (modify directive; setting mark_commands). Its only request goes to 127.0.0.1 (the agent's own Chrome). No updater, no credential access.
entries.title: RainbowOMMA
known_issues: macOS only. On another system the plugin registers nothing but /rainbow, which says so.
The guard reads the command text: it closes the cheap ways to hurt a neighbour, it is not a sandbox.

The document tools need the one-time macOS Automation consent (osascript → System Events and each Office/PDF app); a background gateway is asked separately from a terminal session. Browser, port, process, screen and clipboard tools need none.
Word's sandbox asks for access once per folder; until the human answers, rainbow_convert_to_pdf reports blocked-by-dialog.

Extra document apps (setting extra_apps) are driven with AppleScript's standard document suite and need the one-time macOS Automation consent; only Word, Excel, Acrobat and Preview are exercised by the maintainer.

entries.name: raise
entries.description: Fundraising desk for founders: imports your investor pipeline, ranks investors on cited evidence, checks every draft against code gates (one conversation per firm, a pass closes the firm, 3 touches per channel, working-day cool-downs) and lints it against your verified claims before it reaches your mailbox as a draft. Draft-only: Raise has no send tool, and a pre_tool_call hook refuses send, reply and forward calls to pipeline addresses on mail tools and terminal commands alike. Disclosure — Raise opens no network connections; web search, page fetches, mail, CRM and LinkedIn go through the user's own Hermes tools via dispatch_tool, and LinkedIn tools get daily caps plus a 72-hour pause after a login or rate-limit error. Deck text, profile and investor facts are sent to the user's configured model through ctx.llm. Data stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/raise (SQLite, plus checked draft files for skill-based mail setups); CSV import reads only an existing .csv at the path the user gives, never inside the Hermes folder or hidden folders. No credentials stored, no .env reads, no telemetry, no background processes; automation blueprints exist only if the user adds them. Export and delete via /raise export and /raise delete confirm. Bundles blader/humanizer v3.1.0 (MIT).

entries.name: rapid-mlx
entries.description: Managed Rapid-MLX runtime and model library for Hermes Desktop/CLI on Apple Silicon. Derived from omlx. Disclosure — explicit setup installs Rapid-MLX 1.0.2 and SHA-256-locked PyPI wheels in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/rapid-mlx using an existing Python 3.12; runs a long-running authenticated 127.0.0.1 server; invokes rapid-mlx pull for public aliases/repositories using models.rapidmlx.com and Hugging Face/CDNs with the standard shared HF cache; generates a local API key stored as HERMES_RAPID_MLX_LOCAL_API_KEY in the profile's .env; Use validates generation then rewrites the profile default in config.yaml. Remove forgets library records and never deletes shared model weights. Telemetry is disabled.
entries.title: Rapid-MLX
known_issues: Requires macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon and existing Python 3.12 on the inference host.
The provider needs in-process execution; strict plugin-host isolation is unsupported.
One model at a time; use the owning Hermes process to stop or switch its server.
Pull progress is indeterminate; native logs are available, with cancellation and cache reuse.
Model removal forgets the library record only; shared Hugging Face files are retained.

entries.name: rariflat
entries.description: Live character reactions and local reliability signals for Hermes tool calls; explainable tool/skill recommendations use task fit, reliability, measured rarity, and repeated-call restraint. A local Hermes/A2A registry ranks declared capabilities and caller-supplied completion observations; it only recommends and never executes, installs, or connects to agents. The opt-in failure-streak and repeated-call guard is disabled by default. Tool arguments are inspected in memory for non-secret task tokens and repeat fingerprints; credential-like fields are filtered before learning, and raw arguments/credentials are not intentionally persisted. No network requests, telemetry, or subprocesses are initiated. Disclosure — the Desktop pane shows "Review & install" and "Review A2A Agent Card" buttons for agents the model registers; those repos and URLs are unverified, and the install button opens Hermes' plugin install dialog for that GitHub repo.

entries.name: ratcatcher
entries.description: Scam bouncer for Telegram groups: removes wallet drainers, fake airdrops, fake support and DM bait, doubling scams, look-alike phishing links and admin impersonators before members or Hermes read them, mutes then bans repeat offenders, and DMs admins a report with Release and Ban buttons. Hermes can check a pasted message, report catches, edit the blocklist and release false alarms. Disclosure — deletes group messages and mutes or bans members through your own Hermes bot, in enforce mode with ban-on-sight and AI review on by default for every group the bot is in unless protected_chats is set; removed messages never reach Hermes; sends borderline messages (only) from any group member to your current model via ctx.llm when ai_review is on; blocklist changes and releases by the agent ask for your approval through Hermes, and a blocklist hit removes the message and adds a strike but never bans on sight; stores catches, strikes and member join times in its own plugin data; no third-party network calls.

entries.name: re-call
entries.description: Local agent memory with a trust verdict per recalled memory: before each turn, the memories that pass RE-call's calibrated threshold, each with its memo id and validity dates; superseded memories flagged as retired with the memo that replaced them; and an explicit abstention line when nothing clears the threshold. Facts are stored one per memo by the recall_remember tool and by mirroring the built-in memory tool, with supersession on replace; conversation turns are not captured. Disclosure — runs RE-call's own MCP server (recall-mcp from recall-rag[fastembed,mcp]>=0.15.0, installed separately) as one local child process over stdio for the session, with a minimal environment (none of Hermes's keys) and its working directory in $HERMES_HOME/re-call; by default the memory store lives in the per-user folder <XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else ~/.config>/re-call/, shared with every Hermes profile and any other agent the user points at it, so they read each other's memories (set dsn or memo_folder for a separate store); mirrors writes of Hermes's built-in memory tool into RE-call; its memory-writing tools honour memory.write_approval and refuse writes nobody can approve; config, mirror journal, embedding cache and server log stay in $HERMES_HOME/re-call; RE-call downloads its fastembed embedding model from HuggingFace on first use; no other network, no telemetry, no credentials.
entries.title: RE-call
known_issues: Needs RE-call 0.15.0 or later installed outside Hermes and a store created once with `recall --embedder fastembed setup --lite --memory ~/.config/re-call/memos --store ~/.config/re-call/memory.db --no-register`; until then the provider reports itself unavailable with that command
Two Hermes profiles share one memory by default; set `dsn` to keep a profile separate
A store with very few memos can stay uncalibrated; strict search then refuses and the provider shows the reason instead of recalling

entries.description: Reverse-engineer any video shot by shot: production-method classification per shot (live action / AI video / 3D / screen capture / code-template render), caption and sticker timelines, voice vs music stems, editing rhythm, and a concrete replication plan. Powered by JuneYaooo/rea-video (Apache-2.0, pinned commit d904b1e8). The six stdio-MCP tools expose the full pipeline (incl. mux_tracks for dual-track video downloads); for shots the pipeline flags as low-confidence, the agent reviews the tiled frames with its own vision and merges the verdict back via submit_review — no external VLM key required. Local runtime deps: ffmpeg and the pinned rea-video package (installed from the repo's venv). Disclosure — downloads video/audio from Douyin share and CDN URLs the agent passes in (https only, Douyin hosts only, curl with --noproxy), runs the third-party rea-video package (git-pinned) and ffmpeg on the host, writes all outputs under its own plugin-data folder (falling back to ~/rea-video-out), and the upstream pipeline downloads a ~67 MB audio-separation model on first run.

entries.name: reachmap
entries.description: Hermes knows what it can reach before it says it can't. Scans signed-in browser sessions on DevTools ports, MCP servers, local services, CLIs and drives; freezes a compact map into each new session's prompt (cache-safe system prompt section); and catches replies that deny or hedge about access the map shows is live, with a footer for the user and a one-shot correction for the agent. Opt-in sign-in probes (off by default) tell an installed CLI apart from a signed-in one, and flag replies that plan to use a CLI whose login has lapsed. Keeps a SQLite ledger of when each capability, or a CLI login, appeared or vanished. Disclosure — loopback-only HTTP GETs to Chrome DevTools /json/version and /json/list (tab titles and URLs, never navigates or executes); runs ps, lsof (or ss) and shutil.which on a fixed CLI list (presence only); only for tools the user lists in auth_probes, runs that tool's one fixed read-only status command (e.g. gh auth status, xurl whoami, wrangler whoami; no shell, 6 s timeout, minimal child env: PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/LANG/LC_*/XDG_*/TMPDIR plus only that tool's own variables such as GH_* or AWS_*, so Hermes provider keys never reach it), which contacts that tool's own service, keeping only the verdict and never the output; reads browser.cdp_url and MCP server names via load_config_readonly; the map text, including account emails visible in tab titles unless show_identities is off, is sent to the model provider as part of the prompt; writes plugin-data/reachmap/data.db (and auth.json when probes are on); never reads credential stores; no other network calls, no telemetry.

entries.name: reaction-feedback
entries.description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. entries.name: reaction-ledger
entries.description: Local ledger of the emoji reactions people leave on messages in your Telegram chats with Hermes: /reaction-log counts each message once, with the reactions it has now, and shows per emoji how many messages carry it, in how many chats and how long ago it was last set, or per day with the day's most used emoji, for the last 24 hours, any number of hours or days, or everything recorded; /reaction-log recent lists the newest reaction changes (ten, or up to 100 with /reaction-log recent 50). entries.name: read-once
entries.description: On a repeated identical local read_file, tells the model to answer from the earlier result when READ_ONCE_HITS=1, the file bytes are unchanged, and that exact result is still in the latest model request. Observe-only otherwise. /read-once stats shows hits. Disclosure — reads and SHA-256-hashes regular files under READ_ONCE_ROOT (1 MiB max), inspects the model request in memory for that result digest, and keeps ephemeral metadata only. No network, no telemetry, no disk cache, and no background watcher. It does not hash dotenv names, auth.json, or paths under vault, mcp-tokens, browser-profile, webapp, or pairing. Hits stay off unless READ_ONCE_HITS=1. A repeat of the same read can be Hermes's unchanged-stub rather than the file bytes.

entries.name: read-only-mode
entries.description: Ask/read-only toggle beside the Desktop composer (Cursor Ask-mode equivalent): while it is on, each send is prefixed with a read-only instruction so the agent answers from reading only, and asks before changing anything. Per-chat state, palette command, no agent tools or hooks. It is a prompt-level constraint, not a sandbox: Hermes has no session-level read-only policy, so the model can still disobey. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no tools, hooks, env vars.

entries.name: reading-buddy

entries.name: reading
entries.description: Newsletters out of the Gmail inbox, into a reader in Hermes Desktop (a page in the sidebar) and on your phone (dashboard web app). Setup scans the inbox and suggests the newsletters; native Gmail filters then move the senders you pick into one label, even when Hermes is off. Read with j/k, dark or original colors per sender, unsubscribe in one tap, add or remove senders by hand, and ask Hermes about any issue (a new chat with the issue attached, or the @newsletter: reference in any chat). `hermes reading export` feeds digest cron jobs. Disclosure: uses your own Google OAuth client, declared under oauth: and signed in with `hermes auth add reading:google` (Hermes stores and refreshes the token; the plugin never holds it); calls only the Gmail API through credentialed_provider_request, plus, when you press Unsubscribe, a one-click POST to the sender's List-Unsubscribe URL (public https hosts only) or an unsubscribe email from your account; changes Gmail only to create its label, write and delete its own filters, move routed senders' mail out of the inbox, mark opened emails read and trash emails you delete; `hermes reading setup` runs `hermes config set` and `hermes auth add` in your terminal (without YOLO or auto-approve variables); writes only its own HERMES_HOME/reading folder; @newsletter: and Ask Hermes send the newsletter text to your model provider; no telemetry.
