entries.name: readonly-guard
entries.description: Three-mode, per-session tool guard for Hermes: read-only (writes blocked; inspection tools plus single allowlisted read-only shell commands), plan (the same, plus the plan markdown), and writable. Switched from the status bar, /readonly, the dashboard API, or — in the Desktop app — three contributed keybinds (Ctrl+Alt+R read-only, Ctrl+Alt+P plan, writable left unbound), which appear in Settings -> Keybinds under Session and are rebindable there; keybinds are desktop-only, because the registry belongs to the desktop renderer. A session that is never switched follows a configurable default (read-only). Disclosure — registers a pre_tool_call hook that can block any tool call, and fails closed when the hook raises; writes <HERMES_HOME>/readonly-guard.state (session -> mode) and plugins.entries.readonly-guard.settings.default_mode; a writable lease expires after writable_expiry_minutes (30 by default) minutes without a message from the user, the expiry is latched (a later message does not revive it), and a turn that is already running is never interrupted; in read-only and plan modes it runs single, allowlisted, read-only shell commands through terminal (a speed bump, not a sandbox; on Windows those run under Git Bash); no network calls, no environment variables, no Python dependencies.

entries.name: realcryptocap
entries.description: Live crypto prices, real market cap rankings and AI market briefs from RealCryptoCap, free with no API key. Real market cap ranks native crypto only: stablecoins, wrapped/staked receipts and tokenized assets are left out. Three tools (rcc_price, rcc_top, rcc_market_brief), a /crypto slash command for an instant price table with no model call, and a bundled skill that tells the agent to use live data instead of quoting prices from memory. Disclosure — HTTPS GET requests to realcryptocap.com only (/api/cg, /api/market-analysis, /api/news); an optional REALCRYPTOCAP_API_KEY, read through Hermes's secret scope, is sent as a Bearer header to realcryptocap.com only; rcc_market_brief sends the fetched market data (prices, analysis, headlines, no conversation content) to the user's active model through ctx.llm. No shell, no file writes, no background processes, no telemetry, no stored credentials. Standard library only. Market data, not financial advice.

entries.name: reapx
entries.description: Turn the bookmarks you saved on X into ready-to-load, registered Hermes skills — without the paid X API. The plugin is data-in: `reapx_import` runs the whole pipeline — map, categorize into a fixed set of domains, two-track assess (integrate-into-your-makeup and business-opportunity), generate, register (`reapx:<name>`) — from a bookmarks file you point it at, or from items passed inline (collected by you through the host's own browser tooling); `reapx_status` is read-only state; `reapx_review` surfaces everything LLM-shaped item by item for the human before anything is relied on. Incremental via a persistent seen-ledger (a bookmark is never processed twice). The map / categorize / assess stages optionally run through the host LLM (`ctx.llm`, one registered auxiliary task) with a deterministic rules engine as the bit-for-bit fallback (`enrich: rules` = zero LLM calls); generate is never the LLM. Registration: handler-time `register_skill`, live in the same session; `register_generated_skills` defaults to false — generated skills land in the review and on disk, and register only after you say so. Settings are read from plugin config only (tool args can never flip enrichment, lift a spend cap, or force registration). Disclosure — Derived from starlearner-nexus (same owner; different input and engine). The plugin reads no browser profile, cookie store or keychain; the repo also ships standalone browser-harvest scripts (scripts/fetch_x_bookmarks.py, scripts/cookie_store.py) that copy your browser's Cookies database and drive it over CDP, run by hand only and never imported by the plugin. `reapx_import` reads the bookmarks JSON file at the path you or the agent name (or the configured `import_dir`). LLM enrichment is on by default (`enrich: rules` turns it off) and sends bookmark text to your active provider through Hermes (`ctx.llm`), capped by `llm_max_items`. Generated skills are written to the plugin's own data dir and registered only when `register_generated_skills` is turned on. No other network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

entries.name: recall-vault
entries.description: A policy vault and memory for agent money. The agent remembers its spending rules, per-transaction cap, daily cap, confirm threshold, and allowlist, and Recall Vault blocks over-cap payments, refuses unknown recipients, and escalates over-threshold payments to human approval before any tool runs. Dry-run only, no money moves. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook inspects every tool call and blocks, or sends to Hermes' approval prompt, calls from other plugins whose tool name looks like a payment (pay, transfer, withdraw, payout, settle) and whose arguments carry an amount and a recipient; policy and ledger are stored in this profile's plugin data; the policy and remembered rules are added to the model input every turn; dry-run only, it moves no money itself.

entries.name: recall
entries.description: Local file recall: a private on-device index of the documents already on the user's machine, with a search tool over file content (SQLite FTS5, no network and no embedding service), a recall_open reader for PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, Markdown, CSV, email and source files, an @recall: context reference that expands matching passages into the turn, and a pre_llm_call hook that puts up to three candidate file paths in front of the model before it answers a document question. Five tools (recall_index, recall_search, recall_open, recall_stats, recall_forget), a bounded background refresh on session start, and the /recall slash command. Extraction is standard library only (FlateDecode-aware PDF stream extractor, OOXML text nodes). Disclosure — reads the contents of files under the folders the user points it at (default ~/Documents; any folder can be named, and a folder inside Hermes' own home is refused), and recall_open / @recall: read any absolute file path the model or user names outside the refused set; extracted text is stored in a plaintext SQLite index under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/recall/, short excerpts are injected into the model prompt on turns whose message looks document-related (disable with the ambient setting, or drop paths with recall_forget), and indexed or opened text reaches the user's model provider in the normal course of a turn. Every read is checked on the RESOLVED path first: credential stores (.env, *.pem, id_rsa, .ssh, .aws, .config, auth.json, state.db and a wider built-in denylist), anything inside Hermes' home (vault, session transcripts, mcp-tokens/, webhook_subscriptions.json, dashboard session token, this plugin's own index) and virtual filesystems such as /proc are refused. Files on disk are never modified, moved or deleted; no network calls and no credentials.
entries.title: recall
known_issues: Scanned PDFs and images are indexed by filename only - there is no OCR, and recall_stats reports the skip reasons.
Ranking is lexical (BM25 plus path, recency and phrase boosts), not semantic; no embedding model is used.
The first index of a large folder costs roughly 16 ms per file (measured over 3,000 files of a mixed real tree).
Name-based filtering cannot be complete for a password written inside an ordinary document; the Hermes-home, credential-directory and virtual-filesystem rules are enforced regardless of filename.

entries.name: receipt-printer
entries.description: Your agent says it's done. Get the receipt. Receipts detects action and completion claims and checks observed tool history or explicit local task evidence. Each claim is supported, contradicted, unverified or not evaluable; missing evidence is never called a lie. Output: PNG, ASCII, Desktop pane or optional USB printer. Configure kits, fields, five styles, paper, branding and automatic triggers; verdicts cannot be hidden or recolored. Chat requests stay in the caller's session. Disclosure — Reads this profile's state.db conversation history and kanban.db read-only; an explicit local `hermes receipt fleet --roots` scan can read other profiles' state.db files you choose. Stores a tool-name/argument-hash ledger and receipt PNGs (containing answer excerpts, private, review before sharing) under the profile's plugin data and receipt-printer directories until you delete them. The optional `runtime.jev` classifier, off by default, sends redacted conversation context to OpenRouter; the optional USB printer path uses separately installed python-escpos.

entries.name: receipts
entries.description: Verification receipts tied to Git content; gates terminal pushes and PR creation on a passing check. Disclosure — runs read-only local `git` commands (rev-parse, status, ls-files, hash-object without -w) in the agent's repository on terminal tool calls, and blocks `git push` / `gh pr create` there until the user's configured check has passed on that exact content; also refuses a push that selects its repository indirectly (`--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR`, a path it cannot read) whenever any repository has a check configured, and any publishing command it fails to evaluate; observes `pre_llm_call` to read only the session id and model name (never prompts or history; returns nothing) and records that model, the session id and a locally minted issuer id on each receipt; stores receipts in a local SQLite file under the plugin data dir; no network. While Hermes multiplexed profiles are active the plugin cannot issue receipts and blocks every recognized `git push` / `gh pr create` with an explanation, including in repositories with no check configured; use a single-profile session for the gate.

entries.name: recency-anchor
entries.description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

entries.name: recloc
entries.description: Location reminders that never leave your phone: ask the agent to remind you at a place, and Apple Reminders alerts you when you arrive. The plugin posts a brrr notification whose subtitle is the validated address; an iOS Shortcuts automation turns it into a reminder with a When I Arrive alert, and iOS watches the geofence on-device. Nothing listens on your machine — outbound HTTPS only. Disclosure — each reminder's text and destination address are posted to brrr.now through the user's own BRRR_WEBHOOK_URL and delivered as a push notification; saved place names and addresses are stored in the plugin's data folder.

entries.name: recued
entries.description: Connect Hermes to your own self-hosted Recued server on the same computer: your notes, tasks, mail, calendar and records, through the tools a Recued contract grants. Reads run at once, and every change waits for your approval in Recued. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json and one skill), no plugin code: Hermes starts the installed `recued --mcp` as a local stdio MCP server. Disclosure — the tools reach the services you connected to Recued, such as your mail, only as the contract allows. The contract's key is saved in Recued with `recued mcp-key set`, never in Hermes or the plugin. The plugin makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

An mcp_servers.recued entry in your config.yaml takes precedence over the plugin's server.

entries.name: redactgate
entries.description: Reversible PII pseudonymization at the model boundary. Names, e-mails, phones, payment cards, IBANs and national IDs (CA, US, EU, UA) become [[TYPE_xxxxxx]] placeholders in every main-loop model request, across all roles, tool-call arguments, tool results and the system prompt (Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses shapes). Real values come back in the reply (transform_llm_output with hold_stream) and in the arguments of local tools only (terminal, file tools, execute_code, memory, clarify); web, browser, MCP, other plugins' tools and subagents keep placeholders. Checksum-validated detection (Luhn, mod-97), offset-preserving Unicode normalization, HMAC placeholders per session kept in memory, fail-closed on error, hash-chained audit journal, /redact command (status, what the model received, dry run, audit, verify, custom terms). Flags auxiliary calls that carried personal data, and /redact harden turns off model-made session titles. Disclosure — no network calls, no model downloads, no shell commands, subprocesses, background threads, credentials or telemetry; standard library only. Writes only in its plugin data folder: audit.jsonl (entity type counts, tool names, provider host, hashed session ids; never values) and its state.json (random HMAC secret, user-added terms). Reads the merged Hermes config read-only; writes Hermes config only when the user runs /redact harden (auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled = false). The transform_llm_output hook holds the reply stream until values are restored, so commentary between tool calls is not shown on streaming surfaces. Detection core vendored from RedactGate (same author, AGPL-3.0); see DISCLOSURE.md for what predates the hackathon.
known_issues: Hermes runs auxiliary model calls (titles, context compression, vision) without request middleware; RedactGate flags them and /redact harden turns off model-made titles, but cannot rewrite those calls.
Person names are found from cue words, honorifics and a first-name list; an unusual name with no cue is missed until it is caught once in the session or added with /redact terms add.

entries.name: redreplier
entries.description: Find leads in public conversations through RedReplier's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.redreplier.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): keyword mentions on Reddit, Hacker News, X, Bluesky and Facebook, each scored 0-100 for relevance, with filters by score, keyword, source and date, the reason behind a score, approve and reject triage, monitored websites and keywords, and alert settings. Disclosure — every tool call goes to RedReplier's hosted server (mcp.redreplier.com) and acts on the user's RedReplier account with their own workspace role; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Keywords count against the user's RedReplier plan. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: reflexes
entries.description: Senses for your computer: when a file lands in a folder, a USB stick or SD card is connected, or a log file gets a matching line, Hermes starts a turn in the chat that armed the reflex and acts with its normal tools and approvals. Nobody types anything. Durable queue, loop protection (a reflex firing more than 30 times an hour pauses itself), missed firings are logged, never dropped silently. Includes /reflex commands, a bundled skill and a Hermes Desktop page. Disclosure — starts agent turns nobody typed (via ctx.inject_message) in the chat that armed a reflex. Reflexes are armed only by you (/reflex or the Desktop page) or by the model after a Hermes approval prompt. Gateway, TUI and Desktop delivery also needs plugins.entries.reflexes.allow_gateway_injection, but reflexes armed in the classic `hermes chat` terminal run there without that grant and without being displayed. It lists the folders you name about once a second (names, sizes, times) and opens new files briefly only to check they are complete. For log reflexes it reads the bytes appended to the one file you name and sends matching lines (and any /regex/ you give is run on every new line) to your model. It enumerates connected drives and lists the top level of a newly connected one, runs a background thread while Hermes runs, and stores a local SQLite database at <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/reflexes/reflexes.db. No network, telemetry, shell commands, subprocesses, credentials or dependencies beyond the Python standard library (uses ctypes on Windows to list drives).
entries.title: Reflexes
known_issues: Tested live on Windows 11 with Hermes 0.22.6 and 0.23.1. macOS and Linux code paths are covered by unit tests only.
Needs plugins.entries.reflexes.allow_gateway_injection set to true; until then firings are logged but not delivered.
Runs only while Hermes runs. The classic `hermes chat` terminal runs reflex turns without displaying them.

No network, telemetry, shell commands, subprocesses, credentials or dependencies beyond the Python standard library (uses ctypes on Windows to list drives). This plugin registers tool(s): reflex_add, reflex_manage; hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, pre_llm_call. Requires Hermes >=0.22.6. Known issues: Tested live on Windows 11 with Hermes 0.22.6 and 0.23.1. macOS and Linux code paths are covered by unit tests only.; Needs plugins.entries.reflexes.allow_gateway_injection set to true; until then firings are logged but not delivered.; Runs only while Hermes runs. The classic `hermes chat` terminal runs reflex turns without displaying them..

entries.name: refusal
entries.description: Detects when a model refuses a request or deflects to an educational alternative, and retries the turn on the next model in your fallback_providers chain; optionally appends your own text to the retry's system prompt after a refusal. Detection is local and rule-based (regex patterns over the response prose); tool-calling responses, code blocks and partial answers are treated as genuine answers. Disclosure — an llm_execution middleware inspects every model response before the agent loop uses it, and when it detects a refusal it sets finish_reason to content_filter (Anthropic: stop_reason to refusal) so Hermes activates its fallback model; this is logged and counted identically to a real provider-signalled refusal (reason=content_policy_blocked), with no way for a plugin to register a distinct reason, so the detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id to let the two be told apart by hand; a triggered fallback resends the full conversation to the fallback provider and spends tokens there; with no fallback provider configured, Hermes replaces the response with its standard safety-refusal notice, so a false positive discards a valid answer. Optional (off by default, empty preprompt/preprompt_escalated settings): an llm_request middleware appends your configured text to the system prompt of requests in an armed session, so a same-route retry of the same model carries it; armed state is memory-only unless persist_state is enabled, in which case session ids/levels/turn ids (never text or credentials) are kept in Hermes's plugin state. No network calls, no files read or written outside the plugin package (and, if persist_state is on, its own plugin-data file), no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry sent anywhere.
known_issues: Detection is pattern-based, so an unusual refusal phrasing can be missed and a response that quotes refusal language can occasionally be flagged. Configure at least one fallback model so a false positive does not discard an answer.

A detected refusal appears under Hermes's own content_policy_blocked failover reason, identically to a real provider-signalled refusal; plugins cannot register a distinct reason (hermes-agent#138900). The detection log line carries session/model/provider/api_request_id so the two can be correlated and told apart by hand, but no plugin can fix Hermes's own aggregate counts.

The optional preprompt (off by default) rewrites the system prompt of the retry. Hermes skips a fallback entry that resolves to the same provider+model as the one that just failed, so retrying the SAME model needs a different route to it in fallback_providers (see README). This is a prompt-injection mechanism by design — read the disclosure before enabling it.

entries.name: rehearse
entries.description: Practise any interview or talk out loud: job, technical, case, admission, visa, medical, media and podcast interviews, presentations, investor and sales pitches, product demos, thesis defences and speeches. Hermes asks realistic questions aloud in a natural voice (Hermes's own text-to-speech), you answer on camera on a Desktop page (or by microphone alone, or upload a recording), and you get a scored replay: filler words, pace, pauses, answer length and eye contact on a clickable timeline, plus content feedback with a stronger-answer outline built only from what you said; retries report the points gained. Full interview mode runs it live: the interviewer asks each question aloud, recording starts when it finishes, live nudges appear while you answer (facing, framing, distance, light), and the session ends with a hiring-panel debrief across every answer. /rehearse and three tools bring the same coaching to any chat, answering by text or voice note. Disclosure — uses the camera and microphone only while the practice screen is open (about once a second a small frame is checked locally for the live nudges); speech-to-text (faster-whisper) and eye-contact analysis (OpenCV YuNet face landmarks plus pupil position) run locally and no audio or video leaves the computer; each answer's transcript goes to the user's configured model through ctx.llm for questions and feedback; one-time downloads from official sources: the faster-whisper speech model from Hugging Face and the 230 KB YuNet model from opencv/opencv_zoo at a pinned commit, verified by SHA-256 before use; stores sessions, scores and recordings under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/rehearse (deletable from the page; keep_recordings: false deletes each take after scoring; unused uploads are removed after a day); adds /api/plugins/rehearse/ routes (upload, page calls) behind the dashboard's authentication; no shell commands, no background process beyond analysing a take just recorded, no network service or telemetry of its own; never coaches anyone to misrepresent facts.
entries.title: Rehearse
known_issues: Windows on ARM gets content feedback only: faster-whisper has no build there, as for Hermes's own local speech-to-text.

entries.name: reka-provider
entries.description: Reka as a Hermes model provider: Reka's agent-capable models on Reka's OpenAI-compatible API, each with its context window, tool support and image input declared, and reasoning effort sent as Reka's top-level reasoning_effort. entries.name: rekindra
entries.description: Recover forgotten local files and rebuild them as source-backed original animated worlds. Rekindra reads a folder you name, recovers images and text (including ZIP and PDF text), keeps recovered evidence separate from the agent's interpretation, builds a 3D scene, compares its preview with the source, and holds export until flagged differences are fixed or answered with a recorded reason. Disclosure: the plugin makes no network calls of its own. It reads only the folder you name, read-only, and writes only under its Hermes plugin-data directory. Tool results, including recovered text, go to your active Hermes model like any tool result, and rekindra_plan sends selected images to that model only with send_images=true. It starts short-lived, killable child processes without a shell: an isolated Python reader for images and PDFs, and a headless installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium for previews, with a 45 second limit. The browser is started with a minimal environment (PATH, the system and user profile paths, LANG, and temp and cache paths inside the project), so provider keys and other variables are not passed to it. It stores no credentials and leaves no background processes.
entries.title: Rekindra
known_issues: PDF text is read up to 32 pages and there is no OCR, so a scanned or image-only PDF gives no text.
Worlds built only from notes have no tamper check yet, because the player's integrity check hashes embedded images.
If some selected images have a reference and others do not, the world still builds and the unreferenced image ships with no provenance record.
Palette drift compares horizontal colour bands only. It can flag a band changed on purpose and cannot judge objects, composition or motion.
After three revise and preview cycles that still flag, export is allowed without reasons and the warnings are recorded as unresolved.
End-to-end preview and WebM export are verified on Windows. macOS and Linux pass the core test suite in CI but have not been run end to end in Hermes.

entries.name: relatedb-memory
entries.description: Bi-temporal long-term memory on an embedded RelateDB graph with local fastembed embeddings. Facts are superseded instead of overwritten, so the agent can recall what is true now, what it believed on a past date, and which conversation each fact came from. Six agent tools (remember, recall, forget, as_of, provenance, read-only Cypher). Disclosure — stores primary-session conversation turns and Hermes memory writes in a local RelateDB store under the profile's memory/ directory; downloads the fastembed embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 by default) from Hugging Face on first use; no other network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The optional `hermes relatedb-memory` subcommands run only when you invoke them: `init-diffable` edits `.gitattributes` and sets a `git config` diff driver in the current repository, `mcp --launch` starts the `relate` binary from the relate-db package, and the repo's standalone `tools/migrate_embeddings.py` re-embeds an existing store only when you run it.

entries.name: relay-telegram
entries.description: RELAY incoming agent calls on your Hermes Telegram bot with owner-only Accept and Reject buttons. Disclosure — reads the Telegram home-channel id (or an optional owner_chat_id setting) to identify the owner chat, listens on a local Unix socket (`~/.config/relay/telegram.sock`) for RELAY bridge notifications, sends call metadata to that owner chat through your Hermes Telegram bot, and forwards owner-only Accept/Reject decisions to the bridge's local socket. The separate RELAY CLI and bridge (not installed by this plugin) connect outbound to the author's hosted relay `relay.thecheetah11.com` by default, manage local identity keys and phonebook data, run as a background user service when installed through the repository installer, and answer accepted calls from known contacts through the gateway's loopback A2A endpoint with full agent context.

entries.name: reliability-desk

entries.name: relic-gumi
entries.description: A companion that gets to know you and supports self-reflection, built on published psychometric instruments (TIPI for the Big Five, ECR-RS for attachment) as a self-report baseline plus consented check-ins, with an output safety critic and Telegram or Desktop onboarding. Not a diagnostic tool; based on the paper arXiv:2611.08504. Disclosure — state lives under $RELIC_HOME (default ~/.relic); the installer creates a dedicated relic-gumi profile, edits that profile's config.yaml (enables the plugin, sets cron.wrap_response false, copies the base model provider/model/base_url but never keys), creates an empty .env there that the plugin never reads or writes, moves a relic plugin copy found in the base Hermes home to a backup and removes it from the base plugins.enabled list, and creates Hermes cron jobs in that profile that stay silent until the user consents during onboarding; with the "learn from what you write" consent it reads the profile's own Hermes state.db user messages to update a self-report profile; credentials (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS, TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL, GEMINI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_API_KEYS) are optional plugin secrets read only through Hermes' secret scope; check-ins are delivered by detached subprocesses (job and scoped credentials over a private stdin pipe, minimal environment with proxy/CA settings) straight to the Telegram Bot API; network is the configured Hermes provider, Telegram, local Ollama classifiers, Google Gemini/Lyria media only with RELIC_ENABLE_GOOGLE_MEDIA=1 and a key, Ollama Cloud (ollama.com) only if explicitly configured, and local ComfyUI or ACE-Step servers only if the user enables them; no telemetry, no self-updater.

entries.name: reliquary
entries.description: Local, inspectable long-term memory with source provenance, conversation capture, General/project REL routing, a read-only PHY identity layer, and an interactive relationship-driven 3D graph in Hermes. Disclosure — launches a profile-scoped Rust background host (built by the user from the repo's source or taken from its attested CI build; nothing is downloaded by the plugin) on HMAC-authenticated loopback HTTP that can keep running after a session to finish recovery; reads/writes the selected REL files, reads the selected PHY and a nonsecret processing-routes JSON, and stores copied source text, queues, recovery state and graph caches under the Hermes profile's reliquary directory; setup generates a local host token into the profile .env through Hermes' secret writer and sets memory.provider and plugins.enabled in config.yaml. Optional processing and retrieval send bounded queries, source excerpts and Memories to the model endpoints the user configures and can incur provider charges. Automatic and manual conversation capture and the Desktop graph need Hermes core patches the repo ships but does not apply (patches/hermes-104a7c4-hu08-history-export.patch, patches/hermes-45882968-plugin-rest-bytes.patch); on stock Hermes capture stays paused and Desktop shows list and inspector only. No telemetry or self-updater.
entries.title: Reliquary
known_issues: Build the native host with scripts/build-native.ps1 before running Hermes memory setup; no executable is committed or automatically downloaded.
The attested CI artifact uses optimization level 1; the local source-build script retains full release optimization.
Processing accepts nonsecret JSON routes and a Hermes-managed API key. Reliquary CVCFG credentials and Codex subscription sign-in are unsupported in this catalog package.
Stock Desktop supports browsing. Desktop graph bytes, setup, and writes depend on Hermes SDK/native-admission capabilities; the web dashboard supports setup and writes.
Automatic capture and project routing require trusted Hermes history/project capabilities. Unsupported hosts pause automatic capture and use General memory for new sessions.
Imported Memories without accepted source provenance may be visible while production recall refuses them. The demo labels its imported-memory preview scenes.

entries.name: remesher
entries.description: Bounded image-to-GLB jobs using an isolated Remesher CLI, with existing ComfyUI/Comfy3D or native TRELLIS.2 and Pixal3D runtimes. Four Python SDK tools provide health, generation, persistent job status and hashed GLB assets, plus a setup/generation skill. Apache-2.0 for Remesher code; third-party terms remain separate. Disclosure — reads selected local images and configured files, uploads images to the configured ComfyUI server, launches local CLI subprocesses and detached supervisors, optionally owns a GPU runtime, and stores inputs, logs and assets in profile plugin data. Client/runtime installation and model downloads require separate explicit opt-ins; no model weights are bundled. No credentials or telemetry are required. No Desktop viewer or hosted service is included.
entries.title: Remesher
known_issues: Native inference tested on Linux ARM64 NVIDIA Spark only; macOS, Windows, CPU, MPS and ROCm inference are not certified.
Requires Python 3.11+, a separately installed CLI and configured runtime/model files. Native quality settings are explicit resource-intensive opt-ins, not automatic defaults.
Single-image quality remains provisional; no automatic background removal, manifold, watertightness or production-anatomy guarantee.
One active job per profile; retention is manual and native runtime logs are not size-capped. Local timeout does not cancel work on an existing remote server.

entries.name: reminders-kanban
entries.description: Apple Reminders as a Kanban board in Hermes Desktop: pick lists, move cards between To do, Ready for Agent, In progress, Needs you and Done, and edit titles, notes, due dates, priorities and lists, saved back to Reminders, and delegate reminders to Hermes for a reviewed result. Experimental macOS preview. Disclosure — on an explicit Set up Reminders access click it compiles a small Swift EventKit helper from the plugin's own source with the local Xcode Command Line Tools (offering xcode-select --install when missing), creates a per-user self-signed code-signing certificate with /usr/bin/openssl, imports it into the login keychain and trusts it for code signing only (user domain, no system trust or Gatekeeper change), and signs the helper with it; the helper reads and writes the Apple Reminders lists the user selects, after the macOS Reminders consent prompt; setup files live in ~/Library/Application Support/reminders-kanban and the build in ~/Library/Caches/reminders-kanban; while enabled in a running gateway a background pass runs every five seconds; each delegated run is a Hermes scheduled job named 'Reminders: <task>' that the plugin creates through the public cronjob tool and removes when the run ends, running unattended on the profile's main model under approvals.cron_mode; the plugin registers two tools, reminders_kanban_finish and reminders_kanban_ask, which only accept a call from the job it started for that run; an explicit task-link setup action reads local Tailscale status and can set only dashboard.public_url through the Hermes CLI or add a private Tailscale Serve route; undo retains only the previous URL, not a config copy; helper and setup subprocesses receive a minimal environment without inherited provider credentials; no third-party network calls, telemetry or self-update; uses public Hermes plugin interfaces only.

entries.name: remoet
entries.description: Tech job search: search the public board of open tech roles, find companies by the stack they hire for, star the ones that fit and pull new roles from your shortlist, through Remoet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Remoet's MCP server at api.remoet.dev with the search terms and the profile, job and application details the user asks for, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. search_jobs, search_listings and get_listing work without an account. Write tools change the user's Remoet account, and apply_to_job submits an application to an employer; profiles and saved work, project and education entries are public. The package marks the server untrusted, so write tools ask first, but the sign-in step (`hermes mcp add remoet`) writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from Remoet's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.
entries.title: Remoet
known_issues: Sign in once for the personal tools: hermes mcp add remoet --url https://api.remoet.dev/mcp/oauth --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300, then add `trust: untrusted` under `mcp_servers.remoet` in config.yaml to keep the approval prompt

entries.name: renor
entries.description: Renor memory provider: one durable memory shared by Hermes, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor over MCP, so what you tell one agent the others already know. Recalls before each turn within a hard deadline (1.5 s by default; the turn goes on without it) and saves the durable statements you make (preferences, decisions, rules, "remember that ...") after it, through a bounded background queue with retries; also on compaction and at session end. Stored text never enters the prompt automatically: recall reports a count and the agent reads matches with renor_recall, labelled untrusted data. Hosted (mcp.renor.cloud, connection key) or the open-source engine, offline. Standard library only. Maintained by Renor. Disclosure — in hosted mode each non-trivial user message (as the recall query), the durable statements picked out of user messages, renor_remember saves and Hermes built-in memory entries are sent over HTTPS to mcp.renor.cloud (or the configured RENOR_MCP_URL) under RENOR_API_KEY; RENOR_AUTO_SAVE=turns also sends each turn's user message and reply. The plugin has no telemetry. Renor's own learning setting is the hosted workspace owner's (anonymous usage numbers by default, never text; off under Settings > Learning); in self-hosted mode the plugin starts the user's RENOR_ENGINE_COMMAND as one long-lived child process with DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and RENOR_SHARING=off unless RENOR_ALLOW_SHARING=1, and makes no network calls of its own.

entries.name: repager
entries.description: Evidence-bound hero design lab with approved copy, local layout exploration, revision-bound browser checks and portable review handoffs. Disclosure — captures the public page you name with a locally installed Node.js + Playwright + Chromium (you install the npm dependencies and Chromium; nothing is downloaded at runtime) through a public-address-only local proxy; when you enable allow_model_calls it sends the captured page text, your brief and the approved copy to the host model configured under auxiliary.repager_layout; `hermes repager` opens an optional token-protected workbench on 127.0.0.1; reviews, screenshots and ZIP exports are kept under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/repager.
entries.title: repager
known_issues: Requires Node.js 20+, npm dependencies and separately provisioned compatible Chromium; no browser downloads at runtime.
Linux verified; POSIX file locking is required. Native Windows is unsupported.
Model calls are off until consented. Generation requires an explicit host auxiliary route without fallback chains. Local revisions use no additional inference.
Text-only hero alternatives, not whole-site reconstruction or proven conversion improvement; human review remains necessary.
Chromium sandboxing is on by default. Opt out only with separate appropriate container/VM isolation.

entries.name: requesty
entries.description: Requesty LLM gateway as a Hermes model provider (`--provider requesty`, alias `rq`, or Requesty in `hermes model`). The picker lists Requesty's managed routing policies (curated routes with failover, `@eu` variants for EU-only hosting); any Requesty model id or org policy also works. `/reasoning` maps onto Requesty's `reasoning_effort` for reasoning-capable models, the Hermes session id is sent as `requesty.trace_id`, and context windows and estimated cost come from the Requesty catalog. Prompt caching is done server-side by Requesty. Disclosure — chat requests go to https://router.requesty.ai/v1 (or REQUESTY_BASE_URL) through Hermes' own client with REQUESTY_API_KEY, which Hermes reads; the plugin itself only fetches Requesty's public model catalogs (/v1/models/managed and /v1/models, no credentials), once per process, sometimes on a short-lived background thread. No attribution headers, telemetry, file access or processes. Supersedes #27908.

entries.name: reset-rescue
entries.description: Redeems expiring OpenAI Codex rate-limit reset credits across every openai-codex account in the active Hermes profile's credential pool, with two Hermes one-shot cron attempts 10 and 4 minutes before expiry and success confirmed by backend readback. Includes opt-in early redemption at low weekly quota, per-account overrides, Hermes channel notices, a Desktop status-bar chip and popup, and dashboard settings. Account labels and domains are masked by default. Disclosure — reads every openai-codex row of the profile's credential pool with Hermes' read_credential_pool helper; in a named profile with no Codex rows of its own that helper falls back read-only to the root profile's accounts, so the plugin then redeems the root profile's credits. It holds each account's access token in memory only and sends it only to https://chatgpt.com (redirects refused) with Codex CLI client headers (User-Agent codex-cli, ChatGPT-Account-ID, x-openai-internal-codex-residency, the same headers Hermes' own usage fetcher sends) to list reset credits (/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits), read usage (/backend-api/wham/usage) and consume credits (/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits/consume); the consume POST spends an owned credit through a private, undocumented endpoint. An empty pool falls back to the active sign-in through credentialed_provider_request. On HTTP 401 it runs hermes auth refresh openai-codex <entry>, so Hermes may rotate and save that account's tokens; the plugin itself never reads or writes credential files or stores or logs tokens. Running hermes reset-rescue ensure, or turning on the Desktop status-bar chip (off by default; its first status check arms the jobs), writes five launcher scripts to <HERMES_HOME>/scripts/ and creates no-agent Hermes cron jobs (a recurring scan plus one-shot rescue, backup and reminder jobs per credit); these run the hermes CLI with the inherited environment minus approval-bypass variables. It sends notices with hermes send to notify_target or the home channel, keeps credential-free state under plugin-data/reset-rescue, and its dashboard settings write its own plugins.entries.reset-rescue.settings through Hermes' settings writer. Automatic redemption is on by default and can be turned off globally or per account (dry_run pauses spending); early redemption is off by default and manual redemption requires confirmation. Run hermes reset-rescue uninstall before removing the plugin to delete its jobs and scripts. It does not purchase credits or enable overage.

Running hermes reset-rescue ensure, or turning on the Desktop status-bar chip (off by default; its first status check arms the jobs), writes five launcher scripts to <HERMES_HOME>/scripts/ and creates no-agent Hermes cron jobs (a recurring scan plus one-shot rescue, backup and reminder jobs per credit); these run the hermes CLI with the inherited environment minus approval-bypass variables. It sends notices with hermes send to notify_target or the home channel, keeps credential-free state under plugin-data/reset-rescue, and its dashboard settings write its own plugins.entries.reset-rescue.settings through Hermes' settings writer. Automatic redemption is on by default and can be turned off globally or per account (dry_run pauses spending); early redemption is off by default and manual redemption requires confirmation. Run hermes reset-rescue uninstall before removing the plugin to delete its jobs and scripts. It does not purchase credits or enable overage. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Platforms: linux, macos. Requires Hermes >=0.22.6.

entries.name: restoreproof
entries.description: Recovery drills for real application stacks: restores a declared database backup (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB or SQLite) and uploads archive into an isolated Docker network, boots the app, and proves whether customers' journeys come back (every database file reference, a real user flow, recovery time and RPO), then cleans up and writes a hashed evidence report. entries.name: retake
entries.description: Image-generation workspace for Hermes Desktop. Generate or upload an image, mark regions, request a reference-guided revision, compare versions and download. Disclosure — images, region notes and revision references you send are passed to your configured Hermes image provider, which may use credits or allowance; generated result links are downloaded from that provider; projects and image versions are stored in a local database in your Hermes profile.
entries.title: Retake
known_issues: Still images only. Video generation is not included.
Region notes are guidance, not masks: other parts of an image can change and pixel preservation is not guaranteed.
Generation uses your Hermes image provider and may consume credits or allowance; cost and exact model can be unknown. A failed or lost call is shown as possibly billed and is never retried.
Needs Hermes's mcp extra. If tool search hides image_generate, remove only that name from the profile's effective tools.tool_search.defer list (see the README); Retake never changes config for you.
Optional model picker is hidden on stock Hermes v0.23.1; it appears only if Hermes exposes the image-selection listing.

Screenshots are real Hermes Desktop captures with AI-generated demo art. Mac acceptance includes user-reported checks; Linux used a renderer harness plus one real revision, and native Linux input and upload acceptance is not claimed.

entries.name: retouch
entries.description: Mark the parts of any image that need work in a Hermes Desktop pane, leave a note on each, and Hermes fixes only those areas. Each mark has its own thread; every edit is a new version, checked pixel by pixel and refused if anything outside its mark changed; only you can accept a mark. Tonal and privacy edits need no image provider, removals and replacements use the image_generate provider you configured. Saves new files, never the original. Disclosure — images you open are copied into this profile's plugin-data/retouch folder. Send starts hidden Hermes sessions, one per group of overlapping marks and up to three at a time, with your usual tools, settings and approvals; they use model credits and stay in your session history. Your chat model's provider, or that of the model picked beside Send, receives a downscaled overview of the image, a close-up of each mark and before/after strips. The generate method sends a crop around the mark to your image_generate provider and downloads the result (https only, public addresses only, at most 40 MB). Text inside a picture is treated as picture content by instruction, which is not a barrier, so treat an untrusted picture of text like pasted text. Untouched pasted scratch projects are deleted about a day later. The plugin itself makes no other network calls, runs no shell commands, stores no credentials and sends no telemetry; exports strip GPS and embedded text metadata.

entries.name: return-line
entries.description: Carry the agent's own state and dated excerpts of its own record into every live turn — appended to the message being answered at API time, never the system prompt, so per-conversation prompt caching is untouched. One raw ledger line per turn goes the other way. Works stand-alone; pairs with the biomimetic-brain mind kit, which produces the state file it reads. Disclosure — it appends an agent-state block and retrieved record excerpts to the current user message on every turn, leaving the system prompt untouched; it indexes recent user and assistant messages from $HERMES_HOME/state.db across all sessions and platforms into a local plaintext SQLite index under the configured agent directory, and may surface those excerpts in any later conversation (relevant on multi-user gateways); it appends every turn's inbound and outbound text to <agent_dir>/turn-ledger.jsonl; it loads <agent_dir>/scripts/wander.py from the companion mind kit in-process and may run that script and <agent_dir>/scripts/consolidate-mind.py as background subprocesses with the Hermes environment; no network calls of its own, no credentials, no dependencies beyond the host interpreter (numpy and scikit-learn are optional, with a keyword-search fallback).

entries.name: rh-preflight
entries.description: rh-preflight by quotum with HEY Research Lab. Before Hermes Agent acts on Robinhood Chain (chain 4663), a pre_tool_call hook reads HEY Research Lab's builder record and ten Robinhood Chain projects for the addresses, agent ids, pools or repositories in the call, then applies your own rules: go, ask (a human approval prompt) or stop in detected cron by default; other asks use Hermes Agent approval, including its YOLO bypass. Unsigned transactions and wallet signing requests get a Toll simulation card with sender balance changes. The card lists each source's line with its link; builder_card and /rh-preflight read a card without acting. Desktop page shows recent checks and human answers. Disclosure — sends only the identifiers you act on to the source hosts listed in the README, plus read-only Robinhood Chain RPC, DexScreener and GeckoTerminal reads; when transaction simulation is on, the detected unsigned transaction or signing request goes to Toll (t0ll.xyz) and HookrRouter trades get a read-only Hookr pool check. Keyless and free (an optional TOLL_API_KEY, read from your Hermes Agent profile secrets, is sent only to Toll); no payments, signatures, subprocesses or writes. Stores a local SQLite ledger of checks in its own plugin data folder. Source records describe what each project published; rh-preflight does not call a token good or bad.
entries.title: rh-preflight
known_issues: Fail-closed: when a source does not answer inside the shared timeout (default 4 s), the card says so and your rule may ask instead of go.
Detection covers up to five addresses per call in configured action tools; tool names are matched by the tool_patterns setting.

On Hermes Agent 0.23.0/0.23.1 with Tool Search on, a deferred plugin action tool called through the tool_call bridge skips pre_tool_call, so the gate does not see it; run `hermes config set tools.tool_search.enabled off` or use a newer Hermes Agent with the fix (PR #155527).

entries.name: rhythm-reaper
entries.description: A hip-hop producer desk — 41 lanes across seven families (foundational, trap, drill, melodic, alt, hard, conscious), each with the full production spec (tempo family, key centres, drum programme, low end, harmony and sample source, vocal delivery, metatag vocabulary, exclude list, generation notes) and, for any of them, a complete pasteable Suno deliverable: the style field written out with the dynamic ARC, the Exclude Styles line, a tagged lyric frame with bar targets, an energy map and a pronunciation lexicon. It validates a finished draft against the real platform limits (style <= 1000 chars, lyrics <= 3000, every section carrying a recognised structural tag, no contradictory dynamic tags in one section, a real chorus/hook, known-to-slur proper nouns left un-respelled) and enforces the two character limits in code rather than by eye. It deliberately does not generate lyrics — template bars are slop and the desk says so — it hands the writer a frame that is already correct. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials, no shell, no subprocesses and no files written outside the plugin: the 41-lane catalog is a Python module in the repo and every tool is pure local computation, so no tool is credential-gated (a missing secret can never hide one). 55 offline tests, including a sweep asserting all 41 lanes build a deliverable that passes its own gates.
entries.title: The Rhythm Reaper
known_issues: It refuses to write your bars on purpose — it returns a frame with bar slots and the hook placed, and the lyric is yours. Template lyrics were left out by design, not as a missing feature.
Templates are not evaluations: the desk knows production specs, not how a specific model will render them. Unusual pronunciations still want a 30-second test clip before a full render.

entries.name: riah-swipe
entries.description: Swipe through what your agent made. Hermes puts a batch of options (images, video, audio, names, taglines) into a swipe deck; you keep, cut, or send one back with a note, and Hermes remakes the ones you sent back. On Telegram the deck appears in the chat with Keep, Cut, Redo and Undo buttons, and you type a note on any card to say why; elsewhere you get a sign-in board link for desktop or phone. Runs a small local HTTP server inside Hermes and writes only to its plugin-data folder; no extra dependencies, telemetry or accounts. Full disclosure in the README. Disclosure — runs a local HTTP board server inside Hermes (127.0.0.1 by default; every browser signs in once with a one-time link), and with `lan: true` it listens on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) over plain HTTP; the board page loads fonts from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com), and `https://` media links on cards are loaded by your browser and by Telegram; `swipe_publish` copies local media from the working folder, Hermes' media caches, the temp folders and `media_dirs` into its plugin-data folder; while a Telegram deck is open, the swiper's own text and voice messages become card notes instead of reaching Hermes, and voice notes go through your configured Hermes speech-to-text.

entries.name: rich-paste
entries.description: Paste web pages, screenshots and Finder files into Hermes Desktop with their structure, and send each image to the model where it sits in your text. Web HTML becomes Markdown (headings, links, lists, tables, code) with its images downloaded and attached; an llm_request middleware moves each image block next to its label instead of after all the text (kimi-k3, several images per paragraph: 18/30 today, 30/30 interleaved). Also: screenshot chips placed after what you typed, Finder files and folders as Desktop blocks, TIFF/HEIC/BMP/AVIF sent as PNG, pasted audio transcribed with Hermes's own STT, Markdown preview. A select-all copy of a whole web page keeps only the article (Mozilla Readability 0.6.0, Apache-2.0, bundled and run locally with no network request), with "Restore full page" under the composer. Disclosure — network calls only to download the images of pages you paste (http/https; loopback, private, link-local and reserved addresses refused on every redirect, except DNS answers in 198.18.0.0/15 for proxy fake-ip setups; the pasted page's URL is sent as Referer; at most 50 images per paste and 20 MB each); no telemetry. Runs /usr/bin/osascript once per file paste to read file URLs on the macOS clipboard. Reads image attachments you add (hashes them, converts TIFF/HEIC/BMP/AVIF to PNG) and Desktop's saved long-paste files. Writes only under its cache folder. Pasted audio is transcribed with Hermes's own STT, which uploads it to your configured cloud STT provider when one is set (the plugin asks first). An llm_request middleware reorders the image blocks of every user message that carries its markers in the outgoing request.

Disclosure — network calls only to download the images of pages you paste (http/https; loopback, private, link-local and reserved addresses refused on every redirect, except DNS answers in 198.18.0.0/15 for proxy fake-ip setups; the pasted page's URL is sent as Referer; at most 50 images per paste and 20 MB each); no telemetry. Runs /usr/bin/osascript once per file paste to read file URLs on the macOS clipboard. Reads image attachments you add (hashes them, converts TIFF/HEIC/BMP/AVIF to PNG) and Desktop's saved long-paste files. Writes only under its cache folder. Pasted audio is transcribed with Hermes's own STT, which uploads it to your configured cloud STT provider when one is set (the plugin asks first). An llm_request middleware reorders the image blocks of every user message that carries its markers in the outgoing request. This plugin middleware: llm_request. Requires Hermes >=0.23.0. Known issues: Tested on macOS only. Pasting Finder files needs macOS; elsewhere, drag files into the composer..

entries.name: rollstack
entries.description: Build polished presentations using AI, with advanced charts and data connections built in. Rollstack's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE) comes with eleven workflow skills. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector: Hermes runs no code from the package, and the repository's pi/ and dsh/ folders are for other agents and are not loaded by Hermes. Every tool call goes to Rollstack's MCP server at api.rollstack.com, signed in as the user with their Rollstack account, which they must already have. Report names, slide content, the data behind slides, schedules, and the names and email addresses of workspace members and report recipients are pulled into the session context, and so reach the user's model provider. Tools create and change reports, slides, schedules and sharing, and can send report emails and delete reports; the package declares the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write-capable call, and sending an email or deleting a report also waits for the user to confirm it in Rollstack. The tool list comes from Rollstack's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. Sign in with `hermes mcp add rollstack --url https://api.rollstack.com/public/v1/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`, then run `hermes config set mcp_servers.rollstack.trust untrusted` so the sign-in entry keeps the approval prompts; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.
entries.title: Rollstack
known_issues: Sign in once after installing: hermes mcp add rollstack --url https://api.rollstack.com/public/v1/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300
Then keep Hermes asking before write calls, which the sign-in entry would otherwise drop: hermes config set mcp_servers.rollstack.trust untrusted

entries.name: rom-studio
entries.description: Make your own small game by talking with your agent, one scene at a time, from a decomp (the community-made source of an original handheld game) that you supply. A pane in the desktop app, also a tab in the web dashboard, shows each change as a sentence with a picture from the running game, plus a play link, scenes, gallery, maps, music, dialogue, source search and the agent's questions. Ships a command-line kit the agent runs, a browser player with an always-on flash guard and the make-your-game skill; starts one local page on 127.0.0.1 once a game folder is set. kit agent-play, started by hand, can send game pictures to a model API you name. No agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Linux only. Disclosure — Starts a local page on 127.0.0.1 (port 8778) whenever a game folder is set, restarts it if it stops and stops it when Hermes ends, and `kit play` starts a local player on 127.0.0.1:4870 (with `--phone`, also an https listener on this computer's LAN addresses, opened by a key link). `kit setup` git-clones the decomp address you give, downloads the poryscript 3.6.1 compiler from GitHub (checked against a sha256) and installs the player's npm package, and the build runs your decomp's own Makefile and tools on your computer. `kit agent-play --provider`, run by hand, sends pictures of the game and its on-screen state to the model API you name, using the key from the environment variable you choose.
entries.title: ROM Studio
known_issues: Seen running in the web dashboard tab and in the desktop workspace served by hermes webapp, on Linux with Hermes 0.23. Not yet seen in the packaged desktop app.
Linux only. macOS and Windows are not supported (the build scripts use Linux tools and the script compiler download is a Linux program); Windows through WSL has not been tried.

Needs bun, git and a toolchain for the game that you install yourself: make, python3 with Pillow, C and C++ compilers, flock, libpng with pkg-config, arm-none-eabi-gcc 14.2, cmake and a libmgba 0.10.5 you build once; ffmpeg for sound. kit status lists what is missing and how to get it.
You bring the decomp and, to make a patch, your own copy of the original game file. ROM Studio includes and fetches neither. The first build takes about 7 minutes and a game folder about 1 GB.

The optional base (calm changes inside the game, quick start, the test hook, the cheat codes engine) is patches for one version of one engine and is not shipped. Without it the flag, creature-gift, exact-text and cheat-code steps are unavailable, and each new build plays through the original opening once. The player's flash guard is always on regardless.
The phone link of the player (kit play --phone) has not been tried on a real phone. The kit's MCP server has been tried over stdio by hand, not inside Hermes.
Setup's caches (headless emulator, script compiler, browser emulator) live inside the plugin folder; if an update removes them, run kit setup again.
The kit does not read the plugin's settings: for a game folder other than the default, also set ROM_STUDIO_GAME where your agent's commands run.

entries.name: rookery
entries.description: A step-sequencer DAW inside Hermes Desktop: tell the agent the beat and watch the grid fill in, then add free Soundza loops (Openverse CC0 fallback), arrange a song, and render locally at an exact length, checked for clipping, loudness and the loop seam and reproducible byte for byte. Exports WAV, stems, MIDI and cues.json for video. Disclosure — writes projects, history, renders and exports under plugin_data_dir("rookery") and reads the configured user_kit_dir; loads only the VST3 effect you set as corvus_vst3_path, in-process through pedalboard (third-party native code running with your permissions), and none when it is unset; rookery_samples calls api.soundza.com and follows its signed Cloudflare R2 download links, or api.openverse.org and cdn.freesound.org with source="openverse" (search needs no key; downloads need the optional free SOUNDZA_API_KEY, which is sent only to api.soundza.com); no telemetry.
entries.title: Rookery
known_issues: The Desktop page, live audio playback and Corvus knobs are verified on Windows 11 only; macOS and Linux are untested for the UI and audio path.
The Flock melodic layer is edited in the Rookery page only; the agent has no Flock tool and cannot add or re-voice the wire.
No MIDI import, no audio recording, and no note-to-note 808 portamento.
An arrangement can change mutes, steps and notes per section, but not tempo, meter or automation inside the song.

entries.name: roomsmith
entries.description: One 3D room that you and Hermes both edit. It tells you whether things fit and what they cost. Drag furniture in a live editor inside Hermes Desktop or the dashboard, or tell Hermes what to change: one saved room with undo, and each sees what the other did. Give a budget and Hermes furnishes the room with real products, read from their pages and checked against your room and your money. Start from a photo or measurements. No accounts or keys. Network: only GETs to product pages (public addresses only, rate-capped). Never buys anything. Disclosure — the agent's product tools make GET requests to product-page and product-image URLs that you or the agent give (http/https on public addresses only; private/LAN/loopback hosts and redirects to them are refused; rate-capped; results cached under the plugin's data folder); roomsmith_from_photo reads JPEG/PNG/WebP files at paths the agent names and sends them to your active Hermes model to draft the room; a pre_llm_call hook adds a few lines about your editor changes and furnishing budget to turns in rooms sessions; all data stays in <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/roomsmith; it never buys anything.
entries.title: Roomsmith
known_issues: Sizes read from a photo are estimates until you set one real measurement (a wall, the door, or an object).
iPhone HEIC photos must be exported as JPEG/PNG first.
Furnishing with real products depends on the shops: some refuse automated reads or print no size; the plugin says so and never invents a size or price.

entries.name: rosegold
entries.description: Get offers and rewards matched to what you buy on Amazon, including discount codes, promo codes and influencer codes. Hermes shares the order details in your Amazon order confirmations with rosegold, then looks up the offers, creator codes and spending rosegold has for you. rosegold reads order confirmations from Amazon, limited to order number, email id, date, total, and each item's title, quantity and price; it does not read your address, payment details or any other emails. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json only); hosted MCP server with three tools, sign-in by emailed code over OAuth, no API key; one command after install (see known issues). Disclosure — every tool call goes to rosegold.app, and the remote tools are not covered by the pin; the tools ask the agent to search the user's Gmail, with Hermes's own Gmail tool, for Amazon order confirmations, and to send rosegold each email's id and date and each order's number, items and prices; a look-up brings the user's offers and spending into the chat; under the default trust the tools run without an approval prompt; Hermes keeps the OAuth token.
known_issues: Sign in once after installing, because a portable plugin can't declare an OAuth MCP server: hermes mcp add rosegold --url https://rosegold.app/mcp/v1 --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300

entries.name: rply-platform
entries.description: rply gateway platform: talk to Hermes from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Hermes as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Hermes' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `hermes rply` setup command; credentials read through Hermes' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: rply
entries.capability_summary: rply-platform (community, maintained by joshuaKnauber) rply gateway platform: talk to Hermes from the rply inbox on your phone and laptop, with web push. Messages and files both ways, seen/working/done with a live activity note, clarify questions and command approvals as tappable questions, cron delivery, a pinned table of scheduled jobs, a dashboard app with run/pause/resume, and an rply_request_secret tool that saves API keys to the profile's .env without the value passing through the chat. Each profile joins the channel as its own agent. Disclosure — keeps a long-polling connection to the configured rply server only (RPLY_SERVER, default https://app.rply.sh; self-hostable, AGPL server); messages the channel's members send reach Hermes as user instructions and members answer its approval and clarify prompts; the dashboard sends the server Hermes' cron job list, the titles and previews of the 10 most recent sessions from every platform, token and cost totals and the default model, and runs, pauses or resumes jobs when its buttons are pressed; stores the agent token in the profile's .env, an X25519 keypair in <profile>/rply/secret-key.json (0600) and secrets the human provides in the profile's .env under a variable name the agent picks (core's env denylist applies; the .env path is sent to the server with the request); the secret tool waits up to 15 minutes for the human and refuses under cron; adds a `hermes rply` setup command; credentials read through Hermes' profile-scoped route; no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update. This plugin registers tool(s): rply_request_secret. Requires Hermes >=0.22.2.

entries.name: rss-lite
entries.description: Lightweight RSS, Atom and YouTube reader page for Hermes Desktop: folders, unread/saved, search, a sanitized reader view, and optional AI summaries on your configured model. Disclosure — the gateway fetches only the feeds you add (and a pasted web page or YouTube @handle page once, to find its feed) through the plugin's own SSRF-guarded backend route, sending YouTube's anonymous consent cookie SOCS=CAI to YouTube hosts only; Desktop loads thumbnails and article images directly from publishers (can be turned off) and a YouTube video only after you press Play, through Desktop's own embed; Summarise sends the article title and up to 12,000 characters of its text to your configured model; subscriptions are stored in HERMES_HOME/rss-lite; no shell commands, background processes, credentials or telemetry. Independent implementation, not derived from hermes-rss or rss-reader.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite-docker
entries.description: Community plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local). Docker and remote backends stay unchanged unless opted in; install rtk inside each backend before opting in. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Hermes host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

entries.name: rtk-rewrite
entries.description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/hermes/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

entries.name: ruapi
entries.description: RuAPI as Hermes model providers on one key: `ruapi` serves Claude models over RuAPI's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `ruapi-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other chat models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's chat models from the account's GET /v1/models list, leaving out image and video models, and context windows and image input are declared for the main models. Maintained by RuAPI. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and RUAPI_API_KEY go to https://www.ruapi.ai (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and RuAPI forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The model list is Hermes' standard GET https://www.ruapi.ai/v1/models request with the key; the plugin makes no network requests of its own, adds no headers, sends no telemetry, reads or writes no files and stores no credentials.

entries.name: rubal-oracle
entries.description: Say a goal in Hermes chat with a deadline. Afterward Oracle checks proof (met / not met / couldn't verify) from git, Calendar, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Gmail, kanban, Strava, or Apple Health. Rubal is the forecast from similar past attempts. Disclosure — runs local git log on repo paths the user names; stores commitments in Hermes plugin SQLite under the plugin data dir; caches Calendar event JSON from Hermes terminal/tool output (no Hermes credential reads, no google-workspace subprocess from plugin code); non-git settlers use data the agent already fetched; does not send telemetry.

entries.name: rule-injector
entries.description: Moves agent behavioural rules out of the system prompt and injects each one at the point of need, through three hooks: pre_llm_call for behavioural guards, transform_tool_result for corrections the model reads in place, and pre_verify as a completion gate. A rule is {trigger, inject} — matched on keywords, regex, tool name, tool error, path or session scope, or a boolean compound of those — with a per-turn injection budget and an undroppable always-on floor. An optional adjudicator adds a semantic second pass over ambiguous turns, and propose.py drafts a rule from a user correction. Ships a local web dashboard (`python3 dashboard.py`, FastAPI, read-only) that lists the rule set and the recent activation trace, and seven starter rules; rules.json is a template the user replaces. Disclosure — writes one activation trace line per fired rule, a rule-drafting audit line, and (only with the adjudicator enabled) a 48-hour verdict log holding excerpts of the user message and recent turns, all under the active HERMES_HOME's logs/ directory, and writes the plugin's rules.json when a rule is created through its own CLI; no shell and no telemetry; the optional dashboard (`python3 dashboard.py`, fastapi + uvicorn installed by the user) binds 127.0.0.1 and only reads the rules file and trace log; semantic triggers download a sentence-transformers embedding model from Hugging Face once and then run locally; the optional adjudicator, only when enabled, sends the current turn to the user's active model through Hermes' plugin LLM facade and holds no key of its own.

entries.name: runa
entries.description: Bring your Runa meetings into Hermes: prep for what's next, recap decisions and who owes what, draft the follow-up, and find the exact words behind a claim, through Runa's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1), with four workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to Runa's MCP server at mcp.joinruna.com, signed in as the user through Runa's sign-in (Google or Microsoft), and a first sign-in creates a Runa account. Meeting titles, summaries, transcripts, action items, people and company notes, and reads from apps the user connected to Runa are pulled into the session context, and so reach the user's model provider. No tool changes data in Runa or in those apps; Runa logs each call's metadata. The tool list comes from Runa's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add runa --url https://mcp.joinruna.com/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: runbox
entries.description: Build, run and test Python in an offline container per chat, with results as a plain file:line issue list. The agent syncs files or folders in as copies, then runs run (a shell command), check (ruff error rules) and test (pytest); fixes stay in the box until the user asks for export, which writes changed files back through write_file and reports host files changed since the sync as conflicts. In Hermes Desktop a VS Code-style editor opens beside the chat: file tabs with in-place editing, Run / Check / Test / Stop, and PROBLEMS / OUTPUT / RUNS panels that follow the agent live. Ships the runbox:dev-loop starting-point skill. Disclosure — needs Docker (on macOS a dedicated colima profile 'runbox', started on demand with --activate=false and its own Docker config); pulls the container image pinned by digest and installs a hash-pinned checker toolchain (ruff 0.16.9, pytest 9.1.1 and deps) from PyPI once per image; the work container has no network, hardened flags, and runs commands without Hermes' dangerous-command approval like Hermes' Docker backend; install (PyPI) always asks for approval in a separate installer container; a write_file/patch on an imported original asks for approval (guard_imports); export reads each existing target through read_file before replacing it; a background thread removes idle containers (15 min), stops the VM, and removes boxes of deleted or long-idle chats (reads state.db read-only hourly); adds a short per-turn note (about 80 tokens); no credentials or telemetry.
entries.title: runbox
known_issues: Needs Docker: on macOS install colima and the docker CLI (brew install colima docker); on Linux a running Docker daemon. The first start on macOS downloads the VM image and takes a few minutes.
The Hermes data folder must be under your home folder on macOS (colima shares only that).
The agent may not always pick runbox on its own (the model chooses its tools). Ask it to use runbox.

entries.name: rung
entries.description: Stops an agent from marking its own work done until the tests you approved pass. Tests are approved before any code; when an agent reports claimed work done (rung_report, kanban_complete or a todo item), a deterministic pre_tool_call hook blocks the report until those tests pass on the current code and names the ones that fail. No model is asked. A Desktop pane and dock hold the ladder from need to test result; manual checks stay with a person, and milestones verify whole user journeys. Local SQLite, no network calls of its own. Disclosure — Runs the shell commands a person approved as tests, contract checks, milestone checks and environment probes/migrations on the host, outside the Hermes sandbox, with the user's privileges, including when the agent calls rung_run_tests; those commands execute files in the project folder that the agent can edit, and receive only PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, the project's own virtual environment and the variables a person names in the project's settings. Pressing Send or Suggest in the Rung pane starts `hermes -p <profile> chat` subprocesses that work in the project folder. On first open Rung reads every profile's config.yaml (platform_toolsets only) and runs `hermes -p <profile> tools list` for each one. A profile without its own Rung store shares the root profile's ladder.
