entries.name: saascity
entries.description: Plan a SaaS, AI or developer-tool launch through SaaSCity's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://saascity.io/api/mcp, no sign-in, no keys in config): audit a homepage the way directory scrapers see it, pick launch directories from 1,600+ with Ahrefs DR, link type and price, research products listed on SaaSCity, run SaaS metric calculators, and draft a SaaSCity listing for the user to review. Bundles one workflow skill, launch-plan. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to saascity.io, which runs SaaSCity. check_launch_readiness, check_badge and check_backlink make saascity.io fetch the URL the user gives. submit_project sends the approved product details to SaaSCity and stores them as an inert draft, with the caller's IP for rate limits, that expires after 7 days unless the user claims it; nothing is published or charged unless the user opens the claim link and pays on saascity.io. Every tool is annotated read-only except submit_project; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before it runs and refuses it in unattended runs. saascity.io is not available in every region (HTTP 451 there). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.name: sabbath
entries.description: Your agent never rests. Now it rests with you. Once a week (say Saturday 18:00, for 24 hours) Hermes keeps a day of rest with you: it says goodnight on your phone, pauses its own scheduled jobs (except the ones you exempt), keeps you company in anything but work and offers to set aside what can wait, then sends one gentle digest when the rest ends while the jobs catch up. /sabbath ox lifts it for an hour when something truly can't wait. Desktop page with your week at a glance; /sabbath on every chat surface; try a two-minute Sabbath. Disclosure — pauses and resumes the user's Hermes cron jobs through Hermes' cronjob_manage tool (resuming only the jobs it paused); sends a goodnight and a digest to the chat the user sets by running Hermes' own `hermes send` CLI with the text over stdin; adds rest context to each turn while resting; stores its state in plain text under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/sabbath; no telemetry.

entries.name: safari
entries.description: Drive the user's real Safari on macOS. Safari has no Chrome DevTools Protocol, so this plugin speaks AppleScript (JXA) to Safari for tabs, navigation, DOM reads, and real native mouse/keyboard input. Because it drives the browser the user is already signed into, logged-in sites work without a separate automation profile. Registers a `safari` toolset (eight tools) and a `hermes safari` command that reports every macOS permission gate and the fix for each. Disclosure — drives your real, signed-in Safari: the agent can open any URL (including local `file://` pages), read page text, run arbitrary JavaScript in any open tab, type, submit forms and send real mouse clicks on your logged-in sites without a per-action Hermes approval, and Hermes's browser website blocklist does not apply. Requires macOS Automation consent and, for page reads and scripts, Safari's "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events"; native clicks use `cliclick` or Accessibility, screenshots need Screen Recording. Tabs it opens are closed after an hour idle.

entries.name: safe-swap
entries.description: Rewrites destructive shell commands into safe twins before they run instead of snapshotting afterwards: git push --force becomes --force-with-lease --force-if-includes, rm -r becomes a move into a quarantine folder (with a file and byte count), and git reset --hard, git checkout -- / git restore, git clean and git stash drop take a private snapshot first, with /swaps and /unswap to undo and a visible note whenever a destructive command was left unswapped. Disclosure - rewrites the command of the terminal tool before it executes (modify only: never blocks, never prompts, any error or doubt leaves the command unchanged); writes quarantine files and receipts under the user's home on the machine where the command runs (~/.safe-swap/trash by default) plus one SQLite file in the plugin data directory; for git clean, git reset --hard and git stash drop it writes snapshot commits into the repository's own object store under private refs refs/safe-swap/<id> (a git clean snapshot copies the content of the untracked files, and of the ignored ones with -x, until a purge; sets above 20,000 files or 200 MB are skipped and reported); it prints one marker line to stderr for an rm swap and removes it again from the tool result; the only deletion it ever performs is an explicit /swaps purge (or hermes safe-swap purge) by the user, which runs rm on its own quarantine directories and deletes its own private refs through the terminal tool and is subject to normal approval; no network calls, no telemetry, no background processes, no self-update; reads no credential files or .env, only the receipts it wrote and the sizes of the files an rm swap moves; approvals are respected: the rewritten command goes through Hermes' normal approval gate, and because a swapped rm -r is a move it no longer matches the recursive-delete pattern and does not prompt (the git rewrites keep prompting as before). Targets such as /, ~, $HOME, system directories and anything in the system temp directory, privilege-elevated commands, and commands with heredocs, subshells, command substitution or eval/xargs/find -exec are deliberately left alone, and the agent is told so. Not covered, by design: mv, cp overwrite, sed -i, redirects, write_file/patch, find -delete, git rebase (pair it with undo-effects for those).

entries.name: salesforce-chatter
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from Salesforce Chatter: @mention the bot user in a post or comment, it Likes the message as an acknowledgement and replies in the same thread, keeping the thread as one session. Images and files on the post are passed to the model; MEDIA files are attached back. Community plugin, not affiliated with Salesforce. Disclosure — authenticates as a dedicated bot user with the OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer flow, reading the private key file at SF_CHATTER_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH; talks to the configured Salesforce login host and the org instance (attachment downloads follow Salesforce redirects); image URLs in the agent's replies are fetched from the gateway host over HTTPS (any public host; private, loopback and metadata addresses are refused) and uploaded to Chatter; polls the To Me feed every 60 s and, for allowlisted groups, runs a SOQL probe every 5 s by default (counts against the org API quota); writes Likes, comments, files in the bot user's Files and optional home-channel posts; keeps its ledger in plugin-data/salesforce-chatter/inbox.sqlite. dry_run defaults to true (no Salesforce writes, no outbound image fetch); with SF_CHATTER_ALLOWED_USERS unset nobody is answered. Optional, off by default: html_preview renders model-generated HTML to PNG with Chromium in a network-isolated Docker container (digest-pinned image, pulled if missing). No telemetry.

entries.name: salesforce-guard
entries.description: Salesforce release-impact and scoped-access review: explicit-scope snapshot comparison, source-reference maps, local access evidence and HTML reports. Bounded security heuristics and partial OWASP mappings produce review signals, not org-wide assurance. Dedicated review profile blocks unrelated tools while the plugin is enabled. Custom native inputs require separate operator folder approval with model-sharing acknowledgement. Disclosure — while enabled, its pre_tool_call hook blocks every tool except its nine sfg_* tools and tool/skill discovery in that profile (terminal, files, browser, memory, delegation included), so install it in a dedicated review profile; reads only Salesforce source folders the operator approves in the plugin's input-approvals.json and sends requested source excerpts to the active model; writes reports under the plugin's own data folder; no network, shell or credential access from the plugin; the separate operator CLI in the repo (not installed by the catalog) runs the user's Salesforce CLI, which keeps its own login.
entries.title: Salesforce Guard
known_issues: Use a dedicated review profile. On deferred-tool Hermes clients, set tools.tool_search.enabled to off to expose native schemas; the guard remains enabled.
On Windows, use the documented short-folder route. Arbitrary deep paths are not verified supported.

entries.name: salts-secrets
entries.description: Let strangers talk to your Hermes without reaching your private memory. Built on Hermes' own gateway.profile_routes: only your own DM reaches your profile; everyone else (strangers' DMs, groups, channels, threads, the web) is answered by a separate public profile with its own sessions, an empty working directory, a fail-closed tool allowlist with no file, terminal, memory or session tools, and only the facts, documents and methods you approved, one click per item. Dashboard tab to review, rewrite, publish and revoke; revoking an item deletes every guest session (the store cannot tell which session saw it), and a reply being written at that moment is replaced with an ask-again notice. Disclosure — setup creates profiles/public, turns on gateway.multiplex_profiles, writes gateway.profile_routes named salts-secrets:* (your Telegram/Discord id to your profile, a platform catch-all to the public one) with TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS / DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS (and adds * to DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS when that list names users, because the Discord adapter checks it before any route), stores the public profile's API key as SALTS_PUBLIC_API_KEY through Hermes secrets (and generates the owner profile's API_SERVER_KEY when it is shorter than 16 characters), and installs this plugin into the public profile with `hermes -p public plugins install ... --enable --yes-deps` at the owner copy's revision (with --force for a non-catalog source or an existing copy); messages the routes leave in your profile that are not your DM (your Discord server messages, unrouted platforms) are answered after admission (post_gateway_admission) by the same gateway's /p/public/v1 API over loopback; deliveries on your own signed webhook routes are not chat and go to your agent, as without the plugin; each guest gets 20 messages an hour (guest_rate_per_hour); the Context tab reads the owner's memory, USER.md, skills, session history and configured workspace folders to list them (owner only); opening the Context tab applies local rules only; Classify and Draft send item text, and Rewrite with Hermes sends the disclosure policy and the owner's one-line instruction, to the owner's own configured model, only when the owner clicks; revocation runs `hermes sessions delete` on the public profile, and a guest session it could not delete is never resumed (the guest moves to a fresh session) and `sync` exits 1; writes approvals, the disclosure policy, the owner's own privacy rules (validated before saving), tool-call receipts, the last revocation time and a routing heartbeat under plugin-data/salts-secrets. No telemetry.
entries.title: Salt's Secrets
known_issues: Needs the API server enabled and plugins.isolation: in_process; `hermes salts-secrets setup` checks both and prints the fix.
Guests the routes cannot place (your own Discord server messages, platforms other than Telegram and Discord) are answered over loopback as text, with no streaming or media.
Group chats share one guest session, and the owner is treated as a guest there.

entries.name: samskara
entries.description: Relational memory provider backed by a knowledge graph (MillenniumDB or any SPARQL endpoint): multi-hop recall with provenance on every fact, an ontology that infers subsumption (Incidente ⊑ Evento) at reindex time, per-fact weights that are reinforced by use and decay with disuse, and explicit conflict reporting — when two values disagree, the agent says so instead of guessing. Zero-setup mode: SAMSKARA_ENDPOINT=embedded://seed/demo.ttl serves a built-in demo corpus from an in-process, read-only store (stdlib only, no network, no service to run) for the first minute; it answers the three query shapes the plugin issues and refuses arbitrary SPARQL rather than guessing. Onboarding backfills the graph from the sessions the agent already had (state.db, read-only) and reconciles new entities against existing ones. Disclosure — with session-end extraction enabled (default), the plugin sends the recent turns of a session to the user's own model through ctx.llm (host-owned credentials, no provider override) to extract facts. If the host does not expose ctx.llm — Hermes' in-process memory-provider path does not today — extraction is skipped rather than redirected: the session records its entity mentions lexically and no model is called. The plugin reads no provider API key from the environment and has no default model host. The graph endpoint defaults to loopback and is the only other network call. The CLI tool tools/backfill.py (never imported by the plugin) reads past sessions from state.db and sends them only to the endpoint the user names, via SAMSKARA_LLM_BASE_URL and SAMSKARA_LLM_API_KEY. No telemetry. Credentials (SAMSKARA_PASSWORD) are read through agent.secret_scope.get_secret.

entries.name: sapiens-sinteticos
entries.description: Operate your Sapiens Sintéticos account from Hermes: images, video, music, voice, characters, your repertoire and the members' forum, through the hosted Sapiens MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the 18 house skills bundled (prompting rules, engine choice, cost traps, publishing flows). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (skills/ only; the server is added by the sign-in command below). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to the Sapiens server at https://www.sapiensinteticos.com/api/mcp/mcp, added with `hermes mcp add sapiens --auth oauth` (the README then has you set `trust: untrusted` on mcp_servers.sapiens so Hermes asks before each generation, publish or delete call); generation tools debit Sinapses, the prepaid credit of your Sapiens account, and publishing tools post to the members' forum and to social accounts you connected on Sapiens, only when asked; in companion mode the agent speaks in the persona your Sapiens account sends and, after telling you once per session, saves condensed notes of your conversation (your decisions, preferences, what you tell about yourself) to your Sapiens notebook, which you can view and delete on the site, and skips them if you say no; on request the skills write `.claude/skills/sapiens-voz/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/sapiens-soul/SKILL.md` into the current project; the skills are in Brazilian Portuguese.
entries.title: Sapiens Sintéticos
known_issues: Sign-in needs one extra command after install, because a portable plugin cannot declare an OAuth MCP server: hermes mcp add sapiens --url https://www.sapiensinteticos.com/api/mcp/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300. Then set trust: untrusted on mcp_servers.sapiens in config.yaml, so Hermes asks before each generation, publish or delete call.
A new user needs a Sapiens Sintéticos account; the sign-in page links to the invite request.

Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to the Sapiens server at https://www.sapiensinteticos.com/api/mcp/mcp, added with `hermes mcp add sapiens --auth oauth` (the README then has you set `trust: untrusted` on mcp_servers.sapiens so Hermes asks before each generation, publish or delete call); generation tools debit Sinapses, the prepaid credit of your Sapiens account, and publishing tools post to the members' forum and to social accounts you connected on Sapiens, only when asked; in companion mode the agent speaks in the persona your Sapiens account sends and, after telling you once per session, saves condensed notes of your conversation (your decisions, preferences, what you tell about yourself) to your Sapiens notebook, which you can view and delete on the site, and skips them if you say no; on request the skills write `.claude/skills/sapiens-voz/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/sapiens-soul/SKILL.md` into the current project; the skills are in Brazilian Portuguese. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Known issues: Sign-in needs one extra command after install, because a portable plugin cannot declare an OAuth MCP server: hermes mcp add sapiens --url https://www.sapiensinteticos.com/api/mcp/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300. Then set trust: untrusted on mcp_servers.sapiens in config.yaml, so Hermes asks before each generation, publish or delete call.; A new user needs a Sapiens Sintéticos account; the sign-in page links to the invite request..

entries.name: scansift
entries.description: Exact, local triage of SARIF static-analysis results from any SARIF 2.1.0 tool (CodeQL, Semgrep, ruff, Bandit, ESLint, Trivy, Checkov, gosec, Snyk Code, Clang, ...), from one file or a directory of them. sarif_diff compares a branch scan with a baseline scan and returns the new and the gone results, matched by SARIF fingerprints or by content across two checkouts (never by line number), plus results whose level rose, with an optional fail_on gate; sarif_summary gives exact counts by level, the rules and files with the most results, suppressions, security-severity bands and analysis errors; sarif_findings lists results with rule, message, location and snippet, filtered and paged. Standard library only: no network, no credentials, no subprocess (never runs an analyzer), no third-party dependencies, no self-update. Disclosure: reads the local SARIF paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.

entries.name: scar
entries.description: scar keeps the tool-call shape you denied on a Hermes approval card and stops that shape before it runs. scar does not call a model. hermes chat --cli stores only the choice id deny. The shape is the tool, the argument keys that held an rm command, and the danger tokens, including an rm inside a shell -c body and an rm after env flags, so rm -rf and rm -fr are one scar. Only a tool that has a scar is compared, and only under the argument keys that scar kept, so read_file, write_file, web_search, a sentence, and a touch of nine files are not stopped. A bare rm that dropped a token is not this scar. A path is not part of the match. The block line names the scar, the weekday, the numeric offset, and the words you pressed deny, and it tells the agent not to paraphrase the command and not to run it again. Disclosure — A deny is written only under this profile plugin-data/scar/ledger.json after secret-shaped text is removed by the plugin patterns and then by the Hermes redactor. A secret shape that neither knows can stay in the preview. The ledger is read on every foreign tool call, up to 800KB and 200 scars. An unreadable file stops only a terminal command that carries an rm danger token, and it is left in place. On a tool that has a scar, a kept value over 200,000 characters, a shell nested past 8 levels, or more than 8 wrapper words is not compared and is not run. The block applies on every surface, including yolo, cron, the gateway, and approvals off, once a scar exists. A scar stays until scar_forget removes it or the plugin is disabled. scar_forget asks on the Hermes approval card when it fits in 7 lines of 63 columns. A longer question is not sent, and the scar stays. Each forget asks again. Its rule key changes on every call, so always does not cover the next forget. Yolo and approvals off skip that card when it fits, so that scar can be forgotten with no second prompt. Cron, a single query, a webhook, msgraph_webhook, api_server, and a plugin host do not forget a scar: the hook blocks scar_forget before Hermes's gate, including after always and including when yolo is on. Hermes checks a permanent allowlist before its own cron deny. Those sessions do not store a new scar. scar_list returns each scar, including the redacted preview, on any platform that can call the tool. hermes tools disable scar --platform <platform> hides the tools on that platform and does not stop the block. Disable the plugin to stop the block. A running gateway keeps the hook until it restarts. The plugin registers scar:keep-a-scar. A skills-tool session adds one system prompt skills index line. -t terminal,scar adds none. Nothing is sent off the computer. Yolo and approvals off skip the Hermes prompt, and this plugin does not add a second prompt. Setting isolation to host blocks new scars. This plugin creates no cron job. The install scan is safe, with 15 medium findings, all in the test tree.

entries.name: scenemux
entries.description: Turn an MP3 into a beat-aligned, lip-synced music video from any Hermes agent. Eight tools: scenemux_doctor (health/keys), scenemux_setup (start the studio server via Docker, provisions keys from the agent secret scope), scenemux_project (upload audio + references, beat-grid analysis, Whisper lyrics), scenemux_plan (LLM storyboard with beat-locked scenes, shown for review before anything is generated), scenemux_render (spend-gated: cost estimate first, confirm=true is escalated to a Hermes human-approval gate), scenemux_status, scenemux_export (final MP4, optional 9:16 vertical cut), scenemux_cancel. The storyboard director can run on a cloud LLM, a local Ollama model, or the agent itself (director_backend=hermes) via the local Hermes API server. A bundled skill (scenemux:studio) carries the operator workflow. Disclosure - the plugin talks only to the user's own SceneMux studio server (default http://127.0.0.1:8000) and reads the audio/reference paths the agent passes it; scenemux_setup starts one local server process (Docker container, port-published on 127.0.0.1 only) that runs until the session ends; planning and stills call the LLM/image/video backends configured on that server; the default cloud preset spends Comfy Cloud credits on renders, which is why renders are estimate-first and a confirm=true call is escalated to the user's approval gate; the server is reachable on loopback only (compose publishes 127.0.0.1 ports, no wildcard CORS), and tool calls to non-loopback hosts are refused; secrets are read only through the agent secret scope, are sent only to loopback / host.docker.internal hosts, and the server .env is written (chmod 600) only for a 127.0.0.1-bound server; no telemetry. Disclosure — SceneMux talks to your own SceneMux studio server (default http://127.0.0.1:8000), which scenemux_setup can start as a local Docker container published on 127.0.0.1 only; it uploads the audio and reference images the agent passes it, and the studio sends prompts and images to the LLM, image and video backends configured there (the default cloud preset spends Comfy Cloud credits, so renders show a cost estimate first and confirmed renders go through Hermes' approval prompt); API keys are read through the agent secret scope and sent only to a local studio, the Home Agent address comes only from the plugin's home_agent_url setting, and a ComfyUI address the agent passes for local rendering receives your reference images; no telemetry.
entries.title: SceneMux
known_issues: A running SceneMux studio server is required. scenemux_setup starts one via Docker (needs the repo_path setting pointed at a full repo clone, or the server already running). ffmpeg on PATH is needed for export/assembly.
The cloud pipeline preset spends Comfy Cloud credits on stills and video; the estimate tool reports the rough cost before render.

LLM planning quality depends on the configured model; a local Ollama model works for free and keeps the director lane private. director_backend=hermes needs the Hermes API server (API_SERVER_ENABLED=true + API_SERVER_KEY in ~/.hermes/.env, then `hermes gateway`).
First Docker run builds the image (a few minutes).

entries.name: scope-recall
entries.description: Local, source-backed long-term memory: recalls what you told an agent in your own words, with when you said it, keeps earlier versions as history when you change your mind, and shares one store with your other agents (other Hermes profiles, Codex, Claude Code). Disclosure — captured messages, assistant replies and tool results are kept in a local SQLite store under ~/.scope-recall/shared, outside the Hermes home and shared by every Hermes profile and other agent (Codex, Claude Code) you attach to it; it makes no network calls by default; if you configure a model or embedding route, message excerpts go to that endpoint within the budget you set; keys are read only through Hermes's secret routes; it starts short detached background worker processes that inherit Hermes's environment; setup sets memory.provider in config.yaml and installs two skills (scope-recall-setup, scope-recall-memory) into your Hermes skills folder.

entries.name: screen-overlay
entries.description: Gives Hermes the ability to draw on your screen. On your real Windows desktop it draws a gliding pointer, spotlights, boxes, arrows and numbered steps anchored to live UI Automation elements, a floating step guide with Next and Back, and handwritten glass notes, including ones that stay for you to drag and edit. Works over any app. Marks are click-through and nothing takes focus unless you choose to edit a note; DPI- and multi-monitor-aware, with an emergency clear hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12). Disclosure — Windows only. Starts one detached background process (the overlay, run by Hermes's own Python) on first use; it exits on the hotkey, on stop, or after 10 idle minutes with nothing on screen (a note left open keeps it running). No network: the plugin and the overlay talk over a local named pipe with a random key. The overlay process is started with a minimal environment (Windows basics, PATH and PYTHONPATH), so it inherits no API keys. Reads monitor layout, visible window titles, process names and bounds, and UI Automation names, types and bounds of elements in the window you target; these appear in tool results and so reach the model Hermes is using. Takes no screenshots, logs no keys, never moves the mouse or types, reads no credential or config files. Writes only to its plugin-data folder (pipe key, pid, logs, saved guides). Registers the global hotkey Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12 while the overlay runs. While a guide is open it looks up the current step's target about once a second. Installs PySide6-Essentials (about 215 MB) and comtypes. No telemetry, no self-update, no paid APIs.

entries.capability_summary: screen-overlay (community, maintained by tuancookiez-hub) Gives Hermes the ability to draw on your screen. On your real Windows desktop it draws a gliding pointer, spotlights, boxes, arrows and numbered steps anchored to live UI Automation elements, a floating step guide with Next and Back, and handwritten glass notes, including ones that stay for you to drag and edit. Works over any app. Marks are click-through and nothing takes focus unless you choose to edit a note; DPI- and multi-monitor-aware, with an emergency clear hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12). Disclosure — Windows only. Starts one detached background process (the overlay, run by Hermes's own Python) on first use; it exits on the hotkey, on stop, or after 10 idle minutes with nothing on screen (a note left open keeps it running). No network: the plugin and the overlay talk over a local named pipe with a random key. The overlay process is started with a minimal environment (Windows basics, PATH and PYTHONPATH), so it inherits no API keys. Reads monitor layout, visible window titles, process names and bounds, and UI Automation names, types and bounds of elements in the window you target; these appear in tool results and so reach the model Hermes is using. Takes no screenshots, logs no keys, never moves the mouse or types, reads no credential or config files. Writes only to its plugin-data folder (pipe key, pid, logs, saved guides). Registers the global hotkey Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12 while the overlay runs. While a guide is open it looks up the current step's target about once a second. entries.name: screenrig
entries.description: Free, agent-driven digital signage. Your agent pairs Players, uploads images and video, builds pages from docs, sheets and calendars, publishes playlists to TVs and kiosks, and checks each screen with a screenshot. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugin with two bundled skills, a bundled Node.js CLI (readable JavaScript, no binaries; Node.js 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+ or 26.12.1+) that the skill runs through the terminal tool, and one remote MCP server (screenrig-views, https://api.screenrig.ai/mcp, OAuth). The CLI calls api.screenrig.ai, uploads files and fetches URLs the user names, can launch a local headless Chrome/Chromium for card previews, and keeps its own screenRIG sign-in in its config directory; it never reads Hermes's or other tools' credentials. Web-dashboard connections upload the password, authenticator (TOTP) key and cookies the user supplies to screenRIG, which stores them to sign in to that dashboard. Enrollment and sign-in report the install source ("hermes/catalog"). Under Hermes the bootstrap makes no update check and never replaces its own files. Write operations change what physical screens show and can spend screenRIG account credit on advertising.

Runs on the models your Hermes already has (your vision model tracks and checks, Hermes speech-to-text listens); an optional Meta Model API key switches to SAM 3.1, Muse Spark and Voice Transcribe. entries.name: sealed
entries.description: Secret source that keeps provider credentials in one AES-256-GCM encrypted file instead of plaintext .env: a 32-byte key file unlocks the store at startup and the Hermes secret orchestrator applies the values, so precedence and provenance behave like any other source. Ships `hermes sealed init/set/unset/list/status/rotate`; values are read from a prompt or stdin and are never printed or passed in argv. Disclosure — no network, no helper CLI, no subprocesses. Reads the configured store and key file only (default $HERMES_HOME/secrets/sealed.{store,key}, both 0600); refuses to load when a file is group/world readable if secrets.sealed.strict_permissions is on. The CLI writes those two paths (plus .bak copies on init --force and rotate); values are entered by prompt or stdin. By default sealed values overwrite .env / shell values for the same variable (secrets.sealed.override_existing). No telemetry, no self-updater, no daemon. Requires the `cryptography` package, declared as a plugin dependency.

entries.name: second-key
entries.description: Team approvals for shared Hermes bots. Dangerous commands need N votes from your roster by Telegram DM, sized to the risk. The requester never counts, and an agent that edits its own approval settings is stopped on its next tool call. No answer, an error or too few approvers always means deny. Disclosure — Disclosure: Network: `api.telegram.org` only, with the bot token from `SECONDKEY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. Redirects are refused; What approvers see: the command after Hermes' own redaction, Hermes' reason for asking, and the requester's display name, platform and platform user id. While a ballot is open the DMs are edited in place about every 15 seconds with the current votes and time left. The same ballot text, plus a note that their own vote does not count, is also posted to the Telegram chat the request came from (which may be a group) or to the requester's DM; Re-arming after a change that weakens the settings opens its own critical ballot to the previously armed roster; Background thread: one long-poll thread reads the bot's updates while a request is waiting for votes, and for five minutes after `/secondkey enroll`. It stops on its own once neither holds, and when the plugin unloads; Files: writes its ledger, the armed settings (`armed.json`) and a pane state file (`state.json`: open and last eight closed ballots with the redacted command, requester name and approver names) under `plugin-data/second-key/`. Reads Hermes' `config.yaml` (read-only) before tool calls and in its Desktop Approvals pane, whose dashboard route is read-only; Credentials: reads the bot token through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`. It never reads `.env`, `auth.json` or any other credential store; No telemetry, no self-updater, no shell commands, no dependencies beyond the standard library.

entries.name: secret-drop
entries.description: Give Hermes a secret without the value appearing in the chat. Disclosure — the value is stored in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600), and storing narrows the file to that mode itself instead of inheriting whatever mode it finds. The model references it as {{secret:NAME}}; a pre_tool_call hook substitutes the value in terminal and execute_code arguments in memory, immediately before the call runs, so the transcript, the prompt and the provider request carry the alias. The same hook guards the store as a whole: every string argument of every tool is inspected, including tools it does not know by name; write payloads are walked into nested edits; directory arguments such as workdir are resolved, and a persisted cwd into the profile home is refused; wildcard spellings are compared with the guarded file names; and a path is resolved before a name is matched, so a symlink alias does not slip through. A command that names the store, a bare environment dump, and a mutation aimed at the profile home are refused. Tool output is scrubbed of stored values, of credential-shaped environment entries and of credential values kept in the profile config file, in their common encodings. What it does not do: it is not a sandbox for the effects of a command the model writes, and the guards are denylists - a value that is short or word-like is stored but not searched for globally, and a program that reassembles a value is covered only by scrubbing of the values it knows. The desktop dialog and its nine locale bundles promise the chat, not model-inaccessibility. Adds a static system-prompt section, a /secret command and a desktop drop dialog. An optional username can be entered beside the value and is stored as NAME_USER; it is injectable through an alias but never used as a global output needle. Only a name this plugin wrote as a username is treated that way, tracked in an account index that belongs to the guarded store, so a secret the user stores directly under a NAME_USER name stays a credential whose value is scrubbed. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_hermes_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK). On every session start it rewrites config.yaml to drop stored names from terminal.env_passthrough (migration from versions before 1.5.1), and it reads credential-shaped values from the profile config.yaml only to use them as output-scrub needles. A substituted value still leaves the host with whatever the command sends, and core's local tool-completion display receives the resolved arguments. Optional Vaultwarden backend: with a Bitwarden-compatible vault configured in the plugins hub (backend, vault URL and the two login values as secret fields, stored as VAULTWARDEN_USER/VAULTWARDEN_PASSWORD so the master password is scrubbed from tool output), a stored secret becomes a login item there and the alias resolves from the vault. The vault URL must be https (http is accepted only for a loopback host) and a redirect that leaves the configured host is refused, so neither the master-password hash nor the bearer token can follow a redirect to another server. The item list is cached for the cache TTL with a single re-login on 401, and a configured vault that cannot answer withholds tool output instead of scrubbing with only the file values. The file store stays the default.

entries.description: Enter API keys through a hidden dialog into the macOS keychain, never chat; block and scrub secrets before any model sees them. Disclosure — Secret Guard stores the keys you enter in your macOS login keychain as `hermes-<ENV_VAR>` items created with `-T /usr/bin/security`, so any process running as your user can read them without a prompt; it runs `/usr/bin/security` and `/usr/bin/osascript` (hidden-input dialog), observes every tool call, tool result, terminal output and model reply to block or redact registered secrets, keeps a names-and-fingerprints-only registry under the Hermes root, and makes no network calls.

entries.name: secret-handoff
entries.description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. entries.name: secret-remediation
entries.description: Fingerprint leaked credentials in the Hermes workspace, logs, and session history. Redacts them, blocks the turn, and gives text-only rotation advice. Disclosure — Rewrites credential matches into fingerprint placeholders in tool results, terminal output and replies, blocks turns or tool calls that contain credential-shaped text, and keeps fingerprint-only incident records under its plugin-data directory; it reads state.db and spawn-ledger.json read-only to report affected session ids, and only `hermes secret-remediation purge --shell-history` (operator CLI) rewrites your bash/zsh/fish history files after a safety copy; an operator-run `hermes secret-remediation schedule` adds a no-agent Hermes cron scan; no network calls.
entries.title: secret-remediation
known_issues: After a block, the plugin tries to replace credential text in state.db messages.display_metadata.withheld_prompt, state.db session_admissions.payload_json, and spawn-ledger.json argv with a fingerprint placeholder. payload_digest is recomputed, so replaying the original request is refused. That is expected. A failed attempt is logged and the plaintext can remain. Hermes can write the value again after the short retry window.

Purge writes by default, including shell history outside Hermes and chat history. Opt out with --no-sessions, --no-messages, --no-shell-history, --no-backups, --no-vacuum, including on scan --purge. A blocked-turn /retry reads withheld_prompt. The content, api_content, tool_calls, and display_metadata rewrite is separate, so a replayed tool call sends the placeholder. payload_digest is recomputed and an original replay is refused. VACUUM is skipped and named incomplete when state.db or its WAL is open. backups/pre-update-*.zip and backups/pre-migration-*.zip are counted and not rewritten. Provider logs, Time Machine, and cloud sync are not cleared. Close other shells first, or run history -c, or a running shell can write history back on exit. History mtime is kept.

Detects known token prefixes, PEM blocks including a BEGIN line with no END, equals-assignments named password, api_key, or secret (8 or more characters), URL userinfo for a fixed scheme list, and Authorization Bearer tokens. Unlabelled AWS secrets are detected only when the 40-character token contains + or / and is not hex, and that shape is not registered with Hermes's redactor. Encoded, split, Authorization Basic, colon assignments, and all-hex 40-character strings can pass.
The scheduled scan prints only new fingerprints. A clean tick is silent.

entries.name: secret-vault
entries.description: Keeps API keys and other secrets out of the model's context on gateway chats (Telegram, Discord, …): detected values become {{SECRET:name}} placeholders, are resolved only at tool time, and are redacted from tool/model output. Per-profile vault at <hermes_home>/secret-vault/vault.bin (Windows DPAPI CurrentUser; filekey-dev elsewhere for tests only). /secret set|list|rm|show-placeholder. Limits — CLI, TUI and Desktop input is not scrubbed (no rewrite hook in Hermes v0.23); detection is heuristic and can miss or over-flag; original platform messages (e.g. Telegram) are not deleted and must be removed by you. Disclosure — swaps `{{SECRET:name}}` placeholders for real values in the arguments of any tool call (before Hermes' approval prompt, so a prompt may show the value); stores values at <hermes_home>/secret-vault/vault.bin, encrypted with Windows DPAPI on Windows but with a key file stored beside it on Linux and macOS; secrets typed in chat stay in the platform's own message history until you delete them.

entries.name: secretshield
entries.description: Credentials stop at the tool boundary. Scans every tool call's arguments before dispatch and every finished reply before delivery for credential material (vendor API keys, GitHub/AWS/Google/Slack/Stripe tokens, PEM private keys, JWTs, bearer credentials, passwords in assignments), blocks the call or redacts the value fail-closed, and appends every attempt to a local incident ledger that stores only metadata (kind, length, masked preview), never the secret. Disclosure — SecretShield observes all tool call arguments, tool results and final replies in profiles where it is enabled and scans them locally; in the default enforce mode a detection blocks the tool call and a reply containing a credential is redacted with a notice; reply streaming is held until the reply is complete while it is enabled; it stores only detection metadata under $HERMES_HOME/secretshield/ and makes no network calls.

entries.name: secure-env-ingress
entries.description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing .env secrets and native encrypted Browser Vault login/TOTP/card storage; retained exact-parent login, saved TOTP, protected payment fields, transient codes and approved secret operations outside chat and model input. Browser destinations follow native Vault classification, origins and stamped-control selection, with bounded frame/Shadow extensions and asynchronous owner/profile/lease/cancellation checks. No CSS/history locks, sibling-tab fallback, core override or login backend registration. Disclosure — in-process internal Hermes Vault, browser, gateway, redaction and config APIs can break on host updates; setup instructions require approval for privileged host/TLS changes; TLS listens on all interfaces by default; the gateway hook observes messages for sender binding. Native encrypted card storage includes CVC. Site input callbacks can authorize or auto-submit; unknown outcomes need external verification before retry. SHA-256-pinned administrator-allowlisted operation consumers run unsandboxed with gateway privileges, none enabled by default; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer. Links authorize their holder, not submitter identity. Explicit .env ingress adds approved missing keys; setup bootstrap reads selected-profile .env owner IDs.
known_issues: In-process plugin using internal Hermes Vault/browser/gateway/redaction/config APIs; those dependencies can break on host updates.
Runtime security scan is CAUTION: approved privileged setup instructions, fixed-argv OpenSSL verification, and payment Luhn digit reversal; administrative repository root is not the catalog payload.
One-use links authorize their holder. Native card storage includes CVC; site input callbacks may authorize or submit. Verify unknown write outcomes before retry.

Maintainer policy review required under catalog rule 11: explicit add-only .env ingress reads/writes the selected-profile file; setup bootstrap directly reads .env owner IDs. No exemption is claimed. Allowlisted operation consumers execute unsandboxed with gateway privileges.

entries.name: selenite
entries.description: Takes friction off the person, treated as accessibility: one test, "does this step, wait or check earn its cost to you?", applied to steps handed to a person, agents parking Kanban work on each other for reasons that aren't real, and checks that can't change the decision. Calm mode cues the agent toward no questions and one-line replies when your messages show overload. A read-only cleanse ranks what to clear across skills, plugins, hooks, approvals, runbooks and boards. Walls always stand: credentials, spend, publishing, destructive steps, legal, named freezes. Adds /frictionless, the selenite_ledger and selenite_show tools, two fake-gate tools, skills, a Desktop page and a dashboard tab. Disclosure — no network, no credentials and no shell from the plugin itself; /frictionless starts an agent turn through the gateway only when Hermes's allow_gateway_injection is on, otherwise it prints the text for you to send; selenite_show and ledger, cleanse and evolve tool calls send local Desktop events (short keys only, no paths or private text) that the open Selenite page reacts to; hooks add a context note in Calm mode, and in fake_gate_mode "nudge" (default) or "ask" they add a note to, or hand back once with a question, a kanban_block that reads as agent bureaucracy (they never approve, unblock, close or edit a card, and any error fails open); when you approve a safe command once or for the session, its approval key is logged as an allowlist candidate (denials, timeouts and dangerous commands are never logged); writes a metadata-only ledger (no block reasons or prompt text, 0600, rotates at 4 MB), per-card question counts and a counts-only snapshot under plugin-data/antibeaurocracy/, and reports under the Selenite state directory (SELENITE_STATE, else XDG state, else HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/selenite, else ~/.local/state/selenite); reads kanban.db read-only (the CLI audit's --all-homes flag adds every ~/.hermes* home); the cleanse pass (the selenite_ledger tool, the Desktop page and the dashboard tab can run it) reads, read-only, the hook commands in ~/.claude/settings.json, the skill folders of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and ~/.agents, and Hermes plugin manifests; the `hermes antibeaurocracy audit` CLI also reads agent rule files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md) and the SOUL.md/AGENTS.md of every Hermes home and profile; the bundled frictionless skill's miner script, when the agent runs it, reads your own messages from local agent transcripts (Claude Code, Codex and Hermes state.db, all read-only) and keeps only counts plus a few redacted samples (emails, IPs, tokens, secrets and your home path stripped), 0600, in that state directory; the CLI's opt-in --judge runs a command you name, the plugin never does; all hooks turn off with hooks: false or SELENITE_HOOKS=0.
entries.title: Selenite
known_issues: Loads on the next gateway restart. Disable a standalone antibeaurocracy plugin first, or the fake-gate hooks run twice.
The fake-gate classifier is deterministic and phrase-based; text it has no evidence for is recorded, never nudged or asked.
Pedantry is a skill only; it is not counted in the cleanse ranking yet.
Badges for cards a person unblocks or archives clear within about a minute (Hermes fires no hook for either; Selenite checks the board read-only).
Tested on Linux; macOS and Windows unverified.

entries.name: send-lock
entries.description: Default-deny pre_tool_call hook: it allows a short explicit list (read-only tools, ls/pwd/whoami, a plain `curl -q -s <URL>` GET, and two narrow write_file paths gated by an owner step 0-4) and blocks every other tool call with a plain-English reason. A friendly first layer, not a containment boundary. Disclosure — it reads the owner config file (<HERMES_HOME>/axiom-owner.json or the path in AXIOM_OWNER_CONFIG) and the HERMES_HOME and AXIOM_OWNER_CONFIG environment variables; it writes only one log line per refusal and one at load to <HERMES_HOME>/logs/send-lock.log (tool name and block kind, never arguments); it blocks every tool call not on its allowlist; it makes no network calls, no subprocess calls and no model calls, and it stores no credentials and never updates itself.
entries.title: send-lock
known_issues: The plugin alone is not a containment boundary. In the worker-in-wall test (a real Hermes in a container, driven by a scripted fake model, on fake services only), 14 of 46 attack cases passed the plugin and were stopped by the container wall; 32 were stopped by the plugin. With the plugin off, the wall alone stopped all 46. The test says nothing about how a real model behaves.

Default-deny: after install most tools (patch, memory, skill_manage, browser, web, code execution, messaging) and most shell commands are refused until the owner config opens specific steps. Missing or invalid owner config means step 0.
A permitted curl GET can still carry data in its URL path, and model requests carry prompts. See docs/THREAT-LIST.md in the repository.

The repository also holds non-plugin tooling (a Docker test harness and demo scripts) that Hermes does not load. The wall test runs Hermes with its own approval prompts off (--yolo) inside a throwaway container; the plugin itself never does.

entries.name: senler-io-user
entries.description: Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — Hermes installs the declared `python-socks[asyncio]` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a `senler-io-user` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Hermes) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a `senler-io` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is `trusted_inbound`, so these events bypass Hermes allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Hermes approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in `<HERMES_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native Hermes messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.
entries.title: Senler.io
known_issues: After updating, restart the backend used by Desktop and the gateway; a new chat alone may still use older loaded plugin code.
Preview: Windows Desktop sign-in was previously confirmed; automatic MCP appearance still needs a Desktop UI check, and a real Senler Relay workflow needs end-to-end verification.
Requires current Hermes with native MCP OAuth and Relay transport; gateway proxy mode and multiplexed profiles are unsupported.
Monitoring notifications require a connected messaging channel; arbitrary Desktop/TUI chats are unsupported.

entries.name: sentinel-governance
entries.description: Audit-first Hermes tool governance with profile settings, profile-local policy, exact tool rules and per-event native approval. Settings enforce cannot be loosened by the environment; once resolved, enforce stays on per profile/process until restart. Unknown allow/approval requires named tools excluding terminal/execute_code. Known read_file/search_files/write_file/patch calls receive pre-rule credential/governance path checks and require canonical absolute regular-file targets; directory/default-path searches and ambiguous aliases are refused. Ordinary allowed file alternatives proceed without asking. Other tools remain whole-tool operator trust decisions; arguments/capabilities are not inspected beyond the disclosed file checks. Disclosure — runtime inspects arguments and file metadata, reads configuration/policy and a local audit key, and writes argument-free decision records plus HMAC-signed mode-change/policy-failure records under the active Hermes home (sentinel/). It starts no network calls/subprocesses and reads no external credential contents. Report shows sanitized counts/current policy health; another plugin can veto a Sentinel allow. User-invoked replay copies raw selected history DB/WAL/journal files into 0700 temporary directories with 0600 files, uses an isolated worker and returns counts only; it writes no Sentinel journal events. Current profile is default; --all-profiles is explicit. Copy/scan budget is two seconds with 2,000 calls/20,000 messages/200 sessions; full database copy cost and retained-history limits apply. macOS uses validated per-user system temp outside HOME/profiles, otherwise /tmp; Linux uses /tmp, ignoring TMPDIR/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Normal/timeout/signal shutdown cleans snapshots; killing both processes, power loss or filesystem errors may leave private files. Later replay sweeps eligible marked, unleased, owner-only leftovers older than 60 seconds; unmarked directories remain. Deletion is not secure erasure. Audit defaults to no veto, but host hook timeouts can block. Enforcement is restrictive; filename heuristics are partial and can overmatch benign names. Opaque tools, remote backends, filesystem races and same-privilege/key holders are outside these protections; local HMACs are not an append-only guarantee. Experimental, not a firewall or sandbox.

entries.name: sentinel-security

entries.name: sentinel-vision
entries.description: Tell Hermes what to watch on a camera, screen or video, and Sentinel detects events, stores snapshots and injects alerts into your chat. A local change detector and configurable call caps reduce vision-model usage; rules, event history and feedback make the watcher useful over time. Frames and rule text are sent to your configured model; see the README for setup, privacy and limitations. Disclosure — Captures from local cameras, the screen (mss), image folders, video files and stream/snapshot URLs you configure. A background watcher (capture threads, judge workers, scheduler) starts about 25 s after load when rules exist and sends camera/screen frames and rule text to your configured vision model. Snapshots, events, teaching images and chat routes are stored under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/sentinel-vision/. Fired rules inject alerts as user messages and can replay a rule's stored action prompt as unattended agent turns; outside the classic CLI this needs plugins.entries.sentinel-vision.allow_gateway_injection: true. The model can name local image/video paths to read and send to the vision model.
entries.title: Sentinel Vision
known_issues: Registers a /sentinel slash command, which another listed plugin (SENTINEL OS) also uses; the two conflict only if both are installed.

Outside the classic CLI, alerts are only delivered after you add plugins.entries.sentinel-vision.allow_gateway_injection: true to config.yaml; /sentinel status shows the exact snippet when delivery is refused.
Needs a vision-capable model routed to the sentinel_vision auxiliary task, otherwise judging fails (the gate keeps running).
On Telegram/Discord send /sentinel here once so alerts return to that chat.
Screen capture needs a display; it is not available on a headless server.

Vision only (no audio, no video-site streams such as YouTube). Movement is judged from up to 3 recent frames, not video; the slow-drift check misses very small or very large gradual changes. Expect misses and false alarms. Not a safety device.

Plugins cannot read allow_gateway_injection; run /sentinel setup --test-delivery to test delivery. On a multiplexing gateway, cameras that need a ${SECRET} wait until the first /sentinel command or sentinel_* tool call after start-up.

entries.name: sentinel
entries.description: Local runtime policy, redacted execution history, supported-file recovery, agent preflight tools and a runaway breaker, with Telegram-ready /sentinel commands. Trusted hooks, not an OS sandbox; native approval modes apply and backups retain original bytes.
entries.title: SENTINEL OS
known_issues: Trusted in-process hooks, not an OS sandbox; protection depends on the plugin being enabled and loaded.
Native Hermes approval modes stay authoritative; YOLO can skip approval escalation but never turns a Sentinel BLOCK into an allow.
Shell analysis is conservative; directory-scoped missions block shell work that cannot be confined.
Recovery covers supported local files only; it cannot undo remote APIs, emails, deployments or database writes.
Checkpoint backups keep original file bytes in the local state folder; protect it with OS permissions.
Delivery of /sentinel replies and alerts inside the Telegram app is not yet verified end to end.

entries.name: seomatic
entries.description: SEO agent for your own website through SEOmatic's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.seomatic.ai/api/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): Google Search Console queries and pages, striking-distance keywords, traffic drops, site audits, keyword, backlink and SERP competitor research, AI visibility and AI citations (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews), daily local rankings and Google Business Profile, plus site fixes staged in SEOmatic for WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, Wix and other connected sites. Bundles twenty workflow skills (SEO audit, striking distance, traffic drop, CTR fix, cannibalization, content refresh, keyword research, competitor gap, local SEO and more). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/ in the repo's hermes/ folder), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to SEOmatic's hosted server (app.seomatic.ai) and acts on the user's own SEOmatic workspace with their role in it; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Search Console, stored-data and site audit reads are free; live market data (keyword metrics and suggestions, backlinks, SERP competitors, local SERP visibility), fresh AI visibility scans and approved fixes spend SEOmatic AI credits, content generation quotes its estimate and runs only after the user confirms, and generate_article uses one prepaid article unit. Fixes proposed through the tools are staged in SEOmatic; approving, publishing, undoing and rolling back change the user's live site and require an explicit confirm from the user. SEOmatic's own background agents follow the workspace's autonomy mode set in SEOmatic: in Assisted, the default for new workspaces, reversible changes (titles, descriptions, internal links, schema, page text, articles) go live on their own with a one-click undo, while new pages, bulk changes, redirects and removals wait for the user; in Approval mode every change waits. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which registers an OAuth client, opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth; without a stored token, an unattended run fails at Hermes's connect timeout instead of hanging. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. Users who need longer to sign in, or a headless setup, can replace the server with hermes mcp add seomatic --url https://app.seomatic.ai/api/mcp --auth oauth (or an API key header) and keep the skills.

entries.name: session-cassettes
entries.description: Record one good session's read-only tool results as a cassette, pin the facts a good answer must contain, then replay the same request against another model, prompt or skill: tool_execution middleware answers every tool call of the replayed turn from the recording (exact hit, or a search/slice of a snapshot of the workspace files the session's results named; anything else gets a cassette-miss error) and never calls the real tool; the verdict is PASS, FAIL, DIVERGED or INVALID from the pins, with no judge model. Disclosure — cassettes are plain JSON in the plugin data folder and hold the request, the answer and the full results of recorded tools (file contents, search hits, web search results and extracts, skill text, session-search results, output of a fixed list of read-only terminal commands) plus the redacted text of workspace files those results named; at the end of a recorded turn the plugin reads those files from the session's working directory (hidden paths and secret-looking names such as key files, credentials, auth.json and token.json skipped by file name, Hermes's redact_sensitive_text applied to the rest, which does nothing if the user has switched Hermes's redaction off); `hermes cassette run` starts two `hermes chat -Q` children (argument list, no shell, no -z, no --yolo, HERMES_YOLO_MODE removed from the child, run refused when the gateway's environment has HERMES_YOLO_MODE set at ping time, which is not Hermes's own startup yolo flag; the child's output is held in two temporary files in the system temp folder until the child exits) and the replay's model call goes to whatever model/provider the user names, so a cloud model is sent the request and the recorded results; if no session claims the replay its turn runs live with real tools under the user's own approval settings and is graded INVALID afterwards; the middleware sees every session's tool calls and passes unbound sessions through, keeping only an in-memory count of them so a late claim can be marked INVALID; the pre_llm_call and post_llm_call hooks are called for every turn of every session with the message and the answer, and keep nothing for a session the plugin has not bound; it registers the /cassette slash command and the `hermes cassette` CLI command; no network calls of its own, no telemetry, no self-update, no third-party dependencies.
entries.title: Session Cassettes
known_issues: Tested only on native Windows 11 with Hermes 0.23.1 and local Ollama models; macOS, Linux and cloud providers are untested.
plugins.isolation: host is untested, and by the Hermes source the hermes cassette CLI is not registered in that mode, so replay would not work there.
A replay whose arm no session claims runs live with real tools and is graded INVALID only after it ends; a ping before each run refuses the common causes.
The replay's model call is real: with a cloud model, the request and the recorded tool results go to that provider.
Recording was tested through hermes chat -Q; recording from the desktop app or an interactive session is untested. Do not record through hermes -z, which auto-approves.
Replays are not deterministic: a model can go outside the recording and come up DIVERGED.

Through the current replay child, only the model has been varied. A skill under test must be preloaded with --skill, because skill_view and skills_list are answered from the recording. A prompt change has not been run.
Unmatched searches are answered by a Python re search of the snapshot, an approximation of ripgrep.

entries.name: session-find
entries.description: A search window over your Hermes session history, opened with Cmd+Option+F, from the command palette, or from the glyph in the bottom bar whose hover shows the chord. Finds a session by an exact word, identifier or phrase through the gateway's own full text index, and by meaning as well when a session-find service answers on loopback; typed filters (in:, -in:, after:, before:, me:, repo: and quoted phrases) are mirrored as chips under the box. The empty box lists pinned then recent sessions, the preview pane shows the matching message with its neighbours, and the footer carries the round trip in whole milliseconds. It reads the session database read only, registers no agent tools, hooks or middleware, needs no credentials or environment variables; its only network calls are the loopback checks named below. The window half ships off by default and is switched on in the app's plugin inventory. Disclosure — while the search window is in use, the plugin's dashboard backend checks every 30 seconds for a separate session-find service at http://127.0.0.1:8474 (or the URL in SESSION_FIND_URL) and, when one answers, sends it your search text, preview requests and the ids of sessions you open, and shows the results it returns; otherwise it reads your Hermes session database read-only.

entries.name: session-flow
entries.description: Session pane for Hermes Desktop: Firefox-style session groups with project grouping, list/grid views, Ctrl+Scroll session cycling with a HUD, session-row styling with a rotating status loader (donut ring) per row, and a built-in settings page. All timers are ctx-owned intervals disposed on unload (live-session poll ~30 s, session refresh ~45 s, project cache 60 s, activity expiry 30 s). The standalone full build in this repo (full/plugin.js, install.sh) is not part of this catalog entry. Contact: info@agantila.com. Disclosure — SDK-only Desktop plugin: reads the local Hermes gateway through public RPCs (projects.tree, projects.list, session.list, session.active_list, session.context_breakdown) and, on your actions, writes through public RPCs (projects.create/update/add_folder/remove_folder/set_primary/set_active/delete, session.create, session.cwd.set, session.title, session.branch_stored, session.archive, session.interrupt, session.close, session.delete); deleting a session that is still running first stops its current turn; captures Ctrl+mouse-wheel across the app (browser zoom suppressed except over canvases, editors and zoomable images) to cycle sessions; settings and groups stay in the app's local plugin storage; no outbound network, no shell commands, no credentials, no self-update.

entries.name: session-lens
entries.description: Read-only observability for Hermes Desktop: what each session and turn cost and why, its full trace, recurring tool failures, every profile at a glance, provider quotas and service balances, system prompt weight and prompt-cache health, cron run history, gateway restarts, model comparison with cheaper-route evidence, and instruction-rule grading. Disclosure — reads every profile's state.db read-only plus agent logs, cron records, gateway state, skills/.usage.json, cache/prompt_cache_routes.json and config.yaml; API keys only through agent.secret_scope.get_secret (names declared under optional_env); subscription sign-ins are read only by Hermes' own agent.account_usage, never held by the plugin; calls only each configured vendor's usage or balance endpoint (hosts listed in the README) and sends no inference request; the desktop asks Hermes' model.options (cached, refresh off) for rate-limit holds; runs the local monid CLI when installed; never opens .env, auth.json or another tool's login; writes no Hermes state and sends no session content anywhere.

entries.name: session-mirror
entries.description: Mirrors Hermes Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post_llm_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Hermes's redact_for_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret_scope.get_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $HERMES_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional `hermes session-mirror backfill` CLI command reads $HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.

entries.name: session-receipts
entries.description: Session Receipts turns a Hermes session, a date range, or a kanban card's evidence chain into one self-contained offline HTML document: the original ask, every tool call as a timed node, failures and retries exactly as recorded (never collapsed into the success that followed), per-model token spend, and the cost Hermes recorded, with a reconciliation delta. A client theme renders the same data as a paper document for sharing; `--redact` writes a share-safe copy with a redaction manifest (secrets, emails, user paths, IPs, phones, plus a user word list); and `receipts rollup --since 7d` aggregates a window into a deterministic weekly digest: failure taxonomy, cost by model and card, slowest tools by p50/p95, retry hotspots, week-over-week deltas. Standard library only; reads the local session store and kanban boards read-only; no network, no credentials, no new dependencies. Disclosure — a receipt contains the session's real text; secret masking is pattern-based (a safety net, not a guarantee), and shared copies should be reviewed before they leave the machine.

entries.name: session-relay
entries.description: Hands a long-running conversation over to a fresh session before the context window fills up: a ⚡ chip in the status bar shows live context usage, and at the threshold (45% by default) the agent writes a hand-off note while the plugin opens a new chat, seeded with that note as its first message and named after the current one (+1). On Telegram and other messaging platforms the gateway half provides a session_relay_handoff tool; after /new it attaches that chat's note to the first message of the new session, so the fresh session opens with the hand-off. Disclosure: each relay runs one extra agent turn and therefore uses model tokens.

entries.name: sessioncrew
entries.description: Browse sessions and related projects across profiles in a Hermes Desktop side panel, with observed activity, completion reminders, and project creation. entries.name: sessionguard
entries.description: Work survives the session. Keeps a local work-state checkpoint for every session, built from tool evidence: current task, files touched, recent tool calls and outcomes, failure count, and the agent's own progress notes saved through the session_checkpoint tool. A checkpoint closes only when the agent marks its task done; otherwise the next session from the same origin (same platform and sender) is briefed from the most recent open checkpoint, so work interrupted by a dead process, a dropped gateway, or a compaction resumes from evidence instead of a lossy transcript. Subagent and cron sessions neither record checkpoints nor receive briefings. Disclosure: observes user messages (only the latest task text is kept, truncated, with credential-shaped values redacted), tool call arguments (stored only as short summaries), and turn outcomes, in profiles where it is enabled; all state is stored locally under $HERMES_HOME/sessionguard/; makes no network calls.

entries.name: severian
entries.description: Local-first long-term memory for Hermes agents: a canonical append-only store (SQLite or PostgreSQL+pgvector) with five-dimensional tenant/profile/collection/agent/session scope, hybrid BM25+vector retrieval with a re-ranker, memories that cite the observations they came from, per-turn user facts, real dates next to relative times, truth resolution when a newer fact replaces an older one, and a conflict note when two returned memories disagree. Fully offline by default; Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B semantic embeddings opt-in, locally or in a user-owned sidecar. On OmniMemEval's public long-term-memory leaderboard (its own models, prompts and full public sets) it scores 90.6 LongMemEval (1st), 87.3 LoCoMo (2nd) and 71.6 BEAM 100K (2nd, within noise of the lead); it re-ran LCM-X to check the board's records, and per-question results, a strict second marker and scripts are published in the repo. Disclosure — stores every conversation turn in one SQLite database under the Hermes root (`<hermes root>/severian`) shared by all profiles with rows scoped per profile, or in the PostgreSQL database named by `SEVERIAN_DSN`; the opt-in Qwen/Granite embeddings download a model from Hugging Face on first use, and the opt-in embedding sidecar sends memory text to the URL you configure.

entries.name: sgme
entries.description: SGME (拾光记忆) self-hosted long-term memory engine — tagged memories with provenance, per-turn recall, automatic session refinement, a skills library, wiki knowledge base, care signals, communication roles and a three-pool task system (ideas/demands/projects), all behind one HTTP service you own. The plugin is a thin bridge: no LLM, no database, everything heavy runs in your SGME server (local or remote). Disclosure — the plugin talks only to the SGME server you configure (default http://127.0.0.1:9910, SGME_BASE_URL for a remote server), sending SGME_AGENT_KEY / SGME_ADMIN_KEY read through Hermes's secret scope; each session's user, assistant and tool messages are appended to that server and refined into memories at session end by an LLM you configure on the SGME side; its sgme_* tools let the model read and change memories, skills, wiki pages and tasks on that server and write skill packages under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/sgme/skills/ on the SGME host; credential names in the SGME vault can be listed, and reading a credential value into the conversation is off by default (credential_get_enabled / SGME_ENABLE_CREDENTIAL_GET); no third-party services, no telemetry.

entries.name: shadow-trial
entries.description: Try a model on your real Hermes conversations with blind judging in both orders and switch models with undo, warning first if a saved test does not back the switch. Reads recent saved conversation turns, context, and working-folder metadata from the active profile. Replays read files inside their original working folders and block writes, sends, and commands. Replays, judging, and setup checks spend your provider tokens through Hermes. Optional web lookups use Hermes web tools and are on by default. Stores scrubbed test records and switch state in the plugin's profile-local data folder. The live isolation check reads memory and fingerprints profile data locally. It compares credential-file metadata without reading their contents. To show which models are signed in it checks credential env var names (not values) and uses only the logged-in flag from Hermes's read-only Codex login-status check; credentials are never printed or stored. Makes no network calls of its own. No telemetry. Switching writes model defaults through Hermes config commands. Tests run in background Hermes controllers.

entries.name: shadow
entries.description: Find out which model is better at your work, from your real prompts. After a plain chat turn, the same conversation goes in the background to a second model you choose, through ctx.llm. /shadow vote shows both answers blind in random order; models are revealed after you vote, and your leaderboard shows wins with a 95% range. Off until you set compare_model and allow the override; tool turns are skipped and answers are deleted after each vote. Disclosure — when enabled (compare_model set and llm.allow_model_override on), the last 12 plain-text messages of every eligible chat turn are also sent to the second model/provider you configured, costing one extra model call per compared turn; up to 100 unvoted prompt/answer pairs are kept in plugin-data/shadow until you vote, and each chat can only see the pairs it captured.

entries.name: shapeless
entries.description: Make and publish social media content from Hermes: plan posts, edit video, generate images and clips, design carousels, and publish or schedule to LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky and more, through ShapelessAI's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE), with two skills bundled (get-started and shapelessai). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to shapelessai.com, signed in as the user, with the post text, media and brand notes the session hands it, which also reach the user's model provider through the session. Publishing tools post to the user's real social accounts, and the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks the user before each write tool. Media tools spend the account's credits at the cost each tool states; posting spends none. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The tool list comes from ShapelessAI's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add shapeless --url https://shapelessai.com/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: shared-memory-domains
entries.description: One memory several Hermes profiles share, split into domains with per-agent read/write grants: agents only propose facts, a human verifies them before they are recalled, revocation is immediate and sticky, and decisions are audited. Disclosure — no network, no subprocess, no credentials; reads and writes one local SQLite file (default HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/shared-memory-domains/shared.db, or the shared db_path you configure, which is outside the plugin's data dir by design) and refuses any file it did not create; injects up to 6 verified facts per turn by default (`inject_limit`, 0–20; 0 disables recall) into the agent context (pre_llm_call); blocks the agent's own terminal/execute_code/file-tool calls that name the database (pre_tool_call trip-wire, trivially bypassed, not a sandbox); one /shared-memory admin command; admin commands and cross-domain views only from the cli surface by default. Cooperative access control inside the Hermes process: an agent with shell tools can bypass it, and facts already shown stay in conversation history and in any conversation-recording memory provider.
