entries.name: sharelet
entries.description: Share a Hermes tool as a link anyone can use in a browser. Pick a tool on the local creator page, create the link and send it: guests need no Hermes, account or API key, and the tool runs on your computer. Links have a run limit, expiry and off switch; guests can change only the inputs you leave open. Tools without a read-only hint need a separate confirmation for each share. Works with explicitly allowed native Hermes plugin tools and MCP servers. Default links use a temporary tunnel address; stable links require your own relay or fixed public_origin. Disclosure — while enabled it serves a token-protected creator page and guest pages on 127.0.0.1; when a public link is active it downloads cloudflared 2026.10.7 from Cloudflare's official GitHub release (SHA-256 pinned in code, re-verified before each launch) and runs it as a background process that exposes only the guest port through a Cloudflare quick tunnel; anyone holding a link can run that shared tool on your computer through Hermes with the inputs you leave open, up to its run limit and expiry (tools without a read-only hint need your confirmation per share); relay routing is off by default, and a relay_url you set yourself receives a random host ID, a relay secret and the current tunnel address and serves the guest landing page, so run it yourself; it writes links, run records, uploaded and generated files, its signing keys and any OpenAI key you type into its page (plaintext, owner-only file) to its own data folder; optional image recipes are off until enabled and call api.openai.com with that key or, if you enable it, your Hermes profile's OPENAI_API_KEY, spending its credit. No telemetry, no self-update.
entries.title: Sharelet
known_issues: Your computer must stay online. Raw tunnel addresses change after reconnects; stable addresses require an explicitly configured self-hosted relay or fixed public_origin.
Shared tools run with your Hermes setup. Review each tool's output and costs before sharing; anyone holding a link can use its runs.

Windows ARM64 selects the official Windows AMD64 cloudflared asset using Windows 11 x64 emulation; upstream provides no native ARM64 Windows binary for this pin. This path is not ARM64 hardware-tested.

entries.name: sharewise
entries.description: See what your photos and videos reveal before you share them. Reports, as yes/no counts only, exact location, location detail, time, device, unique IDs, owner name, captions, hidden thumbnails, edit history, depth maps and (videos) per-frame face data; on macOS finds faces, people, street names, house numbers and plates with Apple Vision on this computer; a local review page lets the user switch areas off, draw, move, resize, rotate and reshape them; hidden areas are rebuilt from their surroundings (faces) or become a blank plate in the sign's colour, so nothing of what was there is kept; copies drop all metadata except copyright and are re-read and verified. Videos (MOV, MP4, M4V, 3GP) are cleaned without re-encoding: metadata boxes, timed-metadata tracks and unreferenced media bytes are zeroed in a copy and the whole file is scanned; faces inside videos are not hidden. Disclosure — reads JPEG, HEIC, PNG, WebP and the video types above only in a folder the user names inside the home folder or on an external drive; refuses the operating system, disk roots, the whole home folder, ~/Library, hidden and locked items, symlinks and app-managed libraries. Writes only new copies to a Sharewise/ folder inside that folder and never writes or overwrites originals. sharewise_share takes check ids, photo numbers, fixed keep choices, the user's selection codes and areas to add (never file paths), is validated by its own pre_tool_call hook, and keeping location is escalated to Hermes' human-approval gate (fails closed with no human present). The agent can add areas but cannot switch them off; switching off comes from the review page's selection code (a design rule, not a cryptographic barrier). Stores the last 10 checks (paths, yes/no findings, area boxes), review pages with downsized photos and downsized finished copies in its plugin data folder; never stores metadata values or text read in photos. Sends to the model provider, as part of the conversation, the folder, file names and yes/no and area counts, and, only when the user asks for a visual check (sharewise_look), downsized finished copies that are already hidden and clean. Apple Vision runs on-device via pyobjc-framework-Vision (macOS only; elsewhere detection is off and areas can be drawn by hand). No network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry; no process-wide settings changed.

entries.name: sheets
entries.description: An agentic spreadsheet. Ask for a sheet and a Hermes agent finds the rows on the web, each with its source, or bring your own. Hermes suggests typed columns, fills only the ones you pick, explains what the answers add up to, and, once you allow it, lets any chat read your grids and propose cells, columns and rows that you approve and can undo. Formula columns, a totals row, cell formatting with highlight rules, and Excel import and export are built in. Disclosure — Build sheet, research columns and Ask start hidden Hermes sessions that use your Hermes tools and read third-party web pages; approval prompts inside build and research sessions are denied; import reads and export writes the one file you pick in the system dialog (text, CSV or an Excel workbook), through the plugin's own backend (in the browser webapp, import reads the copy Hermes stages from that file in the profile's uploads folder), and the folder source reads a folder you grant; grids live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy under plugin-data/sheets/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Hermes profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; with the Data or Whiteboard plugin installed, a click hands a table or ticked rows to that page through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; no telemetry, no credentials, no shell commands or background processes of its own. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: shelldrop
entries.description: Set up a Mac or Linux machine so AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, any CLI agent) can be run and checked from an iPhone or iPad over SSH: SSH on, tmux sessions that survive a dropped connection, Tailscale for the route in, the phone's SSH key, then the exact connection details. One skill plus Shell Drop's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.shelldrop.sh/mcp, no key, no sign-in) with four read-only tools: setup_guide, tmux_howto, generate_tmux_conf and troubleshoot_connection. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: the MCP server is a stateless Cloudflare Worker whose source is in the repo; every tool call goes to mcp.shelldrop.sh, which receives only the tool arguments (an OS name, a short task or symptom phrase, tmux.conf options), returns static text, keeps no sessions, stores nothing and does not log inputs; every tool is annotated read-only and the package marks the server untrusted. The skill has the agent run shell commands on the user's own machine under Hermes's normal approvals: it edits ~/.tmux.conf, optionally ~/.zshrc, and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (public keys the user supplies only), and after asking runs sudo to enable SSH, install tmux or Tailscale (Tailscale's official curl | sh installer on Linux) and stop the machine sleeping. No telemetry, no credentials stored or sent. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: shinjuku
entries.description: A private USDC wallet for Hermes that the user holds. It pays paid web services and APIs (x402) privately: the seller and the blockchain do not see which wallet paid. From plain requests Hermes checks a price, finds paid APIs, pays, and shows a wallet card (/shinjuku:wallet), receipts, add funds and a send back to the user's own wallet. New plugin. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/ + a small launch.mjs). The wallet itself is the npm package shinjuku at the exact version in mcp.json (0.3.218), which the user installs once (npm install -g; npm.cmd on Windows) and sets up in a terminal (shinjuku setup; shinjuku.cmd on Windows). Disclosure — Crypto payments: runs the user's own closed-source Shinjuku wallet (npm shinjuku@0.3.218 / shinjuku-shield@0.3.218, installed by the user, not covered by the pinned sha) as an untrusted MCP server; Hermes asks before every price check, payment, send, deposit address, backup and stop, but searches, receipts and balance reads run without asking, and a balance read (and wallet start) moves USDC the user added into the user's own private balance. Payments go through Shinjuku's payment service (pay.shinjukustaition.com or its .onion), which takes a per-payment fee, and paid AI answers send the prompt to api.usepod.ai over Tor; with Tor on, traffic goes over Tor, and on Windows the wallet downloads Tor from torproject.org and runs it in the background. Keys stay in the wallet's folder in the user's account.

entries.name: ship-reel
entries.description: Turns a URL and a one-line brief into a finished product demo reel. The agent plans a shot list and dry-runs it against the live page, records it in headless Chromium, edits it with auto-zoom, a drawn cursor, captions, title and end cards, optional local voice-over and a music bed into 16:9 and 9:16 MP4s, verifies the result (duration, resolution, black or frozen frames, loudness, captions) and fixes what fails, then drafts the post text. It never posts. Disclosure — opens the user-supplied URL and the pages in its shot list in headless Chromium behind a local filtering proxy; runs ffmpeg/ffprobe and local render worker processes; writes only to its plugin data directory (or SHIP_REEL_HOME); with the optional kokoro-onnx extra installed, downloads the Kokoro TTS model (~120 MB) once from its official GitHub release, SHA-256 pinned. Public hosts only: loopback, private, link-local/metadata, CGNAT and reserved addresses are refused for every URL and browser request unless the user sets allow_private_hosts or SHIPREEL_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=1. Sign-in, payment, send, submit and delete clicks trigger a Hermes approval prompt via a pre_tool_call hook; typing into password fields is refused. No telemetry, no API keys.
entries.title: Ship Reel
known_issues: Requires ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH, and Chromium for Playwright (python -m playwright install chromium).
Voice-over is optional and needs pip install "kokoro-onnx>=0.4,<1"; without it reels render with captions and music only.
Records public pages only; flows behind a sign-in are out of scope for this version.
Some sites' own search boxes do not work in a headless browser.
Hosts are refused on machines whose DNS goes through a fake-IP proxy (all names resolve into 198.18.0.0/15); use the allow_private_hosts setting there.

entries.name: shopmate
entries.description: Personal shopper agent: finds products with live Google Shopping prices and photos (SerpAPI, or a labelled demo catalog without a key), quotes delivery to the customer's location with doorstep or pickup-stop options, and on an explicit yes takes payment by Paystack (NGN, GHS, KES, ZAR, USD, XOF, EGP, RWF) or crypto via NOWPayments, verifying amount+currency with the provider before marking the order paid. Supports conversation-scoped order lookup (cross-conversation email/phone lookup is an operator setting, off by default), saved-card charges via Paystack charge_authorization (cards are bound to the conversation that paid and identified by a local opaque card_id; a pre_tool_call hook sends saved-card checkout with confirm=true to a Hermes approval), request_refund (Paystack Refund API + manual crypto payouts; optional NGN bank transfers only when the allow_transfers plugin setting is on, which moves the operator's Paystack balance and is off by default; confirm=true on all refund methods also goes through the same Hermes approval, and bank_transfer requires account_name), webhook signature verification (HMAC x-paystack-signature helper for operators), and contact_support with optional SUPPORT_EMAIL/SUPPORT_WHATSAPP — no BVN/phone identity lookups. 17 tools plus the shopmate:shopping skill. Disclosure — payments plugin: on checkout it creates Paystack payment links / charge_authorization charges and NOWPayments crypto invoices on the operator's own merchant keys (no money moves until the customer pays, or a saved-card charge or refund confirm is approved in Hermes); request_refund can call Paystack Refund / Transfers (transfers gated by the allow_transfers plugin setting) or leave a manual crypto payout pending; the reusable Paystack authorization code is stored in orders.sqlite and is never returned as card_id; network calls to serpapi.com, api.paystack.co, api.nowpayments.io, open.er-api.com, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, ipapi.co (auto-locate is on by default and sends the host's public IP when a conversation has no saved location) and maps.app.goo.gl (expanding shared Maps short links); carts, saved locations, saved card authorizations (last4/brand/bank and conversation binding only), support tickets and orders (customer name, email, phone and address) are stored in the plugin data directory; API keys are optional and read through Hermes's secret scope.

entries.name: shorguard
entries.description: Post-quantum crypto guard. Stops the agent from writing quantum-vulnerable public-key crypto (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, EdDSA, X25519, DH, DSA) before it lands: pre_tool_call checks write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code and, in the default block mode, refuses calls that ADD classical crypto, returning the NIST replacement (ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA) with working cryptography>=48 code so the agent rewrites it (approve mode routes to Hermes's approval gate instead; warn mode only annotates). Tools shorguard_scan / shorguard_explain, /shorguard (status, mode, scan, explain) and `hermes shorguard scan` give a post-quantum readiness grade with text, JSON or SARIF output and CI exit codes. 52 rules across Python, JS/TS, Go, JVM, Rust, .NET, shell/CI, TLS config, PEM keys and JWT algorithms, mapped to NIST IR 8547 (deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035). Disclosure — reads the content of inspected tool calls, the file a write_file is about to overwrite (to flag only newly added crypto) and paths you ask it to scan; writes its own plugin state (counters and the last 50 events: time, action, tool, file name, rule ids — never code or arguments) and its own settings when changed via /shorguard; writes a report only with --output. No network, subprocesses, credentials, telemetry or background work.
entries.title: Shorguard — post-quantum crypto guard
known_issues: Pattern-based: it sees crypto your code calls directly, not crypto inside dependencies or a library's TLS defaults. A clean grade means no obvious classical crypto, not a certification.
approve mode uses Hermes's approval gate, which auto-approves under YOLO; use block mode for enforcement.
With plugins.isolation: host the `hermes shorguard` CLI subcommand is not available; use /shorguard scan or the shorguard_scan tool.

entries.name: shorts-factory
entries.description: The 9:16 short-video pipeline as executable tools, distilled from a production pipeline shipping daily shorts across YouTube/TikTok/Instagram/Facebook/X: sf_loudness (ebur128 measure, two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS/-2 dBTP, sidechain music ducking with amix normalize=0, atempo), sf_concat (mixed stills+video with full in-graph fps/SAR/bt709 normalization, exact still frame counts, post-build VIDEO-STREAM duration asserts — kills the silent concat killers: vanishing overlays, dropped audio, one-frame stills), sf_captions (script-aligned word-timed punch captions rendered as Pillow PNGs — no libass/drawtext needed — with boundary-safe enable windows and pixel-diff band verification), sf_footage_audit (contact sheets, per-second brightness, full-res fine grabs, review checklist), sf_safezone (thumbnail safe band y=400..1500 checks + simulated grid crop), sf_motion_lint (deterministic build-script lint for stutter-prone zoompan/time-driven motion). Disclosure — everything runs locally through ffmpeg/ffprobe subprocesses and every file it writes stays under its output folder (`<hermes home>/plugin-data/shorts-factory/out/` or the `output_dir` you set in plugin config), never replacing an existing file unless the call asks to overwrite; it stores and uses no credentials and makes no network calls except a one-time Bebas Neue font download from github.com/google/fonts when no local font is found, and, if you install the optional faster-whisper package for auto-timed captions, its first-use Whisper model download from Hugging Face; requires ffmpeg and ffprobe installed on the machine.

entries.name: show-your-work
entries.description: An evidence board for a change's acceptance criteria: which requirements your agent actually tested, what the imported results say, whether they still match the code, and whether you signed off. Point it at the requirements you already have (a ticket, bug report or spec in Markdown) and it shows four separate statuses per requirement, never merged into one green check: coverage (is a test linked?), outcome (latest imported JUnit run), freshness (tracked files changed since?) and human review. For review, click a requirement and then a linked test to see that test's source and its own diff against the base branch (new, changed or unchanged), plus the change under review. The agent links tests and imports reports from wherever they ran (terminal, Docker, CI); it has no tool to accept or reject. Sign-off comes from the Desktop page, /syw or hermes syw. Five tools (syw_board, syw_link, syw_import, syw_run_detail, syw_test_evidence), a /syw command, a hermes syw CLI, a Desktop page and a workflow skill. Disclosure — runs no tests and makes no network or model calls; reads syw.toml, the criteria file, tracked files (to hash them) and JUnit XML inside the project folder (paths outside it and symlinks refused), runs read-only git (rev-parse, merge-base, diff, show, ls-files) in the project folder when you open a test's evidence or the change panel, stores links, results, hashes and reviews in SQLite under the profile's plugin-data, and writes show-your-work-review.md into the project only when you export.
entries.title: Show Your Work
known_issues: Sign-off is human-only through the plugin's tools, but `hermes syw accept` is an ordinary CLI command, so an agent with a terminal tool could run it (recorded as human:cli). The bundled skill tells agents never to.

With a remote backend (Docker, SSH), `hermes plugins update` on the server updates only the agent half; update the Desktop page from Desktop (Install from Git / Update with Desktop ticked) and Reload desktop plugins. After installing or updating, restart the dashboard backend so the page's API and the plugin host load the new code.
On native Windows, `hermes plugins install` can fail with WinError 32/5 (Hermes installer, #136120); docs/USAGE.md has a manual-clone workaround.
Finding a test's source from its JUnit id is a best guess (Java/Kotlin/Scala/Groovy, Python, Go, simple JS); when it can't, the panel says so.

entries.name: showly
entries.description: Preview, publish, and manage websites hosted on Showly from Hermes Agent, through the hosted Showly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — tool calls go to Showly's hosted MCP server at mcp.showly.ai. The bundled showly-hosting skill makes Showly the default for any deploy, preview or share request that names no provider, and new links default to public (anyone with the link). The showly-reports skill runs a bundled local Node.js renderer (vendored answer-me-with-html 0.4.14, upstream self-update check removed) through the shell and uploads the report directory to Showly when sharing is requested. Sign-in is out of band: `npx @showly/mcp-server login --to hermes` (unpinned) writes MCP_SHOWLY_API_KEY into ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

known_issues: Sign-in needs one command after install, because a portable mcp.json cannot carry a credential: npx @showly/mcp-server login --to hermes

entries.name: showreel
entries.description: Turn any Hermes session into a demo video under 90 seconds. Six observer hooks record what the session actually did (the ask, terminal commands and output, file edits, screenshots, token usage), scrubbed twice for secrets; a deterministic storyboard keeps a failing test and its fix together and fits a hard 89 s budget; Pillow and your own ffmpeg render a 1080p MP4 (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) with burned-in captions, an .srt and a poster. Desktop half: a Showreel page with a moment editor (drop beats, edit captions) and inline player, a REC chip, and a player card for showreel_render results. Narration is off by default; optional free offline voice (espeak-ng or piper on PATH), Hermes text_to_speech, or the user's own ElevenLabs key only when explicitly chosen, with `hermes showreel plan` showing the exact text and character count first. Disclosure — records every session by default (capture on): the user's prompts, terminal commands and output, file edits, token usage and any image file whose path appears in tool output, scrubbed for secret patterns (best effort; screenshot and image pixels are not scrubbed) into its plugin-data SQLite DB; old recordings are pruned to the newest keep_sessions (30) only when a video is rendered; runs ffmpeg/ffprobe (and espeak-ng or piper with local narration) as subprocesses with fixed argument lists; writes renders to its plugin-data renders folder or the user's output_dir; no network unless narration is set to elevenlabs (HTTPS to api.elevenlabs.io with the caption text, using the user's ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) or hermes (the TTS the user configured); no telemetry, no background processes, no self-updates.
entries.title: Showreel
known_issues: Needs ffmpeg on PATH (not bundled); `hermes showreel status` reports what it found.

entries.name: sidecar
entries.description: Remote brain, local hands: a paired execution backend that lets a remote Hermes run terminal, file, patch, search and execute_code commands on the user's local machine. A local daemon applies a workspace boundary and a hard deny list (privilege escalation, recursive root deletes, download-to-shell, Apple Events, keychain access, outbound network shells), and by default asks the person at the keyboard before anything that is not a side-effect-free read-only command. The pairing token is 32 random bytes, stored mode 0600 and compared in constant time; the daemon binds to loopback by default and warns otherwise. Commands run as the local user with a sanitized environment (no provider keys or SSH agent socket), a timeout and a process-group kill; every decision is written to a local JSONL audit log with command text redacted for common secret shapes and no command output stored. The remote plugin makes no network calls of its own beyond the configured daemon URL, has no Python dependencies, no telemetry and no self-updater. Not a sandbox: an approved command runs with the user's privileges; pair with Glassbox for kernel enforcement. macOS and Linux only.
entries.title: Sidecar
known_issues: Under plugins.isolation: host, Hermes skips plugin CLI subcommands and hands the provider an opaque placeholder; run Sidecar in the default in-process plugin isolation.

entries.name: siemless
entries.description: Agent security telemetry for SIEMs. Every tool call, file read, shell command, outbound request, approval, subagent, scheduled job and configuration change a Hermes agent makes becomes an OCSF 1.9 security event; 14 deterministic rules correlate them into findings (secret access then egress, prompt-injection chains, credential discovery, persistence, governance tampering, …) with MITRE ATT&CK 20.1 mapping and evidence labelled observed or inferred. Exports as JSON Lines (Wazuh), RFC 5424 syslog, CEF, Splunk HEC and Elastic ECS, with a pack and 22 Sigma rules. Desktop page with evidence chains and exporter health; /siemless and hermes siemless incl. replay of recorded sessions. Disclosure — observer hooks only (no pre_tool_call, no middleware, no tools; nothing is blocked or rewritten). Reads only the hook payloads Hermes passes, bounded and redacted before storage; prompt text, model output, tool results, file bodies and message text are never stored (hashes and lengths only; record_prompts adds a 200-char redacted preview). Writes its own SQLite database, JSONL files and spool under plugin-data/siemless/ (0600). Network: none by default; with remote_export true and a destination set, sends the configured event scope to that syslog (UDP/TCP/TLS), Splunk HEC, Elastic or JSON receiver endpoint over verified TLS (plain HTTP to 127.0.0.1 only behind a lab switch); tokens via agent.secret_scope.get_secret, never read from .env. Three daemon threads per process (pipeline, dispatch, settings watch). The dashboard half reads plugin settings through hermes_cli.config.load_config. `/siemless` works in any chat that can run plugin commands: it shows stored findings and events (tool names, targets, hosts, session ids across sessions), `ack` marks findings reviewed, and `replay <file>` reads a JSONL file the user names and runs it through the detections, labelled as a replay. No shell commands, no telemetry to the author, no self-updater. The install scanner reports caution because the detector lists the patterns it looks for (ssh paths, webhook hosts, curl|sh, cron, env dumps) in siemless_core/sensitive.py and in the tests.

entries.name: sieve
entries.description: User-owned notification boundary for Hermes Agent. Event classes route through tiers T0 to T5 under quiet hours. Routine alerts hold for a digest. Urgent ones escalate, and the message names both the requested tier and the arm that actually ran. Disclosure — sends notifications by running `hermes send` to the chats you set with `/sieve target` (default `telegram`), sets phone alarms/timers through the Hermes mobile_device tools for T4/T5 events, runs `tailscale status --json` from the Desktop status poll, and ships an optional macOS launchd watchdog (`scripts/watch.py`) that you render with `scripts/install-watchdog.sh` and load yourself with `launchctl bootstrap`.
entries.title: SIEVE
known_issues: Context slots such as meeting or sleeping are set with /sieve context. This build does not read location or calendar.
T4 is a 60-second timer. T5 is an alarm one minute out. They share one tone. T5 is top priority, not a siren.
Closed-app wake is not available in the current official iOS beta. The phone arm needs the Hermes app open and synced to this profile.
A messaging push is an ordinary notification. Focus can silence it, and it does not ring. It is a weaker interrupt than an alarm.

The desktop status poll and /sieve probe run tailscale status --json. A missing binary, a timeout, and the first reading are not an outage. That probe does not run when Desktop is closed or the Mac is asleep.

The Tailscale/gateway watchdog (scripts/watch.py) is opt-in and does not start itself, and its plist ships as a template. Render and load it once from a terminal: bash scripts/install-watchdog.sh, then launchctl bootstrap. It cannot see an outage while the Mac is asleep.

The Desktop pane cannot write the phone. Desktop chat may refuse /sieve with permission_denied before the plugin starts. Run /sieve doctor in Discord or Telegram. That result is kept and shown on the pane.
A probe gap (Mac asleep, or the watcher not running) means the link state during that gap is unknown. A drop and recovery across a sleep is not observed.
One gallery screenshot (the matrix pane). More follow in a later SHA bump.

That result is kept and shown on the pane.; A probe gap (Mac asleep, or the watcher not running) means the link state during that gap is unknown. A drop and recovery across a sleep is not observed.; One gallery screenshot (the matrix pane). More follow in a later SHA bump..

entries.name: sightline
entries.description: Give your Hermes agent a Solana wallet without giving it your wallet. Intent-level SOL and SPL tools, including Solana Pay payment links; every send is simulated, explained in plain English and checked by a firewall against human-issued, time-boxed, revocable grants (caps per day, week or month) before the plugin signs it. Cron jobs and bots can pay inside a grant unattended. Through its tools the model never sees the key, has no raw-transaction tool and cannot create or widen grants (on Hermes' local terminal backend the agent's shell could read .env or edit the grant database; edited grants are refused, and a sandboxed terminal backend is recommended for real funds). ALLOW / APPROVE / BLOCK with a hash-chained audit log and a Desktop pane. Devnet by default. Disclosure — crypto wallet: stores a Solana secret key in the profile .env (never shown to the model or in tool output) and sends simulation and signed transaction requests to the configured Solana RPC (default api.devnet.solana.com); mainnet only with SIGHTLINE_ALLOW_MAINNET=1. Payments inside a human-issued grant are signed and sent without a prompt, including from cron jobs; everything else needs your approval. On the local terminal backend the agent's shell can read .env and the grant database, so use a sandboxed terminal backend for real funds. No telemetry.

entries.name: signado
entries.description: Find warm leads on LinkedIn through Signado's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.signado.io/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): list and read warm leads and hiring leads, export them, find work emails, draft first messages, and add, preview, schedule or run the LinkedIn sources that watch keywords, posts, creators and company pages. entries.name: signal-dog
entries.description: Listens through the microphone for household sounds (a door knock, an appliance beeping, a smoke alarm or other steady tone) and sends a chat message through the agent's messaging platform. A signal dog is a dog trained to alert a deaf person to sounds; this does the same job with a microphone, and it is built by a deaf developer. Off until the user turns it on with /signaldog on. Not a certified smoke alarm: it can miss sounds and raise false alerts, with measured rates and limits in the README. Disclosure: microphone: while switched on it listens to the microphone continuously. Background process: it runs one long-running ffmpeg process (two for about 30 seconds every 10 minutes while one replaces the other), stopped when the user turns it off or the plugin unloads; ffmpeg must already be installed and the plugin never downloads anything. Audio from the microphone is never kept: it is analysed in memory and dropped, with no option to keep it. /signaldog demo writes one recording made by code (no real sound) to a private temporary folder and deletes it when the demo ends. Stored locally: a size-limited numbers log in $HERMES_HOME/signal-dog/events.log (times, levels, what was detected, plus an optional note of up to 80 characters the user types after /signaldog wrong or right). The read-only tool signal_dog_recent_alerts returns alert times, kinds, pitches, the user's right and wrong marks and the listener state to the agent, so it reaches the user's model provider; it does not check who is asking, so do not use the plugin on an agent that strangers can message. Network: the plugin makes no network calls and has no telemetry; alerts are delivered by the agent through the messaging app the user already set up. No credentials are read or stored. The pre_llm_call hook only notices which chat session is live and reads no message content. While a beep keeps sounding, it edits its own first alert ("still beeping", then "no longer detected") where the messaging app allows edits, and otherwise sends periodic reminder messages (every three minutes by default, for as long as the beep continues); it never edits anyone else's messages.

entries.name: signal-notify
entries.description: Signal texts when a Hermes turn pauses, fails or is interrupted, and when Hermes waits on a clarify question, approval or sudo prompt. Sends through the user's own signal-cli HTTP daemon (the same SIGNAL_* settings as the core Signal gateway); skips Signal-origin, cron and subagent turns, and dedupes identical texts within 60s. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled turns POST to SIGNAL_HTTP_URL (plain HTTP unless that URL is https), which signal-cli delivers as a Signal message; by default each text includes up to 300 characters of the final reply (not secret-redacted) or of the redacted question/command (include_text: false or reply_chars: 0 sends none); each event has its own on/off setting; sudo passwords and clarify answers are never seen; nothing is stored on disk, at most 64 clipped reply previews are kept in memory, and each send runs on a short-lived daemon thread with a 20s timeout.

entries.name: signaldesk
entries.description: Draft-first lead desk for founders and marketers: scan public hiring and launch signals (HN Who is hiring, YC hiring, Show HN, Launch HN, new YC companies; optional Product Hunt with a token) and local businesses on an OpenStreetMap map (LocalLead Map: city + business type or a drawn area, shown on an OpenLayers map), score them against your ICP, draft outreach, and never send without user approval (board, Desktop, or /signaldesk approve; the model cannot approve a lead or move a lead to sent/replied/won). Cron and unattended runs fail closed. Disclosure — fetches public JSON from Algolia HN Search and the yc-oss static API, and (only when you run a map scan) geocodes with Nominatim and queries public Overpass API instances; the board loads OpenStreetMap tiles in the browser; Product Hunt GraphQL is used only when PRODUCTHUNT_TOKEN is set; optional DNS MX lookups; lead data stays in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/signaldesk/; it never sends email itself, and its pre_tool_call hook blocks other send tools unless the lead was approved by you and the run is not a cron job.
entries.title: SignalDesk
known_issues: The Hermes Desktop board page (desktop/plugin.js) passes catalog desktop-surface validation but was not clicked through in a live Desktop window on the build machine. The interactive HTML board is the supported demo and review UI.
Product Hunt is optional and stays off unless PRODUCTHUNT_TOKEN is set through Hermes secret_scope. Product Hunt API terms restrict commercial use without permission.
BetaList is not included; their site terms are not a clean fit for a keyless built-in source.
Show HN posts hosted only on GitHub often have no company inbox, so those leads are scored but usually have no contact.

LocalLead Map: public Overpass instances can be slow or rate-limited; SignalDesk tries them one at a time and falls back to the bundled Zürich demo extract (dentists, cafes) when all fail. The demo video's map scan used the Swiss instance overpass.osm.ch (SIGNALDESK_OVERPASS_URL) because overpass-api.de was unreachable from the build machine.
A live scan needs outbound HTTPS to Algolia and yc-oss.github.io. Each source is capped so a large hiring dump does not flood the board. The offline demo uses bundled fixtures.

entries.name: signet-drive
entries.description: Your agent's own encrypted drive, with dated restore points of its memory, which only you and your agent can open unless you invite someone. Disclosure — Automatically uploads the agent's MEMORY.md and USER.md as encrypted restore points to your Signet Drive (drive.mysignet.ca by default) through the vendor's signed `signet` macOS app, about 30 minutes after a memory change and at each session start; the save tool uploads files from one save folder you choose (default: the plugin's own to-save folder), fetched files land in the plugin's own folder, and once per app version it downloads the published app archive from that server and hashes from raw.githubusercontent.com/prsnex to verify the installed app. Anyone you invite to write to the drive can place files the agent fetches, or restore points it can apply to memory only after you approve them in Hermes.

entries.name: singularity
entries.description: Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend: Hermes's terminal, file and code tools run inside a hardened, rootless container on this machine (--containall --no-home), with CPU/memory limits and an optional per-session persistent overlay (`hermes config set terminal.backend singularity`; image from `terminal.singularity_image`). Your skills and registered credential files are bind-mounted read-only into the container, and because the container is a disposable sandbox Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as for its other container backends.

entries.name: skill-court
entries.description: Skill Court tests the skills your agent writes. With automatic trials turned on (opt-in: `hermes court auto on` or the Desktop page's Turn on switch), after the agent writes or changes a skill, and the first time each agent-written skill's current version is used on a model, it replays that skill's real tasks with and without it in the background, in Docker sandboxes when Docker answers or answer-only (skills, todo and web tools only, judged on final answers) when it does not; `hermes court trial` runs one on demand. Each pair is scored by the task's check or a blind pairwise judge; a skill that hurts is hidden from that model only (skill index, skills_list, skill_view), and the next turn shows the verdict, the cause and the SKILL.md line behind it. An appeal drafts a fix, proves it on the same tasks and writes it only when you apply it (undo restores the original). Usage evidence per skill and model from recent sessions, read-only. CLI (hermes court trial/report/appeal/auto/tasks/quarantine/release/list) plus a Desktop page. Disclosure: automatic trials are off until the user turns them on (the first turn after install and after-install.md say how; `hermes court auto off` stops them), within $1.00 a day of provider-reported replay spend plus 300,000 judge tokens (runs already under way finish). Trials run hermes and docker/podman commands, create and delete two replay profiles cloned from yours (config, API keys, SOUL, memory, skills; never messaging channels; no MCP, other plugins, context engine, shell hooks or inline shell). Replays are single-query sessions with approvals denied, never -z. The judge (your provider, via ctx.llm) sees task text, both runs' answers and sandbox files, and for a cause a transcript excerpt and the skill. Verdicts are posted with ctx.post_message to the conversation that changed or used the skill, never into the model's context. A live SKILL.md is written only by `hermes court appeal apply` or Apply fix.
entries.title: Skill Court
known_issues: Without a reachable Docker or Podman, trials run answer-only: they test what a skill makes the agent say or decide, not procedures that need terminal or file tools.
In codex_app_server mode only quarantines set for every model apply.
Appeals import Hermes' skill frontmatter parser and skills_guard scan, which are not in the published plugin API yet (issue #150975); without them an appeal refuses to draft or apply.

Rapid replay-profile create/delete can trigger a Hermes core race that leaks a hosted-room poller (repeating 'state.db was replaced' log lines until a gateway restart); fix offered in #150937 was closed unmerged.

entries.name: skill-governance
entries.description: Consolidated skill-governance plugin behind one composed hook surface: on_skill_lifecycle, on_session_start, pre_tool_call, pre_llm_call. The manifest engine enforces UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md — arrivals need a manifest row, content changes in manifested skills re-flag until re-acknowledged against a content fingerprint via the preserved /skill-manifest-ack command. The advisor engine observes behavioral skill edits (never blocking) and injects one bounded reminder to run the contrastive-refinement probe cycle (bundled as skill-governance:contrastive-refinement), recording every delivered advisory to ~/.hermes/skill-probes/fire-ledger.jsonl. Both legacy state namespaces import by copy (destination-wins, sources never modified) and a conservative governance.records summary joins them (acknowledged never implies validated). A clearance Automation Blueprint (daily schedule, origin delivery) replaces both legacy schedulers and preserves both clearance procedures verbatim; the user adopts it from the blueprint gallery or /blueprint, and the plugin imports no private cron modules and writes no cron state. Stdlib only, no network calls, fail-soft everywhere (malformed state keeps hooks inert, never aborts the host turn). Disclosure — reads the profile's skills tree (SKILL.md files, fingerprinted read-only) and UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md, and copies the legacy skill-manifest / contrastive-advisor plugin state read-only on first run; writes its own plugin state, `<HERMES_HOME>/skill-probes/fire-ledger.jsonl` when the opt-in advisor fires, and `plugin-data/skill-manifest/acks.json` on a manual `/skill-manifest-ack`; injects advisory reminders into turns; the optional daily clearance blueprint, once the user adopts it with `/blueprint`, runs an unattended agent that edits UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.md and the plugin's dismissed list, reads past session tool calls from state.db, and writes probe notes; never deletes, never blocks tool calls, no network.

entries.name: skill-hint
entries.description: Local-first skill discovery: on each user turn it runs a BM25 query over the installed skill library and injects up to three candidate skill names, only when the match is confident — catches colloquial phrasing, shorthand and non-English wording that a description-written index misses. Pure standard library: no network, no model call, no API key, ~0.03 ms per query, and at most a few lines of injected context. Says nothing when nothing fits; never raises into the conversation. Disclosure — reads SKILL.md front matter and the first 1,000 characters of the body under the profile's skill roots (symlinked skill directories are followed) and keeps the index in memory; it writes nothing and sends nothing anywhere. Skill names and descriptions reach the model only when a hint is injected, exactly as they would if the model had opened the skill itself.

entries.name: skill-lineage
entries.description: Records where each skill version's content came from, so a skill that rewrites itself can be audited afterwards. For every skill write — a foreground skill_manage call, a background-review edit, or a curator consolidation — it stores the skill content fingerprint before and after, the sources present earlier in the same session (the text the user typed, tool results such as a fetched page or a file, and skills that were read), how each source is linked to the added lines — strong (at least three shared 8-word shingles), anchor (a shared operative token: a URL or host, a shell command with its first argument, a package install, a file path, an environment variable, an IP or e-mail address, that is not common across sources), or context (seen in the session, nothing measurable shared; recorded, not followed by default) — and a seq -> prev_hash -> hash chain over the entries. Text is never stored: hashes are keyed per install and the key stays in plugin-data/skill-lineage. `hermes skill-lineage trace <skill>` shows where the newest version came from, `descendants <url|skill>` lists every skill a source produced, `report` lists versions carrying operative lines of no traceable origin, `verify` re-walks the chain, and `head` prints a value to record elsewhere so a later `verify --head` can tell truncation from an intact chain; a key reset is recorded in the chain and shown in `status` rather than happening silently. The plugin does not stop a write and does not judge a skill: it records and it verifies, and it does not claim a source caused an edit. Prior work on memory lineage (MemLineage, arXiv:2605.14421) is acknowledged in the README. Measured on 2026-10-22 against Hermes 3166d61: Python 3.14 62 passed; Python 3.11 54 passed, 1 skipped; `hermes plugins validate` reports no warning other than one known false positive (a test template that quotes a "curl | sh" instruction as data and never runs it). Evaluation (generated scenarios and 120 real-model runs) in the README; raw output in eval/. A manual end-to-end run in an isolated HERMES_HOME (one real session creating a skill through skill_manage, then status/trace/descendants/report/verify/head) passed, raw output in tests/smoke-2026-10-21.txt. Disclosure — four read-only hooks (on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call); reads tool results, user messages and skill files (in this profile, every other profile's skills folder, the project's .hermes/skills and the skills.external_dirs it reads from config.yaml) to compute keyed hashes; keeps hashes (no text) for 7 days per session and the lineage chain (hashes and skill names) under plugin-data/skill-lineage; no network, no credentials, never blocks or changes a tool call.

entries.name: skill-retrieval
entries.description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is declared via pip_dependencies in plugin.yaml, so the installer installs it. On CPython 3.14 the host's hermes_yaml facade is used when PyYAML is unavailable. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (leading injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and the ids and descriptions of up to 12 shortlisted skills (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error); with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_PROVIDER=openrouter the same payload goes to openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone instead, keyed by OPENROUTER_API_KEY (each provider reads only its own key, from the environment only). A local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders, rerank scores) is appended under $HERMES_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

entries.name: skill-stats
entries.description: Skill Stats shows which skills you actually use in Hermes Agent, when, and how much. Type /skill-stats in any chat to see that session's skills ranked by loads with a % share, or run `hermes skill-stats` in the terminal for all-time totals; switch the window from 1 day to 90, page through the rows, group them by category, and answer questions like "which skills did I lean on this week?" or "is this skill still worth keeping?" Point the command at another chat by title or short id (for example -s stageshow-bentora) to compare sessions, or add `global` from a chat to see everything combined. In `hermes --tui` the same numbers open as an interactive modal: browse skills with the arrow keys, open a skill's chart, flip between bars and a cumulative line, and set the period with keys 1 to 6. The web Dashboard gains a Skill Stats tab where you pin the skills you monitor so they stay on top of the table, page 10 to 100 rows, and drill into per-skill charts. Nothing to configure: install it and the counting starts on the next session. Disclosure — no network calls, no telemetry, no shell commands and no credentials; the plugin writes only its own stats files under $HERMES_HOME/skill-stats/ (plus one copy of its TUI widget file into $HERMES_HOME/tui-widgets/ at startup so the modal works) and reads Hermes' session registry read-only to resolve a session title or short id, never message content.

entries.name: skill-workshop
entries.description: Get new skills for Hermes safely: mine them from your past chats (Skill Miner), build them from a description (First Principles Skill Builder), and guard against prompt injection in skills and content you bring in (Taint Shield). Scans skill writes before they land and holds back flagged external skills at first use (Skill Guard); Workshop installs need your approval. Disclosure: Skill Miner reads the Hermes session database read-only through the public hermes_state module (tool names and counts, plus the first request of each session in abstracted, redacted form; for one session you choose, also the ordered tool steps as argument shapes and your own messages as redacted quotes, to draft a skill from it); Skill Builder runs --version on a fixed list of common tools and nvidia-smi with a minimal environment and reads memory, disk space, skill names and model-cache folder names; Taint Shield watches tool calls in memory; Skill Guard reads the text of skills in your skills folders (and external skill folders named in config.yaml, read through Hermes's config loader) when they are installed or loaded and keeps a hash and a decision for each in plugin storage. Drafts, revisions and the trusted list live in plugin storage; installing a skill writes one file into the skills folder after your approval. Two install approvals, the Shield's block-or-ask rules and Skill Guard's install scan use pre_tool_call; Skill Guard also uses transform_tool_result and pre_llm_call (hold back a flagged skill, once) and on_skill_lifecycle (scan a skill after Hermes reports it installed). No network calls.

entries.name: skillcheck
entries.description: CI for agent skills: snapshots the pre-write state of skill writes arriving through Hermes's in-band tool surface (skill_manage create/edit/patch/write_file/remove_file/delete and write_file/patch/edit_file into the skills dir; hooks observe landed writes, no pre-write blocking; creates have no prior state, out-of-band edits are detected at run time but carry no snapshot), LLM-generates regression cases as human-review drafts, re-runs them against the candidate revision in child sessions launched through the Hermes subagent lifecycle API with allowed_toolsets=() (no file, shell, browser or network tools; timed-out children get a cancellation request whose accepted/refused outcome is reported), and reports GREEN / REGRESSION / FIRST-RUN. Promotion and revert are user-invoked only (slash command or CLI; not registered as model tools), and revert validates the skill name, stays strictly inside the skill folder, skips dotfiles and restores byte-exact snapshots. entries.name: skilluminati
entries.description: Your skills, judged blind: finds out whether each skill your Hermes agent loads makes its answers better. /skilluminati <skill> takes the latest 12 times you used the skill, each with the chat as it stood at that moment, and your model answers each one twice, once with the skill and once without. The Owl, a blind judge, sees both answers and the skill's one-line description of its job, never which answer had the skill, and sees every pair twice with the answers swapped; if it picks differently the second time, the pair counts as Same. Verdicts: Enlightened (answers are clearly better with it), Dead weight (the model does this anyway, it only costs tokens), Hindrance (answers are worse with it) or Unproven (too few uses to tell yet), each marked Probable or Plausible. A close Dead weight that is only Plausible reads No clear difference yet, and asking again pools the new run with earlier runs of the same skill version, model and judge. Each result carries flags where they apply: Skill changed, Stale, Tool-driven, Same-model judge and Judge failed, plus a same-vs-same figure for how often the Owl picks a side between two answers from the same setup. Built-in question sets for frontend-design, systematic-debugging and hermes-agent let a fresh install run a test with no history, and /skilluminati selftest plants a helpful, a harmful and an empty skill to prove the Owl can tell them apart. Surfaces: the /skilluminati command, two read-only agent tools, a Desktop page with a sidebar entry (plugin SDK only) and a read-only dashboard backend. Disclosure — opens HERMES_HOME/state.db read-only and reads installed skill files, skills/.usage.json and skills.disabled/model.default from config.yaml; for each test it sends up to 12 past tasks (the stored session system prompt, the chat up to the moment the skill loaded and any tool output in it, after best-effort regex blanking of emails, phone numbers, key-shaped strings, token-carrying URLs, money amounts and names in plugin-data/skilluminati/names.txt) plus the skill text to the active provider and model, or a per-role provider/model you configure, through ctx.llm (a configured judge model must also be on plugins.entries.skilluminati.llm.allowed_models when that list exists), at up to 64 model calls per skill on your own allowance; runs start only from a local CLI/TUI/Desktop/ACP session (never cron or a messaging gateway) on a background thread; registers one plugin skill (skilluminati:skilluminati, about 25 tokens a turn) so the agent quotes saved results instead of guessing; run folders keep only redacted copies of the tasks, and redaction also turns the account name in home-folder paths into ~; writes only under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/skilluminati/; imports one private core helper (agent.skill_utils.get_all_skills_dirs) to list skill folders; no other network calls, no shell commands, no stored credentials.
entries.title: Skilluminati
known_issues: Each test is one fresh answer per task from the moment the skill loaded. Tools are not run again, so skills that mostly drive tools are judged on the answer text only.
The replay puts the skill into the chat directly, so it does not test whether your agent would have chosen to load it.
If the judge is the same model family as the one under test, it may favour answers like its own. The result names the model.
Every test spends your own provider allowance: up to 64 model calls for one skill. The frontend-design built-in set takes about an hour because every answer is a whole web page.

The Owl is noisy: on the author's runs (Opus 5.5 judging its own answers) it picked a side 37 of 59 times between two answers from the same setup, so a single run is a lean. Asking again pools the evidence.
A verdict run needs at least 6 usable past uses of the skill; with fewer, it falls back to a built-in question set where one exists.
The Desktop page appears only after Capabilities -> Plugins -> Skilluminati is switched on in Hermes Desktop.
Lists skill folders through agent.skill_utils.get_all_skills_dirs, a private core helper (validator rule 9 warning); a future Hermes release may move it.

entries.name: slaide
entries.description: AI presentation maker: build, edit and export PowerPoint slide decks, Word documents and Excel workbooks from chat through Slaide's hosted MCP server. Portable Agent Plugin v1 package (plugin.json, Streamable HTTP mcp.json, one skill). entries.name: sluice
entries.description: An airlock for agent changes. A terminal backend that runs the agent's commands and file tools (read_file, write_file, patch, search_files) in a staged copy of the workspace, so the real files are untouched until you review the diff hunk by hunk and apply only what you approve (/sluice diff, /sluice apply, /sluice discard, also as `hermes sluice`). Calls a copy cannot contain (git push, package installs, network writes, deploys, writes or deletes outside the workspace) are sent to Hermes's own approval prompt labelled NOT CONTAINED. Select it with `hermes config set terminal.backend sluice`. Disclosure — No network calls and no background processes. Runs the agent's shell commands and file tools on this host as the user, in a staged copy of the workspace kept under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/sluice (every non-gitignored workspace file plus a copy of .git; stages idle 14 days are deleted), and runs `git ls-files` to list files; it never reads Hermes credential files. Only when the user runs `/sluice apply` does it write the approved changes (including new symlinks) into the workspace. One pre_tool_call hook sends calls the copy cannot contain (installs, network writes, git push, writes outside the workspace) to Hermes's approval prompt and never approves anything itself. Not an operating-system sandbox: the hold list reads command text, so Python in execute_code or a command that builds its target path at run time can write outside the workspace without being held.
entries.title: Sluice
known_issues: Not an OS sandbox: the gate reads command text, so a command that builds its target path at run time can get past it.

entries.title: Smart Dictation
known_issues: Requires configured local faster-whisper and cached model weights. No automatic model download or cloud-STT fallback.

Common Contextual mode is a UI preference, not backend activation. Registration checks are read-only and may connect to selected local backends; unsupported or unavailable backends remain unverified. Package activation and STT provider selection are per profile. No automatic enrollment; the copy-only guide never activates or sends anything.

Native correction is profile-wide. A default ON preference cannot authorize execution without recorded consent; explicit OFF is preserved. Text may go to the configured auxiliary model under Hermes' normal cost, recovery and logging policies. The registration check does not test inference or prove tool-free execution.
Native inherits core insertion and undo, not Contextual draft/session fences or successful raw/corrected comparison. Enabled correction failure inserts a warning plus the entire original transcript.
Contextual requires a local route and sends transcript and explicitly selected reference context to its correction route. Local decoding means the selected Hermes backend host.
Local decoder excludes Windows ARM64 and Intel macOS. Model and reasoning-effort assignments use native Hermes settings; select the intended profile and save targets.

entries.name: smart-model-swap
entries.description: Run a big and a small local LLM on one GPU rig and let the agent switch between them by task: the small one for quick or voice chat and to free VRAM for GPU jobs (ComfyUI), the big one for deep work. SmartModelProvider launches and stops llama.cpp's llama-server itself, swaps in the background without cutting replies, checks per-GPU VRAM before loading, restores the big model when idle, and ships a launch-parameter editor in the dashboard and Desktop, plus a bundled routing skill. Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio are detection-only. Disclosure — starts and stops llama-server as a long-running background process (in a transient systemd-run --user scope when available), autostarts the primary model when the gateway starts and swaps back to it if a smaller model was left serving (GPU memory), and keeps a detached runner per swap and a watcher that restores the primary after inactivity and, by default, loads another registered model if the serving one dies; sends SIGINT/SIGKILL only to the engine process it manages or an engine of the same kind holding its port; runs nvidia-smi, ss, systemctl --user show, systemd-run and llama-server --help/--version with a minimal environment (no provider keys); reads /proc of other processes to identify the engine and GPU users, and its guard reads shell scripts a terminal command is about to run; adds one-line hints to turns, can veto terminal/execute_code calls that manage the engine by hand, and can end a turn with an explanation while the LLM is unloaded on purpose; writes its own settings to config.yaml and, only on request, installs a model-provider plugin under plugins/model-providers/smart-model-provider; HTTP only to the configured engine and ComfyUI endpoints (localhost by default). No telemetry, credentials, self-updater or approval bypass.
entries.title: Smart Model Swap
known_issues: Needs an NVIDIA GPU with nvidia-smi and a built llama.cpp llama-server; only llama.cpp is managed (Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio are detection-only).
On WSL2, GGUFs on a Windows drive (/mnt/<drive>, 9p) load ~10x slower than from the Linux filesystem.
Keep the same -c on every model: Hermes caches one context length per model id (the editor enforces it).

entries.name: smolmachines
entries.description: smol machines' own plugin: runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools in a smol machine, a microVM with its own Linux kernel on this computer (macOS on Apple Silicon, or Linux with KVM), as a terminal backend (`hermes config set terminal.backend smolmachines`). It needs no Docker and no account. Disclosure: installs the `smolmachines` Python SDK (>=1.27.2,<2), which carries the VM engine. Everything runs on this computer: the plugin always asks the SDK for a local machine, so nothing is sent to smol machines' cloud, even with SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN set or the smol CLI signed in (Hermes strips SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN from the commands it runs). Creating a machine pulls its image (default `python:3.12-slim`, from Docker Hub), and the engine pulls with this computer's Docker registry login when one is configured (`~/.docker/config.json`, including a credential helper such as the macOS keychain), read-only and sent only to the registry being pulled from. A machine has outbound network access and mounts nothing from this computer. With `terminal.container_persistent` (the Hermes default) each Hermes home and session keeps one machine, which keeps running after Hermes exits until stopped or deleted with the smolvm CLI, otherwise the machine is deleted when the session ends. Because the machine is a disposable sandbox, Hermes skips its dangerous-command prompts there, as it does for its other container backends.
entries.title: smol machines
known_issues: The engine stops a command once it has printed 11 MiB. Hermes gets the output up to that point, marked OUTPUT TRUNCATED. Send large output to a file in the machine.

The plugin imports tools.environments.base.FileFetchError (in Hermes since 0.21.6), the error fetch_file is documented to raise. It is outside the documented-name allowlist, so a Hermes release that moves it can break file delivery until the plugin is updated.

entries.name: snare
entries.description: Prompt injection tripwire with attack-chain forensics. Plants decoy credentials (PROD_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, PROD_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, PROD_DATABASE_URL) in the environment of every command the agent runs, never in the prompt. A tool call that tries to send one out (plain, URL-encoded, base64, hex, reversed, partial or nested) is blocked, and so is a command that reads a decoy variable or dumps the environment while using the network, including inside a local script the command runs. The alert names the page or file the injected instruction came from, quotes it, shows how the decoy was exposed and what the agent tried, then locks the session behind Hermes approvals until /snare reset. Disclosure — adds three fake variables (PROD_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, PROD_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, PROD_DATABASE_URL) to commands on the local terminal backend (names already set are skipped); reads, never writes, up to four local script files a terminal command runs (64 KB each) to check them; prepends its alert to the agent's reply in the session that tripped it and redacts the decoy values from replies; after a trip, every further tool call in that session goes to Hermes' approval prompt until /snare reset; on /snare selftest, and on /snare status with the local backend until one check is conclusive, runs one command through Hermes' terminal tool that prints which decoy names are set, never their values; stores owner-only files in its plugin-data folder: the decoys, and per incident a JSON line plus an HTML report with the tool name, shortened arguments of the blocked call, destination URLs, the source URL or path, up to 280 characters of the injected text and the session id; no network calls, telemetry or Python dependencies.

entries.name: snippet
entries.description: Connect a Snippet account to manage creator brand deals, sponsorship rates, brand emails, decisions and contract reviews through Snippet's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp, OAuth). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. The hosted server supplies its current tool list at runtime; tool availability can change independently of this catalog entry. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Snippet's hosted MCP server (https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp), which receives tool arguments and returns account data (deals, brand email threads, contract text); the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; some tools write (send_reply sends brand email, answer_decision and draft_reply change account state) and the package declares trust: untrusted so Hermes asks before them and blocks them in unattended runs; a Snippet account is required and some actions need a paid plan; sign-in currently needs `hermes mcp add snippet --url https://usesnippet.app/api/mcp --auth oauth`, and that same-name native entry replaces the package's server entry including its trust setting, so add `trust: untrusted` under mcp_servers.snippet afterwards; Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens; the package ships no credentials, executables, dependencies, self-updater or telemetry.

entries.name: snooze
entries.description: A reminder that repeats in your chat (Telegram, Discord) until you answer it exactly: Ok, your word, an emoji, a Telegram reaction, or one of several choices; reply later to postpone. A wrong answer gets the list of valid answers from the plugin's code, never from the LLM. Then it can hand a follow-up to the agent. Created with /snooze in plain words ("Stop the GPU at 19:00 every 10m then shut it down"), by the agent through the snooze_create tool, or with hermes snooze add. Zero LLM calls per reminder. Disclosure — no network call of its own, no subprocess, no credentials, no telemetry. A timer task in the gateway checks every 15 s and sends due reminders, each showing its follow-up ("Then: ..."), through Hermes's send path to the snooze's chat or home channel. The pre_gateway_dispatch hook sees every inbound gateway text message before Hermes authorization, but acts only on messages from the snooze's owner in that snooze's chat: an answer, a reply to a reminder or the first message after one is consumed, and an answer with a follow-up becomes the follow-up prompt. The post_gateway_admission hook handles snoozes with no owner (created from the CLI for a channel or group), where any sender Hermes has admitted in that chat may answer. The gateway_platform_event hook reads Telegram reactions on reminders in private chats. Follow-ups after a reaction, /snooze ok or an admitted answer are queued with ctx.inject_message, which needs allow_gateway_injection, and in a cron run snooze_create refuses a follow-up unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true. It stores snoozes.json and lock files in its plugin data dir, writes only its own notification_platform setting, and reads private Hermes internals (tools.send_message_tool.send_message_tool, agent.estop.is_engaged, and the gateway runner reference and event loop in gateway.run), so a Hermes release can break it.
entries.title: Snooze
known_issues: The gateway must be running: the timer lives in the gateway, so a CLI or Desktop session alone sends no reminders.
Tested on Telegram and Discord; other Hermes chat platforms are untested. Reaction confirms work in Telegram private chats only.
Uses two private Hermes names (send_message_tool, estop.is_engaged); a Hermes release can break them.

entries.name: so101-arm
entries.description: Give Hermes a robot arm, safely: an SO-101 (a MuJoCo sim on your laptop, or a real arm through LeRobot) driven by named skills, never joint angles. A top-down camera grid corrects its aim, a missed pick is rehearsed on simulated copies before the retry, a plain-code watchdog parks the arm on faults, a pre_tool_call guard refuses motion until a repair is verified, and only a person can lift a freeze (/arm unfreeze). Disclosure — the tools move a robot arm with no Hermes approval prompt: with the arm host started as `serve --real`, the agent drives a physical SO-101 over USB serial, limited to taught poses and motions, ±40 mm aim corrections and no more than the recorded speed (the default `serve` is a MuJoCo sim). The plugin talks only to a local Unix socket (mode 0600, default `<temp dir>/so101-arm.sock`) served by an arm host you start yourself (`python -m so101_host serve`). Any program running as you, Hermes's terminal tool included, can send that socket any command, unfreeze included, and the motion guard lets calls through when the host is down. Its log hooks send tool names, results and token counts (never conversation text) to that socket for the viewer. The arm host is a separate program from the same repository: it writes run records and camera frames under `~/.so101-arm/`, `fetch-model` runs git to download MuJoCo Menagerie's SO-101 model at a pinned commit, and `serve --video` runs ffmpeg.
entries.title: SO-101 Arm
known_issues: Needs the arm host from the same repository running beside Hermes: python -m so101_host fetch-model, then python -m so101_host serve (add --view to watch the arm).
The real-arm driver (LeRobot) is tested against a mock robot only; it hasn't been run on hardware yet.

entries.name: sochen
entries.description: Give Hermes a phone with nothing to set up: Sochen (sochen.dev), a cloud agent for any open-source agent, phones a US business for you and brings back the answer, with no Twilio account, number or voice keys of your own. When the business asks something only you can answer, the question comes to your Hermes chat while they hold the line, and your reply goes straight back into the call. It also runs long research in the cloud and handles email and calendar jobs that wait for your OK, and Hermes is told when each job finishes. Every account gets 100 free Sochen API credits, spread over any number of jobs; after that, packs or a monthly API plan (sochen.dev/pricing#api). Free GST invoices, rent receipts for HRA and UPI bill splits with no account, and your Sochen desk as a page in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — network calls go to sochen.dev only: the Agent API with your SOCHEN_API_KEY (read through Hermes's secret scope) for jobs, job status and the desk, and the public tools endpoint, with no key, for the free tools. Jobs run on your Sochen account and credits, and Hermes asks before each handoff. On your next message the plugin checks up to two open jobs (4 s each; a job whose call is going on, every turn), sochen_job may wait up to 60 s for news while a call goes on, and sochen_answer sends only the answer the user gave. Hermes Desktop reads the desk every 30 s while open. A short list of handed-off jobs (id, label, status) is kept in the plugin's own state. Requests carry a hermes-sochen/<version> client name; there is no other telemetry.
entries.title: Sochen
known_issues: Jobs, job status and the desk need a Sochen key from sochen.dev/agents (every account gets 100 free API credits). Phone calls go to US businesses with nothing to set up, need paid API credits, and other countries have a waitlist.

entries.name: softhalo-usage
entries.description: Shows your Hermes token usage in Soft Halo's always-on-top Windows overlay, which you can resize and make more or less transparent, next to Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw. Observer hooks only: after each model call it writes the token counts (uncached input, cache reads and writes, output), the provider, model and session id to a small file in Soft Halo's local folder on Windows, reached from WSL through /mnt/c. Disclosure — after every model call it writes a small file with token counts, provider, model and session id (never prompts, responses or tool output) into Soft Halo's local usage folder, which on WSL is the Windows user's AppData folder reached through /mnt/c; on a machine without Soft Halo those files are never cleaned up. No network requests and no tools or commands.
entries.title: Soft Halo Usage
known_issues: Needs Soft Halo for Windows 2.0.5.20 or later to show the numbers; without it the plugin only writes small local files.
On Hermes versions without the post_auxiliary_call hook (such as v0.13.0), side calls such as title generation are not counted.

entries.name: sogni
entries.description: Sogni AI image generation backend for image_generate: text-to-image and image-to-image (identity edit) on Sogni's decentralised GPU network, driven through Sogni's own sogni-agent CLI. Registers as an image_gen provider, so the normal image_generate tool works unchanged — aspect ratio and reference images are threaded through. Disclosure — every generation submits a job to the Sogni network via the sogni-agent-hermes CLI, which this plugin spawns as a subprocess, so unlike Hermes's bundled providers it is not zero-install: it needs Node.js and npm install -g @sogni-ai/sogni-creative-agent-skill@3.56.1 (or SOGNI_AGENT_BIN pointing at an existing binary). The prompt and any reference image (including a local file path the model passes) are sent to api.sogni.ai on the way to the network and the finished image is downloaded from media.sogni.ai; the plugin reads SOGNI_API_KEY through Hermes's secret scope and hands the CLI a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, SOGNI_API_KEY and, if set, NODE_OPTIONS, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, XDG_CACHE_HOME), so no other Hermes provider keys reach it, and it presents an honest custom User-Agent because Cloudflare (Error 1010) rejects library-default ones. Generation is billed to your Sogni account per job with no Hermes approval prompt, and the plugin reports the model used but enforces no budget cap, so an unattended run can spend your balance. Generated media is written under $HERMES_HOME/cache/images/. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no background processes beyond the CLI call, no self-updates.
entries.title: Sogni AI Images
known_issues: Not zero-install: requires Node.js plus the separately installed sogni-agent CLI (npm install -g @sogni-ai/sogni-agent). If the CLI is missing the plugin reports it as a typed error instead of failing silently.
Editing is supported only through the identity-edit model families, which take a source image; text-to-image models accept no source image and the plugin rejects the request rather than ignoring it.
Sogni bills per job and the plugin cannot cap spend; allow it to run unattended only with a balance you are willing to burn.
entries.capability_summary: sogni (community, maintained by RichardChua1234) Sogni AI image generation backend for image_generate: text-to-image and image-to-image (identity edit) on Sogni's decentralised GPU network, driven through Sogni's own sogni-agent CLI. Registers as an image_gen provider, so the normal image_generate tool works unchanged — aspect ratio and reference images are threaded through. Disclosure — every generation submits a job to the Sogni network via the sogni-agent-hermes CLI, which this plugin spawns as a subprocess, so unlike Hermes's bundled providers it is not zero-install: it needs Node.js and npm install -g @sogni-ai/sogni-creative-agent-skill@3.56.1 (or SOGNI_AGENT_BIN pointing at an existing binary). The prompt and any reference image (including a local file path the model passes) are sent to api.sogni.ai on the way to the network and the finished image is downloaded from media.sogni.ai; the plugin reads SOGNI_API_KEY through Hermes's secret scope and hands the CLI a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, SOGNI_API_KEY and, if set, NODE_OPTIONS, NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, XDG_CACHE_HOME), so no other Hermes provider keys reach it, and it presents an honest custom User-Agent because Cloudflare (Error 1010) rejects library-default ones. Generation is billed to your Sogni account per job with no Hermes approval prompt, and the plugin reports the model used but enforces no budget cap, so an unattended run can spend your balance. Generated media is written under $HERMES_HOME/cache/images/. No telemetry, no stored credentials, no background processes beyond the CLI call, no self-updates. This plugin requires env var(s): SOGNI_API_KEY, SOGNI_AGENT_BIN. Requires Hermes >=0.20.2. entries.name: sol-pi
entries.description: Two mechanisms ported from NVIDIA's SoL-Pi (NVlabs/SoL-Pi, MIT). ObservationPack: a tool result over 10 KiB goes to the model in full twice, and after that the outgoing request carries a stable placeholder (id, size, 1 KiB head/tail excerpt) that the model pages back with obs_recall. The stored transcript keeps every byte, and the placeholder is byte-identical on every later request, including after a restart. Action Fusion: sol_pi_write / sol_pi_patch run Hermes' own write_file / patch, and with then_run also one follow-up command through Hermes' terminal tool, so an edit and its check take one model turn. Both are off until enabled in sol-pi.json in the Hermes home. Disclosure — rewrites only the per-call provider request copy through llm_request middleware (no context engine, no core patching). Writes archived tool results and an append-only ledger.jsonl under <hermes home>/sol-pi/<session>/ (0700/0600). Reads sol-pi.json in the Hermes home. sol_pi_write / sol_pi_patch are registered only when actionFusion is on. Fused edits and then_run run through Hermes' write_file / patch / terminal in the calling task/session; dangerous-command approval and the write denylist apply, but nested dispatch currently skips ACP/Zed edit approval, /rollback checkpoints and other plugins' pre_tool_call guards. No host-side reads of edited files. No network calls, telemetry or credentials.

entries.name: solana-token-facts
entries.description: Verifiable on-chain facts about Solana tokens and their developers: mint/freeze authority, supply, Token-2022 risky extensions, whether name/symbol/image can still change, top holders and concentration, wallets that bought in the creation block, creation time, creator wallet and launchpad, who funded the dev wallet, a developer's past launches (graduated, dev sold out, minutes to sell out) and the newest pump.fun -> PumpSwap graduations. Adds 8 tools, a /token fact-sheet command, a due-diligence skill and an opt-in automation blueprint that saves dev reports for new graduations. Facts only: no verdicts, no trading advice, no transactions, no wallet keys. Disclosure: makes outbound HTTPS JSON-RPC calls only to the user's configured Solana RPC (default https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com; token_holders, dev_launches, launch_buyers, dev_funding and recent_graduations need a provider such as Helius); an optional private RPC URL is a type: secret read with get_secret; writes local Markdown files only when save_dev_report runs (folder set by reports_dir); no background processes of its own, no telemetry.
