entries.name: soldgraph
entries.description: Check what items sold for on eBay, Poshmark and Mercari, and search live resale listings on Depop, Whatnot, OfferUp, Facebook Marketplace, Vinted and TCGplayer. Portable Agent Plugin with one skill and Soldgraph's hosted MCP server (19 read-only tools). Disclosure — tool calls go to api.soldgraph.com with the user's own Soldgraph API key (SOLDGRAPH_KEY, sent as a bearer header), and the tool set is served by that remote server and is not covered by the pinned sha; each completed search uses 1 request from the user's Soldgraph allowance; listing text comes from marketplace sellers and is untrusted.

entries.name: solverforge-planner
entries.description: Plans your tasks into your week around your meetings, deadlines, task order and focus hours with a SolverForge constraint solver, and proves every hard rule holds before anything is written. The planner keeps its own local calendar (SQLite plus a planner.ics you can subscribe to); Hermes pulls your cloud calendar and pushes the plan with the calendar tool you already use, and the planner only ever creates, moves or deletes its own events, each with a fixed ID so a repeated push adds nothing. Applying a plan and unscheduling a task ask for your approval. Desktop: a plan card in chat, a Planner pane docked beside the chat (week view and tasks) that opens on the week of a pending proposal, and a status-bar chip that shows and hides it. Disclosure — `hermes solverforge-planner install` (or /planner install, or the Desktop Install engine button) downloads one engine binary for your platform from this repository's own engine-v0.1.0 GitHub release, built by its release workflow with a GitHub build attestation, and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches the value pinned in engine_bin.py; the agent cannot start that download. Each solve runs that binary once as a subprocess (JSON on stdin and stdout, stopped at solve_timeout, no network). planner_busy_from_ics fetches an https/http/webcal iCalendar link (up to 10 MB) or reads a local .ics file, only the one you name. All data stays in <hermes home>/plugin-data/solverforge-planner/; no credentials are read or stored, no cloud calendar is touched by the plugin itself, no telemetry, no background process; an optional Morning plan automation blueprint runs only if you schedule it, and never applies.

entries.name: solverforge-routing
entries.description: Personal multi-stop driving trips: tell Hermes where you need to go, review the places it finds, and a SolverForge constraint solver orders the stops on OpenStreetMap roads. Change plans in the conversation (skip a stop, choose the first visit, add a place, finish elsewhere) and the trip is repaired, keeping visited stops, the next stop and before rules; an older solve never overwrites a newer edit, and results are labelled best-found, not proven optimal. Desktop: the road map beside the chat, a route card, a status-bar chip, Google Maps, Apple Maps and OpenStreetMap links, and one QR code at a time for the phone. Disclosure — `hermes solverforge-routing install` (or /routing install) downloads one engine binary for your platform from this repository's own engine-v0.2.4 GitHub release, built by its release workflow with a GitHub build attestation, and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches the value pinned in engine_bin.py; the agent cannot start that download. Place searches the user asks for send the query and region to Nominatim (configurable with geocoder_url). The first solve in a new area sends a bounding box to Overpass to download OpenStreetMap roads (a trip inside an area already downloaded reuses it); each solve then runs the engine once as a subprocess (JSON on stdin and stdout) with only the environment it needs (proxy and CA certificate settings), so no API keys or tokens reach it. The map pane loads OpenStreetMap tiles, which reveal the visible area and your IP to the tile servers. Opening a navigation link or scanning its QR code sends the stop coordinates to that provider. The route database, road cache and engine stay in <hermes home>/plugin-data/solverforge-routing/; a geocoder pacing lock file (a timestamp only, shared by all profiles) is kept in ~/.cache/hermes-solverforge-routing/. No credentials, no location tracking, no telemetry, no background process.

entries.name: soul-finder
entries.description: Build or fix your agent's SOUL.md — the personality file behind every reply. A few plain questions draft one from scratch; /soul audits a stale one and ships a diff. Disclosure — reads $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md and writes it only through the agent's own file tools after you approve the draft (the bundled skill can suggest copying the approved file into other profiles' SOUL.md, again only on approval); on a profile with no real SOUL.md it makes a one-time offer through a system-prompt section and an injected first-run message, and writes two booleans (nudge_sent, flow_complete) to its own plugin-data state so the offer happens once. No network I/O, no credentials.

entries.name: sourcebind
entries.description: Bind one explicit business job to its current local JSON customer ID at one selected native tool's execution boundary. Default mode checks job and customer_id arguments; opt-in ID-only mode checks customer_id for registered customer-only tools while retaining the source-job and native-scope checks. Both modes reread the selected source for each protected call and retain the originating scope through public delegation and compaction events. Disclosure — reads the user-selected local JSON with the process's OS permissions; stores the binding, check mode, absolute source path, native scope aliases and fictional demo records in profile-scoped Hermes plugin state. Source-file writers can change authoritative values. Plugin-initiated network requests, shell commands, background processes, telemetry and credentials: 0.

entries.name: sovereign-finance
entries.description: A self-custodial Smart Agentic Wallet for your agent on BNB Chain and Ethereum, with a Desktop pane. Your passkey is the admin, and the agent's session key is limited onchain to the contracts, functions and daily caps you approve. Powered by Altana. Disclosure — Crypto wallet plugin: the agent signs BNB Chain/Ethereum swaps and liquidity actions with a session key stored in plugin-data; every sovereign_execute call asks for Hermes approval (an "always" answer covers one pool or swap direction for that session key), but YOLO mode, approvals.mode off or approvals.cron_mode approve skip the prompt, and anything that reads the session key file (including the agent's own shell) can sign within the onchain contract/function/daily-cap limits without asking, because those limits do not pin recipients. Signed batches go to the Altana relay; it also talks to publicnode RPCs, DexScreener and skills.altana.network, runs a bundled Node CLI, and serves a localhost-only passkey page during admin actions. Its pre_tool_call guard refuses other tools' calls that mention its files, admin routes or the Hermes gateway socket.
entries.title: Sovereign Finance
known_issues: The session scope limits contracts, functions and daily amounts. Recipients are set by the plugin before signing, so keep the session key file private.
YOLO mode, approvals.mode off and approvals.cron_mode approve skip the approval prompt. The onchain limits still apply.
Verified on BNB Chain, BNB testnet and Sepolia. Ethereum mainnet activation is not verified: start on BNB Chain.
Works best with a capable model. A small model may not find the plugin's tools unless the request names one.

entries.name: spacewise
entries.description: Free up space without the fear of losing what matters. Scans one folder you name for exact duplicates (one copy always stays), leftover .dmg/.pkg installers, similar photos (the sharpest stays) and blurry or near-black photos, and reports large videos, screenshots and other large files without ever proposing them. A local preview page shows what would stay and what would go; only categories you approve move to the Trash of the same disk, and spacewise_undo puts them back. Disclosure — reads image, video and installer files (and the name, size and date of other files) only in a folder you name inside your home folder or on an external drive; refuses the operating system, disk roots, the whole home folder, other users' and shared folders, ~/Library and ~/Applications, hidden and locked items, unreadable folders, symlinks, and app-managed libraries (Photos, Lightroom, Final Cut, iMovie, Music, apps, Time Machine); skips cloud placeholders without opening them. spacewise_trash takes only a scan id and categories (never file paths) and is escalated by its own pre_tool_call hook to Hermes' human-approval gate, so it follows the user's approval settings (YOLO, approvals off or approvals.cron_mode can let it through; with no human present it fails closed); each request gets a one-time rule key. Moves are same-disk renames into ~/.Trash or <drive>/.Trashes/<uid> (freedesktop Trash on Linux), never copies or deletions; files changed since the scan, hard-linked files and RAW+JPEG pairs are left alone. Stores per-file measurements and SHA-256 hashes, recent scans, Trash batches, reports and preview thumbnails in its plugin data folder. Sends to the model provider, as part of the conversation, the scanned folder, counts, sizes and names of listed photos, videos and installers; names of other large files stay in the local report. No network calls, model calls, shell commands or telemetry; no process-wide settings changed. Windows: scan and report only.

entries.description: One Kanban wall for every Hermes session, across every profile: Needs you, Running, Idle, Done (24h) and Failed columns, one card per session. entries.name: spendwarden
entries.description: A spend policy firewall and local ledger for Hermes agents that can move money. A pre_tool_call hook checks payment-shaped tool calls against daily, monthly and per-call USD caps, recipient/asset/network allowlists and an approval threshold; in enforce mode it blocks hard violations and escalates uncertain ones to Hermes's own approval gate. Four tools add spend_check, idempotent spend_record receipts, spend_report totals, and x402_inspect (decodes PAYMENT-REQUIRED / X-PAYMENT without signing). State is a local SQLite ledger under the plugin data directory; no network calls, no credentials, no key handling, no transaction signing. Observe mode logs only; enforce mode is opt-in. Terminal recognition covers cast send, solana transfer, bitcoin-cli sendtoaddress, near call --deposit and curl with X-PAYMENT. Disclosure — detection is best-effort: it recognises payment-shaped calls by tool-name patterns, common amount/recipient argument names and five terminal command shapes (cast send, solana transfer, bitcoin-cli sendtoaddress, near call --deposit, curl with X-PAYMENT), so payments made any other way pass unchecked; the default observe mode only logs, nothing is blocked or sent for approval until you set mode: enforce, and a policy-check error lets the call through unless fail_closed is on; it does not replace wallet-side spending limits.

entries.name: sql-dryrun
entries.description: Shows how many rows a DELETE/UPDATE/DROP/TRUNCATE will touch before it runs, and sends it to Hermes' approval prompt when it is too many. Built-in approval matches command shape only, so UPDATE with no WHERE, DELETE ... WHERE 1=1, a WHERE that matches every row, and DELETE FROM t; SELECT ... WHERE ... all run unprompted; sql-dryrun flags them with the real count ("228,789 of 250,000 rows"). Covers sqlite3, psql and mysql/mariadb (inline -c/-e, heredoc, piped), execute_code, and tools passing SQL in a sql/query/statement argument. Settings: row_threshold (default 100), mode approve|block, count timeout. Adds a sql_impact tool for dry-running a statement and a /sql-dryrun command. Tested on SQLite, Postgres and MariaDB. MIT licensed. Disclosure — reads the arguments of terminal, execute_code and tools with a sql/query/statement argument. For a destructive statement whose database it can reach, it runs read-only SELECT COUNT(*) queries: SQLite in-process (mode=ro, trusted_schema=OFF); Postgres/MySQL only via a bare psql/mysql/mariadb resolved with shutil.which() and never from inside the working tree, with a minimal env (PATH/HOME/LANG/LC_*/TZ plus PG* except PGOPTIONS, or MYSQL_PWD/HOST/TCP_PORT/UNIX_PORT) and allowlisted connection flags only (options= in a conninfo/URI, any other flag including --defaults-file, or a password prompt skips the count; mysql always runs with --no-defaults). A statement containing ';' or a backslash is never sent to a database and goes to approval uncounted. Because the WHERE runs before approval, it is only counted when it is a plain predicate (comparisons, AND/OR, IN/EXISTS subqueries, an allowlist of pure built-in functions); any other function call, INTO, FOR UPDATE, '$' or a comment marker skips the count. Postgres runs BEGIN READ ONLY and verifies SHOW transaction_read_only before counting; MySQL runs inside START TRANSACTION READ ONLY ... ROLLBACK; both with a timeout and no password prompt. entries.name: ss33
entries.description: Find and install agent skills from the ss33 Skill Store without leaving Hermes. The agent searches the store with the ss33_search tool, ranked for your project's stack; /ss33:add reviews a skill and installs it into .agents/skills with a lockfile, /ss33:update and /ss33:list keep installed skills current, and opt-in prompt matching suggests a skill when a prompt needs one. Disclosure — sends search queries plus a short project summary (language, package manager and framework names with versions from manifests; never source code or file contents) to the ss33 Skill Store at mcp.ss33.ai, and, only if you turn prompt matching on with /ss33:setup, each prompt from a project session (truncated to 600 characters); runs its bundled CLI (lib/ss33.cjs) as a subprocess with Hermes's own Node.js, or with Node.js 22+ on PATH, and otherwise downloads the official Node.js v24.22.2 build from nodejs.org once (about 30 MB, checked against a SHA-256 pinned in scripts/ss33, cached in ~/.cache/ss33/runtime) in a background process started at session start; never replaces its own files; /ss33:add and /ss33:update write skill files into the project's .agents/skills and ss33.lock after showing you the skill; an optional API key from the plugin's settings is copied to ~/.config/ss33/config.json (mode 0600) so the /ss33:* commands can use it; no telemetry.

entries.name: stablelens
entries.description: Read-only tools for Arc Network, the stablecoin-native L1 where USDC is the gas token: native USDC and Circle token balances (USDC, EURC, USYC, cirBTC, WETH, plus any ERC-20) read at one block, transaction status with the USDC fee and decoded ERC-20 transfers, the current cost of a transfer, and token, address and block lookups, on mainnet (chain 5042) and testnet (5042002). Standard library only; never signs, sends or holds keys. entries.description: Publish what Hermes builds (reports, dashboards, briefs, proposals) to a private link that opens in any browser with no account for the viewer, set a passcode or limit it to a company's email addresses, update it in place, and see who opened it and what they commented. entries.name: stagehands

entries.name: standing-orders
entries.description: Plain-English camera triggers that wake your agent. Say "tell me if I leave my mug on the desk for 10 seconds"; the camera stays silent until it is true, then Hermes starts a turn with a short clip as evidence. macOS only; not a safety or security system. Disclosure — Runs a gateway platform that opens the macOS webcam in a background thread only while at least one order is armed (1–2 frames per second), or whenever the gateway runs if you turn on `record_when_idle`; keeps a rolling local recording of those periods (60 min / 2 GB, deleted when the last order is disarmed) plus event clips (kept until `hermes orders purge`) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/standing-orders; frame crops and one reference frame per new order are sent to your configured Hermes model through ctx.llm; armed orders start Hermes turns unattended with camera-derived text, and those turns get all core tools unless `platform_toolsets.standing_orders` is set.

entries.name: starlearner-nexus
entries.description: Turn the repositories you star on GitHub into a living library of registered Hermes skills. `starlearner_sync` runs the whole pipeline — fetch, map (the LLM curation pass), categorize into a fixed set of domains, two-track assess (integrate-into-your-makeup and business-opportunity), generate, register (`starlearner-nexus:<name>`) — incrementally via a persistent seen-ledger (a repo is never processed twice); `starlearner_status` is read-only state (including token set / not set); `starlearner_review` surfaces everything LLM-shaped item by item for the human. The map / categorize / assess stages optionally run through the host LLM (`ctx.llm`, one registered auxiliary task) with a deterministic rules engine as the bit-for-bit fallback (`enrich: rules` = zero LLM calls); generate is never the LLM. Registration is opt-in (`register_generated_skills`, off by default): generation writes the skills and lists them for `starlearner_review`; switching registration on registers them. When it is on, registration timing is handler-time `register_skill`, accepted and live in the same session (a skill view on a name the sync just returned resolves the same second); a plugin reload re-registers everything generated before it. Disclosure — contacts api.github.com only (GET /user/starred, HTTPS, paginated with a hard page cap), authenticated with your own read-only GitHub token read through Hermes's secret scope and never written to the plugin's files, logs or results; LLM enrichment (on by default; `enrich: rules` turns it off) sends public repo metadata (name, description, topics, language, stars) to your active provider through Hermes (`ctx.llm`, auxiliary task starlearner_enricher); every new starred repo becomes a generated skill whose description and body carry that repo's own third-party description text, so text written by the repo's author appears in your skills index and in skills the agent loads; writes only to its own plugin-data store; no shell commands, no subprocesses, no telemetry; the bundled "StarLearner-Nexus sync" automation blueprint runs only if you schedule it. Origin of the reapx lineage (same owner).

entries.name: stash
entries.description: A capture bin for the Desktop sidebar: paste links, YouTube urls, image urls, uploaded images or plain notes and they wait there, out of the chat. One item per line, so a block of links becomes several items; titles and thumbnails are filled in server-side, so capture costs no model calls. Each row carries a Chat button that opens a new session with that item as the opening message. Adds stash_add, stash_list and stash_update, so the agent reads and empties the same store the page writes. Disclosure — saving an item issues one GET to that url from the Hermes host (4 s timeout, 400 KB cap) to read its <title> and og: metadata, refused for loopback, link-local, private and reserved targets and re-checked on every redirect hop; YouTube urls also use www.youtube.com/oembed and i.ytimg.com thumbnails, and the Desktop page loads each item's og:image thumbnail directly from whatever host the page names. No credentials, no telemetry, no shell commands, no Python dependencies beyond the FastAPI Hermes already ships. Items are plain JSON at ~/.hermes/stash/items.json (shared by every profile) and uploads (max 8 MB) in ~/.hermes/stash/media/.
entries.title: Stash
known_issues: The desktop half ships switched off: after `hermes plugins enable stash`, restart the app and enable Stash under Capabilities → Plugins.
Install it on the machine that runs the desktop app; a copy installed only on a remote backend never reaches the sidebar.

entries.name: statejar
entries.description: Verifiable memory for Hermes Agent (memory.provider statejar): typed facts with one value per field, append-only content-addressed versions, recall of only what a message needs with the handle of the state it came from, and an audit trail of every disclosure. Disclosure — the user's current message (first 2,000 characters) is sent to api.statejar.com as a recall query on every turn, and the user's own messages (three words or more), every entry Hermes's built-in memory tool saves, and the text or query the agent passes to the statejar_* tools are sent there with STATEJAR_API_KEY; assistant replies and tool output are not captured, and API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords and card numbers are removed locally first (best effort). StateJar's server sends each captured message to a cloud model provider it uses for extraction (today Google Gemini and OpenRouter). entries.name: stats
entries.description: A usage dashboard for Hermes in the style of Oh My Pi's `omp stats`: overview, models, providers, costs, requests, errors, traces, tools, frustration and projects across every profile, plus a Calls page for z0live voice traces and a What to change page whose findings name the config key to change and the estimated impact. `hermes stats serve` runs it on 127.0.0.1, `hermes stats snapshot FILE` writes one offline HTML page, and `/stats [24h|7d|30d|90d|all]` answers in chat without a model call. Optional summaries and questions run on your auxiliary model (task stats_insights) only when you ask; every number in the model's text is checked against its input and the text is dropped if a check fails. Disclosure — reads every Hermes profile's state.db (from any profile, including through the /stats chat command) and, if present, ~/.local/share/z0live/voice-traces, read-only, and selects only ids, timestamps, session source, working-folder names, model and provider names, token counts, costs, tool names and error kinds, never message text; summaries and questions send only those aggregates and findings to your auxiliary model, and only when you ask; the dashboard server binds 127.0.0.1, rejects other Host headers and has no login, so other programs on this machine can read it while it runs; no telemetry, no credentials read. GPL-3.0-only; the dashboard client is forked from Oh My Pi (MIT).

entries.name: stave
entries.description: Describe a piece of music and Hermes writes it as sheet music in Hermes Desktop: it plans the form, writes every bar in ABC notation, checks bar lengths, instrument ranges, guitar chord shapes and syntax and repairs what fails, then engraves the score. Playback lights each note as it sounds, guitar parts get TAB, and you change any bars you select by asking in words, with undo. Exports PDF, SVG, MIDI, WAV and ABC. Two agent tools (stave_check, stave_open) and the stave:compose skill let any chat compose and open pieces on the page. Disclosure — the page makes one stateless llm.oneshot call per step through its own Stave composer auxiliary task (Settings › Models; reasoning off by default) and creates no sessions; playback downloads FluidR3 GM instrument samples from paulrosen.github.io/midi-js-soundfonts the first time each instrument plays; stave_open writes one JSON file per piece to plugin-data/stave/inbox, which the page reads through the plugin's dashboard route and deletes; pieces and undo history live in Desktop plugin storage; files are written only when the user exports; no shell commands, no processes of its own, no telemetry.

entries.name: stepup
entries.description: Authenticator-app 2FA for your agent: on messaging platforms the protected tools (terminal and execute_code by default) stay locked until the sender sends a one-time TOTP code from an authenticator app, so an unlocked phone is not a remote shell. One valid code unlocks that sender for 10 minutes, each code works once, five wrong codes lock the sender out for 15 minutes, and `lock` re-locks at once. Local CLI, Desktop and cron runs are never gated, and nothing waits for input. Disclosure — pre_tool_call may block a protected tool call (never modifies arguments, never approves, never touches the approval system); post_gateway_admission reads the text of admitted gateway messages and consumes only a six-digit code sent while a lock is pending, `unlock <code>` and `lock`, so codes never reach the model; pre_llm_call only records which platform and sender a session belongs to and injects nothing; holds one secret, STEPUP_TOTP_SECRET, read through Hermes's secret scope and never written to state or logs; stores unlock expiries, failure counts and the last used code counter in plugin state; no network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry, no dependencies, no self-update. Not a sandbox: tools outside protected_tools keep their normal reach.

entries.name: steward
entries.description: Your chief of staff in the team chat. entries.description: Work on the embroidery design open in Stitch Slop, watch it in a pane, and digitize artwork into machine stitch files. entries.name: stmp
entries.description: Use a phone as the trust boundary: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, contacts, notifications, a credential vault and SSH over STMP — every gated call waits for a human on the device, and no credential is ever stored on the host. Disclosure — needs the STMP Android app (public repository, Apache-2.0, APK on its releases page) reachable from the Hermes host over LAN or tailnet, so it does nothing without a paired phone; acts on that phone's signed-in Google account (sends mail, writes calendar events, uploads and downloads Drive files — a download writes only inside the configured download_dir and an upload reads only inside upload_dir or outside the credential stores, since the model names those paths and the settings bound them) and runs SSH commands through private keys stored on the device, which never leave it; stores nothing at rest beyond the connected instance's capability snapshot (contract version, plugin and route counts, SSH connection names) in Hermes's own plugin state, rewritten only on change; two routes are gate-exempt by design and say so in their tool descriptions — POST /tts and POST /audio/{cue} play sound only; every other route goes through the phone's approval gate, whose per-route mode (WHITELIST, PARANOID or DONT_DISTURB) is the device owner's policy, not the plugin's; declares and reads no credential (requires_env is empty, no oauth block), no telemetry, no self-updater, and talks to exactly one address: the configured base_url.

entries.name: stoa
entries.description: The CRM for Hermes Agent, a lightweight one you talk to: map a market, find the leads, run the pipeline, see it through to cash, and read it back in reports Stoa counts itself. Hermes runs it and you approve: what it finds waits for your yes or no, and every change can be taken back. Optional paid lookups and network calls happen only with your own keys; the README's Disclosure section lists everything it reads, writes and sends. Disclosure — optional network calls to api.peopledatalabs.com (paid per result, capped), api.exa.ai, public-api.granola.ai and api.fireflies.ai only when their keys are set (from Granola and Fireflies it reads summaries, never a transcript); dictation on the page is the browser's own speech recognition (in Chrome, Google's service) and runs only while its button is on; reads call notes (Markdown, text, Word, subtitle and web-page files) in the notes folders you name and up to three folders below them, handing a PDF there to the agent to read; a connector of Hermes's own that you name as holding notes is read by the agent with that connector's tools, never by the plugin; reads .csv and .tsv files in its imports folder, a folder you name or the working directory, and a file you drop on the page; writes only inside its own data folder, including daily backup copies of each pipeline, and deletes outside it only Hermes's own copy of a file you dropped in its talk box (in the profile's attachments or images folder), seven days after it was dropped or the days you set, or when you press Remove under Setup: never a file from another chat; scheduled jobs reach the desk only when you add cron to its channels setting, and then change only what its autonomy setting allows (by default they only log what they find and leave every other change waiting for your approval; "Run it" lets them make any change); the automations offered under /blueprint run only when you switch them on, and the Google Sheet ones use your own Google connection in Hermes; invoices and payments are records kept on the desk, never sent or charged; a Slack button works only for the person a card was posted for or the people listed in slack_users; with allow_gateway_injection a button click queues one agent turn in the thread; the page's dock, and the market map's research, each send what you type or press to a visible conversation of their own, on the model you pick for it from Hermes's own list; two hooks (post_api_request, post_llm_call) count the model calls, tokens and Hermes's estimated cost of turns that work on a market map, counts only, with no prompt or reply read or kept; a file you drop on the page's talk box (other than a CSV, which the desk reads itself) is handed to Hermes with your next message through the gateway's own attach calls, as the app's chat box does, and Hermes keeps a copy of it until Stoa removes it as said above; reports are counted by the plugin from its own database with no model, and only when you press Ask Hermes about a report, or ask in a chat, do its figures (counts and totals, no list of people) go to the model; pressing Test beside a key makes one small request to that key's service; Look for a folder checks a few usual folders for notes when pressed, counting files and opening none. Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon entry.

entries.name: storage-utility
entries.description: Keep Hermes fast, healthy and tidy from one Desktop panel. Clean up sorts the Hermes home into Safe to clean, Take a quick look and Kept safe on purpose, with plain-language answers to what is it, is it safe and can I undo; it reviews exact items before anything happens and reports the measured space recovered. It runs the maintenance Hermes ships but few people find (sessions prune with preview, pm gc, uv cache prune, checkpoints, worktree prune, session-database packing), finds folders Hermes created elsewhere from its own session history, and moves reviewable items to a restorable 30-day Trash. Checkup explains down or crash-looping Hermes services and stops leftover agent processes; Explore shows a size map with folder descriptions and duplicate finding; optional consented AI explanation via its own auxiliary task. Disclosure — Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd); no network except an optional, consented AI explanation (folder totals and counts only) through Hermes's routing; reads home metadata, tool caches, session history, /proc process and open-file info, systemd unit settings, journal lines, crontab and git ls-files; on macOS instead the process table via psutil, Hermes's own processes.json and spawn ledger, Hermes LaunchAgent plists (label, program, KeepAlive, log path, HERMES_HOME/HOME only), the settings of every LaunchAgent and LaunchDaemon plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchDaemons without their environment entries (to see whether a job starts something from a project folder, kept local), launchctl print/list/print-disabled (state, PID, run count, last exit code only) and the last lines of a service's error log inside <Hermes home>/logs (never .env, auth.json, env files, start scripts, any other process's environment or other launchd environment entries); on user confirmation it permanently deletes chosen files in Hermes-created project folders and ~/.cache, ~/.npm and ~/.pnpm-store tool caches, moves other items to a restorable 30-day Trash, runs allow-listed hermes/uv/pnpm/git maintenance plus journalctl --vacuum-size and apt-get clean when root, starts/restarts/stops/disables Hermes systemd services or (macOS) starts/restarts Hermes LaunchAgents and boots out + disables a crash-looping one (plist kept), can write a Restart=always drop-in (Linux) and enable the disk-cleanup plugin, sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL if it does not exit) to selected leftover processes, and briefly stops Hermes services to pack state.db (Linux; on macOS it shows the manual steps instead); non-Hermes child processes get only PATH, HOME and locale.
entries.title: Tune-up
known_issues: Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd) are tested; Windows is not supported yet. On macOS, Pack now shows manual steps instead of pausing Hermes, and files in project folders outside the Hermes home are listed but not offered for cleanup (macOS cannot show every open folder).

entries.name: strategic-arena
entries.description: Understand the landscape before you invest: give it a link and get the room that reacts — who can block adoption, what each concession buys, and the claims you can score later. Research papers also get a replication clock. Disclosure — sends the documents you give it and the simulation prompts to your active Hermes model via ctx.llm; fetches URLs you or the model supply (http/https, public addresses only, re-checked on every redirect); reads the public Nous model catalog (inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/models, anonymous, cached 6h) to price runs; runs simulations in a background thread; writes run history and exported decision records only under plugin-data/strategic-arena; adds a Desktop page and dashboard API routes.
entries.title: Strategic Arena
known_issues: A run uses the model your Hermes default model setting is on; there is no model picker by design.

Free models are supported but rate-limited: a large input (a research paper, a long technical post) can run several times slower and may be interrupted. A paid model is recommended for those. If a run fails on a rate limit, change the model in the app and run it again.
The desktop UI loads from the machine running the app, so a UI change needs Install from Git with the Desktop target on that machine.
PDFs outside arXiv need a text layer; a link that cannot be read is reported as SKIPPED in the run's provenance, never silently dropped.

entries.name: strunk
entries.description: Document review in Google Docs: publish a draft to Google Docs for review, pull reviewer comments back with the spans they anchor to, revise the doc in place, and reply to and resolve each thread. Existing comments and anchors survive a re-publish. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json) with Strunk's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP; OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE) and two skills, one for setup and one for the review round trip. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to strunk.io with the drafts you publish, and returns reviewers' comments and names, which also reach your model provider through the session. Google access uses the drive.file scope, limited to docs Strunk creates and files you pick. Write tools create and edit Google Docs and reply to and resolve comment threads under your Google account. The package marks the server untrusted so write tools ask first, but the sign-in step (`hermes mcp add strunk`) writes a config.yaml entry that replaces the package's own, trust included, unless you add `trust: untrusted` to it. Hermes stores and refreshes the Strunk OAuth token; WorkOS holds the Google refresh token on Strunk's side. The tool list comes from Strunk's server at run time, so the pinned commit does not cover it.
entries.title: Strunk
known_issues: Sign in once: hermes mcp add strunk --url https://strunk.io/mcp --auth oauth, then add `trust: untrusted` under `mcp_servers.strunk` in config.yaml to keep the approval prompt
The first publish or open asks you to connect Google Docs in your browser

entries.name: study-tree
entries.description: Study with the agent without losing the thread: a side question you ask becomes its own branched session, the side threads show as a tree in a Desktop pane, and each one hands one recall-checked takeaway back to the thread it came from. The agent can also draw interactive widgets and one-question quizzes inline, with follow-up buttons. Disclosure: stores its tree in SQLite and agent-written HTML widgets under the active profile's plugin-data/study-tree/ (a widget over 200 KB or with any network reference is refused; Desktop shows it in its sandboxed preview frame); opens Hermes' state.db read-only to follow compression lineage; adds a short section to every session's system prompt, and through pre_llm_call injects a side-thread frame on each side-thread turn and each takeaway once into the parent's next turn; through transform_llm_output rewrites the final reply (study cards moved to the end as their own paragraphs, cards with unknown ids dropped, widget directives put on their own paragraphs, a widget button's prompt quoted at the top); creates a branched session (session.branch or session.branch_stored), renames it with session.title and sends the side question as its first prompt only when the user clicks Open; the Desktop half keeps the last text selected in the window in memory for 60 seconds to prefill the side-question dialog, and writes the glossary to the clipboard only when the user clicks Export glossary. No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.
entries.title: Study Tree
known_issues: The cards, the pane and the widgets need Hermes Desktop. On the CLI, the TUI and messaging platforms a card shows as a plain ::study-tree-node line and a widget as a plain ::preview line.
The Desktop half is off by default: turn on Study Tree under Capabilities → Plugins after installing.
Widgets in the pane are view-only; their follow-up buttons work in the chat.

entries.name: styx
entries.description: Password-gated Tor onion access to the local Hermes webapp or dashboard. Disclosure — when you start it, Styx publishes your Hermes web UI (which can run commands on this machine) as a Tor onion service: anyone with the onion address and your Styx passphrase gets a full Hermes session. Starting it turns on webapp.enabled in config.yaml, builds the webapp, and may restart the Hermes gateway (interrupting running turns); setup can install Tor through your system package manager after you confirm. The optional Styx Fast chat page, off unless you choose it, uses the same Hermes sign-in and sends chats, files and (only when you allow the microphone) voice recordings to this Hermes instance.

entries.name: submission-desk
entries.description: Readiness ledger for one application (a grant, a scholarship, a university or a job portal). Each requirement you confirm is tied to a verbatim quote from your saved instructions, the exact portal field label and the exact file revision (SHA-256). Local checks run on those bytes (real format, exact size, PDF pages, word counts) and say unknown instead of guessing; a changed file, rule or mapping makes earlier reviews stale. The agent proposes; only you confirm, review and attest, on a Desktop page or with /submission-desk. Exports a hand-back checklist and manifest. It never logs in, uploads, signs or submits. Disclosure: reads files only inside the application folder you choose (a folder the agent proposes is read only after you confirm it); never writes your files; parses PDFs with pypdf in a short-lived child process with CPU, memory and time limits; keeps its ledger and exports in the plugin's own data folder. No network calls, telemetry, credentials, shell commands or background processes.

entries.name: subnano
entries.description: Subnano's local MCP server for the pay-per-post marketplace. Search and read Posts, buy access in Nano (XNO) or USDC on Base, draft and publish Posts, answer comments and Requests, and receive payouts. Bundles seven workflow skills and one CLI skill. Optional task profiles reduce tool discovery; they do not narrow the underlying account credential. Disclosure — spends real money. Native agent installations act within their own account without approval prompts, including paid publication, scheduling, unpublishing and deleting their own drafts; money stays off until the operator sets a rolling asset/network budget and standing immediate-delivery consent bound to current legal version, hash and exact text. Operators control payout addresses, folders, budgets and regime; adding or raising a budget or turning on standing consent requires typing ALLOW SPENDING in an interactive terminal; direct Nano transfers are unavailable to agent tools. Browser signature login is an exception to account actions without prompts: a selected, verified and fully onboarded native `setup new-agent` identity requires fresh human approval of the exact website, account and `nano-signin-v1` request, even in agent mode. Approve only a request started in your own browser. The client signs locally without a Nano transfer and returns no key, signature or session credential to the agent. Proof acceptance alone does not sign the browser in. Continue in the original browser completes login. External Nano identities and delegated connections are unsupported. If the host lacks a qualified approval form, only the human may run `subnano-mcp auth browser-signin --request-url` with the copied public request URL in their own trusted terminal. The agent must never run or answer it for them. A decline or cancellation ends the attempt without another approval route. An existing Full browser connection can request linking its dedicated Base EOA as a lasting sign-in wallet. The authenticated owner must approve the exact saved five-minute request in the browser before the local client signs; this grants sign-in access that survives MCP disconnection, authorizes no payment, and never exports the key. Denial and expiry are terminal; response loss reuses the saved original intent and signature. Browser connections always use human mode with owner-selected Read, Drafts or Full server access. Human public actions follow five browser choices; paid publication/scheduling, draft deletion, payout changes and direct transfers always require exact confirmation. Native human mode has no standing choices or budget. A decline is final. An unavailable or interrupted payment confirmation keeps the original operation pending exact approval even if the rolling budget later covers it. Only a human-requested review can resume that original with fresh approval; older saved declines remain closed. Unsupported hosts receive website guidance, not another approval path. Installations without a saved regime, including new-agent installations upgrading from 0.3.58 or earlier, stay in human mode until the operator runs `permissions regime --regime agent` in a terminal; a brand-new identity created with `setup new-agent` or `first-draft` starts in agent mode with no budget, and the low-level `setup new-agent` and `first-draft` commands create it without a human confirmation step. Legacy grants remain readable/revocable with separate explicit cumulative spending. Local controls are best effort and do not isolate agents with shell/credential access. Calls subnano.ai, the configured Nano RPC, BerryPay's public work endpoint by default (public root/difficulty only), and mainnet.base.org for balance reads. Keys and sessions are stored owner-only in ~/.local/state/subnano-mcp. Connecting an existing account opens the browser and uses a short-lived loopback listener for its approval callback; that account-connection flow is separate from native agent browser signature login. Updates are host-managed through `hermes plugins update subnano`; the plugin never downloads or installs its own updates.

entries.name: sunshine-moonlight
entries.description: Set up and diagnose Moonlight game streaming (Sunshine host <-> Moonlight client) between machines that run Hermes. One tool, action-based: discover hosts on the tailnet/LAN, preflight ports, install+start Sunshine, pair clients, verify encoders, and launch a stream. Writes to remote machines only over SSH and only when the action says so. Disclosure — runs shell commands as your user on this machine and, over SSH, on hosts you name (BatchMode, your existing keys); `install` runs `sudo` with your package manager to install `sunshine` or `moonlight-qt` without a Hermes approval prompt; `configure`/`start` rewrite Sunshine's config (with a backup) and restart its user service; `discover` reads `tailscale status` and port-probes your tailnet peers; `launch` starts a Moonlight process. No credentials stored, no telemetry.

entries.name: super-agent
entries.description: Runs the Hermes chat agent like a secretary with a team of workers: keeps chat turns responsive (60s reminder, 120s edit/execute pause, 30s terminal auto-detach), briefs every subagent before it starts, stops subagents that repeat identical results, brings open decisions back to the main agent, has it ask the user after repeated failed subagents, never takes a subagent that ended without its report as done, tracks background results until they reach the user, and records every delegated task in a SQLite ledger across gateway restarts (`hermes super-agent status` shows it). Governance is a positive allowlist: only the platforms named in governed_platforms (default weixin) and the subagents they spawn are affected, and every other surface runs untouched. Disclosure — registers hooks for pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, subagent_start, subagent_stop, on_session_end, on_session_reset and on_session_finalize, a system-prompt section and a tool_execution middleware, so for governed sessions it can block or amend tool calls and results, LLM request context and subagent handoffs, and asks a governed foreground terminal command still running after 30 s to move to Hermes's background process registry (through core's internal yield flag, which a Hermes release may change); it copies your Hermes USER.md and MEMORY.md memory files in full into every governed delegate_task brief, can start an internal agent turn via inject_message to re-report an unseen subagent result, writes a local ledger.db under the plugin's Hermes data directory, and at startup reads the effective Hermes config through Hermes' own resolver to tell the main agent once about settings that weaken it (inline delegation, a high delegation.max_iterations); it also registers a read-only `hermes super-agent status` CLI command that prints its settings and the ledger's recent tasks; no network calls, no agent tools, no credentials, no shell commands.

entries.name: super-artifacts
entries.description: Publish pages, forms, trackers and proofs as live URLs that open on a phone, and read back what visitors submit, through the hosted Super Artifacts MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR), with the super-artifacts workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no code. Disclosure — hosted-only connector: every tool call goes to superartifacts.app/mcp; published artifacts and what visitors submit to them are stored on Super Artifacts' servers. Artifacts are private by default, and the skill tells the model to publish private and never widen who can open one unless the person asked; Hermes does not prompt before these tools run unless you set `trust: untrusted` on the server. No telemetry. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add super-artifacts --url https://superartifacts.app/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

entries.name: superlist
entries.description: Tasks and lists in Superlist through Superlist's official hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.superlist.com/mcp, OAuth 2.0 sign-in with the user's Superlist account, no keys in config): capture tasks with due dates, reminders, priorities, labels and repetition, plan projects as lists, read the Today and Inbox views, search, update, move, assign, complete, share lists, and read or reply to task messages. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Setup after install and enable: add an mcp_servers.superlist entry to ~/.hermes/config.yaml with url https://app.superlist.com/mcp, auth: oauth and trust: untrusted (required; hermes mcp login fails without auth: oauth, and this entry replaces the package's, trust included), then run hermes mcp login superlist. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to app.superlist.com and acts with the signed-in user's own permissions. Tools can delete and restore tasks and lists and change list sharing; share_list sends the invited person an email and a push notification. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every write-capable call. OAuth tokens are stored by Hermes, not by the plugin. The plugin sends no telemetry, but the Superlist server records each MCP call for product analytics, including the MCP client's name and version, and keeps per-tool usage metrics; this is part of the hosted service and not opt-in. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: surplus-intelligence-seller
entries.description: Sell the full daily Venice DIEM allowance on Surplus Intelligence before 00:00 UTC. Seller-only and Venice-only: lists DIEM-funded Venice inference as Surplus offers, rebalances discount and caps through the epoch, and deepens price late in the day so leftover DIEM (which does not roll over) is avoided. Earnings settle in USDC on Base. Disclosure — Venice API key is sent to Surplus Intelligence (encrypted at rest) so Surplus can proxy buyer traffic; Surplus seller API and Venice billing/rate-limit endpoints are called to manage offers and read remaining DIEM; the tools create, reprice, pause and cancel offers without an approval prompt (price floor 0.10x), and if the Venice account also holds paid USD credit, buyer traffic past the DIEM can bill it unless the key's USD limit is 0; SIWE mint uses a throwaway wallet whose private key is discarded after signing, and the minted seller key is shown in the conversation.

entries.name: swarm-studio
entries.description: A whole creative studio inside Hermes. One prompt, and a crew of agents you can watch and steer builds the whole launch on a live canvas: a multi-page website, a working web app with a database, a playable game (also as a Godot, Unity or Unreal project), a promo film and the social posts. Open it from the Desktop sidebar, ask for a site in any chat (the swarm_design tool), type /swarm, or run `hermes swarm`. The crew uses the models you already set up in Hermes, through three Hermes auxiliary slots (planner, builder and reviewer, set in hermes model). Builds can be posted to Swarm Feed, where others try them live and remix them with credit. Disclosure — starts a small Node server (Node 24+ needed) that listens on 127.0.0.1 only and refuses any other Host. It runs detached, so it outlives Hermes, and exits once it has had nothing to do for 20 minutes (Settings › Background: 10, 20, 60 minutes or never), starting again on next use; after an update it replaces itself with only the environment the launcher gave it. A built app runs on its own 127.0.0.1 port, at most 2 at once, each stopped after 2 minutes nobody looks at it. Model calls (planner, builders, reviewer, and the app engine) go to Hermes through a loopback bridge with a per-process token and are answered with ctx.llm on the plugin's three auxiliary slots, so no provider key leaves Hermes; only when you set SWARM_STUDIO_API_KEY does the server call SWARM_STUDIO_BASE_URL itself with that key. The Studio never receives, sends or stores a model-provider key: Setup has no key field and no route accepts one; a key provider shows `hermes auth add <provider> --type api-key` for you to run in your own terminal, where Hermes asks for the key with its own hidden prompt. Browser sign-in is `hermes auth add <provider> --type oauth`, started with HERMES_HOME only; Hermes opens the browser and keeps the token, and the Studio only shows the link and code Hermes prints. The only Hermes settings it changes are the auxiliary.swarm_studio_planner and auxiliary.swarm_studio_builder slots (provider and model, never a secret) through `hermes config set`, and a test holds it to those two. Setup's model list makes one read-only import outside the public plugin API, hermes_cli.inventory (build_model_options_payload, load_picker_context), because Hermes 0.23.1 has no public way to list providers and models; it writes nothing. On a multiplexed gateway only, and only when Hermes has bound no secret scope, bridge.py binds the scope Hermes builds for the plugin's own profile around a bridge request, in a copied context (a workaround for NousResearch/hermes-agent#132887 until #132898 ships); Hermes reads the keys, the plugin never does. The one-time Setup sheet sends "Say ok" to your planner and builder slots to check they answer. Pictures go through Hermes's image_generate tool and clips through video_generate; MCP tools (e.g. Supabase) go through ctx.call_mcp, only for servers you grant in mcp_allowlist (the studio never edits it, and runs `hermes mcp install` only after you confirm). A Launch kit post to Discord, Slack or Telegram goes out through your Hermes gateway (`hermes send`) only after you confirm its exact text. Keys: the optional keys named in plugin.yaml are read by the launcher through Hermes's secret scope (get_secret) when the server starts and passed to it in its environment. Besides those, you can paste a Vercel or Cloudflare token in the Publish menu, checked with the provider and kept in $HERMES_HOME/swarm-studio/connections.json with mode 0600, or an Octo vault grant (octo_vault_…), which is not stored: connections.json keeps only a 30-day working key for that one vault item, renewed, and every call goes through Octo's relay at octodb.design-bakery.com. A pasted ElevenLabs key is kept in $HERMES_HOME/swarm-studio/media-keys.json with mode 0600. Pasted tokens never go back to the page, onto a command line or into a log. JEV_KEY, an OpenRouter key kept only for the Game room's Autoplay, is sent by the server itself to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, outside Hermes: while Autoplay runs, about once a second, with what is on the game's screen (scene, button labels, dialogue, the hero's health, enemy and object names, up to 300 characters of page text, and a game's own published state); without it the moves are scripted and nothing is sent, and your Hermes model keys are never used for it. It reads no .env file, Hermes's included, and stops the app engine from reading one. Every child process gets a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale, plus only the keys that program needs). Generated pages run in frames sandboxed with allow-scripts and no same origin with the studio. A built app's frame adds allow-forms, and only while the app is served from its own 127.0.0.1 port (an origin other than the studio's) also allow-same-origin, for its own sign-in and storage, and allow-popups; never allow-modals or top navigation. Design-system previews are allow-scripts only, and /site/ and the live video pages are served with a sandbox allow-scripts CSP. Bring in a project copies a folder from your home folder, or fetches a GitHub repository's newest commit with your own git and gh login: files only, at most 200 MB and 20,000 files, never node_modules, .git, build output or .env files, and nothing of it runs. A Vite project is installed, built and started only after you say "install and run it" for that project; it installs with pnpm --ignore-scripts --ignore-pnpmfile, and the app engine's installs for it with the same settings, until you say "run its install scripts" for that one project. A pulled version asks again, no Hermes tool can give either yes, and its install, build and servers get none of your keys. A project's source can be pushed to and pulled from GitHub with your own gh login (gh repo create, private unless you pick Public; git through gh's credential helper; no token is read or kept): it never force-pushes, touches only repositories it made or you named, and refuses a push whose commits hold a key file (.env, *.pem, *.key, .npmrc and the like). When the model asks to publish, deploy, push to GitHub, post, write a project into a folder of yours, import an art pack, use a library picture or add a link or a file from your computer to a project's References, Hermes's approval prompt asks you first, and it is refused with nobody present and in a cron job. Copy the look of a site opens a public link in a headless Chrome already on your machine and walks up to three of its pages; every request it makes goes through a proxy on 127.0.0.1 for that walk only, which resolves each name itself and connects only to public unicast addresses (private, loopback, link-local, 100.64/10, multicast, reserved, cloud-metadata and IPv4-mapped addresses are refused, DNS rebinding included); that Chrome resolves no name itself, sends no WebRTC traffic outside the proxy, and HTTPS is tunnelled, not decrypted. When you ask it to look something up, press Research, or the app engine searches or reads a page, it uses Hermes's own web_search and web_extract tools (at most 3 searches and 4 pages each time, public addresses only). Casting a game's characters searches VRoid Hub (hub.vroid.com) and Sketchfab (api.sketchfab.com) with the role's search words. The canvas loads Tailwind from cdn.tailwindcss.com and fonts from Google Fonts; film pages load GSAP 3.14.2, and a section's check picture html-to-image 1.11.11, from cdn.jsdelivr.net. Publish runs your gh CLI (GitHub Pages) or calls Vercel / Cloudflare Pages with a token you connect; App deploy uploads the app's source to your Vercel. The first promo video installs hyperframes 0.9.26 (telemetry and update checks off) with npm ci --ignore-scripts from a pinned lockfile, and ffmpeg/ffprobe when not on PATH from npm at exact versions, checking the binaries' SHA-256 before running them; the first voiceover installs kokoro-js 1.2.1 the same way and its voice model from Hugging Face; the first picture it resizes installs @napi-rs/image 1.16.0 and thumbhash 0.1.1 with npm ci --ignore-scripts from a pinned lockfile. Cutting a painted sprite out of its key colour runs the plugin's own gamemaker/cut.py, which needs numpy, scipy and Pillow in the Python the Studio runs: the plugin installs none of them, Setup › Game › Sprite cutter reads which Python has them and gives you the exact command to run in your own terminal (`<python> -m pip install numpy scipy Pillow`), and without them a game's sprites keep their magenta or green background; the first app build installs the vendored dyad app engine's packages from npm (about 1.5 GB, once); pressing 'Install Godot 4' in a game plan's chat downloads the Godot 4.7.2 editor from godotengine.org's GitHub releases (about 170 MB, or Homebrew's copy on a Mac) and then Godot's own Web export templates from the same release (1.28 GB, only the 20 MB of Web templates kept), each checked against the SHA-512 that release publishes before it is opened, with the editor into $HERMES_HOME/swarm-studio/godot/ and the templates where Godot looks for them for its version, which is outside $HERMES_HOME (~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/ on a Mac, ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/ on Linux, %APPDATA% Godot export_templates on Windows); a folder that already holds those templates is left alone; while a picture is painted its slot shows a stock photo found on Openverse (and Pexels, with a key), photos from the studio's own library come from files.design-bakery.com, and game art from the assetrizz library on raw.githubusercontent.com, pinned to one commit and written only inside its own library folder; ckff, Fish Audio, ElevenLabs, Meshy, Supabase, Stripe (test keys only) and Resend are called only when you set their key; Swarm Feed (https://swarm.design-bakery.com) is contacted only when you run /swarm connect, post, remix or login. No telemetry. Bundled, with version, licence and SHA-256 beside each, nothing installed: XState 5.33.3, snapDOM 3.7.0, Mermaid 12.2.0 (the build wall's Map, served by the plugin's own server and drawn at Mermaid's strict security level), execa 9.6.1 and tree-kill 1.2.2, and ipaddr.js 2.5.0 (the site walk's address check), and unpdf 2.2.0 (reading a dropped PDF); the next UI is prebuilt in ui/dist. It writes under $HERMES_HOME/swarm-studio/, and also: films to ~/Movies (or ~/Videos) and exports to ~/Documents, each in a Swarm Studio folder (or SWARM_OUTPUT_DIR); the app engine's packages and bundle in the plugin's own dyad/ folder; Hermes's config, only the two model slots above and an MCP server you confirm; your GitHub repositories when you push; and, when you write a project to a folder inside your home folder that you name, its files there (a git checkout gets a new branch of its own, nothing pushed; files it did not write are replaced only after you say yes).

entries.name: switch402
entries.description: switch402 web data tools: public page to markdown (full and lite), site map, page metadata, screenshots and web search, plus a free price and health quote. Disclosure — tool inputs (URLs and search queries) go to api.switch402.com, run by the switch402 team that maintains this plugin; the six paid tools spend USDC on Base ($0.001–$0.012 per call, charged only on success) from the wallet in SWITCH402_WALLET_KEY, which is used only locally to sign one x402 payment per call through Hermes' secret scope and is never sent or logged; every paid call needs a fresh human answer to the Hermes approval prompt (session/always answers do not carry over), stays under a per-request cap (max_spend_usd, default $0.02), and is refused in cron, yolo, approvals-off, smart-approval and other unattended runs; screenshots are saved under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/switch402/; no telemetry, no self-update.

This plugin registers tool(s): s402_quote, s402_scrape, s402_lite, s402_screenshot, s402_search, s402_map, s402_metadata; hook(s): pre_tool_call, post_approval_response; requires env var(s): SWITCH402_WALLET_KEY. Requires Hermes >=0.21.5.

entries.name: switchbot-control
entries.description: SwitchBot OpenAPI v1.1, personal use. The watch does not report Plug Mini on or off. A command can still turn a Plug Mini on or off. The published card sentence ("No Plug Mini on/off.") does not describe a command on this pin. Locks off unless enabled. When safety_devices is on, each lock or door command asks again. setPosition only Curtain/Curtain3 (0=open). Disclosure — Controls real devices through the SwitchBot cloud API (api.switch-bot.com) using your SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Each call reads SWITCHBOT_TOKEN and SWITCHBOT_SECRET for the active profile, and an HTTP proxy set in the environment is not used. On this pin, yolo and approvals off skip the prompt only when a person can answer. A cron job, hermes -q, and a webhook cannot send a command, even after always. Each watch run costs 0 tokens. The unmanned run holds no tools. schedule writes a script under HERMES_HOME/scripts and creates the job with hermes cron create --no-agent --script. Empty stdout sends nothing. A 0.1.x job stays a model turn until the next schedule. That turn allows switchbot_devices, switchbot_watch, tool_search, tool_describe, and tool_call, and blocks every other tool. The script drops every other profile .env key. If hermes cron fails, unschedule still removes the script and says the job was not removed. hermes cron create has no per-job tool list, which does not matter here because the unmanned run holds no tools. switchbot_command is a separate toolset. A cron turn hides it and refuses it, even after always. The published lines ("Every command asks for Hermes approval and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off and unattended sessions."), (Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml each time.), and ("The optional watch is a cron job (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule.") are not this pin. Lock and door devices stay refused unless you turn on safety_devices. When they are enabled, each of those commands asks again, so always does not cover the next one. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a command and approve it. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a toolset off per surface with hermes tools. On this pin, answering always in an interactive chat covers the same device id, command, and parameter, and it does not send from cron, hermes -q, or a webhook. The optional watch is a no-agent cron script (every 5 minutes by default, 0 tokens a run) that stays after uninstall. While the plugin is installed, remove that job with hermes switchbot-control unschedule. After uninstall that command is gone, so remove the job with hermes cron remove. Not tested on real devices. Saved files are under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/switchbot-control for the active profile. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off.

The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can request a command and approve it. Tools are on for every surface, including gateways. Turn a toolset off per surface with hermes tools. On this pin, answering always in an interactive chat covers the same device id, command, and parameter, and it does not send from cron, hermes -q, or a webhook. The optional watch is a no-agent cron script (every 5 minutes by default, 0 tokens a run) that stays after uninstall. While the plugin is installed, remove that job with hermes switchbot-control unschedule. After uninstall that command is gone, so remove the job with hermes cron remove. Not tested on real devices. Saved files are under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/switchbot-control for the active profile. While the plugin is enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session, including surfaces where the tools are turned off. This plugin registers tool(s): switchbot_devices, switchbot_command, switchbot_watch; hook(s): pre_tool_call; requires env var(s): SWITCHBOT_TOKEN, SWITCHBOT_SECRET. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.description: Live video sessions that record themselves. The agent uses a restricted server key, then checks the recording before calling the integration working. entries.name: syrinx
entries.description: Your agent is fast; Syrinx makes it wait for the right moment. In a focus block (/flow 45) the agent's questions are parked with the default it took and it keeps working; when you return you get a catch-up, a list counted by code from the tool calls (files changed, commands run, anything that left your machine, and how much work rests on unconfirmed defaults), and every question in one card. During the block a fixed list of outward actions (git push, publish, send, deploy) is held before it runs and offered back on that card. Settle a question once with /always and it is never asked again. Late-night requests become a morning brief. Deep-work hours, a question budget, a time receipt, a Desktop pane and Argus, a pet whose pose shows the state. Disclosure: pre_tool_call can block the built-in clarify tool (during a focus block, over the question budget you set, or when a standing answer covers it) and tells the agent which default to use, and during a focus block only it blocks tool calls that match a fixed list of outward actions (push, publish, gh create, curl with a body, ssh, docker push, kubectl, terraform, send/post/deploy/upload/pay tools), storing a label, never the command (a guard, not a sandbox: scripts, execute_code and browser or MCP tools still run); hold_outward: false turns that off; parked questions, held actions and queued requests are handed back only to the session that created them; pre_llm_call appends short blocks to your message (standing answers, focus notes, the hand-back, the morning brief) and, after your cutoff and only on cli, tui and desktop (or platforms you add with night_platforms), ends the turn to queue the request; post_tool_call stores tool names, file basenames and program names, never arguments, plus your answers to clarify cards; with auto_focus on (macOS, off by default) it runs ioreg and lsappinfo read-only; /syrinx pet writes the bundled sprite sheet through Hermes' pet store. No network calls of its own, approvals untouched; cron runs, subagents, the API server, kanban workers and messaging users are never refused at night.

entries.name: system-one
entries.description: Provider-neutral client for System One decision models: TypeSafe Jev, Liquid AI d1.2 / d1.2-ultra, Upstage Solar Decide, Microsoft-Decision-1 on Azure AI Foundry, open models in Ollama (Laya, Tev1) or another self-hosted server (llama.cpp), or any endpoint that implements the System One contract. One system_one tool asks typed questions (noul, choice, score, plus the extraction types a model supports) and returns calibrated probabilities; provider and model switch in settings. Each model's supported question types and limits are checked before sending, and total, daily and per-call spend caps are checked against a local ledger before every request. Bundles a skill on writing questions, adapted from TypeSafe's MIT typesafe-ai skill. Standard library only; no dependencies. Disclosure — the state and questions you send go to the selected provider (api.typesafe.ai, api.liquid.ai, api.upstage.ai, your Azure Foundry resource, your own Ollama or self-hosted server, or your https endpoint) and are billed to your account there (self-hosted is free); API keys are secret settings read through get_secret and sent only to their own provider's hosts; the spend ledger and an opt-in payload log (off by default, mode 0600) are written under plugin-data/system-one.

entries.name: tablekeeper
entries.description: Tabletop RPG campaigns for Hermes group chats. Code rolls the dice and owns hit points, positions, initiative and turn order, each player controls only their own character, and the model narrates the results. SRD 5.1 monsters, characters and spells, including a young red dragon with a fire breath cone. With `/table dice phone`, each player throws their own d20 from a Telegram button; code still rolls the number. Disclosure — Disclosure: Storage. `<hermes home>/plugin-data/tablekeeper/campaigns.sqlite3`, resolved per profile, WAL mode, file mode 0600. The Desktop pane and dashboard route open it read-only; Prompt. In a chat that has a campaign, and in a local CLI or Desktop session once it has used `/table` or a `tk_` tool, a compact state summary of at most about 600 tokens is added to each turn and the reply passes through the narration guard. The guard lets a reply quote any hit point or AC figure the state block listed or a tool returned, flags invented damage, rolls and hit points, and appends one compact correction line. A campaign with no table activity for 24 hours adds no prompt tokens until the next `tk_` call or `/table` command wakes it. Other sessions and chats without a campaign are untouched; Network and processes. The plugin opens no connection of its own, starts no subprocess and reads no credentials. With `/table dice phone` on a Telegram session it registers one callback handler scoped to `^tk:throw:<id>` and sends one button message per pending throw through the gateway's own bot; a tap is accepted only from the character's owner id; each throw result, including an automatic throw when the owner does not tap within the timeout (15-600 s, default 120), is queued into that chat as a message from the owner and starts an agent turn without anyone typing; Identity. Platform, chat id and sender id from the turn context, used as the campaign and owner keys.

entries.name: taint-sentry
entries.description: Provenance and taint tracking for tool results. Every tool result is stamped with where it came from; content authored by a third party (web fetches, MCP servers, screenshots, images, and files written from untrusted content) is stripped of invisible characters, wrapped in an <untrusted> marker, and marks the session as tainted. While a session is tainted, side-effecting tool calls are checked against a policy: credential reads, and writes into files the agent reads as instructions (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, hook handlers, Hermes' own config), are refused; network egress and writes outside the workspace go to Hermes's own approval gate, which is never auto-approved. A call is evaluated as the call it really makes: tool_call, execute_code and process_manage are unwrapped to what they actually run, taint is copied into subagents, and an encoded payload is decoded and judged by what it decodes to. What is reliable and what is not: the taint mark is provenance-based — it comes from which tool produced the content, not from guessing at it. The credential, egress and write detectors are best-effort pattern matching over tool arguments, so an obfuscated command, a payload assembled to avoid the patterns, and writes through the memory or cron tools can get past them. A seatbelt, not a sandbox; the README's Known limitations lists exactly what is out of scope. Ten rules, each tunable to allow/monitor/escalate/block; a receipts ledger; a `hermes taint-sentry` CLI with a dry-run policy tester. Ships a Desktop half in the same package: a pane, a status-bar chip and ⌘K commands showing live taint state, the receipt feed and per-rule actions, backed by `/api/plugins/taint-sentry/`. The pane changes a rule on the user's click; a tool call that tries the same thing — the CLI, `config.yaml`, or that API over loopback — is refused. Disclosure — no network access, no credentials, no python dependencies and no core overrides: it reads tool arguments and results in-process, writes its decisions to a local SQLite ledger under the plugin's own data dir, and reads an optional policy file there. Nothing needs configuring; `mode: monitor` records without interfering and `mode: off` disables enforcement.

entries.name: takeover
entries.description: Human-in-the-loop screen takeover. When a step needs you (sign-in, approve/authorize, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment) the agent asks, you take over its browser/desktop from hermes-webui, the dashboard or Desktop (even on a phone), then hand back. Installs TigerVNC + Xfce via Hermes's Bot Desktop installer (root) and runs a local VNC/websocket service. Disclosure — on first deliberate use (the Screen page, the agent's first `request_takeover`, or `hermes takeover setup`) it installs TigerVNC and Xfce as root through Hermes's Bot Desktop installer and sets `browser.headed: true` in your config (turn off with `auto_install: false`); when the plugin loads it copies a Screen page into hermes-webui's extensions folder and runs a loopback Takeover service there (turn off with `webui: false`); whoever holds the takeover controls the agent's browser and desktop, and the agent's screen tools are refused until they hand back.

entries.name: talaria-bench
entries.description: A physics test bench for DIY servo robots: build your robot from a template and a few measurements, see it in 3D next to its photo, run a one-click MuJoCo arena (flat, ramps, bars, pushes, slippery floor) across randomized worlds with a report card that says why it fails, compare design variants or watch a changed version side by side in the Arena, and gate robot_play / robot_pose with an exact-motion preflight in simulation before a move may play on the real robot (ESP32 + PCA9685 firmware included, or a virtual robot). CPU only, no GPU, no CAD. Disclosure — the automatic return to home (before a move and on robot_stop) is speed-limited (at least 3 s) but not simulated on its own; runs benchmark and comparison jobs as background Python subprocesses with worker pools (up to N-1 cores each, at most 2 jobs at once); starts local virtual-robot HTTP servers on 127.0.0.1 (random port, no token) on demand, and `hermes talaria sim` listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 unless --host is given; sends plain HTTP only to the robot address you set (bypassing proxies; the robot token travels unencrypted on your LAN); reads a robot photo only from a path you give under your home or Hermes folder; writes robots, photos, moves, approvals, jobs, reports and caches under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/talaria-bench (the trace cache is not pruned). The optional robot token is a Hermes secret. No third-party services, shell commands, downloads or telemetry.

entries.description: Write, compile, sign and audit iOS Shortcuts from Hermes with no Mac: six tools turn plain-language intent into reviewable Cherri source, compile it to an unsigned .shortcut inside a bwrap sandbox, sign it through RoutineHub HubSign on explicit consent, and audit any .shortcut (signed AEA1 container or plain plist) for what it reads, writes and sends before it is installed. Bundles the shortcuts-authoring skill (file shape, verified action signatures, house patterns, and the traps that make a shortcut compile cleanly and still be broken). Disclosure — the Cherri compiler runs as a subprocess under bwrap with no network namespace, a read-only root, a throwaway HOME and only the job directory writable, and a build is refused rather than run on the host when bwrap is missing; talaria_setup, after Hermes approval, downloads the third-party Cherri v2.4.0 compiler (electrikmilk/cherri) from GitHub and installs it only if both recorded sha256 checksums match. Network call sites: talaria_status opens one TCP connection to the signing host only when called with probe_signer=true; talaria_inspect on an iCloud link fetches that shortcut from Apple's iCloud hosts only; talaria_sign uploads the compiled shortcut as an XML plist plus its name to https://hubsign.routinehub.services/sign (RoutineHub, a third party) only after Hermes approval per artifact, so unattended runs fail closed. Artifacts are written only under $HERMES_HOME/talaria (or $TALARIA_HOME). No telemetry, no credentials.
