entries.name: tallyhand
entries.description: Twitch chat for Hermes Agent that treats chat as untrusted input. Roles come from chat badges and are enforced in code before every tool call: viewers get no moderation tools, and bans, unbans and long timeouts wait for the streamer's approval. The streamer also gets Twitch and OBS tools, chat commands that need no model call, viewer notes kept only with consent, and replies in the stream's language. Disclosure — chat in the configured Twitch channels starts Hermes turns for allowlisted viewers (or everyone, if TWITCH_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true), and those viewers' turns run in this profile with its persona and the questions go to your model provider; while this profile's memory, user profile or an external memory provider is on, only your own questions are answered unless you set allow_profile_memory_for_viewers: true, which puts your MEMORY.md, USER.md and memory-provider recall into viewers' turns; viewers and moderators get no Hermes tools beyond the to-do list and, for moderators, capped Twitch moderation, while bans, unbans and long timeouts need your approval; the bot token is used only against Twitch's own endpoints and OBS is contacted on this computer unless TALLYHAND_OBS_ALLOW_REMOTE=true; viewer notes (!remember) are stored under the profile's plugin-data for 90 days by default, and !forgetme deletes the viewer's notes and their own per-viewer Hermes sessions; the setup wizard writes the token to .env and, after a yes/no, Twitch toolset/context settings to config.yaml. No telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: talos
entries.description: Automatic, unskippable smart-contract security checks for code Hermes writes and deploys (EVM, Solana/Anchor, Sui/Move): scans every .sol/.rs/.move file Hermes writes, feeds open findings back so Hermes fixes its own bugs, and gates deploy commands (anchor/solana/sui/forge/hardhat, including inside scripts) — mainnet blocked on high/critical findings, escalated to Hermes's human approval on medium, allowed with a warning on devnet/testnet; plus a /talos report command and a talos_scan tool. Disclosure — its pre_tool_call hook can block terminal deploy commands (anchor/solana/sui/forge/hardhat, including inside scripts, package.json scripts and Makefiles it reads) or escalate them to Hermes approval; every non-deploy call passes through. Never runs repository code: Slither analyses each .sol file with plain solc from an empty temp directory (no Hardhat/Foundry builds, no repo slither config), with import remappings read from static files. Runs local CLIs when present (slither, sui move build --lint, solana config get, sui client active-env, cast chain-id), each with a minimal environment that excludes Hermes's API keys; cast chain-id contacts the RPC URL named in the deploy command and sui move build may fetch the package's git dependencies. Requests no capabilities. Stores findings and a file-hash scan cache in its plugin data directory. No telemetry, no third-party APIs, no credentials read or stored. Fails closed: unknown network counts as mainnet, and a missing, crashing or timed-out analyzer reports code as unchecked. Heuristic rule packs, not an audit.

entries.name: tameru
entries.description: Big tool outputs, kept small, nothing lost: old tool results shrink to the lines that matter and every distinct error, and the tameru_read_original tool brings back the exact original. You can also Restore or Keep a shortened output in full, pin lines of your own through every summary, and see it all in a Desktop panel and a /tameru command. Deterministic and local, with no LLM calls. Disclosure — Replaces Hermes's context engine and subclasses its built-in ContextCompressor through a private import, overriding its private prune/demote methods (it checks their shape at startup and falls back to stock compaction when they change). Unless you set compression.proactive_prune_tokens yourself, turns on proactive tool-result pruning with a trigger scaled to the model's context window, and after each prune shortens Hermes's re-prune runway for the running session. Adds a model-callable tameru_read_original tool (tameru_expand is still answered but no longer listed) that returns pruned tool output from memory or this session's archive (web, browser and MCP output stays wrapped as untrusted data); complex regex greps run in a short-lived local Python child process (python -I -S, with a timeout). Adds a short note to the system prompt and, only when something changed, a short note to your message for the model. An optional lazy_tool setting (off by default) registers an llm_request middleware that leaves the recovery tool out of requests until a result has been shortened. Optional learned_priors, net_estimate and stats_ledger settings (off by default) keep small files (numbers only) under the Hermes home. Keeps per-chat records (lean mode, pinned lines, Keeps, policy choices) in the plugin's own durable state (ctx.state), under one key per chat, and clears a chat's record after 90 days unused. Registers the hooks pre_llm_call, pre_api_request, post_api_request, api_request_error and post_compaction. No network calls, no credential reads; the render log is off by default.
entries.title: Tameru
known_issues: Full archive recovery requires plugins.isolation to be in_process; host mode limits recovery.
Overrides private ContextCompressor signatures and falls back when the host contract changes.

The default connection requires TAVILY_API_KEY; supports Hermes-managed OAuth through a native MCP override. Disclosure — Connects to Tavily's hosted MCP server at `mcp.tavily.com` and sends it the search queries, URLs and research prompts the agent issues, authenticated with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or a Hermes-managed Tavily OAuth sign-in.

entries.name: teach-back
entries.description: Make sure you understand the code your agent writes. Teach-Back records every file the agent writes or patches, and /teachback quizzes you on it: short questions about what the new code does (behaviour, edge cases, failures), written from the real change by your own model through ctx.llm and graded the same way, with the right answer explained when you miss. /teachback score shows how many agent-written lines you were quizzed on and understood.

entries.name: teamorouter
entries.description: TeamoRouter as Hermes model providers on one key: `teamorouter` serves Claude models over TeamoRouter's native Anthropic Messages API (so Hermes' Anthropic prompt caching and thinking apply), and `teamorouter-openai` serves GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models over its OpenAI-compatible API. Each /model picker lists that side's tool-capable chat models from TeamoRouter's public catalog, leaving out image, service-tier and free-tier variants, and context windows come from the same catalog. Maintained by TeamoRouter. Disclosure — registers two model providers at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Prompts, tool schemas and TEAMOROUTER_API_KEY go to https://api.teamorouter.com (/v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions) through Hermes' own clients, and TeamoRouter forwards each request to the upstream vendor serving the model. The plugin's own request is GET https://api.teamorouter.com/v1/models/pricing, a public endpoint, sent without the key and cached for an hour. `teamorouter-openai` requests carry a fixed `X-Client-Source: hermes-teamorouter-plugin` header (via the profile's default_headers), used only to count traffic from this plugin; Claude requests carry no header from the plugin. No telemetry, no files read or written, no stored credentials, no processes.

entries.name: tebar
entries.description: Publish and schedule social media posts through Tebar's (tebar.app, Indonesian social media scheduler) official hosted MCP server: Instagram, Threads, Facebook Pages, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Pinterest, Telegram and Discord; edit, cancel and retry scheduled posts; read account and post statistics; reply to comments, answer Instagram DMs and run comment-to-DM automations; keep an ideas board. Bundles one workflow skill. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to https://api.tebar.app/mcp, which calls the social platforms' APIs for the user's connected accounts, with the user's API key from TEBAR_API_KEY sent as a Bearer header. Write actions are public and cannot be taken back through Tebar: they publish posts, reply to comments, send DMs and turn on automations that reply to people on their own; posting to X is paid from the user's Tebar balance. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool not annotated read-only. To upload a file from the Hermes machine, the bundled skill has the agent run a curl upload command returned by Tebar's server with that file's path. Account data returned by tools (posts, statistics, comments, DMs, commenter and customer names) reaches the model provider. API access needs a paid Tebar plan or the free trial. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: telegram-app
entries.description: Phone control panel for Hermes inside Telegram: live status and usage, sessions and their messages, agent cron jobs (create, edit, pause, run now, stop, catch-up per job), logs, skills and memory, a send-to-Telegram box and error alerts, opened from your bot's menu button. Login is Telegram initData (HMAC-SHA256 with Ed25519 fallback, freshness window) checked by a token-only dashboard-auth provider on one token route, against a plugin-owned admin list (TELEGRAM_OWNER_ID plus the plugin setting admins) that refuses everyone until set; being allowed to chat with the bot never grants login. Alerts and the send box reach admins only. Built by Muhammad Aiman (aimanmalib) at Sasa Teguh. Disclosure — a verified login returns the dashboard session token, which authorises the whole dashboard API; because Hermes asks every token provider on every token route, valid initData also passes the token gate of /api/gateway/drain when HERMES_DASHBOARD_DRAIN_SECRET is set (a route the session token cannot reach); the plugin's principals carry the scope telegram-app and its login route demands it once Hermes has per-route scopes (#146551), which also closes drain to initData; loopback dashboard mode only, with the phone app (web/ in the repo) served by your own reverse proxy that forwards only /api/plugins/telegram-app/*. Calls api.telegram.org with TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (read through Hermes's secret route) for the send box and alerts. Runs one background alert thread in the dashboard process (polls errors.log and cron state every 30 s; the plugin setting alerts_enabled: false turns it off) and stores its settings under $HERMES_HOME/state/telegram-app. Reads Hermes sessions, cron jobs, logs, skills and memories; writes only agent cron jobs (no script, no_agent or workdir). No telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: telegram-client
entries.description: Telegram client pane for Hermes Desktop: dialogs, message history with image previews and per-post image reload, forum topics, and reviewed send/reply/save/delete/mark-as-read actions via a dedicated Telethon user session (separate from the core gateway bot token). All history is sanitized before rendering. Disclosure — the profile dashboard backend reads dialogs and message history and downloads media for in-page previews (page byte-budgeted and cached in memory); TELEGRAM_API_ID/TELEGRAM_API_HASH come from the profile's Hermes secrets; login challenges stay in process memory; the dedicated Telethon session lives in HERMES_HOME/telegram-plugin-auth/ (directory 0700, .session and its -wal/-shm sidecars 0600), and anyone holding that session file controls the Telegram account; delete removes the selected message for everyone; mutations go prepare -> exact preview -> confirm -> commit -> readback, and the pane's "Confirm actions" switch (on by default) can turn the preview step off; message links open in the system browser (http and https only).

entries.name: telegram-notify
entries.description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Hermes agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/telegram-notify.

entries.name: telegram-stickers
entries.description: Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, read through Hermes' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Hermes answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Hermes. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max_learned_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn_packs: false turns learning off). A pre_llm_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Hermes' sticker_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Hermes like any tool. Uses Hermes functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision_tools.vision_analyze_tool, gateway.session_context.get_session_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.
entries.title: Telegram Stickers
known_issues: Needs plugins.isolation: in_process (the default). Under plugins.isolation: host it cannot see the current chat, so it sends no stickers, learns no packs and adds no hint.

Every person the bot answers in a direct chat adds packs (up to max_learned_packs, default 100), which the agent then uses in every chat. Keep the gateway allowlist to yourself, or set learn_packs: false.
Before Hermes 0.21.5, /stickers in Telegram only shows the status and reloads packs; the owner's other /stickers commands work in the Hermes CLI on the server.
Where tool progress is on, Hermes posts its progress line (such as telegram_sticker_send...) before a sticker; display.platforms.telegram.tool_progress: off hides every tool's lines in Telegram.

entries.name: telegram_dashboard_probe
entries.description: One pinned Telegram message with your Hermes' state on one phone screen, edited in place from inside the gateway. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — reads Hermes' files read-only, the agent's context files wherever it works, and the free space of the disk HERMES_HOME lies on. Disclosure — edits the message through the Telegram adapter, private members included. Disclosure — Hermes' usage facade every 5 min, which may read the Claude Code or Codex CLI login and refresh its token. Disclosure — GitHub releases without a token, at most every 15 min, no off switch. Disclosure — opt-in: loopback limit sources, a drift command. Disclosure — its own code writes only its record; the full list is in the README.
entries.title: Telegram Dashboard
known_issues: Requires in-process plugin execution: the Telegram handler factory receives the platform's native SDK client, which plugins.isolation: host does not allow; under host the plugin does not load and nothing is delivered.
Updating from 1.0.0 or older: restart the gateway once; until then a plugin reload leaves the screen still.
On the launch profile of a gateway that multiplexes profiles, Claude's limits and a keyed limit source show no data: Hermes refuses secret lookups outside a profile scope.

entries.name: telesec
entries.description: Telegram Business secretary: transcribes voice notes, round videos, and speech attachments right in the chat (raw text first, then cleaned up in place), with Settings and per-chat controls in Telegram's Manage Bot panel, plus opt-in text history (with import from a Telegram export) and deletion alerts, correspondence stats, and contact dossiers. In Telegram groups the operator lists (group_chats, empty by default) it also transcribes members' voice notes, circles, and audio files without a Business account, and passes recordings addressed to the bot to the Hermes assistant as the member's voice request. Not affiliated with Nous Research. Disclosure — audio goes to the STT backend Hermes is configured with (local or external); transcript cleanup sends chat text through the host ctx.llm and the bot edits the posted transcript in place; opt-in dossiers send chat text through the Hermes model task telesec_dossier (default Vercel AI Gateway to Google with zero data retention; Hermes may retry with its fallback chain or main model); an optional message check (TypeSafe Jev through Vercel AI Gateway) and optional fact extraction (Cloudflare Workers AI) are off by default, call those services directly over https, and read AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN through the Hermes secret scope; an owner-sent /dossier posts that contact's stored dossier (without the owner note, but written with it) and an owner-sent /stats posts a stats card into the Business chat for the contact to read; with history on, deletion alerts go only to the owner's private chat with the bot, and the deleted text shows only after the owner taps Show text; in a listed group the bot downloads members' recordings, sends them to the same STT backend, posts transcripts as ordinary bot messages, and hands an addressed recording's raw transcript and caption to the Hermes assistant under that member's identity, where Hermes checks the member's rights; group recordings never reach history, stats, or dossiers, and group-media.json under HERMES_HOME/data/telesec keeps only IDs and stages for 24 hours; runs local ffprobe/ffmpeg (argument lists, no shell) on attached audio; a gateway background thread checks the dossier switch every minute and runs dossier cycles only once dossiers are on; switches, modes, opt-in history, and dossiers are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/data/telesec; reads only the numeric bot id prefix of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; opt-in usage stats (event and feature names from a fixed list, error types, version and OS, a random install ID; never message content, names, or IDs) are off until the owner turns them on in Settings, with the Enable button of a one-time notice in the private chat with the bot, or with hermes telesec telemetry on; receiving or reading the notice turns nothing on, and TELESEC_TELEMETRY=1 does not either; once on they go over https to usage.sergeybaus.com; Settings, hermes telesec telemetry off, TELESEC_TELEMETRY=0, or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 turns them off; no self-updater.
entries.title: Telesec
known_issues: Needs in-process plugin mode for native Telegram handlers.

Uses the undocumented host STT entrypoint tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio (no public plugin route yet; NousResearch/hermes-agent#142505). NousResearch/hermes-agent#156570 plans to move it in a future release, so the upper bound is the newest Hermes Telesec was checked on, not a known break; Live Telegram runs used Hermes 0.22.6 (Business transcripts checked; groups by a member's report and logs only). 0.23.3 and 0.23.2 ran in a local gateway against a fake Telegram Bot API with synthetic data, not live Telegram.

entries.name: tenure
entries.description: Revocable trust for Hermes agents, per action type. By default every kind of action works as with Hermes alone (files, memory, subagents, known dev tools: npm, pytest, cargo, git...), and every local change is saved first: file writes and plain rm, mv, cp, sed -i or `> file` on project files act, then tell you, with `/tenure undo` for 24 hours. The first mistake on a kind of action (an undo, a flag, a refusal of Hermes's own prompt, a file it wrote that no longer parses) puts that kind, for every model of the profile, on probation: it asks first, earns back acting-then-notifying on a run of approvals, then acting alone with random spot checks, from a rule preregistered on OSF (Wald SPRT to the middle tier, Dodge's CSP-1 series to the top, a guarantee you choose). What leaves the machine (push, publish, deploy, registry logins, cloud writes, payments), unreadable shell, and anything after the agent read outside content keep asking; one "Allow for this session" covers a session. A call that touches a sensitive field (secrets, bank details, or a field it cannot read such as an opaque id) is its own kind of action and, under the default preset, always asks; the owner can switch on status, e-mail or recipient fields too. The approval prompt shows the target of a call first, recognized secrets masked (including those typed in a terminal command), and every action settled under its watch gets a number for 24 hours, so `/tenure flag 12` faults that exact action, on the model that acted. Signed, hash-chained, replayable autonomy passport (`hermes tenure verify`), a per-model benchmark of your own work, a switch preview before you change model, a Desktop page and a dashboard tab at parity, five languages. Linux, macOS and Windows (on Windows, plain shell file commands keep asking instead of acting with an undo). A friction bench in the repo replays an ordinary 30-call coding session: 3 questions Hermes would not ask, against 23 when every kind of action asks first. Disclosure — hooks only (pre_api_request, pre_tool_call, post_approval_response, post_tool_call, post_llm_call, subagent_start, subagent_stop), no tools; no network, no LLM call, runs no command. It can only add an approval prompt through Hermes' own prompt, never answer one. Reads the profile's config.yaml and its own plugin settings, and writes settings back only through ctx.set_config when the owner saves them. Writes under plugin-data/tenure: a SQLite record and a hash-chained ledger (action types and outcomes, no paths, no commands, no free text), a 24-hour list of recent actions (number, action type, model, time; no arguments), a signing key and an undo HMAC key, and undo snapshots of the project files an action is about to change (file bytes and paths, owner-only, deleted after 24 hours, 5 MB per action). The dashboard tab and Desktop page show the tenure records of every profile on the machine (read-only); revoke, flag, undo and settings act on the current profile only.

entries.name: terraform-drift
entries.description: Compare pinned Terraform provider and module versions with the public registry. Disclosure — tools are on for every Hermes surface, including the gateway. Stop a surface with hermes tools disable --platform <name> terraform-drift, or the plugin with hermes plugins disable terraform-drift. Nothing is written under plugin-data/terraform-drift, and there is no key. Only the directory you name is read, and only .tf, .tf.json, and .terraform.lock.hcl. Symlinks and .. are refused, and .env, tfvars, .terraform, backend values, and hashes are not returned. The provider pin is the lock version, not the required_providers constraint. A module pin is an exact version only. GET calls only registry.terraform.io and, for a github.com source, raw.githubusercontent.com CHANGELOG.md. Redirects and proxy variables are ignored. A timeout or failed read leaves latest empty and is not called current. Semver orders versions, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0. The digest text is not sent and no cron job is created. known keeps newer versions, and omitting it does not call rows new today. There is no approval card. Before the call, name the directory and say there is no init, plan, apply, or state write. Cron, yolo, and approvals off can still run this read. MIT, no daily cap, requires Hermes >=0.21.4.

entries.name: test-drive
entries.description: Don't guess which plugin helps. Test-drive it. When Hermes hits a capability wall (it says it can't, or a tool fails as unavailable) test-drive appends one line naming the best catalog match; /testdrive <need> and test_drive_find show the top 3 with trust cards (tier, pin, keys needed, declared tools/hooks, disclosure); after you approve, test_drive_run or /testdrive run installs the candidate into a throwaway HERMES_HOME, runs your original request once with hermes chat -q, attempts cleanup and reports a before/after with tool-call evidence when available; keep goes through Hermes's own installer; /testdrive history keeps receipts. Disclosure — fetches the public catalog index from hermes-agent.nousresearch.com (redirects only to https Nous hosts, cached 6 h); an approved drive installs the selected catalog repository and pin by URL through Hermes, whose custom-source scanner may block caution verdicts, and installs its Python dependencies from PyPI into the sandbox's own runtime, runs child hermes CLI processes (plugins install, chat -q, sessions export, gateway stop) with hard timeouts and process-group kill, sends your request to your configured model provider (twice with a baseline), and runs the candidate's code as your user inside the temporary profile (not an OS sandbox), including any network calls it makes; every test_drive_run is escalated to Hermes's approval gate (fails closed unattended) and the slash command asks via ask_choice or an explicit --yes; the child runs single-query mode with dangerous commands denied; the child gets only system env vars plus your model route's key and the candidate's declared requires_env, read through agent.secret_scope (literal credential fields are stripped from the model and provider config written to the sandbox's 0600 config.yaml; a drive whose key exists only as a literal is refused); no memory, sessions, .env or auth.json are copied; temp dirs hermes-testdrive-* are removed after drives when cleanup succeeds; cleanup failures are reported; stores the catalog cache, last gap per session and up to 50 drive receipts in its plugin-data folder; a transform_llm_output hook appends one nudge line to gap replies (off with nudges: false); optional llm_check calls your active model; no telemetry.
entries.title: Test Drive
known_issues: A test drive takes about 30-90 s and spends model tokens; plugins that need OAuth sign-ins, a messaging platform, the Desktop app, hardware or keys you don't have can't show their value in a throwaway profile (missing keys are reported and the run is skipped).
Models that sign in with OAuth (Nous Portal, Codex) are not reused in the sandbox; set test-drive's sandbox_provider/sandbox_model/sandbox_key_env to an API-key route.

entries.name: testerswap
entries.description: Manage your TesterSwap account through TesterSwap's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://api.testerswap.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config): check credits, find live Google Play and App Store apps to test, start tests, review and approve or send back tests submitted for your apps, list or pause your apps, read notifications, and plan Google Play closed testing. Bundles the testerswap skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — every tool call goes to TesterSwap's hosted server (api.testerswap.com) and acts on the user's own TesterSwap account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. approve_test transfers held credits to the tester, start_test commits the user to install and use an app themselves, and release_test and reject_test end a test. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: testsift
entries.description: Exact, local analysis of JUnit XML test reports (pytest --junitxml, Maven Surefire, Gradle, Jest/Vitest junit reporters, go-junit-report/gotestsum, PHPUnit, .NET, CI artifacts), from one file or a directory of them. test_report_summary gives exact pass/fail/error/skip counts, failures grouped by cause (messages that differ only in numbers, ids or quoted values share a group), the slowest tests and flaky suspects; test_report_failures lists failing tests with type, message, file/line and the start and end of the trace; test_report_compare diffs two runs into newly failing, fixed, newly skipped, still failing, added, removed and much slower tests. Streamed, standard library only: no network, no credentials, no third-party dependencies, no self-update; DOCTYPE and entity declarations are refused. Disclosure: reads the local report paths you pass it (read-only), only regular files, and honours Hermes' core read denylist.

entries.name: tether
entries.description: One Hermes agent, many machines: lends a remote Hermes agent the terminal, files, screen and apps of your paired desktop machines (macOS and Windows). Say 'tether <machine>' and the agent's terminal, file and computer-use tools act on that machine under its own Hermes rules and approvals; send 'untether' to bring them home. Each machine dials the host over a pinned, mutual TLS 1.3 link (256-bit suites only), and the person at the machine allows every session on its own screen before anything runs. Includes a Tether panel for Hermes Desktop (paired machines, labels, idle limits, connection log). Disclosure — the host listens on the LAN or tailnet address you configure (default 127.0.0.1) and each paired device connects to it over pinned mutual TLS 1.3; no third-party services, no telemetry; while a machine is tethered, the host session's shell commands, file reads/writes and computer use run on that device after the person there allows the session, judged by the device's own Hermes rules (its hardline/deny floors always; commands the host's approval gate already passed skip the device's own approval prompts); skills opened during a tethered session are copied read-only into a per-session workspace on the device and removed when it closes; background tasks: the link listener (host), the device's connection, an idle sweeper and a settings watcher; stores one Ed25519 key per machine, encrypted at rest, with its passphrase in Hermes's secret store; adds a short per-turn note while a machine is tethered; reads private Hermes approval internals (tools.approval) and fails closed if they change.
entries.title: Hermes Tether
known_issues: Devices must be macOS or Windows; the host must be macOS or Linux (it uses a POSIX file lock and Unix socket). On a device, Hermes must run in the signed-in desktop session so the consent prompt can appear.

Computer use on the device needs the companion plugin tether_screen, installed by hand from plugin/tether_screen in the repository. Its validation stops at the capability probe exactly like Hermes's bundled computer-use plugin.
Several Hermes Desktops connected to one backend share it: closing one ends the chat open in the other.
'untether' closes a connection only when it is sent as a message on its own.

entries.name: the-millionaire-matrix
entries.description: Every model family you have a seat for generates a candidate; all of them blind-score each other on a peer validity matrix anchored by real tests (hard and measured gates outrank the matrix), the field steps down round by round to one answer behind a human gate, and verified lessons carry into your next session. Disclosure — after you approve each `critic_run` (Hermes shows the repo and every test/sensor command), this plugin runs those commands on the host against model-generated changes, and can launch your installed coding CLIs (codex, claude, grok, qwen, kimi, agy) to edit files in git worktrees under the repo with your user's permissions. Merging a winner happens only through `/critic gate` or `hermes critic gate`. entries.name: thoth
entries.description: Agents working as one team, each with its own harness: Claude Code, Codex and Hermes today. Ask Hermes for a website, an app, artwork or a doc: it plans the work on a shared board and hands each task to the real Claude Code or Codex CLI, on your own logins and plans, so every improvement their makers ship reaches your team. Each agent works in its own git worktree with a brief of what the team decided and made (goal, decisions, handoffs, what its dependencies produced), reviews the other's work, and Hermes merges what passes once you say yes. In Hermes Desktop, Thoth sits beside each project's chat: a side window with the live canvas and a Team & brain tab (who did what, decisions, reviews, versions), and every Thoth project is also a Hermes project on the same folder. Claude Code or Codex can join the board through the bundled MCP server or take over as coordinator, and a task that needs the web gets a clean Chrome, or yours when it needs your logins. When a Claude or ChatGPT plan runs out, the other agent carries on from its work, and the side window and Team card show how much of each plan is used and when it resets. Approve a plan once and autopilot runs it to the end: it starts, cross-reviews and merges each task, and asks you in the chat only when something needs you; any change to the plan pauses it. Once work is merged, the side window offers it to open, download as a zip or find in Finder. Start a project from the project menu or the chat: a new one gets its own folder in ~/Thoth, and a folder you already have becomes a project that keeps every version. After an update, the Thoth page says what's new, once. Disclosure — after you approve each launch in Hermes, or a plan card for autopilot, runs your installed claude and codex CLIs as background processes (stopped on cancel, timeout (30 min by default), unload or exit) under their own logins and plans, which Thoth never reads, with Claude Code's OS sandbox and Codex's workspace-write sandbox; gives them and project commands only PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, TERM, LANG, the LC_ locale settings, CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from its environment, plus names you list in env_passthrough; inside Codex runs it pre-approves only its own three worker tools (read the board, write a note); writes .thoth/ (SQLite brain, run logs, worktrees), thoth/T<n> branches, exact-path lines in .git/info/exclude and, only when you approve a merge, merge commits on your base branch; makes a new project's folder in ~/Thoth (the projects_dir setting) and, in a folder that is not in git yet, a git repository with its files as the first version (.env and other secrets, dependency folders and files over 50 MB stay in the folder but out of git, through .git/info/exclude), never in your home, Desktop, Documents or Downloads folder; links ignored node_modules/.venv folders into task worktrees, gives each worktree copy-on-write copies of the other files the project keeps out of git (read-only links where the disk can't copy) and moves the new files a merged task made outside git into the project folder without overwriting anything, and never reads or copies .env files or other secrets; a project board is used only if Thoth made it on this computer or you said yes to it on a Hermes card (adopting one starts nothing), and its setup or run command runs as you outside the sandbox only if you approved that exact command for that board on Hermes's card (hashes kept in approvals.json in its data folder, never in the project); starting a run preview asks you first (on a free localhost port from an export under .thoth/previews/); a project whose .thoth folder is committed to git, or a .thoth folder Thoth didn't make, is refused; Thoth's own git commands run without hooks or fsmonitor; static previews are served read-only on 127.0.0.1; the Desktop page's Connect buttons run claude mcp add thoth / codex mcp add thoth only when clicked; in Hermes Desktop it adds two panes (the side window and Team & brain) and a Chat + Thoth layout template that changes your layout only when you pick it, opens one chat per project and pins it in the project's colour once, creates (or reuses) a Hermes project on each Thoth project's folder and moves that project's chat into it through Hermes's own project calls, and keeps which chat and folder belong to which project, and the last version whose notes you saw, in its data folder (chats.json, projects.json, whatsnew.json); reads plan usage from Claude Code's run output and asks `codex app-server` for Codex's limits (a read that uses no tokens), kept in plans.json; autopilot (only after you approve its plan card, never under an always-allow) starts, reviews and merges that plan's tasks without a card for each step, pauses when the plan changes, keeps the Mac from idle sleep with caffeinate -i while it runs and holds .thoth/autopilot.lock; the Download button writes a zip of the merged files (never .env files) to your Downloads folder; completion notices and autopilot's messages reach the chat only with allow_gateway_injection; a task you give a browser has its agent run npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.2.0 (pinned, fetched from npm on first use, usage statistics off): a temporary headless Chrome, or, if you choose your own Chrome, the Chrome you are running once you turn on remote debugging and allow the connection in Chrome, where the agent sees your tab titles, acts with your logins in a tab of its own and is told to only look. No network calls of its own, no telemetry.
entries.title: Thoth
known_issues: Needs the Claude Code and/or Codex CLI installed and signed in; agents run on your own Claude and ChatGPT plans
Agent sandboxes have no network: for per-task installs give the project a setup command (e.g. npm ci), approved once

Completion notices and autopilot's messages in chat need plugins.entries.thoth.allow_gateway_injection: true; without it Hermes hears about finished runs through thoth_wait, and you follow autopilot in the side window
Browsing in your own Chrome needs Chrome 144+ with remote debugging on (chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging), and Chrome asks you to allow each run's connection

entries.name: threadpacket
entries.description: Send a packet (structured Markdown brief plus verbatim original files of any type up to 25 MiB) from one AI assistant to another person's assistant or across your own machines, through Threadpacket's hosted MCP server at threadpacket.com/mcp (or a self-hosted Cloudflare Worker) using OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/threadpacket), configuration only; declares trust: untrusted for threadpacket so write-capable calls prompt before running. Disclosure — hosted connector with no local code; tool calls send user-selected briefs and files to threadpacket.com (or the user's configured server), stored verbatim (not end-to-end encrypted) up to 256 MiB of live files per hosted team and auto-deleted after 7 days by default (30 days max), with no server AI calls and operational event counts that record no packet titles, briefs or filenames. Attaching a local file calls threadpacket_upload_url, checks that the returned URL is on the configured Threadpacket server, and runs a fixed single-file curl/Invoke-WebRequest HTTP PUT to /v1/uploads. A config.yaml `mcp_servers.threadpacket` entry replaces the package's entry, so it must keep `trust: untrusted` for send, revoke, invite and upload calls to ask first. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: threejs-stage
entries.description: Live three.js r187 scenes and GLB, GLTF, STL and OBJ models in Hermes chat. Hermes calls one tool, three_scene, with scene code or a model file. Hermes Desktop draws the result as an interactive card with orbit, zoom, fullscreen, restart, screenshot and Ask Hermes to change this, and other surfaces get a standalone HTML file. With Desktop open, each scene is dry-run in a hidden frame before the tool returns, so a crash or a blank render reaches Hermes in the same turn. Disclosure — scene code written by the model runs in Desktop inside a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin, scripts only) whose content security policy blocks all network requests; three.js r187 is bundled (MIT). The exported HTML file loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened in a browser. Given a model path, the tool reads that file and the .bin, .mtl and image files it references in the same folder (50 MB limit) and copies them to plugin storage; scenes, screenshots and delivered files are stored under plugin-data/threejs-stage and cache/generated/threejs-stage on this machine. The dry run makes the tool wait up to 2.5 s for Desktop and up to 16 s for the result, and can be turned off (verify_scenes). Fix with Hermes and Ask Hermes to change this each send one ordinary chat message. No API keys, no telemetry, no background processes, no self-update.
entries.title: Three.js Stage
known_issues: The live card needs Hermes Desktop. On other surfaces the tool delivers a standalone HTML file and reports the scene as unverified.
Restart the gateway once after installing, so the plugin's backend routes are mounted.
The card runs three.js WebGPURenderer on its WebGL2 backend, because the sandboxed frame is not a secure context. WebGPU-only features such as storage textures are not available.
Draco, meshopt and KTX2/Basis compressed glTF files are refused. Export without compression.

Disclosure — scene code written by the model runs in Desktop inside a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin, scripts only) whose content security policy blocks all network requests; three.js r187 is bundled (MIT). The exported HTML file loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened in a browser. Given a model path, the tool reads that file and the .bin, .mtl and image files it references in the same folder (50 MB limit) and copies them to plugin storage; scenes, screenshots and delivered files are stored under plugin-data/threejs-stage and cache/generated/threejs-stage on this machine. The dry run makes the tool wait up to 2.5 s for Desktop and up to 16 s for the result, and can be turned off (verify_scenes). Fix with Hermes and Ask Hermes to change this each send one ordinary chat message. No API keys, no telemetry, no background processes, no self-update. This plugin registers tool(s): three_scene. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7. Known issues: The live card needs Hermes Desktop. On other surfaces the tool delivers a standalone HTML file and reports the scene as unverified.; Restart the gateway once after installing, so the plugin's backend routes are mounted.; The card runs three.js WebGPURenderer on its WebGL2 backend, because the sandboxed frame is not a secure context. WebGPU-only features such as storage textures are not available.; Draco, meshopt and KTX2/Basis compressed glTF files are refused. Export without compression..

entries.name: tickover
entries.description: Ears for Hermes. Hermes can switch things on; Tickover lets it hear whether they started. tickover_verify listens before and after any action (a relay, a smart plug, a shell command, a robot move) and returns confirmed, no_change, other_change or unclear, with the level change in dB and a card. It needs no setup and no baseline. tickover_hear says what a sound is and whether the recording is usable. tickover_enroll and tickover_check remember a machine from three healthy recordings and report drift in robust sigmas with the frequency band that moved. tickover_watch puts a machine on a Hermes cron schedule, with a person sending voice notes or unattended from a stream or a recorder folder. tickover_fleet shows every machine on one card. Name a repairer with tickover_watch(notify="telegram:<chat_id>") and a confirmed drift reaches them on Telegram, WhatsApp, email or any Hermes channel, once per change, while the fix is still small. bridge/tickover_bridge.py, one standard-library file, turns an old Android phone, a Raspberry Pi or a spare laptop into a listening device that Hermes reads over the local network. tickover_teach (experimental) learns named states from a few recordings. tickover_selftest proves the install with synthetic sound. Training-free: frozen CED-base and EfficientAT mn10 encoders in onnxruntime, about 0.6 s per check on CPU. Benchmarks with their limits are in the README. Disclosure — first use downloads the CED-base ONNX model (87 MB, Apache-2.0) from huggingface.co/mispeech/ced-base at a pinned commit and verifies its sha256; a 12 MB mn10 ONNX graph ships in the repo, checked by sha256 at load. Audio is processed locally and never uploaded. tickover_listen and a source-less tickover_verify record 3-120 seconds from this computer's microphone when the model calls them, with no approval prompt (needs the optional sounddevice package). The tools read any audio or video file, folder or glob the model names, and open a stream URL only for hosts the owner lists in the plugin's allowed_sources setting (empty by default), connecting only to the checked address and re-checking every redirect; private addresses pass only for listed local names or IPs, and link-local and cloud-metadata addresses only when listed literally. ffmpeg (the one on PATH, else the binary shipped by the imageio-ffmpeg wheel) runs as a subprocess with protocol and format whitelists and a minimal environment; http(s) streams are fetched by the plugin and piped in, rtsp goes through a local relay that refuses redirects. tickover_watch creates and replaces Hermes cron jobs (no faster than every 15 minutes, never from inside a cron run unless cron.allow_agent_scheduling is true) that ask the owner for a recording or check a stream unattended. With a repairer set through tickover_watch(notify=...), which only the owner's chat or the local operator can change, a confirmed drift sends the repairer a message and a card through Hermes delivery, via a one-shot cron job with no tools or, when agent scheduling is off, from the listening job itself; this happens without an approval prompt. Three hooks (pre_gateway_dispatch, post_gateway_admission, pre_llm_call) note audio files that arrive in chat and add one context line telling the agent where the file is; the note is stored only after the gateway admits the sender, and they never block a message. The optional bridge script runs on the user's own device, serves only audio it records on request, and requires a key on any non-local address unless started with --open. Baselines, cards and history live in plugin-data/tickover. No credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: tidal
entries.description: TIDAL for Hermes Agent: five tools (playback through local mpv, search, playlists, library, mixes) over the unofficial TIDAL API via tidalapi. Login is TIDAL's own PKCE login flow (hermes tidal login) — no developer app needed. Playback runs on the Hermes machine (mpv); TIDAL has no remote-device API like Spotify Connect. Needs a TIDAL subscription (any tier). Disclosure — unofficial TIDAL integration (community tidalapi library using TIDAL's own app client); stores your TIDAL access and refresh token in plaintext (owner-only, 0600) under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/tidal/ and refreshes it itself; playback spawns a detached local mpv process with an IPC socket and plays audio on the Hermes machine.

entries.name: time-machine
entries.description: Visual timeline scrubber, split diff inspector, surgical per-file rollback, and failure diagnosis for Hermes Agent and Desktop. Captures pre-mutation snapshots in an isolated store, diagnoses broken edits in dry-run mode, and restores files only after the user runs /tm restore or confirms in the Desktop/dashboard pane. Disclosure — snapshots the session working directory with git add -A into its own git store under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/time-machine/ before file-mutating and command tool calls, excluding .env, *.pem, *.key, node_modules, and virtualenvs (.env.example is kept); model-called restores are preview-only; workspace files are overwritten or deleted only when the user runs /tm restore or confirms a restore in the UI, and a full-workspace restore stays unchecked until the user opts in; /tm commit, /tm comment, /tm clone, /tm push, and /tm pull are user-typed commands that write only a private checkpoint, a ledger note, a new directory the user names, or a .bundle file, and they never run git commit, git clone, git push, or git pull on the project repository; no network, no telemetry, no state.db.

entries.name: timecapsule
entries.description: Sealed messages for later — seal a note so it cannot be read until its release condition is met (a date, N days of silence, or the sealer's explicit release), with a grace ladder and slow, announced deletion. Local-only, stdlib-only, no network. Disclosure — the seal is access control, not encryption: capsule text is stored in plaintext in store.json under the plugin data directory, so anything with file access (including the agent's own file tools) can read it, and manual release trusts the author name given by the caller.

entries.name: timeline-replay
entries.description: Animated replays of recorded Hermes activity across the profiles you select: Social, Balanced and Linear paces with up to 16 profiles stacked on one screen, or nine canvas styles: Orbit (a turning ring where every event shoots out as a ray), Galaxy (a spiral with one arm per profile), Skyline (an isometric city of activity), Flow river (profiles to models to tools), Pulse (a heart-monitor trace per profile), Day clock (events at their time of day), Neural net (sessions firing into tools and models), Code rain and Ridgelines; tool calls, sessions, delegations, model/provider switches and token totals. Preview the private HTML player in Desktop or the Webapp (loop or play once), then export MP4 at 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K on the Hermes host, with live progress and an ETA learned on that host. Settings → Plugins holds per-user defaults; `hermes replay` adds the same options in the CLI plus a live terminal HUD. Disclosure — observer hooks only (on_session_start, on_session_end, pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, post_tool_call, post_api_request, subagent_start, subagent_stop); they record metadata, never block or change a turn and never return directives. Prompts, tool arguments, results, command lines and credentials are discarded; session IDs are hashed. Reads outside its own data: the active profile's profile.yaml (display name only) and the state.db of this profile and of profile homes the operator explicitly enrolls, read-only (SQLite mode=ro, query_only) and metadata columns only. Writes only under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/timeline-replay/. Exports show profile labels, timestamps, tool/model labels and totals, so choose neutral labels before sharing. Rendering starts only when the user asks: it runs the preinstalled HyperFrames CLI (Node.js, driving Chromium/chrome-headless-shell) and FFmpeg/ffprobe as argument-list subprocesses with a limited environment (no provider or bot credentials), as a background thread in the gateway process; HyperFrames telemetry and update checks are turned off. No network calls of its own, no telemetry, no installs (video setup only drafts a chat request for the user to review and send), no credentials. When the Desktop page and the plugin on the Hermes host differ, the page shows both versions, a button to Hermes' Capabilities → Plugins tab, and copy buttons for the host command (hermes plugins update timeline-replay && hermes gateway restart) and Hermes' catalog install link (hermes://plugin/install?catalog=timeline-replay), both of which stay on the reviewed build; nothing installs unless the user acts in Hermes, and the plugin never checks for updates online or downloads or replaces its own files. Readiness runs the configured HyperFrames CLI with --version (same limited environment) to report its version. Desktop uses the SDK surface only (routes, sidebar nav, settings page, SandboxedFrame, the MEDIA player, captureGatewayFileDownload).

entries.name: timelinesai-whatsapp
entries.description: WhatsApp CRM inbox automation for teams: ask what needs a reply, then send WhatsApp messages, label, assign and close chats from Hermes. Regular WhatsApp numbers and WhatsApp API numbers, one browser OAuth sign-in to TimelinesAI, no keys in config. Hosted-only connector, no local code (details and disclosure in the README). Disclosure — Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, including the WhatsApp message text and chat history the agent reads, goes to mcp.services.timelines.ai (operated by TimelinesAI) and acts on the WhatsApp account you sign in with, including sending messages, notes and labels and assigning, opening and closing chats; OAuth tokens are stored by Hermes, the server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before write-capable calls, and the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. A TimelinesAI account is required.

Disclosure — Hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call, including the WhatsApp message text and chat history the agent reads, goes to mcp.services.timelines.ai (operated by TimelinesAI) and acts on the WhatsApp account you sign in with, including sending messages, notes and labels and assigning, opening and closing chats; OAuth tokens are stored by Hermes, the server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before write-capable calls, and the tool set is served by the remote server at runtime, not covered by the pinned sha. A TimelinesAI account is required. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.21.6.

entries.name: timestamp-ref
entries.description: @ts: context references that turn timestamps into readable times for the model: @ts:1729468800123 attaches the moment in UTC, in the local time zone and as ISO 8601, with its weekday, how long ago or ahead it is, the same moment in Unix seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, and its ISO week; bare numbers are read as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds by their length (or an s/ms/us/ns suffix) and the block says which; ISO 8601 and RFC 2822 dates and now work too, and up to 10 values in one reference also get the gaps between them; the TUI and Desktop composer preview a value as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's datetime; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @ts: reference provider

entries.name: timetopost
entries.description: Draft social posts for one human approval, schedule at each account's best time, read engagement and run AutoSEO blog workflows through TimeToPost's hosted MCP server, with two workflow skills bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — every tool call goes to https://api.timetopost.co/mcp and needs a TimeToPost account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add timetopost --url https://api.timetopost.co/mcp --auth oauth`, followed by `hermes config set mcp_servers.timetopost.trust untrusted` so Hermes keeps asking before write-capable calls (your own server entry replaces the package's untrusted flag); the bundled mcp.json alone returns 401, and Hermes stores the OAuth tokens. Write tools can schedule or publish to the user's connected social accounts. Post content and account data returned by tools reach the model provider. The tool list comes from the server at run time and is not covered by the pinned sha. One skill includes an offline Python helper that adds campaign parameters to links and makes no network calls.

entries.name: tinfoil-provider
entries.description: Tinfoil confidential inference as a Hermes model provider. Open-weight models from Tinfoil's live catalog (Kimi, GLM, gpt-oss and others) run in attested hardware enclaves that neither the cloud host nor Tinfoil can read. Hermes reaches them only through Tinfoil's local tinfoil-proxy, which verifies the enclave's attestation and pins its TLS key before forwarding anything; there is no fallback to an unverified connection. The proxy starts on demand. Disclosure — Hermes sends requests, including a /v1/models read for the model list, only to the local proxy (127.0.0.1:3301, or TINFOIL_BASE_URL); the proxy is what contacts Tinfoil. When nothing listens on the proxy's port, the plugin starts the user's installed tinfoil-proxy binary in its own session and leaves it running after Hermes exits, logging to proxy.log in the plugin's data directory; it never downloads a binary, and TINFOIL_PROXY_AUTOSTART=0 turns this off. The proxy inherits only an allowlist of the environment (PATH, home, temp and user, locale and time zone, SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR, HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY, and Windows system directories); every other variable, including all TINFOIL_* variables, is withheld. TINFOIL_API_KEY is read through Hermes' provider profile and sent to the proxy as the request's bearer token. The plugin writes catalog.json (the last model list it saw) and proxy.log under its plugin-data directory, registers no tools, hooks or middleware, and sends no telemetry.

entries.name: tinfoil-sandbox
entries.description: A tinfoil terminal backend: Hermes' terminal, file and code tools run inside your own Tinfoil Container, an attested enclave, reached over the Tinfoil CLI's attested SSH tunnel. Select it with terminal.backend: tinfoil and terminal.tinfoil_container. Needs a Tinfoil organization with Containers enabled; the public template https://github.com/counterposition/hermes-tinfoil-workspace sets up a suitable workspace. Dangerous-command approval stays on, and the plugin never creates, starts, stops or bills containers. Disclosure — every tool call runs the user's installed tinfoil CLI (tinfoil ssh) and OpenSSH client as subprocesses; the CLI contacts Tinfoil's control plane to look the container up, then the enclave. The plugin passes TINFOIL_API_KEY, read through Hermes' secret scope, to the CLI as the tunnel key, and the admin key when set (TINFOIL_ADMIN_KEY, or an admin_ key in TINFOIL_API_KEY, which the CLI also accepts); beyond those the CLI and ssh get only an allowlist of Hermes' environment (PATH, home, temp, user, locale, SSH agent socket, certificate and HTTP proxy settings, the CLI's TINFOIL_CONTROLPLANE_URL and TINFOIL_CONFIG, Windows system directories). It never reads the CLI's saved login, and strips TINFOIL_API_KEY, TINFOIL_TUNNEL_API_KEY and TINFOIL_ADMIN_KEY from the environment of commands the agent runs. An SSH control socket under the system temp directory (hermes-tinfoil/) keeps the verified connection open for five idle minutes. A pre_tool_call hook rewrites a leading ~ in the path argument of read_file, write_file, patch and search_files to the container's home directory, only while terminal.backend is tinfoil, because Hermes otherwise expands it to the host's home. No telemetry.

entries.name: tinyfish
entries.description: TinyFish: the web, built into Hermes. Free Search and Fetch power Hermes's own web_search and web_extract, and when a site needs clicks, forms or a login, a remote browser and the tinyfish_agent web agent handle it, signed in through saved TinyFish profiles when needed. Disclosure — sends search queries, URLs to fetch and tinyfish_agent goals with your TINYFISH_API_KEY to the TinyFish API (*.tinyfish.ai). Browser sessions and tinyfish_agent runs spend TinyFish credits. Under the default `request` policy each one goes through Hermes's approval prompt first (a session/always answer covers every later call; cron and unattended runs are denied unless you allow them). Setting `tinyfish.credit_policy.<feature>: allow` or YOLO skips the prompt. `hermes tinyfish setup` / `browser enable` (run by you) save the key to Hermes .env, set web.search_backend/extract_backend and browser.cloud_provider in config.yaml, enable the web/browser toolsets, and can install the agent-browser CLI after asking. Profile tools manage TinyFish Browser Context Profiles (saved website sign-ins) over the same API; you sign in to sites yourself at an agent.tinyfish.ai link and never give Hermes a password; the agent can create, rename and re-default profiles without asking, and deleting a profile goes through Hermes's approval prompt for each profile unless approvals are off (YOLO). Setup telemetry is off by default: only if you opt in (`hermes tinyfish setup --share-usage`, `tinyfish.telemetry: true`, or answering yes to setup's y/N question) does each setup run send one event to agent.tinyfish.ai with its outcome, where the key came from, the plugin version and OS, plus a one-way hash of the key (never the key). TINYFISH_NO_TELEMETRY=1 turns it off regardless.

entries.name: tirith
entries.description: Check every terminal command with your installed tirith before it runs: lookalike and homograph URLs, pipe-to-shell, obfuscated execution, credential and .env exfiltration, malicious packages and terminal injection. tirith blocks and required policy approvals go to Hermes's approval prompt, critical findings are refused, warnings run with the warning added to the result; unattended runs follow approvals.*_mode. Disclosure — runs the user-installed tirith binary (0.5.0 or later; never downloaded, installed or updated by the plugin) on every terminal command and completed shell command sent to a background terminal, in the command's working directory, with the command on stdin; tirith logs each check locally and, unless offline is set, may refresh its signed threat database, query OSV.dev, deps.dev and ecosyste.ms, download the CISA KEV feed, and query Google Safe Browsing (only with your key); fails closed (asks, or refuses when unattended) if tirith is missing, older than 0.5.0, times out or gives no verdict.
entries.title: tirith
known_issues: Hermes 0.21.5 still runs a built-in tirith check before plugins; run `hermes config set security.tirith_enabled false` so each command is not checked twice. Hermes 0.21.6 and later do not have it.

entries.name: tironian
entries.description: Trains a small local model on the requests you keep repeating in Hermes, tests it on held-out steps from your own past sessions, and lets it answer those requests only after it passes, checking every answer and falling back to your usual model silently. Capture uses llm_execution middleware and observer hooks; secrets and personal details are masked before anything is stored. Disclosure: reads this profile's state.db read only on first use and on `hermes tironian import`; stores masked contexts, grades, datasets and GGUF files under plugin-data/tironian; makes no network calls during normal use (the router talks only to student_endpoint, Hermes's local model server on 127.0.0.1 by default); `hermes tironian trainer setup`, run by the user, creates a venv in plugin data and installs the modal client from PyPI; training starts only on an explicit user action and then uploads that family's masked examples to a private Volume in the user's own Modal account (deleted after the run), or runs on the user's own GPU; the optional judge (off by default) sends held-out examples, and in shadow mode differing answers within a daily budget, to the model assigned to the "Tironian judge" auxiliary slot; `hermes tironian verify`, run by the user, downloads only the proof and model URLs the user gives it, into plugin-data/tironian/verify. No telemetry.
entries.title: Tironian
known_issues: Hermes v0.22/v0.23 log 'unknown manifest field: provides_middleware' when loading; it is required by `hermes plugins validate` and harmless.
Live routing supports chat_completions and anthropic_messages providers; Responses API sessions are captured but not routed.

entries.name: tldr
entries.description: One-click summaries of long agent replies in Hermes Desktop. A card shows status first (Done, Blocked, Running, Waiting on you), what changed with each item marked Shown (backed by a tool step) or Stated only, risks, and the decisions the agent left you, with a recommended option and notes; Insert into chat drops your answers into the message box. Scope: last reply, since you last checked, or the whole session (with optional conflict warnings against earlier instructions); S/M/L length; per-reply history; reminders for skipped questions; optional automatic mode with a daily cap. Runs on its own auxiliary task (tldr_summary), so you can pick a cheap model in Models > Auxiliary without touching the chat model. Disclosure — Sends the selected chat text, tool names with short argument previews (up to 160 characters, e.g. commands, paths, URLs) and your preferences note to the model assigned to its `tldr_summary` auxiliary task (Hermes' auxiliary routing, host-owned credentials), only on click or in the opt-in automatic mode (off by default, 30 per day cap); reads this profile's session database and config read-only; stores settings and answers in Desktop plugin storage; no shell, no credentials, no telemetry.
entries.title: TL;DR
known_issues: Needs Hermes Desktop; there is no CLI or TUI surface.
Evidence labels mean a tool step backs a change, not that the result was correct; TL;DR does not see tool output.

entries.name: tmewai
entries.description: Local, offline index for your own Facebook JSON export (Meta's your_activity_across_facebook.zip). Imports messages, comments (including comments_v2), reactions and posts into a seven-table SQLite database without ever extracting the archive to disk, then exposes six tools: archive_scan and archive_ingest validate every ZIP entry in memory (absolute paths, .., drive paths, NUL bytes, duplicate names and symlinks rejected) and give each entry exactly one source_files row so nothing is silently dropped; archive_search runs FTS5 over text folded for Arabic (harakat, alef variants, taa marbuta, alef maqsura, tatweel) while stored text keeps its original spelling; archive_person and archive_overview aggregate over people, conversations, events and attachments; archive_evidence builds a hard-capped bundle (20 events, 4000 characters) with a metadata-only consent row that cannot carry excerpt text. Imports are idempotent by content fingerprint. Python standard library only, no network access, no API key, no environment variable; the database lives under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/tmewai/ and TMEWAI_DB_PATH overrides it. Disclosure — the plugin reads a personal social export the user points it at and stores it unencrypted in that local SQLite file; it never sends archive content anywhere, and archive_evidence only returns its capped bundle to the agent that requested it.

entries.name: tmux-live
entries.description: Live tmux tab for the Hermes web dashboard: pick a pane, watch it in ANSI colour, type into it when needed, and terminate the process, pane or session. Disclosure: calls the local tmux binary with argv lists (capture-pane, send-keys, kill-pane, kill-session), can signal the pane's foreground process group, and probes /proc/<pid>/root/tmp for the tmux socket when the dashboard runs under systemd PrivateTmp. No network access, credentials, telemetry or self-updater. English and Spanish UI.
known_issues: The view is a one-second mirror, not a PTY attachment, so typed characters appear on the next poll.
Only panes belonging to the same user and host as the dashboard are visible.

entries.name: tmux-watch
entries.description: Hermes Desktop pane and status-bar chip showing live tmux sessions on any number of SSH-reachable hosts, with real ANSI colour and an active / idle / possibly-stuck signal per session. Built to watch coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes) on remote dev boxes without attaching. Disclosure: the backend shells out to the system ssh client (BatchMode, your own ~/.ssh/config and keys) and runs only "tmux list-sessions" and "tmux capture-pane -e" on the hosts you list in ~/.config/hermes-tmux-watch/config.json (an example file is written there on first run); an optional per-host shell prefix you configure is prepended to those commands. Every terminal escape except SGR colour codes is stripped server-side. An opt-in per-host allow_control flag (off by default) enables a confirm-gated "tmux kill-session", re-checked by the backend. Polls every 5 seconds while Desktop is open. No credentials handled, no telemetry, no other network calls, no self-updater.
entries.title: Tmux Watch
known_issues: When Desktop connects to a remote Hermes, the pane is installed per Desktop machine; tick the desktop component on each one.
A 5-second snapshot view, not a live PTY: it never sends keys into a session.
Possibly stuck means the screen has not changed for 5 minutes, so a session that is simply idle (a quiet shell) is flagged the same way.

entries.name: token-master
entries.description: Token spend analytics for Hermes Desktop: one stacked daily chart of token consumption across every Hermes profile, provider and account on the machine (7D/30D/90D/1Y, stacked by token class, provider, profile or source), per-provider / per-profile / per-model / per-task breakdowns, and an Accounts and limits card that marks each credential as subscription (quota), pay-per-token API spend or free and shows the live allowance windows Hermes can fetch. It reads the token accounting Hermes already records — every profile's state.db opened read-only, plus DeepSeek Harness session files — and adds no collection of its own. Disclosure — reads every Hermes profile's state.db token accounting read-only, DeepSeek Harness session files under ~/.dsh, and the labels, ids and status of Hermes credential-pool entries (no token values); `Refresh limits` goes through Hermes' read-only fetch_account_usage(provider, read_only=True) to the provider's usage endpoint (no token is refreshed, rotated or stored); the optional `Sync now` button runs ssh with your own SSH setup into a host you added and streams the bundled read-only collector into that host's python3, installing and writing nothing there, and the Remote machines card runs `tailscale status --json` to offer online peers (discovery only — adding a host is still a click); state lives in plugin-data/token-master/ on the root Hermes home only; no telemetry, no background process.
entries.title: Token Master
known_issues: History is per provider and per profile, not per login: neither Hermes' usage table nor the DeepSeek Harness ledger records which credential served a request, so tokens cannot be split by account. Per-account quota is live, but per-account token history would have to be recorded forward-only.
Days are bucketed by last activity (a Hermes row carries last_seen; a DeepSeek Harness session is attributed to its file's last write), so a session spanning midnight lands on the day it finished.

Token counts cover one machine: remote machines are read only after you add an SSH host and press Sync now. Provider quotas are account-wide, so the percentage windows still cover every machine and tool using that account.

Quota sampling is passive: a sample is appended only while the page or a limits refresh is open, so the burn-rate trend means 'what happened while I was watching'. Live windows exist where Hermes ships a fetcher (anthropic, openai-codex, opencode-go, openrouter); nous and xai-oauth expose none and the card says so.

Tested on Windows 11 against Hermes 0.23.0. The backend and Desktop page are platform-neutral; install.ps1 is PowerShell-only, and everywhere else `hermes plugins install token-master` is the install path.

entries.name: token-rate
entries.description: Live output/input tokens-per-second chip in the Hermes Desktop status bar for a local llama.cpp server. Hermes itself reads the server's log ($HERMES_HOME/logs/llama-server.log, last 200 lines: `tg = X t/s` for output and `prompt eval time ... X tokens per second` for input) and serves it at /api/plugins/token-rate/; the chip polls that route once a second. The counter starts off — click the chip, or run the palette entry "Token Rate: start/stop the tok/s counter" (Ctrl/Cmd+K), to start it; the on/off flag is a file ($HERMES_HOME/cache/token-rate-state.json). It also registers the get_token_rate agent tool, so the model can read its own speed. Disclosure — it reads one local file (the llama.cpp log) and nothing else: no network calls, no external process, no extra port, no API key, no credentials, no telemetry. UI is English by default, Italian when the app locale is Italian.

entries.name: toll
entries.description: Safety checks before an agent buys a coin, signs a transaction or pays another agent, through Toll's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://t0ll.xyz/mcp, no key, no sign-in): who is behind a coin (snipers, bundles, linked wallets, the dev's funding and record), whether the LP can be pulled, whether the product a coin claims exists, one word before a buy (BLOCK / WARN / ALLOW / WAIT), ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK before signing a transaction, EIP-712 message or x402 payment, a wallet's live approvals with the unsigned revoke, an ERC-8004 agent's registration and x402 terms, paid x402 APIs and who they pay, and a Uniswap v4 hook's powers, on Robinhood Chain (4663) only; plus Robinhood Stock Token market data (debt securities, not shares), SEC fundamentals, insider trades, 13F institutional holders, earnings guidance, the Stock Token event feed and US macro figures. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to t0ll.xyz, which receives the tool's arguments (token contracts, wallet addresses, agent ids, tickers, the unsigned transaction passed to check_tx); 24 of the 28 tools are lookups annotated read-only; 4 are not (watch_coin and watch_wallet store a watch that makes Toll POST signed events to an https url the caller gives, unwatch_coin and unwatch_wallet remove one) and all 4 refuse without a Toll key, which this keyless package does not send; the server never signs, sends transactions or moves money; the package marks the server untrusted; no key is stored or sent (free daily quota of 10 new coins and 50 market calls, more with a Toll key the user sets in their own config); past the quota answers end with a paid x402 URL the plugin cannot pay; no telemetry (the quota is counted per caller with a daily-rotated keyed hash of the IP, deleted after 3 days). The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: tool-call-salvage
entries.description: Removes tool-call markup that a model wrote into its final reply as text instead of calling the tool (Qwen <function=...>, <invoke>, DeepSeek DSML and tool tokens, Harmony, Kimi, Mistral and Llama formats). Only complete markup that ends the reply is touched; code blocks and markup followed by more text are left as they are. When text is left before the removed markup, a one-line notice names the tools that were not run. An optional salvage mode, off by default and limited to the models you list, turns the markup into a real call to a tool offered in that request. Disclosure: no network, files, shell, subprocesses, telemetry or stored state; logs name the format and tools, never arguments; in salvage mode text the model wrote can become a real tool call (tools offered in the request, or Hermes's tool_call bridge when deferred_tools is on), run through Hermes's normal approvals.

entries.name: topoi
entries.description: Group your Hermes Agent chats into topics, in Hermes Desktop and in the Dashboard. A sidebar lists the topics active in the past week with a status dot per thread (working, waiting, unread, idle), a new chat files under your home topic, threads move between topics, and a topic's threads are searchable by message content. Cron job results arrive as topic threads you can reply to, and the reply continues that run's session. The gateway owns one topic registry and both clients read and write it over the plugin's REST API, so an edit in the Dashboard reaches the desktop app. Disclosure — registers a no-inbound `topoi` gateway platform adapter in the Hermes process; serves an HTTP API at /api/plugins/topoi/ behind the Dashboard's own origin and auth; writes its topic registry and the `home_channel` projection into the `platforms.topoi` section of config.yaml; keeps session-to-topic bindings in a plugin-private SQLite database; reads the per-profile session databases and cron job store (partly through private core helpers that can change between releases) and marks threads read or deletes them through core's own session routes; bundles one skill; no third-party network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: tracekit
entries.description: Tracekit's signer decides every tool call before it runs (deny blocks, ask waits for a person) and signs each call and its outcome into a run you can verify offline. Disclosure — every tool call's name and arguments, plus its result (in full for tools Tracekit's policy marks untrusted, otherwise a SHA-256 digest), go to a Tracekit signer: by default a same-user dev signer (`python -m tracekit signer serve --dev`) that the plugin starts on first use as a detached background process, which keeps running after Hermes exits until 15 minutes idle and stores signed runs plus each call's redacted arguments and results (encrypted, kept 7 days) under your user's data directory (~/.local/share/tracekit on Linux), or a remote signer when you set TRACEKIT_SIGNER to an https:// URL. The plugin fails closed: when tracekit-ai can't load or the signer refuses or can't be reached, tool calls are blocked (including every tool an execute_code script calls), and an `ask` decision holds the call until someone approves it in Tracekit or Hermes's hook timeout runs out.
