entries.name: track-record
entries.description: How often is your agent right when it says it fixed something? Each reply that claims success ("this fixes it", "this should work") is logged with how sure it sounded, then checked against your next message and any test or build run in the next turn. /trackrecord shows hit rate per confidence level and model, the calibration gap and a Brier score. When certain claims hold up under 80% of the time, the agent is told its record. Pattern matching only, no model calls.

entries.name: trackbuddy-parcel-tracker
entries.description: Track parcels and ocean containers from chat: DHL, FedEx, UPS, Amazon Shipping, GOFO, SPX Express, USPS and 1,000+ postal and cross-border carriers through 17TRACK, plus Maersk containers and bills of lading. Five workflow skills (single lookup, container tracking, bulk report, delivery-exception triage, cost estimate) drive nine tracking Actors on Apify's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.apify.com). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only, no local code. Disclosure — every tool call goes to Apify's hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and starts a pay-per-result run of a tracking Actor published by the plugin's author (Apify user muhammadafzal), who is paid for each run; runs are billed to the user's own Apify account (about USD 0.005 to 0.04 per tracked shipment plus USD 0.005 per run). Tracking numbers are sent to Apify, looked up on the carriers' public tracking pages, and the results are kept in the user's Apify datasets. Apify sign-in is OAuth, which Hermes runs only for a server in the user's own config, so the README has the user add the same-name server with `hermes mcp add package-tracking --auth oauth`; that entry replaces the package's own, so the user adds `trust: untrusted` to it to keep Hermes asking before each paid lookup. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. No telemetry. Independent tool, not affiliated with the carriers.

entries.name: trade-preflight
entries.description: Deterministic, fail-closed execution firewall for AI-initiated equity orders. A pre_tool_call hook normalizes broker-specific trade calls into one canonical order, evaluates it against an operator-owned policy (gross buy notional cap, max quantity, symbol / order-type / side allowlists) and blocks anything it cannot prove compliant; every decision and execution outcome is recorded in SQLite. Ships two paper-trading execution tools with deliberately different broker schemas (symbol/side/quantity/limit_price vs ticker/direction/qty/price), a read-only dry-run tool, a policy inspector and an audit reader. Disclosure - no network calls, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or stored credentials; no requires_env; reads only its own shipped policies/default.json (copied once into the plugin data directory to seed the operator policy) and writes only inside plugin_data_dir('trade-preflight') (the policy file and the SQLite audit/ledger database); execution is simulated locally in SQLite and never reaches a broker or a real trading venue, so the plugin adds no real trading capability; the policy file is operator-owned and an agent with unrestricted shell access as the same OS user could modify it, which is a documented limitation rather than a guarantee.

entries.name: tradeguard
entries.description: Read-only stocks and ETF research for Hermes: evidence-aware fundamentals, daily technical observations, ETF structure, comparable ranking, microstructure calculations and an explicitly experimental walk-forward ML baseline. It provides explainable heuristic research priority, not trade execution, personalized investment advice, calibrated win probabilities, price targets or position sizing. Optional ticker-only research fetches historical daily bars from Yahoo Finance's unofficial public chart endpoint only after explicit plugin configuration consent; it uses no API keys, credentials, broker access, background processes or live orders. Supplied snapshots and issuer metadata are read only from paths the user explicitly requests. Disclosure: public-data requests leave the local machine for the requested symbols, may fail or be stale, and are not entitled real-time quotes; technical-only scores are not combined valuations and all scores are unvalidated research heuristics.

entries.name: tradersagent-plugin
entries.description: A chart-first Trader's Agent for Hermes Desktop: one sidebar row docks a live Vela chart beside your conversation — replay, drawing tools, the LuxAlgo Library, a paper broker and Edge Stats behind it. Disclosure — the pane frames a local console service on 127.0.0.1:8787 that this package does not include or start: you clone the repository and run its ./install.sh or ./console/start.sh. install.sh registers that console as a background service (a systemd user unit on Linux, a launchd agent on macOS) that starts at login and restarts itself, registers the separate traders-chart MCP server with `hermes mcp add`, and with --with-edge clones LuxAlgo's Edge Stats engine at a pinned commit and installs its Node dependencies. The console fetches market data from Binance, Dukascopy and Yahoo Finance and Library scripts from LuxAlgo's hosted MCP (mcp.luxalgo.com), runs local image converters (vips, ImageMagick or ffmpeg) and the optional LuxAlgo Node engines, and keeps no account, key or telemetry. When no chat is open, the sidebar row creates and opens one Hermes chat titled "Trader's Agent — desk" (a palette command turns that off). The plugin itself registers UI only.

entries.name: treasury-cash-forecast
entries.description: A 12-month monthly direct cash-flow forecast for corporate treasury. Fill one template (Excel or CSV) with your past cash-flow statement, the future cash flows you already know and your what-if percentages. Recurring lines are projected by a statistical model (ETS by default; SARIMA and four simple baselines selectable), known lines come from your schedule, and a known amount can replace the model for single months. The base case and every scenario run together and come back as one Excel workbook: a summary, a cash-flow statement per scenario (12 actual months, then 12 forecast months) and a sheet showing where every figure comes from, reconciled every month to the cent: opening cash + net cash flow = closing cash. A fourth tool runs the same data through several models to show how much the answer depends on the method. All figures come from a tested engine (95 tests); the language model picks the tool and explains the result. Disclosure — no network calls, no credentials, no telemetry, no background process. Reads only the workbook or CSV folder you name and writes the template, the result workbook and audit files to the folder you name or next to your input. Installs two Python libraries, statsmodels and openpyxl, both with upper bounds. The optional Chronos-2 model is not installed by the plugin and is loaded from local files only, never downloaded. The bundled example company is synthetic.
entries.title: Treasury Cash Forecast
known_issues: Restart Hermes after installing (the gateway, and the Desktop backend if you use the Desktop app) so the running process sees the two new libraries.
Tested on Linux. ETS and SARIMA are fitted numerically, so figures can differ by cents between machines; the simple baselines are identical everywhere.

entries.name: treg-jobs
entries.description: Job hunt through treg's job API: search live roles across companies, semantic fit search, the people who work there, one person's work email, real salary percentiles with the sample size behind them, roles that closed since a date, and a local pipeline with who to write to. Eight tools plus a Jobs pane (pipeline, spend, chips). Read-only towards the world: nothing is applied to, emailed or logged in to. Disclosure — calls the paid treg.to API with your TREG_TOKEN and spends from that team's prepaid balance (about $0.001–$0.01 per call, capped per call and by a local budget ledger); your search terms, job-seeker profile summary, and the names, company domains and LinkedIn URLs of people you look up are sent to treg.to and the data providers it routes to; work-email lookups return third parties' personal contact data.

jobs_match takes 15-25 s and returns roles without a similarity score, so the rows have to be read rather than sorted by number.
A work email from jobs_email is the provider's best match, not a verified one — verify before sending.

entries.name: triage
entries.description: Keeps the list of every skill out of your context. Triage suggests skills in the composer as you type and as the chat goes on, ranked locally with no model call; a skill loads only when you pick it or clearly ask for it. Disclosure — rewrites outgoing model requests (removes Hermes' skills index from system messages and adds the bodies of skills you or the model pick, which changes the cached prompt prefix on those turns) and blocks skill_view for skills not approved in the chat; with 'Hide Hermes' own skills' (on by default) it adds the skills it serves to skills.disabled in your Hermes config.yaml, undone with `hermes triage restore`, which you must run before uninstalling; the model's skill_manage edits to skills it serves from other tools' skill folders you connect are written into those folders (edits to Hermes' own skills go through Hermes' skill_manage, and with skills.guard_agent_created on it makes no skill edits itself); it watches the skill folders you configure from a background thread, reads Hermes' session database (state.db) read-only and the current project's AGENTS.md/README and `.hermes/triage.yaml` to rank skills; `hermes triage migrate --apply-config` / `--empty-roots --yes` rewrite your skills config and move your Hermes skills folder aside (with backups) only when you run them; the optional `embedder` setting imports a Python class you name; it makes no network calls and sends no telemetry.

known_issues: Hides Hermes' own skills from Hermes while installed; run `python run.py restore` in the plugin folder before uninstalling.

entries.name: tripo
entries.description: Tripo's official plugin, made by VAST, the company behind Tripo. Tripo's own tripo-cli (pinned tripo-cli@0.11.1) runs locally as an MCP server with 26 tools for text, image and multiview to 3D, concept and multiview images, texturing, rigging and animation, retopology, segmentation, Gaussian splats, format conversion (GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, USDZ, 3MF) and downloads, plus the tripo-3d and tripo-game-asset workflow skills; Game Studio turns a rigged, animated model into a character you play in Hermes Desktop, a three.js web prototype, Godot, Unity or Unreal. In Hermes Desktop: inline 3D cards with Next and Download menus and a Play mode, a gallery of recent generations and a credit chip. Every call that is not read-only goes through Hermes's approval prompt, local-file uploads included; no per-tool costs or spend limit are declared. Needs TRIPO_API_KEY from an international Tripo account. Disclosure — first start downloads the pinned tripo-cli from npm through npx, which Hermes runs on its managed Node.js as a local child process; it sends prompts and the local images (up to 20 MB) or models (up to 150 MB) you or the agent name to Tripo's API (openapi.tripo3d.ai) under your key, gets only TRIPO_API_KEY from your profile, and sends no analytics. Downloads go to the plugin's data folder or a folder the agent names, replacing files of the same name there; tripo-cli keeps a task history (prompts included) and the Desktop half a record of which chat made each task, both in the plugin's data folder. The Desktop backend reads your balance and recent tasks from Tripo's API, serves models only from the plugin's data folder or your home folder, and downloads results only from Tripo's result storage; the Desktop renderer shows task previews from Tripo's short-lived result links. Through Hermes's terminal tool the skills run `hermes config path`, file-size checks and background sleep timers on chat apps, and, when asked, a preview-video renderer (headless Chromium and ffmpeg already on the machine; its first run downloads three.js 0.180.0 from npm, integrity-checked), Python's http.server on 127.0.0.1 for the web prototype (which loads three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net) and your own Blender for an optimized copy. No telemetry.

entries.name: tripscout
entries.description: Cheap city-break finder: prices flights AND lodging together across a date window, adds the ground cost of reaching each departure airport, and ranks whole trips by total cost, with lodging-type filters (hotel/hostel/apartment) and optional food and attraction estimates. Say where you leave from and it works out the airports serving you: any town on earth is geocoded on OpenStreetMap and its nearest airports with scheduled flights are found in a bundled OurAirports table (4,008 airports), with train/bus costs estimated from distance; 33 hand-checked departure presets and 49 destinations ship with it. Every result carries prefilled booking links (flight, stay, ground, airport transfer). Ships four agent tools plus a Hermes Desktop pane (desktop/plugin.js) whose backend runs the same engine as the tools. Disclosure — no API key and no account: searches read the Google Flights results page and Google Hotels' public batchexecute RPC from your own IP address with a browser TLS fingerprint, so the cities, airports, dates, traveller count and currency you search are sent to Google; a departure place that is not one of the built-in presets is also sent as a search query to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim geocoder (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) to find nearby airports; nothing else about you is sent. Prices, hotel names, geocoding results and cache keys are stored locally in SQLite under Hermes' plugin data directory. A consent cookie declaring essential-only cookies is sent, because from the EU Google otherwise answers with its "Before you continue" interstitial instead of results; no tracking-consent value is ever sent. Results include prefilled search links to Google Flights/Hotels/Maps, Booking.com, Hostelworld and Airbnb that open only when you click them. Python dependencies (fast-flights, primp, typing_extensions) are prepared in the shared plugin environment at install time with the user's consent. Nothing is booked, no card or passport data is taken, and no credentials are stored.

entries.name: tripwire
entries.description: Logs every refused agent action (a tool blocked by a guardrail or plugin, or a dangerous command denied, cancelled or timed out at approval) as one JSON line, so a no-agent cron script can send the owner one short alert. Observer only, fails open. Disclosure — appends one JSON line per refused action to ~/.hermes/tripwire/events.jsonl (owner-only 0700 dir / 0600 file), shared by all profiles (path overridable with TRIPWIRE_EVENTS): timestamp, event kind, and identifier-shaped profile, tool and rejection category or approval choice only. No message or rule snippets, arguments, commands, results, session ids or message text are stored; non-identifier values are recorded as unknown. A pre_tool_call hook reads ~/.hermes/tripwire/TEST_BLOCK and, only while that file exists, blocks the single tool it names for the single profile it names (a drill switch to prove the alarm). No network calls, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.
known_issues: A tool call the model makes outside its toolset is rejected by Hermes before any plugin hook runs, so Tripwire does not see it.
The optional notifier (scripts/tripwire_notify.py) is fetched at the pinned commit and scheduled with `hermes cron create ... --no-agent`; it is not part of the plugin directory. See README.

entries.name: true402-swap-guard
entries.description: Blocks token buys when true402 finds a honeypot or a rug in progress — one pre_tool_call hook in front of every trading tool, MCP server and terminal command (Base, Ethereum, BSC, Solana). Free edition: it never pays, holds no wallet key and has no payment code. Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Hermes approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry.

Disclosure — the pre_tool_call hook reads the command string of every tool call and the parameters of trading-named tools; when a call looks like a buy, each candidate token address and its chain (every 0x address in a trading shell command except well-known majors and an unambiguous sold token, which can include a recipient or wallet address) is sent to true402.dev's free check endpoint, with no prompts, amounts or other tool data. Uses true402's small daily free allowance; when it is used up, a token counts as unchecked and passes by default (configurable to ask or block). Blocks only on a definite danger verdict for a token being bought; a possible sale or a configured caution goes to the Hermes approval gate, and one "always" answer there silences all later guard prompts. No stored data, no shell commands, background processes or telemetry. This plugin hook(s): pre_tool_call. Requires Hermes >=0.22.0.

entries.name: trurl
entries.description: Private taste memory for Hermes with proactive hypotheses, sourced cross-theme discovery, compact context, Taste Atlas and Sunday editions. Disclosure — During new-profile setup the bundled skill proposes a weekly "Sunday edition" (20:00 local time) and, unless you say "one-off only", has the agent create a recurring Hermes cron job that runs a curation turn on your model plan every Sunday. The plugin itself only reads the cron list to confirm it, and `trurl_schedule off` plus pausing that job stops delivery. Your taste profile, feedback and history are stored locally in the plugin's data directory (trurl.sqlite3, taste-atlas.html, editions/).

entries.name: trust-ladder
entries.description: Correct your agent once and it stays corrected. trust-ladder compiles each user correction to the highest rung it can prove: a pre_tool_call guard that blocks the repeat, a check on what a write puts into matching files, a rule injected every turn, or human review through Hermes's own approval prompt. A model-proposed guard is installed only if it matches the mistaken call and spares the corrected one, regexes are profiled against ReDoS before install, verifier commands gate "done", and a ledger counts every catch (/teach, /trust, /verify). Disclosure — local only: stores rules, tasks and a catch ledger (matched snippets, redacted, no full arguments) under <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/trust-ladder/; no network, no telemetry, no credentials or env vars read; verifier commands run only through Hermes's terminal tool (normal approvals apply); the model can add rules but only the user can disable or remove them; guards are best-effort pattern matches, not a sandbox.

entries.name: truthgate
entries.description: Deterministic final-turn verification for newly introduced Python stubs and common embedded-secret patterns, using pre-edit baselines and at most two corrective continuations. Standard-library-only, fail-open, and no network, subprocess, LLM, approval-bypass, or core-patching behavior. Disclosure -- reads only changed-file paths supplied by Hermes (including an absolute changed path outside the session directory), persists sanitized finding metadata in Hermes's profile-scoped plugin data without raw secrets or source text, and can produce false positives or false negatives. Disclosure — reads every file the agent edits (including paths outside the working directory) to compare it with a pre-edit snapshot, can make the agent continue up to two extra times per turn (extra model cost), and stores finding metadata (file path, line, kind; no source or secret values) in its plugin data directory.
entries.title: TruthGate
known_issues: Deterministic patterns can produce false positives and false negatives.
Unsupported mutation tools, missing baselines, unreadable or binary files, non-UTF-8 files, and files over 1 MiB fail open.
Corrective continuations depend on model compliance and can add inference cost; identical findings are suppressed and changed finding sets are bounded to two continuations.

entries.name: ttsbuddy
entries.description: Native TTS Buddy speech provider using the existing TTS Buddy CLI, with offline voice selection, MP3 generation, Hermes voice-message conversion and exact-job recovery, plus terminal-only account deletion through CLI 0.16.0+. Disclosure — runs the user-installed `ttsbuddy` CLI (argument array, speech text on stdin), which sends the text and voice settings to TTS Buddy, downloads the hosted audio and uses the account's quota. Credentials come from the profile's `TTSBUDDY_API_KEY` secret or, when the user selects `cli_config_dir`, from that CLI profile's own saved login, which the CLI may read and update. The model-callable `ttsbuddy_recover` tool downloads an existing job to a new MP3 path the model chooses (never overwrites). The terminal command `hermes ttsbuddy account delete` can permanently delete the TTS Buddy account, its hosted files and identity, and cancel subscriptions, after `--yes` and a fresh email code entered at a hidden prompt or protected stdin.
entries.title: TTS Buddy
known_issues: Account deletion is terminal-only, requires CLI 0.16.0+ and an explicit persistent cli_config_dir; speech credentials do not authorize deletion.
Use fresh unique output filenames/stems: successful Hermes delivery and same-stem Opus conversion can replace files outside the provider's no-clobber checks.
MP3 source audio only; no PCM streaming. A local timeout does not cancel an accepted hosted job; use ttsbuddy_recover with the exact job ID.

entries.name: turn-completion-nudge
entries.description: Nudges the agent to continue when a turn ends prematurely (planning or announcing next steps it has not done). Fail-open: never blocks a turn. Disclosure — when the user sets `send_turn_text: true`, clipped turn text (about 1,200 chars of the user request and 1,500 chars of the assistant reply) is sent to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai, billed to the user's OPENROUTER_API_KEY) after each turn to score whether to nudge; with `amos_fallback: true` the same text may go to the keyless Amos/Scira API (api.amos.scira.ai). Both are off by default.
known_issues: free-model rot: default scorer model `respan/span-01-lite-20260925:free` may be delisted upstream - pin or monitor (see the scorer_model config description in the plugin repo)

privacy default: an absent `send_turn_text` is treated as opted out (dormant) in every context; an explicit `send_turn_text: true` egresses clipped turn text (~1200-char user request + ~1500-char assistant message) to the OpenRouter lane when a key is set — the keyless Amos/Scira fallback is a SEPARATE opt-in (`amos_fallback`, default false)
nudge chains are capped at 2 consecutive nudge-driven turns per session (nudge text recognized on the next request); afterwards the hook stays silent until a real user turn arrives

entries.name: tusk
entries.description: Hermes long-term memory on Walrus mainnet (decentralized storage on Sui) through the official Walrus Memory SDK: encrypted inside the relayer's TEE, owned by your key, survives wiping or reinstalling Hermes, and the same on every machine and for other agents on the same account. Recall before each turn, turn capture, built-in memory mirroring and pre-compression saves; a crash-safe, rate-paced SQLite write outbox with a receipt and public Walruscan proof per memory; a Tusk dashboard tab (semantic search across namespaces, live write queue, one-click verification that downloads the blob from a public Walrus aggregator and checks it is ciphertext); /tusk and hermes tusk (status, recall, proofs, verify, namespaces, import, flush, export, restore). Secrets are redacted before anything is queued. Disclosure — each turn's user message (as the recall query), finished turns (for fact extraction), built-in memory entries and tusk_remember facts are sent over HTTPS to relayer.memory.walrus.xyz (or MEMWAL_SERVER_URL) signed with MEMWAL_PRIVATE_KEY / MEMWAL_ACCOUNT_ID; verify downloads blobs from aggregator.walrus-mainnet.walrus.space; queued writes (until sent) and receipts are kept in plugin-data/tusk/outbox.db (0600); one in-process background writer thread; dashboard routes sit behind the dashboard auth gate; no shell commands, no subprocesses, no telemetry.
entries.title: Tusk
known_issues: The Walrus Memory relayer has no per-memory delete yet (whole-namespace erasure only), so removing a built-in memory entry does not delete its Walrus copy.
Writes are paced (about 6 per minute) and take 20-30 s each; one-shot hermes chat -q runs usually exit before the queue drains. Queued writes go out on the next run or with hermes tusk flush.
The dashboard tab appears after hermes plugins enable tusk (memory providers are otherwise activated through memory.provider only).

entries.name: twitch-assist
entries.description: Put your Hermes in your Twitch chat as a co-host: viewers type !ask (or @mention the bot) and get a real agent answer in chat, and the broadcaster or a mod can run Backseat Mode, a chat vote whose winner becomes Hermes's next task. Stdlib only (asyncio IRC over TLS). Disclosure — network calls go only to irc.chat.twitch.tv:6697 (TLS IRC) and https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/validate; the Twitch token is read through Hermes's secret scope; private by default (broadcaster and TWITCH_ALLOWED_USERS ids only), and opening it to every viewer needs TWITCH_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true, after which non-broadcaster requests are dropped unless both memory flags are off and platform_toolsets.twitch is pinned; viewer turns are limited to web search by a pre_tool_call guard; Hermes injects the owner's SOUL.md persona into every gateway session (skip_context_files does not remove it on 0.23.x) and MEMORY.md/USER.md unless the memory flags are off, and allowlisted viewers are served even then, so run the bot in a dedicated Hermes profile with an empty SOUL.md and memory off.
entries.title: Twitch Assist
known_issues: Needs a Twitch chat OAuth token with chat:read and chat:edit (a dedicated bot account is recommended).

platform_toolsets.twitch is REQUIRED to be pinned to [search, no_mcp] in config.yaml. A plugin cannot change the platform default toolset, so an unresolved adapter would otherwise fall back to the full default (a pre_tool_call guard still blocks every tool except web_search, and a warning is logged at connect).

Hermes injects the owner's SOUL.md persona into every gateway session prompt, and skip_context_files does NOT remove it on Hermes 0.23.x; MEMORY.md and USER.md are removed only by memory.memory_enabled and memory.user_profile_enabled set to false. A plugin cannot switch this off, so run the Twitch bot in its own Hermes profile (hermes profile create) with an empty SOUL.md and no memory. An external memory provider may also record Twitch turns.

Private by default: only the broadcaster and TWITCH_ALLOWED_USERS ids can use the bot. TWITCH_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true is an explicit opt-in and fails closed: non-broadcaster requests are dropped unless both memory flags are false and platform_toolsets.twitch is pinned (the reason is logged once).

Toolsets registered by other plugins are added by Hermes to any platform list (no no-plugins setting); their calls are blocked in Twitch sessions by the guard, but their schemas may still be shown to the model.
The first answer after a gateway start can take up to a minute (Hermes cold start); later answers take seconds.
In-turn gateway notices are matched by English text; outside a pending turn nothing is posted in any language.
A running Backseat vote is lost if the connection drops or the gateway restarts.
Reconnect after a real network drop is proven only against a local fake IRC server.

entries.name: twitchboard
entries.description: Free streamer tools through TwitchBoard's MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://www.twitchboard.net/mcp, no sign-in, no keys): exact image sizes for Twitch, YouTube, Discord, Kick and TikTok, username ideas that follow each platform's rules, Minecraft and Roblox name checks, ready-to-paste OBS widget URLs, OBS bitrate settings, Discord fancy text and timestamps, and Twitch, Kick and TikTok earnings estimates. Bundles one skill on when to use each tool. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to www.twitchboard.net, which logs the tool name and client name only. check_username forwards the requested name to Mojang (or the PlayerDB mirror) and Roblox. All twelve tools are annotated read-only. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: twring
entries.description: Call your Hermes from your phone and let it call you back, through the Twring app (iPhone and Android): live two-way voice calls and typed chat in one Hermes conversation, dangerous-command approvals answered by voice or tap through Hermes's own approval card, and a phone ring when a scheduled job delivers. Twring does the speech; Hermes keeps its model, memory and tools. Disclosure — while the gateway runs, one outbound WebSocket to the linked Twring server (api.twring.com by default, or the TWRING_SERVER you set) carries call and chat turn text in, and Hermes's replies, approval questions (command preview and reason) and cron results out, plus the name and success or failure of each tool Hermes runs while a call or chat turn is in progress (never its arguments or output; Hermes's tool hooks are global, so a tool another chat runs at the same moment can be reported too; the pre_tool_call and post_tool_call hooks never block or change a tool); anyone signed in to the linked Twring account drives this Hermes as its owner and can approve one dangerous command at a time by voice or tap through Hermes's own approval card; HTTPS calls to the same server link the account (sending this computer's hostname as its name), post replies to the chat and ring the phone (cron results ring by default; TWRING_RING_ON_DELIVERY=false turns it off); one link token (TWRING_TOKEN), saved by `hermes twring link` through Hermes's .env route; no files of its own, no shell commands, no telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: twzrd-intel
entries.description: Pre-spend seller screening for x402 agent payments: a free allow/warn/block preflight and merchant card for a payTo address, plus verification of TWZRD signed receipts against the pinned TWZRD Ed25519 issuer key (fixed in the plugin, never a tool argument). Python standard library only, no API key, no wallet. entries.name: uk-companies
entries.description: UK Companies returns one sheet. Disclosure — Names and numbers to api.company-information.service.gov.uk as HTTP Basic with COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY when set. entries.name: ultimate-dashboard
entries.description: A customizable dashboard page for Hermes Desktop and the Webapp, with 16 cards: approvals you can answer, running sessions, scheduled jobs with a 7-day timeline, job results, plan usage, spend, tool activity, health, services, machine stats, logs, agent memory, skills, files made, Workers and live tasks, plus Quick launch shortcuts. Arrange cards into views, save templates, and the layout syncs between Desktop and the Webapp. English and Arabic (RTL); follows the Hermes theme. Disclosure — no telemetry and no third-party requests; the page talks only to your Hermes gateway. Runs one command through cli.exec, `hermes usage --provider <slug> --json`, which asks each signed-in provider for plan usage. Its backend opens state.db read-only (session titles, token and cost columns, tool names and outcomes, MEDIA file paths; no message text), and reads the size of memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (never the text), the dates in skills/.usage.json, the newest file in cron/output/<job id>/, Hermes' Worker transcripts in cache/delegation/live/ (goals, tool names and one-line command previews; never result text), and machine stats via psutil including the hostname. Stores the layout in plugin-data/ultimate-dashboard/state.json. Answers an approval only when you click, with once or deny, never always. Anyone signed in to your dashboard can see what the cards show.

entries.name: umami-digest
entries.description: Each morning one letter arrives with yesterday's pageviews, visitors, day-over-day change, the top five pages by pageviews, and a surge flag from the Umami instance you already run, with no model. Umami 3.4.1 returns expanded paths 500 at a time in visitor order. The letter sends limit 500 and walks offset until a short page, or 20 pages, then ranks by pageviews. A day that hits the cap says the five are the top 5 among the first N paths. Disclosure — GET only to the origin in UMAMI_URL with Authorization Bearer UMAMI_API_KEY; plain http only to loopback, otherwise https; the plugin downloads nothing at runtime; umami_digest is read-only and asks for no approval; anyone you allow on a gateway can call it; turn a surface off with hermes tools; hermes umami-digest schedule writes a no-agent cron script that costs 0 tokens with no daily cap; empty stdout sends nothing; run unschedule before removal; a leftover job stops with hermes cron remove <id>; after hermes plugins remove, hermes cron remove <id> leaves scripts/umami-digest.py and you delete that file yourself; state stays in plugin-data/umami-digest; schedule uses hermes_constants.get_hermes_home, so an update can stop it.

entries.name: unbl0ck
entries.description: One queue of everything blocked on you: live agent prompts, pairing requests, blocked Kanban cards and chats on any platform that ask you something. Answer Kanban cards in place; optional one-line summaries and Ask send item text to your configured model through ctx.llm (both can be turned off). Disclosure — reads every local profile's chat history (state.db, read-only), profile titles and pending pairing requests (through Hermes's PairingStore, never the codes) to build one queue, records live clarify/approval prompt text in its plugin data, and can comment on and unblock Kanban cards when you answer one; by default sends each new queue item's text (other profiles' chats included) to the configured model for a one-line summary, and card data on Ask (turn off with `bluf_enabled: false` / `ask_enabled: false`); on messaging platforms `/unbl0ck` replies with a count only; uses Hermes's internal Kanban modules, so a Hermes update can break it; no network of its own, no shell, no credentials.

entries.name: unblockbruecke
entries.description: Cards to unblock yourself or your agent, drawn by you when you are stuck and by Hermes when its tool calls keep failing. Disclosure — With auto-draw switched on (off by default), once 3 of the last 5 tool calls in a turn failed it adds one card's text to that failing result (one card per turn), so the model reads it, and adds one line naming the card after that turn's reply (not in scheduled jobs, webhooks, the API server or single-query runs); the agent's deck tool can import a deck from any file path and export a .yaml deck file to any folder you name (attended chats only, never overwriting a non-deck file); the page's settings switches save through a short `hermes config set` child process.
entries.title: Unblockbrücke
known_issues: Auto-draw is off by default. Switch on "Hermes draws when stuck" in Settings, Plugins, Unblockbrücke, Agent settings.
With Hermes on a server, install the plugin on the Desktop computer too, on the same version: Desktop loads the Unblockbrücke page from its own computer.

entries.name: unbrowse
entries.description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. entries.name: understudy
entries.description: Audition cheaper models on your real Hermes history before you switch. Understudy replays a sample of your past decisions (replies and tool calls) on candidate models through Hermes's own credentials, has a blind judge compare each step with what your current model actually did, and reports how often each candidate could have taken over (with a 95% confidence interval), its critical misses, a per-category breakdown and projected monthly cost. Two tools, /understudy, hermes understudy, and a Desktop page with an inline scorecard. Disclosure — reads this profile's session history read-only; sends redacted excerpts of past conversations (plus, by default, an excerpt of the agent's system prompt; `include_persona: false` stops it) to the candidate models and the judge model you pick, through ctx.llm on your existing provider credentials; each audition is capped by budget_usd only when Hermes reports the call cost (unpriced models are bounded by the sample size, not the budget); the agent tool spends without its own confirmation prompt (the bundled skill tells the model to dry-run and ask first; /understudy asks unless --yes); reads Hermes's local models.dev cache (active profile, then the default root) for list prices; writes run records and reports under plugin-data/understudy; runs a background worker thread only while an audition runs; requests the llm.model_override and llm.provider_override capabilities; no telemetry, no other network calls.

entries.name: underwriting
entries.description: Commercial real estate underwriting that shows its work: rebuilds net operating income from the rent roll and T-12 instead of trusting the broker's claim, runs buy-box tests against a DSCR-sized loan, returns the counter-price at which a rejected deal actually clears, sweeps price to find where a deal flips, models a hold period, and returns null rather than inventing a number the document never stated. Seven deterministic tools plus an /underwrite command and a skill. Extraction reads a document the user names (local path or URL) and is audited back against the document text: every figure is matched to the line it came from and marked verified, and a citation the document cannot support is reported. The arithmetic is pure Python standard library with no network calls and no third-party packages; only extraction calls the host model, and only a URL passthrough fetches anything over the network. Writes are confined to the plugin's own data directory: memos and extraction audit trails take a bare filename under <data_dir>/exports/, and the deal book is JSON under <data_dir>. Document input is treated as untrusted, because it is: local reads go through Hermes' read block list with no $HOME fallback, and URL input is limited to public http(s) with every redirect hop re-checked. Not investment advice.

entries.name: undo-effects
entries.description: Puts back files an agent deleted or overwrote: before write_file, patch and destructive terminal commands (rm, mv, cp, redirects, tee, sed -i, find -delete) it saves the affected files to a local store and lets the tool run unchanged; /undo-effects lists the effects and restores them, refusing to overwrite later edits unless forced and keeping a safety copy so a restore can be undone. Disclosure — no network; reads the contents of the files and directories a covered tool call is about to change; writes unencrypted copies of them under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/undo-effects/ (files named like credentials, anything inside .ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .docker, .kube, .azure and .gcloud, files above 50 MB, node_modules, .venv and .git are skipped and reported); the same folder also keeps the paths and the first 100 characters of each terminal command, with secrets masked on a best-effort basis; runs no shell command and no background process; never blocks, rewrites or approves a tool call, and runs the tool even if a snapshot fails; covers the local terminal backend only; no telemetry.
entries.title: Undo Effects
entries.capability_summary: undo-effects (community, maintained by Moodtuner997) Puts back files an agent deleted or overwrote: before write_file, patch and destructive terminal commands (rm, mv, cp, redirects, tee, sed -i, find -delete) it saves the affected files to a local store and lets the tool run unchanged; /undo-effects lists the effects and restores them, refusing to overwrite later edits unless forced and keeping a safety copy so a restore can be undone. Disclosure — no network; reads the contents of the files and directories a covered tool call is about to change; writes unencrypted copies of them under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/undo-effects/ (files named like credentials, anything inside .ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .docker, .kube, .azure and .gcloud, files above 50 MB, node_modules, .venv and .git are skipped and reported); the same folder also keeps the paths and the first 100 characters of each terminal command, with secrets masked on a best-effort basis; runs no shell command and no background process; never blocks, rewrites or approves a tool call, and runs the tool even if a snapshot fails; covers the local terminal backend only; no telemetry. This plugin middleware: tool_execution. Platforms: linux, macos, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7.

entries.name: undo-send
entries.description: Undo Send for your agent: outward-facing actions (hermes send / imsg send messages to Telegram, Slack, Signal, SMS and others, app connector and MCP writes, git push, gh pr/issue create, npm publish, curl POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) wait in a short grace window before they run, so you can cancel them from a Desktop status-bar countdown (Undo / Send now), by replying "undo" in Telegram or another gateway chat (owners listed in undo_senders), or with /unsend. On undo the agent is told the action never ran and not to retry it. Disclosure — delays matching outward-facing tool calls (messages, MCP/connector writes, git push, gh/npm/twine publishes, hermes send, curl POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) by up to window_seconds (default 20), including unattended/cron runs, never indefinitely; makes no network calls of its own, reads no credentials and sends no telemetry; stores a one-line summary of each held action (URLs reduced to their host), its chat origin, timestamps and outcome in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/undo-send/pending.db; reads inbound gateway text before gateway auth only to match a bare "undo", acting only for owners listed in undo_senders (empty by default, so chat undo is off) and only on actions held from that same chat; /unsend from the CLI, Desktop or an admitted chat user cancels the newest held action in any session; runs no shell commands or background processes; a classifier error runs the tool unchanged.

entries.name: unibaseio-membase
entries.description: Long-term memory for you and your AI from Membase (membase.com, by Unibase): one memory every connected AI shares. Searches the user's Membase memory before each turn (8 s, fail-open) and adds membase_search, membase_save and membase_profile. Disclosure — user prompts are sent as search queries to the Membase API (api.app.membase.com); with the opt-in capture_turns setting the user's messages are saved there too; on a Hermes build with memory.user_store: provider, what Hermes' memory tool records about the user is saved to their Membase profile instead of USER.md. MEMBASE_API_KEY comes from the Hermes secret scope; the only local file is $HERMES_HOME/unibaseio-membase.json. No background processes, shell commands or telemetry.

entries.name: unicode-ref
entries.description: @unicode: context references that spell text out character by character for the model: @unicode:"text" attaches a table of every character of the quoted text (code point, Unicode name, category) with notes on what does not show on screen: invisible characters and their positions, text-direction controls, spaces other than the ordinary one, Unicode tag characters (decoded), words that mix Latin letters with lookalike Cyrillic, Greek or fullwidth ones, and private-use or unassigned code points; @unicode:U+200B describes up to 20 code points (name, category, UTF-8 bytes, decomposition); the TUI and Desktop composer suggest characters by name. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself, using Python's unicodedata; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials; register() only adds the @unicode: reference provider

entries.name: unifi
entries.description: See which UniFi devices and clients are online, and check Wi-Fi, switch ports, and ISP health in Hermes. This unofficial plugin reads from UniFi Site Manager and, if configured, your local console. It cannot change the network. Disclosure — sends your UniFi API key to UniFi's cloud API at api.ui.com and, if you set a console host, your Network API key to that local UniFi console; reads only, and can show device and client details (IP addresses only if you turn that on) to the agent.
entries.title: Hermes for UniFi
known_issues: If the Site Manager ISP feed fails, Diagnostics can omit those checks without a warning. Open ISP Health to check the feed directly.

entries.name: unified-inbox
entries.description: One inbox for the user's WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn messages through their own Unipile account (API v2): a synced local copy, search in any language, triage with a reason for each chat, memory of people and open items, drafts in the user's own writing style, scam warnings, plans offered for the calendar, translation, a people radar and a spoken brief, plus an Inbox page in the web dashboard and Hermes Desktop. Every send and reaction goes through Hermes's own approval prompt (a pre_tool_call hook) and is refused when approval would be skipped (yolo mode, approvals off, cron), under hard pacing limits. Disclosure — calls the Unipile API (api.unipile.com) with the user's key; Unipile reaches WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn through unofficial access, which may break those platforms' terms. Every send and reaction goes through Hermes's own approval prompt and is refused under yolo mode, approvals off or unattended runs; the model may attach any file the user can read (key and login files excepted), and each file is named in that prompt. Optional and off until configured: a cloud embedding provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere or Voyage AI) that receives message text, the user's own Supabase project for two-way sync (api.supabase.com once, to create tables), a private iCal address read for busy times, a webhook receiver on 127.0.0.1 that accepts only HMAC-signed Unipile deliveries, and alerts injected into a chat the user picks. Runs a background sync thread by default that summarises, drafts and translates new messages with Hermes's model (capped per day); text sent to a model or provider has one-time codes, passwords and card, bank and ID numbers removed first. Stores chats, messages, memory and a send log in SQLite under the plugin's data folder; secrets come only from Hermes's secret store. Calls Hermes internals that are not a stable plugin API (tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio for voice notes, private tools.approval checks). No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-update.

entries.name: unitares
entries.description: Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.

entries.name: unraid
entries.description: Read-only Unraid monitoring for Hermes Desktop: server metadata, array capacity, Docker containers, virtual machines, and grouped alerts. Disclosure — sends fixed GraphQL queries to the user-configured Unraid host and stores a VIEWER key through Hermes secret scope; no telemetry, background process, shell, SSH, MCP, or mutations.
entries.title: Unraid
known_issues: When Hermes Desktop uses a remote backend, install the Desktop part locally and the Agent/backend part on the remote Hermes host.
The Unraid GraphQL schema can vary by release. The monitor was previously tested with Unraid 7.3; the 0.3.2 transport changes were tested offline.

entries.name: upstash-box
entries.description: Terminal backend that runs Hermes terminal, execute_code and file tools in an Upstash Box cloud container, paused and resumed by name per task or created per session and deleted when it ends. Disclosure — requires an Upstash Box API key (UPSTASH_BOX_API_KEY); every command and the files the file tools touch are sent to Upstash Box; your Hermes skills, cache and skill-registered credential files are uploaded to ~/.hermes in the Box and skill and cache files changed in the Box are copied back to your machine; SDK telemetry is turned off; Boxes are created, paused and deleted in the key's account and billed to it; persistent mode keeps one paused Box per task (each Hermes Desktop chat is its own task), and paused Boxes count toward the account's Box limit; if the Upstash account has GitHub connected, every Box holds those GitHub credentials in ~/.git-credentials, and every Box has an UPSTASH_BLOB_TOKEN environment variable, both readable by the commands the agent runs; dangerous-command approval is skipped inside the Box.

entries.name: upstash
entries.description: Long-term memory and searchable chat history for Hermes on Upstash Redis Search, with hybrid recall (keywords and meaning) and no separate vector database. Recalls related memories into each turn, saves every session as a searchable transcript, mirrors the built-in memory tool (adds, corrections and removals), and gives the model upstash_memory_save / upstash_memory_search / upstash_memory_forget and upstash_chat_search. Memories use the same keys as @upstash/agentkit-sdk, so they are shared with AgentKit apps on the same database. Works on the Upstash Free plan (one search index). Disclosure — memories and full chat transcripts are written to the Upstash Redis database you configure (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN) and sent to it over HTTPS on every turn. Memory text and each recall query are embedded by Upstash Redis Search's managed embeddings in that database; chat transcripts are not embedded, and the plugin contacts nothing else. Telemetry is opt-in and off by default: UPSTASH_HERMES_TELEMETRY=1 adds SDK, Python version and platform tags to request headers sent to that same database.

entries.name: us-air-rules
entries.description: Does this EPA air rule apply to me? Screen a plant or a household against Title 40 and get applies / check with EHS / skip, with the citation. Compare two plant scenarios with the same bundled pack (changed inputs, changed verdicts, missing facts, unchanged count) without contacting the network. Read or search current eCFR Title 40 text, list recent EPA Federal Register documents for one part, and look up a state's EPA-approved SIP rules in 40 CFR part 52. Disclosure: HTTPS GET only to www.ecfr.gov (title currency, section or subpart XML, part structure, search words) and www.federalregister.gov (part, optional term, date window, document type). No API key. The citation and the search words are sent; a facility or household profile is not. usair_plant_compare makes no request and does not upload a profile. Writes public regulatory responses (JSON, with fetch time) under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/us-air-rules/cache, capped by cache_max_mb (default 100 MB). Reads only its own plugin settings. At most one request per second per host, 20 s timeout, 10 MB response cap. No hooks, no cron, no background process, no telemetry, no self-update. Screening aid, not a compliance determination and not legal advice. eCFR is an editorial compilation, not the official edition.

entries.name: usage-guard
entries.description: Keeps an agent inside its subscription allowance: refuses a provider dispatch once a subscription usage window is exhausted, so an account that allows paid extra usage stops at the wall instead of spending overage. Reads the usage Hermes already displays, holds no credentials, and never touches account or billing settings. Disclosure — refuses main-loop provider calls (including MoA turns) for the providers in `provider_keys` (Anthropic and OpenAI Codex by default) when a subscription usage window reaches `threshold_percent` (a lone Anthropic reading of exactly 100% with extra usage off is treated as possibly 1%, because Hermes's Anthropic parser scales any utilization <= 1 by 100 until hermes-agent#139916, and passes; a 100% that follows a higher reading in the same window, or any 100% while extra usage is on, refuses), and by default (`fail_open: false`) also refuses when usage data is missing, stale, unreadable, or the guard's own config is malformed; usage is read through Hermes's own account-usage fetcher (no credentials held, at most one read per source every 180 seconds by default) and cached in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/usage-guard/usage.json; a `pre_llm_call` hook adds a short usage note to the next turn's context at 80% and 90% used by default, and an opt-in (off by default) `llm_request` middleware lowers an existing output-token budget near the usage limit; both read only the cache, never the network; a `/usage-guard` slash command and a Hermes Desktop status-bar chip (polling a read-only `GET /api/plugins/usage-guard/status` route every 60 s and after each turn) report the guard's decision from the same cache, never making a usage request; a refusal is an explanatory assistant message by default (`refusal_mode: notice`); with the opt-in `refusal_mode: empty` it is an empty reply instead, so Hermes's empty-response recovery retries (each retry refused again, never dispatched) and then switches to the profile's `fallback_providers`, which the guard gates only when they are listed in `provider_keys`; auxiliary calls (compression, vision, titles, MoA advisors) are not gated. Borrowing is off by default: when `hydrate_from_paths` names files, the guard may read those JSON snapshots instead of reading the endpoint, validating every window and never writing them into its own cache.
known_issues: Multi-profile gateways: Hermes dispatches plugin slash commands in the gateway's launch profile, so `/usage-guard` can report that profile's limit and reading. The guard itself and the Desktop chip use the served profile.

entries.name: ussd-platform
entries.description: Talk to Hermes from any phone by dialling a USSD short code: no app, no data plan, no smartphone. A gateway platform for Africa's Talking-style USSD callbacks: replies are paged into 160-character keypad screens, exec approvals become numbered menus whose choices appear only after the last page of the command, answers that outlive the session wait in an inbox or arrive by SMS, and a dropped call resumes on the page it left. Ships a keypad-phone simulator served to localhost only. Disclosure — runs an HTTP callback server on 127.0.0.1:8788 while the gateway runs (the user exposes it through their own tunnel); callbacks are authenticated by a 16+ character secret in the URL path because USSD gateways do not sign requests; only when AFRICASTALKING_USERNAME and AFRICASTALKING_API_KEY are set, message text and the recipient's number go to api.africastalking.com (or its sandbox) to send SMS; USSD and SMS are readable by the mobile operator and aggregator; inboxes are in memory only; no telemetry, no shell commands, no self-update.
entries.title: USSD
known_issues: Real handsets need a USSD short code from Africa's Talking or another aggregator; the built-in simulator and the Africa's Talking sandbox need neither.

entries.name: utcp-bridge
entries.description: Lets the agent use tools described by UTCP (Universal Tool Calling Protocol) manuals: utcp_search_tools finds tools across the manuals you configure under plugins.entries.utcp-bridge.settings.manuals, and utcp_call_tool calls one directly over its own HTTP API. Native UTCP support was declined for core and suggested as a standalone ctx.register_tool plugin (#151647, #151174). Disclosure — every search or call fetches each configured manual from its URL and sends the tool request to the endpoint that manual names; only manuals you configure are contacted. A manual's $NAME variables resolve only from the Hermes secrets it lists (read with agent.secret_scope.get_secret); the UTCP library's .env and os.environ fallbacks are turned off. Only the http call template is supported, so a manual cannot make the plugin run programs. Nothing is stored on disk.
entries.title: UTCP Bridge
known_issues: Only http manuals and tools; streaming (sse, streamable_http) and MCP call templates are not offered yet.
Manuals are re-fetched on every search or call (no cache), so each call costs one extra request per configured manual.

entries.name: uuid-ref
entries.description: @uuid: context references that decode a UUID or ULID for the model: @uuid:<id> takes a UUID in any common spelling (hyphens or not, braces, upper case, urn:uuid:) or a ULID, and attaches what its bits say, read the way RFC 9562 lays them out: version and variant in words, the creation time a v1, v6, v7 or ULID carries in UTC with how long ago, the clock sequence and node of a v1 or v6 and whether the node is random or looks like a network card (MAC) address, the local id and domain of a v2, a ULID's 128 bits written as a UUID, and the Nil, Max and RFC namespace UUIDs by name; up to 10 identifiers in one reference are compared by creation time; the TUI and Desktop composer preview an identifier as you type it. Disclosure — reads only the text of the reference itself and the system clock, using Python's re, datetime and fractions; nothing is looked up; no network, no files read or written, no subprocess, no credentials read; the plugin keeps no copy of the identifiers, but the @uuid: reference and the decoded text become part of the message sent to your model provider and saved in the session history; register() only adds the @uuid: reference provider.

entries.name: vail-agent-assurance
entries.description: Find, test and fix risky behaviors in your AI agents with the VAIL Agent Assurance Engine: upload an agent's source to scan it for behavior risks and generate probes, then run those probes against the agent locally, graded as VAIL grades them, fix what fails and rerun to prove the fix. Works on LangGraph, Hermes and OpenClaw agents, including your own Hermes profiles. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): the hosted VAIL MCP server plus the agent-assurance and agent-improvement skills. Needs a VAIL account and a personal access token, set as VAIL_TOKEN (the plugin's secret setting, kept in the profile's .env). Disclosure — every call goes to agents.projectvail.com with your VAIL token; scanning uploads the agent source you choose to VAIL, which stores it as that agent's source (replacing the previous upload); the agent-improvement skill downloads VAIL's grading package (a version VAIL's server chooses at run time, sha256-checked against that server's own value), installs it into a local virtual environment, runs it, and sends test messages to the agent you name. No telemetry.

entries.name: valun
entries.description: Let your Hermes agent negotiate service-for-credit deals with other agents (most listed so far are the Valun operator's test agents or its team's own), signing with its own key within limits you set; credit notes, debt transfers and set-offs recorded by a real Basis tracker anchored on Ergo testnet (amounts in nanoERG of Ergo testnet: test coins with no monetary value). Disclosure — Talks to the Valun server set in `server_url` (default https://valun.tech, run by the plugin author's Valun project), sending your participant id, locally signed offers/acceptances/credit notes/consents, deal terms and deliverables, the goals/limits your agent records, and, with the read-only `valun_check_payer` (since 0.7.0), which payer your agent is vetting, for how much and for which offer; whoever runs that server sees all of it. Since 0.7.2 the agent and owner tokens are sent only to that server: no redirect is followed, and over plain http only to a server on the same machine unless `VALUN_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP=1` is set where Hermes runs (since 0.7.3 `hermes valun join` writes the owner token to a new file, by default `~/valun-owner-token-HANDLE.txt`, and never prints it on stdout: see the Owner token note). Your handle, display name, operator name, about text, offered services (`join --services`) and the work you pay others for (`join --wants`), with your public key, when you joined and when your agent was last seen, your deal counts and what you hold and owe, are public on that server (its directory and your agent page, `/agent/<handle>`), and so is your credit policy where it runs circulating credit (the default server does): whether you take payment by debt transfer, whose notes you accept or refuse, `max_issuer_net_debt`. Its public ledger lists every credit note with its issuer, holder and amounts, and every applied set-off is public with its members' handles and the amount cleared (`GET /pilot/v1/loops`, `/loop/<id>` and each member's agent page). A budget card (an agent's owner mandate: its caps, approval threshold and objective, and the room left) is public only if its owner publishes it; the plugin has no command that does. A guarantee (since 0.6.0: your agent backing another agent's IOU to one creditor, up to a cap) is seen in full by its backer, its issuer, its creditor and the server; the counts and amounts of the guarantees a participant gave, was backed by or holds, and of the calls honored, honored late or overdue, are public in its record. With public vouches (since 0.6.2: `hermes valun profile --public-vouches on`, off unless chosen), the guarantees between your agent and agents that also chose them are public on both agent pages: who backed whom, the cap and how calls were honored, never the creditor. `hermes valun profile` (you, at a terminal) also changes the public profile fields you give it (services, wants, about, display name). Stores VALUN_AGENT_TOKEN and VALUN_SIGNING_SECRET via `hermes config set` (passed to it through the child process's environment, not its command line). Commitments go through Hermes' approval prompt by default; `hermes valun join --approvals none` (or `confirm_commitments: false`, `--yolo`, `approvals.mode: off`) lets the agent sign within your server-side limits without asking. `--approvals console` turns that prompt off too: the agent signs its offers, acceptances, guarantee offers and delivery payments without asking, and the server holds them in the owner console until you approve; nothing notifies you (only the agent's tool answers say something waits), an IOU still held about an hour after the agent signed it is never recorded and pays nothing, and a rejected offer, acceptance or IOU stays signed on the server's record. The rest, such as honoring or releasing a guarantee or loosening a limit the agent recorded (never past your mandate), takes effect at once. With `process_consents` on (set by `hermes valun join --sandbox`; off for invited joins) the client also signs, without a prompt, the net-neutral set-offs, transfers of your own debt and payments to you that your policy allows, each capped by `consents.max_PC` (50,000,000 nanoERG by default). When reviewing or sending a delivery it looks up the DNS names of links in it (no page fetch; `check_link_hosts: false` turns it off), which can tell a counterparty's DNS that you reviewed it. `join --direct-tools` sets `tools.tool_search.enabled off` in that profile. The owner's `hermes valun ergo reserve` and `redeem`, run at a terminal, ask the Valun server for a reserve's payment request or a redemption's transaction (with the agent token, also without `--broadcast`) and read what they need from the Ergo testnet node that server names (by default a public testnet node over plain http, so the node and the network path see your IP address, the boxes read and, for a reserve, your agent's Ergo testnet address); they check it and sign the transaction with the agent's own key; only with `--broadcast` is it sent: a reserve straight to that node, a redemption through the Valun server. A note can be redeemed on Ergo testnet against its issuer's reserve, in tERG, test coins with no monetary value.
entries.title: Valun
known_issues: Experimental: one test network (valun-testnet-1). Amounts are nanoERG of Ergo testnet; tERG are test coins with no monetary value. A credit note is an outstanding promise. Where the server offers circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer) or be cancelled against an equal opposite debt (set-off). A set-off's netting is committed by a tracker box, not final: it stays committed only as long as the tracker key never commits an earlier total again (https://valun.tech/trust). An issuer can back its notes with a reserve of tERG, and a creditor redeems against it (`hermes valun ergo redeem`, the owner at a terminal). The earlier pilot network (valun-pilot-1, PC) was retired on 2026-11-13: a profile that joined it must join again, in a new profile.

Consents: with process_consents on (set by `hermes valun join --sandbox`; off for invited joins), the agent's Valun client signs net-neutral set-offs, transfers of its own debt and payments to it by transfer that its owner's policy allows, by itself, before Valun tool calls that are not read-only; set-offs and payments to it also before valun_status and valun_inbox (listed in consents_signed_now). Each consent is capped (consents.max_PC: 50,000,000 nanoERG by default). Nothing runs in the background.
The Hermes Plugins settings page can show the plugin's dotted consents.* settings wrongly (it reads them as flat keys); `hermes valun status` shows the policy in force.

Guarantees (0.6.0): a backer pays a call with its own credit note to the creditor (a commitment, through the approval prompt by default). The issuer's credit note to the creditor stays as it is, since Basis changes no note without its issuer's signature, so the creditor holds both; what it later recovers from the issuer beyond the part the backer did not pay belongs to the backer, which the guarantee shows (recovered_for_backer) but does not enforce. A guarantee without `deals` covers what the issuer owes the creditor when it calls, also debt created after acceptance (the cap is the backer's exposure); with `deals` (0.6.1) it covers only what is unpaid of those deals.

Joining: `hermes valun join --sandbox` needs no invite. It makes a self-serve participant with small limits (5,000,000 nanoERG per deal, 40,000,000 owed) for 7 days, renewed while its agent is active; where the server runs the open network (the default server does) it can deal with any agent whose owner allows it, otherwise only with the always-on sandbox agents. An invited participant (`hermes valun join`, with an invite code from the Valun operator) has the limits its owner sets.

Owner token: `hermes valun join` writes the owner token to a new file, never to stdout: `--owner-token-file FILE`, or `valun-owner-token-HANDLE.txt` in your home folder (0600; on Windows an access list for only you, SYSTEM and Administrators). Before anything is sent it refuses (exit 2, `Nothing was sent`) a file that exists already or cannot be written there (to check, it makes, writes and removes that file and a probe file in its folder). If no file can be written once the join was sent, the token is shown once on stderr only at a terminal (a pseudo-terminal counts), otherwise nowhere (exit 1; the server's operator can issue a new one). The file stays until you move it, and anything running as you can read it. The token opens the owner console (limits, approvals, revoking the agent). Run join yourself at a terminal: `hermes valun` refuses inside a Hermes agent session, but not in another agent's shell.
Windows: with Hermes v0.22.7, enabling a git-installed plugin fails (WinError 3) when the Hermes home path is longer than 44 characters; use a shorter HERMES_HOME or enable Windows long paths.

The tools call the Valun server you configure (default https://valun.tech, run by the Valun project) and look up link hosts in DNS; `hermes valun ergo` also reads from the Ergo testnet node that server names, and `reserve --broadcast` sends its transaction there.
entries.capability_summary: valun (community, maintained by fitzss) Let your Hermes agent negotiate service-for-credit deals with other agents (most listed so far are the Valun operator's test agents or its team's own), signing with its own key within limits you set; credit notes, debt transfers and set-offs recorded by a real Basis tracker anchored on Ergo testnet (amounts in nanoERG of Ergo testnet: test coins with no monetary value). Disclosure — Talks to the Valun server set in `server_url` (default https://valun.tech, run by the plugin author's Valun project), sending your participant id, locally signed offers/acceptances/credit notes/consents, deal terms and deliverables, the goals/limits your agent records, and, with the read-only `valun_check_payer` (since 0.7.0), which payer your agent is vetting, for how much and for which offer; whoever runs that server sees all of it. Since 0.7.2 the agent and owner tokens are sent only to that server: no redirect is followed, and over plain http only to a server on the same machine unless `VALUN_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP=1` is set where Hermes runs (since 0.7.3 `hermes valun join` writes the owner token to a new file, by default `~/valun-owner-token-HANDLE.txt`, and never prints it on stdout: see the Owner token note). Your handle, display name, operator name, about text, offered services (`join --services`) and the work you pay others for (`join --wants`), with your public key, when you joined and when your agent was last seen, your deal counts and what you hold and owe, are public on that server (its directory and your agent page, `/agent/<handle>`), and so is your credit policy where it runs circulating credit (the default server does): whether you take payment by debt transfer, whose notes you accept or refuse, `max_issuer_net_debt`. Its public ledger lists every credit note with its issuer, holder and amounts, and every applied set-off is public with its members' handles and the amount cleared (`GET /pilot/v1/loops`, `/loop/<id>` and each member's agent page). A budget card (an agent's owner mandate: its caps, approval threshold and objective, and the room left) is public only if its owner publishes it; the plugin has no command that does. A guarantee (since 0.6.0: your agent backing another agent's IOU to one creditor, up to a cap) is seen in full by its backer, its issuer, its creditor and the server; the counts and amounts of the guarantees a participant gave, was backed by or holds, and of the calls honored, honored late or overdue, are public in its record. With public vouches (since 0.6.2: `hermes valun profile --public-vouches on`, off unless chosen), the guarantees between your agent and agents that also chose them are public on both agent pages: who backed whom, the cap and how calls were honored, never the creditor. `hermes valun profile` (you, at a terminal) also changes the public profile fields you give it (services, wants, about, display name). Stores VALUN_AGENT_TOKEN and VALUN_SIGNING_SECRET via `hermes config set` (passed to it through the child process's environment, not its command line). entries.name: vape-coach
entries.description: Local-first webcam vape tracker and taper coach. A MediaPipe watcher spots hand-to-mouth puffs plus the exhale, and the target gap between vaping sessions grows ~10%/day after a 1-day baseline. Hitting early climbs a nudge ladder: a roast, a sarcastic (never real) PR threat, a protein-shake order, then jumping jacks the same watcher counts on camera by itself. Nag-only: never blocks a request, never gates a tool, no tool that can touch code. Desktop pane with camera Start/Stop and a live rep counter, a status-bar countdown, pet/toast roasts, /vape and three agent tools. Disclosure — uses the webcam only while the watcher runs (after the user clicks Start camera, which starts `python -m vapecoach.cli watch` as a child process, or while `hermes vape watch` runs in a terminal); frames stay in memory and are never written or sent; stores timestamps, scores and counts in the plugin data dir; downloads three SHA256-pinned MediaPipe models from storage.googleapis.com on first start; the Desktop half polls the plugin's own local API every 3 s. No LLM calls, credentials or telemetry.
entries.title: Vape Coach
known_issues: Needs a webcam. Snacking, face-scratching and phone calls can still trigger false alarms; `hermes vape undo` voids one and its penalty.

entries.name: vault-view
entries.description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Hermes Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, optional per-conversation workspaces, pinned tabs, explicit selection quoting, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are independent opt-ins and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host and records that folder in ~/.hermes/vault-view-root.json; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in; the optional vault_view_present_note agent tool is on by default for anyone who can use the agent on any platform and copies any requested Markdown note from that vault into the Hermes document cache (copies are not cleaned up) to deliver it as a file card.

entries.name: vaultknox
entries.description: Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

entries.name: vector-platform
entries.description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Hermes becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `hermes gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `hermes gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

entries.name: veille
entries.description: Fraud and validity checks for Hermes through the Veille API: emails (with an SMTP inbox check), domains, IPs (VPN, proxy, Tor, data center), phone numbers, EU VAT numbers and IBANs, plus ECB exchange rates. Disclosure — sends the values you check to api.veille.io with your VEILLE_API_KEY, and calls use Veille credits (1 to 5 per call, stated in each tool description). veille_qualify_email has Veille contact the address's mail server. Reads the key only through Hermes's secret scope. Registers 9 tools, no hooks or middleware, writes no files, starts no processes, has no telemetry or self-updater, and uses only the Python standard library.

entries.name: vellum
entries.description: Vellum: Hermes draws inside the paper. Highlight a passage in an arXiv paper (HTML version) in Hermes's browser and your own Hermes session gives you the gist like a friend at a whiteboard, talking while it sketches a live, interactive figure right under the paragraph (built from the paper's own example and numbers); follow-ups, typed or spoken, change the same sketch. Adds tools (vellum_draw / vellum_look / vellum_clear / vellum_read), a skill, hooks on turns started from the paper, a Desktop plugin and dashboard routes under /api/plugins/vellum/. Disclosure — reads arXiv HTML pages (arxiv.org/html, ar5iv) with Desktop's per-site consent and saves the open paper's text when you switch it on; puts Visualize/Ask drafts into your chat box for you to send (never submits a turn itself); the highlighted passage and nearby paper text go to your configured model as part of that turn (the full paper when Hermes calls vellum_read, and a picture of the figure when it calls vellum_look), marked as web text; runs model-written drawing code only in a sandboxed iframe (opaque origin, CSP default-src none with scripts pinned by hash plus 'unsafe-eval' for the drawing steps, WebRTC constructors removed; best effort, since CSP does not cover a frame navigating itself); tools reach the card through plugin events (plugin.vellum.*); speaks with Hermes's own text_to_speech, one call per spoken sentence and at most 60 per turn (Edge TTS by default, an online service; a paid provider bills each sentence); stores the text of the 20 most recently opened papers, the ids of the 50 most recent figure cards opened, the current Ask passage and short-lived request/voice files under plugin-data/vellum; no telemetry, no credentials, no external CLIs, no downloads.
