entries.name: verand
entries.description: Your own website's rankings, Search Console and GA4 data, AI-answer visibility (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Perplexity and Claude), site issues and compliance checks, plus drafts and fixes you approve, through Verand's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://app.verand.ai/mcp, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with one workflow skill. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to Verand's hosted server (app.verand.ai), which reads and writes the signed-in user's own Verand account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned commit. Write tools exist, including drafting, editing, research that draws on the user's Verand plan allowance, and, only when an account owner has switched it on in Verand and the user approves the exact text, publishing an article or applying a fix to their live WordPress or GitHub site; the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs. No tool deletes content or clears a hard-tier compliance block. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.15.2 through npx (Node.js 20.18.1+), which opens a browser and a localhost callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. Requires a Verand paid plan or 7-day trial.

entries.name: vercel-agent-desktop-support
entries.description: Vercel Agent Desktop Support: operate Windows apps through the accessibility tree instead of the screen. Reads a window's real UI as roles, names, states and refs, then clicks, fills a field, selects an option, toggles a checkbox, scrolls, sends a key combo, and manages windows and the clipboard. Actions are semantic and headless by default, so they do not take focus, move the cursor or synthesize keystrokes, and they fail closed rather than guess. desktop_install downloads the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release for the running Windows target, verifies the archive against a sha256 pinned in the plugin, and proves the install by running version and status. Disclosure — the plugin runs the agent-desktop executable as a child process with arguments it builds, using the copy it installed or one already on PATH, in the npm global folder, AGENT_DESKTOP_BIN or the bin_path setting (those are not checksum-checked); starting or closing a program, installing the binary, and the first call that auto-installs a missing binary (auto_install, off by default) go through Hermes's approval prompt (Hermes Agent 0.18.1 or newer), while key presses, field values and clipboard writes into any window, a terminal included, run without a prompt; desktop_install is the only tool that uses the network, downloading the official vercel-labs/agent-desktop release from GitHub, and a release without a digest pinned in the plugin is refused; it reads window titles, labels, field values and the clipboard on request, which can contain private content. Windows only.

entries.name: verifyum
entries.description: Privacy-preserving file proofs on Solana Mainnet through Verifyum (no account, no key): the agent hashes a file on the user's machine, anchors only a domain-separated commitment, follows the proof until it is finalized, and verifies public proofs, with one skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure: the package contains no code and declares two MCP servers. verifyum is Verifyum's hosted server at api.verifyum.com (Streamable HTTP). verifyum-local runs npx -y verifyum-mcp@0.1.1, which downloads that exact npm release (MIT, JavaScript source, published by aisenseapi) on first start and needs Node.js 20 or later. verifyum_anchor_commitment and verifyum_create_proof_from_file write a real, public and permanent Solana Mainnet transaction, so plugin.json marks both servers untrusted and Hermes asks first. The file tool reads only regular files inside the directories listed in VERIFYUM_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS, which the package does not set, so it refuses every path until the user sets it. It writes a private draft the user must keep. Verifyum receives only the commitment, the idempotency key and proof IDs, never the file, filename, raw hash, nonce or private manifest. Tool arguments, local paths included, still reach the user's model provider through the session. Verification also reads from a public Solana RPC endpoint. At most ten new anchors per IP address per rolling hour. The tool lists come from the servers at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover them.
entries.title: Verifyum
known_issues: The file tool stays off until VERIFYUM_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS is set for the verifyum-local server.
verifyum-local needs Node.js 20 or later with npx available.

entries.name: vet402
entries.description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call. ALLOW, and a WARN that only says vet402 has not bought there yet, let it run. Any other WARN, a URL with no record for the paying HTTP method, and a vet402 outage ask for approval, and the call is refused when nobody can answer (yolo, approvals off, cron). vet402 only knows endpoints in public x402 and MPP discovery, so an unlisted URL asks. By default only mpp_fetch is checked, and a payment made inside Hermes HTTPX traffic is not seen. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host, port and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) and its HTTP method to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; a missing record or a vet402 outage asks for approval and is refused when nobody can answer, unless VET402_UNKNOWN=allow lets it pay; while enabled, its skill adds one line to the skills index of every session.

entries.name: vibe-relay
entries.description: Vibecoding without burning your best model. Sets Hermes `delegation.backend` to a quota-aware strategy: when remaining usage is above a threshold (default 51%) the parent model keeps the work (`self`); otherwise each `delegate_task` is routed to a configured cheap executor (provider+model or profile). When the executor lane is selected, a `pre_tool_call` hook blocks the parent from `patch`/`write_file` and obvious terminal writes (`sed -i`, `>`/`>>`, `tee`) so coding work must go through `delegate_task` (children never blocked; `enforce_executor_lane` default true). At `stop_used_percent` (default 90% used) the same hook blocks parent `delegate_task` and writers, auto-parks once per reset window (handoff + one one-shot cron), and injects `parked until …; do not start new work` via `pre_llm_call`. Every task must carry `allowed` path globs and a `gate` command — exit 0 alone is not done; `post_tool_call` captures gate PASS bound to a working-tree hash, `pre_verify` continues the turn until a fresh PASS exists, `vibe_accept` checks changed paths ⊆ allowed. Night shift for large projects left overnight (`vibe_night_start|log|status|arm|report`, `/night`): plan, queue, decisions and timeline in a self-ignored `<repo>/.vibe-relay/night-<stamp>/`; `pre_tool_call` refuses new dispatch after the hard stop or at the quota reserve (running work is not killed); `post_tool_call` keeps a parent liveness stamp so continuation wakes exit instead of becoming a second orchestrator; wakes (early checkpoint, quota reset, report) are armed once from the live session via `cronjob_manage` after a quota preflight on the provider cron will use (the plugin never sets a job's model); the morning report is assembled from records. Ships an Agent Workshop of 15 portable skills, including `night-shift` and `lean-executor-orchestration` 2.0, registered as `vibe-relay:<name>`. Vendors DEV Framework tools (`df_init`, `df_check`, `df_nav`); `df_check` returns the gate command for the agent to run via `terminal` (approvals apply). Disclosure — only documented Hermes surfaces; quota via `fetch_account_usage(..., read_only=True)` at most once per 180s (15s negative TTL) cached per provider in `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/vibe-relay/`, which stores metadata only (no gate commands, gate output, task text or raw usage payloads); night shift writes its plan, queue, decisions, timeline and morning report into the working repo under a self-ignored `.vibe-relay/night-<stamp>/` (refused inside Hermes home); `vibe_night_arm` creates up to three one-shot cron wakes through `cronjob_manage` with the repo as workdir after a quota check, never sets the job's model, provider or delivery, and refuses to run inside a cron job; the night hook blocks new `delegate_task` dispatch after the hard stop or at the quota reserve without stopping running work; park skips its resume cron inside cron runs unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling`; handoff slugs confined to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` under `docs/`; `df_init`/`df_nav` run the plugin's vendored scripts with `python -I` and a scrubbed child env, `df_nav` never executes the target's navigate.py, and `df_init` refuses Hermes home, `$HOME`, `/` and protected dot folders; template scripts may call `git`/`gh` only when the user or agent runs them; no credential-file reads; no YOLO shells.

entries.name: vibeleak-atlas
entries.description: Owner-approved VibeLeak website assessments in a native Hermes Desktop workbench. You approve each scan before it runs, private evidence and fix-plan drafts stay on your machine, and read-only local folder review is opt-in. Website assessments need an optional VibeLeak owner API key (Pro plan). Desktop-only, inside the plugin SDK surface; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or required environment variables. Disclosure — website assessments you approve send the target hostname to VibeLeak (www.vibeleak.app) with your VibeLeak owner API key (Pro plan); the optional hosting map, after a separate approval, sends up to 12 assessed hostnames to Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS and maps them with a bundled DB-IP country database; local folder review reads only a folder you grant and makes no network calls; results are stored under the plugin's data directory.
entries.title: VibeLeak Atlas
known_issues: Website assessments need a VibeLeak owner API key, which is part of the Pro plan. Local folder review needs no key or account.
Rescan comparisons stay non-comparable until VibeLeak returns coverage and version context, which some deployments do not return yet.

entries.name: vibeline
entries.description: Show agent work as rails in the TUI, web and CLI. One lane per agent, tool calls and acceptance-criteria results as marks. Disclosure — `hermes vibeline web` serves a local web UI (127.0.0.1 by default; a token is required for any non-loopback client) that shows every Hermes session transcript on this machine and can open terminals running `hermes --resume` and rewind sessions (soft-deleting later messages via core's `/rewind`); `--peer` URLs you add receive and forward these requests to other machines, and `--read-only` disables open/rewind.

entries.name: video-xray
entries.description: Drop a video file into the chat composer and get a structured report: segment-wise frame observation by whatever vision-capable chat model you already configured (local llama.cpp/Strata or cloud), timestamped dialogue from R2T2, Whisper, or any OpenAI-compatible cloud ASR, and a frame gallery of the key moments inside the job detail. Exports the report as Markdown or as a MiniMax-H3 integrated multimodal description prompt. Ships the R2T2 engine worker source (the same code the panel uses); the heavy R2T2 runtime binaries and any Whisper models are user-supplied, nothing else is downloaded. Spawns ffmpeg/ffprobe and local ASR worker subprocesses; network calls go only to the user's own configured inference and cloud-ASR endpoints, never to third-party services; background analysis jobs run as worker threads tracked in a local job ledger. The panel is pure @hermes/plugin-sdk React and user-visible text goes through ctx.i18n. Disclosure — runs ffmpeg/ffprobe and local ASR worker processes on your computer, and by default starts an analysis job for every video you attach when you press send (turn off "Analyze attached videos on send" in the panel); video frames go to your configured Hermes chat model and audio goes to the cloud ASR endpoint you set, if any; the faster-whisper engine downloads its model weights from Hugging Face on first use when they are not already cached; the cloud ASR key you save in the panel is stored in plain text in an owner-only (0600) file in Hermes' data folder.

entries.name: visor
entries.description: Live holographic canvas for AI agents: the visor_push tool pushes visual blocks — sections, markdown findings, clickable todos, tables, KPI stats, charts, code, images, audio and video — to an infinite-canvas webpage that updates in place over SSE (the page is never rewritten), so agents SHOW work instead of dumping it in chat. Turnkey: the plugin ships its own server, no separate install. Disclosure — on first use, if nothing is listening on localhost:8900, the plugin auto-starts its bundled server as a long-running background process (bare-python subprocess by default, state in ~/.local/share/visor or VISOR_DATA; `docker compose up -d` when VISOR_DOCKER=1), restarted if unreachable, and the child gets only a minimal environment (PATH/HOME/LANG/TZ, VISOR_* values, plus DOCKER_* and proxy vars for compose); it listens on 127.0.0.1:8900 by default, and VISOR_HOST opts in to a non-loopback bind that is refused unless VISOR_TOKEN is set; /api/* and /media/ are always gated by a per-install token (0600, <state>/visor-token), which the page receives automatically only on a loopback bind (otherwise open the page with ?token=...); the page refuses framing and foreign Host headers; the bundled live module polls user-pushed http(s) URLs every 2s (10s timeout, 1MB cap, no redirects) and refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses unless they are listed in VISOR_LIVE_LOCAL_HOSTS; the chat module forwards card sends to a configured Hermes webhook (VISOR_CHAT_URL + VISOR_CHAT_SECRET) and does nothing until those are set; raw-html cards render in a sandboxed iframe whose postMessage bridge can only read board state and edit blocks on the current board; visor_push copies local image/audio/video files the model names (no dotfile paths) into its media dir; no credentials beyond its own VISOR_* settings, no telemetry.

entries.name: visual-gate
entries.description: Lets Hermes check the web UI it just built. Drives a real headless Chrome, diffs the page against a stored baseline and audits WCAG 2.2 AA on the same render, then returns one PASS or FAIL with changed regions, computed contrast ratios and exact CSS selectors. A page that failed to load is an error, never a pass, and text it cannot measure is reported for a person to check.

entries.name: visual-oracle
entries.description: Makes a UI claim measurable before an agent reports success: captures a page as a baseline, then pixel-diffs later renders and answers PASS, FAIL or REVIEW with independent change regions (bbox, pixel count, area, density), a diff image, an overlay and per-region crops. Waits for document.fonts.ready, an optional selector and two identical frames so a capture is settled, records the Chrome version and viewport that produced it, and refuses to guess when rendering never stabilises. An optional visual change contract declares expected changes and protected regions so a declared change can pass while an undeclared one fails; selectors name locations, not meaning. Masks accept rectangles or CSS selectors and are applied before capture, a selector matching nothing is an error, and masks may not cover more than half the viewport. Only public http and https are rendered: file://, data:, private ranges and the cloud metadata address are refused on the URL and on every request the page makes, redirects included, with localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 allowed and VO_ALLOW_HOSTS for anything else. Disclosure - renders the URL you give it in a local Chrome over the DevTools protocol (no Selenium, Playwright or pip install), so the page's own network requests happen in that browser; reads the PNGs it produced and writes baselines, diffs, overlays, crops and report.json under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/; runs no shell command of its own and no background service; the baseline is never updated automatically; image input must be a real PNG and a header claiming more than 8192 px on a side is refused before decompression; no telemetry. Disclosure — renders the http(s) URL you give it in a local headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol (no Selenium, Playwright or pip install), so the page's own network requests happen from your machine; refuses non-http(s) schemes and private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses on the URL and on every request the page makes (localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 allowed, more via VO_ALLOW_HOSTS); launches Chrome with --no-sandbox only when running as root, without user namespaces, or with VO_NO_SANDBOX=1; reads the PNGs you point it at and writes baselines, diffs, overlays, crops and report.json under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/visual-oracle/; a failing or REVIEW check keeps the agent's turn open through the pre_verify hook; runs no shell command of its own and no background service; the baseline is never updated automatically; no telemetry.

entries.name: vitam
entries.description: Turn a modded PS Vita into a voice-powered Hermes handheld: hold-to-talk mic with faster-whisper STT on your own machine, an agent turn through your Hermes gateway, TTS reply spoken through the Vita speaker, and optional rear-camera vision frames. LAN-only; the bridge makes no outbound calls except to your configured gateway. Disclosure — runs a bridge daemon that listens on all network interfaces (port 8643 by default) so the PS Vita can reach it on your LAN; every request except a reachability ping needs the pairing token, and voice audio and camera frames are processed on your machine and sent only to your configured Hermes gateway.
known_issues: Requires a modded PS Vita or PS TV (HENkaku/h-encore 3.60) and a machine on the same LAN to run the bridge daemon.
Speech recognition and TTS use small local models: intelligible, not studio quality.

entries.name: vitrail
entries.description: Live GLSL shaders in the chat. Ask for a visual and the model writes a Shadertoy-style fragment shader that animates inside the reply in Hermes Desktop, with the sliders, colour pickers and switches it declared as annotated uniforms. Before vitrail_render returns, the Desktop half compiles the shader with WebGL 2 on the user's GPU and reports the verdict, so a compile error goes back to the model with the driver log and the model fixes it in the same turn; a still frame comes back too, for models with a vision tool. The card is drawn through a tool media renderer where Desktop has one and through a ::vitrail transcript directive where it does not (Desktop 0.22.5). Other surfaces (Telegram, CLI, TUI) get a standalone HTML player of the same shader. Adds a gallery page with hover-to-play tiles, GLSL copy and 1920x1080 PNG export, the vitrail_render and vitrail_library tools, the vitrail:shader-studio skill, and post_tool_call / transform_llm_output hooks that append the shader's delivery line (MEDIA file or directive) when a reply lacks it. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry; GLSL written by the model runs on the user's GPU through WebGL 2 in the Desktop window; files are written only under plugin-data/vitrail (per shader: source, standalone HTML player, GPU report, a 640x360 JPEG still, exported PNGs); the still's path is given to the model, which may open it with its vision tool; while a Desktop window is open its half calls the plugin's own local route once a minute so the tool knows a GPU is listening and which transcript surface it has, and vitrail_render then waits up to 6 s for the verdict.
entries.title: Vitrail
known_issues: The live card needs Hermes Desktop 0.22.5 or later with the plugin's Desktop switch on in Capabilities → Plugins (it is off by default); other surfaces get the standalone HTML player.
On a Desktop without tool media renderers the card is drawn from a ::vitrail directive; a messaging platform that shares the chat while that Desktop is open shows the directive as a line of text.
GPU verification needs a Desktop window connected to the Hermes that runs the agent; without one the shader is saved unverified and compiles when it is shown.
Shaders are single-pass and procedural: no textures, buffers or audio inputs.

entries.name: vivarium
entries.description: A living artificial-life world inside Hermes. Real tool calls drop nutrients into a 48x48 cellular-automaton dish; creatures carry genomes, forage, reproduce, mutate and go extinct on their own; every skill the agent learns births a new species. Deterministic, mathematically grounded, private. Disclosure — Vivarium starts a background thread in every Hermes process that polls its own state about once per second to repaint the terminal, finds the controlling terminal by reading `/proc/<pid>/environ` and `/proc/<pid>/stat` of parent processes (terminal-type variables only, never stored), and `/vivarium serve` runs an unauthenticated read-only gallery on 127.0.0.1 that shows your installed skill names and the dish (`--keep` leaves it running until Hermes exits).

entries.name: voice-gate
entries.description: Reviews changed prose with 75 mechanical rule families and optional contextual review against the complete humanizer skill and its references. Settings keep everyday controls visible and collapse Vale, bots, and individual rules. Slow inventory requests allow up to two minutes and offer retry; the page includes five-row exceptions and Vale installation guidance. Revision requests allow at most two opportunities and compare protected spans and quantities. Prose em dashes are flagged while bullet label separators and empty table values remain allowed. Reads the changed prose paths reported by Hermes; manual tools can check supplied text. Model review is off by default and sends reviewed documents to the configured Hermes provider when enabled. It provides editorial judgments, not authorship proof. Vale is optional; status, check, and install request approval before starting a program, turn-time findings use only a binary approved that way, and Vale runs with a short environment rather than the host's. No project-file writes or core overrides. Simple PDF text extraction has no OCR. Disclosure — reads the changed prose files Hermes reports after each turn and any text or paths given to its tools; optional model review (off by default) sends reviewed documents to the configured Hermes provider; optional Vale support downloads a sha256-pinned Vale release from GitHub into <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/voice-gate/ only after approval, and runs Vale (status, check, install, and turn-time advisory checks on changed files) only for a binary approved through Hermes' approval prompt and recorded by digest, with a minimal environment.

entries.name: voice-unleashed
entries.description: A hands-free voice interface to Hermes, for any model, on your own VoiceManager server. The plugin serves a web page, so any device with a browser, a microphone and a speaker is the client, a phone, a tablet on a wall or a spare laptop: you talk, Hermes answers out loud while the model writes, and you talk over a reply to stop it. The page shows the conversation, each tool call and the model's reasoning, speaks approval prompts and the model's questions and takes spoken answers, and picks up any session of the profile or starts a new one. Hermes Desktop and Webapp chats get a voice toggle. Disclosure - adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN); the session list and history are read from the profile's own Hermes state and nothing is stored. It registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Hermes use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction (start the reply with a short spoken summary) only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on. The Desktop half ships switched off. No Python dependencies beyond Hermes core (websockets, httpx); VoiceManager's client is vendored. Disclosure — adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token carried in the page URL; whoever holds the token is the platform's one gateway user (owner), is made its slash-command admin, can list, resume and read the history of every session of the profile, and answers approval prompts by voice or by tapping the page's allow-once/session/always/deny buttons, where a single spoken approval word (including "always") or a short approval phrase such as "go ahead", "sure", "yeah" or "allow" (approve once) is sent as the reply, so a misheard word can approve a command; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN), and nothing is stored; it registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Hermes use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on; it reads a few undocumented core helpers and the gateway's session DB read-only, so a Hermes release can break it; the Desktop half ships switched off.
entries.title: Voice Unleashed
known_issues: Needs a VoiceManager server (0.7.0 or later). 0.9.1 or later is recommended: the notices for barge-in that is not ready and for an answer that was not heard need 0.9.0, and 0.9.1 fixes gaps in the reply audio between sentences.

A browser gives the microphone only to a page it treats as secure. On the machine Hermes runs on, localhost works as it is. From another device, either put HTTPS in front of the page (tailscale serve or a reverse proxy; the README has both) or add an exception for the page's address in the browser, for example Chrome's flag unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure. HTTPS is not required when the browser has such an exception.

Disclosure - adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN); the session list and history are read from the profile's own Hermes state and nothing is stored. It registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Hermes use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction (start the reply with a short spoken summary) only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on. The Desktop half ships switched off. No Python dependencies beyond Hermes core (websockets, httpx); VoiceManager's client is vendored. Disclosure — adds the voice_unleashed gateway platform, which listens on VOICE_UNLEASHED_HOST:VOICE_UNLEASHED_PORT (default 127.0.0.1:8765) for the page, its session list and its WebSocket, all behind the VOICE_UNLEASHED_TOKEN access token carried in the page URL; whoever holds the token is the platform's one gateway user (owner), is made its slash-command admin, can list, resume and read the history of every session of the profile, and answers approval prompts by voice or by tapping the page's allow-once/session/always/deny buttons, where a single spoken approval word (including "always") or a short approval phrase such as "go ahead", "sure", "yeah" or "allow" (approve once) is sent as the reply, so a misheard word can approve a command; microphone audio and reply text go only to the VoiceManager server you set (VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_URL, bearer VOICE_UNLEASHED_VOICEMANAGER_TOKEN), and nothing is stored; it registers stream observers (on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_session_end), which makes Hermes use streaming requests on every surface, tool observers (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call) that run for every conversation and never block a call, and pre_llm_call, which adds one instruction only to a Desktop or Webapp chat that has voice on; it reads a few undocumented core helpers and the gateway's session DB read-only, so a Hermes release can break it; the Desktop half ships switched off. Known issues: Needs a VoiceManager server (0.7.0 or later). 0.9.1 or later is recommended: the notices for barge-in that is not ready and for an answer that was not heard need 0.9.0, and 0.9.1 fixes gaps in the reply audio between sentences.; A browser gives the microphone only to a page it treats as secure. On the machine Hermes runs on, localhost works as it is. From another device, either put HTTPS in front of the page (tailscale serve or a reverse proxy; the README has both) or add an exception for the page's address in the browser, for example Chrome's flag unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure. entries.name: vornik-companion
entries.description: Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN (and VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN for memory); broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall, mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon, and asks the daemon to stop recalling (not delete) a mirrored entry that Hermes removes or replaces (/vornik-memory lists and /vornik-forget forgets what Vornik keeps); artifact tools expose only named outputs allowed by the approved workflow from completed runs and read bounded text or return short-lived binary download links from the daemon; task diagnosis tools (offered only when the daemon advertises companion-progress) return a broker task's execution events and closed error classes as the daemon serves them to a broker key; hermes vornik approvals on writes security.approval.transport (and vornik_companion.approval_namespace) to Hermes config, after which Hermes's own dangerous-command prompts (the redacted command text) are sent through the local vornikctl agent host-approval to the daemon and answered on the paired phone, any failure or a Vornik outage denying the command unless transport_fallback: builtin is set, and the plugin never decides itself; hermes vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to Hermes config; the daemon's engineering guidance is added as a system prompt section (vornik.rules); with VORNIK_MEMORY_TOKEN, short hints are appended to the result of the tool call that caused them (after a commit, a design-document write, a failed test run), behind a marker naming Vornik, which hints fired and whether they were followed is reported to the daemon, and the vornik_companion_delegate tool reads the local files the model names (at most 20 files and 2 MB; symlinks, hard links, credential files such as .env, and anything under the Hermes home refused) and sends them to the daemon for a review or a memory ingest.

entries.name: vt-check
entries.description: VirusTotal reputation for downloads and links. Files are hashed locally and looked up by SHA-256 — never uploaded. URLs are checked read-only, and archives are inspected in memory for path traversal, decompression bombs, double extensions and document-named executables. Disclosure — network calls to www.virustotal.com (SHA-256 hash, URL, domain and IP lookups with the user's VT_API_KEY); vt_check_url with submit=true, which the model sets, POSTs the URL to VirusTotal for a new scan and makes it public there; vt_check_file reads (hashes and inspects in memory) whatever local path it is given, and the file itself is never uploaded; no shell, no background processes, no telemetry; lookup cache in plugin state; credential read via get_secret.

entries.name: waiting-on-you-desktop
entries.description: Desktop panel listing every question your agents are waiting on you to answer, across all chats and profiles, sorted by urgency and importance. Yes, No and Reply can be answered in place, with five seconds to undo, but only for a chat whose composer is visible in this Desktop window; other chats get Open instead. Later snoozes an ask from any chat. Disclosure: sends chat excerpts, task context, your priority note and recent priority corrections (as examples) to your configured Hermes model, and to an optional decision provider you choose; see the README for full details. Reads every local profile's state.db and projects.db read-only, plus Hermes config.yaml; saves its plugin settings through Hermes; runs a background scan in the gateway. Optional SSH reads, chat archiving and local action-handler commands are all off by default. Handlers run with a minimal environment plus only the variable names you list, and can do whatever their command does. No telemetry.
entries.title: Waiting On You
known_issues: Inline answers work only for chats open in this Desktop window; chats on another machine or profile get Open instead.
Satellites are not included in this catalog build and will return only once Hermes ships public token routes (upstream PR #151760, issue #143507).

entries.name: wake-me-when
entries.description: Wakes you the moment something happens in live audio or video that has no feed: a keynote reaching pricing, an earnings call giving guidance, a Twitch boss fight, a council agenda item, a launch at T-minus 1 or a scrub. /wakeme <url> when <condition> (or just ask the agent) watches YouTube Live, Twitch, HLS, RTSP or a bundled demo:// stream with local speech recognition (faster-whisper, Hermes's own stt-whisper extra), on-screen OCR and an optional vision check, and posts an alert in the same chat with the quote, the stream time and a jump-in link; replying 'clip' hands you the moment as a video, 'not it' teaches the judge and keeps watching, 'every time …' alerts on each occurrence, /wakeme catchup summarises what you missed, and /wakeme <recording> <question> searches recordings for timestamps; one slash command in all. Cheap cue matching runs first; one LLM judge call (its own auxiliary task, wakeme_judge) confirms, citing transcript rows so times never come from the model; a per-watch hourly budget falls back to unconfirmed cue alerts instead of missing silently. Disclosure — runs one ffmpeg (plus streamlink for Twitch, HLS and web-media links) per active watch in its own process group, killed on stop, unload and exit, and one shared speech-recognition thread; contacts only the stream hosts you give it (via yt-dlp, streamlink, ffmpeg), Hugging Face once for the Whisper model, and Hermes's package index when it installs the stt-whisper extra; sends transcript excerpts, on-screen text and (only for visual conditions) keyframes to your configured model through ctx.llm; external tools (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, streamlink, tesseract, a JS runtime for yt-dlp) are user-installed and detected, never bundled; subprocesses use argv lists, -- before user URLs, an explicit ffmpeg -protocol_whitelist per source and a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale, XDG and proxy/CA settings; no API keys or tokens); refuses private network addresses, including the stream URLs yt-dlp and streamlink resolve a link to, unless allow_private_network is on; direct HLS and web-media links are fetched by streamlink through a loopback proxy on 127.0.0.1 (random port, per-source random credentials) that checks every connection, playlist entries and redirects included, and dials the address it checked, unless you set your own proxy; and local files from messaging chats unless they are in allowed_media_dirs; keeps a 3-minute media buffer per watch, clips for 2 days and transcripts for 7 days under its plugin-data; while a chat has watches, its pre_llm_call hook adds a one-line note naming them to the user's turn; optional allow_gateway_injection (off by default) lets it ask the agent to attach the clip right after an alert (one agent turn on your main model) and hand an alert it could not post to the agent; DRM streams are not supported; no telemetry.

entries.name: wakeshift
entries.description: Wakes your Hermes chats when Wakeshift-enabled MCP servers you've added have news for them: a price drop, a finished build or a reply starts a new turn in the chat that asked for it, even while it's idle, framed as outside information rather than as you. Works for API server (gateway) and CLI chats. Disclosure — contacts only the Wakeshift servers it trusts (https://app.wakeshift.ai unless you set plugins.entries.wakeshift.settings.issuers): fetches their signing keys, exchanges signed beacons from MCP tool results for each chat's stream link, holds those streams open in background threads while Hermes runs, and acknowledges delivered messages; no telemetry. entries.name: wallpaper-theme
entries.description: A Hermes Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/hermes-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @hermes/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG_*_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.

entries.name: warden
entries.description: Defensive security operations plugin for Hermes Agent, built on one rule: model-facing tools read and request, they never configure. A deny-by-default scope engine decides what may be touched before anything runs; scopes are created only by the operator (the hermes warden CLI), never by the model, and adapter directories are operator config, never tool input. Vulnerability assessment runs two engines (Grype and Trivy) over one canonical SBOM from Syft and records their disagreement as finding confidence instead of hiding it. Sigma rules evaluate over the event store through sec_campaign, osquery host telemetry feeds the same store, and a deterministic correlation engine groups actors into campaigns; the anchored membership view (measured precision 1.000, recall 1.000 on the validation corpus) is the only view allowed to justify defensive action. Investigations answer only with citations to stored evidence; uncitable claims are dropped and counted. Containment is a policy-enforced plan engine (approval classes, blast radius, TTL, rollback) whose execution is disabled in this build; apply mode is refused. The agent's own actions are written to a redacted ledger and a hash-chained audit log. Dry run by default. Disclosure — Warden runs operator-installed scanner binaries (nuclei, trivy, grype, syft, osquery; version-attested against their adapter manifests at run time, with an optional operator SHA-256 pin, never bundled) as local subprocesses with a scrubbed environment, only against targets in operator-created scopes; a hostname target is authorised by name and resolved by the scanner at run time. It connects only to those targets and, when configured, to threat-intelligence providers, stores no credentials, and executes no containment action in this build.

entries.name: warm
entries.description: Personal finance dashboard and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server at https://app.warm.io/mcp for reviewing bank balances, spending, recurring bills, budgets, goals, net worth, findings, and confirmed credit card benefits, plus preparing transaction and budget updates you approve in Warm. Bundles three workflow skills: financial-checkin, organize-finances, and card-benefits. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration only. Requires a Warm account and OAuth 2.1 sign-in (hermes mcp login warm); no API key or client secret is stored in the plugin. Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local executable code, binaries, hooks, telemetry, or self-updater; every tool call goes over HTTPS to app.warm.io/mcp. Warm's bank connections are read-only via Plaid and cannot move money. Read-and-write grants expose write tools (describe_operation, invoke_operation, request_handoff) that preview changes and require explicit approval in Warm by default; the package marks the server untrusted (trust: untrusted), so Hermes asks before running non-read-only tools and refuses them in unattended runs. The remote tool inventory is served at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: wavebots
entries.description: Verified AI bots for Hermes, by Wave OS. Browse the official Wave bots from the bots.theta store (Checker, Tally, Planner, Maker and more); each one is checked on the Theta blockchain on your computer (name record, listing, rules, mascot and every knowledge card, fingerprint by fingerprint) before it's marked Verified. Add one and it becomes its own Hermes bot (a wave-<name> profile in your Bots list, with its mascot), answering from its checked cards on your own AI model with code, terminal, file and web tools turned off, re-checked daily. An optional Wave OS bot key lets you ask the real bot on Wave, with Hermes approval for every question. Disclosure: never signs or sends transactions, and needs no account for browsing, checking or adding bots. Network calls go only to Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only name and card reads) and, only if you set a Wave OS bot key and ask the real bot, app.oswave.io (your question to the bot). The optional Wave OS bot key (limited and revocable, spending limit you pick, default 0 TFUEL) is a Hermes secret: declared as config_schema secret WAVE_OS_TOKEN, entered in Hermes's plugin settings, read with get_secret; the plugin never stores it (Disconnect keeps only the key's SHA-256 fingerprint in $HERMES_HOME/wavebots so it stays off here). Creates and removes only its own wave-* Hermes profiles; reads Hermes's profile and plugin lists locally. A background thread re-checks added bots once a day. Opens app.oswave.io in the browser to get a key. No telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating. Disclosure — reads Theta's public RPC eth-rpc-api.thetatoken.org (read-only) and, only if you set the optional Wave OS bot key (a Hermes secret, WAVE_OS_TOKEN), sends your questions and a free key check every 10 minutes at most to app.oswave.io, where a paid bot answer can spend TFUEL from your Wave OS account up to the limit you set on the key, each paid ask after Hermes approval and never from cron; creates and removes its own wave-* Hermes profiles (tools off, SOUL.md built from on-chain card text), rewrites an added bot's SOUL.md from a background re-check once a day, keeps only key fingerprints (never the key) in $HERMES_HOME/wavebots for Disconnect, opens app.oswave.io in your browser to get a key; never signs transactions, no telemetry, no shell commands, no self-updating.

entries.name: waypoint
entries.description: Session status for Hermes Desktop: a thin bar next to every sidebar session with four states — Working (remembers your next step), Waiting on someone (who/what plus a follow-up reminder), Done (outcome plus a fresh-start handoff) and untracked. Suggests 3 next steps per session (instant quick ideas from the chat, opt-in AI ideas from the auxiliary model, priority colours) with one-click Ask, a Power up button that asks a strong model for sharper ideas on demand, and Mark complete to stop suggestions. Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Hermes llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (Hermes default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Hermes log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Hermes reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Hermes llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title_generation (Hermes default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 (registered by __init__.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint_ideas / waypoint_ideas_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Hermes log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Hermes reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them. entries.name: wearos
entries.description: The whole Hermes gateway on a Wear OS watch: the watch enrolls its own tailnet node, pairs with a gateway-minted 6-digit code, and talks to a private tailnet lane from then on — every agent, streaming answers, mid-session tool-call approvals, cron-run notifications, and replies spoken out loud in a voice cloned from ~3 seconds of reference audio, synthesized on your gateway's CPU. A desktop pane runs the checklist (APK, pair, enable) with per-agent voice dropdowns and readiness lights. Parakeet STT and the TTS engine arrive as checksum-pinned source builds at first use — nothing pre-bundled, no telemetry, no calls home after setup. Disclosure — pairing mints single-use Tailscale enrollment keys and `hermes watch setup --fix serve` runs `tailscale funnel --bg --https=443` (mounting the claim door at the root of your node's :443); the plugin runs a loopback claim door (Funnel-fronted, answers only /pair/*) and a private HTTP lane on your tailnet IP for paired watches; checking an agent in the pane lets paired watches receive that profile's API_SERVER_KEY, and un-pairing rotates it (hot for named profiles; for the default profile a watch-initiated unpair restarts the gateway); the optional voice-in/voice-out installers build pinned source from github.com, install Python packages from pypi.org into private venvs, and download multi-GB model weights from huggingface.co (the gated neuphonic/neucodec codec needs a Hugging Face token and loads at its latest revision; the "set agent voice" pane button sets tts.provider to wearkit-gateway); once installed, one resident ~3.4 GB TTS worker stays loaded and the plugin kills any other idle `air_runner.py --serve` process on the machine; cloned-voice reference recordings are stored under the plugin's data dir.

entries.name: web-forage
entries.description: Self-hosted search and extract backend for Hermes. Forage is a small self-hostable service (Docker, GPL v3) that serves web_search and web_extract plus a forage_full_extract tool for full-page text, using a static/browser hybrid strategy server-side. Set FORAGE_URL to your own instance; no third-party API key and no hosted account. Disclosure — every web_search, web_extract and forage_full_extract call goes to the Forage instance set in FORAGE_URL (default http://localhost:3672), which fetches the requested pages itself and may render them in a headless browser on that host; the optional FORAGE_API_KEY is sent to it as a Bearer token; private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata targets are refused by Hermes' URL safety and website policy in the plugin and again by the service after each redirect, unless the Forage config sets extract.allow_private_targets.

entries.name: webgraft
entries.description: Local page and document reading for web_extract, and the pages opened for the answer, as clickable sources. Asks for approval before risky tools once a conversation has read the web, and before Hermes's keyless rescue sends a page or a search to an outside service. What it downloads, runs and stores: see 'What it does, for review' in the README. Disclosure — downloads the URLs web_extract is asked to read, from this machine with Hermes's own User-Agent (HermesAgent; the browser sends the same), and each site's /llms.txt once per hour (on by default, setting llms_txt), through Hermes's SSRF-safe client (private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses refused on every redirect hop; with an HTTP(S) proxy configured, where Hermes's guard leaves hops to the proxy, webgraft checks each redirect target itself; results report the final URL so Hermes re-checks it; before the browser opens a page, webgraft resolves its host, checks every address and pins Chromium to that address, a host with any non-public address gets no browser, and a browser view that ends on a non-public address or on another site is dropped; requests made by the page's own scripts and assets in the browser are not checked); `setup` also checks the SearXNG URL it is given and reads two test pages on iana.org; `setup` optionally creates an isolated `hermes pm` environment with Crawl4AI, which drives Hermes's own Chromium (`hermes pm install chromium` if missing; the plugin downloads no browser), which opens a page only when its download has no text, or every page the site served with setting `browser: always`; each Crawl4AI read is a child process (at most 3 at once per Hermes process, 60 s cap, stopped with its Chromium on timeout or when Hermes cancels the call) that starts that Chromium headless with a DevTools port on 127.0.0.1 and a temporary profile, checks TLS certificates, runs the page's scripts and loads its assets, keeps the browser profile and Crawl4AI's log and cache in a temporary folder that webgraft creates and removes (its own folders left by an earlier, interrupted run are removed after an hour); each document is converted by anydoc in a child process (60 s cap, stopped if Hermes cancels the call); `setup` installs Hermes's `doc-extract` extra if missing, and its `ddgs` extra when DuckDuckGo search is chosen; `setup` optionally creates an OCR environment (RapidOCR, onnxruntime, pypdfium2) whose first run downloads about 32 MB of OCR models from RapidOCR's official modelscope.cn repository, checked by SHA-256, and each scanned PDF is then read in a child process (100 s cap, stopped if Hermes cancels the call); appends a short note (about 110 tokens) to each user message (setting `remind`); once a conversation has read web content (web_search, web_extract, x_search, browser tools, MCP tools, hosted connector tools, pages attached with @url:, vision_analyze / video_analyze on a URL, a terminal command or execute_code script holding an http(s) URL, tools a script runs, a subagent that read the web), sends every tool that is not read-only (terminal, code, browser, file writes, memory, messages, subagents, session_search, unknown tools (a tool_call bridge call is guarded as the tool it runs, and one Hermes cannot resolve is left to Hermes's own error), read_file / search_files outside the folders where Hermes keeps fetched pages, and vision_analyze / video_analyze on a local file) to Hermes's own approval prompt through the pre_tool_call approve directive, refused where nobody can answer such as -Q or cron (setting `tool_guard`: ask by default, block, off), because a web page can hold instructions aimed at the assistant; in a Kanban worker (HERMES_KANBAN_TASK, where nobody can answer), these stay free: the board reads, the tools that hand its own card on, write_file / patch / read_file / search_files inside the card's workspace (HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE; a relative path, or a blank search path, is pinned to that workspace through the pre_tool_call modify directive), read_file of the files its parent cards handed on (artifacts), and a terminal command whose words all stay in that workspace (file and text utilities, or a program with a version flag alone; no URL, expansion, heredoc or script run), whose workdir webgraft sets to that workspace through the pre_tool_call modify directive, Hermes's own command checks running on it as usual; a worker whose own card, a parent card or a recent card listed in its first message was worked after a web read starts guarded; a tool call that cannot be tied to a conversation is guarded as soon as any conversation in the process has read the web; when webgraft cannot read any page of a call, it keeps those pages from Hermes's keyless rescue (web.keyless_rescue, which would send their URLs to Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl or Keenable), and asking for such a page again goes to Hermes's approval prompt first; after a search that the rescue served because the search backend failed, the next searches go to the approval prompt for up to 10 minutes, though that first rescued search has already gone out (setting `keyless_rescue`: ask by default, block, off; under --yolo or approvals off Hermes approves by itself); keeps the ids (no content) of guarded conversations, at most 1000, in plugin-data/webgraft/web_sessions.json, so the guard holds after a restart and after Hermes compresses the history, and the Kanban cards worked after a web read as empty files named after their board and card id in plugin-data/webgraft/kanban_cards (at most 2000); a continuation session or subagent inherits its parent's mark; `setup` writes web.search_backend, web.extract_backend, skills.auto_load and SEARXNG_URL, recording replaced values and the Chromium path under plugin-data/webgraft; `status` reads the model, fallback, auxiliary, web, TTS and STT settings and SEARXNG_URL to list what can leave the machine, and changes nothing; page-reading child processes get a minimal environment, never Hermes's API keys; `setup` optionally raises web.extract_char_limit (only on a yes; the replaced value is restored by `uninstall`); no page text is kept, only the URLs, titles and failure reasons of recent pages, in memory; setting `tool_guard_kanban` (default true): off lets a worker the Kanban dispatcher starts run its tools without tool_guard's approval prompt, which nobody can answer in a worker — Hermes's own worker rules still apply (execute_code and dangerous commands refused where nobody can answer), an ordinary command or a write outside the card's workspace runs unapproved, and the mark still follows the card (a chat reading the board starts guarded); `setup` offers it (step 7, --kanban-guard / --no-kanban-guard) and writes plugins.entries.webgraft.settings.tool_guard_kanban; an explicit null for a webgraft setting reads as its default (a boolean setting no longer fails open on null); a page webgraft reads itself after an earlier failure keeps its true provenance in the footer (no longer labeled as read by the keyless rescue); no telemetry.

appends a short note (about 110 tokens) to each user message (setting `remind`); once a conversation has read web content (web_search, web_extract, x_search, browser tools, MCP tools, hosted connector tools, pages attached with @url:, vision_analyze / video_analyze on a URL, a terminal command or execute_code script holding an http(s) URL, tools a script runs, a subagent that read the web), sends every tool that is not read-only (terminal, code, browser, file writes, memory, messages, subagents, session_search, unknown tools (a tool_call bridge call is guarded as the tool it runs, and one Hermes cannot resolve is left to Hermes's own error), read_file / search_files outside the folders where Hermes keeps fetched pages, and vision_analyze / video_analyze on a local file) to Hermes's own approval prompt through the pre_tool_call approve directive, refused where nobody can answer such as -Q or cron (setting `tool_guard`: ask by default, block, off), because a web page can hold instructions aimed at the assistant; in a Kanban worker (HERMES_KANBAN_TASK, where nobody can answer), these stay free: the board reads, the tools that hand its own card on, write_file / patch / read_file / search_files inside the card's workspace (HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE; a relative path, or a blank search path, is pinned to that workspace through the pre_tool_call modify directive), read_file of the files its parent cards handed on (artifacts), and a terminal command whose words all stay in that workspace (file and text utilities, or a program with a version flag alone; no URL, expansion, heredoc or script run), whose workdir webgraft sets to that workspace through the pre_tool_call modify directive, Hermes's own command checks running on it as usual; a worker whose own card, a parent card or a recent card listed in its first message was worked after a web read starts guarded; a tool call that cannot be tied to a conversation is guarded as soon as any conversation in the process has read the web; when webgraft cannot read any page of a call, it keeps those pages from Hermes's keyless rescue (web.keyless_rescue, which would send their URLs to Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl or Keenable), and asking for such a page again goes to Hermes's approval prompt first; after a search that the rescue served because the search backend failed, the next searches go to the approval prompt for up to 10 minutes, though that first rescued search has already gone out (setting `keyless_rescue`: ask by default, block, off; under --yolo or approvals off Hermes approves by itself); keeps the ids (no content) of guarded conversations, at most 1000, in plugin-data/webgraft/web_sessions.json, so the guard holds after a restart and after Hermes compresses the history, and the Kanban cards worked after a web read as empty files named after their board and card id in plugin-data/webgraft/kanban_cards (at most 2000); a continuation session or subagent inherits its parent's mark; `setup` writes web.search_backend, web.extract_backend, skills.auto_load and SEARXNG_URL, recording replaced values and the Chromium path under plugin-data/webgraft; `status` reads the model, fallback, auxiliary, web, TTS and STT settings and SEARXNG_URL to list what can leave the machine, and changes nothing; page-reading child processes get a minimal environment, never Hermes's API keys; `setup` optionally raises web.extract_char_limit (only on a yes; the replaced value is restored by `uninstall`); no page text is kept, only the URLs, titles and failure reasons of recent pages, in memory; setting `tool_guard_kanban` (default true): off lets a worker the Kanban dispatcher starts run its tools without tool_guard's approval prompt, which nobody can answer in a worker — Hermes's own worker rules still apply (execute_code and dangerous commands refused where nobody can answer), an ordinary command or a write outside the card's workspace runs unapproved, and the mark still follows the card (a chat reading the board starts guarded); `setup` offers it (step 7, --kanban-guard / --no-kanban-guard) and writes plugins.entries.webgraft.settings.tool_guard_kanban; an explicit null for a webgraft setting reads as its default (a boolean setting no longer fails open on null); a page webgraft reads itself after an earlier failure keeps its true provenance in the footer (no longer labeled as read by the keyless rescue); no telemetry. This plugin hook(s): pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, transform_llm_output. Platforms: linux, windows. Requires Hermes >=0.22.6.

entries.name: webly
entries.description: Publish a website, or share files and folders, at a live *.webly.site URL from Hermes Agent with no account, then sign in to claim it, edit it, and publish drafts the person approves through the hosted Webly MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — MCP tool calls go to api.webly.ai/v1/mcp, sending WEBLY_API_KEY as a bearer header when it is set, and the webly server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before each Webly MCP tool that changes something. The bundled webly skill runs a local Node.js 20+ helper (scripts/webly.mjs) through the shell: it uploads only the files and folders the person asks to publish or share to api.webly.ai (sites are public unless password-protected), runs the project's npm/pnpm/yarn install and build first when the folder has a build script, opens the browser for sign-in and claim, and keeps its anonymous-site token and optional OAuth sign-in in ~/.webly (mode 0600). Its doctor command reads ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml only to see whether a webly MCP server is configured there. Publishing, deleting and replacing sites through that helper are gated by skill instructions, not by Hermes approvals. The catalog copy has no update check.
entries.title: Webly
known_issues: The Webly MCP tools need a sign-in, because a portable mcp.json cannot request OAuth: set WEBLY_API_KEY (a wb_ key from the Webly dashboard), or run `hermes mcp add webly --url https://api.webly.ai/v1/mcp --auth oauth` then `hermes mcp login webly`. Publishing without an account works without either.

entries.name: webmint
entries.description: Turn a website into a deterministic tool: a real browser captures the page once, the host's own model writes a declarative extraction spec, two runs must agree (same field set, >=50% fill per field) before it is saved, and every later call runs that spec with no model in the loop (~2.7s). Five tools: setup, mint, run, list, remove. Disclosure — needs Node >= 18 and Playwright; on first mint the plugin installs Playwright and Chromium into its own directory (~120 MB, opt out with WEBMINT_NO_AUTO_SETUP=1). Capture runs in a fresh signed-out browser: actions may fill, click and submit forms, and http specs replay the captured GET or POST (Cookie and Authorization headers are never replayed). Public http(s) URLs only — file:, loopback/private and link-local/metadata addresses are refused, with private/loopback behind WEBMINT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=1 or the host's security.allow_private_urls. Headless Chromium is refused by some bot-protected sites.

entries.name: webtwizz
entries.description: Build, change and publish websites and web apps with WebTwizz through its hosted MCP server (https://app.webtwizz.com/mcp, OAuth sign-in in the browser, no keys in config): landing pages, online stores, booking sites, portfolios and web apps with sign-ins and a database, published to a webtwizz.app address or the user's own domain, with version history, site data and GitHub sync. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json), configuration only. Disclosure: every tool call goes to WebTwizz's hosted server (app.webtwizz.com) and acts on the user's WebTwizz account; the tool set is served by that server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha. Builds and edits spend WebTwizz credits, and publish-site only returns a link: the site goes live when the user presses Publish in the WebTwizz editor. Sign-in runs the pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 through npx (Node.js and npm required), which opens a browser and a local callback port on first use and stores OAuth tokens under ~/.mcp-auth. The package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not mark read-only and refuses them in unattended runs.

entries.name: wechat-social-assistant
entries.description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

entries.name: weft
entries.description: Catch conflicts between coding agents while they edit, before Git merge time. Disclosure — In a checkout linked with `/weft setup` (a `.weft/space.json` plus the saved agent token), every file edit the agent makes is sent to the Weft gateway that checkout names: file paths, symbol keys, full diffs, agent and change ids, the Hermes model name and the Kanban task title. The gateway is local (127.0.0.1) by default, Weft's hosted `https://weft-hosted.elier.ai` when chosen or named by a checkout, or a gateway you add with `/weft trust`. Gateway diagnostics are appended to tool results, and `mode: enforce` blocks conflicting edits, `git commit` and task completion. `/weft setup` and `/weft feed` run `npx -y @celador/weft@0.3.0`, which installs `wrangler@4` from npm, starts a background local gateway that outlives the chat, creates a paired Git worktree and installs Git hooks in the repository. Activity snapshots and logs are kept in `~/.cache/weft-hermes`, shared across profiles.

entries.name: weightscope
entries.description: Offline-by-default safetensors checkpoint inspector: per-tensor and per-layer weight diffs (L2, relative change, cosine, NaN/Inf) via tools ckpt_summary and ckpt_diff, plus `hermes weightscope` and `/weightscope`. Optional remote GPU worker, and an opt-in `demo --fetch` of two pinned public SmolLM2-135M checkpoints. Disclosure — reads only the checkpoint paths you pass; writes recent diff headlines under the plugin data dir (optional) and, with `demo --fetch`, caches 513.2 MiB of pinned public Hugging Face weights plus an SVG heatmap; network is off unless you set remote_url (HTTPS to that worker only, bearer token from a named Hermes secret, no checkpoint upload) or pass `demo --fetch` (HTTPS to huggingface.co / official HF CDNs, no token); no telemetry, no shell, no background processes, no model execution. Numeric differences are not a safety, quality, or alignment verdict.

entries.name: weir
entries.description: Public X (Twitter) and Reddit data through Weir's hosted MCP server: search posts with X's operators, and read profiles, timelines, replies, threads, Lists, subreddits and comments. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package with the hosted MCP server (remote streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 with a client ID metadata document or dynamic client registration, so no keys in config) and one skill; no code, no executables, no stored credentials. Disclosure: every tool call goes to api.weirapp.io and spends Weir credits (5,000 free a month, then prepaid packs); the search terms, handles and links you look up are sent to Weir. Data tools are annotated read-only; the optional monitor tools appear only with the monitors:write scope, and the package marks its server untrusted, so Hermes asks before any call that is not read-only and refuses those calls in unattended runs; a `weir` server you define in config.yaml replaces the package's and drops that prompt unless you add `trust: untrusted`. Weir is not affiliated with X or Reddit. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: werk
entries.description: Plain-language equipment description in, engineering package out: werk triages the description into domains, breaks it into work items, runs them through review roles and domain-pack checks (a build123d STEP model for mechanical work; the elec pack ships SKiDL/KiCad tools but designs nothing in this release), and writes a COVER.md with the gaps it found written down. Proof of concept, NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION. Disclosure — `hermes werk doctor --setup` (after consent in a terminal) creates two worker profiles (werk-builder, werk-reviewer) and a Kanban board `werk`, symlinks werk into those profiles' plugins dirs and their plugin-data/werk to your own werk data dir, and uses uv to download a CPython 3.12 build and hash-pinned pack packages from PyPI (mostly wheels, including build123d/OCP) into the plugin's data dir; the elec pack's sdist-only skidl, hierplace and kinet2pcb are built locally with setuptools fetched unpinned at build time, in a minimal environment with no provider keys; `hermes werk run` is a long foreground run (default caps 60M tokens / 24 h) that spends model tokens through your configured providers and runs `hermes kanban` CLI calls; pack tools run as subprocesses in their own venvs with the network cut via `unshare -rn` when available, the elec pack calls the system `kicad-cli` (GPL) if present, and signed overrides use `ssh-keygen`. Three optional supplier-key settings are declared but unused in this version. No telemetry, no self-update.

entries.name: werracle-evm-guard
entries.description: Autonomous EVM execution guardrail and DeFi liquidation risk radar for Hermes Agent. Intercepts cast send transactions before broadcast to block unlimited token approvals, NFT operator takeovers, and high-value transfers. Performs Radar lookups to api.werracle.com by default on every werracle tool call and intercepted cast send. Disclosure — by default sends the target address and chain of every intercepted `cast send`, and the addresses, accounts and market pairs passed to its werracle_* tools, to api.werracle.com (or the user-configured api_url); WERRACLE_API_KEY is sent only to https://api.werracle.com. The guard is best-effort and fails open when the Radar lookup or key lookup errors.

entries.name: whatsapp-agent-platform
entries.description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. entries.name: which-copy
entries.description: Answers the question that silently decides everything else: which copy of a command is the Hermes process actually going to run? On a Mac the same tool can exist five times over — a Homebrew formula, an npm global install, a pyenv shim, a standalone download, and Hermes's own bundled copy — and the name resolves to whichever one PATH reaches first, with no warning when that is the wrong one. which_copy resolves one name against the PATH of the running Hermes process and, separately, against the PATH your own login shell builds for a terminal (that shell is started from the system default PATH, not Hermes's, so the entries it reports are its own), and says so when the two disagree. It also states, in every report, that Hermes's terminal tool runs commands in a login shell whose PATH gains directories Hermes adds — so it never claims the process PATH is the PATH a terminal command gets. It lists every copy it can find, on PATH and in the usual off-PATH install locations, with the evidence for where each came from (a Homebrew Cellar directory names the formula, a node_modules tree names the npm package including its scope, pyenv versions, uv tools, pipx venvs, nvm, Hermes's own directories, a plain folder, the macOS system), the version it reports, and whether it can even execute here — an Intel-only binary on Apple silicon is named as needing Rosetta to run. Then it gives a verdict in plain language: an older copy shadowing a newer one, a dead symlink earlier in PATH that the shell silently skips, Hermes preferring its own bundle to yours, several copies whose versions were measured (the same version, the winner being the newest, versions that cannot honestly be ordered, copies that reported no version, copies the sweep did not ask, or copies it did not run), or nothing wrong at all. which_copy_scan sweeps the usual AI tools — python, python3, node, npm, npx, bun, pnpm, uv, pip3, pipx, git, gh, brew, hermes, claude, codex, opencode, gemini, grok, aider, cursor-agent, rustc, go, ruby, java — in about a second, one line per tool, worst first. It diagnoses and stops: no installs, no PATH edits, no relinking, no "fix" that hides the problem. Versions are asked with an argv-only probe (three-second deadline, own process group, 8 KB output cap, cwd at the filesystem root, and a stripped environment so a shadowing binary never sees Hermes's API keys), and only for copies this machine put there: an absolute entry on Hermes's PATH, an absolute entry on the login shell's PATH, or one of the fixed install directories. Nothing named in a tool call is ever executed — a file passed as a path, a copy found only in a PATH string the call supplies, and a copy behind a relative or empty PATH entry are described with their version left unchecked — so a prompt-injected repository cannot get its own script run. For a call that supplies `path`, every version probe still runs with Hermes's own process PATH, never the raw supplied string. probe_versions false skips every probe, and the login-shell check is separate, so pair it with check_login_shell false for a call that starts no process at all. When two version strings were never meant to be compared, it says it cannot order them instead of guessing.

entries.name: while
entries.description: while.sh hosts the tools people build with an AI agent, and they choose who to share them with: their team, a client or a supplier with a link and a password, or everyone. The agent deploys them through while's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE): web services and workers, PostgreSQL databases, caches, S3 storage, scheduled jobs, preview environments and private access, plus logs, metrics, read-only SQL, backups and rollbacks. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill), configuration only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every call goes to while's MCP server at app.while.sh. Without an account, the agent can deploy a tool to try it; MCP tools that need the user's account sign them in through while's OAuth, and then act on that user's organizations with the scopes they consented to. MCP tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. Write-capable MCP tools: deploy, apply a plan, roll back, set environment variables and secrets, create previews and projects, back up and restore databases, run scheduled jobs, write files to the project's branch, invite members, grant and revoke roles, create API tokens, declare and call external API connections, and send_feedback (sends a report to the while team). A person approves in while.sh before a tool goes public, data is restored or rights are granted, and the agent never sees the credentials for people's other software. Hermes stores and refreshes the OAuth tokens. The MCP tool list comes from while's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it. The repository's README also documents an optional install script (curl | sh) for other agents, and examples/ holds sample projects; the plugin runs neither. The bundled mcp.json works without an account; for the MCP tools of an account, enable OAuth with `hermes mcp add while --url https://app.while.sh/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`, then add `trust: untrusted` to the `mcp_servers.while` entry in `config.yaml`; the package itself declares the server untrusted in plugin.json.
