entries.name: whiplash
entries.description: Let Hermes jam live on an Elektron Digitakt II over USB MIDI: genre/mood beats with MIDI clock, routed onto a session kit map of what each track holds (tracks 1-16), in any key with chord progressions, arranged into song sections (whiplash_arrange: intro, build, drop, outro on bar lines), written melodies and rhythms, bar-quantized pattern switches with DJ-style transitions (filter swap, drop swap, riser), track levels and pan with saved mixes (whiplash_mix), listening to the unit's real output over USB audio (whiplash_listen: loudness, clipping, band balance, timing and kick offsets as numbers, never audio) with a loudness guard that refuses level increases after clipping, a kit scan (whiplash_scan_kit: with the beat stopped, one note per track, heard and classified into proposed kit-map labels that are never applied without the user's yes), play along (whiplash_play_along / whiplash_follow: reads the unit's MIDI input to show the user's knob moves, stop a ramp on a knob they grab, and answer phrases they play in key on another track; whiplash_undo reverts the last part, mix or arrangement change), named sound parameters, clock-synced parameter ramps, live fills/drops/density/swing/humanize, switching a track among samples already in the project pool, mutes and tempo. Disclosure — controls MIDI hardware (MIDI Start also starts the unit's own sequencer; a clock-only mode is available), can change which already-loaded sample a track plays, runs a background sequencer thread while a pattern plays, and opens a virtual MIDI port named "Whiplash" when no Digitakt is connected. Optional visualiser (whiplash_open_view): an unauthenticated read-only local web page served on 127.0.0.1 from a background thread, opened in the default browser, showing the beat and the live Hermes conversation including tool calls and results (taken from in-memory observer hooks; nothing is stored), readable by any local process while it is open. whiplash_listen opens an audio input (the Digitakt's USB audio by default, or WHIPLASH_AUDIO_INPUT or any input named in the tool call, which can be a microphone) only for the length of one call (at most 24 s), through the optional numpy/sounddevice extra, which needs microphone permission on macOS; the audio is analysed in memory and dropped. whiplash_scan_kit does the same for at most about 35 s and sends only note-on/off. whiplash_play_along and whiplash_follow open the Digitakt's MIDI input (never another device) on a background reader thread that only reads; what it hears is never sent back, and the session (notes and CCs sent and heard) is kept in memory only, at most 65,536 events, never written to disk. Never sends SysEx or program changes; no file transfer, project writes, shell or credentials, and no network beyond that localhost page.
entries.title: Whiplash
known_issues: Needs an Elektron Digitakt II (or any MIDI device/DAW) on USB MIDI to be heard.
With no device connected, Whiplash plays into a virtual MIDI port, which is silent unless a DAW or soft synth listens to it. Every tool result says so.
Windows has no virtual MIDI ports, so the fallback is unavailable there.
On Linux, python-rtmidi needs the ALSA runtime (libasound2).
MIDI Start also starts the Digitakt's own sequencer; select an empty pattern on the unit or use send_transport=false (clock only).
Sample select picks a slot in the unit's current sample bank and can't list or preview samples.

whiplash_listen needs the optional [listen] extra (numpy, sounddevice/PortAudio), USB CONFIG = USB AUDIO/MIDI on the unit, and microphone permission on macOS; without them it returns an error with the fix and every other tool works.

entries.name: whiteboard
entries.description: An agentic whiteboard. Say what you're planning and Hermes lays it out as a route, columns or a map, with hand-drawn stickers. Add rough notes and Hermes proposes groups, owners and action items that you accept one by one and can take back. Hand an action item to Hermes and an agent does it on the board and delivers the result next to the note with its sources, or run the whole route and get a brief at the end. Select anything and ask about it. Once you allow it, any chat can read your boards and propose changes. Link a board to the chat its work is in: the board shows what that chat is doing, and the chat hears what you change on the board. Send notes to Hermes Kanban or lay a Kanban board out as a whiteboard. Disclosure — laying out a board, grouping notes, unpacking a result and the brief each start a hidden Hermes session told to use no tools; Hand to Hermes, Run the route and Ask start hidden sessions that use your Hermes tools and read third-party web pages, at most three at once, each stopped after 4 minutes or 24 tool calls; approval prompts inside these sessions are denied; export writes the one Markdown or CSV file you name in the system dialog, through the plugin's own backend; boards live in Desktop plugin storage, with a copy under plugin-data/whiteboard/ only after you turn on chat access, which starts off, and each Hermes profile that has the plugin keeps its own copy; a Planning model and an Agent model in Settings name a model you are signed in to in Hermes when a session is created, and a refused model stops the run; with the Sheets or Data plugin installed, a click on that page pins notes to the open board through a window event, with no file, backend or model involved; Send to Kanban and New board from Kanban make the plugin's backend run the `hermes kanban` command, with no shell and with note text passed after `--` and on standard input, to list boards, create cards and read a board; cards are created in Blocked with no assignee, and in Triage, which Hermes works through on its own, only when you tick a box; while the page is open on a board that has Kanban cards it reads those Kanban boards about every 25 seconds, and it never changes a card after making it; a board can remember the id of the chat it is linked to, the page places a request in that chat's message box for you to send and never sends it, and after that it listens to that one chat for up to 30 minutes and reads its answer from the transcript; the plugin registers four hooks (pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, on_session_end, post_compaction) that run on every chat turn and return at once unless the chat is linked to a board; for a linked chat they keep the state of its latest turn and the first line of its answer under plugin-data/whiteboard/, and, only while chat access is on, add to the message you send in that chat a short notice that the board exists and the notes you added, edited or removed on it since the chat's last turn; the plugin never sends a message to a chat; the linked chat can put a doing, done or blocked mark on its own board's notes with no review, which changes nothing else and clears with a click; which chat each board is linked to is kept under plugin-data/whiteboard/ as ids only, whether or not chat access is on; no telemetry, no credentials, no background processes of its own, and no command other than `hermes kanban`. Independent community project, not affiliated with Nous Research.

entries.name: whoop-mcp
entries.description: Read the user's WHOOP recovery, HRV, sleep and strain through the local whoop MCP server. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — Unofficial connector, not affiliated with WHOOP. Runs the `whoop-mcp-unofficial@0.7.0` npm package locally over stdio through `npx` (Node.js 20+ required); the package and its dependencies are downloaded from npm on first start. Data source: the official WHOOP OAuth API (v2). The user creates their own WHOOP developer app; its client ID and secret and the OAuth tokens are created by the connector's own `setup`/`auth` commands in the user's terminal, stored under `~/.whoop-mcp/` and refreshed by the connector itself, and sent only to WHOOP's API; the plugin declares no environment variables and reads no Hermes credentials. It also keeps a wellness profile shared with the author's other connectors at `~/.delx-wellness/profile.json` (first run copies an existing `~/.hermes/profiles/delx-wellness/wellness-profile.json` there), and its connection-status tool reads `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to check for an MCP block. entries.name: whos-listening
entries.description: Memory that knows who's listening. Each memory is Private or Shared. Private memories go into a request only when the machine running Hermes (the gateway), the app you chat in (the platform) and the model provider are all trusted. By default, the gateway you install it on is trusted unless it's a hosted Hermes such as Hermes Cloud; the trusted platforms are the terminal and Hermes Desktop, including its Webapp; and the trusted model routes are Venice's private models and models on your own machine or local network. Everything else gets Shared memories only. You can configure all of these options in the plugin's settings: trusting either more or fewer gateways, platforms or model providers. Disclosure — memories stay in $HERMES_HOME/whos-listening/. Once a day it fetches Venice's public model list from api.venice.ai (nothing about you is sent). With a Venice key in Hermes, a duplicate check (on by default) sends each new memory, each memory arriving by sync and each memory in a /memories review scan, together with up to 20 others, Private ones included, to Venice's private Clef model (duplicate_judge off keeps it local). Shared memories sync to your GitHub repository only if you set that up.
entries.title: Who's Listening?
known_issues: Hermes runs plugin middleware only on main chat requests. Compression, the tool-limit summary, mixture-of-agents and side calls skip the guard; see README Limits.
The first turn after a gateway starts carries Shared memories only, and Venice models count as Shared until Venice's model list has loaded on a new gateway.
Subagents and scheduled jobs count as Shared, so they never see Private memories.
Auto-review needs the default in-process plugin mode; under plugins.isolation host, held saves wait for the user.
For /memories to work from the first message, also run `hermes plugins enable whos-listening` (for a memory provider, install --enable only sets memory.provider).
If a model calls a memory tool through tool_call, Hermes answers that it's not a known tool name; the plugin tells models to call its tools directly.

entries.name: why
entries.description: Ask why any line of agent-written code exists. Each time the agent writes or patches a file, Why records the lines it wrote and that turn's user request, locally. /why app.py:42 (or hermes why, or the why_line tool) then names the request, date, model and session behind the line; /why app.py shows which requests wrote which share of a file. Lines are matched by text, not number, so they are found after they move. No model calls, network or dependencies.

entries.name: widespread
entries.description: Earn verified-work bounties on the widespread protocol — discover funded markets across every forge, claim one, ship a signed dg-ship-1 attestation, watch the adjudicator, collect the payout. The earning-side counterpart to payment plugins: wide_* tools let an agent get paid for work it can prove, and the payer side (post a bounty, accept a claim) is approval-gated by the human. Plain HTTPS to the live bridge — no browser, no runtime dependency. Disclosure — sends claims, signed work attestations (commit SHAs, optional proof items) and bounty posts to the widespread bridge (widespread-bridge.widespread.workers.dev) and forge (code.widespread.fyi), overridable with WIDE_BRIDGE / WIDE_FORGE; keeps an Ed25519 agent signing seed (mode 0600) and a claim ledger under the profile's plugin-data/widespread; wide_post (model-chosen amount) and wide_accept (releases a payout) wait for your approval, and an "always" answer for wide_post covers later posts in the same amount band (up to $10, up to $100, over $100) while one for wide_accept covers every later accept.

entries.name: wing
entries.description: Extra features for the Wing Android app: GPT Live voice and email draft cards. GPT Live voice uses ChatGPT subscription access with the selected Hermes profile's context. Email draft cards show recipients, cc/bcc, subject and body, then open the user's chosen email app for final edits and sending. Drafts work independently of voice and need no OpenAI credentials or mail account access. Draft cards adapt arsiktech's hermes-draft-cards design (MIT); the voice integration builds on Synero's hermes-live-voice work (MIT). Disclosure — voice calls send the WebRTC SDP, the selected profile's Hermes-built system prompt (including memory) and client-supplied chat excerpts to chatgpt.com (Codex realtime endpoint) through the profile's openai-codex sign-in, with the headers OpenAI-Alpha: quicksilver=v2, originator: hermes-agent and random session ids; building fresh voice context runs a short-lived Python child that initialises the profile's memory providers and reads context files from the profile's configured terminal.cwd only; email drafts persist in the profile's plugin-data/wing SQLite database; relies on undocumented Hermes prompt-inspection and voice helpers that may break on update; draft cards and voice adapt arsiktech's hermes-draft-cards and Synero's hermes-live-voice (MIT). No telemetry, stored credentials or self-updater.

Live subscription voice requires a profile sign-in with voice access. OpenAI API voice is unavailable pending host-owned per-call instructions/voice support in NousResearch/hermes-agent#151774. Email drafts require neither.

entries.name: wings
entries.description: A private WireGuard network between every Hermes you own and your phone. Two devices are enough: run setup on a computer, scan one code on the phone. Bots and sessions from all your machines in Desktop, the terminal and the Hermes app. Computers link directly when they can. No account, no coordination server, no third party. Disclosure — Wings asks for admin rights once per machine and installs a root helper (/usr/local/libexec/wings-root) with always-on systemd units (wings-sync, wings-watch, wings-relay, wings-address, wings-dns), a WireGuard interface wings0, an nftables table, firewalld/ufw rules, a wings-net system user, a marked /etc/hosts line and a private certificate authority trusted system-wide but limited to .wings names; it may install wireguard-tools and nftables from your package manager and downloads wstunnel 11.1.0 from its official GitHub release (checksum-pinned). It also adds a per-user wings-upkeep timer that runs every minute, installs and starts the Hermes gateway service, and sets webapp.enabled and webapp.public_url in config.yaml. Every device you pair can sign in to Hermes on every machine in your wing net without a password (full dashboard and terminal access), and every joined computer holds the shared wing-net key; turn this off per machine with `hermes wings trust off`. The Wings page lists the bots and recent session titles of every Hermes profile on each of your machines. A hub opens one UDP port (plus TCP 443 for the optional HTTPS relay), and `hermes wings router open` asks your router over UPnP to forward it.
entries.title: Wings
known_issues: Asks for admin rights once per machine to install a root helper. Read plugin/root/wings-root.sh first.
Trusts a private certificate authority system-wide, limited to .wings names.
Devices connect to the computer you ran setup on (the hub). To reach a hub at home from outside, one UDP port must be forwarded on the router.
Computers link directly when their networks allow it and otherwise go through the hub. Phones always do.
Phones run one VPN at a time, so the Wings tunnel replaces any other while it is on.

entries.name: wireguard
entries.description: Read-only status and peer list for a WireGuard server running on the same Windows machine as Hermes. Two tools: vpn_status (service state, tunnel address and port, server public key, per-peer handshake and transfer) and vpn_peers (the peer list only). The plugin runs only wg.exe show, sc.exe query, and one PowerShell adapter lookup; it never changes the tunnel and never reads the tunnel configuration file or any private key material. Windows only (WireGuard for Windows). Disclosure — runs local wg.exe show, sc.exe query and one PowerShell Get-NetIPAddress lookup (read-only, never touches the tunnel config or private key); tool results put peer public keys, allowed IPs and peer endpoint IP addresses into the conversation sent to your model provider.

entries.name: wiro-media
entries.description: Wiro AI's image, video, speech, music, transcription and 3D models as thirteen wiro_* tools: generate and edit images (upscale, remove backgrounds, prompt edits), text or image to video, text to speech, music, transcription, image to 3D, catalog search with prices, any catalog model, task follow-up and Wiro AI workflows. It also registers Wiro AI as an opt-in backend for image_generate, video_generate, text_to_speech and speech-to-text, and ships the wiro-media:wiro skill. Every tool takes any catalog model; outputs are saved in cache/generated/ with MEDIA: tags, and every result reports its cost. Disclosure — prompts, settings and input files go to https://api.wiro.ai/v1 with WIRO_API_KEY, read per call through Hermes secret scope; every generation spends the user's Wiro AI balance with no Hermes approval prompt, and the model can pick costly options such as high resolution or long video. Local input files are read only from Hermes' media cache, or from anywhere the user can read when the terminal backend is local (system and credential folders and the rest of the Hermes home excluded), and only when their bytes are media or documents of the expected kind; they are uploaded to the user's Wiro AI storage. Output files are downloaded only from *.wiro.ai hosts. Ogg Opus voice notes and bmp, tiff or avif images are converted with the local ffmpeg when it is installed.

entries.name: withhuman
entries.description: Human approval for Hermes tool calls, with human in the loop guardrails. entries.name: workout-tracker
entries.description: Plan gym workouts through Workout Tracker's hosted MCP servers (Streamable HTTP at workout.lbyte.app): search a rated exercise catalog and check a draft plan's weekly sets per muscle and session length with no account, then, with a personal access token, save plans to the user's account and make one active. Disclosure: two servers. workout-tracker (/mcp/public) needs no credentials and never receives the token. workout-tracker-account (/mcp/account) acts on the user's account with a token they create in the app, sent as an Authorization header from WORKOUT_TRACKER_TOKEN in the profile environment; when it is unset, Hermes skips that server and the catalog tools still work. entries.name: workroom
entries.description: Gives the agent a room to work on Word, PowerPoint and Excel files while you stay in charge. Figures are linked to their source cells and kept in step when a source changes; the agent can prepare a release but has no tool to approve one; figures in its text are marked supported, calculated or not verified from what it read; a reply that claims a file that does not exist gets one honest line. Desktop panels: Needs you, Made (list or gallery), Room, Rules. Disclosure: reads and writes only inside the folders the user registers and in the plugin data directory; no network calls, no telemetry, no self-updater, no native binary. To be able to put protected files back, the safety net reads, in memory, the bytes of every managed or protected file of a registered project (including .env and key files) before a shell, code or editing tool runs; they are never shown to the agent and are kept in plugin data only if the agent changed the file (the agent's version). Hooks (pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_tool_result, transform_llm_output, pre_llm_call, pre_verify, subagent_start, subagent_stop) can block a tool call, append one line to a tool result or reply, and, after a shell, code or other editing tool runs, put back any Office or protected file of a registered project that changed (the agent's version is kept in plugin data); they never approve or auto-approve. To check the figures in the agent's text it stores, in a local SQLite file in the plugin data directory, the text of tool results the agent read this session (capped at 20 MB per session) and the owner's chat messages; nothing is sent anywhere. Subprocesses: a local Python child to build files; the Windows icacls tool once for the signing key file; PowerShell only on request on Windows with PowerPoint to draw slide pictures, or LibreOffice (soffice) for the same on other systems when it is installed. Starts no scheduled job itself (a user-created Hermes cron job may run its watch script, which can prepare a release but never approves one).
entries.title: Workroom
known_issues: Verified on Windows with the real Hermes Desktop and Office. The test suite passes on Windows, Linux (fresh clone) and in macOS CI; the Hermes Desktop screens were run on Windows only.
The safety net reverts files that other plugins' tools wrote inside registered projects, and appends one line to those tool results; this is by design and listed in docs/LIMITS.md.

A plugin that bundles its own copy of the PowerPoint or Word library (paper-pptx, paper-docx) cannot share an environment with python-pptx and python-docx; Workroom then cannot build new decks or reports, while reading, editing and releasing existing files keep working.
Real-model checks (bypass, approve, injection, folder tidy) were run with one model, 3 to 5 runs per case, so they are counts, not rates.
On a very large report the first import asks many questions (3,841 on one blind run, about 88% of them real).

entries.name: wow-addon-forge
entries.description: Builds World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.1, Interface 16001) addons that load and run, for players who are not programmers. Nine tools: wow_env (install/addon detection), wow_api (queryable index of the real client build's API, events and restrictions), wow_check (six-stage static + headless verification: TOC lint, Lua 5.1 syntax, global resolution, restricted/secret API rules, headless load in an embedded Lua 5.1 VM stub of the game, efficiency lints), wow_test (multi-client headless Lua test runner), wow_new (scaffolds an addon from tested building blocks: core, replicated record log, guild sync, trust, lazy Classic-theme window, Discord bridge), wow_install (installs after wow_check passes, with backup), wow_savedvars and wow_errors (read game data and in-game Lua errors back, via the bundled ForgeProbe companion addon), and wow_bridge (file-based Discord seam: pull an outbox, push an inbox, one /reload of latency each way). Ships Guildhall, a guild-management addon built entirely with these tools (board, calendar, a Marks currency earned automatically by playing, Discord mirror), the wow-addon-builder skill, /wow, hermes wow, and an Addon Forge Desktop pane. entries.name: wow
entries.description: Chat with a Hermes agent from inside World of Warcraft: Forever. The plugin registers a kind: platform gateway adapter that serves a local HTTP endpoint (/v1/wow/message, /v1/wow/outbox, /v1/wow/health) authenticated with a bearer token; one character (Name-Realm) is one Hermes DM session. A companion bridge runs on a Windows 11 PC next to the game client: it captures a 1600x400 pixel strip from the game window with the Windows Graphics Capture API (mss/GDI fallback), decodes chat, POSTs lines to the adapter and long-polls the outbox. It also writes reply/state files into the WoW AddOns tree and reads SavedVariables for reload mode, and plays silent doorbell WAVs. The adapter binds 127.0.0.1 by default and can be bound to a LAN address explicitly; the bridge then makes outbound HTTP requests to that configured Hermes host. Adds five WoW-only tools (wow_addon_search, wow_addon_guide, wow_addon_install, wow_addon_uninstall, wow_quest_help), three per-character toolsets selected with /mode (standard, wow, full; full needs an in-game confirmation and expires after 60 minutes), and a bundled wow-player-guide skill. Disclosure - the plugin opens a local HTTP listener guarded by a shared bearer secret (WOW_BRIDGE_TOKEN, auto-generated in memory when unset, so the bridge cannot pair until it is set); it makes CurseForge API calls (api.curseforge.com) with the player's own CurseForge Core API key, stored as a profile-scoped Hermes secret (WOW_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY in the selected profile) with no plugin-managed credential file; addon installs and uninstalls are queued to the bridge, which writes or moves files under the WoW AddOns directory only after the player confirms in game and keeps a removal backup instead of deleting permanently; a desktop setup page creates or updates a dedicated Hermes profile (wow), writes its .env, config.yaml, SOUL.md and a profile skill, and can hot-serve that profile through a running gateway multiplexer. The bridge is a separate long-running background process (screen pixels plus files only); the plugin does not read the game process or its memory, does not inject input, and does not automate gameplay. Chat text and tool results are sent to the model provider configured for the WoW Hermes profile (cloud or local), with that provider's data-handling terms and the usual token cost. Requires Hermes >=0.22.7, Windows 11 for the bridge, WoW: Forever (Interface 16001), and uv/Python downloaded for the bridge; a CurseForge key is needed only for one-click addon installs (without one the addon tools return a guided CurseForge link). Disclosure — the plugin opens a local HTTP listener (127.0.0.1 by default, plain HTTP if bound to a LAN address) guarded only by a shared bearer token (WOW_BRIDGE_TOKEN); whoever holds that token can chat as any character and, after the in-game `/mode full confirm` step, use terminal, file and code tools on the Hermes host for 60 minutes. It calls the CurseForge API (api.curseforge.com) with the player's own CurseForge key, stored as a Hermes secret in the selected profile. The Desktop setup page creates or updates a dedicated Hermes profile: it copies this plugin into that profile, writes the profile's .env, config.yaml (including turning off tool deferral for that profile), SOUL.md and a profile skill, and can hot-serve it through a running gateway. A separate long-running Windows bridge reads a strip of the game window's pixels, writes reply and state files and installs or backs up addons under the WoW AddOns folder only after an in-game confirmation, opens links the agent sends in the default browser, and downloads a checksum-pinned uv release and Python on setup; it never reads game memory, injects input or automates play. Chat text and tool results go to the model provider configured for the WoW profile.
entries.title: WoW Hermes
known_issues: Two-part install: this Hermes plugin plus a separate Windows 11 bridge process next to the game client. The plugin alone cannot reach the game.
The game client must run windowed or borderless-windowed; exclusive fullscreen exposes no capturable window.
The public repository is a sanitized release mirror, not the private development history; older commits and internal notes are not published.
One-click addon installs need the player's own CurseForge Core API key and an author who allows third-party distribution; otherwise the tools return a CurseForge deep link instead of downloading.

The CurseForge key is a profile-scoped Hermes secret: saving it in the setup page affects only the selected profile. A key stored by v0.2.0 in the retired machine-wide plugin-data/wow/curseforge.key file is not read automatically — re-enter it once in setup after upgrading (the old file is left untouched).

The bridge asserts the character name, so WOW_BRIDGE_TOKEN is the only authentication boundary. Keep the listener on loopback unless the game PC is a separate machine, and firewall the port to that machine.

entries.name: wp-manager
entries.description: Look after a fleet of WordPress sites from Hermes: scan every site for plugin, theme, core and translation updates, install them behind Hermes's approval prompt with an automatic health check afterwards, and draft or edit posts and pages from chat (publishing asks first). Includes a WordPress page in Hermes Desktop and pairs with the "Website Manager: WP Connector for Hermes" WordPress plugin shipped in the repo. Takes no backups. Disclosure — talks only to the WordPress sites you add (REST API, WordPress Application Passwords; plain http refused unless opted in per site; no cross-host redirects with credentials). Passwords resolve through Hermes secrets, or through the 1Password CLI you configure as op_binary, which wp-manager runs as a subprocess (argument list, no shell) to read op:// references, list vault names and, only when you choose it, create a new Login item (password passed on stdin). Stores site addresses, usernames and credential references (never passwords) plus an action log in its own folder under HERMES_HOME. Never reads or writes the Hermes .env. No telemetry.

entries.name: wrenchboard
entries.description: Turn Hermes into a circuit board repair bench: a live boardview beside the chat, opened from 14 boardview formats, test plans with readings pinned on the pads, part cards drawn from the real copper, and your schematic and datasheets read on your computer. Disclosure — needs a WrenchBoard account (RepairMind LTD's hosted service at app.wrenchboard.cloud; free to read boards, Pro for repairs and test plans); boardview files you import, your repairs and readings go to WrenchBoard through Hermes' MCP client; the board view is a page served by WrenchBoard, in a sandboxed frame, that can send chat messages as you and record readings/steps on your WrenchBoard repair without a model turn; pressing Connect (pane, `hermes wrenchboard connect` or `/wb connect`) adds the `wrenchboard` MCP server and its `mcp_allowlist` grant to config.yaml; adds ~5,300 characters of system-prompt sections in Desktop/Webapp; schematics, documents and camera pictures stay on your computer.

entries.name: write-gate
entries.description: Deterministic pre-write content gate for Hermes Agent. A pre_tool_call hook parses the exact bytes about to be written as JSON, TOML or Python (stdlib parsers), rejects NUL bytes, oversized content and user-declared regex contracts, and short-circuits invalid writes with a precise line/column error returned to the model as a tool-call error, so the agent fixes the content in the same tool-calling loop instead of leaving a broken file behind. Also adds a write_gate_check preflight tool, a /writegate slash command and Settings -> Plugins config. Patch/replacement fragments are never parsed as whole documents: NUL, size and regex contracts still run on the fragment, and the reconstructed post-edit file is parsed when it can be rebuilt. Disclosure — no network calls, no shell commands, no subprocesses, no background processes, no credentials, no telemetry; reads the in-memory arguments of the tool call it gates, one optional user-specified JSON rules file named in the rules_file setting, and (for fragment edits only) the size-capped target file named in that same tool call, read-only; persists three integer counters in profile-scoped plugin state; never auto-approves or bypasses Hermes's approval gate; fails open on any internal error.

entries.name: writing-guard
entries.description: Style check for every Hermes answer in German and English: finds em and en dashes outside code, links and quotes (optionally replaces them by rule: ranges and list bullets become hyphens, dashes between words a comma), reports stock AI phrases (German and English) and mixed or switched forms of address (du/Sie) in German. Reports by default with one line appended to the answer; rule based, no model calls. Disclosure — no network calls and no model calls. A transform_llm_output hook reads the final answer of each turn; in report mode it appends one report line when there is a finding, in fix mode it also replaces dashes, with footer: false it never changes the answer; the returned text is what Hermes stores and shows. Stores per chat session id only the last form of address (du or sie) and a timestamp in HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/writing-guard/sessions.json (30 days, at most 2000 sessions); the last report with matched phrases stays in process memory only. Reads only its own plugin settings. Off on cron, subagent, kanban, batch and webhook by default. Registers the tool writing_guard_check (checks a draft, returns JSON), the slash command /writing-guard (settings, last report, check a text) and a skill that adds one line to the skills index of every session while the plugin is enabled.

entries.name: wyoming-voice-bridge
entries.description: Wyoming speech-to-text and text-to-speech for a Wyoming server you run (stt/tts provider `wyoming`), plus a wyoming_voice_status tool that lists the server's models and voices. Disclosure — Audio and text to speak go to the WYOMING_* host:port you set over cleartext, unauthenticated TCP (public addresses accepted). Once selected, the providers send speech in every session, including cron and webhooks. This build imports the installed package only when its file tree is the official wyoming 1.5.4 wheel, and a different tree sends nothing. This build lists no ffmpeg digest, so audio that is not already 16 kHz, 16-bit, mono WAV is not converted. wyoming_voice_status asks with one public pre_tool_call line. Choosing always stores one command_allowlist line for that same which and the same host:port list. A later call skips the question only when a person is present. cron, hermes -q, webhook, msgraph_webhook, and api_server do not send a describe, even after always. yolo and approvals off skip the prompt, and this plugin does not add a refusal for those modes. The plugin does not import Hermes approval, config, or write-guard modules. Hermes 0.21.4 does not list the skill. The v0.21.5 canary and Hermes 0.22.2 add one skill line to every session that loads the plugin, including a surface where the tools are turned off. The status tool is on for every surface, including the gateway, and a guest there can call it and approve it when a person can answer. Turn the wyoming_voice toolset off per surface with hermes tools.

entries.name: xmemo
entries.description: Native XMemo memory provider for Hermes Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall and the search tools), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Hermes memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); keeps a local SQLite cache of recalled results and a queue of unsent writes in $HERMES_HOME/xmemo_cache.db, partitioned by a hashed account identity; reads the key from XMEMO_KEY (also MEMORY_OS_API_KEY / MEMORY_OS_MCP_TOKEN) and, if none is set, falls back to the xmemo login token in ~/.config/xmemo/credentials.json (a catalog rule 11 deviation kept for existing users); workflow and destructive tools and timeline capture are off by default and opt-in.

entries.name: xray
entries.description: Sets traps for plugins instead of watching them. hermes xray detonate runs a plugin in a throwaway child process with a fake home full of honeytokens, fuzzes its tools, fires its hooks and replays it at +30 and +90 days to catch time-bombs, then gives a RED/AMBER/GREEN verdict with file:line proof, a per-version behaviour diff and a drafted disclosure line. Opt-in live bait flags any installed plugin that reads a decoy credential file and can route its next tool call to Hermes' approval prompt. Disclosure — spawns child Python processes to detonate plugins; the child runs as you (fake HOME, real keys stripped) and is not an OS sandbox, so its egress and spawn blocking (Python audit hooks, incl. fork and fork_exec) is a tripwire native code can bypass; reads of your real credential stores are refused and make the verdict RED; runs git clone when you detonate a remote repo, including from the dashboard's detonate button; by default (bait_runtime) installs a Python audit hook in the Hermes process that watches for plugins touching bait files or honeytokens; reads installed plugins' source dirs to attribute events; bait plant (opt-in) writes decoy files only into empty default credential paths of the AWS CLI/SDKs, git credential store, ssh and Solana CLI, so those tools use the fake values until bait remove, which deletes only unchanged files it wrote; enforce (off by default) uses pre_tool_call approve; no LLM calls, no telemetry; X-Ray itself never reads real credentials or patches Hermes core.
entries.title: Plugin X-Ray
known_issues: Detonation is not an OS sandbox: the plugin under test really runs in a child process as you and can reach real files by absolute path; only credential-store reads are refused. Detonate unknown code on a machine you don't mind
Python audit hooks see Python-level actions only; native code can act below them (any ctypes load is reported). Env-variable theft is caught when the value leaves the process, not when it is read
Desktop plugin.js code is not detonated (Python side only)

entries.name: xscapes
entries.description:
xscapes are cozy ASCII scenes that show what your agent is doing, at a glance. They run under Hermes in your terminal.

- See how hard your agent is working and what it just did
- Keep an eye on your session's context
- Never miss a failed command
- Leave the room: your companion knocks with a sound when Hermes needs you
- Multiple scenes and companions, all on your own clock

Needs the xscapes program, installed separately. Disclosure: sends each tool call with its arguments, approval commands, the folder Hermes runs in, and the first line of each prompt and reply to the xscapes program (not covered by this pin), which keeps them under ~/.config/xscapes/.

entries.name: yandex-disk
entries.description: Browse, search and manage files on Yandex Disk. Read and write files, transfer them locally, share links and restore items from the bin. Disclosure — sends every request to cloud-api.yandex.net, or to the https URL in YANDEX_DISK_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_DISK_OAUTH_TOKEN read through Hermes; file bytes go to the upload and download hosts the API hands out, without the token; unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS leaves search out, loading the plugin sends one search request to learn whether the token may search, and yadisk_search is registered only if it may; every tool, permanent delete, emptying the bin and public share links included, is offered unless YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only Disk); yadisk_upload reads a local file and sends it unredacted, and yadisk_download writes one, after Hermes' shared file-safety rules and the plugin's own: upload refuses .env files, Hermes' credential stores, Hermes' own directory and the home directories that hold keys and logins; download refuses credential files, Hermes' own directory, .hermes directories, agent instruction files such as AGENTS.md, system locations and paths outside HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other local files are within reach; YANDEX_DISK_ROOT confines Disk paths, not local ones; an upload from a URL makes Yandex fetch that URL; file names and contents written by other people reach the agent as tool output; no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
entries.title: Yandex Disk
known_issues: Every tool is offered by default, permanent delete and emptying the bin included. Set YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS to register fewer (read, download, write, share, delete, all or single tools, comma-separated; read is the README's advice for a first setup), then restart Hermes

yadisk_search is registered only when the token's application may use Yandex Disk search; a token from a self-registered app or from Poligon usually may not, and the plugin then offers the other fourteen tools

yadisk_upload sends any other local file the Hermes process can read, unredacted, and the write group includes upload; to keep the agent off local files, name the tools without upload and download, e.g. YANDEX_DISK_ACTIONS=read,mkdir,write_file,copy,move,trash_restore

entries.name: yandex
entries.description: Yandex Search API for Hermes web search and generated answers with cited sources. Uses the paid Yandex Cloud service. Disclosure — sends web_search queries and yandex_generative_search questions to searchapi.api.cloud.yandex.net, or to the base URL in YANDEX_SEARCH_API_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_API_KEY and YANDEX_FOLDER_ID read through Hermes; the Search API is a paid Yandex Cloud service billed to the folder that owns the key; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
entries.title: Yandex Search API
known_issues: Paid: every web_search routed to yandex and every yandex_generative_search call is billed by Yandex Cloud to the folder that owns YANDEX_API_KEY; the Search API must be enabled for that folder, with billing active

Installing does not switch web_search over: run hermes config set web.search_backend yandex. The backend is search-only, so web_extract stays with another backend. yandex_generative_search is offered to the agent as soon as the plugin is enabled (toolset yandex_search; hermes tools turns it off per platform)
Searches the Russian market (SEARCH_TYPE_RU) unless YANDEX_SEARCH_TYPE names another: SEARCH_TYPE_COM, SEARCH_TYPE_TR, SEARCH_TYPE_KK, SEARCH_TYPE_BE or SEARCH_TYPE_UZ

entries.name: yandex_calendar
entries.description: Manage events, invitations and RSVPs across Yandex calendars through CalDAV. Choose which calendars and actions Hermes can use. Disclosure — sends every request to caldav.yandex.ru, or to the HTTPS URL in YANDEX_CALENDAR_BASE_URL if you set one, with your YANDEX_CALENDAR_LOGIN and YANDEX_CALENDAR_APP_PASSWORD read through Hermes; all seven tools, delete included, are offered unless YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS narrows them; the tools act as your Yandex account, so adding attendees makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it; delete removes the event from the server and the plugin keeps no copy; event text written by other people, such as whoever invites you, reaches the agent as tool output; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no file or shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
entries.title: Yandex Calendar
known_issues: Every tool is offered by default, yandex_calendar_delete_event included. Set YANDEX_CALENDAR_ACTIONS to register fewer (read, write, delete, all or single actions, comma-separated; read is the README's advice for a new setup), then restart Hermes

The tools act as your Yandex account: adding attendees, to a new event or an existing one, makes Yandex email each of them an invitation from you, and changing, answering, moving or deleting a meeting may notify the people on it

Recurring events are not expanded: a series is listed as stored, with the times of its first occurrence, and one with modified occurrences can be moved or deleted but not edited or answered. A listing over 2 MiB of XML is refused with a request for a shorter range, and a recurring series counts in full
Read-only calendars such as holidays and birthdays accept a new event without storing it, and yandex_calendar_create_event still reports success: keep them out with YANDEX_CALENDAR_CALENDARS

entries.name: yandex_mail
entries.description: Search and read Yandex Mail, organize messages and reply through IMAP/SMTP. Choose which folders and actions Hermes can use; saving attachments and sending require explicit opt-in. Disclosure — reads and changes your Yandex Mail over IMAP at imap.yandex.ru and sends over SMTP at smtp.yandex.ru (or the hosts in YANDEX_MAIL_IMAP_HOST / YANDEX_MAIL_SMTP_HOST if you set them, which are not restricted to Yandex), over verified TLS, with your YANDEX_MAIL_LOGIN and YANDEX_MAIL_APP_PASSWORD read through Hermes; flagging, moving and deleting, including irreversible permanent deletion, are offered unless YANDEX_MAIL_ACTIONS narrows them (read gives a read-only mailbox); saving attachments and sending are off until YANDEX_MAIL_ACTIONS names save_attachment and send_message; once on, sending asks no per-message confirmation, also in cron and other unattended runs, and reaches any address unless YANDEX_MAIL_SEND_TO fences recipients; saved attachments go to Hermes' shared document cache, where other tools can read them, and are pruned after 24 hours; mail written by other people reaches the agent as tool output; uses Hermes' private tools.credential_files helper to map saved paths into sandboxes; no other endpoint, no telemetry, no shell access, no background process. Independent community plugin, not affiliated with Yandex.
entries.title: Yandex Mail
known_issues: Default tools include flagging, moving and deletion, including irreversible permanent deletion. Set YANDEX_MAIL_ACTIONS=read for read-only access, then restart Hermes. Saving attachments and sending require explicit save_attachment and send_message opt-ins.

Sending has no per-message confirmation, including unattended runs. YANDEX_MAIL_SEND_TO limits recipients; an explicit empty value refuses all recipients, while an absent value imposes no recipient restriction.

The login and app password go to imap.yandex.ru and smtp.yandex.ru over verified TLS, or to configured IMAP/SMTP hosts. Host overrides are not restricted to Yandex-owned servers. Message bodies, headers and filenames are untrusted tool output.

Saving writes to the current profile's shared temporary document cache, outside HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT; other Hermes tools can read it and cache cleanup can remove it. Saving needs POSIX directory operations and hard links.

Remote attachment paths use Hermes' private tools.credential_files.to_agent_visible_cache_path helper because no public replacement exists. A helper error fails saving and removes the file; a mapping miss may return a host path that remote tools cannot access. Multiplexed gateway reloads without an active secret scope can fail closed.

entries.name: year-wrapped
entries.description: Your year with your agent as shareable story cards. hermes year-wrapped (terminal) and /year-wrapped (every surface) read your own history and write 13 cards, 1080x1920, each in its own colour: persona (16 types from four axes: night or day, build or ask, terminal or chat, one model or many, with the real shares printed on the card), top tools, most used skill, manners and swear jar, night shift, longest chat, tokens processed, night crew (cron jobs and subagents), main model, projects started vs. archived, word of the year and a black and gold summary. Session titles are hidden unless --show-titles; client names can be excluded or shown under a code name (exclude_words, rename_words). No cost figures. English and German. Disclosure: no network calls, no model calls, standard library only. Reads state.db and, if present, projects.db of the active profile read only (mode=ro); never writes to them. Writes the cards as self-contained HTML (no scripts, no external assets) plus an index.html under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/year-wrapped/<period>/ or the folder given with --out. The terminal command hermes year-wrapped renders PNG files by starting a locally installed headless Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave or Playwright headless shell (or the one set in browser_path) as a subprocess that opens only the local card files; --no-png skips it, and /year-wrapped in a chat never starts a browser. Nothing is downloaded. No credentials, no hooks, no tools, no cron jobs, no background processes, no telemetry.

entries.name: you-should-know
entries.description: A side agent rereads the conversation while Hermes works on longer turns and surfaces the one thing you might have missed — a silent tradeoff, an unverified result, an irreversible action — as a dismissible note above the prompt. Disclosure — on tool-using turns in Desktop, CLI and TUI (configurable via `platforms`), sends up to 12,000 characters of the recent conversation, including clipped tool calls and results, to Hermes's configured auxiliary model up to five extra times per turn (45 s cooldown), which adds model cost; notes are stored in the plugin's own data folder.

entries.name: youtube-dock
entries.description: Open your signed-in YouTube Home recommendations and Shorts in the existing Hermes Desktop Browser beside your conversation, without pasting video URLs or launching an external browser. Desktop-only SDK launcher; no agent tools, hooks, middleware or API keys. Disclosure — explicit user clicks load YouTube and its normal service/CDN requests in the native Browser; this plugin does not read credentials, cookies, recommendations or watch history. No telemetry, shell commands, backend service or self-updater. Uses the native preview toggle (Hide for an already-open destination), not a dedicated PIP player.
entries.title: YouTube Dock
known_issues: v1.1.0 removes the rejected manual-setup beta completely. One-click Open preview/Hide is the only workflow; workspace pinning remains manual.
Activation attempts to remove only the obsolete manualPinGuide preference through plugin-scoped SDK storage. No old-value reads, replacement settings or clipboard access remain.

The host may reuse an existing Browser; pinning is visibility, not exclusive reservation. Native Windows Home/Shorts opening was checked; no fresh cross-platform, restart or long-running player certification is claimed.
Dedicated picture-in-picture is not included; uses the existing docked Browser.
Google sign-in and playback restrictions still apply; no browser-cookie import.
Original 1.0.0 launcher: Windows 11/Desktop 0.22.2 manually verified; macOS/Linux playback not manually tested.

entries.name: yuanbao
entries.description: Tencent Yuanbao messaging platform (DMs and group chats over Yuanbao's bot WebSocket, native media and stickers, DM/group access policies, cron home-channel delivery) plus the yuanbao toolset (yb_query_group_info, yb_query_group_members, yb_send_dm, yb_search_sticker, yb_send_sticker). Formerly built into Hermes core; existing users are migrated automatically. A Hermes Labs plugin: built by Nous Research, not supported, and likely not maintained going forward. Fixes from the community are welcome. Disclosure — messages, media and group member lists travel between Tencent's Yuanbao servers and your Hermes gateway using your own Yuanbao bot App ID and App Secret. The plugin also downloads image URLs that appear in replies or inbound messages, and its sign-token requests carry the Hermes version and an instance id.

entries.name: z-midi-console
entries.description: Universal MIDI control-surface builder — any USB/MIDI synth as live on-screen controls in Hermes Desktop, MIDI-learn bindings, multi-synth deck, spectrum analyzers, software mod matrix, .mid export, seven agent tools. Zero Python dependencies. Disclosure — The MIDI Console chat box sends your typed request (masked for key- or token-shaped text), a summary of the active device preset (names, MIDI channel, control labels, CC numbers, modulation lanes) and the last few chat-box turns to your Hermes model, or the model you pin under Settings → Models → Auxiliary → MIDI Console chat; device presets, recorded takes and a log of every MIDI message sent are stored under plugin-data/z-midi-console in your Hermes home (a pre-0.2 store at %LOCALAPPDATA%/z-midi-console is copied in once and left in place); the audio analyzers read the companion audio-strip plugin's state file; the MIDI engine is Windows-only.

entries.name: zalo-platform
entries.description: Zalo Bot Platform gateway adapter for Hermes Agent — relays messages between Zalo DMs/groups and the agent over the official Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com), long-polling or webhook mode. Adds slash commands and moderation. Zero extra dependencies (uses httpx, already a Hermes dependency). Production-tested on multiple Vietnamese deployments. Disclosure — connects to the third-party Zalo Bot API (bot-api.zaloplatforms.com) with your bot token; long-polling by default, or opt-in webhook mode with a listener on 127.0.0.1 by default that checks the X-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header; the setup wizard writes ZALO_* values to ~/.hermes/.env; group chat history is stored locally under <HERMES_HOME>/zalo-history.

entries.name: zalodesk
entries.description: Read, search and reply to Zalo chats, personal Zalo accounts and Zalo Official Accounts (OA), through the hosted ZaloDesk MCP: catch up on unread conversations, read and search messages, send replies, find customers by phone, labels and friend requests; and for the workspace owner, the team (Phân quyền): invite, change and remove staff, which Zalo accounts and chats each sees, their permissions, routing of new chats and calls, conversation assignment, which PC runs a company Zalo, and the AI credit each staff PC may spend. Everything runs within the user's ZaloDesk role (an employee sees only the chats assigned to them). Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + one skill); OAuth uses pinned mcp-remote@0.1.49 over npx stdio, so Node.js 20.18.1+ and npm are required. Disclosure — send_message sends real Zalo messages from the user's account, the team tools add, change and remove people's access, and set_ai_credit lets a staff PC spend from the owner's AI wallet; the package marks the zalodesk server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every tool the server does not annotate as read-only and refuses them in cron and headless runs. Every tool call goes to app.zalodesk.com; sign-in runs npx mcp-remote@0.1.49 from the npm registry, which stores its OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth. The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha.

entries.name: zambo-receipts
entries.description: Verifiable receipts for Hermes Agent sessions. Lifecycle hooks journal every tool call in a session to Zambo (zambo.dev) as it happens, and when the session ends the plugin wraps it into an AER-1 verifiable receipt that anyone can open and check at a public zambo.dev/run link. Receipt pages are public: anyone with the link can read them, and the summary and goal text passed to zambo_wrap_session is published on the receipt page. Adds three tools (zambo_verify_receipt, zambo_wrap_session, zambo_session_status), a /receipt slash command, and a bundled skill. Disclosure: while enabled, the plugin makes network calls to zambo.dev (the configured MCP endpoint) carrying, per tool call, the tool name, duration, result size and a SHA-256 hash of the result; result text (truncated to 4,000 characters) is sent only when journal_results is set to full; at session finalize (/new, quit, gateway reset) it publishes a receipt as a public zambo.dev/run page, including the summary and goal text passed to zambo_wrap_session; failed entries buffer in a bounded outbox under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/zambo-receipts/ with a stable per-install caller id; no credentials.

entries.name: zaprite
entries.description: Get paid from a Hermes chat. One checkoutUrl for card, bank, Lightning, on-chain bitcoin, and stablecoins, then re-fetch until Paid. Disclosure — every call goes to api.zaprite.com (or the base_url you set in plugin config) with the key you put in the Hermes secret store (ZAPRITE_API_KEY), read on each call and never logged; payment, order, invoice, quote, charge, ticket, webhook, contact-delete and dashboard-handoff writes happen only after you approve that exact call, while contact create/update run without a prompt; writes are refused in cron and while /zaprite kill is active; it registers no webhook of its own, and its only background option is an opt-in daily read-only digest automation that runs nothing unless you add it; payment truth comes from re-fetching the order, because a Zaprite webhook is id-only and unsigned. It cannot reach connections, payment-link creation, POS, events, recurring invoices, refunds, or branding, because those have no API.
entries.title: Zaprite
known_issues: Sandbox org for a first payment (no real money). A live org key opens real checkouts. The plugin cannot switch orgs.
Webhooks are id-only and unsigned. Re-fetch the order. A webhook is not a payment.

No Zaprite API for connections, checkout edits, payment-link create, POS create, event create, recurring invoices, refunds, or branding write. Logo, accent color, and display name are Settings → Profile. API invoices inherit them. zaprite_bridge_handoff gap branding_profile opens that page, not Connections or Checkouts.

Doctor and zaprite_bridge_handoff build dashboard links with org_links(orgId). Once an orgId is known those links use /org/{orgId}/. A first run or a missing key still uses /org/default/ until an orgId is stored.

entries.name: zedmode
entries.description: Every Hermes Desktop conversation in one stack that recedes into the screen, ordered like an inbox: failed, needs you, working, unread, pinned, then the rest. Answer approvals and questions on the card, hold a thread beside the stack, start or branch a chat without leaving, switch a live chat's model, and tune the 3D live. Desktop plugin (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface) plus a read-only dashboard backend that reads the session list from state.db. No network, no credentials, no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — reads every session's titles, prompts and tool-call summaries from state.db read-only for its stack (cache in the profile's plugin-data folder); its Desktop page can send prompts, answer approval and clarify requests you click, rename/branch chats and switch a live chat's model; the backend calls Hermes' private model resolver (`hermes_cli.model_switch.switch_model`) to explain unusable models, which can query your configured provider's model list.
entries.title: Zed Mode
known_issues: Early beta, tested on Hermes v0.23.0 on macOS only.
Pins and stored (not live) transcripts need the Python half enabled under plugins.enabled; without it the stack still works for live chats.

entries.name: zerofactory
entries.description: 24/7 AI multi-agent software engineering factory and durable SQLite Kanban board. Flexible triage with Grill Me clarification and EGM sequential spec audit, isolated Git worktrees, deterministic precommit pipeline, thematic continuous review, autonomous self-healing recovery, and Mem0 vector memory. Disclosure — once you turn on auto_start_dispatcher or start the dispatcher from the dashboard it runs background worker subprocesses using Hermes agent profiles (zf-orchestrator, zf-goldfish, zf-builder, zf-reviewer) inside dedicated Git worktrees that push branches and open pull requests on boards' repos, and gives a stuck task one automatic zf-orchestrator recovery run before handing it to you; workers use the profiles' normal approval policy unless you enable allow_unattended_approvals (which passes --yolo and --accept-hooks); mounts a web dashboard at /zerofactory with an embedded SQLite database; workers run each project's .zerofactory/precommit.sh checks; `report-bug` records internal defects locally, and with auto_create_github_issues on (off by default) or --create-issue it files a public GitHub issue on hotcode-dev/zerofactory through your gh login containing the task title and redacted error output; optional Mem0/Qdrant repository memory (off by default) sends memory text to the LLM endpoint you configure.

entries.name: zeromem
entries.description: Local memory that keeps every message word for word in one SQLite file. Storing and searching make no LLM calls and cost zero tokens. Rust core, with a one-command import of your existing Hermes history. Disclosure — installs the author's compiled `zeromem` Rust extension from PyPI and, on first run, downloads a ~130 MB embedding model from Hugging Face into `<HERMES_HOME>/memory/zeromem-models` (set `use_model: false` to stay offline); stores every user and assistant message as plain text in `<HERMES_HOME>/memory/zeromem.db` and recalls them verbatim into later turns across all sessions of the profile (all chats and senders on a gateway); the agent can permanently delete a past session's stored turns.

entries.name: ziztu
entries.description: Plan, price and make AI micro dramas and anime episodes with the same characters in every shot through the hosted Ziztu MCP server (30 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://getziztu.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE through Hermes' MCP OAuth flow), plus four skills: micro drama series writing, viral faceless reels, YouTube Shorts and TikToks, faceless YouTube videos, and cinematic depth for image and video prompts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted connector: every tool call sends prompts, scripts and project data to getziztu.com under the user's Ziztu account (OAuth sign-in through Hermes' MCP OAuth flow). Tools that make frames, clips, music or scripts spend that account's credits (each takes max_credits, accepts dry_run, and the server asks for confirm above 5,000 credits); the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every call that is not read-only. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned commit. The skills ship four standard-library Python helper scripts the agent may run: three read local text files (episode scripts, season grids, prompts) and one (split_season.py) writes per-episode .fountain files into a folder the agent names; no network calls, install scripts, bundled credentials, background processes or telemetry.
entries.title: Ziztu AI video studio
entries.capability_summary: ziztu (community, maintained by 0xnirlin) Plan, price and make AI micro dramas and anime episodes with the same characters in every shot through the hosted Ziztu MCP server (30 tools, Streamable HTTP at https://getziztu.com/mcp, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE through Hermes' MCP OAuth flow), plus four skills: micro drama series writing, viral faceless reels, YouTube Shorts and TikToks, faceless YouTube videos, and cinematic depth for image and video prompts. Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted connector: every tool call sends prompts, scripts and project data to getziztu.com under the user's Ziztu account (OAuth sign-in through Hermes' MCP OAuth flow). Tools that make frames, clips, music or scripts spend that account's credits (each takes max_credits, accepts dry_run, and the server asks for confirm above 5,000 credits); the package marks the server untrusted, so Hermes asks before every call that is not read-only. The tool list is served by the remote server at run time and is not covered by the pinned commit. The skills ship four standard-library Python helper scripts the agent may run: three read local text files (episode scripts, season grids, prompts) and one (split_season.py) writes per-episode .fountain files into a folder the agent names; no network calls, install scripts, bundled credentials, background processes or telemetry. This plugin declares no tools, hooks, middleware, or env vars. Requires Hermes >=0.22.5.

entries.name: zolva
entries.description: Read Zolva's trading agents on Robinhood Chain (tokenized US stocks and ETFs, ETH and BTC, and Lighter perps) through Zolva's hosted MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, no API key): published agents with their return against simply holding the same markets, every hourly buy, sell, short, cover or hold with the agent's own reason, market prices and recent trades. Two skills are bundled: zolva-agents for questions, and zolva-trade-watch, an hourly cron job that sends an agent's new trades to the user's chat and stays silent otherwise. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/), configuration and Markdown only. Disclosure: hosted-only connector with no local code; every tool call goes to Zolva's MCP server at zolvaagent.app/mcp (60 requests a minute per IP). All five tools are read only and annotated readOnlyHint; none signs, sends, spends or reads a key, and the package marks the server untrusted. The data is paper trading (virtual money at real prices), not investment advice. Tool results enter the session context and so reach the user's model provider. The tool list comes from Zolva's server at run time, so the pinned commit doesn't cover it.

entries.name: zotero
entries.description: Research with your own Zotero library: search it, read your PDF highlights and full text, cite with Zotero's citation engine (any CSL style, BibTeX/RIS export), add papers by DOI/arXiv with PDFs, and check a draft's citations against the library. Reads Zotero desktop's local API on loopback; zotero_add alone writes to the library and calls Crossref/arXiv. No telemetry, no credentials.
entries.title: Zotero Research
known_issues: Requires Zotero 7+ desktop running with Settings -> Advanced -> 'Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero' enabled.
zotero_add saves into the collection currently selected in Zotero.
